# Matsya-purana

## Chapter 1

## \|\| 1.1 \|\|

*pātālādutpatiṣṇor makaravasatayo yasya pucchābhighātād ūrdhvaṃ brahmāṇḍakhaṇḍavyatikaravihitavyatyayenāpatanti \|*  
*viṣṇormatsyāvatāre sakalavasumatīmaṇḍalaṃ vyaśnuvānās*  
*tasyāsyodīritānāṃ dhvanir apaharatād aśriyaṃ vaḥ śrutīnām \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. May the loins feet of Bhava, who shook the diggajas at the time of His (lance, disperse all obstacles.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — The sacred word “Om” is formed by the letters o, u, m. Of these, “a” represents Vishnu, “u” Shiva, “m” Brahma. Pranava is, therefore, the symbol of the sacred Trinity.

Note. — Bhava is a name of the God Shiva. Tandava is a particular kind of dance of which Shiva is very fond. Diggajas: It is laid down in the puranic allegory that the universe lies balanced on the tusks of ten elephants- each elephant supporting a quarter.

## \|\| 1.2 \|\|

*nārāyaṇaṃ namaskṛtya naraṃ caiva narottamam \|*  
*devīṃ sarasvatīṃ caiva tato jayam udīrayet \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. May the words of Lord Vibhu, embodied in the Vedas and uttered by His Matsya-Puranam, in which incarnation, at the time of His sallying forth from the region of the patala, the blow of His tail caused the seven seas to intermingle with the high heavens and then to fall down, spattering the sphere of the earth, steal away all your evil!

**Комментарий:**

Note. — Brahmanda, literally, means the Egg of the Creator, and the word, as it stands, applies to all the regions— both upper and lower. In the above Shloka Brahmanda is coupled with the word Urddha, which means upper. Here the complete word is Urddha Brahmanda which means the upper regions. Matsyavatara is the incarnation of Lord Vishnu in the form of a fish. The Merciful manifests Himself in different forms, whenever Ho finds it necessary — (1) To educate the world in the performance of its manifold duties which, in spite of their being incorporated in the works of Divine revelation, very often remain incomprehensible; (2) To save the world from willful neglect of duty

Compare: —

Old order changed yielding -place to new, God fulfills Himself in many ways, Best one good custom should corrupt the world”

To deal with the doubts that are very often raised on the theory of incarnation, It would be necessary to make copious reference to Vedanta, Upanishads and Nyaya, and to add exhaustive commentaries on those dogmatically aphorisms which would swell the bulk of the Purana. I will therefore confine myself to very brief notes on most Important Items. The necessity of Matsyavatara will later on become clear by going through this Purana. Shruti means the Vedas, that are regarded by the Hindus to be the words of Divine revelation.

## \|\| 1.3 \|\|

*ajo 'pi yaḥ kriyāyogān nārāyaṇa iti smṛtaḥ \|*  
*triguṇāya trivedāya namas tasmai svayambhuve \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Matsyapurana which is the dispeller of all ignorance, should be read after saluting Narayana, Nara, Narottama, Devi Sarasvati.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — Narayana, Narottama, etc., are all analogous expressions, and apply to the Supreme Being, who is omnificent, omnipotent, omnipresent and omniscient. Words cannot describe Him or His glory.

Compare: — …

## \|\| 1.4 \|\|

*sūtamekāgramāsīnaṃ naimiṣāraṇyavāsinaḥ \|*  
*munayo dīrghasattrānte papracchur dīrghasaṃhitām \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. I salute Lord Brahma who, though unborn, manifests Himself for the sake of creation, and is known under different epithets, viz. — Narayana, Triguna

**Комментарий:**

Note, — Trigunas are Sattva, Rajas and Tamas, Maya is the resultant of Trigunas. When Maya combines with any particle of Omnipresent Parabrahma, that particle is known as Brahma, Triveda means the three Vedas, Big, Yajus and Saman. The meter which is prosodical, but cannot be chanted, is called Rik, and Rig-Veda is full of such meters. The metre which is neither prosodical nor can be chanted, is called Yajus and, Yajurveda is full of such metres. The metres that can be chanted are known as Sama, and therefore the Veda containing such metres is called Sama-Veda. Strictly speaking, therefore, there are only three Vedas, The sage Vasistha collected several, metres of the abovementioned three Vedas dealing with Ayurveda and Shantikarma, etc., and compiled the Atharva-Veda, which now forms the fourth Veda?, The Vedas are the works of Divine revelation, and are held very sacred by the Hindus. Lord Brahma is the chief revealer of the sacred Vedas. Now, with the above verse ends the introductory verses, after which the subject matter of the Parana commences. Before proceeding further, something must be said about mangalacharana. Mangala is of three kinds, Namaskaratmak-mangala is that in which there is salutation to some Deity as in “Shree Ganeshanamah” and “Om Namo Bhagavate Vasudevaya”, which occur in the very beginning of the Purana (2) Vastunirdeshatmakamangala is that in which there is some clue to the subject matter of the work, following it. (B) Ashirvadatamkamangala is that in which some Deity Is invoked to shower Its blessings on somebody.

The couplet “Prachand Tandavatope”, etc., contains a prayer to Lord Siva which shows that later on there will be something about the annihilation of the universe. Shiva Is Shanharkarta. The stanza “Patalidyutpattishwo, &c., contains a prayer to Lord Vishnu which shows that there will also be a description- of the Sthiti. Vishnu is Shantikarta. The above two stanzas are both Vastunirdeshatmaka and Ashirvadatmaka. The couplet “ajopi” &c. contains salutations to Lord Svayambhu, i.e., Brahma, which shows that the Purana contains a history of creation also. Brahma is Srishtikarta. This couplet is Namaskaratmaka as well as Vastu Nirdeshatmaka.

We understand from the Mangalacharana that Matsya Purana mainly deals with the history of —

(1) The creation of the Universe by Brahma, the Creator!

(2) The annihilation of the Universe by Shiva, the destroyer!

(3) The preservation of the Universe from total annihilation by Vishnu the savior. Brahma, Vishnu and Shiva are the different manifestations of the one and the same Supreme Being.

## \|\| 1.5-6 \|\|

*pravṛttāsu purāṇīṣu dharmyāsu lalitāsu ca \|*  
*kathāsu śaunakādyās tu abhinandya muhurmuhuḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*kathitāni purāṇāni yānyasmākaṃ tvayānagha \|*  
*tānyevāmṛtakalpāni śrotum icchāmahe punaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. Once upon a time, the inhabitants of Naimisharanya, at the close of a long sacrifice, began to relate to one another pious, charming stories from different Puranas. The great sage, Suta, was present in that assembly, Shaunaka and other sages who were also there on that occasion, after complimenting Suta on his deep lore, said: —

“O sinless one, we wish to hear again the very same nectar-like stories of the Puranas which have been recited to us by you.”

**Комментарий:**

Note. — Naimisharanya is modern Nimkhar-Misrikh in the Sitapur district, Oudh.

## \|\| 1.7-8 \|\|

*kathaṃ sasarja bhagavaṃl lokanāthaścarācaram \|*  
*kasmācca bhagavān viṣṇur matsyarūpatvam āśritaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*bhairavatvaṃ bhavasyāpi purāritvaṃ ca kena hi \|*  
*kasya hetoḥ kapālitvaṃ jagāma vṛṣabhadhvajaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8. “Tell us please, bow Brahma created the Universe, and for what reason Vishnu adopted the form of a fish. We are also anxious to know why Shiva took the goblet of human skull, why He is called Purari, and how Bhava, the cause of our prosperity, came to be known as Bhairava? O, Suta! be gracious enough to relate ail this exhaustively, for we never I feel satiated with listening to your sweet narrations, as one is not with nectar.”

**Комментарий:**

Note. — “Bhava” means the giver of prosperity. This is a synonym of God Shiva.

“Bhairava” means terrific or one who causes fear. This term applies to a form of God Shiva.

Kapali literally means one who carries a human skull. This expression also applies to Shiva.

“Vrishabhadhvaja” means one who has a bull, for his conveyance, Shiva rides the bull; therefore, this term denotes Shiva.

## \|\| 1.9 \|\|

*sarvam etat samācakṣva sūta vistaraśaḥ kramāt \|*  
*tvadvākyenāmṛtasyeva na tṛptiriha jāyate \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Suta said: — “Hear, now, O, Brahmanas, the sacred Matsyapurana which was revealed by Lord Vishnu in the form of a fish.”

**Комментарий:**

Note: — Now follows the narration of the Purana.

## \|\| 1.10-11 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*puṇyaṃ pavitram āuṣyam idānīṃ śṛṇuta dvijāḥ \|*  
*mātsyaṃ purāṇamakhilaṃ yadjagāda gadādharaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*purā rājā manur nāma cīrṇavān vipulaṃ tapaḥ \|*  
*putre rājyaṃ samāropya kṣamāvān ravinandanaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

10-11. In ancient times (Vaivasvata) Manu, the Merciful, the first king of the Solar dynasty, after making over his kingdom to his son, devoted himself to rigid asceticism. On a summit of the Malaya mountain, the devout austerities of that resolute hero, who was adorned with spiritual knowledge, and whose equilibrium of mind was just the same in adversity as in prosperity, were crowned with the attainment of transcendent yoga (that is, union with the Deity.)

**Комментарий:**

Note. — “Ravinandan” means the Son of the Sun.

Vaivasvata Mann was the offspring of the God film from Sajna the daughter of Lord Kuvera. He was the founder of the Solar race, of Kshatriyas.

Note. — Malaya is a range of mountains in Southern India abounding In sandal trees. It is to the west of Malabar.

Samaduhkhasukhavira means the hero who is neither overwhelmed by misfortunes nor is carried away by prosperity, but remains firm under all circumstances. Such a bent of mind is not common. Only those few, who resign themselves to His will and concentrate their minds on the sacred object of their devotion, can remain so firm-minded. Devotion to God alone leads to such a bliss.

It points out to the soul the pitfalls of life and the mundane unrealities. It takes away the shroud of illusion and places the soul on the pinnacle of celestial glory where eternal peace and contentment reign. Bhakti or Yoga begets such knowledge.

The King Vaivasvata Mann, inspite of his worldly glories, was, not negligent of the life after death. Like many ancient kings, the first item of his duty was to acquire this jnana, and he became Raja-Rishi. It is therefore no wonder that a Raja-Rishi, like the King Vaivasvata Manu should have been so firm.

## \|\| 1.12 \|\|

*malayasyaikadeśe tu sarvātmaguṇasaṃyutaḥ \|*  
*samaduḥkhasukho vīraḥ prāptavān yogam uttamam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. After a period of a million of years of continued asceticism, Lord Brahma, became pleased towards him, and told him to ask for a boon,

**Комментарий:**

Note: — Kamalasana is another name of God Brahma, It literally means, one who has a lotus to sit upon, it is laid down in the puranic allegory that at the time of creation, a lotus with Brahma sitting on it, springs from the navel of Vishnu.

## \|\| 1.13-14 \|\|

*babhūva varadaś cāsya varṣāutaśate gate \|*  
*varaṃ vṛṇīṣva provāca prītaḥ sa kamalāsanaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*evamukto 'bravīd rājā praṇamya sa pitāmaham \|*  
*ekam evāham icchāmi tvatto varamanuttamam \|\| 14 \|\|*

13-14. Having been thus addressed (by Brahma), the king, after saluting Him, said: “Lord! I have only one boon to beg of you, which is above all other boons. May I have power, sufficient for the protection of the whole creation, moveable; and immoveable, when the hour of Pralaya will come?”

**Комментарий:**

Note: — “Pitamaha” means paternal grand-father.

Brahma is the Creator of the Universe; He is therefore called Pitamaha.

Note: — Pralaya is chiefly, of kinds, viz. (1) Khanda pralaya, la which there l« a partial dissolution, and (2) Maha-pralaya, in which there is a total dissolution.

In this Purana there is a mention of Khandapralaya. Mark the boon sought by the illustrious sovereign of the Solar race. This shows how selfless, highly virtuous and righteous the kings in ancient times were.

## \|\| 1.15 \|\|

*bhūtagrāmasya sarvasya sthāvarasya carasya ca \|*  
*bhaveyaṃ rakṣaṇāyālaṃ pralaye samupasthite \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Lord Brahma, the Soul of the Universe, after granting the prayer of the king (in the following words, “Be it so”), disappeared then and there, and the Devas profusely showered a rain of flowers from, the ethereal regions.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — Pushpavrishti. The Devas showered flowers on the king to express their unbounded pleasure and appreciation of his highest righteousness.

## \|\| 1.16 \|\|

*evamastviti viśvātmā tatraivāntaradhīyata \|*  
*puṣpavṛṣṭiḥ sumahatī khātpapāta surārpitā \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. One day, in his hermitage, when the king was making a libation of water to the manes of his deceased ancestors, a carp (a small fish) fell into his hands along with the water.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — Tarpana is a libation of water to the manes of the deceased ancestors which a Hindu is in duty bound to perform regularly.

\[Consult “The Daily Practice of the Hindus” by Rai Bahadur Shri Chandra Vidyarnava.\]

Papata, i.e., fell from the king's vessel out of which he was pouring out water for libation.

Shaphari is a very small variety of fish called carp. It is very tiny and always restless, Eastern poets very often employ it in their similes, in their description of the movements of beautiful eyes.

## \|\| 1.17-18 \|\|

*kadācidāśrame tasya kurvataḥ pitṛtarpaṇam \|*  
*papāta pāṇyor upari śapharī jalasaṃyutā \|\| 17 \|\|*

*dṛṣṭvā tacchapharīrūpaṃ sa dayālurmahīpatiḥ \|*  
*rakṣaṇāyākarodyatnaṃ sa tasminkarakodare \|\| 18 \|\|*

17-18. On seeing that tiny fish, the merciful king, out of compassion, wanted to preserve it and put it into his water jar. That tiny fish, in course of a day and night, grew into the form of a large fish, measuring sixteen fingers in length, and (feeling uncomfortable inside the water jar where it was placed by the king), cried for deliverance.

## \|\| 1.19-20 \|\|

*ahorātreṇa caikena ṣoḍaśāṅgulavistṛtaḥ \|*  
*so 'bhavanmatsyarūpeṇa pāhi pāhīti cābravīt \|\| 19 \|\|*

*sa tamādāya maṇike prākṣipadjalacāriṇam \|*  
*tatrāpi caikarātreṇa hastatrayam avardhata \|\| 20 \|\|*

19-20. The king took it out of the water jar and put it in a large pitcher but there also, in course of a night, it grew three hands in length. “I am at your mercy, come to my succour.” The king, again hearing these cries of the fish took it out of the pitcher and deposited it in a well. Later on, the well also proved insufficient. The king then accommodated it in a tank.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — Sahasrakiranatmaja, the Son of the Sun, i.e., king Vaivasvata Manu. Sahasrakirana means the Sun.

## \|\| 1.22-25 \|\|

*tataḥ sa kūpe taṃ matsyaṃ prāhiṇod ravinandanaḥ \|*  
*yadā na māti tatrāpi kūpe matsyaḥ sarovare \|\| 22 \|\|*

*kṣipto 'sau pṛthutāmāgāt punar yojanasaṃmitām \|*  
*tatrāpyāha punar dīnaḥ pāhi pāhi nṛpottama \|\| 23 \|\|*

*tataḥ sa manunā kṣipto gaṅgāyāmapyavardhata \|*  
*yadā tadā samudre taṃ prākṣipanmedinīpatiḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*yadā samudramakhilaṃ vyāpyāsau samupasthitaḥ \|*  
*tadā prāha manurbhītaḥ ko 'pi tvamasureśvaraḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

22-25. In the tank, again, the fish grew a yojana (eight miles) in length, and again appealed to the king, in a plaintive tone, to help it out of the tank. Then the king put the fish in the Gauges and, finding that it increased there too, he placed it in the ocean. The fish went on increasing and increasing in bulk, until it very nearly filled the vast expanse of the great ocean. The king, seeing this, was awe-stricken and said, “Are you the chief of the Asuras? Or are you Vasudeva; who else has such an extraordinary power to assume such a tremendously; big form extending to sixteen, hundred miles?”

**Комментарий:**

Note. — “Asura” means a demon, “Ishwara” literally means master.

## \|\| 1.26 \|\|

*athavā vāsudevastvam anya īdṛkkathaṃ bhavet \|*  
*yojanāutaviṃśatyā kasya tulyaṃ bhavedvapuḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. I have come to know you, O, Keshava! You are puzzling me in the form of a fish. I bow down to You, O, Hrishikesha, Jagannatha, Jagaddhama.” \[these are all different names of God.\]

## \|\| 1.27-33 \|\|

*jñātastvaṃ matsyarūpeṇa māṃ khedayasi keśava \|*  
*hṛṣīkeśa jagannātha jagaddhāma namo 'stu te \|\| 27 \|\|*

*evamuktaḥ sa bhagavān matsyarūpī janārdanaḥ \|*  
*sādhu sādhviti covāca samyagjñātas tvayānagha \|\| 28 \|\|*

*acireṇaiva kālena medinī medinīpate \|*  
*bhaviṣyati jale magnā saśailavanakānanā \|\| 29 \|\|*

*naur iyaṃ sarvadevānāṃ nikāyena vinirmitā \|*  
*mahājīvanikāyasya rakṣaṇārthaṃ mahīpate \|\| 30 \|\|*

*svedāṇḍajodbhido ye vai ye ca jīvā jarāujāḥ \|*  
*asyāṃ nidhāya sarvāṃs tān anāthān pāhi suvrata \|\| 31 \|\|*

*yugāntavātābhihatā yadā bhavati naur nṛpa \|*  
*śṛṅge 'sminmama rājendra tademāṃ saṃyamiṣyasi \|\| 32 \|\|*

*tato layānte sarvasya sthāvarasya carasya ca \|*  
*prajāpatistvaṃ bhavitā jagataḥ pṛthivīpate \|\| 33 \|\|*

27-33. Being thus addressed, Bhagavana Janardana, in the form of a fish, complimented him, and said: “O Spotless One, I have been truly known by you. In a few days time, O King, the Universe shall be deluged with water, along with the mountains and forests. The Devas have made this boat to rescue the creation from such a calamity, placing in it svedajas, andajas, udbhijas and jarayujas. O, King! You take charge of this boat and help the distressed at the time of the impending danger. When you find the boat in danger of being blown away by the strong gusts of wind, tie it to my horn. By rescuing the afflicted from such an awful misfortune, you will be rendering a great paternal service to the creation. And, O, blessed sovereign! You shall reign for one Manvantara, from the beginning of the Kritayuga, and shall be venerated by the Devas.”

## Chapter 2

## \|\| 2.1-2 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*evamukto manustena papraccha madhusūdanam \|*  
*bhagavankiyadbhirvarṣair bhaviṣyatyantarakṣayaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*sattvāni ca kathaṃ nātha rakṣiṣye madhusūdana \|*  
*tvayā saha punaryogaḥ kathaṃ vā bhavitā mama \|\| 2 \|\|*

1-2. Suta, continuing his narration, said, that, on hearing such words of the Lord, the king begged Him to reveal to him in how many years the time of destruction was likely to come. The king also entreated the Lord to point out to him the means of saving the creation from such a distress, and to let him know when he would again be fortunate enough to meet Him face to face.

## \|\| 2.3-4 \|\|

*matsya uvāca*  
*adyaprabhṛtyanāvṛṣṭir bhaviṣyati mahītale \|*  
*yāvadvarṣaśataṃ sāgraṃ durbhikṣam aśubhāvaham \|\| 3 \|\|*

*tato 'lpasattvakṣayadā raśmayaḥ sapta dāruṇāḥ \|*  
*saptasapterbhaviṣyanti prataptāṅgāravarṣiṇaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

3- 4. The fish replied that from that day there would be no rain for a hundred years, and the universe would be overtaken by a dire famine. After that, all the inferior beings of the universe would be scorched to death by the seven ordinary rays of the sun which shall become seven times more powerful.

## \|\| 2.5 \|\|

*aurvānalo 'pi vikṛtiṃ gamiṣyati ugakṣaye \|*  
*viṣāgniścāpi pātālāt saṃkarṣaṇamukhacyutaḥ \|*  
*bhavasyāpi lalāṭotthas tṛtīyanayanānalaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. In addition to all that, the subterranean fire would shoot out, Shesha, from hi abode in the lower regions, would send forth venomous flames from his thousand months, and a furious fire would emerge from the third eye of Shiva.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — It is said in the puranic allegory that the universe rests on the head of a thousand-hooded serpent which is more popularly known as Shesha.

The fire emitting from the third eye of Shiva. He has a third eye in the forehead which always remains shut. The Lord opens that third eye only on occasions of anger, and necessarily at the time of destruction. As soon as the third eye is opened, all objects falling within its range are reduced to ashes, as it sends forth a big flash of fire.

## \|\| 2.6-7 \|\|

*trijagannirdahan kṣobhaṃ sameṣyati mahāmune \|*  
*evaṃ dagdhā mahī sarvā yadā syādbhasmasaṃnibhā \|\| 6 \|\|*

*ākāśamūṣmaṇā taptaṃ bhaviṣyati paraṃtapa \|*  
*tataḥ sadevanakṣatraṃ jagadyāsyati saṃkṣayam \|\| 7 \|\|*

6-7. Thus the three worlds would be crumbled to ashes by the combined fury of all those various fires. The sky, with all the stars and planets, would also be destroyed by the heat thus originated.

## \|\| 2.8-14 \|\|

*saṃvarto bhīmanādaśca droṇaścaṇḍo balāhakaḥ \|*  
*vidyutpatākaḥ śoṇastu saptaite layavāridāḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*agniprasvedasambhūtāḥ plāvayiṣyanti medinīm \|*  
*samudrāḥ kṣobhamāgatya caikatvena vyavasthitāḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*etadekārṇavaṃ sarvaṃ kariṣyanti jagattrayam \|*  
*vedanāvamimāṃ gṛhya sattvabījāni sarvaśaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*āropya radjuyogena matpradattena suvrata \|*  
*saṃyamya nāvaṃ macchṛṅge matsyabhāvābhirakṣitaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*ekaḥ sthāsyasi deveṣu dagdheṣvapi paraṃtapa \|*  
*somasūryāvahaṃ brahmā caturlokasamanvitaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*narmadā ca nadī puṇyā mārkaṇḍeyo mahānṛṣiḥ \|*  
*bhavo vedāḥ purāṇāni vidyābhiḥ sarvatovṛtam \|\| 13 \|\|*

*tvayā sārdhamidaṃ viśvaṃ sthāsyatyantarasaṃkṣaye \|*  
*evamekārṇave jāte cākṣuṣāntarasaṃkṣaye \|\| 14 \|\|*

8-14. Then the seven destructive clouds viz. — Samvarta, Bhimanada, Drona, Chanda, Balahaka, Vidyutpataka and Sona, would spring up from the vapors arising out of such a heat, and would rain in torrents till all the seas become united into one great mass. In fact the whole earth would be covered with one vast expanse of water, then get bold of that yonder boat and put the seed of creation and the sacred Vedas in it. After that, fasten the boat to my born by means of this rope that I give you, and then the contents of the barge will be saved by ray glory.” O, Pious One! when everything will be destroyed, your good-self, the moon, the sun, myself, Brahma, the sacred river Narmada, the great sage Markandeya, the sacred Vedas, the Puranas, the God Shiva, the various sciences, will alone be saved, and the reign of king Chakshusha Manu shall terminate with the coming partial dissolution.

## \|\| 2.15 \|\|

*vedānpravartayiṣyāmi tvatsargādau mahīpate \|*  
*evamuktvā sa bhagavāṃs tatraivāntaradhīyata \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. At the beginning of the re-creation of the Universe which would follow the period of destruction, I shall propagate the Vedic knowledge.” So saying, He suddenly vanished away.

## \|\| 2.16 \|\|

*manur apyāsthito yogaṃ vāsudevaprasādajam \|*  
*abhyasan yāvad ābhūta-samplavaṃ pūrvasūcitam \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. The king, till the time of dissolution, of which intimation was given to him Lord Vasudeva, engaged himself in the practice of Yoga.

## \|\| 2.17-19 \|\|

*kāle yathokte saṃjāte vāsudevamukhodgate \|*  
*śṛṅgī prādurbabhūvātha matsyarūpī janārdanaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*bhujaṃgo radjurūpeṇa manoḥ pārśvamupāgamat \|*  
*bhūtānsarvānsamākṛṣya yogenāropya dharmavit \|\| 18 \|\|*

*bhujaṃgaradjvā matsyasya śṛṅge nāvamayojayat \|*  
*uparyupasthitastasyāḥ praṇipatya janārdanam \|\| 19 \|\|*

17-19. At the commencement of dissolution, the Lord appeared again in the form of horned fish. At the same time, Shesha, the Serpent King, appeared before the King Vaivasvata Manu in the shape of a rope, and the king, through his Yogic power, collected together all living beings and put them in the boat. And, after fastening the boat to the horn of the fish, by means of the rope, the king saluted the Lord and got into it.

## \|\| 2.20-21 \|\|

*ābhūtasamplave tasminn atīte yogaśāyinā \|*  
*pṛṣṭena manunā proktaṃ purāṇaṃ matsyarūpiṇā \|*  
*tadidānīṃ pravakṣyāmi śṛṇudhvamṛṣisattamāḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*yadbhavadbhiḥ purā pṛṣṭaḥ sṛṣṭyādikamahaṃ dvijāḥ \|*  
*tad evaikārṇave tasmin manuḥ papraccha keśavam \|\| 21 \|\|*

20-21. Suta said, “O sages! Hear the history of creation, &c., which you have asked me to narrate. I shall now proceed to relate it in the words of the Lord which were addressed to the King Vaivasvata Manu.”

## \|\| 2.22-24 \|\|

*manuruvāca*  
*utpattiṃ pralayaṃ caiva vaṃśānmanvantarāṇi ca \|*  
*vaṃśyānucaritaṃ caiva bhuvanasya ca vistaram \|\| 22 \|\|*

*dānadharmavidhiṃ caiva śrāddhakalpaṃ ca śāśvatam \|*  
*varṇāśramavibhāgaṃ ca tatheṣṭāpūrtasaṃjñitam \|\| 23 \|\|*

*devatānāṃ pratiṣṭhādi yaccānyadvidyate bhuvi \|*  
*tatsarvaṃ vistareṇa tvaṃ dharmaṃ vyākhyātumarhasi \|\| 24 \|\|*

22-24. Manu entreated the Lord to relate to him, how the dissolution and the creation of the universe took place, how the generations of mankind came into being, the meaning of Manvantara, the biographies of eminent men, the expanse of the universe, the ways of charity, the path of duty, the precepts of shraddha, the divisions of Varna and Ashrama, the ways of sacrificial rites, the greatness of the Devas, etc.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — Shraddha is an act of devotion to the pitris and manes which every Hindu has to perform by means of certain prescribed rites, after which food, etc., is distributed to the Brahmanas.

“Varna” moans tribe, caste, “Ashrama” the four kinds of religious order, viz., (1) Brahmacharya or the student life, (2) Grihastha or the householder’s life, (3) Vanaprastha or the anchorite’s life, (4) Sannyasa or hermit’s life.

## \|\| 2.25-27 \|\|

*matsya uvāca*  
*mahāpralayakālānta etadāsīttamomayam \|*  
*prasuptamiva cātarkyam aprajñātamalakṣaṇam \|\| 25 \|\|*

*avijñeyamavijñātaṃ jagat sthāsnu cariṣṇu ca \|*  
*tataḥ svayambhūr avyaktaḥ prabhavaḥ puṇyakarmaṇām \|\| 26 \|\|*

*vyañjayannetadakhilaṃ prādurāsīt tamonudaḥ \|*  
*yo 'tīndriyaḥ paro vyaktād aṇur jyāyān sanātanaḥ \|*  
*nārāyaṇa iti khyātaḥ sa ekaḥ svayam udbabhau \|\| 27 \|\|*

25-27. Matsya said that during the period of Great Dissolution the universe was enveloped in darkness and was in a slate of trance, as it were, inconceivable, still, and indefinable. In that state of unimaginable and indescribable trance, appeared Lord Svayambhu, who is also known as Narayana, owing to His omnipresence in Sthula-Sharira, made His appearance to create the universe.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — “Sthula-Sharira” is corporeal body, i.e., what is visible to the naked eye.

## \|\| 2.28-30 \|\|

*yaḥ śarīrād abhidhyāya sisṛkṣurvividhaṃ jagat \|*  
*apa eva sasarjādau tāsu vīryam avāsṛjat \|\| 28 \|\|*

*tadevāṇḍaṃ samabhavad dhemarūpyamayaṃ mahat \|*  
*saṃvatsarasahasreṇa sūryāutasamaprabham \|\| 29 \|\|*

*praviśyāntarmahātejāḥ svayam evātmasambhavaḥ \|*  
*prabhāvād api tadvyāptyā viṣṇutvam agamat punaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

28-30. Svayambhu, with the desire of creating the universe, first created water and planted the seed of creation in it. The seed of creation, i.e., chaitanya (consciousness) by coming into contact with water, produced a vast egg (i.e., the egg of Brahma), of golden hue, which, after one thousand years, became ten thousand times more luminous than the sun. After that, Svayambhu merged Himself into that tremendous Brahmanda, and owing, to His omnipresence in it He came to be known as Vishnu.

## \|\| 2.31 \|\|

*tadantarbhagavāneṣa sūryaḥ samabhavatpurā \|*  
*ādityaścādibhūtatvād brahmā brahma paṭhann abhūt \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. He (Svayambhu) then created the Sun by His glory, which owing to its first place in the creation, is known as Aditya.

## \|\| 2.32 \|\|

*divaṃ bhūmiṃ samakarot tadaṇḍaśakaladvayam \|*  
*sa cākaroddiśaḥ sarvā madhye vyoma ca śāśvatam \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. After dividing the huge Brahmanda into two parts. He (Svayambhu) made the Heaven and Earth, Akasha and the quarters. The upper portion of the divided Brahmanda formed the heaven, the lower one the earth. The direction in which the Sun was located was termed, purva i.e., East, the direction on the right hand side of Brahma was named dakshina, i.e., South, the direction to His left Land side was styled Uttara, i.e. North, and the one falling at His back came to be known as pashchima, i.e., West.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — Purva means first, and the direction was so named, because praditya the first object of creation happened to be located that side.

Pashchima means behind. This direction was named so, because it fell to the back of the Creator, who was standi hit faced to the East.

Dakshina means right. This direction fell to the right of Brahma.

“Uttara” means subsequent.

## \|\| 2.33-34 \|\|

*jarāurmerumukhyāś ca śailās tasyābhavaṃs tadā \|*  
*yad aulbaṃ tad abhūn meghas taḍitsaṅghātamaṇḍalam \|\| 33 \|\|*

*nadyo 'ṇḍanāmnaḥ saṃbhūtāḥ pitaro manavas tathā \|*  
*sapta ye 'mī samudrāś ca te 'pi cāntarjalodbhavāḥ \|*  
*lavaṇekṣusurādyāś ca nānāratnasamanvitāḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

33-34. Afterwards, the principal mountains, like the Meru clouds lightning, embryo, rivers, pitris, Manu and the seven oceans, fall of various gems, were created.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — “Pitarah” means manes of the dead, Forethers, the seven oceans are.

The above is the ancient division of oceans.

## \|\| 2.35 \|\|

*sa sisṛkṣur abhūd devaḥ prajāpatir arindama \|*  
*tattejasaś ca tatraiṣa mārtaṇḍaḥ samajāyata \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Brahma created the Brahmanas and, owing to His desire of calling the Universe into being, He is also known as Prajapati. Martanda came into being by the glory of the Creator.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — Bhudeva means the mundane Gods, i.e., the Brahmans. They were so named because they were inspired with Divine knowledge, Prajapati means the father of progeny, i.e., the Creator.

## \|\| 2.36 \|\|

*mṛte 'ṇḍe jāyate yasmān mārtaṇḍas tena saṃsmṛtaḥ \|*  
*rajoguṇamayaṃ yattad rūpaṃ tasya mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*caturmukhaḥ sa bhagavān abhūl lokapitāmahaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. The Sun, owing to its flashing out of the Brahmanda at the time of its breaking, he., being divided into two parts, is known by the name of Martanda, and the image of the Creator, Brahma, the four-headed Deity, who is full of the element of Rajoguna came to be called as Mahatman.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — Rajoguna is the constituent quality of all the material substances.

The Creator Brahma has four mouths that are visible, and that is why He is called so, Mahatman in the phraseology of Sankhya, means Mahatsatva, i.e., the attribute of buddhi and when this attribute has more of rajoguna then it is called Brahma.

## \|\| 2.37 \|\|

*yena sṛṣṭaṃ jagat sarvaṃ sadevāsuramānuṣam \|*  
*tamavehi rajorūpaṃ mahat sattvam udāhṛtam \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. The same Common Cause of the Universe who created all the Devas, Demons, and mankind is known by the name of Brahma, who is full of Rajoguna and who is also styled Mahat-sattva (or Brahma).

## Chapter 3

## \|\| 3.1 \|\|

*manur uvāca*  
*caturmukhatvam agamat kasmāl lokapitāmahaḥ \|*  
*kathaṃ tu lokān asṛjad brahmā brahmavidāṃ varaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. The king asked the Lord, how Brahma created the universe and the reason of His having four heads.

## \|\| 3.2-12 \|\|

*matsya uvāca*  
*tapaś cacāra prathamam amarāṇāṃ pitāmahaḥ \|*  
*āvibhūtās tathā vedāḥ sāṅgopāṅgapadakramāḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*purāṇasarvaśāstrāṇāṃ prathamaṃ brahmaṇā smṛtam \|*  
*nityaṃ śabdamayaṃ puṇyaṃ śatakoṭipravistaram \|\| 3 \|\|*

*anantaraṃ ca vaktrebhyo vedās tasya viniḥsṛtāḥ \|*  
*mīmāṃsānyāyavidyāś ca pramāṇāṣṭakasaṃyutāḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*vedābhyāsaratasyāsya prajākāmasya mānasāḥ \|*  
*manasaḥ pūrvasṛṣṭā vai jātā yat tena mānasāḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*marīcir abhavat pūrvaṃ tato 'trir bhagavān ṛṣiḥ \|*  
*aṅgiraś cābhavat paścāt pulastyas tadanantaram \|\| 6 \|\|*

*tataḥ pulahanāmā vai tataḥ kratur ajāyata \|*  
*pracetāś ca tataḥ putro vasiṣṭhaś cābhavat punaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*putro bhṛgur abhūt tadvan nārado 'py acirād abhūt \|*  
*daśemān mānasān brahmā munīn putrān ajijanat \|\| 8 \|\|*

*śārīrān atha vakṣyāmi mātṛhīnān prajāpateḥ \|*  
*aṅguṣṭhād dakṣiṇād dakṣaḥ prajāpatir ajāyata \|\| 9 \|\|*

*dharmaḥ stanāntād abhavad dhṛdayāt kusumāudhaḥ \|*  
*bhrūmadhyād abhavat krodho lobhaś cādharasaṃbhavaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*buddher mohaḥ samabhavad ahaṃkārād abhūn madaḥ \|*  
*pramodaś cābhavat kaṇṭhān mṛtyur locanato ṇrpa \|*  
*bharataḥ karamadhyāt tu brahmasūnur abhūt tataḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*ete nava sutā rājan kanyā ca daśamī punaḥ \|*  
*aṅgajā iti vikhyātā daśamī brahmaṇaḥ sutā \|\| 12 \|\|*

2-12. The Lord Fish replied that first of all Brahma practised devout austerities, whereby were revealed the sacred Vedas, together with their complements and supplements and the meters. The oldest of all Shastras was first recollected by Brahma — the eternal Brahman — in words, with its ten million elaborations. After that, Brahma revealed the sacred Vedas and the sciences of Mimansa. Nyaya, &c., together with the eightfold proof. Inspired with the Vedic knowledge, Brahma became conscious of His supreme potentiality and through His desire created the tea sages, who are known as the Manasa sons of the Creator, viz., Marichi, Atri, Angira, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu, Pracheta, Bhrigu, Vasistha and Narada.

In addition to the fore-mentioned ten sages, the following came into existence from the various limbs of His body, without.having any mother: from His right thumb appeared Prajapati Daksha, from His breast Dharma, from His heart Cupid, from His brows Anger, from His lips Greed, from His intellect Delusion, from His egoism Arrogance, from His throat Glee, from His eyes Death, from His hands the sage Bharata. These are the nine sons O King and the tenth was a girl, called Angaja.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — “Angaja” means originating from the body.

## \|\| 3.13 \|\|

*manur uvāca*  
*buddher mohaḥ samabhavad iti yat parikīrtitam \|*  
*ahaṃkāraḥ smṛtaḥ krodho buddhir nāma kim ucyate \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. At this, the king Vaivasvata Manu said: — “Lord! I have understood that intellect begot Delusion and egoism begot arrogance, but what is intellect?”

## \|\| 3.14-18 \|\|

*matsya uvāca*  
*sattvaṃ rajas tamaś caiva guṇatrayam udāhṛtam \|*  
*sāmyāvasthitir eteṣāṃ prakṛtiḥ parikīrtitā \|\| 14 \|\|*

*kecit pradhānam ity āhur avyaktam apare jaguḥ \|*  
*etad eva prajāsṛṣṭiṃ karoti vikaroti ca \|\| 15 \|\|*

*guṇebhyaḥ kṣobhamāṇebhyas trayo devā vijajñire \|*  
*ekā mūrtis trayo bhāgā brahmaviṣṇumaheśvarāḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*savikārāt pradhānāt tu mahat tattvaṃ prajāyate \|*  
*mahān iti yataḥ khyātir lokānāṃ jāyate sadā \|\| 17 \|\|*

*ahaṃkāraś ca mahato jāyate mānavardhanaḥ \|*  
*indriyāṇi tataḥ pañca vakṣye buddhivaśāni tu \|*  
*prādur bhavanti cānyāni tathā karmavaśāni tu \|\| 18 \|\|*

14-18. The Lord replied that the presence of the three attributes, viz. — Sattva, Rajas. Tamas, in equipoise, form the Prakriti. The same Prakriti is also known as Pradhana, Avyakta and Maya. The Creation springs from this very Prakriti and ultimately disappears into it. By a disturbance in these attributes, the same one form manifested itself into three, as Brahma, Vishnu and Maheswara. Similarly, the presence of the three attributes in unequal parts begets Mahatatva, which is also known as intellect. Egoism sprang from the Mahatatva, and the five organs of perception and other five organs of action, originated from Egoism.

## \|\| 3.19 \|\|

*śrotraṃ tvak cakṣuṣī jihvā nāsikā ca yathākramam \|*  
*pāyūpasthaṃ hastapādaṃ vākka cendriyasaṃgrahaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. These are: — The ears, the skin, the eyes, the tongue, the nose, the anus, the male and the female organs of generation, the hands, the feet, the speech.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — The first five are the organs of perception, and the last five are the organs of action.

## \|\| 3.20 \|\|

*śabdaḥ sparśaś ca rūpaṃ ca raso gandhaś ca pañcamaḥ \|*  
*utsargānandanādāna-gatyālāpāś ca tatkriyāḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. The five organs of perception produced words, touch, form, flavor, and smell; and the five organs of action brought forth emission, happiness, taking, walking and speech.

## \|\| 3.21-23 \|\|

*mana ekādaśaṃ teṣāṃ karmabuddhiguṇānvitam \|*  
*indriyāvayavāḥ sūkṣmās tasya mūrtiṃ manīṣiṇaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*śrayanti yasmāt tanmātrāḥ śarīraṃ tena saṃsmṛtam \|*  
*śarīrayogāj jīvo 'pi śarīrī gadyate budhaiḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*manaḥ sṛṣṭiṃ vikurute codyamānaṃ sisṛkṣayā \|*  
*ākāśaṃ śabdatanmātrād abhūc chabdaguṇātmakam \|\| 23 \|\|*

21-23. The mind is reckoned to be the eleventh organ, as it helps the faculties of intellect and action in their respective operations. The minute molecules of all the organs from the substratum for the individual soul that lies enshrined in it, and it is for this reason that the frame within which lies the asylum of the individual soul is known by the name of subtle body. The individual soul by coming in contact with this atomic body is called corporeal. The mind, propelled by desire to create, starts the work of creation. The subtle element of sound brought ether into being. Sound is the only attribute of ether.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — Lord Brahma first of all wished to create and then He threw His mind in the achievement of the work of His desire. Helped by His mind, He proceeded with the work of creation.

## \|\| 3.24-25 \|\|

*ākāśavikṛter vāuḥ śabdasparśaguṇo 'bhavat \|*  
*vāyoś ca sparśatanmātrāt tejaś cāvir abhūt tataḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*triguṇaṃ tadvikāreṇa tacchabdasparśarūpavat \|*  
*tejovikārād abhavad vāri rājaṃś caturguṇam \|\| 25 \|\|*

24-25. By a concussion ether, came forth wind, possessing the qualities of sound and tangibility, and the subtle element of tangibility produced brilliancy, which caused water attributed with sound, tangibility and form.

## \|\| 3.26-27 \|\|

*rasatanmātrasaṃbhūtaṃ prāyo rasaguṇātmakam \|*  
*bhūmis tu gandhatanmātrād abhūt pañcaguṇānvitā \|\| 26 \|\|*

*prāyo gandhaguṇā sā tu buddhir eṣā garīyasī \|*  
*ebhiḥ saṃpāditaṃ bhuṅkte puruṣaḥ pañcaviṃśakaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

26-27. The earth was produced by the potency of the subtle element of liquidity inherent in water, and it has the attributes akin to water and also of the subtle element of fragrance. The Mahatatva, which is formed by the five subtle and primary elements, is called the Vijnanamaya-kosha by the Vedantins; buddhi, i.e. intellect, is another name for the same. The man possessed of this twenty-fifth element enjoys and suffers.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — Twenty-fifth (element), i.e. (consciousness). God has laid down certain laws for mankind to follow. Any action, against the established laws leads to wrong which always causes pain. We have been given the faculty to distinguish between right and wrong, and it is our own fault if we choose the latter. A man always reaps the fruits of his actions. He suffers if he deviates from the right path and does wrong, and enjoys as long as he continues to follow the right track and does well.

## \|\| 3.28 \|\|

*īśvarecchāvaśaḥ so 'pi jīvātmā kathyate budhaiḥ \|*  
*evaṃ ṣaḍviṃśakaṃ proktaṃ śarīram iha mānave \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. The body therefore comprises the twenty-six elements, and the individual soul, which is subordinate to the wishes of the Lord, closes the list of the elements that make up the human body.

## \|\| 3.29 \|\|

*sāṃkhyaṃ saṃkhyātmakatvāc ca kapilādibhir ucyate \|*  
*etat tattvātmakaṃ kṛtvā jagad vedhā ajījanat \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Lord Brahma created the Univer.se by the help of the above enumerated elements; and Sankhya, which is one of the six systems of Hindu philosophy, is so called by Kapila, etc., because it enumerates these elements.

## \|\| 3.30-33 \|\|

*sāvitrīṃ lokasṛṣṭyarthe hṛdi kṛtvā samāsthitaḥ \|*  
*tataḥ saṃjapatas tasya bhitvā deham akalmaṣam \|\| 30 \|\|*

*strīrūpam ardham akarod ardhaṃ puruṣarūpavat \|*  
*śatarūpā ca sā khyātā sāvitrī ca nigadyate \|\| 31 \|\|*

*sarasvaty atha gāyatrī brahmāṇī ca parantapa \|*  
*tataḥ svadehasaṃbhūtām ātmajām ity akalpayat \|\| 32 \|\|*

*dṛṣṭvā tāṃ vyathitas tāvat kāmabāṇārdito vibhuḥ \|*  
*aho rūpam aho rūpam iti cāha prajāpatiḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

30-33. Lord Brahma, after creating His manasa putras, was not quite satisfied with the work of His creation. He set about devising some plan which would carry on the work of creation and would relieve Him of the task. With this view, He began to invoke Gayatri. After some time the goddess Gayatri, known under different names, viz. — Satarupa, Savitri, Sarasvati, Brahmani, &c., — appeared in the form of a girl from the half portion of Brahmas body who at the first sight mistakenly took Her for His daughter. Afterwards, the Creator, seeing that form of exquisite beauty, was fired with love and repeatedly uttered, “What an enchanting form!”

## \|\| 3.34 \|\|

*tato vāsiṣṭhapramukhā bhaginīm iti cukruśuḥ \|*  
*brahmā na kiṃcid dadṛśe tanmukhālokanād ṛte \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. At this, the Manasa putras of Brahma, i.e., Vasishtha, taking Savitri for their sister, began to express their feelings of seething indignation and contempt at the attitude of Their Father (Lord Brahma), but He was so much absorbed in love that He did not heed anything in the least.

## \|\| 3.35-41 \|\|

*aho rūpam aho rūpam iti prāha punaḥ punaḥ \|*  
*tataḥ praṇāmanamrāṃ tāṃ punar evābhyalokayat \|\| 35 \|\|*

*atha pradakṣiṇaṃ cakre sā pitur varavarṇinī \|*  
*putrebhyo ladjitasyāsya tadrūpālokanecchayā \|\| 36 \|\|*

*āvirbhūtaṃ tatro vaktraṃ dakṣiṇaṃ pāṇḍugaṇḍavat \|*  
*vismayasphuradoṣṭhaṃ ca pāścātyam udagāt tataḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

*caturtham abhavat paścād vāmaṃ kāmaśarāturam \|*  
*tato 'nyad abhavat tasya kāmāturatayā tathā \|\| 38 \|\|*

*utpatantyās tadākārā ālokanakutūhalāt \|*  
*sṛṣṭyarthaṃ yat kṛtaṃ tena tapaḥ paramadāruṇam \|\| 39 \|\|*

*tat sarvaṃ nāśam agamat svasutopagamecchayā \|*  
*tenordhvaṃ vaktram abhavat pañcamaṃ tasya dhīmataḥ \|*  
*āvirbhavadjaṭābhiś ca tad vaktraṃ cāvṛṇot prabhuḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

*tatas tān abravīd brahmā putrān ātmasamudbhavān \|*  
*prajāḥ sṛjadhvam abhitaḥ sadevāsuramānuṣīḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

35-41. Brahma continued uttering, “Oh! What an enchanting form! Oh, what an enchanting form!” In His love for the goddess Savitri, and the latter, after saluting Him, began to circumambulate Him in reverence. Brahma fixed his gaze on Savitri and could not distract Himself from Her. As she circumambulating Him, He felt shy of turning His head each time to Her direction, as His Manasa putras were standing close by. He therefore created four heads, each pointed to a direction, in order that He may see Savitri undisturbed, without having to turn His head each time in course of Her circumambulations. Seeing Brahma in such a condition, Satarupa went heaven with the Manas sons of the Creator, and as she was travelling towards heaven, Brahma put on a fifth head right on top which afterwards He covered with His long matted hair. This is how Brahma came to have five heads. After this, Brahma lost his powers that He had acquired by practising asceticism, owing to His not controlling His mind and falling into the snares of Cupid. Then Brahma dispersed His sons, after directing them to carry on the work of Creation.

## \|\| 3.42 \|\|

*evam uktās tataḥ sarve sasṛjur vividhāḥ prajāḥ \|*  
*gateṣu teṣu sṛṣṭyarthaṃ praṇāmāvanatām imām \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. The sons of Brahma, in obedience to His instructions, set themselves to complete the work of creation, and afterwards they took leave of Brahma with salutations.

## \|\| 3.43-44 \|\|

*upayeme sa viśvātmā śatarūpām aninditām \|*  
*saṃbabhūva tayā sārdham atikāmāturo vibhuḥ \|*  
*saladjāṃ cakame devaḥ kamalodaramandire \|\| 43 \|\|*

*yāvad abdaśataṃ divyaṃ yathānyaḥ prākṛto janaḥ \|*  
*tataḥkālena mahatā tasyāḥ putro 'bhavan manuḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

43-44. Brahma, fired with passion in Her company, married Satarupa and began to pass His days in enjoyment inside a lotus. He enjoyed the company of Savitri for hundred years, and after a long time Manu was born to them.

## \|\| 3.45-46 \|\|

*svāyaṃbhuvo iti khyātaḥ sa virāḍ iti naḥ śrutam \|*  
*tadrūpaguṇasāmānyād adhipuruṣa ucyate \|\| 45 \|\|*

*vairājā yatra te jātā bahavaḥ śaṃsitavratāḥ \|*  
*svāyaṃbhuvā mahābhāgāḥ sapta sapta tathāpare \|\| 46 \|\|*

45-46. Manu, thus born was Svayambhu Manu, who, owing to his close affinity to Brahma, is also called Adipurusha (the first man). The progeny of Svayambhu Manu multiplied considerably and the Vairajas are among them.

## \|\| 3.47 \|\|

*svārociṣādyāḥ sarve te brahmatulyasvarūpiṇaḥ \|*  
*auttamipramukhās tadvad yesāṃ tvaṃ saptamo 'dhunā \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Svarochisha, &c., the seven Manus, and another set of seven Manus, Auttami, &c., altogether the fourteen Manus, belong to the family of Svayambhu Manu. “O, King Vaivasvata Manu," said the Lord, “You are the seventh of the last set of Manus.”

## Chapter 4

## \|\| 4.1-6 \|\|

*manur uvāca*  
*aho kaṣṭataraṃ caitad aṅgajāgamanaṃ vibho \|*  
*kathaṃ na doṣamagamat karmaṇānena padmabhūḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*parasparaṃ ca sambandhaḥ sagotrāṇām abhūt katham \|*  
*vaivāhikastatsutānāṃ chinddhi me saṃśayaṃ vibho \|\| 2 \|\|*

*matsya uvāca*  
*divyeyamādisṛṣṭistu rajoguṇasamudbhavā \|*  
*atīndriyendriyā tadvad atīndriyaśarīrikā \|\| 3 \|\|*

*divyatejomayī bhūpa divyajñānasamudbhavā \|*  
*na martyairabhitaḥ śakyā vaktuṃ vai māṃsacakṣubhiḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*yathā bhujaṃgāḥ sarpāṇām ākāśaṃ viśvapakṣiṇām \|*  
*vidanti mārgaṃ divyānāṃ divyā eva na mānavāḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*kāryākārye na devānāṃ śubhāśubhaphalaprade \|*  
*yasmāttasmānna rājendra tadvicāro nṛṇāṃ śubhaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

1-6. The king said, “O, Merciful! I feel awfully grieved to hear that Lord Brahma married Angaja. Pray, tell me why he was not regarded as having committed a fearful sin by having done so. Remove my doubts, O, Master of the Universe! By graciously explaining to me why the offspring of Brahma were allowed to intermarry in their paternal circle without any regard for close-knit kinship.”

The Lord Fish replied:

”O King! Such doubts only arise in the case of mankind, for men have atomic bodies and beget children in a different way, while the primeval creation is celestial in which Rajoguna predominates. The Devas not have super-sensuous bodies and they beget progeny in quite different ways the celestial forms come into being in other ways, and it is very difficult for men having sensuous bodies to understand this great secret. Only supernatural intellect causes celestial creation; therefore those alone can understand its great secret who themselves are possessed with such an intellect just as a serpent alone can trace the footprints of another serpent, and aerial tracks can only be discerned by birds and other beings that fly in the air. O, King! The question of any prescribed order on prohibition does not arise in the deeds of the Devas. Only Their desire is taken into consideration in whatever they do. Other beings reap the fruits of their karma (doings) which the Devas do not. No doubts should, therefore be raised regarding the doings of the Devas, nor should the beings having sensuous bodies think of doing the same deed.”

## \|\| 4.7-10 \|\|

*anyacca sarvavedānām adhiṣṭhātā caturmukhaḥ \|*  
*gāyatrī brahmaṇastadvad aṅgabhūtā nigadyate \|\| 7 \|\|*

*amūrtaṃ mūrtimad vāpi mithunaṃ tatpracakṣate \|*  
*viriñcir yatra bhagavāṃs tatra devī sarasvatī \|*  
*bhāratī yatra yatraiva tatra tatra prajāpatiḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*yathātapo na rahitaś chāyayā dṛṣyate kvacit \|*  
*gāyatrī brahmaṇaḥpārśvaṃ tathaiva na vimuñcati \|\| 9 \|\|*

*vedarāśiḥ smṛto brahmā sāvitrī tadadhiṣṭhitā \|*  
*tasmānna kaściddoṣaḥ syāt sāvitrīgamane vibho \|\| 10 \|\|*

7-10. Besides this, as Lord, Brahma is the governor of the Vedas, so is the goddess Gayatri of the Brahmans (the sacred text, i.e., the Vedas). She is the better-half of the Lord, and that is why she appeared from His body. Brahma and Gayatri are inseparables. Sometimes only s one of the two puts on appearance and sometimes both do the same, but all the same both are always together. They never remain apart. As sunshine or light never lives devoid of its shadow, similarly Brahma never lives apart from Gayatri. Brahma is the master of the Vedas and Savitri (another name for Gayatri), is the governess of the same; Brahma is therefore also the master of the latter, and consequently He committed no sin by marrying Her.

## \|\| 4.11 \|\|

*tathāpi ladjāvanataḥ prajāpatir abhūtpurā \|*  
*svasutopagamād brahmā śaśāpa kusumāudham \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. “In spite of all this, Lord Brahma felt ashamed for not being able to suppress His passion in presence of His manasa sons. He therefore got much vexed with the God of love and cursed Him after the departure of His (manasa) sons.”

## \|\| 4.12 \|\|

*yasmānmamābhibhavatā manaḥ saṃkṣobhitaṃ śaraiḥ \|*  
*tasmāttvaddehamacirād rudro bhasmīkariṣyati \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. “The object with which you made me the target of your arrows will ere long lead you to be reduced to ashes 'by Shiva, when you similarly behave with Him, was the curse that Brahma pronounced on Cupid.”

**Комментарий:**

Note. — Professor Wilson Whites: “The Matsya Purana has a little allegory of its own, on the subject of Brahma intercourse with Satarupa for it explains the former to mean the Vedas, and the latter, the Savitri or holy prayer, which Is their chief text; and in their co-habitation there is, therefore, no evil”.

## \|\| 4.13-15 \|\|

*tataḥ prasādayāmāsa kāmadevaścaturmukham \|*  
*na māmakāraṇe śaptuṃ tvamihārhasi mānada \|\| 13 \|\|*

*ahamevaṃvidhaḥ sṛṣṭas tvayaiva caturānana \|*  
*indriyakṣobhajanakaḥ sarveṣāmeva dehinām \|\| 14 \|\|*

*strīpuṃsoravicāreṇa mayā sarvatra sarvadā \|*  
*kṣobhyaṃ manaḥ prayatnena tvayaivoktaṃ purā vibho \|\| 15 \|\|*

13-15. “Hearing this curse of Brahma, the God of love shuddered with fear and cried out in great dismay,” O, Lord! You created me with the object of captivating the minds of men and women and kindling amorous feelings within them. You never instructed me to make any exception in Your case. I only carried out Your mandate and have committed no sin for which I may be subjected to such a dreadful curse.

## \|\| 4.16 \|\|

*tasmādanaparādho 'haṃ tvayā śaptastathā vibho \|*  
*kuru prasādaṃ bhagavan svaśarīrāptaye punaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Therefore, be pleased with me and by Your clemency save me from the effects of Your curse and grant me the boon of assuming form again.”

## \|\| 4.17-18 \|\|

*brahmovāca*  
*vaivasvate 'ntare prāpte yādavānvayasambhavaḥ \|*  
*rāmo nāma yadā martyo matsattvabalamāśritaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*avatīryāsuradhvaṃsī dvārakām adhivatsyati \|*  
*tadbhrātustatsamasya tvaṃ tadā putratvameṣyasi \|\| 18 \|\|*

17-18. “Hearing such entreaties of Cupid, Lord Brahma melted with compassion, and said: ‘ In the reign of King Vaivasvata, Rama the destroyer of many Rakshasas and my compeer in power and prowess, will be born in the family of King Yadu. When Rama, the valiant prince, will fix Dwarika as His headquarters, You will be born as a son of His brother, the God Krishna.”

## \|\| 4.19-20 \|\|

*evaṃ śarīramāsādya bhuktvā bhogānaśeṣataḥ \|*  
*tato bharatavaṃśānte bhūtvā vatsanṛpātmajaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

*vidyādharādhipatyaṃ ca yāvad ābhūtasaṃplavam \|*  
*sukhāni dharmataḥ prāpya matsamīpaṃ gamiṣyasi \|\| 20 \|\|*

19-20. Note. — Rama here means Balarama, the brother of Krishna, and not the king of Ayodhya.

“In that body (as the son of Krishna), you will have a series of enjoyments and afterwards you will be born as a son of Vatsa in the family of King Bharata. After this, you will live till the time of dissolution that will close the reign of Vidyadharas, and then you will again come back to me.”

**Комментарий:**

Note. — Vidyadhara is a class of demy-gods.

## \|\| 4.21 \|\|

*evaṃ śāpaprasādābhyām upetaḥ kusumāudhaḥ \|*  
*śokapramodābhiuto jagāma sa yathāgatam \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. “The God of love took leave of Brahma and departed with mingled feelings of joy and sadness — joy on account of the hope given by the Lord and sadness for fear of sufferings, as the effect of His curse.”

## \|\| 4.22-23 \|\|

*manuruvāca*  
*ko 'sau yaduriti prokto yadvaṃśe kāmasambhavaḥ \|*  
*kathaṃ ca dagdho rudreṇa kimatha kusumāudhaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*bharatasyānvaye kasya kā ca sṛṣṭiḥ purābhavat \|*  
*etatsarvaṃ samācakṣva mūlataḥ saṃśayo hi me \|\| 23 \|\|*

22-23. After hearing this, the King Vaivasvata Manu again addressed the Lord thus: “Lord! Be gracious enough to satisfy my curiosity by telling me who was King Yadu, in whose family the God of Love took His birth, how Lord Shiva reduced Cupid to ashes, who was King Bharata and how the work of creation continued onwards.”

## \|\| 4.24-25 \|\|

*matsya uvāca*  
*yā sā dehārdhasambhūtā gāyatrī brahmavādinī \|*  
*jananī yā manordevī śatarūpā śatendriyā \|\| 24 \|\|*

*ratirmanastapo buddhir mahān diksambhramas tathā \|*  
*tataḥ sa śatarūpāyāṃ saptāpatyānyajījanat \|\| 25 \|\|*

24-25. The Fish-god replied: “King! Gayatri that appeared from the body of Brahma possessed of infinite forms and organs begot the following seven children; — Svayambhu Manu, Rati (the wife of Cupid. It also means desire of something). Tapas, Manas (mind), Dik(e) Sambhrama (delusion), and Mahatatva.”

## \|\| 4.26-27 \|\|

*ye marīcyādayaḥ putrā mānasāstasya dhīmataḥ \|*  
*teṣāmayamabhūllokaḥ sarvajñānātmakaḥ purā \|\| 26 \|\|*

*tato 'sṛjadvāmadevaṃ triśūlavaradhāriṇam \|*  
*sanatkumāraṃ ca vibhuṃ pūrveṣāmapi pūrvajam \|\| 27 \|\|*

26-27. “The Manasa sons of Brahma — Marichi, &c. — who were born first, began to pass their days in the terrestrial globe in the practice of asceticism. The Creator, marking the indifference of His Manasa sons with regard to the work of creation, produced Vamadeva, the wielder of the trident and also Sanatkumar, the first event of the first borns.”

## \|\| 4.28 \|\|

*vāmadevastu bhagavān asṛjanmukhato dvijān \|*  
*rājanyān asṛjadbāhvor viṭchūdrān ūrupādayoḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. From the month of Lord Vamadeva came forth the Brahmanas, from His arms the Kshatriyas, from His thighs the Vaishyas, and from His feet the Madras.”

## \|\| 4.29-30 \|\|

*vidyuto 'śanimeghāṃśca rohitendradhanūṃṣi ca \|*  
*chandāṃsi ca sasarjādau parjanyaṃ ca tataḥ param \|\| 29 \|\|*

*tataḥ sādhyagaṇānīśas trinetrānasṛjatpunaḥ \|*  
*koṭīśca caturaśītiṃ jarāmaraṇavarjitāḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

29-30. ‘'Afterwards came forth lightning, thunderbolt, clouds, rainbow, meters of various kinds, several varieties of medicines, eighty-four crores of Devas, known as Sadhya, and who have three eyes and are immortals, without any fear of getting old”.

## \|\| 4.31-32 \|\|

*vāmo 'sṛjannamartyāṃs tān brahmaṇā vinivāritaḥ \|*  
*naivaṃvidhā bhavetsṛṣṭir jarāmaraṇavarjitā \|\| 31 \|\|*

*śubhāśubhātmikā yā tu saiva sṛṣṭiḥ praśasyate \|*  
*evaṃ sthitaḥ sa tenādau sṛṣṭeḥ sthāṇurato 'bhavat \|\| 32 \|\|*

31-32 Lord Brahma, finding Shiva creating such a race of Immortals, said that it was advisable to create only such beings as would reap the fruit of their own karmas. Shiva, on hearing this, instantly stopped His propaganda.”

**Комментарий:**

Note. — Sthanu, literally, the trunk of a tree. It means that Shiva instantly stopped the work of creation and became fixed like the trunk of a tree. In other words, He did not carry on the work of creation after Brahma offered Him His suggestions. From that day He is also known as Sthanu.

## \|\| 4.33-34 \|\|

*svāyambhuvo manurdhīmāṃs tapastaptvā suduścaram \|*  
*patnīmevāpa rūpāḍhyām anantā nāma nāmataḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

*priyavratottānapādau manustasyām ajījanat \|*  
*dharmasya kanyā caturā sūnṛtā nāma bhāminī \|\| 34 \|\|*

33-34. "Afterwards, Svayambhu Manu became the husband of Ananti, whom he obtained after great penances." By this alliance, Svayambhu Manu was blessed with two sons, viz. — Priyavrata and Uttanapada, and of these, the latter was married to Sunrita the daughter of Dharma’

## \|\| 4.35 \|\|

*uttānapādāttanayān prāpa mantharagāminī \|*  
*apasyatim apasyantaṃ kīrtimantaṃ dhruvaṃ tathā \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. “Uttanapada became the father of the following four children, viz. — Apasyati, Apasyanta, Kirtimana, and Dhruva (Pole Star).”

## \|\| 4.36-37 \|\|

*uttānapādo 'janayat sūnṛtāyāṃ prajāpatiḥ \|*  
*dhruvo varṣasahasrāṇi trīṇi kṛtvā tapaḥ purā \|\| 36 \|\|*

*divyamāpa tataḥ sthānam acalaṃ brahmaṇo varāt \|*  
*tameva purataḥ kṛtvā dhruvaṃ saptarṣayaḥ sthitāḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

36-37. “In the bygone ages, Dhruva practised severe penances for a period of three thousand ears and obtained from Brahma an abode in the eternal celestial regions. The Sapta-Rishis, acknowledging him as their chief clustered themselves round him”

**Комментарий:**

Note. — The seven Rishis (sages), i.e., the Manasa sons of Brahma, It means the constellation known as Ursa Major (the seven stars of which are said to be the seven sages, i.e., the Manasa sons of Brahma).

## \|\| 4.38-42 \|\|

*dhanyā nāma manoḥ kanyā dhruvācchiṣṭam ajījanat \|*  
*agnikanyā tu succhāyā śiṣṭātsā suṣuve sutān \|\| 38 \|\|*

*kṛpaṃ ripuṃ jayaṃ vṛttaṃ vṛkaṃ ca vṛkatejasam \|*  
*cakṣuṣaṃ brahmadauhitryāṃ vīriṇyāṃ sa ripuṃjayaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

*vīraṇasyātmajāyāṃ tu cakṣurmanumajījanat \|*  
*manur vai rājakanyāyāṃ naḍvalāyāṃ sa cākṣuṣaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

*janayāmāsa tanayān daśa śūrānakalmaṣān \|*  
*ūruḥ pūruḥ śatadyumnas tapasvī satyavāgghaviḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

*agniṣṭudatirātraśca sudyumnaścāparājitaḥ \|*  
*abhimanyustu daśamo naḍvalāyām ajāyata \|\| 42 \|\|*

38-42. “Dhruva begot a son, Shishta, from Dhanya, the daughter of Svayambhu Manu, and Shishta had five children, viz. — Kripa, Ripunjaya, Vrita, Vrika, and Vrikatejasa, from Suchchhaya, the daughter of Agni. Ripunjaya became the father of Chakshu from Virini, the grand-daughter of Brahma. Chakshu became the father of Chakshusha Manu from the daughter of Virini, and Chakshusha Manu begot on the princess Nadvala ten valiant and enterprising sons, viz. — Uru, Puru, Shatadyumna, Satyavaka, Havi, Agnistut, Atiratra, Sudyumna, Aparajita, and Abhimanyu.”

## \|\| 4.43 \|\|

*ūror ajanayat putrān ṣaḍ āgneyī tu suprabhān \|*  
*agniṃ sumanasaṃ khyātiṃ kratumaṅgirasaṃ gayam \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. “Uru had the following six sons, viz. — Agni, Suman, Khyati, Ritu, Angira, and Gaya, from his Consort, Agneyi.

## \|\| 4.44 \|\|

*pitṛkanyā sunīthā tu venamaṅgādajījanat \|*  
*venamanyāyinaṃ viprā mamanthus tatkarād abhūt \|*  
*pṛthurnāma mahātejāḥ sa putrau dvāv ajījanat \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. “Amgira became the father of Vena, from Sunitha, the daughter of Pitri. The sages rubbed Vena to death, owing to his tyranny, and as they were rubbing him, King Prithu appeared from his hand. The great King Prithu was the father of Antardhana and Havirdhana.

## \|\| 4.45 \|\|

*antardhānas tu mārīcaṃ śikhaṇḍinyāmajījanat \|*  
*havirdhānāt ṣaḍ āgneyī dhiṣaṇājanayat sutān \|*  
*prācīnabarhiṣaṃ sāṅgaṃ yamaṃ śukraṃ balaṃ śubham \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. “Maricha was the son of Antardhana from Shikhandini, and Havirdhana had six sons, viz. — Prachinavarhisha, Sanga, Yama, Shukra, Vala and Shubha, from Dhishna, the daughter of Agni."

## \|\| 4.40-48 \|\|

*vīraṇasyātmajāyāṃ tu cakṣurmanumajījanat \|*  
*manur vai rājakanyāyāṃ naḍvalāyāṃ sa cākṣuṣaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

*janayāmāsa tanayān daśa śūrānakalmaṣān \|*  
*ūruḥ pūruḥ śatadyumnas tapasvī satyavāgghaviḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

*agniṣṭudatirātraśca sudyumnaścāparājitaḥ \|*  
*abhimanyustu daśamo naḍvalāyām ajāyata \|\| 42 \|\|*

*ūror ajanayat putrān ṣaḍ āgneyī tu suprabhān \|*  
*agniṃ sumanasaṃ khyātiṃ kratumaṅgirasaṃ gayam \|\| 43 \|\|*

*pitṛkanyā sunīthā tu venamaṅgādajījanat \|*  
*venamanyāyinaṃ viprā mamanthus tatkarād abhūt \|*  
*pṛthurnāma mahātejāḥ sa putrau dvāv ajījanat \|\| 44 \|\|*

*antardhānas tu mārīcaṃ śikhaṇḍinyāmajījanat \|*  
*havirdhānāt ṣaḍ āgneyī dhiṣaṇājanayat sutān \|*  
*prācīnabarhiṣaṃ sāṅgaṃ yamaṃ śukraṃ balaṃ śubham \|\| 45 \|\|*

*prācīnabarhir bhagavān mahān āsīt prajāpatiḥ \|*  
*havirdhānāḥ prajās tena bahavaḥ sampravartitāḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

*savarṇāyāṃ tu sāmudryāṃ daśādhatta sutānprabhuḥ \|*  
*sarve pracetaso nāma dhanurvedasya pāragāḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

*tattaporakṣitā vṛkṣā babhur loke samantataḥ \|*  
*devādeśācca tānagnir adahadravinandana \|\| 48 \|\|*

40-48. “Prachinavarhisha begot many children belonging to the Havirdhan clan. He had ten stalwart sons, well versed in archery, who are known as Prachetas, from Savarna, the daughter of Samudra. They all devoted themselves to asceticism, and the trees that they grew to form a small jungle where they could practise their austerities, in process of time developed into a thick forest of vast latitudes which was ultimately burnt down by the fire at the commands of Indra (the God of Rain).”

## \|\| 4.49 \|\|

*somakanyābhavat patnī mārīṣā nāma viśrutā \|*  
*tebhyastu dakṣamekaṃ sā putram agryam ajījanat \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. “The ten Prachetas had Marish, the daughter of Chandrama, for their wife, from whom they begot the Prajapati Daksha.”

## \|\| 4.50 \|\|

*dakṣādanantaraṃ vṛkṣān auṣadhāni ca sarvaśaḥ \|*  
*ajījanatsomakanyā nadīṃ candravatīṃ tathā \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. “After giving birth to Prajapati Daksha the daughter of the moon brought forth the trees, the herbs, and the river Chandravati.”

## \|\| 4.51 \|\|

*somāṃśasya ca tasyāpi dakṣasyāśītikoṭayaḥ \|*  
*vakṣye tāsāṃ tu vistāraṃ loke yaḥ supratiṣṭhitaḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. “Now hear the tale of the multiplication, of the eighty crores of Daksha’s sons.”

## \|\| 4.52-53 \|\|

*dvipadaścābhavan kecit kecid bahupadā narāḥ \|*  
*valīmukhāḥ śaṅkukarṇāḥ karṇaprāvaraṇās tathā \|\| 52 \|\|*

*aśvaṛkṣamukhāḥ kecit kecit siṃhānanāstathā \|*  
*śvasūkaramukhāḥ kecit keciduṣṭramukhās tathā \|\| 53 \|\|*

52-53. “Daksha became the progenitor of a most queer race. Among his children some were bipeds, some had more feet, some had long ears and some broad ones, and some had features resembling those of the horse, the bear, the lion, the dog, the hoar, or the camel. On seeing such a vast multitude of his progeny, Daksha created a large number of women.”

## \|\| 4.54-55 \|\|

*janayāmāsa dharmātmā mlecchānsarvānanekaśaḥ \|*  
*sa sṛṣṭvā manasā dakṣaḥ striyaḥ paścādajījanat \|\| 54 \|\|*

*dadau sa daśa dharmāya kaṣyapāya trayodaśa \|*  
*saptaviṃśatiṃ somāya dadau nakṣatrasaṃjñitāḥ \|*  
*devāsuramanuṣyādi tābhyaḥ sarvamabhūdjagat \|\| 55 \|\|*

54-55. “Out of the girls he created, he gave ten to Dharma, thirteen to Kashyapa, and twenty-seven to the moon that form a certain galaxy of stars. These very same daughters of Daksha produced the further race of Devas, Rakshasas, mankind and the other beings inhabiting the extensive universe.”

## Chapter 5

## \|\| 5.1 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ*  
*devānāṃ dānavānāṃ ca gandharvoragarakṣasām \|*  
*utpattiṃ vistareṇaiva sūta brūhi yathātatham \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. The sages, after hearing this, requested the Sage Suta to relate to them how Devas, Danavas, Gandharvas, serpents and Rakshasas were born.

## \|\| 5.2 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*saṃkalpād darśanātsparśāt pūrveṣāṃ sṛṣṭirucyate \|*  
*dakṣātprācetasād ūrdhvaṃ sṛṣṭir maithunasambhavā \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Suta said that in the days gone by, the work of creation was originated by desire, perception and touch. Later on, Daksha started the work of creation by the conjunction of men and women.

## \|\| 5.3 \|\|

*prajāḥ sṛjeti vyādiṣṭaḥ pūrvaṃ dakṣaḥ svayambhuvā \|*  
*yathā sasarja caivādau tathaiva śṛṇuta dvijāḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. “Hear, O sages! I shall now relate to you how Daksha introduced a new system of creation at the injunction of Brahma.”

## \|\| 5.4 \|\|

*yadā tu sṛjatastasya devarṣigaṇapannagān \|*  
*na vṛddhim agamallokas tadā maithunayogataḥ \|*  
*dakṣaḥ putrasahasrāṇi pāñcajanyāmajījanat \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Daksha begot thousands of issues from Ills wife, Panchajani, when he saw that the Devas, the Riijis, and the serpents, etc., created from the mind of the Creator, had not the same faculty to help the growth of creation.

## \|\| 5.5 \|\|

*tāṃs tu dṛṣṭvā mahābhāgaḥ sisṛkṣurvividhāḥ prajāḥ \|*  
*nāradaḥ prāha haryaśvān dakṣaputrānsamāgatān \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Narada, on seeing the progress of Daksha in the field of creation, said:

## \|\| 5.6 \|\|

*bhuvaḥ pramāṇaṃ sarvatra jñātvordhvam adha eva ca \|*  
*tataḥ sṛṣṭiṃ viśeṣeṇa kurudhvamṛṣisattamāḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. “O, ye Rishis, who are sons of Daksha! first reconnoiter the extent of the universe and then set yourselves to the work of creation.”

## \|\| 5.7 \|\|

*te tu tadvacanaṃ śrutvā prayātāḥ sarvato diśam \|*  
*adyāpi na nivartante samudrādiva sindhavaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. “On hearing the above words of the Sage Narada, the sons of Daksha started to survey the length and breadth of the universe, and ultimately’ lust themselves, as the river's do when they fall into the ocean. They have not returned unto this day.”

## \|\| 5.8 \|\|

*haryaśveṣu pranaṣṭeṣu punardakṣaḥ prajāpatiḥ \|*  
*vairiṇyāmeva putrāṇāṃ sahasramasṛjatprabhuḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. The lost sons of Daksha were known by the name of Haryashva, and the former giving them up for lost, created one thousand Br4hmanas known as Shaval.

## \|\| 5.9-10 \|\|

*śabalā nāma te viprāḥ sametāḥ sṛṣṭihetavaḥ \|*  
*nārado 'nugatānprāha punastānpūrvavatsa tān \|\| 9 \|\|*

*bhuvaḥ pramāṇaṃ sarvatra jñātvā bhrātrin atho punaḥ \|*  
*āgatya cātha sṛṣṭiṃ ca kariṣyatha viśeṣataḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. On finding the Shaval’s carrying on the work of creation, the Sage Narada went to them and said: — “First examine the extent of the universe and try (o reclaim your lost brothers, then carry on the work of creation.”

## \|\| 5.11 \|\|

*te 'pi tenaiva mārgeṇa jagmurbhrātṛpathā tadā \|*  
*tataḥ prabhṛti na bhrātuḥ kanīyānmārgam icchati \|*  
*anviṣyanduḥkhamāpnoti tena tatparivarjayet \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. “Taking to the words of the sage, they started to reclaim their lost brothers, hut met with the same fate; and it is for this reason that no one dares to repeat the same experiment unto this day.”

## \|\| 5.12-14 \|\|

*tatasteṣu vinaṣṭeṣu ṣaṣṭiṃ kanyāḥ prajāpatiḥ \|*  
*vairiṇyāṃ janayāmāsa dakṣaḥ prācetasastathā \|\| 12 \|\|*

*prādātsa daśa dharmāya kaṣyapāya trayodaśa \|*  
*saptaviṃśatiṃ somāya catasro 'riṣṭanemaye \|\| 13 \|\|*

*dve caiva bhṛguputrāya dve kṛśāśvāya dhīmate \|*  
*dve caivāṅgirase tadvat tāsāṃ nāmāni vistarāt \|\| 14 \|\|*

12-14. On losing the latter batch of his sons, Daksha begot sixty daughters from Panchajani, the daughter of Virani, Out of those girls, he gave ten to Dharma, thirteen to Kashyapa, twenty-seven to Chandrama and four to i Arishtanemi. He also gave two to the son of Bhrigu, another two to Krishashva, and two to Angira. Their names will be- related hereafter.

## \|\| 5.15-16 \|\|

*śṛṇudhvaṃ devamātriṇāṃ prajāvistāram āditaḥ \|*  
*marutvatī vasur yāmī lambā bhānur arundhatī \|\| 15 \|\|*

*saṃkalpā ca muhūrtā ca sādhyā viśvā ca bhāminī \|*  
*dharmapatnyaḥ samākhyātās tāsāṃ putrān nibodhata \|\| 16 \|\|*

15-16. Marutvati, Vasu, Yami, Lamba, Bhanu, Arundhati, Sankalpa, i Muhurta, Sadhya, Vishva, who were given to Dharma, were the mothers of the Devas.

## \|\| 5.17-19 \|\|

*viśve devāstu viśvāyāḥ sādhyā sādhyānajījanat \|*  
*marutvatyāṃ marutvanto vasos tu vasavastathā \|\| 17 \|\|*

*bhānostu bhānavastadvan muhūrtāyāṃ muhūrtakāḥ \|*  
*lambāyāṃ ghoṣanāmāno nāgavīthī tu yāmijā \|\| 18 \|\|*

*pṛthivītalasambhūtam arundhatyām ajāyata \|*  
*saṃkalpāyāstu saṃkalpo vasusṛṣṭiṃ nibodhata \|\| 19 \|\|*

17-19. Vishvadeva was born of Vishva, Sadhyaguna from Sadhya, Marutvantagan from Marutvati, Vasava from Vasu, Bhanava from Bhana, Muhurtaka from Muhurta, Ghosha from Lamba, Nagrithi from Yami, the dweller in patala from Arundhati, Sankalpa from Sankalpa.

## \|\| 5.20-21 \|\|

*jyotiṣmantastu ye devā vyāpakāḥ sarvato diśam \|*  
*vasavaste samākhyātās teṣāṃ sargaṃ nibodhata \|\| 20 \|\|*

*āpo dhruvaśca somaśca dharaścaivānilo 'nalaḥ \|*  
*pratyūṣaśca prabhāsaśca vasavo 'ṣṭau prakīrtitāḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

20-21 The most powerful of the Devas that pervade the universe are known by the name of Vasus, who are eight in number, viz.: — Apa, Dhruva, Soma, Dhara, Anila, Anala, Pratyusha and Prabhasa.

## \|\| 5.22 \|\|

*āpasya putrāś catvāraḥ śānto vai daṇḍa eva ca \|*  
*śāmbo 'tha maṇivaktraśca yajñarakṣādhikāriṇaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. The four sons of Apa are Santa, Danda, Samva, and Manivakra. They became the protectors of sacrificial rites.

## \|\| 5.23-24 \|\|

*dhruvasya kālaḥ putrastu varcāḥ somādajāyata \|*  
*draviṇo havyavāhaśca dharaputrāv ubhau smṛtau \|\| 23 \|\|*

*kalyāṇinyāṃ tataḥ prāṇo ramaṇaḥ śiśiro 'pi ca \|*  
*manoharā dharātputrān avāpātha hareḥ sutā \|\| 24 \|\|*

23-24. Dhruva became the father of Kala, Son of Varcha, Dhara of Dravina and Havyavaha. Dravina and Havyavaha were born of Kalyani, and Manohara, the daughter of Hari, was the mother of Prana, Ramana, Shisra,

## \|\| 5.25 \|\|

*śivā manojavaṃ putram avijñātagatiṃ tathā \|*  
*avāpa cānalāt putrāv agniprāyaguṇau punaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Anila became the father of the two powerful sons, viz. Manojava and Avijnatgati from Shiva.

## \|\| 5.26-27 \|\|

*agniputraḥ kumārastu śarastambe vyajāyata \|*  
*tasya śākho viśākhaśca naigameyaś ca pṛṣṭhajāḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*apatyaṃ kṛttikānāṃ tu kārttikeyas tataḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*pratyūṣasa ṛṣiḥ putro vibhur nāmnātha devalaḥ \|*  
*viśvakarmā prabhāsasya putraḥ śilpī prajāpatiḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

26-27. Anala perchance cast his seed in a heap of reeds, whence sprang up Kumara, Sakha, Vishakha and Naigameya. They were fostered by the Pleiades, and that is why they are known as Kartikeya, and the great Rishi Devala was begotten by Pratyusha.

## \|\| 5.28 \|\|

*prāsādabhavanodyāna-pratimābhūṣaṇādiṣu \|*  
*taḍāgārāmakūpeṣu smṛtaḥ so 'maravardhakiḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Prabhasa begot the renowned architect and builder — the great Vishvakarma to make mansions, pleasure gardens, statues, ornaments, tanks, wells, etc.

## \|\| 5.29-32 \|\|

*ajaikapādahirbudhnyo virūpākṣo 'tha raivataḥ \|*  
*haraśca bahurūpaśca tryambakaśca sureśvaraḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*sāvitraśca jayantaśca pinākī cāparājitaḥ \|*  
*ete rudrāḥ samākhyātā ekādaśa gaṇeśvarāḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

*eteṣāṃ mānasānāṃ tu triśūlavaradhāriṇām \|*  
*koṭayaścaturaśītis tatputrāś cākṣayā matāḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

*dikṣu sarvāsu ye rakṣāṃ prakurvanti gaṇeśvarāḥ \|*  
*putrapautrasutāścaite surabhīgarbhasambhavāḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

29-32 Vamadevas, i.e., Rudras, the creators of the Immortals, are eleven in number; viz.: Ajaikapada, Ahirbudhnya, Virapaksha, Raivata, tiara, Bahurupa, Tryamvaka, Savitra, Jayanta, Pinaki, Aparajita. The eleven Rudras were created by the mind of Brahma each holding a trident in his hand. An account of their having created a race of Immortals, numbering 84crores, has been given before. The Rudras pervade and protect the universe and have begotten many children from the womb of Surabhi.

## Chapter 6

## \|\| 6.1-2 \|\|

*kaṣyapasya pravakṣyāmi patnībhyaḥ putrapautrakān \|*  
*aditirditirdanuścaiva ariṣṭā surasā tathā \|\| 1 \|\|*

*surabhir vinatā tadvat tāmrā krodhavaśā irā \|*  
*kadrūrviśvā munis tadvat tāsāṃ putrān nibodhata \|\| 2 \|\|*

1-2. Suta, addressing the sages who were listening to his narrations with wrapt attention at Naimisharanya, said O, sages! I shall now enumerate to you the names of Kashyapa’s sons that he had from his 13 wives. Aditi, Diti, Danu, Arishta, Sursa, Surabhi, Vinata, Tamra, Krodhavasa, Ira, Kadru, Vishva and Muni were the thirteen wives of Kashyapa.

## \|\| 6.3-5 \|\|

*tuṣitā nāma ye devāś cākṣuṣasyāntare manoḥ \|*  
*vaivasvate 'ntare caite ādityā dvādaśa smṛtāḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*indro dhātā bhagas tvaṣṭā mitro 'tha varuṇo yamaḥ \|*  
*vivasvānsavitā pūṣā aṃśumān viṣṇur eva ca \|\| 4 \|\|*

*ete sahasrakiraṇā ādityā dvādaśa smṛtāḥ \|*  
*mārīcātkaṣyapādāpa putrānaditiruttamān \|\| 5 \|\|*

3-5. Devas called Tushita who flourished in the reign of Chakshusha Manu, came to be known as Adityas (Suns), owing to their having been born as the sons of Devas called glorious Kashyapa from his wife, Aditi, during the reign of King Vaivasvata Manu. They were twelve in number, viz., Indra, Dhata, Bhaga, Tvasta, Mitra, Varuna, Tama, Vivasvana, Savita, Pusha, Anshumana, and Vishnu. Those were the 12 Adityas — the centre of rays.

## \|\| 6.6-10 \|\|

*bhṛśāśvasya ṛṣeḥ putrā devapraharaṇāḥ smṛtāḥ \|*  
*ete devagaṇā viprāḥ pratimanvantareṣu ca \|\| 6 \|\|*

*utpadyante pralīyante kalpe kalpe tathaiva ca \|*  
*ditiḥ putradvayaṃ lebhe kaṣyapād iti naḥ śrutam \|\| 7 \|\|*

*hiraṇyakaśipuṃ caiva hiraṇyākṣaṃ tathaiva ca \|*  
*hiraṇyakaśipostadvaj jātaṃ putracatuṣṭayam \|\| 8 \|\|*

*prahlādaś cānuhlādaśca saṃhlādo hlāda eva ca \|*  
*prahlādaputra āuṣmān śibir bāṣkala eva ca \|\| 9 \|\|*

*virocanaś caturthaśca sa baliṃ putramāptavān \|*  
*baleḥ putraśataṃ tv āsīd bāṇajyeṣṭhaṃ tato dvijāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

6-10. The Devapraharanas the sons of Krisasva Rishi, and the twelve Adityas appear at the beginning of every Manvantara and Kalpa and vanish' at their termination, Diti, the second wife of Kashyapa, gave birth to two sons, viz., Hiranyakashipu and Hiranyaksha. Hiranyakashipu had four sons, viz., Prahlada, Anuhlada, Samhlada and Hlada. Prahlada had the following sons: — Ayushmana, Shivi, Bashkala, and Virochana, Bali was the son of Virochana, and the former had one hundred sons, the oldest of whom was Bana.

## \|\| 6.11 \|\|

*dhṛtarāṣṭras tathā sūryaś candraścandrāṃśutāpanaḥ \|*  
*nikumbhanābho gurvakṣaḥ kukṣibhīmo vibhīṣaṇaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. The notable brothers of Buna were: — Dhritarashtra, Surya, Chandra, Chandramsutapana, Nikumbhanabha, Gurbaksha, Kukshibhima, and Vibhishana.

## \|\| 6.12-13 \|\|

*evamādyās tu bahavo bāṇajyeṣṭhā guṇādhikāḥ \|*  
*bāṇaḥ sahasrabāhuś ca sarvāstragaṇasaṃyutaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*tapasā toṣito yasya pure vasati śūlabhṛt \|*  
*mahākālatvam agamat sāmyaṃ yaśca pinākinaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

12-13. These were the most notable of Bana’s brothers. Bana had one thousand anus, and each arm was bedecked with a different kind of weapon. Vana was an ardent devotee of Lord Shiva, and had won over the latter by his deep devotions. In fact, he was such an earnest devotee that be bad almost unified himself with the Lord. His realm was guarded by Shiva Himself, the wielder of the trident.

## \|\| 6.14-15 \|\|

*hiraṇyākṣasya putro 'bhūd ulūkaḥ śakunistathā \|*  
*bhūtasaṃtāpanaś caiva mahānābhastathaiva ca \|\| 14 \|\|*

*etebhyaḥ putrapautrāṇāṃ koṭayaḥ saptasaptatiḥ \|*  
*mahābalā mahākāyā nānārūpā mahaujasaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

14-15. Uluka, Shakuni. Bhuta-samtapana, and Mahanabha were the sons of Hiranyaksha. The four sons of Hiranyaksha begot an invincible band of demons, numbering 77 crores, who had mighty limbs, various kinds of faces, and were most hardy.

## \|\| 6.16 \|\|

*danuḥ putraśataṃ lebhe kaṣyapād baladarpitam \|*  
*vipracittiḥ pradhāno 'bhūd yeṣāṃ madhye mahābalaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Danu, the third wife of Kashyapa, brought forth one hundred mighty demons, the principal one of whom was Viprachitti.

## \|\| 6.17-20 \|\|

*dvimūrdhā śakuniścaiva tathā śaṅkuśirodharaḥ \|*  
*ayomukhaḥ śambaraś ca kapiśo nāmatastathā \|\| 17 \|\|*

*mārīcir meghavāṃścaiva irā garbhaśirās tathā \|*  
*vidrāvaṇaśca ketuśca ketuvīryaḥ śatahradaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*indrajit saptajiccaiva vajranābhastathaiva ca \|*  
*ekacakro mahābāhur vajrākṣas tārakas tathā \|\| 19 \|\|*

*asilomā pulomā ca bindurbāṇo mahāsuraḥ \|*  
*svarbhānurvṛṣaparvā ca evamādyā danoḥ sutāḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

17-20. Dvimurdha, Shakuni, Sankushirodhara, Ayomukha, Sambara, Kapisha, Vamana, Marichi, Meghavana, Ira, Garbhashira, Vidrabana, Ketu, Ketuvirya, Shatrida, Indrajit, Saptajit, Vajranabha, Ekachakra, Mahabahu, Vajraksha, Taraka, Asiloma, Puloma, Vindu, Bana, Svarbhanu, Vrishaparvan were chiefly the noteworthy brothers of Viprachit,

## \|\| 6.21-22 \|\|

*svarbhānostu prabhā kanyā śacī caiva pulomajā \|*  
*upadānavī mayasyāsīt tathā mandodarī kuhūḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*śarmiṣṭhā sundarī caiva candrā ca vṛṣaparvaṇaḥ \|*  
*pulomā kālakā caiva vaiśvānarasute hi te \|\| 22 \|\|*

21-22. Svarbhanu gave birth to a daughter, named Prabha, Puloma gave birth to Shachi, Maya to Updanavi, Mandodari and Kuhu, Vrishaparvan to Sharmishtha, Sundari and Chandra, and Vaishvanara to Puloma and Kalika.

## \|\| 6.23 \|\|

*bahvapatye mahāsattve mārīcasya parigrahe \|*  
*tayoḥ ṣaṣṭisahasrāṇi dānavānāmabhūtpurā \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Puloma and Kalika were married to the demon King, Marichi, who begot another formidable batch of Rakshasas, numbering 60 thousand from them.

## \|\| 6.24-25 \|\|

*paulomānkālakeyāṃśca mārīco 'janayatpurā \|*  
*avadhyā ye 'marāṇāṃ vai hiraṇyapuravāsinaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*caturmukhāllabdhavarās te hatā vijayena tu \|*  
*vipracittiḥ saiṃhikeyān siṃhikāyām ajījanat \|\| 25 \|\|*

24-25. The Paulomas and the Kalikeyas, i.e., the demon progeny of Puloma, and Kalika, after being made invulnerable even against the Devas, began to live in Hiranyapura. Lord Vishnu killed the Paulomas and Kalikeyas, who had become most haughty after they were made invulnerable by Brahma. Only Viprachit survived, and he produced another race of thirteen demons, known as Saihimkeya from the womb of Simhika the sister of Hiranyakashipu.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — The Paulomas and the Kalikeyas were only made invulnerable by Brahma, and only the minor Gods could not kill them, but Lord Vishnu is the Supreme God.

## \|\| 6.26-28 \|\|

*hiraṇyakaśiporye vai bhāgineyās trayodaśa \|*  
*vyaṃsaḥ kalpaśca rājendra nalo vātāpireva ca \|\| 26 \|\|*

*ilvalo namuciścaiva śvasṛpaś cājanas tathā \|*  
*narakaḥ kālanābhaśca saramāṇas tathaiva ca \|\| 27 \|\|*

*kālavīyeś ca vikhyāto danuvaṃśavivardhanāḥ \|*  
*saṃhrādasya tu daityasya nivātakavacāḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

26-28. Vyamsa, Kalpa, Nala, Vatapi, Ilvala, Namuchi, Svasripa, Ajana, Naraka, Kalanabha, Sarmana, Kalavirya, Potarana were among the Saihimkeya class of demons. Samhlada, the son of Hiranyakasipu, produced the race of Nivatkavacha demons.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — Potarana, the thirteenth demon of the Saihimkaiya class, is not mentioned in the text, but the number thirteen is laid down in the text. To complete the list, therefore, I have included the name of Potarana, on the authority of Hari Vamshapurana.

## \|\| 6.29 \|\|

*avadhyāḥ sarvadevānāṃ gandharvoragarakṣasām \|*  
*ye hatā bhargam āśritya tv arjunena raṇājire \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. This class of Nivata-kavacha demons that was made invulnerable to the Devas, demons and serpents, was ultimately destroyed by Arjuna — a hero of Mahabharata — by the grace of Shiva.

## \|\| 6.30 \|\|

*ṣaṭkanyā janayāmāsa tāmrā mārīcabījataḥ \|*  
*śukī śyenī ca bhāsī ca sugrīvī gṛdhrikā śuciḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Kashyapa had the following six daughters, from his wife, Tamra Shuki, Sheni, Bhasi, Sugrivi, Gridhrika, Shuchi.

## \|\| 6.32 \|\|

*gṛdhrī gṛdhrānkapotāṃśca pārāvatavihaṃgamān \|*  
*haṃsasārasakrauñcāṃś ca plavāñchucirajījanat \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Shuki became the mother of l3uka and Uluka, Sheni of Shyena, Bhashi of Kurara, Gridhi of Gridhra and Kapota, Shucbi of Hamsa, Sarasa and Vaka, &c.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — Shuka = Parrot, Uluka = Owl, Shyena = Hawk, Kurara= Osprey, Gridhra = Vulture, Kapota = Pigeon, Hamsa=Swan, Sarasa = Crane, Vaka = Duck.

## \|\| 6.33-34 \|\|

*ajāśvameṣoṣṭrakharān sugrīvī cāpyajījanat \|*  
*eṣa tāmrānvayaḥ prokto vinatāyāṃ nibodhata \|\| 33 \|\|*

*garuḍaḥ patatāṃ nāthaḥ aruṇaśca patatriṇām \|*  
*saudāmanī tathā kanyā yeyaṃ nabhasi viśrutā \|\| 34 \|\|*

33-34. Sugrivi gave birth to goat, horse, ram, camel, mule, &c.

From his wife Vinita, Kashyapa begot Garuda, the lord of birds, the Aruna, and a daughter, named Saudamini (Lightning).

## \|\| 6.35 \|\|

*sampātiś ca jaṭāuśca aruṇasya sutāv ubhau \|*  
*sampātiputro babhruśca śīghragaścāpi viśrutaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Samputi and Jatayuh were the sons of Aruna, and Vabhru and Sighragha were the sons of Sampati.

## \|\| 6.36 \|\|

*jaṭāuṣaḥ karṇikāraḥ śatagāmī ca viśrutau \|*  
*sāraso radjuvālaśca bheruṇḍaścāpi tatsutāḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Jatayuh was the father of Karnikara, Shatagami, Sarasa, Rajjuvala and Bherunda

## \|\| 6.37 \|\|

*teṣāmanantamabhavat pakṣiṇāṃ putrapautrakam \|*  
*surasāyāḥ sahasraṃ tu sarpāṇām abhavatpurā \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. The above-mentioned sons of Jatayuh became the ancestors of different species of birds, and Surasa, one of the wives of Ka43-apa, became the mother of serpents.

## \|\| 6.38-41 \|\|

*sahasraśirasāṃ kadrūḥ sahasraṃ cāpi suvrata \|*  
*pradhānāsteṣu vikhyātāḥ ṣaḍviṃśatir ariṃdama \|\| 38 \|\|*
