*śeṣavāsukikarkoṭa-śaṅkhairāvatakambalāḥ \|*  
*dhanaṃjayamahānīla-padmāśvataratakṣakāḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

*elāpattramahāpadma-dhṛtarāṣṭrabalāhakāḥ \|*  
*śaṅkhapālamahāśaṅkha-puṣpadaṃṣṭraśubhānanāḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

*śaṅkuromā ca bahulo vāmanaḥ pāṇinastathā \|*  
*kapilo durmukhaścāpi patañjaliriti smṛtāḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

38-41. Kadru — a wife of Kashyapa-gave birth to several thousand-hooded serpents, the principal ones of whom are Shesha, Vasuki, Karkota, Shankha, Airavata, Kambala, Dhananjaya, Mahanila, Padma, Asvatara (mule), Takshaka, Elapattra, Mahapadma, Dhritarashtra, Balahaka, Shankhapala, Mahashankha, Pushpadanshtra, Shubhanana, Shankuroma, Bahula, Vamana Panina, Kapila, Durmukha, and Patanjali.

## \|\| 6.42 \|\|

*eṣāmanantamabhavat sarveṣāṃ putrapautrakam \|*  
*prāyaśo yatpurā dagdhaṃ janamejayamandire \|\| 42 \|\|*

42 The above-named sons of Kadru and Kashyapa were the fore-fathers of different classes of serpents, most of whom were consumed in the great sacrifice of Janmejaya.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — Janmejaya was the son of King Parikshita. The latter was bitten by a serpent and died in consequence, Janmejaya, therefore, to avenge his father's death, performed a great sacrifice to consume all the serpents in which a large number of them was destroyed.

## \|\| 6.43 \|\|

*rakṣogaṇaṃ krodhavaśā svanāmānam ajījanat \|*  
*daṃṣṭriṇāṃ niutaṃ teṣāṃ bhīmasenādagātkṣayam \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. From his wife, Krodhvasa, Kashyapa had a race of Krodhavasa demons, numbering a million who were ultimately killed by Bhimasena—a hero of Mahabharata.

## \|\| 6.44 \|\|

*rudrāṇāṃ ca gaṇaṃ tadvad gomahiṣyo varāṅganāḥ \|*  
*surabhirjanayāmāsa kaṣyapātsaṃyatavratā \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Surabhi, one of the wives of Kashyapa, gave birth to the attendants of Rudras, cows, buffaloes, &c.

## \|\| 6.45 \|\|

*munirmunīnāṃ ca gaṇaṃ gaṇamapsarasāṃ tathā \|*  
*tathā kiṃnaragandharvān ariṣṭājanayad bahūn \|\| 45 \|\|*

45 Note. — Rudras are a group of Gods, eleven in number, supposed to be the manifestations of Shiva, who is said to be the head of the group.

Muni and Arista, other two wives of Kashyapa, gave birth to the class of Munis and Apsaras and the race of Kinnaras and Gandharvas, respectively.

## \|\| 6.46 \|\|

*tṛṇavṛkṣalatāgulmam irā sarvam ajījanat \|*  
*viśvā tu yakṣarakṣāṃsi janayāmāsa koṭiśaḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46 From Ira, Kashyapa begot reeds, trees, creepers, &c., and from his wife Vishva, he produced a race of numerous Yakshas and demons.

## \|\| 6.47 \|\|

*tata ekonapañcāśan marutaḥ kaṣyapādditiḥ \|*  
*janayāmāsa dharmajñān sarvānamaravallabhān \|\| 47 \|\|*

47 Diti — a wife of Kashyapa — gave birth to 19 maruts (Gods of wind), who were the beloved of the Devas.

## Chapter 7

## \|\| 7.1 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ*  
*diteḥ putrāḥ kathaṃ jātā maruto devavallabhāḥ \|*  
*devairjagmuśca sāpatnaiḥ kasmātte sakhyamuttamam \|\| 1 \|\|*

1 The Rishis said:--How did Diti again beget the Maruts and how did the latter become the friends of the Devas?

## \|\| 7.2-3 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*purā devāsure uddhe hṛteṣu hariṇā suraiḥ \|*  
*putrapautreṣu śokārtā gatvā bhūlokamuttamam \|\| 2 \|\|*

*syamantapañcake kṣetre sarasvatyāstaṭe śubhe \|*  
*bhartur ārādhanaparā tapa ugraṃ cacāra ha \|\| 3 \|\|*

2-3 Suta said:—In the days gone by, when Lord Vishnu destroyed the offspring of Diti in the great war between the Devas and Asuras, Diti repaired to Syamantapanchaka — a holy place — on the hanks of the Surasvati, and devoted herself to the worship of her husband and practised severe penances for a considerable length of time.

## \|\| 7.4-5 \|\|

*tadā ditir daityamātā ṛṣirūpeṇa suvratā \|*  
*phalāhārā tapas tepe kṛcchraṃ cāndrāyaṇādikam \|\| 4 \|\|*

*yāvadvarṣaśataṃ sāgraṃ jarāśokasamākulā \|*  
*tataḥ sā tapasā taptā vasiṣṭhādīnapṛcchata \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5 Note. — A true Hindu wife al Ways regards her husband as her Supreme Lord, She has the same devotion for her as one has for God. Her salvation lies through her husband.

After a little more than a century, Diti, the mother of demons, who had practised hard penances like a Rishi and had become emaciated and aged owing to her living on phalahara and regularly keeping up Chandrayana and other fasts, asked Vasistha and other Sages.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — Phalahara. The Hindus in course of their fasts do not take cooked food. They only take light things and particularly fruits, Phalahara literally means a repast of fruits.

Chandrayana is a particular fast, the chief feature of which is that one has to regulate his morsels of phalahara to the phases of the moon, i.e., on the new-moon-day he has to take only one morsel which he goes on increasing one by one each day, for a fortnight, when the fast terminates.

## \|\| 7.6 \|\|

*kathayantu bhavanto me putraśokavināśanam \|*  
*vrataṃ saubhāgyaphaladam ihaloke paratra ca \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. “Sages! Tell me some such vrata that would free me from the crushing grief of my son’s destruction and make me feel happy in this world as well as in the next.”

**Комментарий:**

Note.—Vrata means fast, Anyself-imposed religious observance, Restriction, Vow, Precept, Penance.

In this world as well as in the next: The Hindus believe in the transmigration of soul. According to this idea, there is a life after death until the soul becomes totally unified with Brahma, which is Nirvana or final rest. The next world here. therefore, refers to the re-birth after transmigration of soul.

## \|\| 7.7 \|\|

*ūcur vasiṣṭhapramukhā madanadvādaśīvratam \|*  
*yasyāḥ prabhāvādabhavat sutaśokavivarjitā \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. The sage Vasistha advised Diti to observe the Madana-Dvadashi fast, by keeping which Diti became the mother of the Maruts and was liberated from her pangs of grief.

## \|\| 7.8 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ*  
*śrotumicchāmahe sūta madanadvādaśīvratam \|*  
*sutānekonapañcāśad yena lebhe ditiḥ punaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. The Rishis said:—“O, Pious Sage, Suta! we are very anxious to know something of the Madana-Dvadashi fast, by the observance of which Diti begot forty-nine sons again (after her progeny was destroyed by Vishnu).”

## \|\| 7.9 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*yadvasiṣṭhādibhiḥ pūrvaṃ diteḥ kathitamuttamam \|*  
*vistareṇa tadevedaṃ matsakāśānnibodhata \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Suta said: — “Hear, O Rishis! what the Sage Vasistha said to Diti about the fast in question. I shall repeat to you the same in detail.”

## \|\| 7.10-18 \|\|

*caitre māsi site pakṣe dvādaśyāṃ niyatavrataḥ \|*  
*sthāpayedavraṇaṃ kumbhaṃ sitataṇḍulapūritam \|\| 10 \|\|*

*nānāphalautaṃ tadvad ikṣudaṇḍasamanvitam \|*  
*sitavastraugacchannaṃ sitacandanacarcitam \|\| 11 \|\|*

*nānābhakṣyasamopetaṃ sahiraṇyaṃ tu śaktitaḥ \|*  
*tāmrapātraṃ guḍopetaṃ tasyopari niveśayet \|\| 12 \|\|*

*tasmādupari kāmaṃ tu kadalīdalasaṃsthitam \|*  
*kuryāccharkarayopetāṃ ratiṃ tasya ca vāmataḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*gandhaṃ dhūpaṃ tato dadyād gītaṃ vādyaṃ ca kārayet \|*  
*tadabhāve kathāṃ kuryāt kāmakeśavayornaraḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*kāmanāmnā harerarcāṃ snāpayedgandhavāriṇā \|*  
*śuklapuṣpākṣatatilair arcayenmadhusūdanam \|\| 15 \|\|*

*kāmāya pādau sampūjya jaṅghe saubhāgyadāya ca \|*  
*ūrū smarāyeti punar manmathāyeti vai kaṭim \|\| 16 \|\|*

*svacchodarāyetyudaram anaṅgāyetyuro hareḥ \|*  
*mukhaṃ padmamukhāyeti bāhū pañcaśarāya vai \|\| 17 \|\|*

*namaḥ sarvātmane maulim arcayediti keśavam \|*  
*tataḥ prabhāte taṃ kumbhaṃ brāhmaṇāya nivedayet \|\| 18 \|\|*

10-18. “The fast begins in the month of Chaitra, on the 12th day of the bright fortnight. One who observes this fast should place a jar of gold, silver, copper, brass or earth — according to his means — on an earthen platform, after filing it with different fruits, pieces of sugar- cane, and white rice. Before placing the jar on the platform, it should also be painted with white sandal and covered with two pieces of white cloth. After this, a small plate of copper containing some fruits, gold and raw sugar should be placed on the top of the jar. Above it should he placed a plantain leaf, bearing an image of Cupid, and to the left of it should he placed the image of Rati made of sugar. After this, the worship of Cupid and Rati should be performed in the following manner: — The images should first be bathed with incense and water, then white flowers, rice, and sesamum should be offered. Afterwards, the Angapuja (body worship) should follow, as indicated below: — After pronouncing Om Kamaya, worship the feet. After pronouncing Om Saubhagyadaya, worship the legs. After pronouncing Om Smaraya, worship the thighs. After pronouncing Om Manmathaya, worship the waist. After pronouncing Om Svaschodardya, worship the stomach. After pronouncing Om Anangaya, worship the breast. After pronouncing Om Padmamukhaya, worship the mouth. After pronouncing Om Panchasaraya, worship the hands, After pronouncing Om Sarvatmane, worship the head. On the completion of this worship, sandal and incense should be offered, and then prayers should be sung accompained by music. In case there be no one to sing prayers and play on the music, then the glories of Kama and Keshava should be narrated and listened to. On the following morning, the jar should be given to a Brahmana.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — In the text, only Kamaya, Saubhagyadaya, &c., are given. But all those expressions should be prefixed by (Om) and suffixed by (Namah), before being pronounced at the time of worship, Kamaya, thus prefixed and suffixed, becomes, On Kamaya namah, which means “I salute Kama, the God of love. Similarly all the expressions are simply meant to convey the salutations of the worshipper to the Lord of love — expressive of the former's devotion and reverence to the latter, All the expressions are only adjectival that ultimately apply to Cupid, viz.—Kama-God of Love, Cupid.

Ananga, literally, means without a beds, Cupid was destroyed by Siva and became bodiless. He is therefore known as ananga also.

Saubhagyada, literals, moans the giver of good luck, and here applies to the God of Love who brings good luck.

Smara literally means remembrance, Because Cupid appears and begins to exercise His influence merely by thinking of Him, the tern itself has become a name of Cupid. Padmamukha literally, means the mouth of a lotus or (ii) one who has a face as beautiful as a lotus. This expression is often employed by Indian poets to describe a beautiful face. As the face of Cupid is as aromatic, as delicate, as soft and as healthy-looking as a lotus, He is known by this name also.

Panchasara literally, moans one who holds five arrows, Cupid is armed with the \|

following five arrows: — ……..

The same five arrows are also differently named as: — ……..

He is therefor: known as Panchasara also.

Sarvatman means the whole soul and applies to Cupid.

## \|\| 7.19 \|\|

*brāhmaṇānbhojayedbhaktyā svayaṃ ca lavaṇādṛte \|*  
*bhuktyā tu dakṣiṇāṃ dadyād imaṃ mantramudīrayet \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. After making over the jar to a deserving Brahmana, the Worshipper should feast a number of Brahmanas with devotion, and afterwards he should have his own meal devoid of salt, Then, the invited Brahmanas should be dismissed with presents, and the following prayer should be uttered before giving them presents:

## \|\| 7.20 \|\|

*prīyatām atra bhagavān kāmarūpī janārdanaḥ \|*  
*hṛdaye sarvabhūtānāṃ ya ānando 'bhidhīyate \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. “O, Lord Janardana, in the form of Cupid! Who bring bliss to every soul, be pleased with thy devotee.”

## \|\| 7.21-26 \|\|

*anena vidhinā sarvaṃ māsi māsi vrataṃ caret \|*  
*upavāsī trayodaśyām arcayedviṣṇumavyayam \|\| 21 \|\|*

*phalamekaṃ ca saṃprāṣya dvādaśyāṃ bhūtale svapet \|*  
*tatastrayodaśe māsi dhṛtadhenusamanvitām \|\| 22 \|\|*

*śayyāṃ dadyādanaṅgāya sarvopaskarasaṃyutām \|*  
*kāñcanaṃ kāmadevaṃ ca śuklāṃ gāṃ ca payasvinīm \|\| 23 \|\|*

*vāsobhir dvijadāmpatyaṃ pūjyaṃ śaktyā vibhūṣaṇaiḥ \|*  
*śayyāgandhādikaṃ dadyāt prīyatām ityudīrayet \|\| 24 \|\|*

*homaḥ śuklatilaiḥ kāryaḥ kāmanāmāni kīrtayet \|*  
*gavyena haviṣā tadvat pāyasena ca dharmavit \|\| 25 \|\|*

*viprebhyo bhojanaṃ dadyād vittaśāṭhyaṃ vivarjayet \|*  
*ikṣudaṇḍānatho dadyāt puṣpamālāś ca śaktitaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

21-26. The same routine of worship should be observed each month, on the twelfth day of the bright fortnight, and continued on for a whole year. The worshipper should observe a fast on the 13th day of the bright fortnight and worship Vishnu. On the 12th day of every bright fortnight, he should live only on fruits and sleep on the floor. At the beginning of the 13th month, he is to finally complete his cycle of fasts by performing worship as mentioned before, and on its completion he should worship the golden image of Cupid. Afterwards, white sesamum, mixed with clarified butter, should he poured into fire and at the time of each sacrificial offering the various names of Cupid, already mentioned, prefixed with om and suffixed with Svaha, should be pronounced. At the close of the sacrifice, the worshipper should also worship the officiating priest and his consort, and then dismiss all his Brahmana guests after feasting, garlanding, and giving them presents of clarified butter, cows, decently-arranged beds, clothes, ornaments, sugarcane. The golden image of Cupid should be given to the officiating priest along with other presents mentioned above, according to the means of the worshipper.

## \|\| 7.27-28 \|\|

*yaḥ kuryād vidhinānena madanadvādaśīmimām \|*  
*sa sarvapāpanirmuktaḥ prāpnoti harisāmyatām \|\| 27 \|\|*

*ihaloke varān putrān saubhāgyaphalam aśnute \|*  
*yaḥ smaraḥ saṃsmṛto viṣṇur ānandātmā maheśvaraḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

27-28. One who observes the Madana Dvadashi fast in this way, becomes liberated from evils and begets worthy children and, finally, passes away in peace, for Vishnu and Smara are the same.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — Liberated from all evils or sins, or vices. In other words Madan-dvadashi fast, by exercising its influence on the body and mind, improves the man both physically and morally. Later on, by being blessed with children, AE passes away in peace and attains rest; for he feels that his worthy children would discharge their duties unto God, their deceased ancestors, and mankind. It is for the fulfilment of these duties that a Hindu is always so anxious to beget worthy sons.

## \|\| 7.29 \|\|

*sukhārthī kāmarūpeṇa smaredaṅgajamīśvaram \|*  
*etacchrutvā cakārāsau ditiḥ sarvamaśeṣataḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. The worship of Kama fulfills the desires of the worshipper. Hearing the advantages of the Madana Dvadashi fast, Diti observed it devoutly.

## \|\| 7.30-34 \|\|

*kaṣyapo vratamāhātmyād āgatya parayā mudā \|*  
*cakāra karkaśāṃ bhūyo rūpayauvanaśālinīm \|\| 30 \|\|*

*varair āchandayāmāsa sā tu vavre tato varam \|*  
*putraṃ śakravadhārthāya samarthamamitaujasam \|\| 31 \|\|*

*varayāmi mahātmānaṃ sarvāmaraniṣūdanam \|*  
*uvāca kaṣyapo vākyam indrahantāram ūrjitam \|\| 32 \|\|*

*pradāsyāmyahameveha kiṃ tv etat kriyatāṃ śubhe \|*  
*āpastambaḥ karotviṣṭiṃ putrīyāmadya suvrate \|\| 33 \|\|*

*vidhāsyāmi tato garbham indraśatruniṣūdanam \|*  
*āpastambastataścakre putreṣṭiṃ draviṇādhikām \|\| 34 \|\|*

30-34. Kashyapa chanced to meet his wife Diti, and through his powers (of asceticisin) made her young again. On being questioned by Kashyapa, Diti said that she wanted to be mother of such a progeny as would ‘Kill Lord: Indra and conquer all the Devas. Kashyapa promised to beget such a child from her womb when the sage Apastamba performed a putreshti sacrifice. The sage Apastamba eventually began to perform the sacrifice.

**Комментарий:**

Note —Putreshti is a special sacrifice which is performed to beget an offspring.

## \|\| 7.35 \|\|

*indraśatrur bhavasveti juhāva ca savistaram \|*  
*devā mumudire daityā vimukhāḥ syuśca dānavāḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. At the time of performing the sacrifice, the sage Apastamba began to recite Indra Satrurbhavasva Svaha, at which the Devas became pleased and the demons were overpowered with grief.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — Indra Satrurvardha sva and Svaha Indra Satrurvardha sva Svaha mean the same thing, bat, strictly speaking, the latter expression was applied by the sage Apastamba. It has been put in a modified form to suit the metre. It is a compound word, and can be expounded in two ways, viz. (the enemy of Indra) and (Indra is whose enemy). Apastamba, through a coincidence, began to pronounce the expression with such accent and emphasis as would admit the latter way of expounding the compound word which entirely reversed the object of Diti and, consequently, the Devas were pleased and the demons were overtaken with grief. It is therefore said:—

## \|\| 7.36 \|\|

*dityāṃ garbham athādhatta kaṣyapaḥ prāha tāṃ punaḥ \|*  
*tvayā yatno vidhātavyo hy asmingarbhe varānane \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. At the conclusion of the sacrifice, Kashyapa performed the purificatory ceremonies to’ facilitate conception, and began to counsel his wife how a pregnant woman should live

## \|\| 7.37-48 \|\|

*saṃvatsaraśataṃ tv ekam asminn eva tapovane \|*  
*saṃkhyāyāṃ naiva bhoktavyaṃ garbhiṇyā varavarṇini \|\| 37 \|\|*

*na sthātavyaṃ na gantavyaṃ vṛkṣamūleṣu sarvadā \|*  
*nopaskareṣūpaviśen musalolūkhalādiṣu \|\| 38 \|\|*

*jale ca nāvagāheta śūnyāgāraṃ ca varjayet \|*  
*valmīkāyāṃ na tiṣṭheta na codvignamanā bhavet \|\| 39 \|\|*

*vilikhenna nakhairbhūmiṃ nāṅgāreṇa na bhasmanā \|*  
*na śayāluḥ sadā tiṣṭhed vyāyāmaṃ ca vivarjayet \|\| 40 \|\|*

*na tuṣāṅgārabhasmāsthi-kapāleṣu samāviśet \|*  
*varjayetkalahaṃ lokair gātrabhaṅgaṃ tathaiva ca \|\| 41 \|\|*

*na muktakeśā tiṣṭheta nāśuciḥ syātkadācana \|*  
*na śayītottaraśirā na cāparaśirāḥ kvacit \|\| 42 \|\|*

*na vastrahīnā nodvignā na cārdracaraṇā satī \|*  
*nāmaṅgalyāṃ vadedvācaṃ na ca hāsyādhikā bhavet \|\| 43 \|\|*

*kuryāttu guruśuśrūṣāṃ nityaṃ māṅgalyatatparā \|*  
*sarvauṣadhībhiḥ koṣṇena vāriṇā snānamācaret \|\| 44 \|\|*

*kṛtarakṣā subhūṣā ca vāstupūjanatatparā \|*  
*tiṣṭhetprasannavadanā bhartuḥ priyahite ratā \|\| 45 \|\|*

*dānaśīlā tṛtīyāyāṃ pārvaṇyaṃ naktamācaret \|*  
*itivṛttā bhavennārī viśeṣeṇa tu garbhiṇī \|\| 46 \|\|*

*yastu tasyā bhavetputraḥ śīlāurvṛddhisaṃyutaḥ \|*  
*anyathā garbhapatanam avāpnoti na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

*tasmāttvamanayā vṛttyā garbhe 'sminyatnamācara \|*  
*svastyastu te gamiṣyāmi tathetyuktastayā punaḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

37-48. He advised Diti to remain in that hermitage for a century and not to take any meals in the morning and evening. Continuing his advice he said that a pregnant woman should not often go and sit at the root of a tree, nor should she sit on a broom-stick or a pestle. She should not enter or plunge herself in deep waters, and should also avoid living in a solitary house, sitting upon an ant-hill, and also depression of mind. She should not write by her nails, charcoal or ashes, on the fluor, and should avoid much sleeping and labour, She should also abstain from sitting in a place covered with coal, chaff, and bones, as well as from quarreling and yawning, She should not keep her lair unkempt, nor her person unclean, nor should she sleep with her head towards the north. She should never doff her garments, and should not allow her mind to be afflicted or her feet to remain wet. She should avoid much laughing and the use of inauspicious words. She should serve her preceptor, do pious deeds, and bathe in lukewarm medicated water. She should take great care of herself in every way, should wear fine ornaments, worship Vastu household deity), keep herself pleased, and devotedly serve her husband. She should give alms to the poor and worship Gauri (the wile of Siva) on the 3rd day of a bright fortnight. A woman and, particularly one who is in the family wav, if she follow such a course, begets amiable, valiant, and long-lived children; otherwise there is always a danger of miscarriage. “Therefore O beloved! follow the directions just explained to you. May you be blessed. I am now going to practice penances ”.

## \|\| 7.49 \|\|

*paṣyatāṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ tatraivāntaradhīyata \|*  
*tataḥ sā kaṣyapoktena vidhinā samatiṣṭhata \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. After this, Kashyapa vanished then and there, and Diti followed the instructions of her lord to the letter.

## \|\| 7.50-51 \|\|

*atha bhītastathendro 'pi diteḥ pārśvamupāgamat \|*  
*vihāya devasadanaṃ tacchuśrūṣuravasthitaḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

*diteśchidrāntaraprepsur abhavatpākaśāsanaḥ \|*  
*vinīto 'bhavad avyagraḥ praśāntavadano bahiḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

50-51. Indra came to know all this, and became fearfully alarmed. In his consternation, he left His kingdom of Heaven and going to Diti began to serve her. He, putting on a bright appearance, patiently and craftily began to pry into the daily life of Diti, in the hope that she might give Him an opportunity of causing an abortion, by some way neglecting or omitting to follow closely the precautions suggested by her husband.

## \|\| 7.52-53 \|\|

*ajānankila tatkāryam ātmanaḥ śubhamācaran \|*  
*tato varṣaśatānte sā nyūne tu divasais tribhiḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

*mene kṛtārthamātmānaṃ prītyā vismitamānasā \|*  
*akṛtvā pādayoḥ śaucaṃ prasuptā muktamūrdhajā \|\| 53 \|\|*

52-53. Diti, not knowing the foul intentions of Indra, did not entertain any suspicion, and she went on following the injunctions of her husband very closely, till there remained only three days to complete the century. She was so much surcharged with joy that she failed to observe ‘the precautions, and one’ day she did not wash her feet, kept her hair unkempt and went to sleep like that.

## \|\| 7.51-58 \|\|

*diteśchidrāntaraprepsur abhavatpākaśāsanaḥ \|*  
*vinīto 'bhavad avyagraḥ praśāntavadano bahiḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

*ajānankila tatkāryam ātmanaḥ śubhamācaran \|*  
*tato varṣaśatānte sā nyūne tu divasais tribhiḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

*mene kṛtārthamātmānaṃ prītyā vismitamānasā \|*  
*akṛtvā pādayoḥ śaucaṃ prasuptā muktamūrdhajā \|\| 53 \|\|*

*nidrābharasamākrāntā divāparaśirāḥ kvacit \|*  
*tatastadantaraṃ labdhvā praviṣṭastu śacīpatiḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

*vajreṇa saptadhā cakre taṃ garbhaṃ tridaśādhipaḥ \|*  
*tataḥ saptaiva te jātāḥ kumārāḥ sūryavarcasaḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

*rudantaḥ sapta te bālā niṣiddhā giridāriṇā \|*  
*bhūyo 'pi rudataścaitān ekaikaṃ saptadhā hariḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

*cicheda vṛtrahantā vai punastadudare sthitaḥ \|*  
*evamekonapañcāśad bhūtvā te rurudurbhṛśam \|\| 57 \|\|*

*indro nivārayāmāsa māṃ rodiṣṭa punaḥ punaḥ \|*  
*tataḥ sa cintayāmāsa kimetaditi vṛtrahā \|\| 58 \|\|*

51-58. In her recklessness, she slept in course of the day, with her head towards the north. All those irregularities afforded a good opportunity to Indra to enter into her womb in His subtle body; and by His weapon divided the child in the womb into seven parts. ‘To His great “surprise and dismay each part developed into a child. They all began to cry in the womb, then Indra divided each one into seven parts. Indra thus divided the child in the womb into forty-nine parts, but each part became a child, and they all began to cry. On seeing this, He was awfully astonished, and asked them not to cry.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — Marodishta = “do not weep or cry”, said Indra to the crying children in the womb; and that is why they were named “Marut” afterwards.

## \|\| 7.59-61 \|\|

*dharmasya kasya māhātmyāt punaḥ saṃjīvitāstvamī \|*  
*viditvā dhyānayogena madanadvādaśīphalam \|\| 59 \|\|*

*nūnam etat pariṇatam adhunā kṛṣṇapūjanāt \|*  
*vajreṇāpi hatāḥ santo na vināśam avāpnuuḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

*eko 'pyanekatāmāpa yasmādudarago 'pyalam \|*  
*avadhyā nūnamete vai tasmāddevā bhavantviti \|\| 61 \|\|*

59-61. Indra came to know, through His Yogic powers, that it was on account of Diti’s observance of the Dvadashi fast and worship of Kama that His weapon could not destroy her child in the womb. His own thoughts ‘began to oppress Him. He said to Himself that, instead of one, they multiplied into forty-nine. Devas could not destroy them. It would be safer to make them Devas.

## \|\| 7.62-63 \|\|

*yasmānmā rudatetyuktā rudanto garbhasaṃsthitāḥ \|*  
*maruto nāma te nāmnā bhavantu makhabhāginaḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

*tataḥ prasādya deveśaḥ kṣamasveti ditiṃ punaḥ \|*  
*arthaśāstraṃ samāsthāya mayaitad duṣkṛtaṃ kṛtam \|\| 63 \|\|*

62-63. After this, Indra appeared before Diti and besought her to forgive Him for His base action, He said that He did that, because statesmanship dictates that a wise man should always endeavour to put an end to his enemies. They would, from that day forward, be known as the “Marut” and would rank among the Devas and would be entitled to a share in the sacrificial offerings, like other Devas.

## \|\| 7.64 \|\|

*kṛtvā marudgaṇaṃ devaiḥ samānamamarādhipaḥ \|*  
*ditiṃ vimānamāropya sasutāmanayaddivam \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. In this way, Indra, after making the “Maruts’’ into Devas and, taking Diti with Him in His vimana, returned to Heaven.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — Vimana: the conveyance of the Devas, something like the flying machine of the present times.

## \|\| 7.65 \|\|

*yajñabhāgabhujo jātā marutaste tato dvijāḥ \|*  
*na jagmuraikyamasurair ataste suravallabhāḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. Since then, the Maruts are classed among the Devas. They receive their share of sacrificial offerings, and after leaving the demons their kith and kin, they have closely identified themselves with the Devas.

## Chapter 8

## \|\| 8.1 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ*  
*ādisargaśca yaḥ sūta kathito vistareṇa tu \|*  
*pratisargaśca ye yeṣām adhipās tānvadasva naḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. The Rishis said: — O Suta! We have heard with concentrated attention what you have been pleased to relate to us; now we feel desirous to know the lives of the kings that Nourished at each order of creation.

## \|\| 8.3 \|\|

*nakṣatratārādvijavṛkṣagulma-latāvitānasya ca rukmagarbhaḥ \|*  
*apāmadhīśaṃ varuṇaṃ dhanānāṃ rājñāṃ prabhuṃ vaiśravaṇaṃ ca tadvat \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. The Sage Suta said: — At the time when King Prithu was anointed and made lord of the world, Chandrama was made the king of medicinal herbs, sacrifices, fasts, penances, stars, planets, Brahmanas, trees, thickets, creepers; Varuna of waters; Kuvera of wealth and (other) kings; the Sun of the twelve Adityas; Agni of Vasus; Daksha of Prajapatis, Indra of gods; Prahlada of demons; Yama of pitris; Shiva of demons and Yakshas; the Himalayas of the mountains; the Ocean of the waters; Chitraratha of Gandharvas and Kumaras; Vasuki of powerful serpents.

## \|\| 8.2-8 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*yadābhiṣiktaḥ sakalādhirājye pṛthurdharitryāmadhipo babhūva \|*  
*tadauṣadhīnāmadhipaṃ cakāra yajñavratānāṃ tapasāṃ ca candram \|\| 2 \|\|*

*nakṣatratārādvijavṛkṣagulma-latāvitānasya ca rukmagarbhaḥ \|*  
*apāmadhīśaṃ varuṇaṃ dhanānāṃ rājñāṃ prabhuṃ vaiśravaṇaṃ ca tadvat \|\| 3 \|\|*

*viṣṇuṃ ravīṇāmadhipaṃ vasūnām agniṃ ca lokādhipatiścakāra \|*  
*prajāpatīnāmadhipaṃ ca dakṣaṃ cakāra śakraṃ marutāmadhīśam \|\| 4 \|\|*

*daityādhipānāmatha dānavānāṃ prahlādamīśaṃ ca yamaṃ pitriṇām \|*  
*piśācarakṣaḥpaśubhūtayakṣa-vetālarājaṃ tv atha śūlapāṇim \|\| 5 \|\|*

*prāleyaśailaṃ ca patiṃ girīṇām īśaṃ samudraṃ sasarinnadānām \|*  
*gandharvavidyādharakiṃnarāṇām īśaṃ punaścitrarathaṃ cakāra \|\| 6 \|\|*

*nāgādhipaṃ vāsukimugravīryaṃ sarpādhipaṃ takṣakamādideśa \|*  
*diśāṃ gajānāmadhipaṃ cakāra gajendramairāvatanāmadheyam \|\| 7 \|\|*

*suparṇamīśaṃ patatāmathāśva-rājānamuccaiḥśravasaṃ cakāra \|*  
*siṃhaṃ mṛgāṇāṃ vṛṣabhaṃ gavāṃ ca plakṣaṃ punaḥ sarvavanaspatīnām \|\| 8 \|\|*

2-8. Takshaka of other snakes; Airavata of the Diggajas and other elephants: the peacock of birds, Uchaishrava of horses; the lion of the animals living in jungles; the bull of the cows; the trees of the herbs.

## \|\| 8.9-10 \|\|

*pitāmahaḥ pūrvamathābhyaṣiñcac caitānpunaḥ sarvadiśādhināthān \|*  
*pūrveṇa dikpālam athābhyaṣiñcan nāmnā sudharmāṇam arātiketum \|\| 9 \|\|*

*tato 'dhipaṃ dakṣiṇataścakāra sarveśvaraṃ śaṅkhapadābhidhānam \|*  
*sa ketumantaṃ ca digīśamīśaś cakāra paścād bhuvanāṇḍagarbhaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. Similarly, Lord Brahma made the Devas Sudharma, Sankhapada, Ketumana, Hiranyaroma, the kings of East, South, West and North respectively: and They protect the universe by destroying its enemies, unto this day.

## \|\| 8.11-12 \|\|

*hiraṇyaromāṇam udagdigīśaṃ prajāpatir devasutaṃ cakāra \|*  
*adyāpi kurvanti diśām adhīśāḥ śatrūn dahantastu bhuvo 'bhirakṣām \|\| 11 \|\|*

*caturbhir ebhiḥ pṛthunāmadheyo nṛpo 'bhiṣiktaḥ prathamaṃ pṛthivyām \|*  
*gate 'ntare cākṣuṣanāmadheye vaivasvatākhye ca punaḥ pravṛtte \|*  
*prajāpatiḥ so 'sya carācarasya babhūva sūryānvayavaṃśacihnaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-12. The various kings named above, collected together and took part in the coronation of king Prithu, and recognized him as the sovereign of the world. King Prithu reigned till the end of Chakshusha Manvantara, when he was succeeded by King Vaivasvata Manu of the solar dynasty.

## Chapter 9

## \|\| 9.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*evaṃ śrutvā manuḥ prāha punareva janārdanam \|*  
*pūrveṣāṃ caritaṃ brūhi manūnāṃ madhusūdana \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. The Sage Suta said: “After hearing that, King Manu again requested the Fish God to narrate to him the career of the Manus who flourished in bygone ages”.

## \|\| 9.2 \|\|

*matsya uvāca*  
*manvantarāṇi rājendra manūnāṃ caritaṃ ca yat \|*  
*pramāṇaṃ caiva kālasya tāṃ sṛṣṭiṃ ca samāsataḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. The Fish God said: “O King! listen. I shall relate to you briefly the lives of the Manus of yore, and shall give you a short history of Manvantaras and their times.

## \|\| 9.3-6 \|\|

*ekacittaḥ praśāntātmā śṛṇu mārtaṇḍanandana \|*  
*yāmā nāma purā devā āsan svāyambhuvāntare \|\| 3 \|\|*

*saptaiva ṛṣayaḥ pūrve ye marīcyādayaḥ smṛtāḥ \|*  
*āgnīdhraścāgnibāhuśca sahaḥ savana eva ca \|\| 4 \|\|*

*jyotiṣmān dyutimān havyo medhā medhātithir vasuḥ \|*  
*svāyambhuvasyāsya manor daśaite vaṃśavardhanāḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*pratisargamime kṛtvā jagmuryatparamaṃpadam \|*  
*etat svāyambhuvaṃ proktaṃ svārociṣamataḥ param \|\| 6 \|\|*

3-6. “O Son of Martanda, hear attentively, In the bygone ages, at the close of the reign of Svayambhuva Manu there was a group of Devas, known as Yamas. In all Manvantaras, classes, such as Marichi, &., are recorded to have appeared. Svayambhuva Manu had ten sons, viz.: —

Agnidhra, Agnivahu, Riphpha, Savala, Jyotishmana, Dyutimana, Havya, Medha, Medhatithi, Vasu. They having established a code of law and morality departed to felicity. This has been narrated as the Svayambhuva Manvantara.

## \|\| 9.7-10 \|\|

*svārociṣasya tanayāś catvāro devavarcasaḥ \|*  
*nabhonabhasyaprasṛti-bhānavaḥ kīrtivardhanāḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*datto niścyavanastambaḥ prāṇaḥ kaṣyapa eva ca \|*  
*aurvo bṛhaspatiścaiva saptaite ṛṣayaḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*devāśca tuṣitā nāma smṛtāḥ svārociṣe 'ntare \|*  
*hastīndraḥ sukṛto mūrtir āpo jyotirayaḥ smayaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*vasiṣṭhasya sutāḥ sapta ye prajāpatayaḥ smṛtāḥ \|*  
*dvitīyametatkathitaṃ manvantaramataḥ param \|\| 10 \|\|*

7-10. The Svarochisha-manvantara followed it. There were of Svarochisha Manu four sons, viz., Nabha, Nabhashya, Prasuti, Bhavana. Of this Manvantara, the following are recorded as seven Rishis: viz., Datta, Nishchaya, Vanastamba, Prana, Kashyapa, Aurva, and Brihaspati.” The seven Devas of this Manvantara were sons of Vasistha, known as Tushita, Hastindra, Sukrita, Marti, Apa, Jyoti, and Ayasmaya.

## \|\| 9.11-14 \|\|

*auttamīyaṃ pravakṣyāmi tathā manvantaraṃ śubham \|*  
*manurnāmauttamiryatra daśa putrānajījanat \|\| 11 \|\|*

*īṣa ūrjaśca tarjaś ca śuciḥ śukrastathaiva ca \|*  
*madhuś ca mādhavaścaiva nabhasyo 'tha nabhāstathā \|\| 12 \|\|*

*sahaḥ kanīyāneteṣām udāraḥ kīrtivardhanaḥ \|*  
*bhāvanās tatra devāḥ syur ūrjāḥ saptarṣayaḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*kaukuruṇḍiśca dālbhyaśca śaṅgaḥ pravahaṇaḥ śivaḥ \|*  
*sitaśca sasmitaścaiva saptaite yogavardhanāḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

11-14. In the third or Auttamiya Manvantara, Manu named Auttami had ten sons, viz., Isha, Urja, Tarja, Suchi, Shukra, Madhu, Madhava, Nabhasya, Nabha, and Saha” (who was most illustrious). The group of Devas in this Manvantara was known by the name of havana, The following were the seven Rishis in this Manvantara who were also known by the name of Urja: —

Kaukurundi, Dalbhya, Shankha, Pravahana, Shiva, Sita, Sasmita,

## \|\| 9.13-16 \|\|

*sahaḥ kanīyāneteṣām udāraḥ kīrtivardhanaḥ \|*  
*bhāvanās tatra devāḥ syur ūrjāḥ saptarṣayaḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*kaukuruṇḍiśca dālbhyaśca śaṅgaḥ pravahaṇaḥ śivaḥ \|*  
*sitaśca sasmitaścaiva saptaite yogavardhanāḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*manvantaraṃ caturthaṃ tu tāmasaṃ nāma viśrutam \|*  
*kaviḥ pṛthus tathaivāgnir akapiḥ kapireva ca \|\| 15 \|\|*

*tathaiva jalpadhīmānau munayaḥ sapta tāmase \|*  
*sādhyā devagaṇā yatra kathitāstāmase 'ntare \|\| 16 \|\|*

13-16. In the fourth Manvantara, which was called Tamasa, the seven Rishis were: — Kavi, Prithu, Agni, Akapi, Kapi, Jalpa, and Dhimana; and the group of Devas were known by the name of Sadhya ”,

## \|\| 9.17-18 \|\|

*akalmaṣas tathā dhanvī tapomūlastapodhanaḥ \|*  
*taporatistapasyaśca tapodyutiparaṃtapau \|\| 17 \|\|*

*tapobhāgī tapoyogī dharmācāraratāḥ sadā \|*  
*tāmasasya sutāḥ sarve daśa vaṃśavivardhanāḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

17-18. The King Tamasa Manu had ten sons, viz.: — Akalmasha, Dhanvi, Tapomula, Tapodhana, Taporati, Tapasya, Tapodyuti, Parantapa, Tapobhogi and Tapoyogi.

## \|\| 9.19-22 \|\|

*pañcamasya manos tadvad raivatasyāntaraṃ śṛṇu \|*  
*devabāhuḥ subāhuśca parjanyaḥ somapo muniḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

*hiraṇyaromā saptāśvaḥ saptaite ṛṣayaḥ smṛtāḥ \|*  
*devāścābhūtarajasas tathā prakṛtayaḥ śubhāḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*aruṇas tattvadarśī ca vittavānhavyapaḥ kapiḥ \|*  
*yukto nirutsukaḥ sattvo nirmoho 'tha prakāśakaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*dharmavīryabalopetā daśaite raivatātmajāḥ \|*  
*bhṛguḥ sudhāmā virajāḥ sahiṣṇurnāda eva ca \|\| 22 \|\|*

19-22. In the \[fifth\] Raivat Manvantara, Devabahu, Subahu, Parjanya, Somapa, Hiranya-Roma, Saptashva were the seven Rishis; and Abhutarajas was the group of Devas. Aruna, Tatvadarshi, Vittavan, Havyapa, Kapi, Yukta, Nirutsuka, Satva, Nirmoha and Prakashaka were the ten pious and illustrious sons of Raivataka Manu.

## \|\| 9.23-25 \|\|

*vivasvānatināmā ca ṣaṣṭhe saptarṣayo 'pare \|*  
*cākṣuṣasyāntare devā lekhā nāma pariśrutāḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

*ṛbhavo 'tha ṛbhādyāś ca vārimūlā divaukasaḥ \|*  
*cākṣuṣasyāntare proktā devānāṃ pañca yonayaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*ruruprabhṛtayastadvac cākṣuṣasya sutā daśa \|*  
*proktāḥ svāyambhuve vaṃśe ye mayā pūrvameva tu \|\| 25 \|\|*

23-25. In the sixth or Chakshusha Manvantara, Bhrigu, Sudhama, Viraja, Sahishnu, Nada, Vivasvana and Atinama were the seven Rishis. The group of five Devas was, Lekhas, Ribhus, Ribhas, Barimulas and Divankasas in this Manvantara, Chakshusha Manu had ten sons, such as Urn, &c., as has been already mentioned by me in the genealogy of “Svayambhuva Manu in chapter IV”.

## \|\| 9.26 \|\|

*antaraṃ cākṣuṣaṃ caitan mayā te parikīrtitam \|*  
*saptamaṃ tatpravakṣyāmi yadvaivasvatamucyate \|\| 26 \|\|*

26 After the Chakshusha Manvantara, as narrated by me, shall occur the seventh Manvantara, which is called Vaivasvata.

## \|\| 9.27-31 \|\|

*atriś caiva vasiṣṭhaśca kaṣyapo gautamastathā \|*  
*bharadvājastathā yogī viśvāmitraḥ pratāpavān \|\| 27 \|\|*

*jamadagniśca saptaite sāmprataṃ ye maharṣayaḥ \|*  
*kṛtvā dharmavyavasthānaṃ prayānti paramaṃ padam \|\| 28 \|\|*

*sādhyā viśve ca rudrāśca maruto vasavo 'śvinau \|*  
*ādityāśca surāstadvat sapta devagaṇāḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*ikṣvākupramukhāścāsya daśa putrāḥ smṛtā bhuvi \|*  
*manvantareṣu sarveṣu sapta sapta maharṣayaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

*kṛtvā dharmavyavasthānaṃ prayānti paramaṃ padam \|*  
*sāvarṇyasya pravakṣyāmi manorbhāvi tathāntaram \|\| 31 \|\|*

27-31. In the Vaivasvata Manvantara, Atri, Vasistha, Gautama, Kashyapa, Bharadwaja, the powerful Yogi, Vishwamitra, Jamadagni, are the seven Rishis. The seven Rishis, after establishing a code of law and morality depart to felicity. Sadhyas, Visas, Rudras, Maruts, Vasus, Ashvinikumaras, Adityas are the classes of Devas in Vaivasvata Manvantara, The King Vaivasvata Manu had ten renowned sons, viz.—Ikshvaku, &e. In every Manvantara there are seven Rishis who, after establishing a code of law and morality, depart to felicity.

## \|\| 9.32-33 \|\|

*aśvatthāmā śaradvāṃśca kauśiko gālavastathā \|*  
*śatānandaḥ kāṣyapaśca rāmaśca ṛṣayaḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

*dhṛtir varīyān yavasaḥ suvarṇo vaṣṭireva ca \|*  
*cariṣṇur īḍyaḥ sumatir vasuḥ śukraśca vīryavān \|\| 33 \|\|*

32-33 Now I shall explain to you something about the Savarnya Manvantara. Ashvathama, Sharadvana, Kaushika, Galava, Satananda, Kashyapa, Rama, are the seven Rishis in this Manvantara. Dhriti, Variyana, Yavasa, Suvarna, Vrishti, Charishnu, Idya, Sumati, Vasu, Shukra are the ten valiant sons of the Manu Savarni”.

## \|\| 9.34 \|\|

*bhaviṣyā daśa sāvarṇer manoḥ putrāḥ prakīrtitāḥ \|*  
*raucyādayastathānye 'pi manavaḥ saṃprakīrtitāḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Rauchaya, &c., shall be another six Manus after Savarni. From Prajapati Ruchi there shall be Rauchya Manu, from Prajapati Bhutya there shall be Bhautya Manu and from Brahma there shall be Merusavarnya, Rita, Ritadhama, Vishvakeshna Manus.

“I have explained to you something about the past and future Manus, O, King! Similarly, commencing from the age of Devas, in the 994th age, the afore-mentioned fourteen Manus rule in succession. In their time, they play their part in the creation of the moveable and immoveable objects, and afterwards attain final rest with Brahma, at the end of the age. They (the Manus), after 1,000 ages, shall he absorbed in Brahma and be joined to Vishnu”.

## Chapter 10

## \|\| 10.1-2 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ*  
*bahubhir dhāriṇī bhuktā bhūpālaiḥ śrūyate purā \|*  
*pārthivāḥ pṛthivīyogāt pṛthivī kasya yogataḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*kim arthaṃ ca kṛtā saṃjñā bhūmeḥ kiṃ pāribhāṣikī \|*  
*gaur itīyaṃ ca vikhyātā sūta kasmādbravīhi naḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

1-2. The sages said that in ancient times the kings came to be called Parthiva, on account of their sway all over the land; but how did the earth come to be known as Prithvi? O Suta! tell us also why the earth came to be called “ Gau?”.

## \|\| 10.3-5 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*vaṃśe svāyambhuvasyāsīd aṅgo nāma prajāpatiḥ \|*  
*mṛtyostu duhitā tena pariṇītā sudurmukhā \|\| 3 \|\|*

*sunīthā nāma tasyāstu veno nāma sutaḥ purā \|*  
*adharmanirataścāsīd balavān vasudhādhipaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*loke 'pyadharmakṛdjātaḥ parabhāryāpahārakaḥ \|*  
*dharmācārasya siddhyarthaṃ jagato 'tha maharṣibhiḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

3-5. Sita said that Prajapati Anga, in the family of Svayambhuva Manu, was born who was married to the vile daughter of Mrityu, named Sunitha the shrew, who gave birth to Vena. King Vena was valiant, but oppressive and sinful. The sages, seeing the sinful deeds of the king, who used to forcibly seize the wealth and the women of others, approached him with the object of bringing about law and order by giving him good advice.

## \|\| 10.6-7 \|\|

*anunīto 'pi na dadāv anujñāṃ sa yadā tataḥ \|*  
*śāpena mārayitvainam arājakamayārditāḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*mamanthur brāhmaṇāstasya balāddehamakalmaṣāḥ \|*  
*tatkāyānmathyamānāttu nipeturmlecchajātayaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

6-7. But when the king did not listen to the good advice of the gages, they killed him by their curse. After that being afraid of anarchy, the sinless Brahmanas began to churn the dead body of the king from which - first came out the races of Mlechhas.

**Комментарий:**

Note — Mlechhas has been defined by Baudhayana as meaning “Non-Aryan, a foreigner, sinner, outcast, barbarian.”

## \|\| 10.8-10 \|\|

*śarīre māturaṃśena kṛṣṇāñjanasamaprabhāḥ \|*  
*pituraṃśasya cāṃśena dhārmiko dharmacāriṇaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*utpanno dakṣiṇāddhastāt sadhanuḥ saśaro gadī \|*  
*divyatejomayavapuḥ saratnakavacāṅgadaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*pṛthorevābhavadyatnāt tataḥ pṛthurajāyata \|*  
*sa viprairabhiṣikto 'pi tapaḥ kṛtvā sudāruṇam \|\| 10 \|\|*

8-10. Black as soot the barbarian race that came out of Venu was the outcome of the evil qualities of his mother; and from the portion of the good qualities of his pious father, appeared from the right hand of the dead king, a most brilliant figure, wearing an armor, studded with precious stones, and armed with bow and arrow in one hand and holding a club

in the other. The illustrious figure thus produced, after so much difficulty, was named Prithu. King Prithu was anointed by the Brahmanas, bat even then he practiced severe austerities.

## \|\| 10.11-12 \|\|

*viṣṇorvareṇa sarvasya prabhutvam agamat punaḥ \|*  
*niḥsvādhyāyavaṣaṭkāraṃ nirdharmaṃ vīkṣya bhūtalam \|\| 11 \|\|*

*dagdhumevodyataḥ kopāc chareṇāmitavikramaḥ \|*  
*tato gorūpamāsthāya bhūḥ palāyitum udyatā \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-12. Lord Vishnu, greatly moved by the profound devotion of the King Prithu, showered His blessings upon him. The king, after being thus blessed by the Lord, became most powerful and illustrious, On seeing the earth devoid of Vedic rites, he was filled with righteous indignation, and. prepared himself to destroy it with his never-failing arrow. The earthy tropes bling with fear, assumed the farm of a cow and took to fight.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — This expresses a beautiful allegory. The righteous king saw that the people had given up the practice of the Vedic rites and were drifting towards sin by leaps and bounds, Yatha Raja tatha Praja -no wonder, therefore, that the people should have become so much demoralized during the sway of his predecessor-the wicked Vena.

Prithu, the pious, could not possibly tolerate such a chaos, and in his rage he made up his wind to destroy the sinners, when suddenly a thought flashed through his mind that law and order could be evolved even without resorting to such an extreme measure. The land appeared to him like a cow that could give sweet milk, if properly milked, He therefore applied himself to uplift the degenerated and to take good care of the new generation.

Besides this, the Cow is the most important of all animals in India. She plays a great part in the agricultural prosperity of the country by bringing forth oxen. She nourishes the nation with her sweet milk and ghee. She is a very docile and harness creature, Her hide supplies shoes to the people. She takes motherly care of the nation, and that is why she is held so sacred by the Aryans who are the original inhabitants of Bharatavarsha, Even now a man, to seek forgiveness or shelter, put a Ina blade of grass in his month and addresses a real Aryan, “I am your cow, forgive me or save me.” The moment such a man approaches a true Aryan, he is rendered all possible assistance at every risk and stake by the Aryan.

Similarly, when that thought crossed the mind of Prithu, he compared the land to the cow, und then he could not destroy it.

Thirdly, it Is the poetic way of saying that, when the earth became so terribly afraid of the power of the king, it appealed for mercy by appearing before him and telling him that it was his cow.

Fourthly, the sinners, trembling with fear, craved the forgiveness of the sovereign by calling themselves his cow and promising to turn over a new leaf — which will be clear farther on.

## \|\| 10.13 \|\|

*pṛṣṭhato 'nugatastasyāḥ pṛthurdīptaśarāsanaḥ \|*  
*tataḥ sthitvaikadeśe tu kiṃ karomīti cābravīt \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. The earth went on running, and the king continued the chose.

After getting overpowered, she stopped and craved forgiveness and asked what to do.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — The allegory is continued. The king is portrayed as chasing the race of sinners who, to save their lives, are depicted to be running away and calling themselves cows, so that the king may not shoot his arrow at them. The sinners in their consternation have no courage to face their righteous sovereign, until they are deadbeat and can proceed no further. The sovereign would not let them run away, for he is anxious to reclaim and uplift them, He would therefore simply put his arrow on his bow to guard them from evils and also to atop them from running away to any out-of-the-way place.

A cow, when she rung away like this from her waster, is similarly chased by the latter with a stick in hand. The master does not mean to kill the cow with his stick. He carries it with him for his own safety as well as for hers. He also uses his stick in directing the footsteps of the animal. The bow and the arrow were similarly carried by the king in his pursuit of the earth that was running away (rein him in the form of a cow.

## \|\| 10.14-18 \|\|

*pṛthur apyavadad vākyam īpsitaṃ dehi suvrate \|*  
*sarvasya jagataḥ śīghraṃ sthāvarasya carasya ca \|\| 14 \|\|*

*tathaiva sābravīd bhūmir dudoha sa narādhipaḥ \|*  
*svake pāṇau pṛthurvatsaṃ kṛtvā svāyambhuvaṃ manum \|\| 15 \|\|*

*tadannamabhavacchuddhaṃ prajā jīvanti yena vai \|*  
*tatastu ṛṣibhirdugdhā vatsaḥ somastadābhavat \|\| 16 \|\|*

*dogdhā bṛhaspatirabhūt pātraṃ vedastapo rasaḥ \|*  
*devaiśca vasudhā dugdhā dogdhā mitrastadābhavat \|\| 17 \|\|*

*indro vatsaḥ samabhavat kṣīramūrjaskaraṃ balam \|*  
*devānāṃ kāñcanaṃ pātraṃ pitriṇāṃ rājataṃ tathā \|\| 18 \|\|*

14-18. At this, the king addressed the earth and asked her to quickly minister to the needs of all beings, whether moving or fixed. The land promised to obey the behests of the king. Then the king, after making Svayambhuva Manu as the calf, milked the earth in the form of the cow with his own bands, The earth then produced the different kinds of grain, which support mankind; after which the sages, using the moon as the calf and Brihaspati as the milk-man, milked the (earth) cow and extracted the milk of virtue in the pot of the Vedas, Then the Devas, after making the God Indra the calf and the God Mitra as the milkman, milked the (earth) cow. They drew out the milk of elixir-vitae in the pot of gold.

The Pitris also milked the same thing in the pot of silver.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — The allegory goes on. The quality and richness of the milk depend on the care and feeding of the cow, The earth is a cow that will give any kind of milk, provided due care is taken of it, and people milking it know how to do it.

## \|\| 10.19-22 \|\|

*antakaścābhavaddogdhā yamo vatsaḥ svadhā rasaḥ \|*  
*alābupātraṃ nāgānāṃ takṣako vatsako 'bhavat \|\| 19 \|\|*

*viṣaṃ kṣīraṃ tato dogdhā dhṛtarāṣṭro 'bhavatpunaḥ \|*  
*asurairapi dugdheyam āyase śakrapīḍinīm \|\| 20 \|\|*

*pātre māyām abhūd vatsaḥ prāhlādis tu virocanaḥ \|*  
*dogdhā dvimūrdhā tatrāsīn māyā yena pravartitā \|\| 21 \|\|*

*yakṣaiśca vasudhā dugdhā purāntardhānam īpsubhiḥ \|*  
*kṛtvā vaiśravaṇaṃ vatsam āmapātre mahīpate \|\| 22 \|\|*

19-22. Then Antaka, after making the God of death the calf, milked the (earth) cow and took out Svadha from it. Similarly, the Nagas, after making Takshaka the calf and Dhritarashtra as the milkman, got out poison in a gourd, and the Asuras, making Virochana the calf and Dvimurdha as milkman, pressed out Maya into a pot of iron. The Yakshas pressed out in an earthen pot the knowledge of making themselves invisible after making Kuvera the calf.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — Vaishravana is same as Kuvera, tae Gad of wealth.

## \|\| 10.23-28 \|\|

*pretarakṣogaṇairdugdhā dharā rudhiramulbaṇam \|*  
*raupyanābho 'bhavaddogdhā sumālī vatsa eva tu \|\| 23 \|\|*

*gandharvaiśca purā dugdhā vasudhā sāpsarogaṇaiḥ \|*  
*vatsaṃ caitrarathaṃ kṛtvā gandhānpadmadale tathā \|\| 24 \|\|*

*dogdhā vararucirnāma nāṭyavedasya pāragaḥ \|*  
*giribhirvasudhā dugdhā ratnāni vividhāni ca \|\| 25 \|\|*

*auṣadhāni ca divyāni dogdhā merurmahācalaḥ \|*  
*vatso 'bhūddhimavāṃs tatra pātraṃ śailamayaṃ punaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*vṛkṣaiśca vasudhā dugdhā kṣīraṃ chinnaprarohaṇam \|*  
*pālāśapātre dogdhā tu śālaḥ puṣpalatākulaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

*plakṣo 'bhavattato vatsaḥ sarvavṛkṣo dhanādhipaḥ \|*  
*evamanyaiśca vasudhā tadā dugdhā yathepsitam \|\| 28 \|\|*

23-28. The Pretas and Rakshasas, making Sumali the calf and Raupya the milkman, drew out the stream of blood, The Gandharvas and Apsaras made Chaitrarath the call and Vararuchi the milkman and got out on a lotus leaf various kinds of fragrance, and the mountains obtained several kinds of precious gems and medicinal herbs which they extracted in the foot of hill ranges, after making the Mount Himalaya the calf and the Mount Sumeru the milkman. The trees also in their turn took out the power of regerminating even after being lopped, in a leaf of Palisa (Butea frondosa), after making Shala (Shorea rebusta) the milkman and the fig-tree the calf. In the same way, everyone who milked the earth gut the “fruit” he wished for.

## \|\| 10.29-35 \|\|

*āur dhanāni saukhyaṃ ca pṛthau rājyaṃ praśāsati \|*  
*na daridrastadā kaścin na rogī na ca pāpakṛt \|\| 29 \|\|*

*nopasargabhayaṃ kiṃcit pṛthau rājani śāsati \|*  
*nityaṃ pramuditā lokā duḥkhaśokavivarjitāḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

*dhanuṣkoṭyā ca śailendrān utsārya sa mahābalaḥ \|*  
*bhuvastalaṃ samaṃ cakre lokānāṃ hitakāmyayā \|\| 31 \|\|*

*na puragrāmadurgāṇi na cāudhadharā narāḥ \|*  
*kṣayātiśayaduḥkhaṃ ca nārthaśāstrasya cādaraḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

*dharmaikavāsanā lokāḥ pṛthau rājyaṃ praśāsati \|*  
*kathitāni ca pātrāṇi yatkṣīraṃ ca mayā tava \|\| 33 \|\|*

*yeṣāṃ yatra rucistattad deyaṃ tebhyo vijānatā \|*  
*yajñaśrāddheṣu sarveṣu mayā tubhyaṃ niveditam \|\| 34 \|\|*

*duhitṛtvaṃ gatā yasmāt pṛthordharmavato mahī \|*  
*tadānurāgayogācca pṛthivī viśrutā budhaiḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

29-35. In the reign of King Prithu, people were long lived, wealthy, had peaceful relations with their neighbours. None was wicked, poor or sick. In the glorious reign of Prithu, there was no phenomenon fores boding evil that would have caused consternation to his subjects. Every one passed his days in perfect peace und contentment, without getting overcome by grief or pain, Prithu, the Great, by the power of his bow, made many a part of his extensive Empire habitable and culturable.

During the time of that valiant monarch, there was no need of a fortress, it was not necessary for the people to arm themselves, the science of political economy was not in vogue. It was simply lying unhonoured. All the people performed their duties and prescribed rites, “I have explained to you, O King! how they milked the earth and got out of it what they wished, from which it must he understood that, at the time of performing sacrificial rites, the thing that each got out of the earth should be offered to him.” The learned also call the land Prithvi because it was milked by the old King Prithu, the righteous.

## Chapter 11

## \|\| 11.2-3 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*vivasvānkaṣyapāt pūrvam adityāmabhavat sutaḥ \|*  
*tasya patnītrayaṃ tadvat saṃjñā rājñī prabhā tathā \|\| 2 \|\|*

*raivatasya sutā rājñī revataṃ suṣuve sutam \|*  
*prabhā prabhātaṃ suṣuve tvāṣṭrī saṃjñā tathā manum \|\| 3 \|\|*

2-3. The sages said, “O Suta! be pleased to relate to us the history “of the solar-and the lunar races.”

Suta said that in the days gone by Kashyapa begot from his wife, Aditi, a progeny named the Sun, and the latter had three wives, viz.: —

Samjna, Rajni and Prabha. Rajni, the daughter of Raivata, brought forth Revata, Prabha gave birth to Prabhata and Samjna, the daughter of Vishvakarma, became the mother of King (Vaivasvata) Manu.

## \|\| 11.4-7 \|\|

*yamaśca yamunā caiva yamalau tu babhūvatuḥ \|*  
*tatastejomayaṃ rūpam asahantī vivasvataḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*nārīmutpādayāmāsa svaśarīrādaninditām \|*  
*tvāṣṭrī svarūparūpeṇa nāmnā chāyeti bhāminī \|\| 5 \|\|*

*purataḥ saṃsthitāṃ dṛṣṭvā saṃjñā tāṃ pratyabhāṣata \|*  
*chāye taṃ bhaja bhartāram asmadīyaṃ varānane \|\| 6 \|\|*

*apatyāni madīyāni mātṛsnehena pālaya \|*  
*tathetyuktvā tu sā devam agamat kvāpi suvratā \|\| 7 \|\|*

4-7. Samjna also gave birth to Yama and a girl called, Yamuna, who were twins. When Samjna could not bear the power of the Sun, she produced from her body a lady known as Chhaya (shadow), Seeing Chhaya standing “face to face, Samjna directed her to serve her master and also to take motherly care of her progeny. On Chhaya’s agreeing to carry out her injunctions, Samjna went away somewhere.

## \|\| 11.8-12 \|\|

*kāmayāmāsa devo 'pi saṃjñeyamiti cādarāt \|*  
*janayāmāsa tasyāṃ tu putraṃ ca manurūpiṇam \|\| 8 \|\|*

*savarṇatvācca sāvarṇir manorvaivasvatasya ca \|*  
*tataḥ śaniṃ ca tapatīṃ viṣṭiṃ caiva krameṇa tu \|\| 9 \|\|*

*chāyāyāṃ janayāmāsa saṃjñeyamiti bhāskaraḥ \|*  
*chāyā svaputre 'bhyadhikaṃ snehaṃ cakre manau tathā \|\| 10 \|\|*

*pūrvo manustu cakṣāma na yamaḥ krodhamūrchitaḥ \|*  
*saṃtarjayāmāsa tadā pādamudyamya dakṣiṇam \|\| 11 \|\|*

*śaśāpa ca yamaṃ chāyā sakṣataḥ kṛmisaṃyutaḥ \|*  
*pādo 'yameko bhavitā pūyaśoṇitavisravaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

8-12. The Sun mistaking Chhaya for Samjna begot from her Savarni Manu so called because he is of the same Varna as Vaivasvata Mann and Shani, and also the two girls, named Tapati and Vishti. When Chhaya herself became the mother of these children, she began to devote more attention to her own offspring than to the progeny of Samjna. Manu did not mind this, but Yama took it seriously, and one day he lifted his right leg to kick Chhaya. Chhaya also, getting in a fit of rage, cursed Yama, and said that his leg would be eaten by worms and would always discharge pus and blood.

## \|\| 11.13-17 \|\|

*nivedayāmāsa pitur yamaḥ śāpādamarṣitaḥ \|*  
*niṣkāraṇamahaṃ śapto mātrā deva sakopayā \|\| 13 \|\|*

*bālabhāvānmayā kiṃcid udyataś caraṇaḥ sakṛt \|*  
*manunā vāryamāṇāpi mama śāpam adād vibho \|\| 14 \|\|*

*prāyo na mātā sāsmākaṃ śāpenāhaṃ yato hataḥ \|*  
*devo 'pyāha yamaṃ bhūyaḥ kiṃ karomi mahāmate \|\| 15 \|\|*

*maurkhyātkasya na duḥkhaṃ syād athavā karmasaṃtatiḥ \|*  
*anivāryā bhavasyāpi kā kathānyeṣu jantuṣu \|\| 16 \|\|*

*kṛkavākurmayā datto yaḥ kṛmīnbhakṣayiṣyati \|*  
*kledaṃ ca rudhiraṃ caiva vatsāyam apaneṣyati \|\| 17 \|\|*

13-17. Hearing such a dreadful curse, Yama went to his father and told him that he had been cursed for no fault of his by his mother. In a childish freak, he lifted up his foot at her, at which in spite of the entreaties of Manu, she pronounced that curse upon him. Yama, continuing, said that such an attitude of Chhaya showed that she was not their mother. The Sun said, what would he do. Who does not get into trouble by committing an act of folly? What to say of others, even the omnipotent Lord Shiva had to reap the fruits of His actions. But, in spite of all that, he would give him a cock that would destroy all the worms of his foot and would also remove the blood and pus flowing from it.

## \|\| 11.18-19 \|\|

*evamuktastapastepe yamastīvraṃ mahāyaśāḥ \|*  
*gokarṇatīrthe vairāgyāt phalapattrānilāśanaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*ārādhayanmahādevaṃ yāvadvarṣāutāutam \|*  
*varaṃ prādānmahādevaḥ saṃtuṣṭaḥ śūlabhṛttadā \|\| 19 \|\|*

18-19. On getting no redress from his father, Yama went to Gokarna tirtha, and began to practice severe penances by merely living on fruits, leaves and air. After practising penances for one hundred thousand years, Lord Shiva appeared and asked him to seek a boon.

## \|\| 11.20-21 \|\|

*vavre sa lokapālatvaṃ pitṛloke nṛpālayam \|*  
*dharmādharmātmakasyāpi jagatastu parīkṣaṇam \|\| 20 \|\|*

*evaṃ sa lokapālatvam agamacchūlapāṇinaḥ \|*  
*pitriṇāṃ cādhipatyaṃ ca dharmādharmasya cānagha \|\| 21 \|\|*

20-21. Yama asked the Lord for the power of protecting the world, the Kingdom of Pitris, and the faculty of distinguishing virtue from vice. The Lord granted him the boon he asked for, and then disappeared.

## \|\| 11.22-25 \|\|

*vivasvānatha tadjñātvā saṃjñāyāḥ karmaceṣṭitam \|*  
*tvaṣṭuḥ samīpamagamad ācacakṣe ca roṣavān \|\| 22 \|\|*

*tamuvāca tatastvaṣṭā sāntvapūrvaṃ dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*tavāsahantī bhagavan mahastīvraṃ tamonudam \|\| 23 \|\|*

*vaḍabārūpam āsthāya matsakāśam ihāgatā \|*  
*nivāritā mayā sā nu tvayā caiva divākara \|\| 24 \|\|*

*yasmād avijñātatayā matsakāśam ihāgatā \|*  
*tasmānmadīyaṃ bhavanaṃ praveṣṭuṃ na tvamarhasi \|\| 25 \|\|*

22-25 The Sun, causing fear to Chhaya, discovered that Samjna, after leaving her behind, had gone to live with her father. At this, he got very angry and went to Kuvera, and asked him to send Samjna back along with him, Hearing the above words of the Sun, Vishvakarma said that Samjna, not being able to bear his power, ran away in the form of a mare after leaving Chhaya behind. On reaching home, she was very severely taken to task for running away like that, and was denied admittance into the house.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — Vadavarupa means in the form of a mare — which implies that she ran at a great speed from the house of her Lord, the Sun, so that she might not be overtaken by him in the way.

## \|\| 11.26 \|\|

*evamuktā jagāmātha marudeśamaninditā \|*  
*vaḍabārūpam āsthāya bhūtale sampratiṣṭhitā \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Consequently, she repaired to Maru desha, where she was roaming about in the form of a mare.

**Комментарий:**

Note. This implies that even in Maru desha, Samjna was running about here and there at a tremendous pace, in order to find out for herself a good shelter where she could hide herself.

## \|\| 11.27-30 \|\|

*tasmātprasādaṃ kuru me yadyanugrahabhāgaham \|*  
*apaneṣyāmi te tejo yantre kṛtvā divākara \|\| 27 \|\|*

*rūpaṃ tava kariṣyāmi lokānandakaraṃ prabho \|*  
*tathetyuktaḥ sa raviṇā bhramau kṛtvā divākaram \|\| 28 \|\|*

*pṛthakcakāra tattejaś cakraṃ viṣṇor akalpayat \|*  
*triśūlaṃ cāpi rudrasya vajramindrasya cādhikam \|\| 29 \|\|*

*daityadānavasaṃhartuḥ sahasrakiraṇātmakam \|*  
*rūpaṃ cāpratimaṃ cakre tvaṣṭā padbhyāmṛte mahat \|\| 30 \|\|*

27-30. Vishvakarma, continuing his speech, said that, under the circumstances, he would like to diminish his power, provided the Sun would willingly accord him permission to do so. He suggested that he would reduce his power by means of a special instrument, after which he would become agreeably strong to every one; to which the Sun agreed, and.

Vishvakarma by his instrument, Bhrami, sliced away some portions of the Sun's unbearable power. Vishvakarma then made a quoit (Chakra) for Vishnu, a trident for Shiva and a Vajra (thunderbolt) for Indra to destroy the Daityas and Danavas out of the particles of power that he took away from the Sun. The Sun after that, became fairly agreeable; but as he did not allow any power to be reduced from his feet, they continued to be very dazzling.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — The feet of the Sun mean the rays.

## \|\| 11.31-33 \|\|

*na śaśākātha taddraṣṭuṃ pādarūpaṃ raveḥ punaḥ \|*  
*arcāsvapi tataḥ pādau na kaścitkārayet kvacit \|\| 31 \|\|*

*yaḥ karoti sa pāpiṣṭhāṃ gatimāpnoti ninditām \|*  
*kuṣṭharogamavāpnoti loke 'sminduḥkhasaṃyutaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

*tasmācca dharmakāmārthī citreṣvāyataneṣu ca \|*  
*na kvacitkārayetpādau devadevasya dhīmataḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

31-33. Nobody could stand the dazzle of his feet, and consequently let no one ever make the feet of the Sun in his image, for the purpose of worship even. One who makes the feet of the Sun in his image, goes to hell and suffers from leprosy. Let, therefore, no one, who is anxious for his own welfare, make the feet of the Sun, even in pictures or temples.

## \|\| 11.34-37 \|\|

*tataḥ sa bhagavāngatvā bhūrlokam amarādhipaḥ \|*  
*kāmayāmāsa kāmārto mukha eva divākaraḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

*aśvarūpeṇa mahatā tejasā ca samāvṛtaḥ \|*  
*saṃjñā ca manasā kṣobham agamadbhayavihvalā \|\| 35 \|\|*

*nāsāpuṭābhyāmutsṛṣṭaṃ paro 'yamiti śaṅkayā \|*  
*tadretasas tato jātāv aśvināv iti niścitam \|\| 36 \|\|*

*dasrau sutatvāt saṃjātau nāsatyau nāsikāgrataḥ \|*  
*jñātvā cirācca taṃ devaṃ saṃtoṣam agamat param \|\| 37 \|\|*

34-37. The sun, after thus getting his power modified by Vishvakarma, went out in the form of a horse and enjoyed himself in the company of Samjna, who, not recognizing him and taking him for another person, became terrified, but was helpless; she consequently ejected the semen virile through her nostrils, out of which Ashvinikumaras, called otherwise Nasatyas and Dashras, were born. They are called Nasatyas, because they were born from the nose (nasa), and Dashras, because they were born as Sons. Afterwards, Samjna recognized her Lord and became pleased, and went with her Lord in a vimana to heaven.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — Ashvarupena = means in the form of a horse — which implies that the Sun being overpowered with passion ran with the speed of a horse to enjoy himself in the company of Samjna.

Manasakshobham = was agitated in mind, because she could not recognize her Lord at the first sight. She met the Sun after a long time, and quite unexpectedly, and then there was a great difference in his features, as his power was moderated by Vishvakarma, The Son of course recognised Samjna, and mixed with her in the usual way. Samjna, being overpowered, became helpless, but was very much agitated in mind.

## \|\| 11.38-39 \|\|

*vimānenāgamatsvargaṃ patyā saha mudānvitā \|*  
*sāvarṇo 'pi manur merāv adyāpyāste tapodhanaḥ \|*  
*śanistapobalādāpa grahasāmyaṃ tataḥ punaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

*yamunā tapatī caiva punarnadyau babhūvatuḥ \|*  
*viṣṭirghorātmikā tadvat kālatvena vyavasthitā \|\| 39 \|\|*

38-39. Savarnya Manu is still living and practising penances unto this day on Mount Meru, and Shani, by means of his asceticism, brought about domestic concord (between the sons of Chhaya and Samjna). Yamuna and Tapati became rivers, and Vishti obtained dark blue colour and was located in time (Hell).

## \|\| 11.40-42 \|\|

*manor vaivasvatasyāsan daśa putrā mahābalāḥ \|*  
*ilas tu prathamasteṣāṃ putreṣṭyāṃ samajāyata \|\| 40 \|\|*

*ikṣvākuḥ kuśanābhaśca ariṣṭo dhṛṣṭa eva ca \|*  
*nariṣyantaḥ karūṣaśca śaryātiśca mahābalāḥ \|*  
*pṛṣadhraścātha nābhāgaḥ sarve te divyamānuṣāḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

*abhiṣicya manuḥ putram ilaṃ jyeṣṭhaṃ sa dhārmikaḥ \|*  
*jagāma tapase bhūyaḥ sa mahendravanālayam \|\| 42 \|\|*

40-42. Vaivasvata Manu had ten powerful sons, the eldest of whom was la, who was born by the performance of putreshti sacrifice. His brothers were: —

Ikshwaku, Kushanabha, — Arista, Dhrishta, Narishyanta, Karusha, Sharyati, Prishadhra and Nabhaga, who were all very valiant and illustrious.

Manu, after anointing his son Ila and putting the reins of the Government, into his hands, went to practise asceticism in the forest called Mahendravana.

## \|\| 11.43-44 \|\|

*atha digjayasiddhyartham ilaḥ prāyānmahīm imām \|*  
*bhramandvīpāni sarvāṇi kṣmābhṛtaḥ sampradharṣayan \|\| 43 \|\|*

*jagāmopavanaṃ śambhor aśvākṛṣṭaḥ pratāpavān \|*  
*kalpadrumalatākīrṇaṃ nāmnā śaravaṇaṃ mahat \|\| 44 \|\|*

43-44. After sometime, Ila started on an expedition of conquest and visited several countries, Following the horse, he happened to enter Saravana, the pleasure-garden of Shiva which was blooming with various kinds of trees, creepers and perenial foliage,

**Комментарий:**

Note. — Digjaya' means conquest.

‘Ashwakrishtah’ means led by the horse. The ancient practice of conquest was that the sovereign wishing to conquer the world used to let loose a horse and follow it with his army. The monarchs through whose dominions the horse passed would either let it pass on without resistance, which implied their accepting the master of it as their sovereign lord, or would capture and tie it up. In the latter case there used to be a fight between the master of the horse and the monarch tying the animal. If the sovereign led by his horse returned to his kingdom after thus subduing the monarchs offering resistance or being acknowledged as their sovereign lord, then he used to perform the Rajasuya sacrifice, in which all the monarchs were invited to take part; at the conclusion of which the sovereign performing the sacrifice used to be declared and accepted as the sovereign lord of all the kings present.

## \|\| 11.45-46 \|\|

*ramate yatra deveśaḥ śambhuḥ somārdhaśekharaḥ \|*  
*umayā samayastatra purā śaravaṇe kṛtaḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

*puṃnāma sattvaṃ yatkiṃcid āgamiṣyati te vane \|*  
*strītvameṣyati tatsarvaṃ daśayojanamaṇḍale \|\| 46 \|\|*

45-46. At that time, Shiva and Parvati were enjoying themselves in their Saravana, and they had willed it that any male being, coming within a radius of ten yojanas of their forest, would be transformed into a female being.

## \|\| 11.47-50 \|\|

*ajñātasamayo rājā ilaḥ śaravaṇe purā \|*  
*strītvamāpa viśann eva vaḍabātvaṃ hayastadā \|\| 47 \|\|*

*puruṣatvaṃ hṛtaṃ sarvaṃ strīrūpe vismito nṛpaḥ \|*  
*ileti sābhavannārī pīnonnataghanastanī \|\| 48 \|\|*

*unnataśroṇijaghanā padmapattrāyatekṣaṇā \|*  
*pūrṇenduvadanā tanvī vilāsollāsitekṣaṇā \|\| 49 \|\|*

*mūlonnatāyatabhujā nīlakuñcitamūrdhajā \|*  
*tanulomā sudaśanā mṛdugambhīrabhāṣiṇī \|\| 50 \|\|*

47-50. The King Ila entering the Saravana, without knowing the will of Shiva and Parvati, was instantly transformed into a woman, and his horse was also transformed into a mare. The king, thus deprived of manhood, was very much amazed to find himself in the form of a woman, He was named Ila and had breasts like women. His thighs became stouter and his face became like the moon — which made him look more enchanting in that female form, Who would not be enamoured by the glances of such a beautiful form? His arms were long, his black tresses of hair were kissing his feet, there were no hair on his body, his teeth were well-shaped, and his voice was exquisitely sonorous.

## \|\| 11.51 \|\|

*śyāmagaureṇa varṇena haṃsavāraṇagāminī \|*  
*kārmukabhrūyugopetā tanutāmranakhāṅkurā \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. His complexion was a happy admixture of dark and white, his strut was graceful like that of hamsa (crane) and elephant, his brows were like the bow and his nails were tine and red.

## \|\| 11.52-54 \|\|

*bhramantī ca vane tasmiṃś cintayāmāsa bhāminī \|*  
*ko me pitāthavā bhrātā kā me mātā bhavediha \|\| 52 \|\|*

*kasya bharturahaṃ dattā kiyadvatsyāmi bhūtale \|*  
*cintayantīti dadṛśe somaputreṇa sāṅganā \|\| 53 \|\|*

*ilā rūpasamākṣipta-manasā varavarṇinī \|*  
*budhastadāptaye yatnam akarotkāmapīḍitaḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

52-54. Ila, of such unsurpassing beauty. began to roam about in that forest, and was thinking as to who and where were her father, brother and mother. She also thought as to who and where was her lord and how long would she have to remain in the world. As she was lost-in that reverie, the son of the moon appeared before her. On seeing ns, of matchless beauty, Budha — the son of the moon--was fired with passion and began to devise plans for marrying her.

## \|\| 11.55-58 \|\|

*viśiṣṭākāravāndaṇḍī sakamaṇḍalupustakaḥ \|*  
*veṇudaṇḍakṛtāneka-pavitrakagaṇatrikaḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

*dvijarūpaḥ śikhī brahmā nigadankarṇakuṇḍalaḥ \|*  
*baṭubhiścānvito uktaiḥ samitpuṣpakuśodakaiḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

*kilānviṣan vane tasmin nājuhāva sa tāmilām \|*  
*bahir vanasyāntaritaḥ kila pādapamaṇḍale \|\| 57 \|\|*

*sasaṃbhramamakasmāttāṃ sopālambhamivāvadat \|*  
*tyaktvāgnihotraśuśrūṣāṃ kva gatā mandirānmama \|\| 58 \|\|*

55-58. One day Budha, with a mace, a water-pot and a book in his hand, and accompanied by a train of Brahmacharis, each holding a bamboo mace and wearing ear-rings, set out in quest of kusha and sacrificial fuel. He passed close to that forest where Ila was roaming. Seeing Ila, Budha stopped behind a tree, at a distance from the forest, and from there beckoned Ili to come to him.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — Brahmachari means a student. In olden days, students were made to lead the life of perfect celibacy, They carried a bamboo mace and wore ear-rings, Budha was careful enough not to get within the forbidden limits of the pleasuregarden, for fear of being transformed into a woman.

## \|\| 11.59-60 \|\|

*iyaṃ vihāravelā te hy atikrāmati sāmpratam \|*  
*ehyehi pṛthusuśroṇi saṃbhrāntā kena hetunā \|\| 59 \|\|*

*iyaṃ sāyantanī velā vihārasyeha vartate \|*  
*kṛtvopalepanaṃ puṣpair alaṃkuru gṛhaṃ mama \|\| 60 \|\|*

59-60. When Ila approached Budha, the latter said, “Dear! This is not the proper time for you to roam about in the forest. Why did you come away leaving me at home and neglecting the arrangements of agnihotra? Come, come, why are you looking perplexed? This is the time when you should have put the house in order by washing the floor and decorating it with flowers. It is now dusk, and not the time for you to be sauntering about here."

## \|\| 11.61 \|\|

*sā tv abravīd viramṛtāhaṃ sarvametattapodhana \|*  
*ātmānaṃ tvāṃ ca bhartāraṃ kulaṃ ca vada me 'nagha \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Hearing those words of Budha, Ila said, “Lord! I know not why I forgot to do what you have just said. I am really in a peculiar fit of forgetfulness at present, so much so that I am not able to recognise either myself or yourself. Tell me where you live, O Pious one!”

## \|\| 11.62-66 \|\|

*budhaḥ provāca tāṃ tanvīm ilā tvaṃ varavarṇinī \|*  
*ahaṃ ca kāmuko nāma bahuvidyo budhaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

*tejasvinaḥ kule jātaḥ pitā me brāhmaṇādhipaḥ \|*  
*iti sā tasya vacanāt praviṣṭā budhamandiram \|\| 63 \|\|*

*ratnastambhasamāuktaṃ divyamāyāvinirmitam \|*  
*ilā kṛtārthamātmānaṃ mene tadbhavanasthitā \|\| 64 \|\|*

*aho vṛttamaho rūpam aho dhanamaho kulam \|*  
*mama cāsya ca me bhartur aho lāvaṇyam uttamam \|\| 65 \|\|*

*reme ca sā tena samam atikālamilā tataḥ \|*  
*sarvabhogamaye gehe yathendrabhavane tathā \|\| 66 \|\|*

62-66. Budha replied that her name was Ha and that he was Kamuka, who, owing to his versatile genius and deep lore, was known as Budha (a learned scholar), He was born in an illustrious family. His father was the lord of Brahmanas. Hearing those words of Budha, Ila accompanied him to his residence, She was overjoyed to see the house of Budha, with its golden pillars studded with precious stones and erected through divine magic; and greatly admired the character, the appearance, the riches and the family of her husband. Ila, for a long time, thus enjoyed herself in the house of Budha that looked to her like the house of Indra.

## Chapter 12

## \|\| 12.1-7 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*athānviṣanto rājānaṃ bhrātaras tasya mānavāḥ \|*  
*ikṣvākupramukhā jagmus tadā śaravaṇāntikam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*tataste dadṛśuḥ sarve vaḍabām agrataḥ sthitām \|*  
*ratnaparyāṇakiraṇa-dīptakāyām anuttamām \|\| 2 \|\|*

*paryāṇapratyabhijñānāt sarve vismayam āgatāḥ \|*  
*ayaṃ candraprabho nāma vājī tasya mahātmanaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*agamad vaḍabārūpam uttamaṃ kena hetunā \|*  
*tatas tu maitrāvaruṇiṃ papracchuste purodhasam \|\| 4 \|\|*

*kimityetadabhūccitraṃ vada yogavidāṃ vara \|*  
*vasiṣṭhaścābravīt sarvaṃ dṛṣṭvā taddhyānacakṣuṣā \|\| 5 \|\|*

*samayaḥ śambhudayitā-kṛtaḥ śaravaṇe purā \|*  
*yaḥ pumānpraviśed atra sa nārītvamavāpsyati \|\| 6 \|\|*

*ayamaśvo 'pi nārītvam agādrājñā sahaiva tu \|*  
*punaḥ puruṣatāmeti yathāsau dhanadopamaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

1-7. Suta said that sometime after Ikshwaku, &c., the brothers of Ila, set out in quest of him. In their wanderings they chanced to pass by the Saravana, where they came across the mare, on which was the saddle, glittering with jewels. On seeing the mare with that jewelled saddle, they all recognised it to be Chandraprabha, the famous charger of the Monarch Ila. They were highly astonished to find the charger transformed into a mare, and questioned the priest Maitra-Varuna (Vasistha) about it.

The sage began to explain to them the mystery, through his powers of Yoga. The sage Vasistha said that Shiva and Parvati had determined that anyone entering the limits of their pleasure-garden would instantly be transformed into a female figure. Unfortunately, both the king and the horse happened to do so and they were transformed accordingly. The brothers of the transformed monarch then besought the great sage to devise some means by which Ila could be restored to manhood.

## \|\| 12.8-11 \|\|

*tathaiva yatnaḥ kartavyaś cārādhyaiva pinākinam \|*  
*tataste mānavā jagmur yatra devo maheśvaraḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*tuṣṭuvur vividhaiḥ stotraiḥ pārvatīparameśvarau \|*  
*tāv ūcatur alaṅghyo 'yaṃ samayaḥ kiṃtu sāmpratam \|\| 9 \|\|*

*ikṣvākoraśvamedhena yatphalaṃ syāttadāvayoḥ \|*  
*dattvā kimpuruṣo vīraḥ sa bhaviṣyatyasaṃśayam \|\| 10 \|\|*

*tathetyuktāstataste tu jagmur vaivasvatātmajāḥ \|*  
*ikṣvākoścāśvamedhena celaḥ kimpuruṣo 'bhavat \|\| 11 \|\|*

8-11. Vasistha said that, by devoutly worshipping Shiva, the monarch could be restored to manhood, Hearing that, the brothers of Ila (Sons of Manu) repaired to the abode of Shiva; where they pleased Him by their devotion. The God then said that He could not go against His determination, but that if Ikshwaku performed the ashvamedha sacrifice, then Ila would become a Kimpurusha (Mongolian type?), though it would be impossible for him to assume his previous (Aryan?) form, After that, the brothers of Ila performed the ashvamedha sacrifice, and the latter became a Kimpurusha.

## \|\| 12.12-13 \|\|

*māsamekaṃ pumānvīraḥ strī ca māsamabhūtpunaḥ \|*  
*budhasya bhavane tiṣṭhan nilo garbhadharo 'bhavat \|\| 12 \|\|*

*ajījanatputramekam anekaguṇasaṃyutam \|*  
*budhaścotpādya taṃ putraṃ svarlokam agamattataḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

12-13. On becoming a Kimpurusha, Ila used to remain in the form of a man for one month and the next month he used to become a woman again.

Ha, in the form of Ila, conceived in the house of Budha, and gave birth to a notable son, Budha, after the birth of that son, went to heaven.

## \|\| 12.14-15 \|\|

*ilasya nāmnā tadvarṣam ilāvṛtam abhūttadā \|*  
*somārkavaṃśayor ādāv ilo 'bhūnmanunandanaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*evaṃ purūravāḥ puṃsor abhavad vaṃśavardhanaḥ \|*  
*ikṣvākur arkavaṃśasya tathaivoktastapodhanāḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

14-15. That region where this happened, came to be known as Ilavritavarsha (Mongolia?), and Ila ‘in that way appeared at the inception of the Solar and the Lunar races, In other words, Pururava, the son of Budha, from Ila, was the founder of the lunar race, and Ikshvaku of the solar clan.

## \|\| 12.16-19 \|\|

*ilaḥ kimpuruṣatve ca sudyumna iti cocyate \|*  
*punaḥ putratrayamabhūt sudyumnasyāparājitam \|\| 16 \|\|*

*utkalo vai gahas tadvad dharitāśvaś ca vīryavān \|*  
*utkalasyotkalā nāma gayasya tu gayā matā \|\| 17 \|\|*

*haritāśvasya dikpūrvā viśrutā kurubhiḥ saha \|*  
*pratiṣṭhāne 'bhiṣicyātha sa purūravasaṃ sutam \|\| 18 \|\|*

*jagāmelāvṛtaṃ bhoktuṃ varṣaṃ divyaphalāśanam \|*  
*ikṣvākurjyeṣṭhadāyādo madhyadeśamavāptavān \|\| 19 \|\|*

16-19. Ila, after becoming Kimpurusha, came to be known as Sudyumna, Sudyumna became the father of Utkal, Gaya, Haritashva. Utkal became the king of Utkala, Gaya of Gaya, Haritashva of Purvakuru country. Pururava became the monarch of Pratisthana and Ikshvaku of Madhyadesa.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — Utkala is modern Orissa. Pratisthana, the country situated opposite to Allahabad, the modern Jhushi. Madhyadesa, the country lying between the Himalaya and Vindhya mountains. Kuru, about the site of modern Delhi.

## \|\| 12.20-21 \|\|

*nariṣyantasya putro 'bhūc chuco nāma mahābalaḥ \|*  
*nābhāgasyāmbarīṣastu dhṛṣṭasya ca sutatrayam \|\| 20 \|\|*

*dhṛtaketuścitranātho raṇadhṛṣṭaśca vīryavān \|*  
*ānarto nāma śaryāteḥ sukanyā caiva dārikā \|\| 21 \|\|*

20-21. Narishyanta was the father of Shucha, Nibhaga of Ambarisha, Dhrishta of 3 sons, named Dhritaketu, Chitranatha and Ranadhristra, Saryati of Anarta and of a good girl, named Darika.

## \|\| 12.22 \|\|

*ānartasyābhavatputro rocamānaḥ pratāpavān \|*  
*ānarto nābha deśo 'bhūn nagarī ca kuśasthalī \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Rochanana was the son of Anarta. He was very valiant, and was the sovereign of Anarta country which had Kashasthali for its capital.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — Anartadesha is the same as Dwarika; Kushasthali is the country situated in the defiles of the Vindhya.

## \|\| 12.23-24 \|\|

*rocamānasya putro 'bhūd revo raivata eva ca \|*  
*kakudmī cāparaṃ nāma jyeṣṭhaḥ putraśatasya ca \|\| 23 \|\|*

*revatī tasya sā kanyā bhāryā rāmasya viśrutā \|*  
*karūṣasya tu kārūṣā bahavaḥ prathitā bhuvi \|\| 24 \|\|*

23-24. Rochamana was the father of Reva, who became the father of a hundred children, the eldest of whom was Raivata, also named Kakudmi. He had also a daughter, named Revati, who was the wife of Balarama. Karusha begot innumerable progeny, who were known by the name of Karusha. Prishadhra became shudra by the curse of his preceptor for killing a cow.

## \|\| 12.25-30 \|\|

*pṛṣadhro govadhācchūdro guruśāpādajāyata \|*  
*ikṣvākuvaṃśaṃ vakṣyāmi śṛṇudhvamṛṣisattamāḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*ikṣvākoḥ putratām āpa vikukṣir nāma devarāṭ \|*  
*jyeṣṭhaḥ putraśatasyāsīd daśa pañca ca tatsutāḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*meroruttarataste tu jātāḥ pārthivasattamāḥ \|*  
*caturdaśottaraṃ cānyac chatamasya tathābhavat \|\| 27 \|\|*

*merordakṣiṇato ye ye rājānaḥ saṃprakīrtitāḥ \|*  
*jyeṣṭhaḥ kakutstho nāmnābhūt tatsutastu suyodhanaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

*tasya putraḥ pṛthurnāma viśvagaścapṛthoḥ sutaḥ \|*  
*industasya ca putro 'bhūd uvanāśvastato 'bhavat \|\| 29 \|\|*

*śrāvastaśca mahātejā vatsakastatsuto 'bhavat \|*  
*nirmitā yena śrāvastī gauḍadeśe dvijottamāḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

25-30. Rishis! now listen, I am going to relate to you the family of Ikshvaku: —

Of the hundred sons of Ikshvaku, Vikukshi was the eldest whose fifteen sons reigned in the country to the north of Mount Meru, and one hundred and fourteen to the south of it. The eldest of the Kings who reigned south of Meru was Kakutsu, whose son was Suyodhana, the father of Prithu. The latter was the father of Vishvaga, Vishvaga of Indu and Indu of Yuvanashva.

Shravasta, the son of Yuvanashva was the founder of the town of Shravasti, in the country of Gauda.

## \|\| 12.31-32 \|\|

*śrāvastādbṛhadaśvo 'bhūt kuvalāśvas tato 'bhavat \|*  
*dhundhumāratvamagamad dhundhunāmnā hataḥ purā \|\| 31 \|\|*

*tasya putrās trayo jātā dṛḍhāśvo daṇḍa eva ca \|*  
*kapilāśvaśca vikhyāto dhaundhumāriḥ pratāpavān \|\| 32 \|\|*

31-32. Note — Shravasti, a town in northern Koshala, where Lava reigned. It is also called Sravati.in Raghuvamsa. It is identified with Sahet Mahet, north of Ayodhya. Gouila = Gour in Northern Bengal.

Shravasta was the father of Brihadashva, and the latter of Kuvalashva, who was also called Dhundhumara, on account of his having killed \[a demon named\] Dhundhu. The valiant Dhundhumara had three sons, viz., — Dridhashva, Danda and Kapilashva.

## \|\| 12.33 \|\|

*dṛḍhāśvasya pramodaśca haryaśvastasya cātmajaḥ \|*  
*haryaśvasya nikumbho 'bhūt saṃhatāśvas tato 'bhavat \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Dridhashva was the father of Pramoda, the latter of Haryashva, Haryashva of Nikumbha and Nikumbha of Samhatashva.

## \|\| 12.34 \|\|

*akṛtāśvo raṇāśvaśca saṃhatāśvasutāv ubhau \|*  
*yuvanāśvo raṇāśvasya māndhātā ca tato 'bhavat \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Samhatashva had two sons, Akritashva and Ranashva. Ranashva was the father of Yuvanashva, and the latter of Mandhata.

## \|\| 12.35 \|\|

*māndhātuḥ purukutso 'bhūd dharmasenaśca pārthivaḥ \|*  
*mucukundaśca vikhyātaḥ śatrujicca pratāpavān \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Mandhata’s sons were. — Purukutsa, Dharmasena, Muchakunda and Satrajit.

## \|\| 12.36-39 \|\|

*purukutsasya putro 'bhūd vasudo narmadāpatiḥ \|*  
*sambhūtistasya putro 'bhūt tridhanvā ca tato 'bhavat \|\| 36 \|\|*

*tridhanvanaḥ suto jātas trayyāruṇa iti smṛtaḥ \|*  
*tasmātsatyavrato nāma tasmātsatyarathaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

*tasya putro hariścandro hariścandrācca rohitaḥ \|*  
*rohitācca vṛko jāto vṛkādbāhurajāyata \|\| 38 \|\|*

*sagarastasya putro 'bhūd rājā paramadhārmikaḥ \|*  
*dve bhārye sagarasyāpi prabhā bhānumatī tathā \|\| 39 \|\|*

36-39. Purukutsa who had a son, named Vasuda, was the lord of Narmada.

Vasuda became the father of Sambhuti, and the latter of Tridhanva.

Tridhanva was the father of Trayaruna, the latter of Satyavrata and Satyaratha was the son of Satyavrata. Satyaratha was the father of Harishchandra, the latter of Rohita; Rohita of Vrika and Vrika of Bahu. Sagara was the son of Bahu, and Prabha and Bhanumati were the two wives of Sagara the pious.

## \|\| 12.39-41 \|\|

*sagarastasya putro 'bhūd rājā paramadhārmikaḥ \|*  
*dve bhārye sagarasyāpi prabhā bhānumatī tathā \|\| 39 \|\|*

*tābhyāmārādhitaḥ pūrvam aurvo 'gniḥ putrakāmyayā \|*  
*aurvastuṣṭastayoḥ prādād yatheṣṭaṃ varamuttamam \|\| 40 \|\|*
