*ekā ṣaṣṭisahasrāṇi sutamekaṃ tathāparā \|*  
*gṛhṇātu vaṃśakartāraṃ prabhāgṛhṇād bahūṃstadā \|\| 41 \|\|*

39-41. Both the queens of Sagara, desirous of \[begetting\] sons, propitiated the sage, Aurva Agni, who became pleased and said that he would bless one to beget sixty thousand sons and the other he would bless to beget only one son, who would continue the line of the Solar race. They were welcome to make a choice for themselves. Prabha wished to be the mother of sixty thousand sons.

## \|\| 12.42 \|\|

*ekaṃ bhānumatī putram agṛhṇādasamañjasam \|*  
*tataḥ ṣaṣṭisahasrāṇi suṣuve yādavī prabhā \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Bhanumati begot a son, named Asamajnasa, and Prabha of the family of Yadu, became the mother of sixty thousand sons.

## \|\| 12.43-44 \|\|

*khanantaḥ pṛthivīṃ dagdhā viṣṇunā ye 'śvamārgaṇe \|*  
*asamañjasastu tanayo yo 'ṃśumānnāma viśrutaḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

*tasya putro dilīpas tu dilīpāttu bhagīrathaḥ \|*  
*yena bhāgīrathī gaṅgā tapaḥ kṛtvāvatāritā \|\| 44 \|\|*

43-44. Once upon a time, the sixty thousand sons of Prabha were reduced to ashes by the Sage Kapila — an incarnation of Vishnu--while they were digging the earth in search of the Ashvamedha horse. The wife of Asamanjasa gave birth to Amu. Dilipa was the son of Amshu, and Bhagiratha, who brought the mother Ganges to the earth after practising great penances, was the son of Dilipa.

## \|\| 12.45-47 \|\|

*bhagīrathasya tanayo nābhāga iti viśrutaḥ \|*  
*nābhāgasyāmbarīṣo 'bhūt sindhudvīpas tato 'bhavat \|\| 45 \|\|*

*tasyāutāuḥ putro 'bhūd ṛtuparṇastato 'bhavat \|*  
*tasya kalmāṣapādastu sarvakarmā tataḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

*tasyānaraṇyaḥ putro 'bhūn nighnastasya suto 'bhavat \|*  
*nighnaputrāv ubhau jātāv anamitraraghū nṛpau \|\| 47 \|\|*

45-47. The queen of Bhagiratha gave birth to Nabhaga, and the latter was the father of Ambarisha. Ambarisha became the father of Sindhudvipa.

Sindhudvipa was the father of Ayutayu, the latter of Rituparna.

Kalmasapada was the son of Rituparna and the father of Sarvakarma.

Sarvakarma was the father of Anaranya, and the latter of Nighna.

Nighna became the father of Anamitra and Raghu.

## \|\| 12.48 \|\|

*anāmitro vanamagād bhavitā sa kṛte nṛpaḥ \|*  
*raghor abhūddilīpastu dilīpādajakastathā \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Anamitra went to the forest to practice penances, and Raghu became the father of Dilipa, and the latter of Aja.

## \|\| 12.49-51 \|\|

*dīrghabāhurajādjātaś cājapālastato nṛpaḥ \|*  
*tasmāddaśaratho jātas tasya putracatuṣṭayam \|\| 49 \|\|*

*nārāyaṇātmakāḥ sarve rāmasteṣvagrajo 'bhavat \|*  
*rāvaṇāntakarastadvad raghūṇāṃ vaṃśavardhanaḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

*vālmīkistasya caritaṃ cakre bhārgavasattamaḥ \|*  
*tasya putrau kuśalavāv ikṣvākukulavardhanau \|\| 51 \|\|*

49-51. Dirghabahu was the son of Aja, Ajapala of Dirghabahu and Dasharatha of Ajapala, Dasharatha became the father of four sons, who were the incarnations of Narayana, and Rima, who killed Ravana, was the eldest, and whose biography was written by the great poet Valmiki. Rama was the father of Lava and Kusha.

## \|\| 12.57 \|\|

*ete vaivasvate vaṃśe rājāno bhūridakṣiṇāḥ \|*  
*ikṣvākuvaṃśaprabhavāḥ prādhānyena prakīrtitāḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Kuga was the father of Atithi whose son was Nishadha, the latter was father of Nala, and Nala was the father of Nabha. Pundarika was the son of Nabha and father of Kshemadhanva. Kshemadhanva was the father of Devanika. Devanika was the father Ahinagu, and the latter of Sahasrashva. Chandravaloka was the son of Sahasrashva and father of Tarapida. Chandragiri was the son of Tarapida and father of Bhanuchandra. The latter was the father of Shrutayu, who was killed in the great war of Bharata. In the family of Kashyapa there were two Nalas, viz. — one, the son of Virasena and the other of Nishadha.

Suta said: “I have related to you the names of the chief kings of In the dynasty of Vaivasvata and of Ikshvaku race.”

## Chapter 13

## \|\| 13.12-17 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*dakṣasya yajñe vitate prabhūtavaradakṣiṇe \|*  
*samāhūteṣu deveṣu provāca pitaraṃ satī \|\| 12 \|\|*

*kimarthaṃ tāta bhartā me yajñe 'sminnābhimantritaḥ \|*  
*ayogya iti tāmāha dakṣo yajñeṣu śūlabhṛt \|\| 13 \|\|*

*upasaṃhārakṛdrudras tenāmaṅgalabhāgayam \|*  
*cukopātha satī dehaṃ tyakṣyāmīti tvadudbhavam \|\| 14 \|\|*

*daśānāṃ tvaṃ ca bhavitā pitriṇāmekaputrakaḥ \|*  
*kṣatriyatve 'śvamedhe ca rudrāttvaṃ nāśameṣyasi \|\| 15 \|\|*

*ityuktvā yogamāsthāya svadehodbhavatejasā \|*  
*nirdahantī tadātmānaṃ sadevāsurakiṃnaraiḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*kiṃ kimetaditi proktā gandharvagaṇaguhyakaiḥ \|*  
*upagamyābravīddakṣaḥ praṇipatyātha duḥkhitaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

12-17. Manu said: “Lord! I am very eager to hear something about the important family of the Pitris of the Sun and the Moon.” — (1).

The God Fish replied that, out of the seven groups of the ‘Pitris residing in Heaven, the Pitris belonging to three. particular groups are without form, (that is composed of intellectual, not elemental, substance), while the Pitris of the remaining four groups have form (i.e., corporeal), The formless ones are the Pitris of Prajapati Vairaja. (2-3).

The celebrated Vairaja devas, disturbed in their yoga practices having attained to ancient regions, worship there. — (4) These Brahmavadins are reborn at the end of Brahma’s day, and by their previous practice of yoga, they acquire the memory of their past lives and the knowledge of Sankhya Yoga, which begets in them Supernatural faculties and enables them to attain to Nirvana. It is therefore very fruitful to feed the yogis at the time of performing a funeral ceremony in honour of the departed spirits. — (5-6).

Mena, the queen of Himalayas was the manas a daughter of the Pitris.

She was the mother of Menaka and Krauncha of whom the latter was the elder. The continent, surrounded by the ghrita ocean and adorned with the range of Krauncha hills, came to be known as Krauncha continent, Mena also became the mother of the following three daughters: —

Uma, Ekaparne, and Aparna, who were devoted to the practices of yoga and rigorous penances. Himalaya gave Uma to Shiva, Ekaparna to Nita, and Aparna to Jaigishavya. All these were given to performances of great penances. — (7-9).

The Rishis said: “O Sage Suta! tell us why Sati, the daughter of Daksha, consumed herself, and how again she took birth as the daughter of Himalaya. “Also tell us in detail, O Suta, what Daksha, the son of Brahma, told her; the mother of Lokas, at the time of her consuming her body.” — (10-11).

Suta said that when Daksha invited all the Devas to take part in the great sacrifice that he performed, Sati asked him the reason of his having excluded her husband, Shiva. Daksha answered that Shiva was not invited, because he was not considered worthy, since he always remained besmeared with the ashes of the funeral pyre and armed with his trident. He, being the destroyer of the universe also, it would have been utterly inauspicious to invite Shiva on the occasion of that big sacrifice.

Hearing those words of Daksha, Sati was enraged, and said she would give up the body begotten of him. Sati continuing, added that, in the course of the performance of his sacrifice, Daksha would be killed by Her Lord —

Mahadeva — and he would again have to take birth as the son of the ten Pitris. After that, Sati produced a blazing fire by Her yogic power In the sacrificial pool, and began to. consume Herself into it, seeing which all the Devas, Asuras, Kinnaras and Gandharvas present there, asked what was it due to? Daksha became very sad and saluting, said.

## \|\| 13.18-19 \|\|

*tvamasya jagato mātā jagatsaubhāgyadevatā \|*  
*duhitṛtvaṃ gatā devi mamānugrahakāmyayā \|\| 18 \|\|*

*na tvayā rahitaṃ kiṃcid brahmāṇḍe sacarācaram \|*  
*prasādaṃ kuru dharmajñe na māṃ tyaktumihārhasi \|\| 19 \|\|*

18-19. “Devil Thou art the mother of the universe and the giver of happiness to all. Only through sheer kindness thou tookest birth as my daughter. None of the moveables and immoveables can thrive in the universe without thee, he pleased, do not forsake me, O pious one!”

## \|\| 13.20-22 \|\|

*prāha devī yadārabdhaṃ tatkāryaṃ me na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*kiṃtvavaṣyaṃ tvayā martye hatayajñena śūlinā \|\| 20 \|\|*

*prasāde lokasṛṣṭyarthaṃ tapaḥ kāryaṃ mamāntike \|*  
*prajāpatistvaṃ bhavitā daśānāmaṅgajo 'pyalam \|\| 21 \|\|*

*madaṃśenāṅganā ṣaṣṭir bhaviṣyantyaṅgajāstava \|*  
*matsaṃnidhau tapaḥ kurvan prāpsyase yogamuttamam \|\| 22 \|\|*

20-22. Hearing the above words of Daksha, Sati said. ‘I shall accomplish what I wish. Hear! you should practice penances after your sacrifice is destroyed by Shiva, and then you will be born of the ten Prajapatis; you shall then have sixty daughters, and I shall give you yoga after becoming pleased with your austerities.”

## \|\| 13.23 \|\|

*evamukto 'bravīddakṣaḥ keṣu keṣu mayānaghe \|*  
*tīrtheṣu ca tvaṃ draṣṭavyā stotavyā kaiśca nāmabhiḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Daksha then asked the Devi to tell him in which sacred places he would find her abode and under what epithets he should worship her in course of his penances.

## \|\| 13.24-25 \|\|

*devyuvāca*  
*sarvadā sarvabhūteṣu draṣṭavyā sarvato bhuvi \|*  
*sarvalokeṣu yatkiṃcid rahitaṃ na mayā vinā \|\| 24 \|\|*

*tathāpi yeṣu sthāneṣu draṣṭavyā siddhimīpsubhiḥ \|*  
*smartavyā bhūtikāmair vā tāni vakṣyāmi tattvataḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

24-25. Sati replied that she was to be found at every time, in every region, in every being. There was nothing in the universe in which she was not to be found. She was omnipresent. Even then she would name the particular places where penances should be practiced to obtain his desires early.

26-52. She was known under the following different names, at the following different places, where by practising penances one would attain the fruits of his austerities early: —

Vishalakshi in Kashi: Lingadharini in Naimisharanya; Lalita in Prayaga; Kamakashi in the Gandhamadana hills; Kumuda at the Manasa lake: Vishvakaya in Ambara; Gomati in Gomanta; Kamacharini at the Mandar hills; Madotkata in the Chaitraratha forest; Jayanti in Hastinapura; Gauri in Kanyakubja; Rambha on the Mount Malaya; Kirtiwati in Ekambhaka; Vishva in Vishveshvara; Puruhuta in Pushkara; Margadayini in Kedar; Nanda in the Himalayas; Bhadrakarnika in Gokarna: Bhavani in Sthaneshvara; Bilvapatrika in Bilval: Madhavi in Shrisaila; Bhadra in Bhadreshvara; Jaya in Varahakshetra; Kamala in Kamalalaya; Rudrani in Rudrakoti; Kali in Kalanjar hills; Kapila in Mahalinga; Mukuteshvari in Markota; Mahadevi on the banks of the Salagrami river; Jalapriya in Shivalinga; Kumari in Mayapuri; Lalita in Santana; Utpalakshi in Sahasraksha; Mahotpala in Kamalaksha; Mangala in Gangatirtha; Vimala in Purushottama; Amoghakshi on the banks of the Vipasha river; Patala in Pundvardhana; Narayani in Suparshva; Bhadrasundari in Vikuta; Vipula in Vipula; Radha in Vrindavana; Devaki in Mathura; Parameshvari in Patala; Sita in Chitrakuta; Vinduvasini in Vindhyachala; Ekavira in Sahyadri; Chandrika in Harishchandra; Ramana in Rama tirtha; Mrigavati on the banks of the river Yamuna; Mahalakshmi in Karavira; Umeadevi in Vinayaka; Aroga in Vaidyanatha; Maheshvari in Mahakala; Abhaya in Ushnatirtha; Amrita in the caves of Vindhyachala; Mandavi in Mandvaya; Svaha in Maheshvara; Prachanda in Chagalanda; Chandika in Amarakantaka; Vararoha in Someshvara; Pushkaravati in Prabhasa; Devamata on the banks of Paravara of the Sarasvati river; Mahabhaga in Mahalaya; Pingaleshvari in Payoshni; Sinhika in Krita Shaucha; and Shakti in all bodies.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — Malayachala, one of the seven principal chains or mountains in India, It is most probably to be identified with the southern portion of the ghats running from the south of Mysore, and forming the eastern boundary of Travancore.

Hastinapura = Delhi. Kanyakubja = Kanauj. Pushkara = Ajmer. Someshvara = In Kathiawar. Devadaru-vana = In Almora near Yogeshvara, Uttara-kuru = Tibet. Madhavayana = In Muttra, Karavira = Karur. Mahakala = In Ujjain. Mandavya = In Mandvi.

Kapala-Mochan = In Gaya. Hemkuta = Between Meru and Himalaya, Ambara = Amber in Jaipur. Gokarna = In Almora, Bilvabala = In Almora. Rudrakoti = In Koteshvar (Almora).

Shalgrami-nadi = Gandaki river.

## \|\| 13.53-58 \|\|

*etaduddeśataḥ proktaṃ nāmāṣṭaśatamuttamam \|*  
*aṣṭottaraṃ ca tīrthānāṃ śatametadudāhṛtam \|\| 53 \|\|*

*yaḥ smarecchṛṇuyād vāpi sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate \|*  
*eṣu tīrtheṣu yaḥ kṛtvā snānaṃ paṣyati māṃ naraḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

*sarvapāpavinirmuktaḥ kalpaṃ śivapure vaset \|*  
*yastu matparamaṃ kālaṃ karotyeteṣu mānavaḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

*sa bhittvā brahmasadanaṃ padamabhyeti śāṃkaram \|*  
*nāmnāmaṣṭaśataṃ yastu śrāvayecchivasaṃnidhau \|\| 56 \|\|*

*tṛtīyāyāmathāṣṭamyāṃ bahuputro bhavennaraḥ \|*  
*godāne śrāddhadāne vā ahany ahani vā budhaḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

*devārcanavidhau vidvān paṭhan brahmādhigacchati \|*  
*evaṃ vadantī sā tatra dadāhātmānam ātmanā \|\| 58 \|\|*

53-58. The above are the hundred and eight chief names, under which I am usually known. I have also enumerated to you the names of the principal holy places which I have for my abode. One who hears or reads the names mentioned above or bathes in the tirthas and then worships me there, is liberated from all sins and goes to Shivaloka, where he remains for one Kalpa. One who resides in the sacred places mentioned above, attains Nirvana. One who recites the hundred and eight names before Shiva, on Tritiya and Ashtami, is blessed with many children.

One who repeats these names at the time of giving away a cow in charity, or on the occasion of performing a funeral ceremony in honour of the departed spirits, or at the time of worship, goes to Brahma.” After uttering these words, the goddess Sati consumed herself.

## \|\| 13.59-63 \|\|

*svāyambhuvo 'pi kālena dakṣaḥ prācetaso 'bhavat \|*  
*pārvatī sābhavaddevī śivadehārdhadhāriṇī \|\| 59 \|\|*

*menāgarbhasamutpannā bhuktamuktiphalapradā \|*  
*arundhatī japantyetat prāpa yogamanuttamam \|\| 60 \|\|*

*purūravāśca rājarṣi-loke vyajeyatām agāt \|*  
*yayātiḥ putralābhaṃ ca dhanalābhaṃ ca bhārgavaḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

*tathānye devadaityāśca brāhmaṇāḥ kṣatriyāstathā \|*  
*vaiśyāḥ śūdrāśca bahavaḥ siddhimīuryathepsitām \|\| 62 \|\|*

*yatraitallikhitaṃ tiṣṭhet pūjyate devasaṃnidhau \|*  
*na tatra śoko daurgatyaṃ kadācidapi jāyate \|\| 63 \|\|*

59-63. Again, after sometime, Daksha was born as the son of Pracheta, and Parvati after being born as the daughter of Himalaya, became the better half of Shiva. Arundhati, after worshipping Parvati, the daughter of Mena, obtained the highest yoga. By worshipping the same Parvati, Pururava became Rajarshi, Yayati begot progeny and Parashurama obtained wealth.

Similarly, many Devas, Daityas, Brahmanas, Kshatriyas, Vaishyas and Shudras obtained supernatural faculties. Wherever there is a book containing the names of Parvati which is worshipped along with the Gods, no calamity befalls there.

## Chapter 14

## \|\| 14.1-3 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*lokāḥ somapathā nāma yatra mārīcanandanāḥ \|*  
*vartante deva pitaro devā yānbhāvayantyalam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*agniṣvāttā iti khyātā yajvāno yatra saṃsthitāḥ \|*  
*acchodā nāma teṣāṃ tu mānasī kanyakā nadī \|\| 2 \|\|*

*acchodaṃ nāma ca saraḥ pitṛbhirnirmitaṃ purā \|*  
*acchodā tu tapaścakre divyaṃ varṣasahasrakam \|\| 3 \|\|*

1-3. Suta said: The group of Marichinandana Pitris, whom the Devas, constantly meditate upon, live in Somapatha regions. Those known as Agnisvatta pitris (because they performed great sacrifices to fire, i.e., Agni), reside there where these sacrifices dwell, and the river Achchhoda is their Manasa daughter. In days of yore, the stream Achchhoda was brought into existence by Pitris. Achchhoda practiced penance for one thousand years.

## \|\| 14.4-6 \|\|

*ājagmuḥ pitarastuṣṭāḥ kila dātuṃ ca tāṃ varam \|*  
*divyarūpadharāḥ sarve divyamālyānulepanāḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*sarve uvāno balinaḥ kusumāudhasaṃnibhāḥ \|*  
*tanmadhye 'māvasuṃ nāma pitaraṃ vīkṣya sāṅganā \|\| 5 \|\|*

*vavre varārthinī saṅgaṃ kusumāudhapīḍitā \|*  
*yogādbhraṣṭā tu sā tena vyabhicāreṇa bhāminī \|\| 6 \|\|*

4-6. After which, the young and handsome Pitris, wearing beautiful garlands and having sweet scents on their person, appeared before Achchhoda to grant her a boon. She was overcome with passion and expressed the desire of marrying Amavasu Pitri, on account of which sinful desire she lost the power she had obtained from practising asceticism.

## \|\| 14.7-8 \|\|

*dharāṃ tu nāspṛśatpūrvaṃ papātātha bhuvastale \|*  
*tithāv amāvasur yasyām icchāṃ cakre na tāṃ prati \|\| 7 \|\|*

*dhairyeṇa tasya sā lokair amāvāsyeti viśrutā \|*  
*pitriṇāṃ vallabhā tasmāt tasyāmakṣayakārakam \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8. She used to live in heaven, owing to her supernatural powers; but the moment she had such a base desire she fell to the earth. The date on which she expressed such a desire and Amavasu Pitri did not give way to passion, came to be known as Amavasya Tithi. Amavasya is, consequently, very dear to the Pitris, and offerings made to them on that Tithi are very heartily accepted by them.

**Комментарий:**

Note: — See H. H, Wilson’s translation of the Vishnu Purana, Vol. II, p. 301 for other etymologies of Amavasya.

## \|\| 14.9 \|\|

*acchodādhomukhī dīnā ladjitā tapasaḥ kṣayāt \|*  
*sā pitrin prārthayāmāsa pure cātmaprasiddhaye \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Achchhoda, after losing the powers acquired by penances, became ashamed and crest-fallen. She cast her head down and besought the Pitris for her salvation.

## \|\| 14.10 \|\|

*vilapyamānā pitṛbhir idamuktā tapasvinī \|*  
*bhaviṣyamarthamālokya devakāryaṃ ca te tadā \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. The Pitris, seeing her weeping, pondered over the destiny and the work of the future Devas, and addressed her very gently:

## \|\| 14.11-20 \|\|

*idam ūcur mahābhāgāḥ prasādaśubhayā girā \|*  
*divi divyaśarīreṇa yat kiṃcit kriyate budhaiḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*tenaiva tatkarmaphalaṃ bhujyate varavarṇinī \|*  
*sadyaḥ phalanti karmāṇi devatve pretya mānuṣe \|\| 12 \|\|*

*tasmāttvaṃ putri tapasaḥ prāpsyase pretya tatphalam \|*  
*aṣṭāviṃśe bhavitrī tvaṃ dvāpare matsyayonijā \|\| 13 \|\|*

*vyatikramātpitriṇāṃ tvaṃ kaṣṭaṃ kulamavāpsyasi \|*  
*tasmādrājño vasoḥ kanyā tvam avaṣyaṃ bhaviṣyasi \|\| 14 \|\|*

*kanyā bhūtvā ca lokānsvān punarāpsyasi durlabhān \|*  
*parāśarasya vīryeṇa putramekamavāpsyasi \|\| 15 \|\|*

*dvīpe tu badarīprāye bādarāyaṇamacyutam \|*  
*sa vedamekaṃ bahudhā vibhajiṣyati te sutaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*pauravasyātmajau dvau tu samudrāṃśasya śaṃtanoḥ \|*  
*vicitravīryastanayas tathā citrāṅgado nṛpaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*imāv utpādya tanayau kṣetrajāvasya dhīmataḥ \|*  
*prauṣṭhapadyaṣṭakārūpā pitṛloke bhaviṣyasi \|\| 18 \|\|*

*nāmnā satyavatī loke pitṛloke tathāṣṭakā \|*  
*āurārogyadā nityaṃ sarvakāmaphalapradā \|\| 19 \|\|*

*bhaviṣyasi pare kāle nadītvaṃ ca gamiṣyasi \|*  
*puṇyatoṣā saricchreṣṭhā loke hy acchodanāmikā \|\| 20 \|\|*

11-20. “In heaven, a celestial being has to reap the fruit of his deeds, in the same celestial form. Celestial beings instantly reap the harvest of their actions, only the beings residing on the earth reap the fruits of some of their actions in other forms after death. Daughter! on account of your ignoble wish, you will be born from the womb of a fish in the 28th Dwapara, and will become the daughter of Vasu. After that, you will return to your region. In an island covered with a number of jujube trees (Badarikashrama) you will beget, through Parashara, a son, named Badarayana, who will be a particle of Vishnu and will divide the Veda into several parts. You will beget two sons, Chitrangada and Vichitravirya, by becoming the queen of king Shantanu a portion of sea, and having begotten these two Kshetraja sons to that wise one, you will again return to the region of the Pitris, in the form of Praushtha ashtaka. You will be known as ‘Satyavati on earth, and as Ashtaka in Pitriloka. You will be the giver of longevity, of health and fruits of all desires. After some time, you will become the holy and celebrated Achchhoda river in the world ”’.

## \|\| 14.21 \|\|

*ityuktvā sa gaṇasteṣāṃ tatraivāntaradhīyata \|*  
*sāpyavāpa ca tatsarvaṃ phalaṃ yaduditaṃ purā \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. After addressing her thus, the Pitris vanished, and Achchhoda also began to reap the harvest of her actions, as told by the Pitris.

## Chapter 15

## \|\| 15.1-10 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*vibhrājā nāma cānye tu divi santi suvarcasaḥ \|*  
*lokā barhiṣado yatra pitaraḥ santi suvratāḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*yatra barhiṇauktāni vimānāni sahasraśaḥ \|*  
*saṃkalpyā barhiṣo yatra tiṣṭhanti phaladāyinaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*yatrābhyudayaśālāsu modante śrāddhadāyinaḥ \|*  
*yāṃś ca devāsuragaṇā gandharvāpsarasāṃ gaṇāḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*yakṣarakṣogaṇāścaiva yajanti divi devatāḥ \|*  
*pulastyaputrāḥ śataśas tapoyogasamanvitāḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*mahātmāno mahābhāgā bhaktānāmabhayapradāḥ \|*  
*eteṣāṃ pīvarī kanyā mānasī divi viśrutā \|\| 5 \|\|*

*yoginī yogamātā ca tapaścakre sudāruṇam \|*  
*prasanno bhagavāṃstasyā varaṃ vavre tu sā hareḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*yogavantaṃ surūpaṃ ca bhartāraṃ vijitendriyam \|*  
*dehi deva prasannastvaṃ patiṃ me vadatāṃ varam \|\| 7 \|\|*

*uvāca devo bhavitā vyāsaputro yadā śukaḥ \|*  
*bhavitā tasya bhāryā tvaṃ yogācāryasya suvrate \|\| 8 \|\|*

*bhaviṣyati ca te kanyā kṛtvī nāma ca yoginī \|*  
*pāñcālādhipaterdeyā mānuṣasya tvayā tadā \|\| 9 \|\|*

*jananī brahmadattasya yogasiddhā ca gauḥ smṛtā \|*  
*kṛṣṇo gauraḥ prabhuḥ śambhur bhaviṣyanti ca te sutāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

1-10. Suta said: “In heaven, there are other illustrious regions called Vibharajas where dwell the pious Barhishada pitris so named because their Vimanas are carried by peacocks (barhi) and where people making offerings to the manes of their deceased ancestors go and find happiness. These ‘Pitris are venerated by the Devas, Asuras, Apsaras, Gandharvas, Rakshasas and Yakshas. The Barhishada Pitris, possessed of great Yogic powers, are the song of the sage Pulastya. They are the givers of safety and freedom from fear to their devotees, These very Barhishada Pitris had a manasa daughter, named Pivari. She was well versed in, and mother of, Yoga and practiced severe penances for a long time, when Lord Vishnu pleased with her devotion appeared before her and directed her to ask for a boon; she prayed for a husband who would be beautiful, possessed of Yogic powers and able to curb his passions. The Lord , in granting her that boon, said: “Thou shalt be the wife of Shuka the teacher of Yoga, the son of Vyasa. And thou shalt be blessed with a daughter, named Kritvi, who will be well versed in Yoga and will be married to the manly Rajah of Panchala. Kritvi, after practising Yoga, will also be known as Go, and she will beget a son, named Brahmadatta.

## \|\| 15.11 \|\|

*mahātmāno mahābhāgā gamiṣyanti paraṃ padam \|*  
*tānutpādya punar yogāt savarā mokṣameṣyasi \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. “Thou shalt also become the mother of Krishna Gaura Prabhu, and Shambhu, who will be great Mahatmas and will ultimately depart to felicity. Thou shalt also attain Moksha, after giving birth to such illustrious sons.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — Mahatma-magnanimous.

## \|\| 15.12-15 \|\|

*sumūrtimantaḥ pitaro vasiṣṭhasya sutāḥ smṛtāḥ \|*  
*nāmnā tu mānasāḥ sarve sarve te dharmamūrtayaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*jyotirbhāsiṣu lokeṣu ye vasanti divaḥ param \|*  
*virājamānāḥ krīḍanti yatra te śrāddhadāyinaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*sarvakāmasamṛddheṣu vimāneṣvapi pādajāḥ \|*  
*kiṃ punaḥ śrāddhadā viprā bhaktimantaḥ kriyānvitāḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*gaur nāma kanyā yeṣāṃ tu mānasī divi rājate \|*  
*śukrasya dayitā patnī sādhyānāṃ kīrtivardhinī \|\| 15 \|\|*

12-15. Suta said: ‘The group of Manasa Pitris, who are most handsome and virtuous and known as Sumurtimantas (Vasishtha's sons,) reside in the region called Jyotirobhasas where stars and planets light up their surroundings by their rays. This region is a high one where people making offerings to the manes of their deceased ancestors go and have various enjoyments. Even the Shudras performing shraddha go to that region in a vimana; what to say of a Brahmana who performs shraddha devoutly. Go was the manasa daughter of those Pitris, and was married to Shukra and who enhanced the reputation of Sadhyas

## \|\| 15.16-19 \|\|

*marīcigarbhā nāmnā tu lokā mārtaṇḍamaṇḍale \|*  
*pitaro yatra tiṣṭhanti haviṣmanto 'ṅgiraḥsutāḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*tīrthaśrāddhapradā yānti ye ca kṣatriyasattamāḥ \|*  
*rājñāṃ tu pitaraste vai svargamokṣaphalapradāḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*eteṣāṃ mānasī kanyā yaśodā lokaviśrutā \|*  
*patnī hy aṃśumataḥ śreṣṭhā snuṣā pañcajanasya ca \|\| 18 \|\|*

*jananyatha dilīpasya bhagīrathapitāmahī \|*  
*lokāḥ kāmadughā nāma kāmabhogaphalapradāḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

16-19. “In the Solar world, there are regions called Marichigarbhas, where Havishmana Pitris, the sons of Amgira, reside. Kshatriyas performing Shraddha in a holy place go to the same region, and that is why Havishmana Pitris are worshipped by Kshatriyas. Yashoda was the manasa daughter of Havishmana Pitris. She was married to King Amshumana and was the daughter-in-law of Panchajana, mother of Dilipa, and grandmother of Bhagiratha

## \|\| 15.20-24 \|\|

*susvadhā nāma pitaro yatra tiṣṭhanti suvratāḥ \|*  
*ājyapā nāma lokeṣu kardamasya prajāpateḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*pulahāṅgajadāyādā vaiśyāstānbhāvayanti ca \|*  
*yatra śrāddhakṛtaḥ sarve paṣyanti ugapadgatāḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*mātṛbhrātṛpitṛsvasṛ-sakhisambandhibāndhavān \|*  
*api janmāutairdṛṣṭān anubhūtānsahasraśaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*eteṣāṃ mānasī kanyā virajā nāma viśrutā \|*  
*yā patnī nahuṣasyāsīd yayāterjananī tathā \|\| 23 \|\|*

*ekāṣṭakābhavat paścād brahmaloke gatā satī \|*  
*traya ete gaṇāḥ proktāś caturthaṃ tu vadāmyataḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

20-24. “There are other regions known as Kamadughas, where reside the pious Pitris, called Susvada as well as Ajyapa in the region of Prajapata Kardarma. They are the sons of Pulaha and are worshipped by the Vaishyas. The worshippers of these Pitris, by performing shraddha, go to the same region where they see the manes of their deceased ancestors, mother, father, sister, friends, relations, etc.” Viraja was the manasa daughter of Ajyapa Pitris and was the queen of King Nahusha and. the mother of Yayati. She was afterwards known as Ekashtaka in Brahmaloka.

## \|\| 15.25 \|\|

*lokāstu mānasā nāma brahmāṇḍopari saṃsthitāḥ \|*  
*yeṣāṃ tu mānasī kanyā narmadā nāma viśrutā \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Something has been said about the three groups of pitris who are worshipped by men and have forms, now follows the description of the fourth set of Pitris.

## \|\| 15.26-28 \|\|

*somapā nāma pitaro yatra tiṣṭhanti śāśvatāḥ \|*  
*dharmamūrtidharāḥ sarve parato brahmaṇaḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*utpannāḥ svadhayā te tu brahmatvaṃ prāpya yoginaḥ \|*  
*kṛtvā sṛṣṭyādikaṃ sarvaṃ mānase sāmprataṃ sthitāḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

*narmadā nāma teṣāṃ tu kanyā toyavahā sarit \|*  
*bhūtāni yā pāvayati dakṣiṇāpathagāminī \|\| 28 \|\|*

26-28. There is a manasa region in the upper Brahmanda which is the abode of Somapa Pitris. They are eternal, the very incarnation of Dharma, and are as venerable as Brahma’. They are born of Swadha, and having attained Brahmanhood, by their power of yoga, they carried on the work of past creations and now rest in Manasa regions. Narmada, which flows in the southern part, is the manasa daughter of the Somapa Pitris that purifies the people by her sacred waters.

## \|\| 15.29-30 \|\|

*tebhyaḥ sarve tu manavaḥ prajāḥ sargeṣu nirmitāḥ \|*  
*jñātvā śrāddhāni kurvanti dharmābhāve 'pi sarvadā \|\| 29 \|\|*

*tebhya eva punaḥ prāptuṃ prasādādyogasaṃtatim \|*  
*pitriṇāmādisarge tu śrāddhameva vinirmitam \|\| 30 \|\|*

29-30. The Manus have sprung from these Pitris, and their progeny perform Shraddha even when there is an absence of Dharma in the world.

It was they who at the beginning of the Creation started the system of shraddha, after acquiring yoga and begetting children.

## \|\| 15.31 \|\|

*sarveṣāṃ rājataṃ pātram athavā rajatānvitam \|*  
*dattaṃ svadhā purodhāya pitrin prīṇāti sarvadā \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. The Pitris mentioned above, like vessels of silver or of any metal having some admixture of silver. By performing shraddha in such vessels and by giving them away to a deserving priest one makes them feel very happy.

## \|\| 15.32-33 \|\|

*agnīṣomayamānāṃ tu kāryamāpyāyanaṃ budhaḥ \|*  
*agnyabhāve 'pi viprasya prāṇāv api jale 'thavā \|\| 32 \|\|*

*ajākarṇe 'śvakarṇe vā goṣṭhe vā salilāntike \|*  
*pitriṇām ambaraṃ sthānaṃ dakṣiṇā dikpraśasyate \|\| 33 \|\|*

32-33. Offerings should be made to the Pitris in the name of Agnishoma, and Yama. Where fire is not available, then they should be made in water or in the hand of a Brahmana. lt is excellent to make offerings in the ear of a goat or a horse; and, similarly, it is very nice to perform shraddha.

near the place where cows are kept or near a good stream of water. Pitris live in heaven, and offerings should also be made to them by facing towards the south.

## \|\| 15.34-35 \|\|

*prācīnāvītamudakaṃ tilāḥ savyāṅgameva ca \|*  
*darbhā māṃsaṃ ca pāṭhīnaṃ gokṣīraṃ madhurā rasāḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

*khaḍgalohāmiṣamadhu-kuśaśyāmākaśālayaḥ \|*  
*yavanīvāramudgekṣu-śuklapuṣpaghṛtāni ca \|\| 35 \|\|*

34-35. At the time of making offerings, one should put his sacred thread on his right shoulder and offer, water, sesamum, kusha grass, flesh, Pathina, cow’s milk, sweet things, the flesh of rhinoceros, honey, Shyamaka, rice, barley, wild rice, kidney-bean, sugarcane, white flowers, clarified butter.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — Pathina is a kind of fish. Madhu-sweets, honey, nectar of flowers, wine, water, somajuice, milk, vernal season. Shyamaka is a kind of corn.

## \|\| 15.36-39 \|\|

*vallabhāni praśastāni pitriṇāmiha sarvadā \|*  
*dveṣyāṇi sampravakṣyāmi śrāddhe varjyāni yāni tu \|\| 36 \|\|*

*masūraśaṇaniṣpāva-rājamāṣakusumbhikāḥ \|*  
*padmabilvārkadhattūra-pāribhadrāṭarūṣakāḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

*na deyāḥ pitṛkāryeṣu payaścājāvikaṃ tathā \|*  
*kodravodāracaṇakāḥ kapitthaṃ madhukātasī \|\| 38 \|\|*

*etānyapi na deyāni pitṛbhyaḥ priyamicchatā \|*  
*pitrin prīṇāti yo bhaktyā te punaḥ prīṇayanti tam \|\| 39 \|\|*

36-39. The things mentioned already are appreciable to the Pitris and should be offered to them; the things not liked by them and which should be discarded at the time of shraddha are enumerated now, viz. —

Masur, hemp, ripe black mustard, masha, safflower, lotus, wood-apple, sunflower, the white thorn-apple, the fruit of Nima tree, the fruit of Adhatoda vasika, the milk of she-goat, kodrava, split chick pea, liquor ice, linseed, should never be offered in shraddha to the Pitris by one who wishes to win their favour. One who pleases the Pitris by devotion, is blessed by them in return.

## \|\| 15.40-43 \|\|

*yacchanti pitaraḥ puṣṭiṃ svargārogyaṃ prajāphalam \|*  
*devakāryādapi punaḥ pitṛkāryaṃ viśiṣyate \|\| 40 \|\|*

*devatānāṃ ca pitaraḥ pūrvamāpyāyanaṃ smṛtam \|*  
*śīghraprasādāstvakrodhā niḥśastrāḥ sthirasauhṛdāḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

*śāntātmānaḥ śaucaparāḥ satataṃ priyavādinaḥ \|*  
*bhaktānuraktāḥ sukhadāḥ pitaraḥ pūrvadevatāḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

*haviṣmatāmādhipatye śrāddhadevaḥ smṛto raviḥ \|*  
*etadvaḥ sarvamākhyātaṃ pitṛvaṃśānukīrtanam \|*  
*puṇyaṃ pavitram āuṣyaṃ kīrtanīyaṃ sadā nṛbhiḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

40-43. Pitris, when they are pleased, give robust health, heaven, and children to their devotees. The worship of Pitris is more important than that of the Goda. The Pitris should be satisfied first. They are soon pleased and are devoid of anger. They are harmless and of steady affection.

They are of peaceful soul, lovers of purity, always soft speaking, and givers of happiness and prosperity to their devotees. The Sun is their Lord. I have narrated to you the family of Pitris by listening to which one gains life and virtue; therefore everyone should read and listen to it.

## Chapter 16

## \|\| 16.1-3 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*śrutvaitat sarvam akhilaṃ manuḥ papraccha keśavam \|*  
*śrāddhakālaṃ ca vividhaṃ śrāddhabhedaṃ tathaiva ca \|\| 1 \|\|*

*śrāddheṣu bhojanīyā ye ye ca varjyā dvijātayaḥ \|*  
*kasminvāsarabhāge vā pitṛbhyaḥ śrāddhamācaret \|\| 2 \|\|*

*kasmindattaṃ kathaṃ yāti śrāddhaṃ tu madhusūdana \|*  
*vidhinā kena kartavyaṃ kathaṃ prīṇāti tatpitrin \|\| 3 \|\|*

1-3. ‘Suta said, after hearing that, King Manu again enquired from the Lord Keshava, about the periods for the performance of Shraddhas, the different kinds of shraddhas, the twice-horn worthy of being fed on that occasion and those who ought to be discarded from the feast, the time of the day when shraddha should be performed, the vessels that should be used in performing the ceremony, the ways of performing the rite and the mode of giving satisfaction to the Pitris.

## \|\| 16.4 \|\|

*matsya uvāca*  
*kuryādaharahaḥ śrāddham annādyenodakena vā \|*  
*payomūlaphalair vāpi pitṛbhyaḥ prītimāvahan \|\| 4 \|\|*

4 The Lord replied that shraddha should be performed daily and the Pitris should he satisfied by offering any of the following things: — Grain, water, milk, roots, fruits.

## \|\| 16.5-13 \|\|

*nityaṃ naimittikaṃ kāmyaṃ trividhaṃ śrāddhamucyate \|*  
*nityaṃ tāvatpravakṣyāmi arghyāvāhanavarjitam \|\| 5 \|\|*

*adaivaṃ tadvijānīyāt pārvaṇaṃ parvasu smṛtam \|*  
*pārvaṇaṃ trividhaṃ proktaṃ śṛṇu tāvanmahīpate \|\| 6 \|\|*

*pārvaṇe ye niyojyāstu tāñśṛṇuṣva narādhipa \|*  
*pañcāgniḥ snātakaścaiva trisuparṇaḥ ṣaḍaṅgavit \|\| 7 \|\|*

*śrotriyaḥ śrotriyasuto vidhivākyaviśāradaḥ \|*  
*sarvajño vedavinmantrī jñātavaṃśaḥ kulānvitaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*purāṇavettā dharmajñaḥ svādhyāyajapatatparaḥ \|*  
*śivabhaktaḥ pitṛparaḥ sūryabhakto 'tha vaiṣṇavaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*brahmaṇyo yogavicchānto vijitātmā ca śīlavān \|*  
*bhojayeccāpi dauhitraṃ yatnataḥ svasuhṛdgurūn \|\| 10 \|\|*

*viṭpītaṃ mātulaṃ bandhum ṛtvigācāryasomapān \|*  
*yaśca vyākurute vākyaṃ yaśca mīmāṃsate 'dhvaram \|\| 11 \|\|*

*sāmasvaravidhijñaśca paṅktipāvanapāvanaḥ \|*  
*sāmago brahmacārī ca vedaukto 'tha brahmavit \|\| 12 \|\|*

*yatraite bhuñjate śrāddhe tadeva paramārthavat \|*  
*ete bhojyāḥ prayatnena varjanīyānnibodha me \|\| 13 \|\|*

5-13. The shraddhas are of three kinds, viz.: —Nitya (Daily), Naimittika (Occasional), Kamya (Optional). In performing Nitya shraddha, no oblation (arghya), invocation or Vishvadeva Worship is necessary. Naimittika shraddha is that which is performed on the fourth and the eighth day of each half-month and on the days of the full and the new moon (parvana days). Parvanas are of three different kinds, hear it O Lord of the world. First, it should be noted what class of people ought to be invited to the feast of Naimittika (Parvana) shraddha. One who is acquainted with the doctrine of the five mystic fires (Panchagni) a Snataka Brahmachari, one who is well versed in the Vedas with their six angas, the Shrotriya Brahmana, the son of such a Shrotriya Brahmana, one highly proficient in the rules of Vidhi (or Laws, one who is thoroughly acquainted with.

the sacred hymns, the minister, one who belongs to a well-known family, one who has a sound knowledge of the Puranas, one who knows the dharma, a regular reader of the Vedas, and performer of japa, a devotee of ‘Shiva, Pitri, Sun, Vishnu, and Brahma, a Yogi, one who is peaceful, one who can control his passions, one who is virtuous, especially a daughter’s son, a friend, a preceptor, a typical sanyasi, or the head of the Vaishyas, a maternal uncle, a member of the community (kinsman), a Ritvija priest, a teacher, a Soma-sacrificer, a grammarian, a knower of the Mimansa doctrine about Sacrifices, one who performs Vedic sacrifices, one who knows ‘the Samaveda and how to chant it, one who is so learned, respectable or.

eminent that his very presence may he considered to elevate and purify the people who sit to feast with him in the same row, the chanter of the Samaveda, a Brahmachari, a professor of Vedas, one who knows Brahma, are the sort of people worthy of being invited to the shraddha feast. Where such people are feasted, the shraddha is real and earnest.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — Dvija means twice-born, Everyone is horn as a Shudra and becomes twice-born on being invested with the sacred thread.

## \|\| 16.14-17 \|\|

*patito 'bhiśastaḥ klībaḥ piśunavyaṅgarogiṇaḥ \|*  
*kunakhī śyāvadantaśca kuṇḍagolāśvapālakāḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*parivittirniuktātmā pramattonmattadāruṇāḥ \|*  
*baiḍālī bakavṛttiśca dambhī devalakādayaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*kṛtaghnānnāstikāṃs tadvan mlecchadeśanivāsinaḥ \|*  
*triśaṅkur barbaradrāva-vītadraviḍakoṅkaṇān \|\| 16 \|\|*

*varjayelliṅginaḥ sarvāñ śrāddhakāle viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*pūrvedyuraparedyurvā vinītātmā nimantrayet \|\| 17 \|\|*

14-17. Now it should be noted what class of people are to be discarded from such a feast.

The fallen, the cursed, eunuch, backbiters, those deformed by disease, those having deformed nails, those having yellow teeth, bastards, bastards of widows, horse-tamers, offspring of a younger brother married before an elder brother, those who offer themselves for service, those addicted to drunkenness, mad men, the hard-hearted, cheats, swindlers, the conceited, temple priests, the ungrateful, the atheist, inhabitants of a Mlechha country (Non-aryans), Trishankus, of Barbara, and of Dravavita, Dravida, of Konkana, and the Lingis (having prominent sectarian marks), should, under no circumstances, be invited to shraddha feast.

## \|\| 16.18-20 \|\|

*nimantritānhi pitara upatiṣṭhanti tāndvijān \|*  
*vāubhūtā nu gacchanti tathāsīnānupāsate \|\| 18 \|\|*

*dakṣiṇaṃ jānumālabhya tvaṃ mayā tu nimantritaḥ \|*  
*evaṃ nimantrya niyamaṃ śrāvayetpitṛbāndhavān \|\| 19 \|\|*

*akrodhanaiḥ śaucaparaiḥ satataṃ brahmacāribhiḥ \|*  
*bhavitavyaṃ bhavadbhiśca mayā ca śrāddhakāriṇā \|\| 20 \|\|*

18-20. The guests to the Shraddha feast should he courteously invited the same day or a day previous to the feast. The Pitris accompany the invited twice-born, in the form of air, and sit along with them at the time of the feast, The host should go and invite his twice-born guest by touching his right knee and address him thus “thou hast been invited by me, accept my invitation.” After thus addressing, he should remind the guest as well as his paternal kinsmen in these words: — “You should be without anger, observe purity and rules of continence the whole of this day, and I the performer of Shraddha would also observe the same along with you”.

## \|\| 16.21 \|\|

*pitṛyajñaṃ vinirvartya tarpaṇākhyaṃ tu yo 'gnimān \|*  
*piṇḍānvāhāryakaṃ kuryāc chrāddhamindukṣaye sadā \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. One who maintains the sacrificial fire, should perform the Shraddha after offering oblations of water called Tarpana to the Pitris, as well as after offering of pindas to them, on every Amavasya.

## \|\| 16.22-23 \|\|

*gomayenopalipte tu dakṣiṇapravaṇe sthale \|*  
*śrāddhaṃ samācaredbhaktyā goṣṭhe vā jalasaṃnidhau \|\| 22 \|\|*

*agnimānnirvapetpitryaṃ caruṃ ca samamuṣṭibhiḥ \|*  
*pitṛbhyo nirvapāmīti sarvaṃ dakṣiṇato nyaset \|\| 23 \|\|*

22-23. Shraddha should be performed near a cow-pen or by a pool of water, after plastering the floor, which should be sloping towards the south, with cowdung. One who consecrates and maintains the sacred fire, should cook rice (charu), and after offering with equal handfuls and saying (“I am offering to the Pitris),” should place everything toward the south.

## \|\| 16.24 \|\|

*abhighāryaṃ tataḥ kuryān nirvāpatrayamagrataḥ \|*  
*te 'pi tasyāyatāḥ kāryāś caturaṅgulavistṛtāḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Then he should sprinkle with ghee in front of the three nirvapa plates. They should be of the same size, that is four fingers broad, and place on them balls of rice.

## \|\| 16.25-29 \|\|

*darvītrayaṃ tu kurvīta khādiraṃ rajatānvitam \|*  
*ratnimātraṃ pariślakṣṇaṃ hastākārāgramuttamam \|\| 25 \|\|*

*udapātraṃ ca kāṃsyaṃ ca mekṣaṇaṃ ca samitkuśān \|*  
*tilāḥ pātrāṇi sadvāso gandhadhūpānulepanam \|\| 26 \|\|*

*āharedapasavyaṃ tu sarvaṃ dakṣiṇataḥ śanaiḥ \|*  
*evamāsādya tatsarvaṃ bhavanasyāgrato bhuvi \|\| 27 \|\|*

*gomayenopaliptāyāṃ gomūtreṇa tu maṇḍalam \|*  
*akṣatābhiḥ sapuṣpābhis tadabhyarcyāpasavyavat \|\| 28 \|\|*

*viprāṇāṃ kṣālayet pādāv abhinandya punaḥ punaḥ \|*  
*āsaneṣūpakḷpteṣu darbhavatsu vidhānavat \|\| 29 \|\|*

25-29. Three silver-mounted, smooth ladles, of acacia catechu, measuring one hand in length with closed fist, and having the form of the palm of hand at the end, should be made. After putting the sacred thread over the right shoulder, the person performing Shraddha should put a water goblet, and a vessel of bell-metal, and mekshana (name of a sacrificial vessel), sacrificial wood, Kusha, sesamum, leaf plates, sandal, new cloth and scent, incense, and sandal paste towards the south. After thus putting together the articles for worship, the worshipper should draw a circle by the urine of cow on the floor plastered with cowdung, and there he should worship the circle with unhusked rice and flowers. The worshipper should then wash the feet of his Brahmana guests with great respect and courtesy, and after offering them water for rinsing their mouth, should seat them on the kusha mattings.

## \|\| 16.30 \|\|

*upaspṛṣṭodakānviprān upaveśyānumantrayet \|*  
*dvau daive pitṛkṛtye trīn ekaikamubhayatra ca \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Two Brahmanas should be fed at the time of offering oblations to Gods and three at the time of Pitri worship, or one Brahmana may be fed on each occasion.

## \|\| 16.31 \|\|

*bhojayedīśvaro 'pīha na kuryādvistaraṃ budhaḥ \|*  
*daivapūrvaṃ niyojyātha viprānarghyādinā budhaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Even the rich. man should not feast more than this number on this occasion. Water should first be offered to the Brahmana invited to take part in the rite of offering oblations to the Devas, and his feet should be washed first.

## \|\| 16.32-34 \|\|

*agnau kuryādanujñāto viprair vipro yathāvidhi \|*  
*svagṛhyoktavidhānena kāṃsye kṛtvā caruṃ tataḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

*agnīṣomayamābhyāṃ tu kuryādāpyāyanaṃ budhaḥ \|*  
*dakṣiṇāgnau pratīte vā ya ekāgnirdvijottamaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

*yajñopavītī nirvartya tataḥ paryukṣaṇādikam \|*  
*prācīnāvītinā kāryam ataḥ sarvaṃ vijānatā \|\| 34 \|\|*

32-34. By the permission of the Brahmanas, the worshipper, according to the rules of his Grihya Sutras, should take the boiled rice (Charu), in a vessel of bell-metal and offer it to fire, the Moon, and Yama, in the Dakshinagni, or Ekagni if he does not keep all the fires. Ho should perform) Paryukshana with the sacred thread on the left Shoulder, and one who knows all the rites should perform it with the sacred thread thrown on the right shoulder,

**Комментарий:**

Note. — Paryukshana = sprinkling round water silently and without uttering any ritual formulae.

## \|\| 16.35-38 \|\|

*ṣaṭ ca tasmāddhaviḥśeṣāt piṇḍānkṛtvā tatodakam \|*  
*dadyādudakapātrais tu satilaṃ savyapāṇinā \|\| 35 \|\|*

*jānv ācya savyaṃ yatnena darbhaukto vimatsaraḥ \|*  
*vidhāya lekhā yatnena nirvāpeṣvavanejanam \|\| 36 \|\|*

*dakṣiṇābhimukhaḥ kuryāt kare darvīṃ nidhāya vai \|*  
*nidhāya piṇḍam ekaikaṃ sarvadarbheṣvanukramāt \|\| 37 \|\|*

*ninayedatha darbheṣu nāmagotrānukīrtanaiḥ \|*  
*teṣu darbheṣu taṃ hastaṃ vimṛjyāllepabhāginām \|\| 38 \|\|*

35-38. After that, six bails should be made of the remaining boiled rice and water mixed with sesamum, and offered with the left hand. Then the worshipper should sit on his left knee, with concentrated attention, and draw a line on the sacrificial altar with kusha blade, and turning his fade towards the south he should sprinkle water on the darbha grass with a ladle.

After that, he should offer the balls of rice by putting a kusha on the line drawn on the altar and by uttering the name and clan of the ancestor.

Then he should wipe his hands with the kusha and thus satisfy the Lepabhagas. (A paternal ancestor in the 4th, 5th and 6th degree).

## \|\| 16.39 \|\|

*tathaiva ca tataḥ kuryāt punaḥ pratyavanejanam \|*  
*ṣaḍapyṛtūnnamaskṛtya gandhadhūpārhaṇādibhiḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Then water should again be sprinkled on the darbha grass and the six Pitris should be saluted and worshipped with incense, &c.

## \|\| 16.40 \|\|

*evamāvāhya tatsarvaṃ vedamantrairyathoditaiḥ \|*  
*ekāgnereka eva syān nirvāpo darvikā tathā \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. After thus invoking them by Vedic hymns, one, who is Ekagni, should offer only one ball of rice with a ladle

**Комментарий:**

Note. — Ekagni = one who performs agnihotra.

## \|\| 16.41 \|\|

*tataḥ kṛtvāntare dadyāt patnībhyo 'nnaṃ kuśeṣu saḥ \|*  
*tadvatpiṇḍādike kuryād āvāhanavisarjanam \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. After satisfying the male ancestors, offerings should be made to the female ancestors by means of the kusha grass, who should also be invoked and dismissed in the same way.

## \|\| 16.42 \|\|

*tato gṛhītvā piṇḍebhyo mātrāḥ sarvāḥ krameṇa tu \|*  
*tāneva viprānprathamaṃ prāśayedyatnato naraḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Then he should take a little out of the balls of rice and offer it to the invited guests, according to precedence, making the first offer to the Brahmanas.

## \|\| 16.43 \|\|

*yasmādannāddhṛtā mātrā bhakṣayanti dvijātayaḥ \|*  
*anvāhāryakam ityuktaṃ tasmāttaccandrasaṃkṣaye \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Because the twice-born eat the particles from the rice-balls on the occasion of the Amavasya feast, it is called Anvaharya

## \|\| 16.44 \|\|

*pūrvaṃ dattvā tu taddhaste sapavitraṃ tilodakam \|*  
*tatpiṇḍāgraṃ prayaccheta svadhaiṣāmastviti bruvan \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. First of all, the twice-born invited to the feast, should be given rings of kusha grass to wear on their ring fingers, and then a portion of the ball of rice should be presented to them, after putting a little water and sesamum in their hand by uttering Swadhaishamastu.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — Swadhaishamastu = Here is the food to the manes personified.

## \|\| 16.45 \|\|

*varṇayanbhojayedannaṃ miṣṭaṃ pūtaṃ ca sarvadā \|*  
*varjayetkrodhaparatāṃ smarannārāyaṇaṃ harim \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. At the time of feasting the invited guests, the host should enquire whether they relish the food. He should on no account be in angry mood.

He should concentrate his mind on Narayana Hari.

## \|\| 16.46 \|\|

*tṛptāñjñātvā tataḥ kuryād vikiransārvavarṇikam \|*  
*sodakaṃ cānnamuddhṛtya salilaṃ prakṣipedbhuvi \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. After the invited (Brahmana} guests are satisfied, the host should, on unsanctified earth, place food with water and vice for the acceptance of all classes. This is called Vikira (scattering).

## \|\| 16.47 \|\|

*ācānteṣu punardadyāj jalapuṣpākṣatodakam \|*  
*svastivācanakaṃ sarvaṃ piṇḍopari samāharet \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. After the invited guests have washed their hands and mouths, the host should place water, flowers and unhuskeed rice in their hands, and ask them to sprinkle it on the balls of rice offered to the Pitris, pronouncing Swastu (Be comfortable).

## \|\| 16.48 \|\|

*devādyantaṃ prakurvīta śrāddhanāśo 'nyathā bhavet \|*  
*visṛjya brāhmaṇāṃstadvat teṣāṃ kṛtvā pradakṣiṇam \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. The Gods should also be satisfied on the occasion of the performance of Shraddha; for otherwise Shraddha is not complete. The Brahmana guests invited, should be circumambulated before being respectfully dismissed.

## \|\| 16.49-51 \|\|

*dakṣiṇāṃ diśamākāṅkṣan pitrin yāceta mānavaḥ \|*  
*dātāro no 'bhivardhantāṃ vedāḥ saṃtatireva ca \|\| 49 \|\|*

*śraddhā ca no mā vyagamad bahu deyaṃ ca no 'stviti \|*  
*annaṃ ca no bahu bhaved atithīṃśca labhemahi \|\| 50 \|\|*

*yācitāraśca naḥ santu mā ca yāciṣma kaṃcana \|*  
*etadastviti tatproktam anvāhāryaṃ tu pārvaṇam \|\| 51 \|\|*

49-51. Facing south, the following boon should be sought from the Pitris:

“You may continue to be our donors. The Vedas may exist, and our progeny may prosper. Let our devotion not diminish, we may have ample wealth to give to the needy, we may have plenty of grain, we may be visited by many guests. People may ask for help from us, we may not have to seek anything from others.” ‘This is the Anvaharya Shraddha, which is also called Parvana.

## \|\| 16.52-53 \|\|

*yathendusaṃkṣaye tadvad anyatrāpi nigadyate \|*  
*piṇḍāṃstu gojaviprebhyo dadyādagnau jale 'pi vā \|\| 52 \|\|*

*viprāgrato vā vikired vayobhir abhivāśayet \|*  
*patnī tu madhyamaṃ piṇḍaṃ prāśayed vinayānvitā \|\| 53 \|\|*

52-53. The Kamya or the third kind of Shraddha should be performed also in the same manner as the Parvana Shraddha described above. It should be performed on Amavasya. The balls of rice should afterwards he given to cows, goats, Brahmanas, or should be thrown into fire or water, or they should be made over to birds.

## \|\| 16.54 \|\|

*ādhatta pitaro garbham atra saṃtānavardhanam \|*  
*tāvaduccheṣaṇaṃ tiṣṭhed yāvadviprā visarjitāḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. The ball of rice in the middle should be given to the wife of the host (this is the peculiarity in this Shraddha). It begets progeny, She should eat the ball of rice after pronouncing the following words:

“Adhatta pitaro yarbhamatra santena vardhanam” (Pitris grant to me progeny that would continue the line of the house). The lost should remain standing till the Brahmanas depart. He should then perform the remaining rites.

## \|\| 16.55 \|\|

*vaiśvadevaṃ tataḥ kuryān nivṛtte pitṛkarmaṇi \|*  
*iṣṭaiḥ saha tataḥ śānto bhuñjīta pitṛsevitam \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. After the Shraddha rites are over, the lost should make an offering to Vaishvadevas by presenting oblations to fi re, and then he should enjoy a hearty repast in company of his friends, concentrating his mind on the Pitris.

## \|\| 16.56 \|\|

*punar bhojanamadhvānaṃ yānamāyāsamaithunam \|*  
*śrāddhakṛcchrāddhabhukcaiva sarvametadvivarjayet \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. That day one who performs Shraddha, as well as those who partake in the Shraddha feast, should not take their food twice. They should not go out of the village when the Shraddha is performed. They should neither use any conveyance nor approach their wires.

## \|\| 16.57 \|\|

*svādhyāyakalahaṃ caiva divāsvapnaṃ ca sarvadā \|*  
*anena vidhinā śrāddhaṃ nirudvāsyeha nirvapet \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. The Veda should not be read on that day; the Worshipper should not quarrel with anyone, nor should he sleepy: in course of the day. This is how Shraddha should be performed.

## \|\| 16.58 \|\|

*kanyākumbhavṛṣasthe 'rke kṛṣṇapakṣeṣu sarvadā \|*  
*yatra yatra pradātavyaṃ sapiṇḍīkaraṇāt param \|*  
*tatrānena vidhānena deyam agnimatā sadā \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. ss In this way, an Agnihotri should perform Shraddha in the dark fortnights of the mouths when the sun is in the sign of Virgo, Aquarius, and Taurus. Whenever the Sapindi karana Shraddha is to be performed, there also the above ceremonial should be observed by one who keeps the sacred fire.

## Chapter 17

## \|\| 17.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi viṣṇunā yadudīritam \|*  
*śrāddhaṃ sādhāraṇaṃ nāma bhuktimuktiphalapradam \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Suta said: I shall now relate to you what Lord Vishnu said about the general ritual of Shraddha (applicable to all whether they keep sacred fire or not), that gives prosperity and emancipation.

## \|\| 17.2-5 \|\|

*ayane viṣuve ugme sāmānye cārkasaṃkrame \|*  
*amāvāsyāṣṭakākṛṣṇa-pakṣe pañcadaśīṣu ca \|\| 2 \|\|*

*ārdrāmaghārohiṇīṣu dravyabrāhmaṇasaṃgame \|*  
*gajacchāyāvyatīpāte viṣṭivaidhṛtivāsare \|\| 3 \|\|*

*vaiśākhasya tṛtīyāyāṃ navamī kārttikasya ca \|*  
*pañcadaśī ca māghasya nabhasye ca trayodaśī \|\| 4 \|\|*

*yugādayaḥ smṛtā hy etā dattasyākṣayyakārikāḥ \|*  
*tathā manvantarādau ca deyaṃ śrāddhaṃ vijānatā \|\| 5 \|\|*

2-5. Summer solstice, winter solstice, the period when the sun is in the equinoctial points, the period when the sun passes from one zodiacal sign into another, the period when any planetary body passes from one zodiacal sign into another, on the Amavasya and the ashtaka of the dark fortnight and on the fifteenth day of the moon, the period of the (Ardra) sixth, the (Magha) tenth and the (Rohini) fourth lunarmansiors, the presence of materials and Brahmanas, the time of a gajachchhaya, the day of full moon on a Monday, the days called Vishtis and Vaidhritis, the third day of the bright fortnight of the month Vaishakha which is the anniversary day of the Satya Yuga, the 9th day of the bright fortnight the month Kartika.

the anniversary day of the ‘Treta Yuga’, the 15th day (full moon) ‘of Magha, the anniversary day of the Kali Yuga, the thirteenth day of the dark fortnight of the month Bhadra, corresponding to August-September, which is the anniversary day of the Dvapara Yuga, are the periods and occasions when, by performing Shraddha, one gets bliss and exhaustless merits. So also on the anniversary days of the beginning of a Manvantara as detailed below.

## \|\| 17.6-8 \|\|

*aśvaukchuklanavamī dvādaśī kārttike tathā \|*  
*tṛtīyā caitramāsasya tathā bhādrapadasya ca \|\| 6 \|\|*

*phālgunasya hy amāvāsyā pauṣasyaikādaśī tathā \|*  
*āṣāḍhasyāpi daśamī māghamāsasya saptamī \|\| 7 \|\|*

*śrāvaṇasyāṣṭamī kṛṣṇā tathāṣāḍhī ca pūrṇimā \|*  
*kārttikī phālgunī caitrī jyeṣṭhapañcadaśī sitā \|*  
*manvantarādayaś caitā dattasyākṣayyakārikāḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

6-8. The ninth day of the bright fortnight of the month Ashvin, the twelfth tithi of the month Kartika, the third lunar day of the month Chaitra, the third lunar tithi of Bhadra, the Amavasya of the month Phalguna, the 11th lunar tithi of the month Pausha, the 10th lunar tithi of the month Ashadha, the 7th tithi of the month Magha, the 8th of dark fortnight in the month Shravana, the full moon days of the months Asadha, the full moon ‘days of the months Kartika, Phalguna, Chaitra and Jyeshtha, these fourteen days are anniversary days of the beginning of fourteen Manvantaras respectively.

These are the periods in which, if the Shraddha is performed, it gives unbounded satisfaction to the Pitris and brings exhaustless merit to the worshipper.

## \|\| 17.9 \|\|

*yasyāṃ manvantarasyādau rathamāste divākaraḥ \|*  
*māghamāsasya saptamyāṃ sā tu syādrathasaptamī \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The seventh day of the month of Magha is called Ratha-Saptami day, named after the Sun’s ascending the chariot already mentioned above as the anniversary day of the beginning of a Manvantara.

## \|\| 17.10 \|\|

*pānīyamapyatra tilairvimiśraṃ dadyātpitṛbhyaḥ prayato manuṣyaḥ \|*  
*śrāddhaṃ kṛtaṃ tena samāḥ sahasraṃ rahasyametatpitaro vadanti \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. The Pitris say that one who offers them a libation of ‘even water and sesamum on the Ratha-Saptami day, gets the same benefit as he would by performing Shraddha regularly for a the us and years.

## \|\| 17.11-12 \|\|

*vaiśākhyāmuparāgeṣu tathotsavamahālaye \|*  
*tīrthāyatanagoṣṭheṣu dīpodyānagṛheṣu ca \|\| 11 \|\|*

*vivikteṣūpalipteṣu śrāddhaṃ deyaṃ vijānatā \|*  
*viprānpūrve pare cāhni vinītātmā nimantrayet \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-12. Shraddha should he performed on the full moon day, in the month of Vaishakha, at the time of an eclipse, on the occasion of the sacred-thread ceremony and Mahalaya festival, in a holy city (tirtha), near a place where cows are kept, in gardens illuminated with lamps and in villas after plastering the floor with cowdung; and the Brahmana guests should he Invited to the feast the same day or a day previous in the manner mentioned before.

## \|\| 17.13 \|\|

*śīlavṛttaguṇopetān vayorūpasamanvitān \|*  
*dvau daive trīṃstathā pitrya ekaikamubhayatra vā \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. The Brahmanas invited to the feast should he well behaved, of good deeds and habits, young and good-looking. Two Brahmanas should be invited at Daiva-Shraddha and three at the Pitriya Shraddha feast, or only one may be invited on each: occasion.

## \|\| 17.14 \|\|

*bhojayetsusamṛddho 'pi na prasadjate vistare \|*  
*viśvāndevānyavaiḥ puṣpair abhyarcyāsanapūrvakam \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. A large number need not be invited, even if the host has great resources at his command. First, the Brahmana invited to Daiva-Shraddha should be attended. He should be seated and offered barley and flowers.

## \|\| 17.18-20 \|\|

*darbhāsanaṃ tu dattvādau trīṇi pātrāṇi pūrayet \|*  
*khapavitrāṇi kṛtvādau śaṃ no devīty apaḥ kṣipet \|\| 18 \|\|*

*tilo 'sīti tilānkuryād gandhapuṣpādikaṃ punaḥ \|*  
*pātraṃ vanaspatimayaṃ tathā parṇamayaṃ punaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

*jalajaṃ vātha kurvīta tathā sāgarasambhavam \|*  
*sauvarṇaṃ rājataṃ vāpi pitriṇāṃ pātramucyate \|\| 20 \|\|*

18-20. Two vessels should be placed with kusha rings, and water should be poured in one, after uttering, “Om Sanno Devi,” etc., and barley should be, pot in the other, after uttering, “Om yacho si.” etc. Flower and sandal should also be put in’ the vessels offered to the Vaidva devas with the mantra, “Om Vishvedeva.” etc., who should he thus invoked and barley should he thrown. After offering flowers and sandal, the host should offer Arghya water to them with the mantra "Yadivya” &c. - When the Vishvadeva worship is finished, the Pitri worship should be commenced, First three kusha should he placed for the Pitris to take their seats on, and then - kusha rings should be placed in three vessels in which water should he poured, after reciting, “Om Sanno Devi.” etc. “Sesamum should be offered by reciting, “Om Tilo si,” etc. after which sandal and flowers should be offered, The vessels for the Pitris should he made of any of the following materials, viz: — Lotus leaves, wood, conch-shell, gold and silver.

## \|\| 17.21-23 \|\|

*rajatasya kathā vāpi darśanaṃ dānameva vā \|*  
*rājatair bhājanaireṣām athavā rajatānvitaiḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*vāryapi śraddhayā dattam akṣayāyopakalpate \|*  
*tathārghyapiṇḍabhojyādau pitriṇāṃ rājataṃ matam \|\| 22 \|\|*

*śivanetrodbhavaṃ yasmāt tasmāttatpitṛvallabham \|*  
*amaṅgalaṃ tadyatnena devakāryeṣu varjayet \|\| 23 \|\|*

21-23. If a silver vessel may not be available, then the worshipper may give away a little silver; if he cannot afford that, then he may simply look at it or merely mention its name. By devoutly offering even water, out of silver or vessels made of alloyed silver, the worshipper gains everlasting bliss. The silver vessels are the best to be used at the time of offering libation and of pindas and of food to the pitris of water. Silver has come out, of the eyes of Shiva, and consequently it is so much appreciated by the Pitris; but it should not be employed at the time of Deva worship, for it is inauspicious there.

## \|\| 17.24 \|\|

*evaṃ pātrāṇi saṃkalpya yathālābhaṃ vimatsaraḥ \|*  
*yā divyeti piturnāma gotrairdarbhakaro nyaset \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. According to his means the worshipper should give away the vessels, and perform Sankalpa by taking a kusha in his hand and by reciting, “Om Ya Divya,” etc. and the name, etc. of his father and gotra.

## \|\| 17.25 \|\|

*pitrin āvāhayiṣyāmi kurvityuktastu taiḥ punaḥ \|*  
*uśantastvā tathāyantu ṛgbhyām āvāhayetpitrin \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Then the worshipper should say, “Pitrinavadhaishyami,” \[I shall now invoke the pitris\] when the assembled priests \[Brahmanas\] permit him by saying “Kuru.’ Afterwards, the worshipper should say, “Ushantastva”, “Ayentuvah Pitarah,” and thus invoke the Pitris with these two Rig Verses.

## \|\| 17.26-27 \|\|

*yā divyetyarghyamutsṛjya dadyādgandhādikāṃstataḥ \|*  
*hastāttadudakaṃ pūrvaṃ dattvā saṃsravamāditaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*pitṛpātre nidhāyātha nyubjamuttarato nyaset \|*  
*pitṛbhyaḥ sthānamasīti nidhāya pariṣecayet \|\| 27 \|\|*

26-27. After saying, “Va divya” etc., the worshipper should offer argya, that is, some water in a pot, along with flowers and sandal, and should put kusha rings in the dishes and pour on them the offered water out of the pot, and, after saying “ Pitribhya sthitnamasi,” should place the pot downwards, to the left of the Pitri's seat.

## \|\| 17.28-30 \|\|

*tatrāpi pūrvavatkuryād agnikāryaṃ vimatsaraḥ \|*  
*ubhābhyāmapi hastābhyām āhṛtya pariveṣayet \|\| 28 \|\|*

*praśāntacittaḥ satataṃ darbhapāṇiraśeṣataḥ \|*  
*guṇāḍhyaiḥ sūpaśākaistu nānābhakṣyairviśeṣataḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*annaṃ tu sadadhikṣīraṃ goghṛtaṃ śarkarānvitam \|*  
*māsaṃ prīṇāti vai sarvān pitrinityāha keśavaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

28-30. Afterwards the homa “Agni Karana” rite should be performed, as explained before, and then the worshipper should fetch the pot of food with both hands and put it in the dishes. At the time of putting the food in the dishes, kusha should be held in the hand with serene mind.

Several kinds of pulses, vegetables, and other victuals should also be arranged in the dishes. In offering food, curds, milk, clarified butter of cow’s milk and sugar should also be put in the dishes, Pitris are exceedingly fond of flesh, so Lord Keshava has said.

## \|\| 17.31-36 \|\|

*dvau māsau matsyamāṃsena trīnmāsānhāriṇena tu \|*  
*aurabhreṇātha caturaḥ śākunenātha pañca vai \|\| 31 \|\|*

*ṣaṇmāsaṃ chāgamāṃsena tṛpyanti pitarastathā \|*  
*sapta pārṣatamāṃsena tathāṣṭāv eṇajena tu \|\| 32 \|\|*

*daśa māsāṃstu tṛpyanti varāhamahiṣāmiṣaiḥ \|*  
*śaśakūrmajamāṃsena māsānekādaśaiva tu \|\| 33 \|\|*

*saṃvatsaraṃ tu gavyena payasā pāyasena ca \|*  
*rauraveṇa ca tṛpyanti māsānpañcadaśaiva tu \|\| 34 \|\|*

*vārdhrīṇasasya māṃsena tṛptir dvādaśavārṣikī \|*  
*kālaśākena cānantā khaḍgamāṃsena caiva hi \|\| 35 \|\|*

*yatkiṃcinmadhusammiśraṃ gokṣīraṃ ghṛtapāyasam \|*  
*dattamakṣayamityāhuḥ pitaraḥ pūrvadevatāḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

31-36. The Pitris say that the offering of fish keeps them satisfied for two months, the flesh of deer for three months, mutton for four months, the flesh of birds for five months, goat’s flesh for six months, Parshat’s flesh for seven months, Ena’s flesh for eight months, ham and buffaloes’ flesh for ten months, hare and turtle’s flesh for eleven months, cow’s (flesh? and)\* milk and rice cooked in cow’s milk for a year, the flesh of Ruru for 15 months, lion’s flesh for twelve years, Kelashaka (pot herb) and flesh of the rhinoceros for a great number of years, the cow’s milk mixed with honey and rice cooked in cow’s milk, clarified butter made of cow’s milk offered even, in a small measure satisfies the Pitris — the Parvadevatas to an extreme degree.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — Parsat, Ruru, Ena = species of deer.

\* Professor H. H, Wilson writes:

“The expression gavya implies all that is derived from a cow; but, in the text it is associated with ‘flush’; and, as the commentator observes some consider the flesh of the cow to be here intended. But this, he adds, relates to other ages. In the Kali or present age, it implies milk and preparations of milk. The Sacrifice of ‘a cow or calf formed part of the ancient Shraddha. It then became typical; or, as a boll was turned loose, instead of being slaughtered, and this is still practiced, on some occasions, In Manu, the term Gavya is coupled with others, which limit its application: —

‘A whole year with the milk of cows, and food made of that milk.” (Vishnu Purana Vol, III p. 198.)

## \|\| 17.37-39 \|\|

*svādhyāyaṃ śrāvayetpitryaṃ purāṇānyakhilāni ca \|*  
*brahmaviṣṇvarkarudrāṇāṃ sūktāni vividhāni ca \|\| 37 \|\|*

*indrāgnisomasūktāni pāvanāni svaśaktitaḥ \|*  
*bṛhadrathaṃtaraṃ tadvaj jyeṣṭhasāma sarauhiṇam \|\| 38 \|\|*

*tathaiva śāntikādhyāyaṃ madhubrāhmaṇameva ca \|*  
*maṇḍalaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ tadvat prītikāri tu yatpunaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

37-39. The worshipper should read some of the following: — the Vedic mantras relating to Pitrimedha, Puranas of all kinds, Brahma Sukta, Vishnu Sukta, Surya Sukta, Rudra Sukta, Indra Sukta, Agni Sukta, Soma — Sukta, Pavanani Sukta, according to one’s capacity, as well as Vrihadrathantar Sama, Jyeshtha Sama, Rauhina Sama, Santikadhyaya, Madhu: Brahmana, Mandala Brahmana, any other thing that may appeal to the worshipper and the Brahmanas.

## \|\| 17.40-41 \|\|

*viprāṇāmātmanaścaiva tatsarvaṃ samudīrayet \|*  
*bhuktavatsu tatasteṣu bhojanopāntike nṛpa \|\| 40 \|\|*

*sārvavarṇikamannādyaṃ saṃnīyāplāvya vāriṇā \|*  
*samutsṛjedbhuktavatām agrato vikiredbhuvi \|\| 41 \|\|*

40-41. When the Brahmanas are about to finish their meal, then Vikira rite should be performed for all the classes. The food should be put in one plate and scattered in front of the Brahmans along with some water.

## \|\| 17.42-44 \|\|

*agnidagdhāstu ye jīvā ye 'pyadagdhāḥ kule mama \|*  
*bhūmau dattena tṛpyantu prayāntu paramāṃ gatim \|\| 42 \|\|*

*yeṣāṃ na mātā na pitā na bandhur na gotraśuddhirna tathānnam asti \|*  
*tattṛptaye 'nnaṃ bhuvi dattametat prayāntu lokeṣu sukhāya tadvat \|\| 43 \|\|*

*asaṃskṛtapramītānāṃ tyaktānāṃ kulayoṣitām \|*  
*ucchiṣṭabhāgadheyaḥ syād darbhe vikirayośca yaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

42-44. At the time of performing Vikira rite, the following mantras should be read. These mean: — Those beings that have been burnt in the fire, those beings that have not been cremated in my family, may feel satisfied by the Vikira rite and attain emancipation. Those who have no father or mother, no brother, no clansman to offer them food, may feel satisfied with the food offered in the Vikira rite and attain peace. Those who were not invested with the sacred thread, those women discarded by their kinsmen, may feel satisfied with the food offered in Vikira.

## \|\| 17.45-46 \|\|

*tṛptāñjñātvodakaṃ dadyāt sakṛdviprakare tathā \|*  
*upalipte mahīpṛṣṭhe gośakṛnmūtravāriṇā \|\| 45 \|\|*

*nidhāya darbhānvidhivad dakṣiṇāgrān prayatnataḥ \|*  
*sarvavarṇena cānnena piṇḍāṃstu pitṛyajñavat \|\| 46 \|\|*

45-46. When the Brahmanas have finished their meal and are satisfied, then water should be poured out on their hands and on the floor plastered with cowdung. Kusha should be strewn towards the south, and on them the balls of various eatables should be offered.

## \|\| 17.47-48 \|\|

*avanejanapūrvaṃ tu nāmagotreṇa mānavaḥ \|*  
*gandhadhūpādikaṃ dadyāt kṛtvā pratyavanejanam \|\| 47 \|\|*

*jānvācya savyaṃ savyena pāṇinātha pradakṣiṇam \|*  
*pitryamānīya tatkāryaṃ vidhivaddarbhapāṇinā \|\| 48 \|\|*

47-48. The balls should be offered after sprinkling water and reciting the name and the gotra of the worshipper as mentioned before in avanejana rite, then incense, sandal, &c., should be offered, and then water should be sprinkled again. This sprinkling is called pratyaranejana. By putting the left knee down on the floor and by holding water along with kusha in the left hand, the Pitris should be invoked and circumambulated.

## \|\| 17.49 \|\|

*dīpaprajvālanaṃ tadvat kuryātpuṣpārcanaṃ budhaḥ \|*  
*athācānteṣu cācamya vāri dadyātsakṛtsakṛt \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Similarly, sandal and dipa should also be offered. After the Brahmanas have washed their hands and mouth, the worshipper should himself rinse his mouth with water and offer water to his guests.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — Dipa = waving alight before the object of worship.

## \|\| 17.50 \|\|

*atha puṣpākṣatān paścād akṣayyodakam eva ca \|*  
*satilaṃ nāmagotreṇa dadyācchaktyā ca dakṣiṇām \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Then flowers, rice (unhusked), sesamum, should he offered ‘to the Brahmanas, after which they should be given some Dakshina, according to the means of the worshipper, who should offer it to each Brahmana or calling out his name and lineage.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — Dakshina is money offered to Brahmanas.

## \|\| 17.51 \|\|

*gobhūhiraṇyavāsāṃsi bhavyāni śayanāni ca \|*  
*dadyādyadiṣṭaṃ viprāṇām ātmanaḥ pitureva ca \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. The worshipper should give away cows, land, gold, clothes liked by the Brahmanas, appreciated by the Pitris and appealing: to the worshipper’s own fancy.

## \|\| 17.52-53 \|\|

*vittaśāṭhyena rahitaḥ pitṛbhyaḥ prītimāvahan \|*  
*tataḥ svadhāvācanakaṃ viśvadeveṣu codakam \|\| 52 \|\|*

*dattvāśīḥ pratigṛhṇīyād dvijebhyaḥ prāṅmukho budhaḥ \|*  
*aghorāḥ pitaraḥ santu santvityuktaḥ punar dvijaiḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

52-53. There should be no niggardliness in the giving of Dakshina, and to please the Pitris the worshipper should ask the Brahmanas to do Swadha Vachana. Water should be put in the hands of the Brahmanas after vishva deva ceremony and the worshipper should receive the blessings of the ‘Brahmanas by facing himself towards the East. He should first say “Aghorah Pitarah Santu,” (“let the pitris be auspicious”), in reply to which the Brahmanas should say “Shantu” “(let it be so) ’.

## \|\| 17.54-55 \|\|

*gotraṃ tathā vardhatāṃ nas tathetyuktaśca taiḥ punaḥ \|*  
*dātāro no 'bhivardhantām iti caivamudīrayet \|\| 54 \|\|*

*etāḥ satyāśiṣaḥ santu santvityuktaśca taiḥ punaḥ \|*  
*svastivācanakaṃ kuryāt piṇḍānuddhṛtya bhaktitaḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

54-55. The host should again say, ‘Gotram tatha Vardhatamnah, to which the Brahmanas should reply, “ Vardhatim (let similarly our clan be increased)”, the worshipper should say, “Dataronobhivardhan tam (let the giver of presents increase in our family,”) the Brahmanas should say, “Vardhantam (may they increase)” the worshipper “Etahsatyashishah santu (let these blessings be true),” the Brahmanas “Shantu (may it be so)." After finishing svadhavichana like this, the worshipper should perform “uchchhaigana ” at the time of lismissing his invited guests, and, after, that he should perform “graha bali.”

## \|\| 17.56-58 \|\|

*uccheṣaṇaṃ tu tattiṣṭhed yāvadviprā visarjitāḥ \|*  
*tato grahabaliṃ kuryād iti dharmavyavasthitiḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

*uccheṣaṇaṃ bhūmigatam ajihmasyāstikasya ca \|*  
*dāsavargasya tatpitryaṃ bhāgadheyaṃ pracakṣate \|\| 57 \|\|*

*pitṛbhir nirmitaṃ pūrvam etadāpyāyanaṃ sadā \|*  
*aputrāṇāṃ saputrāṇāṃ strīṇāmapi narādhipa \|\| 58 \|\|*

56-58. Uchcheshana = is defined below.

Grahabali = domestic oblation. Offering of the remnants of meal to all creatures, such as animals, supernatural beings and particularly household Deities.

"Uchchheshana” is to leave some food scattered on the floor, for the acceptance of the attendants of the Pitris known as Astika and Akutila.

The Pitris themselves started! this rite for the satisfaction of their attendants which should be performed by all — those who have children and those who are childless.

## \|\| 17.59-60 \|\|

*tatastānagrataḥ sthitvā parigṛhyodapātrakam \|*  
*vāje vāja iti japan kuśāgreṇa visarjayet \|\| 59 \|\|*

*bahiḥ pradakṣiṇāṃ kuryāt padāny aṣṭāv anuvrajan \|*  
*bandhuvargeṇa sahitaḥ putrabhāryāsamanvitaḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

59-60. Afterwards, the worshipper should stand before the Brahmanas, made of kusha, with a pot of water, and after reciting “Vaje, Vaje,” etc. should dismiss them with the kusha end. The worshipper should then move eight steps out of the house, and along with his wife, son and kinsmen should complete the rite of shraddha.

## \|\| 17.61 \|\|

*nivṛtya praṇipatyātha paryukṣyāgniṃ samantravat \|*  
*vaiśvadevaṃ prakurvīta naityakaṃ balimeva ca \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Then he should. alter sprinkling water silently round the fire, without uttering any ritual formulae, perform Vaishyadeva and Nityabali.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — Vaishvadeva = an offering to all the Deities (made by presenting oblations to fire before meals.) Nityabali = daily offering.

## \|\| 17.62 \|\|

*tatastu vaiśvadevānte sabhṛtyasutabāndhavaḥ \|*  
*bhuñjītātithisaṃyuktaḥ sarvaṃ pitṛniṣevitam \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. After the Vaishva deva ceremony he may partake of the food with his servants, sons, kith and kin and other guests.

## \|\| 17.63-64 \|\|

*etaccānupanīto 'pi kuryātsarveṣu parvasu \|*  
*śrāddhaṃ sādhāraṇaṃ nāma sarvakāmaphalapradam \|\| 63 \|\|*

*bhāryāvirahito 'pyetat pravāsastho 'pi bhaktimān \|*  
*śūdro 'pyamantravatkuryād anena vidhinā budhaḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

63-64. This form of Sadharana shraddha can be performed even by those, who have not been invested with the sacred thread, those who are in a foreign country and have not their wives with them. The Shudras may also perform it without reciting any sacred formulae.

## \|\| 17.65 \|\|

*tṛtīyamābhyudayikaṃ vṛddhiśrāddhaṃ taducyate \|*  
*utsavānandasambhāre yajñodvāhādimaṅgale \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. The third shraddha is called Abhyudaikam, which is also known as Vriddhi Shraddha. It is performed on auspicious occasions such as a big sacrifice, marriage, &c.

## \|\| 17.66 \|\|

*mātaraḥ prathamaṃ pūjyāḥ pitarastadanantaram \|*  
*tato mātāmahā rājan viśve devāstathaiva ca \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. In Vriddhi shraddha, offerings are made in the following order: —

Mother, grandmother, great-grandmother, father, grandfather, great-grandfather, maternal-grandfather, maternal great-grandfather, maternal-greatgreat-grandfather, Vishvadeva.

## \|\| 17.67 \|\|

*pradakṣiṇopacāreṇa dadhyakṣataphalodakaiḥ \|*  
*prāṅmukho nirvapetpiṇḍān dūrvayā ca kuśairyutān \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. The worshipper should, after circumambulating, turn his face towards the East and should then remove the balls made of curds, uncooked rice, fruits, water, and laden with kusha and durva grass.

## \|\| 17.68 \|\|

*sampannam ityabhyudaye dadyādarghyaṃ dvayor dvayoḥ \|*  
*yugmā dvijātayaḥ pūjyā vastrakārtasvarādibhiḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. The Brahmanas should be offered water (arghya) twice, with the words, ‘Sampannam, (accomplished) and should he worshipped and offered clothes, gold, &c., by the twice-born.

## \|\| 17.69 \|\|

*tilārthastu yavaiḥ kāryo nāndīśabdānupūrvakaḥ \|*  
*māṅgalyāni ca sarvāṇi vācayeddvijapuṃgavaiḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. Barley should be offered in lieu of sesamum; this is also called Nandimukha shraddha, and propitions mantras in performing it should be uttered.

## \|\| 17.70 \|\|

*evaṃ śūdro 'pi sāmānya-vṛddhiśrāddhe 'pi sarvadā \|*  
*namaskāreṇa mantreṇa kuryādāmānnataḥ sadā \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. A Shudra can also perform tie ordinary as well as the Vridhi Shraddha with uncooked grain, by uttering the formula of namah instead of Vedic mantras.

## \|\| 17.71 \|\|

*dānapradhānaḥ śūdraḥ syād ityāha bhagavānprabhuḥ \|*  
*dānena sarvakāmāptir asya saṃjāyate yataḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. For thus said the Lord Bhagavan: — Charity is the best thing for a Shudra, by performing which he gains all his ends.

## Chapter 18

## \|\| 18.1-5 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*ekoddiṣṭamato vakṣye yaduktaṃ cakrapāṇinā \|*  
*mṛte putrairyathā kāryam āśaucaṃ ca pitaryapi \|\| 1 \|\|*

*daśāhaṃ śāvamāśaucaṃ brāhmaṇeṣu vidhīyate \|*  
*kṣatriyeṣu daśa dve ca pakṣaṃ vaiśyeṣu caiva hi \|\| 2 \|\|*

*śūdreṣu māsamāśaucaṃ sapiṇḍeṣu vidhīyate \|*  
*naiśaṃ vākṛtacūḍasya trirātraṃ parataḥ smṛtam \|\| 3 \|\|*

*janane 'pyevameva syāt sarvavarṇeṣu sarvadā \|*  
*tathāsthisaṃcayād ūrdhvam aṅgasparśo vidhīyate \|\| 4 \|\|*

*pretāya piṇḍadānaṃ tu dvādaśāhaṃ samācaret \|*  
*pātheyaṃ tasya tatproktaṃ yataḥ prītikaraṃ mahat \|\| 5 \|\|*

1-5. Suta said: I shall now relate to you the Ekoddishta shraddha, as explained by the Lord, and will also tell you for what period a son should consider himself defiled after the death of his father. By the death of a kinsman (Sapinda), a Brahmana remains defiled for ten days, a Kshatrya for 12 days, a Vaishya for 15 days, a Sidra for a month. By the demise of one whose tonsure ceremony was not performed, one remains defiled for a nights. Similarly, people of all classes are defiled for a period when there is a child-birth in the house. At the time of a death till the corpse is burnt and the ashes are collected, the person in whose family the death occurs should not be considered contaminated. Commencing from the day of the demise of the person, a lump of food should be offered to the ‘departed spirit, for a period of twelve days. That offering is Patheya (that is viaticum) and is consequently most agreeable.

## \|\| 18.6-7 \|\|

*tasmātpretapuraṃ preto dvādaśāhaṃ na nīyate \|*  
*gṛhaṃ putraṃ kalatraṃ ca dvādaśāhaṃ prapaṣyati \|\| 6 \|\|*

*tasmānnidheyamākāśe daśarātraṃ payastathā \|*  
*sarvadāhopaśāntyartham adhvaśramavināśanam \|\| 7 \|\|*

6-7. In case of offering Pinda to the deceased on the 12th day after his death, the attendants of Yama do not carry the spirit to the city of the God of Death, and during this period the departed spirit sees his sous, wife or any other member of the family, and observes whether they provide it with something for its comfort on its long journey or not. It is for this reason that a pitcher full of water is suspended from a tree, for a period of ten days. Its water soothes the heat of cremation and also refreshes the spirit when it gets weary on the great journey.

## \|\| 18.8-10 \|\|

*tata ekādaśāhe tu dvijānekādaśaiva tu \|*  
*kṣatrādiḥ sūtakānte tu bhojayedaujo dvijān \|\| 8 \|\|*

*dvitīye 'hni punastadvad ekoddiṣṭaṃ samācaret \|*  
*āvāhanāgnaukaraṇaṃ daivahīnaṃ vidhānataḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*ekaṃ pavitrameko 'rgha ekaḥ piṇḍo vidhīyate \|*  
*upatiṣṭhatāmityetad deyaṃ paścāttilodakam \|\| 10 \|\|*

8-10. A Brahmana on the 11th day after death should feast 11 Brahmanas and Kshatriyas, &c., should feast an uneven number of Brahmanas. On the day following the completion of the period of defilement, one should perform the Ekoddishta Shraddha in which all the ceremonies previously described, barring invocation and homa ceremony of Vishvadeva, should be performed. in this Shraddha, only one kusha ring should be put on, and only one offering of water (arghya) and ball of food (pinda) Should be made, After reciting “ Upatishthatam,” sesamum and a handful of water should be offered.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — Upatishthatam = It is offered to thee.

## \|\| 18.11-18 \|\|

*svaditaṃ vikiredbrūyād visarge cābhiramyatām \|*  
*śeṣaṃ pūrvavadatrāpi kāryaṃ vedavidā pituḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*anena vidhinā sarvam anumāsaṃ samācaret \|*  
*sūtakāntāddvitīye 'hni śayyāṃ dadyādvilakṣaṇām \|\| 12 \|\|*

*kāñcanaṃ puruṣaṃ tadvat phalavastrasamanvitām \|*  
*saṃpūjya dvijadāmpatyaṃ nānābharaṇabhūṣaṇaiḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*vṛṣotsargaṃ prakurvīta deyā ca kapilā śubhā \|*  
*udakumbhaśca dātavyo bhakṣyabhojyasamanvitaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*yāvadabdaṃ naraśreṣṭha satilodakapūrvakam \|*  
*tataḥ saṃvatsare pūrṇe sapiṇḍīkaraṇaṃ bhavet \|\| 15 \|\|*

*sapiṇḍīkaraṇādūrdhvaṃ pretaḥ pārvaṇabhāgbhavet \|*  
*vṛddhipūrveṣu yogyaśca gṛhasthaśca bhavettataḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*sapiṇḍīkaraṇe śrāddhe devapūrvaṃ niyojayet \|*  
*pitrin nivāsayettatra pṛthakpretaṃ vinirdiśet \|\| 17 \|\|*

*gandhodakatilairyuktaṃ kuryātpātracatuṣṭayam \|*  
*arghārthaṃ pitṛpātreṣu pretapātraṃ prasecayet \|\| 18 \|\|*

11-18. Svahitam should be recited at the time of performing the Vikira rite, and Abhiramyatam should be uttered at the time of dismissing the departed spirit. The rest of the rite should be performed, as explained before. Similarly, Shraddha should be performed each month, and, on the second day of the completion of the period of defilement, a well-bedecked bed should be given away. At the same time, an image made of gold and well dressed, should also be given away and the Brahmana as well as his consort should he worshipped, after being well dressed and made to wear good ornaments. A bull should be set free, and a really good cow and a pitcher full of water, along with nice eatables, should also be given away. The pitcher should be filled with sesamum along with water.

After a year, the Sapindi-karana shraddha should be performed. After the performance of Sapindi-karana shraddha the deceased (preta) becomes entitled to receive a share out of the Parvana shraddha and become legible for worship at Vriddhi shraddha, and the householder also becomes entitled to perform Nandimukha shraddha, &c. Vishvadeva rite is performed in sapindi-karana shraddha, and the ancestors and the fresh departed spirits are offered separate seats. Water, mixed with sandal and sesamum, should be put in four different vessels for offering. The vessels meant for the Pitris and the departed spirit should be mixed together.

## \|\| 18.19-25 \|\|

*tadvatsaṃkalpya caturaḥ piṇḍānpiṇḍapradastathā \|*  
*ye samānā iti dvābhyām antyaṃ tu vibhajettridhā \|\| 19 \|\|*

*caturthasya punaḥ kāryaṃ na kadācidato bhavet \|*  
*tataḥ pitṛtvamāpannaḥ sarvatastuṣṭimāgataḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*agniṣvāttādimadhyatvaṃ prāpnotyamṛtamuttamam \|*  
*sapiṇḍīkaraṇādūrdhvaṃ tasmai tasmānna dīyate \|\| 21 \|\|*

*pitṛṣveva tu dātavyaṃ tatpiṇḍo yeṣu saṃsthitaḥ \|*  
*tataḥ prabhṛti saṃkrāntāv uparāgādiparvasu \|\| 22 \|\|*
