*tripiṇḍamācarecchrāddham ekoddiṣṭe mṛte 'hani \|*  
*ekoddiṣṭaṃ parityajya mṛtāhe yaḥ samācaret \|\| 23 \|\|*

*sadaiva pitṛhā sa syān mātṛbhrātṛvināśakaḥ \|*  
*mṛtāhe pārvaṇaṃ kurvan nadho 'dho yāti mānavaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*saṃpṛkteṣvākulībhāvaḥ preteṣu tu gato bhavet \|*  
*pratisaṃvatsaraṃ tasmād ekoddiṣṭaṃ samācaret \|\| 25 \|\|*

19-25. Similarly, four balls of food should be offered, and, after reciting ye samanah samansah, the balls meant four the departed spirit should be divided into three parts and mixed with the balls of food meant for the Pitris, Excepting in Sapindi-karana shraddha, there is no separate rite for the deceased in any other ceremony. The departed spirit becomes delighted by the performance of sapindi-karana, for it then joins the Pitris (and ceases to be a preta). The departed spirit joins the Agnishvatta group of Pitris and drinks with them nectar; and it is for this reason that no Pindidana is performed for the departed spirit after the sapindi-karana. The ball of food (pinda) should only be offered to those who join the group of Pitris. After sapindi-karana, three balls are offered on the occasion of an eclipse or when the sun or any planetary body passes from one zodiacal sign into another; and on the date of demise only one ball is offered. If on the date of death one leaves the Ekoddishta shraddha and performs the Parvana, he commits a sin equal to that of murder of father, mothers and brother, and goes to hell.

## \|\| 18.25-26 \|\|

*saṃpṛkteṣvākulībhāvaḥ preteṣu tu gato bhavet \|*  
*pratisaṃvatsaraṃ tasmād ekoddiṣṭaṃ samācaret \|\| 25 \|\|*

*yāvadabdaṃ tu yo dadyād udakumbhaṃ vimatsaraḥ \|*  
*pretāyānnasamāuktaṃ so 'śvamedhaphalaṃ labhet \|\| 26 \|\|*

25-26. The deceased, after living with the Pretas (spirits) for a long time, begins to feel uncomfortable. It is therefore necessary that Ekoddishta should he performed every year. One who, being devoid of jealousy, gives away a jar full of water along with grain for one full year, for the benefit of the departed spirit, has the same reward as is obtained by performing the Ashvamedha sacrifice.

## \|\| 18.27-29 \|\|

*āmaśrāddhaṃ yadā kuryād vidhijñaḥ śrāddhadastadā \|*  
*tenāgnaukaraṇaṃ kuryāt piṇḍāṃstenaiva nirvapet \|\| 27 \|\|*

*tribhiḥ sapiṇḍīkaraṇe aśeṣatritaye pitā \|*  
*yadā prāpsyati kālena tadā mucyeta bandhanāt \|\| 28 \|\|*

*mukto 'pi lepabhāgitvaṃ prāpnoti kuśamārjanāt \|*  
*lepabhājaścaturthādyāḥ pitrādyāḥ piṇḍabhāginaḥ \|*  
*piṇḍadaḥ saptamasteṣāṃ sāpiṇḍyaṃ sāptapauruṣam \|\| 29 \|\|*

27-29. When a shraddha is performed with uncooked grain, then Agnikarana and Pindadana should also be performed with the same. By the performance of sapindi-karana, the deceased soul joins the first three groups of Pitris, and then it finds emancipation in process of time. Even after attaining emancipation they get their share of (lepa) shraddha by the hands being wiped with a kusha. From the 4th to the 6th generation, the forefathers get their share of shraddha from the kusha wiping (lepa) and not pindas, and three generations, father, grandfather and great grandfather, they are entitled to the ball of food (pinda), the seventh being the giver of the Pinda. These seven are known as sapindas for the sapinda hood includes these seven counting the performer of the sacrifice.

## Chapter 19

## \|\| 19.1-2 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ*  
*kathaṃ kavyāni deyāni havyāni ca janairiha \|*  
*gacchanti pitṛlokasthān prāpakaḥ ko 'tra gadyate \|\| 1 \|\|*

*yadi martyo dvijo bhuṅkte hūyate yadi vānale \|*  
*śubhāśubhātmakaiḥ pretair dattaṃ tadbhujyate katham \|\| 2 \|\|*

1-2. The Rishis asked: — How the offerings to the ancestors and the Devas are to be made here by men. They also requested him to explain to them in what way the offerings made in this world reach the Pitris in the Pitriloka and who is the medium between the Pitris and the man who makes offerings. We see that men eat and offerings are made in the fire, how do they then reach the deceased?

## \|\| 19.3-4 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*vasūnvadanti ca pitrin rudrāṃścaiva pitāmahān \|*  
*prapitāmahāṃstathādityān ityevaṃ vaidikī śrutiḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*nāma gotraṃ pitriṇāṃ tu prāpakaṃ havyakavyayoḥ \|*  
*śrāddhasya mantrāḥ śraddhā ca upayojyātibhaktitaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

3-4. Suta said: — It is written in the Veda that the eight Vasus are the Pitris, the eleven Rudras are the Pitamahas, and the twelve Adityas are the Prapitamahas. The recitation of name and clan of the Pitris by means of the sacred formula with devotion, carries the offerings made to the Pitris.

## \|\| 19.5-9 \|\|

*agniṣvāttādayasteṣām ādhipatye vyavasthitāḥ \|*  
*nāmagotrakāladeśā bhavāntaragatānapi \|\| 5 \|\|*

*prāṇinaḥ prīṇayantyete tadāhāratvamāgatān \|*  
*devo yadi pitā jātaḥ śubhakarmānuyogataḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*tasyānnamamṛtaṃ bhūtvā divyatve 'pyanugacchati \|*  
*daityatve bhogarūpeṇa paśutve ca tṛṇaṃ bhavet \|\| 7 \|\|*

*śrāddhānnaṃ vāurūpeṇa sarpatve 'pyupatiṣṭhati \|*  
*pānaṃ bhavati yakṣatve rākṣasatve tathāmiṣam \|\| 8 \|\|*

*danujatve tathā māyā pretatve rudhirodakam \|*  
*manuṣyatve 'nnapānāni nānābhogarasaṃ bhavet \|\| 9 \|\|*

5-9. Agnishvatta, &c., are appointed as rulers of deceased ancestors. They transport the offerings made to the ancestors even though they have been reborn in the meanwhile ‘under another name, clan, place and time.

The Pitris carry the ball of food offered in the form of nectar if the deceased ancestor has become a Deva through his good karma. If he is reborn as a Daitya, the offering reaches him in the form of worldly enjoyment. If taking birth as a beast, he gets it in the form of grass; those in the body of serpents get it in the form of air; those in form of Yaksha get it as wine: those in the body of the Rakshasa get it in the form of flesh; those in the body of danavas get it in the form of maya (delusion or glamour), those in the form of ghosts get it as blood and water; and those who are born as human beings get it in the form of grain and water and other multifarious objects of enjoyments.

## \|\| 19.10-11 \|\|

*ratiśaktiḥ striyaḥ kāntā bhojyaṃ bhojanaśaktitā \|*  
*dānaśaktiḥ savibhavā rūpamārogyameva ca \|\| 10 \|\|*

*śraddhā puṣpamidaṃ proktaṃ phalaṃ brahmasamāgamaḥ \|*  
*āuḥ putrān dhanaṃ vidyāṃ svargaṃ mokṣaṃ sukhāni ca \|\| 11 \|\|*

10-11. The faculty of sensuous enjoyment, beautiful women, delicious victuals and the power of enjoying them, wealth, the power of charity, handsome form, health are the flowers offered in Shraddha performed with devotion. The attainment of Brahma, good age, suns, wealth, knowledge, heaven, bliss of emancipation are the fruits offered in Shraddha.

## \|\| 19.12 \|\|

*rājyaṃ caiva prayacchanti prītāḥ pitṛgaṇā nṛṇām \|*  
*śrūyate ca purā mokṣaṃ prāptāḥ kauśikasūnavaḥ \|*  
*pañcabhirjanmasambandhair gatā viṣṇoḥ paraṃ padam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. The Pitris confer kingdoms on their devotees when they are pleased and it is also said that the sons of Kaushika Rishi attained Nirvana through the glory of the Pitris, in their fifth cycle of birth.

## Chapter 20

## \|\| 20.1 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ*  
*kathaṃ kauśikadāyādāḥ prāptāste yogamuttamam \|*  
*pañcabhirjanmasambandhaiḥ kathaṃ karmakṣayo bhavet \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. The Rishis asked the sage Suta to relate to them how the song of Kaushika in their fifth cycle of birth, putting an end to their desires, attained emancipation by their power of Yoga.

## \|\| 20.2-3 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*kauśiko nāma dharmātmā kurukṣetre mahānṛṣiḥ \|*  
*nāmataḥ karmatastasya sutānsapta nibodhata \|\| 2 \|\|*

*śvasṛpaḥ krodhano hiṃsraḥ piśunaḥ kavireva ca \|*  
*vāgduṣṭaḥ pitṛvartī ca gargaśiṣyāstadābhavan \|\| 3 \|\|*

2-3. Suta said, once upon a time there lived in Kurukshetra a virtuous Rishi named Kaushika. He had seven sons. Every one of whom did the deeds as connoted by their respective names. They were: — Svasripa, Krodhana, Hinsra, Pishuna, Kavi, Vagdushta, Pitrivarti. They were pupils of Garga.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — Svasripa = Moving at pleasure or will. Krodhana = Irascible. Hinsra = Savage.

Pishuna = Backbiter. Kavi = Poet. Vagdushta = Scurrilous. Pitrivarti = Devotee of the Pitris.

## \|\| 20.4-9 \|\|

*pitaryuparate teṣām abhūddurbhikṣamulbaṇam \|*  
*anāvṛṣṭiśca mahatī sarvalokabhayaṃkarī \|\| 4 \|\|*

*gargādeśādvane dogdhrīṃ rakṣantaste tapodhanāḥ \|*  
*khādāmaḥ kapilāmetāṃ vayaṃ kṣutpīḍitā bhṛśam \|\| 5 \|\|*

*iti cintayatāṃ pāpaṃ laghuḥ prāha tadānujaḥ \|*  
*yadyavaṣyamiyaṃ vadhyā śrāddharūpeṇa yojyatām \|\| 6 \|\|*

*śrāddhe niyojyamāneyaṃ pāpāttrāsyati no dhruvam \|*  
*eva kurvityanujñātaḥ pitṛvartī tadānujaiḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*cakre samāhitaḥ śrāddham upaujya ca tāṃ punaḥ \|*  
*dvau daive bhrātarau kṛtvā pitre trīnapyanukramāt \|\| 8 \|\|*

*tathaikamatithiṃ kṛtvā śrāddhadaḥ svayameva tu \|*  
*cakāra mantravacchrāddhaṃ smaranpitṛparāyaṇaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

4-9. After the death of their father the land was visited with a terrible famine when a large number of people were ruined owing to the cessation of rain and many died of starvation. In those days the seven sons of Kaushika used to look after the cow of Garga and were residing in a forest. One day not getting anything to eat them felt fearfully oppressed with the pangs of hunger. In those circumstances they, resolved saying we shall eat the cow to appease our hunger. At that stage the youngest of them all, said to his brothers: — “If this cow must be killed, let us Sacrifice her to our pitris in Shraddha for the cow sacrificed with that view would decidedly save us from all sin.” “Do so” said the other brothers to Pitrivarti. The cow was sacrificed and Pitrivarti performed the shraddha with great devotion. Two brothers officiated for the Brahmanas invited to Vishvedeva rite, the rest three similarly officiated for the Brahmanas, invited to take part in the Pitri-karma and the seventh one represented the Atithi. In this way they all after performing the shraddha with due Mantras and Meditating on Pitris feasted on the sacrificed cow.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — Atithi = guest. According to Manu.

## \|\| 20.10 \|\|

*vinā gavā vatsako 'pi gurave viniveditaḥ \|*  
*vyāghreṇa nihatā dhenur vatso 'yaṃ pratigṛhyatām \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. After that they repaired to their preceptor — Garga and delivering the calf. to him said “Guru! the cow has been devoured by the lion, this calf was saved, which take back.”

## \|\| 20.11 \|\|

*evaṃ sā bhakṣitā dhenuḥ saptabhistaistapodhanaiḥ \|*  
*vaidikaṃ balamāśritya krūre karmaṇi nirbhayāḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Bled In that way the seven ascetics committed fearlessly a cruel act on the strength of the Vedic injunction and ate the cow.

## \|\| 20.12-14 \|\|

*tataḥ kālāvakṛṣṭāste vyādhā dāśapure 'bhavan \|*  
*jātismaratvaṃ prāptāste pitṛbhāvena bhāvitāḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*yatkṛtaṃ krūrakarmāpi śrāddharūpeṇa taistadā \|*  
*tena te bhavane jātā vyādhānāṃ krūrakarmiṇām \|\| 13 \|\|*

*pitriṇāṃ caiva māhātmyāj jātā jātismarāstu te \|*  
*te tu vairāgyayogena āsthāyānaśanaṃ punaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

12-14. In process of time they were all gathered to their fathers and were re-born in the house of a hunter; but as they performed the shraddha with great, devotion they had a recollection of their previous life through the glory of the Pitris They were however born in the family of a hunter on account; of their having committed a cruel deed: but as they had a recollection of their previous life, they in a fit of asceticism spurned at all mundane luxuries and put an end to their existence by fasting.

## \|\| 20.15 \|\|

*jātismarāḥ sapta jātā mṛgāḥ kālañjare girau \|*  
*nīlakaṇṭhasya purataḥ pitṛbhāvānubhāvitāḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Afterwards they were re-born as deer on the Kalanjara hill and through the glory of the Pitris maintained their recollection of their previous lives. They then devoted themselves to the Pitris and the God Shiva.

## \|\| 20.16-18 \|\|

*tatrāpi jñānavairāgyāt prāṇānutsṛjya dharmataḥ \|*  
*lokair avekṣyamāṇāste tīrthānte 'naśanena tu \|\| 16 \|\|*

*mānase cakravākāste saṃjātāḥ sapta yoginaḥ \|*  
*nāmataḥ karmataḥ sarvāñ chṛṇudhvaṃ dvijasattamāḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*sumanāḥ kumudaḥ śuddhaś chidradarśī sunetrakaḥ \|*  
*sunetraścāṃśumāṃścaiva saptaite yogapāragāḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

16-18. They again gave up the ghost by carrying on the penance of fasting; and were re-born in the form of Chakravaka bird on the banks of the Mana Sarovara lake, under the following names: — Sumana, Kumuda, Shudddha, Chhidradarshi, Sunetraka, Sunetra, and Amshuman. They were endowed with the attributes connoted by their respective names and did similar deeds

**Комментарий:**

Note. — Sumana = Pleasing to the mind. Beautiful. Kumuda = lotus. Shudddha = Pure.

Chhidra-darshi = Captious, Critic, Sunetraka = Having good eyes. Sunetra = Having beautiful eyes. Amshuman = Illustrious.

## \|\| 20.19-20 \|\|

*yogabhraṣṭāstrayasteṣāṃ babhramuś cālpacetanāḥ \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā vibhrājamānaṃ tam udyāne strībhiranvitam \|\| 19 \|\|*

*krīḍantaṃ vividhairbhāvair mahābalaparākramam \|*  
*pañcālānvayasambhūtaṃ prabhūtabalavāhanam \|\| 20 \|\|*

19-20. Out of those seven, the three fallen from yoga began to roam about hither and thither. One day they came across Vibhraja the valiant king of Panchala who was enjoying himself in his pleasure garden and had a large retinue of followers and conveyances.

## \|\| 20.21-24 \|\|

*rājyakāmo 'bhavaccaikas teṣāṃ madhye jalaukasām \|*  
*pitṛvartī ca yo vipraḥ śrāddhakṛt pitṛvatsalaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*aparau mantriṇau dṛṣṭvā prabhūtabalavāhanau \|*  
*mantritve cakratuścecchām asminmartye dvijottamāḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*tanmadhye ye tu niṣkāmās te babhūvur dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*vibhrājaputrastveko 'bhūd brahmadatta iti smṛtaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

*mantriputrau tathā cobhau kaṇḍarīkasubālakau \|*  
*brahmadatto 'bhiṣiktaḥ san purohitavipaścitā \|\| 24 \|\|*

21-24. Pitravarti the youngest of all the brothers and who had performed the Shraddha, became desirous of becoming a king; the other two brothers wished to become the courtiers of a king; the remaining four did not cherish any wish and they were consequently born as Brahmanas. One of them (Pitrivati) was born as Brahmadatta, the son of King Vibhraja, two brothers were born as Kandarika and Subalaka the sons of the king’s minister; and sometime after that, Brahmadatta was anointed and proclaimed as king.

## \|\| 20.25 \|\|

*pañcālarājo vikrāntaḥ sarvaśāstraviśāradaḥ \|*  
*yogavitsarvajantūnāṃ rutavettābhavattadā \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Brahmadatta was the most illustrious sovereign of Panchala. He ruled the country with great piety and even-handed justice. He was well-versed in all the shastras, yoga and understood the languages of all animals.

## \|\| 20.26-27 \|\|

*tasya rājño 'bhavadbhāryā devalasyātmajā śubhā \|*  
*saṃnatirnāma vikhyātā kapilā yābhavatpurā \|\| 26 \|\|*

*pitṛkārye niuktatvād abhavadbrahmavādinī \|*  
*tayā cakāra sahitaḥ sa rājyaṃ rājanandanaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

26-27. The cow that was sacrificed and feasted upon by them as the sons of Kaushika was born as Sannati the daughter of Devala and was eventually married to Brahmadatta. Because she had served as an offering of the Pitris, she became learned in the Brahma lore, and the king ruled the country to the satisfaction and prosperity of his subjects in conjunction with his noble consort Sanati.

## \|\| 20.28-34 \|\|

*kadācidudyānagatas tayā saha sa pārthivaḥ \|*  
*dadarśa kīṭamithunam anaṅgakalahākulam \|\| 28 \|\|*

*pipīlikāmanunayan paritaḥ kīṭakāmukaḥ \|*  
*pañcabāṇābhitaptāṅgaḥ sagadgadamuvāca ha \|\| 29 \|\|*

*na tvayā sadṛśī loke kāminī vidyate kvacit \|*  
*madhyakṣāmātijaghanā bṛhadvakṣo 'bhigāminī \|\| 30 \|\|*

*suvarṇavarṇā suśroṇī mañjūktā cāruhāsinī \|*  
*sulakṣyanetrarasanā guḍaśarkaravatsalā \|\| 31 \|\|*

*bhokṣyase mayi bhukte tvaṃ snāsi snāte tathā mayi \|*  
*proṣite sati dīnā tvaṃ kruddhe 'pi bhayacañcalā \|\| 32 \|\|*

*kimarthaṃ vada kalyāṇi saroṣavadanā sthitā \|*  
*sā tamāha sakopā tu kim ālapasi māṃ śaṭha \|\| 33 \|\|*

*tvayā modakacūrṇaṃ tu māṃ vihāya vineṣyatā \|*  
*pradattaṃ samatikrānte dine 'nyasyāḥ samanmatha \|\| 34 \|\|*

28-34. On one occasion the king in company of his queen in his pleasure garden saw an ant attempting to please his better-half. Being overpowered with the arrows of Cupid, the ant crawled behind its help-mate and said. “Ah! my love! I have not seen a prettier and sweeter form than thine in any of the three regions. See how delicate thy waist is? Both thy thighs resemble the plantain trunk, thy swelling breasts, thy strut of an elephant, thy golden complexion, thy melodious voice resembling that of the cuckoo, thy enchanting smile, thy eyes like lotus, thy tongue that loves the taste of pure sugar, are indeed matchless.

Thou art an ardent devotee of thy husband so much so that thou wilt never breakfast before me, thou wilt always bathe after me, thou art always gloomy during my absence, thou always shiverest when I am in an angry mood, what is the reason of thy turning your face away “from me in anger to-day”? Hearing such a speech of the ant his wife said: “Do not talk like that; you are false tome. I know all thy tricks, yesterday thou feasted another with the particles of sweet.”

## \|\| 20.35-36 \|\|

*pipīlika uvāca*  
*tvatsādṛśyānmayā dattam anyasyai varavarṇini \|*  
*tadekamaparādhaṃ me kṣantumarhasi bhāmini \|\| 35 \|\|*

*naitadevaṃ kariṣyāmi punaḥ kvāpīha suvrate \|*  
*spṛśāmi pādau satyena prasīda praṇatasya me \|\| 36 \|\|*

35-36. The ant said “Dear! I mistook her for you as she resembled you so minutely and through this over sight I feasted her with sweets. This is however my first fault which you should forget and forgive. I shall never repeat such a blunder, I promise this sincerely, be pleased, I fall at your feet."

## \|\| 20.37 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*iti tadvacanaṃ śrutvā sā prasannābhavattataḥ \|*  
*ātmānam arpayāmāsa mohanāya pipīlikā \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Suta said that on hearing the flattering words of her lord, the ant dismissed all her rage and offered herself to him.

## \|\| 20.38 \|\|

*brahmadatto 'pyaśeṣaṃ taṃ jñātvā vismayam āgamat \|*  
*sarvasattvarutajñatvāt prasādāc cakrapāṇinaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. The King Brahmadatta who knew the language of all creatures by the grace of Vishnu, was highly astonished to hear what transpired between the couple.

## Chapter 21

## \|\| 21.1 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ*  
*kathaṃ sattvarutajño 'bhūd brahmadatto dharātale \|*  
*taccābhavatkasya kule cakravākacatuṣṭayam \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. The Rishis asked: — How did the King Brahmadatta acquire the faculty of understanding the language of all creatures and in what family were the other four cranes born?

## \|\| 21.2 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*tasminneva pure jātās te ca cakrāhvayāstadā \|*  
*vṛddhadvijasya dāyādā viprā jātismarāḥ purā \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Suta replied: — They were born in the family of a poor and old Brahmana in the kingdom of Brahmadatta and they had a recollection of their previous lives.

## \|\| 21.3 \|\|

*dhṛtimāṃstattvadarśī ca vidyācaṇḍas tapotsukaḥ \|*  
*nāmataḥ karmataścaite sudaridrasya te sutāḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3 Dhritimana, Tattvadarshi, Vidyachanda and Tapotsuka were the four sons of the poor Brahmana — Sudaridra — and they all had the attributes connoted by their respective names.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — Dhritiman = Steadfast, Tattvadarshi = Philosopher. Vidyachanda = Very learned.

Tapotsuka = eager to practice asceticism.

## \|\| 21.4 \|\|

*tapase buddhirabhavat tadā teṣāṃ dvijanmanām \|*  
*yāsyāmaḥ paramāṃ siddhim ity ūcus te dvijottamāḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. They all determined to acquire emancipation by practising asceticism.

## \|\| 21.5-8 \|\|

*tatastadvacanaṃ śrutvā sudaridro mahātapāḥ \|*  
*uvāca dīnayā vācā kimetaditi putrakāḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*adharma eṣa iti vaḥ pitā tān abhyavārayat \|*  
*vṛddhaṃ pitaramutsṛjya daridraṃ vanavāsinaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*ko nu dharmo 'tra bhavitā mattyāgādgatireva vā \|*  
*ūcuste kalpitā vṛttis tava tāta vadasva tat \|\| 7 \|\|*

*vittametatpuro rājñaḥ sa te dāsyati puṣkalam \|*  
*dhanaṃ grāmasahasrāṇi prabhāte paṭhatastava \|\| 8 \|\|*

5-8. Sudaridra felt very miserable when he came to know of the resolution of his sons and in a very plaintive tone asked them the reason of their doing so. He tried his best to dissuade his sons from doing that and said that to repair to forest leaving an aged father behind in a helpless condition was no virtue, and what would be their fate for doing that act.

Hearing those words of their old and infirm father they said that he should not stand in their way and that God had made ample provision for his subsistence. By reading the following shloka before his king he would get plenty of money and villages.

## \|\| 21.9 \|\|

*ye vipramukhyāḥ kurujāṅgaleṣu dāśāstathā dāśapure mṛgāśca \|*  
*kālañjare sapta ca cakravākā ye mānase te vayamatra siddhāḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. “The seven sons of the Brahmanan in Kurujangala were re-born as the sons of a hunter in Dasapura, again they were re-born as deer on the Kalinjar bills and then again as cranes on the banks of the Manasa lake we are those very same who have now attained final beatitude.

## \|\| 21.10 \|\|

*ityuktvā pitaraṃ jagmus te vanaṃ tapase punaḥ \|*  
*vṛddho 'pi rājabhavanaṃ jagāmātmārthasiddhaye \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Thus addressing their father they departed from him to practice penances in the forest. ‘The father crawled towards the King’s palace in order to get some money from him.

## \|\| 21.11-13 \|\|

*anagho nāma vaibhrājaḥ pāñcālādhipatiḥ purā \|*  
*putrārthī devadeveśaṃ hariṃ nārāyaṇaṃ prabhum \|\| 11 \|\|*

*ārādhayāmāsa vibhuṃ tīvravrataparāyaṇaḥ \|*  
*tataḥ kālena mahatā tuṣṭastasya janārdanaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*varaṃ vṛṇīṣva bhadraṃ te hṛdayenepsitaṃ nṛpa \|*  
*evamuktastu devena vavre sa varamuttamam \|\| 13 \|\|*

11-13. Anagha, the son of Vibhr4ja the valiant sovereign of Panchala adored the God Vishnu with the object of getting an heir. ‘Sometime after, the Lord being pleased with the King’s devotion appeared before him and asked him to seek a boon. On hearing those words of the Lord, the King sought the following boon.

## \|\| 21.14-17 \|\|

*putraṃ me dehi deveśa mahābalaparākramam \|*  
*pāragaṃ sarvaśāstrāṇāṃ dhārmikaṃ yogināṃ param \|\| 14 \|\|*

*sarvasattvarutajñaṃ me dehi yoginamātmajam \|*  
*evamastviti viśvātmā tamāha parameśvaraḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*paṣyatāṃ sarvadevānāṃ tatraivāntaradhīyata \|*  
*tataḥ sa tasya putro 'bhūd brahmadattaḥ pratāpavān \|\| 16 \|\|*

*sarvasattvānukampī ca sarvasattvabalādhikaḥ \|*  
*sarvasattvarutajñaśca sarvasattveśvareśvaraḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

14-17. “Sire, grant me a son who may be powerful, illustrious, dutiful, very well versed in all the shastras and yoga, and who may be conversant with the languages of all the creatures.” The Lord said “Be it so” and vanished then and there. Consequently his son Brahmadatta was so illustrious. He was Sympathetic, valiant, conversant in the languages of all the creatures, the ruler of all the beings.

## \|\| 21.18 \|\|

*ahasattena yogātmā sa pipīlikarāgataḥ \|*  
*yatra tatkīṭamithunaṃ ramamāṇamavasthitam \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Brahmadatta understanding What transpired between the ant and his helpmate, laughed.

## \|\| 21.19-20 \|\|

*tataḥ sā saṃnatirdṛṣṭvā taṃ hasantaṃ suvismitā \|*  
*kimapyāśaṅkya manasā tamapṛcchannareśvaram \|\| 19 \|\|*

*saṃnatiruvāca*  
*akasmādatihāsaste kimarthamabhavannṛpa \|*  
*hāsyahetuṃ na jānāmi yadakāle kṛtaṃ tvayā \|\| 20 \|\|*

19-20. The Queen Sannati seeing his lord laughing apparently without any rhyme or reason asked him the cause of his doing so. She said “Sire, why are you laughing without any reason, will you please explain it to me?”

## \|\| 21.21-23 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*avadadrājaputro 'pi sa pipīlikabhāṣitam \|*  
*rāgavāgbhiḥ samutpannam etaddhāsyaṃ varānane \|\| 21 \|\|*

*na cānyatkāraṇaṃ kiṃcid dhāsyahetau śucismite \|*  
*na sāmanyat tadā devī prāhālīkamidaṃ vacaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*ahamevādya hasitā na jīviṣye tvayādhunā \|*  
*kathaṃ pipīlikālāpaṃ martyo vetti vinā surān \|\| 23 \|\|*

21-23. Suta said that after hearing those words of his consort the king said that the conversation between the ant and his better half made him laugh so much and so suddenly. There was no other reason for his doing so.

The queen said that the explanation was not true, and that he laughed at her. She would give up her life. How could a mortal understand the language of lower beings without being a God?

## \|\| 21.24-26 \|\|

*tasmāttvayāham eveha hasitā kimataḥ param \|*  
*tato niruttaro rājā jijñāsustatpuro hareḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*āsthāya niyamaṃ tasthau saptarātramakalmaṣaḥ \|*  
*svapne prāha hṛṣīkeśaḥ prabhāte paryaṭanpuram \|\| 25 \|\|*

*vṛddhadvijo yastadvākyāt sarvaṃ jñāsyasyaśeṣataḥ \|*  
*ityuktvāntardadhe viṣṇuḥ prabhāte 'tha nṛpaḥ purāt \|\| 26 \|\|*

24-26. “What more disgrace can there be than this.’ Hearing those words of the queen the king became speechless. In order to please the queen the king observed a penance and began to worship Lord Vishnu without tasting any food for a week. The God appeared to him in a dream and said “you will come across an old Brahmana to-morrow in course of your rambles in the town and you must acquaint yourself with everything from him.” Saying that the Lord vanished.

## \|\| 21.27-28 \|\|

*nirgacchanmantrisahitaḥ sabhāryo vṛddhamagrataḥ \|*  
*gadantaṃ vipram āyāntaṃ taṃ vṛddhaṃ saṃdadarśa ha \|\| 27 \|\|*

*brāhmaṇa uvāca*  
*ye vipramukhyāḥ kurujāṅgaleṣu dāśāstathā dāśapure mṛgāśca \|*  
*kālañjare sapta ca cakravākā ye mānase te vayamatra siddhāḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

27-28. In the morning the king in the company of his queen and courtiers came across the old Brahmana in the suburbs of the town. The Brahmana recited the same shloka which his sons had taught him at the time of their departure to the forest.

## \|\| 21.29-31 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*ityākarṇya vacastābhyāṃ sa papāta śucā tataḥ \|*  
*jātismaratvamagamat tau ca mantrivarāv ubhau \|\| 29 \|\|*

*kāmaśāstrapraṇetā ca bābhravyastu subālakaḥ \|*  
*pāñcāla iti lokeṣu viśrutaḥ sarvaśāstravit \|\| 30 \|\|*

*kaṇḍarīko 'pi dharmātmā vedaśāstrapravartakaḥ \|*  
*bhūtvā jātismarau śokāt patitāv agratastadā \|\| 31 \|\|*

29-31. The king along with two of his ministers instantly got the recollection of their previous lives on hearing the shloka and the sovereign fainted and fell on the ground. Subalaka the son of Vabhru and the author of the erotic science and the scholar of all the shastras; Kandarika the propagator of the vedas; getting a recollection of their previous lives fell on the ground in a swoon.

## \|\| 21.32 \|\|

*hā vayaṃ yogavibhraṣṭāḥ kāmataḥ karmabandhanāḥ \|*  
*evaṃ vilapya bahuśas trayaste yogapāragāḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Recovering from their fainting fit, they all three repented of their fate and said “Oh! we have become devoid of Yoga by falling into the snares of desires”.

## \|\| 21.33 \|\|

*vismayācchrāddhamāhātmyam abhinandya punaḥ punaḥ \|*  
*tatastasmai dhanaṃ dattvā prabhūtagrāmasaṃyutam \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Afterwards they extolled the blessings of shraddha and dismissed the Brahmana with presents of money and villages.

## \|\| 21.34-35 \|\|

*visṛjya brāhmaṇaṃ taṃ ca vṛddhaṃ dhanamudānvitam \|*  
*ātmīyaṃ nṛpatiḥ putraṃ nṛpalakṣaṇasaṃyutam \|\| 34 \|\|*

*viṣvaksenābhidhānaṃ tu rājā rājye 'bhyaṣecayat \|*  
*mānase militāḥ sarve tataste yogināṃ varāḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

34-35. On the departure of the Brahmana, the king handed over the reins of the Government to his son Vishvaksena and afterwards left the empire along with his two ministers. They all seven joined one another at the Manasa lake.

## \|\| 21.36-37 \|\|

*brahmadattādayastasmin pitṛsaktā vimatsarāḥ \|*  
*saṃnatiścābhavadbhraṣṭā mayaitatkila kāritam \|\| 36 \|\|*

*rājyatyāgaphalaṃ sarvaṃ yadetad abhilaṣyate \|*  
*tatheti prāha rājā tu punastāmabhinandayan \|\| 37 \|\|*

36-37. Brahmadatta and his brothers the great devotee of the Pitris were very pleased, but Sannati was very sad on the idea of her being the cause of her husband’s abdication and said “Dear! It is owing to me that you have abandoned your mundane empire.”

## \|\| 21.38-39 \|\|

*tvatprasādādidaṃ sarvaṃ mayaitatprāpyate phalam \|*  
*tataste yogamāsthāya sarva eva vanaukasaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

*brahmarandhreṇa paramaṃ padamāpustapobalāt \|*  
*evamāurdhanaṃ vidyāṃ svargaṃ mokṣaṃ sukhāni ca \|\| 39 \|\|*

38-39. The king said “Darling! Indeed it is through thee that we all have liberated ourselves from the bonds of the world.” Thus praising the queen they all after practising yoga attained final beatitude after letting the Jiva-Atma escape from their body through the Brahmarandhra.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — Brahmarandhra an aperture in the crown of the head through which the soul is said to escape on its leaving the body. See the Sacred Books of the Hindus — Vol. XV. — The Yoga Shastra.

## \|\| 21.40 \|\|

*prayacchanti sutānrājyaṃ nṛṇāṃ prītāḥ pitāmahāḥ \|*  
*ya idaṃ pitṛmāhātmyaṃ brahmadattasya ca dvijāḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. The Pitris on becoming pleased thus bestow on their devotees, long life, knowledge, heaven, emancipation, comfort, and empire.

## \|\| 21.41 \|\|

*dvijebhyaḥ śrāvayedyo vā śṛṇotyatha paṭhettu vā \|*  
*kalpakoṭiśataṃ sāgraṃ brahmaloke mahīyate \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. One who relates, reads or listens to the history of the Pitris and king Brahmadatta enjoys pleasures for ages and ages in the Brahmaloka.

## Chapter 22

## \|\| 22.1 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ*  
*kasminkāle ca tacchrāddham anantaphaladaṃ bhavet \|*  
*kasminvāsarabhāge tu śrāddhakṛcchrāddhamācaret \|*  
*tīrtheṣu keṣu ca kṛtaṃ śrāddhaṃ bahuphalaṃ bhavet \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. The Rishis said. — “When does that shraddha give everlasting benefit?

In what parts of the day and at what sacred places should it be performed?”

## \|\| 22.2-3 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*aparāhṇe tu samprāpte abhijidrauhiṇodaye \|*  
*yatkiṃciddīyate tatra tadakṣayamudāhṛtam \|\| 2 \|\|*

*tīrthāni yāni śastāni pitriṇāṃ vallabhāni ca \|*  
*nāmatastāni vakṣyāmi saṃkṣepeṇa dvijottamāḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

2-3. Suta said: — Charity performed a little after midday in the third part of the day in Abhijit or Rohini gives everlasting benefit. I shall enumerate to you in a nutshell the chief holy places that are dear to the Pitris.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — Abhijit is the name of asterism.

## \|\| 22.4-5 \|\|

*pitṛtīrthaṃ gayā nāma sarvatīrthavaraṃ śubham \|*  
*yatrāste devadeveśaḥ svayameva pitāmahaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*tatraiṣā pitṛbhirgītā gāthā bhāgamabhīpsubhiḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. Gaya is the principal Pitritirtha. Lord Brahma Himself resides there and the Pitris anxious for a share in the offerings have sung this story there.

## \|\| 22.6-7 \|\|

*eṣṭavyā bahavaḥ putrā yadyeko 'pi gayāṃ vrajet \|*  
*yajeta vāśvamedhena nīlaṃ vā vṛṣamutsṛjet \|\| 6 \|\|*

*tathā vārāṇasī puṇyā pitriṇāṃ vallabhā sadā \|*  
*yatrāvimuktasāṃnidhyaṃ bhuktimuktiphalapradam \|\| 7 \|\|*

6-7. It is well to wish for a number of sons, hut if even one son goes and performs shraddha there at Gaya, or performs the Ashvamedha sacrifice or sets free a black bull, it is more than ample for the satisfaction of the Pitris. The sacred Varanasi (Benares) which is the abode of Vimaleshvar the giver of Prosperity and Emancipation, is also dear to the Pitris.

## \|\| 22.8-9 \|\|

*pitriṇāṃ vallabhaṃ tadvat puṇyaṃ ca vimaleśvaram \|*  
*pitṛtīrthaṃ prayāgaṃ tu sarvakāmaphalapradam \|\| 8 \|\|*

*vaṭeśvarastu bhagavān mādhavena samanvitaḥ \|*  
*yoganidrāśayastadvat sadā vasati keśavaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

8-9. Prayaga is another Pitritirtha that fulfills the desires of the worshipper. It is the abode of Vateshvar who was located there by Vishnu and Lord Keshava always is lost there in His reveries of yoga.

## \|\| 22.10-11 \|\|

*daśāśvamedhikaṃ puṇyaṃ gaṅgādvāraṃ tathaiva ca \|*  
*nandātha lalitā tadvat tīrthaṃ māyāpurī śubhā \|\| 10 \|\|*

*tathā mitrapadaṃ nāma tataḥ kedāramuttamam \|*  
*gaṅgāsāgaramityāhuḥ sarvatīrthamayaṃ śubham \|\| 11 \|\|*

10-11. Dashashvamedha, Gangadvara, Nanda, Lalita, Mayapuri, Mitrapada, Kedara, Ganga-sagara, are also the sacred places where shraddha should be performed.

## \|\| 22.12 \|\|

*tīrthaṃ brahmasarastadvac chatadrusalile hrade \|*  
*tīrthaṃ tu naimiṣaṃ nāma sarvatīrthaphalapradam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. So is Brahmasara a pool in the Shatadru river and Naimisha the trysting place of all the tirthas, are also very dear to the Pitris.

## \|\| 22.13-16 \|\|

*gaṅgodbhedastu gomatyāṃ yatrodbhūtaḥ sanātanaḥ \|*  
*tathā yajñavarāhastu devadevaśca śūlabhṛt \|\| 13 \|\|*

*yatra tatkāñcanaṃ dvāram aṣṭādaśabhujo haraḥ \|*  
*nemistu haricakrasya śīrṇā yatrābhavatpurā \|\| 14 \|\|*

*tadetannaimiṣāraṇyaṃ sarvatīrthaniṣevitam \|*  
*devadevasya tatrāpi vārāhasya tu darśanam \|\| 15 \|\|*

*yaḥ prayāti sa pūtātmā nārāyaṇapadaṃ vrajet \|*  
*kṛtaśaucaṃ mahāpuṇyaṃ sarvapāpaniṣūdanam \|\| 16 \|\|*

13-16. Gangodbheda, in the Gomati, Varaha-kshetra which is the abode of Mahadeva and the eighteen handed Shiva, the place where the quoit (chakra) of Vishnu fell is Naimisharanya which is the most sacred of all the tirthas and where Lord Varaha is worshipped are all sacred places.

One who goes there is liberated from all his sins and attains emancipation.

## \|\| 22.17 \|\|

*yatrāste nārasiṃhastu svayameva janārdanaḥ \|*  
*tīrthamikṣumatī nāma pitriṇāṃ vallabhaṃ sadā \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Ikshumati tirtha where resides the God Nrisinha is held very dear to the Pitris; it is on the confluence of the Ganges

## \|\| 22.18 \|\|

*saṃgame yatra tiṣṭhanti gaṅgāyāḥ pitaraḥ sadā \|*  
*kurukṣetraṃ mahāpuṇyaṃ sarvatīrthasamanvitam \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Kurukshetra is another most sacred place where all the Pitris are always present

## \|\| 22.19-20 \|\|

*tathā ca sarayūḥ puṇyā sarvadevanamaskṛtā \|*  
*irāvatī nadī tadvat pitṛtīrthādhivāsinī \|\| 19 \|\|*

*yamunā devikā kālī candrabhāgā dṛṣadvatī \|*  
*nadī veṇumatī puṇyā parā vetravatī tathā \|\| 20 \|\|*

19-20. The river Sharayu venerated by all the Devas is holy and so is the sacred Irawati, the rivers Yamuna, Devika, Kali, Chandrabhaga, Drishadvati, Venumati, Vetravati are sacred and dear to the Pitris, and shraddha performed on their banks confers great benefits on the worshipper.

## \|\| 22.21-23 \|\|

*pitriṇāṃ vallabhā hy etāḥ śrāddhe koṭiguṇā matāḥ \|*  
*jambūmārgaṃ mahāpuṇyaṃ yatra mārgo hi lakṣyate \|\| 21 \|\|*

*adyāpi pitṛtīrthaṃ tat sarvakāmaphalapradam \|*  
*nīlakuṇḍamiti khyātaṃ pitṛtīrthaṃ dvijottamāḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*tathā rudrasaraḥ puṇyaṃ saro mānasameva ca \|*  
*mandākinī tathācchodā vipāśātha sarasvatī \|*  
*pūrvamitrapadaṃ tadvad vaidyanāthaṃ mahāphalam \|*  
*kṣiprā nadī mahākālas tathā kālañjaraṃ śubham \|\| 23 \|\|*

21-23. Jambumarga whence the path of the Pitris is visible is a Pitritirtha unto this day. The Pitritirtha Nilakunda, Rudrasarovara, Mansarovara, Mandakini, Achchhoda, Vipasha, Sarasvati are also sacred tirthas.

## \|\| 22.24 \|\|

*vaṃśodbhedaṃ harodbhedaṃ gaṅgodbhedaṃ mahāphalam \|*  
*bhadreśvaraṃ viṣṇupadaṃ narmadādvārameva ca \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Purvamitrapada, Vaidyanatha, the river Kshipra, Mahakala, Kalinjarahill are also very sacred places.

## \|\| 22.25-26 \|\|

*gayāpiṇḍapradānena samānyāhurmaharṣayaḥ \|*  
*etāni pitṛtīrthāni sarvapāpaharāṇi ca \|\| 25 \|\|*

*smaraṇādapi lokānāṃ kim u śrāddhakṛtāṃ nṛṇām \|*  
*oṃkāraṃ pitṛtīrthaṃ ca kāverī kapilodakam \|\| 26 \|\|*

25-26. Vanshodbheda, Harodbheda, Gangodbheda, are among the sacred places and so are Bhadreshvara, Vishnupada, Narmadadwara, Offering Pinda there is equivalent to offering it in Gaya. These are the Pitritirthas that wash off all the sins of man.

## \|\| 22.27-48 \|\|

*sambhedaś caṇḍavegāyās tathaivāmarakaṇṭakam \|*  
*kurukṣetrācchataguṇaṃ tasminsnānādikaṃ bhavet \|\| 27 \|\|*

*śukratīrthaṃ ca vikhyātaṃ tīrthaṃ someśvaraṃ param \|*  
*sarvavyādhiharaṃ puṇyaṃ śatakoṭiphalādhikam \|\| 28 \|\|*

*śrāddhe dāne tathā home svādhyāye jalasaṃnidhau \|*  
*kāyāvarohaṇaṃ nāma tathā carmaṇvatī nadī \|\| 29 \|\|*

*gomatī varaṇā tadvat tīrthamauśanasaṃ param \|*  
*bhairavaṃ bhṛgutuṅgaṃ ca gaurītīrthamanuttamam \|\| 30 \|\|*

*tīrthaṃ vaināyakaṃ nāma bhadreśvaramataḥ param \|*  
*tathā pāpaharaṃ nāma puṇyātha tapatī nadī \|\| 31 \|\|*

*mūlatāpī payoṣṇī ca payoṣṇīsaṃgamastathā \|*  
*mahābodhiḥ pāṭalā ca nāgatīrthamavantikā \|\| 32 \|\|*

*tathā veṇā nadī puṇyā mahāśālaṃ tathaiva ca \|*  
*mahārudraṃ mahāliṅgaṃ daśārṇā ca nadī śubhā \|\| 33 \|\|*

*śatarudrā śatāhvā ca tathā viśvapadaṃ param \|*  
*aṅgāravāhikā tadvan nadau tau śoṇaghargharau \|\| 34 \|\|*

*kālikā ca nadī puṇyā vitastā ca nadī tathā \|*  
*etāni pitṛtīrthāni śasyante snānadānayoḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

*śrāddhameteṣu yaddattaṃ tadanantaphalaṃ smṛtam \|*  
*droṇī vāṭanadī dhārā saritkṣīranadī tathā \|\| 36 \|\|*

*gokarṇaṃ gajakarṇaṃ ca tathā ca puruṣottamaḥ \|*  
*dvārakā kṛṣṇatīrthaṃ ca tathārbudasarasvatī \|\| 37 \|\|*

*nadī maṇimatī nāma tathā ca girikarṇikā \|*  
*dhūtapāpaṃ tathā tīrthaṃ samudro dakṣiṇastathā \|\| 38 \|\|*

*eteṣu pitṛtīrtheṣu śrāddhamānantyamaśnute \|*  
*tīrthaṃ meghakaraṃ nāma svayameva janārdanaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

*yatra śārṅgadharo viṣṇur mekhalāyāmavasthitaḥ \|*  
*tathā mandodarītīrthaṃ tīrthaṃ campā nadī śubhā \|\| 40 \|\|*

*tathā sāmalanāthaśca mahāśālanadī tathā \|*  
*cakravākaṃ carmakoṭaṃ tathā janmeśvaraṃ mahat \|\| 41 \|\|*

*arjunaṃ tripuraṃ caiva siddheśvaramataḥ param \|*  
*śrīśailaṃ śāṃkaraṃ tīrthaṃ nārasiṃhamataḥ param \|\| 42 \|\|*

*mahendraṃ ca tathā puṇyam atha śrīraṅgasaṃjñitam \|*  
*eteṣvapi sadā śrāddham anantaphaladaṃ smṛtam \|\| 43 \|\|*

*darśanādapi caitāni sadyaḥ pāpaharāṇi vai \|*  
*tuṅgabhadrā nadī puṇyā tathā bhīmarathī sarit \|\| 44 \|\|*

*bhīmeśvaraṃ kṛṣṇaveṇā kāverī kuḍmalā nadī \|*  
*nadī godāvarī nāma trisaṃdhyā tīrthamuttamam \|\| 45 \|\|*

*tīrthaṃ traiyambakaṃ nāma sarvatīrthanamaskṛtam \|*  
*yatrāste bhagavānīśaḥ svayameva trilocanaḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

*śrāddhameteṣu sarveṣu koṭikoṭiguṇaṃ bhavet \|*  
*smaraṇādapi pāpāni naṣyanti śatadhā dvijāḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

*śrīparṇī tāmraparṇī ca jayā tīrthamanuttamam \|*  
*tathā matsyanadī puṇyā śivadhāraṃ tathaiva ca \|\| 48 \|\|*

27-48. The: mere recollection of these sacred places gives great benefit; what to say of those who perform shraddha there. Omkara, Kaveri, Kapilodaka, the confluence of the river Chandavega, Amarkantaka are also sacred places where by bathing one gets hundred times more benefit than by bathing at Kurukshetra. Shukratirtha, Pindara, Someshvar are the sacred places that dispel all impediments and it is very pious to perform shraddha or give charity there. Kayavarohana, Charmanvati river, Gomati, Varana, Aushanas, Bhairavakshetra, Bhrigutunga, Gauritirtha, are also holy places. Vainayaka, Bhadreshvara are the holy places that release one from sins and so also Tapti river is sacred. Mulatapi, Payoshni, and her confluence Mahabodhi, Patala, Nagatirtha, Avanti, Mahashala, river Vena, Maharudra, Mahalinga, river Dasharna, Shatarudra, Shatahva river, Vishvapada, the river Ningarvahika, Shona river, Ghaghara river, Kalika river, Vitasta river, Droni river, Vata river, Dhara, Kshira river, are also the places where shraddha being performed gives great satisfaction to the Pitris. Gokarna, Gajakarna, Purushottama, Dwarika, Arvuda, Sarasvati river are among the holy places. The rivers Manimati, Girikarnika, Dhutapapam, the southern ocean, Meghakara tirtha which is the abode of Janardana and Vishnu, Mandodari tirtha, the river Champ, Samalnatha, Mahashal river, Chakravaka, Charmakota tirtha, Janmeshvara, Arjunakshetra, Tripuratirtha, Sidheshvara, Shrishaila, Narasinha, are also the places fit for performing shraddha for the satisfaction of the Pitris. Mahendra, Shriranga are the places where Shraddha should be performed. They are so sacred as to free one from sins merely by going there. The rivers Tungabhadra and Bhimarathi, Bhimeshvar, Krishna Vena, the rivers Kaveri, Kudmala and Godavari, Trisandhya tirtha, Traiyamvaka the abode of Shiva and which is universally venerated, are very holy places.

A mere recollection of these holy places dispels all sins and the performance of shraddha there gives unbounded satisfaction to the Pitris.

## \|\| 22.49-61 \|\|

*bhadratīrthaṃ ca vikhyātaṃ pampātīrthaṃ ca śāśvatam \|*  
*puṇyaṃ rāmeśvaraṃ tadvad elāpuramalaṃ puram \|\| 49 \|\|*

*aṅgabhūtaṃ ca vikhyātam āmardakam alambhuṣam \|*  
*āmrātakeśvaraṃ tadvad ekāmbhakamataḥ param \|\| 50 \|\|*

*govardhanaṃ hariścandraṃ kṛpucandraṃ pṛthūdakam \|*  
*sahasrākṣaṃ hiraṇyākṣaṃ tathā ca kadalī nadī \|\| 51 \|\|*

*rāmādhivāsastatrāpi tathā saumitrisaṃgamaḥ \|*  
*indrakīlaṃ mahānādaṃ tathā ca priyamelakam \|\| 52 \|\|*

*etānyapi sadā śrāddhe praśastānyadhikāni tu \|*  
*eteṣu sarvadevānāṃ sāṃnidhyaṃ dṛṣyate yataḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

*dānameteṣu sarveṣu dattaṃ koṭiśatādhikam \|*  
*bāhudā ca nadīpuṇyā tathā siddhavanaṃ śubham \|\| 54 \|\|*

*tīrthaṃ pāśupataṃ nāma nadī pārvatikā śubhā \|*  
*śrāddhameteṣu sarveṣu dattaṃ koṭiśatottaram \|\| 55 \|\|*

*tathaiva pitṛtīrthaṃ tu yatra godāvarī nadī \|*  
*yutā liṅgasahasreṇa sarvāntarajalāvahā \|\| 56 \|\|*

*jāmadagnyasya tattīrthaṃ kramādāyātamuttamam \|*  
*pratīkasya bhayādbhinnaṃ yatra godāvarī nadī \|\| 57 \|\|*

*tattīrthaṃ havyakavyānām apsaroyugasaṃjñitam \|*  
*śrāddhāgnikāryadāneṣu tathā koṭiśatādhikam \|\| 58 \|\|*

*tathā sahasraliṅgaṃ ca rāghaveśvaramuttamam \|*  
*sendraphenā nadī puṇyā yatrendraḥ patitaḥ purā \|\| 59 \|\|*

*nihatya namuciṃ śakras tapasā svargamāptavān \|*  
*tatra dattaṃ naraiḥ śrāddham anantaphaladaṃ bhavet \|\| 60 \|\|*

*tīrthaṃ tu puṣkaraṃ nāma śālagrāmaṃ tathaiva ca \|*  
*somapānaṃ ca vikhyātaṃ yatra vaiśvānarālayam \|\| 61 \|\|*

49-61. The rivers Shriparni and Tamraparni, Jayatirtha, the sacred river Matsya, Shivadhar tirtha, Bhadra, the river Pampa, Rameshvara, Elapura, Alampura, Angabhata, Anandakamala, Budha, Amratikeshvara, Ekambhaka, Govardhana, Harishchandra, Kripuchandra, Prithudaka, Sahasraksha, Hiranyaksha, the river Kadali the abode of Rama, Saumitri Sangama, Indrakila, Mahanada, Elakkshetra, are very sacred places owing to the abode of gods and shraddha performed there highly satisfies the Pitris.

The sacred Bahu river, Siddhavana, Pashupata, the river Parvatika, are the places where the performance of shraddha is many times more beneficial. Pitritirtha near the Godavari river which teems with myriads of images of Shiva is an exceedingly sacred place. It is also known as Jamadagni tirtha. It is there that the river Godavari has become ruptured through the fear of Pratika Rishi. It is both Deva as well as Pitri tirtha and is also known under the name of Apsaroyuga.

There the performance of shraddha, Agnihotra and charity is held millions of times more sacred. Sahasralinga, Raghaveshvara the river Indraphena where Indra had His downfall and where He after destroying the demon Namuchi went to Heaven by the practice of penances, are the places where the performance of shraddha by men bears everlasting fruit. Pushkara, Saligrama, so also Somapana, the home of Vaishwanara are Sacred tirthas.

## \|\| 22.62-78 \|\|

*tīrthaṃ sārasvataṃ nāma svāmitīrthaṃ tathaiva ca \|*  
*malaṃdarā nadī puṇyā kauśikī candrikā tathā \|\| 62 \|\|*

*vaidarbhā vātha vairā ca payoṣṇī prāṅmukhā parā \|*  
*kāverī cottarā puṇyā tathā jālaṃdharo giriḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

*eteṣu śrāddhatīrtheṣu śrāddhamānantyamaśnute \|*  
*lohadaṇḍaṃ tathā tīrthaṃ citrakūṭastathaiva ca \|\| 64 \|\|*

*vindhyayogaśca gaṅgāyās tathā nadītaṭaṃ śubham \|*  
*kubjābhraṃ tu tathā tīrtham urvaśīpulinaṃ tathā \|\| 65 \|\|*

*saṃsāramocanaṃ tīrthaṃ tathaiva ṛṇamocanam \|*  
*eteṣu pitṛtīrtheṣu śrāddham ānantyamaśnute \|\| 66 \|\|*

*aṭṭahāsaṃ tathā tīrthaṃ gautameśvarameva ca \|*  
*tathā vasiṣṭhatīrthaṃ nu hārītaṃ tu tataḥ param \|\| 67 \|\|*

*brahmāvartaṃ kuśāvartaṃ hayatīrthaṃ tathaiva ca \|*  
*piṇḍārakaṃ ca vikhyātaṃ śaṅkhoddhāraṃ tathaiva ca \|\| 68 \|\|*

*ghaṇṭeśvaraṃ bilvakaṃ ca nīlaparvatameva ca \|*  
*tathā ca dharaṇītīrthaṃ rāmatīrthaṃ tathaiva ca \|\| 69 \|\|*

*aśvatīrthaṃ ca vikhyātam anantaṃ śrāddhadānayoḥ \|*  
*tīrthaṃ vedaśiro nāma tathaivaughavatī nadī \|\| 70 \|\|*

*tīrthaṃ vasupradaṃ nāma chāgalāṇḍaṃ tathaiva ca \|*  
*eteṣu śrāddhadātāraḥ prayānti paramaṃ padam \|\| 71 \|\|*

*tathāca badarītīrthaṃ gaṇatīrthaṃ tathaiva ca \|*  
*jayantaṃ vijayaṃ caiva śakratīrthaṃ tathaiva ca \|\| 72 \|\|*

*śrīpateśca tathā tīrthaṃ tīrthaṃ raivatakaṃ tathā \|*  
*tathaiva śāradātīrthaṃ bhadrakāleśvaraṃ tathā \|\| 73 \|\|*

*vaikuṇṭhatīrthaṃ ca paraṃ bhīmeśvaramathāpi vā \|*  
*eteṣu śrāddhadātāraḥ prayānti paramāṃ gatim \|\| 74 \|\|*

*tīrthaṃ mātṛgṛhaṃ nāma karavīrapuraṃ tathā \|*  
*kuśeśayaṃ ca vikhyātaṃ gaurīśikharameva ca \|\| 75 \|\|*

*nakuleśasya tīrthaṃ ca kardamālaṃ tathaiva ca \|*  
*diṇḍipuṇyakaraṃ tadvat puṇḍarīkapuraṃ tathā \|\| 76 \|\|*

*saptagodāvarītīrthaṃ sarvatīrtheśvareśvaram \|*  
*tatra śrāddhaṃ pradātavyam anantaphalamīpsubhiḥ \|\| 77 \|\|*

*eṣa tūddeśataḥ proktas tīrthānāṃ saṃgraho mayā \|*  
*vāgīśo 'pi na śaknoti vistarāt kim u mānuṣaḥ \|\| 78 \|\|*

62-78. Sarasvata, Swami, the river Malandara, Jalandhara, Mount Lohadanda, Kaushiki river, the river Chandrika, the river Vaidarbha, Vaira, the river Payoshni, Prangmukha river, the Kaveri, Chitrakuta, Vindhyachala.

Kubjabhra, the banks of the Urvashi river, Samsaramochana, Rinamochana, Attahasa Gautameshvara, Vasistha, Harita, Brahmavarta, Kushavarta, Haya, Pindaraka, Shankhodhara, Ghanteshvara, Vilvakeshvara, Nilkeshvara, Dharanidhara, Ramtirtha, Ashva, Vedashira, Aughavati river, Vasuprada, Chaglanda, Badari, Gana, Jayant, Vijayashakra tirtha, Shripati, Raivata, Sharada, Bhadrakaleshvara, Vaikuntha, Bhimeshvara, Mahadeva, Matrigraha, Karavirapura, Kusheshaya, Gaurishikhara, Nakulesha, Kardamala, Dindi, Pundarikapura, Godavari the abode of Tirtheshvara, are the places where by performing shraddha one gives complete satisfaction to the Pitris and paves the way for the attainment of final beatitude.

## \|\| 22.79 \|\|

*satyaṃ tīrthaṃ dayā tīrthaṃ tīrthamindriyanigrahaḥ \|*  
*varṇāśramāṇāṃ gehe 'pi tīrthaṃ tu samudāhṛtam \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. I have enumerated to you the names of the Tirthas very briefly. Even Brihaspati cannot adequately describe their glory what to say of a man.

## \|\| 22.80 \|\|

*etattīrtheṣu yacchrāddhaṃ tatkoṭiguṇamiṣyate \|*  
*yasmāttasmātprayatnena tīrthe śrāddhaṃ samācaret \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. Satya tirtha (observance of truth), Daya tirtha ‘performance of charity), Indriyanigraha (control of passions) should be considered as tirthas even by those who cannot leave their homes for purposes of pilgrimage

## \|\| 22.81 \|\|

*prātaḥkālo muhūrtāṃs trīn saṃgavas tāvadeva tu \|*  
*madhyāhnastrimuhūrtaḥ syād aparāhṇastataḥ param \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. Shraddba performed at these place is millions of times more sacred. One should therefore perform shraddha with devotion and according to the rules laid down, at these holy places.

## \|\| 22.82-84 \|\|

*sāyāhnastrimuhūrtaḥ syāc chrāddhaṃ tatra na kārayet \|*  
*rākṣasī nāma sā velā garhitā sarvakarmasu \|\| 82 \|\|*

*ahno muhūrtā vikhyātā daśa pañca ca sarvadā \|*  
*tatrāṣṭamo muhūrto yaḥ sa kālaḥ kutapaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 83 \|\|*

*madhyāhne sarvadā yasmān mandībhavati bhāskaraḥ \|*  
*tasmādanantaphaladas tadārambho viśiṣyate \|\| 84 \|\|*

82-84. The three morning muhurtas are called sangava, the three muhurtas in the midday and afternoon are uttama, the evening muhurta which should be avoided, or shraddha is Rakshasi. There are fifteen muhurtas in the day and the 8th of them is called the kutupa.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — Muhurta — A period of 48 minutes.

## \|\| 22.85 \|\|

*madhyāhnaḥ khaḍgapātraṃ ca tathā nepālakambalaḥ \|*  
*rūpyaṃ darbhāstilā gāvo dauhitraścāṣṭamaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. In the noon the movement of the sun becomes slow therefore it is best to perform shraddha at that time.

## \|\| 22.86-87 \|\|

*pāpaṃ kutsitamityāhus tasya saṃtāpakāriṇaḥ \|*  
*aṣṭāv ete yatastasmāt kutapā iti viśrutāḥ \|\| 86 \|\|*

*ūrdhvaṃ muhūrtātkutapād yanmuhūrtacatuṣṭayam \|*  
*muhūrtapañcakaṃ caitat svadhābhavanamiṣyate \|\| 87 \|\|*

86-87. The hour of midday, a vessel of rhinoceros horn, a Nepal blanket, silver, Darbha grass, sesamum, kine, and a daughter's son, are the eight essentials of a shraddha. Kuts it is another synonym of Papa (sin) and the eight things enumerated above consume (tapa) all sin (ku), therefore they are known as kutupas.

## \|\| 22.88 \|\|

*viṣṇor dehasamudbhūtāḥ kuśāḥ kṛṣṇāstilāstathā \|*  
*śrāddhasya rakṣaṇāyālam etatprāhurdivaukasaḥ \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. The nine muhurtas after the kutupa muhurta are known as Svadha.

## \|\| 22.89-90 \|\|

*tilodakāñjalirdeyo jalasthaistīrthavāsibhiḥ \|*  
*sadarbhahastenaikena śrāddhamevaṃ viśiṣyate \|\| 89 \|\|*

*śrāddhasādhanakāle tu pāṇinaikena dīyate \|*  
*tarpaṇaṃ tūbhayenaiva vidhireṣa sadā smṛtaḥ \|\| 90 \|\|*

89-90. Kusha and black sesamum were produced from the body of Vishnu, that is why they are necessarily employed in the performance of shraddha.

The devas have also said that a handful of water mixed with sesamum and offered by the residents of a sacred place by holding kusha in one hand is also a kind of shraddha.

## \|\| 22.91 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*puṇyaṃ pavitramāuṣyaṃ sarvapāpavināśanam \|*  
*purā malaye na kathitaṃ tīrthaśrāddhānukīrtanam \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. Shraddha should be performed with one hand only but Tarpana with both hands.

## \|\| 22.92 \|\|

*śṛṇoti yaḥ paṭhedvāpi śrīmānsaṃjāyate naraḥ \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. Suta said that the performance of shraddha in a holy place gives long life and washes off all sins, this has been said by the Lord Matsya

## \|\| 22.93 \|\|

*śrāddhakāle ca vaktavyaṃ tathā tīrthanivāsibhiḥ \|*  
*sarvapāpopaśāntyartham alakṣmīnāśanaṃ param \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. One should recite it at the time of shraddha one who reads it or hears it becomes wealthy, consequently the residents of a holy place should recite it to dispel all their sins.

## \|\| 22.94 \|\|

*idaṃ pavitraṃ yaśaso nidhānam idaṃ mahāpāpaharaṃ ca puṃsām \|*  
*brahmārkarudrairapi pūjitaṃ ca śrāddhasya māhātmyamuśanti tadjñāḥ \|\| 94 \|\|*

94\. This shraddha mahatmya is the dispeller of all sins and it is venerated by Shiva, Brahma and the God sun.

## Chapter 23

## \|\| 23.1 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ*  
*somaḥ pitriṇāmadhipaḥ kathaṃ śāstraviśārada \|*  
*tadvaṃśyā ye ca rājāno babhūvuḥ kīrtivardhanāḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. The Rishis said: How did the moon O! scholar of all the Shastras, become the sovereign of the Pitris and how did the Rajas of the lunar dynasty become so illustrious?

## \|\| 23.2 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*ādiṣṭo brahmaṇā pūrvam atriḥ sargavidhau purā \|*  
*anuttamaṃ nāma tapaḥ sṛṣṭyarthaṃ taptavānprabhuḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Suta said: — At the time of the first creation, the sage Atri as desired by Brahma practiced austerities for the purpose of creation.

## \|\| 23.3-6 \|\|

*yadānandakaraṃ brahma jagatkleśavināśanam \|*  
*brahmaviṣṇvarkarudrāṇām abhyantaramatīndriyam \|\| 3 \|\|*

*śāntikṛc chāntamanasas tadantarnayane sthitam \|*  
*māhātmyāttapasā viprāḥ paramānandakārakam \|\| 4 \|\|*

*yasmādumāpatiḥ sārdham umayā tamadhiṣṭhitaḥ \|*  
*taṃ dṛṣṭvā cāṣṭamāṃśena tasmātsomo 'bhavacchiśuḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*adhaḥ susrāva netrābhyāṃ dhāma taccāmbusambhavam \|*  
*dīpayanviśvamakhilaṃ jyotsnayā sacarācaram \|\| 6 \|\|*

3-6. The Blissful Brahma, the dispeller of all troubles of the world and who is enshrined within Vishnu, Shiva, and the sun Rudra and who is supersensuous and is the giver of all peace and who is enthroned in the eyes of peaceful beings; the same Brahma becoming pleased with the austerities of Atri was the cause of his happiness, in other words, He caused the moon to be produced from the eyes of Atri. At that time Lord Shiva with His Consort the goddess Parvati became highly pleased to see the moon and decorated His head with It; and the power prod aced from the water and emitted from the eyes of Atri illumined the universe with Its lustre.

## \|\| 23.7-10 \|\|

*taddiśo jagṛhurdhāma strīrūpeṇa sutecchayā \|*  
*garbho bhūtvodare tāsām āsthito 'bdaśatatrayam \|\| 7 \|\|*

*āśāstaṃ mumucurgarbham aśaktā dhāraṇe tataḥ \|*  
*samādāyātha taṃ garbham ekīkṛtya caturmukhaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*yuvānamakarodbrahmā sarvāudhadharaṃ naram \|*  
*syandane 'tha sahasrāśve vedaśaktimaye prabhuḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*āropya lokamanayad ātmīyaṃ sa pitāmaha \|*  
*tatra brahmarṣibhiḥ proktam asmatsvāmī bhavatvayam \|\| 10 \|\|*

7-10. All the directions anxious to beget progeny absorbed that lustre in the form of damsels and then it remained in their womb for three hundred - years. After that period the directions could not bear the power in their womb and so they ejected it. Brahma collected it together and created an illustrious Being bedecked with all the arms. He then gave him vedic powers and seated Him on a chariot drawn by a thousand horses and thus took Him to His region where seeing Him all the Brahma-Rishis acknowledged Him as their Sovereign Lord.

## \|\| 23.11 \|\|

*ṛṣibhirdevagandharvair oṣadhībhistathaiva ca \|*  
*tuṣṭuvuḥ somadevatyair brahmādyā mantrasaṃgrahaiḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Afterwards the Pitris, Devas, Gandharvas, herbs along with the God Indra began to adore Brahma by reciting the Somadeva mantras.

## \|\| 23.12-13 \|\|

*stūyamānasya tasyābhūd adhiko dhāmasambhavaḥ \|*  
*tejovitānādabhavad bhuvi divyauṣadhīgaṇaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*taddīptiradhikā tasmād rātrau bhavati sarvadā \|*  
*tenauṣadhīśaḥ somo 'bhūd dvijeśaścāpi gadyate \|\| 13 \|\|*

12-13. Then by the Yogic glory of the Lord Brahma, that, became still more illustrious and merged into the moon. By Its lustre the herbs in the world profusely thrived and the moon became much more radiant in the night and consequently it (the moon) came to be the sovereign of the herbs and the Brahmanas.

## \|\| 23.14 \|\|

*vedadhāmarasaṃ cāpi yadidaṃ candramaṇḍalam \|*  
*kṣīyate vardhate caiva śukle kṛṣṇe ca sarvadā \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. This disc of the moon is the resort of the Vedas and the nectar. It waxes in the bright fortnight and wanes in the dark fortnight

## \|\| 23.15-19 \|\|

*viṃśatiṃ ca tathā sapta dakṣaḥ prācetaso dadau \|*  
*rūpalāvaṇyasaṃyuktās tasmai kanyāḥ suvarcasaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*tataḥ padmasahasrāṇāṃ sahasrāṇi daśaiva tu \|*  
*tapaścacāra śītāṃśur viṣṇudhyānaikatatparaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*tatastuṣṭastu bhagavāṃs tasmai nārāyaṇo hariḥ \|*  
*varaṃ vṛṇīṣva provāca paramātmā janārdanaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*tato vavre varānsomaḥ śakralokaṃ jayāmyaham \|*  
*pratyakṣameva bhoktāro bhavantu mama mandire \|\| 18 \|\|*

*rājasūye suragaṇā brahmādyāḥ santu me dvijāḥ \|*  
*rakṣaḥpālaḥ śivo 'smākam āstāṃ śūladharo haraḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

15-19. In the days gone by Daksha Prajapati son of Prachetas gave his twenty seven beautiful daughters to the moon. The moon to please Lord Vishnu practiced austerities for a considerable length of time. The Lord became pleased with his devotion and directed Him to ask for a boon.

The moon wished, that he might conquer the realm of Indra, the Devas might go to His region and officiate as Brahman as in His Rajasuya sacrifice, and Lord Shiva might protect it (sacrifice,) with his trident standing at his door.

## \|\| 23.20-21 \|\|

*tathetyuktaḥ sa ājahre rājasūyaṃ tu viṣṇunā \|*  
*hotātrir bhṛguradhvaryur udgātābhūccaturmukhaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*brahmatvamagamattasya upadraṣṭā hariḥ svayam \|*  
*sadasyāḥ sanakādyāstu rājasūyavidhau smṛtāḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

20-21. On Vishnu’s granting this boon, the moon performed. the Rajasuya sacrifice in which the sage Atri became the Hot a priest, Bhrigu officiated as Adhvaryu, Brahma was the Udgata, Lord Hari officiated as Brahmana priest, and the Sages Shaunaka, &c. were the Sadasyas in that Rajasuya sacrifice.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — Adhvaryu — An officiating priest whose duty is to measure the ground,’ build the altar, prepare sacrificial vessels, fetch wood and water, light the fire, bring the animal and immolate it and while doing this to repeat the Yajurveda.

\*Udgata — one of the priests at the sacrifice who chants the Samaveda.

## \|\| 23.22 \|\|

*camasādhvaryavastatra viśve devā daśaiva tu \|*  
*trailokyaṃ dakṣiṇā tena ṛtvigbhyaḥ pratipāditam \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Hota’s function was.to recite Rigveda and he was also the Chief priest, while Brahma priest superintended the others and was in charge of the Atharvaveda.

The ten Vishvadevas officiated as chamasa-adhvaryu. In that sacrifice the moon gave the three lokas as Dakshina to the sacrificial priests.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — Chamasa — A vessel used at sacrifices for drinking the Soma juice.

## \|\| 23.23 \|\|

*tataḥ samāpte 'vabhṛthe tadrūpālokanecchavaḥ \|*  
*kāmabāṇābhitaptāṅgyo nava devyaḥ siṣevire \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. On the conclusion of that sacrificial bath, the nine goddesses fired with love went to have a look at the moon.

## \|\| 23.24-28 \|\|

*lakṣmīrnārāyaṇaṃ tyaktvā sinīvālī ca kardamam \|*  
*dyutirvibhāvasuṃ tadvat tuṣṭirdhātāramavyayam \|\| 24 \|\|*

*prabhā prabhākaraṃ tyaktvā haviṣmantaṃ kuhūḥ svayam \|*  
*kīrtirjayantaṃ bhartāraṃ vasurmārīcakaṣyapam \|\| 25 \|\|*

*dhṛtis tyaktvā pītaṃ nandiṃ somamevābhajaṃstadā \|*  
*svakīyā iva somo 'pi kāmayāmāsa tāstadā \|\| 26 \|\|*

*evaṃ kṛtāpacārasya tāsāṃ bhartṛgaṇastadā \|*  
*na śaśākāpacārāya śāpaiḥ śastrādibhiḥ punaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

*tathāpyarājata vidhur daśadhā bhāvayandiśaḥ \|*  
*somaḥ prāpyātha duṣprāpyam aiśvaryamṛṣisaṃskṛtam \|*  
*saptalokaikanāthatvam avāpa tapasā tadā \|\| 28 \|\|*

24-28. Lakshmi went after leaving Narayana, Sinivali went after leaving Kardama, Dyuti went after forsaking Vibhavasu, Tushti went after leaving Dhatara, Prabha went after leaving the Sun, Kula went after leaving Havishman, Kirti went after leaving Jayanti, Vasu went after leaving Marichi Kashyapa, Dhriti went after leaving her husband Nandi. All those goddesses went and adorned the Moon. The Moon also looked upon them as His own wives. Their Lords even seeing them go astray like that did not use their missile of curse against the Moon. The Iuminous Moon shed its light on all directions and became the sole Monarch of the seven worlds owing to His Yogic powers, even after attaining such a store of happiness which is envied by sages

## \|\| 23.29-34 \|\|

*kadācidudyānagatāmapaṣyad anekapuṣpābharaṇaiśca śobhitām \|*  
*bṛhannitambastanabhārakhedāt puṣpasya bhaṅge 'pyatidurbalāṅgīm \|\| 29 \|\|*

*bhāryāṃ ca tāṃ devaguror anaṅga bāṇābhirāmāyatacārunetrām \|*  
*tārāṃ sa tārādhipatiḥ smarārtaḥ keśeṣu jagrāha viviktabhūmau \|\| 30 \|\|*

*sāpi smarārtā saha tena reme tadrūpakāntyā hṛtamānasena \|*  
*ciraṃ vihṛtyātha jagāma tārāṃ vidhurgṛhītvā svagṛhaṃ tato 'pi \|\| 31 \|\|*

*na tṛptirāsīcca gṛhe 'pi tasya tārānuraktasya sukhāgameṣu \|*  
*bṛhaspatis tadvirahāgnidagdhas taddhyānaniṣṭhaikamanā babhūva \|\| 32 \|\|*

*śaśāka śāpaṃ na ca dātum asmai na mantraśastrāgniviṣairaśeṣaiḥ \|*  
*tasyāpakartuṃ vividhairupāyair naivābhicārairapi vāgadhīśaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

*sa yācayāmāsa tatastu dainyāt somaṃ svabhāryārthamanaṅgataptaḥ \|*  
*sa yācyamāno 'pi dadau na tārāṃ bṛhaspatestatsukhapāśabaddhaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

29-34. Once upon a time the Moon came across Tara, the wile of Brihaspati whilst she was roaming in the garden. On seeing Tara adorned with flowers, having projected breasts and too delicate to cull a flower even, the Moon was fired with passion. He approached that figure of exquisite beauty whose eyes were so lovely, and caught her by the hair. Tara also seeing the enchanting form of the moon was fired with passion and enjoyed herself in his company. The Moon enjoyed in her company for a very long time and then took her to his realm. The Moon became: so enamored of her that he did not feel sufficiently satisfied even after enjoying himself in her company for such a long time. Brihaspati was pining away for Tara during her absence. He came to know all about her through meditation, but could not overcome the Moon by curses, incantations, arms, fire, poison. Then Brihaspati burning with passion went to the Moon and very humbly besought him to restore him his wife. The Moon who was much attached to Tara refused to do so.

## \|\| 23.35-37 \|\|

*maheśvareṇātha caturmukheṇa sādhyair marudbhiḥ saha lokapālaiḥ \|*  
*dadau yadā tāṃ na kathaṃcid indus tadā śivaḥ krodhaparo babhūva \|\| 35 \|\|*

*yo vāmadevaḥ prathitaḥ pṛthivyām anekarudrārcitapādapadmaḥ \|*  
*tataḥ saśiṣyo giriśaḥ pinākī bṛhaspatisnehavaśānubaddhaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

*dhanurgṛhītvājagavaṃ purārir jagāma bhūteśvarasiddhajuṣṭaḥ \|*  
*yuddhāya somena viśeṣadīpta-tṛtīyanetrānalabhīmavaktraḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

35-37. Afterwards the moon refused the similar request even of Shiva, Brahma, Sadhya Devas, the Maruts, &c., which threw Lord Shiva in a fearful rage and befriending Brihaspati, Vamadeva armed with His Ajgava bow and followed by His attendants and the Bhuteshvar Siddhas, started to fight with the Moon. At that time Shiva emitting fire from His third eye looked awfully fearful by the reflection of the dazzle cast on Him by the Moon.

## \|\| 23.38 \|\|

*sahaiva jagmuśca gaṇeśakādyā viṃśaccatuḥṣaṣṭigaṇāstrauktāḥ \|*  
*yakṣeśvaraḥ koṭiśatair anekair uto 'nvagāt syandanasaṃsthitānām \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Seeing Shiva going out on a fight, His other attendants Ganesha, &c., armed with various. Weapons, and Kuvera also-with. His innumerable army followed Him.

## \|\| 23.39 \|\|

*vetālayakṣoragakiṃnarāṇāṃ padmena caikena tathārbudena \|*  
*lakṣais tribhir dvādaśabhī rathānāṃ somo 'pyagāttatra vivṛddhamanyuḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Seeing his foe marching against him, the Moon, seething with wrath, started along with his vast retinue of Vetalas, Yakshas, Serpents, and a train of a million and a half of chariots, to measure swords with Him.

## \|\| 23.40 \|\|

*nakṣatradaityāsurasainyayuktaḥ śanaiścarāṅgārakavṛddhatejāḥ \|*  
*jagmurbhayaṃ sapta tathaiva lokāś cacāla bhūr dvīpasamudragarbhā \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. When the Moon in his martial array surrounded by his followers — the demons, stars, planets Saturn, Mars, &c., appeared before Shiva to meet, Him in fight, the seven worlds became terrified and the Earth with the ocean and mountains began to tremble.

## \|\| 23.41-42 \|\|

*sa somamevābhyagamatpinākī gṛhītadīptāstraviśālavahniḥ \|*  
*athābhavad bhīṣaṇabhīmasena-sainyadvayasyāpi mahāhavo 'sau \|\| 41 \|\|*

*aśeṣasattvakṣayakṛtpravṛddhas tīkṣṇāudhāstrajvalanaikarūpaḥ \|*  
*śastrairathānyonyamaśeṣasainyaṃ dvayorjagāma kṣayamugratīkṣṇaiḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

41-42. Shiva approached His adversary armed to the teeth, glittering like fire. A dreadful battle ensued between the two armies. Various kinds of weapons were used and the onslaught was so terrible that both the armies were destroyed.

## \|\| 23.43 \|\|

*patanti śastrāṇi tathodjvalāni svarbhūmipātālamatho dahanti \|*  
*rudraḥ kopādbrahmaśīrṣaṃ mumoca somo 'pi somāstramamoghavīryam \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Afterwards the mightiest of the glittering and barbed arms that consume the heaven, the earth and the lower regions were employed which made Shiva still more furious and He hurled His formidable Brahmastra at the Moon and. the latter made use of his fearful Somastra.

## \|\| 23.44-46 \|\|

*tayornipātena samudrabhūmyor athāntarikṣasya ca bhītirāsīt \|*  
*tadastraugmaṃ jagatāṃ kṣayāya pravṛddhamālokya pitāmaho 'pi \|\| 44 \|\|*

*antaḥ praviśyātha kathaṃ kathaṃcin nivārayāmāsa suraiḥ sahaiva \|*  
*akāraṇaṃ kiṃ kṣayakṛdjanānāṃ soma tvayāpīttham akāri kāryam \|\| 45 \|\|*

*yasmātparastrīharaṇāya soma tvayā kṛtaṃ uddhamatīva bhīmam \|*  
*pāpagrahastvaṃ bhavitā janeṣu śānto 'pyalaṃ nūnamatho sitānte \|*  
*bhāryāmimāmarpaya vākpatestvaṃ na cāvamāno 'sti parasvahāre \|\| 46 \|\|*

44-46. By the clash and fall of those two mighty weapons the heaven and the earth shivered with consternation. Finding the universe in peril Lord Brahma realized the gravity of the situation. Somehow or other He put Himself between the two dreadful missiles and saved the Moon along with other Devas from that impending calamity. Afterwards He thus addressed the Moon: — “You have indulged yourself in this gory onslaught for such an ignoble object on account of which even after ceasing to carry on the warfare, you will become a planet of malignant aspect at the end of the white fortnight. Give away the wife of Brihaspati, there is no disgrace in retiring from war which is conducted for the retention of ill-gotten booty”.

## \|\| 23.47 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*tatheti covāca himāṃśumālī uddhād apākrāmadataḥ praśāntaḥ \|*  
*bṛhaspatiḥ svāmapagṛhya tārāṃ hṛṣṭo jagāma svagṛhaṃ sarudraḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Suta said that on being thus reprimanded by Brahma, the Moon retired from the battle and Brihaspati also returned home completely satisfied in the company of his wife Tara

## Chapter 24

## \|\| 24.1-3 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*tataḥ saṃvatsarasyānte dvādaśādityasaṃnibhaḥ \|*  
*divyapītāmbaradharo divyābharaṇabhūṣitaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*tārodarādviniṣkrāntaḥ kumāraścandrasaṃnibhaḥ \|*  
*sarvārthaśāstraviddhīmān hastiśāstrapravartakaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*nāma yadrājaputrīyaṃ viśrutaṃ gajavaidyakam \|*  
*rājñaḥ somasya putratvād rājaputro budhaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

1-3. Suta said. — After a year a handsome cherub-boy shining like the twelve suns, wearing yellow raiment’s and resembling the Moon, was born from the womb of Tara. He was a master of all the shastras and was the author of a treatise on elephants. He was known as Rajputra, the doctor of elephants, and was afterwards named Budha owing to his being the son of the Moon.

## \|\| 24.4-5 \|\|

*jātamātraḥ sa tejāṃsi sarvāṇyevājayadbalī \|*  
*brahmādyāstatra cājagmur devā devarṣibhiḥ saha \|\| 4 \|\|*

*bṛhaspatigṛhe sarve jātakarmotsave tadā \|*  
*apṛcchaṃste surāstārāṃ kena jātaḥ kumārakaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. He conquered all the powers since the time of his birth, Brahma and other deities in company with the sages assembled at the house of Brihaspati to take part in the ceremony in connection with the birth of the child Budha, and asked Tara from whom the babe was born.

## \|\| 24.6-7 \|\|

*tataḥ sā ladjitā teṣāṃ na kiṃcidavadattadā \|*  
*punaḥ punastadā pṛṣṭā ladjayantī varāṅganā \|\| 6 \|\|*

*somasyeti cirādāha tato 'gṛhṇādvidhuḥ sutam \|*  
*budha ityakaronnāmnā prādādrājyaṃ ca bhūtale \|\| 7 \|\|*

6-7. Hearing that Tara at first held her peace out of shyness, but on being questioned repeatedly she said bashfully after a long silence that the child was born from the Moon, hearing which the latter accepted him as his son. and naming him Budha (Mercury) gave him a region below the Earth.

## \|\| 24.8-9 \|\|

*abhiṣekaṃ tataḥ kṛtvā pradhānamakarodvibhuḥ \|*  
*gṛhasāmyaṃ pradāyātha brahmā brahmarṣisaṃyutaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*paṣyatāṃ sarvadevānāṃ tatraivāntaradhīyata \|*  
*ilodare ca dharmiṣṭhaṃ budhaḥ putramajījanat \|\| 9 \|\|*

8-9. Then Brahma along with the Brahmarishis anointed him as a Planetary Lord and placed him on a par with other planets. Afterwards He vanished from the sight of the Devas then and there, and Budha begot his pious son from his wife Ila.

## \|\| 24.10 \|\|

*aśvamedhaśataṃ sāgram akarodyaḥ svatejasā \|*  
*purūravā iti khyātaḥ sarvalokanamaskṛtaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. That progeny performed many ax ashvamedha sacrifice by his glory and was universally venerated under the name of Pururava who afterwards became the sovereign Lord of the seven worlds by practising asceticism on the glorious snow-clad peaks of the Himalayas.

## \|\| 24.11-13 \|\|

*himavacchikhare ramye samārādhya janārdanam \|*  
*lokaiśvaryamagādrājā saptadvīpapatistadā \|\| 11 \|\|*

*keśiprabhṛtayo daityāḥ koṭiśo yena dāritāḥ \|*  
*urvaśī yasya patnītvam agamadrūpamohitā \|\| 12 \|\|*

*saptadvīpā vasumatī saśailavanakānanā \|*  
*dharmeṇa pālitā tena sarvalokahitaiṣiṇā \|\| 13 \|\|*

11-13. It was he who annihilated the demons Keshi, &c., and whose wife the celestial nymph Urvashi became on being enamored of him. It was he who ruled the seven worlds with even-handed justice and sympathy and thus, benefited his empire.

## \|\| 24.17-21 \|\|

*āsanatrayamānīya divyaṃ kanakabhūṣitam \|*  
*niviśyāthākarotpūjām īṣaddharme 'dhikāṃ punaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*jagmatustena kāmārthāv atikopaṃ nṛpaṃ prati \|*  
*arthaḥ śāpamadāttasmai lobhāttvaṃ nāśameṣyasi \|\| 18 \|\|*

*kāmo 'pyāha tavonmādo bhavitā gandhamādane \|*  
*kumāravanamāśritya viyogādurvaśībhavāt \|\| 19 \|\|*

*dharmo 'pyāha cirāus tvaṃ dhārmikaśca bhaviṣyasi \|*  
*saṃtatistava rājendra yāvaccandrārkatārakam \|\| 20 \|\|*

*śataśo vṛddhimāyātu na nāśaṃ bhuvi yāsyati \|*  
*ityuktvāntardadhuḥ sarve rājā rājyaṃ tadanvabhūt \|\| 21 \|\|*

17-21. Above all that, he attained divine fame and through the grace of Vishnu, Indra used to offer him a seat by His side. He guarded Dharma, Artha and Kama dutifully. All the three, viz., Dharma, Artha and Kama went to that King to see whether the latter viewed them with equality.

The king seeing them come accorded them greetings and offered them Note. — Dharma, Duty, Artha, Riches. Kama, Desire, Argha respecital offering to venerable men consisting of Durva grass, &c., with or without water, Padya, water for washing the feet of revered persons.

Then he seated them on three different golden seats and worshipped them devoutly, but maintained greater devotion for Dharma. At that Kama and Artha became displeased with the King and Artha cursed him to get destroyed by avarice. Kama cursed him to the effect that he would turn mad from the separation of Urvashi, in the Kumaravana on the Gandhamadana hill. On hearing the curses of the two, Dharma blessed him with long life and said that he would have his lineage till the sun and the moon exist.. He would flourish thousands of years and his progeny would never become extinct. Saying so, they all three disappeared instantly and the king afterwards occupied himself with the affairs of the state.

## \|\| 24.22-23 \|\|

*ahanyahani devendraṃ draṣṭuṃ yāti sa rājarāṭ \|*  
*kadācidāruhya rathaṃ dakṣiṇāmbaracāriṇam \|\| 22 \|\|*

*sārdhamarkeṇa so 'paṣyan nīyamānāmathāmbare \|*  
*keśinā dānavendreṇa citralekhāmathorvaśīm \|\| 23 \|\|*

22-23. That king used to go to see the god Indra every day, One day seated in his Dakshinambarachari chariot he was on his way to the realm of Indra, when he accidentally saw the Daitya Keshi carrying away Chitralekha and Urvashi forcibly.

## \|\| 24.28 \|\|

*lakṣmīsvayaṃvaraṃ nāma bharatena pravartitam \|*  
*menakāmurvaśīṃ rambhāṃ nṛtyateti tadādiśat \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Seeing that the king, anxious for his glory, made use of several weapons, and then ultimately subdued him by Vayavyastra by which he had overpowered Indra. After thus subjugating the demon, the king delivered the rescued Urvashi to Indra and became his fast friend. Indra thus becoming his friend and getting highly pleased with him, made him most valiant, heroic, illustrious, wealthy, and famous in all the worlds; and that nymph also becoming highly delighted sang the glories of the Pururava The celestial dramatist Bharata had composed a drama, called the svayamvara of Lakshmi to which he had asked Menaka, Rambha and Urvashi to play several parts.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — Svayamvara — self election by the bride of her husband, self-marriage.

## \|\| 24.29-31 \|\|

*nanarta salayaṃ tatra lakṣmīrūpeṇa corvaśī \|*  
*sā purūravasaṃ dṛṣṭvā nṛtyantī kāmapīḍitā \|\| 29 \|\|*

*vismṛtābhinayaṃ sarvaṃ yatpurā bharatoditam \|*  
*śaśāpa bharataḥ krodhād viyogādasya bhūtale \|\| 30 \|\|*

*pañcapañcāśadabdāni latā sūkṣmā bhaviṣyasi \|*  
*purūravāḥ piśācatvaṃ tatraivānubhaviṣyati \|\| 31 \|\|*

29-31. Then Urvashi who was playing the part of Lakshmi and was dancing and singing melodiously in unison with the music, saw Pururava and being fired with passion forgot the part which Bharata had taught her.

Bharata in a rage cursed Urvashi saying that she would become a subtle creeper on the earth for 55 years on account of the separation from Pururava and the latter would lapse into a Pishacha.

## \|\| 24.32-34 \|\|

*tatastamurvaśī gatvā bhartāramakarocciram \|*  
*śāpānte bharatasyātha urvaśī budhasūnutaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

*ajījanatsutānaṣṭau nāmatastānnibodhata \|*  
*āur dṛḍhāur aśvāur dhanāur dhṛtimānvasuḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

*śucividyaḥ śatāuśca sarve divyabalaujasaḥ \|*  
*āuṣo nahuṣaḥ putrau vṛddhaśarmā tathaiva ca \|\| 34 \|\|*

32-34. After that Urvashi made Pururava her Lord and on the conclusion of the effects of curses she brought forth the following eight valiant sons: —

Ayu, Dridhayu, Ashvayu, Dhanayu, Dhritiman, Vasu, Suchi Vidya, and Satayu. Ayu the eldest of them all became the father of Nahusha, Vriddhasharma, Raji, Dambha and Vipapma. These five were all heroes.

## \|\| 24.35-36 \|\|

*rajirdambho vipāpmā ca vīrāḥ pañca mahārathāḥ \|*  
*rajeḥ putraśataṃ jajñe rājeyamiti viśrutam \|\| 35 \|\|*

*rajirārādhayāmāsa nārāyaṇamakalmaṣam \|*  
*tapasā toṣito viṣṇur varānprādānmahīpate \|\| 36 \|\|*

35-36. Raji became the father of one hundred children who camp to be known as Rajeya. He devoutly practiced penances and was granted a boon by Vishnu, on account of which he was powerful enough to conquer the Devas, demons and men.

## \|\| 24.37-39 \|\|

*devāsuramanuṣyāṇām abhūtsa vijayī tadā \|*  
*atha devāsuraṃ uddham abhūd varṣaśatatrayam \|\| 37 \|\|*

*prahlādaśakrayorbhīmaṃ na kaścidvijayī tayoḥ \|*  
*tato devāsuraiḥ pṛṣṭaḥ prāha devaścaturmukhaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

*anayorvijayī kaḥ syād rajiryatreti so 'bravīt \|*  
*jayāya prārthito rājā sahāyastvaṃ bhavasva naḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

37-39. Once upon a time a pitched battle ensued between the Devas and the Asuras for three centuries, in which there was a tremendous light between Prahlada and Indra. The battle was indecisive. At that both the Devas and the Asuras asked Brahma, as to who was likely to bear away the palm of victory. Brahma said that the party headed by Raji would be victorious. Hearing that the Devas eager for their victory requested the King Raji to take their part in the great war.

## \|\| 24.40-41 \|\|

*daityaiḥ prāha yadi svāmī vo bhavāmi tatastvalam \|*  
*nāsuraiḥ pratipannaṃ tat pratipannaṃ suraistathā \|\| 40 \|\|*

*svāmī bhava tvamasmākaṃ saṃgrāme nāśaya dviṣaḥ \|*  
*tato vināśitāḥ sarve ye 'vadhyā vajrapāṇinā \|\| 41 \|\|*

40-41. The Asuras also approached him with a similar request, but Raji had accepted the invitation of the Devas so he refused the proposal of the Asuras. The Devas then entreated him to lead their army and destroy the Asuras. I he king then killed those Asuras who could not be conquered even by Indra.

## \|\| 24.42 \|\|

*putratvamagamattuṣṭas tasyendraḥ karmaṇā vibhuḥ \|*  
*dattvendrāya tadā rājyaṃ jagāma tapase rajiḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Indra was highly delighted at that valourous feat of the king, so much so that he took birth as his son. When Indra was born as his son, the king making over the charge of his vast dominions to him went to devote himself to contemplation and meditation.

## \|\| 24.43-44 \|\|

*rajiputraistadācchinnaṃ balādindrasya vaibhavam \|*  
*yajñabhāgaṃ ca rājyaṃ ca tapobalaguṇānvitaiḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

*rājyabhraṣṭastadā śakro rajiputrairnipīḍitaḥ \|*  
*prāha vācaspatiṃ dīnaḥ pīḍito 'smi rajeḥ sutaiḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

43-44. The other valiant sons of haji forcibly dethroned Indra and usurped all the kingdom and share of sacrifices from him. - Indra thus bereft of his position went and laid himself at the mercy of Brihaspati. He said to Brihaspati that he had been deprived of his realm as well as of the right of a share in sacrifices and appealed to him to advise him to get back his kingdom.

## \|\| 24.45-46 \|\|

*na yajñabhāgo rājyaṃ me nirjitaśca bṛhaspate \|*  
*rājyalābhāya me yatnaṃ vidhatsva dhiṣaṇādhipa \|\| 45 \|\|*

*tato bṛhaspatiḥ śakram akarodbaladarpitam \|*  
*grahaśāntividhānena pauṣṭikena ca karmaṇā \|\| 46 \|\|*

45-46. Brihaspati then restored Indra to power by performing a rite called Graha Shanti or pacifying the malignant influence of the planets.

## \|\| 24.47-49 \|\|

*gatvātha mohayāmāsa rajiputrānbṛhaspatiḥ \|*  
*jinadharmaṃ samāsthāya vedabāhyaṃ sa vedavit \|\| 47 \|\|*

*vedatrayīparibhraṣṭāṃś cakāra dhiṣaṇādhipaḥ \|*  
*vedabāhyānparijñāya hetuvādasamanvitān \|\| 48 \|\|*

*jaghāna śakro vajreṇa sarvāndharmabahiṣkṛtān \|*  
*nahuṣasya pravakṣyāmi putrānsaptaiva dhārmikān \|\| 49 \|\|*

47-49. Brihaspati then went and deluded the other sons of Raji with false philosophy and established the Jina religion opposed to the vedas, though himself a knower of the Vedas and Indra on finding the sons of Brihaspati propagating a religion different from the Vedas based on a show of reason only killed them with his mighty thunderbolt.

## \|\| 24.50 \|\|

*yatiryayātiḥ saṃyātir udbhavaḥ pācireva ca \|*  
*śaryātirmeghajātiśca saptaite vaṃśavardhanāḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Now hear something about the seven pious sons of Nahusha. They were: — Yati, Yayati, Samyati, Udbhava, Pachi, Saryati, Meghayati.

## \|\| 24.51 \|\|

*yatiḥ kumārabhāve 'pi yogī vaikhānaso 'bhavat \|*  
*yayātiścākarodrājyaṃ dharmaikaśaraṇaḥ sadā \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Yati turned an anchorite since his very early days and Yayati began to rule his kingdom with piety.

## \|\| 24.52 \|\|

*śarmiṣṭhā tasya bhāryābhūd duhitā vṛṣaparvaṇaḥ \|*  
*bhārgavasyātmajā tadvad devayānī ca suvratā \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. Yayati had two queens, viz., Devayani the daughter of Shukra and Sharmishtha the daughter of Vrishaparvana.

## \|\| 24.53-56 \|\|

*yayāteḥ pañca dāyādās tānpravakṣyāmi nāmataḥ \|*  
*devayānī yaduṃ putraṃ turvasuṃ cāpyajījanat \|\| 53 \|\|*

*tathā druhyumanuṃ pūruṃ śarmiṣṭhājanayatsutān \|*  
*yaduḥ pūruścābhavatāṃ teṣāṃ vaṃśavivardhanau \|\| 54 \|\|*

*yayātirnāhuṣaścāsīd rājā satyaparākramaḥ \|*  
*pālayāmāsa sa mahīm īje ca vidhivanmakhaiḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

*atibhaktyā pitrinarcya devāṃśca prayataḥ sadā \|*  
*athājayatprajāḥ sarvā yayātiraparājitaḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

53-56. Yayati had five sons; Yadu and Turvasu from Devayani; and three sons: Druhya, Anu and Puru from Sharmishtha. Of them Yadu and Puru were the promoters of the dynasty. King Yayati was the protector of the realm with truth and heroism - and was also the performer of many sacrifices.

He was a great lover of sacrifices and worshipped the Pitris with great devotion. He won over his subjects and protected them dutifully.

## \|\| 24.57-59 \|\|

*sa śāśvatīḥ samā rājā prajā dharmeṇa pālayan \|*  
*jarām ārchan mahāghorāṃ nāhuṣo rūpanāśinīm \|\| 57 \|\|*

*jarābhibhūtaḥ putrān sa rājā vacanamabravīt \|*  
*yaduṃ pūruṃ turvasuṃ ca druhyuṃ cānuṃ ca pārthivaḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

*yauvanena calānkāmān uvā uvatibhiḥ saha \|*  
*vihartum ahamicchāmi sāhāyyaṃ kurutātmajāḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

57-59. Once upon a time the king grew aged and was deprived of the vigour of youth. Finding himself infirm, he summoned his sons Yadu, Anu, Turvasu, Druhya, and Puru and said to- them, “Sons! I wish to become young again and carry on amorous frolics with damsels, you come to my succour.

## \|\| 24.60 \|\|

*taṃ putro devayāneyaḥ pūrvajo yadurabravīt \|*  
*sāhāyyaṃ bhavataḥ kāryam asmābhiryauvanena kim \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Hearing those words of the king, Yadu the eldest son from Devayani said “In what way can L help you with my youth?"

## \|\| 24.61 \|\|

*yayātirabravīt putrāñ jarā me pratigṛhyatām \|*  
*yauvanenātha bhavatāṃ careyaṃ viṣayānaham \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Then Yayati asked his sons to exchange their youth with his old age and thus make him fit for carnal enjoyments.

## \|\| 24.62-63 \|\|

*yajato dīrghasattrairme śāpāccośanaso muneḥ \|*  
*kāmārthaḥ parihīno me 'tṛpto 'haṃ tena putrakāḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

*svakīyena śarīreṇa jarāmenāṃ praśāstu vaḥ \|*  
*ahaṃ tanvābhinavayā uvā kāmānavāpnuyām \|\| 63 \|\|*

62-63. “Sons! after performing great many sacrifices, I have become old by the curse of Shukra, but my thirst for enjoyments has not yet been quenched. You, therefore, give me your vigour, and thus enable me to fulfil my desires.”

## \|\| 24.64 \|\|
