*na te 'sya pratyagṛhṇanta yaduprabhṛtayo jarām \|*  
*caturastānsa rājarṣir aśapacceti naḥ śrutam \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. Yadu and his three brothers did not agree to the proposal of his father which enraged the latter and he cursed them saying that none from their family would ever succeed to the throne.

## \|\| 24.65 \|\|

*tamabravīttataḥ pūruḥ kanīyānsatyavikramaḥ \|*  
*jarāṃ mā dehi navayā tanvā me yauvanātsukhī \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. Then the younger Puru said “Sire! give me your old age and take my vigour and satisfy yourself, With your permission I will succeed you as an old monarch.”

## \|\| 24.66 \|\|

*ahaṃ jarāṃ tavādāya rājye sthāsyāmi cājñayā \|*  
*evamuktaḥ sa rājarṣis tapovīryasamāśrayāt \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. Then Yayati transferred his old age to him and taking his. vigour became young again.

## \|\| 24.67 \|\|

*saṃsthāpayāmāsa jarāṃ tadā putre mahātmani \|*  
*pauraveṇātha vayasā rājā yauvanamāsthitaḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. Puru began to rule the vast empire with the old age of the king.

## \|\| 24.68-69 \|\|

*yayāteścātha vayasā rājyaṃ pūrurakārayat \|*  
*tato varṣasahasrānte yayātiraparājitaḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

*atṛpta iva kāmānāṃ pūruṃ putramuvāca ha \|*  
*tvayā dāyādavān asmi tvaṃ me vaṃśakaraḥ sutaḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

68-69. The king not satisfied with his mundane pleasures, even after a period of a thousand years, addressed his son Puru thus: — “ You are the promoter of my dynasty, by your having a son, I am not heirless, in. this world my dynasty will be named Paurava, after you.”

## \|\| 24.71 \|\|

*kālena mahatā paścāt kāladharmam upeyivān \|*  
*pūruvaṃśaṃ pravakṣyāmi śṛṇudhvamṛṣisattamāḥ \|*  
*yatra te bhāratā jātā bharatānvayavardhanāḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. Afterwards. Yayati got Poru anointed and then sometime after now something will be related about that dynasty of Puru in which Kings Bharata, &c., the promoters of the Bharata dynasty were born. Hear, O! Sages, this relation with attention

## Chapter 25

## \|\| 25.1-2 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ*  
*kimarthaṃ pauravo vaṃśaḥ śreṣṭhatvaṃ prāpa bhūtale \|*  
*jyeṣṭhasyāpi yadorvaṃśaḥ kimarthaṃ hīyate śriyā \|\| 1 \|\|*

*anyadyayāticaritaṃ sūta vistarato vada \|*  
*yasmāttatpuṇyamāuṣyam abhinandyaṃ surairapi \|\| 2 \|\|*

1-2. The Rishis asked: — Why Paurava dynasty became so illustrious and way Yadu the oldest of Yayati's sons became the founder of an inferior and poor dynasty. Besides this O! Suta, relate to us at length other things connected with the history of Yayati, because his virtue which is the giver of long life is held in high esteem even by the Devas.

## \|\| 25.3 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*etadeva purā pṛṣṭaḥ śatānīkena śaunakaḥ \|*  
*puṇyaṃ pavitramāuṣyaṃ yayāticaritaṃ mahat \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Suta said: — Rishis, the same question was put by Shatanika who asked Shaunaka about the sacred history of Yayati.

## \|\| 25.4-5 \|\|

*śatānīka uvāca*  
*yayātiḥ pūrvajo 'smākaṃ daśamo yaḥ prajāpateḥ \|*  
*kathaṃ sa śukratanayāṃ lebhe paramadurlabhām \|\| 4 \|\|*

*etadicchāmyahaṃ śrotuṃ vistareṇa tapodhana \|*  
*ānupūrvyācca me śaṃsa pūrorvaṃśadharānnṛpān \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. Shatanika asked: — “Shaunaka, how my ancestor Yayati who was tenth in descent from Prajapati married the daughter of Shukra. O, Sage! I am anxious to hear about it. I am still more anxious to hear the history of the Paurava kings serially. Be gracious enough to relate alt that in detail.

## \|\| 25.6-7 \|\|

*śaunaka uvāca*  
*yayātirāsīdrājarṣir devarājasamadyutiḥ \|*  
*taṃ śukravṛṣaparvāṇau vavrāte vai yathā purā \|\| 6 \|\|*

*tatte 'haṃ sampravakṣyāmi pṛcchato rājasattama \|*  
*devayānyāśca saṃyogaṃ yayāternāhuṣasya ca \|\| 7 \|\|*

6-7. Shaunaka answered: — King Yayati was as handsome as Indra and was blessed both by Shukra and Vrishaparvana. I shall relate to you all about that and will also explain to you how Yayati the son of Nahusha matted: Devayani.

## \|\| 25.8-14 \|\|

*surāṇāmasurāṇāṃ ca samajāyata vai mithaḥ \|*  
*aiśvaryaṃ prati saṃgharṣas trailokye sacarācare \|\| 8 \|\|*

*jigīṣayā tato devā vavrurāṅgirasaṃ munim \|*  
*paurohitye ca yajñārthe kāvyaṃ tūśanasaṃ pare \|\| 9 \|\|*

*brāhmaṇau tāv ubhau nityam anyonyaṃ spardhinau bhṛśam \|*  
*tatra devā nijaghnuryān dānavān udhi saṃgatān \|\| 10 \|\|*

*tānpunar jīvayāmāsa kāvyo vidyābalāśrayāt \|*  
*tataste punarutthāya yodhayāṃcakrire surān \|\| 11 \|\|*

*asurāstu nijaghnuryān surānsamaramūrdhani \|*  
*na tānsaṃjīvayāmāsa bṛhaspatirudāradhīḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*na hi veda sa tāṃ vidyāṃ yāṃ kāvyo veda vīryavān \|*  
*saṃjīvanīṃ tato devā viṣādamagamanparam \|\| 13 \|\|*

*atha devā bhayodvignāḥ kāvyāduśanasastadā \|*  
*ūcuḥ kacamupāgamya jyeṣṭhaṃ putraṃ bṛhaspateḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

8-14. Once upon a time the Devas and the Asuras fell out with each other for the kingdom of the three worlds. Then the Devas anxious to have the best of the contest made Brihaspati their sacrificial priest and similarly the Asuras made Shukra their priest. Both the sages — Brihaspati and Shukra – were at daggers drawn with each other. Shukra by his lore brought into life all the Asuras that wore killed by the devas and they again appeared to face them on the battle field. Brihaspati could not similarly restore to life the Devas killed by the Asuras, because he did not possess the same Knowledge, at which the Devas were greatly dismayed.

The Devas getting fearfully alarmed went to the son of Brihaspati named Kacha.

## \|\| 25.15-19 \|\|

*bhajamānānbhajasvāsmān kuru sāhāyyamuttamam \|*  
*yāsau vidyā nivasati brāhmaṇe 'mitatejasi \|\| 15 \|\|*

*śukre tāmāhara kṣipraṃ bhāgabhāṅno bhaviṣyasi \|*  
*vṛṣaparvaṇaḥ samīpe 'sau śakyo draṣṭuṃ tvayā dvijaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*rakṣate dānavāṃstatra na sa rakṣatyadānavān \|*  
*tam ārādhayituṃ śakto nānyaḥ kaścidṛte tvayā \|\| 17 \|\|*

*devayānī ca dayitā sutā tasya mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*tām ārādhayituṃ śakto nānyaḥ kaścana vidyate \|\| 18 \|\|*

*śīladākṣiṇyamādhuryair ācāreṇa damena ca \|*  
*devayānyāṃ tu tuṣṭāyāṃ vidyāṃ tāṃ prāpsyasi dhruvam \|\| 19 \|\|*

15-19. The Devas said: — Kacha, we are at your mercy, do come to our rescue. We beseech you to somehow acquire the sanjivani (Resuscitation) knowledge from Shukra, by doing that you will become entitled to receive a share out of the offerings made to us. You should try to meet Shukra in the court of Vrishaparvan. Who guards the Asuras and not the Devas, You alone can propitiate him none else can do it. None excepting you can also please Devayani the daughter of Shukra. By pleasing her with tact, ‘shrewdness, and sweetness you will be able to acquire that wonderful sanjivani knowledge.”

## \|\| 25.20-21 \|\|

*tadā hi preṣito devaiḥ samīpe vṛṣaparvaṇaḥ \|*  
*tathetyuktvā tu sa prāyād bṛhaspatisutaḥ kacaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*sa gatvā tvarito rājan devaiḥ sampūjitaḥ kacaḥ \|*  
*asurendrapure śukraṃ praṇamyedamuvāca ha \|\| 21 \|\|*

20-21. With those words the Devas after worshipping Kacha sent him to Vrishvaparvan. Kacha, after being worshipped by the Devas went straight to Shukra and after saluting him said:

## \|\| 25.22-23 \|\|

*ṛṣer aṅgirasaḥ pautraṃ putraṃ sākṣādbṛhaspateḥ \|*  
*nāmnā kaceti vikhyātaṃ śiṣyaṃ gṛhṇātu māṃ bhavān \|\| 22 \|\|*

*brahmacaryaṃ cariṣyāmi tvayyahaṃ paramaṃ guro \|*  
*anumanyasva māṃ brahman sahasraparivatsarān \|\| 23 \|\|*

22-23. “O, Preceptor, accept me named Kacha, the grandson of Angirasa and son of Brihaspati as your pupil. Preceptor, I shall lead a typical disciple’s life, keep me as your pupil for thousands of years.”

## \|\| 25.24 \|\|

*śukra uvāca*  
*kaca susvāgataṃ te 'stu pratigṛhṇāmi te vacaḥ \|*  
*arcayiṣye 'hamarcyaṃ tvām arcito 'stu bṛhaspatiḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Shukra said: — “Kacha, you are welcome and so also your words. You are worthy of being adored and so also Brihaspati."

## \|\| 25.25-26 \|\|

*śaunaka uvāca*  
*kacastu taṃ tathetyuktvā pratijagrāha tadvratam \|*  
*ādiṣṭaṃ kaviputreṇa śukreṇośanasā svayam \|\| 25 \|\|*

*vrataṃ ca vratakālaṃ ca yathoktaṃ pratyagṛhṇata \|*  
*ārādhayannupādhyāyaṃ devayānīṃ ca bhārata \|\| 26 \|\|*

25-26. Shaunaka said that afterwards Kacha followed all the injunctions of Shukra and observed the fasts at the proper periods according to the prescribed rites, and began to serve Shukra and Devayani.

## \|\| 25.27-28 \|\|

*nityamārādhayiṣyaṃstāṃ uvā yauvanagocarām \|*  
*gāyannṛtyanvādayaṃśca devayānīmatoṣayat \|\| 27 \|\|*

*saṃśīlayandevayānīṃ kanyāṃ samprāptayauvanām \|*  
*puṣpaiḥ phalaiḥ preṣaṇaiśca toṣayāmāsa bhārgavīm \|\| 28 \|\|*

27-28. He pleased Devayani who had attained puberty by singing, dancing playing music and offering of flowers and other presents.

## \|\| 25.29 \|\|

*devayānyapi taṃ vipraṃ niyamavratacāriṇam \|*  
*anugāyantī lalanā rahaḥ paryacarattadā \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Devayani also interested herself in that pious Brahmana and took every care of him.

## \|\| 25.30-32 \|\|

*pañca varṣaśatānyevaṃ kacasya carato bhṛśam \|*  
*tattattīvraṃ vrataṃ buddhvā dānavāstaṃ tataḥ kacam \|\| 30 \|\|*

*gā rakṣantaṃ vane dṛṣṭvā rahasyenamamarṣitāḥ \|*  
*jaghnur bṛhaspater dveṣān nijarakṣārtham eva ca \|\| 31 \|\|*

*hatvā sālāvṛkebhyaśca prāyacchaṃstilaśaḥ kṛtam \|*  
*tato gāvo nivṛttāstā agopāḥ svaniveśanam \|\| 32 \|\|*

30-32. In that way Kacha went on for a period of five hundred years. The Asuras, knowing the piety of Kacha and out of their spite for Brihaspati, took him to a secluded place in the forest where he was grazing the cows, and slaughtered him for the sake of their own protection. After that they divided his corpse into many parts and then got it devoured by wolves and jackals. Then the cows bereft of their keeper returned to their abode.

## \|\| 25.33-35 \|\|

*tā dṛṣṭvā rahitā gāstu kacenābhyāgatā vanāt \|*  
*uvāca vacanaṃ kāle devayānyatha bhārgavam \|\| 33 \|\|*

*hutaṃ caivāgnihotraṃ te sūryaścāstaṃ gataḥ prabho \|*  
*agopāścāgatā gāvaḥ kacastāta na dṛṣyate \|\| 34 \|\|*

*vyaktaṃ hato dhṛto vāpi kacastāta bhaviṣyati \|*  
*taṃ vinā naiva jīvāmi vacaḥ satyaṃ bravīmyaham \|\| 35 \|\|*

33-35. Devayani seeing the cows returning home without Kacha addressed.

Shukra thus: —

“Sire, you have finished your Agnihotra, the sun has descended below the horizon, these cows are without their keeper, and Kacha is nowhere visible to-day. Undoubtedly Kacha has been either killed or captured and if this be the case I say truly I cannot live without him.”

## \|\| 25.36 \|\|

*śukra uvāca*  
*athehyehīti śabdena mṛtaṃ saṃjīvayāmyaham \|*  
*tataḥ saṃjīvanīṃ vidyāṃ prauktvā kacamāhvayat \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Shukra said: — “I am just going to recall Kacha,” so he called Kacha back to life by means of his Sanjivani knowledge.

## \|\| 25.37 \|\|

*āhūtaḥ prādurabhavat kacaḥ śukraṃ nanāma sa \|*  
*hato 'hamiti cācakhyau rākṣasair dhiṣaṇātmajaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Then the murdered Kacha came running to Shukra and saluted him from a distance and told him all about his being killed by the Asuras.

## \|\| 25.38-39 \|\|

*sa punardevayānyuktaḥ puṣpāhāre yadṛcchayā \|*  
*vanaṃ yayau kaco vipraḥ paṭhanbrahma ca śāśvatam \|\| 38 \|\|*

*vane puṣpāṇi cinvantaṃ dadṛśur dānavāśca tam \|*  
*tato 'dvitīyaṃ taṃ hatvā dagdhaṃ kṛtvā ca cūrṇavat \|*  
*prāyacchan brāhmaṇāyaiva surāyāmasurāstadā \|\| 39 \|\|*

38-39. Once again Kacha went reciting the Vedas to fetch flowers for Devayani from the forest. The demons seeing him gathering flowers in the forest powdered him to death and mingling his remains in the wine gave it to Shukra to drink.

## \|\| 25.40-41 \|\|

*devayānyatha bhūyo 'pi pitaraṃ vākyamabravīt \|*  
*puṣpāhārapreṣaṇakṛt kacastāta na dṛṣyate \|\| 40 \|\|*

*vyaktaṃ hato mṛto vāpi kacastāta bhaviṣyati \|*  
*taṃ vinā naiva jīvāmi vacaḥ satyaṃ bravīmi te \|\| 41 \|\|*

40-41. Devayani on not seeing Kacha return again spoke to her father “He was sent by me to gather flowers for me but he has not returned. Assuredly he has been killed again and I tell you honestly that I cannot live without him.

## \|\| 25.42-44 \|\|

*śukra uvāca*  
*bṛhaspateḥ sutaḥ putri kacaḥ pretagatiṃ gataḥ \|*  
*vidyayā jīvito 'pyevaṃ hanyate karavāṇi kim \|\| 42 \|\|*

*mainaṃ śuco mā ruda devayāni na tvādṛśī martyamanu praśocet \|*  
*yasyāstava brahma ca brāhmaṇāśca sendrāśca devā vasavo 'śvinau ca \|\| 43 \|\|*

*suradviṣaścaiva jagacca sarvam upasthitaṃ mattapasaḥ prabhāvāt \|*  
*aśakyo 'yaṃ jīvayituṃ dvijātiḥ saṃjīvito yo vadhyate caiva bhūyaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

42-44. Shukra said: — “Devayani, that son of Brihaspati was restored to life after being murdered, what can I do when he has been killed again. You should not lament. — It does not behoove persons like you to mourn in this world, You, who through my power of asceticism are being courted by Brahma, Ashvinikumaras, Indra and other Gods, and Asuras, aye, everyone in the universe. should by no means mourn like this. The Brahmana who has been killed again after being restored to life once is beyond my power to be recalled to life again.”

## \|\| 25.46 \|\|

*sa brahmacārī ca tapodhanaśca sadotthitaḥ karmasu caiva dakṣaḥ \|*  
*kacasya mārgaṃ pratipatsye na bhokṣye priyo hi me tāta kaco 'bhirūpaḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Devayani said: — “The grandson of Angirasa, the son of Brihaspati, “Kacha, who is a scion of such an illustrious family, who is so clever and chaste is very dear to me. Why shall not weep for him. I shall not take my meals and will set out in quest of him”.

## \|\| 25.47-49 \|\|

*śaunaka uvāca*  
*sa tv evamukto devayānyā maharṣiḥ saṃrambheṇa vyājahārātha kāvyaḥ \|*  
*asaṃśayaṃ māmasurā dviṣanti ye me śiṣyānāgatānsūdayanti \|\| 47 \|\|*

*abrāhmaṇaṃ kartumicchanti raudrā ebhir vyarthaṃ prastuto dānavairhi \|*  
*tatkarmaṇāpyasya bhavedihāntaḥ kaṃ brahmahatyā na dahedapīndram \|\| 48 \|\|*

*sa tenāpṛṣṭo vidyayā copahūtaḥ śanairvācaṃ jaṭhare vyājahāra \|*  
*tamabravītkena cehopanīto mamodare tiṣṭhasi brūhi vatsa \|\| 49 \|\|*

47-49. Shaunaka said: — Hearing those words of Devayani, Kavya Shukra said in his mind that “undoubtedly, the Asuras hate me, because they constantly destroy my disciples. The Asuras perhaps wish to annihilate the Brahmanas. I am worshipped by the Danavas as their preceptor in vain, for the Brahmagni can destroy Indra even, who then can escape the consequences of the foul deed perpetrated by them in-killing the Brahmana Kacha.” Shukra again revived Kacha by means of his sanjivani knowledge. At that Kacha began to speak slowly in the stomach of Shukra. Then Shukra asked him: — By whom killed, thou art inside my stomach, tell me that, O child”.

## \|\| 25.50-51 \|\|

*kaca uvāca*  
*bhavatprasādānna jahāti māṃ smṛtiḥ sarvaṃ smareyaṃ yacca yathā ca vṛttam \|*  
*na tv evaṃ syāttapasaḥ kṣayo me tata kleśaṃ ghorataraṃ smarāmi \|\| 50 \|\|*

*asuraiḥ surāyāṃ bhavato 'smi datto hatvā dagdhvā cūrṇayitvā ca kāvya \|*  
*brāhmīṃ māyāṃ tv āsurī tv atra māyā tvayi sthite katham evābhibādhate \|\| 51 \|\|*

50-51. Kacha said: — “Through your grace I remember everything. Under these circumstances, I am not losing my power of asceticism; but I feel a great discomfort. The Asuras after powdering me to death mixed my remains with the wine and made you drink it, but through the glory of your Brahmanism I am not oppressed by the diabolical freaks of the Asuras."

## \|\| 25.52 \|\|

*śukra uvāca*  
*kiṃ te priyaṃ karavāṇyadya vatse vinaiva me jīvitaṃ syātkacasya \|*  
*nānyatra kukṣermama bhedanācca dṛśyet kaco madgato devayāni \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. Shukra said: — “Devayani, how am I to satisfy you? It seems difficult to save Kacha whilst I am living, because how can he come cut without tearing my stomach.

## \|\| 25.53 \|\|

*devayānyuvāca*  
*dvau māṃ śokāv agnikalpau dahetāṃ kacasya nāśastava caivopaghātaḥ \|*  
*kacasya nāśe mama nāsti śarma tavopaghāte jīvituṃ nāsmi śaktā \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Devayani said: — “The double pains that I am undergoing are consuming-me like fire, i.e., the destruction of Kacha and the prospect, of your not living in the event of his escaping death. I can have no comfort on the death of Kacha nor can I live if you are destroyed.”

## \|\| 25.54-56 \|\|

*śukra uvāca*  
*saṃsiddharūpo 'si bṛhaspateḥ suta yattvāṃ bhaktaṃ bhajate devayānī \|*  
*vidyāmimāṃ prāpnuhi jīvanīṃ tvaṃ na cedindraḥ kacarūpī tvamadya \|\| 54 \|\|*

*na nivartetpunarjīvan kaścidanyo mamodarāt \|*  
*brāhmaṇaṃ varjayitvaikaṃ tasmādvidyām avāpnuhi \|\| 55 \|\|*

*putro bhūtvā niṣkramasvodarānme bhittvā kukṣiṃ jīvaya māṃ ca tāta \|*  
*avekṣethā dharmavatīmavekṣāṃ guroḥ sakāśātprāpya vidyāṃ savidyaḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

54-56. Shukra said: — “O, son of Brihaspati! who ‘is prized by Devayani, become a seer and acquire my sanjivani knowledge for IT am assured now that you are not Indra in the disguise of Kacha. Because none excepting a Brahmana can live in my stomach, and Indra being a Kshatriya would have been digested by me. Therefore learn this science from me. Come out of my stomach as my son, i.e., first acquire the sanjivani knowledge and then come out of my stomach after ripping it open and restore me to life and then satisfy the expectation of this dutiful daughter of mine, after having mastered this science from me, thy guru.”

## \|\| 25.57 \|\|

*śaunaka uvāca*  
*guroḥ sakāśātsamavāpya vidyāṃ bhittvā kukṣiṃ nirvicakrāma vipraḥ \|*  
*prāleyādreḥ śuklamudbhidya śṛṅgaṃ rātryāgame paurṇamāsyāmivenduḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Shaunaka said that the Brahmana then acquired that knowledge from his preceptor, and, after opening the stomach of Shukra, emerged from it as does the full moon at the approach of night by bursting open through the eastern horizon.

## \|\| 25.58-59 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā ca taṃ patitaṃ vedarāśim utthāpayāmāsa tataḥ kaco 'pi \|*  
*vidyāṃ siddhāṃ tāmavāpyābhivādya tataḥ kacastaṃ gurumityuvāca \|\| 58 \|\|*

*nidhiṃ nidhīnāṃ varadaṃ varāṇāṃ ye nādriyante gurumarcanīyam \|*  
*prāleyādriprodjvaladbhālasaṃsthaṃ pāpāṃllokāṃste vrajantyapratiṣṭhāḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

58-59. On finding his preceptor lying dead, Kacha by means of that sanjivani knowledge recalled him to life, and then addressed him thus: —

“Worthy one, you are bounteous like an ocean and the most generous among the givers of boons. Those who do not show due regard to such a preceptor, are sinners doomed to hell after being wrecked.”

## \|\| 25.61 \|\|

*samanyurutthāya mahānubhāvas tadośanā viprahitaṃ cikīrṣuḥ \|*  
*kāvyaḥ svayaṃ vākyamidaṃ jagāda surāpānaṃ pratyasau jātaśaṅkaḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Shaunaka said that Shukra (Ushana), who was deluded through drinking, on getting back his lost disciple, and seeing his graceful form and powers of asceticism, desirous of doing a good turn to the Brahmanas, taking the wine, uttered the following words against drinking and its evil consequences:

## \|\| 25.62-63 \|\|

*śukra uvāca*  
*yo brāhmaṇo 'dyaprabhṛtīha kaścin mohātsurāṃ pāsyati mandabuddhiḥ \|*  
*apetadharmā brahmahā caiva sa syādasmiṃlloke garhitaḥ syātpare ca \|\| 62 \|\|*

*mayā cemāṃ vipradharmoktasīmāṃ maryādāṃ vai sthāpitāṃ sarvaloke \|*  
*santo viprāḥ śuśruvāṃso gurūṇāṃ devā daityāścopaśṛṇvantu sarve \|\| 63 \|\|*

62-63. “Henceforth the foolish Brahmana who drinks wine shall become devoid of Dharma and commit the sin of murdering a Brahmana and be despised in this world as well as in the next. I have laid down this Law for the Brahmanas in the whole universe, and let the pious Brahmanas know the injunctions of the preceptor and let the Devas and Daityas also listen to these words.”

## \|\| 25.64-65 \|\|

*śaunaka uvāca*  
*itīdamuktvā sa mahāprabhāvas taponidhīnāṃ nidhir aprameyaḥ \|*  
*tāndānavāṃścaiva nigūḍhabuddhīn idaṃ samāhūya vaco 'bhyuvāca \|\| 64 \|\|*

*śukra uvāca*  
*ācakṣe vo dānavā bāliśāḥ stha śiṣyaḥ kaco vatsyati matsamīpe \|*  
*saṃjīvanīṃ prāpya vidyāṃ mayāyaṃ tulyaprabhāvo brāhmaṇo brahmabhūtaḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

64-65. Shaunaka said that the illustrious seer Shukra, after saying that, called all the Danavas of clouded intellect and said: — ~ Hear, you foolish.

Danavas! My disciple, Kacha, after acquiring sanjivani knowledge from me, has become equally powerful like myself; and has become a true Brahmana and one with Brahma.

## \|\| 25.66 \|\|

*śaunaka uvāca*  
*guroruṣya sakāśe ca daśa varṣaśatāni saḥ \|*  
*anujñātaḥ kaco gantum iyeṣa tridaśālayam \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. Shaunaka said that Kacha, after residing with his preceptor for another century, took leave of him to go to heaven."

## Chapter 26

## \|\| 26.1 \|\|

*śaunaka uvāca*  
*samāpitavrataṃ taṃ tu visṛṣṭaṃ guruṇā tadā \|*  
*prasthitaṃ tridaśāvāsaṃ devayānīdamabravīt \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Shaunaka said: — On the fulfilment of his vow when Kacha, after taking leave of Shukra, was about to start for heaven, Devayani addressed the following words to him:

## \|\| 26.2-5 \|\|

*devayānyuvāca*  
*ṛṣer aṅgirasaḥ pautra vṛttenābhijanena ca \|*  
*bhrājase vidyayā caiva tapasā ca damena ca \|\| 2 \|\|*

*ṛṣir yathāṅgirā mānyaḥ piturmama mahāyaśāḥ \|*  
*tathā mānyaśca pūjyaśca mama bhūyo bṛhaspatiḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*evaṃ jñātvā vijānīhi yadbravīmi tapodhana \|*  
*vratasthe niyamopete yathā vartāmyahaṃ tvayi \|\| 4 \|\|*

*sa samāpitavidyo māṃ bhaktāṃ na tyaktumarhasi \|*  
*gṛhāṇa pāṇiṃ vidhivan mama mantrapuraskṛtam \|\| 5 \|\|*

2-5. Devayani said: — “O, grandson of Angiras! You shine on account of your wealth, family status, learning, pious conduct, asceticism, and sobriety. As the sage Angira, of great renown, is respected by my father, so is Brihaspati respected and revered by me. Knowing this, O ‘Seer! consider what I say unto you. You know how I behaved towards you, while you were observing the vow with its restrictions. Your learning is now accomplished. You should not forsake me, who am devoted to you; therefore accept my hand in marriage according to due rites and Mantras.”"

## \|\| 26.6-8 \|\|

*kaca uvāca*  
*pūjyo mānyaśca bhagavān yathā mama pitā tava \|*  
*tathā tvamanavadyāṅgi pūjanīyatamā matā \|\| 6 \|\|*

*ātmaprāṇaiḥ priyatamā bhārgavasya mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*tvaṃ bhadre dharmataḥ pūjyā guruputrī sadā mama \|\| 7 \|\|*

*yathā mama gururnityaṃ mānyaḥ śukraḥ pitā tava \|*  
*devayāni tathaiva tvaṃ naivaṃ māṃ vaktumarhasi \|\| 8 \|\|*

6-8. Kacha said: — “Your father, being my preceptor, is just like my own father and commands my respect and honour. Similarly you, too, being the daughter of my preceptor and the beloved of Bhargava (Shukra), are worthy of being venerated and adored by me. Your father, the sage Shukra, is my venerable preceptor, consequently it does not behoove you to make any such proposal to me because you are to be honored as a daughter of my guru and therefore should be honored as my guru.”

## \|\| 26.9-11 \|\|

*devayānyuvāca*  
*guruputrasya putro me na tu tvamasi me pituḥ \|*  
*tasmānmānyaśca pūjyaśca mamāpi tvaṃ dvijottama \|\| 9 \|\|*

*asurairhanyamāne tu kace tvayi punaḥ punaḥ \|*  
*tadāprabhṛti yā prītis tāṃ tvameva smarasva me \|\| 10 \|\|*

*sauhārde cānurāge ca vettha me bhaktimuttamām \|*  
*na māmarhasi dharmajña tyaktuṃ bhaktāmanāgasam \|\| 11 \|\|*

9-11. Devayani said: — “You are the son of Brihaspati and not of my father; and consequently you are worthy of being respected and honored by me. You must recall to your mind my unceasing warm love for you ever since you were killed by the Asuras again and again. Is not this a sufficient proof of my unbounded love, attachment and devotion towards you. I, therefore, O You, who know the law, your devotee, do not deserve being discarded by you.”

## \|\| 26.12-16 \|\|

*kaca uvāca*  
*aniyojye niyoge māṃ niunakṣi śubhavrate \|*  
*prasīda subhrūrmahyaṃ tvaṃ guror gurutarā śubhe \|\| 12 \|\|*

*yatroṣitaṃ viśālākṣi tvayā candranibhānane \|*  
*tatrāhamuṣito bhadre kukṣau kāvyasya bhāmini \|\| 13 \|\|*

*bhaginī dharmato me tvaṃ maivaṃ vocaḥ śubhānane \|*  
*sukhenādhyuṣito bhadre na manyurvidyate mama \|\| 14 \|\|*

*āpṛcche tvāṃ gamiṣyāmi śivamastvatha me pathi \|*  
*avirodhena dharmasya smartavyo 'smi kathāntare \|*  
*apramattodyatā nityam ārādhaya guruṃ mama \|\| 15 \|\|*

*devayānyuvāca*  
*daityairhatastvaṃ yadbhartṛ-buddhyā tvaṃ rakṣito mayā \|*  
*yadi māṃ dharmakāmārthaṃ pratyākhyāsyasi dharmataḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

12-16. Kacha said: — O, Pious one! You ask me to enter into an engagement which is so improper. You are greater even than the preceptor. Be pleased, O moon-faced! I have also lived in the stomach of Shukra where you had also lived; in this way you are lawfully my sister. I passed my days in comfort here. I have committed no fault, am not angry with you at your illegal proposal, Now I take leave of you; wish me a happy journey. You may think of me in connection with anything which hay be in conformity with Dharma. You should always adore my preceptor with constant attention.”

## \|\| 26.17 \|\|

*tataḥ kaca na te vidyā siddhimeṣā gamiṣyati \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Devayani said: — “I rescued you, with the idea of making you my husband, when you were killed by the Asuras. Now as you are abandoning me who makes a lawful request, you will not be able to successfully apply this sanjivani knowledge.”

## \|\| 26.18-21 \|\|

*kaca uvāca*  
*guruputrīti kṛtvāhaṃ pratyākhyāsye na doṣataḥ \|*  
*guruṇā cābhyanujñātaḥ kāmameva śapasva mām \|\| 18 \|\|*

*ārṣaṃ dharmaṃ bruvāṇo 'haṃ devayāni yathā tvayā \|*  
*śaptuṃ nārho 'smi kalyāṇi kāmato 'dya ca dharmataḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

*tasmādbhavatyā yaḥ kāmo na tathā sambhaviṣyati \|*  
*ṛṣiputro na te kaścij jātu pāṇiṃ grahīṣyati \|\| 20 \|\|*

*phaliṣyati na me vidyā tvadvacaśceti tattayā \|*  
*adhyāpayiṣyāmi ca yaṃ tasya vidyā phaliṣyati \|\| 21 \|\|*

18-21. Kacha said: — “Why are you pronouncing such a curse on me? I am going away with the permission of my preceptor and have not accepted you, on account of your being the daughter of my preceptor, and not in consideration of there being any fault in you. Devayani! You ought not to curse me who has only expounded the Law of the Rishis to you \[for according to that Law, our marriage would be illegal\]. Because you have cursed me, you will never be able to gain your desire. No son of a Rishi will ever accept you as his wife. My sanjivani knowledge will, of course, not be fruitful to me on account of your curse, but it will most decidedly hear fruit to one to whom I shall impart it.”

## \|\| 26.22-24 \|\|

*śaunaka uvāca*  
*evamuktvā nṛpaśreṣṭha devayānīṃ kacastadā \|*  
*tridaśeśālayaṃ śīghraṃ jagāma dvijasattamaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*tamāgatamabhiprekṣya devāḥ sendrapurogamāḥ \|*  
*bṛhaspatiṃ sabhājyedaṃ kacamāhurmudānvitāḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

*devā ūcuḥ*  
*tvaṃ kacāsmaddhitaṃ karma kṛtavānmahadadbhutam \|*  
*na te yaśaḥ praṇaśitā bhāgabhākca bhaviṣyasi \|\| 24 \|\|*

22-24. Shaunaka said: — Kacha, after thus addressing Devayani, instantly went to heaven, where Indra and other Devas finding him returned said to him: — “Kacha! You have done a great deed for our sake; consequently your fame will never diminish; it will diffuse all round.”

## Chapter 27

## \|\| 27.1-4 \|\|

*śaunaka uvāca*  
*kṛtavidye kace prāpte hṛṣṭarūpā divaukasaḥ \|*  
*kacādavetya tāṃ vidyāṃ kṛtārthā bharatarṣabha \|\| 1 \|\|*

*sarva eva samāgamya śatakratumathābruvan \|*  
*kālastvadvikramasyādya jahi śatrūnpuraṃdara \|\| 2 \|\|*

*evamuktastu saha tais tridaśair maghavāṃstadā \|*  
*tathetyuktvopacakrāma so 'paṣyadvipine striyaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*krīḍantīnāṃ tu kanyānāṃ vane caitrarathopame \|*  
*vāurbhūtaḥ sa vastrāṇi sarvāṇyeva vyamiśrayat \|\| 4 \|\|*

1-4. Shaunaka said: — The Devas, on seeing Kacha back with sanjivani knowledge, accorded him a most cordial welcome, and after acquiring that supreme knowledge from him, became highly satisfied; and then having approached Indra, said thus: — ‘‘ To-day is the time to show valor, kill thy enemies, O Purandara.” Accepting the request of the Devas, the Maghavan, along with them, set out on his mission and, in the way, He came across a group of women in the forest. He saw those damsels bathing and enjoying themselves, as they do in the pleasure-garden of Kuvera, Then Indra, in the form of a gust of wind, blew away and mixed up their garments.

## \|\| 27.5-6 \|\|

*tato jalāt samuttīrya tāḥ kanyāḥ sahitāstadā \|*  
*vastrāṇi jagṛhustāni yathāsaṃsthānyanekaśaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*tatra vāso devayānyāḥ śarmiṣṭhā jagṛhe tadā \|*  
*vyatikramamajānantī duhitā vṛṣaparvaṇaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. At that, all the maidens, hastily coming out of water, dressed themselves with the clothes as they found them. In that hurry-scurry, Sharmishtha, the daughter of Vrishaparvan put on the clothes of Devayani through oversight, at which, there ensued a quarrel between the two — Sharmishtha and Devayani.

## \|\| 27.7 \|\|

*tatastayor mithastatra virodhaḥ samajāyata \|*  
*devayānyāśca rājendra śarmiṣṭhāyāśca tatkṛte \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Devayani, in a fit of rage, said: “O daughter of an Asura! You being my father’s disciple, how dare you put on my garments. You will never prosper on account of your ignorance of laws of good conduct.”

## \|\| 27.8-11 \|\|

*devayānyuvāca*  
*kasmādgṛhṇāsi me vastraṃ śiṣyā bhūtvā mamāsuri \|*  
*samudācārahīnāyā na te śreyo bhaviṣyati \|\| 8 \|\|*

*śarmiṣṭhovāca*  
*āsīnaṃ ca śayānaṃ ca pitā te pitaraṃ mama \|*  
*stauti pṛcchati cābhīkṣṇaṃ nīcasthaḥ suvinītavat \|\| 9 \|\|*

*yācatastvaṃ ca duhitā stuvataḥ pratigṛhṇataḥ \|*  
*sutāhaṃ stūyamānasya dadato na tu gṛhṇataḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*anāudhā sāudhāyāḥ kiṃ tvaṃ kupyasi bhikṣuki \|*  
*lapsyase pratiyoddhāraṃ na ca tvāṃ gaṇayāmyaham \|\| 11 \|\|*

8-11. Sharmishtha said: “Your father sits and sleeps at-the command of my father; he praises him and asks and answers questions put by my father from his throne, while your father sits humbly on lower seat. You are the daughter of a father who always begs, sings panegyrics and receives gifts.

from my father: whilst I am the daughter of one who is always praised, is the giver of gifts, but accept no gifts from any one. You beggar! I do not care a straw for you. How dare you unarmed, show your wrath to me who is armed?”

## \|\| 27.12 \|\|

*śaunaka uvāca*  
*sā vismayaṃ devayānīṃ gatāṃ saktāṃ ca vāsasi \|*  
*śarmiṣṭhā prākṣipatkūpe tataḥ svapuramāviśat \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Shaunaka said: — Saying so, Sharmishtha put on her garments. Afterwards she threw the astonished and bewildered Devayani into a well and then returned to her palace.

## \|\| 27.13 \|\|

*hateyamiti vijñāya śarmiṣṭhā pāpaniścayā \|*  
*anavekṣya yayau tasmāt krodhavegaparāyaṇā \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Thus Sharmishtha, after committing such a sinful act and taking Devayani to be killed, and not waiting for her, returned home full of wrath

## \|\| 27.14-18 \|\|

*atha taṃ deśamabhyāgād yayātirnahuṣātmajaḥ \|*  
*śrāntaugyaḥ śrāntarūpo mṛgalipsuḥ pipāsitaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*nāhuṣiḥ prekṣamāṇo hi sa nipāne gatodake \|*  
*dadarśa kanyāṃ tāṃ tatra dīptāmagniśikhām iva \|\| 15 \|\|*

*tāmapṛcchatsa dṛṣṭvaiva kanyāmamaravarṇinīm \|*  
*sāntvayitvā nṛpaśreṣṭhaḥ sāmnā paramavalgunā \|\| 16 \|\|*

*kā tvaṃ cārumukhī śyāmā sumṛṣṭamaṇikuṇḍalā \|*  
*dīrghaṃ dhyāyasi cātyarthaṃ kasmācchvasiṣi cāturā \|\| 17 \|\|*

*kathaṃ ca patitā hy asmin kūpe vīruttṛṇāvṛte \|*  
*duhitā caiva kasya tvaṃ vada sarvaṃ sumadhyame \|\| 18 \|\|*

14-18. After that, Yayati, the son of Nahusha, getting tired and thirsty in course of his shoot, went to drink water at the same well. As soon as that thirsty monarch: peeped into the well, he saw a beauty, gleaming like the flame of fire, inside it. On seeing that girl of Divine form and consoling her, that best of kings, said in words full of sweetness: — “O young beauty, adorned with ornaments, how and for what reason, have you fallen into this well covered with grass? Whose daughter are you? Tell me all this”.

## \|\| 27.19-21 \|\|

*devayānyuvāca*  
*yo 'sau devairhatān daityān utthāpayati vidyayā \|*  
*tasya śukrasya kanyāhaṃ tvaṃ māṃ nūnaṃ na budhyase \|\| 19 \|\|*

*eṣa me dakṣiṇo rājan pāṇis tāmranakhāṅguliḥ \|*  
*samuddhara gṛhītvā māṃ kulīnastvaṃ hi me mataḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*jānāmi tvāṃ ca saṃśāntaṃ vīryavantaṃ yaśasvinam \|*  
*tasmānmāṃ patitāṃ kūpād asmād uddhartumarhasi \|\| 21 \|\|*

19-21. Devayani replied: “I am the daughter of that Shukra who, through his science, restores the Daityas to life, when they are killed by the Gods. You do not know me full well. King! Catch hold of my right hand with its fingers decked with copper-coloured nails and pull me out of this well; I know you are of noble birth. I know you to be self-controlled, Strong, and illustrious; therefore I know you are capable of delivering me from this well.”

## \|\| 27.22-23 \|\|

*śaunaka uvāca*  
*tāmatha brāhmaṇīṃ strīṃ ca vijñāya nahuṣātmajaḥ \|*  
*gṛhītvā dakṣiṇe pāṇāv udjahāra tato 'vaṭāt \|\| 22 \|\|*

*uddhṛtya caināṃ tarasā tasmātkūpānnarādhipaḥ \|*  
*āmantrayitvā suśroṇīṃ yayātiḥ svapuraṃ yayau \|\| 23 \|\|*

22-23. Shaunaka said. — King Yayati, knowing her to be of the Brahmana caste and also & woman, caught hold of her night hand, and by his force pulled her out of the well. After that, the king saluted and welcomed Devayani and returned to his metropolis,

## \|\| 27.24-25 \|\|

*gate tu nāhuṣe tasmin devayānyapi ninditā \|*  
*uvāca śokasaṃtaptā ghūrṇikāmāgatāṃ punaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*devayānyuvāca*  
*tvaritaṃ ghūrṇike gaccha sarvamācakṣva me pituḥ \|*  
*nedānīṃ tu pravekṣyāmi nagaraṃ vṛṣaparvaṇaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

24-25. Devayani, thus abused and. full of sorrow, commanded her maid, Ghurnika, “who had returned in search of her, thus: — “go quickly, O Ghurnika, and acquaint my father with all that has happened, and also tell him that I have made up my mind not to enter the King Vrishaparvan’s city.”

## \|\| 27.26-27 \|\|

*śaunaka uvāca*  
*sā tu vai tvaritaṃ gatvā ghūrṇikāsuramandiram \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā kāvyamuvācedaṃ kampamānā vicetanā \|\| 26 \|\|*

*ācakhyau ca mahābhāgā devayānī vane hatā \|*  
*śarmiṣṭhayā mahāprājña duhitrā vṛṣaparvaṇaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

26-27. Shaunaka said. — Ghurnika instantly repaired to the palace of the Asura and seeing the high priest Shukra there, said to him trembling and confusedly: — “Sage! Sharmishtha, the daughter of King Vrishaparvan, has injured Devayani.”

## \|\| 27.28 \|\|

*śrutvā duhitaraṃ kāvyas tadā śarmiṣṭhayā hatām \|*  
*tvarayā niryayau duḥkhān mārgamāṇaḥ sutāṃ vane \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Shukra on getting the ill tidings of her daughter being injured at the hands of Sharmishtha, was overwhelmed with grief and immediately started in quest of Devayani in the forest.

## \|\| 27.29-30 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā duhitaraṃ kāvyo devayānīṃ tapovane \|*  
*bāhubhyāṃ sampariṣvajya duḥkhito vākyamabravīt \|\| 29 \|\|*

*ātmadoṣair niyacchanti sarve duḥkhasukhe janāḥ \|*  
*manye duścaritaṃ te 'sti tasyeyaṃ niṣkṛtiḥ kṛtā \|\| 30 \|\|*

29-30. On meeting Devayani face to face in that forest, Shukra embraced her with open arms and sorrowfully said: “Every being reaps the harvest of pain and pleasure in this world, according to his actions; consequently, I look upon this affair, as Sharmishtha taking revenge upon you for some evil deed of yours”.

## \|\| 27.31-35 \|\|

*devayānyuvāca*  
*niṣkṛtir vāstu vā māstu śṛṇuṣvāvahito mama \|*  
*śarmiṣṭhayā yaduktāsmi duhitrā vṛṣaparvaṇaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

*satyaṃ kilaitatsā prāha daityānāmasmi gāyanā \|*  
*evaṃ hi me kathayati śarmiṣṭhā vārṣaparvaṇī \|\| 32 \|\|*

*vacanaṃ tīkṣṇaparuṣaṃ krodharaktekṣaṇā bhṛśam \|*  
*stuvato duhitāsi tvaṃ yācataḥ pratigṛhṇataḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

*sutāhaṃ stūyamānasya dadato 'pratigṛhṇataḥ \|*  
*iti māmāha śarmiṣṭhā duhitā vṛṣaparvaṇaḥ \|*  
*krodhasaṃraktanayanā darpapūrṇānanā tataḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

*yadyahaṃ stuvatastāta duhitā pratigṛhṇataḥ \|*  
*prasādayiṣye śarmiṣṭhām ityuktā hi sakhī mayā \|\| 35 \|\|*

31-35. Devayani said: “There may or may not have been a revenge; but listen to what the daughter of Vrishaparvan said.

Is it true, that I am merely a singer in the palace of the Daityas, for Sharmishtha, the daughter of Vrishaparvan tells me so. She, with harsh and sharp words and eyes red with anger, spoke: — ‘I am the daughter of a king, who is praised by thy father and who gives gifts to him, but accepts nothing from any body and whilst thou art the daughter of him who sings the praises of my father and begs and accepts gifts from him.’

Thus said Sharmishtha, the daughter Vrishaparvan, with eyes red with anger and face flushed with pride, Father, I then said to Sharmishtha that if I were the daughter of a panegyrist, and a beggar, I would also please her similarly.”

## \|\| 27.36-37 \|\|

*śukra uvāca*  
*stuvato duhitā na tvaṃ bhadre na pratigṛhṇataḥ \|*  
*atastvaṃ stūyamānasya duhitā devayānyasi \|\| 36 \|\|*

*vṛṣaparvaiva tadveda śakro rājā ca nāhuṣaḥ \|*  
*acintyaṃ brahma nirdvaṃdvam aiśvaraṃ hi balaṃ mama \|\| 37 \|\|*

36-37. Shukra said, “O child! thou art not the daughter of a panegyrist or of a beggar: on the other hand, thou art the daughter of one who is always praised by others, O Devayani. King Vrishaparvan knows that my pure, matchless and inconceivable spirituality is my power; so also know Indra and King Yayati.

## Chapter 28

## \|\| 28.1-7 \|\|

*śukra uvāca*  
*yaḥ pareṣāṃ naro nityam ativādāṃstitikṣati \|*  
*devayāni vijānīhi tena sarvamidaṃ jitam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*yaḥ samutpatitaṃ krodhaṃ nigṛhṇāti hayaṃ yathā \|*  
*sa yantetyucyate sadbhir na yo raśmiṣu lambate \|\| 2 \|\|*

*yaḥ samutpatitaṃ krodham akrodhane niyacchati \|*  
*devayāni vijānīhi tena sarvamidaṃ jitam \|\| 3 \|\|*

*yaḥ samutpatitaṃ kopaṃ kṣamayaiva nirasyati \|*  
*yathoragastvacaṃ jīrṇāṃ sa vai puruṣa ucyate \|\| 4 \|\|*

*yastu bhāvayate dharmaṃ yo 'timātraṃ titikṣati \|*  
*yaśca tapto na tapati bhṛśaṃ so 'rthasya bhājanam \|\| 5 \|\|*

*yo yajedaśvamedhena māsi māsi śataṃ samāḥ \|*  
*yastu kupyenna sarvasya tayorakrodhano varaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*ye kumārāḥ kumāryaśca vairaṃ kuryuracetasaḥ \|*  
*naitatprājñastu kurvīta viduste na balābalam \|\| 7 \|\|*

1-7. Shukra said. — “Devayani hear, one who calmly and patiently endures the hard speech of others, conquers all One, who curbs his rising anger, like a fiery steed, is called the real driver by the wise, and not he who merely holds the reins. One who conquers another's arising anger by not getting angry himself, conquers the universe Know this, O Devayani. One who throws aside the out bursting of his wrath by forgiveness, as a serpent discards its worn out skin, is said to be truly a man. One who hankers after virtue, always shows forbearance to all, and does not cause pain to others even after suffering great pain, is the receptacle of high and sublime merits. Between the one who performs many Ashvamedha sacrifices each month for hundreds of years, and the other who does ‘not get angry with any one, the latter is decidedly superior. As in childhood, boys and girls, through their folly become enemies, not do so the sensible, and after considering their power and the weakness of their foes, never entertain any feeling of enmity.”

## \|\| 28.8-13 \|\|

*devayānyuvāca*  
*vedāhaṃ tāta bālāpi kāryāṇāṃ tu gatāgatam \|*  
*krodhe caivātivāde vā kāryasyāpi balābale \|\| 8 \|\|*

*śiṣyasyāśiṣyavṛttaṃ hi na kṣantavyaṃ bubhūṣuṇā \|*  
*asatsaṃkīrṇavṛtteṣu vāso mama na rocate \|\| 9 \|\|*

*puṃso ye nābhinandanti vṛttenābhijanena ca \|*  
*na teṣu nivasetprājñaḥ śreyorthī pāpabuddhiṣu \|\| 10 \|\|*

*ye nainamabhijānanti vṛttenābhijanena ca \|*  
*teṣu sādhuṣu vastavyaṃ sa vāsaḥ śreṣṭha ucyate \|\| 11 \|\|*

*tanme mathnāti hṛdayam agnikalpamivāraṇam \|*  
*vāgduruktaṃ mahāghoraṃ duhiturvṛṣaparvaṇaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*na hy ato duṣkaraṃ manye tāta lokeṣvapi triṣu \|*  
*yaḥ sapatnaśriyaṃ dīptāṃ hīnaśrīḥ paryupāsate \|\| 13 \|\|*

8-13. Devayani said. — “Father! In spite of my girlhood, I know the causes and consequences of actions in the matter of anger, reproof and relative strength or weakness of acts. A sensible man should not tolerate an unbecoming action of his disciple. I have therefore no desire to live among people whose conscience is loaded with vice. A person desirous of his welfare and prosperity should not live among those vicious men who are not well spoken of, by men of character and position. People who are considered high, by men of character and position, are worthy of company. Consequently, the harsh words of Vrishaparvan's daughter are rubbing against my mind like Arani (the two pieces of wood used in kindling the sacred fire). Father! I do not think there is anything baser in the world than the adoration of an enemy, howsoever majestic he may be, by one who is in the humbler walk of life and is devoid of riches.”

## Chapter 29

## \|\| 29.1-6 \|\|

*śaunaka uvāca*  
*tataḥ kāvyo bhṛguśreṣṭhaḥ samanyurupagamya ha \|*  
*vṛṣaparvāṇam āsīnam ityuvācāvicārayan \|\| 1 \|\|*

*nādharmaścarito rājan sadyaḥ phalati gaur iva \|*  
*śanairāvartyamānastu mūlānyapi nikṛntati \|\| 2 \|\|*

*yadi nātmani putreṣu na cetpaṣyati naptṛṣu \|*  
*pāpamācaritaṃ karma trivargamativartate \|\| 3 \|\|*

*phalatyevaṃ dhruvaṃ pāpaṃ gurubhuktamivodare \|*  
*yadā ghātayase vipraṃ kacamāṅgirasaṃ tadā \|\| 4 \|\|*

*apāpaśīlaṃ dharmajñaṃ śuśrūṣuṃ madgṛhe ratam \|*  
*vadhādanarhatastasya vadhācca duhiturmama \|\| 5 \|\|*

*vṛṣaparvannibodha tvaṃ tyakṣyāmi tvāṃ sabāndhavam \|*  
*sthātuṃ tvadviṣaye rājan na śaknomi tvayā saha \|\| 6 \|\|*

1-6. Shaunaka said: — On hearing those words of Devayani, Shukra the best of the Bhrigus also got angry and going to the King Vrishaparvan who was sitting on his throne spoke to him without caring for the consequences.

“King! a sinful act does not instantly fructify, but is like a cow which does not give birth at once after (conception). A sin is sure to produce its fruit, just like a heavy meal to produce colic in the stomach, not at once but after sometime. In process of time it entirely roots out the sinner. He who overlooks his own faults or those of his sons, and grandsons, etc., loses his Trivarga, the three objects of worldly existence, viz., Artha (riches or worldly prosperity), Dharma (religion), Kama (enjoyments). You are sure to reap the fruit of your sin of killing the grandson of Angirasa and son of Brihaspati, and then causing his remains to be deposited in my stomach by mixing them with my wine.

King! on account of your having killed my disciple, who was sinless, chaste, submissive and unworthy of being slain, as well as for the injury done to my daughter, I leave you along with your kinsmen. I do not consider it proper to stay in your empire any more. As you do not heed the actions of your vicious and proud daughter, I consider you from today a Daitya who talks much but does not think of keeping his promises; thou thinkest me, O Daitya! censurable and a talker of falsehoods.”

## \|\| 29.7-9 \|\|

*adyaivamabhijānāmi daityaṃ mithyāpralāpinam \|*  
*yatastvamātmanodīrṇāṃ duhitāṃ kimupekṣase \|\| 7 \|\|*

*vṛṣaparvovāca*  
*nāvadyaṃ na mṛṣāvādaṃ tvayi jānāmi bhārgava \|*  
*tvayi satyaṃ ca dharmaśca tatprasīdatu māṃ bhavān \|\| 8 \|\|*

*adyāsmānapahāya tvam ito yāsyasi bhārgava \|*  
*samudraṃ sampravekṣyāmi nānyadasti parāyaṇam \|\| 9 \|\|*

7-9. Vrishaparvan said: — "Bhargava! I do not consider you as censurable or a talker of falsehood because I am so well aware of your truth and asceticism; therefore be pleased with me. Excepting you, none can protect me; and if you are going to leave me today, I will drown myself in the ocean, for there is no other refuge for me.’

## \|\| 29.10-11 \|\|

*śukra uvāca*  
*samudraṃ praviśadhvaṃ vo diśo vā vrajatāsurāḥ \|*  
*duhiturnāpriyaṃ soḍhuṃ śakto 'haṃ dayitā hi me \|\| 10 \|\|*

*prasādyatāṃ devayānī jīvitaṃ yatra me sthitam \|*  
*yogakṣemakaraste 'ham indrasyeva bṛhaspatiḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

10-11. Shukra said: — “You may either drown yourself in the ocean or roam about in the world, my daughter is very dear to me, and I cannot make her feel hurt. You should please Devayani. ‘I shall settle down with her wherever she goes. If you will please her, I shall guard you as Brihaspati does Indra and other Devas.”

## \|\| 29.12 \|\|

*vṛṣaparvovāca*  
*yatkiṃcid asurendrāṇāṃ vidyate vasu bhārgava \|*  
*bhuvi hastirathāśvaṃ vā tasya tvaṃ mama ceśvaraḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Vrishaparvan said: — “Bhargava! you are the master of elephants, chariots, horses and all the riches of the Asuras; and, similarly, you are, the master of all my wealth and belongings.”

## \|\| 29.13 \|\|

*śukra uvāca*  
*yatkiṃcid asti draviṇaṃ daityendrāṇāṃ mahāsura \|*  
*tasyeśvaro 'smi yadyetad devayānī prasādyatām \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Shukra said: — “King of Asuras! I will consider myself the master of the Daityas then only when you please Devayani and not otherwise.”

## \|\| 29.14 \|\|

*śaunaka uvāca*  
*tatastu tvaritaḥ śukras tena rājñā samaṃ yayau \|*  
*uvāca caināṃ subhage pratipannaṃ vacastava \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Shaunaka said: — Hearing that, Shukra went to Devayani along with Vrishaparvana and said to her: — “Now thy words are realized, for I am considered as lord of all.”’

## \|\| 29.15 \|\|

*devayānyuvāca*  
*yadi tvamīśvarastāta rājño vittasya bhārgava \|*  
*nābhijānāmi tatte 'haṃ rājā vadatu māṃ svayam \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Devayani said: — “If, O Father! thou art the lord of the king's wealth then I will believe it if the king himself says so to me.”

## \|\| 29.16 \|\|

*vṛṣaparvovāca*  
*yaṃ kāmamabhijānāsi devayāni śucismite \|*  
*tatte 'haṃ sampradāsyāmi yadyapi syātsudurlabham \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Vrishaparvan said: — “Devayani! I shall fulfil your desires, howsoever difficult they may be.”

## \|\| 29.17 \|\|

*devayānyuvāca*  
*dāsīṃ kanyāsahasreṇa śarmiṣṭhāmabhikāmaye \|*  
*anuyāsyati māṃ tatra yatra dāsyati me pitā \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Devayani said: — “When you promise to fulfil my desires, I wish Sharmishtha to be my maid, with a thousand damsels; and she should go with me wherever my father may please to marry me”.

## \|\| 29.18 \|\|

*vṛṣaparvovāca*  
*uttiṣṭha dhātri gaccha tvaṃ śarmiṣṭhāṃ śīghramānaya \|*  
*yaṃ ca kāmayate kāmaṃ devayānī karotu tam \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Vrishaparvan said: — “O Nurse, get up, go and bring Sharmishtha once in my presence. I shall do exactly as Devayani desires”.

## \|\| 29.19-20 \|\|

*śaunaka uvāca*  
*tato dhātrī tatra gatvā śarmiṣṭhām idamabravīt \|*  
*uttiṣṭha bhadre śarmiṣṭhe jñātīnāṃ sukhamāvaha \|\| 19 \|\|*

*tyajati brāhmaṇaḥ śiṣyān devayānyā pracoditaḥ \|*  
*yaṃ sā kāmayate kāmaṃ sa kāryo 'tra tvayānaghe \|*  
*dāsītvam abhijātāsi devayānyāḥ suśobhane \|\| 20 \|\|*

19-20. Shaunaka said: — On being thus commanded by the king, the nurse at once went to Sharmishtha and told her O Sharmishtha! get up and save your kinsmen from impending calamity; because incited by his daughter, Shukra is forsaking his disciples and the fulfilment of Devayani’s desires rests on you. Yon have become the maid of Devayani.”

## \|\| 29.21 \|\|

*śarmiṣṭhovāca*  
*yaṃ ca kāmayate kāmaṃ karavāṇyahamadya tam \|*  
*mā gānmanyuvaśaṃ śukro devayānī ca matkṛte \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Sharmishtha said: “I shall do what she wants, let Shukra not go away in a fit of anger nor Devayani get offended at what I have done”.

## \|\| 29.22-23 \|\|

*śaunaka uvāca*  
*tataḥ kanyāsahasreṇa vṛtā śibikayā tadā \|*  
*piturnideśāttvaritā niścakrāma purottamāt \|\| 22 \|\|*

*śarmiṣṭhovāca*  
*ahaṃ kanyāsahasreṇa dāśī te paricārikā \|*  
*dhruvaṃ tvāṃ tatra yāsyāmi yatra dāsyati te pitā \|\| 23 \|\|*

22-23. Shaunaka said: — Then at the behest of her father Sharmishtha in a palanquin went to Devayani along with a thousand maids; and said, “Devayani! I have come with a thousand maids to serve you and shall accompany you wherever you go, after being married by your father.”

## \|\| 29.24 \|\|

*devayānyuvāca*  
*stuvato duhitā cāhaṃ yācataḥ pratigṛhṇataḥ \|*  
*stūyamānasya duhitā kathaṃ dāsī bhaviṣyasi \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Devayani said: — “I am the daughter of a panegyrist, one who begs and receives, how then do you, who are the daughter of one praised, serve me as my maid?”

## \|\| 29.25 \|\|

*śarmiṣṭhovāca*  
*yena kenacidārtānāṃ jñātīnāṃ sukhamāvahet \|*  
*anuyāsyāmyahaṃ tatra yatra dāsyati te pitā \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Sharmishtha said: — “It is my bounden duty to do that which may bring relief to my distressed kinsmen: consequently I shall follow you as your maid, and will also accompany you after your marriage wherever your father may wed your”.

## \|\| 29.26-27 \|\|

*śaunaka uvāca*  
*pratiśrute dāsabhāve duhitrā vṛṣaparvaṇaḥ \|*  
*devayānī nṛpaśreṣṭha pitaraṃ vākyamabravīt \|\| 26 \|\|*

*devayānyuvāca*  
*praviśāmi puraṃ tāta tuṣṭāsmi dvijasattama \|*  
*amoghaṃ tava vijñānam asti vidyābalaṃ ca te \|\| 27 \|\|*

26-27. Shaunaka said: — “After the daughter of Vrishaparvan made up her mind to serve Devayani as her maid, the latter said to her father: —

“Father! I am satisfied: Indeed, the power of thy knowledge and wisdom is infallible and fruitful. I shall now enter the city.”

## \|\| 29.28 \|\|

*śaunaka uvāca*  
*evamukto dvijaśreṣṭho duhitrā sumahāyaśāḥ \|*  
*praviveśa puraṃ hṛṣṭaḥ pūjitaḥ sarvadānavaiḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Hearing those words of his daughter, Shukra, worshipped by the Danavas, cheerfully entered the town.

## Chapter 30

## \|\| 30.1-8 \|\|

*śaunaka uvāca*  
*atha dīrgheṇa kālena devayānī nṛpottama \|*  
*vanaṃ tadaiva niryātā krīḍārthaṃ varavarṇinī \|\| 1 \|\|*

*tena dāsīsahasreṇa sārdhaṃ śarmiṣṭhayā tadā \|*  
*tameva deśaṃ samprāptā yathākāmaṃ cacāra sā \|\| 2 \|\|*

*tābhiḥ sakhībhiḥ sahitā sarvābhirmuditā bhṛśam \|*  
*krīḍantyo 'bhiratāḥ sarvāḥ pibantyo madhu mādhavam \|\| 3 \|\|*

*khādantyo vividhānbhakṣyān phalāni vividhāni ca \|*  
*punaśca nāhuṣo rājā mṛgalipsuryadṛcchayā \|\| 4 \|\|*

*tameva deśaṃ samprāpto jalalipsuḥ pratarṣitaḥ \|*  
*dadarśa devayānīṃ ca śarmiṣṭhāṃ tāśca yoṣitaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*pibantyo lalanāstāśca divyābharaṇabhūṣitāḥ \|*  
*upaviṣṭāṃ ca dadṛśe devayānīṃ śucismitām \|\| 6 \|\|*

*rūpeṇāpratimāṃ tāsāṃ strīṇāṃ madhye varāṅganām \|*  
*śarmiṣṭhayā sevyamānāṃ pādasaṃvāhanādibhiḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*yayātiruvāca*  
*dvābhyāṃ kanyāsahasrābhyāṃ dve kanye parivārite \|*  
*gotre ca nāmanī caiva dvayoḥ pṛcchāmyato hy aham \|\| 8 \|\|*

1-8. Shaunaka said: — O king! Long after that, Devayani again went to amuse herself in the same forest in the company of Sharmishtha and a thousand maids. Whilst she, along with her companions was thus amusing herself there by drinking wine and eating various victuals and fruits, King Yayati, also chanced to visit the same forest with the object of enjoying a shoot, and feeling thirsty whilst he was in search of water, he saw Devayani and Sharmishtha along with other women folk drinking. Among them he marked Devayani, the beautiful, who, wearing lovely ornaments, was sitting, attended by Sharmishtha and other maids. Then King Yayati said: “Two of you are charming beauties horizoned by two thousand women. I request you to please tell me your names and clan.”

## \|\| 30.9-10 \|\|

*devayānyuvāca*  
*ākhyāsyāmyaham ādatsva vacanaṃ me narādhipa \|*  
*śuko nāmāsuraguruḥ sutāṃ jānīhi tasya mām \|\| 9 \|\|*

*iyaṃ ca me sakhī dāsī yatrāhaṃ tatra gāminī \|*  
*duhitā dānavendrasya śarmiṣṭhā vṛṣaparvaṇaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. Devayani replied: — “King! Hear what I say. Tam the daughter of the Sage Shukra who is preceptor of the Asuras and she is my maid-in-chief, Sharmishtha, the daughter of Vrisaparvan, the mighty king of the Danavas. She always accompanies me wherever I go.”

## \|\| 30.11 \|\|

*yayātiruvāca*  
*kathaṃ tu te sakhī dāsī kanyeyaṃ varavarṇinī \|*  
*asurendrasutā subhūḥ paraṃ kautūhalaṃ hi me \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Yayati, who was astonished to hear that, enquired how that daughter of the king of the Asuras came to be her maid-in-chief.

## \|\| 30.12-13 \|\|

*devayānyuvāca*  
*sarvameva naravyāghra vidhānamanuvartate \|*  
*vidhinā vihitaṃ jñātvā mā vicitraṃ manaḥ kṛthāḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*rājavadrūpaveṣau te brāhmīṃ vācaṃ bibharṣi ca \|*  
*kiṃnāmā tvaṃ kutaścāsi kasya putraśca śaṃsa me \|\| 13 \|\|*

12-13. Devayani said: — Do not be astonished. All this has been ordained by Brahma. You look like a king from your bearing and sweet and dignified speech. Tell me your name and parentage.”

## \|\| 30.14 \|\|

*yayātiruvāca*  
*brahmacaryeṇa vedo me kṛtsnaḥ śrutipathaṃ gataḥ \|*  
*rājāhaṃ rājaputraśca yayātiriti viśrutaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Yayati said: — “I have studied all the Vedas after leading a student's life, and I am King Yayati, the son of King Nahusha.”

## \|\| 30.15 \|\|

*devayānyuvāca*  
*kena cārthena nṛpate hy enaṃ deśaṃ samāgataḥ \|*  
*jighṛkṣurvāri yatkiṃcid athavā mṛgalipsayā \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Devayani said: — “King! What for have you come here — to drink water or to enjoy a shoot?”

## \|\| 30.16 \|\|

*yayātiruvāca*  
*mṛgalipsurahaṃ bhadre pānīyārtham ihāgataḥ \|*  
*bahudhāpyanuukto 'smi tvam anujñātumarhasi \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Yayati said: — “In course of my shoot I have happened to come to this spot to satisfy my thirst and am ready to obey your commands.’

## \|\| 30.17 \|\|

*devayānyuvāca*  
*dvābhyāṃ kanyāsahasrābhyāṃ dāsyā śarmiṣṭhayā saha \|*  
*tvadadhīnāsmi bhadraṃ te sakhe bhartā ca me bhava \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Devayani said: — “Friend! I am at your disposal with Sharmishtha and my retinue of maids, be my lord."

## \|\| 30.18 \|\|

*yayātiruvāca*  
*viddhyauśanasi bhadraṃ te na tvadarho 'smi bhāmini \|*  
*avivāhyāḥ sma rājāno devayāni pitustava \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Yayati said: — “Lady! You are the daughter of Shukra, who is a Brahmana, and consequently you cannot be wedded by a Kshatriya sovereign.”

## \|\| 30.19-20 \|\|

*devayānyuvāca*  
*saṃsṛṣṭaṃ brahmaṇā kṣatraṃ kṣatraṃ brahmaṇi saṃśritam \|*  
*ṛṣiśca ṛṣiputraśca nāhuṣādya bhajasva mām \|\| 19 \|\|*

*yayātiruvāca*  
*ekadehodbhavā varṇāś catvāro 'pi varānane \|*  
*pṛthagdharmāḥ pṛthakchaucās teṣāṃ vai brāhmaṇo varaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

19-20. Devayani said: — “King! the race of the Kshatriyas has been created by Brahma and is supported by him. O, son of Nahusha! you area sage; and also the son of a sage; by all means marry me.’

## \|\| 30.21-22 \|\|

*devayānyuvāca*  
*pāṇigraho nāhuṣāyaṃ na puṃbhiḥ sevitaḥ purā \|*  
*tvaṃ pāṇimagrahīdagre vṛṇomi tvāmahaṃ tataḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*kathaṃ tu me manasvinyāḥ pāṇimanyaḥ pumānspṛśet \|*  
*gṛhītamṛṣiputreṇa svayaṃ vāpyṛṣiṇā tvayā \|\| 22 \|\|*

21-22. Yayati said: — O, Lady! Though all the four castes have sprung from one and the same body of Brahma, vet their duties and rules of life are entirely different from one another, and a Brahmana is superior to Devayani said: — “O, son of Nahusha! this hand of mine has not been touched by any other person and you have once grasped it. I therefore choose you to be my partner in life. Who else can take my hand? You took me by the hand, because you are the son of a sage or because you are a sage yourself.”

## \|\| 30.23 \|\|

*yayātiruvāca*  
*kruddhādāśīviṣāt sarpāj jvalanātsarvatomukhāt \|*  
*durādharṣataro vipraḥ puruṣeṇa vijānatā \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Yayati said: — “The sages of hoary lore have said that a Brahmana is more formidable than the mouth of an angry venomous serpent and the raging fire.”

## \|\| 30.24 \|\|

*devayānyuvāca*  
*kathamāśīviṣāt sarpāj jvalanāt sarvatomukhāt \|*  
*durādharṣataro vipra ityāttha puruṣarṣabha \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Devayani said: — “O, Blessed one! How do you describe a Brahmana to be ‘more formidable than an angry venomous snake and the raging fire?”

## \|\| 30.25-26 \|\|

*yayātiruvāca*  
*daśedāśīviṣastvekaṃ śastreṇaikaśca vadhyate \|*  
*hanti vipraḥ sarāṣṭrāṇi purāṇyapi hi kopitaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*durādharṣataro vipras tasmādbhīru mato mama \|*  
*ato 'dattāṃ ca pitrā tvāṃ bhadre na vivahāmyaham \|\| 26 \|\|*

25-26. Yayati said: — “By the bite of a poisonous serpent and by the blow OF a weapon only one life is lost, but by the anger of a Brahmana the whole realm and country is devastated; this is my reason for having described a Brahmana as such, and I therefore cannot accept you in marriage without your father’s consent.

## \|\| 30.27 \|\|

*devayānyuvāca*  
*dattāṃ vahasva pitrā māṃ tvaṃ hi rājanvṛto mayā \|*  
*ayācato bhayaṃ nāsti dattāṃ ca pratigṛhṇataḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Devayani said: — “King! When my father gives me away to you of his own accord, you will then accept me as yours, You cannot beg, know: and consequently I have accepted yon as my lord; now there is no question of receiving on your part.”

## \|\| 30.28-29 \|\|

*śaunaka uvāca*  
*tvaritaṃ devayānyātha preṣitā piturātmanaḥ \|*  
*sarvaṃ nivedayāmāsa dhātrī tasmai yathātatham \|\| 28 \|\|*

*śrutvaiva ca sa rājānaṃ darśayāmāsa bhārgavaḥ \|*  
*dṛṣṭvaivam āgataṃ vipraṃ yayātiḥ pṛthivīpatiḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

28-29. Shaunaka said. — After that, the nurse, deputed by Devayani, went and explained all that to Shukra. Shukra on hearing that went to the king, and both of them were pleased to meet each other.

## \|\| 30.30 \|\|

*vavande brāhmaṇaṃ kāvyaṃ prāñjaliḥ praṇataḥ sthitaḥ \|*  
*taṃ cāpyabhyavadatkāvyaḥ sāmnā paramavalgunā \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. The king, seeing Shukra, saluted him with folded hands; and the latter also spoke to him mildly and sweetly.

## \|\| 30.31 \|\|

*devayānyuvāca*  
*rājāyaṃ nāhuṣastāta durgame pāṇimagrahīt \|*  
*namaste dehi māmasmai loke nānyaṃ patiṃ vṛṇe \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. See Devayani said to her father that the King Yayati had once grasped her hand, when she was in great difficulty and be should, therefore, dedicate her to him, and that she would marry no one excepting him.

## \|\| 30.32 \|\|

*śukra uvāca*  
*vṛto 'nayā patirvīra sutayā tvaṃ mameṣṭayā \|*  
*gṛhāṇemāṃ mayā dattāṃ mahiṣīṃ nahuṣātmaja \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Shukra then said to Yayati, that he had been chosen by her daughter before, whom he should accept as his queen after being willingly made over to him by her father.

## \|\| 30.33 \|\|

*yayātiruvāca*  
*adharmo māṃ spṛśedevaṃ pāpam asyāśca bhārgava \|*  
*varṇasaṃkarato brahmann iti tvāṃ pravṛṇomyaham \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Yayati said: — “Bhargava: By such deeds, I fear, I will commit a sin therefore beseech you to parry off the sin of creating a confusion of castes by such intermarriage.”

## \|\| 30.34-36 \|\|

*śukra uvāca*  
*adharmāttvāṃ vimuñcāmi varaṃ varaya cepsitam \|*  
*asminvivāhe tvaṃ ślāghyo rahaḥ pāpaṃ nudāmi te \|\| 34 \|\|*

*vahasva bhāryāṃ dharmeṇa devayānīṃ śucismitām \|*  
*anayā saha samprītim atulāṃ samavāpnuhi \|\| 35 \|\|*

*iyaṃ cāpi kumārī te śarmiṣṭhā vārṣaparvaṇī \|*  
*saṃpūjyā satataṃ rājan na caināṃ śayane hvaya \|\| 36 \|\|*

34-36. Shukra Said: — “I shall free you from all sins, “Accept this gift chosen by her. You will become laudable by this marriage; I free you from the future sin; marry this amiable Devayani, according to law and have every, enjoyment in her company; this Sharmishtha the daughter of Vrishaparvan, will attend on you, and you should never invite her to your bed

## \|\| 30.37 \|\|

*śaunaka uvāca*  
*evamukto yayātistu śukraṃ kṛtvā pradakṣiṇam \|*  
*jagāma svapuraṃ hṛṣṭaḥ so 'nujñāto mahātmanā \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Shaunaka said: — On hearing those words of the Seer Shukra that king circumambulated the latter, and with his permission entered his city with great rejoicings.

## Chapter 31

## \|\| 31.1-5 \|\|

*śaunaka uvāca*  
*yayātiḥ svapuraṃ prāpya mahendrapurasaṃnibham \|*  
*praviśyāntaḥpuraṃ tatra devayānīṃ nyaveśayat \|\| 1 \|\|*

*devayānyāścānumate sutāṃ tāṃ vṛṣaparvaṇaḥ \|*  
*aśokavanikābhyāśe gṛhaṃ kṛtvā nyaveśayat \|\| 2 \|\|*

*vṛtāṃ dāsīsahasreṇa śarmiṣṭhām āsurāyaṇīm \|*  
*vāsobhirannapānaiśca saṃvibhajya susaṃvṛtām \|\| 3 \|\|*

*devayānyā tu sahitaḥ sa nṛpo nahuṣātmajaḥ \|*  
*vijahāra bahūnabdān devavanmudito bhṛśam \|\| 4 \|\|*

*ṛtukāle tu samprāpte devayānī varāṅganā \|*  
*lebhe garbhaṃ prathamataḥ kumāraśca vyajāyata \|\| 5 \|\|*

1-5. Shaunaka said: — Yayati entered his capital, which was as beautiful as the city of Indra He then ushered Devayani into his palace and, according to the advice of the queen, located Sharmishtha, the daughter of King Vrishaparvan, in a separate house in Ashokavana. Thus Sharmishtha, along with her retinue of a thousand maids, was separated after being provided with clothes, provisions, and ornaments. Then that son of King Nahusha enjoyed himself like the Devas, in the company of Devayani, for a great number of years. In the fullness of time, Devayani conceived, and after ten mouths gave birth to a child.

## \|\| 31.6-13 \|\|

*gate varṣasahasre tu śarmiṣṭhā vārṣaparvaṇī \|*  
*dadarśa yauvanaṃ prāptā ṛtuṃ sā kamalekṣaṇā \|\| 6 \|\|*

*cintayāmāsa dharmajñā ṛtuprāptau ca bhāminī \|*  
*ṛtukālaśca samprāpto na kaścinme patirvṛtaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*kiṃ prāptaṃ kiṃca kartavyaṃ kathaṃ kṛtvā sukhaṃ bhavet \|*  
*devayānī prasūtāsau vṛthāhaṃ prāptayauvanā \|\| 8 \|\|*

*yathā tayā vṛto bhartā tathaivāhaṃ vṛṇomi tam \|*  
*rājñā putraphalaṃ deyam iti me niścitā matiḥ \|*  
*apīdānīṃ sa dharmātmā raho me darśanaṃ vrajet \|\| 9 \|\|*

*śaunaka uvāca*  
*atha niṣkramya rājāsau tasminkāle yadṛcchayā \|*  
*aśokavanikābhyāśe śarmiṣṭhāṃ prāpya vismitaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*tamekaṃ rahasi dṛṣṭvā śarmiṣṭhā cāruhāsinī \|*  
*pratyudgamyāñjaliṃ kṛtvā rājānaṃ vākyamabravīt \|\| 11 \|\|*

*śarmiṣṭhovāca*  
*somaścendraśca vāuśca yamaśca varuṇaśca vā \|*  
*tava vā nāhuṣa gṛhe kaḥ striyaṃ draṣṭumarhati \|\| 12 \|\|*

*rūpābhijanaśīlairhi tvaṃ rājanvettha māṃ sadā \|*  
*sā tvāṃ yāce prasādyeha rantumehi narādhipa \|\| 13 \|\|*

6-13. After a thousand years, Sharmishtha, the daughter of Vrishaparvan, when she was in her full bloom of youth, felt very sad on not having a husband. She said in her mind: “What will be meet for me to do? How am I to get happiness? Devayani has given birth to a son, but my youth is declining for nothing. T will also make the king mv husband, as she has done. I will request the king to give me a similar fruit in the shape of a son.” With these thoughts, she longed to see the king privately.

Now, at that time the King, coming out at pleasure, was astonished to meet Sharmishtha, outside the Ashokavana. Sharmishtha meeting the king in private, addressed him with folded hands: —

“King! Even Soma, Indra, Varuna and the wind are incapable of seeing the women in your palace. You know me to be a beauty, full of modesty and coming of good parents; I beseech you to enjoy my company.’

## \|\| 31.14-15 \|\|

*yayātiruvāca*  
*vedmi tvāṃ śīlasampannāṃ daityakanyāmaninditām \|*  
*rūpaṃ tu te na paśyāmi sūcyagramapi ninditam \|\| 14 \|\|*

*māmabravīttadā śukro devayānīṃ yadāvaham \|*  
*neyam āhvayitavyā te śayane vārṣaparvaṇī \|\| 15 \|\|*

14-15. Yayati replied: — “I know all thy qualifications. I know thou art the chaste daughter of the valiant king of the Daityas. Thou art modest, but I cannot look at thee with any feeling of lust, because at the time of Devayani’s marriage Shukra enjoined on me not to invite thee to my bed.”

## \|\| 31.16-17 \|\|

*śarmiṣṭhovāca*  
*na narmauktaṃ vacanaṃ hinasti na strīṣu rājan na vivāhakāle \|*  
*prāṇātyaye sarvadhanāpahāre pañcānṛtānyāhur apātakāni \|\| 16 \|\|*

*pṛṣṭāstu sākṣye pravadanti cānyathā bhavanti mithyāvacanā narendra te \|*  
*ekārthatāyāṃ tu samāhitāyāṃ mithyā vadantaṃ hy anṛtaṃ hinasti \|\| 17 \|\|*

16-17. Sharmishtha said: — “King! there is no sin in speaking untruth at the time of indulging in sexual pleasures, on the occasion of marriage, when life is in danger, wealth is at stake, and in joke. Lying on these five occasions is venal. It is only a sin to speak an untruth at the time of being summoned as a witness, or when one is entrusted to dispose of a thing, or when one is asked his advice on any point.”

## \|\| 31.18 \|\|

*yayātiruvāca*  
*rājā pramāṇaṃ bhūtānāṃ sa vinaśyenmṛṣā vadan \|*  
*arthakṛcchramapi prāpya na mithyā kartumutsahe \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Yayati said: — “A king, being the authority for his people, should abstain from untruth, even at the time of danger."

## \|\| 31.20 \|\|

*yayātiruvāca*  
*dātavyaṃ yācamānasya hīti me vratamāhitam \|*  
*tvaṃ ca yācasi kāmaṃ māṃ brūhi kiṃ karavāṇi tat \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Sharmishtha said; — “One’s own husband and the husband of her companion are equal; and as you are the lord of my companion, you must also “Yayati said: — One should give away according to one’s means to one’s supplicants; and it is also my vow not to have any matrimonial connections with you; now you yourself tell me what am I to do of these two things.”

## \|\| 31.21-23 \|\|

*śarmiṣṭhovāca*  
*adharmāttrāhi māṃ rājan dharmaṃ ca pratipādaya \|*  
*tvatto 'patyavatī loke careyaṃ dharmamuttamam \|\| 21 \|\|*

*traya evādhanā rājan bhāryā dāsastathā sutaḥ \|*  
*yatte samadhigacchanti yasya te tasya taddhanam \|\| 22 \|\|*

*devayānyā bhujiṣyāsmi vaśyā ca tava bhārgavī \|*  
*sā cāhaṃ ca tvayā rājan bharaṇīyāṃ bhajasva mām \|\| 23 \|\|*

21-23. Sharmishtha said: — “King! Save me from immorality by your righteousness. I shall lead the life of highest virtue after getting a child through you. King! a women, a servant and a son — all these three have been said to be poor; for the wealth acquired by them belongs to their master, I also take my meals with Devayani and live as a maid, dependent on her; therefore receive me also. I am worthy of your Support."

## \|\| 31.24-27 \|\|

*śaunaka uvāca*  
*evamuktastayā rājā tathyam ityabhijajñivān \|*  
*pūjayāmāsa śarmiṣṭhāṃ dharmaṃ ca pratipādayan \|\| 24 \|\|*

*sa samāgamya śarmiṣṭhāṃ yathākāmamavāpya ca \|*  
*anyonyaṃ cābhisaṃpūjya jagmatustau yathāgatam \|\| 25 \|\|*

*tasminsamāgame subhrūḥ śarmiṣṭhā vārṣaparvaṇī \|*  
*lebhe garbhaṃ prathamatas tasmānnṛpatisattamāt \|\| 26 \|\|*

*prajajñe ca tataḥ kāle rājñī rājīvalocanā \|*  
*kumāraṃ devagarbhābham ādityasamatejasam \|\| 27 \|\|*

24-27. Shaunaka said: — Hearing those words of Sharmishtha, the king accepted her and guarded her virtue. They then enjoyed themselves in each other’s company and were immensely pleased. Through that conjunction, the daughter of Vrishaparvan, conceived and gave birth to illustrious sons gleaming with the radiance of the sun.

## Chapter 32

## \|\| 32.1-2 \|\|

*śaunaka uvāca*  
*śrutvā kumāraṃ jātaṃ sā devayānī śucismitā \|*  
*cintayāviṣṭaduḥkhārtā śarmiṣṭhāṃ prati bhārata \|\| 1 \|\|*

*tato 'bhigamya śarmiṣṭhāṃ devayānyabravīdidam \|*  
*kimarthaṃ vṛjinaṃ subhrūḥ kṛtaṃ te kāmalubdhayā \|\| 2 \|\|*

1-2. Shaunaka said: — On hearing the news of Sharmishtha giving birth to a child, Devayani became deeply afflicted and went and asked her, why she committed that sin by being a slave to Cupid.

## \|\| 32.3-4 \|\|

*śarmiṣṭhovāca*  
*ṛṣir abhyāgataḥ kaścid dharmātmā vedapāragaḥ \|*  
*sa mayā tu varaḥ kāmaṃ yācito dharmasaṃhatam \|\| 3 \|\|*

*nāhamanyāyataḥ kāmam ācarāmi śucismite \|*  
*tasmād ṛṣer mamāpatyam iti satyaṃ bravīmi te \|\| 4 \|\|*

3-4. Committed said: — “A seer, well-versed in the Vedas, came to me wham I pleased, taking him as my lord; and this son has been born of him. O blessed one! I have not base-fully been a slave to passions. — This child has been born of a Rishi; believe this without doubt.’

## \|\| 32.5-6 \|\|

*devayānyuvāca*  
*padyetadevaṃ śarmiṣṭhe na manyurvidyate mama \|*  
*apatyaṃ yadi te labdhaṃ jyeṣṭhācchreṣṭhācca vai dvijāt \|\| 5 \|\|*

*śobhanaṃ bhīru satyaṃ cet kathaṃ sa jñāyate dvijaḥ \|*  
*gotranāmābhijanataḥ śrotumicchāmi taṃ dvijam \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. Devayani said: — “Sharmishtha! If this is true, I am no more angry with you, but how can it be made certain that you have got this progeny from a high class Brahmana? I wish to know his clan and lineage.

## \|\| 32.7 \|\|

*śarmiṣṭhovāca*  
*ojasā tejasā caiva dīpyamānaṃ raviṃ yathā \|*  
*taṃ dṛṣṭvā mama saṃpraṣṭuṃ śaktir nāsīcchucismite \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Sharmishtha said: — “Lady! I felt myself overpowered by his glory. He was so valiant and illustrious, I could: not therefore ask him anything.

## \|\| 32.8 \|\|

*śaunaka uvāca*  
*anyonyamevam uktvā ca samprahasya ca te mithaḥ \|*  
*jagāma bhārgavī veśma tathyamityabhijānatī \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Shaunaka said: — After that mutual conversation, Devayani believed what Sharmishtha told her, and then she returned to her mansion.

## \|\| 32.9 \|\|

*yayātirdevayānyāṃ tu putrāv ajanayannṛpaḥ \|*  
*yaduṃ ca turvasuṃ caiva śakraviṣṇū ivāparau \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Then King Yayati begot two sons — Yadu and Turvasu — as glorious as Indra and Vishnu, from Devayani.

## \|\| 32.10-11 \|\|

*tasmādeva tu rājarṣeḥ śarmiṣṭhā vārṣaparvaṇī \|*  
*druhyaṃ cānuṃ ca pūruṃ ca trīnkumārānajījanat \|\| 10 \|\|*

*tataḥ kāle ca kasmiṃścid devayānī śucismitā \|*  
*yayātisahitā rājañ jagāma haritaṃ vanam \|\| 11 \|\|*

10-11. Druhya, Anu and Puru, those three sons were born from Sharmishtha. After that, Devayani went with King Yayati to the Harit forest

## \|\| 32.12-13 \|\|

*dadarśa ca tadā tatra kumārāndevarūpiṇaḥ \|*  
*krīḍamānān tu visrabdhān vismitā cedamabravīt \|\| 12 \|\|*

*devayānyuvāca*  
*kasyaite dārakā rājan devaputropamāḥ śubhāḥ \|*  
*varcasā rūpataścaiva dṛṣyante sadṛśāstava \|\| 13 \|\|*

12-13. There she saw the three boys of divine elegance, as beautiful as Sanat Kumaras, playing, at which she amazingly said: — “King! whose sons these boys of divine lustre, and bearing such a close affinity to you are?’

## \|\| 32.14-17 \|\|

*evaṃ pṛṣṭvā tu rājānaṃ kumārānparyapṛcchata \|*  
*kiṃ nāmadheyagotre vaḥ putrakā brāhmaṇaḥ pitā \|\| 14 \|\|*

*vibrūta me yathātathyaṃ śrotukāmāsmyato hy aham \|*  
*te 'darśayanpradeśinyā tameva nṛpasattamam \|\| 15 \|\|*

*śaunaka uvāca*  
*ityuktvā sahitāstena rājānam upacakramuḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*nābhyanandata tānrājā devayānyās tadāntike \|*  
*rudantaste 'tha śarmiṣṭhām abhyayur bālakāstadā \|\| 17 \|\|*

14-17. After putting that question to the king, she then approached the boys and asked them to tell her frankly and sincerely whose sons they were and what was their clan. The hoys in reply to her query pointed with their finger to Yayati as their father and Sharmishtha as their mother. Shaunaka said, that, on ascertaining that from the boys, she, along with the boys, hurried back to the king. The king, afraid of the presence of Devayani, did not fondle those boys, as usual, at which they went weeping to Sharmishtha.

## \|\| 32.18-19 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā teṣāṃ tu bālānāṃ praṇayaṃ pārthivaṃ prati \|*  
*buddhvā ca tattvato devī śarmiṣṭhāmidamabravīt \|\| 18 \|\|*

*devayānyuvāca*  
*madadhīnā satī kasmād akārṣīrvipriyaṃ mama \|*  
*tamevāsuradharmaṃ tvam āsthitā na bibheṣi kim \|\| 19 \|\|*

18-19. Devayani, knowing them to be the sons of the king, went and spoke to Sharmishtha: — “You liar! why do you incur my displeasure, in spite of being my dependent? Do you not fear me, and dare you continue to follow your asurik ways?”

## \|\| 32.20-22 \|\|

*śarmiṣṭhovāca*  
*yaduktamṛṣirityeva tatsatyaṃ cāruhāsini \|*  
*nyāyato dharmataścaiva carantī na bibhemi te \|\| 20 \|\|*

*yadā tvayā vṛto rājā vṛta eva tadā mayā \|*  
*sakhībhartā hi dharmeṇa bhartā bhavati śobhane \|\| 21 \|\|*

*pūjyāsi mama mānyā ca śreṣṭhā jyeṣṭhā ca brāhmaṇī \|*  
*tvatto hi me pūjyataro rājarṣiḥ kiṃ na vetsi tat \|\| 22 \|\|*

20-22. Sharmishtha said: — “O Sweet smiling lady! What I told you before about the Rishi is truth and nothing but truth. Jam leading a life, as dictated by religion and morality. Why should then I be afraid of you. O Beautiful one! the moment you made this king your husband, he became my lord as well, on account of his being the husband of my companion.

You are honored by me on account of being a Brahmani and my elder in age, and consequently this Rajarshi, who is your husband, is worthy of being shown more honor and respect by me. Do you not know it?”

## \|\| 32.23-24 \|\|

*śaunaka uvāca*  
*śrutvā tasyāstato vākyaṃ devayānyabravīd idam \|*  
*rājannādyeha vatsyāmi vipriyaṃ me tvayā kṛtam \|\| 23 \|\|*

*sahasotpatitāṃ śyāmāṃ dṛṣṭvā tāṃ sāśrulocanām \|*  
*tūrṇaṃ sakāśaṃ kāvyasya prasthitāṃ vyathitastadā \|\| 24 \|\|*

23-24. Shaunaka said: — On hearing those words of Sharmishtha, Devayani said to the king that she would no longer stay with him, because he had done what was extremely hateful to her. Saying that, she went to her father, the sage Shukra, with her eyes full of tears.

## \|\| 32.25-26 \|\|

*anuvavrāja saṃbhrāntaḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ sāntvayannṛpaḥ \|*  
*nyavartata na sā caiva krodhasaṃraktalocanā \|\| 25 \|\|*

*avibruvantī kiṃcicca rājānaṃ sāśrulocanā \|*  
*acirādeva samprāptā kāvyasyośanaso 'ntikam \|\| 26 \|\|*

25-26. The king also followed her and did his best to pacify her, but Devayani, whose eyes were red with anger, did not heed him; and shedding tears and mumbling something to the king, she hastened to her father. The king also followed her there.

## \|\| 32.27 \|\|

*sā tu dṛṣṭvaiva pitaram abhivādyāgrataḥ sthitā \|*  
*anantaraṃ yayātistu pūjayāmāsa bhārgavam \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. After taking a little pause, Devayani saluted her father and. Yayati also showed his reverence to the sage.

## \|\| 32.28-30 \|\|

*devayānyuvāca*  
*adharmeṇa jito dharmaḥ pravṛttamadharottaram \|*  
*śarmiṣṭhā yātivṛttāsti duhitā vṛṣaparvaṇaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

*trayo 'syāṃ janitāḥ putrā rājñānena yayātinā \|*  
*durbhagāyā mama dvau tu putrau tāta bravīmi te \|\| 29 \|\|*

*dharmajña iti vikhyāta eṣa rājā bhṛgūdvaha \|*  
*atikrāntaśca maryādāṃ kāvyaitatkathayāmi te \|\| 30 \|\|*

28-30. Then Devayani said: — “Father! righteousness has been conquered by unrighteousness, because this king has begotten three sons from Sharmishtha, that discarded daughter of Vrishaparvan, whilst he has begotten only two from my unfortunate self. Father! this king is called righteous, but he is the transgessor of the bounds of virtue”.

## \|\| 32.31 \|\|

*śukra uvāca*  
*dharmajñastvaṃ mahārāja yo 'dharmam akṛthāḥ priyam \|*  
*tasmādjarā tvām acirād dharṣayiṣyati durjayā \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Shukra said: — “King! as you have committed a sin, in spite of your being virtuous, you will be visited soon with invincible old age”.

## \|\| 32.32-34 \|\|

*yayātiruvāca*  
*ṛtuṃ yo yācyamānāyā na dadāti pumānvṛtaḥ \|*  
*bhrūṇahetyucyate brahman sa ceha brahmavādibhiḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

*ṛtukāmāṃ striyaṃ yastu gamyāṃ rahasi yācitaḥ \|*  
*nopaiti yo hi dharmeṇa brahmahetyucyate budhaiḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

*ityetāni samīkṣyāhaṃ kāraṇāni bhṛgūdvaha \|*  
*adharmabhayasaṃvignaḥ śarmiṣṭhām upajagmivān \|\| 34 \|\|*

32-34. Yayati said: — “O Brahman! One who does not satisfy the desire of a damsel, after the termination of her menstruation, commits the sin of slaying a Brahmana; and one who does not grant the desire of a damsel, even on her making such a request, he is said to commit a sin equal to the sin of slaughtering a great Brahmana, O Preceptor! for fear of such sins, I tremblingly offered myself to Sharmishtha.”

## \|\| 32.35 \|\|

*śukra uvāca*  
*na tv ahaṃ pratyavekṣyaste madadhīno 'si pārthiva \|*  
*mithyācaraṇadharmeṣu cauryaṃ bhavati nāhuṣa \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Shukra said: — “King! you depend on me, you ought to have taken my advice, therefore, your doing such an act without my permission, even on the score of righteousness, is nothing short of theft”.

## \|\| 32.36 \|\|

*śaunaka uvāca*  
*krodhenośanasā śapto yayātirnāhuṣastadā \|*  
*pūrvaṃ vayaḥ parityajya jarāṃ sadyo 'nvapadyata \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Shaunaka said: — Then the King Yayati, after being thus cursed by the wrathful sage Shukra, instantly turned old.

## \|\| 32.39 \|\|

*yayātiruvāca*  
*rājyabhāk sa bhavedbrahman puṇyabhākkīrtibhāktathā \|*  
*yo dadyānme vayaḥ putras tadbhavānanumanyatām \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Yayati then said to the sage that he had not had enough of enjoyment with the young Devayani therefore he might mercifully ward off. his old Shukra said — “King! My words cannot prove false. You are therefore bound to be old, but you can exchange it with the youth of some Yayati said: — “Brahman! Be pleased to grant this favour that one who exchanges his youth with my old age will inherit my kingdom and will get fame and honor”.

## \|\| 32.40-41 \|\|

*śukra uvāca*  
*saṃkrāmayiṣyasi jarāṃ yatheṣṭaṃ nahuṣātmaja \|*  
*māmanudhyāya tattvena na ca pāpamavāpsyasi \|\| 40 \|\|*

*vayo dāsyati te putro yaḥ sa rājā bhaviṣyati \|*  
*āuṣmānkīrtimāṃścaiva bahvapatyas tathaiva ca \|\| 41 \|\|*

40-41. Shukra said: — “By my favour, O King! You will exchange your old age with youth without committing any sin; and any of your sons, willingly giving you his youth in exchange for your old age, will certainly be blessed with many children and will be illustrious and long-lived.”

## Chapter 33

## \|\| 33.5-7 \|\|

*yaduruvāca*  
*sitaśmaśrudharo dīno jarasā śithilīkṛtaḥ \|*  
*valīsaṃtatagātraśca durdarśo durbalaḥ kṛśaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*aśaktaḥ kāryakaraṇe paribhūtaḥ sa yauvane \|*  
*sahopajīvibhiścaiva tadjarāṃ nābhikāmaye \|\| 6 \|\|*

*santi te bahavaḥ putrā mattaḥ priyatarā nṛpa \|*  
*jarāṃ grahītuṃ dharmajña putramanyaṃ vṛṇīṣva vai \|\| 7 \|\|*

5-7. Shaunaka said. — On being visited with old age, King Yayati went to his capital and said to his eldest son, Yadu, that owing to the curse of Shukra he had become old, though he had not had ample satisfaction of his desires in his youth; that he might therefore exchange his youth with his old age and thus enable him to satisfy his cravings, and that after a thousand years he would return his youth to him and take back his -Yadu refused to exchange his youth with the old age of the king, who, on account of it, looked lean, decrepit and furrowed and incapable of indulging in enjoyments; and said that the king had other sons dearer than him to whom he might transfer his old age.

## \|\| 33.8-11 \|\|

*yayātiruvāca*  
*yastvaṃ me hṛdayādjāto vayaḥ svaṃ na prayacchasi \|*  
*pāpānmātulasambandhād duṣprajā te bhaviṣyati \|\| 8 \|\|*

*turvaso pratipadyasva pāpmānaṃ jarayā saha \|*  
*yauvanena careyaṃ vai viṣayāṃstava putraka \|\| 9 \|\|*

*pūrṇe varṣasahasre nu punardāsyāmi yauvanam \|*  
*tathaiva pratipatsyāmi pāpmānaṃ jarayā saha \|\| 10 \|\|*

*turvasuruvāca*  
*na kāmaye jarāṃ tāta kāmabhogapraṇāśinīm \|*  
*balarūpāntakaraṇīṃ buddhimānavināśinīm \|\| 11 \|\|*

8-11. At that Yayati got vexed and cursed Yadu that, as he being his son, refused to give him his youth, his sons would be wicked like his maternal uncle; and afterwards he made a similar request to his son Turvasu, making the same promise to him of restoring back to him his youth after a thousand years. Turvasu also refused to accept the proposal of the king, saying that he would not accept the old age which made one devoid of potency, power, enjoyment, beauty, intellect and honour.

## \|\| 33.12-14 \|\|

*yayātiruvāca*  
*yastvaṃ me hṛdayādjāto vayaḥ svaṃ na prayacchasi \|*  
*tasmātprajā samucchedaṃ turvaso tava yāsyati \|\| 12 \|\|*

*saṃkīrṇāścoradharmeṣu pratilomacareṣu ca \|*  
*piśitāśiṣu lokeṣu nūnaṃ rājā bhaviṣyasi \|\| 13 \|\|*

*gurudāraprasakteṣu tiryagyonirateṣu ca \|*  
*paśudharmiṣu mleccheṣu pāpeṣu prabhaviṣyasi \|\| 14 \|\|*

12-14. Yayati cursed him for his refusing to accommodate his father with his youth, and said that his clan would become extinct; and that he would be the king of the vilest of the Mlechchha races who would be thieves, the doers of unnatural deeds, -flesh-eaters, indulging in immoralities with the wife of their preceptor and lower animals.

## \|\| 33.15-20 \|\|

*śaunaka uvāca*  
*evaṃ sa turvasuṃ śaptvā yayātiḥ sutamātmanaḥ \|*  
*śarmiṣṭhāyāḥ sutaṃ jyeṣṭhaṃ druhyuṃ vacanamabravīt \|\| 15 \|\|*

*yayātiruvāca*  
*druhyo tvaṃ pratipadyasva varṇarūpavināśinīm \|*  
*jarāṃ varṣasahasraṃ me yauvanaṃ svaṃ prayacchatām \|\| 16 \|\|*

*pūrṇe varṣasahasre tu te pradāsyāmi yauvanam \|*  
*svaṃ cādāsyāmi bhūyo 'haṃ pāpmānaṃ jarayā saha \|\| 17 \|\|*

*druhyuruvāca*  
*na rājyaṃ na rathaṃ nāśvaṃ jīrṇo bhuṅkte na ca striyam \|*  
*na rāgaścāsya bhavati tadjarāṃ te na kāmaye \|\| 18 \|\|*

*yayātiruvāca*  
*yastvaṃ me hṛdayādjāto vayaḥ svaṃ na prayacchasi \|*  
*taddruhyo vai priyaḥ kāmo na te sampatsyate kvacit \|\| 19 \|\|*

*naur upaplavasaṃcāro yatra nityaṃ bhaviṣyati \|*  
*arājyabhojaśabdaṃ tvaṃ tatra prāpsyasi sānvayaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

15-20. After cursing them thus, he asked his son, Druhya, from Sharmishtha, to accede to his wishes on the same condition of getting back his youth after one thousand years.
