## \|\| 44.51-56 \|\|

*yajñe devāvṛdho rājā bandhūnāṃ mitravardhanaḥ \|*  
*aputrastvabhavadrājā cacāra paramaṃ tapaḥ \|*  
*putraḥ sarvaguṇopeto mama bhūyāditi spṛhan \|\| 51 \|\|*

*saṃyojya mantramevātha parṇāśājalamaspṛśat \|*  
*tadopasparśanāttasya cakāra priyamāpagā \|\| 52 \|\|*

*kalyāṇatvānnarapates tasmai sā nimnagottamā \|*  
*cintayātha parītātmā jagāmātha viniścayam \|\| 53 \|\|*

*nādhigacchāmyahaṃ nārīṃ yasyāmevaṃvidhaḥ sutaḥ \|*  
*jāyeta tasmādadyāhaṃ bhavāmyatha sahasraśaḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

*atha bhūtvā kumārī sā bibhratī paramaṃ vapuḥ \|*  
*jñāpayāmāsa rājānaṃ tāmiyeṣa mahāvrataḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

*atha sā navame māsi suṣuve saritāṃ varā \|*  
*putraṃ sarvaguṇopetaṃ babhruṃ devāvṛdhānnṛpāt \|\| 56 \|\|*

51-56. Devavridha improved the relations with his kinsmen, but was issueless, and with the intention of having a son he practiced devout austerities. With that view, he touched the holy waters of the Parnasha at which that river brooded over the desires of Devavridha. She decided in her mind that Devavridha should beget a handsome child like herself, but could not hit upon any lady who would bear him such an offspring.

Therefore, she determined in her mind that she herself, having the power of manifesting herself in thousands of ways, would give birth to a child like that; for him. With that resolution, she appeared before the king in the form of a young beauty and attracted the ascetic king towards her; after which they became enamoured of each other and enjoyed themselves. Nine months after, she gave birth to Vabhru.

## \|\| 44.57-60 \|\|

*anuvaṃśe purāṇajñā gāyantīti pariśrutam \|*  
*guṇāndevāvṛdhasyāpi kīrtayanto mahātmanaḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

*yathaiva śṛṇumo dūrād apaśyāmas tathāntikāt \|*  
*babhruḥ śreṣṭho manuṣyāṇāṃ devairdevāvṛdhaḥ samaḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

*ṣaṣṭiśca pūrvapuruṣāḥ sahasrāṇi ca saptatiḥ \|*  
*ete 'mṛtatvaṃ samprāptā babhror devāvṛdhānnṛpa \|\| 59 \|\|*

*yajvā dānapatir vīro brahmaṇyaśca dṛḍhavrataḥ \|*  
*rūpavānsumahātejāḥ śrutavīryadharastathā \|\| 60 \|\|*

57-60. The learned in the Puranas sing the praises of that virtuous king, Devavridha, as follows: — “As we heard his praises from a distance, so we find them true when seeing him from near. Vabhru is best amongst men, and equal to Devas and his father, Devavridha. By the glory of Vabhru, the son of Devavridha, 70,080 of his ancestors were liberated and attained final bliss. That King Vabhru was the performer of great sacrifices, the giver of alms, valiant, stead y observer of religious rites, handsome, most illustrious, ambitious and fond of listening to the Shastras.”

## \|\| 44.61 \|\|

*atha kaṅkasya duhitā suṣuve caturaḥ sutān \|*  
*kukuraṃ bhajamānaṃ ca śaśiṃ kambalabarhiṣam \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. His queen, the daughter of the King Kanka, gave birth to four sons, viz., Kukura, Bhajmana, Sashi, Kambal Varhisha.

## \|\| 44.62-63 \|\|

*kukurasya suto vṛṣṇir vṛṣṇestu tanayo dhṛtiḥ \|*  
*kapotaromā tasyātha taittiristasya cātmajaḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

*tasyāsīttanujaḥ sarpo vidvānputro nalaḥ kila \|*  
*khyāyate tasya nāmnā sa nandano daradundubhiḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

62-63. Vrishni was the son of Kukura and the father of Dhriti, who begot Kapotroma, the father of Taittiri. Taittiri was the father of the learned Nala, and is known as Nandanodaradundubhi of worldwide fame.

## \|\| 44.64-65 \|\|

*tasminpravitate yajñe abhijātaḥ punarvasuḥ \|*  
*aśvamedhaṃ ca putrārtham ājahāra narottamaḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

*tasya madhye 'tirātrasya sabhāmadhyātsamutthitaḥ \|*  
*atastu vidvānkarmajño yajvā dātā punarvasuḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

64-65. He performed ashvamedha sacrifice with the desire of getting a son. At the end of Atirattra ceremony, his son, named Punarvasu, arose in the midst of the assembly from the sacrificial pool. Therefore, he was learned, renowned for his love of sacrifices, charities, &c.

## \|\| 44.66 \|\|

*tasyāsīt putramithunaṃ babhūvāvijitaṃ kila \|*  
*āhukaścāhukī caiva khyātaṃ mātematāṃ vara \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. Punarvasu begot a twin, named Ahuka and Ahukti. The following Shlokas are recited about Ahuka.

## \|\| 44.67-69 \|\|

*imāṃścodāharantyatra ślokānprati tamāhukam \|*  
*sopāsaṅgānukarṣāṇāṃ sadhvajānāṃ varūthinām \|\| 67 \|\|*

*rathānāṃ meghaghoṣāṇāṃ sahasrāṇi daśaiva tu \|*  
*nāsatyavādī nātejā nāyajvā nāsahasradaḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

*nāśucirnāpyavidvān hi yo bhojeṣvabhyajāyata \|*  
*āhukasya bhṛtiṃ prāptā ityetadvai taducyate \|\| 69 \|\|*

67-69. “He always lived equipped with an army of armoured chariots, with banners flying over them. His army consisted of ten thousand chariots thundering like the clouds. He was never untruthful, never lustreless, never remained without performing sacrifices and never gave less than a thousand in charity. He was never impure, never ignorant of learning. Such was Ahuka, born in the Bhoja family, and after him Ahuka and other clans came to be known”.

## \|\| 44.70-73 \|\|

*āhukaścāpyavantīṣu svasāraṃ cāhukīṃ dadau \|*  
*āhukātkāṣyaduhitā dvau putrau samasūyata \|\| 70 \|\|*

*devakaścograsenaśca devagarbhasamāv ubhau \|*  
*devakasya sutā vīrā jajñire tridaśopamāḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

*devavānupadevaśca sudevo devarakṣitaḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ svasāraḥ saptāsan vasudevāya tā dadau \|\| 72 \|\|*

*devakī śrutadevī ca mitradevī yaśodharā \|*  
*śrīdevī satyadevī ca sutāpī ceti saptamī \|\| 73 \|\|*

70-73. He married his sister, Ahuki, to Avanti, and begot from his queen, the daughter of Kashya, the two sons, viz., Devaka and Ugrasena, who were born like the Devas. Devaka also begot four sons and seven daughters, viz., Devavana, Upadeva, Sudeva and Devarakshita. Their seven sisters were Devaki, Shrutadevi, Mitradevi, Yashodhara, Shridevi, Satyadevi, and Sutapi, the seventh, who were married to Vasudeva.

## \|\| 44.74-76 \|\|

*navograsenasya sutāḥ kaṃsasteṣāṃ tu pūrvajaḥ \|*  
*nyagrodhaśca sunāmā ca kaṅkaḥ śaṅkuśca bhūyasaḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

*ajabhū rāṣṭrapālaśca uddhamuṣṭiḥ sumuṣṭidaḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ svasāraḥ pañcāsan kaṃsā kaṃsavatī tathā \|\| 75 \|\|*

*sutantū rāṣṭrapālī ca kaṅkā ceti varāṅganāḥ \|*  
*ugrasenaḥ sahāpatyo vyākhyātaḥ kukurodbhavaḥ \|\| 76 \|\|*

74-76. Ugrasena was father of nine sons. Amongst them, Kamsa was the eldest. The others were Nyagrodha, Sunama, Katha, Sanku, Ajabhu, Rashtrapala, Yudhamushti, Sumushti. Their sisters were five, viz., Kamsa, Kamsavati, Sutantu, Rashtrapali and Kanka. Ugrasena and his descendants all belonged to the Kukura clan.

## \|\| 44.77 \|\|

*bhajamānasya putro 'tha rathimukhyo vidūrathaḥ \|*  
*rājādhidevaḥ śūraśca vidūrathasuto 'bhavat \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. Bhoja was the father of the famous Viduratha, who begot the valiant Rajadhideva

## \|\| 44.79 \|\|

*śoṇāśvasya sutāḥ pañca śūrā raṇaviśāradāḥ \|*  
*śamī ca devaśarmā ca nikuntaḥ śakraśatrujit \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. Rajadhideva begot two deva-like, virtuous sons, named Shonashva and Shonashva had five sons, all heroic and well-versed in war. They were: — Sami, Vedasharma, Nikunta, Shukra and Shatrujita.

## \|\| 44.80 \|\|

*śamiputraḥ pratikṣatraḥ pratikṣatrasya cātmajaḥ \|*  
*pratikṣetraḥ suto bhojo hṛdīkastasya cātmajaḥ \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. Sami was the father of Pratikshatra, who begot Pratikshetra, the father of Bhoja, who became the father of Hridika.

## \|\| 44.81-83 \|\|

*hṛdīkasyābhavanputrā daśa bhīmaparākramāḥ \|*  
*kṛtavarmāgrajas teṣāṃ śatadhanvā ca madhyamaḥ \|\| 81 \|\|*

*devārhaścaiva nābhaśca bhīṣaṇaśca mahābalaḥ \|*  
*ajāto vanajātaśca kanīyakakarambhakau \|\| 82 \|\|*

*devārhasya suto vidvāñ jajñe kambalabarhiṣaḥ \|*  
*asāmañjāḥ sutastasya tamojātasya cātmajaḥ \|\| 83 \|\|*

81-83. Hridika had ten valiant sons: — Kritavarma, was the eldest amongst them. Shatadhanva was the second. The others were Devarha, Nabha, Bhishana, Mahabala, Ajata, Vanajata, Kaniyaka, and Karambhaka. Devarha was the father of the learned Kambalavarhisha, who begot Asamanja, the father of Ta-Moja.

## \|\| 44.84 \|\|

*ajātaputrā vikrāntās trayaḥ paramakīrtayaḥ \|*  
*sudaṃṣṭraśca sunābhaśca kṛṣṇa ityandhakā matāḥ \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. Ajata begot the following three illustrious sons, who were known under the name of Andhakas: — Sudanshtra, Sunabha, Krishna.

## \|\| 44.85 \|\|

*andhakānāmimaṃ vaṃśaṃ yaḥ kīrtayati nityaśaḥ \|*  
*ātmano vipulaṃ vaṃśaṃ prajāvānāpnute naraḥ \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. One who daily recites the family of the Andhakas obtains a large family.

## Chapter 45

## \|\| 45.1-2 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*gāndhārī caiva mādrī ca vṛṣṇibhārye babhūvatuḥ \|*  
*gāndhārī janayāmāsa sumitraṃ mitranandanam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*mādrī udhājitaṃ putraṃ tato vai devamīḍhuṣam \|*  
*anamitraṃ śibiṃ caiva pañcamaṃ kṛtalakṣaṇam \|\| 2 \|\|*

1-2. Suta. — Gandhari and Madri were the wives of Vrishni, and Sumitra, the rejoicer of his friends, was born from Gandhari. — Madri begot five sons, named Yudhajita, Devamidhusha, Anamitra, Shibi, Kritalakshana.

## \|\| 45.3 \|\|

*anamitrasuto nighno nighnasyāpi tu dvau sutau \|*  
*prasenaśca mahāvīryaḥ śaktisenaśca tāv ubhau \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Anamitra became the father of Nighva, who begot two sons, viz., the most powerful Prasena and Shaktisena, also known as Satrajita.

## \|\| 45.4-5 \|\|

*syamantakaḥ prasenasya maṇiratnamanuttamam \|*  
*pṛthivyāṃ sarvaratnānāṃ rājā vai so 'bhavanmaṇiḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*hṛdi kṛtvā tu bahuśo maṇiṃ tamabhiyācitaḥ \|*  
*govindo 'pi na taṃ lebhe śakto 'pi na jahāra saḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. Prasena possessed Syamantaka, which was the best of all gems on the earth, and was known as the king of all gems. Prasena used always to wear his beautiful Syamantaka jewel on his breast and Krishna more than once expressed a desire to have it, but was refused by Prasena; and even though Krishna was powerful to take it by force, he did not like to do that

## \|\| 45.6-8 \|\|

*kadācinmṛgayāṃ yātaḥ prasenastena bhūṣitaḥ \|*  
*yathāśabdaṃ sa śuśrāva bile sattvena pūrite \|\| 6 \|\|*

*tataḥ praviṣya sa bilaṃ praseno hy ṛkṣamaikṣata \|*  
*ṛkṣaḥ prasenaṃ ca tathā ṛkṣaṃ caiva prasenajit \|\| 7 \|\|*

*hatvā ṛkṣaḥ prasenaṃ tu tatastaṃ maṇimādadāt \|*  
*adṛṣṭastu hatastena antarbilagatastadā \|\| 8 \|\|*

6-8. Once upon a time, Prasena wearing his Syamantaka gem went out for a hunt, when hearing the voices of some wild beasts in a cave he entered it and found a bear inside, and they looked at each other. He fought with the animal, but was killed by the latter. After that, the bear took the matchless jewel from the person of the dead king and retired into the deeper cavities of the cave. In the meantime the news of Prasena’s death became public.

## \|\| 45.9-11 \|\|

*prasenaṃ tu hataṃ jñātvā govindaḥ pariśaṅkitaḥ \|*  
*govindena hato vyaktaṃ praseno maṇikāraṇāt \|\| 9 \|\|*

*prasenastu gato 'raṇyaṃ maṇiratnena bhūṣitaḥ \|*  
*taṃ dṛṣṭvā sa hatastena govindaḥ pratyuvāca ha \|*  
*hanmi cainaṃ durācāraṃ śatrubhūtaṃ hi vṛṣṇiṣu \|\| 10 \|\|*

*atha dīrgheṇa kālena mṛgayāṃ nirgataḥ punaḥ \|*  
*yadṛcchayā ca govindo bilasyābhyāśamāgamat \|\| 11 \|\|*

9-11. Knowing him to be dead, Shrikrishna was dismayed. Someone gave currency to the rumour that Prasena was murdered by Krishna for the sake of the Syamantaka gem. It was insinuated that Prasena went out wearing his priceless Syamantaka gem and was decidedly killed by Krishna, who usurped the jewel from him. Satrajita, the brother of the deceased, also thought the same

## \|\| 45.12-15 \|\|

*taṃ dṛṣṭvā tu mahāśabdaṃ sa cakre ṛkṣarāḍbalī \|*  
*śabdaṃ śrutvā tu govindaḥ khaḍgapāṇiḥ praviṣya saḥ \|*  
*apaṣyadjāmbavantaṃ tam ṛkṣarājaṃ mahābalam \|\| 12 \|\|*

*tatastūrṇaṃ hṛṣīkeśas tamṛkṣapatimañjasā \|*  
*jāmbavantaṃ sa jagrāha krodhasaṃraktalocanaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*tuṣṭāvainaṃ tadā ṛkṣaḥ karmabhirvaiṣṇavaiḥ prabhum \|*  
*tatastuṣṭastu bhagavān vareṇainamarocayat \|\| 14 \|\|*

*jāmbavānuvāca*  
*icche cakraprahāreṇa tvatto 'haṃ maraṇaṃ prabho \|*  
*kanyā ceyaṃ mama śubhā bhartāraṃ tvāmavāpnuyāt \|*  
*yo 'yaṃ maṇiḥ prasenaṃ tu hatvā prāpto mayā prabho \|\| 15 \|\|*

12-15. Sometime after Shrikrishna, also went out to hunt in the forest and approached the very cave of the bear, when the beast-seeing him began to groan and growl, at which he entered the cave with sword in hand. He found the bear to be Jambavanta, the King of all bears. He then hastily, with great valour, made Jambavanta a captive and then turned his eyes full of wrath towards him. The King of the bears then pleased Lord Shrikrishna, the manifestation of Vishnu, with his devotion

## \|\| 45.16-17 \|\|

*tataḥ sa jāmbavantaṃ taṃ hatvā cakreṇa vai prabhuḥ \|*  
*kṛtakarmā mahābāhuḥ sakanyaṃ maṇimāharat \|\| 16 \|\|*

*dadau satrājitāyainaṃ sarvasātvatasaṃsadi \|*  
*tena mithyāpavādena saṃtapto 'yaṃ janārdanaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

16-17. Krishna becoming pleased wanted to grant him some boon. Jambavanta said; — I wish that I may be killed by Thee, O Lord, through the striking of Sudarshana Chakra, and this auspicious daughter of mine be accepted by Thee as Thy wife. This gem which I had obtained, O Lord, by killing Prasena, be accepted by Thee.

## \|\| 45.18 \|\|

*tataste yādavāḥ sarve vāsudevamathābruvan \|*  
*asmākaṃ tu matirhyāsīt prasenastu tvayā hataḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. After that, Krishna: killed Jambavanta by his Sudarshana Chakra and then returned with the Syamantaka and the daughter of the King of bears, named Jambavati.

## \|\| 45.19-20 \|\|

*kaikeyasya sutā bhāryā daśa satrājitaḥ śubhāḥ \|*  
*tāsūtpannāḥ sutāstasya śatamekaṃ tu viśrutāḥ \|*  
*khyātimanto mahāvīryā bhaṅgakārastu pūrvajaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

*atha vratavatī tasmād bhaṅgakārāttu pūrvajāt \|*  
*suṣuve sukumārīstu tisraḥ kamalalocanāḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

19-20. Then Krishna presented Syamantaka to Satrajita in the assemblage of the Satvatas, and told them how much aggrieved he was by the false accusation leveled by them against him.

## \|\| 45.21 \|\|

*satyabhāmā varā strīṇāṃ vratinī ca dṛḍhavratā \|*  
*tathā padmāvatī caiva tāśca kṛṣṇāya so 'dadāt \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Then all the Yadavas thus spoke to Vasudeva: — “Our idea was that Prasena was killed by Thee.”

## \|\| 45.22-24 \|\|

*anamitrācchinirjajñe kaniṣṭhādvṛṣṇinandanāt \|*  
*satyakastasya putrastu sātyakistasya cātmajaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*satyavānyuudhānastu śinernaptā pratāpavān \|*  
*asaṅgo uyudhānasya dyumnistasyātmajo 'bhavat \|\| 23 \|\|*

*dyumneryugaṃdharaḥ putra iti śainyāḥ prakīrtitāḥ \|*  
*anamitrānvayo hy eṣa vyākhyāto vṛṣṇivaṃśajaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

22-24. King Kaikaya had ten daughters, who all were married to Satrajita, The sons born of them were one hundred and one, of worldwide fame and the eldest of them was Bhangakara. Then Bhangakara begot from his wife Vratavati three graceful and lotus-eyed daughters named, Satyabhama the best amongst women, and Vratini, of strong vows, and Padmavati, All three of them were the most virtuous of all women. Satrajita, to please Krishna, gave them all in marriage to him.

## \|\| 45.25-26 \|\|

*anamitrasya saṃjajñe pṛthvyāṃ vīro udhājitaḥ \|*  
*anyau tu tanayau vīrau vṛṣabhaḥ kṣatra eva ca \|\| 25 \|\|*

*vṛṣabhaḥ kāśirājasya sutāṃ bhāryāmavindata \|*  
*jayantastu jayantyāṃ tu putraḥ samabhavacchubhaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

25-26. Anamitra, the youngest of the sons of Vrishni, was the father of Shini, whose son was Satyaka, whose son was, Satyaka, — Yuyudhana, , the truthful, was the grandson of Shini and was powerful. Asanga was the son of Yuyudhana and the father of Dyumna. Yugandhara was the son of Dyumna. This is how the family of Shini has been described.

## \|\| 45.27-28 \|\|

*sadāyajño 'tivīraśca śrutavānatithipriyaḥ \|*  
*akrūraḥ suṣuve tasmāt sadāyajño 'tidakṣiṇaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

*ratnā kanyā ca śaibyasya akrūrastāmavāptavān \|*  
*putrānutpādayāmāsa ekādaśa mahābalān \|\| 28 \|\|*

27-28. Sets ‘The family of Animitra belonging to the Vrishni clan, has been thus described: Animitra was the father of Yudhajita, the brave, whose brothers were Vrishabha and Kshatra, both great heroes. Vrishabha was married to the daughter of the King of Kashi. His wife, Jayanti, bore him Jayanta who performed many sacrifices and was renowned for his prowess and hospitality.

## \|\| 45.29-30 \|\|

*upalambhaḥ sadālambho vṛkalo vīrya eva ca \|*  
*savītaraḥ sadāpakṣaḥ śatrughno vārimejayaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*dharmabhṛddharmavarmāṇau dhṛṣṭamānastathaiva ca \|*  
*sarve ca pratihotāro ratnāyāṃ jajñire ca te \|\| 30 \|\|*

29-30. Jayanta was the father of Akrura, who was also famous for the performance of sacrifices and giving of many presents. He was married. to Ratna, the daughter of Shaivya from whom he begot eleven sons, viz., — Upalambha, Sadalambha, Vrikala, Virya, Shini (Savitara), Mahapaksha.

(Sadapaksha), Shatrughna, Varimejaya, Dharmabhrit, Dharmavarma and Dhrishtamana. Those sons of Ratna were all very pious.

## \|\| 45.31 \|\|

*akrūrād ugrasenāyāṃ sutau dvau kulavardhanau \|*  
*devavānupadevaśca jajñāte devasaṃnibhau \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Akrura was also the father of two sons, named Devavana and Upadeva, from his other wife, Ugrasena. Both of them were handsome like the Devas.

## \|\| 45.32-33 \|\|

*aśvinyāṃ ca tataḥ putrāḥ pṛthur vipṛthureva ca \|*  
*aśvatthāmā subāhuśca supārśvakagaveṣaṇau \|\| 32 \|\|*

*vṛṣṭinemiḥ sudharmā ca tathā śaryātireva ca \|*  
*abhūmir varjabhūmiśca śramiṣṭhaḥ śravaṇastathā \|\| 33 \|\|*

32-33. Besides them, Akrura had the following sons from his wife, Ashvini: — Prithu, Viprithu, Ashvathama, Subahu, Suparshva, Gaveshana, Vrishtinemi, Sudharmas, Saryati, Abhumi, Vajrabhumi, Sharmishtha and Shravana.

## \|\| 45.34 \|\|

*imāṃ mithyābhiśastiṃ yo veda kṛṣṇādapohitām \|*  
*na sa mithyābhiśāpena abhiśāpyo 'tha kenacit \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Shrikrishna saved Himself from the calumny of stealing the Syamantaka jewel, by killing Jambavana. One who hears or recites to others this piece, will never be liable to be falsely defamed a thief.

## Chapter 46

## \|\| 46.1-4 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*aikṣvākī suṣuve śūraṃ khyātamadbhutamīḍhuṣam \|*  
*pauruṣādjajñire śūrād bhojāyāṃ putrakā daśa \|\| 1 \|\|*

*vasudevo mahābāhuḥ pūrvamānakadundubhiḥ \|*  
*devamārgastato jajñe tato devaśravāḥ punaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*anādhṛṣṭiḥ śiniścaiva nandaścaiva sasṛñjayaḥ \|*  
*śyāmaḥ śamīkaḥ saṃyūpaḥ pañca cāsya varāṅganāḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*śrutakīrtiḥ pṛthā caiva śrutādevī śrutaśravāḥ \|*  
*rājādhidevī ca tathā pañcaitā vīramātaraḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

1-4. Suta said: — Aikshvaki, the daughter of King Ikshvaku bore Sara, a heroic son, named and renowned as Adbhutamidhusham, to her lord, Purusha. Sura, the son of Purusha, begot from Bhoja ten sons, named, the famous and mighty-armed Vasudeva, known also as Anakadundubhi, Devamarga, Devashrava, Anddhrishti, Shini, Nanda, Srinjaya, Syama, Shamika, Samyupa, and the following five daughters, viz., — Shrutakirti, Pritha, Shrutadevi, Shrutashrava, Rajadhidevi. All these five girls were mothers of heroes.

## \|\| 46.5-6 \|\|

*kṛtasya tu śrutādevī sugrīvaṃ suṣuve sutam \|*  
*kaikeyyāṃ śrutakīrtyāṃ tu jajñe so 'nuvrato nṛpaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*śrutaśravasi caidyasya sunīthaḥ samapadyata \|*  
*bahuśo dharmacārī sa saṃbabhūvārimardanaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. Krita begot from Shrutadevi his son, Sugriva; Kaikaya be got Anuvrata from Shrutakirti; the King Chaidya became the father of Sunitha, from his wife, Shrutashrava, who was the conqueror of his enemies and the observer of all religious rites in the year.

## \|\| 46.7-8 \|\|

*atha sakhyena vṛddhe 'sau kuntibhoje sutāṃ dadau \|*  
*evaṃ kuntī samākhyātā vasudevasvasā pṛthā \|\| 7 \|\|*

*vasudevena sā dattā pāṇḍorbhāryā hy aninditā \|*  
*pāṇḍorarthena sā jajñe devaputrān mahārathān \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8. After that Sara, out of friendship, gave his daughter, Pritha, for being adopted by Kuntibhoja, who was very old, and for that reason she also came to be known as Kunti, the sister of Vasudeva, Vasudeva gave in marriage his sister, Kunti, to King Pandu, for whom he bore several brave sons, through Devas

## \|\| 46.9-10 \|\|

*dharmādyudhiṣṭhiro jajñe vāyorjajñe vṛkāderaḥ \|*  
*indrāddhanaṃjayaś caiva śakratulyaparākramaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*mādravatyāṃ tu janitāv aśvibhyābhiti śuśruma \|*  
*nakulaḥ sahadevaśca rūpaśīlaguṇānvitau \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. Kunti gave birth to Yudhisthira, through Dharma, Bhimasena through Vayu, Arjuna, as powerful as Shakra, through Indra. Madri gave birth to Nakula and Sahadeva, through the glory of the Ashvini Kumaras. Both of the brothers were brave, modest and handsome.

## \|\| 46.11-12 \|\|

*rohiṇī pauravī nāma bhāryā hy ānakadundubheḥ \|*  
*lebhe jyeṣṭhaṃ sutaṃ rāmaṃ sāraṇaṃ ca sutaṃ priyam \|\| 11 \|\|*

*durdamaṃ damanaṃ subhruṃ piṇḍārakamahāhanū \|*  
*citrākṣyau dve kumāryau tu rohiṇyāṃ jajñire tadā \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-12. Rohini, of the Puru family, the wife of Vasudeva known as Anakadundubhi, gave birth to the eldest son, Balarama, and to his brothers, Sarana, Durduma, Damana, Subhru, Pindaraka, and Mehabanu. She also gave birth to two beautiful daughters, named Chitra and Akshi.

## \|\| 46.13 \|\|

*devakyāṃ jajñire śaureḥ suṣeṇaḥ kīrtimānapi \|*  
*udāsī bhadrasenaśca ṛṣivāsastathaiva ca \|*  
*ṣaṣṭho bhadravidehaśca kaṃsaḥ sarvānaghātayat \|\| 13 \|\|*

13 Vasudeva ‘begot from his other wife, Devaki: — Sushena, Kirtimana, Udashi, Bhadrasena, Rishivasa, and Bhadravideha the sixth, who were all killed by the King Kamsa, as soon as they were born.

## \|\| 46.14 \|\|

*prathamā yā amāvāsyā vārṣikī tu bhaviṣyati \|*  
*tasyāṃ jajñe mahābāhuḥ pūrvaṃ kṛṣṇaḥ prajāpatiḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Lord Krishna was born on the first Amavasya of the year, in the month of Vaishakha.

## \|\| 46.15 \|\|

*anujā tv abhavatkṛṣṇā subhadrā bhadrabhāṣiṇī \|*  
*devakyāṃ tu mahātejā jajñe śūro mahāyaśāḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. (It is so stated in the Puranas, owing to the difference in Kalpa: otherwise it is laid down in the Bhagavata that Krishna was born in the month of Bhadra, on the 8th of the dark fortnight.) The sweet-speaking Subhadra, the beautiful sister of Krishna, was born after him. Both ‘Krishna and Subhadra were born of Devaki.

## \|\| 46.16 \|\|

*sahadevastu tāmrāyāṃ jajñe śauriḥ kulodvahaḥ \|*  
*upāsaṅgadharaṃ lebhe tanayaṃ devarakṣitā \|*  
*ekāṃ kanyāṃ ca subhagāṃ kaṃsastām abhyaghātayat \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Vasudeva begot from his wife, Tamra, Sahadeva, after whom Upasangadhara and his sister were born. She was also killed by Kamsa.

## \|\| 46.17-19 \|\|

*vijayaṃ rocamānaṃ ca vardhamānaṃ tu devalam \|*  
*ete sarve mahātmāno hy upadevyāṃ prajajñire \|\| 17 \|\|*

*avagāho mahātmā ca vṛkadevyāmajāyata \|*  
*vṛkadevyāṃ svayaṃ jajñe nandako nāma nāmataḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*saptamaṃ devakīputraṃ madanaṃ suṣuve nṛpa \|*  
*gaveṣaṇaṃ mahābhāgaṃ saṃgrāmeṣvaparājitam \|\| 19 \|\|*

17-19. Vasudeva begot from Upadevi: — Rochmana, Vardhamana, Devala, and from Vrikadevi be begot: — Mahatma, Avagaha, and Nandaka.

## \|\| 46.20 \|\|

*śraddhādevyā vihāre tu vane hi vicaranpurā \|*  
*vaiśyāyāmadadhācchauriḥ putraṃ kauśikamagrajam \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Afterwards, Vasudeva begot Madana, the seventh son of Devaki, and from Shraddhadevi he begot Gaveshana, Formerly, he had begotten Kaushika from his wife of the Vaidya clan.

**Комментарий:**

Note — This is an instance of an intermarriage between a Kshatriya and a Vaishya.

## \|\| 46.21 \|\|

*sutanū ratharājī ca śaurerāstāṃ parigrahau \|*  
*puṇḍraśca kapilaścaiva vasudevātmajau balau \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Pandra and. Kapila were born from the wives of Vasudeva, Sutanu and Ratharji, respectively.

## \|\| 46.22 \|\|

*jarā nāma niṣādo 'bhūt prathamaḥ sa dhanurdharaḥ \|*  
*saubhadraśca bhavaścaiva mahāsattvau babhūvatuḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Of whom, the first came to be known as a great archer among the Nishadha clan, known as Jora. After him, Saubhadra and Bhava were born of his wife, of the Vaishya caste.

## \|\| 46.23 \|\|

*devabhāgasutaścāpi nāmnāsāv uddhavaḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*paṇḍitaṃ prathamaṃ prāhur devaśravaḥsamudbhavam \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Uddhava was the son of Devamarga, who is known to be a man of great learning.

## \|\| 46.24 \|\|

*aikṣvākyalabhatāpatyam anādhṛṣṭeryaśasvinī \|*  
*nidhūtasattvaṃ śatrughnaṃ śrāddhastasmādajāyata \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Anadhrishti became the father of Shatrughna from Ikshvaku, who also begot Shraddha.

## \|\| 46.25 \|\|

*karūṣāyānapatyāya kṛṣṇastuṣṭaḥ sutaṃ dadau \|*  
*sucandraṃ tu mahābhāgaṃ vīryavantaṃ mahābalam \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. King Karusha, who had no issue, was given in adoption a powerful son, named Suchandra, by Sri Krishna.

## \|\| 46.26 \|\|

*jāmbavatyāḥ sutāv etau dvau ca satkṛtalakṣaṇau \|*  
*cārudeṣṇaśca sāmbaśca vīryavantau mahābalau \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Krishna begot Charudeshna and Samba from his wife, Jambavati.

## \|\| 46.27 \|\|

*tantipālaśca tantiśca nandanasya sutāv ubhau \|*  
*śamīkaputrāś catvāro vikrāntāḥ sumahābalāḥ \|*  
*virājaśca dhanuścaiva śyāmaśca sṛñjayastathā \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Tantipala and Tanti were the sons of Nandana. Samika begot four powerful sons, named Viraja, Dhanu, Shyamya and Srinjaya

## \|\| 46.28 \|\|

*anapatyo 'bhavacchyāmaḥ śamīkastu vanaṃ yayau \|*  
*jugupsamāno bhojatvaṃ rājarṣitvamavāptavān \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Shyamya had no issue, and Samika despising all. pleasures went to the forest, where he attained to Rajarshihood.

## \|\| 46.29 \|\|

*kṛṣṇasya janmābhyudayaṃ yaḥ kīrtayati nityaśaḥ \|*  
*śṛṇoti mānavo nityaṃ sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. One who daily hears or recites the birth and family history of Lord Sri Krishna, will become liberated from all his sins and go to heaven.

## Chapter 47

## \|\| 47.1-4 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*atha devo mahādevaḥ pūrvaṃ kṛṣṇaḥ prajāpatiḥ \|*  
*vihārārthaṃ sa deveśo mānuṣeṣviha jayate \|\| 1 \|\|*

*devakyāṃ vasudevasya tapasā puṣkarekṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*caturbāhustadā jāto divyarūpo jvalañśriyā \|\| 2 \|\|*

*śrīvatsalakṣaṇaṃ devaṃ dṛṣṭvā divyaiśca lakṣaṇaiḥ \|*  
*uvāca vasudevastaṃ rūpaṃ saṃhara vai prabho \|\| 3 \|\|*

*bhīto 'haṃ deva kaṃsasya tatastvetadbravīmi te \|*  
*mama putrā hatāstena jyeṣṭhāste bhīmavikramāḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

1-4. Suta said: — The Lord of all, the Protector of the universe, manifested Himself as Shrikrishna for the purpose of His pastime. Through the asceticism of Vasudeva, Shrikrishna was born in the womb of Devaki. His eyes wore. like lotus. He had four arms, and His Divine form was of unsurpassing splendour. When He was born like that in His glory, wearing the Shrivatsa jewel, Vasudeva besought Him with folded hands, saying “Hide that form. O Lord, I make this request to you, on account of my fear of Kamsa, who has killed my powerful sons, thy elder brothers"

## \|\| 47.5-6 \|\|

*vasudevavacaḥ śrutvā rūpaṃ saṃharate 'cyutaḥ \|*  
*anujñāpya tataḥ śauriṃ nandagopagṛhe 'nayat \|\| 5 \|\|*

*dattvainaṃ nandagopasya rakṣyatāmiti cābravīt \|*  
*atastu sarvakalyāṇaṃ yādavānāṃ bhaviṣyati \|*  
*ayaṃ tu garbho devakyāṃ jātaḥ kaṃsaṃ haniṣyati \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. In compliance with those words of Vasudeva, Lord Krishna hid His form of ‘Divine glory and asked Him to send him to the house of Nanda.

Accordingly, Vasudeva took him to the house of Nanda, and requested the latter to look after the Divine babe, like his own child, and added that the celestial infant would bring prosperity to the Yadavas; and this child, born of the womb of Devaki, will kill Kamsa.

## \|\| 47.7-8 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ*  
*ka eṣa vasudevastu devakī ca yaśasvinī \|*  
*nandagopaśca kastveṣa yaśodā ca mahāvratā \|\| 7 \|\|*

*yo viṣṇuṃ janayāmāsa yaṃ ca tātetyabhāṣata \|*  
*yā garbhaṃ janayāmāsa yā cainaṃ tv abhyavardhayat \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8. The Sages said: — Suta! Who were Vasudeva and Devaki, to whom the manifestation of Lord Vishnu was born as a son and called them. His parents; and who were Nanda and Yashoda, who saw the childish freaks of that Divine babe?

## \|\| 47.9 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*puruṣaḥ kaṣyapastvāsīd aditistu priyā smṛtā \|*  
*brahmaṇaḥ kaṣyapastvaṃśaḥ pṛthivyāstvaditistathā \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Suta said: — Kashyapa became man and had Aditi for his wife. The former was born by the glory of the Creator and the latter was created from a particle of the Earth.

**Комментарий:**

Note — It means that Kashyapa was a partial incarnation of the Creator, whilst his wife, Aditi, was that of the goddess of earth.

## \|\| 47.10 \|\|

*atha kāmānmahābāhur devakyāḥ samapūrayat \|*  
*ye tayā kāṅkṣitā nityam ajātasya mahātmanaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Afterwards Devaki. in the form of Aditi, was granted all. the fulfilment of her desires by Vishnu.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — It means that Aditi was afterwards born as Devaki, through the process of transmigration of the soul, in which life her desires were fulfilled by the pleasure of Vishnu.

## \|\| 47.11-12 \|\|

*so 'vatīrṇo mahīṃ devaḥ praviṣṭo mānuṣīṃ tanum \|*  
*mohayansarvabhūtāni yogātmā yogamāyayā \|\| 11 \|\|*

*naṣṭe dharme tathā jajñe viṣṇurvṛṣṇikule prabhuḥ \|*  
*kartuṃ dharmasya saṃsthānam asurāṇāṃ praṇāśanam \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-12. Lord Vishnu manifested Himself in the human form and deluded the world by His Yogic powers. Its history is that, when the earth became deprived of righteousness and the Asuras swelled the world, Lord Vishnu, in order to r e-establish righteousness, incarnated Himself in the human form in the Vrishni family.

## \|\| 47.13-14 \|\|

*rukmiṇī satyabhāmā ca satyā nāgnajitī tathā \|*  
*subhāmā ca tathā śaibyā gāndhārī lakṣmaṇā tathā \|\| 13 \|\|*

*mitravindā ca kālindī devī jāmbavatī tathā \|*  
*suśīlā ca tathā mādrī kauśalyā vijayā tathā \|*  
*evamādīni devīnāṃ sahasrāṇi ca ṣoḍaśa \|\| 14 \|\|*

13-14. Sri Krishna had sixteen thousand wives, of whom Rukmini, Satyabhama, Satya, Nagnajiti, Subhama, Shaivya, Gandhari, Lakshmana, Mitravinda, Kalindi, Jamba-Vati, Sushila, Madri, Kaushalya, Vijaya were the principal ones

## \|\| 47.15-16 \|\|

*rukmiṇī janayāmāsa putrānraṇaviśāradān \|*  
*cārudeṣṇaṃ raṇe śūraṃ pradyumnaṃ ca mahābalam \|\| 15 \|\|*

*sucāruṃ bhadracāruṃ ca sudeṣṇaṃ bhadrameva ca \|*  
*paraśuṃ cāruguptaṃ ca cārubhadraṃ sucārukam \|*  
*cāruhāsaṃ kaniṣṭhaṃ ca kanyāṃ cārumatīṃ tathā \|\| 16 \|\|*

15-16. Rukmini gave birth to the following sons, proficient in the art of war, viz., Charudeshna, Pradyumna, Sucharu, Bhadracharu, Sudeshna, Bhadra, Parashu, Charugupta, Charubhadra, Sucharuka, Charuhasa, and a girl named Charumati.

## \|\| 47.17-18 \|\|

*jajñire satyabhāmāyāṃ bhānurbhramaratekṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*rohito dīptimāṃścaiva tāmraś cakro jalaṃdhamaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*catasro jajñire teṣāṃ svasārastu yavīyasīḥ \|*  
*jāmbavatyāḥ suto jajñe sāmbaḥ samitiśobhanaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

17-18. Shri Krishna, the beautiful-eyed, begot from Satyabhama four sons, named Rohita, Diptamana, Tamra Chakra, and Jalandhama, who had four younger sisters also.

## \|\| 47.18-19 \|\|

*catasro jajñire teṣāṃ svasārastu yavīyasīḥ \|*  
*jāmbavatyāḥ suto jajñe sāmbaḥ samitiśobhanaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*mitravānmitravindaśca mitravindā varāṅganā \|*  
*mitrabāhuḥ sunīthaśca nāgnajityāḥ prajā hi sā \|\| 19 \|\|*

18-19. Jambavati gave birth to Samba, who was an ornament to all assemblages. — Mitravinda became the mother of Mitravana and Mitravinda.

Sunitha and Mitra Bahu were born from Nagnajiti.

## \|\| 47.20-21 \|\|

*evamādīni putrāṇāṃ sahasrāṇi nibodhata \|*  
*śataṃ śatasahasrāṇāṃ putrāṇāṃ tasya dhīmataḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*aśītiśca sahasrāṇi vāsudevasutāstathā \|*  
*lakṣamekaṃ tathā proktaṃ putrāṇāṃ ca dvijottamāḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

20-21. Beginning with these, there were thousands and, according to some, hundreds. of thousands, and according to others eighty thousand sons born to Vasudeva. While others say that he had a hundred thousand sons.

## \|\| 47.22 \|\|

*upasaṅgasya tu sutau vajraḥ saṃkṣipta eva ca \|*  
*bhūrīndraseno bhūriśca gaveṣaṇasutāv ubhau \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Upasanga had two sons, named Vajra and Sankshipta, and Bharindrasena and Bhuri were the two sons of Gaveshana.

## \|\| 47.24 \|\|

*kāśyā supārśvatanayā sāmbāllebhe tarasvinaḥ \|*  
*satyaprakṛtayo devāḥ pañca vīrāḥ prakīrtitāḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Pradyumna begot from his wife, the daughter of the King of Vidarbha (Modern Berar) named, Aniruddha, who was most brave and steady in battle. That is why he came to be known as Aniruddha. He begot Mrigaketana. Samba begot five valiant and truthful sons from his wife, Kashya, the daughter of King Suparshva

## \|\| 47.15-27 \|\|

*rukmiṇī janayāmāsa putrānraṇaviśāradān \|*  
*cārudeṣṇaṃ raṇe śūraṃ pradyumnaṃ ca mahābalam \|\| 15 \|\|*

*sucāruṃ bhadracāruṃ ca sudeṣṇaṃ bhadrameva ca \|*  
*paraśuṃ cāruguptaṃ ca cārubhadraṃ sucārukam \|*  
*cāruhāsaṃ kaniṣṭhaṃ ca kanyāṃ cārumatīṃ tathā \|\| 16 \|\|*

*jajñire satyabhāmāyāṃ bhānurbhramaratekṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*rohito dīptimāṃścaiva tāmraś cakro jalaṃdhamaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*catasro jajñire teṣāṃ svasārastu yavīyasīḥ \|*  
*jāmbavatyāḥ suto jajñe sāmbaḥ samitiśobhanaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*mitravānmitravindaśca mitravindā varāṅganā \|*  
*mitrabāhuḥ sunīthaśca nāgnajityāḥ prajā hi sā \|\| 19 \|\|*

*evamādīni putrāṇāṃ sahasrāṇi nibodhata \|*  
*śataṃ śatasahasrāṇāṃ putrāṇāṃ tasya dhīmataḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*aśītiśca sahasrāṇi vāsudevasutāstathā \|*  
*lakṣamekaṃ tathā proktaṃ putrāṇāṃ ca dvijottamāḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*upasaṅgasya tu sutau vajraḥ saṃkṣipta eva ca \|*  
*bhūrīndraseno bhūriśca gaveṣaṇasutāv ubhau \|\| 22 \|\|*

*pradyumnasya tu dāyādo vaidarbhyāṃ buddhisattamaḥ \|*  
*aniruddho raṇe 'ruddho jajñe 'sya mṛgaketanaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

*kāśyā supārśvatanayā sāmbāllebhe tarasvinaḥ \|*  
*satyaprakṛtayo devāḥ pañca vīrāḥ prakīrtitāḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*tisraḥ koṭyaḥ pravīrāṇāṃ yādavānāṃ mahātmanām \|*  
*ṣaṣṭiḥ śatasahasrāṇi vīryavanto mahābalāḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*devāṃśāḥ sarva eveha hy utpannāste mahaujasaḥ \|*  
*devāsure hatā ye ca tv asurā ye mahābalāḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*ihotpannā manuṣyeṣu bādhante sarvamānavān \|*  
*teṣāmutsādanārthāya utpanno yādave kule \|\| 27 \|\|*

15-27. The valiant Yadavas multiplied themselves into a race of three crores, out of whom 60000 powerful ones were born as incarnations of Devas on this earth. - The incarnations of Asuras who were killed in the war between Devas and Asuras, were born on earth as obstructors of all human progress, and in order to destroy whom Sri Krishna was born in the clan of the Yadavas.

## \|\| 47.28-29 \|\|

*kulānāṃ śatamekaṃ ca yādavānāṃ mahātmanām \|*  
*sarvametatkulaṃ yāvad vartate vaiṣṇave kule \|\| 28 \|\|*

*viṣṇusteṣāṃ praṇetā ca prabhutve ca vyavasthitaḥ \|*  
*nideśasthāyinastasya kathyante sarvayādavāḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

28-29. The Yadavas, among whom Lord Krishna was born, had one hundred different families, all of which were supported by Vishnu; and it was for that reason that the Yadava clan went on prospering. All the Yadavas were the companions of Lord Krishna.

## \|\| 47.30-33 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ*  
*saptarṣayaḥ kuberaśca yakṣo māṇicarastathā \|*  
*śālakir nāradaścaiva siddho dhanvantaristathā \|\| 30 \|\|*

*ādidevastathā viṣṇur ebhistu saha daivataḥ \|*  
*kimarthaṃ saṃghaśo bhūtāḥ smṛtāḥ sambhūtayaḥ kati \|\| 31 \|\|*

*bhaviṣyāḥ kati caivānye prādurbhāvā mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*brahmakṣatreṣu śānteṣu kimarthamiha jāyate \|\| 32 \|\|*

*yadarthamiha sambhūto viṣṇurvṛṣṇyandhakottamaḥ \|*  
*punaḥ punarmanuṣyeṣu tannaḥ prabrūhi pṛcchatām \|\| 33 \|\|*

30-33. The Rishis said — Suta! How did Vishnu, the prime cause of the universe; come to be born on this earth, along with the seven Rishis, Kuvera, Yaksha, the sages Manichara, Salaki and Narada, Siddha, Dhanvantari? How many manifestations have there been of Vishnu, and how many of them will be in future? Why does the Lord Vishnu incarnate Himself exclusively among the tranquil Brahmans, and, the Kshatryas? O Suta!

Pray tell us the object of Vishnu’s incarnating Himself in the family of Vrishni, Andhaka, &c., and also the cause of manifesting Himself again and again in human form.

## \|\| 47.34-36 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*tyaktvā divyāṃ tanuṃ viṣṇur mānuṣeṣviha jāyate \|*  
*yuge tv atha parāvṛtte kāle praśithile prabhuḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

*devāsuravimardeṣu jāyate harirīśvaraḥ \|*  
*hiraṇyakaśipau daitye trailokyaṃ prākpraśāsati \|\| 35 \|\|*

*balinādhiṣṭhite caiva purā lokatraye kramāt \|*  
*sakhyamāsītparamakaṃ devānāmasuraiḥ saha \|\| 36 \|\|*

34-36. Suta said: — At the end of a Yuga, and when morals of the time becomes lax, owing to the loss of righteousness in the universe, Lord Vishnu casts: off His Divine form and assumes that of a man; or, when the Devas and the Asuras combine to oppress the world, then the Lord Hari incarnates Himself. Thus he incarnated when, in the days gone by, the Daitya Hiranya Kashyapu was ruling the three worlds. Similarly, He incarnated when Bali of yore ruled the three worlds. In the reigns of these two rulers there was great friendship between the Devas and the asuras

## \|\| 47.37-39 \|\|

*yugākhyāsurasampūrṇaṃ hy āsīd atyākulaṃ jagat \|*  
*nideśasthāyinaścāpi tayordevāsurāḥ samam \|\| 37 \|\|*

*mṛdho balivimardāya sampravṛddhaḥ sudāruṇaḥ \|*  
*devānāmasurāṇāṃ ca ghoraḥ kṣayakaro mahān \|\| 38 \|\|*

*kartuṃ dharmavyavasthānaṃ jāyate mānuṣeṣviha \|*  
*bhṛgoḥ śāpanimittaṃ tu devāsurakṛte tadā \|\| 39 \|\|*

37-39. But all the same, the world was agitated by the presence of the Asuras; for it was an age of Asuras, the Devas being in minority. The Devas and the demons residing under the sway of Hiranyakashyapu and Bali were on equal footing. In other words, the Devas and the Asuras under their sway enjoyed equal rights and privileges. At the same time, on account of the curse of Bhrigu, there was a destructive warfare between the Devas and the Asuras to cause pain to Bali, when Lord Vishnu manifested Himself in the human form to re-establish righteousness, for the sake of the Devas and the Asuras.

## \|\| 47.40 \|\|

*munaya ūcuḥ*  
*kathaṃ devāsurakṛte vyāpāraṃ prāptavānsvataḥ \|*  
*devāsuraṃ yathā vṛttaṃ tannaḥ prabrūhi pṛcchatām \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. The Rishis said: — Suta! Why did Lord Vishnu interest Himself personally in the affairs of the Devas and the Asuras? How did this conflict arise of itself between the Devas and the Asuras, who were living on friendly terms before? Pray tell us all that

## \|\| 47.41-45 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*teṣāṃ dāyanimittaṃ te saṃgrāmāstu sudāruṇāḥ \|*  
*varāhādyā daśa dvau ca śaṇḍāmarkāntare smṛtāḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

*nāmatastu samāsena śṛṇutaiṣāṃ vivakṣataḥ \|*  
*prathamo nārasiṃhastu dvitīyaścāpi vāmanaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

*tṛtīyastu varāhaśca caturtho 'mṛtamanthanaḥ \|*  
*saṃgrāmaḥ pañcamaścaiva saṃjātastārakāmayaḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

*ṣaṣṭho hy āḍībakākhyastu saptamastraipurastathā \|*  
*andhakākhyo 'ṣṭamasteṣāṃ navamo vṛtraghātakaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

*dhātraśca daśamaścaiva tato hālāhalaḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*prathito dvādaśasteṣāṃ ghoraḥ kolāhalastathā \|\| 45 \|\|*

41-45. Suta said: — There were twelve hard fought battles between the Devas and the Asuras on account of getting their heritage, beginning from ‘the Varaha (Boar) incarnation and ending with Shanda and Marka times; and there were incarnations on the occasion of each war. The first was that of Man-lion (Nrisimha), the second that of Vamana, third that of Varaha, the fourth incarnation was on the occasion of the churning of the ocean for the nectar, the filth took place at Tarakamaya war, the sixth was called the Adivaka war, the seventh was the Traipura war, the eighth was the Andhaka war; the war for the destruction of Vritrasura was the ninth, the Dhatri war was the tenth, the Halahala war was the eleventh and the twelfth was the terrific war, named Kolahala.

## \|\| 47.46-47 \|\|

*hiraṇyakaśipur daityo nārasiṃhena pātitaḥ \|*  
*vāmanena balir baddhas trailokyākramaṇe purā \|\| 46 \|\|*

*hiraṇyākṣo hato dvaṃdve pratighāte tu daivataiḥ \|*  
*daṃṣṭrayā tu varāheṇa samudrastu dvidhā kṛtaḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

46-47. Nrisimha killed the Daitya king, Hiranyakashyapu, Vamana made the Daitya king Bali a captive, by measuring the three regions. Varsha killed the Daitya Hiranyaksha with His tusks and divided the ocean into two.

## \|\| 47.48-49 \|\|

*prahlādo nirjito uddhe indreṇāmṛtamanthane \|*  
*virocanastu prāhlādir nityam indravadhodyataḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

*indreṇaiva tu vikramya nihatastārakāmaye \|*  
*aśaknuvansa devānāṃ sarvaṃ soḍhuṃ sadaivatam \|\| 49 \|\|*

48-49. At the time of churning the ocean for nectar, Indra conquered Prahlada, and then He killed Virochana, the son of Prahlada, in the Tarakamaya war; for the latter was always after the life of Indra and never was friendly to the deeds of the Devas.

## \|\| 47.50 \|\|

*nihatā dānavāḥ sarve trailokye tryambakeṇa tu \|*  
*asurāśca piśācāśca dānavāścāndhakāhave \|\| 50 \|\|*

50 At the time of Adivaka war, Lord Shiva killed the Daitya Tripura, along with other Danavas, besides those that He killed in the Andhaka war.

## \|\| 47.51-53 \|\|

*hatā devamanuṣye sve pitṛbhiścaiva sarvaśaḥ \|*  
*saṃpṛkto dānavairvṛtro ghoro hālāhale hataḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

*tadā viṣṇusahāyena mahendreṇa nivartitaḥ \|*  
*hato dhvaje mahendreṇa māyācchannastu yogavit \|*  
*dhvajalakṣaṇamāviṣya vipracittiḥ sahānujaḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

*daityāṃśca dānavāṃścaiva saṃyatānkila saṃyutān \|*  
*jayankolāhale sarvān devaiḥ parivṛto vṛṣā \|\| 53 \|\|*

51-53. In the Vritra-nashaka war, Indra, by the help of Vishnu, killed Vritrasura, who was sided with by men, Pitris and Devas and then He also killed most fearful Danavas in the Dhatri and Halahala wars. He killed the Daitya Viprachit in the Kolahala war, which was an offshoot of the Shanda Marka wars that ensued between the Devas and the Daityas over the right of Avabhritha bath; when Viprachit was hiding himself with the army of Danavas under his banner.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — Avabhritha = Bathing at the end of a principal sacrifice, for purification.

## \|\| 47.54 \|\|

*yajñasyāvabhṛthe dṛṣyau śaṇḍāmarkau tu daivataiḥ \|*  
*ete devāsure vṛttāḥ saṃgrāmā dvādaśaiva tu \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. In that way, there were a dozen battles between the Devas and the Asuras in which the military classes of Devas and Asuras. were killed but it was good for the general populace.

## \|\| 47.55-57 \|\|

*devāsurakṣayakarāḥ prajānāṃ tu hitāya vai \|*  
*hiraṇyakaśipū rājā varṣāṇāmarbudaṃ babhau \|\| 55 \|\|*

*dvisaptati tathānyāni niutānyadhikāni ca \|*  
*aśītiṃ ca sahasrāṇi trailokyaiśvaryatāṃ gataḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

*paryāyeṇa nu rājābhūd balirvarṣāutaṃ punaḥ \|*  
*ṣaṣṭivarṣasahasrāṇi niutāni ca viṃśatiḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

55-57. Hiranyakashyapu ruled the land with all the mundane glory at his command, for a period of one hundred million seventy eight crores and eighty thousand years, after whom Bali ruled for 20,080,000 years and Prahlada also ruled for a similar period with other Asuras.

## \|\| 47.58-59 \|\|

*bale rājyādhikārastu yāvatkālaṃ babhūva ha \|*  
*tāvatkālaṃ tu prahlādo nivṛtto hy asuraiḥ saha \|\| 58 \|\|*

*indrāstrayaste vijñeyā asurāṇāṃ mahaujasaḥ \|*  
*daityasaṃsthamidaṃ sarvam āsīddaśaugaṃ punaḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

58-59. All three of them were the most powerful Daitya Kings, and known as Indras of Daityas. This world was under the sway of. the Daityas for ten yugas. After which, Indra ruled over the three regions with marvellous tact and statesmanship.

## \|\| 47.60 \|\|

*trailokyamidamavyagraṃ mahendreṇānupālyate \|*  
*asapatnamidaṃ sarvam āsīddaśaugaṃ punaḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Indra ruled, since the close of the sway of Prahlada, when the seer, Shukra, deserted the Daityas and joined the Devas.

## \|\| 47.61-65 \|\|

*prahlādasya hate tasmiṃs trailokye kālaparyayāt \|*  
*paryāyeṇa tu samprāpte trailokyaṃ pākaśāsane \|*  
*tato 'surānparityajya śukro devānagacchata \|\| 61 \|\|*

*yajñe devānatha gataṃ ditijāḥ kāvyamāhvayan \|*  
*kiṃ tvaṃ no miṣatāṃ rājyaṃ tyaktvā yajñaṃ punargataḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

*sthātuṃ na śaknumo hy atra praviśāmo rasātalam \|*  
*evamukto 'bravīddaityān viṣaṇṇānsāntvayangirā \|\| 63 \|\|*

*mā bhaiṣṭa dhārayiṣyāmi tejasā svena vo 'surāḥ \|*  
*mantrāścauṣadhayaścaiva rasā vasu ca yatparam \|\| 64 \|\|*

*kṛtsnāni mayi tiṣṭhanti pādasteṣāṃ sureṣu vai \|*  
*tatsarvaṃ vaḥ pradāsyāmi uṣmadarthe dhṛtā mayā \|\| 65 \|\|*

61-65. Once the sage Shukra happened to go to the sacrifice of the Devas, when the Daityas called him and asked him how he did that during their loss of kingdom. The Daityas said that they could no longer stay in that region and would repair to Rasatala — which grieved the seer, who said that they need not fear, he would sustain them by his power, for it was he alone who had spells, medicines, nectar, and the best of things, in his possession to the fall, The Devas had only one-fourth of them. He would give everything to them, for he had preserved them with him for their sake.

## \|\| 47.67-68 \|\|

*kāvyo hy eṣa idaṃ sarvaṃ vyāvartayati no balāt \|*  
*sādhu gacchāmahe tūrṇaṃ yāvannādhyāpayiṣyati \|\| 67 \|\|*

*prasahya hatvā śiṣṭāṃstu pātālaṃ prāpayāmahe \|*  
*tato devāstu saṃrabdhā dānavān upasṛtya ha \|\| 68 \|\|*

67-68. The Devas on seeing the Daityas clustering around the sage Shukra (Kavya), held a council of their own to devise means to acquire all those boons from the sage. They all discussed among themselves that the sage was forcibly usurping their dues, and so before he conferred them on the Daityas they would all go and manage to let the Daityas go to Patala by their stubbornness. With that resolution, the Devas went and caused trouble to the Danavas.

## \|\| 47.69-70 \|\|

*tataste vadhyamānāstu kāvyamevābhidudruvuḥ \|*  
*tataḥ kāvyastu tāndṛṣṭvā tūrṇaṃ devair abhidrutān \|\| 69 \|\|*

*rakṣāṃ kāvyena saṃhṛtya devāste 'pyasurārditāḥ \|*  
*kāvyaṃ dṛṣṭvā sthitaṃ devā niḥśaṅkamasurāñjahuḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

69-70. At that, the Daityas, overpowered with affliction, went and sought the succour of Shukra and were rescued by him instantly. Afterwards they started their operations against the Devas who, defying the support of Shukra, began to annihilate them.

## \|\| 47.71-75 \|\|

*tataḥ kāvyo 'nucintyātha brāhmaṇo vacanaṃ hitam \|*  
*tānuvāca tataḥ kāvyaḥ pūrvaṃ vṛttamanusmaran \|\| 71 \|\|*

*trailokyaṃ vo hṛtaṃ sarvaṃ vāmanena tribhiḥ kramaiḥ \|*  
*balirbaddho hato jambho nihataśca virocanaḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

*mahāsurā dvādaśasu saṃgrāmeṣu surair hatāḥ \|*  
*taistairupāyairbhūyiṣṭhaṃ nihatā vaḥ pradhānataḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

*kiṃcicchīṣṭāstu yūyaṃ vai uddhaṃ māstviti me matam \|*  
*nītiṃ yāṃ vo 'bhidhāsyāmi tiṣṭhadhvaṃ kālaparyayāt \|\| 74 \|\|*

*yāsyāmyahaṃ mahādevaṃ mantrārthaṃ vijayāvaham \|*  
*apratīpāṃstato mantrān devātprāpya maheśvarāt \|*  
*yudhyāmahe punardevāṃs tataḥ prāpsyatha vai jayam \|\| 75 \|\|*

71-75. Then the sage, thinking of the past, addressed the Daityas for their well-being: — “Vamana has deprived you of all your realm by measuring it with his three strides, and has made Bali a captive.

Besides, He has killed Jambhasura and Virochana. In course of the twelve. battles, the Devas have killed most of your powerful members, by their various stratagems. Very few of you are left now, therefore follow my advice and cease fighting for some time. I shall teach you a useful contrivance. I will go to acquire the spell of victory from Shiva, and, after acquiring those powerful charms from him, shall make you victorious in your fight with the Devas."

## \|\| 47.76-78 \|\|

*tataste kṛtasaṃvādā devān ūcustadāsurāḥ \|*  
*nyastaśastrā vayaṃ sarve niḥsaṃnāhā rathairvinā \|\| 76 \|\|*

*vayaṃ tapaścariṣyāmaḥ saṃvṛtā valkalairvane \|*  
*prahlādasya vacaḥ śrutvā satyābhivyāhṛtaṃ tu tat \|\| 77 \|\|*

*tato devā nyavartanta vijvarā muditāśca te \|*  
*nyastaśastreṣu daityeṣu vinivṛttāstadā surāḥ \|\| 78 \|\|*

76-78. Hearing those words of their Preceptor, the Asuras spoke to the Devas, O Devas! We are without arms, our armours are broken, we have no chariots; consequently, we will now go and practise austerities in the forest after covering ourselves with the bark of trees.” Hearing those words of the Asuras and believing the utterances of Prahlada to be true, the Devas cast off their wrath and cheerfully stopped fighting with the defenseless Asuras.

## \|\| 47.79-80 \|\|

*tatastānabravītkāvyaḥ kaṃcitkālamupāsyatha \|*  
*nirutsiktās tapoyuktāḥ kālaṃ kāryārthasādhakam \|\| 79 \|\|*

*piturmamāśramasthā vai māṃ pratīkṣata dānavāḥ \|*  
*tatsaṃdiśyāsurānkāvyo mahādevaṃ prapadyata \|\| 80 \|\|*

79-80. Sometime afterwards, the seer Shukra said to his disciples: — “For the accomplishment of your desires, keep yourselves engaged in your penances, and, O Daityas! go and reside in my. father’s house and await my return there.” Giving that piece of advice to the Danavas, Shukra went to Mahadeva

## \|\| 47.80 \|\|

*piturmamāśramasthā vai māṃ pratīkṣata dānavāḥ \|*  
*tatsaṃdiśyāsurānkāvyo mahādevaṃ prapadyata \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. Shukra-said: — “O, Mahadeva! I wish to acquire the spells, that are not possessed by Brihaspati even, for the defeat of the Devas and the victory of the Asuras.”

## \|\| 47.82 \|\|

*evamukto 'bravīddevo vrataṃ tvaṃ cara bhārgava \|*  
*pūrṇaṃ varṣasahasraṃ tu kaṇadhūmamavākśirāḥ \|*  
*yadi pāsyasi bhadraṃ te tato mantrānavāpsyasi \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. Mahadeva said: — “Bhargava! You shall acquire those spells after practising austerities with your head suspended down and imbibing the smoke of chaff for a thousand years. If thou succeeds in this, thou shalt obtain the mantras.”

## \|\| 47.83 \|\|

*tatheti samanujñāpya śukrastu bhṛgunandanaḥ \|*  
*pādau saṃspṛṣya devasya bāḍhamityabravīdvacaḥ \|*  
*vrataṃ carāmyahaṃ deva tvayādiṣṭo 'dya vai prabho \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. Then Shukra, accepting the injunctions of the Lord Shiva, touched His feet and said, “Sire! In obedience to your will, I start to observe the penances dictated by you.”

## \|\| 47.84 \|\|

*tato 'nusṛṣṭo devena kuṇḍadhāro 'sya dhūmakṛt \|*  
*tadā tasmingate śukre hy asurāṇāṃ hitāya vai \|*  
*mantrārthaṃ tatra vasati brahmacaryaṃ maheśvare \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. Afterwards, the sage, to acquire the spells for the well-being of the Asuras, went to practice asceticism by the side of the altar from which smoke emitted fire

## \|\| 47.85 \|\|

*tadbuddhvā nītipūrvaṃ tu rājye nyaste tadāsuraiḥ \|*  
*asmiṃśchidre tadāmarṣād devāstānsamupādravan \|*  
*daṃśitāḥ sāudhāḥ sarve bṛhaspatipuraḥsarāḥ \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. The Devas, understanding the treacherous policy of the Asuras, tried to turn them out of the region where they were residing.

## \|\| 47.86-87 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvāsuragaṇā devān pragṛhītāudhānpunaḥ \|*  
*utpetuḥ sahasā te vai saṃtrastāstānvaco 'bruvan \|\| 86 \|\|*

*nyaste śastre 'bhaye datta ācārye vratamāsthite \|*  
*dattvā bhavanto hy abhayaṃ samprāptā no jighāṃsayā \|\| 87 \|\|*

86-87. The Asuras, on seeing the Devas unexpectedly advancing towards them well-armed, in company of their. Preceptor Brihaspati, became grieved and said:

## \|\| 47.88-91 \|\|

*anācāryā vayaṃ devās tyaktaśastrāstvavasthitāḥ \|*  
*cīrakṛṣṇājinadharā niṣkriyā niṣparigrahāḥ \|\| 88 \|\|*

*raṇe vijetuṃ devāṃśca na śakṣyāmaḥ kathaṃcana \|*  
*auddhena prapatsyāmaḥ śaraṇaṃ kāvyamātaram \|\| 89 \|\|*

*yāpayāmaḥ kṛcchramidaṃ yāvadabhyeti no guruḥ \|*  
*nivṛtte ca tathā śukre yotsyāmo daṃśitāudhāḥ \|\| 90 \|\|*

*evamuktvā tato 'nyonyaṃ śaraṇaṃ kāvyamātaram \|*  
*prāpadyanta tato bhītās tebhyo 'dādabhayaṃ tu sā \|\| 91 \|\|*

88-91. We have disarmed ourselves at your request on giving us the assurance of safety, and our preceptor is engaged in the observance of his vow. How have you come to fight us after giving us an assurance of peace. O Devas, we have not our preceptor by us and are living peacefully without weapons, and we are dressed in deer skin and tree barks and without any occupation or possessions. O Devas! We are not in a position to fight with you. We will go and seek shelter from the mother of our preceptor without offering you any resistance. We will live with her in peace and safety till the return of the sage, after which we will fight with you.”

## \|\| 47.92 \|\|

*na bhetavyaṃ na bhetavyaṃ bhayaṃ tyajata dānavāḥ \|*  
*matsaṃnidhau vartatāṃ vo na bhīr bhavitumarhati \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. All the terrified Asuras afterwards went and took shelter with the mother of the sage who gave them assurance of safety.

## \|\| 47.93 \|\|

*tayā cābhyupapannāṃstān dṛṣṭvā devāstato 'surān \|*  
*abhijagmuḥ prasahyaitān avicārya balābalam \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. She said, “Danavas, do not be afraid of anything; drive away all your fears from your mind. Nothing will happen to you in course of your stay with me.

## \|\| 47.94-95 \|\|

*tatastānbādhyamānāṃstu devairdṛṣṭvāsurāṃstadā \|*  
*devī kruddhābravīddevān anindrānvaḥ karomyaham \|\| 94 \|\|*

*saṃbhṛtya sarvasambhārān indraṃ sābhyacarattadā \|*  
*tastambha devī balavad yogauktā tapodhanā \|\| 95 \|\|*

94-95. Then the Devas, without any regard for their comparative strength, went for the Asuras, who had placed themselves at the mercy of Shukra’s mother; seeing which the mother of their preceptor very angrily said that she would make them Indraless.

## \|\| 47.96-97 \|\|

*tatastaṃ stambhitaṃ dṛṣṭvā indraṃ devāśca mūkavat \|*  
*prādravanta tato bhītā indraṃ dṛṣṭvā vaśīkṛtam \|\| 96 \|\|*

*gateṣu surasaṃgheṣu śakraṃ viṣṇurabhāṣata \|*  
*māṃ tvaṃ praviśa bhadraṃ te nayiṣye tvāṃ surottama \|\| 97 \|\|*

96-97. After saying that, she, mustering all her will-force, advanced towards Indra and made him helpless and spell-bound by her great power of yoga and austerities. The Devas, seeing Indra thus spell-bound and helpless like a dumb person by the mother of Shukra, took to flight

## \|\| 47.98 \|\|

*evamuktastato viṣṇuṃ praviveśa puraṃdaraḥ \|*  
*viṣṇunā rakṣitaṃ dṛṣṭvā devī kruddhā vaco 'bravīt \|\| 98 \|\|*

98\. After the retreat of the Devas, Lord Vishnu said :— “Indra! You enter yourself within me and I shall carry you away from this place.”

## \|\| 47.99 \|\|

*eṣā tvāṃ viṣṇunā sārdhaṃ dahāmi maghavanbalāt \|*  
*miṣatāṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ dṛṣyatāṃ me tapobalam \|\| 99 \|\|*

99\. Hearing those words of Vishnu, Indra Purandara instantly entered himself within Him, when the mother of the sage seeing him thus protected by Vishnu said in anger:

## \|\| 47.100 \|\|

*tayā 'bhibhūtau tau devāv indrāviṣṇū babhūvatuḥ \|*  
*kathaṃ mucyeva sahitau viṣṇurindram abhāṣata \|\| 100 \|\|*

100\. “Indra! I have ‘such powers of asceticism that I shall reduce you to ashes along with Vishnu, in presence of all creatures”.

## \|\| 47.103 \|\|

*tatastu tvarayā uktaḥ śīghrakārī bhayānvitaḥ \|*  
*jñātvā viṣṇustatastasyā krūraṃ devyāścikīrṣitam \|*  
*kruddhaḥ svamastramādāya śiraściccheda vai bhiyā \|\| 103 \|\|*

103\. Bay “At that, both Indra and Vishnu were overcome with fear and began to contrive some means of escape. Vishnu said to Indra: — “How shall we ‘escape from her?” Indra replied: — “Lord! kill her before she consumes the, I am solely protected by you, destroy her soon without delay,”

Vishnu thought over the greats in of killing a woman, but, in spite of that, he took up his Sudarshana Chakra to free Himself from that impending calamity

## \|\| 47.104 \|\|

*taṃ dṛṣṭvā strīvadhaṃ ghoraṃ cukrodha bhṛgurīśvaraḥ \|*  
*tato 'bhiśapto bhṛguṇā viṣṇur bhāryāvadhe tadā \|\| 104 \|\|*

104\. Trembling with fear, on thinking over the consequences of her anger and being afraid of the consequences of His own wrath, He severed her head with His Chakra

## \|\| 47.105 \|\|

*yasmātte jānato dharma-pravadhyā strī niṣūditā \|*  
*tasmāttvaṃ saptakṛtveha mānuṣeṣūpapatsjase \|\| 105 \|\|*

105\. The sage Bhrigu then cursed Vishnu for killing his wife.

## \|\| 47.106 \|\|

*tatastenābhiśāpena naṣṭe dharme punaḥpunaḥ \|*  
*lokasya ca hitārthāya jāyate mānuyeṣviha \|\| 106 \|\|*

106\. He said i Vishnu! You will be born seven times among men for the sin of killing a woman, knowing that a woman under no circumstances is to be killed”.

## \|\| 47.107 \|\|

*anuvyāhṛtya viṣṇuṃ sa tadādāya śirastvaran \|*  
*samānīya tataḥ kāyam asau gṛhyedamabravīt \|\| 107 \|\|*

107 Since then, owing to that curse of the sage, Vishnu manifests Himself among men for the good of mankind, whenever there is a decay in righteousness”.

## \|\| 47.108-110 \|\|

*eṣā tvaṃ viṣpunā devi hatā saṃjīvayāmyaham \|*  
*tatastāṃ yojya śirasā abhijīveti so 'bravīt \|\| 108 \|\|*

*yadi kṛtsno mayā dharmo jñāyate carito 'pi vā \|*  
*tena satyena jīvasva yadi satyaṃ vadāmyaham \|\| 109 \|\|*

*tatastāṃ prokṣya śītābhir adbhir jīveti so 'bravīt \|*  
*tato 'bhivyāhṛte tasya devī saṃjīvitā tadā \|\| 110 \|\|*

108-110. Afterwards, the seer Bhrigu at once picked up the severed head of his wife and joined it to the trunk, saying: — Devi! You have been killed-by Lord Vishnu, and now I recall you to life again.” Saying that, he joined the head and the trunk together, and said “Abhijiva”; (“Be revived”); if I have fulfilled all the rules of law and acted righteously, and if I have always spoken the truth, then through that truth you come back to life. I say so truthfully.

## \|\| 47.111 \|\|

*tatastāṃ sarvabhūtāni dṛṣṭvā suptotthitāmiva \|*  
*sādhu sādhviti cakruste vacasā sarvatodiśam \|\| 111 \|\|*

111\. After that, he sprinkled cold water and again pronounced the spell; “Abhijiva”, and the lady at once came back to life.

## \|\| 47.112 \|\|

*evaṃ pratyāhṛtā tena devī sā bhṛguṇā tadā \|*  
*miṣatāṃ devatānāṃ hi tadadbhutam ivābhavad \|\| 112 \|\|*

112\. On seeing her thus coming to life, as if rising from her slumber, everyone present, there repeatedly expressed his delight by saying, “Well done”, “Well done”.

## \|\| 47.113 \|\|

*asaṃbhrāntena bhṛguṇā patnī saṃjīvitā punaḥ \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā cendro nālabhata śarma kāvyabhayātpunaḥ \|*  
*prajāgare tataścendro jayantīmidamabravīt \|\| 113 \|\|*

113\. Thus that lady was revived by Bhrigu, in the presence of the astonished Devatas, and the whole thing was considered a miracle

## \|\| 47.114-117 \|\|

*saṃcintya matimān vākyaṃ svāṃ kanyāṃ pākaśāsanaḥ \|*

*tenāhaṃ vyākulaḥ putri kṛto matimatā bhṛśam \|\| 114 \|\|*

*gaccha saṃsādhayasvainaṃ śramāpanayanaiḥ śubhaiḥ \|*  
*taistairmanonukūlaiśca hy upacārair atandritā \|\| 115 \|\|*

*kāvyamārādhayasvainaṃ yathā tuṣyeta sa dvijaḥ \|*  
*gaccha tvaṃ tasya dattā'si prayatnaṃ kuru matkṛte \|\| 116 \|\|*

*evamuktā jayantī sā vacaḥ saṃgṛhya vai pituḥ \|*  
*agacchadyatra ghoraṃ sa tapa ārabhya tiṣṭhati \|\| 117 \|\|*

114-117. Indra seeing the sage Bhrigu quietly bringing back his wife to life, became terribly afraid and had no peace He said to his daughter, Jayanti:

— “Daughter! This seer Shukra is practising rigid and devout asceticism for the sake of my foes, which is causing me deep pain; so you should go to him and please him by your service and conduct, Do just what he wishes, and serve him with all diligence. Do exactly what would please him. Go, I have dedicated you to him. Worship him and try all that lies in you to serve my end.”

## \|\| 47.118 \|\|

*taṃ dṛṣṭvā tu pibantaṃ sā kaṇadhūmam avāṅmukham \|*  
*yakṣeṇa pātyamānaṃ ca kuṇḍadhāreṇa pātitam \|\| 118 \|\|*

118\. Hearing those words of her father, Jayanti went to the spot where the sage was engaged in his rigid austerities.

## \|\| 47.119-125 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā ca taṃ pātyamānaṃ devī kāvyamavasthitam \|*

*pitrā yathoktaṃ vākyaṃ sā kāvye kṛtavatī tadā \|\| 119 \|\|*

*gīrbhiścaivānukūlābhiḥ stuvatī valgubhāṣiṇī \|*  
*gātrasaṃvāhanaiḥ kāle sevamānā tvacaḥ sukhaiḥ \|*  
*vratacaryānukūlābhir uvāsa bahulāḥ samāḥ \|\| 120 \|\|*

*pūrṇe dhūmavrate tasmin ghore varṣasahasrake \|*

*mahādeva uvāca*  
*etadvrataṃ tvayaikena cīrṇaṃ nānyena kenacit \|*  
*tasmādvai tapasā buddhyā śrutena ca balena ca \|\| 122 \|\|*

*tejasā ca surānsarvāṃs tvameko 'bhibhaviṣyasi \|*  
*yaccābhilaṣitaṃ brahman vidyate bhṛgunandana \|\| 123 \|\|*

*prapatsyase tu tatsarvaṃ nānuvācyaṃ tu kasyacit \|*

*etāndattvā varāṃstasmai bhārgavāya bhavaḥ punaḥ \|*  
*prajeśatvaṃ dhaneśatvam avadhyatvaṃ ca vai dadau \|\| 125 \|\|*

119-125. There she saw the sage suspended with his head downwards and imbibing the smoke of the chaff; while a Yaksha had just thrown him down the side of the Kunda. She found him all absorbed in his austerities, looking very lean and having all his body covered with ashes.

Seeing the sage like that, she set herself to serve him according to the injunctions of her father. In other words, she began to serve the sage by shampooing his legs and winning his pleasure by her sweet and flattering speech; and, adapting herself to suit his pleasure, she practiced penances along with him for many a year. On the lapse of a thousand years of practising this vow of smoke, the God Shiva, becoming satisfied, appeared to grant boons to Shukra, and said: — “Shukra! You alone have undergone this penance, none other has done so, consequently, you alone will have the glory of conquering all the Devas by your asceticism, intellect, knowledge of the Shastras, splendour, and power; and O, Bhrigunandana! in addition to all these, you will achieve all the rest of your desires.” Do not say so before any one, but you alone will accomplish everything.

## \|\| 47.126 \|\|

*etāṃllabdhvā varānkāvyaḥ samprahṛṣṭatanūruhaḥ \|*

*tathā tiryaksthitaścaiva tuṣṭuve nīlalohitam \|\| 126 \|\|*

126\. The Lord Shiva, after granting all those boons to Shukra, also made him master of mankind and riches as well as invulnerable.

*śukra uvāca*  
*namo 'stu śitikaṇṭhāya kaniṣṭhāya suvarcase \|*

127\. On getting all those boons, Shukra (Kavya) had such an unbounded pleasure that all the hair of his body were thrilled with joy. After that, the sage pleased the Lord by standing curved and singing the hymn of praises to the God of blue red color.

silver, all-pervading, the omnipresent, the holy, the forcible, the sovereign Lord, the far-seeing, the possessor of high class arrows and horses, the benefactor, the giver of emancipation, whose complexion is reddish (Kapila), the Lord of Deities, the most learned and intellectual, of the. mighty form, the illustrious, known under the epithet of Rodana, the patron of all, the renowned archer, the wearer of the armour, the great charioteer (Rathin), the guardian of all, the Lord of Bhrigu, the radiant, the dweller in the cavity of the heart, the creator, the unfailing, the serene, the wise, the best, the glorious, the soul of the universe, the wearer of the deer-skin, the Lord of animals and ghosts, the Sacred Symbol (...), the soul of the Rik, Yajus and Sama (Vedas), as well as of the oblations made to the Gods and the Manes of ancestors, and the Deities, the creative power, the chief agent, the great ocular evidence, the Vedic knowledge, the Master of the past and the future of the universe, the soul of actions, who manifests Himself as Vasu, Sadhya, Rudra, Aditya, Sura, Visa, Maruta, Devatma, the knower of the ceremony of bringing out Agni and Soma, the supreme soul, the sacred text, the Lord of medicaments, who calls Himself. into being at His will (Swayambhu), who is not born (in the ordinary course), the magnificent, the Prime, the father of creation, the soul of Brahma, the Master of soul, the Master of all, the infinite, the omnipresent among all the purified souls, devoid of the properties belonging to all created things, the most excellent, the manifest, the immortal, the great nameless, the universal friend, the deliverer of the soul from the fetters of the phenomenal creation by conveying a correct knowledge of the other tattvas, the life of the seven worlds, viz., the earth, the astral plane, the heaven-world, the space, the sky, and of the regions Maha, Jana, Tapa and Satya, the unmanifest (Prakriti) the Mahattattwa, the elements, the senses, the Atman, the subtle element called - Vishesha, salutation to Thee, O Soul of all, Thou art the Arial bliss, the omnipresent in the three regions and existing beyond these three, the pervader in the four higher realms, viz.: — Maha, Jana, Tapa and Satya

## \|\| 47.168 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*evamābhāṣya deveśam īśvaraṃ nīlalohitam \|*  
*prahvo 'bhipraṇatastasmai prāñjalirvāgyato 'bhavat \|\| 168 \|\|*

168\. O Lord Shiva! if in course of this hymn of devotion, I have failed to describe Thee adequately, forgive me in consideration of my being your staunch adherent, for Thou art always a friend to a Brahmana.

## \|\| 47.169-174 \|\|

*kāvyasya gātraṃ saṃspṛṣya hastena prītimānbhavaḥ \|*  
*nikāmaṃ darśanaṃ dattvā tatraivāntaradhīyata \|\| 169 \|\|*

*tataḥ so 'ntarhite tasmin deveśe 'nucarīṃ tadā \|*  
*tiṣṭhantīṃ pārśvato dṛṣṭvā jayantīmidamabravīt \|\| 170 \|\|*

*kasya tvaṃ subhage kā vā duḥkhite mayi duḥkhitā \|*  
*mahatā tapasā uktā kimarthaṃ māṃ niṣevase \|\| 171 \|\|*

*anayā saṃstuto bhaktyā praśrayeṇa damena ca \|*  
*snehena caiva suśroṇi prīto 'smi varavarṇini \|\| 172 \|\|*

*kimicchasi varārohe kaste kāmaḥ samṛdhyatām \|*  
*tatte sampādayāmyadya yadyapi syātsuduṣkaraḥ \|\| 173 \|\|*

*evamuktābravīdenaṃ tapasā jñātumarhasi \|*  
*cikīrṣitaṃ hi me brahmaṃs tvaṃ hi vettha yathātatham \|\| 174 \|\|*

169-174. Suta said: — The sage, after thus saluting Mahadeva, stood quietly, with folded hands, before Him. Then the Lord became still more pleased with Shukra; and, after placing His Divine hand on the seer, vanished instantly. — After that, the sage addressed Jayanti, who was standing close by him. He said, “Who art Thou, and why art thon sorrowing for me, on account of my penances? Why art thon serving me with so much devotion and austerity? O Beautiful one! I am very much pleased with thy devotion and affection, What dost thou wish? Tell that to, me, I shall certainly do anything for thy sake, howsoever difficult it may be.

## \|\| 47.175 \|\|

*evamukto 'bravīdenāṃ dṛṣṭvā divyena cakṣuṣā \|*  
*mayā saha tvaṃ suśroṇi daśa varṣāṇi bhāmini \|\| 175 \|\|*

175\. Hearing those words of the sage, Jayanti said: — “Brahman! Ascertain my desires through the powers of your asceticism.

## \|\| 47.176-178 \|\|

*sarvabhūtairadṛśyā ca saṃprayogamihecchasi \|*  
*devi cendīvaraśyāme varārhe vāmalocane \|*  
*evaṃ vṛṇoṣi kāmaṃ tvaṃ matto vai valgubhāṣiṇi \|\| 176 \|\|*

*evaṃ bhavatu gacchāmo gṛhānno mattakāśini \|*  
*tataḥ svagṛhamāgatya jayantyāḥ pāṇimudvahan \|\| 177 \|\|*

*tayā sahāvasaddevyā daśa varṣāṇi bhārgavaḥ \|*  
*adṛṣyaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ māyayā saṃvṛtaḥ prabhuḥ \|\| 178 \|\|*

176-178. At that expression of Jayanti, the sage realized everything through his Divine sight, and said to her: — “O Enchanting one! Thou hast thought of living with me for ten years. This is your desire, which will be fulfilled; follow me to my abode.” Afterwards, Shukra took her home and married her there

## \|\| 47.179 \|\|

*kṛtārthamāgataṃ dṛṣṭvā kāvyaṃ sarve diteḥ sutāḥ \|*  
*abhijagmurgṛhaṃ tasya muditāste didṛkṣavaḥ \|\| 179 \|\|*

179\. Then the sage Bhargava, to enjoy himself in her company undisturbed, made himself invisible by means of his magical power.

## \|\| 47.180-181 \|\|

*yadā gatā na paṣyanti māyayā saṃvṛtaṃ gurum \|*  
*lakṣaṇaṃ tasya tadbuddhvā pratijagmuryathāgatam \|\| 180 \|\|*

*bṛhaspatistu saṃruddhaṃ kāvyaṃ jñātvā vareṇa tu \|*  
*tuṣṭyarthaṃ daśa varṣāṇi jayantyā hitakāmyayā \|\| 181 \|\|*

180-181. The Daityas, getting news of the return of their preceptor crowned with success, went exhilarated to pay their homage to him; but net, being able to see him owing to his being enveloped in illusion, they returned as they had gone

## \|\| 47.182-183 \|\|

*buddhvā tadantaraṃ so 'pi daityānāmindranoditaḥ \|*  
*kāvyasya rūpamāsthāya asurān samupāhvayat \|\| 182 \|\|*

*tatastānāgatāndṛṣṭvā bṛhaspatiruvāca ha \|*  
*svāgataṃ mama yājyānāṃ prāpto 'haṃ vo hitāya ca \|\| 183 \|\|*

182-183. Unfortunately for the Daityas, Brihaspati came to know of the doing of Shukra. He knew for certain that the preceptor of the Daityas would not break his shell of magic for ten years, as he was enjoying himself with Jayanti the Devas, on the other hand, also came to know of the weak point of the Daityas, that the latter were ignorant of the distinctive features of their preceptor. They consequently entreated Brihaspati to do something for them, Brihaspati thus incited by his disciples, personating as Shukra, went and rallied the Daityas round him.

## \|\| 47.184 \|\|

*ahaṃ vo 'dhyāpayiṣyāmi vidyāḥ prāptāstu yā mayā \|*  
*tataste hṛṣṭamanaso vidyārthamupapedire \|\| 184 \|\|*

184\. He, in the form of Shukra, then addressed the Daityas that had flocked to him, He said: — “O, my disciples! You are welcome. I have also come here to do you good. I shall teach you the knowledge that I have acquired from Shiva,” The Daityas were carried away by joy, and began to take lessons from him.

## \|\| 47.185-187 \|\|

*pūrṇe kāvyastadā tasmin samaye daśavārṣike \|*  
*samayānte devayānī tadotpannā iti śrutiḥ \|*  
*buddhiṃ cakre tataḥ so 'tha yājyānāṃ pratyavekṣaṇe \|\| 185 \|\|*

*devi gacchāmyahaṃ draṣṭuṃ mama yājyāñśucismite \|*  
*vibhrāntavīkṣite sādhvi trivarṇāyatalocane \|\| 186 \|\|*

*evamuktābravīd enaṃ bhaja bhaktānmahāvrata \|*  
*eṣa dharmaḥ satāṃ brahman na dharmaṃ lopayāmi te \|\| 187 \|\|*

185-187. After the lapse of ten years, the sage Shukra was also free from his enjoyments with Jayanti, and it is heard that Devayani was born of her. Then the Sage Shukra made up his mind to see his disciples — the Daityas and said to Jayanti, “Lady, I am going out to see my disciples.

## \|\| 47.189-190 \|\|

*kāvyaṃ māṃ vo vijānīdhvaṃ toṣito giriśo vibhuḥ \|*  
*vañcitā bata yūyaṃ vai sarve śṛṇuta dānavāḥ \|\| 189 \|\|*

*śrutvā tathā bruvāṇaṃ taṃ saṃbhrāntāste tadābhavan \|*  
*prekṣantas tāv ubhau tatra sthitāsīnau suvismitāḥ \|\| 190 \|\|*

189-190. Jayanti said: — Lord! go and look after your devotees. This is the duty of high-minded folks and I will not keep you away from it,” — a Shukra, on finding the Asuras deceived. by Brihaspati, said to them: — “Asuras! I am Shukra, who has pleased Lord Shiva. All of you have been deceived by Brihaspati, who was personating me.”

## \|\| 47.191-193 \|\|

*sampramūḍhās tataḥ sarve na prābudhyanta kiṃcana \|*  
*abravīt sampramūḍheṣu kāvyastānasurāṃstadā \|\| 191 \|\|*

*ācāryo vo hy ahaṃ kāvyo devācāryo 'yamaṅgirāḥ \|*  
*anugacchata māṃ daityās tyajatainaṃ bṛhaspatim \|\| 192 \|\|*

*ityuktā hy asurāstena tāv ubhau samavekṣya ca \|*  
*yadāsurā viśeṣaṃ tu na jānantyubhayostayoḥ \|\| 193 \|\|*

191-193. The Danavas were bewildered to hear those words of the sage, and began to look amazingly at both of them sitting there. At that time, the bewildered Danavas could not say anything, nor could they distinguish their preceptor, at which the sage Shukra said-: — Asuras! I am your preceptor Shukra: this is Brihaspati, the preceptor of the Devas. Leave him and follow me.”

## \|\| 47.194 \|\|

*bṛhaspatir uvācainān asambhrāntastapodhanaḥ \|*  
*kāvyo vo 'haṃ gururdaityā madrūpo 'yaṃ bṛhaspatiḥ \|\| 194 \|\|*

194\. Then the Asuras again looked at both of them, but did not perceive any difference between Shukra and Brihaspati

## \|\| 47.195-197 \|\|

*saṃmohayati rūpeṇa māmakenaiṣa vo 'surāḥ \|*  
*śrutvā tasya tataste vai sametya tu tato 'bruvan \|\| 195 \|\|*

*ayaṃ no daśa varṣāṇi satataṃ śāsti vai prabhuḥ \|*  
*eṣa vai gururasmākam antarepsurayaṃ dvijaḥ \|\| 196 \|\|*

*tataste dānavāḥ sarve praṇipatyābhinandya ca \|*  
*vacanaṃ jagṛhustasya cirābhyāse na mohitāḥ \|\| 197 \|\|*

195-197. At that time, the sage Brihaspati instantly addressed the ‘Asuras —

“Asuras! I am your preceptor, Shukra. This is Brihaspati, who has come here after assuming my form, Asuras! Brihaspati is trying to deceive you by assuming my form.” After that, all the Asuras held a council and discussed among themselves that, that preceptor (Brihaspati) had been giving them lessons since ten years who, according to their judgment, was their real preceptor

## \|\| 47.198 \|\|

*ūcus tamasurāḥ sarve krodhasaṃraktalocanāḥ \|*  
*ayaṃ gurur hito 'smākaṃ gaccha tvaṃ nāsi no guruḥ \|\| 198 \|\|*

198\. After that, all the Danavas paid obeisance to the sage Brihaspati, in the guise of Shukra, and accepted what he said to them; for they were deluded by him during his stay with them for ten years.

## \|\| 47.199-200 \|\|

*bhārgavo vāṅgirā vāpi bhagavāneṣa no guruḥ \|*  
*sthitā vayaṃ nideśe 'sya sādhu tvaṃ gaccha māciram \|\| 199 \|\|*

*evamuktvāsurāḥ sarve prāpadyanta bṛhaspatim \|*  
*yadā na pratyapadyanta kāvyenoktaṃ mahaddhitam \|\| 200 \|\|*

199-200. Then all the Asuras, with their eyes burning with rage, most angrily said to Shukra: — “He, Brihaspati, is our well-wisher and preceptor; depart thou (Shukra), for the thou art not our guru, He might be Shukra or Brihaspati, but he is our guru, We remain under his instruction.”

## \|\| 47.201-203 \|\|

*cukopa bhārgavasteṣām avalepena tena tu \|*  
*bodhitā hi mayā yasmān na māṃ bhajatha dānavāḥ \|\| 201 \|\|*

*tasmātpranaṣṭasaṃjñā vai parābhavamavāpsyatha \|*  
*iti vyāhṛtya tānkāvyo jagāmātha yathāgatam \|\| 202 \|\|*

*śaptāṃstānasurāñjñātvā kāvyena sa bṛhaspatiḥ \|*  
*kṛtārthaḥ sa tadā hṛṣṭaḥ svarūpaṃ pratyapadyata \|\| 203 \|\|*

201-203. Saying so, the Asuras acknowledged Brihaspati under the garb of Shukra, as their preceptor. At that, the sage Shukra, in a fit of anger, pronounced the following curse upon the Danavas: — “Danavas, in spite of my advice, you have refused to acknowledge me as your guru, in consequence of which you will lose your intellect and will be routed by the Devas.” Afterwards, he departed from there.

## \|\| 47.205 \|\|

*aho vivañcitāḥ smeti parasparamathābruvan \|*  
*pṛṣṭhato 'bhimukhāścaiva tāḍitāṅgirasena tu \|\| 205 \|\|*

205\. Brihaspati became immensely pleased to find his object gained when the Daityas were cursed by Shukra, Then he assumed his own form, end instantly disappeared, after which the Danavas were confused when they saw him thus vanishing.

## \|\| 47.206 \|\|

*vañcitāḥ sopadhānena sve sve vastuni māyayā \|*  
*tatastvaparituṣṭāste tameva tvaritā yayuḥ \|*  
*prahlādamagrataḥ kṛtvā kāvyasyānupadaṃ punaḥ \|\| 206 \|\|*

206 They then said among themselves: “Oh, we have been: grossly; deluded on all sides by Brihaspati and got cursed by the sage Shukra.”

## \|\| 47.207-209 \|\|

*tataḥ kāvyaṃ samāsādya upatasthuravāṅmukhāḥ \|*  
*samāgatānpunardṛṣṭvā kāvyo yājyānuvāca ha \|\| 207 \|\|*

*mayā saṃbodhitāḥ sarve yasmānmā nābhinandatha \|*  
*tatastenāvamānena gatā yūyaṃ parābhavam \|\| 208 \|\|*

*evaṃ bruvāṇaṃ śukraṃ tu bāṣpasaṃdigdhayā girā \|*  
*prahlādastaṃ tadovāca mā nastvaṃ tyaja bhārgava \|\| 209 \|\|*

207-209. They got very vexed; and all the Asuras, under the leadership of Prahlada, immediately went to their preceptor; and with their heads cast down in shame, they stood before him in repentance. The sage, finding his disciples come back, addressed them thus: — “Though I tried my best to enlighten you all as to the true state of affairs, you did not. pay heed to my warning. On account of this disregard of my advice, you will surely be defeated in future”.

## \|\| 47.210-212 \|\|

*svāśrayān bhajamānāṃśca bhaktāṃstvaṃ bhaja bhārgava \|*  
*tvayyadṛṣṭe vayaṃ tena devācāryeṇa mohitāḥ \|*  
*bhaktānarhasi vai jñātuṃ tapodīrgheṇa cakṣuṣā \|\| 210 \|\|*

*yadi nastvaṃ na kuruṣe prasādaṃ bhṛgunandana \|*  
*apadhyātās tvayā hy adya praviśāmo rasātalam \|\| 211 \|\|*

*jñātvā kāvyo yathātattvaṃ kāruṇyādanukampayā \|*  
*evaṃ pratyanunīto vai tataḥ kopaṃ niyamya saḥ \|*  
*uvācaitānna bhetavyaṃ na gantavyaṃ rasātalam \|\| 212 \|\|*

210-212. Hearing those words of Shukra, Prahlada, with his eyes full of tears, falteringly said to the preceptor: — “O Bhargava, do not abandon us, we all are your devotees and look to you for protection; shield us.

O preceptor of the Divine Vision! You are capable of knowing, that not having the good luck of seeing you, we were deluded by Brihaspati, the preceptor of the Devas. And, O Bhrigunandana! if you will not show Kindness to us, then all of us, discarded by you, shall go to Rasatala.”

## \|\| 47.213-224 \|\|

*avaṣyaṃ bhāvino hy arthāḥ prāptavyā mayi jāgrati \|*  
*na śakyamanyathā kartuṃ diṣṭaṃ hi balavattaram \|\| 213 \|\|*

*saṃjñā pranaṣṭā yā vo 'dya tāmetāṃ pratipatsyatha \|*  
*devāñjitvā sakṛccāpi pātālaṃ pratipatsyatha \|\| 214 \|\|*

*prāpte paryāyakāle ca hīti brahmābhyabhāṣata \|*  
*matprasādācca trailokyaṃ bhuktaṃ uṣmābhirūrjitam \|\| 215 \|\|*

*yugākhyā daśa sampūrṇā devānākramya mūrdhani \|*  
*etāvantaṃ ca kālaṃ vai brahmā rājyamabhāṣata \|\| 216 \|\|*

*rājyaṃ sāvarṇike tubhyaṃ punaḥ kila bhaviṣyati \|*  
*lokānāmīśvaro bhāvyas tava pautraḥ punarbaliḥ \|\| 217 \|\|*

*evaṃ kila mithaḥ proktaḥ pautraste viṣṇunā svayam \|*  
*vācā hṛteṣu lokeṣu tāstāstasyābhavankila \|\| 218 \|\|*

*yasmātpravṛttayaścāsya saṃkāśād abhisaṃdhitāḥ \|*  
*tasmādvṛttena prītena tubhyaṃ dattaṃ svayambhuvā \|\| 219 \|\|*

*devarājye balirbhāvya iti māmīśvaro 'bravīt \|*  
*tasmādadṛśyo bhūtānāṃ kālāpekṣaḥ sa tiṣṭhati \|\| 220 \|\|*

*prītena cāparo datto varastubhyaṃ svayambhuvā \|*  
*tasmānnirutsukastvaṃ vai paryāyaṃ sahito 'suraiḥ \|\| 221 \|\|*

*na hi śakyaṃ mayā tubhyaṃ purastād viprabhāṣitum \|*  
*brahmaṇā pratiṣiddho 'haṃ bhaviṣyaṃ jānatā vibho \|\| 222 \|\|*

*imau ca śiṣyau dvau mahyaṃ samāv etau bṛhaspateḥ \|*  
*daivataiḥ saha saṃsṛṣṭān sarvānvo dhārayiṣyataḥ \|\| 223 \|\|*

*ityuktā hy asurāḥ sarve kāvyenākliṣṭakarmaṇā \|*  
*hṛṣṭāstena yayuḥ sārdhaṃ prahlādena mahātmanā \|\| 224 \|\|*

213-224. The sage Shukra, on hearing these words, curbed his anger and, moved by pity and compassion, said: “You need not entertain any fear, ho need you go to the Rasatala. Certainly, you will obtain prosperity in future, so long as I am away, but your destiny must be fulfilled. I cannot make it otherwise, for fate is stronger. You must lose your intelligence from to-day, though you will regain it hereafter. Yow will conquer the Devas only once, and after that you had better go to Patala. Now the ten ages of your prosperity have come to an end; for that was the period predicted by Brahma in which you had world-dominion. You will again regain your kingdom in the Savarnika Manvantara, after which, O Prahlada, your grandson, King Bali, will reign with all glory, in different realms; for, even, Lord Vishnu will promise this secretly to your grandson, when He will deprive him of his kingdom in His Dwarf incarnation. Because you were devoted to Vishnu and your mind was regulated according to His will; therefore Brahma being pleased with you, gave you this world-sovereignty. Shiva, the most supreme Lord of the entire universe, has spoken to me, as a secret, that Bali will be the future king of the Devas; and therefore He, invisible to all, is awaiting that time.

O Prahlada! Brahma, on being pleased with you, has granted another boon to you which I am not in a position to reveal to you, because Brahma, the knower of the future, has not authorized me to do so. He has also said that both these my disciples (Shanda and Marka) are equal in wisdom to Brihaspati. These two will protect you against all the machinations of the Devas in my absence”.

## \|\| 47.225-227 \|\|

*avaṣyaṃ bhāvyamarthaṃ tu śrutvā śukreṇa bhāṣitam \|*  
*sakṛdāśaṃsamānāstu jayaṃ śukreṇa bhāṣitam \|*  
*daṃśitāḥ sāudhāḥ sarve tato devānsamāhvayan \|\| 225 \|\|*

*devāstadāsurāndṛṣṭvā saṃgrāme samupasthitān \|*  
*sarve saṃbhṛtasambhārā devāstān samayodhayan \|\| 226 \|\|*

*devāsure tadā tasmin vartamāne śataṃ samāḥ \|*  
*ajayannasurā devāṃs tato devā hy amantrayan \|\| 227 \|\|*

225-227. On hearing these words of Shukra, the rigid follower of ritualistic rites, all the Asuras retired pleased, along with the high-souled Prahlada, and being assured by their preceptor, Shukra, that they would gain at least one victory over the Devas, the Asuras, acting on these words, put on their armours and challenged the Devas to fight them. The Devas, seeing the Asuras standing in the battle-field well-equipped to fight, came out to give battle.

## \|\| 47.228-230 \|\|

*yajñenopāhvayāmas tau tato jeṣyāmahe 'surān \|*  
*tadopāmantrayandevāḥ śaṇḍāmarkau tu tāv ubhau \|\| 228 \|\|*

*yajñe cāhūya tau proktau tyajetāmasurān dvijau \|*  
*vayaṃ uvāṃ bhajiṣyāmaḥ saha jitvā tu dānavān \|\| 229 \|\|*

*evaṃ kṛtābhisaṃdhī tau śaṇḍāmarkau surāstathā \|*  
*tato devā jayaṃ prāpur dānavāśca parājitāḥ \|\| 230 \|\|*
