228-230. The great war between the Asuras and the Devas lasted for a century in which the Devas were repulsed and the Asuras were victorious. The Devas held a conference and decided to invite Shanda and Marka (as guests of the Devas), on the occasion of their sacrifice, after which they would get victory in the next war. After coming to that conclusion, the Devas invited both of them to their sacrifice, and said: — “O, twice-born ones! You forsake these Asuras, we will be yours always, after conquering them through your support.”

## \|\| 47.231-232 \|\|

*śaṇḍāmarkaparityaktā dānavā hy abalāstathā \|*  
*evaṃ daityāḥ purā kāvya-śāpenābhihatāstadā \|\| 231 \|\|*

*kāvyaśāpābhibhūtāste nirādhārāśca sarvaśaḥ \|*  
*nirasyamānā devaiśca viviśuste rasātalam \|\| 232 \|\|*

231-232. The Devas, thus made friends with Shanda and Marka, and then fought with the Danavas, when they were victorious. As the Danavas became powerless by being deserted by Shanda and Marka, so they were defeated easily, and thus the curse of Shukra took effect.

## \|\| 47.233-234 \|\|

*evaṃ nirudyamā devaiḥ kṛtāḥ kṛcchreṇa dānavāḥ \|*  
*tataḥ prabhṛti śāpena bhṛgornaimittikena tu \|\| 233 \|\|*

*jajñe punaḥ punarviṣṇur dharme praśithile prabhuḥ \|*  
*kurvandharmavyavasthānam asurāṇāṃ praṇāśanam \|\| 234 \|\|*

233-234. The Asuras, thus cursed by their preceptor, and Without any spiritual support from any side, and repulsed by the Devas, found themselves in a most helpless condition and eventually entered Rasatala (infernal regions).

The Danavas, being thus dispirited by the victory of the Devas and through the instrumentality of Bhrigu, went to Patala.

## \|\| 47.235 \|\|

*prahlādasya nideśe tu na sthāsyantyasurāśca ye \|*  
*manuṣyavadhyāste sarve brahmeti vyāharatprabhuḥ \|\| 235 \|\|*

235\. Again, whenever there is decay in righteousness, Vishnu takes birth, in order to establish righteousness by destroying the Asuras.

## \|\| 47.236 \|\|

*dharmānnārāyaṇasyāṃśaḥ sambhūtaś cākṣuṣe 'ntare \|*  
*yajñaṃ vai vartayāmāsur devā vaivasvate 'ntare \|\| 236 \|\|*

236\. Brahma had also ordained this, that those Asuras who go against the righteous injunctions of Prahlada would also be killed by men.

## \|\| 47.237-238 \|\|

*prādurbhāve tatastasya brahmā hy āsītpurohitaḥ \|*  
*yugākhyāyāṃ caturthyāṃ tu āpanneṣu sureṣu vai \|\| 237 \|\|*

*sambhūtastu samudrānte hiraṇyakaśiporvadhe \|*  
*dvitīye narasiṃhākhye rudro hy āsītpurohitaḥ \|\| 238 \|\|*

237-238. In accordance with that ordinance of Brahma, there was a partial incarnation of Narayana as Dharma, at the end of the Chakshusha Manvantara, when the Devas performed a sacrifice at the beginning of the Vaivasvata Manvantara. At this incarnation, Brahma was the officiating priest. This was the first incarnation. There was another incarnation of the Supreme Soul. When the Devas were in distress, then, on the fourth day of the Moon, which was the anniversary of the beginning of a Yuga, Lord Vishnu manifested Himself on the sea-coast. He incarnated Himself as Nrisimha for the destruction of Hiranyakashipu. Rudra officiated as the sacrificial priest. This was His second incarnation.

## \|\| 47.239-240 \|\|

*balisaṃstheṣu lokeṣu tretāyāṃ saptamaṃ prati \|*  
*tṛtīye vāmanasyārthe dharmeṇa tu purodhasā \|\| 239 \|\|*

*etās tisraḥ smṛtāstasya divyāḥ sambhūtayo dvijāḥ \|*  
*mānuṣāḥ sapta yānyāstu śāpajāstā nibodhata \|\| 240 \|\|*

239-240. In the seventh Treta Yuga, when King Bali was in power, Dharma was the sacrificial priest at the time of the Lord manifesting Himself as O Sages! these three are the celestial incarnations of Vishnu; and there are seven more human incarnations which the Lord underwent owing to the curse of Bhrigu.

## \|\| 47.241 \|\|

*tretāuge tu prathame dattātreyo babhūva ha \|*  
*naṣṭe dharme caturthāṃśe mārkaṇḍeyapuraḥsaraḥ \|\| 241 \|\|*

241\. In the first ‘Treta Yuga, when the fourth part of righteousness was lost, the Lord incarnated as Dattatreya, and the sage Markandeya was the officiating priest. This was His fourth incarnation

## \|\| 47.242 \|\|

*pañcamaḥ pañcadaśyāṃ ca tretāyāṃ saṃbabhūva ha \|*  
*māndhātā cakravartī tu tadottaṅkapuraḥsare \|\| 242 \|\|*

242\. The fifth incarnation was that of the world-Emperor, Mandhatri, which took place in the fifteenth Treta, when Uttanga was the officiating priest.

## \|\| 47.243 \|\|

*ekonaviṃśyāṃ tretāyāṃ sarvakṣatrāntakṛdvibhuḥ \|*  
*jāmadagnyastathā ṣaṣṭho viśvāmitrapuraḥsaraḥ \|\| 243 \|\|*

243\. In the 19th Treta, there was the sixth incarnation, as Parashurama, to root out the Kshatriyas, when Vishvamitra officiated as the sacrificial.

## \|\| 47.244-245 \|\|

*caturviṃśe uge rāmo vasiṣṭhena purodhasā \|*  
*saptamo rāvaṇasyārthe jajñe daśarathātmajaḥ \|\| 244 \|\|*

*aṣṭame dvāpare viṣṇur aṣṭāviṃśe parāśarāt \|*  
*vedavyāsastathā jajñe jātūkarṇyapuraḥsaraḥ \|\| 245 \|\|*

244-245. In the 24th Treta. Yuga, the seventh manifestation was. that of Shri Ramachandra, as the son of Dasharatha, and with Vasistha as the priest, to In the 28th Dvapara, Vishnu incarnated Himself as Vedavyasa, the son of Parashara, when Jatukarnya sage was the officiating priest. This was the eighth incarnation of Vishnu.

## \|\| 47.246 \|\|

*kartuṃ dharmavyavasthānam asurāṇāṃ praṇāśanam \|*  
*buddho navamako jajñe tapasā puṣkarekṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*devasundararūpeṇa dvaipāyanapuraḥsaraḥ \|\| 246 \|\|*

246\. For the establishment of righteousness and the destruction of Asuras, through asceticism, there was the 9th incarnation, in the form of Buddha of Divine splendour, with His Eyes as beautiful as lotus, and with the sage Dvaipayana. Vyasa as the officiating priest.

## \|\| 47.247-248 \|\|

*tasminneva uge kṣīṇe saṃdhyāśiṣṭe bhaviṣyati \|*  
*kalkī tu viṣṇuyaśasaḥ pārāśaryapuraḥsaraḥ \|\| 247 \|\|*

*daśamo bhāvyasambhūto yājñavalkyapuraḥsaraḥ \|*  
*sarvāṃśca bhūtāṃs timitān pāṣaṇḍāṃścaiva sarvaśaḥ \|\| 248 \|\|*

247-248. At the close of Kaliyuga (the present iron age), there will be the Kalki manifestation, in the house of Vishnuyasha, and the sage, Parasharya Vyasa will -be the officiating priest. This will be the tenth. incarnation, and Yajanavalkya will make his appearance before this coming manifestation.

## \|\| 47.249-253 \|\|

*pragṛhītāudhair viprair vṛtaḥ śatasahasraśaḥ \|\| 249 \|\|*

*niḥśeṣāñchūdrarājñastu tadā sa tu kariṣyati \|*  
*brahmadviṣaḥ sapatnāṃstu saṃhṛtyaiva ca tadvapuḥ \|\| 250 \|\|*

*pañcaviṃśe sthitaḥ kalkiś caritārthaḥ sasainikaḥ \|*  
*śūdrān saṃśodhayitvā tu samudrāntaṃ ca vai svayam \|\| 251 \|\|*

*pravṛttacakro balavān saṃhāraṃ tu kariṣyati \|*  
*utsādayitvā vṛṣalān prāyaśastānadhārmikān \|\| 252 \|\|*

*tatastadā sa vai kalkiś caritārthaḥ sasainikaḥ \|*  
*prajāstaṃ sādhayitvā tu samṛddhāstena vai svayam \|\| 253 \|\|*

249-253. This incarnation will destroy all the wicked ones and the hypocrites; and, with a large army of the Brahmanas, He will kill Shudra Kings and drive away all hypocrisy. After killing the enemies of Brahmanas and other enemies, He will march on with His army in the 28th of the Kaliyuga, and then, after purifying the Shudras, will cross the ocean, where He will destroy the sinful mixed castes and, thus fulfilling His mission, He will educate his peoples.

## \|\| 47.254 \|\|

*akasmātkopitānyonyaṃ bhaviṣyantīha mohitāḥ \|*  
*kṣapayitvā tu te 'nyonyaṃ bhāvinārthena coditāḥ \|\| 254 \|\|*

254\. Afterwards, the people, by becoming enraged and deluded with each other, will kill each other to fulfil the future destiny.

## \|\| 47.255 \|\|

*tataḥ kāle vyatīte tu sa devo 'ntaradhīyata \|*  
*nṛpeṣvatha pranaṣṭeṣu prajānāṃ saṃgrahāttadā \|\| 255 \|\|*

255\. When, in process of time, the incarnation of Kalki will vanish, then the future kings will be destroyed, through the rebellion of their subjects.

## \|\| 47.256 \|\|

*rakṣaṇe vinivṛtte tu hatvā cānyonyamāhave \|*  
*parasparaṃ ca hatvā tu nirākrandāḥ suduḥkhitāḥ \|\| 256 \|\|*

256\. The people, not finding any one as their protector, will fight amongst themselves, and will then land themselves in great troubles after killing one another.

## \|\| 47.257 \|\|

*purāṇi hitvā grāmāṃśca tulyatve niṣparigrahāḥ \|*  
*pranaṣṭāśramadharmāśca naṣṭavarṇāśramāstathā \|\| 257 \|\|*

257\. All cities and villages will be devastated, and the duties of castes and the stages of life will disappear.

## \|\| 47.258 \|\|

*aṭṭaśūlā nānapadāḥ śivaśūlāścatuṣpathāḥ \|*  
*pramadāḥ keśaśūlāśca bhaviṣyanti ugakṣaye \|\| 258 \|\|*

258\. At that juncture — the end of the Iron Ago — men will open markets to sell boiled rice, the Brahmanas will sell the Vedas and the women will earn their living by selling their hair.

## \|\| 47.259 \|\|

*hrasvadehāuṣaścaiva bhaviṣyanti vanaukasaḥ \|*  
*saritparvatavāsinyo mūlapattraphalāśanāḥ \|\| 259 \|\|*

259\. People will be very short of stature, and they will be short-lived. They will make forest, as their place of dwelling, or they will reside by rivers and hills, subsisting on roots, fruits and leaves.

## \|\| 47.260 \|\|

*cīracarmājinadharāḥ saṃkaraṃ ghoramāśritāḥ \|*  
*utpātaduḥkhāḥ svalpārthā bahubādhāśca tāḥ prajāḥ \|\| 260 \|\|*

260\. They will clothe themselves with tattered clothes, the deer-skin, &c. All the castes will mingle into one mass, and the people will be reduced to penury and will find themselves in great distress and subjected to many troubles.

## \|\| 47.261 \|\|

*evaṃ kaṣṭamanuprāptāḥ kāle saṃdhyaṃśake tadā \|*  
*tataḥ kṣayaṃ gamiṣyanti sārdhaṃ kaliugena tu \|\| 261 \|\|*

261\. Being thus tormented with myriads of troubles and difficulties, all the population will become annihilated along with the end of the Kaliyuga.

## \|\| 47.262-263 \|\|

*kṣīṇe kaliuge tasmiṃs tataḥ kṛtamavartata \|*  
*ityetatkīrtitaṃ samyag devāsuraviceṣṭitam \|\| 262 \|\|*

*yaduvaṃśaprasaṅgena samāsādvaiṣṇavaṃ yaśaḥ \|*  
*turvasostu pravakṣyāmi pūror druhyostathā hy anoḥ \|\| 263 \|\|*

262-263. Satyayuga (the Age of Truth) will follow on the heels of the disappearing Kaliyuga. ‘This is the narration of the doing of the Devas and the Asuras that I have related at some length to you, O sages; now hear an account of Yaduvamsha, Turvasu, Puru, Druhya, Anu, along with the glory of Vishnu.”

## Chapter 48

## \|\| 48.1-2 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*turvasostu suto garbho gobhānustasya cātmajaḥ \|*  
*gobhānostu suto vīras trisāriraparājitaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*karaṃdhamastu traisārir bharatastasya cātmajaḥ \|*  
*duṣyantaḥ pauravasyāpi tasya putro hy akalmaṣaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

1-2. Suta said: — Turvasu was the father of Garbha,-who begot Gobhanu, the father of the heroic Trisari. Trisari was the father of Karandhama, and Bharata was his son. This Bharata should not be confounded with Bharata, the son of Dushyanta. Dushyanta the father of Bharata, who was sinless belonged to the family of Puru.

## \|\| 48.3 \|\|

*evaṃ yayātiśāpena jarāsaṃkramaṇe purā \|*  
*turvasoḥ pauravaṃ vaṃśaṃ praviveśa purā kila \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Because Turvasu did not exchange his youth with the infirmity of Yayati, through the curse of the latter, therefore, the family of Turvasu did not become prominent, but it lapsed into the house of Puru.

## \|\| 48.4-5 \|\|

*duṣyantasya tu dāyādo varūtho nāma pārthivaḥ \|*  
*varūthāttu tathāṇḍīraḥ saṃdhānastasya cātmajaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*pāṇḍyaśca keralaścaiva colaḥ karṇastathaiva ca \|*  
*teṣāṃ janapadāḥ sphītāḥ pāṇḍyāścolāḥ sakeralāḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. Dushyanta was the father of Varutha, who begot Andhra, who was the father of Sandhana. He also begot Pandya, Kerala, Chola, Karna, and their respective countries were named after them.

## \|\| 48.6-7 \|\|

*druhyostu tanayau śūrau setuḥ ketustathaiva ca \|*  
*setuputraḥ śaradvāṃstu gandhārastasya cātmajaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*khyāyate yasya nāmnāsau gandhāraviṣayo mahān \|*  
*āraṭṭadeśajāstasya turagā vājināṃ varāḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

6-7. Druhya was the father of two heroic sons, named Setu and Ketu. Setu begot Saradvana, the father of Gandhara, after whose name the vast Gandhara country is known. He had choice horses of the Aratta country.

## \|\| 48.8-9 \|\|

*gandhāraputro dharmastu ghṛtastasyātmajo 'bhavat \|*  
*ghṛtācca viduṣo jajñe pracetāstasya cātmajaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*pracetasaḥ putraśataṃ rājānaḥ sarva eva te \|*  
*mleccharāṣṭrādhipāḥ sarve udīcīṃ diśam āśritāḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

8-9. Gandhara was the father of Dharma, who begot Dhrita, the father of Vidusha; whose son was Pracheta. Pracheta was the father of a hundred sons, all of whom ruled as sovereigns in the Mlechha country lying in the north.

## \|\| 48.10 \|\|

*anoścaiva sutā vīrās trayaḥ paramadhārmikāḥ \|*  
*sabhānaraścākṣuṣaśca parameṣus tathaiva ca \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Ana was the father of the following three pious sons, viz., Sabhanara, Chakshusha, Parameshu.

## \|\| 48.11 \|\|

*sabhānarasya putrastu vidvānkolāhalo nṛpaḥ \|*  
*kolāhalasya dharmātmā saṃjayo nāma viśrutaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Sabhanara was the father of the learned Kolahala who became a king. Kolahala became the father of the holy Sanjaya, of worldwide reputation.

## \|\| 48.12-15 \|\|

*saṃjayasyābhavatputro vīro nāma puraṃjayaḥ \|*  
*janamejayo mahārāja puraṃjayasuto 'bhavat \|\| 12 \|\|*

*janamejayasya rājarṣer mahāśālo 'bhavatsutaḥ \|*  
*āsīd indrasamo rājā pratiṣṭhitayaśābhavat \|\| 13 \|\|*

*mahāmanāḥ sutastasya mahāśālasya dhārmikaḥ \|*  
*saptadvīpeśvaro jajñe cakravartī mahāmanāḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*mahāmanāstu dvau putrau janayāmāsa viśrutau \|*  
*uśīnaraṃ ca dharmajñaṃ titikṣuṃ caiva tāv ubhau \|\| 15 \|\|*

12-15. Sanjaya was the father of Puranjaya, who begot Janamejaya, the father of Mahashala. Mahashala was the father of the renowned and pious king Mahamana, who was the lord of seven continents and a universal monarch. He was the father of two famous sons, called Ushinara and Titikshu.

## \|\| 48.16 \|\|

*uśīnarasya patnyastu pañca rājarṣisambhavāḥ \|*  
*bhṛśā kṛśā navā darśā yā ca devī dṛṣadvatī \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Ushinara had Bhrisha, Krisha, Nava, Darsha and Drishadvati as his five queens, all daughters of a Rajarshi.

## \|\| 48.17-18 \|\|

*uśīnarasya putrāstu tāsu jātāḥ kulodvahāḥ \|*  
*tapasā te tu mahatā jātā vṛddhasya dhārmikāḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*bhṛśāyāstu nṛgaḥ putro navāyā nava eva ca \|*  
*kṛśāyāstu kṛśo jajñe darśāyāḥ suvrato 'bhavat \|*  
*dṛṣadvatyāḥ sutaścāpi śibir auśīnaro nṛpaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

17-18. The old king Ushinara, through his piety and righteousness, begot from his queens, the following pious and worthy sons, viz. Nrigu from Bhrisha, Nava from Nava, Krisha from Krisha, Suvrata from Darsha, Shibi Aushinara from Drishadvati.

## \|\| 48.19 \|\|

*śibestu śibayaḥ putrāś catvāro lokaviśrutāḥ \|*  
*pṛthudarbhaḥ suvīraśca kekayo bhadrakastathā \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. a Shibi begot four famous sons, viz., Prithudarbha, Sutisha, Kekaya, and Bhadraka; and their countries were named after them, viz., Kekaya, Bhadraka, Sanvira, and Paura, and the country of king Nrigu was also known as Kekaya.

## \|\| 48.20-21 \|\|

*teṣāṃ janapadāḥ sphītāḥ kekayā bhadrakāstathā \|*  
*sauvīrāścaiva paurāśca nṛgasya kekayāstathā \|\| 20 \|\|*

*suvratasya tathāmbaṣṭhā kṛśasya vṛṣalā purī \|*  
*navasya navarāṣṭraṃ tu titikṣostu prajāṃ śṛṇu \|\| 21 \|\|*

20-21. Ambashtha was the name of the capital town of Suvrata’s country, and Vrishala was the capital of Krisha, and Navarashtra was the capital of Nava. Now listen to the family of Titikshu

## \|\| 48.22 \|\|

*titikṣurabhavadrājā pūrvasyāṃ diśi viśrutaḥ \|*  
*bṛhadrathaḥ sutastasya tasya seno 'bhavatsutaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Titikshu became a renowned king and ruled in the East. He was the father of Vrishadratha, who begot Sena.

## \|\| 48.23-25 \|\|

*senasya sutapā jajñe sutapastanayo baliḥ \|*  
*jāto mānuṣayonyāṃ tu kṣīṇe vaṃśe prajecchayā \|\| 23 \|\|*

*mahāyogī tu sa balir baddho bandhairmahātmanā \|*  
*putrānutpādayāmāsa kṣetrajānpañca pārthivān \|\| 24 \|\|*

*aṅgaṃ sa janayāmāsa vaṅgaṃ suhmaṃ tathaiva ca \|*  
*puṇḍraṃ kaliṅgaṃ ca tathā bāleyaṃ kṣetramucyate \|*  
*bāleyā brāhmaṇāścaiva tasya vaṃśakarāḥ prabho \|\| 25 \|\|*

23-25. Sena begot Sutapa, whose son was Bali. Bali, the Daitya King, was without an issue; for he was bound by the Mahatma \[in bonds of captivity.\] But, as he was a great Yogi, he took birth in human body as Bali, the son of Sutapa, and procured five Kshetraja sons for himself. These were Anga, Vanga, Suhma, Pundra and Kalinga, and their country is called Baleya. The Baleyas and the Brahmanas\* were the sons of that lord Bali.”

**Комментарий:**

\*Brahmanas here does not refer evidently to the Brahmana, caste, but, those descendants of Bali from whom the modern Burma got its name.

## \|\| 48.26-28 \|\|

*baleśca brahmaṇā datto varaḥ prītena dhīmataḥ \|*  
*mahāyogitvamāuśca kalpasya parimāṇakam \|\| 26 \|\|*

*saṃgrāme cāpyajeyatvaṃ dharme caivottamā matiḥ \|*  
*traikālyadarśanaṃ caiva prādhānyaṃ prasave tathā \|\| 27 \|\|*

*jayaṃ cāpratimaṃ uddhe dharme tattvārthadarśanam \|*  
*caturo niyatānvarṇān sa vai sthāpayitā prabhuḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

26-28. Lord Brahma, satisfied with Bali, gave him a boon, namely, that Bali would be a great Yogi, would live for a Kalpa, would be invincible in war, superior in wisdom, and his mind would always be inclined towards religion. He would be endowed with knowledge of the past, present and future, the chief in his community, victorious in wars, a philosopher, and the establisher of the prescribed orders.

It was through the glory of Brahma that Bali was favoured with children (even though made a captive by Vishnu).

## \|\| 48.29 \|\|

*teṣāṃ ca pañca dāyādā vaṅgāṅgāḥ suhmakāstathā \|*  
*puṇḍrāḥ kaliṅgāśca tathā aṅgasya tu nibodhata \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. The family of Anga will now be described.

## \|\| 48.30-31 \|\|

*munaya ūcuḥ*  
*kathaṃ baleḥ sutā jātāḥ pañca tasya mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*kiṃnāmnī mahiṣī tasya janitā katama ṛṣiḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

*kathaṃ cotpāditāstena tannaḥ prabrūhi pṛcchatām \|*  
*māhātmyaṃ ca prabhāvaṃ ca nikhilena vadasva tat \|\| 31 \|\|*

30-31. The sages said: — “Suta! How was Bali blessed with five children? What was the name of the mother of those children? Which Rishi begot them? How did he do so? Be good enough to relate to us all this, and, also explain to us the glory of that sage (who begot those children for Bali).

## \|\| 48.32-36 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*athośija iti khyāta āsīdvidvānṛṣiḥ purā \|*  
*patnī vai mamatā nāma babhūvāsya mahātmanaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

*uśijasya yavīyānvai bhrātṛpatnīmakāmayat \|*  
*bṛhaspatirmahātejā mamatāmetya kāmataḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

*uvāca mamatā taṃ tu devaraṃ varavarṇinī \|*  
*antarvatnyasmi te bhrātur jyeṣṭhasya tu viramyatām \|\| 34 \|\|*

*ayaṃ tu me mahābhāga garbhaḥ kupyedbṛhaspate \|*  
*auśijo bhrātṛjanyaste sopāṅgaṃ vedamudgiran \|\| 35 \|\|*

*amogharetāstvaṃ cāpi na māṃ bhajitumarhasi \|*  
*asminn evaṃ gate kāle yathā vā manyase prabho \|\| 36 \|\|*

32-36 Suta said: — In the days gone by, there was a great sage, named Ushija, and Mamata was his wife. Brihaspati, the younger brother of Ushija, entertained a desire to enjoy in the company of the latter’s wife. Mamata, understanding the intentions of Brihaspati, told him not to think of anything of the kind, as she was bearing a child to his brother; and added: “O! Brihaspati, the child in my womb will get angry, for being of the seed of Ushija, thy brother, he knows all the Vedas \[and will not allow thy seed to fecundate in my womb\]. Thou, O Brihaspati, art also one, whose seed lever goes in vain. So do not approach me now. After I am delivered of this seed of Ushija, do as thou thinkest proper, O Lord”.

## \|\| 48.37-38 \|\|

*evamuktastathā samyag bṛhattejā bṛhaspatiḥ \|*  
*kāmātmā sa mahātmāpi na manaḥ so 'bhyavārayat \|\| 37 \|\|*

*saṃbabhūvaiva dharmātmā tayā sārdhamakāmayā \|*  
*utsṛjantaṃ tu tadreto-vācaṃ garbho 'bhyabhāṣata \|\| 38 \|\|*

37-38. In spite of her remonstrance, Brihaspati, even though he was such a mighty sage, could not check his passion, and forcibly carried out his intention. When he was about to emit his seed, the child in the womb cried out:

## \|\| 48.39 \|\|

*bho tāta vācāmadhipa dvayornāstīha saṃsthitiḥ \|*  
*amogharetāstvaṃ cāpi pūrvaṃ cāhamihāgataḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. “Sire! There is no room for two souls in the embryo; and I have come here before:

## \|\| 48.40-41 \|\|

*so 'śapattaṃ tataḥ kruddha evamukto bṛhaspatiḥ \|*  
*putraṃ jyeṣṭhasya vai bhrātur garbhasthaṃ bhagavānṛṣiḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

*yasmāttvamīdṛśe kāle garbhastho 'pi niṣedhasi \|*  
*māmevamuktavāṃstasmāt tamo dīrghaṃ pravekṣyasi \|\| 41 \|\|*

40-41. Hearing those words, Brihaspati became enraged, and thus cursed his brother's son in the womb: — “You, who are present in the embryo and are putting an obstruction in. my way of enjoyment, will suffer from blindness”.

## \|\| 48.42 \|\|

*tato dīrghatamā nāma śāpādṛṣirajāyata \|*  
*ato 'ṃśajo bṛhatkīrtir bṛhaspatirivaujasā \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Afterwards on account of the curse of Brihaspati, the child was born blind and named Dirghatama. \[Deep darkness\]. He was illustrious and percevering like Brihaspati.

## \|\| 48.43-45 \|\|

*ūrdhvaretāstato 'sau vai vasate bhrāturāśrame \|*  
*sa dharmānsaurabheyāṃstu vṛṣabhācchrutavāṃstataḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

*tasya bhrātā pitṛvyo yaś cakāra bharaṇaṃ tadā \|*  
*tasminnivasatastasya yadṛcchātastu vai vṛṣaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

*yajñārthamāhṛtāndarbhāṃś cacāra surabhīsutaḥ \|*  
*jagrāha taṃ dīrghatamāḥ śṛṅgayostu catuṣpadam \|\| 45 \|\|*

43-45. Dirghatama settled himself in the house of his brother, leading a life of total celibacy. Whilst so dwelling, he learnt from a bull, the dharma of the cattle, that of promiscuous intercourse without regard to relationship. He was supported by his brother and uncle Sometime after, an ox happened to go there of his own accord, and began to feast himself on the Kusha grass, planted there for sacrificial purposes, when Dirghatama caught him by the horns.

## \|\| 48.46-47 \|\|

*tenāsau nigṛhītaśca na cacāla padātpadam \|*  
*tato 'bravīdvṛṣastaṃ vai muñca māṃ balināṃ vara \|\| 46 \|\|*

*na mayāsāditastāta balavāṃstvatsamaḥ kvacit \|*  
*mama cānyaḥ samo vāpi na hi me balasaṃkhyayā \|*  
*muñca tāteti ca punaḥ prītaste 'haṃ varaṃ vṛṇu \|\| 47 \|\|*

46-47. The ox, thus taken hold of by him, could not extricate himself from his grip, and, finding himself in a helpless condition said:- — “O, bravest of the brave! Let me go. I have never come across a valiant man like you, nor was there any one as powerful as myself. Now leave me. I am pleased with you, and you can ask for any boon from me.

## \|\| 48.48 \|\|

*evamukto 'bravīdenaṃ jīvanme tvaṃ kva yāsyasi \|*  
*eṣa tvāṃ na vimokṣyāmi parasvādaṃ catuṣpadam \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Dirghatama replied: — “Where will you go, so long as I am alive? I shall not let you — the encroacher on other’s rights - go”.

## \|\| 48.49-50 \|\|

*vṛṣabha uvāca*  
*nāsmākaṃ vidyate tāta pātakaṃ steyameva ca \|*  
*bhakṣyābhakṣyaṃ tathā caiva peyāpeyaṃ tathaiva ca \|\| 49 \|\|*

*dvipadāṃ bahavo hy ete dharma eṣa gavāṃ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*kāryākārye na vāgamyā-gamanaṃ ca tathaiva ca \|\| 50 \|\|*

49-50. The ox said: — ‘Sire! I have com mitted neither any sin nor I heft. There is no hard and fast rule laid down to dictate to us, animals, what to eat and what not to eat, what to drink and what not to drink. Many of these duties are imposed on bipeds, and not on us, the quadrupeds.

We are not guided by any such restrictions as to what should be done and what should not be done; and whom we should approach for sexual intercourse and whom not."

## \|\| 48.51 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*gavāṃ dharmaṃ tu vai śrutvā saṃbhrāntastu visṛjya tam \|*  
*śaktyānnapānadānāttu gopatiṃ saṃprasādayat \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Suta said: — Hearing from the ox the natural Jaws of cattle, he released him from his grasp. Afterwards, he fed him with corn, etc.

## \|\| 48.52 \|\|

*prasādite gate tasmin godharmaṃ bhaktitastu saḥ \|*  
*manasaiva samādadhyau tanniṣṭhastatparo hi saḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. On the ox going away satisfied with the repast, Dirghatama began to meditate on the natural laws of cattle, and being convinced of its being the true law, he became a devoted follower of it.

## \|\| 48.53-56 \|\|

*tato yavīyasaḥ patnīṃ gautamasyābhyapadyata \|*  
*kṛtāvalepāṃ tāṃ matvā so 'naḍvāniva na kṣamaḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

*godharmaṃ tu paraṃ matvā snuṣāṃ tāmabhyapadyata \|*  
*nirbhartsya cainaṃ ruddhvā ca bāhubhyāṃ sampragṛhya ca \|\| 54 \|\|*

*bhāvyamarthaṃ tu taṃ jñātvā māhātmyāttamuvāca sā \|*  
*viparyayaṃ tu tvaṃ labdhvā anaḍvāniva vartase \|\| 55 \|\|*

*gamyāgamyaṃ na jānīṣe godharmātprārthayansutām \|*  
*durvṛttaṃ tvāṃ tyajāmyadya gaccha tvaṃ svena karmaṇā \|\| 56 \|\|*

53-56. On one occasion he met. the wife of his younger brother’s son, Gautama, and, in spite of her being with child, he taking the laws relating to cattle to be of superior importance, did not desist from her, and caught hold of her with a violent jerk and enjoyed himself in her company, though she was like his daughter-in-law in relation. Knowing about futurity, he began to dilate upon the cattle law, when that lady said: — “You going against nature are behaving like an ox, and without having regard for the rules of prohibited relationships in sexual intercourse; but following the natural law of the beast, you have committed an incest on your daughter. Consequently, I forsake you base and mean, and now go away on account of your doings”.

## \|\| 48.57 \|\|

*kāṣṭhe samudge prakṣipya gaṅgāmbhasi samutsṛjat \|*  
*yasmāttvamandho vṛddhaśca bhartavyo duradhiṣṭhitaḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. With those words, she packed him in a wooden case and threw him into the Ganges, saying, “I abandon you (and do not kill you, pitying) your blindness and old age.”

## \|\| 48.58-59 \|\|

*tamuhyamānaṃ vegena srotaso 'bhyāśamāgataḥ \|*  
*jagrāha taṃ sa dharmātmā balir vairocanistadā \|\| 58 \|\|*

*antaḥpure jugopainaṃ bhakṣyabhojyaiśca tarpayan \|*  
*prītaścaiva vareṇaiva cchandayāmāsa vai balim \|\| 59 \|\|*

58-59. That case, after a long run, was drifted ashore and was taken possession of by Bali, the son of Virochana. Bali made over the contents of the case to his queen, where he was taken out of the case and nourished with various kinds of dainties. After that, he told Bali that he would grant him any boon he would ask for.

## \|\| 48.60 \|\|

*tasmācca sa varaṃ vavre putrārthe dānavarṣabhaḥ \|*  
*saṃtānārthaṃ mahābhāga-bhāryāyāṃ mama mānada \|*  
*putrāndharmārthatattvajñān utpādayitumarhasi \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Bali, the king of the Danavas, besought him to beget progeny from his wife.

## \|\| 48.61-62 \|\|

*evamukto 'tha devarṣis tathāstvityuktavān prabhuḥ \|*  
*sa tasya rājā svāṃ bhāryāṃ sudeṣṇāṃ nāma prāhiṇot \|*  
*andhaṃ vṛddhaṃ ca taṃ jñātvā na sā devī jagāma ha \|\| 61 \|\|*

*śūdrāṃ dhātreyikāṃ tasmāv andhāya prāhiṇottadā \|*  
*tasyāṃ kakṣīvadādīṃśca śūdrayonāv ṛṣir vaśī \|\| 62 \|\|*

61-62. In reply to the request of the king, that sage said, “This will be so;” hearing which, Bali sent his queen, Sudeshna, to him; but she, thinking him to be old and blind, did not approach him. She, however, sent the daughter of her nurse who, through her contact with that sage, gave birth to Kakshivana and others

## \|\| 48.63-66 \|\|

*janayāmāsa dharmātmā śūdrān ityevamādikam \|*  
*uvāca taṃ balī rājā dṛṣṭvā kakṣīvadādikān \|\| 63 \|\|*

*rājovāca*  
*pravīṇān ṛṣidharmasya ceśvarān brahmavādinaḥ \|*  
*vidvān pratyakṣadharmāṇāṃ buddhimān vṛttimāñchucīn \|\| 64 \|\|*

*mamaiva ceti hovāca taṃ dīrghatamasaṃ baliḥ \|*  
*natyuvāca munistaṃ vai mamaivamiti cābravīt \|\| 65 \|\|*

*utpannāḥ śūdrayonā tu bhavacchande surottama \|*  
*andhaṃ vṛddhaṃ ca māṃ jñātvā sudeṣṇā mahiṣī tava \|*  
*prāhiṇod avamānānme śūdrāṃ dhātreyikāṃ nṛpa \|\| 66 \|\|*

63-66. King Bali, seeing the Shudra sons, Kakshivana, etc., so well up in saintly precepts, so illustrious, so sacred and so versed in saintly lore, said to Dirghatama that they were his sons. The sage said they were not the sons of Bali and claimed them to be his own, on account of their having been born of the Shudra nurse sent by the queen, who herself had discarded him on account of his age and blindness.

## \|\| 48.67-68 \|\|

*tataḥ prasādayāmāsa balis tamṛṣisattamam \|*  
*baliḥ sudeṣṇāṃ tāṃ bhāryāṃ bhartsayāmāsa dānavaḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

*punaścainām alaṃkṛtya ṛṣaye pratyapādayat \|*  
*tāṃ sa dīrghatamā devīṃ tathā kṛtavatīṃ tadā \|\| 68 \|\|*

67-68. After that, King Bali appeased that sage and was furious with his wife; and sent her again well-dressed, after her toilet, to the sage, when the seer said.

## \|\| 48.69 \|\|

*dadhnā lavaṇamiśreṇa tv abhyaktaṃ madhukena tu \|*  
*liha mām ajugupsantī āpādatalamastakam \|*  
*tatastvaṃ prāpsyase devi putrānvai manasepsitān \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. “O, Devi! Cast off your bashfulness and then lick the whole of my body with your tongue, after rubbing it with salt, curds and honey; you will then attain your wish and get sons.”

## \|\| 48.70 \|\|

*tasya sā tadvaco devī sarvaṃ kṛtavatī tadā \|*  
*tasya sāpānam āsādya devī pariharattadā \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. The queen followed the directions of the seer, but omitted to lick the hind private parts.

## \|\| 48.71 \|\|

*tāmuvāca tataḥ so 'tha yatte parihṛtaṃ śubhe \|*  
*vināpānaṃ kumāraṃ tu janayiṣyasi pūrvajam \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. When the sage said: “O, blessed one! Your eldest son will be without that part of the. body which you have omitted to lick.”

## \|\| 48.72 \|\|

*sudeṣṇovāca*  
*nārhasi tvaṃ mahābhāga putraṃ me dātumīdṛśam \|*  
*toṣitaśca yathāśakti prasādaṃ kuru me prabho \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. The queen said: — “Sire! It is not worthy of you to bless me with such an offspring. Be pleased at my devotion and show your mercy to me”.

## \|\| 48.73-76 \|\|

*dīrghatamā uvāca*  
*tavāpacārāddevyeṣa nānyathā bhavitā śubhe \|*  
*naiva dāsyati putraste pautrau vai dāsyate phalam \|\| 73 \|\|*

*tasyāpānaṃ vinā caiva yogyabhāvo bhaviṣyati \|*  
*tasmād dīrghatamāṅgeṣu kukṣau spṛṣṭvedam abravīt \|\| 74 \|\|*

*prāśitaṃ yadyadaṅgeṣu na sopasthaṃ śucismite \|*  
*tena tiṣṭhanti te garbhe paurṇamāsyām ivoḍurāṭ \|\| 75 \|\|*

*bhaviṣyanti kumārāstu pañca devasutopamāḥ \|*  
*tejasvinaḥ suvṛttāśca yajvāno dhārmikāśca te \|\| 76 \|\|*

73-76. Dirghatama said: — “O, Blessed one, through your fault this will happen exactly as I have told you and this son of yours will not delight you in any way, but your grandson will; he will, however, not feel the necessity of the missing part of his body.” Then the sage, touching her abdomen, said, “O, queen because you have licked all parts of my body except the privates, your sons will be like the full moon, and, in all you.

will be blessed with five sons of Divine beauty who will be most illustrious, renowned, righteous and performers of sacrifices”.

## \|\| 48.77-78 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*tadaṃśastu sudeṣṇāyā jyeṣṭhaḥ putro vyajāyata \|*  
*aṅgastathā kaliṅgaśca puṇḍraḥ suhmastathaiva ca \|\| 77 \|\|*

*vaṅgarājastu pañcaite baleḥ putrāśca kṣetrajāḥ \|*  
*ityete dīrghatamasā balerdattāḥ sutāstathā \|\| 78 \|\|*

77-78. Suta said: — O Rishis, Sudeshna begot, through the favour of Dirghatama, Aga, the eldest, along with his brothers, Kalinga, Pundra, Suhuma, and Vangaraja. Thus the sage begot the above-named five sons to the king Bali.

## \|\| 48.80-82 \|\|

*tatastaṃ dīrghatamasaṃ surabhirvākyamabravīt \|*  
*vicārya yasmādgodharmaṃ pramāṇaṃ te kṛtaṃ vibho \|\| 80 \|\|*

*śaktyā cānanyayāsmāsu tena prītāsmi te 'nagha \|*  
*tasmāttubhyaṃ tamo dīrgham āghrāyāpanudāmi vai \|\| 81 \|\|*

*bārhaspatyastathaivaiṣa pāpmā vai tiṣṭhati tvayi \|*  
*jarāṃ mṛtyuṃ tamaścaiva āghrāyāpanudāmi te \|\| 82 \|\|*

80-82. Afterwards, the sage took all the five sons through a course of ceremony, enjoined on all the twice-born, Thus that posterity was Then the divine cow Surabhi said to Dirghatama: — “As you followed the cattle law deliberately and took it to be superior to all, O, sinless! I am very much pleased with you and hereby remove your blindness by smelling you. The sin of Brihaspati is inherent in you.

I however relieve you of your old age, death and loss of vision, by merely smelling you”.

## \|\| 48.84-87 \|\|

*go 'bhyāhate tamasi vai gautamastu tato 'bhavat \|*  
*kākṣīvāṃstu tato gatvā saha pitrā girivrajam \|\| 84 \|\|*

*dṛṣṭvā spṛṣṭvā piturvai sa hy upaviṣṭaściraṃ tapaḥ \|*  
*tataḥ kālena mahatā tapasā bhāvitastu saḥ \|\| 85 \|\|*

*vidhūya mātṛjaṃ kāyaṃ brāhmaṇyaṃ prāptavānvibhuḥ \|*  
*tato 'bravītpitā taṃ vai putravānasmyahaṃ tvayā \|\| 86 \|\|*

*satputreṇa tu dharmajña kṛtārtho 'haṃ yaśasvinā \|*  
*muktvātmānaṃ tato 'sau vai prāptavānbrahmaṇaḥ kṣayam \|\| 87 \|\|*

84-87. That sage was instantly restored to his vision after being smelled by Surabhi, and got a long lease of life, along with beautiful eyes and form. He came to be known as Gautama, on account of his being relieved of his blindness by (the smelling of) the cow. — Afterwards, Kakshivana, the son of that Shudra nurse, went with his father, Dirghatama, to Girivraja, and after seeing and touching him practiced penances for a long time, and in the fullness of time, through his asceticism, he purified the body obtained from a Shudra mother and became a Brahmana, at which his father told him: “I consider myself to-day blessed with a son through you, and O pious one! I feel blessed on getting a righteous and renowned son like you, who after casting off his previous sheath, has become a Brahmana.”

## \|\| 48.88 \|\|

*brāhmaṇyaṃ prāpya kākṣīvān sahasramasṛjatsutān \|*  
*kauṣmāṇḍā gautamāścaiva smṛtāḥ kākṣīvataḥ sutāḥ \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. Kakshivana, on becoming a Brahmana begot a thousand sons, who came to be known as Kaushamanda and Gautamas.

## \|\| 48.89 \|\|

*ityeṣa dīrghatamaso balervairocanasya ca \|*  
*samāgamo vaḥ kathitaḥ saṃtatiścobhayostathā \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. Thus the circumstances bringing Bali, the son of Virrochana, into contact with the sage, Dirghatama, as well as the family of Bali, have been explained.

## \|\| 48.90 \|\|

*balistānabhinandyāha pañca putrānakalmaṣān \|*  
*kṛtārthaḥ so 'pi dharmātmā yogamāyāvṛtaḥ svayam \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. Bali said to his five pious sons that he considered himself highly blessed on having them as his sons; and then encasing himself in his Yoga Maya, he became invisible to all, and began to wait for the predicted period, in the Patalapuri.

## \|\| 48.91-92 \|\|

*adṛṣyaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ kālāpekṣaḥ sa vai prabhuḥ \|*  
*tatrāṅgasya tu dāyādo rājāsīddadhivāhanaḥ \|\| 91 \|\|*

*dadhivāhanaputrastu rājā divirathaḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*āsīd divirathāpatyaṃ vidvāndharmaratho nṛpaḥ \|\| 92 \|\|*

91-92. The son of Anga was the King Dadhivahana. Dadhivahana’s son was King Diviratha, who begot the learned Dharmaratha.

## \|\| 48.93-95 \|\|

*sa hi dharmarathaḥ śrīmāṃs tena viṣṇupade girau \|*  
*somaḥ śukreṇa vai rājñā saha pīto mahātmanā \|\| 93 \|\|*

*atha dharmarathasyābhūt putraścitrarathaḥ kila \|*  
*tasya satyarathaḥ putras tasmāddaśarathaḥ kila \|\| 94 \|\|*

*lomapāda iti khyātas tasya śāntā sutābhavat \|*  
*atha dāśarathir vīraś caturaṅgo mahāyaśāḥ \|\| 95 \|\|*

93-95. That Dharmaratha the great, drank the draught of nectar with the seer Shukra, on the Vishnupada mount; after which he became the father of Chitraratha, who begot Satyaratha, the father of Dasharatha, who is also known as Lomapada. He was the father of a girl, named Santa and a renowned son, named Chaturanga.

## \|\| 48.98-100 \|\|

*pūrṇabhadraprasādena haryaṅgo 'sya suto 'bhavat \|*  
*yajñe vibhāṇḍakāccāsya vāraṇaḥ śatruvāraṇaḥ \|\| 98 \|\|*

*avatārayāmāsa mahīṃ mantrairvāhanamuttamam \|*  
*haryaṅgasya tu dāyādo jāto bhadrarathaḥ kila \|\| 99 \|\|*

*atha bhadrarathasyāsīd bṛhatkarmā janeśvaraḥ \|*  
*bṛhadbhānuḥ sutastasya tasmādjajñe mahātmavān \|\| 100 \|\|*

98-100. Chaturanga, through the blessings of the sage Shringi, was the promoter of his clan. He was the father of Prithulaksha, who begat.

Champa, after whose name the country Champipuri is known. It first Champaka, through tie favour of Purnabhadra, begot Haryanga, the father of Vibhanda, who begot Varana, the resister of his foes, who made the celestial conveyances descend on earth through his supernatural powers. Haryanga was the father of Bhadraratha, who begot the King Brihatkarma, the father of Brihatbhanu

## \|\| 48.101-102 \|\|

*bṛhadbhānustu rājendro janayāmāsa vai sutam \|*  
*nāmnā jayadrathaṃ nāma tasmādbṛhadratho nṛpaḥ \|\| 101 \|\|*

*āsīdbṛhadrathāccaiva viśvajidjanamejayaḥ \|*  
*dāyādastasya cāṅgo vai tasmātkarṇo 'bhavannṛpaḥ \|\| 102 \|\|*

101-102. Brihatbhanu was the father of Jayadratha, whose son was Brihadratha. Janamejaya, the great conqueror, was the son of Brihadratha, who became the father of the King Anga, the father of Karna.

## \|\| 48.103 \|\|

*karṇasya vṛṣasenastu pṛthusenastathātmajaḥ \|*  
*ete 'ṅgasyātmajāḥ sarve rājānaḥ kīrtitā mayā \|*  
*vistareṇānupūrvyācca pūrostu śṛṇuta dvijāḥ \|\| 103 \|\|*

103\. Karna became the father of Vrishasena who begot Prithusena. “Rishis! I have enumerated to you the family of Anga; now I shall relate to you the family of Puru”.

## \|\| 48.104 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ*  
*kathaṃ sūtātmajaḥ karṇaḥ kathamaṅgasya cātmajaḥ \|*  
*etad icchāmahe śrotum atyantakuśalo hy asi \|\| 104 \|\|*

104\. The Rishis said: — “Suta! How is it that Karna is said to be the son of Suta, when you say that he was the son of Anga? We wish to know about it, for you-are an expert in these matters.

## \|\| 48.105 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*bṛhadbhānusuto jajñe rājā nāmnā bṛhanmanāḥ \|*  
*tasya patnīdvayaṃ hy āsīc chaibyasya tanaye hy ubhe \|*  
*yaśodevī ca satyā ca tayorvaṃśaṃ ca me śṛṇu \|\| 105 \|\|*

105\. Suta said: — Brihadbhanu begot a son, called Brihanmana, who had two queens, viz.: — Yashodevi and Satya, the daughters of the king Saivya.

## \|\| 48.106 \|\|

*jayadrathaṃ tu rājānaṃ yaśodevī hy ajījanat \|*  
*sā bṛhanmanasaḥ satyā vijayaṃ nāma viśrutam \|\| 106 \|\|*

106\. Jayadratha was born of Yashodevi, and Vijaya was born of Satya.

## \|\| 48.108 \|\|

*satyakarmaṇo 'dhirathaḥ sūtaścādhirathaḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*yaḥ karṇaṃ pratijagrāha tena karṇastu sūtajaḥ \|*  
*taccedaṃ sarvamākhyātaṃ karṇaṃ prati yathoditam \|\| 108 \|\|*

108\. Brihat was the son of Vijaya and the father of Brihadratha, who begot Satyakarma, the father of Adhiratha, who was the \[Suta\] chariotdriver of Satyakarma. He had nurtured Karna, the son of Anga, and so Karna is known as the son of Suta also.

## Chapter 49

## \|\| 49.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*pūroḥ putro mahātejā rājā sa janamejayaḥ \|*  
*prācītvataḥ sutastasya yaḥ prācīmakaroddiśam \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Puru was the father of the most Illustrious Janamejaya who begot Prachitvata and ruled in the East, and gave his name to the Eastern quarter (Prachi means East).

## \|\| 49.2-3 \|\|

*prācītvatasya tanayo manasyuśca tathābhavat \|*  
*rājā pītāudho nāma manasyorabhavatsutaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*dāyādastasya cāpyāsīd dhundhurnāma mahīpatiḥ \|*  
*dhundhorbahuvidhaḥ putraḥ sampātistasya cātmajaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

2-3. Prachitvata became the father of Manasyu, who begot Pitayudha, whose heir was Dhundhu, whose son was Bahuvidha, the father of Sampati.

## \|\| 49.4-8 \|\|

*sampātestu raṃhavarcā bhadrāśvastasya cātmajaḥ \|*  
*bhadrāśvasya dhṛtāyāṃ tu daśāpsarasi sūnavaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*auceuśca hṛṣeuśca kakṣeuśca saneukaḥ \|*  
*dhṛteuśca vineuśca sthaleuścaiva sattamaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*dharmeuḥ saṃnateuśca puṇyeuśceti te daśa \|*  
*auceyorjvalanā nāma bhāryā vai takṣakātmajā \|\| 6 \|\|*

*tasyāṃ sa janayāmāsa antināraṃ mahīpatim \|*  
*antināro manasvinyāṃ putrāñjajñe parāñchubhān \|\| 7 \|\|*

*amūrtarayasaṃ vīraṃ trivanaṃ caiva dhārmikam \|*  
*gaurī kanyā tṛtīyā ca māndhāturjananī śubhā \|\| 8 \|\|*

4-8. Sampati begot Rahamvarcha, the father of Bhadrashva, who begot from the Apsara, named, Dhrita, ten sons, viz., Aucheyu, Hrisheyu, Kaksheyu, Saneyu, Dhriteyu, Vineyu, Sthaleyu, Dharmeyu, Sanateyu and Puneyu.

Jvalana, the daughter of Takshaka, became the wife of Aucheyu, from whom he begot the King Antinara (another reading is Rantinara), who became the father of many good sons, through his queen, Manasvini. The heroic Amurtarayas, the pious Trivana, and, third, a daughter, named Gauri, who afterwards became the mother of Mandhata, (were born to him).

## \|\| 49.10 \|\|

*upadānavī sutāṃllebhe caturastvilinātmajāt \|*  
*ṛṣyantamatha duṣyantaṃ pravīram anadhaṃ tathā \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Ilina, the daughter of Yama, who was an auspicious lady (and was another queen of Antinara), begot sons who were gifted with Divine The son of Ilina begot four sons through his wife Upadanavi, viz., Rishyanta, Dushyanta, Pravira and Anagha.

## \|\| 49.11 \|\|

*cakravartī tato yajñe duṣyantātsamitiṃjayaḥ \|*  
*śakuntalāyāṃ bharato yasya nāmnā ca bhāratāḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Dushyanta became the father of a world-conquering and Universal Emperor, Bharata, from his wife Shakuntala, whose descendants are called Bharatas

## \|\| 49.12-13 \|\|

*dauṣyantīṃ prati rājānaṃ vāgūce cāśarīriṇī \|*  
*mātā bhastrā pituḥ putro yena jātaḥ sa eva saḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*bharasva putraṃ duṣyanta māvamaṃsthāḥ śakuntalām \|*  
*retodhāṃ nayate putraḥ paretaṃ yamasādanāt \|*  
*tvaṃ cāsya dhātā garbhasya satyamāha śakuntalā \|\| 13 \|\|*

12-13. To the King Dushyanta, an incorporeal Voice thus addressed: —

“Mother is like a pair of bellows to the father, from whom the son is horn. The son is thus identical with the father. Therefore, O Dushyanta! foster your son and do not discard Shakuntala. The son raises his deceased father back from the hell of Yama to heaven. Thou art the generator of this child. What Shakuntala said is true.

## \|\| 49.14-15 \|\|

*bharatasya vinaṣṭeṣu tanayeṣu purā kila \|*  
*putrāṇāṃ mātṛkāt kopāt sumahānsaṃkṣayaḥ kṛtaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*tato marudbhirānīya putraḥ sa tu bṛhaspateḥ \|*  
*saṃkrāmito bharadvājo marudbhirbharatasya tu \|\| 15 \|\|*

14-15. a Thus Bharata Was born of Shakuntala and Dushyanta. In ancient times, when all the sons of Bharata perished, through a widespread and virulent epidemic, brought on by the wrath of the Goddess Matrika \[? smallpox\], then the Marut Devas brought Bharadvaja, the son of Brihaspati, and gave him to Bharata.

## \|\| 49.16 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ*  
*bharatasya bharadvājaḥ putrārthaṃ mārutaiḥ katham \|*  
*saṃkrāmito mahātejās tanno brūhi yathātatham \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. The sages said: — “Suta! Please explain to us fully how the Marut Devas gave the most illustrious Bharadvaja to Bharata.”

## \|\| 49.17-28 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*patnyāmāpannasattvāyām uśijaḥ sa sthito bhuvi \|*  
*bhrāturbhāryāṃ sa dṛṣṭvā tu bṛhaspatiruvāca ha \|\| 17 \|\|*

*upatiṣṭha svalaṃkṛtya maithunāya ca māṃ śubhe \|*  
*evamuktābravīdenaṃ svayameva bṛhaspatim \|\| 18 \|\|*

*garbhaḥ pariṇataścāyaṃ brahma vyāharate girā \|*  
*amogharetāstvaṃ cāpi dharmaṃ caivaṃ vigarhitam \|\| 19 \|\|*

*evamukto 'bravīdenāṃ svayameva bṛhaspatiḥ \|*  
*nopadeṣṭavyo vinayas tvayā me varavarṇini \|\| 20 \|\|*

*dharṣamāṇaḥ prasahyaināṃ maithunāyopacakrame \|*  
*tato bṛhaspatiṃ garbho dharṣamāṇamuvāca ha \|\| 21 \|\|*

*saṃniviṣṭo hy ahaṃ pūrvam iha nāma bṛhaspate \|*  
*amogharetāśca bhavān nāvakāśa iha dvayoḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*evamuktaḥ sa garbheṇa kupitaḥ pratyuvāca ha \|*  
*yasmāttvamīdṛśe kāle sarvabhūtepsite sati \|*  
*abhiṣedhasi tasmāttvaṃ tamo dīrghaṃ pravekṣyasi \|\| 23 \|\|*

*tataḥ kāmaṃ saṃnivartya tasyānandādbṛhaspateḥ \|*  
*tadretastvapatadbhūmau nivṛttaṃ śiśuko 'bhavat \|\| 24 \|\|*

*sadyojātaṃ kumāraṃ tu dṛṣṭvā taṃ mamatābravīt \|*  
*gamiṣyāmi gṛhaṃ svaṃ vai bharasvainaṃ bṛhaspate \|\| 25 \|\|*

*evamuktvā gatā sā tu gatāyāṃ so 'pi taṃ tyajat \|*  
*mātāpitṛbhyāṃ tyaktaṃ tu dṛṣṭvā taṃ marutaḥ śiśum \|*  
*jagṛhustaṃ bharadvājaṃ marutaḥ kṛpayā sthitāḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*tasminkāle tu bharato bahubhir ṛtubhirvibhuḥ \|*  
*putranaimittikairyajñair ayajatputralipsayā \|\| 27 \|\|*

*yadā sa yajamānastu putraṃ nāsādayatprabhuḥ \|*  
*tataḥ kratuṃ marutsomaṃ putrārthe samupāharat \|\| 28 \|\|*

17-28. Suta said: — Brihaspati, whilst staying on Earth, one day saw the wife of his brother, Ushija, who was big with child, and addressed her thus: —

“Dress thyself well and Jet us enjoy.” She, being thus addressed, replied to Brihaspati thus: — “The embryo in my womb is mature and is already reciting the Vedas. Thy seed will also not be fruitless and thy proposal is sinful.” Hearing which, Brihaspati said: — “I need not be taught morality by thee, O sweet one.” After saying that, he carried out his desire by force; when on the verge of his final enjoyment, the child from her womb

cried out to Brihaspati: — “I have entered the womb first, O Brihaspati, thy seed will also not go in vain. There is no room for a second body in this womb.” Brihaspati being thus addressed by the child in the womb, replied in anger: — “Because on such an occasion, dear to every creature, thou preventest me from enjoyment, thou shouldst see lasting darkness \[Dirghatamas\].”

## \|\| 49.24-25 \|\|

*tataḥ kāmaṃ saṃnivartya tasyānandādbṛhaspateḥ \|*  
*tadretastvapatadbhūmau nivṛttaṃ śiśuko 'bhavat \|\| 24 \|\|*

*sadyojātaṃ kumāraṃ tu dṛṣṭvā taṃ mamatābravīt \|*  
*gamiṣyāmi gṛhaṃ svaṃ vai bharasvainaṃ bṛhaspate \|\| 25 \|\|*

24-25. Afterwards, Brihaspati cast his seed on the floor which at once became a child; seeing whom, Mamata said to Brihaspati, “I am going home, you should support \[Bhara\] this child \[born of us two (dvaja)\], O Brihaspati.”

## \|\| 49.26 \|\|

*evamuktvā gatā sā tu gatāyāṃ so 'pi taṃ tyajat \|*  
*mātāpitṛbhyāṃ tyaktaṃ tu dṛṣṭvā taṃ marutaḥ śiśum \|*  
*jagṛhustaṃ bharadvājaṃ marutaḥ kṛpayā sthitāḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Afterwards, she went away, and the child was also given up by Brihaspati. Seeing the child thus forsaken by both his father and mother, the Maruts, through pity, carried that child, Bharadvaja, to Bharata.

## \|\| 49.27-30 \|\|

*tasminkāle tu bharato bahubhir ṛtubhirvibhuḥ \|*  
*putranaimittikairyajñair ayajatputralipsayā \|\| 27 \|\|*

*yadā sa yajamānastu putraṃ nāsādayatprabhuḥ \|*  
*tataḥ kratuṃ marutsomaṃ putrārthe samupāharat \|\| 28 \|\|*

*tena te marutastasya marutsomena tuṣṭuvuḥ \|*  
*upaninyurbharadvājaṃ putrārthaṃ bharatāya vai \|\| 29 \|\|*

*dāyādo 'ṅgirasaḥ sūnor aurasastu bṛhaspateḥ \|*  
*saṃkrāmito bharadvājo marudbhirbharataṃ prati \|\| 30 \|\|*

27-30. At the same time, King Bharata performed a big sacrifice to beget a progeny, but his object was not gained. Then he performed the Marut soma sacrifice, when the Marut Devas becoming pleased with the devotion of the king, gave him the child Bharadvaja. In that way, the Marut Devas presented this son Of Brihaspati, the son of Angiras, to the king Bharata.

## \|\| 49.31 \|\|

*bharatastu bharadvājaṃ putraṃ prāpya vibhur bravīt \|*  
*ādāv ātmahitāya tvaṃ kṛtārtho 'haṃ tvayā vibho \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Bharata on getting Bharadvaja said: — “I consider myself blessed on getting you”.

## \|\| 49.33-34 \|\|

*tasmādapi bharadvājād brāhmaṇāḥ kṣatriyā bhuvi \|*  
*dvyāmuṣyāyaṇakaulīnāḥ smṛtāste dvividhena ca \|\| 33 \|\|*

*tato jāte hi vitathe bharataśca divaṃ yayau \|*  
*bharadvājo divaṃ yāto hy abhiṣicya sutamṛṣiḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

33-34. Bharadvaja was named Vitatha \[futile\], owing to his being futile as a son, for he never entered the mother's womb, The Brahmanas and Kshatriyas born on this Earth of Bharadvaja, came to be known as. Dvyamusyayana Kaulinas. When Vitatha was thus brought to Bharata, then Bharata went to heaven, and the sage Bharadvaja also went there, after anointing his son.

## \|\| 49.35-40 \|\|

*dāyādo vitathasyāsīd bhuvamanyur mahāyaśāḥ \|*  
*mahābhūtopamāḥ putrāś catvāro bhuvamanyavaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

*bṛhatkṣatro mahāvīryo naro gargaśca vīryavān \|*  
*narasya saṃkṛtiḥ putras tasya putro mahāyaśāḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

*gurudhī rantidevaśca satkṛtyāṃ tāv ubhau smṛtau \|*  
*gargasya caiva dāyādaḥ śibirvidvānajāyata \|\| 37 \|\|*

*smṛtāḥ śaibyāstato gargāḥ kṣatropetā dvijātayaḥ \|*  
*āhāryatanayaścaiva dhīmānāsīd urukṣavaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

*tasya bhāryā viśālā tu suṣuve putrakatrayam \|*  
*tryuṣaṇaṃ puṣkariṃ caiva kaviṃ caiva mahāyaśāḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

*urukṣavāḥ smṛtā hy ete sarve brāhmaṇatāṃ gatāḥ \|*  
*kāvyānāṃ tu varā hy ete trayaḥ proktā maharṣayaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

35-40. Vitatha begot the renowned Bhuvamanyana, who had four famous sons, viz., Brihatkshatra, Mahavirya, Nara and Garga. Nara became the father of Sankriti, who begot Mahayasha, who, through Satkriti, had two sons, named Gurudhi and Rantideva. Garga’s heir was the learned Shibi, whose sons, known as Shaibyas and Garga’s, were twice-horn Kshatriyas as well as Brahmanas. Urukshvata was the worthy son of Aharya (Mahavirya) who begot, through Vishala, three sons, named Triyushna, Pushkari and Kavi, and they became Brahmanas and were called Urukshavas, and these three were the highest Rishis amongst Kavyas.

## \|\| 49.41-44 \|\|

*gargāḥ saṃkṛtayaḥ kāvyāḥ kṣatropetā dvijātayaḥ \|*  
*saṃbhṛtāṅgiraso dakṣā bṛhatkṣatrasya ca kṣitiḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

*bṛhatkṣatrasya dāyādo hastināmā babhūva ha \|*  
*tenedaṃ nirmitaṃ pūrvaṃ puraṃ tu gajasāhvayam \|\| 42 \|\|*

*hastinaścaiva dāyādās trayaḥ paramakīrtayaḥ \|*  
*ajamīḍho dvimīḍhaśca purumīḍhastathaiva ca \|\| 43 \|\|*

*ajamīḍhasya patnyastu tisraḥ kurukulodvahāḥ \|*  
*nīlinī dhūminī caiva keśinī caiva viśrutā \|\| 44 \|\|*

41-44. The Gargas, the Sankritayas and the Kavyas are twice-born Brahmanas with Kshatriya strain in them. They were all very learned. Kshiti, the eon of Brihatkshatra, is known as Hasti. He was the founder of vote, of the city, called Gajasahvaya (Hastinapura). Hasti had three sons of great glory; named, Ajamidha Dwimidha, and Purumidha, Ajamidha had three wives, born of Kuru clan, Nilini, Dhumini and Reshini.

## \|\| 49.45-46 \|\|

*sa tāsu janayāmāsa putrānvai devavarcasaḥ \|*  
*tapaso 'nte mahātejā jātā vṛddhasya dhārmikāḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

*bhāradvājaprasādena vistaraṃ teṣu me śṛṇu \|*  
*ājamīḍhasya keśinyāṃ kaṇvaḥ samabhavatkila \|\| 46 \|\|*

45-46. From his wives, Ajamidha begot sons of Divine lustre; because they were born to him in his old age, on the completion of his asceticism; therefore, they were very pious and powerful. They were all born through the blessings of Bharadvaja. Hear now their names in detail.

## \|\| 49.47-50 \|\|

*medhātithiḥ sutastasya tasmātkāṇvāyanā dvijāḥ \|*  
*ajamīḍhasya bhūminyāṃ jajñe bṛhadanur nṛpaḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

*bṛhadanor bṛhanto 'tha bṛhantasya bṛhanmanāḥ \|*  
*bṛhanmanaḥsutaścāpi bṛhaddhanuriti śrutaḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

*bṛhaddhanor bṛhadiṣuḥ putrastasya jayadrathaḥ \|*  
*aśvajittanayastasya senajit tasya cātmajaḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

*atha senajitaḥ putrāś catvāro lokaviśrutāḥ \|*  
*rucirāśvaśca kāvyaśca rājā dṛḍharathastathā \|\| 50 \|\|*

47-50. Ajamidha begot from Keshini, Kanva, who became the father of Medhatithi, the progenitor of the Kanvaya clan of Brahmanas; from his wife Dhumini, Ajamidha begot the King Brihadanu, who was the father of Brihamta, who begot Brihanmana the father of Brihadhanu, who begot Brihadishu, the father of Jayadratha, who begot Ashvajit, the — father of Senajit, who had four world-famous sons, viz., Ruchirashva, Kavya, King Dhridaratha and Vatsaraja.

## \|\| 49.51-53 \|\|

*vatsaścāvartako rājā yasyaite parivatsakāḥ \|*  
*rucirāśvasya dāyādaḥ pṛthuseno mahāyaśāḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

*pṛthusenasya paurastu paurānnīpo 'tha jajñivān \|*  
*nīpasyaikaśataṃ tv āsīt putrāṇām amitaujasām \|\| 52 \|\|*

*nīpā iti samākhyātā rājānaḥ sarva eva te \|*  
*teṣāṃ vaṃśakaraḥ śrīmān nīpānāṃ kīrtivardhanaḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

51-53. Vatsaraja was the founder of the dynasty of Parivatsaka, and Ruchirashva became the father of Prithusena, who begot Paura the father of Nipa, who begot one hundred valiant sons, who all were known as Nipas. Among them Shrimana was the most renowned.

## \|\| 49.54-58 \|\|

*kāvyācca samaro nāma sadeṣṭasamaro 'bhavat \|*  
*samarasya pārasampārau sadaśva iti te trayaḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

*putrāḥ sarvaguṇopetā jātā vai viśrutā bhuvi \|*  
*pāraputraḥ pṛthurjātaḥ pṛthostu sukṛto 'bhavat \|\| 55 \|\|*

*jajñe sarvaguṇopeto vibhrājastasya cātmajaḥ \|*  
*vibhrājasya tu dāyādas tv aṇuho nāma vīryavān \|\| 56 \|\|*

*babhūva śukajāmātā kṛtvībhartā mahāyaśāḥ \|*  
*aṇuhasya tu dāyādo brahmadatto mahīpatiḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

*yugadattaḥ sutastasya viṣvakseno mahāyaśāḥ \|*  
*vibhrājaḥ punar ājātaḥ sukṛteneha karmaṇā \|\| 58 \|\|*

54-58. Kavya begot Samara, who was only fond of wars; and he begot three sons, namely, Para, Samp4ra, and Sadashva. They were renowned as great men in the world, and of them Para begot Prithu, the father of Sukrita, who begot Vibhraja of versatile genius, who became the father of Anuha, who was the son-in-law of Shukra and the husband of Kritvi, Anuha begot Brahmadatta, the father of Yugadatta, who begot Vishvaksena who, again, came back to this Earth on account of his good deeds.

## \|\| 49.60 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ*  
*ugrāudhaḥ kasya sutaḥ kasya vaṃśe sa kathyate \|*  
*kimarthaṃ tena te nīpāḥ sarve caiva praṇāśitāḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Vishvaksena begot Udakasena, the father of Bhallata who begot Janamejaya Ugrayudba, for the sake of Janamejaya, then put an end to the Rishis said: — “Suta! Whose son was Ugrayudha, and in what” family was he born, and why did he annihilate the Nipa Kings? Pray tell as all that fully.”

## \|\| 49.62-66 \|\|

*tasya rājyaṃ pratiśrutya nīpān ājaghnivān prabhuḥ \|*  
*uvāca sāntvaṃ vividhaṃ jaghnuste vai hy ubhāv api \|\| 62 \|\|*

*hanyamānāgatān ūce yasmāddhetorna me vacaḥ \|*  
*śaraṇāgatarakṣārthaṃ tasmādevaṃ śapāmi vaḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

*yadi me 'sti tapastaptaṃ sarvānnayatu vo yamaḥ \|*  
*tatastān kṛpyamāṇāṃstu yamena purataḥ sa tu \|\| 64 \|\|*

*kṛpayā parayāviṣṭo janamejayam ūcivān \|*  
*gatānetānimānvīrāṃs tvaṃ me rakṣitumarhasi \|\| 65 \|\|*

*janamejaya uvāca*  
*are pāpā durācārā bhavitāro 'sya kiṃkarāḥ \|*  
*tathetyuktastato rājā yamena uyudhe ciram \|\| 66 \|\|*

62-66. Suta said: — Ugrayudha was born in the Solar dynasty and practiced penances for eighteen thousand years, when he was dried up like a pillar. King Janamejaya adored him for getting kingdom; and he, after promising kingdom to him, killed the Nipas. Once, the Nipas attacked the Rishi Ugrayudha and Janamejaya, who was serving him in his Ashrama. Ugrayudha addressed the Nipas with many conciliatory speeches, but they, heedless of them, Injured them. Then Ugrayudha, when being thus injured, addressed them: — “Since you have not paid heed to my words asking protection and safety from you, therefore, I curse you thus: May you all be taken away by Yama, if there is any force in my asceticism.” After that, they were all taken before the God of Death. Seeing which, Ugrayudha, overcome with pity, said: “Janamejaya, you are worthy of rescuing these misguided, but brave men;” hearing which Janamejaya began to fight Yama, after crying out to his victims, “O, sinners! become the slaves of Ugrayudha.”

## \|\| 49.67 \|\|

*vyādhibhirnārakairghorair yamena saha tānbalāt \|*  
*vijitya munaye prādāt tadadbhutamivābhavat \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. Strange to say, Janamejaya vanquished his foe and captured Yama, along with hells and their tortures

## \|\| 49.69 \|\|

*yeṣāṃ tu caritaṃ gṛhya hanyate nāpamṛtyubhiḥ \|*  
*iha loke pare caiva sukhamakṣayyamaśnute \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. The God of Death, becoming pleased at the end, gave the knowledge of emancipation to Janamejaya, after which all the Nipas went to Lord One who hears their history does not die an unnatural death, but attains bliss in both the worlds.

## \|\| 49.70 \|\|

*ajamīḍhasya dhūminyāṃ vidvāñjajñe yavīnaraḥ \|*  
*dhṛtimāṃstasya putrastu tasya satyadhṛtiḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*atha satyadhṛteḥ putro dṛḍhanemiḥ pratāpavān \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. Now the family from Dhumini — another queen of Ajamidha. Ajamidha begot from his wife, Dhumini, the learned Yuvinara, who became the father of Dhritiman, who begot Satyadhriti, the father of the valiant Dridhanemi.

## \|\| 49.71-75 \|\|

*dṛḍhanemisutaścāpi sudharmā nāma pārthivaḥ \|*  
*āsītsudharmatanayaḥ sārvabhaumaḥ pratāpavān \|\| 71 \|\|*

*sārvabhaumeti vikhyātaḥ pṛthivyām ekarāḍ babhau \|*  
*tasyānvavāye mahati mahāpauravanandanaḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

*mahāpauravaputrastu rājā rukmarathaḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*atha rukmarathasyāsīt supārśvo nāma pārthivaḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

*supārśvatanayaścāpi sumatirnāma dhārmikaḥ \|*  
*sumaterapi dharmātmā rājā saṃnatimānapi \|\| 74 \|\|*

*tasyāsītsaṃnatimataḥ kṛto nāma suto mahān \|*  
*hiraṇyanābhinaḥ śiṣyaḥ kauśalyasya mahātmanaḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

71-75. Dridhanemi became the father of Sudharma, who begot the illustrious Sarvabhauma, who became the world-emperor, and Mahapaurava was born in his famous family. Mahapaurava begot the King Rukmaratha, the father of Suparshva, who begot the righteous Sumati, the father of Sannatimana, who begot Krita, who became the disciple of Hiranyanabhi Kaushalya.

## \|\| 49.76 \|\|

*caturviṃśatidhā yena proktā vai sāmasaṃhitāḥ \|*  
*smṛtāste prācyasāmānaḥ kārtā nāmeha sāmagāḥ \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. This Krita was the promulgator of twenty-four kinds of Sama Vedic Samhita, and the chanter of these Samas came to be known as Eastern Kartasamagas

## \|\| 49.78 \|\|

*nīlo nāma mahārājaḥ pāñcālādhipatirvaśī \|*  
*ugrāudhasya dāyādaḥ kṣemo nāma mahāyaśāḥ \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. Ugrayudha was the son of Krita, and was known as Karti. He was the promoter of his, family, and it was he who killed the father of Prithu That father of Prithu was Nila, the king of the Panchala, and Kshema the renowned, was the son of Ugrayudha.

## \|\| 49.79 \|\|

*kṣemātsunīthaḥ saṃjajñe sunīthasya nṛpaṃjayaḥ \|*  
*nṛpaṃjayācca viratha ityete pauravāḥ stutāḥ \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. Kshema was the father of Sunitha, who begot Nripaijaya, the father of Viratha, This completes the line of the Paurava Kings.

## Chapter 50

## \|\| 50.1-4 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*ajamīḍhasya nīlinyāṃ nīlaḥ samabhavannṛpaḥ \|*  
*nīlasya tapasogreṇa suśāntirudapadyata \|\| 1 \|\|*

*purujānuḥ suśāntestu pṛthustu purujānutaḥ \|*  
*bhadrāśvaḥ pṛthudāyādo bhadrāśvatanayāñchṛṇu \|\| 2 \|\|*

*mudgalaśca jayaścaiva rājā bṛhadiṣustathā \|*  
*javīnaraśca vikrāntaḥ kapilaścaiva pañcamaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*pañcānāṃ caiva pañcālān etāñjanapadānviduḥ \|*  
*pañcālarakṣiṇo hy ete deśānāmiti naḥ śrutam \|\| 4 \|\|*

1-4. Suta said: — Ajamidha begot from Nilini, Nila, who was the father or Sushanti, through his severe austerities. Sushanti begot Purujanu, the father of Prithu, who begot Bhadrashva, Now listen to the progeny of Bhadrashva He had five sons, namely, Mudgala, Jaya, Brihadishu, Javihara and Kapila, They all five, it is heard, were the kings in different parts of the Panchala and ruled with righteousness. Hence their country was called Panchala, or ruled by the five. Thus we have heard.

## \|\| 50.5 \|\|

*mudgalasyāpi maudgalyāḥ kṣatropetā dvijātayaḥ \|*  
*ete hy aṅgirasaḥ pakṣaṃ saṃśritāḥ kāṇvamudgalāḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. The sons of Mudgala became Brahmanas from Kshatriyas and were founders of the family of Maudgalyas. Maudgalas and Kanvas, mentioned before, were the followers of the school of Angira.

## \|\| 50.6-7 \|\|

*mudgalasya suto jajñe brahmiṣṭhaḥ sumahāyaśāḥ \|*  
*indrasenaḥ sutastasya vindhyāśvastasya cātmajaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*vindhyāśvānmithunaṃ jajñe menakāyāmiti śrutiḥ \|*  
*divodāsaśca rājarṣir ahalyā ca yaśasvinī \|\| 7 \|\|*

6-7. Mudgala begot the renowned Brahmishtha, the father of Indrasena, who begot Vindhyashva, the father of a pair of twins, called Divodasa and the daughter Ahilya, from his wife Menaka.

## \|\| 50.8 \|\|

*śaradvatastu dāyādam ahalyā samprasūyata \|*  
*śatānandamṛṣiśreṣṭhaṃ tasyāpi sumahātapāḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Ahilya begot the famous Rishi, Satananda, who was the son of Saradvana.

## \|\| 50.9 \|\|

*sutaḥ satyadhṛtirnāma dhanurvedasya pāragaḥ \|*  
*āsītsatyadhṛteḥ śukram amoghaṃ dhārmikasya tu \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Satananda begot Satyadhriti, who was a famous archer. He was the father of Amoghavirya.

## \|\| 50.10 \|\|

*skannaṃ retaḥ satyadhṛter dṛṣṭvā cāpsarasaṃ jale \|*  
*mithunaṃ tatra saṃbhṛtaṃ tasminsarasi saṃbhṛtam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. At the sight of a nymph, Satyadhriti cast his seed in a pool of water, out of which, one son and a daughter were horn.

## \|\| 50.11 \|\|

*tataḥ sarasi tasmiṃstu kramamāṇaṃ mahīpatiḥ \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā jagrāha kṛpayā śaṃtanurmṛgayāṃ gataḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. At the same time, King Shantanu chanced to go for a hunt and, seeing the babies, took pity on them and brought them with him

## \|\| 50.12 \|\|

*ete śaradvataḥ putrā ākhyātā gautamā varāḥ \|*  
*ata ūrdhvaṃ pravakṣyāmi divodāsasya vai prajāḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. All those sons of Sharadvana came to be known as Gautamas. Now the family of Divodasa will be narrated.

## \|\| 50.13-14 \|\|

*divodāsasya dāyādo dharmiṣṭho mitraurnṛpaḥ \|*  
*maitrāyaṇāvaraḥ so 'tha maitreyastu tataḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*ete vaṃśyā yateḥ pakṣāḥ kṣatropetāstu bhārgavāḥ \|*  
*rājā caidyavaro nāma maitreyasya sutaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

13-14. Mitrayu was the son of Divodasa, and he begot Maitreya, the founder of the family of Maitrayanas. They were all Kshatriyas, but became Bhargava Brahmanas, belonging to the gotra Yati. King Chaidyavara was the son of Maitreya.

## \|\| 50.15-18 \|\|

*atha caidyavarādvidvān sudāsastasya cātmajaḥ \|*  
*ajamīḍhaḥ punarjātaḥ kṣīṇe vaṃśe tu somakaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*somakasya suto jantur hate tasmiñchataṃ babhau \|*  
*putrāṇāmajamīḍhasya somakasya mahātmanaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*mahiṣī tv ajamīḍhasya dhūminī putravardhinī \|*  
*putrābhāve tapastepe śataṃ varṣāṇi duścaram \|\| 17 \|\|*

*hutvāgniṃ vidhivatsamyak pavitrīkṛtabhojanā \|*  
*agnihotrakrameṇaiva sā suṣvāpa mahāvratā \|\| 18 \|\|*

15-18. Chaidyavara became the father of the learned Sudasa, who begot Ajamidha the second, the father of Somaka, who begot Janta. From him, a hundred sons were born in the line of Ajamidha and Somaka.. When Somaka was killed, then Dhumini, the wife of Ajamidha, practiced most trying and rigid penances on the loss of her promising son. She went; to sleep, after duly performing Agnihotra and. finishing her meals.

## \|\| 50.19-21 \|\|

*tasyāṃ vai dhūmavarṇāyām ajamīḍhaḥ samīyivān \|*  
*ṛkṣaṃ sā janayāmāsa dhūmavarṇaṃ śatāgrajam \|\| 19 \|\|*

*ṛkṣātsaṃvaraṇo jajñe kuruḥ saṃvaraṇāt tataḥ \|*  
*yaḥ prayāgamatikramya kurukṣetramakalpayat \|\| 20 \|\|*

*kṛṣyatastu mahārājo varṣāṇi subahūnyatha \|*  
*kṛṣyamāṇastataḥ śakro bhayāttasmai varaṃ dadau \|\| 21 \|\|*

19-21. Ajamidha then enjoyed himself with Dhumini, when she begot smoke colored Riksha, the valiant. Riksha begot Samvarana, the father of Kuru, who forsaking Prayaga, built up Kurukshetra. He practiced long asceticism to call Indra, who at last appeared before him out of fear and granted him a boon.

## \|\| 50.22-23 \|\|

*puṇyaṃ ca ramaṇīyaṃ ca kurukṣetraṃ tu tatsmṛtam \|*  
*tasyānvavāyaḥ sumahān yasya nāmnā tu kauravāḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*kurostu dayitāḥ putrāḥ sudhanvā jahnureva ca \|*  
*parīkṣicca mahātejāḥ prajanaścārimardanaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

22-23. It is for this reason that Kurukshetra is so sacred. The family of Kuru multiplied; the members of which came to be known as the Kauravas. The five favourite sons of Kuru, viz., — Sudhanva, Jahnu, Parikshita, Prajana and Arimardana were all very pious and illustrious.

## \|\| 50.24-32 \|\|

*sudhanvanastu dāyādaḥ putro matimatāṃ varaḥ \|*  
*cyavanastasya putrastu rājā dharmārthatattvavit \|\| 24 \|\|*

*cyavanasya kṛmiḥ putra ṛkṣādjajñe mahātapāḥ \|*  
*kṛmeḥ putro mahāvīryaḥ khyātastvindrasamo vibhuḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*caidyoparicaro vīro vasurnāmāntarikṣagaḥ \|*  
*caidyoparicarādjajñe girikā sapta vai sutān \|\| 26 \|\|*

*mahāratho magadharāḍ viśruto yo bṛhadrathaḥ \|*  
*pratyaśravāḥ kuśaścaiva caturtho harivāhanaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

*pañcamaśca yajuścaiva matsyaḥ kālī ca saptamī \|*  
*bṛhadrathasya dāyādaḥ kuśāgro nāma viśrutaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

*kuśāgrasyātmajaścaiva vṛṣabho nāma vīryavān \|*  
*vṛṣabhasya tu dāyādaḥ puṇyavānnāma pārthivaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*puṇyaḥ puṇyavataścaiva rājā satyadhṛtistataḥ \|*  
*dāyādastasya dhanuṣas tasmātsarvaśca jajñivān \|\| 30 \|\|*

*sarvasya sambhavaḥ putras tasmādrājā bṛhadrathaḥ \|*  
*dve tasya śakale jāte jarayā saṃdhitaś ca saḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

*jarayā saṃdhito yasmāj jarāsaṃdhastataḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*jetā sarvasya kṣatrasya jarāsaṃdho mahābalaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

24-32. Sudhanva begot Chyavana, who was very learned, and he became the father of Riksha, who begot Krimi, the great ascetic, who was the father of Chaidyoparichara, also known as Vasu. ‘He was a remarkable warrior like Indra, and had the power of traversing the sky. He begot from Girika the following seven issues, named Maharatha, known also as Brihadratha, King of Magadha (Bihar); Pratishrava; Kusha; Harivahana; was the fourth; Yaju was the fifth; Matsya and a daughter, named Kali who was the seventh. Bribadratha was the father of Kushagra, who begot Vrishabha, the father of King Punyavana, who begot the King Punya, the father of Satyadhrita, who begot Dhanusha, the father of Sarva, who begot Sambhava, the father of the King Bribadratha, Brihadratha's son was born in two parts, which Jara joined together (Sandhita), who, on account of being joined by Jara, came to be known as Jarasandha. He was the conqueror of all the Kshatriyas.

## \|\| 50.33 \|\|

*jarāsaṃdhasya putrastu sahadevaḥ pratāpavān \|*  
*sahadevātmajaḥ śrīmān somavit sa mahātapāḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Jarasandha begot the illustrious Sahadeva, the father of the illustrious Somavi, who was a great ascetic. Sutashrava was the son o Somavi. Thus the Kings of Magadha have been described.

## \|\| 50.34-39 \|\|

*śrutaśravāstu somāder māgadhāḥ parikīrtitāḥ \|*  
*jahnustvajanayatputraṃ surathaṃ nāma bhūmipam \|\| 34 \|\|*

*surathasya tu dāyādo vīro rājā vidūrathaḥ \|*  
*vidūrathasutaścāpi sārvabhauma iti smṛtaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

*sārvabhaumādjayatseno rucirastasya cātmajaḥ \|*  
*rucirāttu tato bhaumas tvaritāustato 'bhavat \|\| 36 \|\|*

*akrodhanas tv āusutas tasmāddevātithiḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*devātithestu dāyādo dakṣa eva babhūva ha \|\| 37 \|\|*

*bhīmasenastato dakṣād dilīpas tasya cātmajaḥ \|*  
*dilīpasya pratīpastu tasya putrās trayaḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

*devāpiḥ śaṃtanuścaiva vāhlīkaścaiva te trayaḥ \|*  
*vāhlīkasya tu dāyādāḥ sapta vāhlīśvarā nṛpāḥ \|*  
*devāpistu hy apadhyātaḥ prajābhirabhavanmuniḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

34-39. King Jahnu was the father of the King Suratha, who begot Viduratha, the father of Sarvabhauma, who begot Jayatsena, the father of Ruchira, who begot Bhauma, the father of Tvaritayu, who begot Akrodhana, the father of Devatithi, who begot. Daksha, the father of Bhimasena, who begot Dilipa, the father of Pratipa, who was the father of three sons, viz., Devapi, Shantanu, Bahlika. Bahlika was the father of the seven sons, known as Bahlishvaras. Devapi, forsaken by his subjects turned a muni.

## \|\| 50.40 \|\|

*munaya ūcuḥ*  
*prajābhistu kimarthaṃ vai hy apadhyāto janeśvaraḥ \|*  
*ko doṣo rājaputrasya prajābhiḥ samudāhṛtaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. The Rishis asked: — Suta! Why was the King Devapi forsaken by his subjects. For what fault of his did the subjects not accept him?”

## \|\| 50.41 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*kilāsīdrājaputrastu kuṣṭhī taṃ nābhyapūjayan \|*  
*kāryaṃ caiva tu devānāṃ kṣatraṃ prati dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*bhaviṣyaṃ kīrtayiṣyāmi śaṃtanostu nibodhata \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Suta said: — That prince Devapi became a leper, and that is why he was forsaken by everybody. Now I will narrate the future family of Shantanu (as given in the Bhavishya Purana)

## \|\| 50.42-44 \|\|

*śaṃtanustvabhavadrājā vidvānsa vai mahābhiṣak \|*  
*idaṃ codāharantyatra ślokaṃ prati mahābhiṣak \|\| 42 \|\|*

*yaṃ yaṃ karābhyāṃ spṛśati jīrṇaṃ rogiṇameva ca \|*  
*punaryuvā ca bhavati tasmāttaṃ śaṃtanuṃ viduḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

*tattasya śaṃtanutvaṃ hi prajābhiriha kīrtyate \|*  
*tato 'vṛṇuta bhāryārthaṃ śaṃtanurjāhnavīṃ nṛpa \|\| 44 \|\|*

42-44. King Shantanu was a very learned physician, and was highly accomplished. It is laid down in the books on medicine that by his mere touch even the patient suffering from a most dreadful disease would be instantly cured and become young. He was for that reason “known as Shantanu, He married the sacred Ganges.

## \|\| 50.45-47 \|\|

*tasyāṃ devavrataṃ nāma kumāraṃ janayadvibhuḥ \|*  
*kālī vicitravīryaṃ tu dāśeyī janayatsutam \|\| 45 \|\|*

*śaṃtanordayitaṃ putraṃ śāntātmānamakalmaṣam \|*  
*kṛṣṇadvaipāyano nāma kṣetre vaicitraviryake \|\| 46 \|\|*

*dhṛtarāṣṭraṃ ca pāṇḍuṃ ca viduraṃ cāpyajījanat \|*  
*dhṛtarāṣṭrastu gāndhāryāṃ putrānajanayacchatam \|\| 47 \|\|*

45-47. Shantanu begot, from Jahnavi, the famous Devavrata; and from his second wife, Satyavati, the daughter of a fisherman, he begot Kali and Vichitravirya. The favourite and sinless son of Shantanu, namely, Vichitravirya, had died childless, and, consequently, Krishna Dvaipayana was appointed to produce a son on the widow of Vichitravirya. He, thus begot one hundred sons, named Dhritarashtra, Pandu, and Vidura, Dhritarashtra begot one Hundred sons, from Gandhari

## \|\| 50.48 \|\|

*teṣāṃ duryodhanaḥ śreṣṭhaḥ sarvakṣatrasya vai prabhuḥ \|*  
*mādrī kuntī tathā caiva pāṇḍorbhārye babhūvatuḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Of his hundred sons Duryodhana was the most remarkable. Panda has Kunti and Madri as his wives

## \|\| 50.49-50 \|\|

*devadattāḥ sutāḥ pañca pāṇḍorarthe 'bhijajñire \|*  
*dharmādyudhiṣṭhiro jajñe mārutācca vṛkodaraḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

*indrāddhanaṃjayaścaiva indratulyaparākramaḥ \|*  
*nakulaṃ sahadevaṃ ca mādryaśvibhyāmajījanat \|\| 50 \|\|*

49-50. Then Pandu became the father of the five sons, given to him by the Doss, biz, Yudhisthira, from Dharma; Bhima, from Vayu, Arjuna, from Indra, From his second wife, Madi, Pandu got Nakula and Sahadeva, through the two gods Ashwini

## \|\| 50.51-56 \|\|

*pañcaite pāṇḍavebhyastu draupadyāṃ jajñire sutāḥ \|*  
*draupadyajanayacchreṣṭhaṃ prativindhyaṃ udhiṣṭhirāt \|\| 51 \|\|*

*śrutasenaṃ bhīmasenāc chrutakīrtiṃ dhanaṃjayāt \|*  
*caturthaṃ śrutakarmāṇaṃ sahadevād ajāyata \|\| 52 \|\|*

*nakulācca śatānīkaṃ draupadeyāḥ prakīrtitāḥ \|*  
*tebhyo 'pare pāṇḍaveyāḥ ṣaḍevānye mahārathāḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

*haiḍambo bhīmasenāttu putro jajñe ghaṭotkacaḥ \|*  
*kāśī baladharādbhīmāj jajñe vai sarvagaṃ sutam \|\| 54 \|\|*

*suhotraṃ tanayaṃ mādrī sahadevādasūyata \|*  
*kareṇumatyāṃ caidyāyāṃ niramitrastu nākuliḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

*subhadrāyāṃ rathī pārthād abhimanyurajāyata \|*  
*yaudheyaṃ devakī caiva putraṃ jajñe udhiṣṭhirāt \|\| 56 \|\|*

51-56. The five sons of Pandu had Draupadi, as their common wife, from whom Yudhisthira begot Prativindhya, Bhima: begot Shrutasena, Arjuna, begot Shrutakirti, Sahadeva begot Shruta Karma and Nakula begot Shatanika, Thus Draupadi begot those five sous to the Pandavas, and they are known as Draupadeyas. The five Pandavas also begot another half a dozen sons, in addition to those five born of Draupadi. They are known as Pandaveyas to distinguish them from Draupadeyas, Thus, Bhima begot from the Asura girl Hidamba, a son, called Ghatotkacha and Sarvaga from Kashi; Sahadeva begot Suhotra from his wife Madri; and Nakula from Karenumati begot Niramitra. Arjuna begot from Subhadra, Abhimanyu, and Yudhisthira begot a son, named Yaudheya, from Devaki.

## \|\| 50.57-59 \|\|

*abhimanyoḥ parīkṣittu putraḥ parapurajayaḥ \|*  
*janamejayaḥ parīkṣitaḥ putraḥ paramadhārmikaḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

*brahmāṇaṃ kalpayāmāsa sa vai vājasaneyakam \|*  
*sa vaiśampāyanenaiva śaptaḥ kila maharṣiṇā \|\| 58 \|\|*

*na sthāsyatīha durbuddhe tavaitadvacanaṃ bhuvi \|*  
*yāvatsthāsyasi tvaṃ loke tāvadeva prapatsyati \|\| 59 \|\|*

57-59. Parikshit, the conqueror of enemies’ towns, was the son of Abhimanyu, and he became the father of Janamejaya, the Pious. When Janamejaya favored Rishi Yajnavalkya, whom he appointed as his Brahma priest at the Sacrifice. then the sage Vaishampayana cursed him to the effect: “The innovations introduced by you O man of perverted intelligence, will not be respected. ‘They will be honored only so long as thou wilt remain on earth?

## \|\| 50.60-61 \|\|

*kṣatrasya vijayaṃ jñātvā tataḥprabhṛti sarvaśaḥ \|*  
*abhigamya sthitāścaiva nṛpaṃ ca janamejayam \|\| 60 \|\|*

*tataḥprabhṛti śāpena kṣatriyasya tu yājinaḥ \|*  
*utsannā yājino yajñe tataḥprabhṛti sarvaśaḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

60-61. Thus all the subjects, seeing the Victory of Kshatriyas over the Brahmanas, flocked round the King Janamejaya. From that day’s curse the priests officiating at sacrifices performed by Kshatriyas began to decline and refused to attend on occasions of their sacrifices.

## \|\| 50.62-64 \|\|

*kṣatrasya yājinaḥ kecic chāpāttasya mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*paurṇamāsena haviṣā iṣṭvā tasminprajāpatim \|*  
*sa vaiśampāyanenaiva praviśanvāritastataḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

*parīkṣitaḥ suto 'sau vai pauravo janamejayaḥ \|*  
*dvir aśvamedhamāhṛtya mahāvājasaneyakaḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

*pravartayitvā taṃ sarvam ṛṣiṃ vājasaneyakam \|*  
*vivāde brāhmaṇaiḥ sārdham abhiśapto vanaṃ yayau \|\| 64 \|\|*

62-64. When, after finishing the sacrifice of Prajapati, on a full-moon day, Janamejaya was entering the hall of Sacrifice, he was prevented from doing s0, by Vaishampayana, but the former did not heed him. On the contrary, Janamejaya, the son of Parikshit, after performing two Ashvamedha sacrifices, became a great Vajasaneyaka, and went to the forest on account of his being cursed for entering into hostility with the Brahmanas.

## \|\| 50.65-66 \|\|

*janamejayācchatānīkas tasmādjajñe sa vīryavān \|*  
*janamejayaḥ śatānīkaṃ putraṃ rājye 'bhiṣiktavān \|\| 65 \|\|*

*athāśvamedhena tataḥ śatānīkasya vīryavān \|*  
*jajñe 'dhisomakṛṣṇākhyaḥ sāmprataṃ yo mahāyaśāḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

65-66. Shatanika, the son of Janamejaya, was very valiant; and he was anointed and proclaimed king by Janamejaya; Shatanika begot the most illustrious Adhisoma Krishna, by performing ashvamedha sacrifice.

## \|\| 50.67 \|\|

*tasmiñchāsati rāṣṭraṃ tu uṣmābhiridamāhṛtam \|*  
*durāpaṃ dīrghasattraṃ vai trīṇi varṣāṇi puṣkare \|*  
*varṣadvayaṃ kurukṣetre dṛṣadvatyāṃ dvijottamāḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. Suta said: — Rishis! This Adhisoma Krishna is reigning now; and it is in his reign that you have engaged in this big sacrificial session, of which three years have passed in Pushkara and two years. in Kurukshetra and Drishadvati.

## \|\| 50.68-71 \|\|

*munaya ūcuḥ*  
*bhaviṣyaṃ śrotumicchāmaḥ prajānāṃ lomaharṣaṇe \|*  
*purā kila yadetadvai vyatītaṃ kīrtitaṃ tvayā \|\| 68 \|\|*

*yeṣu vai sthāsyate kṣatram utpatsyante nṛpāśca ye \|*  
*teṣām āuṣpramāṇaṃ ca nāmataścaiva tānnṛpān \|\| 69 \|\|*

*kṛtaugapramāṇaṃ ca tretādvāparayostathā \|*  
*kaliugapramāṇaṃ ca ugadoṣaṃ ugakṣayam \|\| 70 \|\|*

*sukhaduḥkhapramāṇaṃ ca prajādoṣaṃ ugasya tu \|*  
*etatsarvaṃ prasaṃkhyāya pṛcchatāṃ brūhi naḥ prabho \|\| 71 \|\|*

68-71. The Rishis said: — Suta! all this is past history now. We wish to hear something about the future kings. Pray tell us about the kings who will be the rulers of the land. Be pleased to tell us their names and duration of their reigns; please also tell us the extent of Satya, Treta, Dvapara and Kaliyugas, and also explain to us about the prosperity, adversity and vices of those ages.

## \|\| 50.72-73 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*yathā me kīrtitaṃ pūrvaṃ vyāsenākliṣṭakarmaṇā \|*  
*bhāvyaṃ kaliugaṃ caiva tathā manvantarāṇi ca \|\| 72 \|\|*

*anāgatāni sarvāṇi bruvato me nibodhata \|*  
*ata ūrdhvaṃ pravakṣyāmi bhaviṣyā ye nṛpāstathā \|\| 73 \|\|*

72-73. Suta said: — Rishis! listen, while I narrate all which have not yet Come to pass, as told to me by Vyasa, of untiring energy, both with regard to the future Kaliyuga and the Manvantaras. After that, I shall tell you of the future kings

## \|\| 50.74 \|\|

*aiḍekṣvākvanvaye caiva paurave cānvaye tathā \|*  
*yeṣu saṃsthāsyate tacca aiḍekṣvākukulaṃ śubham \|*  
*tānsarvānkīrtayiṣyāmi bhaviṣye kathitānnṛpān \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. I shall narrate the kings who are to be in the families of Aila and Ikshvaku, as well as in the family of Paurava, among whom, the auspicious stock of the Aila and Ikshvaku families was established. All that I shall declare, as mentioned in the Bhavishya \[Purana\].

## \|\| 50.75-76 \|\|

*tebhyo 'pare 'pi ye tv anye hy utpatsyante nṛpāḥ punaḥ \|*  
*kṣatrāḥ pāraśavāḥ śūdrās tathānye ye bahiścarāḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

*andhāḥ śakāḥ pulindāśca cūlikā yavanāstathā \|*  
*kaivartābhīraśabarā ye cānye mlecchasambhavāḥ \|*  
*paryāyataḥ pravakṣyāmi nāmataścaiva tānnṛpān \|\| 76 \|\|*

75-76. Besides these, other kings will also arise, belonging to the castes of Kshatras, Parashavas, and Shudras as well as those who are outside these \[foreigners\]; namely, Audhras, Sakes, Pulindas, Chulikas, Yavanas, Kaivartas, Abhiras and Shabaras, and those having a Mlechchha origin. I shall declare! those kings, according ‘to their succession and by name.

**Комментарий:**

Notes: According to Mr. Pargiter, these lines follow after the words “ Mlechcha origin” viz., Pauravas, Vitihotras, Vaidishas, five (Panchalas?) Kosalas, Mekalas, Kosalas, Paundras dad Svasphrakas, Sunidharmas, Sakas, Nipas.”

## \|\| 50.77 \|\|

*adhisomakṛṣṇaś caiteṣāṃ prathamaṃ vartate nṛpaḥ \|*  
*tasyānvavāye vakṣyāmi bhaviṣye kathitānnṛpān \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. Adhisoma Krishna is the first king, and I shall first relate to you his dyhasty, as told in the Bhavishya \[Purana\].

## \|\| 50.78-79 \|\|

*adhisomakṛṣṇaputrastu vivakṣurbhavitā nṛpaḥ \|*  
*gaṅgayā tu hṛte tasmin nagare nāgasāhvaye \|\| 78 \|\|*

*tyaktvā vivakṣurnagaraṃ kauśāmbyāṃ tu nivatsyati \|*  
*bhaviṣyāṣṭau sutāstasya mahābalaparākramāḥ \|\| 79 \|\|*

78-79. Adhisoma Krishna shall have Vivakshu for his son, and after Hastinapura is’ washed away by the Ganges, the latter shall make Kaushambi his capital and he shall be the father of eight powerful sons.

## \|\| 50.80-85 \|\|

*bhūrirjyeṣṭhaḥ sutastasya tasya citrarathaḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*śucidravaścitrarathād vṛṣṇimāṃśca śucidravāt \|\| 80 \|\|*

*vṛṣṇimataḥ suṣeṇaśca bhaviṣyati śucirnṛpaḥ \|*  
*tasmātsuṣeṇādbhavitā sunītho nāma pārthivaḥ \|\| 81 \|\|*

*nṛpātsunīthādbhavitā nṛcakṣuḥ sumahāyaśāḥ \|*  
*nṛcakṣuṣastu dāyādo bhavitā vai sukhīvalaḥ \|\| 82 \|\|*

*sukhīvalasutaścāpi bhāvī rājā pariṣṇavaḥ \|*  
*pariṣṇavasutaścāpi bhavitā sutapā nṛpaḥ \|\| 83 \|\|*

*medhāvī tasya dāyādo bhaviṣyati na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*medhāvinaḥ sutaścāpi bhaviṣyati puraṃjayaḥ \|\| 84 \|\|*

*urvo bhāvyaḥ sutastasya tigmātmā tasya cātmajaḥ \|*  
*tigmādbṛhadratho bhāvyo vasudāmā bṛhadrathāt \|\| 85 \|\|*

80-85. Bhuri will be the eldest and shall beget Chitraratha, the father of Suchidrava, who shall beget Vrishniman, the father of King Sushena, who shall beget Sunitha, (the father of Rucha, who will be) the father of Nrichakshu, who shall beget Sukhibala, the father of Parishnava, who will, beget Sutapa, the father of Madhavi; and Puranjaya will be the son of the latter, and the father of Urva, who shall beget Tigmatma, the father of Brihadratha, who shall beget Vasudama.

## \|\| 50.86 \|\|

*vasudāmnaḥ śatānīko bhaviṣyodayanastataḥ \|*  
*bhaviṣyate codayanād vīge rājā vahīnaraḥ \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. Vasudama will be the father of Shatanika, who will beget Udayana, the father of the brave Vahinara.

## \|\| 50.87-88 \|\|

*vahīnarātmajaścaiva daṇḍapāṇirbhaviṣyati \|*  
*daṇḍapāṇerniramitro niramitrāttu kṣemakaḥ \|\| 87 \|\|*

*atrānuvaṃśaśloko 'yaṃ gīto vipraiḥ purātanaiḥ \|*  
*brahmakṣatrasya yo yonir vaṃśo devarṣisatkṛtaḥ \|*  
*kṣemakaṃ prāpya rājānaṃ saṃsthāsyati kalau uge \|\| 88 \|\|*

87-88. Dandapani will be the son of Vahinara and the father of Niramitra, who shall beget Kshemaka. The following shloka has been sung by the ancient prophets: — The source of Brahma-Kshatra stock the family honored by Devarshis, will come to conclusion in the Kali age, when it reaches King Kshemaka.”

## \|\| 50.89 \|\|

*ityeṣa pauravo vaṃśo yathāvadiha kīrtitaḥ \|*  
*dhīmataḥ pāṇḍuputrasya cārjunasya mahātmanaḥ \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. Suta said: — Rishis! I have narrated to you this dynasty of Pauravas who descended from Arjuna, the son of Pandu.

## Chapter 51
