## \|\| 51.1 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ*  
*ye pūjyāḥ syur dvijātīnām agnayaḥ sūta sarvadā \|*  
*tānidānīṃ samācakṣva tadvaṃśaṃ cānupūrvaśaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. The Rishis. — O! Sita! Pray tell us about those Agni’s or Fires which are honored amongst the twice-born, and narrate the history of the descendants of that dynasty in detail.

## \|\| 51.2-3 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*yo 'sāv agnirabhīmānī smṛtaḥ svāyambhuve 'ntare \|*  
*brahmaṇo mānasaḥ putras tasmātsvāhā vyajījanat \|\| 2 \|\|*

*pāvakaṃ pavamānaṃ ca śuciragniśca yaḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*nirmathyaḥ pavamāno 'gnir vaidyutaḥ pāvakātmajaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

2-3. Suta. — Rishis! In Svayambhuva Manvantara, Agni Abhimani (the presiding spirit of Fire), was born from the mind of Brahma, and Svaha was his wife. She gave birth to Pavaka (Subterranean), Pavamana (Terrestrial) and Suchi (Celestial) Fires. Pavamana or Terrestrial Fire is produced by friction, and Pavaka (Subterranean) Fire produces the magnetic fire, called Vidyuta.

## \|\| 51.4 \|\|

*śuciragniḥ smṛtaḥ sauraḥ sthāvarāścaiva te smṛtāḥ \|*  
*pavamānātmajo hy agnir havyavāhaḥ sa ucyate \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Suchi is also called Saura (Solar or Celestial Fire). These fires are known as Sthavaras or Fixed Fires. Havyavaha is. the son of Pavamana.

## \|\| 51.5 \|\|

*pāvakaḥ saharakṣastu havyavāhamukhaḥ śuciḥ \|*  
*devānāṃ havyavāho 'gniḥ prathamo brahmaṇaḥ sutaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Pavaki, Saharaksha and Havyavahamukha are sons of Pavaka, Pavamana and Suchi respectively. The Havyavahamukha Agni is sacred to the Devas, and the first-born of Brahma (Pavamana) is the Fire sacred to men

## \|\| 51.6 \|\|

*saharakṣaḥ surāṇāṃ tu trayāṇāṃ te trayo 'gnayaḥ \|*  
*eteṣāṃ putrapautrāśca catvāriṃśattathaiva ca \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Saharaksha is the Agni sacred to the Asuras. These three Fires belong to the three classes. Their sons and grandsons number forty.

## \|\| 51.7-9 \|\|

*pravakṣye nāmatastānvai pravibhāgena tānpṛthak \|*  
*pāvano laukiko hy agniḥ prathamo brahmaṇaśca yaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*brahmaudanāgnis tatputro bharato nāma viśrutaḥ \|*  
*vaiśvānaro havyavāho vahanhavyaṃ mamāra saḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*sa mṛto 'tharvaṇaḥ putro mathitaḥ puṣkarodadhiḥ \|*  
*yo 'tharvā laukiko hy agnir dakṣiṇāgniḥ sa ucyate \|\| 9 \|\|*

7-9. They are now described and named separately. Pavana (Pavamana), the Fire of human beings (Laukika), is the first-begotten of Brahma, and Brahmanandana known also as Bharata, was the son of Pavamana. Havyavaha is also known as Vaishvanara Agni. He died while carrying Havya offerings to the Gods. He being dead, the son of Atharvan (Angirasa) produced the Fire Pushkarodadhi (produced by the churning the cloud), which is known as Atharva Alaukika Agni and also as Dakshina Agni, by nonrubbing.

## \|\| 51.10 \|\|

*bhṛgoḥ prajāyatātharvā hy aṅgirātharvaṇaḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*tasya hy alaukiko hy agnir dakṣiṇāgniḥ sa vai smṛtaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Atharvan was begotten from Bhrigu, and Angiras was the son of Atharvan, who begot the above-mentioned Alaukika Dakshina Agni.

## \|\| 51.11 \|\|

*atha yaḥ pavamānastu nirmathyo 'gniḥ sa ucyate \|*  
*sa ca vai gārhapatyo 'gniḥ prathamo brahmaṇaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Pavamana is called Nirmathya Agni, also produced. by (rubbing fire sticks or) any friction, and the same is known as Garhapatya Agni or Household Fire, the first fire amongst the Brahmanas.

## \|\| 51.12 \|\|

*tataḥ sabhyāvasathyau ca saṃśatyās tau sutāvubhau \|*  
*tataḥ ṣoḍaśa nadyastu cakame havyavāhanaḥ \|*  
*yaḥ khalvāhavanīyo 'gnir abhimānī dvijaiḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. He produced, from Samshati, two sons, named Sabhya and Avasathya, than Havyavahana was enamoured of sixteen rivers. The-twice born call this Agni Abhimani Ahavaniya Fire also.

## \|\| 51.13-16 \|\|

*kāverīṃ kṛṣṇaveṇīṃ ca narmadāṃ yamunāṃ tathā \|*  
*godāvarīṃ vitastāṃ ca candrabhāgāmirāvatīm \|\| 13 \|\|*

*vipāśāṃ kauśikīṃ caiva śatadruṃ sarayūṃ tathā \|*  
*sītāṃ manasvinīṃ caiva hrādinīṃ pāvanāṃ tathā \|\| 14 \|\|*

*tāsu ṣoḍaśadhātmānaṃ pravibhajya pṛthakpṛthak \|*  
*tadā tu viharaṃstāsu dhiṣṇyecchaḥ sa babhūva ha \|\| 15 \|\|*

*svābhidhānasthitā dhiṣṇyās tāsūtpannāśca dhiṣṇavaḥ \|*  
*dhiṣṇyeṣu jajñire yasmāt tataste dhiṣṇavaḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

13-16. The sixteen above-mentioned rivers are: — Kaveri, Krishnaveni, Narmada, Yamuna, Godavari, Vitasta, Chandrabhaga, Irivati, Vipasha, Kaushiki, Shatadru, Sarayu, Sita, Manasvini, Hradini and Pavana.

After dividing his body into sixteen different parts, he dallied with these sixteen river-goddesses, when he was attracted towards Dhishnyas. Produced from these Dhishnyas was the progeny known as Dhishnus since they were the sons of Dhishnyas, they are called Dhishnus.

## \|\| 51.17-18 \|\|

*ityete vai nadīputrā dhiṣṇyeṣu pratipedire \|*  
*teṣāṃ viharaṇīyā ye upastheyāśca tāñśṛṇu \|*  
*vibhuḥ pravāhaṇo 'gnīdhras tatrasthā dhiṣṇavo 'pare \|\| 17 \|\|*

*viharati yathāsthānaṃ puṇyāhe samupakrame \|*  
*anirdeśyānivāryāṇām agnīnāṃ śṛṇuta kramam \|\| 18 \|\|*

17-18. All the sons of the rivers made friends with these Dhishnyas, Listen now about the Viharaniyas (those which are removable from the altar) and Upastheyas (those which are fixed in their places and worshipped there), amongst then. Vibhu, Pravahana and Agnidhra are fixed in their altars, while the remaining Dhishnus are shifting and moving, and taken from their places when some auspicious occasions arise. Hear the names of Anirdeshya and Anvarya Agnis, in order.

## \|\| 51.19 \|\|

*vāsavo 'gniḥ kṛśānuryo dvitīyottaravedikaḥ \|*  
*samrāḍagnisuto hyaṣṭāv upatiṣṭhanti tāndvijāḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Vasava and Krishanu are both the Agnis of Dvitiya and Uttara veda (altars). Samrat was the son of Agni, and the Brahmands worship these eight Fires.

## \|\| 51.20 \|\|

*parjanyaḥ pavamānastu dvitīyaḥ so 'nudṛṣyate \|*  
*pāvakoṣṇaḥ samūhyastu vottare so 'gnirucyate \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Parjaniya and Pavamana are also Agnis and are seen on the Dvitiya altar. Pavakoshna and Samuhya are the Agnis found in the North or uttara altar.

## \|\| 51.21-22 \|\|

*havyasūdo hy asaṃmṛjyaḥ śāmitraḥ sa vibhāvyate \|*  
*śatadhāmā sudhājyotī raudraiśvaryaḥ sa ucyate \|\| 21 \|\|*

*brahmajyotir vasudhāmā brahmasthānīya ucyate \|*  
*ajaikapādupastheyaḥ sa vai śālāmukho yataḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

21-22. Havyasuda and Asamrijya are both known as Shamitra. Shatadhama and Sudhajyoti are described as Raudraishvarya agnis. Brahmajyoti and Vasudhama are said to be Brahmasthaniya. The Upastheya Agni by Ajekapada is known to be Salamukha.

## \|\| 51.23 \|\|

*anirdeśyo hyahirbudhnyo bahirante tu dakṣiṇau \|*  
*putrā hyete tu sarvasya upastheyā dvijaiḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Anirdeshya and Ahirbudhnya are carried to the south. The Brahmanas say that these Upastheya Agnis should be worshipped by all.

**Комментарий:**

Dhishya. — A sort of, subordinate or side altar, generally a heap of earth, covered with ‘sand, on which the fire is placed, and of which 8 are enumerated, viz., besides the agnidhriya \[in the Agnidhra\], those in the Sadas. belonging to the Hotri, the Maitravaruna or Pra-tashtri, the Brahmanachchansin, the Potri, Nestri, and Achcha-vaka and the Marjaliya, (Monier-Williams’ Sanskrit-English Dictionary.)

## \|\| 51.24 \|\|

*tato viharaṇīyāṃstu vakṣyāmyaṣṭau tu tānsutān \|*  
*hautriyasya suto hyagnir barhiṣo havyavāhanaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Now I shall describe the Viharaniyas and their eight sons. Barhisha Agni, the carrier of sacrifice, was the son of Hotriya

## \|\| 51.25 \|\|

*praśaṃsyo 'gniḥ pracetāstu dvitīyaḥ saṃsahāyakaḥ \|*  
*suto hyagner viśvavedā brāhmaṇācchaṃsirucyate \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Pracheta Agni is the son of Prashamsya. He is the second Agni. Samsahayaka Vishveveda is the son of Agni, called Brahmana chamshi.

## \|\| 51.26 \|\|

*apāṃ yoniḥ smṛtaḥ svāmbhaḥ seturnāma vibhāvyate \|*  
*dhiṣṇya āharaṇā hyete somenejyanta vai dvijaiḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Svambha Agni is described having its origin in the waters. His name is Setu. These Dhishnya Aharana (shifting) Agnis are worshipped along with the Soma in the Soma sacrifice by Brahmanas.

## \|\| 51.27 \|\|

*tato yaḥ pāvako nāmnā yaḥ sadbhiryoga ucyate \|*  
*agniḥ so 'vabhṛtho jñeyo varuṇena sahejyate \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. The good call Pavaka Agni to be Yoga, and that Agnis are worshipped along with Varuna at the time of purificatory bath.

## \|\| 51.28 \|\|

*hṛdayasya suto hyagner jaṭhare 'sau nṛṇāṃ pacan \|*  
*manyumāñjaṭharaścāgnir viddhāgniḥ satataṃ smṛtaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Agni, the son of Hridaya, that digests the food, is known as Manyuman, Jatharagni, and Vidhagni.

## \|\| 51.29 \|\|

*parasparotthito hyagnir bhūtānīha vibhurdahan \|*  
*agnermanyumataḥ putro ghoraḥ saṃvartakaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. The Agni that is produced spontaneously by friction and consumes all beings, is the son of the Agni Manyuman, called Ghorasamvartaka.

## \|\| 51.31 \|\|

*saharakṣastu vai kāmān gṛhe sa vasate nṛṇām \|*  
*kravyādagniḥ sutastasya puruṣānyo 'tti vai mṛtān \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. This Agni dwells in the ocean, drinking water, in the mouth of Vadava (? oceanic volcano), and the son of Samudravasi (oceanic fire) is Saharaksha Agni resides in the houses of the people, and fulfills their desires. Kravyada Agni, the son of Saharaksha, devours the dead (i.e, the funeral fire).

## \|\| 51.33 \|\|

*mathito yastvaraṇyāṃ tu so 'gnirāpa samindhanam \|*  
*āur nāmnā tu bhagavān paśau yastu praṇīyate \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. These are the sons of Pavaka Agni, as related by the Brahmanas, Their sons, through Sauvirya, were stolen by the Gandharvas and the Agni obtained by the rubbing of Arani went to dwell in the sacrificial fuel. This fire is called Lord Ayu, in which sacrificial victims are immolated.

## \|\| 51.34-35 \|\|

*āuṣo mahimānputro dahanastu tataḥ sutaḥ \|*  
*pākayajñeṣv abhīmānī hutaṃ havyaṃ bhunakti yaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

*sarvasmāddevalokācca havyaṃ kavyaṃ bhunakti yaḥ \|*  
*putro 'sya sahito hyagnir adbhutaḥ sa mahāyaśāḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

34-35. Ayu begot Mahimana, the father of Dahana. This Dahana is the presiding Fire in Pakayajna domestic sacrifices, and eats the fire oblations made into it; and it eats also offerings made to the Devas and the pitris.

His son is Sahita Adbhuta, who is very celebrated.

## \|\| 51.37 \|\|

*vividhāgnistatastasya tasya putro mahākaviḥ \|*  
*vividhāgnisutādarkād agnayo 'ṣṭau sutāḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. He eats the offerings, &c., made at Prayashchitta (atonement). He (Adbhuta) is the father of a portion of the heroic Devamsha, known as Vividhagni was born of the Vira Devamsha, who begot Mahakavi. Arka, the second son of Vividhagni, begot eight sons.

## \|\| 51.38-39 \|\|

*kāmyāsviṣṭiṣvabhīmānī rakṣohāyatikṛcca yaḥ \|*  
*surabhirvasumānnādo haryaśvaścaiva rukmavān \|\| 38 \|\|*

*pravargyaḥ kṣemavāṃścaiva ityaṣṭau ca prakīrtitāḥ \|*  
*śucyagnestu prajā hyeṣā agnayaśca caturdaśa \|\| 39 \|\|*

38-39. He who is known as Rakshohayatikrit is the presiding deity all Kamya sacrifices. The second son is Surabhi (the fifth); Rukmavan (the sixth); Vasuman (the third), Aunada (the fourth), Haryashva (the fifth) Pravargya (the seventh), and lastly Kshemavana (the eighth), and including the progeny of Suchi Agni, these are fourteen.

## \|\| 51.40 \|\|

*ityete hyagnayaḥ proktāḥ praṇītā ye hi cādhvare \|*  
*samatīte tu sarge ye yāmaiḥ saha surottamaiḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Thus have been described the Fires, which were employed in sacrifice in previous. world periods by the Devas, along with the Yamas (a class of gods).

## \|\| 51.41 \|\|

*svāyambhuve 'ntare pūrvam agnayaste 'bhimāninaḥ \|*  
*ete viharaṇīyeṣu cetanācetaneṣviha \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. These Agnis were the presiding deities of sacrifices in Svaymbhuva Manvantara. Now, these are subsidiary fires, shifting from one altar to another and roaming among animate and inanimate beings.

## \|\| 51.42 \|\|

*sthānābhimānino 'gnīdhrāḥ prāgāsanhavyavāhanāḥ \|*  
*kāmyanaimittikādyāste ye te karmasvavasthitāḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. They were the presiding’ deities of altars and were known as Agnidhra Fires in ancient times, and were then carriers of sacrificial offerings, and were employed in those days, and may be employed in present days in voluntary (Kamya) and occasional (naimittika) rites.

## \|\| 51.43 \|\|

*pūrve manvantare 'tīte śukrairyāmaiśca taiḥ saha \|*  
*ete devagaṇaiḥ sārdhaṃ prathamasyāntare manoḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. They were worshipped in the first Manvantara by Shukras, Yamas and Devas.

## \|\| 51.44 \|\|

*ityetā yonayo hyaktāḥ sthānākhyā jātavedasām \|*  
*svārociṣādiṣu jñeyāḥ savarṇānteṣu saptasu \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Thus have been described the altars and the sources of the various Fires; they should be known as existing in the seven. Manvantaras, beginning with Svarochis and ending with Savarna

## \|\| 51.45 \|\|

*tairevaṃ tu prasaṃkhyātaṃ sāmpratānāgateṣviha \|*  
*manvantareṣu sarveṣu lakṣaṇaṃ jātavedasām \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Thus have been described the Agnis of the past Manvantaras. Now will be described the characteristic marks of the Fires to be worshipped in the present and the future Manvantaras.

## \|\| 51.46 \|\|

*manvantareṣu sarveṣu nānārūpaprayojanaiḥ \|*  
*vartante vartamānaiśca yāmairdevaiḥ sahāgnayaḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. In all Manvantaras, these Fires, along with Yamas and Devas, make their appearance in various forms and for diverse objects.

## \|\| 51.47 \|\|

*anāgataiḥ suraiḥ sārdhaṃ vatsyanto 'nāgatāstvatha \|*  
*ityeṣa pracayo 'gnīnāṃ mayā prokto yathākramam \|*  
*vistareṇānupūrvyā ca kimanyacchrotumicchatha \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. These Fires live along with future Devas; and thus I have described the Past Agnis; what more do you wish to hear now, O Rishis.

## Chapter 52

## \|\| 52.1 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ*  
*idānīṃ prāha yadviṣṇuḥ pṛṣṭaḥ paramamuttamam \|*  
*tadidānīṃ samācakṣva dharmādharmasya vistaram \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. The Rishis said: — “Suta! Be good enough to relate to us the difference between Virtue (Dharma) and Vice (Adharma) In detail, as explained by the Lord Vishnu, at the respectful enquiries of the King Vaivasvata Manu.

## \|\| 52.2-3 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*evamekārṇave tasmin matsyarūpī janārdanaḥ \|*  
*vistāramādisargasya pratisargasya cākhilam \|\| 2 \|\|*

*kathayāmāsa viśvātmā manave sūryasūnave \|*  
*karmayogaṃ ca sāṃkhyaṃ ca yathāvadvistarānvitam \|\| 3 \|\|*

2-3. Suta — “Rishis! Lord Janardana, in the form of Fish, has explained at length Karma Yoga and Sankhya Yoga to Manu, the most illustrious son of the Sun, at the time when the world was a vast sheet of water.

He explained them at length the first creation and the destruction of the World”.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — Karma Yoga = Performance of wordly and religious rites. Sankhya here means Jana Yoga, as opposed to Karma Yoga.

## \|\| 52.4 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ*  
*śrotumicchāmahe sūta karmayogasya lakṣaṇam \|*  
*yasmādaviditaṃ loke na kiṃcittava suvrata \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Hearing those words of the sage, the Rishis cried out: — Suta! We are also most eager to understand the characteristics of Karma Yoga, because, Oh Pious Suta, there is nothing concealed from you in this world, and you are the knower of all”.

## \|\| 52.5-6 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*karmayogaṃ ca vakṣyāmi yathā viṣṇuvibhāṣitam \|*  
*jñānayogasahasrāddhi karmayogaḥ praśasyate \|\| 5 \|\|*

*karmayogodbhavaṃ jñānaṃ tasmāttatparamaṃ padam \|*  
*karmajñānodbhavaṃ brahma na ca jñānamakarmaṇaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. Suta: — Rishis! I repeat the Karma Yoga, as taught by Vishnu. Karma Yoga is superior to a thousand Jnana Yogis, because Jnana Yoga is produced by Karma Yoga, and from Jnana Yoga, one attains the final emancipation. The divine knowledge of Brahma springs from Karma Yoga and Java combined. Jnana Yoga in its turn does not arise without Karma Yoga.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — Jnana Yoga = contemplation. Akarma Jnana = Renunciation.

## \|\| 52.7 \|\|

*tasmātkarmaṇi uktātmā tattvamāpnoti śāśvatam \|*  
*vedo 'khilo dharmamūlam ācāraścaiva tadvidām \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Consequently a person devoted to Karma Yoga attains to eternal Truth. The entire Veda is the fountain-head of all Dharma; so also the conduct of those good men who know the Vedas is also a root from which Dharma arises.

## \|\| 52.8-10 \|\|

*aṣṭāvātmaguṇās tasmin pradhānatvena saṃsthitāḥ \|*  
*dayā sarveṣu bhūteṣu kṣāntī rakṣāturasya tu \|\| 8 \|\|*

*anasūyā tathā loke śaucamantarbahirdvijāḥ \|*  
*anāyāseṣu kāryeṣu māṅgalyācārasevanam \|\| 9 \|\|*

*na ca dravyeṣu kārpaṇyam ārteṣūpārjiteṣu ca \|*  
*tathāspṛhā paradravye parastrīṣu ca sarvadā \|\| 10 \|\|*

8-10. The eight spiritual qualities must exist in pre-eminence, in order to produce “Dharma: — They are, — (1) Clemency to all living beings, (2) forbearance, (3) protection of him who seeks aid in distress, (4) freedom from envy in the world, (5) external and internal purification, (6) to calmly meet sudden emergencies in all works, (7) not to exercise niggardliness in the case of the distressed and with regard to one’s earnings, (8) not to hanker after the riches or the wives of others

## \|\| 52.11 \|\|

*aṣṭāvātmaguṇāḥ proktāḥ purāṇasya tu kovidaiḥ \|*  
*ayameva kriyāyogo jñānayogasya sādhakaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. The above eight spiritual qualifications of the soul are enumerated by those learned in the Puranas, and the possession of these qualities is essential which is, for Kriya Yoga, the means to the attainment of Jnana Yoga.

## \|\| 52.12 \|\|

*karmayogaṃ vinā jñānaṃ kasyacin neha dṛṣyate \|*  
*śrutismṛtyuditaṃ dharmam upatiṣṭhetprayatnataḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. None in this world attains Jnana without Karma Yoga; consequently, the duties enjoined by the Shruti and Smriti ought to be closely followed with diligence.

## \|\| 52.13 \|\|

*devatānāṃ pitriṇāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca sarvadā \|*  
*kuryādaharaharyajñair bhūtarṣigaṇatarpaṇam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Every day, one ought to perform the five sacrifices, viz., (1) worshipping the Devas, (2) the Pitris, (3) feeding men (4) and the lower creatures, (5) and honoring the Rishis.

## \|\| 52.14 \|\|

*svādhyāyairarcayeccarṣīn homairvidvānyathāvidhi \|*  
*pitriñchrāddhair annadānair bhūtāni balikarmabhiḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. The learned, according to the prescribed rites, ought to (1) adore the Devas by performing sacrifices to the fire, (2) worship the Rishis by the showing hospitality to guests, (5) honour all lower living creatures by scattering food for them on the ground, as described in Balikarma

## \|\| 52.15 \|\|

*pañcaite vihitā yajñāḥ pañcasūnāpanuttaye \|*  
*kaṇḍanī peṣaṇī cullī jalakumbhī pramārjanī \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. To ward off the five sins by which the animal life is accidentally destroyed by a house-holder, viz., (1) the threshing of the grain, (2) grinding of condiments and grain, (3) lighting the fire-place, (4) fetching water, by the water-pot, (5) sweeping by the broom; the above five sacrifices have been laid down.

## \|\| 52.16 \|\|

*pañca sūnā gṛhasthasya tena svargaṃ na gacchati \|*  
*tatpāpanāśanāyāmī pañca yajñāḥ prakīrtitāḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. By the above-mentioned five deeds the householder commits the five sins that are known as panchaguna; and he does not go to heaven without freeing himself from the sins, which are wiped out by the performance of the five sacrifices mentioned above.

## \|\| 52.17 \|\|

*dvāviṃśatistathāṣṭau ca ye saṃskārāḥ prakīrtitāḥ \|*  
*tadyukto 'pi na mokṣāya yastvātmaguṇavarjitaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. The twenty-two as well as the eight Samskaras laid down in the law-books, put together, do not lead to emancipation if the man does not possess the eight spiritual qualifications mentioned above.

## \|\| 52.18 \|\|

*tasmādātmaguṇopetaḥ śrutikarma samācaret \|*  
*gobrāhmaṇānāṃ vittena sarvadā bhadramācaret \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Consequently, a man possessing these qualifications ought to perform the rites laid down in the Vedas and should support the cow and the Brahmanas with his wealth, and always do good to others and should be well-condused.

## \|\| 52.19 \|\|

*gobhūhiraṇyavāsobhir gandhamālyodakena ca \|*  
*pūjayedbrahmaviṣṇvarka-rudravasvātmakaṃ śivam \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. One ought to worship Shiva. (Vasudeva) containing within Him Brahma, Vishnu, the Sun, Rudra, and the Vasus, by means of cows, land, Bid, cloth, Incense, flower-garland and water.

## \|\| 52.20-21 \|\|

*vratopavāsair vidhivac-chraddhayā ca vimatsaraḥ \|*  
*yo 'sāv atīndriyaḥ śāntaḥ sūkṣmo 'vyaktaḥ sanātanaḥ \|*  
*vāsudevo jaganmūrtis tasya sambhūtayo hy amī \|\| 20 \|\|*

*brahmā viṣṇuśca bhagavān mārtaṇḍo vṛṣavāhanaḥ \|*  
*aṣṭau ca vasavastadvad ekādaśa gaṇādhipāḥ \|*  
*lokapālādhipāścaiva pitaro mātarastathā \|\| 21 \|\|*

20-21. One should devoutly, free from jealousy, worship Shiva (Vasudeva), according to the prescribed rites, and observe fasts and vows. Shiva (Vasudeva) is super-sensuous, peaceful, unmanifest, subtle, all-pervading, eternal. And the whole universe is His form. All the following Devas are his manifestations: — vie., Vasudeva, Lord of the universe. Brahma, Vishnu, the adorable Sun, Shiva, the eight Vasus, the eleven lords of hosts (eleven Rudras), the Lord of the Lokapalas, Pitris, and the Matriganas.

## \|\| 52.22 \|\|

*imā vibhūtayaḥ proktāś carācarasamanvitāḥ \|*  
*brahmādyāś caturo mūlam avyaktādhipatiḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. These above-mentioned Devas are said to be the powers of God. These powers include all moveable and immoveable objects and belong to that Supreme Spirit who is the root of Brahma, Vishnu, Shiva and the Sun; and who is said to be the overlord of the Unmanifested (Prakriti).

## \|\| 52.23 \|\|

*oṃ oṃ brahmaṇā cātha sūryeṇa viṣṇunātha śivena vā \|*  
*abhedātpūjitena syāt pūjitaṃ sacarācaram \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. He who has adored all the four (Brahma, Surya, Vishnu and Shiva) without observing any difference among them, has worshipped, in fact, the whole universe, including the moveable and the immoveable.

## \|\| 52.24 \|\|

*brahmādīnāṃ paraṃ dhāma trayāṇāmapi saṃsthitiḥ \|*  
*vedamūrtāv ataḥ pūṣā pūjanīyaḥ prayatnataḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. He who is the supreme abode of Brahma and the rest, in whom all the three (Vedas) reside, He is Pusham, the personification of Vedas; and consequently he should be worshipped with great diligence.

## \|\| 52.25 \|\|

*tasmādagnidvijamukhān kṛtvā sampūjayedimān \|*  
*dānairvratopavāsaiśca japahomādinā naraḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. These Deities, Brahma, &c., should be worshipped by feeding the fire and the Brahmanas. Moreover, they should be adored by utterance of mantras, sacrifices, gifts, penances, fasts, silent recitation of the sacred name, and by fire oblation

## \|\| 52.26 \|\|

*iti kriyāyogaparāyaṇasya vedāntaśāstrasmṛtivatsalasya \|*  
*vikarmabhītasya sadā na kiṃcit prāptavyamastīha pare ca loke \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. For those who are devoted to the above-described Kriya Yoga and who love the Vedanta, the Smritis and the Shastras and who are afraid of sinful deeds there is nothing in this world as well as in the next which is beyond their reach, i.e., such people attain everything.

## Chapter 53

## \|\| 53.1 \|\|

*munaya ūcuḥ*  
*purāṇasaṃkhyāmācakṣva sūta vistaraśaḥ kramāt \|*  
*dānadharmamaśeṣaṃ tu yathāvadanupūrvaśaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. The Rishis — Suta! Be pleased to describe to us the number and bulk of all the Puranas in due order and in detail and also about the giving of gifts and charity (Dana Dharma)

## \|\| 53.2 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*idameva purāṇeṣu purāṇapuruṣastadā \|*  
*yaduktavānsa viśvātmā manave tannibodhata \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Suta — I shall tell you exactly what the Universal Soul, the ancient Male Lord, said to the King Vaivasvata Manu

## \|\| 53.3 \|\|

*matsya uvāca*  
*purāṇaṃ sarvaśāstrāṇāṃ prathamaṃ brahmaṇā smṛtam \|*  
*anantaraṃ ca vaktrebhyo vedāstasya vinirgatāḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Lord said to Manu! Brahma remembered in the beginning first the Puranas among all the Shastras. So Puranas are the first among the Shastras, Afterwards, Brahma uttered out the four Vedas from His four mounts.

## \|\| 53.4 \|\|

*purāṇamekamevāsīt tadā kalpāntare 'nagha \|*  
*trivargasādhanaṃ puṇyaṃ śatakoṭipravistaram \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. There was only one Purana in the beginning of the Kalpa, It was s alone the means of the accomplishment of the three ends of man (Dharma, Artha and Kama). And it was the only holy book consisting of thousand millions of stanzas.

## \|\| 53.12 \|\|

*nāmatastāni vakṣyāmi śṛṇudhvaṃ munisattamāḥ \|*  
*brahmaṇābhihitaṃ pūrvaṃ yāvanmātraṃ marīcaye \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. When all the regions perished by fire at the Great Dissolution, then I recited the four Vedas, with their six Angas as well as the Puranas, the manifold Nyayas, the Mimamsas and the Dharmashastra. In the beginning of the new age, I immersed myself in the furious waters, at the time of dissolution of the universe and explained them fully to Brahma, Who in His turn reavealed them to the Devas and the sages, after which they spread all over the world. Therefore, the Puranas became the source of all other Shastras.. Later on, seeing the neglect of the Puranas under the changed circumstances, I repromulgated then in every yuga, through my partial incarnation of Vyasa. In every Dwapara yuga I compiled the Puranas to the extent of 4 lacs of shlokas, and spread them in the world after dividing them into eighteen. Even now the bulk of the Purana extends to a hundred crore verses in the Deva Loka. On the universe; however, its bulk is abridged only to 4 lacs of shlokas, and is divided into eighteen Puranas, —

Suta. — Hear, O Rishis! the names of the different eighteen Puranas.

I shall enumerate them to you, as they were described to Marichi by Brahma.

## \|\| 53.13 \|\|

*brāhmaṃ tridaśasāhasraṃ purāṇaṃ parikīrtyate \|*  
*likhitvā tacca yo dadyāj jaladhenusamanvitam \|*  
*vaiśākhapūrṇimāyāṃ ca brahmaloke mahīyate \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. (1) The Brahma Purana. — Brahma Purana contains 13,000 shlokas.

One who writes and gives it away in charity, along with a cow and water, in the month of Vaishakha, on the full-moon day, passes his days in Brahmaloka, in happiness.

## \|\| 53.14 \|\|

*etadeva yadā padmam abhūddhairaṇmayaṃ jagat \|*  
*tadvṛttāntāśrayaṃ tadvat pādmamityucyate budhaiḥ \|*  
*pādmaṃ tatpañcapañcāśat-sahasrāṇīha kathyate \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. (2) The Padma Purana. — At the time when this universe came out of the cosmic waters, in the beginning of the Lotus Kalpa, and in the form of a golden lotus, then the Padma Purana was revealed, describing that creation, and it is called Padma Purana by the wise. And it consists of 55,000 shlokas

## \|\| 53.15 \|\|

*tatpurāṇaṃ ca yo dadyāt suvarṇakamalānvitam \|*  
*jyeṣṭhe māsi tilairyuktam aśvamedhaphalaṃ labhet \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. One who gives away Padma Purana in charity, along with a golden lotus and sesamum, in the month of Jyaishtha, gets the benefit of performing an ashvamedha sacrifice.

## \|\| 53.16 \|\|

*vārāhakalpavṛttāntam adhikṛtya parāśaraḥ \|*  
*yatprāha dharmānakhilāṃs tadyuktaṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ viduḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. (3) The Vishnu Purana, — Similarly, the rules of virtue laid down by Parashara, for the period when there was the Varaha incarnation of Vishnu, in the beginning of Varaha Kalpa, form the Vishnu Purana.

## \|\| 53.17 \|\|

*tadāṣāḍhe ca yo dadyād ghṛtadhenusamanvitam \|*  
*paurṇamāsyāṃ vipūtātmā sa padaṃ yāti vāruṇam \|*  
*trayoviṃśatisāhasraṃ tatpramāṇaṃ vidurbudhāḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. That Purana contains 23,000 shlokas, and one who gives it away in charity, along with a cow and clarified butter, in the mouth of Ashadha, on the full-moon day, is purified of all sin and goes and rests in peace in the region of Varuna.

## \|\| 53.18 \|\|

*śvetakalpaprasaṅgena dharmānvāurihābravīt \|*  
*yatra tadvāyavīyaṃ syād rudramāhātmyasaṃyutam \|*  
*caturviṃśasahasrāṇi purāṇaṃ tadihocyate \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. (4) The Vayu Purana. — The rules of virtue laid down by Vayu, along with the glory of Rudra, in the Shveta-kalpa, is known as Vayaviya Purana. It contains 24,000 shlokas.

## \|\| 53.19 \|\|

*śrāvaṇyāṃ śrāvaṇe māsi guḍadhenusamanvitam \|*  
*yo dadyādvṛṣasaṃyuktaṃ brāhmaṇāya kuṭumbine \|*  
*śivaloke sa pūtātmā kalpamekaṃ vasennaraḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. One who gives it away in charity, along with a cow, sugar and an ox, to a Brahmana, whose family is large, on the day when Rakhi thread is tied on the wrist, in the month of Shravana, goes and resides for a Kalpa in the region of Shiva.

## \|\| 53.20-21 \|\|

*yatrādhikṛtya gāyatrīṃ varṇyate dharmavistaraḥ \|*  
*vṛtrāsuravadhopetaṃ tadbhāgavatamucyate \|\| 20 \|\|*

*sārasvatasya kalpasya madhye ye syurnarottamāḥ \|*  
*tadvṛttāntodbhavaṃ loke tadbhāgavatamucyate \|\| 21 \|\|*

20-21. (5) The Bhagavata Purana. — The Purana which begins with the description of the sacred Gayatri worship, and goes on to mention various Dharmas and which contains a narration of the destruction of the demon Vritrasura as well as an. account of the famous men who flourished in the Sarasvata Kalpa, is known as Bhagavata.

## \|\| 53.22 \|\|

*likhitvā tacca yo dadyād dhemasiṃhasamanvitam \|*  
*paurṇamāsyāṃ prauṣṭhapadyāṃ sa yāti paramāṃ gatim \|*  
*aṣṭādaśa sahasrāṇi purāṇaṃ tatpracakṣate \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. One who writes Bhagavata and gives it away in charity, along with a golden lion, on the full-moon day, in the month of Bhadrapada, attains final emancipation. It contains 18,000 shlokas.

## \|\| 53.23 \|\|

*yatrāha nārado dharmān bṛhatkalpāśrayāṇi ca \|*  
*pañcaviṃśatsahasrāṇi nāradīyaṃ taducyate \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. (6) The Naradiya Purana, — The Naradiya Purana, containing 25,000 shlokas is that In which Narada has described the Brihatkalpa and the dharmas of the Brihatkalpa

## \|\| 53.24 \|\|

*āśvine pañcadaśyāṃ tu dadyāddhenusamanvitam \|*  
*paramāṃ siddhimāpnoti punarāvṛttidurlabhām \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. One who gives away this Purina in charity, on the full-moon day of Ashvin, along with a cow, attains bliss, and is liberated from the cycles of birth.

## \|\| 53.25-26 \|\|

*yatrādhikṛtya śakunīn dharmādharmavicāraṇā \|*  
*vyākhyātā vai munipraśne munibhirdharmacāribhiḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*mārkaṇḍeyena kathitaṃ tatsarvaṃ vistareṇa tu \|*  
*purāṇaṃ navasāhasraṃ mārkaṇḍeyam ihocyate \|\| 26 \|\|*

25-26. (7) The Markandeya Purana — The Purana which begins with the story of the birds solving the difficulty of Dharma and Adharma, and which the pious sages explain in an answer to the question of the sage (Jaimini), which has been described at great length by the sage Markandeya, at the request of the Rishis, and which contains 9,000 couplets, is known as Markandeya Purana.

## \|\| 53.27 \|\|

*pratilikhya ca yo dadyāt sauvarṇakarisaṃyutam \|*  
*kārttikyāṃ puṇḍarīkasya yajñasya phalabhāgbhavet \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. One who writes this Purana, and gives it away in charity, along with a golden elephant, on the full-moon day, in the month of Kartika, attains the benefit of performing Pundarika sacrifice

## \|\| 53.28 \|\|

*yat tad īśānakaṃ kalpaṃ vṛttāntamadhikṛtya ca \|*  
*vasiṣṭhāyāgninā proktam āgneyaṃ tatpracakṣate \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. 8. The Agni Purana, — The Purana which commences with the description of the Ishana Kalpa, and which was a path of virtue revealed to Agni by Vasistha, is known as the Agneya Purana, and contains 16,000 shlokas.

## \|\| 53.29 \|\|

*likhitvā tacca yo dadyād dhemapadmasamanvitam \|*  
*mārgaśīrṣyāṃ vidhānena tiladhenusamanvitam \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. One who writes this Purina and gives it away in charity, along with a golden lotus, a cow and sesamum, on the full-moon day, in Margashira, attains the benefit of performing 16,000 sacrifices

## \|\| 53.30-31 \|\|

*tacca ṣoḍaśasāhasraṃ sarvakratuphalapradam \|*  
*yaḥ pradadhannaraḥ so 'tha svargaloke mahīyate \|\| 30 \|\|*

*yatrādhikṛtya māhātmyam ādityasya caturmukhaḥ \|*  
*aghorakalpavṛttānta-prasaṅgena jagatsthitim \|*  
*manave kathayāmāsa bhūtagrāmasya lakṣaṇam \|\| 31 \|\|*

30-31. 9. The Bhavishya Purana.--The Purina in which Brahma has described the history of Aghorakalpa, the glory of the Sun, the existence.

of the Universe, the characteristics of the aggregate multitude to Manu, is known as the Bhavishya Purana, and contains 14,500 Shlokas.

## \|\| 53.32 \|\|

*caturdaśa sahasrāṇi tathā pañca śatāni ca \|*  
*bhaviṣyacaritaprāyaṃ bhaviṣyaṃ tadihocyate \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. One who gives away this Purana in charity, free from the feeling of jealousy, on the full-moon day of Pausha, along with a pitcher of raw sugar, attains the benefit of performing the Agnishtoma sacrifice

## \|\| 53.33-34 \|\|

*tatpauṣe māsi yo dadyāt paurṇamāsyāṃ vimatsaraḥ \|*  
*guḍakumbhasamāuktam agniṣṭomaphalaṃ bhavet \|\| 33 \|\|*

*rathaṃtarasya kalpasya vṛttāntamadhikṛtya ca \|*  
*sāvarṇinā nāradāya kṛṣṇamāhātmyamuttamam \|\| 34 \|\|*

33-34. 10. The Brahmavaivarta Purana. — The Purana which commences with the description of Rathantara Kalpa, and in which Savarni Manu has described to Narada the glory of Krishna and the history of the Rathantara Kalpa, and in which there is also a constant allusion to Brahmavaraha, is known as Brahmavaivarta Purana, and contains 18,000 shlokas.

## \|\| 53.35 \|\|

*yatra brahmavarāhasya codantaṃ varṇitaṃ muhuḥ \|*  
*tadaṣṭādaśasāhasraṃ brahmavaivartamucyate \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. One who gives away this Brahmavaivarta Purina in charity to a Brahmana on an auspicious day, in the month of Magha, on the full moon day, goes and enjoys in the region of Brahma.

## \|\| 53.36-37 \|\|

*purāṇaṃ brahmavaivartaṃ yo dadyānmāghamāsi ca \|*  
*paurṇamāsyāṃ śubhadine brahmaloke mahīyate \|\| 36 \|\|*

*yatrāgniliṅgamadhyasthaḥ prāha devo maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*dharmārthakāmamokṣārtham āgneyamadhikṛtya ca \|\| 37 \|\|*

36-37. 11. The Linga Purana. — The Purana in which Shiva explained the wirtues of Agni and the four Vargas, viz., Dharma, Artha, Kama and Moksha, by manifesting Himself through the pillar of fire, which comtmences with the description of Agneya Kalpa, and which was uttered by Brahma Himself, is styled Linga Purana, and it contains 11,000 shlokas.

One who gives away this Purana, along with sesamum and cow in charity, on the full-moon day, in the month of Phalguna, attains the form of and similarity with Shiva

## \|\| 53.38-39 \|\|

*kalpānte laiṅgamityuktaṃ purāṇaṃ brahmaṇā svayam \|*  
*tadekādaśasāhasraṃ phālgunyāṃ yaḥ prayacchati \|*  
*tiladhenusamāuktaṃ sa yāti śivasāmyatām \|\| 38 \|\|*

*mahāvarāhasya punar māhātmyamadhikṛtya ca \|*  
*viṣṇunābhihitaṃ kṣoṇyai tadvārāham ihocyate \|\| 39 \|\|*

38-39. 12. The Varaha Purana. — The Purana in which Vishnu has described the glories of the Great Boar to the goddess Earth, and which was recited in connection with the Manava Kalpa, is known as the Varaha Purana, and contains 24,000 stanzas.

## \|\| 53.40 \|\|

*mānavasya prasaṅgena kalpasya munisattamāḥ \|*  
*caturviṃśatsahasrāṇi tatpurāṇamihocyate \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. One who gives away this Purana in charity, along with a golden eagle (Grauda), cow and sesamum, on the full-moon day, in the month of Chaitra, to a Brahmana with a large family, reaches the region of Vishnu by the favour of Varaha.

## \|\| 53.41-42 \|\|

*kāñcanaṃ garuḍaṃ kṛtvā tiladhenusamanvitam \|*  
*paurṇamāsyāṃ madhau dadyād brāhmaṇāya kuṭumbine \|*  
*varāhasya prasādena padamāpnoti vaiṣṇavam \|\| 41 \|\|*

*yatra māheśvarāndharmān adhikṛtya ca ṣaṇmukhaḥ \|*  
*kalpe tatpuruṣaṃ vṛttaṃ caritairupabṛṃhitam \|\| 42 \|\|*

41-42. 13. The Skanda Purana. — The Purana in which the six-faced Kartika has expressed the virtues of high-class men and also about the worship of Mahadeva, is known as Skanda Purana. It commences with the description of the Maheshvara Dharmas, as found in. the Satpurusha Kalpa, and contains 81,100 shlokas, in this mortal region

## \|\| 53.43 \|\|

*skāndaṃ nāma purāṇaṃ ca hy ekāśītirnigadyate \|*  
*sahasrāṇi śataṃ caikam iti martyeṣu gadyate \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. One who gives away this Purana, along with a golden trident, after writing it out at the time of the Sun being in the 12th sign of the Zodiac (Pisces), goes to the region of Shiva.

## \|\| 53.44-45 \|\|

*parilikhya ca yo dadyād dhemaśūlasamanvitam \|*  
*śaivaṃ padamavāpnoti mīne copāgate ravau \|\| 44 \|\|*

*trivikramasya māhātmyam adhikṛtya caturmukhaḥ \|*  
*trivargamabhyadhāttacca vāmanaṃ parikīrtitam \|\| 45 \|\|*

44-45. 14. The Vamana Purana — The Purana in which the four-faced Brahma has related the glories of Trivikrama, and which describes the three Vargas also to the Devas, after declaring the glory of Vamana, is known as the Vamana Purana, and contains 10,000 Shlokas. It describes, the Kalpa, and is auspicious. Following Karma Kalpa, one who gives it away in charity, after writing it out neatly in the autumnal equinox, goes to the region of Vishnu.

## \|\| 53.46-47 \|\|

*purāṇaṃ daśasāhasraṃ kūrmakalpānugaṃ śivam \|*  
*yaḥ śaradviṣuve dadyād vaiṣṇavaṃ yātyasau padam \|\| 46 \|\|*

*yatra dharmārthakāmānāṃ mokṣasya ca rasātale \|*  
*māhātmyaṃ kathayāmāsa kūrmarūpī janārdanaḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

46-47. 15. The Kurma Purana. — The Purana in which Vishnu has dwelt on she glories of the four Vargas (Dharma, Artha, Kama and Moksha), in the form of a Kurma, in the Rasatala regions, before the sages, in connection with the story of Indradyumna, where Indra was also present, through his companion Indradyumna, is known as Kurma-Purana, and is related to Lakshmi Kalpa. It contains 18,000 shlokas.

## \|\| 53.48 \|\|

*indradyumnaprasaṅgena ṛṣibhyaḥ śakrasaṃnidhau \|*  
*aṣṭādaśa sahasrāṇi lakṣmīkalpānuṣaṅgikam \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. One who gives it away in charity, along with a golden turtle, at the time of the equinox, gets the benefit of giving away thousands of cows.

## \|\| 53.49-50 \|\|

*yo dadyādayane kūrmaṃ hemakūrmasamanvitam \|*  
*gosahasrapradānasya phalaṃ samprāpnuyānnaraḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

*śrutīnāṃ yatra kalpādau pravṛttyarthaṃ janārdanaḥ \|*  
*matsyarūpeṇa manave narasiṃhopavarṇanam \|\| 50 \|\|*

49-50. 16. The Matsya Purana. — The Purana in which the Lord has related the glory of Nrisimha to Vaivasvata Manu, at the beginning of the Kalpa, with a view to propagate the Shrutis, in the form of a fish, and in which thy Matsya Purana. It contains 14,000 shlokas.

## \|\| 53.51 \|\|

*adhikṛtyābravītsapta-kalpavṛttaṃ munīśvarāḥ \|*  
*tanmātsyamiti jānīdhvaṃ sahasrāṇi caturdaśa \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. One who gives this Purana away in charity, along with a golden fish and a cow, at the time of the summer solstice, acquires the benefit of giving in gift the entire earth

## \|\| 53.52 \|\|

*viṣuve hemamatsyena dhenvā caiva samanvitam \|*  
*yo dadyātpṛthivī tena dattā bhavati cākhilā \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. The Garuda Purana. — The Purana in which Krishna has described the birth of Garuda out of the cosmic egg, in the Garuda Kalpa, is known as Garuda Purana, and contains 18,000 shlokas

## \|\| 53.53 \|\|

*yadā ca gāruḍe kalpe viśvāṇḍādgaruḍodbhavam \|*  
*adhikṛtyābravītkṛṣṇo gāruḍaṃ tadihocyate \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. One who gives away this Purana in charity, along with a golden flamingo, attains a place in the region of Shiva, endowed with highest perfection.

## \|\| 53.54-55 \|\|

*tad aṣṭādaśakaṃ caikaṃ sahasrāṇīha paṭhyate \|*  
*sauvarṇahaṃsasaṃyuktaṃ yo dadāti pumāniha \|*  
*sa siddhiṃ labhate mukhyāṃ śivaloke ca saṃsthitim \|\| 54 \|\|*

*brahmā brahmāṇḍamāhātmyam adhikṛtyābravītpunaḥ \|*  
*tacca dvādaśasāhasraṃ brahmāṇḍaṃ dviśatādhikam \|\| 55 \|\|*

54-55. (18) The Brahmanda Purana — The Purina commencing with the glory of the cosmic egg, and in which Brahma has described the future Kalpas as well as the history of the Universe to the Devas, is known as the Brahmanda Purana, and contains 12,200 shlokas.

## \|\| 53.56 \|\|

*bhaviṣyāṇāṃ ca kalpānāṃ śrūyate yatra vistaraḥ \|*  
*tadbrahmāṇḍapurāṇaṃ ca brahmaṇā samudāhṛtam \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. One who gives away this Purana in charity, along with a yellow woolen garment, and a golden cow at the time of Vyatipata, attains the benefit of a thousand Rajasuya sacrifices

## \|\| 53.57 \|\|

*yo dadyāttadvyatīpāte pītorṇāugasaṃyutam \|*  
*rājasūyasahasrasya phalamāpnoti mānavaḥ \|*  
*hemadhenvā utaṃ tacca brahmalokaphalapradam \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Suta said: — Vyasa, of wonderful activity, explained these eighteen Puranas, to the. extent of 4 lacs of shlokas, to my father, and the latter told me about it; and I, O Rishis! have described the same to you.

## \|\| 53.58 \|\|

*caturlakṣamidaṃ proktaṃ vyāsenādbhutakarmaṇā \|*  
*matpiturmama pitrā ca mayā tubhyaṃ niveditam \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. The venerable sage has abridged the Puranas for the sake of the good of the world; otherwise, the entire Purana existing in the Deva Loka, contains a hundred crore shlokas.

## \|\| 53.59 \|\|

*iha lokahitārthāya saṃkṣiptaṃ paramarṣiṇā \|*  
*idamadyāpi deveṣu śatakoṭipravistaram \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. Upapuranas — (1) Nrisimha. — I shall now tell you about the difference between the Puranas that exist in the universe and the secondary Puranas. There is a mention of Nrisimha in the Padma Purana, and the 18,000 shlokas (dealing with the history of Narasimha) forms the Narsimha Purana (which is one of the secondary Puranas)

## \|\| 53.60 \|\|

*upabhedānpravakṣyāmi loke ye sampratiṣṭhitāḥ \|*  
*pādme purāṇe yatroktaṃ narasiṃhopavarṇanam \|*  
*taccāṣṭādaśasāhasraṃ nārasiṃhamihocyate \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. (2) Nandi-upapurana. — Where Swamikartika has described the glory of the great goose Nanda (the portion dealing with that), is known as the Nandi Purana

## \|\| 53.62 \|\|

*yatra sāmbaṃ puraskṛtya bhaviṣyati kathānakam \|*  
*procyate tatpunarloke sāmbametanmunivratāḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. (3) Samba-upapurana. — That Purana in which Lord Shiva, taking. His most noble consort, Gauri, as his audience, has related about the future, as found in the Bhavishya Purina and also is styled by the sages as Samba Purana.

## \|\| 53.63 \|\|

*purātanasya kalpasya purāṇāni vidurbudhāḥ \|*  
*dhanyaṃ yaśasyamāuṣyaṃ purāṇānāmanukramam \|*  
*evamādityasaṃjñā ca tatraiva parigadyate \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. (4) Aditya-upapurana, — The learned who know, say that the recitation of the list of the Puranas dealing with the ancient Kalpa, is conducive to glory, fame and long life. This is the order of the Puranas, as described above. Similarly, the Aditya Upapurana is also mentioned therein.

O Rishis! the secondary Puranas have been deduced from the original eighteen Puranas.

## \|\| 53.64 \|\|

*aṣṭādaśabhyastu pṛthak purāṇaṃ yatpradiṣyate \|*  
*vijānīdhvaṃ dvijaśreṣṭhās tadetebhyo vinirgatam \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. The following are the five characteristics of the Puranas: — They describe (1) the creation of the universe, (2) its genealogy and dissolution, (3) the dynasties, (4) the Manvantaras, (5) the dynastic chronicles.

## \|\| 53.65 \|\|

*pañcāṅgāni purāṇeṣu ākhyānakamiti smṛtam \|*  
*sargaśca pratisargaśca vaṃśo manvantarāṇi ca \|*  
*vaṃśyānucaritaṃ caiva purāṇaṃ pañcalakṣaṇam \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. The Puranas, with these five characteristics, sing the glory of Brahma, Vishnu, the Sun and Rudra, as well as they describe also the creation and dissolution of the Earth

## \|\| 53.66 \|\|

*brahmaviṣṇvarkarudrāṇāṃ māhātmyaṃ bhuvanasya ca \|*  
*sasaṃhārapradānāṃ ca purāṇe pañcavarṇake \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. The four Vargas (Dharma, Artha, Kama and Moksha) have also been described in all the Puranas, along with evil consequences following from sin.

## \|\| 53.67-68 \|\|

*dharmaścārthaśca kāmaśca mokṣaścaivātra kīrtyate \|*  
*sarveṣvapi purāṇeṣu tadviruddhaṃ ca yatphalam \|\| 67 \|\|*

*sāttvikeṣu purāṇeṣu māhātmyamadhikaṃ hareḥ \|*  
*rājaseṣu ca māhātmyam adhikaṃ brahmaṇo viduḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

67-68. In the Satvika Puranas, there is largely a mention of Hari’s glory.

In the Rajas Puranas there is the greater mention of Brahma’s glory.

In the Tamasika Puranas, there is a mention of Shiva and Agni’s glory.

In all kinds of Puranas, of all the three attributes, the glory of Sarasvati and the pitris have been described.

## \|\| 53.69 \|\|

*tadvadagneśca māhātmyaṃ tāmaseṣu śivasya ca \|*  
*saṃkīrṇeṣu sarasvatyāḥ pitriṇāṃ ca nigadyate \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. The great sage Vyasa, after compiling the 18 Puranas, indulged in the composition of the story of Mahabharata, in order to magnify their bulk, which was an addition to the Puranas, by another lakh of shlokas. And in which he has condensed the sense of the Vedas.

## \|\| 53.70 \|\|

*aṣṭādaśa purāṇāni kṛtvā satyavatīsutaḥ \|*  
*bhāratākhyānamakhilaṃ cakre tadupabṛṃhitam \|*  
*lakṣeṇaikena yatproktaṃ vedārthaparibṛṃhitam \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. The glorious story of Ramayana, sung by the sage Valmiki, at the instance of Brahma, also extends to a hundred crore of shlokas.

## \|\| 53.72 \|\|

*āhṛtya nāradāyaivaṃ tena vālmīkaye punaḥ \|*  
*vālmīkinā ca lokeṣu dharmakāmārthasādhanam \|*  
*evaṃ sapādāḥ pañcaite lakṣā martye prakīrtitāḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. Brahma narrated the original Ramayana to Narada; the latter revealed it to Valmiki, who gave it to the world, and which is a means of giving Dharma, Kama and Artha. And in which way the famous epic exists in The learned know of the Puranas of the ancient Kalpa. The recitation of this list of the Puranas is conducive to prosperity, fame and long life. He who reads or listens to it, gets wealth, reputation, long life and emancipation.

## \|\| 53.73 \|\|

*purātanasya kalpasya purāṇāni vidurbudhāḥ \|*  
*dhanyaṃ yaśasyamāuṣyaṃ purāṇānāmanukramam \|*  
*yaḥ paṭhecchṛṇuyādvāpi sa yāti paramāṃ gatim \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. This list is the most sacred. It is the giver of fame and the destroyer of sins. It is very dear to the pitris, and is prized by the Devas as a nectar. It is external and destroyer of sin of all men.

## Chapter 54

## \|\| 54.1-2 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi dānadharmānaśeṣataḥ \|*  
*vratopavāsasaṃyuktān yathāmatsyoditāniha \|\| 1 \|\|*

*mahādevasya saṃvāde nāradasya ca dhīmataḥ \|*  
*yathāvṛttaṃ pravakṣyāmi dharmakāmārthasādhakam \|\| 2 \|\|*

1-2. Suta said: — Rishis! I shall now relate to you in full about the gifts (Dana Dharma), vows (Vrata) and fasts, as explained by the Lord in the form of fish, This narration is in the form of a dialogue between the great Lord Shiva and wise Narada and also a mention of trivarga. (Dharma, Kama and Arthra). I shall relate exactly as the dialogue took place.

## \|\| 54.4-5 \|\|

*nārada uvāca*  
*bhagavandevadeveśa brahmaviṣṇvindranāyaka \|*  
*śrīmadārogyarūpāur bhāgyasaubhāgyasampadā \|*  
*saṃyuktastava viṣṇorvā pumānbhaktaḥ kathaṃ bhavet \|\| 4 \|\|*

*nārī vā vidhavā sarva-guṇasaubhāgyasaṃyutā \|*  
*kramānmuktipradaṃ deva kiṃcidvratamihocyatām \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. In ancient times, Narada questioned the Lord Shiva, who resides on the summit of Kailasa, has three eyes, and is the enemy and destroyer of The Sage Narada said: — “O Adorable God of gods! O Ruler of Brahma, Vishnu and Indra! pray tell me how one may become your devotee or a devotee of Vishnu and so attain wealth, life, health, beauty, luck, and prosperity? Pray also tell me which Vrata is the giver of gradual emancipation to married women or widows, possessing all good and auspicious qualities”.

## \|\| 54.6-7 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca*  
*samyakpṛṣṭaṃ tvayā brahman sarvalokahitāvaham \|*  
*śrutamapyatra yacchāntyai tadvrataṃ śṛṇu nārada \|\| 6 \|\|*

*nakṣatrapuruṣaṃ nāma vrataṃ nārāyaṇātmakam \|*  
*pādādi kuryādvidhivad viṣṇunāmānukīrtanam \|\| 7 \|\|*

6-7. Lord Shiva said: — Narada! You have put a very useful question for the. benefit of all. Hear about the vow which is beneficial to widows.

There is a religious observance (Vrata) which is known as nakshatrapurusha Vrata, which should he devoutly kept. It (nakshatrapurusha Vrata) is worship of Narayana in the figure which should be made according to rule, having feet, etc., and the names of Vishnu should be recited.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — Nakshatrapurusha — A figure of a man, on the limbs of which various asterisms are marked.

## \|\| 54.8 \|\|

*pratimāṃ vāsudevasya mūlarkṣādiṣu cārcayet \|*  
*caitramāsaṃ samāsādya kṛtvā brāhmaṇavācanam \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. The devotee should get an image of the Lord Vasudeva made according to the instructions of the Brahmana, and should then commence to worship it from the month of Chaitra, at the time when the moon is in the Mula, etc.

## \|\| 54.9-19 \|\|

*mūle namo viśvadharāya pādau gulphāvanantāya ca rohiṇīṣu \|*  
*jaṅghe 'bhipūjye varadāya caiva dve jānunī vāśvikumāraṛkṣe \|\| 9 \|\|*

*pūrvottarāṣāḍhauge tathorū namaḥ śivāyetyabhipūjanīyau \|*  
*pūrvottarāphalguniugmake ca meḍhraṃ namaḥ pañcaśarāya pūjyam \|\| 10 \|\|*

*kaṭiṃ namaḥ śārṅgadharāya viṣṇoḥ sampūjayennārada kṛttikāsu \|*  
*tathārcayedbhādrapadādvaye ca pārśve namaḥ keśiniṣūdanāya \|\| 11 \|\|*

*kukṣidvayaṃ nārada revatīṣu dāmodarāyetyabhipūjanīyam \|*  
*ṛkṣe 'nurādhāsu ca mādhavāya namastathoraḥsthalameva pūjyam \|\| 12 \|\|*

*pṛṣṭhaṃ dhaniṣṭhāsu ca pūjanīyam aghaughavidhvaṃsakarāya tacca \|*  
*śrīśaṅkhacakrāsigadādharāya namo viśākhāsu bhujāśca pūjyāḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*haste tu hastā madhusūdanāya namo 'bhipūjyā iti kaiṭabhāreḥ \|*  
*punarvasāvaṅgulipūrvabhāgāḥ sāmnāmadhīśāya namo 'bhipūjyāḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*bhujaṃganakṣatradine nakhāni sampūjayenmatsyaśarīrabhājaḥ \|*  
*kūrmasya pādau śaraṇaṃ vrajāmi jyeṣṭhāsu kaṇṭhe harirarcanīyaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*śrotre varāhāya namo 'bhipūjyā janārdanasya śravaṇena samyak \|*  
*puṣye mukhaṃ dānavasūdanāya namo nṛsiṃhāya ca pūjanīyam \|\| 16 \|\|*

*namo namaḥ kāraṇavāmanāya svātīṣu dantāgramathārcanīyam \|*  
*āsyaṃ harerbhārgavanandanāya saṃpūjanīyaṃ dvija vāruṇe tu \|\| 17 \|\|*

*namo 'stu rāmāya maghāsu nāsā saṃpūjanīyā raghunandanasya \|*  
*mṛgottamāṅge nayane 'bhipūjye namo 'stu te rāma vighūrṇitākṣa \|\| 18 \|\|*

*buddhāya śāntāya namo lalāṭaṃ citrāsu saṃpūjyatamaṃ murāreḥ \|*  
*śiro 'bhipūjyaṃ bharaṇīṣu viṣṇor namo 'stu viśveśvara kalkirūpiṇe \|\| 19 \|\|*

9-19. He should recite the following mantras on the various limbs, beginning from the feet and ending with the hair of the figure: —

(1) Namo Vishvadharma — on the two feet, sacred to Mula asterism.

(2) Namo Anantaya — on the two ankles of the leg, sacred to Rohini asterism.

(3) Nano Varadaya — on the two shanks, from the ankle to the knee, as well as the two knees, sacred to the Ashvini asterism.

(4) Namah Shivaya — on the two thighs, sacred to the Parva Asadha and Uttara Asadha.

(5) Namah Panchasharaya — on the organ of generation, sacred to Purvaphalguni and Uttaraphalguni.

(6) Namah Sharngadharaya — on the waist, where Vishnu should be worSlipped, sacred to Krittika asterism.

(7) Namah Keshinisudanaya--on the two sides of the ribs, sacred to Purvabhadrapada and Uttarabhadrapada.

(8) Namah Damodaraya — on the two arm-pits, sacred to Revati asterism.

(9) Namah Madhavaya — on the chest, sacred to Anuradha asterism.

(10) Namah Aghanghavidhvamsakaraya — on the back, sacred to Dhanistha asterism.

(11) Namah Shrishankhachakrasigadadharaya - on sacred to Vishakha asterism.

(12) Namah Madhusudanaya,-- on the hands, sacred to Hasta asterism.

(13) Namah Samnimadhisaya---on the tips of the finger, sacred to Punarvastu.

(14) Namah Matsyaya. Then the nails of the Fish (Matsaya) should be worshipped, sacred to Aslesha asterism. No mantra in original.

(15) Namah Karmaya Kurmasya Padan Sharanam vrajami —

on the throat, and the feet of the tortoise (Kurma), sacred to Jyeshtha.

(16) Namah Varihdaya — on the two ears, sacred to Shravana asterism and the Boar (Varaha).

(17) Namah Nrisimhaya Danavasudanaya — on the mouth, sacred to Pushya asterism - Man-lion.

(18) Namah Karanavamamaya — on the fore of the teeth, sacred to Svati asterism and Vamana (Dwarf) avatara.

(19) Bhargavanandanaya — on the gullet of the mouth, sacred to Satabhisha asterism and Parashu Rama.

(20) Namah Ramaya — in the nose, sacred to Magha asterism and Raghunandana Rama.

(21) Namah Ramaya Vighurnitakshaya — in the eyes, sacred to Mrigasira asterism and Bala Rama.

(22) Namah Buddbaya Santaya — on the forehead, sacred to Chitra (23) Namah Vishveshvara Kalkirupine — on the head, sacred to Bhavani asterism and Kalki.

(24) Namah Haraye — on the hair, sacred to Ardra asterism and Purushottama.

## \|\| 54.20 \|\|

*ārdrāsu keśāḥ puruṣottamasya saṃpūjanīyā haraye namaste \|*  
*upoṣitenarkṣadineṣu bhaktyā saṃpūjanīyā dvijapuṃgavāḥ syuḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. On the day of the fast worthy Brahmanas should be honored.

## \|\| 54.21-22 \|\|

*pūrṇe vrate sarvaguṇānvitāya vāgrūpaśīlāya ca sāmagāya \|*  
*haimīṃ viśālāyatabāhudaṇḍāṃ muktāphalendūpalavajrauktām \|\| 21 \|\|*

*jalasya pūrṇe kalaśe niviṣṭām arcāṃ harervastragavā sahaiva \|*  
*śayyāṃ tathopaskarabhājanādi-yuktāṃ pradadyāddvijapuṃgavāya \|\| 22 \|\|*

21-22. On the completion of the Vrata, the devotee should give away a beautiful and big golden mace, studded with pearls and other jewels, cows, garments, bedstead, &c., to a pious Brahmana, versed in the Samaveda.

The mace should be placed in a pitcher of water.

## \|\| 54.23 \|\|

*yadyasti yatkiṃcidihāsti deyaṃ dadyāddvijāyātmahitāya sarvam \|*  
*manorathānnaḥ saphalīkuruṣva hiraṇyagarbhācyutarudrarūpin \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Besides all that, the devotee should give away other things worthy of being offered to a Brahmana, after which he should devoutly pray to the Lord to fulfil his desires in the words: “Manoratham nab Saphalikurushva hiranya garbhachyutarudrarapin”. O thou having the form of Brahma, Vishnu and Shiva, fulfill all my cherished desires.

## \|\| 54.24 \|\|

*salakṣmīkaṃ sabhāryāya kāñcanaṃ puruṣottamam \|*  
*śayyāṃ ca dadyānmantreṇa granthibhedavivarjitām \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. The image of Vishnu along with that of Lakshmi, should be given away to the Brahmana and his wife. with a peaceful mind So also should be given a bedstead, made of wood, without any joints.

## \|\| 54.25-26 \|\|

*yathā na viṣṇubhaktānāṃ vṛjinaṃ jāyate kvacit \|*  
*tathā surūpatārogyaṃ keśave bhaktimuttamām \|\| 25 \|\|*

*yathā na lakṣmyā śayanaṃ tava śūnyaṃ janārdana \|*  
*śayyā mamāpyaśūnyāstu kṛṣṇa janmani janmani \|\| 26 \|\|*

25-26. The devotee should recite the following: — “As the worshippers of Vishnu never get any sufferings or sin, so let me get beauty and health as well as highest devotion towards Keshava; as the house of the Lord is never devoid of Lakshmi, so my house, may never be bereaft of my consort in all my life; O Krishna.”

## \|\| 54.27-28 \|\|

*evaṃ nivedya tatsarvaṃ vastramālyānulepanam \|*  
*nakṣatrapuruṣajñāya viprāyātha visarjayet \|\| 27 \|\|*

*bhuñjītātailalavaṇaṃ sarvarkṣeṣvapyupoṣitaḥ \|*  
*bhojanaṃ ca yathāśakti vittaśāṭhyavivarjitaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

27-28 After that, the Brahmana versed in astronomy, should be dismissed by giving away the image of the nakshatra purusha, along with clothes, garland, sandal paste, &c. The worshipper should abstain from salt and only food during all the twenty-seven days of his observance of the Vrata, and should feed others according to his means, without giving way to miserliness.

## \|\| 54.29-30 \|\|

*iti nakṣatrapuruṣam upāsya vidhivatsvayam \|*  
*sarvānkāmānavāpnoti viṣṇuloke mahīyate \|\| 29 \|\|*

*brahmahatyādikaṃ kiṃcid iha vāmutra vā kṛtam \|*  
*ātmanā vātha pitṛbhis tatsarvaṃ kṣayamāpnuyāt \|\| 30 \|\|*

29-30. The worshipper of the nakshatra purusha attains all his desires, and at the end passes his days in the region of Vishnu with happiness. He washes off all his sins as well as all the sins of his deceased ancestors committed in his present and past lives.

## \|\| 54.31 \|\|

*iti paṭhati śṛṇoti vātibhaktyā puruṣavaro vratamaṅganātha kuryāt \|*  
*kalikaluṣavidāraṇaṃ murāreḥ sakalavibhūtiphalapradaṃ ca puṃsām \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. The married woman or the man who reads or hears the story of this observance with devotion, will free herself or himself from all the sins by hearing and reading it. This observance confers many blessings on the worshippers

## Chapter 55

## \|\| 55.1 \|\|

*nārada uvāca*  
*upavāseṣvaśaktasya tadeva phalamicchataḥ \|*  
*anabhyāsena rogādvā kimiṣṭaṃ vratamuttamam \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Hearing all that Narada said: — Lord! What should one, who, owing ‘to delicate health or otherwise, is not in a position to go through the ordinance of fasting just explained by you, do?”

## \|\| 55.2 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca*  
*upavāse 'pyaśaktānāṃ naktaṃ bhojanamiṣyate \|*  
*yasminvrate tadapyatra śrūyatāmakṣayaṃ mahat \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. The Lord said: — One who is not in a position to keep up the fast should take his meals in the night which will also give him everlasting benefit

## \|\| 55.3-5 \|\|

*ādityaśayanaṃ nāma yathāvacchaṃkarārcanam \|*  
*yeṣu nakṣatrayogeṣu purāṇajñāḥ pracakṣate \|\| 3 \|\|*

*yadā hastena saptamyām ādityasya dinaṃ bhavet \|*  
*sūryasya cātha saṃkrāntis tithiḥ sā sārvakāmikī \|\| 4 \|\|*

*umāmaheśvarasyārcām arcayetsūryanāmabhiḥ \|*  
*sūryārcāṃ śivaliṅge ca prakurvan pūjayedyataḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

3-5. Hear about the Vrata, called Aditya Sayana Shankararchana observance, as described by the learned in the Puranas, as well as the method of worshipping Shankara, on the conjunction of the moon with particular asterism. That day is most auspicious which falls on a Sunday, when there is Shankranti and the 7th day of the dark fortnight and when the moon 'is in the asterism Hasti, On that day, the images of Uma and Maheshvara: should be worshipped, the former after reciting the names.

Of the God, Sun, and the latter along with the invisible form of Shiva.

## \|\| 55.6-15 \|\|

*umāpate ravervāpi na bhedo dṛṣyate kvacit \|*  
*yasmāttasmānmuniśreṣṭha gṛhe śambhuṃ samarcayet \|\| 6 \|\|*

*haste ca sūryāya namo 'stu pādāv arkāya citrāsu ca gulphadeśam \|*  
*svātīṣu jaṅghe puruṣottamāya dhātre viśākhāsu ca jānudeśam \|\| 7 \|\|*

*tathānurādhāsu namo 'bhipūjyam ūrudvayaṃ caiva sahasrabhānoḥ \|*  
*jyeṣṭhāsvanaṅgāya namo 'stu guhyam indrāya somāya kaṭī ca mūle \|\| 8 \|\|*

*pūrvottarāṣāḍhauge ca nābhiṃ tvaṣṭre namaḥ saptataraṃgamāya \|*  
*tīkṣṇāṃśave ca śravaṇe ca kukṣau pṛṣṭhaṃ dhaniṣṭhāsu vikartanāya \|\| 9 \|\|*

*cakṣuḥsthalaṃ dhvāntavināśanāya jalādhiparkṣe paripūjanīyam \|*  
*pūrvottarābhādrapadādvaye ca bāhū namaścaṇḍakarāya pūjyau \|\| 10 \|\|*

*sāmnāmadhīśāya karadvayaṃ ca saṃpūjanīyaṃ dvija revatīṣu \|*  
*nakhāni pūjyāni tathāśvinīṣu namo 'stu saptāśvadhuraṃdharāya \|\| 11 \|\|*

*kaṭhoradhāmne bharaṇīṣu kaṇṭhaṃ divākarāyetyabhipūjanīyā \|*  
*grīvāgniṛkṣe 'dharamambujeśe sampūjayennārada rohiṇīṣu \|\| 12 \|\|*

*mṛgottamāṅge daśanā murāreḥ saṃpūjanīyā haraye namaste \|*  
*namaḥ savitre rasanāṃ śaṃkare ca nāsābhipūjyā ca punarvasau ca \|\| 13 \|\|*

*lalāṭamambhoruhavallabhāya puṣye 'lakā vedaśarīradhāriṇe \|*  
*sārpe 'tha mauliṃ vibudhapriyāya maghāsu karṇāviti gogaṇeśe \|\| 14 \|\|*

*pūrvāsu gobrāhmaṇavandanāya netrāṇi saṃpūjyatamāni śambhoḥ \|*  
*athottarāphalgunibhe bhruvau ca viśveśvarāyeti ca pūjanīye \|\| 15 \|\|*

6-15. There is absolutely no difference between Shiva and the Sun, and consequently, the devotee. when worshipping the Shiva, uses the mantras addressed to the Sun. They are as follows: —

With (1) Suryaya namah, let him adore the feet of the image, along with Hasta asterism; With (2) Arkaya namah, the ankles, with Chitra asterism; With (3) Purushottamaya namah, the Shanks, along with Svati asterism; With (4) Dhatre nama, the region of the knees, along with Vishakha With (5) Sahasra Bhinave namah, the two thighs should be worshipped along with Anuradha asterism; With (6) Anaigaya namah, the generative organ, along with Jyeshtha asterism; With (7) Indraya Somaya namah, the waist, along with Mula asterism; With (8) Tvashtre Saptaturamgamaya namah, the navel, along with Purva and Uttara Asadha asterism; With (9) Tikshnamshave namah, the arm-pits, along with Shravana asterism; With (10) Vikartanaya namah, on the back, with the asterism Dhanishtha; With (11) Dhvantavindshanaya namah, in the eyes, with the Satabhisha asterism; With (12) Chandakraya namah, on the arms, along with Parva and Uttarabhadrapada asterisms; With (13) Samnamadhisaya namah, the two hands, along with Revati asterism; With (14) Saptvasvadhurandharaya namah, the nails, along with Ashvini asterism; With (15) Kathoradhamne namah, on the throat, along with Bharani asterism; With (16) Divakaraya namah, on the neck, with the Krittika asterism; With (17) Ambujesiya namah, on the lips, with the Rohini asterism; With (18) Haraye namah, on the teeth, with Mrigashira asterism; With (19) Savitre namah, the tongue, along with Ardra asterism; With (20) Shamkareya namah, in the nose, along with Punarvasu asterism; With (21) Ambhoruvallabheya namah, on the forehead, along with Pushya asterism; With (22) Vedashariradhdrine namah, on the crown of the head, along with the asterism Ashlesha; With (23) Vibudhapriydya namah, the ears, along with Magha asterism; With (24) Gobrahmanavandanaya namah, the eyes, along with Purvaphalguni asterism; With (25) Vishveshvaraya namah, the eye-brows, along with the Uttaraphalguni asterism.

## \|\| 55.16 \|\|

*namo 'stu pāśāṅkuśaśūlapadma-kapālasarpendudhanurdharāya \|*  
*gajāsurānaṅgapurāndhakādi-vināśamūlāya namaḥ śivāya \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Afterwards the devotee should pray to Shiva: ‘“O, Lord! armed with a noose, a hook, a trident, a lotus, a human skull; and the wearer of the snake and the moon and the bow, I salute Thee. O Lord! the destructor of Gaja, Demons, Cupid and Pura and Andhaka, etc., I salute Thee”.

## \|\| 55.17 \|\|

*ityādi cāstrāṇi ca pūjya nityaṃ viśveśvarāyeti śivo 'bhipūjyaḥ \|*  
*bhoktavyamatraivamatailaśākam amāṃsamakṣāramabhuktaśeṣam \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. The worshipper should also worship the different weapons (mentioned above), and should salute the Lord by bowing down his head, with the mantra Vishveshvaraya namah, and every day abstain from oil, flesh, green vegetables and salt, and eat moderately.

## \|\| 55.18-19 \|\|

*ityevaṃ dvija naktāni kṛtvā dadyāt punarvasau \|*  
*śāleyataṇḍulaprastham audumbaramaye ghṛtam \|\| 18 \|\|*

*saṃsthāpya pātre viprāya sahiraṇyaṃ nivedayet \|*  
*saptame vastraugmaṃ ca pāraṇe tvadhikaṃ bhavet \|\| 19 \|\|*

18-19. After thus taking his meals in the night, the devotee, on the Punarvasu asterism day, should put some rice, along with some ghee, in a vessel made of fig-leaves, And should then give it away to the Brahmana, after putting some gold in it. Then, on the seventh day of the fast, he should give to the Brahmana a couple of raiments

## \|\| 55.20 \|\|

*caturdaśe tu samprāpte pāraṇe nāradābdike \|*  
*brāhmaṇānbhojayedbhaktyā guḍakṣīraghṛtādibhiḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. On the day of the fourteenth repast after the fast, the worshipper should feed the Brahmanas with raw-sugar, milk and clarified butter.

## \|\| 55.21-25 \|\|

*kṛtvā tu kāñcanaṃ padmam aṣṭapattraṃ sakarṇikam \|*  
*śuddhamaṣṭāṅgulaṃ tacca padmarāgadalānvitam \|\| 21 \|\|*

*śayyāṃ vilakṣaṇāṃ kṛtvā viruddhagranthivarjitām \|*  
*sopadhānakaviśrāma-svāstaravyajanāni ca \|\| 22 \|\|*

*bhājanopānahachattra-cāmarāsanadarpaṇaiḥ \|*  
*bhūṣaṇairapi saṃyuktāṃ phalavastrānulepanaiḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

*tasyāṃ vidhāya tatpadmam alaṃkṛtya guṇānvitam \|*  
*kapilāṃ vastrasaṃyuktāṃ suśīlāṃ ca payasvinīm \|\| 24 \|\|*

*raupyakhurīṃ hemaśṛṅgīṃ savatsāṃ kāṃsyadohanām \|*  
*dadyānmantreṇa pūrvāhṇe na caināmabhilaṅghayet \|\| 25 \|\|*

21-25. And after that, he should get a golden lotus, eight fingers in length, made with eight leaves and studded with gems, and -bedecking it with nice cloth, should give it away to a Brahmana, along with bedsheet, pillow, utensils, shoes, chamara, a piece of mattress, looking-glass, garments, fruits, incense, bedstead, a cow with its horns covered with gold and hoofs with silver, along with her calf and a vessel of bell-metal for milking the cow. The cow must necessarily be given away on, that occasion.

## \|\| 55.26 \|\|

*yathaivādityaśayanam aśūnyaṃ tava sarvadā \|*  
*kāntyā dhṛtyā śriyā ratyā tathā me santu siddhayaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. These the devotee should pray to the Sun: “God! as Your, house is not benefit of lustre, fortune and prosperity, similarly let mine be also in the enjoyment of same blessings.

## \|\| 55.27 \|\|

*yathā na devāḥ śreyāṃsaṃ tvadanyamanaghaṃ viduḥ \|*  
*tathā mām uddharāśeṣa-duḥkhasaṃsārasāgarāt \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. “Lord! who else is there, excepting Thyself, to grant me prosperity; consequently, be pleased to safely and comfortably see me through this mundane. sea of trials and troubles”

## \|\| 55.28 \|\|

*tataḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya praṇipatya visarjayet \|*  
*śayyāgavādi tatsarvaṃ dvijasya bhavanaṃ nayet \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. After that prayer, the devotee should circumambulate and salute the Deity, and then dismiss the Brahmana and send to his house all the things given in charity. None of them should be kept in the house of the worshipper.

## \|\| 55.29 \|\|

*naitadviśīlāya na dāmbhikāya kutarkaduṣṭāya vinindakāya \|*  
*prakāśanīyaṃ vratamindumauler yaścāpi nindāmadhikāṃ vidhatte \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Nothing should be said about this sacred observance to a blasphemer, to a person of evil conduct, to a hypocrite, or to a false reasoner, for they are liable to profane it — Doing so, would lead to sin.

## \|\| 55.30 \|\|

*bhaktāya dāntāya ca guhyametad ākhyeyam ānandakaraṃ śivasya \|*  
*idaṃ mahāpātakabhin narāṇām apyakṣaraṃ vedavido vadanti \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. The self-controlled and the devout are worthy of being told about the mystery of this observance. Those learned in the Vedas assert that it is the destroyer of all sins and giver of all peace and happiness to men.

## \|\| 55.31 \|\|

*na bandhuputreṇa dhanairviuktaḥ patnībhirānandakaraḥ surāṇām \|*  
*nābhyeti rogaṃ na ca śokaduḥkhaṃ yā vātha nārī kurute 'tibhaktyā \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Those women and men who observe this ordinance with devotion, are never bereft of their sons ani other dear ones. They attain the Divine felicity, and are free from the curse of disease, grief and suffering.

## \|\| 55.32 \|\|

*idaṃ vasiṣṭhena purārjunena kṛtaṃ kubereṇa puraṃdareṇa \|*  
*yatkīrtanenāpyakhilāni nāśam āyānti pāpāni na saṃśayo 'sti \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. This ordinance was at first observed by Vasishtha, Arjuna, Kuvera and Indra. The mere recitation of this liberates one from all sins.

## \|\| 55.33 \|\|

*iti paṭhati śṛṇoti vā ya itthaṃ raviśayanaṃ puruhūtavallabhaḥ syāt \|*  
*api narakagatānpitrin aśeṣān api divamānayatīha yaḥ karoti \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. fortes One who reads or hears about this Ravi Sayana observance, endears himself to Indra and helps his deceased manes to go to heaven from hell.

## Chapter 56

## \|\| 56.1-6 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca*  
*kṛṣṇāṣṭamīmatho vakṣye sarvapāpapraṇāśinīm \|*  
*śāntirmuktiśca bhavati jayaḥ puṃsāṃ viśeṣataḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*śaṃkaraṃ mārgaśirasi śambhuṃ pauṣe 'bhipūjayet \|*  
*māghe maheśvaraṃ devaṃ mahādevaṃ ca phālgune \|\| 2 \|\|*

*sthāṇuṃ caitre śivaṃ tadvad vaiśākhe tvarcayennaraḥ \|*  
*jyeṣṭhe paśupatiṃ cārced āṣāḍhe ugramarcayet \|\| 3 \|\|*

*pūjayecchrāvaṇe śarvaṃ nabhasye tryambakaṃ tathā \|*  
*haramāśvauje māsi tatheśānaṃ ca kārttike \|\| 4 \|\|*

*kṛṣṇāṣṭamīṣu sarvāsu śaktaḥ sampūjayeddvijān \|*  
*gobhūhiraṇyavāsobhiḥ śivabhaktānupoṣitaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*gomūtraghṛtagokṣīra-tilān yavakuśodakam \|*  
*gośṛṅgodaśirīṣārka-bilvapattradadhīni ca \|*  
*pañcagavyaṃ ca saṃprāṣya śaṃkaraṃ pūjayenniśi \|\| 6 \|\|*

1-6. The adorable Shiva said: — I shall now explain to you about the Krishnashtami Vrata (ordinance) which is the destroyer of all evils. This fast gives victory, peace and emancipation to men.

Shankara should be worshipped on the eighth day of the dark fortnight in the month of Margashirsha, Shambhu, on the corresponding day of Pausha, Maheshvara in Magha, Mahadeva in Phalguna, Sthanu in Chaitra, Shiva in Vaishakha, Pashupati in Jyaishtha, Ugra in Ashadha, Sarva in Shravana, Trayambaka in Bhadra, Hara in the month of Ashvina, Ishana in Kartika, These pujas should be performed every month, on all the 8th days of the dark fortnight. The devotee should worship the Brahmanas,’ and should observe a fast after giving away cow, land, gold and. cloth to them, especially to the devotees of Shiva. In the night time, Shiva should be worshipped with Panchagavya and with urine of the cow, clarified-butter, cow’s milk, sesamum, barley, Kusha grass, water, the water of the washing of the cows’ horns, the leaves of Shirisha, arka (Calatropis gigantea), leaves of Bilva (aegle marmelos) and curds.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — Panchagavaya — Five products of the. cow, taken collectively; i.e. milk, curds, clarified butter, urine and cowduing.

## \|\| 56.7-9 \|\|

*aśvatthaṃ ca vaṭaṃ caivo-dumbaraṃ plakṣameva ca \|*  
*palāśaṃ jambuvṛkṣaṃ ca viduḥ ṣaṣṭhaṃ maharṣayaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*mārgaśīrṣāṣāḍhamāsābhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ dvābhyāmitikramāt \|*  
*ekaikaṃ dantapavanaṃ vṛkṣeṣveteṣu bhakṣayet \|\| 8 \|\|*

*devāya dadyādarghyaṃ ca kṛṣṇāṃ gāṃ kṛṣṇavāsasam \|*  
*dadyātsamāpte dadhyannaṃ vitānadhvajacāmaram \|\| 9 \|\|*

7-9. The worshipper should feast the learned and the pious, from Margashirsha after an interval of two months, under the following trees: — ashvatha (the holy fig-tree:, vata (the banyan tree), ulumbara (Ficus glomerata), plaksha (the rose-apple), palasha (butea frondosa), jambu (eugenia jambolana); and he should use the tooth-brush made of these trees to cleanse his teeth on those days. An offering of arghya water and black cloth and black cow should be made to the Deity, and at the conclusion of the fast, curds, grain, canopy, flags and chamara, &c., should be given away in charity.

## \|\| 56.10-11 \|\|

*dvijānāmudakumbhāṃśca pañcaratnasamanvitān \|*  
*gāvaḥ kṛṣṇāḥ suvarṇaṃ ca vāsāṃsi vividhāni ca \|*  
*aśaktastu punardadyād gāmekāmapi śaktitaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*na vittaśāṭhyaṃ kurvīta kurvandoṣamavāpnuyāt \|*  
*kṛṣṇāṣṭamīmupoṣyaiva saptakalpaśatatrayam \|*  
*pumānsampūjito devaiḥ śivaloke mahīyate \|\| 11 \|\|*

10-11. Brahmanas should he given the five gems, along with a vase of water and a black cow, gold and different kinds of cloths. If the worshipper be not a position to give away all that, le should give a cow at all events. Close-fistedness should not be exercised in charity, for it leads to sin. One who observes the Krishnashtami fast according to the rules laid down, enjoys happiness after being venerated by the Devas, for 307 kalpas, in the region of Shiva.

## Chapter 57

## \|\| 57.1 \|\|

*Matsya-Purāṇa 57*  
*nārada uvāca*  
*dīrghāurārogyakulābhivṛddhi-yuktaḥ pumānbhūpakulāutaḥ syāt \|*  
*muhurmuhurjanmani yena samyag vrataṃ samācakṣva tadindumaule \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Narada said: — “O Lord! with moon as thy crest-jewel, pray tell me all about the ordinance, the observance of which begets long life, health, fecundity of the race, kingdom, in several successive lives”.

## \|\| 57.2 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca*  
*tvayā pṛṣṭamidaṃ samyag uktaṃ cākṣayyakārakam \|*  
*rahasyaṃ tava vakṣyāmi yatpurāṇavido viduḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. The Lord Shiva said: — Narada! I have already explained to you about the ordinance that confers everlasting blessing on the devotee, and I shall now also explain to you more clearly about it, as described by those learned in the Puranas.

## \|\| 57.3 \|\|

*rohiṇīcandraśayanaṃ nāma vratamihottamam \|*  
*tasminnārāyaṇasyārcām arcayad indunāmabhiḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Rohinichandra Sayanavrata is most sacred. The devotee should worship, the image of Narayana, after reciting the names of the moon in observing it.

## \|\| 57.4-5 \|\|

*yadā somadine śuklā bhavetpañcadaśī kvacit \|*  
*athavā brahmanakṣatraṃ paurṇamāsyāṃ prajāyate \|\| 4 \|\|*

*tadā snānaṃ naraḥ kuryāt pañcagavyena sarṣapaiḥ \|*  
*āpyāyasveti tu japed vidvānaṣṭaśataṃ punaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. When the full moon day falls on Monday, or when the Rohini asterism falls on the fall moon day; the learned should bathe with panchagavya and mustard, and, after that, should ‘recite “Apyasva” Mantra for a hundred and eight times.

## \|\| 57.6 \|\|

*śūdro 'pi parayā bhaktyā pāṣaṇḍālāpavarjitaḥ \|*  
*somāya varadāyātha viṣṇave ca namo namaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. The Shudra also may observe this Vrata with extreme devotion, freeing himself from the company of all unbelievers, and should devoutly salute the Gods, Moon and Vishnu, with the following mantra, instead of the Vedic one: — Somaya Varadayatha Vishnave cha namo namah.

## \|\| 57.7 \|\|

*kṛtajapyaḥ svabhavanam āgatya madhusūdanam \|*  
*pūjayetphalapuṣpaiśca somanāmāni kīrtayan \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. After finishing his bath and the recitation (japa) of the mantra, he should return to his house and. worship Madhusudana, by offering fruits and flowers and singing the names of Moon (Soma), as given below.

## \|\| 57.8 \|\|

*somāya śāntāya namo 'stu pādāv anantadhāmneti ca jānujaṅghe \|*  
*ūrudvayaṃ cāpi jalodarāya sampūjayenmeḍhramanantabāhave \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. After reciting (1) ... Somaya Santaya namah, should be worshipped the feet (of the Divine image), and after reciting (2) .... Anantadhamne namah, should be worshipped the shanks and knees, after reciting (3) .... Jalodaraya namah, the two thighs, and after reciting (4) .... Anautabahve namah, the organ of generation.

## \|\| 57.9 \|\|

*namo namaḥ kāmasukhapradāya kaṭiḥ śaśāṅkasya sadārcanīyā \|*  
*tathodaraṃ cāpyamṛtodarāya nābhiḥ śaśāṅkāya namo 'bhipūjyā \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. After reciting (5) .... Kamiya sukhapradaya namah, the waist of the moon should be worshipped. After reciting (6) .... Amritodaraya namah the stomach, after reciting (7) ... Shashankaya namah, the navel should be worshipped.

## \|\| 57.10 \|\|

*namo 'stu candrāya mukhaṃ ca pūjyaṃ dantā dvijānāmadhipāya pūjyāḥ \|*  
*hāsyaṃ namaścandramase 'bhipūjyam oṣṭhau kumudvantavanapriyāya \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. After reciting (8) …. Chandriya namah, the mouth should be worshipped, after recitind (9) ... Dwijadhipaya namah, the teeth, after reciting (10) ... Chandramase namah, the face (hasyam), after reciting (11) .... Kunudvantavana priydya namah, the lips.

## \|\| 57.11 \|\|

*nāsā ca nāthāya vanauṣadhīnām ānandabhūtāya punarbhruvau ca \|*  
*netradvayaṃ padmanibhaṃ tathendor indīvaraśyāmakarāya śaureḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. After reciting (12) .... Vanausadhinasaya namah, the nose, after reciting (13) ..... Anandabhateya nama, the brows, after reciting (14) .... Indivarasyamakacaya namah, the eyes like lotus.

## \|\| 57.12 \|\|

*namaḥ samastādhvaravanditāya karṇadvayaṃ daityaniṣūdanāya \|*  
*lalāṭamindorudadhipriyāya keśāḥ suṣumnādhipateḥ prapūjyāḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. After reciting (15) ..... Samastadhvaravanditaya namah and ... Daityanisudanaya hamah, the two ears, after reciting (16) …. Udadhipriyaya namah, the forehead, and after reciting (17) ... Susumnadhipataye namah, the hair.

## \|\| 57.16 \|\|

*kadambanīlotpalaketakāni jātī sarojaṃ śatapattrikā ca \|*  
*amlānakubjānyatha sinduvāraṃ puṣpaṃ punarnārada mallikāyāḥ \|*  
*śubhraṃ ca viṣṇoḥ karavīrapuṣpaṃ śrīcampakaṃ candramasaḥ pradeyam \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. After reciting (18) ... Shashamkaya namah, the head of Murari, after reciting (19) ... Visheshvaraya namah, the coronet (of the Divine image), Rohini should also be worshipped. The devotee, by praying: “O, Robin, the beloved of the Lord, also known under the name of Lakshmi, O blessed one,” should, offer sweet-smelling flowers, incense and eatables, etc., and sleep on the floor in course of the night on getting up early in the morning, and after taking his bath, he should offer a vase of water, gold and eatables to the Brahmana, with the mantra ... and then hear the recitation of some sacred book (itihasa), for a couple of muhurtas (96 minutes), after taking twenty-eight morse is of food with clarified butter, milk and urine of the cow, but devoid of flesh and salt. —

Then he should worship the Moon and Vishnu with Kadamba, bluelotus, Ketaki, jasmine, lotus, sevatt, kuvaja, white kannair and champaka.

## \|\| 57.17 \|\|

*śrāvaṇādiṣu māseṣu kramādetāni sarvadā \|*  
*yasminmāse vratādiḥ syāt tatpuṣpairarcayeddharim \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Hari should be worshiped with all the various kinds of flowers that bloom in various months, from the beginning of the month of Shravana.

## \|\| 57.18 \|\|

*evaṃ saṃvatsaraṃ yāvad upāsya vidhivannaraḥ \|*  
*vratānte śayanaṃ dadyād darpaṇopaskarānvitam \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. In this way, the devotee should go on with the worship, according to the prescribed rites till the end of the year, after which he should give away a bedstead, along with a mirror and other things in charity.

## \|\| 57.19-20 \|\|

*rohiṇīcandramithunaṃ kārayitvātha kāñcanam \|*  
*candraḥ ṣaḍaṅgulaḥ kāryo rohiṇī caturaṅgulā \|\| 19 \|\|*

*muktāphalāṣṭakautaṃ sitanetrapaṭāvṛtam \|*  
*kṣīrakumbhopari punaḥ kāṃsyapātrākṣatānvitam \|*  
*dadyānmantreṇa pūrvāhṇe śālīkṣuphalasaṃyutam \|\| 20 \|\|*

19-20. Then he should make an image of Rohini and the Moon in gold. The image of the latter should be six fingers in length and that of the former four fingers. And he should give them away to a good Brahmana, along with eight white pearls, white cloths, milk, some utensil of bell, metal, rice, raw sugar, sugar-cane and fruits.

## \|\| 57.21 \|\|

*śvetāmatha suvarṇāsyāṃ khurai raupyaiḥ samanvitām \|*  
*savastrabhājanāṃ dhenuṃ tathā śaṅkhaṃ ca śobhanam \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. He should also give away after that, a white cow, with its horns plaited with gold and hoofs covered with silver and its back covered with a cloth, along with utensils and a couch.

## \|\| 57.22 \|\|

*bhūṣaṇairdvijadāmpatyam alaṃkṛtya guṇānvitam \|*  
*candro 'yaṃ dvijarūpeṇa sabhārya iti kalpayet \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Afterwards, the worshipper should bedeck the Brahmana along with his consort with fine clothes, &c., and should look upon him as the moon in company of Rohini.

## \|\| 57.23 \|\|

*yathā na rohiṇī kṛṣṇa śayyāṃ saṃtyajya gacchati \|*  
*somarūpasya te tadvan mamābhedo 'stu bhūtibhiḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. And he should then pray, “O Lord! as Rohini shines in Thy house, go, let my house, too, be full of Iustre.

## \|\| 57.24 \|\|

*yathā tvameva sarveṣāṃ paramānandamuktidaḥ \|*  
*bhuktirmuktistathā bhaktis tvayi candrāstu me sadā \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Lord Moon! as you bring happiness and emancipation to all, be merciful enough to shower the same blessings on me; and let my devotion in you always remain firm.”

## \|\| 57.25 \|\|

*iti saṃsārabhītasya muktikāmasya cānagha \|*  
*rūpārogyāuṣāmetad vidhāyakamanuttamam \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. “O Lord Moon, grant me health and prosperity. I am afraid of this world, and desire bliss at your hands”.

## \|\| 57.26 \|\|

*idameva pitriṇāṃ ca sarvadā vallabhaṃ mune \|*  
*trailokyādhipatirbhūtvā saptakalpaśatatrayam \|*  
*candralokamavāpnoti vidyudbhūtvā tu mucyate \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. This ordinance is very dear to the Pitris, and the observer of it attains the region of the moon, after being the lord of the three worlds for 307 Kalpas, and then gets final rest.

## \|\| 57.27 \|\|

*nārī vā rohiṇī candra-śayanaṃ yā samācaret \|*  
*sāpi tatphalamāpnoti punarāvṛttidurlabham \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. The women folk, observing this fast, beget the same fruits, and are liberated from the cycle of births.

## \|\| 57.28 \|\|

*iti paṭhati śṛṇoti vā ya itthaṃ madhumathanārcanam indukīrtanena \|*  
*matimapi ca dadāti so 'pi śaurer bhavanagataḥ paripūjyate 'maraughaiḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. One who reads or listens to this form of ordinance, gets pure intellect and goes to heaven where he is venerated by the Devas

## Chapter 58

## \|\| 58.1-2 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*jalāśayagataṃ viṣṇum uvāca ravinandanaḥ \|*  
*taḍāgārāmakūpānāṃ vāpīṣu nalinīṣu ca \|\| 1 \|\|*

*vidhiṃ pṛcchāmi deveśe devatāyataneṣu ca \|*  
*ke tatra cartvijo nātha vedī vā kīdṛśī bhavet \|\| 2 \|\|*

1-2.
