Suta said: — The King Vaivasvata Manu asked the Lord, who was lying in the water in the form of fish, to explain to him when should the sacrifice be performed and what feasts should be employed therein, and what kind of altar should be made for the occasion to consecrate a newly built tank, well and pool, grove and temple.

## \|\| 58.3 \|\|

*dakṣiṇāvalayaḥ kālaḥ sthānamācārya eva ca \|*  
*dravyāṇi kāni śastāni sarvamācakṣva tattvataḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. He also asked the Lord to explain what fees to the officiating priest, and Sacred offerings to the Deity should then be made. What are the proper time and place for this observance, and what preceptor should be appointed

## \|\| 58.4-5 \|\|

*matsya uvāca*  
*śṛṇu rājanmahābāho taḍāgādiṣu yo vidhiḥ \|*  
*purāṇeṣvitihāso 'yaṃ paṭhyate vedavādibhiḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*prāpya pakṣaṃ śubhaṃ śuklam atīte cottarāyaṇe \|*  
*puṇye 'hni viprakathite kṛtvā brāhmaṇavācanam \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. The Lord Fish said: — Hear, O Mighty-armed, the rules about tanks, etc., as laid down in the Itihasa and the Puranas, by knowers of the Vada. At the end of the summer solstice, the man performing the ceremony should get the preparatory rites to the observance performed in an auspicious bright fortnight, after consulting a Brahmana,

## \|\| 58.6 \|\|

*prāgudakpravaṇe deśe taḍāgasya samīpataḥ \|*  
*caturhastāṃ śubhāṃ vedīṃ caturasrāṃ caturmukhām \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. After that, he should get a nice Vedi (square altar), measuring fourhande in length, with four openings made, near the tank, etc., to be consecrated, in the north-eastern direction.

## \|\| 58.7-8 \|\|

*tathā ṣoḍaśahastaḥ syān maṇḍapaśca caturmukhaḥ \|*  
*vedyāśca parito gartā ratnimātrāstrimekhalāḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*nava saptātha vā pañca nātiriktā nṛpātmaja \|*  
*vitastimātrā yoniḥ syāt ṣaṭsaptāṅgulivistṛtā \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8. A pandal (mandapa, measuring sixteen hands, with four openings should also be made, and then around the altar should be made pits (gartas); five, seven or nine, but not more in number, one cubit deep and three circles round them. The receptacle (yoni: of the altar should be one span long and six or seven fingers broad

**Комментарий:**

Note: — Vitasti = A measure of length equal to 12 fingers (being the distance between The extended thumb and the little finger.)

## \|\| 58.9 \|\|

*gartāśca tatra sapta syus triparvocchritamekhalāḥ \|*  
*sarvatastu savarṇāḥ syuḥ patākādhvajasaṃyutāḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The gartas or pits should be seven in number, and the circles should, be three inches (parvas i.e., digits) in height. Flags and buntings of the same colour should be on all sides

## \|\| 58.10 \|\|

*aśvatthodumbaraplakṣa-vaṭaśākhākṛtāni tu \|*  
*maṇḍapasya pratidiśaṃ dvārāṇyetāni kārayet \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. In all the four directions of the pandal, arches of the twings of the Ashvatha, Udumbara, Plaksha and Vata trees, should be made

## \|\| 58.11 \|\|

*śubhāstatrāṣṭa hotāro dvārapālāstathāṣṭa vai \|*  
*aṣṭau tu jāpakāḥ kāryā brāhmaṇā vedapāragāḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Then eight Brahmanas, versed in the Vedas, should be employed as sacrificial priests (hota), eight as warders and another eight as Japakas.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — Japakas = Ono who mutters pagers.

## \|\| 58.12 \|\|

*sarvalakṣaṇasampūrṇo mantravidvijitendriyaḥ \|*  
*kulaśīlasamāuktaḥ purodhāḥ syāddvijottamaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. The Brahmana who has all the virtues in him, who is able to restrain his passions and knows the mantras, is calm and belongs to a good family, should be chosen to perform the functions of the priest (Purohita)

## \|\| 58.14 \|\|

*tatastvanekavarṇāḥ syuś caravaḥ pratidaivatam \|*  
*ācāryaḥ prakṣipedbhūmāv anumantrya vicakṣaṇaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Water-pot and materials of sacrifice should be placed at each of the gartas (pits), after which a fall and a white chamara should be placed.

Afterwards, the family guru (Acharya) should scatter on, the ground the different kinds of boiled rice and barley for presentation to the Gods, after reciting the Vedic text.

## \|\| 58.15 \|\|

*tryaratnimātro yūpaḥ syāt kṣāravṛkṣavinirmitaḥ \|*  
*yajamānapramāṇo vā saṃsthāpyo bhūtimicchatā \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. The sacrificial posts should be made of the glomerous fig, measuring three cubits, with closed fist, in length, of the hand of the sacrificer, It is also auspicious to get them made of the size of the worshipper.

## \|\| 58.16-17 \|\|

*hemālaṃkāriṇaḥ kāryāḥ pañcaviṃśatiṛtvijaḥ \|*  
*kuṇḍalāni ca haimāni keyūrakaṭakāni ca \|\| 16 \|\|*

*tathāṅgulyaḥ pavitrāṇi vāsāṃsi vividhāni ca \|*  
*pūjayettu samaṃ sarvān ācāryo dviguṇaṃ punaḥ \|*  
*dadyācchayanasaṃyuktam ātmanaścāpi yatpriyam \|\| 17 \|\|*

16-17. Twenty-five Ritvijas (the eight Hotas, eight Dvarapalas, eight Japakas and one Purohita), arrayed in ornaments of gold, should be presented with golden ear-rings, armlets, rings and different kinds of cloths, without making any difference between them. But the family (Acharya) should be worshipped with double the number of things offered to the Ritvijas. After that, the worshipper should give away in charity the things liked by him the best, along with a bedstead.

## \|\| 58.18 \|\|

*sauvarṇakūrmamakarau rājatau matsyadundubhau \|*  
*tāmrau kulīramaṇḍūkāv āyasaḥ śiśumārakaḥ \|*  
*evamāsādya tatsarvam ādāveva viśāṃ pate \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. The turtle and the crocodile should be made of gold, the fish and the unvenomous water-snake should be of. silver, the frog and the crab of copper, and the Shishumara (porpoise) fish of iron, All these things should be prepared from before, O Lord of men.

## \|\| 58.19-20 \|\|

*śuklamālyāmbaradharaḥ śuklagandhānulepanaḥ \|*  
*sarvauṣadhyudakaistatra snāpito vedapāragaiḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

*yajamānaḥ sapatnīkaḥ putrapautrasamanvitaḥ \|*  
*paścimaṃ dvāramāsādya praviśedyāgamaṇḍapam \|\| 20 \|\|*

19-20. ‘Then the worshipper (yajamana), bathed in the water of different herbs, according to the Vedic injunctions, by those Veda-knowing priests, should enter the sacred pavilion, wearing a garland of white flowers, white garments and smeared with white sandal paste, through the western arch, in company of his consort, sons and grandsons, etc.

## \|\| 58.21 \|\|

*tato maṅgalaśabdena bherīṇāṃ niḥsvanena ca \|*  
*añjasā maṇḍalaṃ kuryāt pañcavarṇena tattvavit \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Then the learned should draw up a ring with powders of five colors by uttering auspicious sound, while the music of drums is playing.

## \|\| 58.22 \|\|

*ṣoḍaśāraṃ tataścakraṃ padmagarbhaṃ caturmukham \|*  
*caturasraṃ ca parito vṛttaṃ madhye suśobhanam \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Then a circle should be made, with sixteen spokes in it, and in the centre a figure of a beautiful lotus of four leaves should be made.

## \|\| 58.23 \|\|

*vedyāścopari tatkṛtvā grahāṃllokapatīṃstataḥ \|*  
*vinyasenmantrataḥ sarvān pratidikṣu vicakṣaṇaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Afterwards, images of the planets and the regents of the world should be established in the proper directions on the different altars, after reciting the Vedic hymns (prescribed for the occasion).

## \|\| 58.24 \|\|

*kūrmādi sthāpayenmadhye vāruṇaṃ mantramāśritaḥ \|*  
*brahmāṇaṃ ca śivaṃ viṣṇuṃ tatraiva sthāpayedbudhaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Then, images of the turtle and other water animals should be established in the middle, after reciting the hymns of Varuna (the God of waters), and afterwards images of the Deities, Brahma, Shiva and Vishnu, should be established.

## \|\| 58.25 \|\|

*vināyakaṃ ca vinyasya kamalāmambikāṃ tathā \|*  
*śāntyarthaṃ sarvalokānāṃ bhūtagrāmaṃ nyasettataḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. After establishing the images of Ganesha, Lakshmi and Ambika, and for the peace of the Universe, the images of the group of the Bhutas should be established.

## \|\| 58.26 \|\|

*puṣpabhakṣyaphalairyuktam evaṃ kṛtvādhivāsanam \|*  
*kumbhān sajalagarbhāṃstān vāsobhiḥ pariveṣṭayet \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Then the pitchers full of water should be covered with clothes, in cenced with, the odour of flowers and fruits.

## \|\| 58.27 \|\|

*puṣpagandhairalaṃkṛtya dvārapālānsamantataḥ \|*  
*paṭhadhvamiti tānbrūyād ācāryastvabhipūjayet \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. After garlanding the warders and pasting sandal paste of them, the Acharya priest should ask the warders (the Dvarapala priests) by saying "pathadvam" to chant the Veda.

## \|\| 58.28 \|\|

*bahvṛcau pūrvataḥ sthāpyau dakṣiṇena yajurvidau \|*  
*sāmagau paścime tadvad uttareṇa tvatharvaṇau \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. In the east should be seated the Vahavrichas (the two priests versed in the Rigveda), in the south the two Dvarapalas (learned in the Yajur-veda), in the west the two Dvarapalas (learned in the Samveda), and in the north, similarly, the two Dvarapalas (learned in the Atharva-Veda).

## \|\| 58.29-30 \|\|

*udaṅmukho dakṣiṇato yajamāna upāviśet \|*  
*yajadhvamiti tānbrūyād dhautrikānpunareva tu \|\| 29 \|\|*

*utkṛṣṭānmantrajāpena tiṣṭhadhvamiti jāpakān \|*  
*evamādiṣya tānsarvān paryukṣyāgniṃ sa mantravit \|\| 30 \|\|*

29-30. The worshipper should seat himself on the south side, facing the north and the Acharya should ask the eight (Hota) priests “Yajadhvam” to commence the sacrifice; and to the skillful Japakas he should say “tishthadvam” (to sit down). Thus directing them, the Acharya, versed in the sacred text, should sprinkle water silently round the fire without uttering any ritual formula

## \|\| 58.31 \|\|

*juhuyādvāruṇairmantrair ājyaṃ ca samidhastathā \|*  
*ṛtvigbhiścātha hotavyaṃ vāruṇaireva sarvataḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Sacrificial fuel and clarified butter should be offered to the Fire, after reciting the hymns of Varuna, and the sacrificing priests should also, be made to do the same all round.

## \|\| 58.32 \|\|

*grahebhyo vidhivaddhutvā tathendrāyeśvarāya ca \|*  
*marudbhyo lokapālebhyo vidhivadviśvakarmaṇe \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Afterwards according to the prescribed rites, offerings should be made to the planets, Indra, Ishvara, Maruts, Lokapalas and Vishvakarma.

## \|\| 58.33-34 \|\|

*rātrisūktaṃ ca raudraṃ ca pāvamānaṃ sumaṅgalam \|*  
*japeuḥ pauruṣaṃ sūktaṃ pūrvato bahvṛcaḥ pṛthak \|\| 33 \|\|*

*śākraṃ raudraṃ ca saumyaṃ ca kūṣmāṇḍaṃ jātavedasam \|*  
*saurasūktaṃ japenmantraṃ dakṣiṇena yajurvidaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

33-34. Then the knowers of the Rigveda, seated in the east, should separately mutter the formulae of Ratrisukta, Rudrasukta, the auspicious Pavamanasukta, and Purushasukta; in the same way the Dvarapalas, the Yajurveda, seated in the south, should separately mutter peor of Indra, Rudra, Soma, Kushmanda, Fire (Jatavedas), and mead.

## \|\| 58.35-36 \|\|

*vairājyaṃ pauruṣaṃ sūktaṃ sauvarṇaṃ rudrasaṃhitām \|*  
*śaiśavaṃ pañcanidhanaṃ gāyatraṃ jyeṣṭhasāma ca \|\| 35 \|\|*

*vāmadevyaṃ bṛhatsāma rauravaṃ sarathaṃtaram \|*  
*gavāṃ vrataṃ ca kāṇvaṃ ca rakṣoghnaṃ vayasastathā \|*  
*gāyeuḥ sāmagā rājan paścimaṃ dvāramāśritāḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

35-36. Similarly, the Dvarapalas, the chanters of the Samveda, seated in the west should chant the hymns of Vairajya, Paurushasukta, Suvarna, Rudra Samhita, Shaishava, Panchanidhans, Gayatrisukta, Jyestha Sima, Vamadevya, Brihatasama, Raurava, Rathantara, Kanva, Gavam Vratam; Raksoghna and Vayas.

## \|\| 58.37 \|\|

*atharvaṇaścottarataḥ śāntikaṃ pauṣṭikaṃ tathā \|*  
*japeurmanasā devam āśritya varuṇaṃ prabhum \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Afterwards, the learned (Dvarapalas) in the Atharva Veda, seated in the north, meditating on Varuna, should devoutly mutter the formulae of the Shantikas and the Paushtikas.

## \|\| 58.38 \|\|

*pūrvedyuramito rātrāv evaṃ kṛtvādhivāsanam \|*  
*gajāśvarathyāvalmīkāt saṃgamāddhradagokulāt \|*  
*mṛdamādāya kumbheṣu prakṣipeccatvarāttathā \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. After performing the above-mentioned ceremonies on the first day, adhivasana should be done, and then the earth of the following laces, viz., Elephant ward, stable, well, lane, pool, cattle-shed, ant-hill, the place where four streets meet, should be put into the pitchers full of water (placed in the pandal).

**Комментарий:**

Notes. — Adhivasana = Scenting with perfumes, (2) Preliminary consecration of an image, its invocation and worship by suitable mantras, before the commencement of a sacrifice, (3) Making a divinity assume its abode in an image.

## \|\| 58.39 \|\|

*rocanāṃ ca sasiddhārthāṃ gandhaṃ guggulameva ca \|*  
*snapanaṃ tasya kartavyaṃ pañcagavyasamanvitam \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Then the worshipper should bathe in the water, incensed with the following things: — the yellow pigment white mustard, sandal paste and resin together with panchagavya (five products of the cow)

## \|\| 58.40-41 \|\|

*pratyekaṃ tu mahāmantrair eva kṛtvā vidhānataḥ \|*  
*evaṃ kṣapātivāhyātha vidhiuktena karmaṇā \|\| 40 \|\|*

*tataḥ prabhāte vimale saṃjāte 'tha śataṃ gavām \|*  
*brāhmaṇebhyaḥ pradātavyam aṣṭaṣaṣṭiśca vā punaḥ \|*  
*pañcāśadvātha ṣaṭtriṃśat pañcaviṃśatirapyatha \|\| 41 \|\|*

40-41. Having thus finished the preliminary rites performed with the utterance of great mantras, with regard to each ceremony, the worshipper should pass the night in sleep. In the morning, the worshipper should give away cows to the Brahmana, i.e., 100 cows or 68 or 50 or 30 or 25.

## \|\| 58.42-43 \|\|

*tataḥ sāṃvatsaraprokte śubhe lagne suśobhane \|*  
*vedaśabdaiśca gāndharvair vādyaiśca vividhaiḥ punaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

*kanakālaṃkṛtāṃ kṛtvā jale gāmavatārayet \|*  
*sāmagāya ca sā deyā brāhmaṇāya viśāṃ pate \|\| 43 \|\|*

42-43. Later on, on some auspicious day and hour, as calculated by the astrologer (Samvatsara), the worshipper should give away after making her pass through the water of the pond, etc., to be consecrated, a cow decked with gold, to the Brahmana versed in the Samaveda, after chanting the text of the Vedas accompanied with music.

## \|\| 58.44-45 \|\|

*pātrīmādāya sauvarṇīṃ pañcaratnasamanvitām \|*  
*tato nikṣipya makara-matsyādīṃścaiva sarvaśaḥ \|*  
*dhṛtāṃ caturvidhair viprair vedavedāṅgapāragaiḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

*mahānadījalopetāṃ dadhyakṣatasamanvitām \|*  
*uttarābhimukhīṃ dhenuṃ jalamadhye tu kārayet \|\| 45 \|\|*

44-45. Afterwards, the worshipper should put, five different kinds of gems on a plate of gold, and give away to the Brahmana, and should place the alligator, fish, &c., in a pond. Then he should worship the abovementioned cow standing in water, held by the Brahmanas versed in all the four Vedas, with the Ganges water, curd and rice, and should afterwards make it swim in the water facing towards the north.

## \|\| 58.46-47 \|\|

*atharvaṇena saṃsnātāṃ punarmāmetyatheti ca \|*  
*āpo hi ṣṭheti mantreṇa kṣiptvāgatya ca maṇḍapam \|\| 46 \|\|*

*pūjayitvā sarastatra baliṃ dadyātsamantataḥ \|*  
*punardināni hotavyaṃ catvāri munisattamāḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

46-47. The cow should then be bathed by reciting the text of the Atharva-Veda, such as punarameti, etc., as well as apohistha, etc., and then the worshipper should return to the circle of priests. Then the. tank should be worshipped and bali offerings should be made on four sides of it.

Afterwards, homa sacrifice should be performed for four days.

## \|\| 58.48 \|\|

*caturthīkarma kartavyaṃ deyā tatrāpi śaktitaḥ \|*  
*dakṣiṇā rājaśārdūla varuṇakṣmāpaṇaṃ tataḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. At the end of these ceremonies the Chaturthi-Karma should be performed, when the worshipper should give dakshina to the Brahmanas, according to his means, and should mutter mantras of Varuna.

## \|\| 58.49 \|\|

*kṛtvā tu yajñapātrāṇi yajñopakaraṇāni ca \|*  
*ṛtvigbhyastu samaṃ dattvā maṇḍapaṃ vibhajetpunaḥ \|*  
*hemapātrīṃ ca śayyāṃ ca sthāpakāya nivedayet \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Then the entire materials employed in the performance of the sacrifice, including the pandal, should be equally distributed to the Ritvijas, and the golden bedstead should be conferred on the chief pries

## \|\| 58.50 \|\|

*tataḥ sahasraṃ viprāṇām athavāṣṭaśataṃ tathā \|*  
*bhojanīyaṃ yathāśakti pañcāśadvātha viṃśatiḥ \|*  
*evameṣa purāṇeṣu taḍāgavidhirucyate \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Afterwards, the worshipper should feast either 1,000, 800, 50 or 20 Brahmanas, according to his means, which is the way of consecrating the tank, as described in the Puranas

## \|\| 58.51 \|\|

*kūpavāpīṣu sarvāsu tathā puṣkariṇīṣu ca \|*  
*eṣa eva vidhirdṛṣṭaḥ pratiṣṭhāsu tathaiva ca \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. And, similarly, it has been laid down for the consecreation of wells pools, small tanks, &c.

## \|\| 58.52 \|\|

*mantratastu viśeṣaḥ syāt prāsādādyānabhūmiṣu \|*  
*ayaṃ tvaśaktāvardhena vidhirdṛṣṭaḥ svayambhuvā \|*  
*alpeṣvekāgnivatkṛtvā vittaśāṭhyādṛte nṛṇām \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. As to the consecration of palaces, groves, lands and buildings, the ritual formulae are somewhat different from the consecration of tanks, Lord Brahma has prescribed these rites for the wealthy. Forty people, in less favourable circumstances, should follow the Ekagni rites, without giving way to miserliness

## \|\| 58.53 \|\|

*prāvṛṭkāle sthite toye hy agniṣṭomaphalaṃ smṛtam \|*  
*śaratkāle sthitaṃ yatsyāt taduktaphaladāyakam \|*  
*vājapeyātirātrābhyāṃ hemante śiśire sthitam \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Consecration of tanks in the rainy seasons and autumn begets the fruit of Agnishtoma sacrifice, and of the Vajapeya and Atiratra sacrifice in the seasons of Hemanta and Shishira.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — Agnishtoma = a protracted ceremony, extending over several days in spring.

Vajapeya = a particular sacrifice, Hemanta = winter season, Shishira = spring season.

## \|\| 58.54 \|\|

*aśvamedhasamaṃ prāhur vasantasamaye sthitam \|*  
*grīṣme 'pi tatsthitaṃ toyaṃ rājasūyādviśiṣyate \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. The consecration in the vernal season (Vasanta) begets the benefit of ashvamedha sacrifices, and of the Rajasuya in the summer season.

## \|\| 58.55 \|\|

*etānmahārāja viśeṣadharmān karoti yo 'pyāgamaśuddhabuddhiḥ \|*  
*sa yāti rudrālayamāśu pūtaḥ kalpānanekāndivi modate ca \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. The Lord has said that one who performs the ceremonies mentioned above; with the mind purified by scriptures and with full faith in them, goes to the region of Shiva and resides in heaven for many ages.

## \|\| 58.56 \|\|

*anekalokānsa mahattamādīn bhuktvā parārdhadvayamaṅganābhiḥ \|*  
*sahaiva viṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padaṃ yat prāpnoti tadyāgaphalena bhūyaḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. Afterwards, that man goes and enjoys in higher regions, and remining there for the full life of Brahma, to the extent of two Parardhas, gets emancipation and enters into the highest stage with Vishnu. And all this he gets through the merit acquired by the performance of this ceremony.

## Chapter 59

## \|\| 59.1-2 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ*  
*pādapānāṃ vidhiṃ sūta yathāvadvistarādvada \|*  
*vidhinā kena kartavyaṃ pādapodyāpanaṃ budhaiḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*ye ca lokāḥ smṛtāsteṣāṃ tānidānīṃ vadasva naḥ \|*  
*yatphalaṃ labhate pretya tatsarvaṃ vaktumarhasi \|\| 2 \|\|*

1-2. The Rishis, — Suta! Tell us in detail the rites which the wise should observe in dedicating and consecrating a tree, and also the region in which he would go after his death.

## \|\| 59.3-4 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*pādapānāṃ vidhiṃ vakṣye tathaivodyānabhūmiṣu \|*  
*taḍāgavidhivatsarvam āsādya jagadīśvara \|\| 3 \|\|*

*ṛtviṅmaṇḍapasambhāraś cācāryaścaiva tadvidhaḥ \|*  
*pūjayedbrāhmaṇāṃstadvad dhemavastrānulepanaiḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

3-4. Suta. — l hall explain to you, O Lord of the world, the rites of dedication as well as those prescribed for the laying out groves. One should follow the rites, as dictated for the consecration of a tank, and should then plant the trees; the Ritvijas, the pavilion and the Acharyas should be arranged in the same way, and the Brahmanas should be adored with sandal paste, &c.

## \|\| 59.5 \|\|

*sarvauṣadhyudakaiḥ siktān piṣṭātakavibhūṣitān \|*  
*vṛkṣānmālyairalaṃkṛtya vāsobhirabhiveṣṭayet \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Afterwards, the trees should be bathed with the water, mingled with all the prescribed medicinal herbs, and then, garlanding them, they should be wrapped with cloth

## \|\| 59.6 \|\|

*sūcyā sauvarṇayā kāryaṃ sarveṣāṃ karṇavedhanam \|*  
*añjanaṃ cāpi dātavyaṃ tadvaddhemaśalākayā \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Then with a needle of gold, the Karnavedha ceremony should be performed on the tree and, similarly, with the same golden stick the eyes of the tree should be painted with black pigment.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — Karnavedha — The piercing of the ear with needle to put on earring.

## \|\| 59.7 \|\|

*phalāni sapta cāṣṭau vā kāladhautāni kārayet \|*  
*pratyekaṃ sarvavṛkṣāṇāṃ vedyāṃ tānyadhivāsayet \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. After that, seven or eight fruits made of gold should be placed on the altars.

## \|\| 59.8 \|\|

*dhūpo 'tra guggulaḥ śreṣṭhas tāmrapātrairadhiṣṭhitān \|*  
*saptadhānyasthitānkṛtvā vastragandhānulepanaiḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. The incense of the resin (guggula) is considered. best on such an occasion. Copper pitchers, full of water, should be placed and worshipped with cloth and incense, &c., after placing corn on them.

## \|\| 59.11 \|\|

*tataḥ śuklāmbaradharāṃ sauvarṇakṛtabhūṣaṇām \|*  
*sakāṃsyadohāṃ sauvarṇa-śṛṅgābhyām atiśālinīm \|*  
*payasvinīṃ vṛkṣamadhyād utsṛjedgāmudaṅmukhīm \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Then the pitchers containing gold, &., inside them, should be Placed close to the trees and sacrifice should be made after which offerings should be made to Indra, Vanaspati, Lokapalas, &., according to the After that a milk cow, covered with a piece of white cloth and wearing. gold ornaments and having, her horns covered with gold, should be let loose between the trees planted, with her face turned towards the north, A milking vessel of bell-metal should also he included among other things to be given away with the cow.

## \|\| 59.12 \|\|

*tato 'bhiṣekamantreṇa vādyamaṅgalagītakaiḥ \|*  
*ṛgyajuḥsāmamantraiśca vāruṇairabhitastathā \|*  
*taireva kumbhaiḥ snapanaṃ kuryādbrāhmaṇapuṃgavaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Then the trees should be watered with (the water contained in) the copper pitchers, alter reciting the Mantras of the Rik, Yaju, and Sama, addressed to Varana, accompanied by music and song.

## \|\| 59.13-14 \|\|

*snātaḥ śuklāmbarastadvad yajamāno 'bhipūjayet \|*  
*gobhir vibhavataḥ sarvān ṛtvijastānsamāhitaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*hemasūtraiḥ sakaṭakair aṅgulīyapavitrakaiḥ \|*  
*vāsobhiḥ śayanīyaiśca tathopaskarapādukaiḥ \|*  
*kṣīreṇa bhojanaṃ dadyād yāvaddinacatuṣṭayam \|\| 14 \|\|*

13-14. Afterwards the worshipper should bathe with water, taken from the above pitchers, and wear white garments, and then with a peaceful ‘mind should confer on the officiating priests the cows, the riches, bedsteads, sacred threads, bracelets, rings of gold, clothes, sandals, along with other things, and feed them on milk for four days.

## \|\| 59.15 \|\|

*homaśca sarṣapaiḥ kāryo yavaiḥ kṛṣṇatilaistathā \|*  
*palāśasamidhaḥ śastāś caturthe 'hni tathotsavaḥ \|*  
*dakṣiṇā ca punastadvad deyā tatrāpi śaktitaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Libations consisting of mustard, barley and black sesamum and wood of butea-frondosa, should be offered in the Fire, and on the fourth day, festivities should be observed and Dakshina should he given to the Brahmanas, according to the means of the worshipper.

## \|\| 59.16 \|\|

*yadyadiṣṭatamaṃ kiṃcit tattad dadyādamatsarī \|*  
*ācārye dviguṇaṃ dadyāt praṇipatya visarjayet \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. The worshipper should also give away with an easy mind other things which he likes, and should salute and dismiss the chief priest (Acharya), after giving him twice as much as he gave to other officiating priests

## \|\| 59.17-20 \|\|

*anena vidhinā yastu kuryādvṛkṣotsavaṃ budhaḥ \|*  
*sarvānkāmānavāpnoti phalaṃ cānantyamaśnute \|\| 17 \|\|*

*yaścaikamapi rājendra vṛkṣaṃ saṃsthāpayennaraḥ \|*  
*so 'pi svarge vasedrājan yāvadindrāutatrayam \|\| 18 \|\|*

*bhūtānbhavyāṃśca manujāṃs tārayeddrumasaṃmitān \|*  
*paramāṃ siddhimāpnoti punarāvṛttidurlabhām \|\| 19 \|\|*

*ya idaṃ śṛṇuyānnityaṃ śrāvayedvāpi mānavaḥ \|*  
*so 'pi sampūjito devair brahmaloke mahīyate \|\| 20 \|\|*

17-20. The wise who observes these rites in dedicating the plantation of trees, obtains all his desires and attains to endless felicity.

One who plants even one tree, O King! according to the prescribed rites, resides in heaven for 30,000 years of Indra. The planter of trees, according to the prescribed rites, liberates the same number of his past and future manes and attains the highest perfection, and is never re-born on earth. One who hears or relates to others these prescribed ceremonies goes to the region of Brahma and is venerated by the Devas.

## Chapter 60

## \|\| 60.1 \|\|

*matsya uvāca*  
*tathaivānyatpravakṣyāmi sarvakāmaphalapradam \|*  
*saubhāgyaśayanaṃ nāma yatpurāṇavido viduḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. The Lord Fish said: — I shall now relate to you the Saubhagya Sayana Vrata (ordinance), the giver of all bliss which is known to the Pauranikas.

## \|\| 60.2-4 \|\|

*purā dagdheṣu lokeṣu bhūrbhuvaḥsvarmahādiṣu \|*  
*saubhāgyaṃ sarvabhūtānām ekasthamabhavattadā \|*  
*vaikuṇṭhaṃ svargamāsādya viṣṇor vakṣaḥsthalasthitam \|\| 2 \|\|*

*tataḥ kālena mahatā punaḥ sargavidhau nṛpa \|*  
*ahaṃkārāvṛte loke pradhānapuruṣānvite \|\| 3 \|\|*

*spardhāyāṃ ca pravṛttāyāṃ kamalāsanakṛṣṇayoḥ \|*  
*liṅgākārā samudbhūtā vahnerjvālātibhīṣaṇā \|*  
*tayābhitaptasya harer vakṣasastadviniḥsṛtam \|\| 4 \|\|*

2-4. When the regions Bhah, Bhuvah, Svar and Maha, &c., were consumed, then the good fortune of all creatures went and centred itself in the heart of the Lord Vishnu, in Vaikuntha heaven. Again, long time after, with the object of creating the world, O King! the plastic material, consisting of Pradhana (root matter), and conscious souls called Purushas, was enveloped with self-consciousness (ahankara), when there arose a rivalry between Brahma and Krishna, regarding the fashioning of the future world. Then (from their clashing wills), a terrifying flame of fire arose in the form of a linga (pillar), by the warmth of which the good luck of the world resting in the heart of Hari came out (in the form of perspiration).

## \|\| 60.5-6 \|\|

*vakṣaḥsthalaṃ samāśritya viṣṇoḥ saubhāgyamāsthitam \|*  
*rasarūpaṃ tato yāvat prāpnoti vasudhātalam \|\| 5 \|\|*

*utkṣiptamantarikṣe tad brahmaputreṇa dhīmatā \|*  
*dakṣeṇa pītamātraṃ tad rūpalāvaṇyakārakam \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. That good fortune emerging from the heart of Vishnu, passed through the Intermediate plane (antariksha) before it could reach the earth in liquid form, and Daksha the wise son of Brahma, drank up this giver of beauty and loveliness.

## \|\| 60.7-9 \|\|

*balaṃ tejo mahadjātaṃ dakṣasya parameṣṭhinaḥ \|*  
*śeṣaṃ yadapatadbhūmāv aṣṭadhā samajāyata \|\| 7 \|\|*

*tato janānāṃ saṃjātāḥ sapta saubhāgyadāyikāḥ \|*  
*ikṣavo rasarājāśca niṣpāvājājidhānyakam \|\| 8 \|\|*

*vikāravacca gokṣīraṃ kusumbhaṃ kuṅkumaṃ tathā \|*  
*lavaṇaṃ cāṣṭamaṃ tadvat saubhāgyāṣṭakamucyate \|\| 9 \|\|*

7-9. Thence Daksha got mighty power and great lusture, and the remainder of (the good luck) which reached the Earth was divided into eight parts. From them were produced the seven givers of prosperity, to all men, namely, (1) sugarcanes, the Kings of all juices Rasarajam (2) Nishpava, (ghrita), (5) cow’s milk (Kshira), (6) saffron (Kusumbha), (7) safflower (Kumkuma.) So also the common salt was produced as the eighth, and these are called saubhagya Ashtaka, the eight blessings.

## \|\| 60.10-12 \|\|

*pītaṃ yadbrahmaputreṇa yogajñānavidā punaḥ \|*  
*duhitā sābhavattasya yā satītyabhidhīyate \|\| 10 \|\|*

*lokānatītya lālityāl lalitā tena cocyate \|*  
*trailokyasundarīm enām upayeme pinākadhṛk \|\| 11 \|\|*

*yā devī saubhāgyamayī bhuktimuktiphalapradā \|*  
*tāmārādhya pumānbhaktyā nārī vā kiṃ na vindati \|\| 12 \|\|*

10-12. That which was drunk by Daksha, the son of Brahma, the knower of Yoga, became his daughter, known as Sati (Parvati). Parvati, owing to Her matchless beauty, came to be known as Lalita; and that paragon of beauty was afterwards married by the Lord Shiva. The very Sati is called the Goddess who gives bliss (Saubhagyamayi), and also prosperity and emancipation. Those men and women who worship Her with devotion may obtain everything.

## \|\| 60.13 \|\|

*manuruvāca*  
*kathamārādhanaṃ tasyā jagaddhātryā janārdana \|*  
*tadvidhānaṃ jagannātha tatsarvaṃ ca vadasva me \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Manu said: — O Lord! explain tome the ways of worshipping that sublime Goddess, the upholder of the Universe, and tell me completely the ritual of Her worship.

## \|\| 60.14-17 \|\|

*matsya uvāca*  
*vasantamāsamāsādya tṛtīyāyāṃ janapriya \|*  
*śuklapakṣasya pūrvāhṇe tilaiḥ snānaṃ samācaret \|\| 14 \|\|*

*tasminnahani sā devī kila viśvātmanā satī \|*  
*pāṇigrahaṇakair mantrair udūḍhā varavarṇinī \|\| 15 \|\|*

*tayā sahaiva deveśaṃ tṛtīyāyām athārcayet \|*  
*phalairnānāvidhairdhūpair dīpanaivedyasaṃyutaiḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*pratimāṃ pañcagavyena tathā gandhodakena tu \|*  
*snāpayitvārcayed gaurīm induśekharasaṃyutām \|\| 17 \|\|*

14-17. The Lord Fish said: — The devotes should bathe himself with sesamum in the forenoon, on the third day of the lunar fortnight, in the month of Chaitra during the vernal season; for, on that day, the Goddess was united to Shiva, the soul of the Universe, with marital rites. On that day, Shiva, along with His consort, Parvati, should be worshipped with flowers, fruits, incense, lamps, and offerings of foods, &c; and the image (of Gauri) should be bathed with Panchagavya and scented waters, after which Gauri and Shankara should be worshipped as follows:

## \|\| 60.18-19 \|\|

*namo 'stu pāṭalāyai tu pādau devyāḥ śivasya tu \|*  
*śivāyeti ca saṃkīrya jayāyai gulphayor dvayoḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*triguṇāyeti rudrāya bhavānyai jaṅghayoryugam \|*  
*śivāṃ rudreśvarāyai ca vijayāyeti jānunī \|*  
*saṃkīrtya harikeśāya tathorū varade namaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

18-19. By pronouncing (1) ... Patalayai namah, the feet of the Devi should be worshipped, and those of Shiva should be worshipped with the mantra ... Shivayanamah Their ankles should he worshipped after pronouncing (2) ... Siveyanamah and ... Jayayainamah; after saluting Rudra with (3) ... Trigunayanamah and the Goddess, with .... Bhavanyai namah, their shanks should be worshipped, After saluting Gauri with (5) ... Radregvardyai namah, Shiva and with ... Vijayaya namah, their knees should be worshipped. After saluting Shiva with (6) ... Harikeshayanamah and Gauri with ... Varade namah (the giver of boons), the thighs should be worshipped.

## \|\| 60.20 \|\|

*īśāyai ca kīṭaṃ devyāḥ śaṃkarāyeti śaṃkaram \|*  
*kukṣidvayaṃ ca koṭavyai śūline śūlapāṇaye \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Their waist should be worshipped, after saluting the goddess with (7) ... Ishayai namah I salute the goddess, Is4, He should salute Shankara with ... Satkariya namah. The abdomen should be worshipped by saying (8) ... Kotavai namah, I salute the goddess Kotavi, and by ... Suline namah, I salute the wielder of the trident."

## \|\| 60.21 \|\|

*maṅgalāyai namastubhyam udaraṃ cābhipūjayet \|*  
*sarvātmane namo rudram īśānyai ca kucadvayam \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. The stomach of the Goddess, after saying (9) ... Mangalayai namastubhyam, “I salute Mangala,” (the giver of bliss); the stomach of Shiva, after pronouncing ... Shivaya namah “I salute Shiva; the breasts of the Goddess, after saying (10) ... ishanyai namah, “I salute ishani;” and of the God by saying ... Sarvatmane namah, I salute the All-Soul

## \|\| 60.22 \|\|

*śivaṃ vedātmane tadvad rudrāṇyai kaṇṭhamarcayet \|*  
*tripuraghnāya viśveśam anantāyai karadvayam \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. The throat of the Lord, after saying (11) ... Vedatmane namah, “ I salute the soul of the Vedas;” the throat of the Goddess, after saying ... Rudrainyei namah, “ I salute Rudrani,” their hands, after pronouncing (12) ... Tripuraghnaya namah, I salute the god, the destroyer of the demon Tripura, and the goddess with ... Anantayai hamah, “I salute the Infinite.”

## \|\| 60.23 \|\|

*trilocanāya ca haraṃ bāhū kālānalapriye \|*  
*saubhāgyabhavanāyeti bhūṣaṇāni sadārcayet \|*  
*svāhāsvadhāyai ca mukham īśvarāyeti śūlinam \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Their arms, after pronouncing (13) ... Trilochandya tamah “I salute the three-eyed, Hara; and the goddess by ... Kalanalapriy ayai namah, “I salute the beloved of the Lord,” the ornaments, after saying (14) ... Saubhagyabhavaniya namah,” their mouths, after reciting (15) ... “syahdsvadhayai namah, for the goddess and ... ishvaraya namah, for the god.”

## \|\| 60.24 \|\|

*aśokamadhuvāsinyai pūjyāvoṣṭhau ca bhūtidau \|*  
*sthāṇave tu haraṃ tadvad dhāsyaṃ candramukhapriye \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. The lips of the Goddess, the giver of prosperity, should be worshipped by reciting (16) waergafeee wa: Ayokamadhuvdsinyai namah and of the god by ... Shivaya namah. The cheeks of the Lord should be worshipped by saying (17) ... Sthanave namah and of the goddess by saying ... Chandramukhapriyayai namah

## \|\| 60.25 \|\|

*namo 'rdhanārīśaharam asitāṅgīti nāsikām \|*  
*nama ugrāya lokeśaṃ laliteti punarbhruvau \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. The nose of the Lord should be worshipped by reciting (18) ... Andhangridiya namah and of the goddess by ... Asitangyai namah. The eye-brows of the Lord of the world should be worshipped by reciting (19) ... Namah Ugraya, and of the goddess by ... Lalitayainamah

## \|\| 60.26 \|\|

*śarvāya purahantāraṃ vāsavyai tu tathālakān \|*  
*namaḥ śrīkaṇṭhanāthāyai śivakeśāṃstato 'rcayet \|*  
*bhīmograsamarūpiṇyai śiraḥ sarvātmane namaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. The tresses of Shiva, after reciting (20) ... Sarvaya namah, “I salute sarva”, the destructor of Pura, the tresses of the hair of the Goddess, after saying ... Vasayai hamah, “I salute Vasavi, the hair of the god, after reciting (21) ... namah Srikanthe pathaya and of the goddess with the same mantra. The head of the goddess, after pronouncing (22) ... Bhimograsamarupinye, “I salute Bhimograsamardpint” and of the God by ... Sarvatmane namah.

## \|\| 60.27-28 \|\|

*śivamabhyarcya vidhivat saubhāgyāṣṭakamagrataḥ \|*  
*sthāpayeddhṛtaniṣpāva-kusumbhakṣīrajīrakam \|\| 27 \|\|*

*rasarājaṃ ca lavaṇaṃ kustumburu tathāṣṭakam \|*  
*dattaṃ saubhāgyamityasmāt saubhāgyāṣṭakamityataḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

27-28. After thus worshipping Shiva, the devotee should place before Him the Saubhagya Ashtaka, the eight blessings consisting of the following eight things: clarified butter (ghee) nishpava, (?), saffron, cow's milk, cumin seed, sugarcane (rasaraja), salt and coriander seed.

All these eight things are considered as boons, and therefore their mixture is called Saubhagya Ashtaka.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — The enumeration here is slightly different from that of Shloka 9.

## \|\| 60.29 \|\|

*evaṃ nivedya tatsarvam agrataḥ śivayoḥ punaḥ \|*  
*rātrau śṛṅgodakaṃ prāṣya tadvadbhūmāvariṃdama \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. After offering these things to Shiva and Parvati, the devotee should wash the horns of the cow in the night and drink the same and sleep on the floor.

## \|\| 60.30 \|\|

*punaḥ prabhāte tu tathā kṛtasnānajapaḥ śuciḥ \|*  
*saṃpūjya dvijadāmpatyaṃ vastramālyavibhūṣaṇaiḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Getting up in the morning, the devotee should bathe, and after Turning his rosary, should offer clothes, garlands, ornaments, &c., to the Brahmana and to his Consort.

## \|\| 60.31 \|\|

*saubhāgyāṣṭakasaṃyuktaṃ suvarṇacaraṇadvayam \|*  
*prīyatāmatra lalitā brāhmaṇāya nivedayet \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. The devotee should get a pair of golden feet made and give them away, along with the eight blessings to the Brahmana, after invoking blessing of the Goddess Lalita, saying “piyatam atra Lalita.”

## \|\| 60.32 \|\|

*evaṃ saṃvatsaraṃ yāvat tṛtīyāyāṃ sadā mano \|*  
*kartavyaṃ vidhivadbhaktyā sarvasaubhāgyamīpsubhiḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Similarly, for a year, the worship should be performed according to the prescribed sites, on each tied day of the moon, by those who desire blessings.

## \|\| 60.33-37 \|\|

*prāśane dānamantre ca viśeṣo 'yaṃ nibodha me \|*  
*śṛṅgodakaṃ caitramāse vaiśākhe gomayaṃ punaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

*jyeṣṭhe mandārakusumaṃ bilvapattraṃ śucau smṛtam \|*  
*śrāvaṇe dadhi saṃprāṣyaṃ nabhasye ca kuśodakam \|\| 34 \|\|*

*kṣīramāśvauje māsi kārttike pṛṣadājyakam \|*  
*mārge māse tu gomūtraṃ pauṣe saṃprāśayedghṛtam \|\| 35 \|\|*

*māghe kṛṣṇatilāṃstadvat pañcagavyaṃ ca phālgune \|*  
*lalitā vijayā bhadrā bhavānī kumudā śivā \|\| 36 \|\|*

*vāsudevī tathā gaurī maṅgalā kamalā satī \|*  
*umā ca dānakāle tu prīyatāmiti kīrtayet \|\| 37 \|\|*

33-37. The following special articles of diet and mantra of gift (Dana) should be observed hear them from me. The devotee should drink the washing of the cow's horns in the month of Chaitra, eat cowdung in the month of Vaishakha. The flower of Mandara tree in the month of Jyaishtha, the leaves of the woodapple (Vilvapatra) in. the month of Ashadha, curds in the month of Shravana, the water sprinkled with the Kusha grass in the mounth of Bhadra. Milk in Ashvina, clarified butter, mixed with curd in Kartika, the cow's urine in Margashira, clarified butter in the Black sesamum in Magha, Panchagavya in Phalguna. At the time of giving away’ the gifts, the devotes should recite the following mantra:

“Lalita, Vijaya, Bhadra, Bhavani, Kumuda, Shiva, Vasudevi, Gauri, Mangala, Kamala, Sati, Uma, be pleased.” Ta other words, the devotee should in each month invoke the pleasure of the Goddess by reciting a fresh name out of the twelve names mentioned, viz., in Chaitra he should say, “Lalita be pleased,” in Vaishakha, “ Vijaya be pleased,” and so on.

## \|\| 60.38-40 \|\|

*mallikāśokakamalaṃ kadambotpalamālatīḥ \|*  
*kubjakaṃ karavīraṃ ca bāṇamamlānakuṅkumam \|\| 38 \|\|*

*sindhuvāraṃ ca sarveṣu māseṣu kramaśaḥ smṛtam \|*  
*japākusumbhakusumaṃ mālatī śatapattrikā \|\| 39 \|\|*

*yathālābhaṃ praśastāni karavīraṃ ca sarvadā \|*  
*evaṃ saṃvatsaraṃ yāvad upoṣya vidhivannaraḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

38-40. He should offer the following varieties of flowers (one each month), at the time of worship: — Mallika, Ashoka, Lotus, Kadamba, Utpala, Malati, Kubjaka, Karabira, Banam, Amlana, Kunkuma , an d Sindhuvara; or any of the following flowers, as procurable, should be offered, viz. — Jasmine, Safflower, Malati, Lotus and Karabira

## \|\| 60.42 \|\|

*umāmaheśvaraṃ haimaṃ vṛṣabhaṃ ca gavā saha \|*  
*sthāpayitvātha śayane brāhmaṇāya nivedayet \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Married woman or maid, after devoutly worshipping Shiva, at the end of the ordinance, should give away a bedstead, along with all the necessary At the time of giving away the bedstead, the following things should also be placed on it and given away along with it: — The golden images of Shiva and Parvati, the golden figures of ox and cow.

## \|\| 60.43 \|\|

*anyānyapi yathāśakti mithunānyambarādibhiḥ \|*  
*dhānyālaṃkāragodānair abhyarceddhanasaṃcayaiḥ \|*  
*vittaśāṭhyena rahitaḥ pūjayedgatavismayaḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Besides this, according to his means, the devotee should give to the Brahmanas and their wives, clothes, grain, ornaments, cows, cash, and should not give way to niggardliness or doubt.

## \|\| 60.44 \|\|

*evaṃ karoti yaḥ samyak saubhāgyaśayanavratam \|*  
*sarvānkāmānavāpnoti padamatyantamaśnute \|*  
*phalasyaikasya tyāgena vratametatsamācaret \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. One who observes this ordinance — Saubhagya-sayana — achieves all his ends and emancipation. This ordinance had better be observed without any object of bearing fruits.

## \|\| 60.45-46 \|\|

*ya icchankīrtimāpnoti pratimāsaṃ narādhipa \|*  
*saubhāgyārogyarūpāur vastrālaṃkārabhūṣaṇaiḥ \|*  
*na viukto bhavedrājan navārbudaśatatrayam \|\| 45 \|\|*

*yastu dvādaśa varṣāṇi saubhāgyaśayanavratam \|*  
*karoti sapta cāṣṭau vā śrīkaṇṭhabhavane 'maraiḥ \|*  
*pūjyamāno vasetsamyag yāvatkalpāutatrayam \|\| 46 \|\|*

45-46. One who observes this ordinance every month, begets good fortune, health, beauty, longevity, clothes, ornaments, etc., which last him for 9000000300 years. One who observes this ordinance for 12 years, 8 years, or 7 years, goes and enjoys in the region of Shiva, for three Kalpas.

## \|\| 60.47 \|\|

*nārī vā kurute vāpi kumārī vā nareśvara \|*  
*sāpi tatphalamāpnoti devyanugrahalālitā \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. The Married woman or the maid who keeps up this ordinance also attains the same benefits through the grace of the Goddess Lalita.

## \|\| 60.48 \|\|

*śṛṇuyādapi yaścaiva pradadyādathavā matim \|*  
*so 'pi vidyādharo bhūtvā svargaloke ciraṃ vaset \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. One who hears or advises others to listen to the account of this ordinance, passes his days in heaven for a long time in the form of Vidyadhara.

## \|\| 60.49 \|\|

*idamiha madanena pūrvamiṣṭaṃ śatadhanuṣā kṛtavīryasūnunā ca \|*  
*kṛtamatha varuṇena nandinā vā kim u jananātha tato yadudbhavaḥ syāt \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Cupid was the first to observe this ordinance, and Sahasrabahu, the son of Kartavirya, was the second to observe it; and afterwards it was kept up by Varuna and Nandi, and consequently this is considered so sacred in this world.

## Chapter 61

## \|\| 61.1 \|\|

*nārada uvāca*  
*bhūrloko 'tha bhuvarlokaḥ svarloko 'tha maharjanaḥ \|*  
*tapaḥ satyaṃ ca saptaite devalokāḥ prakīrtitāḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Narada said: — Shiva! There are named the following seven regions of the Devas, viz. — Bhuh, Bhuvah, Svah, Mahah, Janah, Tapah, Satyam.

## \|\| 61.2 \|\|

*paryāyeṇa tu sarveṣām ādhipatyaṃ kathaṃ bhavet \|*  
*iha loke śubhaṃ rūpam āuḥ saubhāgyameva ca \|*  
*lakṣmīśca vipulā nātha kathaṃ syātpurasūdana \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. How may mastery be obtained in succession over these lokas, and how one may obtain in this earth prosperity, beauty, long life and blessing. Please also explain to me how they become blessed with fortune, beauty and wealth.

## \|\| 61.3 \|\|

*maheśvara uvāca*  
*purā hutāśanaḥ sārdhaṃ mārutena mahītale \|*  
*ādiṣṭaḥ puruhūtena vināśāya suradviṣām \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Shiva said — Formerly, a fearful fire was ablaze on this earth accompanied with a strong wind. The friction caused by the wind produced the fire for the destruction of the demons, at the command of Puruhuta (Indra)

## \|\| 61.4 \|\|

*nirdagdheṣu tatastena dānaveṣu sahasraśaḥ \|*  
*tārakaḥ kamalākṣaśca kāladaṃṣṭraḥ parāvasuḥ \|*  
*virocanaśca saṃgrāmād apalāyaṃstapodhana \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. That terrific fire reduced many demons to ashes, when Tarakasura, Kamalaksha, Kaladanshtra, Paravasu, and Virochana fled from their warfare with the Devas

## \|\| 61.5 \|\|

*ambhaḥ sāmudramāviṣya saṃniveśamakurvata \|*  
*aśakyā iti te 'pyagni-mārutābhyāmupekṣitāḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. They all plunged themselves into the waters of the sea and took up their abode there, where fire with the help of air could not consume them.

## \|\| 61.6 \|\|

*tataḥ prabhṛti te devān manuṣyānsaha jaṅgamān \|*  
*saṃpīḍya ca munīnsarvān praviśanti punarjalam \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Afterwards, the demons began to come out of the waters and persecute the Devas, men, sages and other living beings, and disappear again into the sea.

## \|\| 61.8 \|\|

*tataḥ paramatho vahni-mārutāvamarādhipaḥ \|*  
*ādideśa cirādambu-nidhireṣa viśoṣyatām \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. In that way, the demons asserted their boldness for twelve thousand years and continued their campaign of persecuting the three worlds, for a period of five or seven years at a time, by taking shelter in the fortress Later on, Indra directed the fire and the wind to dry up the ocean in the following words: — Dry up this receptacle of water quickly.

## \|\| 61.9 \|\|

*yasmādasmaddviṣāmeṣa śaraṇaṃ varuṇālayaḥ \|*  
*tasmādbhavadbhyāmadyaiva kṣayameṣa praṇīyatām \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. "Because it shelters my foes. They have taken their refuge in the home of Varuna. It should therefore be dried up as quick as possible

## \|\| 61.10-12 \|\|

*tāvūcatustataḥ śakram ubhau śambarasūdanam \|*  
*adharma eṣa devendra sāgarasya vināśanam \|\| 10 \|\|*

*yasmādjīvanikāyasya mahataḥ saṃkṣayo bhavet \|*  
*tasmānna pāpamadyāvāṃ karavāva puraṃdara \|\| 11 \|\|*

*asya yojanamātre 'pi jīvakoṭiśatāni ca \|*  
*nivasanti suraśreṣṭha sa kathaṃ nāśamarhati \|\| 12 \|\|*

10-12. Hearing that mandate of Indra, both fire and wind said to Him, the destroyer of Sambara: — “It would be a great sin to destroy the ocean. Because innumerable beings had made it their home, and the destruction of the ocean meant their annihilation along with it, therefore, we, O Purandara, cannot do it. Lacs and lacs of beings inhabit the ocean, within the space of every yojana. It was not meet for us to annihilate them. What fault have they done to be destroyed, O chief of the Devas.”

## \|\| 61.13 \|\|

*evamuktaḥ surendrastu kopāt saṃraktalocanaḥ \|*  
*uvācedaṃ vaco roṣān nirdahanniva pāvakam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Hearing the speech of the fire and the wind, Indra became full of wrath.: His eyes turned crimson red, and it appeared as if He was going to eat cup both fire and wind. In his rage, be said:

## \|\| 61.14-17 \|\|

*na dharmādharmasaṃyogaṃ prāpnuvantyamarāḥ kvacit \|*  
*bhavatostu viśeṣeṇa māhātmyaṃ cādhitiṣṭhatoḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*madājñālaṅghanaṃ yasmān mārutena samaṃ tvayā \|*  
*munivratamahiṃsādi parigṛhya tvayā kṛtam \|*  
*dharmārthaśāstrarahitaṃ śatruṃ prati vibhāvaso \|\| 15 \|\|*

*tasmādekena vapuṣā munirūpeṇa mānuṣe \|*  
*mārutena samaṃ loke tava janma bhaviṣyati \|\| 16 \|\|*

*yadā ca mānuṣatve 'pi tvayāgastyena śoṣitaḥ \|*  
*bhaviṣyatyudadhirvahne tadā devatvamāpsyasi \|\| 17 \|\|*

14-17. "There is no question of Dharma or adharma where Immortals are concerned, and your glory is still more high. O Agni and Vayu!

Since you have violated my injunction and have adopted the duties of the Munis not to injure any being, and since you have leaned towards the enemies who are devoid of religion and politics losing sight of duty and Shastra; therefore You, O fire, will now be borne by assuming one body along with Maruta, among the mortals, in the form of a sage.

In that form of the sage Agastya, you will dry up the ocean, after which you will again come back to your Divine form.”

## \|\| 61.18-19 \|\|

*itīndraśāpātpatitau tatkṣaṇāttau mahītale \|*  
*avāptāvekadehena kumbhādjanma tapodhana \|\| 18 \|\|*

*mitrāvaruṇayorvīryād vasiṣṭhasyānujo 'bhavat \|*  
*agastya ityugratapāḥ saṃbabhūva punarmuniḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

18-19. After thus being cursed by Indra, both of them fell on the earth, where they were jointly born out of the pitcher by the seeds of Mitra Varuni and came to be known as Agastya — the younger brother of Vasistha, and one of the most renowned ascetics.

## \|\| 61.20 \|\|

*nārada uvāca*  
*sambhūtaḥ sa kathaṃ bhrātā vasiṣṭhasyābhavanmuniḥ \|*  
*kathaṃ ca mitrāvaruṇau pitarāvasya tau smṛtau \|*  
*janma kumbhādagastyasya kathaṃ syātpurasūdana \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Narada asked Shiva how Agastya became the brother of Vasistha, and how Mitra Varuna became his father, and how the sage Agastya was born out of the pitcher.

## \|\| 61.21-22 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca*  
*purā purāṇapuruṣaḥ kadācidgandhamādane \|*  
*bhūtvā dharmasuto viṣṇuś cacāra vipulaṃ tapaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*tapasā tasya bhītena vighnārthaṃ preṣitāvubhau \|*  
*śakreṇa mādhavānaṅgāv apsarogaṇasaṃyutau \|\| 22 \|\|*

21-22. Shiva said that, once upon a time Lord Vishnu, the son of Dharma, — began to practice rigid asceticism on the summit of the Gandhamadana Mountain. Indra being afraid of His austerities, sent a group of nymphs in company of the Vernal-season and Cupid to distract Him from His penances and destroy His austerities.

## \|\| 61.23 \|\|

*yadā na gītavādyena nāṅgarāgādinā hariḥ \|*  
*na kāmamādhavābhyāṃ ca viṣayānprati cukṣubhe \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. The Lord Hari was not in any way moved by the songs and music, gestures and tones of the Cupid and the spring, nor was his mind attracted to external objects

## \|\| 61.24-25 \|\|

*tadā kāmamadhustrīṇāṃ viṣādam agamadgaṇaḥ \|*  
*saṃkṣobhāya tatasteṣāṃ svorudeśānnarāgrajaḥ \|*  
*nārīmutpādayāmāsa trailokyajanamohinīm \|\| 24 \|\|*

*saṃkṣubdhāstu tayā devās tau tu devavarāvubhau \|*  
*apsarobhiḥ samakṣaṃ hi devānāmabravīddhariḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

24-25. Finding the Lord remaining firm, the agents of Indra began to shiver with fear, when the Lord, in order to further bewilder them, produced from His thigh a damsel of exquisite beauty, fascinating the dwellers of the three world

## \|\| 61.26 \|\|

*apsarā iti sāmānyā devānāmabravīddhariḥ \|*  
*urvaśīti ca nāmneyaṃ loke khyātiṃ gamiṣyati \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Seeing whom, all the Devas, along with Cupid and spring, became enamoured of her, when the Lord said to them, in the presence of the “This is the nymph Urvashi, O Devas! and I have created her to become the head of all Apsaras”.

## \|\| 61.27 \|\|

*tataḥ kāmayamānena mitreṇāhūya sorvaśī \|*  
*uktā māṃ ramayasveti bāḍham ityabravīttu sā \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Then the God Mitra called her, and asked her to enjoy with Him, which she accepted.

## \|\| 61.28-29 \|\|

*gacchantī cāmbaraṃ tadvat stokamindīvarekṣaṇā \|*  
*varuṇena dhṛtā paścād varuṇaṃ nābhyanandata \|\| 28 \|\|*

*mitreṇāhaṃ vṛtā pūrvam adya bhāryā na te vibho \|*  
*uvāca varuṇaścittaṃ mayi saṃnyasya gamyatām \|\| 29 \|\|*

28-29 Afterwards, the lotus-eyed Urvashi, while moving. in the sky slowly, was caught by Varuna, who slowly pulled her by her cloth, at which she told Him: “Your action is not proper. Because I have accepted Mitra first, and consequently I cannot be your wife, O Varuna.” Varuna told her, “Keep me at least in your favor and then go elsewhere.”

## \|\| 61.30-31 \|\|

*gatāyāṃ bāḍhamityuktvā mitraḥ śāpamadāttadā \|*  
*tasyai mānuṣaloke tvaṃ gaccha somasutātmajam \|\| 30 \|\|*

*bhajasveti yato veśyā dharma eṣa tvayā kṛtaḥ \|*  
*jalakumbhe tato vīryaṃ mitreṇa varuṇena ca \|*  
*prakṣiptamatha saṃjātau dvāveva munisattamau \|\| 31 \|\|*

30-31. She replied: — “All right.” When Mitra heard this, he cursed her:

“You go, down. to the world of the mortals and be married to the son of moon, Budha, because you have followed the ways of a courtesan”. Saying that, both Varuna and Mitra threw Their seed in a pitcher of water, out of which two sages (Agastya and Vasishtha) came out

## \|\| 61.32-33 \|\|

*nimirnāma saha strībhiḥ purā dyūtamadīvyata \|*  
*tatrāntare 'bhyājagāma vasiṣṭho brahmasambhavaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

*tasya pūjāmakurvantaṃ śaśāpa sa munirnṛpam \|*  
*videhastvaṃ bhavasveti tatastenāpyasau muniḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

32-33. Once upon a time King Nimi was playing with women the game of dice, where Vasishtha, the son of Brahma, chanced to go. At that time the king did not show his respect to the sage, at which the latter got annoyed and cursed him to become bodiless, and the king also pronounced another curse on the sage.

## \|\| 61.34 \|\|

*anyonyaśāpācca tayor vigate iva cetasī \|*  
*jagmatuḥ śāpanāśāya brahmāṇaṃ jagataḥ patim \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. They both became bereft of reason, as it were, through the curse of each other, and went to Brahma, the Lord of the Universe, to remedy the effects of the curses.

## \|\| 61.35-36 \|\|

*atha brahmaṇa ādeśāl locaneṣvavasannimiḥ \|*  
*nimeṣāḥ syuśca lokānāṃ tadviśrāmāya nārada \|\| 35 \|\|*

*vasiṣṭho 'pyabhavattasmiñ jalakumbhe ca pūrvavat \|*  
*tataḥ śvetaścaturbāhuḥ sākṣasūtrakamaṇḍaluḥ \|*  
*agastya iti śāntātmā babhūva ṛṣisattamaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

35-36. With the orders of Brahma, Nimi entered the eyes of the mankind, and this causes them to open their eyes; but when Nimi takes rest, they close their eyes; and hence this shutting and closing of the eyes is called winking or nimesha. Vasishtha, similarly, entered that pitcher of water and was born out of it, and after him the sage Agastya was born, of the same pitcher, of white colour, with four hands, sacred thread, kamandalu, and garland.

## \|\| 61.37 \|\|

*malayasyaikadeśe tu vaikhānasavidhānataḥ \|*  
*sabhāryaḥ saṃvṛto viprais tapaścakre suduścaram \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. The sage Agastya went to the Malaya mountain, along with his better-half, and began to practice rigid austerities, surrounded with a number of other sages, according to the rules of forest-dwellers, hermits.

## \|\| 61.38 \|\|

*tataḥ kālena mahatā tārakād atipīḍitam \|*  
*jagadvīkṣya sa kopena pītavānvaruṇālayam \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. A long time after, the sage Agastya, seeing the world oppressed by the demon Tarakasura, drank the ocean.

## \|\| 61.39-41 \|\|

*tato 'sya varadāḥ sarve babhūvuḥ śaṃkarādayaḥ \|*  
*brahmā viṣṇuśca bhagavān varadānāya jagmatuḥ \|*  
*varaṃ vṛṇīṣva bhadraṃ te yadabhīṣṭaṃ ca vai mune \|\| 39 \|\|*

*agastya uvāca*  
*yāvadbrahmasahasrāṇāṃ pañcaviṃśatikoṭayaḥ \|*  
*vaimāniko bhaviṣyāmi dakṣiṇācalavartmani \|\| 40 \|\|*

*madvimānodaye kuryād yaḥ kaścitpūjanaṃ mama \|*  
*sa saptalokādhipatiḥ paryāyeṇa bhaviṣyati \|\| 41 \|\|*

39-41. Wen Brahma, Vishnu and Shiva went to grant him a boon and asked him to seek any boon he wished, Agastya said: — I wish to have the privilege of moving about in the Vimanas on the Dakshinachala mount, till a thousand Brahmas come and go in turn for 25 crores of times; and those who worship me at the time of the appearance of my Vimana, should be the monarchs of all the seven realms, till the time of the re-establishment of fresh sovereignty in the seven climes.”

## \|\| 61.42 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca*  
*evamastviti te 'pyuktvā jagmurdevā yathāgatam \|*  
*tasmādarghaḥ pradātavyo hy agastyasya sadā budhaiḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Lord Shiva said: — “It will be so; and afterwards all the Devas went back to their respective regions. It is therefore proper for every sensible man to give a libation of water (arghya) to the sage Agastya.

## \|\| 61.43 \|\|

*nārada uvāca*  
*kathamarghapradānaṃ tu kartavyaṃ tasya vai vibho \|*  
*vidhānaṃ yadagastyasya pūjane tadvadasva me \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Narada — “How should a libation of water be offered to the sage Agastya; be pleased to explain to me the ways of worshipping him”.

## \|\| 61.44 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca*  
*pratyūṣasamaye vidvān kuryādasyodaye niśi \|*  
*snānaṃ śuklatilaistadvac chuklamālyāmbaro gṛhī \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. The Lord said: — The learned should get up early ix the morning, with ho rising of Agastya, and bathe in water mixed with white sesamum and should wear garland of white flowers and white clothes.

## \|\| 61.45 \|\|

*sthāpayedavraṇaṃ kumbhaṃ mālyavastravibhūṣitam \|*  
*pañcaratnasamāuktaṃ ghṛtapātrasamanvitam \|*  
*nānābhakṣyaphalairyuktaṃ tāmrapātrasamanvitam \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. And then a good pitcher, free from perforations, should be placed, after decorating it with flowers, cloths, and filled in with Pancharatna, and having a pot, full of clarified butter, put on top of it.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — Pancharatna, Lit, five gems. They are variously enumerated, viz.

## \|\| 61.46 \|\|

*aṅguṣṭhamātraṃ puruṣaṃ tathaiva sauvarṇam atyāyatabāhudaṇḍam \|*  
*caturmukhaṃ kumbhamukhe nidhāya dhānyāni saptāmbarasaṃyutāni \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Afterwards, a golden image, of the size of a thumb, with extensive arms and four heads, should be made and placed on top of the pitcher; and then, after filling it in with sapta-dhanya and decorating with cloth

**Комментарий:**

Note — Sapta-dhanya seven grains.

## \|\| 61.47 \|\|

*sakāṃsyapātrākṣataśuktiuktaṃ mantreṇa dadyāddvijapuṃgavāya \|*  
*utkṣipya lambodaradīrghabāhum ananyacetā yamadiṅmukhaḥ san \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. It should be given away to a Brahmana, along with a vessel of bell metal, rice, shell, and then the image of gold should be given away in charity, with the devotee’s face turned towards the south.

## \|\| 61.48 \|\|

*śvetāṃ ca dadyādyadi śaktirasti raupyaiḥ khurair hemamukhīṃ savatsām \|*  
*dhenuṃ naraḥ kṣīravatīṃ praṇamya savatsaghaṇṭābharaṇāṃ dvijāya \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. The devotee, if he can afford it, should give away a milk cow, along with her calf, after getting her hoofs covered with silver, and horns covered with gold, and wearing a bell round her neck, to a Brahmana

## \|\| 61.49 \|\|

*ā saptarātrodayam etadasya dātavyametatsakalaṃ nareṇa \|*  
*yāvatsamāḥ sapta daśāthavā syur athordhvamapyatra vadanti kecit \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. The devotee should observe this rite for seven days from the rising of Agastya. Some say that it should be observed for seventeen years.

## \|\| 61.50 \|\|

*kāśapuṣpapratīkāśa vahnimārutasambhava \|*  
*mitrāvaruṇayoḥ putra kumbhayone namo 'stu te \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. “O Thou, as white as Kasha flower, O Thou born of Agni and Marut, O Thou son of Mitra and Varuna, I salute Thee, born of a pitcher.” The devotee worshipping like this with fruits and flowers, never gets aggrieved

## \|\| 61.51 \|\|

*vindhyavṛddhikṣayakara meghatoyaviṣāpaha \|*  
*ratnavallabha deveśa laṅkāvāsinnamo 'stu te \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Afterwards, homa sacrifice should be performed, without any desire of obtaining any fruits. The devotee should thus offer libation of water.

## \|\| 61.52-53 \|\|

*vātāpī bhakṣito yena samudraḥ śoṣitaḥ purā \|*  
*lopāmudrāpatiḥ śrīmān yo 'sau tasmai namo namaḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

*rājaputri mahābhāge ṛṣipatni varānane \|*  
*lopāmudre namastubhyam argho me pratigṛhyatām \|*  
*pratyabdaṃ tu phalatyāgam evaṃ kurvanna sīdati \|\| 53 \|\|*

52-53. The devotee offering a libation of water once, according to the rites prescribed, gets beauty and health; the one offering it twice gets a place in Bhuvara region, the one performing it thrice goes to heaven.

In the same way, one who performs it seven times goes and enjoys in all the seven realms, one after the other: and the one who offers it during the whole of his lifetime, becomes united with Brahma.

## \|\| 61.54 \|\|

*homaṃ kṛtvā tataḥ paścād varjayenmānavaḥ phalam \|*  
*anena vidhinā yastu pumānarghyaṃ nivedayet \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. One who hears, reads or relates to others this ordinance, goes to the clime of Vishnu, and is respected by the Devas there

## Chapter 62

## \|\| 62.1 \|\|

*manuruvāca*  
*saubhāgyārogyaphaladam amutrākṣayyakārakam \|*  
*bhuktimuktipradaṃ deva tanme brūhi janārdana \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. King Vaivasvata Manu said: — Lord! pray tell me about a vrata (ordinance) that may be the giver of good luck, health, prosperity; emancipation, and everlasting fruit in the next world

## \|\| 62.2-3 \|\|

*matsya uvāca*  
*yadumāyāḥ purā deva uvāca purasūdanaḥ \|*  
*kailāsaśikharāsīno devyā pṛṣṭastadā kila \|\| 2 \|\|*

*kathāsu sampravṛttāsu dharmyāsu lalitāsu ca \|*  
*tadidānīṃ pravakṣyāmi bhuktimuktiphalapradam \|\| 3 \|\|*

2-3. Lord Matsya said: — I shall relate to you what Shiva, the destroyer of Pura; said to Parvati, in answer to a question put by her, while he was sitting on the beautiful peak of the Kailasa. I shall explain to you now the ordinance which gives prosperity and emancipation, -as enunciated by Him, in the course of a conversation on religious and pleasant subjects in which they were engaged.

## \|\| 62.4-6 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca*  
*śṛṇuṣvāvahitā devi tathaivānantapuṇyakṛt \|*  
*narāṇāmatha nārīṇām ārādhanamanuttamam \|\| 4 \|\|*

*nabhasye vātha vaiśākhe puṇyamārgaśirasya ca \|*  
*śuklapakṣe tṛtīyāyāṃ susnāto gaurasarṣapaiḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*gorocanaṃ sagomūtram uṣṇaṃ gośakṛtaṃ tathā \|*  
*dadhicandanasammiśraṃ lalāṭe tilakaṃ nyaset \|*  
*saubhāgyārogyadaṃ yasmāt sadā ca lalitāpriyam \|\| 6 \|\|*

4-6. Shiva said: Hear, O lady, attentively, the vow which gives. endless, merit; the best of vows, worthy of being followed by men and women. The devotee should put the tilaka mark on his forehead made with a paste of gorochana, fresh urine of the cow, cowdung and sandal, mixing them with curds; after bathing well and rubbing white mustard on his body, in the month of Bhadra, Vaishakha or the holy Margashirsha (Agrahayan and), on the third day of the bright fortnight. This is giver of auspiciousness and health, and is very much appreciated by the goddess Lalita.

## \|\| 62.7-10 \|\|

*pratipakṣaṃ tṛtīyāsu pumānāpītavāsasī \|*  
*dhārayedatha raktāni nārī cedatha saṃyatā \|\| 7 \|\|*

*vidhavā dhāturaktāni kumārī śuklavāsasī \|*  
*devīṃ tu pañcagavyena tataḥ kṣīreṇa kevalam \|*  
*snāpayenmadhunā tadvat puṣpagandhodakena ca \|\| 8 \|\|*

*pūjayecchuklapuṣpaiśca phalairnānāvidhairapi \|*  
*dhānyakājājilavaṇair guḍakṣīraghṛtānvitaiḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*śuklākṣatatilairarcyāṃ tato devīṃ sadārcayet \|*  
*pādādyabhyarcanaṃ kuryāt pratipakṣaṃ varānane \|\| 10 \|\|*

7-10. On every third day of the bright and the dark fortnights, the male devotees, with their minds controlled, should wear yellow garments, the married women red garments; the widows should put on ochre-coloured garments, and maidens should be clad in white, Afterwards, the devotee should bathe the goddess with panchagavya and milk, then with honey and then with water aromatic with flowers and sandal. Then white flowers, various kinds of fruits, salt, raw-sugar, milk, clarified butter, white rice, sesamum, coriander and cumin seed should be offered to the goddess, and a libation of water should be made on the third days to the bright and dark fortnights with the following mantras.

## \|\| 62.11-14 \|\|

*varadāyai namaḥ pādau tathā gulphau namaḥ śriyai \|*  
*aśokāyai namo jaṅghe pārvatyai jānunī tathā \|\| 11 \|\|*

*ūrū maṅgalakāriṇyai vāmadevyai tathā kaṭim \|*  
*padmodarāyai jaṭharam uraḥ kāmaśriyai namaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*karau saubhāgyadāyinyai bāhū haramukhaśriyai \|*  
*mukhaṃ darpaṇavāsinyai smaradāyai smitaṃ namaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*gauryai namastathā nāsām utpalāyai ca locane \|*  
*tuṣṭyai lalāṭamalakān kātyāyanyai śirastathā \|\| 14 \|\|*

11-14. The feet should be worshipped after reciting: (1) “ Varadayai namah,” At salute the giver of boons), the ankles after reciting (2) “ Shriyai namah,” (I salute you Lakshmi, the goddess of wealth), the legs after reciting (3) “Ashokayai namah,” the knees, after reciting (4) “ Parvatyai namah,” the hips, after reciting (3) “ Mangala Karinyai namah,” “I salute the giver of happiness,” the waist, after reciting (6)" Vamadevyai namah,” the stomach, after reciting (7) “ Padmodarayai namah,” the breast, after reciting. (8) “Kamadviyai namah,” the hands after reciting (9) “Saubhagyadayinyai namah,” the arms and the mouth, after reciting (10) “Shriyai namah,” the face after reciting (11) “Darpana visinyai nama,” one cheeks after reciting (12) “Smaradayai namah,” the nose after reciting (13) “Gauryai namah,” the eyes after reciting (14) “Utpaleyai namah”, the forehead and the tresses, after reciting (15) “ Tushtyai namah,” the head after reciting, (16) “ Katyayanyai namah.”

## \|\| 62.15-16 \|\|

*namo gauryai namo dhiṣṇyai namaḥ kāntyai namaḥ śriyai \|*  
*rambhāyai lalitāyai ca vāsudevyai namo namaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*evaṃ sampūjya vidhivad agrataḥ padmamālikhet \|*  
*pattrairdvādaśabhiryuktaṃ kuṅkumena sakarṇikam \|\| 16 \|\|*

15-16. The Goddesses Gauri, &c., should be worshipped also after pronouncing the mantra: ...... “ Salutations to Gauri , Dhisna, Kanti, Sri, Rambha, Lalita, and Vasudevi.” Then the devotee, having thus worshipped, according to ‘rule, should draw in front of the goddess, the figure of a lotus with twelve petals, with the pericarp made of saffron.

## \|\| 62.17-19 \|\|

*pūrveṇa vinyasedgaurīm aparṇāṃ ca tataḥ param \|*  
*bhavānīṃ dakṣiṇe tadvad rudrāṇīṃ ca tataḥ param \|\| 17 \|\|*

*vinyasetpaścime saumyāṃ sadā madanavāsinīm \|*  
*vāyavye pāṭalāmugrām antareṇa tato 'pyumām \|\| 18 \|\|*

*madhye yathāsvaṃ māṃsāṅgāṃ maṅgalāṃ kumudāṃ satīm \|*  
*rudraṃ ca madhye saṃsthāpya lalitāṃ karṇikopari \|*  
*kusumairakṣatairvārbhir namaskāreṇa vinyaset \|\| 19 \|\|*

17-19. The Goddess Gauri should be fixed on the Eastern petal, Arpana on the South-Eastern petal, Bhavani on the Southern petal, Rudrani on the Southwestern petal, Saumya on the Western petal, Madanavasini on the Northwestern petal; and after that Uma on the Northern petal; followed by the terrible Patala on the North-Eastern petal; in the Centre, in due order, should be placed, 1. Mamsanga, 2. Mangala, 3. Kumuda, 4. Sati; and the Lord Rudra in the midst of all these goddesses, the goddess Lalita on the pericarp of the lotus flower, the goddesses should be located with flowers, rice, and water by uttering the salutation, namah.

## \|\| 62.20 \|\|

*gītamaṅgalanirghoṣān kārayitvā suvāsinīḥ \|*  
*pūjayedraktavāsobhī raktamālyānulepanaiḥ \|*  
*sindūraṃ snānacūrṇaṃ ca tāsāṃ śirasi pātayet \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Afterwards, auspicious songs should be sung, conches blown, and the goddesses, adorned with red sandal, red cloth, red flowers, should be worshipped and the devotee should put red pigment and bathing powder on them after bathing them, for, red sindura and saffron are extremely aggreeable to them.

## \|\| 62.21 \|\|

*sindūrakuṅkumasnānam atīveṣṭatamaṃ yataḥ \|*  
*tathopadeṣṭāramapi pūjayedyatnato gurum \|*  
*na pūjyate gururyatra sarvāstatrāphalāḥ kriyāḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. The teacher (guru) should also be adored, with prescribed rites, because where the guru is left unadored, all the rites prove fruitless.

## \|\| 62.23-24 \|\|

*jātīpuṣpairmārgaśīrṣe pauṣe pītaiḥ kuraṇṭakaiḥ \|*  
*kundakuṅkumapuṣpaistu devīṃ māghe tu pūjayet \|*  
*sinduvāreṇa jātyā vā phālgune 'pyarcayedumām \|\| 23 \|\|*

*caitre tu mallikāśokair vaiśākhe gandhapāṭalaiḥ \|*  
*jyeṣṭhe kamalamandārair āṣāḍhe ca navāmbujaiḥ \|*  
*kadambairatha mālatyā śrāvaṇe pūjayetsadā \|\| 24 \|\|*

23-24. The Goddess Gauri should be worshipped with blue lotus, during the month of Bhadrapada; with red Bandhujiva flower in the month of Ashvina; with white lotus (Satapatra) during the month of Kartika; with jasmine flowers in the month of Margashirsha (Agrahayana); with the yellow amaranth flower in the month of Pausha; with the white jasmine or safflower in the month of Magha; and with the white jasmine or Sindhuvara flowers in the month of Phalguna; with the Champaka and the Ashoka flowers in the month of Chaitra; with Patala flowers in the month of Vaishakha; with lotus flowers in the month of Jyeshtha; with fresh lotus during Ashadha, with Kadamba and Malati flowers during Shravana.

## \|\| 62.25-26 \|\|

*gomūtraṃ gomayaṃ kṣīraṃ dadhi sarpiḥ kuśodakam \|*  
*bilvapattrārkapuṣpaṃ ca yavāngośṛṅgavāri ca \|\| 25 \|\|*

*pañcagavyaṃ ca bilvaṃ ca prāśayetkramaśastadā \|*  
*etadbhādrapadādyaṃ tu prāśanaṃ samudāhṛtam \|\| 26 \|\|*

25-26. The devotee should take the following things, one after the other, from the month of Bhadrapada: — Cow’s urine, cowdung, cow's milk, curds, clarified butter, the water of Kusha grass, the leaves of the wood-apple (bilva), the flowers of - Calotropis-gigantea, (arka), barley (yava), the ‘washing of the cow’s horns, Panchagavya and Bael fruit; and offer. these to the Goddess as Prashana. They should be taken one by one, viz., on the third day of Bhadrapada cow’s urine, in the month of Ashvina cowdung, and so on.

## \|\| 62.27 \|\|

*pratipakṣaṃ ca mithunaṃ tṛtīyāyāṃ varānane \|*  
*pūjayitvārcayedbhaktyā vastramālyānulepanaiḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. In the same way, on every third day of the bright and dark fortnights, the devotee should, after adoring the God (Shiva) with his consort,\* offer them cloths, garlands, flowers, sandal, etc. To a male God, a yellow garment should be offered and to a female goddess, saffron-colored dress

**Комментарий:**

\* This offering may be made also to a Brahmana and his wife.

## \|\| 62.28-29 \|\|

*puṃsaḥ pītāmbare dadyāt striyai kausumbhavāsasī \|*  
*niṣpāvājājilavaṇam ikṣudaṇḍaguḍānvitam \|*  
*tasyai dadyātphalaṃ puṣpaṃ suvarṇotpalasaṃyutam \|\| 28 \|\|*

*yathā na devi deveśas tvāṃ parityajya gacchati \|*  
*tathā mām uddharāśeṣa-duḥkhasaṃsārasāgarāt \|\| 29 \|\|*

28-29. The following things should also be given away to the Goddess: —

Nispava, cuminseed, salt, sugarcane, raw sugar, flowers, fruits, a lotus of gold, ‘with these words: “Goddess! as Shiva does not go any where forsaking: you, so you should save this devotee of yours through this mundane sea of troubles.

## \|\| 62.30-31 \|\|

*kumudā vimalānantā bhavānī ca sudhā śivā \|*  
*lalitā kamalā gaurī satī rambhātha pārvatī \|\| 30 \|\|*

*nabhasyādiṣu māseṣu prīyatāmityudīrayet \|*  
*vratānte śayanaṃ dadyāt suvarṇakamalānvitam \|\| 31 \|\|*

30-31. The Goddesses Kumuda, Vimala, Ananta, Bhavani, Sudha, Shiva, Lalita, Kamala, Gauri, Sati, Rambha, Parvati should also be worshipped. The devotes should invoke the pleasure of the Goddess by reciting each of the names mentioned above, one by one, from ‘Bhadrapada, viz. —

“Kumuda Priyatam,” Kumuda be pleased and satisfied, and so on. On the, completion of the ordinance, a bedstead, along with a golden lotus, should be given away to the Brahmana.

## \|\| 62.32 \|\|

*mithunāni caturviṃśad daśa dvo ca samarcayet \|*  
*aṣṭau ṣaḍvāpyatha punaś cānumāsaṃ samarcayet \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Every month, 24, 10, 8, 6 or 2 Brahmanas, with their wives, should be adored by the devotee and by his consort.

## \|\| 62.33 \|\|

*pūrvaṃ dattvā tu gurave śeṣānapyarcayedbudhaḥ \|*  
*uktānantatṛtīyaiṣā sadānantaphalapradā \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. After first giving Dakshina to the guru, it should be given to other Brahmanas. This is what has been laid down for the observance of this Ordinance — the giver of infinite benefit.

## \|\| 62.34 \|\|

*sarvapāpaharāṃ devi saubhāgyārogyavardhinīm \|*  
*na caināṃ vittaśāṭhyena kadācidapi laṅghayet \|*  
*naro vā yadi vā nārī vittaśāṭhyāt patatyadhaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. It is the destroyer of all sin, and the giver of good luck and health. It should ‘not be missed through miserliness, for the man or the woman who exercises miserliness goes to the lower regions.

## \|\| 62.35 \|\|

*garbhiṇī sūtikā naktaṃ kumārī vātha rogiṇī \|*  
*yadyaśuddhā tadānyena vārayetprayatā svayam \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Women who are in the family way, maids, those in confinement due to delivery, and those who are ailing, should take their food at night (not keeping the full fast). If one is in her menses, and so cannot observe it through impurity, she should get it observed by others, according to the prescribed rites. She herself should observe continence.

## \|\| 62.36 \|\|

*imāmanantaphaladāṃ yastṛtīyāṃ samācaret \|*  
*kalpakoṭiśataṃ sāgraṃ śivaloke mahīyate \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. One who observes this Tritiya, giver of endless fruit, with devotion, remains in the realm of Shiva for a hundred crore of Kalpas

## \|\| 62.37 \|\|

*vittahīno 'pi kurute varṣatrayamupoṣaṇaiḥ \|*  
*puṣpamantravidhānena so 'pi tatphalamāpnuyāt \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Even the poor who observes it with devotion for three years, according to the prescribed rites, using flowers alone for worship, gets the same benefit.

## \|\| 62.38 \|\|

*nārī vā kurute yā tu kumārī vidhavāthavā \|*  
*sāpi tatphalamāpnoti gauryanugrahalālitā \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. The maid, the married woman or the widow observing it, also gets the same benefits through the grace of the Goddess Gauri

## \|\| 62.39 \|\|

*iti paṭhati śṛṇoti vā ya itthaṃ giritanayāvratam indravāsasaṃsthaḥ \|*  
*matimapi ca dadāti so 'pi devair amaravadhūjanakiṃnaraiśca pūjyaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. One who reads or hears the relation of this Gauri Vrata or advises others to follow it, is honored by celestial beings and by the Devas and their consorts and the Kinnaras

## Chapter 63

## \|\| 63.1-3 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca*  
*athānyāmapi vakṣyāmi tṛtīyāṃ pāpanāśinīm \|*  
*rasakalyāṇinīmetāṃ purākalpavido viduḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*māghamāse tu samprāpte tṛtīyāṃ śuklapakṣataḥ \|*  
*prātargavyena payasā tilaiḥ snānaṃ samācaret \|\| 2 \|\|*

*snāpayenmadhunā devīṃ tathaivekṣurasena ca \|*  
*gandhodakena tu punar lepayetkuṅkumena tu \|*  
*dakṣiṇāṅgāni sampūjya tato vāmāni pūjayet \|\| 3 \|\|*

1-3. ‘The Lord Shiva said: — I shall now describe to you another Tritiya ordinance that washes off all the sins and is known as “Rasakalyanini tritiya” by knowers of ancient rituals. In observing it the devotee should bathe in cow's milk and sesamum on the third day of the bright fortnight in the month of Magha, The Goddess should be bathed with honey and the juice of sugarcane. The right hand side of the Goddess should be worshipped first and the left hand side afterwards, with the following mantras.

## \|\| 63.4 \|\|

*lalitāyai namo devyāḥ pādau gulphau tato 'rcayet \|*  
*jaṅghāṃ jānuṃ tathā śāntyai tathaivoruṃ śriyai namaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. The feet and the ankle should be worshipped, after reciting (1) ... “I salute the Goddess Lalita,” the legs and the knees, after pronouncing (2) ... Santyai namah the thighs, after reciting (8) ... “Sriyai namah."

## \|\| 63.5 \|\|

*madālasāyai tu kaṭim amalāyai tathodaram \|*  
*stanau madanavāsinyai kumudāyai ca kandarām \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. The waist, after reciting (4) ... “Madalasayai namah,” the stomach, after reciting (5) ... “Amalayai namah,” the breasts, after reciting (6) ... Madavasinyai namah,” the shoulders, after reciting (7) ... Kamudayai namah.

## \|\| 63.6 \|\|

*bhujaṃ bhujāgraṃ mādhavyai kamalāyai mukhasmite \|*  
*bhūlalāṭaṃ ca rudrāṇyai śaṃkarāyai tathālakān \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. The arms and the hands, after reciting (8) ... “Madhavyai namab,” the mouth and the face, after reciting (9) ... “Kamalayai -namah,” the brows and the forehead, after reciting (10) ... “ Rudranyai namah,” the locks of hair, after reciting (11)... “Shankarayainamah.”

## \|\| 63.7 \|\|

*mukuṭaṃ viśvavāsinyai śiraḥ kāntyai tathārcayet \|*  
*madanāyai lalāṭaṃ tu mohanāyai punarbhruvau \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. The Coronet, after saying (12) “Vishvavasinyai namah,” the head, after reciting (18) ... “Kantyai namah,” the left forehead, after reciting (14) ...

“Madantyal namab,” the brows, after reciting (15) ... “Mohandyat mamah.”

## \|\| 63.8 \|\|

*netre candrārdhadhāriṇyai tuṣṭyai ca vadanaṃ punaḥ \|*  
*utkaṇṭhinyai namaḥ kaṇṭham amṛtāyai namaḥ stanau \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. The eyes, after reciting (16) ... “Chandrardhadherinyai. namah,” the mouth after reciting (17) ... “Tushtyai nama,” the throat, after rotting (18) ... Utkanthinyai namah,” the breasts, after reciting (19) ... Amritayai namah”

## \|\| 63.9 \|\|

*rambhāyai vāmakukṣiṃ ca viśokāyai namaḥ kaṭim \|*  
*hṛdayaṃ manmathādhiṣṇyai pāṭalāyai tathodaram \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The left abdomen by reciting (20) ... “Rambhayai namah” the waist, after reciting. (21) Visokayai namah,” the host, after reciting (22). “Mantathadhiggyai namah,” the stomach, after reciting (23) ... “Patalayai namah.

## \|\| 63.10 \|\|

*kaṭiṃ suratavāsinyai tathoruṃ campakapriye \|*  
*jānujaṅghe namo gauryai gāyatryai ghuṭike namaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. The waist, after reciting (24) ... “Suratvasinyay namah, the things, after reciting (25) ... “Champakapriyayai namah”, the knees and the legs, after reciting (26) “Gauryai namah”, the ankles, after reciting (27) ... “Gayatryai namah”.

## \|\| 63.11 \|\|

*dharādharāyai pādau tu viśvakāyai namaḥ śiraḥ \|*  
*namo bhavānyai kāminyai kāmadevyai jagatpriye \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. The feet, after reciting (28) ... “Dharadharayai namah”, the head, after reciting “Vishvakaryai namah”. Namobhavaniyai, Kaminyai, Kamadevyai, Jagatapriya, should also be said.

## \|\| 63.12 \|\|

*ānandāyai sunandāyai subhadrāyai namo namaḥ \|*  
*evaṃ sampūjya vidhivad dvijadāmpatyam arcayet \|*  
*bhojayitvānnapānena madhureṇa vimatsaraḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. The Goddess should be worshipped like this, and then the Brahmana and his wife should also be honoured and feasted with sweet food and drink.

## \|\| 63.13 \|\|

*jalapūritaṃ tathā kumbhaṃ śuklāmbaraugadvayam \|*  
*dattvā suvarṇakamalaṃ gandhamālyaiḥ samarcayet \|\| 13 \|\|*

13 A pitcher, full of water and decorated with a pair of white cloths, along with a golden lotus and flower-garlands and sandal, should be given away in-charity to the Brahmana.

## \|\| 63.14 \|\|

*prīyatāmatra kumudā gṛhṇīyāllavaṇavratam \|*  
*anena vidhinā devī māsi māsi sadārcayet \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Afterwards, the devotee should say, O Kumuda Goddess! be pleased And accept this way, the Goddess should be worshipped each month. The Goddess Kumuda becomes pleased with the devotee by the observance of this ordinance

## \|\| 63.15 \|\|

*lavaṇaṃ varjayenmāghe phālgune ca guḍaṃ punaḥ \|*  
*tailaṃ rājiṃ tathā caitre varjyaṃ ca madhu mādhave \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. In the month of Magha, salt should not be taken, raw sugar should be avoided in Phalguna, oil and mustard should be discarded in Chaitra, and honey and sweets should be avoided in Vaishakha

## \|\| 63.16 \|\|

*pānakaṃ jyeṣṭhamāse tu āṣāḍhe cātha jīrakam \|*  
*śrāvaṇe varjayetkṣīraṃ dadhi bhādrapade tathā \|\| 16 \|\|*

16 In the month of Jaishtha puddings should be avoided, cumin-seed should be discarded in Asadha, milk in Shravana, curds in Bhadrapada.

## \|\| 63.17 \|\|

*ghṛtamāśvauje tadvad ūrje varjyaṃ ca mākṣikam \|*  
*dhānyakaṃ mārgaśīrṣe tu pauṣe varjyā ca śarkarā \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Clarified butter in Ashvina, honey in Karttika, coriander in Margashirsha sugar in Pausha

## \|\| 63.18 \|\|

*vratānte karakaṃ pūrṇam eteṣāṃ māsi māsi ca \|*  
*dadyāddvikālavelāyāṃ pūrṇapātreṇa saṃyutam \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. On the completion of the ordinance, a Kamandalu, full of water, &c., along with full vessel, should be given away in charity, each month, in the afternoon

## \|\| 63.19-20 \|\|

*laḍḍukāñchvetavarṇāṃśca saṃyāvamatha pūrikāḥ \|*  
*ghārikān apyapūpāṃśca piṣṭāpūpāṃśca maṇḍakān \|\| 19 \|\|*

*kṣīraṃ śākaṃ ca dadhyannam iṇḍaryo 'śokavartikāḥ \|*  
*māghādikramaśo dadyād etāni karakopari \|\| 20 \|\|*

19-20. White balls of sweet (Laddu), (2) mohanbhoga, pudding, (3) cake (puri); (4) gharika cake, (5) sweet cake, (6) sweet cake mixed with spices, (7) mandake, (8) milk, (9) vegetable, (10) curd rice, (11) indari marti, (12) and avokavartika Gojha, should be given, one by one, after putting them on the top of the Kamandalu in each month, i.e., in Magha, white balls of sweet should be given, in the next month mohanbhoga, and so on,

## \|\| 63.21-22 \|\|

*kumudā mādhavī gaurī rambhā bhadrā jayā śivā \|*  
*umā ratiḥ satī tadvan maṅgalā ratilālasā \|\| 21 \|\|*

*kramānmāghādi sarvatra prīyatāmiti kīrtayet \|*  
*sarvatra pañcagavyena prāśanaṃ samudāhṛtam \|*  
*upavāsī bhavennityam aśakte naktamiṣyate \|\| 22 \|\|*

21-22. Kumuda, Madhavi, Gauri, Rambha, Bhadra, Jaya, Shiva, Uma, Rati, Sati, Mangala, Ratilalasa should be invoked, turn, by turn each month, beginning with Magha, and say ‘priyatem’. The devotee should offer to the goddess the pridana with pan chagavya, and should observe a fast on each of the prescribed days; if he cannot keep the full fast, he might eat something in the night

## \|\| 63.23-25 \|\|

*punarmāghe tu samprāpte śarkarāṃ karakopari \|*  
*kṛtvā tu kāñcanīṃ gaurīṃ pañcaratnasamanvitām \|\| 23 \|\|*

*haimīmaṅguṣṭhamātrāṃ ca sākṣasūtrakamaṇḍalum \|*  
*caturbhujāminduutāṃ sitanetrapaṭāvṛtām \|\| 24 \|\|*

*tadvadgomithunaṃ śuklaṃ suvarṇāsyaṃ sitāmbaram \|*  
*savastrabhājanaṃ dadyād bhavānī prīyatāmiti \|\| 25 \|\|*

23-25. Again in the month of Magha, sugar should be placed on the Kamandalu, and, after saying, “Goddess be pleased,” should be given away to a Brahmana in charity: — the golden image of Parvati, of the size of an inch, after decorating it with the five gems, rosary, sacred thread, Kamandalu, the figure of the moon with four arms, white eyes and white clothes; a pair of white cows, decorated with gold and covered with white cloth, along with a milking vessel.

## \|\| 63.26-27 \|\|

*anena vidhinā yastu rasakalyāṇinīvratam \|*  
*kuryātsa sarvapāpebhyas tatkṣaṇādeva mucyate \|\| 26 \|\|*

*navārbudasahasraṃ tu na duḥkhī jāyate naraḥ \|*  
*suvarṇakamalaṃ gauri māsi māsi dadannaraḥ \|*  
*agniṣṭomasahasrasya yatphalaṃ tadavāpnuyāt \|\| 27 \|\|*

26-27. One who observes this Rasa Kalyanini Tritiya ordinance, becomes instantly liberated from sins and never remains crieved for 9000001000 years. One who gives away an image of Parvati, with a golden lotus, each month, gets the benefit of performing a thousand agnistoma sacrifices.

## \|\| 63.28 \|\|

*nārī vā kurute yā tu kumārī vā varānane \|*  
*vidhavā yā tathā nārī sāpi tatphalamāpnuyāt \|*  
*saubhāgyārogyasampannā gaurīloke mahīyate \|\| 28 \|\|*
