28\. The married woman, or the maid, or the widow who observes this ordinance, derives the same benefit and gets good luck and health, and goes to the realm of Parvati.

## \|\| 63.29 \|\|

*iti paṭhati śṛṇoti śrāvayedyaḥ prasaṅgāt kalikaluṣavimuktaḥ pārvatīlokameti \|*  
*matimapi ca narāṇāṃ yo dadāti priyārthaṃ vibudhapativimāne nāyakaḥ syādamoghaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. One who reads or hears this, is liberated from the sins of the Kali Age and goes to the region of Parvati. One who relates this to others or induces others to observe this vrata, also becomes like the Lord of the Devas and moves about in aerial chariots

## Chapter 64

## \|\| 64.1 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca*  
*tathaivānyāṃ pravakṣyāmi tṛtīyāṃ pāpanāśinīm \|*  
*nāmnā ca loke vikhyātām ārdrānandakarīmimām \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Shiva said: — Narada! I shall now explain to you about the ordinance known as Ardranandakari trittya, which is the destroyer of all sing

## \|\| 64.2 \|\|

*yadā śuklatṛtīyāyām āṣāḍharkṣaṃ bhavetkvacit \|*  
*brahmarkṣaṃ vā mṛgarkṣaṃ vā hasto mūlamathāpi vā \|*  
*darbhagandhodakaiḥ snānaṃ tadā samyaksamācaret \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. On the third day of the bright fortnight, whenever the moon is in the mansion of ‘any one of the following asterisms, Purvashadha (or Uttarashadha), Rohini, Mrigashira, Hasta or Mala, the devotee should bathe a in water mingled with kusha and incense.

## \|\| 64.3 \|\|

*śuklamālyāmbaradharaḥ śuklagandhānulepanaḥ \|*  
*bhavānīmarcayedbhaktyā śuklapuṣpaiḥ sugandhibhiḥ \|*  
*mahādevena sahitām upaviṣṭāṃ mahāsane \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Afterwards, he should wear a garland of white flowers, white raiment’s, and use white sandal paste, and then worship goddess Bhavani, along with Her consort, Mahadeva, with white flowers and incense, and then seat them in their proper places, and recite the following mantras

## \|\| 64.5 \|\|

*rambhāyai pūjayedūrū śivāya ca pinākinaḥ \|*  
*adityai ca kaṭiṃ devyāḥ śūlinaḥ śūlapāṇaye \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Parvati’s feet should be worshipped, after reciting “Vasudevyai namah”, Shiva's feet should be worshipped, after reciting “Vasudevyai namah”, and their legs after reciting “Shokavinashinyai namah and Their hips, after reciting — “Rambhayayi namah” for the goddess, and “Shivayaa namah” for the God Shiva. The waist of the goddess, after reciting “Adityai namah”, and of the God by reciting “Sulapanaye namah.”

## \|\| 64.6 \|\|

*mādhavyai ca tathā nābhim atha śambhorbhavāya ca \|*  
*stanāvānandakāriṇyai śaṃkarasyendudhāriṇe \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. The navel of the Goddess, after reciting “Madhavyai namah,” and of the God Shambhu, by reciting “Bhavaya namah.” The breast of the Chas, after reciting “Anandakarinyai namah,” and of Shankara by Indudharine namah.”

## \|\| 64.7 \|\|

*utkaṇṭhinyai namaḥ kaṇṭhaṃ nīlakaṇṭhāya vai haram \|*  
*karāvutpaladhāriṇyai rudrāya ca jagatpate \|*  
*bāhū ca parirambhiṇyai triśūlāya harasya ca \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. The throat of the Goddess, after reciting “Utkanthinyai namah” and of the God Hara by “Nilakanthaya namah.” The hands of the Goddess, after reciting “Utpaladharinyai namah,” and of the Lord of the world by “Rudraya namah.” The arms of the Goddess, after reciting “ Parirambhinyai namah,” and of Hara by “ Trishulaya namah.”

## \|\| 64.8 \|\|

*devyā mukhaṃ vilāsinyai vṛṣeśāya punarvibhoḥ \|*  
*smitaṃ sasmeralīlāyai viśvavaktrāya vai vibho \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. The mouth of the Goddess, after reciting “Vilashayai namah,” and the mouth of Shiva, after reciting “Vrisesaya namah.” The cheek of the Goddess after reciting “ Sasmeralilayai namah,” and of the God by “Vishvavaktraya namah.”

## \|\| 64.9-10 \|\|

*netre madanavāsinyai viśvadhāmne triśūlinaḥ \|*  
*bhruvau nṛtyapriyāyai tu tāṇḍaveśāya śūlinaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*devyā lalāṭamindrāṇyai havyavāhāya vai vibhoḥ \|*  
*svāhāyai mukuṭaṃ devyā vibhorgaṅgādharāya vai \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. The eyes of the Goddess, by reciting “ Madanavasinyai namah,” and of the God Trishulin by “ Vishvadhamne namah.” The brows of the Goddess, far reciting “ Nrityapriyayai namah,” and of the Lord by ‘Tandaveshaya namah.” The forehead of the goddess, after reciting “Indrayai namah, and of the God by “Havyavahaya namah,” ‘The coronet of the Goddess, alter reciting “Svahayai namah,” and of the God “ Gangadharaya namah.”

## \|\| 64.11 \|\|

*viśvakāyau viśvamukhau viśvapādakarau śivau \|*  
*prasannavadanau vande pārvatīparameśvarau \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Then the following prayer should be said to them ... I salute Parvati and Parameshvara, the whole universe is whose body, mouth, hand and feet, the auspicious ones with gracious countenance.

## \|\| 64.12-13 \|\|

*evaṃ sampūjya vidhivad agrataḥ śivayoḥ punaḥ \|*  
*padmotpalāni rajasā nānāvarṇena kārayet \|\| 12 \|\|*

*śaṅkhacakre sakaṭake svastikāṅkuśacāmarān \|*  
*yāvantaḥ pāṃsavastatra rajasaḥ patitā bhuvi \|*  
*tāvadvarṣasahasrāṇi śivaloke mahīyate \|\| 13 \|\|*

12-13. Having worshipped in this way, he should make, according to rules, in front of the image of Shiva and Parvati, pictures of. lotus, etc., with various coloured powders. He should also make pictures of conch, quoit, flags, tridents (svastika, goad) and chamara, As many grains of the coloured Powder as fall on the ground, the devotes remains for the same number of thousands of years in the realm of Shiva.

## \|\| 64.14 \|\|

*catvāri ghṛtapātrāṇi sahiraṇyāni śaktitaḥ \|*  
*dattvā dvijāya karakam udakānnasamanvitam \|*  
*pratipakṣaṃ caturmāsaṃ yāvadetannivedayet \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. For four months, in the dark as well as in the bright fortnight, the devotee should give away to the Brahmanas four kamandalus full of water, grain and gold, and having a vessel of clarified butter and gold out op of them.

## \|\| 64.15-18 \|\|

*tatastu caturo māsān pūrvavatkarakopari \|*  
*catvāri saktupātrāṇi tilapātrāṇyataḥ param \|\| 15 \|\|*

*gandhodakaṃ puṣpavāri candanaṃ kuṅkumodakam \|*  
*apakvaṃ dadhi dugdhaṃ ca gośṛṅgodakameva ca \|\| 16 \|\|*

*piṣṭodakaṃ tathā vāri kuṣṭhacūrṇānvitaṃ punaḥ \|*  
*uśīrasalilaṃ tadvad yavacūrṇodakaṃ punaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*tilodakaṃ ca saṃprāṣya svapenmārgaśirādiṣu \|*  
*māseṣu pakṣadvitayaṃ prāśanaṃ samudāhṛtam \|\| 18 \|\|*

15-18. Then, for another four months, the 4 kamandalus should be given away, after placing 4 posts of barley meal (Saktu), along with a vessel, full of sesamum on top of them, and after that, for another four months, 4 pots to sesamum should be placed on top of the kamandalus and for one year from the month of Margashira on the tritiya tithi the devotee should offer the following eatables to the deities, one in each month (1) Incense: with water (2) flower, (3) sandal and water, (4) saffron and water, (5) curd, (6) unboiled milk (7) washing of the cow's horns, (8) water and flour, (9) water mixed with powdered kushtha (a kind of Plant, called Costus spesiosus), (10) Andropogan Muricatus, (11) water mixed with powdered barley, (12) cumin seed, sesamum and water.

## \|\| 64.19 \|\|

*sarvatra śuklapuṣpāṇi praśastāni sadārcane \|*  
*dānakāle ca sarvatra mantrametamudīrayet \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. In the worship of this Goddess, White flowers are said to be the best; and at the time of giving away dana (presents. to the Brahmanas) the following mantra should he uttered.

## \|\| 64.20 \|\|

*gaurī me prīyatāṃ nityam aghanāśāya maṅgalā \|*  
*saubhāgyāyāstu lalitā bhavānī sarvasiddhaye \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. “O Goddess Gauri, be pleased, O Goddess Mangala, the giver of happiness, liberate me from sins, O Goddess Lalita, promote my good luck, O Bhavani, fulfil all my desires.

## \|\| 64.21-22 \|\|

*saṃvatsarānte lavaṇaṃ guḍakumbhaṃ ca sarjikām \|*  
*candanaṃ netrapaṭṭaṃ ca sahiraṇyāmbujena tu \|\| 21 \|\|*

*umāmaheśvaraṃ haimaṃ tadvadikṣuphalairyutam \|*  
*satūlāvaraṇāṃ śayyāṃ saviśrāmāṃ nivedayet \|*  
*sapatnīkāya viprāya gaurī me prīyatāmiti \|\| 22 \|\|*

21-22. After a year, the devotee should give away to the Brahmana and his wife, after saying, “O Gauri, be pleased with me,” the following things: pitchers, full of salt and raw usar, natron, sandal, cloth (netra, patta), Totus, along with gold, the images of Shiva and Parvati made in gold, suparcane, cotton and bedstead, along with mattress and pillows.

## \|\| 64.23-24 \|\|

*ārdrānandakarī nāmnā tṛtīyaiṣā sanātanī \|*  
*yāmupoṣya naro yāti śambhoryatparamaṃ padam \|\| 23 \|\|*

*iha loke sadānandam āpnoti dhanasampadaḥ \|*  
*āurārogyasampattyā na kaścicchokamāpnuyāt \|\| 24 \|\|*

23-24. One who observes this ordinance, called Ardranandakaritrittya, goes to the region of Shiva and attains healthy longevity, wealth and happiness this world and never gets grief or woe.

## \|\| 64.25 \|\|

*nārī vā kurute yā tu kumārī vidhavā ca yā \|*  
*sāpi tatphalamāpnoti devyanugrahalālitā \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Married women, or maidens, or widows also, through the grace of the Goddess, attain the same benefits.

## \|\| 64.26 \|\|

*pratipakṣamupoṣyaivaṃ mantrārcanavidhānavit \|*  
*rudrāṇīlokamabhyeti punarāvṛttidurlabham \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. The person, acquainted with the rites, duly observing this ordinance, goes to the realm of the Goddess Parvati.

## \|\| 64.27 \|\|

*ya idaṃ śṛṇuyānnityaṃ śrāvayedvāpi mānavaḥ \|*  
*śakraloke sa gandharvaiḥ pūjyate 'pi ugatrayam \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. One, who hears or relates this ordinance to others goes to the region of Indra, and is venerated by the Gandharvas for three ages.

## \|\| 64.28 \|\|

*ānandadāṃ sakaladuḥkhaharāṃ tṛtīyāṃ yā strī karotyavidhavā vidhavātha vāpi \|*  
*sā sve gṛhe sukhaśatānyanubhūya bhūyo gaurīpadaṃ sadayitā dayitā prayāti \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. The woman, whose husband is alive, and the widow, who observes this ordinance, attain unbounded happiness in their houses, and in the end goes to the region of Parvati, along with her husband, and the widow rejoins her husband there.

## Chapter 65

## \|\| 65.1 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca*  
*athānyāmapi vakṣyāmi tṛtīyāṃ sarvakāmadām \|*  
*yasyāṃ dattaṃ hutaṃ japtaṃ sarvaṃ bhavati cākṣayam \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Shiva said: — I shall now explain to you about the Akshayatritya (giver of all desires) vrata, on which day the performance of charity, sacrifice or Japa gives inexhaustible benefit to the devotee.

## \|\| 65.2 \|\|

*vaiśākhaśuklapakṣe tu tṛtīyā yairupoṣitā \|*  
*akṣayaṃ phalamāpnoti sarvasya sukṛtasya ca \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. One who keeps a fast on the third day of bright fortnight, in the month of Vaishakha, derives inexhaustible fruit of all his good deeds.

## \|\| 65.3 \|\|

*sā tathā kṛttikopetā viśeṣeṇa supūjitā \|*  
*tatra dattaṃ hutaṃ japtaṃ sarvamakṣayamucyate \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. lf the asterism Krittika happens to fall on that day, it becomes still more sacred, and charity, sacrifice or yapa performed then, begets inexhaustible benefits.

## \|\| 65.4-5 \|\|

*akṣayā saṃtatistasyās tasyāṃ sukṛtamakṣayam \|*  
*akṣataiḥ pūjyate viṣṇus tena sāpyakṣayā smṛtā \|*  
*akṣataistu narāḥ snātā viṣṇordattvā tathākṣatān \|\| 4 \|\|*

*vipreṣu dattvā tāneva tathā saktūn susaṃkṛtān \|*  
*yathānnabhuṅmahābhāgaḥ phalamakṣayyamaśnute \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. The progeny of the devotee will be unlimited and her good deeds will have no end, since Vishnu is worshipped on that day with Akshata, it is called Akshaya tritiya. On that day, the devotee should bathe in water mixed with unhusked rice (Akshata). He should also offer unhusked rice to Vishnu and to the Brahmanas, or well-made barley meal (Shaktu) should be offered to the Brahmanas as well as taken by the devotee himself. The devotes who does this gets everlasting benefitt

## \|\| 65.6-7 \|\|

*ekāmapyuktavatkṛtvā tṛtīyāṃ vidhivannaraḥ \|*  
*etāsāmapi sarvāsāṃ tṛtīyānāṃ phalaṃ bhavet \|\| 6 \|\|*

*tṛtīyāyāṃ samabhyarcya sopavāso janārdanam \|*  
*rājasūyaphalaṃ prāpya gatimagryāṃ ca vindati \|\| 7 \|\|*

6-7. One who keeps up, according to rules, this tritiya ordinance even once, begets the benefit of having observed all the tritiyas, and one who keeps a complete fast on this tritiya and worships Janardana, gets the benefit of having performed a Rajasuya sacrifice, and attains bliss.

## Chapter 66

## \|\| 66.1-2 \|\|

*manuruvāca*  
*madhurā bhāratī kena vratena madhusūdana \|*  
*tathaiva janasaubhāgyam atividyāsu kauśalam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*abhedaścāpi dampatyos tathā bandhujanena ca \|*  
*āuśca vipulaṃ puṃsāṃ tanme kathaya mādhava \|\| 2 \|\|*

1-2. Vaivasvata Manu asked: — Lord! By what vrata does one get sweet speech, worldly prosperity, intelligence, skill in all arts and sciences, inseparable conjugal union, fast friendship and longevity. Pray explain all this to me.

## \|\| 66.3 \|\|

*matsya uvāca*  
*samyakpṛṣṭaṃ tvayā rājañ chṛṇu sārasvataṃ vratam \|*  
*yasya saṃkīrtanādeva tuṣyatīha sarasvatī \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. The Lord answered: — King! you have put a very useful question to me. Now listen attentively to the description of Sarasvata ordinance, the mere recitation of which gives so much pleasure to the Goddess Sarasvati.

## \|\| 66.4 \|\|

*yo yadbhaktaḥ pumānkuryād etadvratamanuttamam \|*  
*tadvāsarādau sampūjya viprānetānsamācaret \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. The devotee should begin this vrata by adoring the Brahmanas on the morning of the day which is most proper for the worship of the Goddess he usually worships.

## \|\| 66.5 \|\|

*athavādityavāreṇa grahatārābalena ca \|*  
*pāyasaṃ bhojayedviprān kṛtvā brāhmaṇavācanam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Or, the fast should be observed on a Sunday and the Brahmanas fell with rive, cooked in milk and sugar, after consulting the stars and determining as auspicious hour for the feast.

## \|\| 66.6 \|\|

*śuklavastrāṇi dattvā ca sahiraṇyāni śaktitaḥ \|*  
*gāyatrīṃ pūjayedbhaktyā śuklamālyānulepanaiḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. According to his means, the devotee should give away gold and cloth in charity, and should then worship Gayatri with garlands of white flowers, and with white sandal, &c.

## \|\| 66.7 \|\|

*yathā na devi bhagavān brahmaloke pitāmahaḥ \|*  
*tvāṃ parityajya saṃtiṣṭhet tathā bhava varapradā \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. And then pray, “O Goddess! as Brahma, the father of the universe, never lives in the Brahmaloka separate from you; in the same way be pleased to give me boon

## \|\| 66.8 \|\|

*vedāḥ śāstrāṇi sarvāṇi gītanṛtyādikaṃ ca yat \|*  
*na vihīnaṃ tvayā devi tathā me santu siddhayaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. “Goddess! the sacred Vedas, the Shastras, the songs and the dances, &c., are not apart from you; let by your grace success attend me.

## \|\| 66.9 \|\|

*lakṣmīrmedhā dharā puṣṭir gaurī tuṣṭiḥ prabhā matiḥ \|*  
*etābhiḥ pāhi cāṣṭābhis tanubhirmāṃ sarasvati \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. “O Goddess Sarasvati! protect me with your eightfold body, viz., Lakshmi, Medha, Dhara, Pushti, Gauri, Tushti, Prabha and Mati.

## \|\| 66.10-11 \|\|

*evaṃ sampūjya gāyatrīṃ vīṇākṣamaṇidhāriṇīm \|*  
*śuklapuṣpākṣatair bhaktyā sakamaṇḍalupustakām \|*  
*maunavratena bhuñjīta sāyaṃ prātastu dharmavit \|\| 10 \|\|*

*pañcamyāṃ pratipakṣaṃ ca pūjayedbrahmavāsinīm \|*  
*tathaiva taṇḍulaprasthaṃ ghṛtapātreṇa saṃyutam \|*  
*kṣīraṃ dadyāddhiraṇyaṃ ca gāyatrī prīyatāmiti \|\| 11 \|\|*

10-11. Gayatri with a Vina (a kind of harp), a rosary of Aksha, a Kamanduln and a book in each hand, should be worshipped with devotion, with white flowers and unhusked rice, &c. The pious devotee should, then in silence, take his meals, morning and evening, without speaking a word at the time.

He should worship the Brahmavasini (Gayatri), on the fifth day of both the fortnights. He should also offer her a quantity of (Prastha) measure of rice, placed in a vessel and full of clarified butter and milk and gold, by invoking her in the following words: — “Gayatri, be pleased with these”.

## \|\| 66.12 \|\|

*saṃdhyāyāṃ ca tathā maunam etatkurvansamācaret \|*  
*nāntarā bhojanaṃ kuryād yāvanmāsāstrayodaśa \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. The devotee, following this rite, should observe the vow of silence in the evening, and should have in the daytime no meal, till 13 months are over.

## \|\| 66.13 \|\|

*samāpte tu vrate kuryād bhojanaṃ śuklataṇḍulaiḥ \|*  
*pūrvaṃ savastraugmaṃ ca dadyādviprāya bhojanam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. On the completion of the ordinance (vrata), the devotes should take white rice, and, before doing so, should feed a Brahmana and give him couple of clothes.

## \|\| 66.14-15 \|\|

*devyā vitānaṃ ghaṇṭāṃ ca sitanetre payasvinīm \|*  
*candanaṃ vastraugmaṃ ca dadyācca śikharaṃ punaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*tathopadeṣṭāramapi bhaktyā sampūjayedgurum \|*  
*vittaśāṭhyena rahito vastramālyānulepanaiḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

14-15. Then he should give away, in honour of the Goddess, the flags, bells, a silver — eyed milk cow, sandal, a pair of-clothes, and a crest jewel.

Afterwards, the preceptor should be worshipped with. devotion, with garlands, cloths and sandal paste, without giving way to miserliness.

## \|\| 66.16-17 \|\|

*anena vidhinā yastu kuryātsārasvataṃ vratam \|*  
*vidyāvānarthasaṃyukto raktakaṇṭhaśca jāyate \|\| 16 \|\|*

*sarasvatyāḥ prasādena brahmaloke mahīyate \|*  
*nārī vā kurute yā tu sāpi tatphalagāminī \|\| 17 \|\|*

16-17. One who worships Sarasvati in this way, becomes learned, wealthy and gets a melodious voice. Besides this, he goes to the region of Brahma through the grace of the Goddess. The women folk, observing this ordinance, too, get the same benefit. Such devotees reside in the Brahmaloka for three Ayuta Kalpas.

## \|\| 66.18 \|\|

*brahmaloke vased rājan yāvat kalpāutatrayam \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. One who reads or hears this, goes and enjoys In the region of Vidyadhara, for three Kalpas.

## Chapter 67

## \|\| 67.1 \|\|

*candrādityoparāge tu yatsnānamabhidhīyate \|*  
*tadahaṃ śrotumicchāmi dravyamantravidhānavit \|\| 1 \|\|*

1 Manu said: — Lord! Knower of the rites, the mantras and of the things to be given away in charity at the time of solar and lunar eclipses, I wish do hear from you the method of bathing at those times.

## \|\| 67.2-4 \|\|

*matsya uvāca*  
*yasya rāśiṃ samāsādya bhavedgrahaṇasamplavaḥ \|*  
*tasya snānaṃ pravakṣyāmi mantrauṣadhavidhānataḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*candroparāgaṃ samprāpya kṛtvā brāhmaṇavācanam \|*  
*sampūjya caturo viprāñ śuklamālyānulepanaiḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*pūrvamevoparāgasya samāsādyauṣadhādikam \|*  
*sthāpayec caturaḥ kumbhān avraṇānsāgarāniti \|\| 4 \|\|*

2-4. The Lord said: When the eclipse takes place, at the time when the sun or the moon is in that particular sign of the zodiac under which a person is born, it is necessary that he should bathe in water mixed with herbs, according to the prescribed rituals, as mentioned below. When there is a lunar eclipse, the devotee should get blessings invoked by Brahmanas and worship four of them with white flowers and sandal paste, and place four flawless pitchers, full of water and herbs, before the commencement of the eclipse, and consider these pitchers as representing oceans.

## \|\| 67.5-7 \|\|

*gajāśvarathyāvalmīka-saṃgamāddhradagokulāt \|*  
*rājadvārapradeśācca mṛdamānīya cākṣipet \|\| 5 \|\|*

*pañcagavyaṃ ca kumbheṣu śuddhamuktāphalāni ca \|*  
*rocanāṃ padmaśaṅkhau ca pañcaratnasamanvitam \|\| 6 \|\|*

*sphaṭikaṃ candanaṃ śvetaṃ tīrthavāri sasarṣapam \|*  
*rājadantaṃ sakumudaṃ tathaivośīraguggulam \|*  
*etatsarvaṃ vinikṣipya kumbheṣvāvāhayetsurān \|\| 7 \|\|*

5-7. "Then the Devas should be invoked, after putting the following things in the pitchers — The earth of the elephant ward, of the stable, of the chariot-house (or, road), of the anthill, of the tank, of the. confluence of two fivers, of the cattle-yard and of the king’s gateway, as well as panchagavya, good and genuine pearls, gorochane, lotus, conch-shell, pancharatna (five jevels), quartz (crystal), white sandal, Ganges water, mustard, andropogan muricatus, Kumudini (lotus), Rajadanta (ivory), and resin (guggul).

## \|\| 67.8-16 \|\|

*sarve samudrāḥ saritas tīrthāni jaladā nadāḥ \|*  
*āyāntu yajamānasya duritakṣayakārakāḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*yo 'sau vajradharo deva ādityānāṃ prabhurmataḥ \|*  
*sahasranayanaścendro grahapīḍāṃ vyapohatu \|\| 9 \|\|*

*mukhaṃ yaḥ sarvadevānāṃ saptārciramitadyutiḥ \|*  
*candroparāgasambhūtām agniḥ pīḍāṃ vyapohatu \|\| 10 \|\|*

*yaḥ karmasākṣī bhūtānāṃ dharmo mahiṣavāhanaḥ \|*  
*yamaścandroparāgotthāṃ mama pīḍāṃ vyapohatu \|\| 11 \|\|*

*rakṣogaṇādhipaḥ sākṣāt pralayānalasaṃnibhaḥ \|*  
*khaḍgavyagro 'tibhīmaśca rakṣaḥpīḍāṃ vyapohatu \|\| 12 \|\|*

*nāgapāśadharo devaḥ sākṣānmakaravāhanaḥ \|*  
*sa jalādhipatiś candra-grahapīḍāṃ vyapohatu \|\| 13 \|\|*

*prāṇarūpeṇa yo lokān pāti kṛṣṇamṛgapriyaḥ \|*  
*vāuścandroparāgotthāṃ pīḍāmatra vyapohatu \|\| 14 \|\|*

*yo 'sau nidhipatirdevaḥ khaḍgaśūlagadādharaḥ \|*  
*candroparāgakaluṣaṃ dhanado me vyapohatu \|\| 15 \|\|*

*yo 'sāvindudharo devaḥ pinākī vṛṣavāhanaḥ \|*  
*candroparāgajāṃ pīḍāṃ vināśayatu śaṃkaraḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

8-16. The Devas should be invoked with the following mantras: — “All the sacred places, seas, rivers, tanks, rivulets, come here to wash off the sins of the devotee. — May the God Indra, the wielder of the thunderbolt, known as sovereign of the Adityas, and having thousand eyes, come and remove my suffering caused by the (inauspicious) Planet. — May Agni, the mounth of the Devas, having seven flames, of immeasurable brightness, come and remove my suffering caused by. the lunar eclipse, — May Yama, the rider of the buffalo, representative of justice (Dharma), the witness of the deeds of all men, come and soothe my pain caused by the lunar eclipes. — May the living god Varuna, the ruler of all waters, the rider of the alligator, and wielder of the noose, consisting of sea serpents, come and remove my suffering caused by the lunar eclipse. — May Vayu, who nourishes all creatures in the shape of vital breath, who loves black antelope, come and remove my suffering caused by the lunar eclipse. — May Kuvera, the giver of wealth and master of riches, and armed with sword, trident, club, &c. come and drive away my sin caused by the lunar eclipse. —

May Shankara, the rider of the bull and the - wearer of the crescent and armed with the bow, called pindka, come and destroy the pain arising out of the lunar eclipse. — May Brahma, Vishnu and Arka as well as all mobile and immobile beings existing in the three worlds, come and burn up my sin.”

## \|\| 67.17 \|\|

*trailokye yāni bhūtāni sthāvarāṇi carāṇi ca \|*  
*brahmaviṣṇvarkauktāni tāni pāpaṃ dahantu vai \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. After thus invoking all Devas and other beings, the devotee should sprinkle upon himself the water of those medicated pitchers which are adored with white garlands and sandal paste, and then worship the Brahmanas and the family Deity by reciting the mantras laid down in the Rig, Same and Yajur Vedas, and then give away a cow, along with cloth to the Brahmana

## \|\| 67.18-20 \|\|

*evamāmantrya taiḥ kumbhair abhiṣikto guṇānvitaiḥ \|*  
*ṛgyajuḥsāmamantraiśca śuklamālyānulepanaiḥ \|*  
*pūjayedvastragodānair brāhmaṇāniṣṭadevatāḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*etāneva tato mantrān vilikhet karakānvitān \|*  
*vastrapaṭṭe 'thavā padme pañcaratnasamanvitān \|\| 19 \|\|*

*yajamānasya śirasi nidadhyuste dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*tato 'tivāhayedvelām uparāgānugāminīm \|\| 20 \|\|*

18-20. The mantras mentioned above, (in the verses 8-16,) should be written on a piece of cloth or on a lotus leaf, and, placed in an earthen dish with five jewels (gold, diamond sapphire, ruby and pearl, or gold, silver, coral, pearl and ragapatta). The Brahmanas should place on the head of the devotee, the said dish and await the time of passing away of the eclipse. At the time of the eclipse, the devotee should turn his face towards the east and worship his family God. On the cessation of the eclipse, cows should be given away in charity, and then after a bath, the cloth, on which the above mantras are written, should be given away to the Brahmana.

## \|\| 67.21-23 \|\|

*prāṅmukhaḥ pūjayitvā tu namasyanniṣṭadevatām \|*  
*candragrahe vinirvṛtte kṛtagodānamaṅgalaḥ \|*  
*kṛtasnānāya taṃ paṭṭaṃ brāhmaṇāya nivedayet \|\| 21 \|\|*

*anena vidhinā yastu grahasnānaṃ samācaret \|*  
*na tasya grahapīḍā syān na ca bandhujanakṣayaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*paramāṃ siddhimāpnoti punarāvṛttidurlabhām \|*  
*sūryagrahe sūryanāma sadā mantreṣu kīrtayet \|\| 23 \|\|*

21-23. Ono who bathes according to these rites, after an eclipse, never gets any trouble through unlucky stars, and his family and kinsmen will also The person following the above rites with devotion, attains highest At the time of a solar eclipse, the mantras mentioned above should be recited by substituting the word Surya (the Sun) in the place of Chandra or Moon. The additional gift in the case of solar eclipse must consist of rubies. A beautiful cow should be given away at the time of any eclipse (either solar or lunar), in honour of the moon.

## \|\| 67.24 \|\|

*adhikāḥ padmarāgāḥ syuḥ kapilāṃ ca suśobhanām \|*  
*prayacchecca niśāṃ patye candrasūryoparāgayoḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. One who hears or causes others to hear about this ritual goes to the realm of Indra, after being liberated from all sins, and is glorified there.

## Chapter 68

## \|\| 68.1 \|\|

*nārada uvāca*  
*kimudvegādbhute kṛtyam alakṣmīḥ kena hanyate \|*  
*mṛtavatsābhiṣekādi-kāryeṣu ca kimiṣyate \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Narada said: — Lord! What should be done to restore the equilibrium of mind in times of distress? How is poverty to be got over? What should be done at the time of the ablution of a woman whose offspring do not survive?

## \|\| 68.2 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca*  
*purā kṛtāni pāpāni phalantyasmiṃstapodhana \|*  
*rogadaurgatyarūpeṇa tathaiveṣṭavadhena ca \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Lord said: — The sins of the past fructify in one’s present life. Disease, misery, loss of dear ones, are only the results of past sins.

## \|\| 68.3-5 \|\|

*tadvighātāya vakṣyāmi sadā kalpāṇakārakam \|*  
*saptamīsnapanaṃ nāma janapīḍāvināśanam \|\| 3 \|\|*

*bālānāṃ maraṇaṃ yatra kṣīrapāṇāṃ pradṛṣyate \|*  
*tadvadvṛddhāturāṇāṃ ca yauvane cāpi vartatām \|\| 4 \|\|*

*śāntaye tatra vakṣyāmi mṛtavatsābhiṣecanam \|*  
*etad evādbhutodvega-cittabhramavināśanam \|\| 5 \|\|*

3-5. I shall now describe to you the rituals of bathing on the seventh day of bright fortnight, that washes of all the sins, which causes prosperity, and destroys all human troubles. I shall also describe to you the rituals of the ablution of a woman, whose offspring’s do not survive, as well as for the longevity of old and diseased men as well as of young men. This ablation which is done according to special rites, drives away the uneasiness of the mind.

## \|\| 68.6 \|\|

*bhaviṣyati ca vārāho yatra kalpastapodhana \|*  
*vaivasvataśca tatrāpi yadā tu manuruttamaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. In a future Varaha Kalpa, O King, there will be a Vaivasvata Manu also.

## \|\| 68.7 \|\|

*bhaviṣyati ca tatraiva pañcaviṃśatimaṃ yadā \|*  
*kṛtaṃ nāma ugaṃ tatra haihayānvayavardhanaḥ \|*  
*bhavitā nṛpatirvīraḥ kṛtavīryaḥ pratāpavān \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Then in the 25th Satyayuga, of that Vaivasvata Manvantara, an illustrious and powerful king, Kritavirya, the promoter of the HayaHaya dynasty will be born and thrive.

## \|\| 68.8 \|\|

*sa saptadvīpamakhilaṃ pālayiṣyati bhūtalam \|*  
*yāvadvarṣasahasrāṇi saptasaptati nārada \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. That king will rule the world, consisting of seven continents for seventy thousand years, O Narada, with great statesmanship

## \|\| 68.9 \|\|

*jātamātraṃ ca tasyāpi yāvatputraśataṃ tathā \|*  
*cyavanasya tu śāpena vināśamapayāsyati \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. He, will have one hundred sons who will all die as soon as born, owing to the curse of the sage Chyavana.

## \|\| 68.10 \|\|

*sahasrabāhuśca yadā bhavitā tasya vai sutaḥ \|*  
*kuraṅganayanaḥ śrīmān sambhūto nṛpalakṣaṇaiḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Sometime after that the King Kritavirya will be blessed with a renowned son, named Sahasrabahu (thousand-armed). He will have beautiful eyes like elephant, will be Iucky and possess all the auspicious marks of a king

## \|\| 68.11-12 \|\|

*kṛtavīryastadārādhya sahasrāṃśuṃ divākaram \|*  
*upavāsairvratairdivyair vedasūktaiśca nārada \|*  
*putrasya jīvanāyālam etatsnānamavāpsyati \|\| 11 \|\|*

*kṛtavīryeṇa vai pṛṣṭa idaṃ vakṣyati bhāskaraḥ \|*  
*aśeṣaduṣṭaśamanaṃ sadā kalmaṣanāśanam \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-12. His father, Kritavirya will worship the thousand-rayed Sun according to the Vedic hymns with fasts and vows, in order to ward off the sage’s curse, so that the son may not die in infancy. He will then come to know of the rituals of this particular ablution from the God Sun, who will relate to the king the ways of the ordinance that would wash off all sins and allay all misfortunes.

## \|\| 68.13 \|\|

*sūrya uvāca*  
*alaṃ kleśena mahatā putrastava narādhipa \|*  
*bhaviṣyati ciraṃjīvī kiṃtu kalmaṣanāśanam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. The God-Sun will say: “King Kritavirya! I am very mach pleased with your devotion and penances: there is no further need of them. I bless you that this son of yours will be long-lived”.

## \|\| 68.14 \|\|

*saptamīsnapanaṃ vakṣye sarvalokahitāya vai \|*  
*jātasya mṛtavatsāyāḥ saptame māsi nārada \|*  
*athavā śuklasaptamyām etatsarvaṃ praśasyate \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. I shall now explain to you about the rituals of ablation on the seventh day of a lunar fortnight, in order that all men may be benefited by it. The woman, whose ‘offspring does’ not survive, ought to bathe on the seventh day of the lunar fortnight, or on the seventh month after the birth of the child.

## \|\| 68.15 \|\|

*grahatārābalaṃ labdhvā kṛtvā brāhmaṇavācanam \|*  
*bālasya janmanakṣatraṃ varjayettāṃ tithiṃ budhaḥ \|*  
*tadvadvṛddhāturāṇāṃ ca kṛtyaṃ syāditareṣu ca \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. The worshipper should consult Brahmanas about his lucky stars and then fix some auspicious day for the rituals, avoiding the birth asterism of the child. This ritual applies to old men and to others suffering from illness etc.

## \|\| 68.16 \|\|

*gomayenānuliptāyāṃ bhūmāvekāgnivattadā \|*  
*taṇḍulai raktaśālīyaiś caruṃ gokṣīrasaṃyutam \|*  
*nirvapetsūryarudrābhyāṃ tanmantrābhyāṃ vidhānataḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. According to the rites of the Ekagni fire ceremony, the devotee should locate the Fire on an altar, plastered over with cowdung, and cook on that fire pudding (charu), with red rice and cow’s milk, and offer it to Surya and Rudra by reciting the mantras of Rudra and the God Sun.

## \|\| 68.17 \|\|

*kīrtayetsūryadevatyaṃ saptarcaṃ ca ghṛtāhutīḥ \|*  
*juhuyādrudrasūktena tadvadrudrāya nārada \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. An offering of clarified butter should also be poured into the fire, after reciting the seven Rik mantras of the Sun, and, similarly, he should offer to Rudra with hymn sacred to Rudra

## \|\| 68.18-19 \|\|

*hotavyāḥ samidhaścātra tathaivārkapalāśayoḥ \|*  
*yavakṛṣṇatilairhomaḥ kartavyo 'ṣṭaśataṃ punaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*vyāhṛtībhistathājyena tathaivāṣṭaśataṃ punaḥ \|*  
*hutvā snānaṃ ca kartavyaṃ maṅgalaṃ yena dhīmatā \|\| 19 \|\|*

18-19. In this sacrifice, the fuel of Calotropis gigantea and Butea frondosa should be used. An offering of barley and black sesamum should be made 108 times in this homa. In the same way, another 108 offerings of clarified butter should be made, after reciting Vyahriti mantras. Afterwards, the worshipper should bathe.

## \|\| 68.20-21 \|\|

*vipreṇa vedaviduṣā vidhivaddarbhapāṇinā \|*  
*sthāpayitvā tu caturaḥ kumbhānkoṇeṣu śobhanān \|\| 20 \|\|*

*pañcamaṃ ca punarmadhye dadhyakṣatavibhūṣitam \|*  
*sthāpayedavraṇaṃ kumbhaṃ saptarcenābhimantritam \|\| 21 \|\|*

20-21. Four pitchers should be placed in four corners by a Brahmana versed in the Vedas, with a Kusha grass in his hand, and a fifth one should be placed in the centre, after filling it in with curds, uncooked rice, etc., reciting the seven Rik verses, and then Agni should be invoked.

## \|\| 68.22 \|\|

*saureṇa tīrthatoyena pūrṇaṃ ratnasamanvitam \|*  
*sarvānsarvauṣadhairyuktān pañcagavyasamanvitān \|*  
*pañcaratnaphalaiḥ puṣpair vāsobhiḥ pariveṣṭayet \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. The central pitcher, which must have no flaw in it, should also be filled in with the sacred water of the Surya-tirtha. All kinds of gems, and different kinds of herbs, panchagavya, panchratna, fruits and flowers, should be placed in the corner pitchers. — Afterwards, the pitchers should be covered with cloth, and then located at their respective places.

## \|\| 68.23 \|\|

*gajāśvarathyāvalmīkāt saṃgamāddhradagokulāt \|*  
*saṃśuddhāṃ mṛdamānīya sarveṣveva vinikṣipet \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. The earth of the following places should also be put into those pitchers, along with the things mentioned above: — stable, elephant yard, chariot house, anthill, confluence of two rivers, tank, cattle-fold, royal palace gate.

## \|\| 68.24 \|\|

*caturṣvapi ca kumbheṣu ratnagarbheṣu madhyamam \|*  
*gṛhītvā brāhmaṇastatra saurānmantrānudīrayet \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. The Brahmana touching the central pitcher, which is surrounded by four other pitchers, each containing precious stones within them, should recite the Vedic mantras relating to the God Sun

## \|\| 68.25-28 \|\|

*nārībhiḥ saptasaṃkhyābhir avyaṅgāṅgībhiratra ca \|*  
*pūjitābhiryathāśaktyā mālyavastravibhūṣaṇaiḥ \|*  
*saviprābhiśca kartavyaṃ mṛtavatsābhiṣecanam \|\| 25 \|\|*

*ete 'bhiṣekamantrāḥ*  
*dīrghāurastu bālo 'yaṃ jīvatputrā ca bhāminī \|*  
*ādityaścandramāḥ sārdhaṃ grahanakṣatramaṇḍalaiḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*saśakrā lokapālā vai brahmaviṣṇumaheśvarāḥ \|*  
*te te cānye ca devaughāḥ sadā pāntu kumārakam \|\| 27 \|\|*

*mitraḥ śanirvā hutabhug ye ca bālagrahāḥ kvacit \|*  
*pīḍāṃ kurvantu bālasya mā māturjanakasya vai \|\| 28 \|\|*

25-28. Seven Brahmana, ladies, along with their husbands, should be worshipped with garlands, cloths, ornaments, etc., according to the means of the devotee. These women should have no bodily defect. Afterwards, the Brahmana women should perform the ablution ceremony of the woman whose children do not survive, and recite the following words: —

“May this child be long-lived, may this progeny of this woman be long-lived. O Sun, Moon, planets, Stars, Indra, Devas, Lokapalas, Brahma, Vishnu, Shiva and other groups of Devas, always protect this child. O Mitra, O Saturn, O other Devas, O Agni, O Balagraha, be pleased and never injure the child and his parents.”

**Комментарий:**

Note: .... = A demon or any planetary influence, that injures the child.

## \|\| 68.29 \|\|

*tataḥ śuklāmbaradharā kumārapatisaṃyutā \|*  
*saptakaṃ pūjayedbhaktyā strīṇāmatha guruṃ punaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. After this, the seven Brahmana women with their husbands and children and wearing white raiments, chould be honoured along with the preceptor.

## \|\| 68.30 \|\|

*kāñcanīṃ ca tataḥ kuryāt tāmrapātroparisthitām \|*  
*pratimāṃ dharmarājasya gurave vinivedayet \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Then the image of Dharmaraja, made in gold and placed on a copper vessel should be given away to the preceptor.

## \|\| 68.31 \|\|

*vastrakāñcanaratnaughair bhakṣyaiḥ saghṛtapāyasaiḥ \|*  
*pūjayedbrāhmaṇāṃstadvad vittaśāṭhyavivarjitaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Afterwards with his mind free from jealousy and miserliness, gold, cloth, gems, clarified butter, milk, &c., should be given to the Brahmanas.

## \|\| 68.32 \|\|

*bhuktvā ca guruṇā ceyam uccāryā mantrasaṃtatiḥ \|*  
*dīrghāurastu bālo 'yaṃ yāvadvarṣaśataṃ sukhī \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. The Brahmanas should be fed first and then the devotee should take his meals. After meals, the preceptor should pronounce his blessings in the following words: — “This child may live for a century and may always remain prosperous.

## \|\| 68.33-34 \|\|

*yatkiṃcidasya duritaṃ tatkṣiptaṃ vaḍavānale \|*  
*brahmā rudro vasuḥ skando viṣṇuḥ śakro hutāśanaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

*rakṣantu sarve duṣṭebhyo varadāḥ santu sarvadā \|*  
*evamādīni vākyāni vadantaṃ pūjayedgurum \|\| 34 \|\|*

33-34. “All his sins be instantly consumed in the submarine fire. O Brahma, Vishnu, Shiva, Vasu, Svamikartika, Indra, Agni, protect this child from all calamities and bless him.” The preceptor pronouncing the above blessings should be worshipped.

## \|\| 68.35-36 \|\|

*śaktitaḥ kapilāṃ dadyāt praṇamya ca visarjayet \|*  
*caruṃ ca putrasahitā praṇamya raviśaṃkarau \|\| 35 \|\|*

*hutaśeṣaṃ tadāśnīyād ādityāya namo 'stviti \|*  
*idamevādbhutodvega-duḥsvapneṣu praśasyate \|\| 36 \|\|*

35-36. Then a milk cow should be given away in charity to the preceptor who should then be dismissed with proper honors.. Then the woman holding her child should salute the Sun and Shankara and eat the remaindor of the charu (Sakalya), and then pronounce “Adityeya namah.” - This is the way which should be followed to restore the peace of mind caused by evil dreams or calamities, &c.

**Комментарий:**

Note: ..... = The thing which is offered as a libation it the Fire at the time of sacrifice. .... = I salute the sun.

## \|\| 68.37 \|\|

*karturjanmadinarkṣaṃ ca tyaktvā sampūjayetsadā \|*  
*śāntyarthaṃ śuklasaptamyām etatkurvanna sīdati \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. One who observes these rituals on a seventh day of a bright fortnight, avoiding his birth-day and asterism, never comes to grief.

## \|\| 68.38 \|\|

*sadānena vidhānena dīrghāurabhavannaraḥ \|*  
*saṃvatsarāṇāmautaṃ śaśāsa pṛthivīmimām \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. King Kritavirya, most renowned, got long life, and ruled the world for a period of ten thousand years, Owing to his having observed the above-mentioned rituals repeatedly.

## \|\| 68.39 \|\|

*puṇyaṃ pavitramāuṣyaṃ saptamīsnapanaṃ raviḥ \|*  
*kathayitvā dvijaśreṣṭha tatraivāntaradhīyata \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. The deity Surya, having described this ablution called Saptamisnana, and which is sacred, sanctifying and giver of long life, vanished then and there.

## \|\| 68.40 \|\|

*etatsarvaṃ samākhyātaṃ saptamīsnānamuttamam \|*  
*sarvaduṣṭopaśamanaṃ bālānāṃ paramaṃ hitam \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. This Saptamisnana which has been thus described, is most sacred and dispeller of all evils. It is the giver of great benefit to children.

## \|\| 68.41 \|\|

*ārogyaṃ bhāskarādicched dhanamiccheddhutāśanāt \|*  
*īśvarādjñānam anvicchen mokṣam icchedjanārdanāt \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. knowledge from Ishvara, and emancipation from Janardana.

## \|\| 68.42 \|\|

*etanmahāpātakanāśanaṃ syāt paraṃ hitaṃ bālavivardhanaṃ ca \|*  
*śṛṇoti yaścainamananyacetās tasyāpi siddhiṃ munayo vadanti \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. This ritual is the destroyer of great sins and giver of happiness to the children, and the Munis say that one who hears about it attains success.

## Chapter 69

## \|\| 69.1 \|\|

*matsya uvāca*  
*purā rathaṃtare kalpe paripṛṣṭo mahātmanā \|*  
*mandarastho mahādevaḥ pinākī brahmaṇā svayam \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. The Lord said: --In the past, during the Rathantara Kalpa, Brahma asked Shiva on the summit of the Mandarachala Mountain.

## \|\| 69.2 \|\|

*brahmovāca*  
*kathamārogyamaiśvaryam anantamamareśvara \|*  
*svalpena tapasā deva bhavenmokṣo 'thavā nṛṇām \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Brahma said, ‘ How one may with the performance of slight austerities get unending prosperity and health, O Lord of immortals? How may men attain emancipation by practising brief austerities?

## \|\| 69.3 \|\|

*kimajñātaṃ mahādeva tvatprasādādadhokṣaja \|*  
*svalpakenātha tapasā mahatphalamihocyatām \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Mahadeva, nothing is unknown to thee. Through thy grace one knows everything. Pray, be pleased to explain to me how, by practising small austerities, one may get large reward.”

## \|\| 69.4 \|\|

*matsya uvāca*  
*evaṃ pṛṣṭaḥ sa viśvātmā brahmaṇā lokabhāvanaḥ \|*  
*umāpatiruvācedaṃ manasaḥ prītikārakam \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. The Lord Matsya said: — On thus being asked by Brahma, Shiva, the lord of Uma, the Soul of the universe, the creator of all worlds, began to explain the ordinance, so pleasant to the mind.

## \|\| 69.8 \|\|

*dvaipāyana ṛṣistadvad rauhiṇeyo 'tha keśavaḥ \|*  
*kaṃsādidarpamathanaḥ keśavaḥ kleśanāśanaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Shiva said:--After this 23rd Rathantara Kalpa, will again follow Varaha Kalpa. In that Kalpa, also, there will be 14 manvantaras, The seventh of these will be Vaivaswata manvantara. In the 28th Dvapara yuga of the Vaivasvata manvantara will be born the great God, VasudevaJanardana. By the end of the same (28th Dwapara) age, Lord Vishnu will manifest Himself in three different ways, to relieve the world of its He will manifest Himself as (1) Dvaipayana Vyasa, (2) Baladeva, (3) Shrikrishna, and will bring relief to the world by crushing the pride of the wretches like Kamsa, etc.

## \|\| 69.9 \|\|

*purīṃ dvāravatīṃ nāma sāmprataṃ yā kuśasthalī \|*  
*divyānubhāvasaṃyuktām adhivāsāya śārṅgiṇaḥ \|*  
*tvaṣṭā mamājñayā tadvat kariṣyati jagatpateḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The puri Dwaravati, which is now known as Kushasthali, will become Dwarika and will be planned for the residence of Krishna by Vishvakarma, according to my instructions.

## \|\| 69.10-12 \|\|

*tasyāṃ kadācidāsīnaḥ sabhāyāmamitadyutiḥ \|*  
*bhāryābhirvṛṣṇibhiścaiva bhūbhṛdbhir bhūridakṣiṇaiḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*kurubhirdevagandharvair abhitaḥ kaiṭabhārdanaḥ \|*  
*pravṛttāsu purāṇīṣu dharmasambandhinīṣu ca \|\| 11 \|\|*

*kathānte bhīmasenena paripṛṣṭaḥ pratāpavān \|*  
*tvayā pṛṣṭasya dharmasya rahasyasyāsya bhedakṛt \|\| 12 \|\|*

10-12. In the noble assemblage which will be attended in that sacred city, in company of their beautiful ladies, by Vrishni, Yadava and the Kauravas, the Pandava Bhimsena, the most illustrious of all assembled — there, will, at the close of the pauranic discourses, ask Lord Krishna, attended by the Devas and the Gandharvas, and He will them explain about the ordinance just now asked by you.

## \|\| 69.13 \|\|

*bhavitā sa tadā brahman kartā caiva vṛkodaraḥ \|*  
*pravartako 'sya dharmasya pāṇḍuputro mahābalaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. O Brahma! after that Bhimasena will follow the rituals, dictated by, Lord Krishna and will promulgate it in the world.

## \|\| 69.14 \|\|

*yasya tīkṣṇo vṛko nāma jaṭhare havyavāhanaḥ \|*  
*mayā dattaḥ sa dharmātmā tena cāsau vṛkodaraḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Bhimasena is called Vrikodara, on account of his having Vrika or wolf-like fire given by me in his stomach. His hunger will never be appeased.

**Комментарий:**

Notes: Vrikodara: A wolf in the stomach.”

## \|\| 69.15 \|\|

*matimānmānaśīlaśca nāgāutabalo mahān \|*  
*bhaviṣyatyajaraḥ śrīmān kandarpa iva rūpavān \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Bhima will be most wise, charitable, wealthy, handsome like Cupid, and will have the power of ten-thousand elephants

## \|\| 69.16 \|\|

*dhārmikasyāpyaśaktasya tīvrāgnitvādupoṣaṇe \|*  
*idaṃ vratamaśeṣāṇāṃ vratānāmadhikaṃ yataḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. The pious who are unable to suppress: their hunger and keep up a fall fast, should observe this ordinance, which is the best of all for them.

## \|\| 69.17-18 \|\|

*kathayiṣyati viśvātmā vāsudevo jagadguruḥ \|*  
*aśeṣayajñaphaladam aśeṣāghavināśanam \|\| 17 \|\|*

*aśeṣaduṣṭaśamanam aśeṣasurapūjitam \|*  
*pavitrāṇāṃ pavitraṃ ca maṅgalānāṃ ca maṅgalam \|*  
*bhaviṣyaṃ ca bhaviṣyāṇāṃ purāṇānāṃ purātanam \|\| 18 \|\|*

17-18. For the benefit of the pious, unable to suppress their hunger, Lord Vasudeva, the Jagadguru, the soul of the universe, will explain the rituals relating to the ordinance, which will be the giver of the benefits of all the sacrifices, the destroyer of all sins and \| calamities, the giver of the highest prosperity, the most ancient of all the forms of ordinances and venerated by the Devas.”

**Комментарий:**

Note — Now follows the explanation of the rituals by Lord Vasudeva, which is another epithet of Krishna.

## \|\| 69.19-20 \|\|

*vāsudeva uvāca*  
*yadyaṣṭamīcaturdaśyor dvādaśīṣvatha bhārata \|*  
*anyeṣvapi dinarkṣeṣu na śaktastvam upoṣitum \|\| 19 \|\|*

*tataḥ puṇyāṃ tithimimāṃ sarvapāpapraṇāśinīm \|*  
*upoṣya vidhinānena gaccha viṣṇoḥ paraṃ padam \|\| 20 \|\|*

19-20. Vasudeva said: — The devotee who may not be able to fast on the eighth, fourteenth and twelfth day of a bright fortnight, or on any other prescribed day, attains unification with Vishnu, by keeping a fast on this sacred day only.

## \|\| 69.21 \|\|

*māghamāsasya daśamī yadā śuklā bhavettadā \|*  
*ghṛtenābhyañjanaṃ kṛtvā tilaiḥ snānaṃ samācaret \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. On the tenth day of the bright fortnight, in the month of Magha, the devotee should bathe in water mixed with sesamum, after anointing his body with clarified butter.

## \|\| 69.22-26 \|\|

*tathaiva viṣṇumabhyarcya nabho nārāyaṇeti ca \|*  
*kṛṣṇāya pādau sampūjya śiraḥ sarvātmane namaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*vaikuṇṭhāyeti vaikuṇṭham uraḥ śrīvatsadhāriṇe \|*  
*śaṅkhine cakriṇe tadvad gadine varadāya vai \|*  
*sarve nārāyaṇasyaivaṃ saṃpūjyā bāhavaḥ kramāt \|\| 23 \|\|*

*dāmodarāyetyudaraṃ meḍhraṃ pañcaśarāya vai \|*  
*ūrū saubhāgyanāthāya jānunī bhūtadhāriṇe \|\| 24 \|\|*

*namo nīlāya vai jaṅghe pādau viśvasṛje namaḥ \|*  
*namo devyai namaḥ śāntyai namo lakṣmyai namaḥ śriyai \|\| 25 \|\|*

*namaḥ puṣṭyai namastuṣṭyai dhṛṣṭyai hṛṣṭyai namo namaḥ \|*  
*namo vihaṃganāthāya vāuvegāya pakṣiṇe \|*  
*viṣapramāthine nityaṃ garuḍaṃ cābhipūjayet \|\| 26 \|\|*

22-26. He should then worship Vishnu with the words, “Namah Narayanaya”. The feet the Lord should be worshipped with “Krishaya namah,” the head with“ Sarvatmane namah,” the throat with “ Vaikunthaya namah,” the breast with “Srivatsadhardya namah,” the four arms with “ Chakrine namah” “Gaildine namah,” “ Varadaya namah,” “Sankhine namah,” the stomach with “ Damodaraya nama ,” the region of Cupid with “ Panchasharaya namah,” the thighs with “Saubhasyanathaya. namah,”” the knees with Bhuvadharine namah,” the shanks with “ Nilekanthaya nama,” the feet with , Vidvasrije namah.” Then the Goddess ‘Lakshmi) should, be worshipped with “Devyai namab,” “Sintyai namah,” “Lakshmyai namah,” “Shriyai namah,” “Pushtyai namah,” “Tustyai namah,” “Dhristyai namah,” “Hristyai mamah.” Afterwards, Garuda, the king of birds, swift like the wind; the destroyer of serpents, should always be saluted.

## \|\| 69.27-28 \|\|

*evaṃ sampūjya govindam umāpativināyakau \|*  
*gandhairmālyaistathā dhūpair bhakṣyairnānāvidhairapi \|\| 27 \|\|*

*gavyena payasā siddhāṃ kṛsarāmatha vāgyataḥ \|*  
*sarpiṣā saha bhuktvā ca gatvā śatapadaṃ budhaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

27-28. Having thus worshipped Govinda, Shiva and Gangesha should be worshipped with sandal, incense, flowers, and various kinds of victuals. Then the devotee should take, in silence, with ghee, the porridge made of nice sesamum and grain, cooked with cow’s milk, sugar, and walk a hundred steps.

## \|\| 69.29-34 \|\|

*naiyagrodhaṃ dantakāṣṭham athavā khādiraṃ budhaḥ \|*  
*gṛhītvā dhāvayeddantān ācāntaḥ prāgudaṅmukhaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*brūyāt sāyantanīṃ kṛtvā saṃdhyāmastamite ravau \|*  
*namo nārāyaṇāyeti tvāmahaṃ śaraṇaṃ gataḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

*ekādaśyāṃ nirāhāraḥ samabhyarcya ca keśavam \|*  
*rātriṃ ca sakalāṃ sthitvā snānaṃ ca payasā tathā \|\| 31 \|\|*

*sarpiṣā cāpi dahanaṃ hutvā brāhmaṇapuṃgavaiḥ \|*  
*sahaiva puṇḍarīkākṣa dvādaśyāṃ kṣīrabhojanam \|\| 32 \|\|*

*kariṣyāmi yatātmāhaṃ nirvighnenāstu tacca me \|*  
*evamuktvā svapedbhūmāv itihāsakathāṃ punaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

*śrutvā prabhāte saṃjāte nadīṃ gatvā viśāṃ pate \|*  
*snānaṃ kṛtvā mṛdā tadvat pāṣaṇḍān abhivarjayet \|\| 34 \|\|*

29-34. Afterwards, the devotee should brush his teeth with a stick of banyan or khadir and then rinse his mouth, facing the east or the north, and holding a kusha in his hand. After sunset he should perform his sandhya and then — utter: “Om namonarayanaya namah, twimaham sharnangatah. I salute Narayana, I throw myself under your protection.” On the Ekadashi day, I shall keep a fast and worship Narayana and keep a vigil at night; have a bath early in the morning (i.e., on the Dvadashi) and make an oblation of clarified butter to Fire. Pundarikaksha, I shall, with mind controlled, eat rice, cooked with milk, with a few good Brahmans, May that be fulfilled by Thy grace, without any obstruction.’ With these words, he should sleep on the bare earth. Then, on daybreak, he should hear recitations from the Itihasa, and go and bathe in a river, after rubbing earth on his holy. At this time, he should avoid the company of wicked persons.

## \|\| 69.35-36 \|\|

*upāsya saṃdhyāṃ vidhivat kṛtvā ca pitṛtarpaṇam \|*  
*praṇamya ca hṛṣīkeśaṃ saptalokaikamīśvaram \|\| 35 \|\|*

*gṛhasya purato bhaktyā maṇḍapaṃ kārayedbudhaḥ \|*  
*daśahastamathāṣṭau vā karānkuryādviśāṃ pate \|\| 36 \|\|*

35-36. After that, he should perform his sandhya prayers and offer libations of water to the manes of his deceased ancestors, and then salute Hrishikesha, the sole sovereign of the seven worlds. Then he should erect a pandal measuring ten or eleven hands, in front of his house

**Комментарий:**

Note. — Sandhya — The morning, noon and the evening prayer, performed by a twice-born.

## \|\| 69.37 \|\|

*caturhastāṃ śubhāṃ kuryād vedīmariniṣūdana \|*  
*caturhastapramāṇaṃ ca vinyasettatra toraṇam \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. An altar, measuring four hands, should be made in the pandal, and a portal of the same measurement should be made.

## \|\| 69.38-39 \|\|

*āropya kalaśaṃ tatra dikpālānpūjayettataḥ \|*  
*chidreṇa jalasampūrṇam atha kṛṣṇājinasthitaḥ \|*  
*tasya dhārāṃ ca śirasā dhārayetsakalāṃ niśām \|\| 38 \|\|*

*tathaiva viṣṇoḥ śirasi kṣīradhārāṃ prapātayet \|*  
*aratnimātraṃ kuṇḍaṃ ca kuryāttatra trimekhalam \|\| 39 \|\|*

38-39. He should place there a pitcher of water and worship the Guardians of the quarters (Dikpala). — There the devotee should sit on a black deer skin and over his head place the pitcher of water, after making a hole in its contre. He should allow the water to trickle, drop by drop on his head, and, in the same way, should allow a stream of milk to fall on the head of the symbol of Vishnu.

## \|\| 69.40-43 \|\|

*yonivaktraṃ ca tatkṛtvā brāhmaṇaiḥ yavasarpiṣī \|*  
*tilāṃśca viṣṇudevatyair mantrairekāgnivattadā \|\| 40 \|\|*

*hutvā ca vaiṣṇavaṃ samyak caruṃ gokṣīrasaṃyutam \|*  
*niṣpāvārdhapramāṇāṃ vai dhārāmājyasya pātayet \|\| 41 \|\|*

*jalakumbhānmahāvīrya sthāpayitvā trayodaśa \|*  
*bhakṣyairnānāvidhairyuktān sitavastrairalaṃkṛtān \|\| 42 \|\|*

*yuktānaudumbaraiḥ pātraiḥ pañcaratnasamanvitān \|*  
*caturbhirbahvṛcairhomas tatra kārya udaṅmukhaiḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

40-43. There should be made a sacrificial pond, one hand deep, of the shape of a conical triangle and surrounded by three circles, and after that the Brahmanas. should be asked to make an offering of milk, clarified butter and sesamum to Lord Vishnu, after the rituals of Ekagni, with mantras sacred to Vishnu, after which a stream of clarified butter, of half the size of a winnowing basket (Nispava), should be poured! into the fire an well as the charu, mixed with cow's milk. Thirteen pitchers, full of water, should be placed. The mouths of these pitchers should be covered with plates of fig leaves containing different kinds of estables and five jewels and covered with white cloths. Four Rigvedi Brahmanas should offer sacrifices to Fire, facing north.

## \|\| 69.44 \|\|

*rudrajāpaścaturbhiśca yajurvedaparāyaṇaiḥ \|*  
*vaiṣṇavāni tu sāmāni caturaḥ sāmavedinaḥ \|*  
*ariṣṭavargasahitāny abhitaḥ paripāṭhayet \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Four Brahmanas, well up in the Yajurveda, should recite the mantra, sacred to Rudra, Another group of four Brahmanas, versed in the Samaveda, should, be asked to chant the hymns of the Samaveda, sacred to Vishnu, along with Arishta hymns.

## \|\| 69.45-46 \|\|

*evaṃ dvādaśa tānviprān vastramālyānulepanaiḥ \|*  
*pūjayedaṅgulīyaiśca kaṭakairhemasūtrakaiḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

*vāsobhiḥ śayanīyaiśca vittaśāṭhyavivarjitaḥ \|*  
*evaṃ kṣapātivāhyā ca gītamaṅgalaniḥsvanaiḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

45-46. The twelve Brahmanas thus employed should be honoured with garlands of flowers, sandal paste, bed sheets, gold rings, gold sacred threads, gold bangles, and different kinds of cloths. Miserliness should not be exercised in this respect. That night should thus be passed in rejoicings, accompanied with singing and music.

## \|\| 69.47-49 \|\|

*upādhyāyasya ca punar dviguṇaṃ sarvameva tu \|*  
*tataḥ prabhāte vimale samutthāya trayodaśa \|\| 47 \|\|*

*gā vai dadyātkuruśreṣṭha sauvarṇamukhasaṃyutāḥ \|*  
*payasvinīḥ śīlavatīḥ kāṃsyadohasamanvitāḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

*raupyakhurāḥ savastrāśca candanenābhiṣecitāḥ \|*  
*tāstu teṣāṃ tato bhaktyā bhakṣyabhojyānnatarpitān \|\| 49 \|\|*

47-49. Double of all these Dakshinas should be given to the preceptor, and, O Bhimasena,” on the following morning thirteen quiet and good milk cows, with their horns covered with gold, hoofs with silver, covered with cloth and painted with sandal, should be given away in charity, along with milking pots of bell metal to Brahmanas well fed with nice eatables.

## \|\| 69.50 \|\|

*kṛtvā vai brāhmaṇān sarvān annairnānāvidhaistathā \|*  
*bhuktvā cākṣāralavaṇam ātmanā ca visarjayet \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Then the devotee should take his meal, without acid and salt. Afterwards, the Brahmanas should be dismissed, after being satisfied with dainty dishes

## \|\| 69.51-52 \|\|

*anugamya padānyaṣṭau putrabhāryāsamanvitaḥ \|*  
*prīyatāmatra deveśaḥ keśavaḥ kleśanāśanaḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

*śivasya hṛdaye viṣṇur viṣṇośca hṛdaye śivaḥ \|*  
*yathāntaraṃ na paśyāmi tathā me svasti cāuṣaḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

51-52. The devotee should follow the Brahmanas for eight steps in company of his son, wife, etc., and should say: “Keshava! the destroyer of all evils, be pleased. Shiva is enthroned in the heart of Vishnu and the Vishnu in the heart of Shiva. As I do not see any» difference between the two, so there may be long life and prosperity to me”.

## \|\| 69.53 \|\|

*evamuccārya tānkumbhān gāścaiva śayanāni ca \|*  
*vāsāṃsi caiva sarveṣāṃ gṛhāṇi prāpayedbudhaḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. With these words, the devotee should send the pitchers, the cows, the bedding, the clothes, &c., to the house of the Brahmanas.

## \|\| 69.54 \|\|

*abhāve bahuśayyānām ekāmapi susaṃskṛtām \|*  
*śayyāṃ dadyāddvijāteśca sarvopaskarasaṃyutām \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. If many beddings cannot be given, then only one should be given away, with all necessary requisites.

## \|\| 69.55 \|\|

*itihāsapurāṇāni vācayitvātivāhayet \|*  
*taddinaṃ naraśārdūla ya icchedvipulāṃ śriyam \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. One who wishes to acquire vast wealth should read the Puranas that day.

## \|\| 69.56-60 \|\|

*tasmāttvaṃ sattvamālambya bhīmasena vimatsaraḥ \|*  
*kuru vratamidaṃ samyak snehāttava mayeritam \|\| 56 \|\|*

*tvayā kṛtamidaṃ vīra tvannāmākhyaṃ bhaviṣyati \|*  
*sā bhīmadvādaśī hyeṣā sarvapāpaharā śubhā \|*  
*yā tu kalyāṇinī nāma purā kalpeṣu paṭhyate \|\| 57 \|\|*

*tvamādikartā bhava saukare 'smin kalpe mahāvīravarapradhāna \|*  
*yasyāḥ smarankīrtanamapyaśeṣaṃ vinaṣṭapāpastridaśādhipaḥ syāt \|\| 58 \|\|*

*kṛtvā ca yāmapsarasām adhīśā veśyā kṛtā hyanyabhavāntareṣu \|*  
*ābhīrakanyātikutūhalena saivorvaśī samprati nākapṛṣṭhe \|\| 59 \|\|*

*jātāthavā vaiṣyakulodbhavāpi pulomakanyā puruhūtapatnī \|*  
*tatrāpi tasyāḥ paricārikeyaṃ mama priyā samprati satyabhāmā \|\| 60 \|\|*

56-60. “O Bhimasena! You should also keep up this ordinance (vrata), without pride and with purity of heart. I have dictated all this out of affection for thee. Bhima! The ordinance observed by you will be known after your name.” “The ordinance (vrata) of Bhimasena dwadashi is the dispeller of all ills, and was. known as. Kalyanini in the past Kalpas. O Valiant one! You will be the first to observe this ordinance (vrata) during this Varaha Kalpa, having remembered all about it; you will be liberated from all sins and attain the rank of the Lord of Devas (Tridashas), The public women of other Kalpas having observed this vrata, have beconte celestial nymphs (Apsaris). One dairy maid, of a previous Kalpa (Avira Kanya), having observed this vrata out of curicsity alone, has now become Urvashi in the heaven of Indra. The daughter of a Vaishya became the daughter of Pulama and the queen of Indra, by virtue of this ordinance; and, similarly, Satyabhama, the maid of that girl, has become My beloved.”

## \|\| 69.61 \|\|

*snātaḥ purā maṇḍalameṣa tadvat tejomayaṃ vedaśarīramāpa \|*  
*asyāṃ ca kalyāṇatithau vivasvān sahasradhāreṇa sahasraraśmiḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. The Sun also on account of having bathed in a thousand torrents on the Kalyanadwidasi, got His shining body, surrounded by halos, and has become the thousand-rayed Vivasvan.

## \|\| 69.62 \|\|

*idameva kṛtaṃ mahendramukhyair vasubhirdevasurāribhistathā tu \|*  
*phalamasya na śakyate 'bhivaktuṃ yadi jihvāutakoṭayo mukhe syuḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. In former times, the same ordinance was observed by Mahendra and other gods, by the Vasus and by Asuras. No one, even with a thousand tongues, can adequately describe its effect.

## \|\| 69.63 \|\|

*kalikaluṣavidāriṇīmanantām iti kathayiṣyati yādavendrasūnuḥ \|*  
*api narakagatānpitrin aśeṣān alamuddhartumihaiva yaḥ karoti \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. Krishna, the King of Yadavas, will describe this tithi which, when observed, dispels all the sins of the iron (Kali) age, and liberates all his manes from the region of Yama, (Naraka).

## \|\| 69.64 \|\|

*ya idamaghavidāraṇaṃ śṛṇoti bhaktyā paripaṭhatīha paropakārahetoḥ \|*  
*tithimiha sakalārthabhāṅnarendras tava caturānana sāmyatāmupaiti \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. One who devoutly hears about it or reads it for the good of others, gets whatever he desires and even becomes unified with Brahma.

## \|\| 69.65 \|\|

*kalyāṇinī nāma purā babhūva yā dvādaśī māghadineṣu pūjyā \|*  
*sā pāṇḍuputreṇa kṛtā bhaviṣyaty anantapuṇyānagha bhīmapūrvā \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. What was in the former Kalpa, known as Kalyani-dwadashi of the month of Magha, will come to be known as Bhimadwadashi, when observed by Bhimasena, the son of Pandu.

## Chapter 70

## \|\| 70.1 \|\|

*brahmovāca*  
*varṇāśramāṇāṃ prabhavaḥ purāṇeṣu mayā śrutaḥ \|*  
*sadācārasya bhagavan dharmaśāstraviniścayaḥ \|*  
*paṇyastrīṇāṃ sadācāraṃ śrotumicchāmi tattvataḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1 Brahma. said: — Shiva! I have heard of the efficacy of Varna Ashrama as well as of good conduct, as prescribed by the Dharma Shastras. I am now desirous of hearing the practice and conduct of public women.

## \|\| 70.2-6 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca*  
*tasminneva uge brahman sahasrāṇi tu ṣoḍaśa \|*  
*vāsudevasya nārīṇāṃ bhaviṣyantyambujodbhava \|\| 2 \|\|*

*tābhirvasantasamaye kokilālikulākule \|*  
*puṣpite pavanotphulla-kahlārasarasastaṭe \|\| 3 \|\|*

*nirbharāpānagoṣṭhīṣu prasaktābhiralaṃkṛtaḥ \|*  
*kuraṅganayanaḥ śrīmān mālatīkṛtaśekharaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*gacchansamīpamārgeṇa sāmbaḥ parapuraṃjayaḥ \|*  
*sākṣātkandarpo rūpeṇa sarvābharaṇabhūṣitaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*anaṅgaśarataptābhiḥ sābhilāṣamavekṣitaḥ \|*  
*pravṛddho manmathastāsāṃ bhaviṣyati yadātmani \|\| 6 \|\|*

2-6. Shiva said: — There will be 16,000 wives of Krishna in the Yuga mentioned before. When once, in the spring time, those ladies, having decorated themselves with ornaments, would be drinking together on the banks of a pond studded with full-budded lotus flowers, dancing with the wind and resounding with the melodious notes of the cuckoo and musical tunes of the big black bee, they will see Lord Samba, beautiful like Cupid, having eyes. handsome like those of a gazelle, and wearing the garlands of malati, passing by. They will cast on him amorous: glances, their hearts being fired with lustful feelings and they being targets of the arrows of Cupid.

## \|\| 70.7 \|\|

*tadāvekṣya jagannāthaḥ sarvato jñānacakṣuṣā \|*  
*śāpaṃ vakṣyati tāḥ sarvā vo hariṣyanti dasyavaḥ \|*  
*matparokṣaṃ yataḥ kāma-laulyādīdṛgvidhaṃ kṛtam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Lord Krishna will come to Know all that with his mental vision, and will curse them as follows: ‘Because you cherished the desire of Amorous pastime during my absence, all of you will be taken away by bandits’

## \|\| 70.8-10 \|\|

*tataḥ prasādito deva idaṃ vakṣyati śārṅgabhṛt \|*  
*tābhiḥ śāpābhitaptābhir bhagavān bhūtabhāvanaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*uttārabhūtaṃ dāsatvaṃ samudrādbrāhmaṇapriyaḥ \|*  
*upadekṣyatyanantātmā bhāvikalyāṇakārakam \|\| 9 \|\|*

*bhavatīnām ṛṣirdālbhyo yadvrataṃ kathayiṣyati \|*  
*tadaivottāraṇāyālaṃ dāsatve 'pi bhaviṣyati \|*  
*ityuktvā tāḥ pariṣvajya gato dvāravatīśvaraḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

8-10. Then those ladies, overcome with grief on account of such a curse, will please Krishna (by their prayers), when the Lord will say: ‘Dalbbya Rishi of eternal soul, the favourite of the Brahmanas, will teach you a vrata, which will be the means of your liberation from the bondage and which will actually free you all. This vrata will be of great benefit to futurity. With these words, the Lord of Dvaravati left them.

## \|\| 70.11-16 \|\|

*tataḥ kālena mahatā bhārāvataraṇe kṛte \|*  
*nivṛtte mausale tadvat keśave divamāgate \|\| 11 \|\|*

*śūnye yadukule sarvaiś caurairapi jite 'rjune \|*  
*hṛtāsu kṛṣṇapatnīṣu dāsabhogyāsu cāmbudhau \|\| 12 \|\|*

*tiṣṭhantīṣu ca daurgatya-saṃtaptāsu caturmukha \|*  
*āgamiṣyati yogātmā dālbhyo nāma mahātapāḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*tāstamarghyeṇa sampūjya praṇipatya punaḥ punaḥ \|*  
*lālapyamānā bahuśo bāṣpaparyākulekṣaṇāḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*smarantyo vipulānbhogān divyamālyānulepanān \|*  
*bhartāraṃ jagatāmīśam anantamaparājitam \|\| 15 \|\|*

*divyabhāvāṃ tāṃ ca purīṃ nānāratnagṛhāṇi ca \|*  
*dvārakāvāsinaḥ sarvān devarūpānkumārakān \|*  
*praśnamevaṃ kariṣyanti munerabhimukhaṃ sthitāḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

11-16. Then, ages after, there will be a great slaughter, owing to the mushala affair; and Lord Krishna, after relieving the universe of its great burden, will go to heaven. ‘The Yadavas will have ceased to exist; and the ladies of Krishna will he seized by robbers, a warrior, like Arjuna, being defeated (and unable to protect them). These robbers will take them to the seashore and enjoy with them there. When these ladies will bemoan their hard lot, the sage Dalbhya, will appear before them.

Those ladies will worship the sage by offering him arghya and salute him again and again. They will then, with tearful eyes, remember their past enjoyments, use of garlands and sandal paste, and think of their Lord, the unconquerable master of the universe, as well as of flowers and the beautiful city of Dwarika, glittering with its riches and gems, and of their respective abodes therein, the Divine forms of their sons dwelling in that sacred city, Then they will put the following question to the sage, standing before him:

## \|\| 70.17-19 \|\|

*striya ūcuḥ*  
*dasyubhirbhagavānsarvāḥ paribhuktā vayaṃ balāt \|*  
*svadharmāccyavane 'smākam asminnaḥ śaraṇaṃ bhava \|\| 17 \|\|*

*ādiṣṭo 'si purā brahman keśavena ca dhīmatā \|*  
*kasmādīśena saṃyogaṃ prāpya veśyātvamāgatāḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*veśyānāmapi yo dharmas taṃ no brūhi tapodhana \|*  
*kathayiṣyatyatastāsāṃ sa dālbhyaścaikitāyanaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

17-19. “Sage! We have all been forcibly defiled by these robbers. Now we have lost our Dharma and place ourselves at your mercy. O, Seer! Pray explain, why we have been degraded to the status of concubines, we, who have been united with God. You have been ordained by the wise Krishna to be our guide. Pray explain to us the duties of concubines.” Thus questioned, the sage will say.

## \|\| 70.20-28 \|\|

*dālbhya uvāca*  
*jalakrīḍāvihāreṣu purā sarasi mānase \|*  
*bhavatīnāṃ ca sarvāsāṃ nārado 'bhyāśamāgataḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*hutāśanasutāḥ sarvā bhavantyo 'psarasaḥ purā \|*  
*apraṇamyāvalepena paripṛṣṭaḥ sa yogavit \|*  
*kathaṃ nārāyaṇo 'smākaṃ bhartā syād ityupādiśa \|\| 21 \|\|*

*tasmādvarapradānaṃ vaḥ śāpaścāyamabhūtpurā \|*  
*śayyādvayapradānena madhumādhavamāsayoḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*suvarṇopaskarotsargād dvādaśyāṃ śuklapakṣataḥ \|*  
*bhartā nārāyaṇo nūnaṃ bhaviṣyatyanyajanmani \|\| 23 \|\|*

*yadakṛtvā praṇāmaṃ me rūpasaubhāgyamatsarāt \|*  
*paripṛṣṭo 'smi tenāśu viyogo vo bhaviṣyati \|*  
*caurairapahṛtāḥ sarvā veśyātvaṃ samavāpsyatha \|\| 24 \|\|*

*evaṃ nāradaśāpena keśavasya ca dhīmataḥ \|*  
*veśyātvamāgatāḥ sarvā bhavantyaḥ kāmamohitāḥ \|*  
*idānīmapi yadvakṣye tacchṛṇudhvaṃ varāṅganāḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*dālbhya uvāca*  
*purā devāsure uddhe hateṣu śataśaḥ suraiḥ \|*  
*dānavāsuradaityeṣu rākṣaseṣu tatastataḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*teṣāṃ vrātasahasrāṇi śatānyapi ca yoṣitām \|*  
*pariṇītāni yāni syur balādbhuktāni yāni vai \|*  
*tāni sarvāṇi deveśaḥ provāca vadatāṃ varaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

*indra uvāca*  
*veśyādharmeṇa vartadhvam adhunā nṛpamandire \|*  
*bhaktimatyo varārohās tathā devakuleṣu ca \|\| 28 \|\|*

20-28. Dalbhya said: — “Ladies! in the days gone by, all of you were sporting. in the Mansarovara lake, when Narada chanced to go there, Then you. were the daughters of Agni, in the form of nymphs, You did not salute the sage, but asked him how Narayana, the Lord of the universe, would be your husband, Narada blessed you with the boon asked for, but also cursed you for not saluting him, He said that, by giving away two beddings, according to prescribed rites, on the twelfth day of the bright fortnight, in the months of -Chaitra and Vaishakha, you would get Krishna as your husband in the next life.’

## \|\| 70.24-25 \|\|

*yadakṛtvā praṇāmaṃ me rūpasaubhāgyamatsarāt \|*  
*paripṛṣṭo 'smi tenāśu viyogo vo bhaviṣyati \|*  
*caurairapahṛtāḥ sarvā veśyātvaṃ samavāpsyatha \|\| 24 \|\|*

*evaṃ nāradaśāpena keśavasya ca dhīmataḥ \|*  
*veśyātvamāgatāḥ sarvā bhavantyaḥ kāmamohitāḥ \|*  
*idānīmapi yadvakṣye tacchṛṇudhvaṃ varāṅganāḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

24-25. And cursed you as follows: — ‘Because ‘in your conceit. of beauty and prosperity you have omitted to salute me before‘ putting me this question, you will also be separated from Krishna and will be lowered to the rank of public women, after being forcibly carried away by thieves. In consequence of the curses of Narada and Krishna you gave way to lustful feelings and have become prostitutes. Now listen ‘to what I say.

## \|\| 70.26-28 \|\|

*dālbhya uvāca*  
*purā devāsure uddhe hateṣu śataśaḥ suraiḥ \|*  
*dānavāsuradaityeṣu rākṣaseṣu tatastataḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*teṣāṃ vrātasahasrāṇi śatānyapi ca yoṣitām \|*  
*pariṇītāni yāni syur balādbhuktāni yāni vai \|*  
*tāni sarvāṇi deveśaḥ provāca vadatāṃ varaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

*indra uvāca*  
*veśyādharmeṇa vartadhvam adhunā nṛpamandire \|*  
*bhaktimatyo varārohās tathā devakuleṣu ca \|\| 28 \|\|*

26-28. Once upon a time thousands and thousands of the demons (Danavas, Asuras, Daityas and Rakshasas: were killed in the war between the Devas and the demons. Indra told their numberless widows and those women who were forcibly seized and enjoyed, to lead the life of prostitutes and remain devoted to the kings and the Devas.

## \|\| 70.29-32 \|\|

*rājānaḥ svāminastulyāḥ sutā vāpi ca tatsamāḥ \|*  
*bhaviṣyati ca saubhāgyaṃ sarvāsāmapi śaktitaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*yaḥ kaścicchulkamādāya gṛhameṣyati vaḥ sadā \|*  
*nidhanenopacāryo vaḥ sa tadānyatra dāmbhikāt \|\| 30 \|\|*

*devatānāṃ pitriṇāṃ ca puṇyāhe samupasthite \|*  
*gobhūhiraṇyadhānyāni pradeyāni svaśaktitaḥ \|*  
*brāhmaṇānāṃ varārohāḥ kāryāṇi vacanāni ca \|\| 31 \|\|*

*yaccāpyanyadvrataṃ samyag upadekṣyāmyahaṃ tataḥ \|*  
*avicāreṇa sarvābhir anuṣṭheyaṃ ca tatpunaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

29-32. Indra continued, ‘You should look upon, with equal eye, the kings your masters and on Shudra. All of you will attain prosperity, according to your fate. You should satisfy those who would come to you with adequate sum of money to enjoy your company, even if they be poor. But you should not give pleasure to proud men. You should give away cow, land, grain and gold, according to your means, in charity on the sacred day of worshipping the Devas or the ancestors. You should act as the Brahmanas will say. In addition to this, \[ shall also tell you an ordinance (or vrata), which all of you should blindly practise.’

## \|\| 70.33-38 \|\|

*saṃsārottāraṇāyālam etadvedavido viduḥ \|*  
*yadā sūryadine hastaḥ puṣyo yātha punarvasuḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

*bhavetsarvauṣadhīsnānaṃ samyaṅnārī samācaret \|*  
*tadā pañcaśarasyāpi saṃnidhātṛtvameṣyati \|*  
*arcayetpuṇḍarīkākṣam anaṅgasyānukīrtanaiḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

*kāmāya pādau sampūjya jaṅghe vai mohakāriṇe \|*  
*meḍhraṃ kandarpanidhaye kīṭaṃ prītimate namaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

*nābhiṃ saukhyasamudrāya vāmāya ca tathodaram \|*  
*hṛdayaṃ hṛdayeśāya stanāvāhlādakāriṇe \|\| 36 \|\|*

*utkaṇṭhāyeti vaikuṇṭham āsyamānandakāriṇe \|*  
*vāmāṅgaṃ puṣpacāpāya puṣpabāṇāya dakṣiṇam \|\| 37 \|\|*

*mānasāyeti vai mauliṃ vilolāyeti mūrdhajam \|*  
*sarvātmane ca sarvāṅgaṃ devadevasya pūjayet \|\| 38 \|\|*

33-38. This ordinance has been held to be the best means of crossing unscathed the sea of the evils of life, by those learned in the Vedas, The women folk should bathe in the water mixed with several herbs, on a Sunday, when there falls Hasta, Pushya or Punarvasu asterism. They should then approach the God of Love and worship Pundarikaksha, by reciting the names of Cupid, wiz. — The feet of Vishnu, the God of the gods, should be worshipped with the words, “Kamaya namah,” the legs with “Mohakarine namah,” the region of Cupid with “Kandarpanidhaye namah,” the waist with “Priti mate namah,” the navel with “Sankhyasamudraya namah,” the stomach with “Ramaya namah,” the heart with “Hridayeshaya namah,” the breasts with “Abladakarine namah,” the throat with “Utkanthaya namah,” the mouth with Anandakartne, namah,” the left limbs with Puspadhanvaéya namah,” the right limbs with Pushpabanaya namah, the head with “ Manasaya namah,” the hair of the head with “Vilolaya namah,” and all the body with “Sarvatmane namah.”

## \|\| 70.39-40 \|\|

*namaḥ śivāya śāntāya pāśāṅkuśadharāya ca \|*  
*gadine pītavastrāya śaṅkhacakradharāya ca \|\| 39 \|\|*

*namo nārāyaṇāyeti kāmadevātmane namaḥ \|*  
*sarvaśāntyai namaḥ prītyai namo ratyai nama śriyai \|\| 40 \|\|*

39-40. They should then salute the respective Gods and Godesses with the following mantras, “Namah Shivaya, namah Santiya,” “Namah Pashankudadhardya,” “ Namah Gadine,” “Namah Pitavastraya” (yellow-robed one)” “Namah Sankhachakra-dharaya,” “Namah Narfyandya,” “Namah Kamatmane,” “Namah Sarvagantyai,” “Namah Prityai,” “Namah Ratyai,” “Namah Sriyai,” “Namah Pustyai,” “ Namah Tustyai,” “Namah Sarvartha sampade.”

## \|\| 70.41 \|\|

*namaḥ puṣṭyai namastuṣṭyai namaḥ sarvārthasampade \|*  
*evaṃ sampūjya deveśam anaṅgātmakamīśvaram \|*  
*gandhairmaulyaistathā dhūpair naivedyena ca kāminī \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. The women folk should then worship the Lord, whose body is cupid himself, by offering Him incense, flowers, sandal and eatables.

## \|\| 70.42 \|\|

*tata āhūya dharmajñaṃ brahmāṇaṃ vedapāragam \|*  
*avyaṅgāvayavaṃ pūjya gandhapuṣpārcanādibhiḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Afterwards, the Brahmana, well versed in the Vedanta. who must be virtuous and free from bodily deformity, should be honoured with the offerings of incense, flowers, sandal.

## \|\| 70.43 \|\|

*śāleyataṇḍulaprasthaṃ ghṛtapātreṇa saṃyutam \|*  
*tasmai viprāya sā dadyān mādhavaḥ prīyatāmiti \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. And a quantity (of the measure Prastha) of uncooked rice, along with a pot, full of clarified butter, should be given away to the same Brahmana, after saying, ‘Lord Madhava, be pleased’.

## \|\| 70.44 \|\|

*yatheṣṭāhārauktaṃ vai tameva dvijasattamam \|*  
*ratyarthaṃ kāmadevo 'yam iti citte 'vadhārya tam \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. That Brahmana should be well fed and be devoutly looked upon as cupid, for the sake of sexual enjoyment.

## \|\| 70.45 \|\|

*yadyadicchati viprendras tattatkuryādvilāsinī \|*  
*sarvabhāvena cātmānam arpayetsmitabhāṣiṇī \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Each and every desire of that. Brahmana should be satisfied by the woman devotee. She should, with all heart and soul and with a smile on her face, yield herself up to him.

## \|\| 70.46-48 \|\|

*evamādityavāreṇa sarvametatsamācaret \|*  
*taṇḍulaprasthadānaṃ ca yāvanmāsāstrayodaśa \|\| 46 \|\|*

*tatastrayodaśe māsi samprāpte tasya bhāminī \|*  
*viprasyopaskarairyuktāṃ śayyāṃ dadyādvilakṣaṇām \|\| 47 \|\|*

*sopadhānakaviśrāmāṃ sāstarāvaraṇāṃ śubhām \|*  
*pradīpopānahacchattra-pādukāsanasaṃyutām \|\| 48 \|\|*

46-48. This rite should be observed on every Sunday; and the devotee should give away the above-mentioned quantity of uncooked rice for a period of thirteen months; at the expiry of which, the same Brahmana should he given a full bedding, with all its requisites, viz. — pillows, good sheets, dipa (lamp), a pair of shoes, umbrella, sandals, a small piece of mattress to sit upon.

## \|\| 70.49 \|\|

*sapatnīkamalaṃkṛtya hemasūtrāṅgulīyakaiḥ \|*  
*sūkṣmavastraiḥ sakaṭakair dhūpamālyānulepanaiḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Next, that Brahmana, with his wife, should be honoured with gold threads, gold rings, fine cloth, bangles, and with incense, garlands of flowers and sandal paste.

## \|\| 70.50-51 \|\|

*kāmadevaṃ sapatnīkaṃ guḍakumbhopari sthitam \|*  
*tāmrapātrāsanagataṃ haimanetrapaṭāvṛtam \|\| 50 \|\|*

*sakāṃsyabhājanopetam ikṣudaṇḍasamanvitam \|*  
*dadyādetena mantreṇa tathaikāṃ gāṃ payasvinīm \|\| 51 \|\|*

50-51. The images of Cupid and Rati, seated on a plate of copper, placed on a vessel full of molasses, their eyes being of gold and they being well dressed, should be given away, along with a fine milk cow, a vessel of bell ‘metal and a piece of sugar cane, by reciting the mantra of the following signification

## \|\| 70.52 \|\|

*yathāntaraṃ na paśyāmi kāmakeśavayoḥ sadā \|*  
*tathaiva sarvakāmāptir astu viṣṇo sadā mama \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. ‘As I do not make any difference between Vishnu and Cupid, so O Lord Vishnu, be pleased to always fulfil my desires.’

## \|\| 70.53 \|\|

*yathā na kamalā dehāt prayāti tava keśava \|*  
*tathā mamāpi deveśa śarīre sve kuru prabho \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. ‘O Keshava! as the Goddess Lakshmi never remains apart from you, in the same way make my body Your dwelling place’

## \|\| 70.54 \|\|

*tathā ca kāñcanaṃ devaṃ pratigṛhṇandvijottamaḥ \|*  
*ka idaṃ kasmā adāditi vaidikaṃ mantramīrayet \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. Alter that, the Brahmana, accepting the image of Cupid, should pronounee the following Vedic mantra. ‘Ka Idam Kasmat, &c.’

## \|\| 70.55 \|\|

*tataḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya visarjya dvijapuṃgavam \|*  
*śayyāsanādikaṃ sarvaṃ brāhmaṇasya gṛhaṃ nayet \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Then the Brahmana should be dismissed, after being circumambulated, and beddings and other things should be sent to the house of the Brahmana.

## \|\| 70.56 \|\|

*tataḥ prabhṛti yo vipro ratyarthaṃ gṛhamāgataḥ \|*  
*sa mānyaḥ sūryavāre ca sa mantavyo bhavettadā \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. Henceforth, any Brahmana coming to them for the sake of sexual enjoyment on a Sunday, should be respected and honoured.

## \|\| 70.57 \|\|

*evaṃ trayodaśaṃ yāvan māsamevaṃ dvijottamān \|*  
*tarpayeta yathākāmaṃ proṣite 'nyaṃ samācaret \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. In this way, the good Brahmanas should be kept satisfied for a period of thirteen months - but if. they go abroad, their course of action will be different.

## \|\| 70.58-59 \|\|

*tadanujñayā rūpavānyo yāvadabhyāgato bhavet \|*  
*ātmano 'pi yathāvighnaṃ garbhabhūtikaraṃ priyam \|\| 58 \|\|*

*daivaṃ vā mānuṣaṃ vā syād anurāgeṇa vā tataḥ \|*  
*sācārānaṣṭapañcāśad yathāśaktyā samācaret \|\| 59 \|\|*

58-59. If, with the consent of that Brahmana, another handsome person come to them, these women should, with love and affection and to the best of their ability, perform all the fifty-eight kinds of observances of Love, favourite of man and gods, which would lead to pregnancy and which is not harmful to their soul’s welfare.

## \|\| 70.60 \|\|

*etaddhi kathitaṃ samyag bhavatīnāṃ viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*adharmo 'yaṃ tato na syād veśyānāmiha sarvadā \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. I have described to you this vrata in detail, which, when always performed, never leads the prostitutes to sin.

## \|\| 70.61 \|\|

*puruhūtena yatproktaṃ dānavīṣu purā mayā \|*  
*tadidaṃ sāmprataṃ sarvaṃ bhavatīṣvapi ujyate \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. I have fully related to you what Indra said to the women of, the Danavas (demons) in ancient days

## \|\| 70.62 \|\|

*sarvapāpapraśamanam anantaphaladāyakam \|*  
*kalyāṇīnāṃ ca kathitaṃ tatkurudhvaṃ varānanāḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. O, Women of beauty! This vrata is the dispeller of all sins and giver of innumerable benefits. I wish well of you: hence you should do as I told you

## \|\| 70.63 \|\|

*karoti yāśeṣamakhaṇḍametat kalyāṇinī mādhavalokasaṃsthā \|*  
*sā pūjitā devagaṇair aśeṣair ānandakṛtsthānam upaiti viṣṇoḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. She (the well-favoured), who follows this ordinance strictly, goes to the region of Madhava, and is honoured by the Devas, and in the end obtains a place in the Vishnu-loka.

## \|\| 70.64 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca*  
*tapodhanaḥ so 'pyabhidhāya caivaṃ tadā ca tāsāṃ vratamaṅganānām \|*  
*svasthānameṣyatyanu tāḥ samastaṃ vrataṃ kariṣyanti ca devayānaiḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. The Lord said: — The sage Dalabhya, having thus taught those women how to observe this ordinance, will go to his own place; and those women of divine origin will practice the vrata, as directed.”

## Chapter 71

## \|\| 71.1 \|\|

*brahmovāca*  
*mohādvāpi madādvāpi yaḥ parastrīṃ samāśrayet \|*  
*tasyāpi niṣkṛtiṃ deva vada sarvakṛpākara \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Brahma said. — “Lord be pleased to explain to me the ordinance, by the observance of which there may be no separation between husband and wife, nor should there be any grief, disaster or pain.”

## \|\| 71.2 \|\|

*bhagavanpuruṣasyeha striyāśca virahādikam \|*  
*śokavyādhibhayaṃ duḥkhaṃ na bhavedyena tadvada \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Lord said. — Keshava always reposes in company with Lakshmi, in the ocean of milk, on the second day of the dark fortnight, in the month of Shravana.

## \|\| 71.3 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca*  
*śrāvaṇasya dvitīyāyāṃ kṛṣṇāyāṃ madhusūdanaḥ \|*  
*kṣīrārṇave sapatnīkaḥ sadā vasati keśavaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. By worshipping Govinda on that day all the desires are fulfilled; and by giving away cows, land, gold, &., the devotee goes and resides in the region of Vishnu for a period of 700 Kalpas

## \|\| 71.4 \|\|

*tasyāṃ sampūjya govindaṃ sarvānkāmānsamaśnute \|*  
*gobhūhiraṇyadānādi saptakalpaśatānugam \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. The ordinance is known under the name of Ashunyashayanadvitiya, on which day Vishnu should be worshipped, according to the rituals and mantras mentioned hereafter.

## \|\| 71.5 \|\|

*aśūnyaśayanaṃ nāma dvitīyā saṃprakīrtitā \|*  
*tasyāṃ sampūjayedviṣṇum ebhirmantrairvidhānataḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. The devotee should pray: — “O, Shrivatsadhari, Shrikanta, Shridhamana, Shripati, Avinashi, let this house-holder’s life of mine which is the giver of trivarga (dharma, artha and kama) may never be destroyed.

## \|\| 71.6 \|\|

*śrīvatsadhāriñchrīkānta śrīdhāmañchrīpate 'vyaya \|*  
*gārhasthyaṃ mā praṇāśaṃ me yātu dharmārthakāmadam \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. O Purushottama! let there be no destruction of my Agni or Pitris, nor let there be any separation between husband and wife.

## \|\| 71.7 \|\|

*agnayo mā praṇaṣyantu devatāḥ puruṣottama \|*  
*pitaro mā praṇaṣyantu māstu dāmpatyabhedanam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Deva, as you never remain apart from your consort, Lakshmi, similarly, let there be no aloofness between me and my wife.

## \|\| 71.8 \|\|

*lakṣmyā viujyate deva na kadācidyathā bhavān \|*  
*tathā kalatrasambandho deva mā me viujyatām \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Madhusudana! as your household is never bereft of the goddess Lakshmi, similarly, let not mine be devoid of my wife’

## \|\| 71.9 \|\|

*lakṣmyā na śūnyo varada śayyāṃ tvaṃ śayanaṃ gataḥ \|*  
*śayyā mamāpyaśūnyāstu tathaiva madhusūdana \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. After this prayer, the hymns of Vishnu should be sung in accompaniment of various kinds of musical instruments; if that may not be feasible, then the mere ringing of the bell is sufficient, for a bell is an embodiment of all musical instruments

## \|\| 71.10 \|\|

*gītavāditranirghoṣaṃ devadevasya kīrtayet \|*  
*ghaṇṭā bhavedaśaktasya sarvavādyamayī yataḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. After thus worshipping Govinda, the devotee should have his meals at night, avoiding oil and salt and acids.

## \|\| 71.11 \|\|

*evaṃ sampūjya govindam aśnīyāttailavarjitam \|*  
*naktamakṣāralavaṇaṃ yāvattatsyāccatuṣṭayam \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. In the morning, the image of Lakshmi and Vishnu, candle, food grain, cloth, utensils, and bedstead should be given away.

## \|\| 71.12 \|\|
