*tataḥ prabhāte saṃjāte lakṣmīpatisamanvitām \|*  
*dīpānnabhājanairyuktāṃ śayyāṃ dadyādvilakṣaṇām \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. A pair of sandles, shoes, umbrella, chamara, mattress, white sheet should also be given away with the bedstead.

## \|\| 71.13-14 \|\|

*pādukopānahacchattra-cāmarāsanasaṃyutām \|*  
*abhīṣṭopaskarairyuktāṃ śuklapuṣpāmbarāvṛtām \|\| 13 \|\|*

*sopadhānakaviśrāmāṃ phalairnānāvidhairyutām \|*  
*tathābharaṇadhānyaiśca yathāśaktyā samanvitām \|\| 14 \|\|*

13-14. Pillows, bedding, fruits, ornaments, should also be given away, along with: the bedstead, according to the means of the worshipper, without exercising jealousy and miserliness, to a Brahmana. who may be versed in the Vedas and be a devotee of Vishnu, having a large family and having no bodily defects.

## \|\| 71.15 \|\|

*avyaṅgāṅgāya viprāya vaiṣṇavāya kuṭumbine \|*  
*dātavyā vedaviduṣe bhāvenāpatitāya ca \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. At the time of giving away the bedstead, the Brahmana, along with his wife, should be seated on it, and the former should be given a vessel, full of nice eatables.

## \|\| 71.16 \|\|

*tatropaviṣya dāmpatyam alaṃkṛtya vidhānataḥ \|*  
*patnyāstu bhājanaṃ dadyād bhakṣyabhojyasamanvitam \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. The image of Vishnu should be given away to the- Brahmana after placing it on a pitcher full of water.

## \|\| 71.17-18 \|\|

*brāhmaṇasyāpi sauvarṇīm upaskarasamanvitām \|*  
*pratimāṃ devadevasya sodakumbhāṃ nivedayet \|\| 17 \|\|*

*evaṃ yastu pumānkuryād aśūnyaśayanaṃ hareḥ \|*  
*vittaśāṭhyena rahito nārāyaṇaparāyaṇaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

17-18. A woman with a husband, or a widow, who keeps up this ordinance according to the prescribed rites, without niggardliness, goes to and resides in heaven, They, being always dutiful and free from sorrow and blessed with sons, cattle and. wealth, always remain in comp any of their husband, without being separated so long as the sun, moon and stars remain in heaven.

## \|\| 71.19 \|\|

*na tasya patnyā virahaḥ kadācidapi jāyate \|*  
*nārī vā vidhavā brahman yāvaccandrārkatārakam \|*  
*na virūpau na śokārtau dampatī bhavataḥ kvacit \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Their sons, cattle and wealth are never destroyed, and the devotee goes to the region of Vishnu where he resides for 77,000 kalpas.

## Chapter 72

## \|\| 72.1 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca*  
*śṛṇu cānyadbhaviṣyaṃ yad rūpasampadvidhāyakam \|*  
*bhaviṣyati uge tasmin dvāparānte pitāmaha \|*  
*pippalādasya saṃvādo udhiṣṭhirapuraḥsaraiḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Shiva said." Brahma! Now listen to the ordinance that will be the giver of wealth, and will come in vogue at the end of future Dwapara. It is in the form of a conversation between Yudhisthira and the sages, Pippalada, etc.”

## \|\| 72.2 \|\|

*vasantaṃ naimiṣāraṇye pippalādaṃ mahāmunim \|*  
*abhigamya tadā cainaṃ praśnamekaṃ kariṣyati \|*  
*yudhiṣṭhiro dharmaputro dharmauktastapodhanam \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. “Yudhisthira, the pious, will go to Naimnisharanya before the sage Pippalada, and put this question to him.”

## \|\| 72.3 \|\|

*yudhiṣṭhira uvāca*  
*kathamārogyamaiśvaryaṃ matirdharme gatistathā \|*  
*avyaṅgatā śive bhaktir vaiṣṇavo vā bhavetkatham \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Yudhisthira said:--“O sage! How health, prosperity and firm faith in religion can be maintained, and how can unflinching devotion be centred in Shiva and Vishnu, and how may one be free from all bodily defects.”

## \|\| 72.4 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca*  
*tasyottaramidaṃ brahman pippalādasya dhīmataḥ \|*  
*śṛṇuṣva yadvakṣyati vai dharmaputrāya dhārmikaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Shiva said: — ‘‘ Brahma! I shall now tell you the reply of the sage Pippalada to the queries of Yudhisthira.”

## \|\| 72.5 \|\|

*pippalāda uvāca*  
*sādhu pṛṣṭaṃ tvayā bhadra idānīṃ kathayāmi te \|*  
*aṅgāravratam ityetat sa vakṣyati mahīpateḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Pippalada said: — “King! you have put a most useful question. I shall now tell you something about it.” So savings, he will describe the Angaravrata. About this, there is the following ancient story:

## \|\| 72.6 \|\|

*atrāpyudāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam \|*  
*virocanasya saṃvādaṃ bhārgavasya ca dhīmataḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. There took place a dialogue between Virochana and Bhargava.

## \|\| 72.7-8 \|\|

*prahlādasya sutaṃ dṛṣṭvā dviraṣṭaparivatsaram \|*  
*rūpeṇāpratimaṃ kāntyā so 'hasadbhṛgunandanaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*sādhu sādhu mahābāho virocana śivaṃ tava \|*  
*tattathā hasitaṃ tasya papraccha surasūdanaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8. Once upon a time, the mighty sage, Shukra, seeing Virochana, the handsome, sixteen-years-old son of Prahlada, laughed, and saying, Sadhu, Sadhu, addressed him, “O mighty armed Virochana! O prince! O may you be always prosperous.” Then Virochana, the enemy of the Devas, wondering at the laughing of the sage, inquired.

## \|\| 72.9 \|\|

*brahmankimarthametatte hāsyamākasmikaṃ kṛtam \|*  
*sādhusādhviti māmevam uktavāṃstvaṃ vadasva me \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. O Brahmana! tell me the reason of your laughter without any apparent cause and why did you again say, Sadhu, Sadhu, to me.

## \|\| 72.10 \|\|

*tamevaṃvādinaṃ śukra uvāca vadatāṃ varaḥ \|*  
*vismayādvratamāhātmyād dhāsyametatkṛtaṃ mayā \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Shukra said: — “I laughed on the sudden remembrance of the glory of the Vrata (which you lad the good luck of Witnessing in your past life and which gave you this handsome form),

## \|\| 72.11 \|\|

*purā dakṣavināśāya kupitasya tu śūlinaḥ \|*  
*atha tadbhīmavaktrasya svedabindurlalāṭajaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. In ancient times, a drop of perspiration trickled down the forehead of of Shiva at the time of His getting Into rage to annihilate Daksha.

## \|\| 72.12-13 \|\|

*bhittvā sa sapta pātālān adahatsapta sāgarān \|*  
*anekavaktranayano jvaladjvalanabhīṣaṇaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*vīrabhadra iti khyātaḥ karapādāutairyutaḥ \|*  
*kṛtvāsau yajñamathanaṃ punarbhūtalasambhavaḥ \|*  
*trijagannirdahanbhūyaḥ śivena vinivāritaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

12-13. That drop penetrated into all the seven lower regions and dried up all the seven oceans. Afterwards, out-of the same drop, Virabhadra, with many a mouth and eyes emitting flashes of fire from them, was born. He was endowed with myriads of hands and. feet, and destroyed the sacrifice of Daksha. This Earth-born Virabhadra destroyed the sacrifice of Daksha-and then attempted to burn up the three worlds. Whereupon, Shiva intervened, when He saw Virabhadra was going to consume the universe, and made him abstain from his campaign of destruction

## \|\| 72.14-15 \|\|

*kṛtaṃ tvayā vīrabhadra dakṣayajñavināśanam \|*  
*idānīmalametena lokadāhena karmaṇā \|\| 14 \|\|*

*śāntipradātā sarveṣāṃ grahāṇāṃ prathamo bhava \|*  
*prekṣiṣyante janāḥ pūjāṃ kariṣyanti varānmama \|\| 15 \|\|*

14-15. Gen said Virabhadra! You have destroyed the sacrifice of Daksha, and now you should not consume the universe. Be calm, You will he prime in the mansion of auspicious planets, and people will worship you through my favour.

## \|\| 72.16 \|\|

*aṅgāraka iti khyātiṃ gamiṣyasi dharātmaja \|*  
*devaloke 'dvitīyaṃ ca tava rūpaṃ bhaviṣyati \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. “You will be known as Angaraka (the planet Mars), the son of the Earth, and your form in the Divine region will be a pearless one in beauty.

## \|\| 72.17 \|\|

*ye ca tvāṃ pūjayiṣyanti caturthyāṃ tvaddine narāḥ \|*  
*rūpamārogyamaiśvaryaṃ teṣvanantaṃ bhaviṣyati \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. “On the fourth day of a bright fortnight, when it falls on a Tuesday, the people worshipping you will get everlasting beauty and prosperity and health."

## \|\| 72.18 \|\|

*evamuktastadā śāntim agamat kāmarūpadhṛk \|*  
*saṃjātastatkṣaṇādrājan grahatvam agamatpunaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Hearing such words of Shiva, that son of the Earth, instantly became placid and afterwards turned into a planet.

## \|\| 72.19-22 \|\|

*sa kadācidbhavāṃstasya pūjārghyādikamuttamam \|*  
*dṛṣṭavānkriyamāṇaṃ ca śūdreṇa ca vyavasthitaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

*tena tvaṃ rūpavāñjātaḥ suraśatrukulodvaha \|*  
*vividhā ca rucirjātā yasmāttava vidūragā \|\| 20 \|\|*

*virocana iti prāhus tasmāttvāṃ devadānavāḥ \|*  
*śūdreṇa kriyamāṇasya vratasya tava darśanāt \|*  
*īdṛśīṃ rūpasampattiṃ dṛṣṭvā vismitavānaham \|\| 21 \|\|*

*sādhu sādhviti tenoktam aho māhātmyamuttamam \|*  
*paṣyato 'pi bhavedrūpam aiśvaryaṃ kimu kurvataḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

19-22. “Some Shudra was worshipping that planet Mars, and you saw the ceremony, on account of which you are so handsome and renowned, O you son. of Prahlada. You are known as Virochana by the Devas and the Asuras, because you possess various (vi) far-reaching intelligence (Rochi), and hence you are called Virochana (far-reaching light). I was astonished to see the great beauty possessed by you simply by your looking at the ceremony of Angarakavrata, and consequently I greeted you with the words Sadhu, Sadhu, thinking of the great mahatmya of that vrata, When, by merely looking at that ceremony, one gets beauty and lordliness as yours, I do not know what would he the case if a man were to observe this ordinance”.

## \|\| 72.24 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca*  
*atha tadvacanaṃ śrutvā bhārgavasya mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*prahrādanandano vīraḥ punaḥ papraccha vismitaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. “O Prince! You looked with faith at the ceremony of giving away the cows, &c , in charity, at the conclusion of the vrata performed in honour of Mars, the son of Earth, by a low- born despicable Shudra, and consequently you have been given such a handsome form and are born in the royal ae Shiva said: “On hearing those words of Shukra. Virochana was very much astonished and asked him.”

## \|\| 72.25 \|\|

*virocana uvāca*  
*bhagavaṃstadvrataṃ samyak śrotumicchāmi tattvataḥ \|*  
*dīyamānaṃ tu yaddānaṃ mayā dṛṣṭaṃ bhavāntare \|\| 25 \|\|*

25 Virochana said. — “O sage! I am eager to hear about the ordinance as well as about the charities witnessed by me in my previous life.”

## \|\| 72.26 \|\|

*māhātmyaṃ ca vidhiṃ tasya yathāvadvaktumarhasi \|*  
*iti tadvacanaṃ śrutvā punaḥ provāca vistarāt \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. “Pray explain to me the glory and the-rituals connected with that ordinance,” — Hearing those words of Virochana, Shukra, began to explain it in detail.

## \|\| 72.27 \|\|

*śukra uvāca*  
*caturthyaṅgārakadine yadā bhavati dānava \|*  
*mṛdā snānaṃ tadā kuryāt padmarāgavibhūṣitaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Shukra said. — O Danava! if the 4th day of the bright fortnight fall on a Tuesday, the devotee should bathe after rubbing earth over his body, and then wear rubies.

## \|\| 72.28 \|\|

*agnirmūrdhā divo mantraṃ japannāste udaṅmukhaḥ \|*  
*śūdrastūṣṇīṃ smaranbhaumam āste bhogavivarjitaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. He should ‘mutter the mantras, “Agnimurdha diva,” by turning his face towards the north. If the devotee be a Shudra, he should silently, without uttering any mantra, meditate over the form of Bhauma (Mars). The company of women should be avoided that day.

## \|\| 72.29 \|\|

*tathāstamita āditye gomayenānulepayet \|*  
*prāṅgaṇaṃ puṣpamālābhir akṣatābhiḥ samantataḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. At dusk the court-yard of the house should be plastered with cow dung and adorned with floral wreaths, and uncooked rice should be placed all round.

## \|\| 72.30 \|\|

*abhyarcyābhilikhetpadmaṃ kuṅkumenāṣṭapattrakam \|*  
*kuṅkumasyāpyabhāve tu raktacandanamiṣyate \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Thereafter worshipping Bhauma, a lotus of eight petals should be drawn in saffron. If saffron is not available, then it should be drawn by red-sandal.

## \|\| 72.31 \|\|

*catvāraḥ karakāḥ kāryā bhakṣyabhojyasamanvitāḥ \|*  
*taṇḍulai raktaśālīyaiḥ padmarāgaiśca saṃyutāḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Four pitchers, full of eatables, should be placed, and uncooked rice and rubies should be placed in-them.

## \|\| 72.32 \|\|

*catuṣkoṇeṣu tānkṛtvā phalāni vividhāni ca \|*  
*gandhamālyādikaṃ sarvaṃ tathaiva vinivedayet \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. The pitchers should be located in the four corners, and fruits, flowers, incense, etc., should be placed over them.

## \|\| 72.33 \|\|

*suvarṇaśṛṅgīṃ kapilām athārcya raupyaiḥ suraiḥ kāṃsyadohāṃ savatsām \|*  
*dhuraṃdharaṃ raktamatīva saumyaṃ dhānyāni saptāmbarasaṃyutāni \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Then a milk cow, with her horns covered with gold, and hoofs with silver, should be given away to a Brahmana in charity, along with a milking vessel of bell metal, and her calf. So also should be given an ox, and the seven kinds of grains tied in seven different pieces of cloths.

## \|\| 72.34 \|\|

*aṅguṣṭhamātraṃ puruṣaṃ tathaiva sauvarṇamatyāyatabāhudaṇḍam \|*  
*caturbhujaṃ hemamaye niviṣṭaṃ pātre guḍasyopari sarpiukte \|\| 34 \|\|*

34 An image of the size of a thumb should be made in gold. Its four arms should be extensive. The image should be placed on a vessel of gold, and the vessel should be placed on raw sugar and clarified butter

## \|\| 72.35 \|\|

*samastayajñāya jitendriyāya pātrāya śīlānvayasaṃyutāya \|*  
*dātavyametatsakalaṃ dvijāya kuṭumbine naiva tu dāmbhikāya \|*  
*samarpayedvipravarāya bhaktyā kṛtāñjaliḥ pūrvamudīrya mantram \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Afterwards, all that should be given away in charity to a Brahmana, who is versed in the sacrificial rites, is able to restrain his passions, is calm and modest, is well-born and has large family. It should never be given to a Brahmana, who is a hypocrite. — Then the devotee should recite the following mantras, with his hands folded.

## \|\| 72.36 \|\|

*bhūmiputra mahābhāga svedodbhava pinākinaḥ \|*  
*rūpārthī tvāṃ prapanno 'haṃ gṛhāṇārghyaṃ namo 'stu te \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. O, Son of Earth, O blessed one, you have been born of the sweat drop of lord Shiva, I pray you for beauty and have taken shelter under you.

Be pleased to accept this arghya, I salute you. Pray accept this libation.

**Комментарий:**

Note: — The mantra in the original is this: — ...

## \|\| 72.37 \|\|

*mantreṇānena dattvārghyaṃ raktacandanavāriṇā \|*  
*tato 'rcayedvipravaraṃ raktamālyāmbarādibhiḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. The libation of water (arghya), mingled with red sandal, should be made by reciting the above mantras, and the Brahmana should be worshipped with red sandal, red flowers, and red cloths, etc.

## \|\| 72.38 \|\|

*dadyāttenaiva mantreṇa bhaumaṃ gomithunānvitam \|*  
*śayyāṃ ca śaktito dadyāt sarvopaskarasaṃyutām \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. By uttering the same mantra, a cow, with an ox, should be given away in charity in honour of Mars, and a bedstead, well-arranged with all its requisites, should also be given away

## \|\| 72.39 \|\|

*yadyadiṣṭatamaṃ loke yaccāsya dayitaṃ gṛhe \|*  
*tattadguṇavate deyaṃ tadevākṣayyamicchatā \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. All the nice things available or the things appreciated by the devotee wishing to acquire everlasting benefits, should be given away in charity to the Brahmana.

## \|\| 72.40 \|\|

*pradakṣiṇaṃ tataḥ kṛtvā visarjya dvijapuṃgavam \|*  
*naktamakṣāralavaṇam aśnīyādghṛtasaṃyutam \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. After this, the Brahmana should be circumambulated and dismissed, and the devotee should take his evening meal with clarified butter, avoiding salt and acid.

## \|\| 72.41 \|\|

*bhaktyā yastu punaḥ kuryād evamaṅgārakāṣṭakam \|*  
*caturo vātha vā tasya yatpuṇyaṃ tadvadāmi te \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. I shall now describe to you the benefits that accrue to the devotee by observing this Angaraka vrata for eight times or even four times with devotion.

## \|\| 72.42 \|\|

*rūpasaubhāgyasampannaḥ punarjanmani janmani \|*  
*viṣṇau vātha śive bhaktaḥ saptadvīpādhipo bhavet \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. He gets handsomeness, luck, and devotion to Shiva and Vishnu in all his lives, and becomes the king of the seven realms.

## \|\| 72.43 \|\|

*sapta kalpasahasrāṇi rudraloke mahīyate \|*  
*tasmāttvamapi daityendra vratametatsamācara \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. He lives for seven Kalpas in the clime of Shiva after death, and, O Prince of the Daityas! You should also therefore perform this Vrata.

## \|\| 72.44 \|\|

*pippalāda uvāca*  
*ityevamuktvā bhṛgunandano 'pi jagāma daityaśca cakāra sarvam \|*  
*tvaṃ cāpi rājankuru sarvametad yato 'kṣayaṃ vedavido vadanti \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Pippalada said. — After thus describing the rituals, the sage Shukra went away and Virochana, the Prince of the Daityas, afterwards kept this observance, according to the prescribed rites, and O King Yudhisthira!

You should also keep it, For the knowers of Veda say that its fruit is inexhaustible.

## \|\| 72.45 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca*  
*tatheti sampūjya sa pippalādaṃ vākyaṃ cakārādbhutavīryakarmā \|*  
*śṛṇoti yaścainamananyacetās tasyāpi siddhiṃ bhagavānvidhatte \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Shiva said. — Hearing all this. from the sage. Pippalada, the King Yudhisthira, of the wonderful deeds and prowess, said: — “Let it be so.”

He then performed this Vrata. One who hears about it, after pondering over the words of Pippalada with attention, also gets the same benefit by the grace of the lord Mars.

## Chapter 73

## \|\| 73.1-2 \|\|

*pippalāda uvāca*  
*athātaḥ śṛṇu bhūpāla pratiśukraṃ praśāntaye \|*  
*yātrārambhe 'vasāne ca tathā śukrodaye tviha \|\| 1 \|\|*

*rājate vātha sauvarṇe kāṃsyapātre 'thavā punaḥ \|*  
*śuklapuṣpāmbaraute sitataṇḍulapūrite \|\| 2 \|\|*

1-2. Pippalada said. — “King! now listen to the rituals pertaining to the pacification of the malignant aspect of the planet Shukra (Venus), On the beginning of a journey or its end, or on the occasions of the appearance and the disappearance of Shukra, a vessel of silver, gold or bell metal should be made and filled in with white flowers, white cloth and uncooked rice.

## \|\| 73.3 \|\|

*vidhāya rājataṃ śukraṃ śucimuktāphalānvitam \|*  
*mantreṇānena tatsarvaṃ sāmagāya nivedayet \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. A silver image of Shukra should be made and given away to a Brahmana versed in the Samaveda, after decorating it with pearls and placing it on the top of the vessel.

## \|\| 73.4 \|\|

*namaste sarvalokeśa namaste bhṛgunandana \|*  
*kave sarvārthasiddhyarthaṃ gṛhāṇārghyaṃ namo 'stu te \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. At the time of giving away the image, the following mantra should be uttered: — ‘O, master of all realms, O, Bhrigunandana, O Kavi, salutations to you. Accept this arghya for the fulfilment of my desires’. The arghya mantra is.

## \|\| 73.5 \|\|

*evamasyodaye kurvan yātrādiṣu ca bhārata \|*  
*sarvānkāmānavāpnoti viṣṇuloke mahīyate \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. The person who thus gives away all the things, mentioned above, in charity, according to the aforementioned rites, when undertaking a journey, etc., at the time of the appearance of Shukra, goes to the region of Vishnu, after getting all his desires fulfilled.

## \|\| 73.6 \|\|

*yāvacchukrasya na hṛtā pūjā sā mālyakaiḥ śubhaiḥ \|*  
*vaṭakaiḥ pūrikābhiśca godhūmaiścaṇakairapi \|*  
*tāvadannaṃ na cāśnīyāt tribhiḥ kāmārthasiddhaye \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. The devotee should not take his meals until he has finished his worship of Shukra by offering Him white flowers, fried cakes and cakes of urad pulse and things made of wheat and gram. The person who does so attains trivarga (religious merit, wealth and enjoyments)

## \|\| 73.7-8 \|\|

*tadvadvācaspateḥ pūjāṃ pravakṣyāmi udhiṣṭhira \|*  
*suvarṇapātre sauvarṇam amareśapurohitam \|\| 7 \|\|*

*pītapuṣpāmbarautaṃ kṛtvā snātvātha sarṣapaiḥ \|*  
*palāśāśvatthayogena pañcagavyajalena ca \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8. Yudhisthira! the worship of Brihaspati (Jupiter) has been described in the same way, to which now listen. An image of Brihaspati should be made in gold and placed in & golden vessel, after being dressed in yellow The devotee then should bathe in water mixed with sesamum, or with water mixed with the juice of butea-frondosa or Panchagavya.

## \|\| 73.9 \|\|

*pītāṅgarāgavasano ghṛtahomaṃ tu kārayet \|*  
*praṇamya ca gavā sārdhaṃ brāhmaṇāya nivedayet \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. He should then put on yellow raiments and paint his head with sandal mixed with saffron, and then pour libations of clarified butter in the fire. Then, after saluting Brihaspati, the image should be given away to a Brahmana, along with a cow.

## \|\| 73.10 \|\|

*namaste 'ṅgirasāṃ nātha vākpate ca bṛhaspate \|*  
*krūragrahaiḥ pīḍitānām amṛtāya namo namaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10.\* Brihaspati should thus be saluted: — ‘Salutations to Brihaspati, the giver of solace to those falling under the influence of evil stars”,

**Комментарий:**

Note — The pranama mantra of Brihaspati is as follows ...

## \|\| 73.11 \|\|

*saṃkrāntāvasya kaunteya yātrāsvabhyudayeṣu ca \|*  
*kurvanbṛhaspateḥ pūjāṃ sarvānkāmānsamaśnute \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. O, son of Kunti! One who thus worships Brihaspati on a Shankranta or on undertaking a journey or on other auspicious occasions, attains all his wishes.

## Chapter 74

## \|\| 74.1 \|\|

*brahmovāca*  
*bhagavan bhavasaṃsāra-sāgarottārakāraka \|*  
*kiṃcidvrataṃ samācakṣva svargārogyasukhapradam \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Brahma said: — Lord Shiva! you are the One, who sees all beings safely through the ocean of the world, pray therefore describe some such ordinance, as. may lead people to cross the sea of the world in safety and attain health, heaven and happiness.

## \|\| 74.3-4 \|\|

*śarkarāsaptamīṃ puṇyāṃ tathā kamalasaptamīm \|*  
*mandārasaptamīṃ tadvac chubhadāṃ śubhasaptamīm \|\| 3 \|\|*

*sarvānantaphalāḥ proktāḥ sarvā devarṣipūjitāḥ \|*  
*vidhānamāsāṃ vakṣyāmi yathāvadanupūrvaśaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

3-4. Shiva said: — Brahma! I shall describe to you the Saura dharma, consisting of the following vratas: (2) Kalyana Saptami (ii) Vishokasaptami. So also (iii) Phala Saptami, the destroyer of sins and giver of great merit. Similarly, (iv) the sacred Sharkara Saptami (v) Kamala Saptami (vi) Mandara Saptami, (vii) Shubha Saptami, the giver of auspiciousness. These are the givers of endless merit. All these have been respected by the Devas and the Riis, and I shall describe their rituals to you, one by one, in due order.

## \|\| 74.5-9 \|\|

*yadā tu śuklasaptamyām ādityasya dinaṃ bhavet \|*  
*sā tu kalyāṇinī nāma vijayā ca nigadyate \|\| 5 \|\|*

*prātargavyena payasā snānamasyāṃ samācaret \|*  
*tataḥ śuklāmbaraḥ padmam akṣatābhiḥ prakalpayet \|\| 6 \|\|*

*prāṅmukho 'ṣṭadalaṃ madhye tadvadvṛttāṃ ca karṇikām \|*  
*puṣpākṣatābhirdeveśaṃ vinyasetsarvataḥ kramāt \|\| 7 \|\|*

*pūrveṇa tapanāyeti mārtaṇḍāyeti cānale \|*  
*yāmye divākarāyeti vidhātra iti nairṛte \|\| 8 \|\|*

*paścime varuṇāyeti bhāskarāyeti cānile \|*  
*saumye vikartanāyeti ravaye cāṣṭame dale \|\| 9 \|\|*

5-9. When a Sunday falls on the 7th day of a bright fortnight, it is known as Kalyanini or Vijaya Saptami. On that day the devotee should. bathe in cow’s milk, in the morning, and put on white clothes, and then sit facing the east and draw the picture of an eight-petalled lotus flower, made of uncooked rice powder. He should, then, draw a circle round that lotus, and in the centre of it draw its pericarp, with the same material.

Then, on all sides of it, he should draw eight pictures of the Sun with flowers and rice. The devotee should put a pinch of uncooked rice on each petal of the lotus, after reciting the following mantras: — “Tapanaya namah, Martandiya namah, Divakariya namah, Vidhatre namah, Varunaya namah, Bhiskariya namah Vikartanya namah, and Ravaye namah, respectively, beginning with the picture of the Sun on the Eastern petal, and then on ‘those on the South-Eastern, Southern, South-Western, Western, North-Western, Northern, and, lastly, on the North-Eastern petals.

**Комментарий:**

Note — A pinch of uncooked rice should be placed on each petal after reciting one fame each time, until it is placed on each eight petals, viz. — On the petal in the eastern direction by reciting Tapanaya namah, and so on.

## \|\| 74.10 \|\|

*ādāvante ca madhye ca namo 'stu paramātmane \|*  
*mantrairebhiḥ samabhyarcya namaskārāntadīpitaiḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. At the commencement, as well as at the end, and so also in the middle, of placing rice, he should recite the Mantra Paramat-mane namah Then at the end, the God-Sun should be saluted.

## \|\| 74.11 \|\|

*śuklavastraiḥ phalairbhakṣyair dhūpamālyānulepanaiḥ \|*  
*sthaṇḍile pūjayedbhaktyā guḍena lavaṇena ca \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. The Sun should be worshipped on the altar by being offered white cloth, fruits, incense, flowers, sandal paste, eatables and raw sugar, along with salt, all of which should be given away in charity to Brahmanas.

## \|\| 74.12 \|\|

*tato vyāhṛtimantreṇa visṛjeddvijapuṃgavān \|*  
*śaktitaḥ pūjayedbhaktyā guḍakṣīraghṛtādibhiḥ \|*  
*tilapātraṃ hiraṇyaṃ ca brāhmaṇāya nivedayet \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Afterwards, good Brahmanas should be devoutly worshipped with raw sugar, clarified butter and milk, and then they should be given gold, placed on a dish, containing sesamum.

## \|\| 74.13 \|\|

*evaṃ niyamakṛtsuptvā prātarutthāya mānavaḥ \|*  
*kṛtasnānajapo vipraiḥ sahaiva ghṛtapāyasam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Then the Brahmanas should be dismissed with fees, after reciting the ‘vyahriti’ mantras. The devotee should then go to sleep and then, after getting up in the morning, he should bathe and finish his japa (prayers) and take rice cooked in clarified butter and sugar in company of the Brahmanas

## \|\| 74.14 \|\|

*bhuktvā ca vedaviduṣe biḍālavratavarjite \|*  
*ghṛtapātraṃ sakanakaṃ sodakumbhaṃ nivedayet \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. After meals, the devotee should give away to the Brahmanas. who may be free from hypocrisy, a pot, full of clarified butter, and a piece of gold, along with a pitcher, full of water

## \|\| 74.15-16 \|\|

*prīyatāmatra bhagavān paramātmā divākaraḥ \|*  
*anena vidhinā sarvaṃ māsi māsi vrataṃ caret \|\| 15 \|\|*

*tatastrayodaśe māsi gā vai dadyāttrayodaśa \|*  
*vastrālaṃkārasaṃyuktāḥ suvarṇāsyāḥ payasvinīḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

15-16. At that time the devotee shoud say: “O, Adorable Sun, the Supreme Self, be pleased.” The worship of the Sun should thus be followed for a year, on the bright Saptami of every month, and in the 13th month, 13 cows, with their mouths covered with gold and bodies adorned with clothes and ornaments, should be given away.

## \|\| 74.17 \|\|

*ekāmapi pradadyādvā vittahīno vimatsaraḥ \|*  
*na vittaśāṭhyaṃ kurvīta yato mohātpatatyadhaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. If one cannot afford 13 cows, he may give only one, The observer of this ordinance should not exercise miserliness and jealousy. Those who do so, go to hell.

## \|\| 74.18 \|\|

*anena vidhinā yastu kuryātkalyāṇasaptamīm \|*  
*sarvapāpavinirmuktaḥ sūryaloke mahīyate \|*  
*āurārogyamaiśvaryam anantamiha jāyate \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. One who thus observes the Kalyana Saptami. ordinance, goes to the region of the ‘Sun, after being liberated from all sins, and obtains long life, health and prosperity on this earth.

## \|\| 74.19 \|\|

*sarvapāpaharā nityaṃ sarvadaivatapūjitā \|*  
*sarvaduṣṭopaśamanī sadā kalyāṇasaptamī \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. This Saptami, which is the destroyer of all sins and venerated by the Devas, is known as Kalyana Saptami, the remover of all evils.

## \|\| 74.20 \|\|

*imāmanantaphaladāṃ yastu kalyāṇasaptamīm \|*  
*śṛṇoti paṭhate ceha sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. One who reads or hears about this kalyana Saptami, the giver of endless merits, is freed from all sins on this earth.

## Chapter 75

## \|\| 75.1 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca*  
*viśokasaptamīṃ tadvad vakṣyāmi munipuṃgava \|*  
*yāmupoṣya naraḥ śokaṃ na kadācidihāśnute \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Shiva said: — O sage! I shall now tell you about the Vishoka Saptami (the Sorrow-Destroying fast) the observance of which fast frees the devotee from all grief

**Комментарий:**

Note: — Vishoka = Free from grief.

## \|\| 75.2 \|\|

*māghe kṛṣṇatilaiḥ snātvā ṣaṣṭhyāṃ vai śuklapakṣataḥ \|*  
*kṛtāhāraḥ kṛsarayā dantadhāvanapūrvakam \|*  
*upavāsavrataṃ kṛtvā brahmacārī bhavenniśi \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. On the sixth day of the bright fortnight, in the month of Magha, the devotee, after brushing his teeth in the morning and rubbing the body with black sesamum, and bathing, should fast the whole. day; and at night, again brushing his teeth, he should take krisara pudding (consisting of rice, sesamum and a pulse cooked in milk and eaten with ghee and without salt). Then go to bed as a Brahmachari.

## \|\| 75.3 \|\|

*tataḥ prabhāta utthāya kṛtasnānajapaḥ śuciḥ \|*  
*kṛtvā tu kāñcanaṃ padmam arkāyeti ca pūjayet \|*  
*karavīreṇa raktena raktavastraugena ca \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. On the following morning, after bathing and finishing his daily prayer and so being pure, he should have a lotus made of gold, and worship it by pronouncing ‘Arkaya namah.’

**Комментарий:**

Note: — Arakaya namah = Salutations to the Sun.

## \|\| 75.4 \|\|

*yathā viśokaṃ bhuvanaṃ tvayaivāditya sarvadā \|*  
*tathā viśokatā me 'stu tvadbhaktiḥ pratijanma ca \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. The lotus should be worshipped with red kanera flowers and a piece of red cloth . The devotee should Pray to the Sun in these words: —

‘O Aditya! as this world becomes free from all grief at Thy rising, in the same way. let me also be free from sorrow, in all my lives, and may I have always firm faith in ‘Thee’.

## \|\| 75.5-6 \|\|

*evaṃ sampūjya ṣaṣṭhyāṃ tu bhaktyā sampūjayeddvijān \|*  
*suptvā saṃprāṣya gomūtram utthāya kṛtanaityakaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*sampūjya viprānannena guḍapātrasamanvitam \|*  
*tadvastraugmaṃ padmaṃ ca brāhmaṇāya nivedayet \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. Thus, having performed Puja on the sixth day of the bright fortnight, the Brahmanas Should be worshipped with devotion, The worshipper, after taking cow's urine, should go to bed.\* Then, on the following morning, rising from his bed, bathing and finishing his daily prayers, he should offer food to the Brahmanas, in a vessel containing raw sugar. Then the golden lotus should be given away to a Brahmana, along with a pair of red clothes mentioned above.

**Комментарий:**

\*This ceremony relates to the sashthi day.

## \|\| 75.7 \|\|

*atailalavaṇaṃ bhuktvā saptamyāṃ maunasaṃyutaḥ \|*  
*tataḥ purāṇaśravaṇaṃ kartavyaṃ bhūtimicchatā \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. On the Saptami (seventh) day, oil and salt should be avoided, and the devotee should observe a vow of silence and listen to some Purana.

## \|\| 75.8 \|\|

*anena vidhinā sarvam ubhayorapi pakṣayoḥ \|*  
*kṛtvā yāvatpunarmāgha-śuklapakṣasya saptamī \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. The ordinance should then be continued on the seventh day of each fortnight, till the next month of Magha.

## \|\| 75.9 \|\|

*vratānte kalaśaṃ dadyāt suvarṇakamalānvitam \|*  
*śayyāṃ sopaskarāṃ dadyāt kapilāṃ ca payasvinīm \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. On the conclusion of the ordinance, a pitcher of water, along with a golden lotus, should be given away, and a bedstead, with all its requisites and a milk cow, should also be given away.

## \|\| 75.10-12 \|\|

*anena vidhinā yastu vittaśāṭhyavivarjitaḥ \|*  
*viśokasaptamīṃ kuryāt sa yāti paramāṃ gatim \|\| 10 \|\|*

*yāvadjanmasahasrāṇāṃ sāgraṃ koṭiśataṃ bhavet \|*  
*tāvanna śokamabhyeti rogadaurgatyavarjitaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*yaṃ yaṃ prārthayate kāmaṃ taṃ tamāpnoti puṣkalam \|*  
*niṣkāmaḥ kurute yastu sa paraṃ brahma gacchati \|\| 12 \|\|*

10-12. One who keeps up the Vishoka Saptami ordinance, according to the rites mentioned above, without giving way to miserliness, attains bliss, and never gets any sorrow for a period of ten padmas, and is also free from disease. He also attains his wishes, and if he observes it without any desires, he becomes unified with Brahma

## \|\| 75.13 \|\|

*yaḥ paṭhecchṛṇuyādvāpi viśokākhyāṃ ca saptamīm \|*  
*so 'pīndralokamāpnoti na duḥkhī jāyate kvacit \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. One who reads, listens to, or relates this vrata of Vishoka Saptami, goes to the realm of Indra and never gets any sorrow.

## Chapter 76

## \|\| 76.1 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca*  
*anyāmapi pravakṣyāmi nāmnā tu phalasaptamīm \|*  
*yāmupoṣya naraḥ pāpād vimuktaḥ svargabhāgbhavet \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Shiva said: — “I shall now describe to you the Phala Saptami, (fruit gift fast) the observance of which liberates the devotee from sins and leads him to heaven.

## \|\| 76.2-3 \|\|

*mārgaśīrṣe śubhe māsi saptamyāṃ niyatavrataḥ \|*  
*tāmupoṣyātha kamalaṃ kārayitvā tu kāñcanam \|\| 2 \|\|*

*śarkarāsaṃyutaṃ dadyād brāhmaṇāya kuṭumbine \|*  
*raviṃ kāñcanakaṃ kṛtvā palasyaikasya dharmavit \|*  
*dadyāddvikālavelāyāṃ bhānurme prīyatāmiti \|\| 3 \|\|*

2-3. In the month of Margashira, on the seventh day of the bright fortnight, the devotee, after fasting, should give away a lotus of gold, along with sugar, to some Brahmana with a large family. A golden image of the Sun, weighing one pala in measure, should also be given away to a Brahmana in the afternoon, when the devotee should say, ‘O Sun; be pleased on me.’

## \|\| 76.4 \|\|

*bhaktyā tu viprānsampūjya cāṣṭamyāṃ kṣīrabhojanam \|*  
*dattvā kuryātphalautaṃ yāvatsyātkṛṣṇesaptamī \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. On the following day, that is, on Ashtami, the Brahmanas should be worshipped with devotion and fed with milk and fruits; during that period of the day, so long as there Is any portion of the Krishna Saptami remaining, and on every seventh day of the dark fortnight, fruits should be given away in charity

## \|\| 76.5-6 \|\|

*tāmapyupoṣya vidhivad anenaiva krameṇa tu \|*  
*tadvaddhaimaphalaṃ dattvā suvarṇakamalānvitam \|\| 5 \|\|*

*śarkarāpātrasaṃyuktaṃ vastramālyasamanvitam \|*  
*saṃvatsaraṃ ca tenaiva vidhinobhayasaptamīm \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. In the same way, any fruit made of gold, and a lotus, along with sugar, utensils, cloths and flowers should be given away on each seventh day of the dark and the bright fortnights in the month, for a full year.

## \|\| 76.7 \|\|

*upoṣya dattvā kramaśaḥ sūryamantramudīrayet \|*  
*bhānurarko ravirbrahmā sūryaḥ śakro hariḥ śivaḥ \|*  
*śrīmānvibhāvasustvaṣṭā varuṇaḥ prīyatāmiti \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. The following names should be recited, one after the other, each month: — Bhanu, Arka, Ravi, Brahma, Surya, Shukra, Hari, Shiva, Shriman, Vibhavasu, Tvashta, and Varuna.

## \|\| 76.8 \|\|

*pratimāsaṃ ca saptamyām ekaikaṃ nāma kīrtayet \|*  
*pratipakṣaṃ phalatyāgam etatkurvansamācaret \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Out of the names mentioned above, one name, turn by turn, should be recited monthly, on the seventh day of the dark or bright fortnight. The desire of obtaining any fruit or merit, by the observance of this vrata, should be renounced by the devotee.

## \|\| 76.9-10 \|\|

*vratānte vipramithunaṃ pūjayedvastrabhūṣaṇaiḥ \|*  
*śarkarākalaśaṃ dadyād dhemapadmadalānvitam \|\| 9 \|\|*

*yathā na viphalāḥ kāmās tvadbhaktānāṃ sadā rave \|*  
*tathānantaphalāvāptir astu me saptajanmasu \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. At the end of the ordinance, a Brahmana and his wife should be adored, and then cloth as well as a pitcher, full of sugar, along with a lotus of gold, should be given, and the following prayer should be offered — “O Ravi! as the wishes of your devotees never proven fruitless, so the attainment of endless fruits be mine, throughout my future seven lives’.

## \|\| 76.11-13 \|\|

*imāmanantaphaladāṃ yaḥ kuryātphalasaptamīm \|*  
*sarvapāpaviśuddhātmā sūryaloke mahīyate \|\| 11 \|\|*

*surāpānādikaṃ kiṃcid yadatrāmutra vā kṛtam \|*  
*tatsarvaṃ nāśamāyāti yaḥ kuryātphalasaptamīm \|\| 12 \|\|*

*kurvāṇaḥ saptamīṃ cemāṃ satataṃ rogavarjitaḥ \|*  
*bhūtānbhavyāṃśca puruṣāṃs tārayedekaviṃśatim \|*  
*yaḥ śṛṇoti paṭhedvāpi so 'pi kalyāṇabhāgbhavet \|\| 13 \|\|*

11-13. One who observes this Phala Saptami, the giver of endless fruits, being liberated from all his sins, goes to the realm of the sun. He is freed from the sins arising out of drinks, &c.. whether committed in this or the next world. All that is destroyed, who observes this Phala Saptami fast. He who observes this Phala Saptami, becomes free from all diseases and liberates his past ancestors as well as his successors, for 21 generations from bondage. One who reads, hears or relates this to others, gets also prosperity.

## Chapter 77

## \|\| 77.1 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca*  
*śarkarāsaptamīṃ vakṣye tadvatkalmaṣanāśinīm \|*  
*āurārogyamaiśvaryaṃ yayānantaṃ prajāyate \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Shiva said — “I shall now explain to you something about the Sarkari Saptami, (gift of sugar) the destroyer of sin, by the observance of which one gets longevity, prosperity and health.

## \|\| 77.2 \|\|

*mādhavasya site pakṣe saptamyāṃ niyatavrataḥ \|*  
*prātaḥ snātvā tilaiḥ śuklaiḥ śuklamālyānulepanaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. In the month of Vaishakha, on the seventh d ay of the bright fortnight, the devotee should bathe in water, mixed with white sesamum and then put on white sandal paste and a garland of white flowers.

## \|\| 77.3 \|\|

*sthaṇḍile padmamālikhya kuṅkumena sakarṇikam \|*  
*tasminnamaḥ savitre tu gandhadhūpau nivedayet \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. A lotus with its petals and pericarp, should be drawn on an altar with saffron, and flowers and incense should be put on it, after reciting ‘Savitre namah’.

## \|\| 77.4 \|\|

*sthāpayedudakumbhaṃ ca śarkarāpātrasaṃyutam \|*  
*śuklavastrairalaṃkṛtya śuklamālyānulepanaiḥ \|*  
*suvarṇena samāuktaṃ mantreṇānena pūjayet \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Afterwards, a pitcher of water, with a vessel of sugar, should be placed on it, The pitcher should he covered with a piece of white cloth and white flowers, sandal paste, and gold should be put on it. Then the puja should be made with the following mantra:

## \|\| 77.5 \|\|

*viśvavedamayo yasmād vedavādīti paṭhyase \|*  
*sarvasyāmṛtameva tvam ataḥ śāntiṃ prayaccha me \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. ‘O Pitcher, You are the Vedamaya, and, consequently, you are praised as knower of all the Vedas. You are like nectar to all, bring please unto me’.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — Vedamaya = Full of all Vedas, Vedavadi = The knower of the Vedas.

## \|\| 77.6 \|\|

*pañcagavyaṃ tataḥ pītvā svapettatpārśvataḥ kṣitau \|*  
*saurasūktaṃ smarannāste purāṇaśravaṇena ca \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Afterwards, the devotee should drink panchagavya and sleep on the floor, by the side of the pitchers, and should recite the Vedic mantras relating to the Sun and listen to the Puranas.

## \|\| 77.7 \|\|

*ahorātre gate paścād aṣṭamyāṃ kṛtanaityakaḥ \|*  
*tatsarvaṃ viduṣe tadvad brāhmaṇāya nivedayet \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. After the lapse of a day and night, on the 8th day of the fortnight, the devotee should give away all the things to the Brahmanas after performing his daily prayers.

## \|\| 77.8-12 \|\|

*bhojayecchaktito viprāñ charkarāghṛtapāyasaiḥ \|*  
*bhuñjītātailalavaṇaṃ svayamapyatha vāgyataḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*anena vidhinā sarvaṃ māsi māsi samācaret \|*  
*saṃvatsarānte śayanaṃ śarkarākalaśānvitam \|\| 9 \|\|*

*sarvopaskarasaṃyuktaṃ tathaikāṃ gāṃ payasvinīm \|*  
*gṛhaṃ ca śaktimāndadyāt samastopaskarānvitam \|\| 10 \|\|*

*sahasreṇātha niṣkāṇāṃ kṛtvā dadyācchatena vā \|*  
*daśabhirvātha niṣkeṇa tadardhenāpi śaktitaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*suvarṇāśvaḥ pradātavyaḥ pūrvavanmantravādanam \|*  
*na vittaśāṭhyaṃ kurvīta kurvandoṣaṃ samaśnute \|\| 12 \|\|*

8-12. He should feed the Brahmanas, according to his means, with sugar, clarified butter and rice cooked in milk and sugar, but should avoid oil and, salt. He himself should take his meals in silence, The same rule should be observed each month for a year, after which a pitcher of water, with a vessel of sugar, a bedstead, with all its requisites, and a milk cow, and if means permit, then a house containing all the necessities of a householder’s life as well as eatables, should be given away. Miserliness should not be exercised, for it leads to sin. The devotee should, in addition to the things mentioned above, give away a horse of gold worth 1,000 Nishkas; 100 Nishkas, or 10 Nishkas, or of even 5 Nishkas, according to his means, by reciting the mantras pertaining to the Sun.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — One Nishka is equivalent to Rs. 4.

## \|\| 77.13-14 \|\|

*amṛtaṃ pibato vaktrāt sūryasyāmṛtabindavaḥ \|*  
*nipeturye dharaṇyāṃ tu śālimudgekṣavaḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*śarkarā tu parā tasmād ikṣusāro 'mṛtātmavān \|*  
*iṣṭā raverataḥ puṇyā śarkarā havyakavyayoḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

13-14. The nectar fell from the mouth of the Sun, whilst He was quaffing it, out of which (Shali) rice, manga pulse and sugarcane were produced, Sugarcane is the best of all these three, because out of it sugar is prepared. Its juice is just like nectar; consequently, an offering of sugar to Devas and Pitris is dear to the Sun also.

## \|\| 77.15-17 \|\|

*śarkarāsaptamī ceyaṃ vājimedhaphalapradā \|*  
*sarvaduṣṭapraśamanī putrapautrapravardhinī \|\| 15 \|\|*

*yaḥ kuryātparayā bhaktyā sa vai sadgatimāpnuyāt \|*  
*kalpamekaṃ vasetsvarge tato yāti paraṃ padam \|\| 16 \|\|*

*idamanaghaṃ śṛṇoti yaḥ smaredvā paripaṭhatīha divākarasya loke \|*  
*matimapi ca dadāti so 'pi devair amaravadhūjanamālayābhipūjyaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

15-17. This Sharkara Saptami is said to give the same benefit as Ashvamedha sacrifice. It removes all diseases an d makes the sons and the grandsons thrive. One who observes this fast with un flinching devotion, gets bliss. He passes his days for one Kalpa in heaven, and then attains emancipation. One who hears, listens, or reads about. this, goes to the region of the Sun. One who advises others to observe this ordinance, is also venerated by Devas and Heavenly damsels, and passes his days in heaven.

## Chapter 78

## \|\| 78.1 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca*  
*ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi tadvatkamalasaptamīm \|*  
*yasyāḥ saṃkīrtanādeva tuṣyatīha divākaraḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Shiva said: — I shall now describe to you that Kamala Saptami vrata, by the mere mention of which. the God Sun becomes pleased.

## \|\| 78.2 \|\|

*vasantāmalasaptamyāṃ snātaḥ sangaurasarṣapaiḥ \|*  
*tilapātre ca sauvarṇe vidhāya kamalaṃ śubham \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. In the spring, on the 7th day of a bright fortnight, the devotee should bathe in water mixed with white mustard and should then make a golden lotus and place it in a golden vessel, full of sesamum.

## \|\| 78.3-5 \|\|

*vastraugmāvṛtaṃ kṛtvā gandhapuṣpaiḥ samarcayet \|*  
*namaḥ kamalahastāya namaste viśvadhāriṇe \|\| 3 \|\|*

*divākara namastubhyaṃ prabhākara namo 'stu te \|*  
*tato dvikālavelāyām udakumbhasamanvitām \|\| 4 \|\|*

*viprāya dadyātsampūjya vastramālyavibhūṣaṇaiḥ \|*  
*śaktyā ca kapilāṃ dadyād alaṃkṛtya vidhānataḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

3-5. The lotus should be covered with a pair of cloths, and then the Lord Sun should be worshipped with incense, flowers, &c. The following mantras should be recited at the time of worship. ‘Kamalahastiya namah, ‘Vishvadharine namah’, ‘Divakaraya namah’, ‘Prabhakaraya namah;’ and he.

should then give away the golden lotus in the evening, along with the pitcher of water adorning it, with ornaments, cloths and garlands, an do then give it to a Brahmana. So, also, according to his means, he may give away a milk cow after adorning her well.

## \|\| 78.6 \|\|

*ahorātre gate paścād aṣṭamyāṃ bhojayeddvijān \|*  
*yathāśaktyatha bhuñjīta māṃsatailavivarjitam \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. On the following day i.e., on the ashtami the Brahmanas should be fed according to the means of the devotee, but he himself should not take flesh and oil.

## \|\| 78.7 \|\|

*anena vidhinā śukla-saptamyāṃ māsi māsi ca \|*  
*sarvaṃ samācaredbhaktyā vittaśāṭhyavivarjitaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. In this way, the devotee, without giving way to miserliness, should observe the same rituals, on the 7th day of a bright fortnight each month.

## \|\| 78.8-9 \|\|

*vratānte śayanaṃ dadyāt suvarṇakamalānvitam \|*  
*gāṃ ca dadyātsvaśaktyā tu suvarṇāḍhyāṃ payasvinīm \|\| 8 \|\|*

*bhājanāsanadīpādīn dadyād iṣṭānupaskarān \|*  
*anena vidhinā yastu kuryātkamalasaptamīm \|*  
*lakṣmīmanantāmabhyeti sūryaloke mahīyate \|\| 9 \|\|*

8-9. On the conclusion of the ordinance, a bedstead along with the golden lotus, should be given away, and a cow with its horns plaited with gold as well as utensils asana (seats) and candle sticks should also be given away, along with other necessary articles. One, who observes this ordinance, according to the prescribed rites, becomes possessed of inexhaustible wealth and goes to the kingdom of the Sun.

## \|\| 78.10-11 \|\|

*kalpe kalpe tato lokān saptagatvā pṛthakpṛthak \|*  
*apsarobhiḥ parivṛtas tato yāti parāṃ gatim \|\| 10 \|\|*

*yaḥ paṣyatīdaṃ śṛṇuyācca martyaḥ paṭhecca bhaktyātha matiṃ dadāti \|*  
*so 'pyatra lakṣmīmacalāmavāpya gandharvavidyādharalokabhāksyāt \|\| 11 \|\|*

10-11. He also goes to all the seven lokas, in each kalpa, where he enjoys in the company of the nymphs and gets bliss. One who hears, sees, relates or observes this ordinance also becomes wealthy and goes to heaven, where he ‘enjoys the company of Gandharvas and Vidyadharas.

## Chapter 79

## \|\| 79.1 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca*  
*athātaḥ sampravakṣyāmi sarvapāpapraṇāśinīm \|*  
*sarvakāmapradāṃ ramyāṃ nāmnā mandārasaptamīm \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Shiva said: — L now relate to you about the Mandara Saptami, the giver of all desires, the most excellent, and the destroyer of all sins.

## \|\| 79.2 \|\|

*māghasyāmalapakṣe tu pañcamyāṃ laghubhuṅnaraḥ \|*  
*dantakāṣṭhaṃ tataḥ kṛtvā ṣaṣṭhīmupavasedbudhaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. The devotee should take some light food on the fifth day of the bright fortnight in the month of Magha, and, having arisen from his bed in the morning and brushing his teeth and bathing, should keep fast on that day viz., on the Shashthi day

## \|\| 79.3-5 \|\|

*viprān sampūjayitvā tu mandāraṃ prāśayenniśi \|*  
*tataḥ prabhāta utthāya kṛtvā snānaṃ punardvijān \|\| 3 \|\|*

*bhojayecchaktitaḥ kṛtvā mandārakusumāṣṭakam \|*  
*sauvarṇaṃ puruṣaṃ tadvat padmahastaṃ suśobhanam \|\| 4 \|\|*

*padmaṃ kṛṣṇatilaiḥ kṛtvā tāmrapātre 'ṣṭapattrakam \|*  
*haimamandārakusumair bhāskarāyeti pūrvataḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

3-5. That day he should honor a few Brahmanas and feed them with delicious food at night. Mandara\* prashana should be offered to the Deva. On the following morning, that is, the saptami day, he should feed the Brahmanas again, according to his means, after his morning ablutions. Then procure sight Mandara flowers and prepare a golden image of the Sun carrying a lotus in his hand and place it in a copper-vessel containing sesamum, and prepare also an eight-petalled lotus and invoke the God Sun He should offer one mandara flower on each petal.

**Комментарий:**

\*Mandara is the name given to several species of plants, viz., Calotropis gigantea, Erythrina indica, and thorn-apple.

## \|\| 79.6-7 \|\|

*namaskāreṇa tadvacca sūryāyetyānale dale \|*  
*dakṣiṇe tadvadarkāya tathāryamṇe ca nairṛte \|\| 6 \|\|*

*paścime vedadhāmne ca vāyavye caṇḍabhānave \|*  
*pūṣṇetyuttarataḥ pūjyam ānandāyetyataḥ param \|\| 7 \|\|*

6-7. He should then salute the Sun and put some flowers and uncooked rice on the lotus leaf, in the Eastern direction by saying ‘ Bhashkarayanamah’ in the South-East by saying ‘Suryaya namah’ in the South, by saying ‘Arkaya namah.’ in the South-West, by saying “ Aryamne namah,”

in the West by saying: — “Veda dhamne namah,” in the North-West direction by saying “Chanda Bhanave namah,” in the North by saying “Pushne namali,” in the North-East by saying ‘Anandaya namah.’

## \|\| 79.8 \|\|

*karṇikāyāṃ ca puruṣaṃ sarvātmana iti nyaset \|*  
*śuklavastraiḥ samāveṣṭya bhakṣyairmālyaphalādibhiḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. The devotee should place the image of the Male Purusha on the pericarp of the lotus, and after saying ‘Sarvatmane namah,’ white cloth should be put on the image, and eatables, flowers and fruits should be offered.

## \|\| 79.9 \|\|

*evamabhyarcya tatsarvaṃ dadyādvedavide punaḥ \|*  
*bhuñjītātailalavaṇaṃ vāgyataḥ prāṅmukho gṛhī \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Then all these things should be given away to a Brahmana versed in the Vedas. ‘He himself should take his meals, but then oil and salt should be avoided. He should observe the vow of silence while eating, and take his meals facing the East.

## \|\| 79.10 \|\|

*anena vidhinā sarvaṃ saptamyāṃ māsi māsi ca \|*  
*kuryātsaṃvatsaraṃ yāvad vittaśāṭhyavivarjitaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. This ordinance should be observed, according to the prescribed rites for a year, on the seventh day of a fortnight, each month, without giving way to miserliness.

## \|\| 79.11 \|\|

*etadeva vratānte tu nidhāya kalaśopari \|*  
*gobhirvibhavataḥ sārdhaṃ dātavyaṃ bhūtimicchatā \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. On the conclusion of the ordinance, the lotus of gold should be given away after being placed on a pitcher of water. One wishing to acquire prosperity, should give away a cow in addition to it,

## \|\| 79.12 \|\|

*namo mandāranāthāya mandārabhavanāya ca \|*  
*tvaṃ rave tārayasvāsmān saṃsārabhayasāgarāt \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. ‘The following prayer should then he offered ‘TI salute Mandaranatha and Mandarabhavana, O Lord Sun! see me throngh this wordly ocean of troubles.’

## \|\| 79.13-15 \|\|

*anena vidhinā yastu kuryānmandārasaptamīm \|*  
*vipāpmā sa sukhī martyaḥ kalpaṃ ca divi modate \|\| 13 \|\|*

*imāmaghaughapaṭala-bhīṣaṇadhvāntadīpikām \|*  
*gacchanpragṛhya saṃsāre sarvārthāṃśca labhennaraḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*mandārasaptamīm etām īpsitārthaphalapradām \|*  
*yaḥ paṭhecchṛṇuyādvāpi sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate \|\| 15 \|\|*

13-15. One who observes this Mandara Saptami fast in this way is freed from all sins and: goes to heaven where he resides for a kalpa. This ordinance is like a torch that dispels all the sins like pitched darkness. One who keeps it up gets his desires “fulfilled. One who reads or listens about this ordinance becomes freed from all sins.

## Chapter 80

## \|\| 80.1 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca*  
*athānyāmapi vakṣyāmi śobhanāṃ śubhasaptamīm \|*  
*yāmupoṣya naro roga-śokaduḥkhaiḥ pramucyate \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Shri Bhagavan said: — I shall now explain to you about the excellent. Subba saptami fasting, which frees the devotee from all diseases, sorrows and troubles.

## \|\| 80.2 \|\|

*puṇyena cāśvauje māsi kṛtasnānajapaḥ śuciḥ \|*  
*vācayitvā tato viprān ārabhecchubhasaptamīm \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. The devotee should observe this ordinance on the seventh day of the bright fortnight, in the month of Ashvina, after ablutions and morning prayers, when the Brahmanas have done the svastivachana.

## \|\| 80.3 \|\|

*kapilāṃ pūjayedbhaktyā gandhamālyānulepanaiḥ \|*  
*namāmi sūryasambhūtām aśeṣabhuvanālayām \|*  
*tvāmahaṃ śubhakalyāṇa-śarīrāṃ sarvasiddhaye \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. A milk cow should be worshipped with incense, flowers and sandal paste and the devotee should say, ‘O, One who has been born of the Sun and one who resides in the various climes, whose body is goodness itself, TI salute Thee for the fulfilment of my desires.’

## \|\| 80.4-5 \|\|

*atha kṛtvā tilaprasthaṃ tāmrapātreṇa saṃyutam \|*  
*kāñcanaṃ vṛṣabhaṃ tadvad gandhamālyaguḍānvitaiḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*phalair nānāvidhair bhakṣyair ghṛtapāyasasaṃyutaiḥ \|*  
*dadyāddvikālavelāyām aryamā prīyatāmiti \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. After this, a quantity (of the Prastha measure} of sesamum put in a vessel of copper, an ox of gold with incense, garland, molasses, various kinds of fruits, eatables and dishes made of milk and clarified butter, should be given away in the evening by reciting the mantra, “Aryama Priyatam.”

## \|\| 80.6-8 \|\|

*pañcagavyaṃ ca saṃprāṣya svapedbhūmau vimatsaraḥ \|*  
*tataḥ prabhāte saṃjāte bhaktyā sampūjayeddvijān \|\| 6 \|\|*

*anena vidhinā dadyān māsi māsi sadā naraḥ \|*  
*vāsasā vṛṣabhaṃ haimaṃ tadvadgāṃ kāñcanodbhavām \|\| 7 \|\|*

*saṃvatsarānte śayanam ikṣudaṇḍaguḍānvitam \|*  
*sopadhānakaviśrāmaṃ bhājanāsanasaṃyutam \|\| 8 \|\|*

6-8. The devotee should offer Panchagavya as Prashana, He should be free from all pride and sleep on the floor. On the following morning, he Shoal. get up and worship the Brahmanas with devotion. Thus men should give away each month a couple of cloths, a golden ox and a golden cow, and; at the end of the year, sugarcane, molasses, bedding,: pillows, utensils, and mattresses.

## \|\| 80.9 \|\|

*tāmrapātre tilaprasthaṃ sauvarṇaṃ vṛṣabhaṃ tathā \|*  
*dadyādvedavide sarvaṃ viśvātmā prīyatāmiti \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Afterwards, a quantity (of the Prastha measure) of sesamum placed in A vessel of copper and a golden ox, should be given to a Brahmana versed in the Vedas, with the words, “Vishvatma Priyatam”.

## \|\| 80.10 \|\|

*anena vidhinā vidvān kuryādyaḥ śubhasaptamīm \|*  
*tasya śrīrvipulā kīrtir bhavedjanmani janmani \|\| 10 \|\|*

10 One who keeps up this ordinance in this way becomes wealthy and renowned in each birth.

## \|\| 80.11 \|\|

*apsarogaṇagandharvaiḥ pūjyamānaḥ surālaye \|*  
*vasedgaṇādhipo bhūtvā yāvadābhūtasaṃplavam \|*  
*kalpādāvavatīrṇastu saptadvīpādhipo bhavet \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. He is also honoured by the nymphs (i.e., Apsaras and Gandharvas), and resides in heaven as the Lord of Hosts (i.e., Ganas) till the end of the kalpa, after which le is born as a king.

## \|\| 80.12 \|\|

*brahmahatyāsahasrasya bhrūṇahatyāśatasya ca \|*  
*nāśāyālamiyaṃ puṇyā paṭhyate śubhasaptamī \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Thousands of the sins accruing by the killing of Brahmanas and by willful abortion, are expiated by the reading of this sacred vrata of Sapami.

## \|\| 80.13 \|\|

*imāṃ paṭhedyaḥ śṛṇuyānmuhūrtaṃ paśyetprasaṅgādapi dīyamānam \|*  
*so 'pyatra sarvāghavimuktadehaḥ prāpnoti vidyādharanāyakatvam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. One who reads this or hears it, even for a moment, or sees the vrata performed and things given away, is freed from all sing and becomes the Lord of the Vidyidharas

## \|\| 80.14 \|\|

*yāvatsamāḥ sapta naraḥ karoti yaḥ saptamīṃ saptavidhānauktām \|*  
*sa saptalokādhipatiḥ krameṇa bhūtvā padaṃ yāti paraṃ murāreḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. One who keeps up this Saptami vrata (ordinance), of sevenfold prescription, for a period of seven years, becomes the Lord of seven regions, turn by turn, alter which he goes to the region of ‘Vishnu and attains bliss

## Chapter 81

## \|\| 81.1 \|\|

*manuruvāca*  
*kim abhīṣṭaviyogaśokasaṃghādalam uddhartumupoṣaṇaṃ vrataṃ vā \|*  
*vibhavodbhavakāri bhūtale 'smin bhavabhīterapi sūdanaṃ ca puṃsaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Manu asked: — Lord! which is that ordinance, by the observance of which, separation from the dear ‘vies ceases to be painful and which confers prosperity on the devotee and which saves men from the evils of this life.

## \|\| 81.2 \|\|

*matsya uvāca*  
*paripṛṣṭamidaṃ jagatpriyaṃ te vibudhānāmapi durlabhaṃ mahattvāt \|*  
*tava bhaktimatastathāpi vakṣye vratamindrāsuramānaveṣu guhyam \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. The Lord said:- — The question put by you, O Manu! is beneficial to the world, and, owing to the sublimity of the subject-matter, is beyond the reach of heaven even; and, though kept secret from Suras and Asuras, now, I shall relate it to yon on account of your intense devotion.

## \|\| 81.3 \|\|

*puṇyamāśvauje māsi viśokadvādaśīvratam \|*  
*daśamyāṃ laghubhugvidvān ārabhenniyamena tu \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. The Vishokadvadashi ordinance falls in the month of Ashvina. On the tenth day of the fortnight, the devotee should take some light food and commence the ordinance by observing the prescribed rites.

## \|\| 81.4-5 \|\|

*udaṅmukhaḥ prāṅmukho vā dantadhāvanapūrvakam \|*  
*ekādaśyāṃ nirāhāraḥ samabhyarcya tu keśavam \|*  
*śriyaṃ vābhyarcya vidhivad bhokṣyāmi tvapare 'hani \|\| 4 \|\|*

*evaṃ niyamakṛtsuptvā prātarutthāya mānavaḥ \|*  
*snānaṃ sarvauṣadhaiḥ kuryāt pañcagavyajalena tu \|*  
*śuklamālyāmbaradharaḥ pūjayecchrīśamutpalaiḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. On the Ekadashi day, he should brush his teeth by, turning his face towards the north or the. east. Then he should worship the Lord Keshava and the Goddess Lakshmi, and fast the day. ‘I shall take my meal consisting of many dishes next day.” With this thought, he should go to sleep, and, on getting up in the morning, he should bathe in Pancha(gavya. water, mixed with various medicines, and put on white clothes and garlands of white flowers, Afterwards, the worship of Lakshmi and Narayana should be commenced with white lotus flowers.

## \|\| 81.6-11 \|\|

*viśokāya namaḥ pādau jaṅghe ca varadāya vai \|*  
*śrīśāya jānunī tadvad ūrū ca jalaśāyine \|\| 6 \|\|*

*kandarpāya namo guhyaṃ mādhavāya namaḥ kaṭim \|*  
*dāmodarāyetyudaraṃ pārśve ca vipulāya vai \|\| 7 \|\|*

*nābhiṃ ca padmanābhāya hṛdayaṃ manmathāya vai \|*  
*śrīdharāya vibhorvakṣaḥ karau madhujite namaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*cakriṇe vāmabāhuṃ ca dakṣiṇaṃ gadine namaḥ \|*  
*vaikuṇṭhāya namaḥ kaṇṭham āsyaṃ yajñamukhāya vai \|\| 9 \|\|*

*nāsāmaśokanidhaye vāsudevāya cākṣiṇī \|*  
*lalāṭaṃ vāmanāyeti haraye ca punarbhruvau \|\| 10 \|\|*

*alakānmādhavāyeti kirīṭaṃ viśvarūpiṇe \|*  
*namaḥ sarvātmane tadvac chira ityabhipūjayet \|\| 11 \|\|*

6-11. The feet should he worshipped, after reciting ‘Vishokaya namah,’ the legs after reciting ‘Varadiya namah,’ the knees after reciting ‘Shrishaya namah,’ the thighs after reciting ‘Jalashiyine namah,’ the private parts after reciting ‘ Kandarpisa namab. the waist after reciting ‘Madhavaya namah, the stomach after reciting ‘Damedariya namah,’ the ribs after reciting ‘Vipuliya namah, the navel after reciting ‘Padmanabhaya namah,’ the heart after reciting ‘Maumathaya namah,’ the breasts after reciting Sridharaya namah. the hands after reciting ‘Madhujite namah,’ the left arm after reciting ‘Chakrine namah,’ the right arm after reciting ‘ Gadi-ne namah,’ the throat after reciting ‘ Vaikunthaya namah,’ the mouth after reciting ‘ Yajiivamukhiva namah,’ the nose after reciting ‘ Asokanidhaye namah ) the eyes after. reciting ‘ Vasudleviva n am ah,’ the forehead. after reciting VAmandya namah.’ the eye brows after reciting ‘Haraye namah,’ the locks of hair after reciting ‘Madhavaya namah, the crown after reciting Vishvarupine namah, the head after reciting ‘Sarvatmane namah.

## \|\| 81.12 \|\|

*evaṃ sampūjya govindaṃ phalamālyānulepanaiḥ \|*  
*tatastu maṇḍalaṃ kṛtvā sthaṇḍilaṃ kārayenmudā \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Thus worshiping Vishnu with sandal, fruits and flowers, an altar should be made on the ground alter making a circle.

## \|\| 81.13 \|\|

*caturasraṃ samantācca ratnimātramudakplavam \|*  
*ślakṣṇaṃ hṛdyaṃ ca parito vapratrayasamāvṛtam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. The altar should he a square in shape, and of the dimensions of a cubit, and should slant towards the north. It must he smooth and soft, surrounded by three small mud-walls.

## \|\| 81.14 \|\|

*aṅgulenocchritā vaprās tadvistārastu dvyaṅgulaḥ \|*  
*sthaṇḍilasyopariṣṭācca bhittiraṣṭāṅgulā bhavet \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. The upper surface should be eight fingers \| high from. the ground; and the mudwalls one finger high and two fingers thick.

**Комментарий:**

N.B.: One finger is a little less than one inch.

## \|\| 81.15 \|\|

*nadīvālukayā śūrpe lakṣmyāḥ pratikṛtiṃ nyaset \|*  
*sthaṇḍile śūrpamāropya lakṣmīmityarcayedbudhaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. On it should be placed an image of Lakshmi, made of river sand, and placed 1 a winnowing basket, and worshipped according to the rites hereafter mentioned.

## \|\| 81.16 \|\|

*namo devyai namaḥ śāntyai namo lakṣmyai namaḥ śriyai \|*  
*namaḥ puṣṭyai namastuṣṭyai vṛṣṭyai hṛṣṭyai namo namaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Lakshmi should he worshipped, after reciting the following mantras, Devyat namah, Santyai namah, Lakshmyai namah, Shrtyai namah, Pusshyal namahh, Tushyai namah Vrishtyai namah, Hrishtyai namah.

## \|\| 81.17 \|\|

*viśokā duḥkhanāśāya viśokā varadāstu me \|*  
*viśokā cāstu sampattyai viśokā sarvasiddhaye \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. The devotee should also say, ‘O Vishoka goddess, destroy all grief, grant some boon, give wealth, and fulfil all desires.

## \|\| 81.18 \|\|

*tataḥ śuklāmbaraiḥ śūrpaṃ veṣṭya sampūjayetphalaiḥ \|*  
*vastrairnānāvidhaistadvat suvarṇakamalena ca \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. After this, he should wrap up the winnowing basket in a piece of cloth, and worship Lakshmi with fruits and various kinds of clothes and with a golden lotus

## \|\| 81.19-23 \|\|

*rajanīṣu ca sarvāsu pibeddarbhodakaṃ budhaḥ \|*  
*tatastu gītanṛtyādi kārayetsakalāṃ niśām \|\| 19 \|\|*

*yāmatraye vyatīte tu suptvāpyutthāya mānavaḥ \|*  
*abhigamya ca viprāṇāṃ mithunāni tadārcayet \|\| 20 \|\|*

*śaktitas trīṇi caikaṃ vā vastramālyānulepanaiḥ \|*  
*śayanasthāni pūjyāni namo 'stu jalaśāyine \|\| 21 \|\|*

*tatastu gītavādyena rātrau jāgaraṇe kṛte \|*  
*prabhāte ca tataḥ snānaṃ kṛtvā dāmpatyamarcayet \|\| 22 \|\|*

*bhojanaṃ ca yathāśaktyā vittaśāṭhyavivarjitaḥ \|*  
*bhuktvā śrutvā purāṇāni taddinaṃ cātivāhayet \|\| 23 \|\|*

19-23. The devotee should drink the water purified by the Kusha grass, and carry on music and singing throughout the night: and, on the lapse of three quarters of the night thus past in vigil and prayer, the devotee should sleep in the last quarter, and then waking up, go and worship them, along with three couples of Brahmanas and Brahmanas according to his means: if not three, at least, one couple should be worshipped. He should offer them sandal, flowers and cloths as well as bedsteads, with the mantra, “Namastu Jalashayine.” The night thus passed with watching, music and gongs, the devotee, after bathing in the morning, should worship the Brahmana couples, as mentioned above. They should be fed according to his ‘means, free from niggardliness. And then, after taking his meals, he should pass that day in listening to the Purina

## \|\| 81.24 \|\|

*anena vidhinā sarvaṃ māsi māsi samācaret \|*  
*vratānte śayanaṃ dadyād guḍadhenusamanvitam \|*  
*sopadhānakaviśrāmaṃ sāstarāvaraṇaṃ śubham \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. The devotee should observe the same rituals every month till the ordinance is over; after which, he should give away a bedstead, along with the guda dhenu\* (sugar cow), pillows, bedding, sheets and cloths.

## \|\| 81.25 \|\|

*yathā na lakṣmīrdeveśa tvāṃ parityajya gacchati \|*  
*tathā surūpatārogyam aśokaścāstu me sadā \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Then he should say, ‘O Lord! as Lakshmi does not forsake you, similarly, beauty, health, and pleasure may always be mine’.

## \|\| 81.26 \|\|

*yathā devena rahitā na lakṣmīrjāyate kvacit \|*  
*tathā viśokatā me 'stu bhaktiragryā ca keśave \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. ‘As Lakshmi does not go without Vishnu, let there always he happiness with me. Let my devotion always remain centred in Vishnu.’

## \|\| 81.27 \|\|

*mantreṇānena śayanaṃ guḍadhenusamanvitam \|*  
*śūrpaṃ ca lakṣmyā sahitaṃ dātavyaṃ bhūtimicchatā \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. With the above words, the devotee should give away the bedstead, and: guda dhenu, the image of Lakshmi and the winnowing basket, to the Brahmana

## \|\| 81.28 \|\|

*utpalaṃ karavīraṃ ca bāṇamamlānakuṅkumam \|*  
*ketakī sinduvāraṃ ca mallikā gandhapāṭalā \|*  
*kadambaṃ kubjakaṃ jātiḥ śastānyetāni sarvadā \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. The following flowers are always desirable in this form of worship viz., ‘Lotus, Kanera, Bana, fresh Safron flower, Ketaki, Sindhuvara, Jasmine, Gaudhapatala, Kadamba, Kubjaka and Champaka.

## Chapter 82

## \|\| 82.1 \|\|

*manuruvāca*  
*guḍadhenuvidhānaṃ me samācakṣva jagatpate \|*  
*kiṃrūpaṃ kena mantreṇa dātavyaṃ tadihocyatām \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Manu asked: — O, Lord of the Universe! pray tell me about Gudadhenu. How should it be made, and by what mantra should it be given away?

## \|\| 82.2 \|\|

*matsya uvāca*  
*guḍadhenuvidhānasya yadrūpamiha yatphalam \|*  
*tadidānīṃ pravakṣyāmi sarvapāpavināśanam \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. The Lord Matsya answered: — O King! I shall explain to you the form of Gudadhenu, and the fruits of its gift, as well as the mantras, according to which it should be given away. It is the destroyer of all sins.

## \|\| 82.3-4 \|\|

*kṛṣṇājinaṃ caturhastaṃ prāggrīvaṃ vinyasedbhuvi \|*  
*gomayenānuliptāyāṃ darbhānāstīrya sarvataḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*laghveṇakājinaṃ tadvad vatsaṃ ca parikalpayet \|*  
*prāṅmukhīṃ kalpayeddhenum udakpādāṃ savatsakām \|\| 4 \|\|*

3-4. The floor should be plastered with cowdung, the kusha grass should be spread on all sides, and then over it should be placed a black antelope skin of four hands in length with its neck towards the east. This is meant for the cow. A smaller deerskin should be spread on the floor, near the first, and it should be meant for her calf. The cow should be made to face the east and the calf the north

## \|\| 82.5-6 \|\|

*uttamā guḍadhenuḥ syāt sadā bhāracatuṣṭayam \|*  
*vatsaṃ bhāreṇa kurvīta dvābhyāṃ vai madhyamā smṛtā \|\| 5 \|\|*

*ardhabhāreṇa vatsaḥ syāt kaniṣṭhā bhārakeṇa tu \|*  
*caturthāṃśena vatsaḥ syād gṛhavittānusārataḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. The image of Gudadhenu (Sugar cow) should be made of 4 mounds of raw sugar, and the calf of one mound of raw sugar, which-is considered to be the first class; the image of the cow made of two mounds and the calf of half a mound. of raw sugar is considered to be the next best. The image of the cow made of one mound and the calf of ten seers of raw sugar is considered to be the last best. The devotee is to choose between the three, according to his means.

## \|\| 82.7-8 \|\|

*dhenuvatsau ghṛtāsyau ca sitasūkṣmāmbarāvṛtau \|*  
*śuktikarṇāvikṣupādau śucimuktāphalekṣaṇau \|\| 7 \|\|*

*sitasūtraśirālau tau sitakambalakambalau \|*  
*tāmragaṇḍakapṛṣṭhau tau sitacāmararomakau \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8. The mouths of the images of the cow and the calf should be made of Clarified butter, and both should be covered with five silk cloths. Their ears should be made of mother-of-pearl and legs of sugarcane and the tendons, nerves, &e., of these images should be made of white threads, white blankets to represent their dewlaps, cheeks and backs should be made of copper, the white hair trimmed from a chamara (antelope hair) should represent the hair of the body.

## \|\| 82.9-10 \|\|

*vidrumabhrūyugopetau navanītastanāvubhau \|*  
*kṣaumapucchau kāṃsyadohāv indranīlakatārakau \|\| 9 \|\|*

*suvarṇaśṛṅgābharaṇau rājataiḥ khurasaṃyutau \|*  
*nānāphalasamāuktau ghrāṇagandhakaraṇḍakau \|*  
*ityevaṃ racayitvā tau dhūpadīpairathārcayet \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. The eyebrows should be made of corals, the udders of fresh butter, the tail of silk cloth, a vessel of bell metal should be placed to represent the milking vessel, the horns should be made of gold, the pupils of the eyes of sapphire, the hoofs of silver, the scented fruits in place of the nostrils. After thus making the images of the cow and the calf, the devotee should worship them with incense, lights, &c., with the following prayer:

## \|\| 82.11-15 \|\|

*yā lakṣmīḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ yā ca deveṣvavasthitā \|*  
*dhenurūpeṇa sā devī mama śāntiṃ prayacchatu \|\| 11 \|\|*

*dehasthā yā ca rudrāṇī śaṃkarasya sadā priyā \|*  
*dhenurūpeṇa sā devī mama pāpaṃ vyapohatu \|\| 12 \|\|*

*viṣṇorvakṣasi yā lakṣmīḥ svāhā yā ca vibhāvasoḥ \|*  
*candrārkaśakraśaktiryā dhenurūpāstu sā śriye \|\| 13 \|\|*

*caturmukhasya yā lakṣmīr yā lakṣmīrdhanadasya ca \|*  
*lakṣmīryā lokapālānāṃ sā dhenurvaradāstu me \|\| 14 \|\|*

*svadhā yā pitṛmukhyāṇāṃ svāhā yajñabhujāṃ ca yā \|*  
*sarvapāpaharā dhenus tasmācchāntiṃ prayaccha me \|\| 15 \|\|*

11-15. The Goddess, who is inherent in all beings, in the form of Lakshmi and who also resides among the Devas, let that Goddess, in the symbol of a cow, May confer peace upon me. The Goddess who is known as Rudrani, The favourite of the Lord Shiva, in whose form she resides, may that very same Goddess in the symbol of the cow, dispel all my sins. The Goddess, who reclines on the breast of Vishnu, as Lakshmi, who is present in the form of Svaha in the fire, and is called the power and the energy of the sun and the moon and Indra, the same Goddess, in the symbol of the cow may grant me wealth. She who is the Lakshmi (wealth) of Brahma, Kuvera, Lokapalas may grant me boons in the symbol of the cow. She who is Swadha, of the highest Pitris, is Svaha of the Devas, may she remove all my sons and bring me peace in the symbol of the cow.’

## \|\| 82.16 \|\|

*evamāmantrya tāṃ dhenuṃ brāhmaṇāya nivedayet \|*  
*vidhānametaddhenūnāṃ sarvāsām abhipaṭhyate \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. The Gudadhenu, thus invoked by the above prayer should be given away to the Brahmana. The same ritual is observed in giving away all sorts of cows.

## \|\| 82.17 \|\|

*yāstāḥ pāpavināśinyaḥ paṭhyante daśa dhenavaḥ \|*  
*tāsāṃ svarūpaṃ vakṣyāmi nāmāni ca narādhipa \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. O King! there are ten sorts of cows that are said to remove all sins, and I shall enumerate them to you.

## \|\| 82.18-19 \|\|

*prathamā guḍadhenuḥ syād ghṛtadhenus tathāparā \|*  
*tiladhenustṛtīyā tu caturthī jalasaṃjñitā \|\| 18 \|\|*

*kṣīradhenuśca vikhyātā madhudhenustathā parā \|*  
*saptamī śarkarādhenur dadhidhenustathāṣṭamī \|*  
*rasadhenuśca navamī daśamī syāt svarūpataḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

18-19. They are: — 1. Cow made of rary sugar (guda dhenu). 2. Cow made of clarified butter (ghyita dhenu). 3. Cow made of sesamum (Tila dhenu), 4. Cow made of water (ala dhenu), 5. Cow made of milk (Ksira dhenu), 6. Cow made of honey (Madhu dhenu) 7. Coy mate of sugar (Sarkara dhenu), 8. Cow made of curds (dadhi dhenu), 9. Cow made of syrup (Rasa dhenu) and 10. the real, that is, the living cow.

## \|\| 82.20 \|\|

*kumbhāḥ syurdravadhenūnām itarāsāṃ tu rāśayaḥ \|*  
*suvarṇadhenumapyatra kecidicchanti bhānavaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. The symbols of cows made of liquid should be placed in pitchers filled to the brim, and the symbols of the cow made of other substances should be arranged in a heap. In this matter of gift, some also like to make a symbol of the cow of gold.

## \|\| 82.21 \|\|

*navanītena ratnaiśca tathānye tu maharṣayaḥ \|*  
*etadevaṃvidhānaṃ syāt ta evopaskarāḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Some sages have also said that the symbol of the cow made of fresh butter and gems should be given away. The above-mentioned rituals should be observed in giving away all sorts of cows (described above).

## \|\| 82.22-23 \|\|

*mantrāvāhanasaṃyuktāḥ sadā parvaṇi parvaṇi \|*  
*yathāśraddhaṃ pradātavyā bhuktimuktiphalapradāḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*guḍadhenuprasaṅgena sarvāstāvanmayoditāḥ \|*  
*aśeṣayajñaphaladāḥ sarvāḥ pāpaharāḥ śubhāḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

22-23. The devotee should give away, with faith, these cows to attain prosperity and emancipation, on occasions of different festivals, accompanied with the invocation of mantras. I have already explained in connection with this guda dhenu gift, the gilt of other symbolical cows. These gifts are destroyers of all sins, the givers of the fruits of innumerable sacrifices, and are very auspicious.

## \|\| 82.24 \|\|

*vratānāmuttamaṃ yasmād viśokadvādaśīvratam \|*  
*tadaṅgatvena caivātra guḍadhenuḥ praśasyate \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Of all the ordinances the one of Ashokadvadashi is the best, and the gift of guda dhenu, as being an ingredient of that vrata, is, therefore, praised as the best.

## \|\| 82.25 \|\|

*ayane viṣuve puṇye vyatīpāte 'thavā punaḥ \|*  
*guḍadhenvādayo deyās tūparāgādiparvasu \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. It is most appropriate to give away the guda dhenu, &c., on the days of equinoxes, and solstices, on the occasion of au eclipse and Vyatipata (i.e., when the Sun and the Moon are in opposite Ayana and have the same declination, the sum of their longitude being equal to 180°.)

## \|\| 82.26-30 \|\|

*viśokadvādaśī caiṣā puṇyā pāpaharā śubhā \|*  
*yāmupoṣya naro yāti tadviṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padam \|\| 26 \|\|*

*iha loke ca saubhāgyam āurārogyameva ca \|*  
*vaiṣṇavaṃ puramāpnoti maraṇe ca smaranharim \|\| 27 \|\|*

*navārbudasahasrāṇi daśa cāṣṭau ca dharmavit \|*  
*na śokaduḥkhadaurgatyaṃ tasya saṃjāyate nṛpa \|\| 28 \|\|*

*nārī vā kurute yā tu viśokadvādaśīvratam \|*  
*nṛtyagītaparā nityaṃ sāpi tatphalamāpnuyāt \|\| 29 \|\|*

*tasmādagre harernityam anantaṃ gītavādanam \|*  
*kartavyaṃ bhūtikāmena bhaktyā tu parayā nṛpa \|\| 30 \|\|*

26-30. This Vishokadvadashi is most sacred and dispeller of all sins, and is auspicious. He who fasts on this Dvadashi goes to Vishnu’s highest seat.

He attains prosperity, longevity and health in this world, and, after death, he goes to the city of Vishnu, remembering him always at that critical moment. The virtuous devotee never gets grief ‘or pain for a period of mine arbuda and eighteen thousand years. A married woman, observing this Vishokadvadashi vrata, with music and dance, obtains also the same benefits. Consequently, one, full of faith, should always have music and songs in honor of Hari, on the occasion of this vrata, for, thereby, he gets prosperity.

## \|\| 82.31 \|\|

*iti paṭhati ya itthaṃ yaḥ śṛṇotīha samyaṅ madhumuranarakārer arcanaṃ yaśca paśyet \|*  
*matimāpa ca janānāṃ yo dadātīndraloke vasati sa vibudhaughaiḥ pūjyate kalpamekam \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. One who reads, listens to, or sees the worship of Lord Madhusudana or advises others to observe this ordinance, goes to the kingdom of Indra where he is venerated by the Devas for a period of one kalpa

## Chapter 83

## \|\| 83.1 \|\|

*nārada uvāca*  
*bhagavañchrotumicchāmi dānamāhātmyamuttamam \|*  
*yadakṣayaṃ pare loke devarṣigaṇapūjitam \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Narada said: — O Lord of the Universe! I wish to hear the benefits of that best of all gifts, that may be the giver of everlasting benefits in the next life and that may also be venerated by the Devas and Rishis.

## \|\| 83.2 \|\|

*umāpatiruvāca*  
*meroḥ pradānaṃ vakṣyāmi daśadhā munipuṃgava \|*  
*yatpradānānnaro lokān āpnoti surapūjitān \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Shiva said:--O Sage! I shall explain to you the ten ways of the gift or dana known as the Sumeruparvata gift, by virtue of which, the devotee attains the highest of the climes and is respected by the Devas

## \|\| 83.3 \|\|

*purāṇeṣu ca vedeṣu yajñeṣvāyataneṣu ca \|*  
*na tatphalamadhīteṣu kṛteṣviha yadaśnute \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. The blessings conferred by this form of charity cannot be attained otherwise, not even by the reading of, or listening to, the Puranas, Vedas, performing sacrifices and worshipping, or — erecting temples to the Devas

## \|\| 83.4-6 \|\|

*tasmādvidhānaṃ vakṣyāmi parvatānāmanukramāt \|*  
*prathamo dhānyaśailaḥ syād dvitīyo lavaṇācalaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*guḍācalastṛtīyastu caturtho hemaparvataḥ \|*  
*pañcamastilaśailaḥ syāt ṣaṣṭhaḥ kārpāsaparvataḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*saptamo ghṛtaśailaśca ratnaśailastathāṣṭamaḥ \|*  
*rājato navamastadvad daśamaḥ śarkarācalaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

4-6. Consequently, I shall relate to you the ways of this form of charity serially. 'The following ten hills should be made and given away, viz.: — 1. the hill of grain, 2. the hill of salt, 3. the hill of raw sugar, 4. the hill of gold, 5. the hill of sesamum, 6. the hill of cotton, 7. the hill of clarified butter, 8. the hill of jewels, 9. the hill of silver, 10. the hill of sugar.

## \|\| 83.7-9 \|\|

*vakṣye vidhānameteṣāṃ yathāvadanupūrvaśaḥ \|*  
*ayane viṣuve puṇye vyatīpāte dinakṣaye \|\| 7 \|\|*

*śuklapakṣe tṛtīyāyām uparāge śaśikṣaye \|*  
*vivāhotsavayajñeṣu dvādaśyāmatha vā punaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*śuklāyāṃ pañcadaśyāṃ vā puṇyarkṣe vā vidhānataḥ \|*  
*dhānyaśailādayo deyā yathāśāstraṃ vijānatā \|\| 9 \|\|*

7-9. Now I shall explain to you the ways of giving away the different hills enumerated above. The hills made of grain, salt, &c., should be given away on the following occasions: — on the day of the sacred equinoctial and solsticial sankrantis, at the time of Vyatipata, on the day of the conjunction of three tithis (tryahasparsha), on the third. day of the bright fortnight, on the occasion of an eclipse, on the amavasya day, on the occasion of the sacrificial rites connected with the marriage ceremonies, and other festivals, on the 12th day of the bright fortnight, on the full moon day, and on the day of the moon being in a sacred asterism.

## \|\| 83.10-12 \|\|

*tīrtheṣvāyatane vāpi goṣṭhe vā bhavanāṅgaṇe \|*  
*maṇḍapaṃ kārayedbhaktyā caturasramudaṅmukham \|*  
*prāgudakpravaṇaṃ tadvat prāṅmukhaṃ ca vidhānataḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*gomayenānuliptāyāṃ bhūmāvāstīrya vai kuśān \|*  
*tanmadhye parvataṃ kuryād viṣkambhaparvatānvitam \|\| 11 \|\|*

*dhānyadroṇasahasreṇa bhavedgiririhottamaḥ \|*  
*madhyamaḥ pañcaśatikaḥ kaniṣṭhaḥ syāt tribhiḥ śataiḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

10-12. A four-cornered (square) pandal should be erected with devotion, within a temple yard, in a sacred place, within the limits of a cattle-shed or in the devotee’s own Courtyard. It should face the north and be slightly slanting towards East and North, and the floor should be plastered with cowdung and covered with kusha grass, In the centre should be made the hill, surrounded by posts as props. (Four hills should be made in the corners, with Sumeru in the centre), The hill of (1,000 dronas or) 1,6000 seers of grain is the first best, of 8,000 seers of grain is the second best, and of 4,800 seers of grain the last best.

## \|\| 83.13-14 \|\|

*merurmahāvrīhimayastu madhye suvarṇavṛkṣatrayasaṃyutaḥ syāt \|*  
*pūrveṇa muktāphalavajraukto yāgyena gomedakapuṣparāgaiḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*paścācca gārutmatanīlaratnaiḥ saumyena vaidūryasarojarāgaiḥ \|*  
*śrīkhaṇḍakhaṇḍairabhitaḥ pravālair latānvitaḥ śuktiśilātalaḥ syāt \|\| 14 \|\|*

13-14. The Sumeru hill in the centre should be made of rice (vrihi), three “trees of gold should be in it. Pearls and ‘diamonds should be studded in ‘the: east side of the hill, cat’s eye and topaz in the south, emerald and sapphire in the west and lapislazuli and ruby in the north. Pieces of Sandal wood should be placed on all sides. So also a creeper of corals should surround it, and the surface and the bottom of the rock should he bedecked with oyster shells.

## \|\| 83.15 \|\|

*brahmātha viṣṇurbhagavānpurārir divākaro 'pyatra hiraṇmayaḥ syāt \|*  
*mūrdhanyavasthānamamatsareṇa kāryaṃ tvanekaiśca punardvijaughaiḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. The images of Brahma, Vishnu and Shiva as well as of the Sun should be made of gold by holy Brahmanas, and placed on the summit of the hill.

## \|\| 83.16 \|\|

*catvāri śṛṅgāṇi ca rājatāni nitambabhāgeṣvapi rājataḥ syāt \|*  
*tathekṣuvaṃśāvṛtakandarastu ghṛtodakaprasravaṇaiśca dikṣu \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. The four peaks should be made of silver, and silver should also be plaited at the bottom, Sugarcane should be put in place of bamboos, the caves should he made of butter, and the streams, of clarified butter.

## \|\| 83.17 \|\|

*śuklāmbarāṇyambudharāvalī syāt pūrveṇa pītāni ca dakṣiṇena \|*  
*vāsāṃsi paścādatha karburāṇi raktāni caivottarato ghanālī \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. The clouds surrounding this hill on four sides, should be made of cloths of four colors, viz., those on the east of white cloth, those on the south, of yellow, those on the west of pigeon-grey, and those’ on the north of red-colored cloths,

## \|\| 83.18 \|\|

*raupyānmahendrapramukhāṃs tathāṣṭau saṃsthāpya lokādhipatīnkrameṇa \|*  
*nānāphalālī ca samantataḥ syān manoramaṃ mālyavilepanaṃ ca \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Fruits of different kinds, fine garlands of flowers and sandal should be put on all the sides. Eight silver Lokapalas representing 1. Indra. E., 2. Agni S. E., 3. Yama S., 4. Surya S. W., 5. Varuna W., 6. Vayu, N. W., 7. Kuvera, N., and 8, Chandra N. F,, should be made and located in their ascribed places. The hill in this way should be decorated.

## \|\| 83.19-20 \|\|

*vitānakaṃ copari pañcavarṇam amlānapuṣpābharaṇaṃ sitaṃ ca \|*  
*itthaṃ niveśyāmaraśailamagryaṃ merostu viṣkambhagirīn krameṇa \|\| 19 \|\|*

*turīyabhāgeṇa caturdiśaṃ ca saṃsthāpayetpuṣpavilepanāḍhyān \|*  
*pūrveṇa mandaramanekaphalāvalībhir uktaṃ yavaiḥ kanakabhadrakadambacihnaiḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

19-20. The canopy should be made of five colours, and it should be garlanded with white unfading flowers. The Sumeru hill should thus be located in the centre, and its four spurs decorated with flowers, and sandal should be located in their proper places. Then the Mandarachala hill should be erected with barley in the east and adorned with the row of fruits and on the top, should be planted a tree of gold, representing the Madra Kadamba tree.

## \|\| 83.21 \|\|

*kāmena kāñcanamayena virājamānam ākārayetkusumavastravilepanāḍhyam \|*  
*kṣīrāruṇodasarasātha vanena caivaṃ raupyeṇa śaktighaṭitena virājamānam \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. That hill should be adorned with a golden image of Cupid, arrayed with beautiful dresses, garlands of flowers and sandal. There should be on one side of it a vessel, containing milk, representing the sea of milk and on the opposite side, another vessel, representing the sea called Arunodha. The forests of the hill should be represented by silver trees, according to the means of the devotee.

## \|\| 83.22 \|\|
