*yāmyena gandhamadanaśca niveśanīyo godhūmasaṃcayamayaḥ kaladhautauktaḥ \|*  
*haimena yajñapatinā ghṛtamānasena vastraiśca rājatavanena ca saṃyutaḥ syāt \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. On the south, the Gandhamadana hill should be made of wheat, putting some gold in it; on the top of which should be placed a golden image of Yajnapati and the Jake Manasarovara, of clarified butter and a garden of white cloth and silver should adorn it.

## \|\| 83.23 \|\|

*paścāt tilācalam anekasugandhipuṣpa-sauvarṇapippalahiraṇmayahaṃsauktam \|*  
*ākārayedrajatapuṣpavanena tadvad vastrānvitaṃ dadhisitodasaras tathāgre \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. On the west, the Hiranmaya hill of sesamum should be made and adorned with sweet flowers. Silver, fig tree and swan of gold, garden of silver-flowers, a pond of curds representing the Sitodha sarovara and clouds represented by white cloths, should also be made

## \|\| 83.24-26 \|\|

*saṃsthāpya taṃ vipulaśailamathottareṇa śailaṃ supārśvamapi māṣamayaṃ suvastram \|*  
*puṣpaiśca hemavaṭapādapaśekharaṃ tam ākārayet kanakadhenuvirājamānam \|\| 24 \|\|*

*mākṣīkabhadrasarasātha vanena tadvad raupyeṇa bhāsvaravatā ca utaṃ vidhāya \|*  
*homaścaturbhiratha vedapurāṇavidbhir dāntair anindyacaritākṛtibhirdvijendraiḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*pūrveṇa hastamitamatra vidhāya kuṇḍaṃ kāryastilairyavaghṛtena samitkuśaiśca \|*  
*rātrau ca jāgaramanuddhatagītatūryair āvāhanaṃ ca kathayāmi śiloccayānām \|\| 26 \|\|*

24-26. On the north, the Supardva hill, of urad pulse (Phaseolus radiatus) should be made. A golden vata tree and a cowof gold, should be placed on the top of the hill. A pond of honey, representing Bhadra sarovara, and a garden of silver trees, should also be made at the bottom of it.

The Brahmanas, versed in the Vedas and Puranas, and able to control their passions and of blameless character and sound bodies, should be made Hotas performing Homa. The sacrificial pond should measure one cubit square in size and east of Sumeru hill. Sacrificial offerings should be made of sesamum, barley, clarified butter, sacrificial fuel, and Kuga grass. The devotee should keep himself awake during the night and blow conches, etc., and sing. Now I shall describe to you the way of invoking the hills

## \|\| 83.27-30 \|\|

*tvaṃ sarvadevagaṇadhāmanidhe viruddham asmadgṛheṣvamaraparvata nāśayāśu \|*  
*kṣemaṃ vidhatsva kuru śāntimanuttamāṃ naḥ sampūjitaḥ paramabhaktimatā mayā hi \|\| 27 \|\|*

*tvameva bhagavānīśo brahmā viṣṇurdivākaraḥ \|*  
*mūrtāmūrtātparaṃ bījam ataḥ pāhi sanātana \|\| 28 \|\|*

*yasmāttvaṃ lokapālānāṃ viśvamūrteśca mandiram \|*  
*rudrādityavasūnāṃ ca tasmācchāntiṃ prayaccha me \|\| 29 \|\|*

*yasmādaśūnyamamarair nārībhiśca śivena ca \|*  
*tasmānmām uddharāśeṣa-duḥkhasaṃsārasāgarāt \|\| 30 \|\|*

27-30. In invoking the Sumeru hill, the devotee should say, ‘O hill! Thou art the best resort of all the Devas. O hill of immortals! destroy quickly all ill-luck in our houses and confer all prosperity on us as well as the highest peace. I have commenced worship with unalloyed devotion Thou art the adorable Shiva, Brahma, Vishnu, and the Sun. Thou art formless, with and beyond all forms. Thou art the seed of all, protect me, therefore, O Eternal One. Thou art the temple of the Lokapalas and of Vishvamurti, the Great Omni present, as well as of Rudra; the Adityas and Vasus, therefore give me peace. Since Thou art never: bereft of the Devas or Devis or by Shiva, therefore take me across the mundane ocean of sufferings in safety.

## \|\| 83.31-35 \|\|

*evamabhyarcya taṃ meruṃ mandaraṃ cābhipūjayet \|*  
*yasmāccaitrarathena tvaṃ bhadrāśvena ca varṣataḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

*śobhase mandara kṣipram atastuṣṭikaro bhava \|*  
*yasmāccūḍāmaṇirjambū-dvīpe tvaṃ gandhamādana \|\| 32 \|\|*

*gandharvavanaśobhāvān ataḥ kīrtirdṛḍhāstu me \|*  
*yasmāttvaṃ ketumālena vaibhrājena vanena ca \|\| 33 \|\|*

*hiraṇmayāśvatthaśirās tasmātpuṣṭirdhruvāstu me \|*  
*uttaraiḥ kurubhiryasmāt sāvitreṇa vanena ca \|\| 34 \|\|*

*supārśva rājase nityam ataḥ śrīrakṣayāstu me \|*  
*evamāmantrya tānsarvān prabhāte vimale punaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

31-35. After thus worshipping the Sumeru hill, the Mandarachala should also be, worshipped with the following words: — ‘O Mandarachala! Thou art embellished with the forest called. Chaitra-ratha, and the continent, called Bhadrashva, therefore, soon bring happiness unto me. O, Gandhamadana!

Thou art the crest jewel of the continent, Jambudvipa, and art adorned with Gandharvavana, therefore, grant me high renown. O, Hiranmaya hill, Thou art adorned by the Ketumala continent as well as by the garden called Vaibhraja. The golden fig tree is on your summit, let my power therefore be everlasting. O Suparshva hill, Thou standest majestic, beautified by- the ‘northern Kuru country and the Savitri forest, therefore, let my prosperity be inexhaustible.’ After thus invoking those hills, the devotee should bathe in the morning and give away the best central hill, to the guru (preceptor).

## \|\| 83.36 \|\|

*snātvātha gurave dadyān madhyamaṃ parvatottamam \|*  
*viṣkambhaparvatāndadyād ṛtvigbhyaḥ kramaśo mune \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. The four corner hills should be given away, in due order, to the four Ritvijas, and, O Narada! twenty-four or ten cows should also be given away.

## \|\| 83.37 \|\|

*gāśca dadyāccaturviṃśat yathavā daśa nārada \|*  
*nava sapta tathāṣṭau vā pañca dadyād aśaktimān \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Nine, eight, seven, five or even one milk cow should be given away to the preceptor (guru), according to the means of the devotee.

## \|\| 83.38-40 \|\|

*ekāpi gurave deyā kapilā ca payasvinī \|*  
*parvatānāmaśeṣāṇām eṣa eva vidhiḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

*ta eva pūjane mantrās ta evopaskarā matāḥ \|*  
*grahāṇāṃ lokapālānāṃ brahmādīnāṃ ca sarvadā \|\| 39 \|\|*

*svamantreṇaiva sarveṣu homaḥ śaileṣu paṭhyate \|*  
*upavāsī bhavennityam aśakte naktamiṣyate \|\| 40 \|\|*

38-40. This is the way of the worship of all the hills. The same mantras and materials. for worship should be employed in worshipping them all. The sacrificial offerings to the different asterisms, Lokapalas, Brahma and other Devas should also be offered by applying their respective mantras.

Diurnal fasts should be observed. “In case the devotee cannot do so, he may take his meals in thought. O Narada! Now listen to the Dana mantras of all hills serially.

## \|\| 83.41-42 \|\|

*vidhānaṃ sarvaśailānāṃ kramaśaḥ śṛṇu nārada \|*  
*dānakāle ca ye mantrāḥ parvateṣu ca yatphalam \|\| 41 \|\|*

*annaṃ brahma yataḥ proktam anne prāṇāḥ pratiṣṭhitāḥ \|*  
*annādbhavanti bhūtāni jagadannena vartate \|\| 42 \|\|*

41-42. Hear also the rituals of their being given away. “The (Anna) grain is Brahms and is known as the giver of life. ‘The grain nourishes the universe; consequently, it is Vishnu and Lakshmi. O, Supreme of all the hills! protect me in the form of a hill of grain.”

## \|\| 83.43-45 \|\|

*annameva tato lakṣmīr annameva janārdanaḥ \|*  
*dhānyaparvatarūpeṇa pāhi tasmānnagottama \|\| 43 \|\|*

*anena vidhinā yastu dadyāddhānyamayaṃ girim \|*  
*manvantaraśataṃ sāgraṃ devaloke mahīyate \|\| 44 \|\|*

*apsarogaṇagandharvair ākīrṇena virājatā \|*  
*vimānena divaḥ pṛṣṭham āyāti sma niṣevita \|*  
*dharmakṣaye rājarājyam āpnotīha na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

43-45. One who gives away the hill of grain in this way, resides in Devaloka during the reign of a hundred Manus, and traverses through the skies seated in an serial chariot in company of -the nymphs and the Gandharvas. On the exhaustion of his merit, he is re-born In the family of a great king.

## Chapter 84

## \|\| 84.1 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca*  
*athātaḥ sampravakṣyāmi lavaṇācalamuttamam \|*  
*yatpradānānnaro lokān āpnoti śivasaṃyutān \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Shiva said: — I am now going to tell you about the mount of salt, the donor of which goes to My region.

## \|\| 84.2 \|\|

*uttamaḥ ṣoḍaśadroṇaiḥ kartavyo lavaṇācalaḥ \|*  
*madhyamaḥ syāttadardhena caturbhiradhamaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. The first best mount of salt is of 256 seers (of the measure of 16 dronas), the next best is of 128 scers (eight dronas}, and the last is of 64 seers (i.e., 4 dronas)

## \|\| 84.3 \|\|

*vittahīno yathāśaktyā droṇādūrdhvaṃ tu kārayet \|*  
*caturthāṃśena viṣkambha-parvatānkārayetpṛthak \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. The poor may make. it of any weight rising from 16 seers (one drona) onwards. The four corner mounts (vishkambha) should be of the quarter measurement of this main mount.

## \|\| 84.4 \|\|

*vidhānaṃ pūrvavatkuryād brahmādīnāṃ ca sarvadā \|*  
*tadvaddhemamayānsarvāṃl lokapālānniveśayet \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. And Brahma, along with the other Devas. should be arranged in the same way as mentioned before, and the golden Lokapalas should also be so located.

## \|\| 84.5-6 \|\|

*sarāṃsi kāmadevādīṃs tadvadatrāpi kārayet \|*  
*kuryādjāgaraṇaṃ cāpi dānamantrānnibodhata \|\| 5 \|\|*

*saubhāgyasaraḥ sambhūto yato 'yaṃ lavaṇo rasaḥ \|*  
*taddānakartṛkatvena tvaṃ māṃ pāhi nagottama \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. The ponds and Kamadeva and others should be made as before. The devotee should keep up all the night. I now explain to you the mantra of giving it away. ‘O Salt! Thou hast been horn of the ocean of fortune, in consequence of which thou art styled as the best of all the flavours. Hence this gift of the mount of salt may protect me from the evils of this mundane world.

## \|\| 84.7 \|\|

*yasmādannarasāḥ sarve notkaṭā lavaṇaṃ vinā \|*  
*priyaṃ ca śivayornityaṃ tasmācchāntiṃ prayaccha me \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. ‘There is no flavour in anything without a pinch of salt. It is always dear to both Shiva and Shiva (Gauri). Hence, O Salt! give me peace.

## \|\| 84.8 \|\|

*viṣṇudehasamudbhūtaṃ yasmādārogyavardhanam \|*  
*tasmātparvatarūpeṇa pāhi saṃsārasāgarāt \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. ‘The salt that has sprung from the body of Vishnu is the giver of health. Therefore, O Salt in the shape of a mountain, carry me through the mundane ocean of troubles in peace.’

## \|\| 84.9 \|\|

*anena vidhinā yastu dadyāllavaṇaparvatam \|*  
*umāloke vasetkalpaṃ tato yāti parāṃ gatim \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. One who gives away the mount of salt in this way, attains bliss after passing a Kalpa in the realm of Shiva and Parvati.

## Chapter 85

## \|\| 85.1 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca*  
*ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi guḍaparvatamuttamam \|*  
*yatpradānānnaraḥ svargam āpnoti surapūjitam \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Shiva said: — I now relate to you about the gift of the mountain of molasses, the donor of which, honoured by the Devas, remains in heaven.

## \|\| 85.2 \|\|

*uttamo daśabhirbhārair madhyamaḥ pañcabhirmataḥ \|*  
*tribhirbhāraiḥ kaniṣṭhaḥ syāt tadardhenālpavittavān \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. The mount of 50 maunds (10 bharas) of molasses is the first best, of 25 maunds (5 bharas) the second best, and of 15 maunds (3 bharas) the last best. The poor may make it of 74 maunds even.

## \|\| 85.5-6 \|\|

*yathā deveṣu viśvātmā pravaro 'yaṃ janārdanaḥ \|*  
*sāmavedastu vedānāṃ mahādevastu yoginām \|\| 5 \|\|*

*praṇavaḥ sarvamantrāṇāṃ nārīṇāṃ pārvatī yathā \|*  
*tathā rasānāṃ pravaraḥ sadaivekṣuraso mataḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. The invocation, worship, the golden tree, the worship of the Devas, the four corner mounts (vishkambha), the ponds, the forest, the Devas, and the sacrifice, the keeping up of the night and the Lokapalas and the preliminary ceremonies, all these should be done according to the rituals connected with the mount of grain, and the following mantras should be ‘As Vishnu is supreme among the Devas, the Samaveda-among the Vedas, Lord Mahadeva among the yogis, the sacred Om among the mantras, the Goddess Parvati among the ladies; similarly, the sugarcane juice is superior to all.’

## \|\| 85.7 \|\|

*mama tasmātparāṃ lakṣmīṃ guḍaparvata dehi vai \|*  
*yasmātsaubhāgyadāyinyā bhrātā tvaṃ guḍaparvata \|*  
*nivāsaścāpi pārvatyās tasmācchāntiṃ prayaccha me \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Therefore, O mountain of molasses, give me unbounded wealth; you are the brother of the Goddess Parvati (the giver) of good luck, and the abode of Parvati; therefore grant me peace.’

## \|\| 85.8 \|\|

*anena vidhinā yastu dadyādguḍamayaṃ girim \|*  
*pūjyamānaḥ sa gandharvair gaurīloke mahīyate \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. One who gives away the mount of molasses in this way, goes to the region of Parvati and is honoured by the Gandharvas.

## \|\| 85.9 \|\|

*tataḥ kalpaśatānte tu saptadvīpādhipo bhavet \|*

The mount of 4,000 tolas (1,000 palas) of gold is the first best, of 2,000 tolas (500 palas) is the second best and of 1,000 tolas (250 palas) is the last. The poor may make, leaving pride aside, one of less weight, but greater than one pala, according to his means.

*dhānyaparvatavatsarvaṃ vidadhyānmunipuṃgava*

The rituals prescribed for the mount of grain should be observed. The four corner mounts (viskambha) should be given away to the sacrificing priests, as before, with the following words : “I salute you, О Mount of gold, you are the seed, the womb of Brahma, you are the giver of unbounded fruits. The gold is most sacred on account of its being born of Fire; therefore, О Nagottama! Protect me'.

## \|\| 86.6 \|\|

*anena vidhinā yastu dadyātkanakaparvatam*

One who gives away the mount of gold, according to these rites, goes to the blissful realm of Brahma where he resides for a period of one kalpa, after which he attains emancipation.

## \|\| 92.4 \|\|

*dhānyaparvatavatsarvam āsādyāmarasaṃyutam \|*

## \|\| 92.18 \|\|

*somasūryādayo yasya tejasā vigataprabhāḥ \|*  
*bhavanti śataśo yena śatravaścāparājitāḥ \|*  
*yathecchārūpadhārī ca manuṣyo 'pyaparājitaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. He eclipsed even the sun and the moon by his lustre, and he destroyed hundreds of enemies, and was ever victorious. In spite of his being a mortal, he had access to every region; and, roaming about hither and thither, he subjugated many of his foes.

## \|\| 92.19-20 \|\|

*tasya bhānumatī nāma bhāryā trailokyasundarī \|*  
*lakṣmīvad divyarūpeṇa nirjitāmarasundarī \|\| 19 \|\|*

*rājñastasyāgryamahiṣī prāṇebhyo 'pi garīyasī \|*  
*daśanārīsahasrāṇāṃ madhye śrīriva rājate \|\| 20 \|\|*

19-20. His queen, Bhanumati, was the most beautiful of all the ladies in the three regions. She was matchless, like the Goddess Lakshmi, and excelled all the beautiful ladies of her time. She was dearer than life to the king. She shone like Lakshmi, even in a group of 10,000 ladies.

## \|\| 92.21 \|\|

*nṛpakoṭisahasreṇa na kadācitsa mucyate \|*  
*kadācidāsthānagataḥ papraccha sa purodhasam \|*  
*vismayenāvṛto rājā vasiṣṭhamṛṣisattamam \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Thousands, aye, millions of Rajas, could not be compared to him, On one occasion, that remarkable sovereign, whilst seated on his throne, asked his Purohita, the sage Vasistha, with mind full of bewilderment.

## \|\| 92.22 \|\|

*rājovāca*  
*bhagavankena dharmeṇa mama lakṣmīranuttamā \|*  
*kasmācca vipulaṃ tejo maccharīre sadottamam \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. The King said: — O Sage! be pleased to tell me, on account of What good deeds in my past lives, I have become so illustrious and wealthy in my present life?

## \|\| 92.23 \|\|

*vasiṣṭha uvāca*  
*purā līlāvatī nāma veśyā śivaparāyaṇā \|*  
*tayā dattaścaturdaśyāṃ gurave lavaṇācalaḥ \|*  
*hemavṛkṣādibhiḥ sārdhaṃ yathāvadvidhipūrvakam \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Vasistha said: — Sometime in the past, there was a public woman, named Lilavati, who was devoted to Shiva. She gave to her preceptor (guru), a mount of salt, along with the trees of gold, &c., as prescribed in the rituals, on the fourteenth day of the bright fortnight.

## \|\| 92.24-25 \|\|

*śūdraḥ suvarṇakāraśca nāmnā śauṇḍo 'bhavattadā \|*  
*bhṛtyo līlāvatīgehe tena hemnā vinirmitāḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*taravaḥ suramukhyāśca śraddhāuktena pārthiva \|*  
*atirūpeṇa sampannā ghaṭayitvā vinā bhṛtim \|*  
*dharmakāryamiti jñātvā na gṛhṇāti kathaṃcana \|\| 25 \|\|*

24-25. In the house of Lilavati used to live a Shudra servant, named Saunda, goldsmith by profession, who was very clever. He had made beautiful golden trees and images of Devas, with faith, and with marked skill, and did not charge anything for his labour. He never charged any wages. He thought that these were all meant for religious purposes.

## \|\| 92.26 \|\|

*udjvālitāśca tatpatnyā sauvarṇāmarapādapāḥ \|*  
*līlāvatī gireḥ pārśve paricaryāṃ ca pārthiva \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. The wife of that goldsmith, O King! fixed those trees artistically on that mount, after polishing them well.

## \|\| 92.27-28 \|\|

*kṛtvā tābhyām aśāṭhyena guruśuśrūṣaṇādikam \|*  
*sā ca līlāvatī veśyā-kālena mahatāpi ca \|\| 27 \|\|*

*kāladharmamanuprāptā karmayogeṇa nārada \|*  
*sarvapāpavinirmuktā jagāma śivamandiram \|\| 28 \|\|*

27-28. Lilavati, along with those two, whilst worshipping the mount with faith, showed great devotion to their preceptor (guru). After a long time, Lilavati died, and by virtue of her charity, she was liberated from her sins and went to the kingdom of Shiva.

## \|\| 92.29 \|\|

*yo 'sau suvarṇakārastu daridro 'pyatisattvavān \|*  
*na maulyamādādveśyātaḥ sa bhavāniha sāmpratam \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. The poor, but high-minded, goldsmith, who was in the house of Lilavati) and who did not charge anything for manufacturing those trees of gold and images, has been born in your person.

## \|\| 92.30 \|\|

*saptadvīpapatirjātaḥ sūryāutasamaprabhaḥ \|*  
*yayā suvarṇakārasya taravo hemanirmitāḥ \|*  
*samyagudjvālitāḥ patnyā seyaṃ bhānumatī tava \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. By the same Virtue, you are so illustrious and have your sway over the seven continents. Your wife of the past life had polished up the trees and had fixed them up on the mount, in consequence of which she has now been born as your queen Bhanumati

## \|\| 92.31 \|\|

*udjvālanādudjvalarupamasyāḥ saṃjātamasminbhuvanādhipatyam \|*  
*yasmātkṛtaṃ tatparikarma rātrāv anuddhatābhyāṃ lavaṇācalasya \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. She is of matchless (polished) beauty, on account of her polishing those trees, and both of you had devotedly served in the gift of the mount of salt? consequently, you have obtained health, wealth and kingdom

## \|\| 92.32 \|\|

*tasmācca lokeṣvaparājitatvam ārogyasaubhāgyayutā ca lakṣmīḥ \|*  
*tasmāttvamapyatra vidhānapūrvaṃ dhānyācalādīndaśadhā kuruṣva \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. You should give away in your present life the ten kinds of hills according to the prescribed rites.” Acting on that advice of the sage Vasistha, the king performed the gift of ten hills beginning with Dhanyachala, and went to the realm of Vishnu,

## \|\| 92.33 \|\|

*tatheti satkṛtya sa dharmamūrtir vaco vasiṣṭhasya dadau ca sarvān \|*  
*dhānyācaladīñchataśo murārer lokaṃ jagāmāmarapūjyamānaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. One, who himself cannot perform, hut merely touches, hears or even advises others to give these gifts, is liberated from sins and goes to the region of Vishnu. So, also, one who is poor, but who, full of faith, sees this Puja performed by others.

## \|\| 92.34-35 \|\|

*paśyedapīmānadhano 'tibhaktyā spṛśenmanuṣyairapi dīyamānān \|*  
*śṛṇoti bhaktyātha matiṃ dadāti vikalmaṣaḥ so 'pi divaṃ prayāti \|\| 34 \|\|*

*duḥsvapnaṃ praśamamupaiti paṭhyamānaiḥ śailendrairbhavabhayabhedanairmanuṣyaiḥ \|*  
*yaḥ kuryātkimu munipuṃgaveha samyak śāntātmā sakalagirīndrasampradānam \|\| 35 \|\|*

34-35. By reading this, evil dreams do not come, and their effects are removed. One who gives the gifts with devotion, undoubtedly consumes all worldly fears.

## Chapter 93

## \|\| 93.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*vaiśampāyanam āsīnam apṛcchacchaunakaḥ purā \|*  
*sarvakāmāptaye nityaṃ kathaṃ śāntikapauṣṭikam \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Suta said: — In the days gone by, Shaunaka asked Vaishampayana, whowas seated at his leisure, to explain to him the ways of the acquirement of all desires by the performance of Shanti and Pushti rites.

**Комментарий:**

Note: — The past Karmas of a man tend to produce either some bad or some good results. These Karmik tendencies ire indicated by the aspects of the planets, at the time of one’s birth. The influences, which tend to the production of sorrow, are malignant, and those which tend to the production of happiness, are beneficial, The effects of Karmas being the results of actions performed in past lives, can naturally be modified by appropriate actions done in this life. Hence, the necessity of Shantika and Paushtika rites, Those which pacify or neutralize the malignant influences are called Shantika rites, and those which strengthen and augment the beneficent tendencies, are called Paushtika rites.

As karmas by themselves are Inert, but work through the agencies of the Lords of Karmas designated by the names of planets, hence the worship of the planets, or, their propitiation.

## \|\| 93.2 \|\|

*vaiśampāyana uvāca*  
*śrīkāmaḥ śāntikāmo vā grahayajñaṃ samārabhet \|*  
*vṛddhyāuḥ puṣṭikāmo vā tathaivābhicaranpunaḥ \|*  
*yena brahmanvidhānena tanme nigadataḥ śṛṇu \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Vaishampayana said: — I shall now relate to you, listen to it attentively what should be done by persons desirous of acquiring wealth, peace, longevity, and of freeing themselves from malignant influences and how the offerings to the planets should he made by a person desirous of Shanti and Pushti

## \|\| 93.3 \|\|

*sarvaśāstrāṇyanukramya saṃkṣipya granthavistaram \|*  
*grahaśāntiṃ pravakṣyāmi purāṇaśruticoditām \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. I shall explain to you, in brief, on the basis of all Shastras the ways of propitiating the planets.

## \|\| 93.4 \|\|

*puṇye 'hni viprakathite kṛtvā brāhmaṇavācanam \|*  
*grahāngrahādhidevāṃśca sthāpya homaṃ samārabhet \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. On an auspicious day as pointed out by almanacs and Brahmanas, and after inviting the Brahmanas, the different planets and their rulers should be located in their proper places, through a Brahmana, and homa sacrifice should be performed.

## \|\| 93.5-7 \|\|

*grahayajñastridhā proktaḥ purāṇaśrutikovidaiḥ \|*  
*prathamo 'yutahomaḥ syāl lakṣahomastataḥ param \|\| 5 \|\|*

*tṛtīyaḥ koṭihomastu sarvakāmaphalapradaḥ \|*  
*autenāhutīnāṃ ca navagrahamakhaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*tasya tāvadvidhiṃ vakṣye purāṇaśrutibhāṣitam \|*  
*gartasyottarapūrveṇa vitastidvayavistṛtām \|\| 7 \|\|*

5-7. The knowers of the Puranas and Shrutis have described the planetary offerings as being of three kinds, viz. — 1. of the thousand homas (fire oblations); 2. of a lakh or a hundred thousand homas; 3. of ten millions of homas, that fulfil all desires. Hear the ways of performing the homa with a thousand offerings, as told in the Puranas. This is called Navagraha yajna, or the sacrifice to the. Nine Planets. An altar, measuring two vitasti wide, within the sacrificial pond, should be made in the direction of north-east of the fire pit

## \|\| 93.8-9 \|\|

*vapradvayāvṛtāṃ vediṃ vitastyucchrāyasaṃmitām \|*  
*saṃsthāpanāya devānāṃ caturasrāmudaṅmukhām \|\| 8 \|\|*

*agnipraṇayanaṃ kṛtvā tasyāmāvāhayetsurān \|*  
*devatānāṃ tataḥ sthāpyā viṃśatirdvādaśādhikā \|\| 9 \|\|*

8-9. The vedi (altar) should be one vitasti in height and square, facing the north. It should have two buttresses on which the Devas should be located. Afterwards fire should be lighted in the fire pit and the thirtytwo Devas should be invoked in that fire.

## \|\| 93.10 \|\|

*sūryaḥ somastathā bhaumo budhajīvasitārkajāḥ \|*  
*rāhuḥ keturiti proktā grahā lokahitāvahāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. The following are the nine planets, viz.: — The Sun, the Moon, the Mars, the Mercury, the Jupiter, the Venus, the Saturn, the Rahu and the Ketu. They always bring good to all creatures (to call some of them malignant, is a mere mode of speech).

## \|\| 93.11-12 \|\|

*madhye tu bhāskaraṃ vidyāl lohitaṃ dakṣiṇena tu \|*  
*uttareṇa guruṃ vidyād budhaṃ pūrvottareṇa tu \|\| 11 \|\|*

*pūrveṇa bhārgavaṃ vidyāt somaṃ dakṣiṇapūrvake \|*  
*paścimena śaniṃ vidyād rāhuṃ paścimadakṣiṇe \|*  
*paścimottarataḥ ketuṃ sthāpayecchuklataṇḍulaiḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-12. (1) The Sun should be located in the centre, (2) the Mars in the south, (3) the Mercury in the north-east, (4) the Jupiter in the north, (5) the Venus in the east, (6) the Moon in the south-east, (7) the Saturn in the west, (8) the Rahu in the south-west and (9) the Ketu in north-west. All the planets should be drawn with uncooked rice powder,

## \|\| 93.14-16 \|\|

*brahmāṇaṃ ca gurorvidyāc chukrasyāpi śacīpatim \|*  
*śanaiścarasya tu yamaṃ rāhoḥ kālaṃ tathaiva ca \|\| 14 \|\|*

*ketorvai citraguptaṃ ca sarveṣāmadhidevatāḥ \|*  
*agnirāpaḥ kṣitirviṣṇur indra aindrī ca devatāḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*prajāpatiśca sarpāśca brahmā pratyadhidevatāḥ \|*  
*vināyakaṃ tathā durgāṃ vāurākāśameva ca \|*  
*āvāhayedvyāhṛtibhis tathaivāśvikumārakau \|\| 16 \|\|*

14-16. (10) Shiva is the Presiding Deity (adhidevata) of the Sun, (11) the Goddess Parvati of the Moon, (12) Skanda (Kartika) of the Mars, and (13) Hari of the Mercury, (14) Brahma of the Jupiter, (15) Indra of the Venus, (16) Yama (Dharmaraja) of the Saturn, (17) Kala of the Rahu, and (18) Chitragupta of the Ketu, (19) Agni, (20) Water, (21) Earth, (22) Vishnu, (23) Indra (24) Aindri (wife of Indra), (25; Prajapati, (26) Sarpa, (27) Brahma, (28) Ganesha, (29) Durga, (30) Vayu and (31) Akasha are the secondary presiding Deities (Pratyadhidevata). All these make up 31, to which number adding the Twin Ashvinikumaras, the group becomes of 32. All of them should be invoked in the sacrificial fire by Vyahritis

**Комментарий:**

Note: — Vyahriti moans utterance. A mystic word, viz., the Syllables, 'Bhuvah, Svah, Mahah, Janah, tapah, Satyam, and Om.

## \|\| 93.17 \|\|

*saṃsmaredraktamādityam aṅgārakasamanvitam \|*  
*somaśukrau tathā śveto budhajīvau ca piṅgalau \|*  
*mandarāhū tathā kṛṣṇau dhūmraṃ ketugaṇaṃ viduḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. The colours of these planets should be as follows: — The Sun should be drawn in rec, the Moon in white, the Mars in red, the Mercury and the Jupiter in yellow, the Venus in white, the Saturn and the Rahu in black and the Ketu in smoke colour.

## \|\| 93.18 \|\|

*grahavarṇāni deyāni vāsāṃsi kusumāni ca \|*  
*dhūpāmodo 'tra surabhir upariṣṭād vitānikam \|*  
*śobhanaṃ sthāpayetprājñaḥ phalapuṣpasamanvitam \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Their forms are of the same colour as indicated above. They should be dressed in the same colour of cloth and offered the same colour of flowers. Incense, highly fragrant, should be offered to them, and a nice canopy should be placed over the altar, which must be well decorated, by banging flowers and fruits.

## \|\| 93.19-20 \|\|

*guḍaudanaṃ raverdadyāt somāya ghṛtapāyasam \|*  
*aṅgārakāya saṃyāvaṃ budhāya kṣīraṣaṣṭike \|\| 19 \|\|*

*dadhyodanaṃ ca jīvāya śakrāya ca ghṛtaudanam \|*  
*śanaiścarāya kṛsarām ajāmāṃsaṃ ca rāhave \|*  
*citraudanaṃ ca ketubhyaḥ sarvabhakṣyairathārcayet \|\| 20 \|\|*

19-20. Rice, cooked i coarse sugar, should be offered to the Sun, clarified butter and rice cooked in milk and sugar to the Moon, mohanabhoga (pudding) to the Mara, milk and rice to the Mercury, rice and curds to the Jupiter, coarse sugar and rice to the Venus, rice, sesamum and pulses, cooked in milk to the Saturn, mutton to the Rahu, and coloured rice to the Ketu.

## \|\| 93.21-22 \|\|

*prāguttareṇa tasmācca dadhyakṣatavibhūṣitam \|*  
*cūtapallavasaṃchannaṃ phalavastraugānvitam \|\| 21 \|\|*

*pañcaratnasamāuktaṃ pañcabhaṅgasamanvitam \|*  
*sthāpayedavraṇaṃ kumbhaṃ varuṇaṃ tatra vinyaset \|\| 22 \|\|*

21-22. To the north-east of that altar, a lawless pitcher of water painted with rice and curds (five powders) and decorated with pancha-ratna (five gems), the leaves of the mango tree, fruit and cloth, should )e placed, and Varuna should be located on it.

## \|\| 93.23-25 \|\|

*gaṅgādyāḥ saritaḥ sarvāḥ samudrāṃśca sarāṃsi ca \|*  
*gajāśvarathyāvalmīka-saṃgamāddhradagokulāt \|\| 23 \|\|*

*mṛdamānīya viprendra sarvauṣadhijalānvitām \|*  
*snānārthaṃ vinyasettatra yajamānasya dharmavit \|\| 24 \|\|*

*sarve samudrāḥ saritaḥ sarāṃsi ca nadāstathā \|*  
*āyāntu yajamānasya duritakṣayakārakāḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

23-25. The earth of the elephant ward, stable, chariot-house, ant-hill, tank, cattle-shed should be mixed with water, along with the different herbs and Ganges water, and the devotee should bathe in it, after reciting the following mantras: ‘All the rivers, seas, tanks and rivulets, come to wipe out the sins of the devotee.’

## \|\| 93.26 \|\|

*evamāvāhayedetān amarānmunisattama \|*  
*homaṃ samārabhetsarpir yavavrīhitilādinā \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. O, sages! the Deities should be, similarly, invoked, and afterwards Homa offerings of clarified butter, barley, uncooked rice, and sesamum should be made to the fire.

## \|\| 93.27-28 \|\|

*arkaḥ palāśakhadirāv apāmārgo 'tha pippalaḥ \|*  
*audumbaraḥ śamī dūrvā kuśāśca samidhaḥ kramāt \|\| 27 \|\|*

*ekaikasyāṣṭakaśatam aṣṭaviṃśatireva vā \|*  
*hotavyā madhusarpirbhyāṃ dadhnā caiva samanvitāḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

27-28 The wood of Arka (Calotropis-gigantea), Palasha (Buteafrondosa), Khadira (Catechu), Apamarga (Achyranthes-spera), Ashwatha (the holy fig tree), Udambara (the fig tree), Sami (Prosopis spicigera), Kusha and Durva grasses are to be used for lighting the sacrificial fire. The Homa offerings, consisting of honey, ghee and curds of milk, should be made either 101 times or only 28 times to each planet.

## \|\| 93.29 \|\|

*prādeśamātrā aśiphā aśākhā apalāśinīḥ \|*  
*samidhaḥ kalpayetprājñaḥ sarvakarmasu sarvadā \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. The sacrificial twigs (of the plants named above), in all homas, should each. measure a span in length (pradesha), and should not contain roots, branches and leaves. Such a kind of fuel should be used by the wise in all sacrificial offerings.

**Комментарий:**

Note: — Pradeshamatra. A Span measured from the tip of the thumb to that of the forefinger.

## \|\| 93.30 \|\|

*devānāmapi sarveṣām upāṃśu paramārthavit \|*  
*svena svenaiva mantreṇa hotavyāḥ samidhaḥ pṛthak \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Particular kind of sacrificial fuel should be used for the particular Deity (named above), and offerings should be made, after uttering the particular mantras in low voice, with the name of the Deity for whom it is intended.

## \|\| 93.31 \|\|

*hotavyaṃ ca ghṛtābhyaktaṃ carubhakṣādikaṃ punaḥ \|*  
*mantrairdaśāhutīrhutvā homaṃ vyāhṛtibhistataḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. The sacrificial twigs should be soaked in- clarified butter and then thrown into the fire. Afterwards, the eatables, like charu, etc., should also be put into the fire, ‘Ten offerings should be made at first to one’s own particular mantra. The completion of the sacrifice should be performed by the vyahriti mantras.

## \|\| 93.32 \|\|

*udaṅmukhāḥ prāṅmukhā vā kuryurbrāhmaṇapuṃgavāḥ \|*  
*mantravantaśca kartavyāś caravaḥ pratidaivatam \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. The learned Brahmanas should be placed, either facing the North or the East, and the cooked rice, charu (pudding), should he placed in front of each Devata, with recitation of the proper mantras.

## \|\| 93.33-48 \|\|

*hutvā ca tāṃścarūnsamyak tato homaṃ samācaret \|*  
*ākṛṣṇeti ca sūryāya homaḥ kāryo dvijanmanā \|\| 33 \|\|*

*āpyāyasveti somāya mantreṇa juhuyātpunaḥ \|*  
*agnirmūrdhā divo mantra iti bhaumāya kīrtayet \|\| 34 \|\|*

*agne vivasvaduṣasa iti somasutāya vai \|*  
*bṛhaspate paridīyā ratheneti gurormataḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

*śukraṃ te anyaditi ca śukrasyāpi nigadyate \|*  
*śanaiścarāyeti punaḥ śaṃ no devīti homayet \|\| 36 \|\|*

*kayā naścitra ābhuvad iti rāhorudāhṛtaḥ \|*  
*ketuṃ kṛṇvann api brūyāt ketūnāmapi śāntaye \|\| 37 \|\|*

*ā vo rājeti rudrasya balihomaṃ samācaret \|*  
*āpo hi ṣṭhetyumāyāstu syoneti svāminastathā \|\| 38 \|\|*

*viṣṇoridaṃ viṣṇuriti tamīśeti svayambhuvaḥ \|*  
*indram iddevatāteti indrāya juhuyāttataḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

*tathā yamasya cāyaṃ gaur iti homaḥ prakīrtitaḥ \|*  
*kālasya brahma jajñānam iti mantraḥ praśasyate \|\| 40 \|\|*

*citraguptasya cājñātam iti mantravido viduḥ \|*  
*agniṃ dūtaṃ vṛṇīmaha iti vahnerudāhṛtaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

*ud uttamaṃ varuṇamity apāṃ mantraḥ prakīrtitaḥ \|*  
*bhūmeḥ pṛthivyantarikṣam iti vedeṣu paṭhyate \|\| 42 \|\|*

*sahasraśīrṣā puruṣa iti viṣṇorudāhṛtaḥ \|*  
*indrāyendo marutvata iti śakrasya śasyate \|\| 43 \|\|*

*uttānaparṇe subhage iti devyāḥ samācaret \|*  
*prajāpateḥ punarhomaḥ prajāpatiriti smṛtaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

*namo 'stu sarpebhya iti sarpāṇāṃ mantra ucyate \|*  
*eṣa brahmā ya ṛtvigbhya iti brahmaṇyudāhṛtaḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

*vināyakasya cānūnam iti mantro budhaiḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*jātavedase sunavāma durgāmantro 'yamucyate \|\| 46 \|\|*

*āditpratnasya retasa ākāśasya udāhṛtaḥ \|*  
*krāṇā śiśurmahīnāṃ ca vāyormantraḥ prakīrtitaḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

*eṣo uṣā apūrvyā ity aśvinormantra ucyate \|*  
*pūrṇāhutistu mūrdhānaṃ diva ityabhipātayet \|\| 48 \|\|*

33-48. Alter the Homa. of cooked rice (charu), the remaining offerings should be made with the twigs (samidhs), in honor of the planets, viz., offering (1) to the Sun should be made after reciting ‘ Akrisnai,’ etc., (2) to the Moon after reciting ‘Apyasva,’ (3) to the Mars after reciting ‘Agnirmardhadivah,’ (4) to the Mercury after reciting ‘ Agnevivasvadudase,’ (5) to the Jupiter after reciting ‘ Brihaspate paridtyarathena’, (6) to the Venus after reciting ‘Shukran te anyat, (7) to the Saturn after reciting ‘Sannodevirabhista,’ (8i to the Rahu after reciting ‘ Kayanaschitribhuvat’, (9) to the Ketu after reciting ‘ Ketunkrinvan,’ (19) to Rudra after reciting ‘ Avordja,’ (11) to Uma after reciting ‘ Apohista, (12) to Kartika after reciting ‘Syonaprithvi,’ (13) to Vishnu alter reciting “Idam Vishnu,’ (14) to Brahma after reciting ‘Tamisana,’ (15) Indra should be invoked by reciting ‘Indramiddevataya,’ (16) to Yama by reciting ‘Ayangau,’ (17) to Kala by reciting’ ‘Brahmajajnanam,’ offering should be made (18) to Chitragupta after reciting ‘Ajnatame,’ (19) to Fire after reciting ‘Agnimdutamvrinimahe.’ ‘Uduttamam Varunam’ is the mantra for (20) Varona, ‘Prithivyantariksam ’ for (21) the Karth, ‘SahasrasirsApurusa’ for (22) Vishnu. ‘Indrayendomarutrata’ for(23) Indra, ‘Uttanaparne subhage’ for (24) the Goddess (Indrani’, ‘Prajapati’ for (25) Prajapati, ‘Namostu Sarpebhyah’ for (26) Serpents, ‘ Esabrahmayaritvigbbyah ’ for (27) Brahm, ‘Anunam’ for (28) Vinayaka (Ganesha), ‘Jatavedasesunavama’ for (29) Durga, ‘Aditpratnasyaretasa’ for (30) the Akasha, ‘Kranashishur mahinancha’ for (31) the Vayu, ‘Egousa apurvy4’ for (32) the Twin Advintkuméras. Murdhanamdivah is the mantra for offering the last libation, called the Purnahuti, to complete the sacrifice.

## \|\| 93.49 \|\|

*athābhiṣekamantreṇa vādyamaṅgalagītakaiḥ \|*  
*pūrṇakumbhena tenaiva homānte prāgudaṅmukham \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Afterwards, the devotee, facing the east or the north, should get himself sprinkled with the water of the pitcher, by the prescribed mantras accompanied with music, blowing of conch and songs.

## \|\| 93.50 \|\|

*avyaṅgāvayavairbrahman hemasragdāmabhūṣitaiḥ \|*  
*yajamānasya kartavyaṃ caturbhiḥ snapanaṃ dvijaiḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Four Brahmanas, free from natural deformity and wearing garlands and golden ornaments, should bathe the devotee.

## \|\| 93.51 \|\|

*surāstvāmabhiṣiñcantu brahmaviṣṇumaheśvarāḥ \|*  
*vāsudevo jagannāthas tathā saṃkarṣaṇo vibhuḥ \|*  
*pradyumnaścāniruddhaśca bhavantu vijayāya te \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. At that time they should utter the following mantras: “Brahma, Vishnu, Mahesha, all the three Gods may sprinkle you with the holy waters, and may Vasudeva, Jaggannatha, Sankarshana, Pradyumna and Aniruddha lead you to victory.

## \|\| 93.52 \|\|

*ākhaṇḍalo 'gnirbhagavān yamo vai nirṛtistathā \|*  
*varuṇaḥ pavanaścaiva dhanādhyakṣastathā śivaḥ \|*  
*brahmaṇā sahitaḥ śeṣo dikpālāstvāmavantu te \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. “Indra, Agni, Yama, Nirriti, Varuna, Vayu, Kuvera, Shiva, Brahma, Sheshanaga and Dikpalas may protect you.

## \|\| 93.53 \|\|

*kīrtirlakṣmīrdhṛtirmedhā puṣṭiḥ śraddhā kriyā matiḥ \|*  
*buddhirladjā vapuḥ śāntis tuṣṭiḥ krāntiśca mātaraḥ \|*  
*etāstvāmabhiṣiñcantu dharmapatnyaḥ samāgatāḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. “Kirti, Lakshmi, Dhriti, Medha, Pushti, Shraddha, Kriya, Mati, Buddhi, Lajja, Vapu, Shanti, Tushti, Kanti, who are called the Mothers, and are Dharmapatnis may come and sprinkle you with holy waters

**Комментарий:**

Note. — Kirti, Renown; Lakshmi, wealth, Goddess of wealth: Dhriti, Firmneds, fortitude, satisfaction, joy; Medha, Power, Intellect; Lajja, Bashfulness, modesty, sereneness; Pushti, nourishment; Shraddha, Devotion; Kriyi Accomplishment; Mati, Sense; Baddhi, Talent; Vapu, Body: “anti, Peace; Tushti, Contentment: Kanti, Lustre.

## \|\| 93.54 \|\|

*ādityaścandramā bhaumo budho jīvaḥ sito 'rkajaḥ \|*  
*grahāstvāmabhiṣiñcantu rāhuḥ ketuśca tarpitāḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. The Sun, the Moon, the Mars, the Mercury, the Jupiter, the Venus, the Saturn, the Rahu and the Ketu may also sprinkle you with holy waters, after being satisfied

## \|\| 93.55-57 \|\|

*devadānavagandharvā yakṣarākṣasapannagāḥ \|*  
*ṛṣayo munayo gāvo devamātara eva ca \|\| 55 \|\|*

*devapatnyo drumā nāgā daityāścāpsarasāṃ gaṇāḥ \|*  
*astrāṇi sarvaśastrāṇi rājāno vāhanāni ca \|\| 56 \|\|*

*auṣadhāni ca ratnāni kālasyāvayavāśca ye \|*  
*saritaḥ sāgarāḥ śailās tīrthāni jaladā nadāḥ \|*  
*ete tvāmabhiṣiñcantu sarvakāmārthasiddhaye \|\| 57 \|\|*

55-57. The Devas, the Danavas, the Gandharvas, the Yakshas, the Rakshasas, the Serpents, the Seers and Sages, the Cows, the Divine Mothers, the trees, the nymphs, the Nagas, the Daityas, the weapons, the arms, the kings, the king’s vehicles, the herbs, the gems, the various parts of Time, the rivers, the oceans. the mountains, the sacred places, the clouds and the rivulets, may also sprinkle you with holy waters, for the fulfilment of all your desives.”

## \|\| 93.58 \|\|

*tataḥ śuklāmbaradharaḥ śuklagandhānulepanaḥ \|*  
*sarvauṣadhaiḥ sarvagandhaiḥ snāpito dvijapuṃgavaiḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. Afterwards, the devotee should get himself sprinkled by the Brahmanas, with the water mixed with different herbs and incense and then put on white clothes, and white sandal paste.

## \|\| 93.59 \|\|

*yajamānaḥ sapatnīka ṛtvijaḥ susamāhitān \|*  
*dakṣiṇābhiḥ prayatnena pūjayedgatavismayaḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. Then the devotee should fasten his garments with those of his wife and worship the priests with devotion, and offer them appropriate fees, with full faith

## \|\| 93.60-63 \|\|

*sūryāya kapilāṃ dhenuṃ śaṅkhaṃ dadyāttathendave \|*  
*raktaṃ dhuraṃdharaṃ dadyād bhaumāya ca kakudminam \|\| 60 \|\|*

*budhāya jātarūpaṃ tu gurave pītavāsasī \|*  
*śvetāśvaṃ daityagurave kṛṣṇāṃ gāmarkasūnave \|\| 61 \|\|*

*āyasaṃ rāhave dadyāt ketubhyaśchāgamuttamam \|*  
*suvarṇena samā kāryā yajamānena dakṣiṇā \|\| 62 \|\|*

*sarveṣāmathavā gāvo dātavyā hemabhūṣitāḥ \|*  
*suvarṇamathavā dadyād gururvā yena tuṣyati \|*  
*samantreṇaiva dātavyāḥ sarvāḥ sarvatra dakṣiṇāḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

60-63. A milk cow should be given away in the name of the Sun, a conch in the name of the Moon, a red ox in the name of the Mars, gold in the name of the Mercury, a pair of yellow garments in the name of the Jupiter, a white horse in the name of the Venus, a black cow in the name of the Saturn, iron in the name of the Rahu, goat in the name of the Ketu. The fee in each case must be a piece of gold, called suvarna (a golden coin), or cows adorned with gold, in the case of every one of these planets, or a suvarna coin in the case of each planet. If he cannot do that, then, he may give whatever may appeal to the fancy of the preceptor (guru). Everything should be given away, after reciting the prescribed mantras with fees, as noted below.

## \|\| 93.64-76 \|\|

*kapile sarvadevānāṃ pūjanīyāsi rohiṇī \|*  
*tīrthadevamayī yasmād ataḥ śāntiṃ prayaccha me \|\| 64 \|\|*

*puṇyastvaṃ śaṅkha puṇyānāṃ maṅgalānāṃ ca maṅgalam \|*  
*viṣṇunā vidhṛtaścāsi tataḥ śāntiṃ prayaccha me \|\| 65 \|\|*

*dharmastvaṃ vṛṣarūpeṇa jagadānandakāraka \|*  
*aṣṭamūrteradhiṣṭhānam ataḥ śāntiṃ prayaccha me \|\| 66 \|\|*

*hiraṇyagarbhagarbhastvaṃ hemabījaṃ vibhāvasoḥ \|*  
*anantapuṇyaphaladam ataḥ śāntiṃ prayaccha me \|\| 67 \|\|*

*pītavastraugaṃ yasmād vāsudevasya vallabham \|*  
*pradānāttasya me viṣṇo hy ataḥ śāntiṃ prayaccha me \|\| 68 \|\|*

*viṣṇustvamaśvarūpeṇa yasmādamṛtasambhavaḥ \|*  
*candrārkavāhano nityam ataḥ śāntiṃ prayaccha me \|\| 69 \|\|*

*yasmāttvaṃ pṛthivī sarvā dhenuḥ keśavasaṃnibhā \|*  
*sarvapāpaharā nityam ataḥ śāntiṃ prayaccha me \|\| 70 \|\|*

*yasmādāyāsakarmāṇi tavādhīnāni sarvadā \|*  
*lāṅgalādyāudhādīni tasmācchāntiṃ prayaccha me \|\| 71 \|\|*

*yasmāttvaṃ sarvayajñānām aṅgatvena vyavasthitaḥ \|*  
*yānaṃ vibhāvasornityam ataḥ śāntiṃ prayaccha me \|\| 72 \|\|*

*gavāmaṅgeṣu tiṣṭhanti bhuvanāni caturdaśa \|*  
*yasmāttasmācchriye me syād iha loke paratra ca \|\| 73 \|\|*

*yasmādaśūnyaṃ śayanaṃ keśavasya ca sarvadā \|*  
*śayyā mamāpyaśūnyāstu dattā janmani janmani \|\| 74 \|\|*

*yathā ratneṣu sarveṣu sarve devāḥ pratiṣṭhitāḥ \|*  
*tathā ratnāni yacchantu ratnadānena me surāḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

*yathā bhūmipradānasya kalāṃ nārhanti ṣoḍaśīm \|*  
*dānānyanyāni me śāntir bhūmidānādbhavatviha \|\| 76 \|\|*

64-76. “O Cow! Thou art worshipped by all the Devas, Thou art Rohini, Thou art the sacred pilgrimage, containing all the Devas, let there be Anti to me. O Conch! thou art sacred amongst all, thou art auspicious amongst all auspicious things; thou art held by the Lord Vishnu, therefore let there be anti to me. O, Ox! thou art the symbol of justice, source of the world’s happiness, the conveyance of the Lord Shiva possessing eight forms, therefore grant me shanti. O Gold! thou art the womb of the Golden Child (born of the golden egg of the Lord) and art also the seed of the Sun and the giver of everlasting rewards of good deeds, ‘therefore grant me shanti. Since yellow raimants are beloved to Thee, O Vasudeva (Krishna), hence, be pleased with me by their gifts, O Vishnu, and grant me shanti.

O Vishnu, Thou, in the form of the horse, rose out of the ocean of nectar, and Thou art the: eternal carrier of the Sun and the Moon, therefore, grant me shanti. Cow! Thou art the symbol of the Earth and Thou art the beloved of Keshava, destroyer of all sins, so grant me shanti. O Iron! since all difficult works are under thy control, thou helpest in the forging of the plough and arms, &c., therefore grant me shanti. O Gold, thou art an ingredient of all sacrifices, thou art the eternal vehicle of the sun, therefore grant me Shanti. O Cow! Fourteen regions are present in thy body, therefore give me wealth in this world, as well as happiness in the next.

As the bed of Vishnu is never devoid of Lakshmi, therefore, my bed may never remain unoccupied by my wife, by the virtue of my giving away this bed in charity. As there is always the presence of the Devas in all gems, so may the Devas grant me all jewels, by virtue of my giving away precious stones in charity. All the forms of charity do not come up to even 1/16th of the gift of land, therefore, let there be shanti to me by virtue of gift of this land”.

## \|\| 93.77 \|\|

*evaṃ sampūjayedbhaktyā vittaśāṭhyena varjitaḥ \|*  
*ratnakāñcanavastraughair dhūpamālyānulepanaiḥ \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. With devotion, devoid of miserliness. worship should be performed with jewels, gold, cloth, incense, flowers, and sandal.

## \|\| 93.78 \|\|

*anena vidhinā yastu grahapūjāṃ samācaret \|*  
*sarvānkāmānavāpnoti pretya svarge mahīyate \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. One who worships the planets in this way, attains all his wishes and goes to heaven after death

## \|\| 93.79 \|\|

*yastu pīḍākaro nityam alpavittasya vā grahaḥ \|*  
*taṃ ca yatnena sampūjya śeṣānapyarcayedbudhaḥ \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. The particular unlucky planet should be worshipped with great care, according to the prescribed full rites. Other planets should, then, be worshipped with abridged rites his is for a man of limited means; otherwise all planets should be worshipped with full rites.

## \|\| 93.80 \|\|

*grahā gāvo narendrāśca brāhmaṇāśca viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*pūjitāḥ pūjayantyete nirdahantyavamānitāḥ \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. she planets, cows, King and Brahmanas, especially, are worthy of being worshipped. Those, who worship them, are nourished by them, and those, who insult them, are destroyed.

## \|\| 93.81 \|\|

*yathā bāṇaprahārāṇāṃ kavacaṃ bhavati vāraṇam \|*  
*tadvaddaivopaghātānāṃ śāntirbhavati vāraṇam \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. As the armour shields the warrior from the blows of arrows, similarly, the propitiation ceremony (Anti) protects them, from the effects of the pad destiny.

## \|\| 93.82 \|\|

*tasmānna dakṣiṇāhīnaṃ kartavyaṃ bhūtimicchatā \|*  
*sampūrṇayā dakṣiṇayā yasmādeko 'pi tuṣyati \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. The person desirous of acquiring prosperity should not perform any, sacrifice without giving away the fees (Dakshina), since by the giving of handsome fees, even the Deva is propitiated.

## \|\| 93.83 \|\|

*sadaivāutahomo 'yaṃ navagrahamakhe sthitaḥ \|*  
*vivāhotsavayajñeṣu pratiṣṭhādiṣu karmasu \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. Homa sacrifice with ten thousand offerings is prescribed, in the ceremony of the propitiation of the Nine Planets. “The same number of Homa offerings should be made in connection with the nuptial, festive, yajna ceremonies as well as with the ceremonies of the installation of sacred images,

## \|\| 93.84 \|\|

*nirvighnārthaṃ muniśreṣṭha tathodvegādbhuteṣu ca \|*  
*kathito 'yutahomo 'yaṃ lakṣahomamataḥ śṛṇu \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. O Sage! the ways of performing the sacrifice of ten thousand offerings to ward off obstacles, &c., caused by one’s past karmas, as well as the dangers arising from evil spirits, have been described. Now I shall explain to you the ways of performing the Homa sacrifice of a hundred thousands of offerings.

## \|\| 93.85 \|\|

*sarvakāmāptaye yasmāl lakṣahomaṃ vidurbudhāḥ \|*  
*pitriṇāṃ vallabhaṃ sākṣād bhuktimuktiphalapradam \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. The learned have said that a sacrifice of a lakh of offerings should be performed for the fulfilment of all desires. It is very pleasing to the Pitris, and is the giver of prosperity and emancipation.

## \|\| 93.86-87 \|\|

*grahatārābalaṃ labdhvā kṛtvā brāhmaṇavācanam \|*  
*gṛhasyottarapūrveṇa maṇḍapaṃ kārayedbudhaḥ \|\| 86 \|\|*

*rudrāyatanabhūmau vā caturasramudaṅmukham \|*  
*daśahastamathāṣṭau vā hastānkuryādvidhānataḥ \|\| 87 \|\|*

86-87. The devotee should get the blessings invoked by Brahmanas, after selecting an auspicious day, according to the benign influences of planets and stars, and then make a pandal to the north-east of the house, or a square pandal, measuring 10 or 8 hands, should be made to the northeast of a temple of Shiva.

## \|\| 93.88-89 \|\|

*prāgudakplavanāṃ bhūmiṃ kārayedyatnato budhaḥ \|*  
*prāguttaraṃ samāsādya pradeśaṃ maṇḍapasya tu \|\| 88 \|\|*

*śobhanaṃ kārayetkuṇḍaṃ yathāvallakṣaṇānvitam \|*  
*caturasraṃ samantāttu yonivaktraṃ samekhalam \|\| 89 \|\|*

88-89. The altar should have a slant towards north-east, and it should be a made with great care. The same north-east corner of the pandal, should be selected for the purpose of digging the fire pit. This pit should be a square, beautiful and according to rules. The pit should have girdles round it and of the form of the mouth of a yoni.

## \|\| 93.90 \|\|

*caturaṅgulavistārā mekhalā tadvaducchritā \|*  
*prāgudakplavanā kāryā sarvataḥ samavasthitā \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. The girdle should he 4 fingers in breadth and of the same height, slanting from east to north. It should be even in other directions

## \|\| 93.91 \|\|

*śāntyarthaṃ sarvalokānāṃ navagrahamakhaḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*mānahīnādhikaṃ kuṇḍam anekabhayadaṃ bhavet \|*  
*yasmāttasmāt susampūrṇaṃ śāntikuṇḍaṃ vidhīyate \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. The sacrifice for the propitiation of the nine planets has been laid down for the peace of all. It is dangerous to make the sacrificial pond of more or less dimensions than prescribed. — Therefore, it should be made carefully, as described above.

## \|\| 93.92 \|\|

*asmāddaśaguṇaḥ prokto lakṣahomaḥ svayambhuvā \|*  
*āhutībhiḥ prayatnena dakṣiṇābhistathaiva ca \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. Brahma has said that the sacrificial pit in the ceremony of a hundred thousands of Homa, should be ten times the demensions given above. The dakshina to the priests should be ten times that given in the ordinary ten thousand homas.

## \|\| 93.93 \|\|

*dvihastavistṛtaṃ tadvac caturhastāyataṃ punaḥ \|*  
*lakṣahome bhavetkuṇḍaṃ yonivaktraṃ trimekhalam \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. To perform the sacrifice of a lakh of offerings, a sacrificial pond of 4 hands in length and 2 in breadth should be made. Its mouth should be made of the shape of a conical-triangle. Three ‘girdles should also be made to surround the pit.

## \|\| 93.94 \|\|

*tasya cottarapūrveṇa vitastitrayasaṃsthitam \|*  
*prāgudakplavanaṃ tacca caturasraṃ samantataḥ \|\| 94 \|\|*

94\. To the north-east of the pandal, after leaving a space of three vitastas, the sacrificial pond should be dug. On the land selected for it, a square altar slanting north-east should be erected.

## \|\| 93.95 \|\|

*viṣkambhārdhocchritaṃ proktaṃ sthaṇḍilaṃ viśvakarmaṇā \|*  
*saṃsthāpanāya devānāṃ vapratrayasamāvṛtam \|\| 95 \|\|*

95\. Vishvakarma has said that the buttress of the altar should be 14 Vitasti, that is, half of the above measurement, and should have three girdles, The Deities should be located on this buttress.

## \|\| 93.96 \|\|

*dvyaṅgulo hyucchrito vapraḥ prathamaḥ sa udāhṛtaḥ \|*  
*aṅgulocchrayasaṃyuktaṃ vapradvayamathopari \|\| 96 \|\|*

96\. The first girdles should be 2 fingers high and the remaining two should be only one finger high.

## \|\| 93.97 \|\|

*tryaṅgulasya ca vistāraḥ sarveṣāṃ kathyate budhaiḥ \|*  
*daśāṅgulocchritā bhittiḥ sthaṇḍile syāttathopari \|*  
*tasminnāvāhayeddevān pūrvavatpuṣpataṇḍulaiḥ \|\| 97 \|\|*

97\. The breadth of all the three girdles should be three fingers, and the wall round the altar should be ten fingers high. The Devas should be invoked on it, with flowers and uncooked rice.

## \|\| 93.98 \|\|

*ādityābhimukhāḥ sarvāḥ sādhipratyadhidevatāḥ \|*  
*sthāpanīyā muniśreṣṭha nottareṇa parāṅmukhāḥ \|\| 98 \|\|*

98\. O Sage! the presiding (Adhi-devatas) and the minor (Pratyadhi devatas) Deities should all face the east, and not the north or the west.

## \|\| 93.99 \|\|

*garutmānadhikastatra saṃpūjyaḥ śriyamicchatā \|*  
*sāmadhvaniśarīrastvaṃ vāhanaṃ parameṣṭhinaḥ \|*  
*viṣapāpaharo nityam ataḥ śāntiṃ prayaccha me \|\| 99 \|\|*

99\. Persons, desirous of acquiring wealth, should worship Garuda also, in addition, by reciting the following mantra: — ‘the chanting of the Samayeda, is Thy pody; Thou art the vehicle of Vishnu and the destroyer of poison and sins, therefore grant me shanti.’

## \|\| 93.100 \|\|

*pūrvavatkumbhamāmantrya tadvaddhomaṃ samācaret \|*  
*sahasrāṇāṃ śataṃ hutvā samitsaṃkhyādhikaṃ punaḥ \|*  
*ghṛtakumbhavasordhārāṃ pātayedanalopari \|\| 100 \|\|*

100\. In the former manner, the pitcher of water should be placed, and then the homa should be performed. The sacrifice of a lakh of offerings being finished, if there remain some more sacrificial fuels, then these should be thrown into the fire, with the pouring of ghee on the pitcher, in the form of a continuous stream as a Vasudhara.

## \|\| 93.101 \|\|

*audumbarīṃ tathārdrāṃ ca ṛjvīṃ koṭaravarjitām \|*  
*bāhumātrāṃ srucaṃ kṛtvā tataḥ stambhadvayopari \|*  
*ghṛtadhārāṃ tayā samyag agnerupari pātayet \|\| 101 \|\|*

101\. The sacrificial ladle should be made of the fig tree. It should be of fragh, sappy wood, and straight, and free from rot. It should be one hand in length. This ladle should be placed on two supports, and clarified butter should he poured through it in a continuous stream into the fire

## \|\| 93.102 \|\|

*śrāvayetsūktamāgneyaṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ raudramaindavam \|*  
*mahāvaiśvānaraṃ sāma jyeṣṭhasāma ca vācayet \|\| 102 \|\|*

102\. The hymns of the Agneya-sukta, Vaishnava-sukta, Raudra-sukta, Chandra-sukta, Mahavaisvanara sukta, Sama and Jyeshtha Sama should be recited, whilst so pouring.

## \|\| 93.104-105 \|\|

*kāmakrodhavihīnena ṛtvigbhyaḥ śāntacetasā \|*  
*navagrahamakhe viprāś catvāro vedavedinaḥ \|\| 104 \|\|*

*athavā ṛtvijau śāntau dvāveva śrutikovidau \|*  
*kāryāvautahome tu na prasajyeta vistare \|\| 105 \|\|*

104-105. The bathing of the devotee with the holy waters and the Svastivachana should be done as before, and the devotee should also give Dakshina The Dakshina to the sacrificial priests should be given free from anger and bias, and with a calm mind. There should be four Brahmanas, wall-versed in the Vedas, to officiate on the occasion of the sacrifice of the Nine Planets, or only two such Brahmanas, of peaceful disposition and versed in the Vedas, should be made officiating priests. This is in case of the sacrifice of ten thousand Homa offerings. The number of Brahmanas need not be greater than those mentioned above.

## \|\| 93.106 \|\|

*tadvacca daśa cāṣṭau ca lakṣahome tu ṛtvijaḥ \|*  
*kartavyāḥ śaktitastadvac catvāro vā vimatsaraḥ \|\| 106 \|\|*

106\. In the sacrifice of a lakh of offerings, there may be eight or ten priests, or even four, according to one’s means.

## \|\| 93.107-108 \|\|

*navagrahamakhātsarvaṃ lakṣahome daśottaram \|*  
*bhakṣyāndadyānmuniśreṣṭha bhūṣaṇānyapi śaktitaḥ \|\| 107 \|\|*

*śayanāni savastrāṇi haimāni kaṭakāni ca \|*  
*karṇāṅgulipavitrāṇi kaṇṭhasūtrāṇi śaktimān \|\| 108 \|\|*

107-108. The sacrificial material should be ten times more for the sacrifice of a lakh of offerings, than what it is in the sacrifice in connection with the worship of Nine Planets. Eatables, ornaments, bedsteads, necklaces, sacred threads, rings, etc., should be given away, according to the means of the devotee

## \|\| 93.109 \|\|

*na kuryāddakṣiṇāhīnaṃ vittaśāṭhyena mānavaḥ \|*  
*adadallobhato mohāt kulakṣayam avāpnute \|\| 109 \|\|*

109\. Dakshina should be given according to the means of the devotee. It should not be reduced through miserliness. If he does not give any dakshina, through avarice or delusion, his family becomes extinct.

## \|\| 93.110 \|\|

*annadānaṃ yathāśaktyā kartavyaṃ bhūtimicchatā \|*  
*annahīnaḥ kṛto yasmād durbhikṣaphalado bhavet \|\| 110 \|\|*

110\. The devotee, anxious for prosperity, should give away also grain in charity, according to his means, because the ceremony without the gift of grain brings famine on the sacrificer and his country

## \|\| 93.111 \|\|

*annahīno dahedrāṣṭraṃ mantrahīnastu ṛtvijaḥ \|*  
*yaṣṭāraṃ dakṣiṇāhīnaṃ nāsti yajñasamo ripuḥ \|\| 111 \|\|*

111\. There is no greater enemy of mankind than an ill-conducted sacrifice; for the priests, if not versed in the rituals, are destroyed, and the devotee is destroyed by not giving Dakshina, and the country is destroyed where food grain is not given in charity.

## \|\| 93.112 \|\|

*na vāpyalpadhanaḥ kuryāl lakṣahomaṃ naraḥ kvacit \|*  
*yasmātpīḍākaro nityaṃ yajñe bhavati vigrahaḥ \|\| 112 \|\|*

112\. A man in narrow circumstances should never perform a sacrifice of a lakh of offerings, for the spending of even a small fortune in that case leads to disease and distress.

## \|\| 93.113 \|\|

*tameva pūjayedbhaktyā dvau vā trīnvā yathāvidhi \|*  
*ekamapyarcayedbhaktyā brāhmaṇaṃ vedapāragam \|*  
*dakṣiṇābhiḥ prayatnena na bahūnalpavittavān \|\| 113 \|\|*

113\. The sacrificer, with devotion, according to prescribed rites, should engage even one, two, or three Brahmanas, and the man in straitened circumstances may employ only one Brahmana, well versed in the Vedas whom he should properly honor and give full Dakshina.

## \|\| 93.114 \|\|

*lakṣahomastu kartavyo yathāvittaṃ bhavedbahu \|*  
*yataḥ sarvānavāpnoti kurvankāmānvidhānataḥ \|\| 114 \|\|*

114\. The sacrifice of a lakh of offerings should be performed only by that man who possesses a large fortune; for the man performing such a sacrifice accurately, according to the prescribed rites, attains all his desires.

## \|\| 93.115 \|\|

*pūjyate śivaloke ca vasvādityamarudgaṇaiḥ \|*  
*yāvatkalpaśatānyaṣṭāv atha mokṣamavāpnuyāt \|\| 115 \|\|*

115\. The man who does so, is venerated by Vasu, Aditya, Marutgana, in the realm of Shiva, and attains emancipation after 800 kalpas.

## \|\| 93.116 \|\|

*sakāmo yastvimaṃ kuryāl lakṣahomaṃ yathāvidhi \|*  
*sa taṃ kāmamavāpnoti padamānantyam aśnute \|\| 116 \|\|*

116 The man who performs this. sacrifice of a lakh of homas, with any object in view, attains his desire and goes to heaven, where he gets bliss.

## \|\| 93.117 \|\|

*putrārthī labhate putrān dhanārthī labhate dhanam \|*  
*bhāryārthī śobhanāṃ bhāryāṃ kumārī ca śubhaṃ patim \|\| 117 \|\|*

117\. The man desirous of sons, obtains sons, one desirous of riches, gets riches, the devotee, eager for a wife, gets a beautiful wife, and if a maiden performs this sacrifice, she gets a good husband by virtue of it.

## \|\| 93.118 \|\|

*bhraṣṭarājyastathā rājyaṃ śrīkāmaḥ śriyamāpnuyāt \|*  
*yaṃ yaṃ prārthayate kāmaṃ sa vai bhavati puṣkalaḥ \|*  
*niṣkāmaḥ kurute yastu sa paraṃ brahma gacchati \|\| 118 \|\|*

118\. Further more, by the virtue of this sacrifice, a dethroned sovereign gets back his realm, the man hankering after prosperity gets prosperity, in fact, the devotee, desirous of anything, gets that thing. But the one, who performs it without any object in view, attains the Supreme Brahman.

## \|\| 93.119 \|\|

*asmācchataguṇaḥ proktaḥ koṭihomaḥ svayambhuvā \|*  
*āhutībhiḥ prayatnena dakṣiṇābhiḥ phalena ca \|\| 119 \|\|*

119\. Lord Brahma has described the sacrifice of ten millions of homas, a hundred times more efficacious than the sacrifice of a lakh of offerings.

The money given away in Dakshina, and the effect and the result are a hundred times more than the last.

## \|\| 93.120 \|\|

*pūrvavadgrahadevānām āvāhanavisarjane \|*  
*homamantrāsta evoktāḥ khāne dāne tathaiva ca \|*  
*kuṇḍamaṇḍapavedīnāṃ viśeṣo 'yaṃ nibodha me \|\| 120 \|\|*

120\. In performing this bigger sacrifice, invocation and dismissal of Devas should be done as before. The same mantras are to be used in ablutions, offering libations and giving charity. I shall now describe the special mode of preparing sacrificial pond, altar and pandal; pay attention to my words.

## \|\| 93.122-123 \|\|

*dvyaṅgulābhyucchritā kāryā prathamā mekhalā budhaiḥ \|*  
*tryaṅgulābhyucchritā tadvad dvitīyā parikīrtitā \|\| 122 \|\|*

*ucchrāyavistarābhyāṃ ca tṛtīyā caturaṅgulā \|*  
*dvyaṅgulaśceti vistāraḥ pūrvayoreva śasyate \|\| 123 \|\|*

122-123. In the sacrifice of a crore of offerings, the receptacle should measure four hands and should be made of a conical shape, on a square base, and surrounded by three girdles: while the pond should have two openings, A wise man should make the first girdle two fingers high, the second three fingers, and the height as well as the thickness of the third one, should be four fingers. The thickness of the first and the second girdles should also be two fingers

## \|\| 93.124 \|\|

*vitastimātrā yoniḥ syāt ṣaṭsaptāṅgulavistṛtā \|*  
*kūrmapṛṣṭhonnatā madhye pārśvayoścāṅgulocchritā \|\| 124 \|\|*

124\. The receptacle should be one vitasti (half a cubit, or 12 fingers) in extent, but the height should he of 6 or 7 fingers. It should be raised in ‘the centre as the back of a tortoise, and one finger high on the sides.

## \|\| 93.125 \|\|

*gajauṣṭhasadṛśī tadvad āyatā chidrasaṃyutā \|*  
*etatsarveṣu kuṇḍeṣu yonilakṣaṇamucyate \|\| 125 \|\|*

125\. It should resemble the lips of an elephant in extent and in having a hole. Such will be the receptacle as regards all kinds of sacrificial ponds.

## \|\| 93.126 \|\|

*mekhalopari sarvatra aśvatthadalasaṃnibham \|*  
*vedī ca koṭihome syād vitastīnāṃ catuṣṭayam \|\| 126 \|\|*

126\. Over the girdles everywhere, an altar of 4 vitasti in measurement (i.e. 2 cubits or 1 yard) and of the shape of a peepal leaf, should be made. This is in the case of the sacrifice of a crore of offerings

## \|\| 93.127 \|\|

*caturasrā samantācca tribhirvapraistu saṃyutā \|*  
*vaprapramāṇaṃ pūrvoktaṃ vedīnāṃ ca tathocchrayaḥ \|\| 127 \|\|*

127\. In this form of ‘Sacrifice the altar should be made square, measuring four vitasti: and having three girdles, Their height and extent should be as indicated before.

## \|\| 93.128 \|\|

*tathā ṣoḍaśahastaḥ syān maṇḍapaśca caturmukhaḥ \|*  
*pūrvadvāre ca saṃsthāpya bahvṛcaṃ vedapāragam \|\| 128 \|\|*

128\. The pandal should be made of sixteen cubits in extent and should have 4 doorways. On the eastern gate, a Brahmans, proficient in the Rigveda, should be located.

## \|\| 93.129 \|\|

*yajurvidaṃ tathā yāmye paścime sāmavedinam \|*  
*atharvavedinaṃ tadvad uttare sthāpayedbudhaḥ \|\| 129 \|\|*

129\. A Brahmana, versed in the Yajurveda, should be located in the south, one versed in the Samaveda in the west, one knowing the Atharva Veda in the north.

## \|\| 93.130 \|\|

*aṣṭau tu homakāḥ kāryā vedavedāṅgavedinaḥ \|*  
*evaṃ dvādaśa viprāḥ syur vastramālyānulepanaiḥ \|*  
*pūrvavatpūjayedbhaktyā vastrābharaṇabhūṣaṇaiḥ \|\| 130 \|\|*

130\. Eight more Brahmanas, well up in the Vedas and Vedangas, should be made to officiate as Homa-offering priests. These twelve Brahmanas should be sincerely honoured with cloths, sandal, garlands, and ornaments, as before.

## \|\| 93.131 \|\|

*rātrisūktaṃ ca raudraṃ ca pāvamānaṃ sumaṅgalam \|*  
*pūrvato bahvṛcaḥ śāntiṃ paṭhannāste hyudaṅmukhaḥ \|\| 131 \|\|*

131\. In the east, hymns from the Ratri-sukta, Raudra and Pavamana, and Sumangala mantras, for the peace of the universe, should be chanted by the Brahmana versed in the Rigveda and facing north.

## \|\| 93.132 \|\|

*śāktaṃ śākraṃ ca saumyaṃ ca kauṣmāṇḍaṃ śāntimeva ca \|*  
*pāṭhayeddakṣiṇadvāri yajurvedinamuttamam \|\| 132 \|\|*

132\. The Yajurvedi Brahmana, seated in the south, should recite the mantras relating to Shanti, God Indra, Saumya, Kushmanda, &c.

## \|\| 93.133-135 \|\|

*suparṇamatha vairājam āgneyaṃ rudrasaṃhitām \|*  
*jyeṣṭhamāsa tathā śāntiṃ chandogaḥ paścime japet \|\| 133 \|\|*

*śāntisūktaṃ ca sauraṃ ca tathā śākunakaṃ śubham \|*  
*pauṣṭikaṃ ca mahārājyam uttareṇāpyatharvavit \|\| 134 \|\|*

*pañcabhiḥ saptabhirvāpi homaḥ kāryo 'tra pūrvavat \|*  
*snāne dāne ca mantrāḥ syus ta eva munisattama \|\| 135 \|\|*

133-135. The Samavedi Brahmana, sitting in the west, should sing the hymns of Suparna Vairaja, Agneya, Rudrasamhita, Jyeshthasama, and peace chant.

The Atharvavedi Brahmana, seated in the north, should read the following mantras: — Shanti Shakta, Saura, Shakunaka, Paushtika, Maharaja.

Five or seven Brahmanas should perform the homa sacrifice as before, (the remaining Homakas helping them). “The mantras relating to hath and the gift are the same as before.

## \|\| 93.136 \|\|

*vasordhārāvidhānaṃ ca lakṣahome viśiṣyate \|*  
*anena vidhinā yastu koṭihomaṃ samācaret \|*  
*sarvānkāmānavāpnoti tato viṣṇupadaṃ vrajet \|\| 136 \|\|*

136\. The Vasudhara or the way of letting the stream of clarified butter fall in the fire from a vase is the only peculiar rite of the sacrifice of a lakh of offerings (as mentioned before. That should be done here also).

One who performs this sacrifice of a crore of offerings, according to the prescribed rites, attains all his wishes and obtains the rank of Vishnu

## \|\| 93.137 \|\|

*yaḥ paṭhecchṛṇuyādvāpi grahayajñatrayaṃ naraḥ \|*  
*sarvapāpaviśuddhātmā padamindrasya gacchati \|\| 137 \|\|*

137\. He who reads or hears this description of these three sacrifices of the Grahas (Planets), becomes purified of all sins and attains the rank of Indra.

## \|\| 93.138 \|\|

*aśvamedhasahasrāṇi daśa cāṣṭau ca dharmavit \|*  
*kṛtvā yatphalamāpnoti kauṭihomāt tadaśnute \|\| 138 \|\|*

138\. The benefits of this sacrifice are similar to those derived by the performance of 18,000 Ashvamedha sacrifices.

## \|\| 93.139 \|\|

*brahmahatyāsahasrāṇi bhrūṇahatyārbudāni ca \|*  
*koṭihomena naṣyanti yathāvacchivabhāṣitam \|\| 139 \|\|*

139\. Shiva has said that the sin of killing a crore of. Brahmanas and of making 10 crores of abortions, is washed off by the performance of this sacrifice

## \|\| 93.140 \|\|

*vaṣyakarmābhicārādi tathaivoccāṭanādikam \|*  
*navagrahamakhaṃ kṛtvā tataḥ kāmyaṃ samācaret \|\| 140 \|\|*

140\. The sacrifice relating to the worship of the nine planets should be performed’ before the performance of the. rites of Abhichara (sorcery), Uchchatana and Vashya Karma, &c.

**Комментарий:**

Note. - Uchchatana = A magical incantation that causes a man to go away out of disgust. Vashya Karma = A magical spell that fascinates and subdues a foe.

## \|\| 93.141 \|\|

*anyathā phaladaṃ puṃsāṃ na kāmyaṃ jāyate kvacit \|*  
*tasmādautahomasya vidhānaṃ pūrvamācaret \|\| 141 \|\|*

141\. Otherwise, no rite has the desired effect; so this sacrifice of ten thousand offerings to the planets should necessarily be performed , as a preliminary.

## \|\| 93.142-143 \|\|

*vṛttaṃ voccāṭane kuṇḍaṃ tathā ca vaṣyakarmaṇi \|*  
*trimekhalaṃ caikavaktram aratnirvistareṇa tu \|\| 142 \|\|*

*palāśasamidhaḥ śastā madhugorocanānvitāḥ \|*  
*candanāguruṇā tadvat kuṅkumenābhiṣiñcitāḥ \|\| 143 \|\|*

142-143. In the sacrifice connected with Vashikarana and Uchchatana, the sacrificial pond should be made of the measure of a handful (ell); it should be surrounded with three girdles, be circular in shape, and have one Tae and the offering of the wood of Butea frondosa, sprinkled with honey, camphor, gorochana and agara, dissolved in water, mixed with saffron, should be made.

## \|\| 93.144 \|\|

*homayenmadhusarpirbhyāṃ bilvāni kamalāni ca \|*  
*sahasrāṇi daśaivoktaṃ sarvadaiva svayambhuvā \|\| 144 \|\|*

144\. An offering of wood-apple (Bael) and lotuses, mixed with honey and clarified butter, should be made. Brahma has said that ten thousand offerings should be made in such sacrifices.

## \|\| 93.145 \|\|

*vaṣyakarmaṇi bilvānāṃ padmānāṃ caiva dharmavit \|*  
*sumitriyā na āpa oṣadhaya iti homayet \|\| 145 \|\|*

145\. In a sacrifice for Vashikarana, the offerings of wood-apple (Bael) and lotuses should be made, and the Sumitriyana Apa oshadha mantra should be recited in offering Homa.

## \|\| 93.146-147 \|\|

*na cātra sthāpanaṃ kāryaṃ na ca kumbhābhiṣecanam \|*  
*snānaṃ sarvauṣadhaiḥ kṛtvā śuklapuṣpāmbaro gṛhī \|\| 146 \|\|*

*kaṇṭhasūtraiḥ sakanakair viprān samabhipūjayet \|*  
*sūkṣmavastrāṇi deyāni śuklā gāvaḥ sakāñcanāḥ \|\| 147 \|\|*

146-147. No sprinkling with holy waters or location of a pitcher of water should be made it these forms of sacrifices. A householder should bathe in the water mixed with herbs, dress in white, put on white flowers, worship the Brahmanas with gold threads. They should also be given fine costumes and Dakshina of gold. A white cow should also be given

## \|\| 93.148 \|\|

*avaśyāni vaśī kuryāt sarvaśatrubalānyapi \|*  
*amitrāṇyapi mitrāṇi homo 'yaṃ pāpanāśanaḥ \|\| 148 \|\|*

148\. This sacrifice subdues the worst of enemies, endears those who have no love, and dispels ills.

## \|\| 93.149 \|\|

*vidveṣaṇe 'bhicāre ca trikoṇaṃ kuṇḍamiṣyate \|*  
*dvimekhalaṃ koṇamukhaṃ hastamātraṃ ca sarvaśaḥ \|\| 149 \|\|*

149\. The sacrificial pond for the performance of the sacrifice intended for Abhichara and Vidveshana, should be triangular in shape, measuring one hand, surrounded by two girdles, and having openings towards the vertices.

**Комментарий:**

Note — Vidveshana = A spell that causes friction.

## \|\| 93.150 \|\|

*homaṃ kuryustato viprā raktamālyānulepanāḥ \|*  
*nivītalohitoṣṇīṣā lohitāmbaradhāriṇaḥ \|\| 150 \|\|*

150\. Then the Brahmanas wearing red garland, red sandal, red sacred thread, red turban, and red raiment’s, should perform the sacrifice.

## \|\| 93.151 \|\|

*navavāyasaraktāḍhya-pātratrayasamanvitāḥ \|*  
*samidho vāmahastena śyenāsthibalasaṃyutāḥ \|*  
*hotavyā muktakeśaistu dhyāyadbhiraśivaṃ ripau \|\| 151 \|\|*

151\. With three vessels containing the blood of the young crows before them, bones of the hawks in their left hand and sacrificial fuel in the other, and their hair loose, the Brahmanas should perform the sacrifice, all the while’ thinking ill of the enemies at the time of making these offerings.

## \|\| 93.152-153 \|\|

*durmitriyās tasmai santu tathā huṃphaḍitīti ca \|*  
*śyenābhicāramantreṇa kṣuraṃ samabhimantrya ca \|\| 152 \|\|*

*pratirūpaṃ ripoḥ kṛtvā kṣureṇa parikartayet \|*  
*ripurūpasya śakalān yathaivāgnau viniṣkṣipet \|\| 153 \|\|*

152-153. With the shyenamantra, ‘durmitriydstasmai santu hum phata,’ the razor should be sanctified; with this the image of the enemy should be cut piecemeal and offered to the fire.

## \|\| 93.154 \|\|

*grahayajñavidhānānte sadaivābhicaranpunaḥ \|*  
*vidveṣaṇaṃ tathā kurvan netadeva samācaret \|\| 154 \|\|*

154\. Having performed the sacrifice of the Grahas, the proper “Avichara” sacrifice should be performed. Such is the rule for “Vidveshana” sacrifice as well.

## \|\| 93.155 \|\|

*ihaiva phaladaṃ puṃsām etannāmutra śobhanam \|*  
*tasmācchāntikamevātra kartavyaṃ bhūtimicchatā \|\| 155 \|\|*

155\. Such deeds only bear fruit in the present life and do not beget good results in the next, so a man, desirous of ultimate good, should not indulge in such deeds.

## \|\| 93.156 \|\|

*grahayajñatrayaṃ kuryād yas tvakāmyena mānavaḥ \|*  
*sa viṣṇoḥ padamāpnoti punarāvṛttidurlabham \|\| 156 \|\|*

156\. One who performs the worship of the stairs, along with the prescribed sacrifices, without any object in view, goes to the clime of Vishnu, whence he never returns to this world.

## \|\| 93.157 \|\|

*ya idaṃ śṛṇuyānnityaṃ śrāvayedvāpi mānavaḥ \|*  
*na tasya grahapīḍā syān na ca bandhujanakṣayaḥ \|\| 157 \|\|*

157\. One who hears or relates this to others, never suffers from any pain, owing to the evil influence of the planets or to the destruction of friends

## \|\| 93.158 \|\|

*grahayajñatrayaṃ gehe likhitaṃ yatra tiṣṭhati \|*  
*na pīḍā tatra bālānāṃ na rogo na ca bandhanam \|\| 158 \|\|*

158\. The children of the house in which these sacrifices are written down, never suffer from any ill, mental or physical, or any other calamity.

## \|\| 93.159-160 \|\|

*aśeṣayajñaphaladaṃ niḥśeṣāghavināśanam \|*  
*koṭihomaṃ viduḥ prājñā bhuktimuktiphalapradam \|\| 159 \|\|*

*aśvamedhaphalaṃ prāhur lakṣahomaṃ surottamāḥ \|*  
*dvādaśāhamakhas tadvan navagrahamakhaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 160 \|\|*

159-160. The sages are of opinion that this sacrifice of a crore of offerings begets fruits of many a sacrifice and dispels all ills; it is the giver of worldly prosperity and final emancipation. The sacrifice of a lakh of offerings gives the benefit of the ashvamedha sacrifice. The sacrifice performed in course of a twelve days and the sacrifice connected with the worship of stars, give equal benefits.

## \|\| 93.161 \|\|

*iti kathitamidānīmutsavānandahetoḥ sakalakaluṣahārī devayajñābhiṣekaḥ \|*  
*paripaṭhati ya itthaṃ yaḥ śṛṇoti prasaṅgād abhibhavati sa śatrūnāurārogyayuktaḥ \|\| 161 \|\|*

161\. Thus I have told the mode of the sacrifices of the Nine Grahas and the Abhiseka in divine sacrifices (the sprinkling of the devotee with the holy waters.) These are to be done to dispel all ills and hindrances to ceremonies of rejoicings. These purge all sins. One who reads or listens to it subdues all his foes and gets longevity and health

## Chapter 94

## \|\| 94.1 \|\|

*śiva uvāca*  
*padmāsanaḥ padmakaraḥ padmagarbhasamadyutiḥ \|*  
*saptāśvaḥ saptaradjuśca dvibhujaḥ syātsadā raviḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Shiva said: — The image of the God Sun who causes the lotus so bud should be made as seated on a lotus (Padmasana), with color like that of a lotus, with two hands, with a lotus in one hand and the other hand raised in the posture Of giving blessings, and having seven horses in His chariot, drawn by seven reins.

**Комментарий:**

Note. Padmasana = A lotus-seat. An epithet of Sun. A particular posture in religious meditation, (See Sacred Books of the Hindus, Vol. XV. — The Yoga Sutra.)

## \|\| 94.2 \|\|

*śvetaḥ śvetāmbaradharaḥ śvetāśvaḥ śvetavāhanaḥ \|*  
*gadāpāṇirdvibāhuśca kartavyo varadaḥ śaśī \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. The image of the Moon, the giver of boons, should be made in white color, dressed in white robes, seated on a white chariot, having a white horse for His conveyance, having two hands, one holding a club and the other raised, in the posture of giving blessings.

## \|\| 94.3 \|\|

*raktamālyāmbaradharaḥ śaktiśūlagadādharaḥ \|*  
*caturbhujaḥ śvetaromā varadaḥ syād dharāsutaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. The image of the Mars should be made, having white hair, four hands, armed with a spear, a lance and club, with the fourth hand raised in the posture of giving blessings, wearing red robes and garland.

## \|\| 94.4 \|\|

*pītamālyāmbaradharaḥ karṇikārasamadyutiḥ \|*  
*khaḍgacarmagadāpāṇiḥ siṃhastho varado budhaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. The image of the Mercury should be made yellow, dressed in yellow robes and wearing a yellow garland, with four hands armed with a sword, shield and club, and the fourth hand raised in the posture of giving blessings, and having a lion for his conveyance.

## \|\| 94.5 \|\|

*devadaityagurū tadvat pītaśvetau caturbhujau \|*  
*daṇḍinau varadau kāryau sākṣasūtrakamaṇḍalū \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. The Venus and the Jupiter should be made in white and yellow respectively. They should have four hands, holding staff, rosary, and kamandala, and the fourth hand raised in the posture of giving blessings.

## \|\| 94.6 \|\|

*indranīladyutiḥ śūlī varado gṛdhravāhanaḥ \|*  
*bāṇabāṇāsanadharaḥ kartavyo 'rkasutas tathā \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. The Saturn should be of the colour and the lustre of an emerald, having a vulture for His conveyance and four hands armed with a lance, bow and arrow, and the fourth hand raised in the posture of giving blessings.

## \|\| 94.7-8 \|\|

*karālavadanaḥ khaḍga-carmaśūlī varapradaḥ \|*  
*nīlasiṃhāsanasthaśca rāhuratra praśasyate \|\| 7 \|\|*

*dhūmrā dvibāhavaḥ sarve gadino vikṛtānanāḥ \|*  
*gṛdhrāsanagatā nityaṃ ketavaḥ syurvarapradāḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8. The image of Rahu should be made, having # terrible mouth or appearance, seated on a blue-colored lion, having four hands, armed with a sword, a leather ‘shield, a spear, and the fourth hand raised in the posture of giving blessings. The image of Ketu should be made of smoky color, with a vulture for His conveyance and having two hands one hand holding a mace and the other raised in the posture of giving Blessings, and having a distorted face.

## \|\| 94.9 \|\|

*sarve kirīṭinaḥ kāryā grahā lokahitāvahāḥ \|*  
*svāṅgulenocchritāḥ sarve śatamaṣṭottaraṃ sadā \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. All the planets should he made with a crown on their head, and the images should be two fingers high (or, of the height of one’s own finger).

The mantras relating ‘to the planets should be recited on the rosary 108 times each. (It may also mean that the size of the planets should be 108 fingers or digits in height. If the anguli be one, inch in length, the images will be nine feet high; if the measure of the anguli be 3/4th of an inoh, then the height will be 6¾ feet. The sense is obscure)

## Chapter 95

## \|\| 95.1 \|\|

*nārada uvāca*  
*bhagavanbhūtabhavyeśa tathānyadapi yacchrutam \|*  
*bhuktimuktiphalāyālaṃ tatpunar vaktumarhasi \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Narada said: — O Lord, presiding over the Past and the Future! pray tell me about some other ordinance that may be the giver of happiness and emancipation.

## \|\| 95.2-3 \|\|

*evamukto 'bravīcchambhur ayaṃ vāṅmayapāragaḥ \|*  
*matsamastapasā brahman purāṇaśrutivistaraiḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*dharmo 'yaṃ vṛṣarūpeṇa nandī nāma gaṇādhipaḥ \|*  
*dharmānmāheśvarān vakṣyat yataḥprabhṛti nārada \|\| 3 \|\|*

2-3. Hearing the above words of the sage, Lord Shiva, the knower of all things, understood the inclination of Narada, and said: “ Narada! this sacred bull, who is my principal attendant and who has become unified with me on account of his asceticiszm and knowledge of the Shruti and the Puranas, will explain to you the rituals connected with my ordinance (Maheshvara Dharma)”.

## \|\| 95.4 \|\|

*matsya uvāca*  
*ityuktvā devadeveśas tatraivāntaradhīyata \|*  
*nārado 'pi hi śuśrūṣur apṛcchannandikeśvaram \|*  
*ādiṣṭastvaṃ śiveneha vada māheśvaraṃ vratam \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Lord Matsya said: — Having said so, that Lord of the God of gods, vanished then and there, Narada also, being anxious to hear, asked Nandikeshvara thus: — O Nandikeshvara, thou hast been ordered by Shiva, therefore, tell me the Maheshvara vrata,

## \|\| 95.5 \|\|

*nandikeśvara uvāca*  
*śṛṇuṣvāvahito brahman vakṣye māheśvaraṃ vratam \|*  
*triṣu lokeṣu vikhyātā nāmnā śivacaturdaśī \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Nandikeshvara said . — Hear with attention, O Brahmana! I shall tell you the Maheshvara vrata. It is well-known in all the three worlds by the name of Shiva Chaturdashi.

## \|\| 95.6-7 \|\|

*mārgaśīrṣatrayodaśyāṃ sitāyāmekabhojanaḥ \|*  
*prārthayeddevadeveśaṃ tvāmahaṃ śaraṇaṃ gataḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*caturdaśyāṃ nirāhāraḥ samyagabhyarcya śaṃkaram \|*  
*suvarṇavṛṣabhaṃ dattvā bhokṣyāmi ca pare 'hani \|\| 7 \|\|*

6-7. In the month of Margashira, on the thirteenth day of the bright fortnight, the devotee should take his meals once and pray to Shiva with this Sankalpa mantra, “O Lord of all the Deities! I take refuge ini Thee.

To-morrow, the Chaturdashi day, I shall observe a complete fast, without eating anything, and worship Shiva. I shall also give away a bull, made of gold, and then take my meals the next day

## \|\| 95.8 \|\|

*evaṃ niyamakṛtsuptvā prātarutthāya mānavaḥ \|*  
*kṛtasnānajapaḥpaścād umayā saha śaṃkaram \|*  
*pūjayetkamalaiḥ śubhrair gandhamālyānulepanaiḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Having made this Sankalpa, the devotee should go to bed and then rise early on the next morning and worship Shiva along with His Consort (Uma), with white lotus flowers, sandal, etc.

## \|\| 95.9-18 \|\|

*pādau namaḥ śivāyeti śiraḥ sarvātmane namaḥ \|*  
*trinetrāyeti netrāṇi lalāṭaṃ haraye namaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*mukhamindumukhāyeti śrīkaṇṭhāyeti kaṃdharām \|*  
*sadyojātāya karṇau tu vāmadevāya vai bhujau \|\| 10 \|\|*

*aghorahṛdayāyeti hṛdayaṃ cābhipūjayet \|*  
*stanau tatpuruṣāyeti tatheśānāya codaram \|\| 11 \|\|*

*pārśvau cānantadharmāya jñānabhūtāya vai kaṭim \|*  
*ūrū cānantavairāgya-siṃhāyetyabhipūjayet \|\| 12 \|\|*

*anantaiśvaryanāthāya jānunī cārcayedbudhaḥ \|*  
*pradhānāya namo jaṅghe gulphau vyomātmane namaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*vyomakeśātmarūpāya keśānpṛṣṭhaṃ ca pūjayet \|*  
*namaḥ puṣṭyai namastuṣṭyai pārvatīṃ cāpi pūjayet \|\| 14 \|\|*

*tatastu vṛṣabhaṃ haimam udakumbhasamanvitam \|*  
*śuklamālyāmbaradharaṃ pañcaratnasamanvitam \|*  
*bhakṣyairnānāvidhairyuktaṃ brāhmaṇāya nivedayet \|\| 15 \|\|*

*prīyatāṃ devadevo 'tra sadyojātaḥ pinākadhṛk \|*  
*tato viprānsamāhūya tarpayedbhaktitaḥ śubhān \|*  
*pṛṣadājyaṃ ca saṃprāṣya svapedbhūmāvudaṅmukhaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*pañcadaśyāṃ ca sampūjya viprānbhuñjīta vāgyataḥ \|*  
*tadvatkṛṣṇacaturdaśyām etatsarvaṃ samācaret \|\| 17 \|\|*

*caturdaśīṣu sarvāsu kuryātpūrvavadarcanam \|*  
*ye tu māse viśeṣāḥ syus tānnibodha kramādiha \|\| 18 \|\|*

9-18. (1) The feet should he worshipped, after reciting ... Shivaya namah,’ (2) the head, after reciting ... ‘Sarvatmane namah. (3) the eyes, after reciting fetera .... ‘Trinetraya namah. (4) the forehead, after reciting ... ‘Haraye namah,’ (6) the mouth, after reciting ... Indumukhaya numah.’ (6) the throat after reciting ... ‘Srikanthaya vamah.’ (7) the ears, after reciting ... ‘ Sadyojataya namah.’ (8) the arms, after reciting ... ‘Vamadevaya namah.' (9) the heart, after’ reciting .... Aghorahridayaiya namah,.’ (10) the breasts, after ‘ reciting:... ‘Tatpurasaya namiuh,’ (11) the stomach, alter reciting tora ‘Idindya namah.’(12) the ribs, after reciting .... Anantadharnfya namah,’ . (13) the waist, after reciting ... Jnanabhutaya namah,’ (14) the thighs, after reciting ...... ‘Ananta Vairdgyasiyhiya namah.’ (15) the knees should be worshipped, after reciting ... “Ananiaiivaryandthdya namab.’ (16) the legs, after reciting ... “Pradhandya namah. (17) the ankles, after reciting ... “‘Vyomateinia; papal (18) the hair, after reciting ... Vyomakeshatmarupaya namah (19) the bask, after reciting ... Pushtyai namah. (20) ... Tushtyayi namah.

## \|\| 95.14 \|\|
