*vyomakeśātmarūpāya keśānpṛṣṭhaṃ ca pūjayet \|*  
*namaḥ puṣṭyai namastuṣṭyai pārvatīṃ cāpi pūjayet \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Then the devotee should give to the Brahmanas: a golden bull, along with a pitcher, full of water, white garments, Pancharatna, various Kinds of eatables.

## \|\| 95.15-16 \|\|

*tatastu vṛṣabhaṃ haimam udakumbhasamanvitam \|*  
*śuklamālyāmbaradharaṃ pañcaratnasamanvitam \|*  
*bhakṣyairnānāvidhairyuktaṃ brāhmaṇāya nivedayet \|\| 15 \|\|*

*prīyatāṃ devadevo 'tra sadyojātaḥ pinākadhṛk \|*  
*tato viprānsamāhūya tarpayedbhaktitaḥ śubhān \|*  
*pṛṣadājyaṃ ca saṃprāṣya svapedbhūmāvudaṅmukhaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

15-16. Really good Brahmanas should be invited and well-fed, after which curd mixed with clarified butter, saved from the sacrificial offerings, should be taken by the devotee, who should sleep on the ground, with his head towards the north. On the full moon-day, he should feed the Brahmanas and then take his own meals in silence. Similarly, he should do on the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight.

## \|\| 95.17 \|\|

*pañcadaśyāṃ ca sampūjya viprānbhuñjīta vāgyataḥ \|*  
*tadvatkṛṣṇacaturdaśyām etatsarvaṃ samācaret \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. The worship should be performed in the same way all the fourteenth days of each fortnight of very month. Now the especial mantras to be recited in each month will be explained.

## \|\| 95.18-22 \|\|

*caturdaśīṣu sarvāsu kuryātpūrvavadarcanam \|*  
*ye tu māse viśeṣāḥ syus tānnibodha kramādiha \|\| 18 \|\|*

*mārgaśīrṣādimāseṣu kramādetadudīrayet \|*  
*śaṃkarāya namaste 'stu namaste karavīraka \|\| 19 \|\|*

*tryambakāya namaste 'stu maheśvaramataḥ param \|*  
*namaste 'stu mahādeva sthāṇave ca tataḥ param \|\| 20 \|\|*

*namaḥ paśupate nātha namaste śambhave punaḥ \|*  
*namaste paramānanda namaḥ somārdhadhāriṇe \|\| 21 \|\|*

*namo bhīmāya ityevaṃ tvāmahaṃ śaraṇaṃ gataḥ \|*  
*gomūtraṃ gomūyaṃ kṣīraṃ dadhi sarpiḥ kuśodakam \|\| 22 \|\|*

18-22 Commencing with the month of Margashira, the mantras hereafter mentioned should be pronounced one by one: — (1) Shankaraya namah, (2) Karavirakaya nameh, (3) Tryamvaka yanamah, (4) Maheshvaraya namah, (5) Mahadevaya namah, (6) Sthanave namah, (7) Pashupataye namah, (8) Nathaya cnamah, (9) Sambhave namah, (10) Namaste Paramananda, (11) Namah Somardhadharine, (12) Bhimaya nawah. I am at Thy Mercy.

These names should be recited one by one, each month, from Margashira.

The devotee should offer as Prasana - (1) cow’s urine, (2) cow-dung, (3), milk, (4) curds, (5) clarified butter, (6) water mixed with kusha-grass, (7) panchagavya, (8) wood-apple (bael), (9) camphor, (10) agaru, (11) barley, (12) black-sesamum, on the Chaturdashi of each. month.

## \|\| 95.23-12 \|\|

*pañcagavyaṃ tato bilvaṃ karpūraṃ cāguruṃ yavāḥ \|*  
*tilāḥ kṛṣṇāśca vidhivat prāśanaṃ kramaśaḥ smṛtam \|*  
*pratimāsaṃ caturdaśyor ekaikaṃ prāśanaṃ smṛtam \|\| 23 \|\|*

*mandāramālatībhiśca tathā dhattūrakairapi \|*  
*sinduvārairaśokaiśca mallikābhiśca pāṭalaiḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*nārada uvāca*  
*bhagavanbhūtabhavyeśa tathānyadapi yacchrutam \|*  
*bhuktimuktiphalāyālaṃ tatpunar vaktumarhasi \|\| 1 \|\|*

*evamukto 'bravīcchambhur ayaṃ vāṅmayapāragaḥ \|*  
*matsamastapasā brahman purāṇaśrutivistaraiḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*dharmo 'yaṃ vṛṣarūpeṇa nandī nāma gaṇādhipaḥ \|*  
*dharmānmāheśvarān vakṣyat yataḥprabhṛti nārada \|\| 3 \|\|*

*matsya uvāca*  
*ityuktvā devadeveśas tatraivāntaradhīyata \|*  
*nārado 'pi hi śuśrūṣur apṛcchannandikeśvaram \|*  
*ādiṣṭastvaṃ śiveneha vada māheśvaraṃ vratam \|\| 4 \|\|*

*nandikeśvara uvāca*  
*śṛṇuṣvāvahito brahman vakṣye māheśvaraṃ vratam \|*  
*triṣu lokeṣu vikhyātā nāmnā śivacaturdaśī \|\| 5 \|\|*

*mārgaśīrṣatrayodaśyāṃ sitāyāmekabhojanaḥ \|*  
*prārthayeddevadeveśaṃ tvāmahaṃ śaraṇaṃ gataḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*caturdaśyāṃ nirāhāraḥ samyagabhyarcya śaṃkaram \|*  
*suvarṇavṛṣabhaṃ dattvā bhokṣyāmi ca pare 'hani \|\| 7 \|\|*

*evaṃ niyamakṛtsuptvā prātarutthāya mānavaḥ \|*  
*kṛtasnānajapaḥpaścād umayā saha śaṃkaram \|*  
*pūjayetkamalaiḥ śubhrair gandhamālyānulepanaiḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*pādau namaḥ śivāyeti śiraḥ sarvātmane namaḥ \|*  
*trinetrāyeti netrāṇi lalāṭaṃ haraye namaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*mukhamindumukhāyeti śrīkaṇṭhāyeti kaṃdharām \|*  
*sadyojātāya karṇau tu vāmadevāya vai bhujau \|\| 10 \|\|*

*aghorahṛdayāyeti hṛdayaṃ cābhipūjayet \|*  
*stanau tatpuruṣāyeti tatheśānāya codaram \|\| 11 \|\|*

*pārśvau cānantadharmāya jñānabhūtāya vai kaṭim \|*  
*ūrū cānantavairāgya-siṃhāyetyabhipūjayet \|\| 12 \|\|*

23-24. Note. — The mantras to be recited in twelve months, beginning with Agrahayana, are given below:

1\) Salutation to Shankara. I take refuge in Thee.” This should be pronounced in the month of Margashira.

2\) Salutation be Karaviraka. I take refuge in Thee.” This should be pronounced in the month of Pausha.

3\) “To Tryambaka; in Magha.”

4\) “To Maheshvara; in Phalguna.”

5\) To Mahadeva; in Chaitra.”

6\) “To Sthanu; in Vaishakha.”

7\) “To Pashupati; in Jyaishtha,”

8\) “To Natha; in Ashada”

9\) “To Shambhu; in Shravana.”

10\) To Paramananda; in Bhadra.”

11\) To Somardhadharin; in Asvina.”

12\) “To Bhima; in Kartika.”

The worship of Shiva should be conducted from the month of Margashira onward, by offering the following flowers, turn by turn, viz,: — (1) Mandara, (2) jasmine, (3) Dhatura, (4) Sambhalu (Sindulvara), (5) Ashoka, (6) Mallika, (7) Patala, (8) Arka flower, (9) Kadamba, (10) lotus (Satapatri), (11) Kamalini (Utpala).

## \|\| 95.25 \|\|

*arkapuṣpaiḥ kadambaiśca śatapattryā tathotpalaiḥ \|*  
*ekaikena caturdaśyor arcayetpārvatīpatim \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Again, when the month of Kartika arrives, the Brahmanas should be fed with various kinds of eatables and offered garments, ornaments and garlands.

## \|\| 95.26-27 \|\|

*punaśca kārttike māse prāpte saṃtarpayeddvijān \|*  
*annair nānāvidhair bhakṣyair vastramālyavibhūṣaṇaiḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*kṛtvā nīlavṛṣotsargaṃ śrutyuktavidhinā naraḥ \|*  
*umāmaheśvaraṃ haimaṃ vṛṣabhaṃ ca gavā saha \|\| 27 \|\|*

26-27. Afterwards, the devotee should let loose a black bull, in conjunction with the Vedic rites. A golden image of Shiva and Parvati should be made and given away to a Brahmana, along with a bull and a cow. A bedstead, with the following things, should also be given away: Eight white pearls, sheets, pillows, and a vase, full of water.

## \|\| 95.28 \|\|

*muktāphalāṣṭakautaṃ sitanetrapaṭāvṛtām \|*  
*sarvopaskarasaṃyuktāṃ śayyāṃ dadyāt sakumbhakām \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. The images of Shiva and Parvati should be placed in a copper vessel, full of rice, and then located on top of the pitcher of water, after which they should be given away to a Brahmana versed in the Vedas, observing ordinances and having a calm disposition.

## \|\| 95.29 \|\|

*tāmrapātropari punaḥ śālitaṇḍulasaṃyutam \|*  
*sthāpya viprāya śāntāya vedavrataparāya ca \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. It is best to give it to one acquainted with Samaveda: it should never and on no account be given to a hypocrite. Only one versed in the Vedas, knowing the Vedic principles, is fit to receive such an offering.

## \|\| 95.30-31 \|\|

*jyeṣṭhasāmavide deyaṃ navakavratine kvacit \|*  
*guṇajñe śrotriye dadyād ācārye tattvavedini \|\| 30 \|\|*

*avyaṅgāṅgāya saumyāya sadā kalpāṇakāriṇe \|*  
*sapatnīkāya sampūjya vastramālyavibhūṣaṇaiḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

30-31. A Brahmana, free from deformity and of simple habits, should be worshipped, along with his wife, with garments, garlands and ornaments, These things might be given to the preceptor (Guru), if there be one; otherwise, to a really good Brahmana, free from all feeling of miserliness; for such a feeling leads one to the lower region.

## \|\| 95.32 \|\|

*gurau sati gurordeyaṃ tadabhāve dvijātaye \|*  
*na vittaśāṭhyaṃ kurvīta kurvandoṣātpatatyadhaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. One who observes the Shiva Chaturdashi ordinance, according to these rites, gets the benefit of a thousand Ashvamedha sacrifices.

## \|\| 95.33 \|\|

*anena vidhinā yastu kuryācchivacaturdaśīm \|*  
*so 'śvamedhasahasrasya phalaṃ prāpnoti mānavaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. And the sins of killing a Brahmana and also against the parents, committed in this or in the previous life, are destroyed in a moment.

## \|\| 95.34 \|\|

*brahmahatyādikaṃ kiṃcid yadatrāmutra vā kṛtam \|*  
*pitṛbhirbhrātṛbhirvāpi tatsarvaṃ nāśamāpnuyāt \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. The devotee gets long life, health, domestic prosperity, and promotion in his husbandry. He then eventually goes near the Lord of four hands, whose chief attendant he becomes; and then after, passing crores of kalpas in the heaven, he becomes unified with Shiva.

## \|\| 95.35 \|\|

*dīrghāurārogyakulānnavṛddhir atrākṣayāmutra caturbhujatvam \|*  
*gaṇādhipatyaṃ divi kalpakoṭi-śatānyuṣitvā padameti śambhoḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Even the sage Brihaspati, the Devas, like the mighty Indra, and Brahma, cannot adequately describe the glories of this ordinance. Even I cannot do so with a crore of tongues.

## \|\| 95.36 \|\|

*na bṛhaspatirapyanantamasyāḥ phalamindo na pitāmaho 'pi vaktum \|*  
*na ca siddhagaṇo 'pyalaṃ na cāhaṃ yadi jihvāutakoṭayo 'pi vaktre \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. One who reads, hears or thinks about this ordinance becomes Liberated from all his sins. The Divine Consorts also venerate it; therefore, a devotee should always observe it, free from all feelings of despise.

## \|\| 95.37 \|\|

*bhavatyamaravallabhaḥ paṭhati yaḥ smaredvā sadā śṛṇotyapi vimatsaraḥ sakalapāpanirmocanīm \|*  
*imāṃ śivacaturdaśīmamarakāminīkoṭayaḥ stuvanti tamaninditaṃ kimu samācaredyaḥ sadā \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. The woman who observes this ordinance with the permission of her husband, son or the preceptor also attains bliss by the glory of Shiva.

## Chapter 96

## \|\| 96.1 \|\|

*nandikeśvara uvāca*  
*phalatyāgasya māhātmyaṃ yadbhavecchṛṇu nārada \|*  
*yadakṣayaṃ paraṃ loke sarvakāmaphalapradam \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Nandikeshvara said: — O Narada! also hear the benefits that accrue to the devotee in his next life, by his relinquishing the fruits of this ordinance.

## \|\| 96.2 \|\|

*mārgaśīrṣe śubhe māsi tṛtīyāyāṃ mune vratam \|*  
*dvādaśyāmathavāṣṭamyāṃ caturdaśyāmathāpi vā \|*  
*ārabhecchuklapakṣasya kṛtvā brāhmaṇavācanam \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. O Sage! the ordinance (vrata) should be commenced on any one of the following days, in the month of Margashir: the third, the twelfth, the eight or the fourteenth day of the bright fortnight, after invoking the Brahmanas.

## \|\| 96.3 \|\|

*anyeṣvapi hi māseṣu puṇyeṣu munisattama \|*  
*sadakṣiṇaṃ pāyasena bhojayecchaktito dvijān \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. O Narada! In other auspicious months also, the devotee should, to the best of his ability, feed the Brahmanas with rice cooked in milk and mixed with sugar, and then satisfy them with Dakshina.

## \|\| 96.4 \|\|

*aṣṭādaśānāṃ dhānyānām anyacca phalamūlakam \|*  
*varjayedabdamekaṃ tu ṛte auṣadhakāraṇam \|*  
*savṛṣaṃ kāñcanaṃ rudraṃ dharmarājaṃ ca kārayet \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. The prohibited grains of eighteen kinds and fruits and roots should be avoided for a period of one year; but there is no harm in taking anything in the form of a medicine. A golden image of Shiva and a bull should be made. The image of Dharmaraja should be made similarly.

## \|\| 96.5-6 \|\|

*kūṣmāṇḍaṃ mātuliṅgaṃ ca vārtākaṃ panasaṃ tathā \|*  
*āmrātakaṃ kapitthāni kaliṅgamatha vālukam \|\| 5 \|\|*

*śrīphalāśvatthabadaraṃ jambīraṃ kadalīphalam \|*  
*kāśmaraṃ dāḍimaṃ śaktyā kāladhautāni ṣoḍaśa \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. The following sixteen kinds of fruits should be made in gold, according to the means of the devotee, viz.: — pumpkins, citrons, egg-plants, bread-fruits, mangoes, hog-plums, wood-apples, Indra grains, cucumbers, cocoanuts, the holy figs, the jujubes, the lemons, the plantains, saffron, and pomegranates.

## \|\| 96.7-8 \|\|

*mūlakāmalakaṃ jambū-tintiḍīkaramardakam \|*  
*kaṅkolailākatuṇḍīra-karīrakuṭajaṃ śamī \|\| 7 \|\|*

*audumbaraṃ nārikelaṃ drākṣātha bṛhatīdvayam \|*  
*raupyāṇi kārayecchaktyā phalānīmāni ṣoḍaśa \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8. The following should be made of silver, according to the means of the devotee, viz.: — Muti (a kind of root vegetable), Emblica officinalis rose apple, tamarind, Karaunda, Kankolaberry, cardamom, cotton, bamboo, Kutaja, Sami, Udumbara, cocoanut, grapes, two kinds of egg-plants.

## \|\| 96.9-11 \|\|

*tāmraṃ tālaphalaṃ kuryād agastiphalameva ca \|*  
*piṇḍārakāśmaryaphalaṃ tathā sūraṇakandakam \|\| 9 \|\|*

*raktālukākandakaṃ ca kanakāhvaṃ ca cirbhiṭam \|*  
*citravallīphalaṃ tadvat kūṭaśālmalijaṃ phalam \|\| 10 \|\|*

*āmraniṣpāvamadhuka-vaṭamudgapaṭolakam \|*  
*tāmrāṇi ṣoḍaśaitāni kārayecchaktito naraḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

9-11. The fruits of the following should be made of copper, according to the means of the devotee: — Palms, Agasti grandiflora, Kayaphala, Gambhari, esculent root, the red esculent root, a bulbous root, svarnakhhiri, cucumber, chitravalti, Salmali, mango, liquorice, kidney-bean, fig tree, patola (a species of cucumber).

## \|\| 96.12 \|\|

*udakumbhadvayaṃ kuryād dhānyopari savastrakam \|*  
*tataśca kārayecchayyāṃ yathopari suvāsasī \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Two pitchers of water, covered with cloth, should be placed on grain, and a bed should also be arranged and covered with cloth.

## \|\| 96.13 \|\|

*bhakṣyapātratrayopetaṃ yamarudravṛṣānvitam \|*  
*dhenvā sahaiva śāntāya viprāyātha kuṭumbine \|*  
*sapatnīkāya sampūjya puṇye 'hni vinivedayet \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. On some sacred day, the devotee should give away all these things as well as three food plates, the images of Dharmaraja, Shiva, with that of the sacred bull and a cow, to a peaceful Brahmana couple who may have a big family, having first worshipped them.

## \|\| 96.14 \|\|

*yathā phaleṣu sarveṣu vasantyamarakoṭayaḥ \|*  
*tathā sarvaphalatyāga-vratādbhaktiḥ śive 'stu me \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. “As the nuraberless Devas dwell in all kinds of fruits, so let my devotion be to Shiva, as a consequence of my performing this vrata of relinquishing the fruits of my actions.

## \|\| 96.15 \|\|

*yathā śivaśca dharmaśca sadānantaphalapradau \|*  
*tadyuktaphaladānena tau syātāṃ me varapradau \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. “Shiva and Dharmaraja are known to be the great Givers of boons; let Them therefore confer boons on me for giving away these likenesses, together with these appropriate fruits in charity.’

## \|\| 96.16 \|\|

*yathā phalānyanantāni śivabhakteṣu sarvadā \|*  
*tathānantaphalāvāptir astu janmani janmani \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. “As in the devotees of Shiva are always (to be found) endless fruits, so let me also have fruits endless, in life after life’

## \|\| 96.17 \|\|

*yathā bhedaṃ na paśyāmi śivaviṣṇvarkapadmajān \|*  
*tathā mamāstu viśvātmā śaṃkaraḥ śaṃkaraḥ sadā \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. “I do not make any (invidious) distinction between Shiva, Vishnu, Sun, Brahma; let the Lord Shiva, the soul of the universe, bless me with eternal happiness.”

## \|\| 96.18-20 \|\|

*iti dattvā ca tatsarvam alaṃkṛtya ca bhūṣaṇaiḥ \|*  
*śaktiścecchayanaṃ dadyāt sarvopaskarasaṃyutam \|\| 18 \|\|*

*aśaktastu phalānyeva yathoktāni vidhānataḥ \|*  
*tathodakumbhasaṃyuktau śivadharmau ca kāñcanau \|\| 19 \|\|*

*viprāya dattvā bhuñjīta vāgyatastailavarjitam \|*  
*anyānyapi yathāśaktyā bhojayecchaktito dvijān \|\| 20 \|\|*

18-20. The articles (to be given away) should be given to the Brahmana, having first decorated him. The devotee may also give a bedding, with all its requisites, if he had the means to do on, otherwise je may only give away the fruits mentioned before. The golden images of Shiva and Dharmaraja being given to the Brahmana, with the pitchers of water, he should feed himself on food devoid of oil, by observing the vow of silence, and should also feed the Brahmanas, according to his means.

## \|\| 96.21 \|\|

*etadbhāgavatānāṃ tu sauravaiṣṇavayoginām \|*  
*śubhaṃ sarvaphalatyāga-vrataṃ vedavido viduḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. This is the way of a devotee of Vishnu, Sun or a Yogi or a Bhagwat to relinquish the fruits of their actions, as laid down by the Brahmanas versed in the Vedas.

## \|\| 96.22 \|\|

*nārībhiśca yathāśaktyā kartavyaṃ dvijapuṃgava \|*  
*etasmānnāparaṃ kiṃcid iha loke paratra ca \|*  
*vratamasti muniśreṣṭha yadanantaphalapradam \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. “O Sage Narada! this ordinance should be observed, to the best of their ability, by the womenfolk, too. There is no ordinance like this “that can give such everlasting boons in this world, as well as in the next.

## \|\| 96.23 \|\|

*sauvarṇaraupyatāmreṣu yāvantaḥ paramāṇavaḥ \|*  
*bhavanti cūrṇyamāneṣu phaleṣu munisattama \|*  
*tāvadyugasahasrāṇi rudraloke mahīyate \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. “O Sage! the devotee remains in the region of Shiva for as ‘many thousand Yugas as there are atoms of gold, silver and copper, in this world, when these latter are ground to a powder.

## \|\| 96.24 \|\|

*etatsamastakaluṣāpaharaṃ janānām ājīvanāya manujeṣu ca sarvadā syāt \|*  
*janmāntareṣvapi na putraviyogaduḥkham āpnoti dhāma ca puraṃdaralokajuṣṭam \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. This ordinance washes off all the lifelong sins of the devotee. He fever has the pain of losing his son, and he attains the region inhabited by Gods.

## \|\| 96.25 \|\|

*yo vā śṛṇoti puruṣo 'lpadhanaḥ paṭhedvā devālayeṣu bhavaneṣu ca dhārmikāṇām \|*  
*pāpairviuktavapuratra puraṃ murārer ānandakṛtpadamupaiti munīndra so 'pi \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. The poor man who hears or reads this, either in some sacred place (place of a God), or in the house of a pious man, goes to the region of Shiva where he gets into the place of Deities and enjoys, after being liberated from all his sins.

## Chapter 97

## \|\| 97.1 \|\|

*nārada uvāca*  
*yadārogyakaraṃ puṃsāṃ yadanantaphalapradam \|*  
*yacchāntaye ca martyānāṃ vada nandīśa tadvratam \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Narada said: — Nandikeshvara! Pray describe to me the ordinance that may be the giver of peace, health and everlasting benefits to the people.

## \|\| 97.2-3 \|\|

*nandikeśvara uvāca*  
*yattadviśvātmano dhāma paraṃ brahma sanātanam \|*  
*sūryāgnicandrarūpeṇa tattridhā jagati sthitam \|\| 2 \|\|*

*tadārādhya pumānvipra prāpnoti kuśalaṃ sadā \|*  
*tasmādādityavāreṇa sadā naktāśano bhavet \|\| 3 \|\|*

2-3. Nandikeshvara said: — That which is the eternal abode of the soul of the universe, is known as the Sun, the Fire and the Moon, in the world; by the worship of these a man attains happiness The devotee observing is should always take his meals at night time only on Sundays.

## \|\| 97.4 \|\|

*yadā hastena saṃyuktam ādityasya ca vāsaram \|*  
*tadā śanidine kuryād ekabhaktaṃ vimatsaraḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. In the case of the asterism Hasti falling on Sunday, the devotee should take his meals only once on Saturday, purging his heart of all vanity.

## \|\| 97.5-9 \|\|

*naktamādityavāreṇa bhojayitvā dvijottamān \|*  
*pattrairdvādaśasaṃyuktaṃ raktacandanapaṅkajam \|\| 5 \|\|*

*vilikhya vinyasetsūryaṃ namaskāreṇa pūrvataḥ \|*  
*divākaraṃ tathāgneye vivasvantamataḥ param \|\| 6 \|\|*

*bhagaṃ tu nairṛte devaṃ varuṇaṃ paścime dale \|*  
*mahendramanile tadvad ādityaṃ ca tathottare \|\| 7 \|\|*

*śāntamīśānabhāge tu namaskāreṇa vinyaset \|*  
*karṇikāpūrvapattre tu sūryasya turagānnyaset \|\| 8 \|\|*

*dakṣiṇe 'ryamanāmānaṃ mārtaṇḍaṃ paścime dale \|*  
*uttare tu raviṃ devaṃ karṇikāyāṃ ca bhāskaram \|\| 9 \|\|*

5-9. On Sunday night, the devotee, after feeding good Brahmanas, should draw a lotus of twelve petals with red sandal. To the east of it he should place, after salutations, the Sun (Surya), to the south-east Divakara, to the south Vivasvana, to the south-west Bhaga, to the west Varana, to the north-west Mahendra, to the north Aditya, to the north-east Santa.

In the forepart of the lotus, the horses of the Sun should be inscribed, in the south the Aryama Devas, in the west Martanda, and on the northern petal Ravi Bhaskara on the pericarp of the lotus.

## \|\| 97.10 \|\|

*raktapuṣpodakenārghyaṃ satilāruṇacandanam \|*  
*tasminpadme tato dadyād imaṃ mantramudīrayet \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Afterwards, red flowers, red sandal, sesamum, mixed with water, should be poured on the lotus, and the following mantra should be recited at the time:

## \|\| 97.11 \|\|

*kālātmā sarvabhūtātmā vedātmā viśvatomukhaḥ \|*  
*yasmādagnīndrarūpastvam ataḥ pāhi divākara \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. “O Divakara (the giver of day)! You are the soul of time, creation and the Vedas. You have your face turned to each direction. You are’ of the form of Indra and Agni: therefore shelter me.”

## \|\| 97.12-13 \|\|

*agnim īḍe namastubhyam iṣetvorje ca bhāskara \|*  
*agna āyāhi varada namaste jyotiṣāṃ pate \|\| 12 \|\|*

*arghyaṃ dattvā visṛjātha niśi tailavivarjitam \|*  
*bhuñjīta vatsarānte tu kāñcanaṃ kamalottamam \|*  
*puruṣaṃ ca yathāśaktyā kārayeddvibhujaṃ tathā \|\| 13 \|\|*

12-13. “Apnimile namastubhamisetvérje cha bhaskara.” “Agna ayahi varada na aste jyotisam pate.” With this mantra Arghya should be offered, and the Deity dismissed. He should take his meals at night free from oil. When a year has elapsed in this way, he should make a lotus of gold and an image with two hands.

## \|\| 97.14 \|\|

*suvarṇaśṛṅgīṃ kapilāṃ mahārghyāṃ raupyaiḥ khuraiḥ kāṃsyadohāṃ savatsām \|*  
*pūrṇe guḍasyopari tāmrapātre nidhāya padmaṃ puruṣaṃ ca dadyāt \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. He should then give away in charity a milk cow, with her horns covered with gold, the hoofs with silver, along with her calf, and a milking vessel of bell metal, while the lotus and image should be placed in a pot of copper completely full of molasses.

## \|\| 97.15 \|\|

*sampūjya raktāmbaramālyadhūpair dvijaṃ ca raktairatha hemaśṛṅgaiḥ \|*  
*saṃkalpayitvā puruṣaṃ sapadmaṃ dadyādanekavratadānakāya \|*  
*avyaṅgarūpāya jitendriyāya kuṭumbine deyamanuddhatāya \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. The devotee, after worshipping the Brahmana with red cloth, sandal, garland, incense, etc., should bestow his gifts, viz. — the lotus and the image, etc., on him, he having a large family, and being free from deformity and pride, and able to restrain his passions and the object of charity in many other vratas.

## \|\| 97.16 \|\|

*namo namaḥ pāpavināśanāya viśvātmane saptaturaṃgamāya \|*  
*sāmargyajurdhāmanidhe vidhātre bhavābdhipotāya jagatsavitre \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. At that time, the devotee should utter the following words: — “Namo namah papavinasanaya, “Vidvatmane saptatarahgamaya, “Samargyajurdhamidhe Vidhatre, “Bhavabdhipataya jagatsavitre.”

“O Dispeller of sins, the Soul of the universe, your chariot drawn by seven horses, the vase of Rika, Yaju and Sama Vedas, the boat of the ocean of universe, I salute Thee oft and often”.

## \|\| 97.17 \|\|

*ityanena vidhinā samācared abdabhekamiha yastu mānavaḥ \|*  
*so 'dhirohati vinaṣṭakalmaṣaḥ sūryadhāma dhutacāmarāvaliḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. One who observes these rituals and keeps up this vrata for a year, is freed from all sins and goes to the solar region fanned by chamara.

## \|\| 97.18 \|\|

*dharmasaṃkṣayamavāpya bhūpatiḥ śokaduḥkhabhayarogavarjitaḥ \|*  
*dvīpasaptakapatiḥ punaḥ punar varmamūrtir amitaujasā utaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. On the consumption of his store of piety he becomes the sovereign of the seven Dvipas, and never gets pain, suffering or disease. — He becomes most powerful and virtuous.

## \|\| 97.19 \|\|

*yā ca bhartṛgurudevatatparā vedamūrtidinanaktamācaret \|*  
*sāpi lokamamareśavanditā yāti nārada raverna saṃśayaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. O Narada! the woman who is devoted to her husband, God and preceptor, and observes this ordinance, and eats at night only on Sundays, undoubtedly reaches the solar region, which is honoured by the Devas.

## \|\| 97.20 \|\|

*yaḥ paṭhedapi śṛṇoti mānavaḥ paṭhyamānamatha vānumodate \|*  
*so 'pi śakrabhuvanasthito 'maraiḥ pūjyate vasati cākṣayaṃ divi \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. The person who reads or hears, or approves of the reading of this ordinance, also goes to the region of Indra where he is served by the Devas, and remains there for innumerable kalpas.

## Chapter 98

## \|\| 98.1 \|\|

*nandikeśvara uvāca*  
*athānyadapi vakṣyāmi saṃkrāntyudyāpane phalam \|*  
*yadakṣayaṃ pare loke sarvakāmaphalapradam \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Nandikeshvara said: — Narada! I shall now describe to you the way how the ordinance of Sankranti, which in the next world gives everlasting boons of all kinds, is to be brought to a close.

## \|\| 98.2 \|\|

*ayane viṣuve vāpi saṃkrāntivratamācaret \|*  
*pūrvedyurekabhaktena dantadhāvanapūrvakam \|*  
*saṃkrāntivāsare prātas tilaiḥ snānaṃ vidhīyate \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. The Sankranti ordinance should be observed on the day of equinoxes or solstices. The day, prior to Sankranti, the devotee should have his meals only once; and, on the following day, he should bathe in water nixed with sesamum, after brushing his teeth

## \|\| 98.3 \|\|

*ravisaṃkramaṇe bhūmau candanenāṣṭapattrakam \|*  
*padmaṃ sakarṇikaṃ kuryāt tasminnāvāhayedravim \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. On the day of the Sankranti, the devotee should draw on the earth a lotus of eight petals with sandal, in the centre of which pericarps should be made, where the presence of the Sun should be invoked.

## \|\| 98.4-6 \|\|

*karṇikāyāṃ nyasetsūryam ādityaṃ pūrvatastataḥ \|*  
*nama uṣṇārciṣe yāmye namo ṛṅmaṇḍalāya ca \|\| 4 \|\|*

*namaḥ savitre nairṛtye vāruṇe tapanaṃ punaḥ \|*  
*vāyavye tu bhagaṃ nyasya punaḥ punarathārcayet \|\| 5 \|\|*

*mārtaṇḍamuttare viṣṇum īśāne vinyasetsadā \|*  
*gandhamālyaphalairbhakṣyaiḥ sthaṇḍile pūjayettataḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

4-6. The Sun should be located in the pericarp, Aditya in the east, and salutations should be made in the south, after reciting Ushnarchise namah, Ringmandalaya namah’ “Savitre namal” in the south-west, “Tapanaya namah” in the west, Bhaga in the north-west should be located and worshipped constantly. Martanda should be located. in the north and Vishnu in the north-east. These should be adored with incense, flowers, fruits and eatables on an altar

## \|\| 98.7 \|\|

*dvijāya sodakumbhaṃ ca ghṛtapātraṃ hiraṇmayam \|*  
*kamalaṃ ca yathāśaktyā kārayitvā nivedayet \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. A golden vessel of clarified butter, with a pitcher of water, should be given away to the Brahmana; and the lotus should also be made of gold, according to the means of the devotee, and giver away to the Brahmana.

## \|\| 98.8-9 \|\|

*candanodakapuṣpaiśca devāyārghyaṃ nyasedbhuvi \|*  
*viśvāya viśvarūpāya viśvadhāmne svayambhuve \|*  
*namo 'nanta namo dhātre ṛksāmayajuṣāṃ pate \|\| 8 \|\|*

*anena vidhinā sarvaṃ māsi māsi samācaret \|*  
*vatsarānte 'thavā kuryāt sarvaṃ dvādaśadhā naraḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

8-9. Afterwards, the Arghya, consisting of water, sandal and flowers, should be placed on the floor as an oblation to the Sun, by reciting the following mantra: “Vidvaya Vishvaripaya Vishvadhimne Svayambhube. Namananta namo dhatre Riksam Yajusimpati.” This ritual should be observed each month, or at the end of the year. All the twelve vratas should be done at the same time.

## \|\| 98.10-11 \|\|

*saṃvatsarānte ghṛtapāyasena saṃtarpya vahniṃ dvijapuṃgavāṃśca \|*  
*kumbhānpunardvādaśa dhenuuktān saratnahairaṇmayapadmauktān \|\| 10 \|\|*

*payasvinīḥ śīlavatīśca dadyād dharmaiḥ śṛṅgaiḥ raupyakhuraiśca uktāḥ \|*  
*gāvo 'ṣṭa vā sapta sakāṃsyadohā mālyāmbarā vā caturo 'pyaśaktaḥ \|*  
*daurgatyayuktaḥ kapilāmathaikāṃ nivedayedbrāhmaṇapuṃgavāya \|\| 11 \|\|*

10-11. Then libations of rice, cooked in milk and sugar, should be poured into the fire and Brahmanas should be satisfied with eatables. On that occasion, 12 pitchers of water, with a few gems, 12 golden lotus flowers and 12 milk cows of gentle disposition, or only 8, 7 or 4 such cows (in the last case, the cows being dressed and garlanded), according to the means of the devotee, should be given to a poor and deserving Brahmana, after their horns being covered with gold, their hoofs with silver, along with milking pots of ell metal. In case, the devotee be a very poor man, he may give only one milk cow.

## \|\| 98.12 \|\|

*haimīṃ ca dadyātpṛthivīṃ saśeṣām ākārya rūpyāmatha vā ca tāmrīm \|*  
*paiṣṭīmaśaktaḥ pratimāṃ vidhāya sauvarṇasūryeṇa samaṃ pradadyāt \|*  
*na vittaśāṭhyaṃ puruṣo 'tra kuryāt kurvannadho yāti na saṃśayo 'tra \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Afterwards, an image of earth, along with that of the serpent Shesha, should be made in gold, silver, copper or even of kneaded flour, according to the means of the devotee, and given away to the Brahmana, along with a golden image of the Sun. As far as possible, no miserliness should be exercised in this ritual; for the man doing so, in spite of having riches undoubtedly goes to hell

## \|\| 98.14 \|\|

*tatastu karmakṣayamāpya sapta-dvīpādhipaḥ syātkulaśīlauktaḥ \|*  
*sṛṣṭermukhe 'vyaṅgavapuḥ sabhāryaḥ prabhūtaputrānvayavanditāṅghriḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Narada! One who observes this ordinance, enjoys in heaven the honour and respect by all the Gandharvas, for as long as Indra and other gods, earth and the seven oceans, the Himalayas and other mountains His piety being consumed, the devotee is born, in the beginning of creation, a sovereign of good family, endowed with all kingly virtues and blessed with handsome form (devoid of deformity) and many a child, wife, friend and relation.

## \|\| 98.15 \|\|

*iti paṭhati śṛṇoti vātha bhaktyā vidhimakhilaṃ ravisaṃkramasya puṇyam \|*  
*matimapi ca dadāti so 'pi devair amarapaterbhavane prapūjyate ca \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. One who ready about this Surya Sankranti with devotion, or hears or advises others to read it, is honoured by the Devas in the realm of Indra.

## Chapter 99

## \|\| 99.1 \|\|

*nandikeśvara uvāca*  
*śṛṇu nārada vakṣyāmi viṣṇorvratamanuttamam \|*  
*vibhūtidvādaśī nāma sarvadevanamaskṛtam \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Nandikeshvara said: — Narada! I shall now relate to you Vishnu vrata, known as the Vibhuti-Dvadashi vrata, which is held in veneration by all the Devas."

## \|\| 99.2 \|\|

*kārttike caitravaiśākhe mārgaśīrṣe ca phālgune \|*  
*āṣāḍhe vā daśamyāṃ tu śuklāyāṃ laghubhuṅnaraḥ \|*  
*kṛtvā sāyantanīṃ saṃdhyāṃ gṛhṇīyānniyamaṃ budhaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. On the tenth day of the bright fortnight, in the month of Kartika, Chaitra, Vaishakha, Margashirsha, Phalguna or Asiddha, the devotee should have a light meal; and in the day time, after performing his evening prayers, make the following resolution:

## \|\| 99.3 \|\|

*ekādaśyāṃ nirāhāraḥ samabhyarcya janārdanam \|*  
*dvādaśyāṃ dvijasaṃyuktaḥ kariṣye bhojanaṃ vibho \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. “Oh God, on the eleventh day I shall keep a rigid fast and worship Janardana. I shall break the fast on the twelfth day, in company of the Brahmanas.

## \|\| 99.4 \|\|

*tadavighnena me yātu saphalaṃ syācca keśava \|*  
*namo nārāyaṇāyeti vācyaṃ ca svapatā niśi \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. “O Keshava! let there be no hindrance in the observance of my fast.”

He should utter “Om namo Narayanaya namah” (Om, Salutations be to Narayana), before retiring to bed.

## \|\| 99.5 \|\|

*tataḥ prabhāta utthāya kṛtasnānajapaḥ śuciḥ \|*  
*pūjayetpuṇḍarīkākṣaṃ śuklamālyānulepanaiḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. On getting up in the morning, he should recite Gayatri 108 times, and then worship Lord Vishnu with white sandal and flowers.

## \|\| 99.6-9 \|\|

*vibhūtaye namaḥ pādāv aśokāya ca jānunī \|*  
*namaḥ śivāyetyūrū ca viśvamūrte namaḥ kaṭim \|\| 6 \|\|*

*kandarpāya namo meḍhram ādityāya namaḥ karau \|*  
*dāmodarāyetyudaraṃ vāsudevāya ca stanau \|\| 7 \|\|*

*mādhavāyetyuro viṣṇoḥ kaṇṭham utkaṇṭhine namaḥ \|*  
*śrīdharāya mukhaṃ keśān keśavāyeti nārada \|\| 8 \|\|*

*pṛṣṭhaṃ śārṅgadharāyeti śravaṇau varadāya vai \|*  
*svanāmnā śaṅkhacakrāsi-gadājalajapāṇaye \|*  
*śiraḥ sarvātmane brahman nama ityabhipūjayet \|\| 9 \|\|*

6-9. The feet should he worshipped after reciting “Vibhutaye namah,”

the knees after reciting “ Ashokaya namah,” the thighs after reciting ‘‘Shivaya namah,” the waist after reciting “Vishvamurtaye namah,” the male organ of generation after reciting “‘ Kandarpiya namah,” the hands after reciting “Adityaya namah,” the stomach after reciting “Damodariya namah,” the breasts after reciting ‘ Vasudevaya namah,” the chest after reciting “Madhavaya namah,” the neck after reciting “Utkanthine namah,” the mouth after reciting “Shridharaya namah,” and the hair after reciting “Kedavaya namah,” the back after reciting “Sharangadharaya namal,” the ears after reciting “Varadiya namah,” the head after reciting Sarvatmane namah,” with His other names, viz., “Sankapanye namah,”

“Chakrapanye namah,” “Asipanaye namah,” “Gadapanaye namah,” and “Padmapanaye namah.”

## \|\| 99.10 \|\|

*matsyamutpalasaṃyuktaṃ haimaṃ kṛtvā tu śaktitaḥ \|*  
*udakumbhasamāuktam agrataḥ sthāpayedbudhaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. A golden fish should be made and also a lotus of gold, according to the means and wishes of the devotee; and a pitcher, full of water, should be placed in front of it.

## \|\| 99.11 \|\|

*guḍapātraṃ tilairyuktaṃ sitavastrābhiveṣṭitam \|*  
*rātrau jāgaraṇaṃ kuryād itihāsakathādinā \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Afterwards, a vessel, full of molasses and covered with a white cloth, together with some sesamum, should be placed. The devotee should keep up the night with the recitation of Itihasas

## \|\| 99.12 \|\|

*prabhātāyāṃ tu śarvaryāṃ brāhmaṇāya kuṭumbine \|*  
*sakāñcanotpalaṃ devaṃ sodakumbhaṃ nivedayet \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. On the following morning the golden fish and lotus, along with the pitcher of water, should be given away to some good Brahmana with large family

## \|\| 99.13 \|\|

*yathā na mucyase deva sadā sarvavibhūtibhiḥ \|*  
*tathā māmuddharāśeṣa-duḥkhasaṃsārakardamāt \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. At that time, the devotee should pray: “As Thou, O Lord Vishnu, art never devoid of any prosperity (Vibhuti), so please extricate me from the meshes and manifold calamities of this world”.

## \|\| 99.14 \|\|

*daśāvatārarūpāṇi pratimāsaṃ kramānmune \|*  
*dattātreyaṃ tathā vyāsam utpalena samanvitam \|*  
*dadyādevaṃ samā yāvat pāṣaṇḍānabhivarjayet \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. The devotee should give away one in each month of the year the golden images of the ten incarnations (of the supreme God) as well as of Dattatreya and Vedavyasa, along with a lotus of gold. During this period the devotee should avoid the company of rogues and the wicked,

## \|\| 99.15 \|\|

*samāpyaivaṃ yathāśaktyā dvādaśa dvādaśīḥ punaḥ \|*  
*saṃvatsarānte lavaṇa-parvatena samanvitām \|*  
*śayyāṃ dadyānmuniśreṣṭha gurave dhenusaṃyutām \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. After observing the fast like this for twelve months, on each Dvadashi, the devotee at the conclusion of the year, should give away to his preceptor a bedding, a mount of salt and a cow.

## \|\| 99.16 \|\|

*grāmaṃ ca śaktimāndadyāt kṣetraṃ vā bhavanānvitam \|*  
*guruṃ sampūjya vidhivad vastrālaṃkārabhūṣaṇaiḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. A man of means may also give away a village or a house and honor his preceptor with diverse raiment’s and ornaments.

## \|\| 99.17 \|\|

*anyānapi yathāśaktyā bhojayitvā dvijottamān \|*  
*tarpayed vastragodānai ratnaughadhanasaṃcayaiḥ \|*  
*alpavitto yathāśaktyā stokaṃ stokaṃ samācaret \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Other Brahmanas should be feasted, according to the means of the devotee and satisfied by being given clothes, jewels, money, ornaments vows, &c. A man with limited means should give only as much as he can afford.

## \|\| 99.18 \|\|

*yaścāpyatīva niḥsvaḥ syād bhaktimānmādhavaṃ prati \|*  
*puṣpārcanavidhānena sa kuryādvatsaradvayam \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. A very poor man, but having sincere devotion to Lord Madhava, may worship Lord Vishnu for a couple of years with flowers alone.

## \|\| 99.19-21 \|\|

*anena vidhinā yastu vibhūtidvādaśīvratam \|*  
*kuryātpāpavinirmuktaḥ pitriṇāṃ tārayecchatam \|\| 19 \|\|*

*janmanāṃ śatasāhasraṃ na śokaphalabhāgbhavet \|*  
*na ca vyādhirbhavettasya na dāridryaṃ na bandhanam \|*  
*vaiṣṇavo vātha śaivo vā bhavedjanmani janmani \|\| 20 \|\|*

*yāvadyugasahasrāṇāṃ śatamaṣṭottaraṃ bhavet \|*  
*tāvatsvarge vasedbrahman bhūpatiśca punarbhavet \|\| 21 \|\|*

19-21. One who observes the Vibhuti-dvadashi ordinance like this, liberates himself from all sins and also frees hundreds of his ancestors. He is not oppressed with grief, disease or poverty during thousands of births. He is always born as a devotee of Vishnu or Shiva, and, after spending 108 thousand yugas in heaven, is born as a king.

## Chapter 100

## \|\| 100.1 \|\|

*nandikeśvara uvāca*  
*purā rathaṃtare kalpe rājāsītpuṣpavāhanaḥ \|*  
*nāmnā lokeṣu vikhyātas tejasā sūryasaṃnibhaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Nandikeshvara said: — In the days gone by, during the Rathantara Kalpa, there lived a mighty king, as illustrious as the Sun, who was known by the name of Pushpavahana.

## \|\| 100.2 \|\|

*tapasā tasya tuṣṭena caturvaktreṇa nārada \|*  
*kamalaṃ kāñcanaṃ dattaṃ yathākāmagamaṃ mune \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. O Narada! Brahma, being pleased with his asceticism, presented him with a lotus of gold that could move about at will

## \|\| 100.3 \|\|

*lokaiḥ samastair nagara-vāsibhiḥ sahito nṛpaḥ \|*  
*dvīpāni suralokaṃ ca yatheṣṭaṃ vyacarattadā \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. (With its help) the king began to wander about at his pleasure in the seven dvipas as well as in the abode of the gods, in company of his citizens.

## \|\| 100.4 \|\|

*kalpādau saptamaṃ dvīpaṃ tasya puṣkaravāsinaḥ \|*  
*loke ca pūjitaṃ yasmāt puṣkaradvīpamucyate \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. At the beginning of the kalpa, the kingdom of this king, who lived in the lotus, was the seventh dvipa: — on account: of the great praise and honour given to it by the people, it came to be known as Pushkara

## \|\| 100.5 \|\|

*devena brahmaṇā dattaṃ yānamasya yato 'mbujam \|*  
*puṣpavāhanamityāhus tasmāttaṃ devadānavāḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. The King was called Pushpavahana by the Devas and the Danavas on account of his having received the lotus for his conveyance.

## \|\| 100.6 \|\|

*nāgamyamasyāsti jagattraye 'pi brahmāmbujasthasya tapo 'nubhāvāt \|*  
*patnī ca tasyāpratimā munīndra nārīsahasrairabhito 'bhinandyā \|*  
*nāmnā ca lāvaṇyavatī babhūva sā pārvatīveṣṭatamā bhavasya \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Owing to his powers, acquired by the practice of penances, no place in the three worlds was inaccessible to him, seated on his lotus given by Lord Brahma. His queen, Lavanyavati, was worthy to be honoured by thousands of ladies. In beauty and womanly virtues, she had no equal.

She was like the Goddess Parvati, the noble Consort of the Lord Shiva.

## \|\| 100.7 \|\|

*tasyātmajānāmautaṃ babhūva dharmātmanām agryadhanurdharāṇām \|*  
*tadātmanaḥ sarvamavekṣya rājā muhurmuhur vismayamāsasāda \|*  
*so 'bhyāgataṃ vīkṣya munipravīraṃ prācetasaṃ vākyamidaṃ babhāṣe \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. The king became the father of ten thousand virtuous princes, who all were renowned in archery. The king began to wonder at his incomparable prosperity. One day, seeing the great sage Pracheta, approaching, he addressed him thus:

## \|\| 100.8-9 \|\|

*kasmādvibhūtir amalāmaramartyapūjyā jātā ca sarvavijitāmarasundarīṇām \|*  
*bhāryā mamālpatapasā paritoṣitena dattaṃ mamāmbujagṛhaṃ ca munīndra dhātrā \|\| 8 \|\|*

*yasminpraviṣṭamapi koṭiśataṃ nṛpāṇāṃ sāmātyakuñjararathaughajanāvṛtānām \|*  
*no lakṣyate kva gatamambaramadhya indus tārāgaṇairiva gataḥ paritaḥ sphuradbhiḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

8-9. “O Sage! how is it that there is such an abundance of prosperity in my house? How have I got a queen who is venerated even by the Devas, and who has no equal even among the goddesses? Why has Brahma become so much pleased with my little asceticism as to present me with such a lotus, (vast wonderful), that when myriads of kings, with ministers, elephants, people, and chariots entered into it, they appear small indeed, like so many galaxies of twinkling stars with the moon herself in the immeasurable expanse of the firmament.

## \|\| 100.10 \|\|

*tasmātkimanyajananījaṭharodbhavena dharmādikaṃ kṛtamaśeṣaphalāptihetuḥ \|*  
*bhagavanmayātha tanayair athavānayāpi bhadraṃ yadetadakhilaṃ kathaya pracetaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. “Hence, O Lord, what is the use of being horn in the separate womb of the mother? To obtain endless (good) results, I have performed many a religious rite. Now please tell us what is of ultimate good to me, my wife and sons.”

## \|\| 100.11 \|\|

*munirabhyadhādatha bhavāntaritaṃ samīkṣya pṛthvīpateḥ prasabhamadbhutahetuvṛttam \|*  
*janmābhavattava tu lubdhakule 'tighore jātastvamapyanudinaṃ kila pāpakārī \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Hearing the above words of the king, the sage, after meditation, spoke the following words, about the wonderful former lives of the king: —

“King! Previously you were born in the house of a hunter, and you led a life of sin from day to day.

## \|\| 100.12 \|\|

*vapurapyabhūttava punaḥ puruṣāṅgasaṃdhir durgandhisattvabhujagāvaraṇaṃ samantāt \|*  
*na ca te suhṛn na sutabandhujano na tātas tv ādṛksvasā na jananī ca tadābhiśastā \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. “Your body was hard, rough and also offensively stinking. Snakes coiled all over it. You had no friend, nor sons; neither kinsmen, nor sisters, nor parents. All were abused and cursed by you. This beloved consort of yours was also against you.

## \|\| 100.13 \|\|

*abhisaṃgatā paramabhīṣṭatamā vimukhī mahīśa tava yoṣidiyam \|*  
*abhūdanāvṛṣṭiratīva raudrā kadācidāhāranimittamasmin \|*  
*kṣutpīḍitenātha tadā na kiṃcid āsāditaṃ dhānyaphalāmiṣādyam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. “Then the land was visited by a terrible drought, when you were over-whelmed with hunger, bat could not get grain, fruits, flesh or any kind of eatables to quench it, though you searched for them everywhere.

## \|\| 100.14 \|\|

*athābhidṛṣṭaṃ mahadambujāḍhyaṃ sarovaraṃ paṅkaparītarodhaḥ \|*  
*padmānyathādāya tato bahūni gataḥ puraṃ vaidiśanāmadheyam \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. “On that occasion you came to a tank, full. of muddy banks, but which was abundantly full of lotus flowers. You culled a heap of lotuses out of that tank and carried them home to Vaidisha the city in which you lived.)

## \|\| 100.15 \|\|

*tanmaulyalābhāya puraṃ samastaṃ bhrāntaṃ tvayāśeṣam ahas tadāsīt \|*  
*kretā na kaścitkamaleṣu jātaḥ śrānto bhṛśaṃ kṣutparipīḍitaśca \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. You wandered about the whole city to sell those lotuses, but could not find a purchaser. Eventually you were. overpowered with hunger and fatigue.

## \|\| 100.16 \|\|

*upaviṣṭastvamekasmin sabhāryo bhavanāṅgaṇe \|*  
*atha maṅgalaśabdaśca tvayā rātrau mahāñśrutaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. “And you went and sat with your wife in the courtyard of some one whence in the night you heard some nice and auspicious sound.

## \|\| 100.17 \|\|

*sabhāryastatra gatavān yatrāsau maṅgaladhvaniḥ \|*  
*tatra maṇḍapamadhyasthā viṣṇorarcāvalokitā \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. You went to the spot whence the sound was heard with your wife. There you saw the worship of Lord Vishnu conducted in a pandal.

## \|\| 100.18-20 \|\|

*veśyānaṅgavatī nāma vibhūtidvādaśīvratam \|*  
*samāptau māghamāsasya lavaṇācalamuttamam \|\| 18 \|\|*

*nivedayantī gurave śayyāṃ copaskarānvitām \|*  
*alaṃkṛtya hṛṣīkeśaṃ sauvarṇāmarapādapam \|\| 19 \|\|*

*tāṃ tu dṛṣṭvā tatastābhyām idaṃ ca paricintitam \|*  
*kimebhiḥ kamalaiḥ kāryaṃ varaṃ viṣṇuralaṃkṛtaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

18-20. “The worship in question was the concluding chapter of Vibhutidvadasi ordinance, in the month of Magha, which was kept up by a conrtezan, named Anamgavati. At that time, she was giving away the mount of salt, the bedstead along with other things, the decorated image of the merciful Lord Vishnu and the golden Kalpa tree, to her preceptor. On seeing all that, you said to yourself, ‘What would. I now do with these lotus flowers, I should better offer them to Vishnu’.

## \|\| 100.21 \|\|

*iti bhaktistadā jātā dampatyostu narādhipa \|*  
*tatprasaṅgātsamabhyarcya keśavaṃ lavaṇācalam \|*  
*śayyā ca puṣpaprakaraiḥ pūjitā bhūśca sarvataḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. O King! thus devotion came to the hearts of both of you: and you: worshipped the Lord as well as the mount of salt, the bedding, and even the earth with your lotus flowers.

## \|\| 100.22-25 \|\|

*athānaṅgavatī tuṣṭā tayordhanaśatatrayam \|*  
*dīyatāmādideśātha kaladhautaśatatrayam \|\| 22 \|\|*

*na gṛhītaṃ tatastābhyāṃ bahusattvāvalambanāt \|*  
*anaṅgavatyā ca punas tayorannaṃ caturvidham \|*  
*ānīya vyāhṛtaṃ cātra bhujyatāmiti bhūpate \|\| 23 \|\|*

*tābhyāṃ tu tadapi tyaktaṃ bhokṣyāvo vai varānane \|*  
*prasaṅgādupavāsena tavādya sukhamāvayoḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*janmaprabhṛti pāpiṣṭhau kukarmāṇau dṛḍhavrate \|*  
*tatprasaṅgāttayormadhye dharmaleśastu te 'nagha \|\| 25 \|\|*

22-25. “The courtesan was very much pleased with your devotion and offered you 300 gold coins which both of you did not accept, as you were both then filled with sattvaguna (i.e., your hearts became pure,) at which the courtezan became still more pleased with you, had four kinds of delicious foods brought and asked you to cat. You again declined to partake of her hospitality, and said, ‘ We shall have food at some other time, We are exceedingly glad to-day With your acquaintance and the keeping fast. Hitherto we have been carrying a vicious life and have been sinners all along.’ By her contact. you had then acquired some virtue

## \|\| 100.26-27 \|\|

*iti jāgaraṇaṃ tābhyāṃ tatprasaṅgādanuṣṭhitam \|*  
*prabhāte ca tadā dattā śayyā salavaṇācalā \|\| 26 \|\|*

*grāmāśca gurave bhaktyā vipreṣu dvādaśaiva tu \|*  
*vastrālaṃkārasaṃyuktā gāvaśca karakānvitāḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

26-27. “In that way, you kept up all the night with that courtesan and, on the following morning, she gave the mount of salt and the bedding as well as villages to her preceptor and to a dozen Brahmanas, garments, ornaments, kamandalu and cows.

## \|\| 100.28 \|\|

*bhojanaṃ ca suhṛnmitra-dīnāndhakṛpaṇaiḥ samam \|*  
*tacca lubdhakadāmpatyaṃ pūjayitvā visarjitam \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. “After that, she fed her friends, poor men, blind men, misers, compéers and kinsmen, and at the same time she also honoured in the same way and dismissed you both.

## \|\| 100.29-31 \|\|

*sa bhavāṃl lubdhako jātaḥ sapatnīko nṛpeśvaraḥ \|*  
*puṣkaraprakarāttasmāt keśavasya na pūjanāt \|\| 29 \|\|*

*vinaṣṭāśeṣapāpasya tava puṣkaramandiram \|*  
*tasya sattvasya māhātmyād alpena tapasā nṛpa \|\| 30 \|\|*

*yathākāmagamaṃ jātaṃ lokanāthaścaturmukhaḥ \|*  
*saṃtuṣṭastava rājendra brahmarūpī janārdanaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

29-31. “King! owing to this worship of Keshava by lotus flower, the same hunter and his wife have been now born in the persons of yourself and your consort. You have been freed of all your sins by the virtue of your little self-denial and purity of heart. Hence this wonderful lotus moving at will. This has been given to you by Janardana, the Lord of creation in the person of four-faced Brahma, because he was pleased with you.

## \|\| 100.32 \|\|

*sāpyanaṅgavatī veśyā kāmadevasya sāmpratam \|*  
*patnī sapatnī saṃjātā ratyāḥ prītiriti śrutā \|*  
*lokeṣvānandajananī sakalāmarapūjitā \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. “That courtesan is now the rival of Rati, the wife of Cupid, and is known as Priti. She is the giver of happiness to the womenfolk, and is venerated by the Devas.

## \|\| 100.33 \|\|

*tasmādutsṛjya rājendra puṣkaraṃ tanmahītale \|*  
*gaṅgātaṭaṃ samāśritya vibhūtidvādaśīvratam \|*  
*kuru rājendra nirvāṇam avaṣyaṃ samavāpsyasi \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. “King! Even now abandon this Pushkara-dvipa and observe the vibhuti-dvadashi fast on the banks of the Ganges, so that you may attain Nirvana.’

## \|\| 100.34 \|\|

*ityuktvā sa munir brahmaṃs tatraivāntaradhīyata \|*  
*rājā yathoktaṃ ca punar akarotpuṣpavāhanaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Nandikeshvara said: — “Narada! That sage vanished then and there, after telling all that to the king, and the latter observed the ordinance, as cetated.

## \|\| 100.35-36 \|\|

*idamācarato brahmann akhaṇḍavratam ācaret \|*  
*yathākathaṃcit kamalair dvādaśa dvādaśīr mune \|\| 35 \|\|*

*kartavyāḥ śaktito deyā viprebhyo dakṣiṇānagha \|*  
*na vittaśāṭhyaṃ kurvīta bhaktyā tuṣyati keśavaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

35-36. “Narada! the devotee, observing this ordinance, should keep up the penance and perform the rites with molasses of any kind whatsoever, as prescribed, for 12 months, and give aims to the Brahmanas, without any feeling of miserliness. Keshava is pleased with devotion alone.

## \|\| 100.37 \|\|

*iti kaluṣatridāraṇaṃ janānāmapi paṭhatīha śṛṇoti cātha bhaktyā \|*  
*matimapi ca dadāti devaloke vasati sa koṭiśatāni vatsarāṇām \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. “One who reads, listens to or produces in others a desire to observe this ordinance, which dispels all sins, remains in the heaven for a hundred crores of years.”

## Chapter 101

## \|\| 101.1 \|\|

*nandikeśvara uvāca*  
*athātaḥ sampravakṣyāmi vrataṣaṣṭhīmanuttamām \|*  
*rudreṇābhihitāṃ divyāṃ mahāpātakanāśanam \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Nandikeshvara said:--Narada! Hear, I am now going to tell you about the sixty ordinances, as explained by the Lord Shiva and which dispel great sins.

## \|\| 101.2-3 \|\|

*naktamabdaṃ caritvā tu gavā sārdhaṃ kuṭumbine \|*  
*haimaṃ cakraṃ triśūlaṃ ca dadyādviprāya vāsasī \|\| 2 \|\|*

*śivarūpastato 'smābhiḥ śivaloke sa modate \|*  
*etaddevavrataṃ nāma mahāpātakanāśanam \|\| 3 \|\|*

2-3. The ordinance, known as, (1) Deva-Vrata, is the dispeller of all sins. The observer of it should have his meal only in the night for a year, after which he should give away one cow, quoit and trident, all made of gold along with a pair of clothes, to a Brahmana having a large family. One who does so becomes unified with Shiva and lives in His region.

## \|\| 101.4 \|\|

*yastvekabhaktena samāṃ śivaṃ haimavṛṣānvitam \|*  
*dhenuṃ tilamayīṃ dadyāt sa padaṃ yāti śāṃkaram \|*  
*etadrudravrataṃ nāma pāpaśokavināśanam \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. The devotee keeping up the (2) Rudra-Vrata should, for a year, have only one meal a day, after which he should give away one bull of gold and a cow of sesamum. This observance is also the destroyer of ills and helps the devotee to go to the region of Shiva, and raises him to the rank of Shiva

## \|\| 101.5 \|\|

*yastu nīlotpalaṃ haimaṃ śarkarāpātrasaṃyutam \|*  
*ekāntaritanaktāśī samānte vṛṣasaṃyutam \|*  
*sa vaiṣṇavaṃ padaṃ yāti līlāvratamidaṃ smṛtam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. One who gives away a bull and a blue lotus, made of gold, as well as a vessel, full of sugar, and lives on nightly meal only for a year, eating in a secluded place, obtains the rank of Vishnu. This is known as (3) Lila-Vrata.

## \|\| 101.6 \|\|

*āṣāḍhādicaturmāsam abhyaṅgaṃ varjayennaraḥ \|*  
*bhojanopaskaraṃ dadyāt sa yāti bhavanaṃ hareḥ \|*  
*jane prītikaraṃ nriṇāṃ prītivratamihocyate \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. He, giving up of all unguents and giving away of nice and clean cooking utensils, in the four months, beginning with Ashadha leads the devotee to the realm of Vishnu. This observance is known as (4) PritVrata, because it pleases everybody.

## \|\| 101.7-8 \|\|

*varjayitvā madhau yastu dadhikṣīraghṛtaikṣavam \|*  
*dadyādvastrāṇi sūkṣmāṇi rasapātraiśca saṃyutam \|\| 7 \|\|*

*sampūjya vipramithunaṃ gaurī me prīyatāmiti \|*  
*etadgaurīvrataṃ nāma bhavānīlokadāyakam \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8. One who observes the (5) Gauri-Vrata, in the month of Chaitra, by invoking the pleasure of the goddess, with the words, “Gauri me priyatam,” and by giving up honey, milk, curds, clarified butter, molasses, and similar articles, gives fine cloths, and the vessels full of sugarcane juice, &c., and worships the Brahmana with his wife, goes to the realm of Parvati.

## \|\| 101.9-10 \|\|

*puṣyādau yastrayodaśyāṃ kṛtvā naktaṃ madhau punaḥ \|*  
*aśokaṃ kāñcanaṃ dadyād ikṣuuktaṃ daśāṅgulam \|\| 9 \|\|*

*viprāya vastrasaṃyuktaṃ pradyumnaḥ prīyatāmiti \|*  
*kalpaṃ viṣṇupade sthitvā viśokaḥ syātpunarnaraḥ \|*  
*etat kāmavrataṃ nāma sadā śokavināśanam \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. The (6) Kama-Vrata, the destroyer of all woes should be observed on the thirteenth day of Pausha. The devotee should take his meal at night and give away to a Brahmana, a golden tree of Asoka, ten fingers in height after covering it with a cloth and pieces of sugarcane. He should invoke the -pleasure of Pradyumna, with the words: “Pradyumnah priyatam” at the time of giving it away. By doing so, the devotee resides without care and anxiety in the region of Vishnu, till the end of the kalpa.

## \|\| 101.11-12 \|\|

*āṣāḍhādivrataṃ yastu varjayennakhakartanam \|*  
*vārtākaṃ ca caturmāsaṃ madhusarpirghaṭānvitam \|\| 11 \|\|*

*kārttikyāṃ tatpunarhaimaṃ brāhmaṇāya nivedayet \|*  
*sa rudralokamāpnoti śivavratamidaṃ smṛtam \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-12. (7) Shiva-Vrata should be observed during the four months of. Asadha, &c. in course of which the devotee should not get his nails, &c, trimmed, He. should avoid the use of brinjals and give away to a Brahmana a pitcher full of honey, clarified butter and golden brinjal in the month of Kartika. By doing so, he goes to the realm of Rudra

## \|\| 101.13-14 \|\|

*varjayedyastu puṣpāṇi hemantaśiśirāvṛtū \|*  
*puṣpatrayaṃ ca phālgunyāṃ kṛtvā śaktyā ca kāñcanam \|\| 13 \|\|*

*dadyāddvikālavelāyāṃ prīyetāṃ śivakeśavau \|*  
*dattvā paraṃ padaṃ yāti saumyavratamidaṃ smṛtam \|\| 14 \|\|*

13-14. One who abstains from flowers during winter (i.e., the seasons of Hemanta and Shishira) and in the month of Phalguna, and gets three flowers of gold made according to his means and gives them away in charity at dusk, after invoking the pleasure of Shiva and Vishnu, with the words “Priyatam. Shiva-Keshavam,” attains final beatitude. This is Known as (8) Saumya-Vrata.

## \|\| 101.15-16 \|\|

*phālgunyāditṛtīyāyāṃ lavaṇaṃ yastu varjayet \|*  
*samāpte śayanaṃ dadyād gṛhaṃ copaskarānvitam \|\| 15 \|\|*

*sampūjya vipramithunaṃ bhavānī prīyatāmiti \|*  
*gaurīloke vasetkalpaṃ saubhāgyavratamucyate \|\| 16 \|\|*

15-16. (9) Saubhigya-Vrate should be kept up by avoiding on the third day of every month, beginning from Phalguna, the use of salt for a year. At the conclusion of the ordinance, he should give to a Brahmana couple a properly equipped bedstead, a house with all its necessary appurtenances, after showing due honour to them, and should invoke the pleasure of the goddess, with the words, “Bhavani priyatam.” By doing so, he resides for a hundred kalpas in the realm of Parvati.

## \|\| 101.17-18 \|\|

*saṃdhyāmaunaṃ tataḥ kṛtvā samānte ghṛtakumbhakam \|*  
*vastraugmaṃ tilānghaṇṭāṃ brāhmaṇāya nivedayet \|\| 17 \|\|*

*sārasvataṃ padaṃ yāti punarāvṛttidurlabham \|*  
*etatsārasvataṃ nāma rūpavidyāpradāyakam \|\| 18 \|\|*

17-18. The devotee who maintains the vow of silence on the evenings for a year and at the end of it gives a jar of clarified butter, a pair of clothes, sesamum, and a bell to a Brahmana, goes to the domain of Sarasvati — the Goddess of letters — and is liberated from the cycle of birth. This is known as (10) Sarasvata ordinance — the giver of beauty and learning.

## \|\| 101.19-20 \|\|

*lakṣmīmabhyarcya pañcamyām upavāsī bhavennaraḥ \|*  
*samānte hemakamalaṃ dadyāddhenusamanvitam \|\| 19 \|\|*

*sa vaiṣṇavaṃ padaṃ yāti lakṣmīvāñjanmajanmani \|*  
*etat sampadvrataṃ nāma sadā pāpavināśanam \|\| 20 \|\|*

19-20. One who worships Lakshmi — the Goddess of wealth — and keeps the fast on the fifth day of a month, for a year, and at the end of it gives away a cow, along with a lotus of gold, goes to the kingdom of Vishnu and is always born in good circumstances, This is culled the (11) Sampada-Vrata and is the destroyer of all ills.

## \|\| 101.21-22 \|\|

*kṛtvopalepanaṃ śambhor agrataḥ keśavasya ca \|*  
*yāvadabdaṃ punardadyād dhenuṃ jalaghaṭānvitām \|\| 21 \|\|*

*janmāutaṃ sa rājā syāt tataḥ śivapuraṃ vrajet \|*  
*etad āurvrataṃ nāma sarvakāmapradāyakam \|\| 22 \|\|*

21-22. One who washes the floor in front of Vishnu or Shiva for a full year and then gives a way a cow with a pitcher of water, is born a king on this earth, ten thousand times, and at the end goes to the realm of Shiva. This is known as (12) Ayur-Vrata, and is the giver of all desires.

## \|\| 101.23-24 \|\|

*aśvatthaṃ bhāskaraṃ gaṅgāṃ praṇamyaikatra vāgyataḥ \|*  
*ekabhaktaṃ naraḥ kuryād abdamekaṃ vimatsaraḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

*vratānte vipramithunaṃ pūjyaṃ dhenutrayānvitam \|*  
*vṛkṣaṃ hiraṇmayaṃ dadyāt so'śvamedhaphalaṃ labhet \|*  
*etat kīrtivrataṃ nāma bhūtikīrtiphalapradam \|\| 24 \|\|*

23-24. One who takes his meal once a day, in silence, bereft of vice for a full year and salutes the peepul tree, the sun and the Ganges together, and at the end of the ordinance adores the Brahmana with his consort, having given then a golden tree with three cows, attains the benefit of Ashvamedha sacrifice. Tits is called the (13) Kirti-Vrata — the giver of every fame and prosperity.

## \|\| 101.25-26 \|\|

*ghṛtena snapanaṃ kuryāc chambhor vā keśavasya ca \|*  
*akṣatābhiḥ supuṣpābhiḥ kṛtvā gomayamaṇḍalam \|\| 25 \|\|*

*tiladhenusamopetaṃ samānte hemapaṅkajam \|*  
*śuddhamaṣṭāṅgulaṃ dadyāc chivaloke mahīyate \|*  
*sāmagāya tataścaitat sāmavratamihocyate \|\| 26 \|\|*

25-26. The observer of the (14) Sama-Vrata should make an altar of cowdang bathe Shiva or Vishnu with clarified butter, worship them with uncooked rice and flowers, for a year. At the end of the year, the devotee should give away a lotus of gold, eight fingers in height, with a cow of sesamum to a Brahmana versed in the Sama-Veda. As a result, the devotee is respected in Shiva loka

## \|\| 101.27-28 \|\|

*navamyāmekabhaktaṃ tu kṛtvā kanyāśca śaktitaḥ \|*  
*bhojayitvāsanaṃ dadyād dhaimakañcukavāsasī \|\| 27 \|\|*

*haimaṃ siṃhaṃ ca viprāya dattvā śivapadaṃ vrajet \|*  
*janmārbudaṃ surūpaḥ syāc chatrubhiścāparājitaḥ \|*  
*etadvīravrataṃ nāma nārīṇāṃ ca sukhapradam \|\| 28 \|\|*

27-28. One who takes only one meal a day on the 9th day of a month and then gives to 9 virgin, alter feasting her, according to his means, a pair of clothes embroidered with gold and raiments of silk, and a lion of gold to a Brahmana, gets a handsome form and he is never defeated by his foes and lives for a considerable time in the realm of Shiva, This is known as (15) Vira-Vrata — the giver of all prosperity to women kind.

## \|\| 101.29-30 \|\|

*yāvatsamā bhavedyastu pañcadaśyāṃ payovrataḥ \|*  
*samānte śrāddhakṛddadyāt pañca gāstu payasvinīḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*vāsāṃsi ca piśaṅgāni jalakumbhautāni ca \|*  
*sa yāti vaiṣṇavaṃ lokaṃ pitriṇāṃ tārayecchatam \|*  
*kalpānte rājarājaḥ syāt pitṛvratam idaṃ smṛtam \|\| 30 \|\|*

29-30. One who takes milk only on each full moon day, for a year, and at its conclusion, after performing Shraddha, gives away five milk cows, along with pitchers of water and cloths of tawny col our, goes to the domain of Vishnu, where he saves hundreds of his ancestors and becomes the King of Kings at the end of a kalpa. ‘This is called (16) Pitri-Vrata

## \|\| 101.31-32 \|\|

*caitrādicaturo māsāñ jalaṃ dadyādayācitam \|*  
*vratānte maṇikaṃ dadyād annavastrasamanvitam \|\| 31 \|\|*

*tilapātraṃ hiraṇyaṃ ca brahmaloke mahīyate \|*  
*kalpānte bhūpatirnūnam ānandavratamucyate \|\| 32 \|\|*

31-32. One who voluntarily gives drinking water to the needy, from the beginning of Chaitra for four months, and after it gives away a big water jar (Manika), with grain, cloths, gold sad a pot containing sesamum, goes to the region of Brahma and becomes a king at the end of a kalpa. This is called the (17) Ananda-Vrata.

## \|\| 101.33-34 \|\|

*pañcāmṛtena snapanaṃ kṛtvā saṃvatsaraṃ vibhoḥ \|*  
*vatsarānte punardadyād dhenuṃ pañcāmṛtena hi \|\| 33 \|\|*

*viprāya dadyācchaṅkhaṃ ca sa padaṃ yāti śāṃkaram \|*  
*rājā bhavati kalpānte dhṛtivratamidaṃ smṛtam \|\| 34 \|\|*

33-34. One who bathes in Panchamrita for a year, and then gives away a conch, Panchamrita and a cow to a Brahmana, goes to the realm of Shiva and becomes a king at the end of a kalpa. This is called the (18) Dhriti Vrata.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — ... = Consisting of five ingredients viz., ... i.e., milk, sugar, clarified butter, Curd and Honey.

## \|\| 101.30 \|\|

*vāsāṃsi ca piśaṅgāni jalakumbhautāni ca \|*  
*sa yāti vaiṣṇavaṃ lokaṃ pitriṇāṃ tārayecchatam \|*  
*kalpānte rājarājaḥ syāt pitṛvratam idaṃ smṛtam \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. One who gives up meat for a year and at the end gives away a cow or a deer of gold gets the benefit of Ashvamedha sacrifice, and, after reaping the fruits of his virtue for one full kalpa, 1s born as a king. This is (19) Ahimsa-Vrata.

## \|\| 101.36 \|\|

*māghamāsyuṣasi snānaṃ kṛtvā dāmpatyamarcayet \|*  
*bhojayitvā yathāśaktyā mālyavastravibhūṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*sūryaloke vasetkalpaṃ sūryavratamidaṃ smṛtam \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. One who, in the month of Magha, bathes in the small hours of the morning and then worships a Brahmana and his wife with garlands, ornaments and clothes and then feeds them to their satisfaction, resides in the region of the Sun for a kalpa. This is (20) Surya-Vrata.

## \|\| 101.37 \|\|

*āṣāḍhādicaturmāsaṃ prātaḥsnāyī bhavennaraḥ \|*  
*vipreṣu bhojanaṃ dadyāt kārttikyāṃ goprado bhavet \|*  
*sa vaiṣṇavaṃ padaṃ yāti viṣṇuvratamidaṃ śubham \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. One who bathes early in the morning and feeds the Brahmanas for a period of four months from Ashadha, and gives away a cow in the month of Kartika, goes to the realm of Vishnu. This is (21) Vishnu-Vrata.

## \|\| 101.38-39 \|\|

*ayanādayanaṃ yāvad varjayetpuṣpasarpiṣī \|*  
*tadante puṣpadāmāni ghṛtadhenvā sahaiva tu \|\| 38 \|\|*

*dattvā śivapadaṃ gacched viprāya ghṛtapāyasam \|*  
*etacchīlavrataṃ nāma śīlārogyaphalapradam \|\| 39 \|\|*

38-39. One who abstains from flowers and clarified butter from one solstice to another and at the end of that period gives garlands, clarified butter, and cows to a Brahmana, and feeds them on clarified butter, rice cooked in milk and sugar, goes to the region of Shiva. This is (22) Shila-Vrata, the giver of modesty and good health.

## \|\| 101.40-41 \|\|

*saṃdhyādīpaprado yastu samāṃ tailaṃ vivarjayet \|*  
*samānte dīpikāṃ dadyāc cakraśūle ca kāñcane \|\| 40 \|\|*

*vastraugmaṃ ca viprāya tejasvī sa bhavediha \|*  
*rudralokamavāpnoti dīptivratamidaṃ smṛtam \|\| 41 \|\|*

40-41. One who voluntarily provides light (to the needy) every evening for a year and abstains from oil and then gives a lamp, 4 quoit and a trident of gold, along with a pair of cloths to a Brahmana, is born as a man of greatness and power in this world and ultimately goes to the domain of Shiva. This is (23) Dipti-Vrata.

## \|\| 101.42-43 \|\|

*kārttikyāditṛtīyāyāṃ prāṣya gomūtrayāvakam \|*  
*naktaṃ caredabdamekam abdānte goprado bhavet \|\| 42 \|\|*

*gaurīloke vasetkalpaṃ tato rājā bhavediha \|*  
*etadrudravrataṃ nāma sadā kalyāṇakārakam \|\| 43 \|\|*

42-43. One who takes for a year barley soaked in the cow’s urine at night, on the third day of the month of Kartika, etc., and then gives away a cow, resides in the realm of the Goddess Parvati, and is afterwards born as a king on this land. ‘This is (24) Rudra-Vrata, the giver of everlasting happiness

## \|\| 101.44 \|\|

*varjayeccaitramāse ca yaśca gandhānulepanam \|*  
*śuktiṃ gandhabhṛtāṃ dattvā viprāya sitavāsasī \|*  
*vāruṇaṃ padamāpnoti dṛḍhavratamidaṃ smṛtam \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. One who does 10t use sandal, incense, etc., in the month of Chaitra and gives away mother-of-pearl, full of scent, along with a pair of white cloths, goes to the region of Varuna. This is (25) Dridha-Vrata.

## \|\| 101.45 \|\|

*vaiśākhe puṣpalavaṇaṃ varjayitvātha gopradaḥ \|*  
*bhūtvā viṣṇupade kalpaṃ sthitvā rājā bhavediha \|*  
*etatkāntivrataṃ nāma kāntikīrtiphalapradam \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. One who gives up flowers and salt during Vaishakha, and gives away a cow, goes to the kingdom of Vishnu where he resides for a kalpa, and then is born a king. This is (26) Kanti-Vrata, the giver of lustre and fame.

## \|\| 101.46-48 \|\|

*brahmāṇḍaṃ kāñcanaṃ kṛtvā tilarāśisamanvitam \|*  
*tryahaṃ tilaprado bhūtvā vahniṃ saṃtarpya sadvijam \|\| 46 \|\|*

*sampūjya vipradāmpatyaṃ mālyavastravibhūṣaṇaiḥ \|*  
*śaktitastripalādūrdhvaṃ viśvātmā prīyatāmiti \|\| 47 \|\|*

*puṇye 'hni dadyātsa paraṃ brahma yātyapunarbhavam \|*  
*etadbrahmavrataṃ nāma nirvāṇapadadāyakam \|\| 48 \|\|*

46-48. One who makes a golden globe of the universe weighing more than 12 tolas, (3 palas), according to his means, places it on a mound of sesamum, and offers the latter to the Brahmanas for three days, and libation to fire, honours the Brahmana couple with clothes, garlands, ornaments, etc., after reciting, ‘O Lord of the Universe, be pleased’ (Vishvatma priyatam), liberates himself from the cycle of birth and becomes unified with Brahma. This is (27) Brahma-Vrata, the giver of Nirvana.

## \|\| 101.49 \|\|

*yaścobhayamukhīṃ dadyāt prabhūtakanakānvitām \|*  
*dinaṃ payovratastiṣṭhet sa yāti paramaṃ padam \|*  
*etaddhenuvrataṃ nāma punarāvṛttidurlabham \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. One who lives on milk in course of the day, and gives away a twofaced (ubhaimukhi) cow (i.e., half delivered of her calf) made of a big lump of gold, attains the highest bliss. This is (28) Dhenu-Vrata, which makes re-birth almost impossible.

## \|\| 101.50 \|\|

*tryahaṃ payovrate sthitvā kāñcanaṃ kalpapādapam \|*  
*palādūrdhvaṃ yathāśaktyā taṇḍulais tūpasaṃyutam \|*  
*dattvā brahmapadaṃ yāti kalpavratamidaṃ smṛtam \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. One who lives on milk for three days and then gets a kalpa tree of gold made, weighing more than 4 tolas (one pala), according to his means, and then gives it away with a heap of rice, becomes unified with Brahma. This is (29) Kalpa-Vrata,

## \|\| 101.51 \|\|

*māsopavāsī yo dadyād dhenuṃ viprāya śobhanām \|*  
*sa vaiṣṇavaṃ padaṃ yati bhīmavratamidaṃ smṛtam \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. One who fasts for a month, gives away a beautiful cow to a Brahmana, goes to the realm of Vishnu. This is (30) Bhumi-Vrata.

## \|\| 101.52 \|\|

*dadyād viṃśatpalādūrdhvaṃ mahīṃ kṛtvā tu kāñcanīm \|*  
*dinaṃ payovratastiṣṭhed rudraloke mahīyate \|*  
*dharāvratamidaṃ proktaṃ saptakalpaśatānugam \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. One who after living on milk on the day, gives away an image of earth made of gold, weighing more than 20 palas, resides respected in the domain of Shiva for 700 kalpas. This is (31) Dhara-Vrata.

## \|\| 101.53 \|\|

*māghe māse 'thavā caitre guḍadhenuprado bhavet \|*  
*guḍavratastṛtīyāyāṃ gaurīloke mahīyate \|*  
*mahāvratamidaṃ nāma paramānandakārakam \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. One who gives away a cow, made of molasses, on the third day of Magha or Chaitra, having observed the Guda-Vrata on that day, goes to the realm of Gauri. This is (32) Maha-Vrata.

## \|\| 101.54 \|\|

*pakṣopavāsī yo dadyād viprāya kapilādvayam \|*  
*brahmalokamavāpnoti devāsurasupūjitam \|*  
*kalpānte rājarājaḥ syāt prabhāvratamidaṃ smṛtam \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. One who gives a pair of tawny colour cows (kapila) to a Brahmana, after fasting for a fortnight, goes to the Brahmaloka honoured by Devas and Asuras, and at the end of the kalpa becomes the monarch of kings. This is (33) Prabha-Vrata.

## \|\| 101.55 \|\|

*vatsaraṃ tvekabhaktāśī sabhakṣyajalakumbhadaḥ \|*  
*śivaloke vasetkalpaṃ prāptivratamidaṃ smṛtam \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. One who lives upon only one meal a day for a year, and then gives away a pitcher of water, along with various kinds of eatables, resides in the dominion of Shiva for a kalpa. This is (34) Prapti-Vrata.

## \|\| 101.56 \|\|

*naktāśī cāṣṭamīṣu syād vatsarānte ca dhenudaḥ \|*  
*pauraṃdaraṃ puraṃ yāti sugativratamucyate \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. One who has only one meal in the evening, on the 8th day of a month, for one year, and then gives away cows in charity, goes to the region of Indra. This is (35) Sugati-Vrata.

## \|\| 101.57 \|\|

*viprāyendhanado yastu varṣādicaturastvṛtūn \|*  
*ghṛtadhenuprado 'nte ca sa paraṃ brahma gacchati \|*  
*vaiśvānaravrataṃ nāma sarvapāpavināśanam \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. One who gives fuel to the Brahmanas during the rainy season and at the end of the year gives away a cow of clarified butter, becomes unified with the supreme Brahma. This is (36) Vaishvanara-Vrata — the destroyer of all ills.

## \|\| 101.58 \|\|

*ekādaśyāṃ ca naktāśī yaścakraṃ vinivedayet \|*  
*samānte vaiṣṇavaṃ haimaṃ sa viṣṇoḥ padamāpnuyāt \|*  
*etat kṛṣṇavrataṃ nāma kalpānte rājyabhāgbhavet \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. The devotee who, on the 11th day of each month, has his meal in the night and then gives to the Vaishnava a quoit made of gold, goes and resides in the realm of Vishnu for one kalpa, at the end of which he is born a great king. This is (37) Krishna-Vrata.

## \|\| 101.59 \|\|

*pāyasāśī samānte tu dadyādviprāya goyugam \|*  
*lakṣmīlokamavāpnoti hy etad devīvrataṃ smṛtam \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. One who gives away a pair of cows after living on milk for a year, goes to the kingdom of Lakshmi. This is (38) Devi-Vrata.

## \|\| 101.60 \|\|

*saptamyāṃ naktabhugdadyāt samānte gāṃ payasvinīm \|*  
*sūryalokamavāpnoti bhānuvratamidaṃ smṛtam \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. One who gives away 2 milk cow at the end of a year, after living only on milk, on the night of every seventh day of each month, goes to the domain of the Sun. This is (39, Bhanu-Vrata.

## \|\| 101.61 \|\|

*caturthyāṃ naktabhugdadyād abdānte hemavāraṇam \|*  
*vrataṃ vaināyakaṃ nāma śivalokaphalapradam \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. One who has his meals at night of the 4th day of each month, and at the end of the year gives away an elephant, made of gold, goes to the realm of Shiva. This is (40) Vainayaka-Vrata.

## \|\| 101.62 \|\|

*mahāphalāni yastyaktvā caturmāsaṃ dvijātaye \|*  
*haimāni kārttike dadyād goyugena samanvitam \|*  
*etat phalavrataṃ nāma viṣṇulokaphalapradam \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. One who abstains from larger fruits (Maha-phala’ during the Chaturmasa, and gives away the same fruits made of gold, along with a pair of cows to a Brahmana, goes to the realm of Vishnu. This is (41) Phala-Vrata.

**Комментарий:**

\[Note. — Chaturmasa = A period of four months reckoned from the eleventh day in the bright half of Ashadha to the 11th day in the bright half of Kartika.\]

## \|\| 101.63 \|\|

*yaścopavāsī saptamyāṃ samānte haimapaṅkajam \|*  
*gāśca vai śaktito dadyād dhemānnaghaṭasaṃyutāḥ \|*  
*etat sauravrataṃ nāma sūryalokaphalapradam \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. One who keeps a (total: fast on the seventh day of each month for a year, and then gives away a lotus of gold, a golden vase, full of grain, and cows, according to his means, goes to the domain of the Sun. This is (42) Surya-Vrata.

## \|\| 101.64 \|\|

*dvādaśa dvādaśīryastu samāpyopoṣaṇena ca \|*  
*govastrakāñcanairviprān pūjayecchaktito naraḥ \|*  
*paramaṃ padaṃ prāpnoti viṣṇuvratamidaṃ smṛtam \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. One who keeps a (total) fast on the L2th day of each month, and then at the end of the year gives away to the Brahmanas, according to his means cows, cloths and gold, attains beatitude. This is (43) Vishnu-Vrata,

## \|\| 101.65 \|\|

*kārttikyāṃ ca vṛṣotsargaṃ kṛtvā naktaṃ samācaret \|*  
*śaivaṃ padamavāpnoti vārṣavratamidaṃ smṛtam \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. One who, after performing Vrishotsarga in the month of Kartika, lives on only one meal a day and that at night, for a full year, goes to the realm of Shiva. This is (44) Varsha-Vrata.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — Vrishotsarga = Setting free a bull on the occasion of a funeral rite, or as a religious act generally.

## \|\| 101.66 \|\|

*kṛcchrānte gopradaḥ kuryād bhojanaṃ śaktitaḥ padam \|*  
*viprāṇāṃ śāṃkaraṃ yāti prājāpatyamidaṃ vratam \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. One who, on the conclusion of Chandrayana (or Krichhra) observance gives away a cow and feeds the Brahmanas, according to his means goes to the realm of Shiva. This is (45) Prajapatya-Vrata.

## \|\| 101.67 \|\|

*caturdaśyāṃ tu naktāśī samānte godhanapradaḥ \|*  
*śaivaṃ padamavāpnoti traiyambakamidaṃ vratam \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. Ono who lives only on the nightly meal, on the 14th day of each month. for a year, and then gives away cows, goes to the region of Shiva. This is (46) Trayambaka-V rata.

## \|\| 101.68 \|\|

*saptarātroṣito dadyād ghṛtakumbhaṃ dvijātaye \|*  
*ghṛtavratamidaṃ prāhur brahmalokaphalapradam \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. One who keeps a continuous fast for seven nights, and then gives a pot of clarified butter to a Brahmana, goes to the region of Brahma. This is (47) Ghrita-Vrata.

## \|\| 101.69 \|\|

*ākāśaśāyī varṣāsu dhenumante payasvinīm \|*  
*śakraloke vasennityam indravratamidaṃ smṛtam \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. One who sleeps in Akasha during the rainy season, and then gives away a milk cow, goes to the region of Indra. This is (48) Indra-Vrata.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — Akasha, — Ether, Vacuity, Place in general, Light, Hole, in the air, etc.

## \|\| 101.70 \|\|

*anagnipakkam aśnāti tṛtīyāyāṃ tu yo naraḥ \|*  
*gāṃ dattvā śivamabhyeti punarāvṛttidurlabham \|*  
*iha cānandakṛtpuṃsāṃ śreyovratamidaṃ smṛtam \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. One who takes the uncooked eatables on the third day of each month, and then gives away cows, goes to the realm of Shiva, after being liberated from the cycle of birth. This is (49) Kalyana (or Shreyo) Vrata, the giver of happiness.

## \|\| 101.71 \|\|

*haimaṃ paladvayādūrdhvaṃ rathamaśvaugānvitam \|*  
*dadatkṛtopavāsaḥ syād divi kalpaśataṃ vaset \|*  
*kalpānte rājarājaḥ syād aśvavratamidaṃ smṛtam \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. One who gives away a chariot with the horses made of gold weighing more than 8 tolas (2 palas), after fasting in course of the day, resides in the heaven for a hundred kalpas, and then becomes the King of Kings. This is (50) Ashva-Vrata.

## \|\| 101.72 \|\|

*tadvaddhemarathaṃ dadyāt karibhyāṃ saṃyutaṃ naraḥ \|*  
*satyaloke vasetkalpaṃ sahasramatha bhūpatiḥ \|*  
*bhavedupoṣito bhūtvā karivratamidaṃ smṛtam \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. And one who, similarly, observes the fast and gives away a chariot, with a pair of elephants made of gold, resides in the Satyaloka for a thousand kalpas, and is then horn as a King. This is (51) Hasti-Vrata.

## \|\| 101.73 \|\|

*upavāsaṃ parityajya samānte goprado bhavet \|*  
*yakṣādhipatyamāpnoti sukhavratamidaṃ smṛtam \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. One who gives away a cow at the end of his yearly fast, becomes the Lord of Yakshas. ‘This is (62) Sukha-Vrata.

## \|\| 101.74 \|\|

*niśi kṛtvā jale vāsaṃ prabhāte goprado bhavet \|*  
*vāruṇaṃ lokamāpnoti varuṇavratamucyate \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. One who gives away a cow in the morning, after passing the night In water, goes to the realm of Varuna. Tis is (53) Varuna-Vrata.

## \|\| 101.75 \|\|

*cāndrāyaṇaṃ ca yaḥ kuryād dhaimaṃ candraṃ nivedayet \|*  
*candravratamidaṃ proktaṃ candralokaphalapradam \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. One who gives away a moon of gold at the end of the Chandrayana ordinance, goes to the realm of the moon, This is (54) Chandra-Vrata.

## \|\| 101.76 \|\|

*jyeṣṭhe pañcatapāḥ sāyaṃ hemadhenuprado divam \|*  
*yātyaṣṭamīcaturdaśyo rudravratamidaṃ smṛtam \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. One who gives away cows in the evening, after warming himself with five fires (panchatapa), on the 8th and the 14th day in the month of Jyaishtha, goes to heaven. This is Rudra-Vrata.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — A modification Vrata №2.

## \|\| 101.77 \|\|

*sakṛdvitānakaṃ kuryāt tṛtīyāyāṃ śivālaye \|*  
*samānte dhenudo yāti bhavānīvratamucyate \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. One who makes a canopy, in a temple of Shiva, on the third day of a month and gives away a cow at the end of the year, goes to the region of Shiva. — This is (55) Bhavani-Vrata.

## \|\| 101.78 \|\|

*māghe niśyārdravāsāḥ syāt saptamyāṃ goprado bhavet \|*  
*divi kalpamuṣitveha rājā syātpavanaṃ vratam \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. In the month of Magha, one who wears wet garments in the night and on the seventh day of the month gives away cows, goes and resides in the heaven for a kalpa, after which he is born as a King. This is (56) Pavana-Vrata

## \|\| 101.79 \|\|

*trirātropoṣito dadyāt phālgunyāṃ bhavanaṃ śubham \|*  
*ādityalokamāpnoti dhāmavratamidaṃ smṛtam \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. One who maintains a fast for three nights and gives away a good house in the month of Phalguna, goes-to-the domain of the San. This is (57) Dhama Vrata

## \|\| 101.80 \|\|

*trisaṃdhyaṃ pūjya dāmpatyam upavāsī vibhūṣaṇaiḥ \|*  
*annaṃ gāśca samāpnoti mokṣamindravratādiha \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. One who adores the Brahmana and his wife with ornaments and gives away cows along with grain, on three evenings, after observing a fast in the day, attains beatitude. This is (58) Indra-Vrata.

## \|\| 101.81 \|\|

*dattvā sitadvitīyāyām indorlavaṇabhājanam \|*  
*samānte goprado yāti viprāya śivamandiram \|*  
*kalpānte rājarājaḥ syāt somavratamidaṃ smṛtam \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. One who gives away a vessel of salt in the name of the moon, on the second day of the bright fortnight, and at the end of the year gives cows to the Brahmanas, goes to the realm of Shiva, and at the end of the kalpa becomes the King of Kings. ‘This is (59) Soma-Vrata.

## \|\| 101.82 \|\|

*pratipadyekabhaktāśī samānte kapilāpradaḥ \|*  
*vaiśvānarapadaṃ yāti śivavratamidaṃ smṛtam \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. One who has only one meal a day on each Pratipada (first day of a fortnight), and at the end of the year gives away a tawny coloured cow (kapila), goes to the domain of Agni. This is called Shiva-Vrata.

## \|\| 101.83 \|\|

*daśamyām ekabhaktāśī samānte daśadhenudaḥ \|*  
*diśaśca kāñcanairdadyād brahmāṇḍādhipatirbhavet \|*  
*etad viśvavrataṃ nāma mahāpātakanāśanam \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. One who has only one meal a day on the tenth day of the month, and alter a year gives away ten cows, along with the images of ten directions made of gold, becomes the lord of the universe. This is called the (60) Vishva-Vrata, the destroyer of all ills.

## \|\| 101.84 \|\|

*yaḥ paṭhecchṛṇuyādvāpi vrataṣaṣṭim anuttamām \|*  
*manvantaraśataṃ so 'pi gandharvādhipatirbhavet \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. One who reads, or relates about these sixty ordinances, remains the lord of Gandharvas, for a period of one hundred Manvantaras.

## \|\| 101.85 \|\|

*ṣaṣṭivrataṃ nārada puṇyametat tavoditaṃ viśvajanīnamanyat \|*  
*śrotuṃ tavecchā tadudīrayāmi priyeṣu kiṃ vākathanīyam asti \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. Narada! I have related to you about the sixty ordinances; now let me know what more you desire to hear, which is for the benefit of the world, IT shall tell you all. What may I not say to my favoured ones?

## Chapter 102

## \|\| 102.1 \|\|

*nandikeśvara uvāca*  
*nairmalyaṃ bhāvaśuddhiśca vinā snānaṃ na vidyate \|*  
*tasmānmanoviśuddhyarthaṃ snānamādau vidhīyate \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Nandikeshvara said: — Narada! There cannot be purity of body gad mind without bathing, therefore to keep the mind refreshed it is essential to bathe first of all.

## \|\| 102.2 \|\|

*anuddhṛtairuddhṛtairvā jalaiḥ snānaṃ samācaret \|*  
*tīrthaṃ ca kalpayedvidvān mūlamantreṇa mantravit \|*  
*namo nārāyaṇāyeti mūlamantra udāhṛtaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2 “Om Namo Narayanaya” is the principal mantra, by the recitation of which the tirtha should be conceived in the water in which bath is to be taken, whether that water is taken out from the main source (e.g., river), or well, tank, etc.

**Комментарий:**

Notes —

(a) Tirtha. — A holy place, A place of water.

(b) Namo Narayaniya. — Salutations to Narayana.

(c) This means that-a person bathing at a well or elsewhere — other than in.

the sacred waters, wiz — the Ganges, the Narmada, &c. — if one recites the above formula with devotion and philosophically conceives and invokes the presence of some sacred tirtha in his bathing water, his fervent devotion fulfills his object. A good bath in a pure and running stream is essential to refresh the mind thoroughly, The Ganges, the Narmada, &c., are undauntedly the best of the rivers for the purpose from many points of view, and consequently so much sanctity is attached to such invigorating streams, A true Aryan is expected to bathe daily in such streams, bub everyone is not so situated as to have the benefit of such a bath daily. Those, therefore, who are not so placed, may bathe as stated above which would fulfil their duty of bathing unavoidably in a place other than a tirtha, for under the influence of a fervent devotion they will feel as if they were bathing in some sacred waters; and the feeling of sanctity that attaches in the mind of an Aryan to invigorating streams would be kept evergreen which would take him oftener to such Briefly speaking, therefore, a man should bathe daily Lo refresh his mind.
