He should bathe in a pure and fresh stream, as far as possible, barring which he should work up his devotion to help him in not breaking the rile and in keeping his mind refreshed and his desire fixed on some sacred stream.

## \|\| 102.3-5 \|\|

*darbhapāṇistu vidhinā ācāntaḥ prayataḥ śuciḥ \|*  
*caturhastasamāuktaṃ caturasraṃ samantataḥ \|*  
*prakalpyāvāhayed gaṅgām ebhirmantrairvicakṣaṇaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*viṣṇoḥ pādaprasūtāsi vaiṣṇavī viṣṇudevatā \|*  
*pāhi nas tvenasas tasmād ājanmamaraṇāntikāt \|\| 4 \|\|*

*tisraḥ koṭyo 'rdhakoṭī ca tīrthānāṃ vāurabravīt \|*  
*divi bhuvyantarikṣe ca tāni te santi jāhnavi \|\| 5 \|\|*

3-5. He should put on the rings of kusha grass and rinse his mouth with a little water — according to the prescribed form — and then with a calm mind he should conceive within a square, measuring four bands, the sacred Gauges and invoke Her there thus: — ‘O Ganges! Thou art born from the foot of Vishnu, thou art a Vishnu force, and loved by Vishnu, Thou art Vishnu-devata; ward my sins off from the time of my birth to death. The 33 crores of tirthas of heaven, earth and sky are absorbed in Thee, as stated by Vayu

## \|\| 102.6-8 \|\|

*nandinītyeva te nāma deveṣu nalinīti ca \|*  
*dakṣā pṛthvī ca vihagā viśvakāyāmṛtā śivā \|\| 6 \|\|*

*vidyādharī supraśāntā tathā viśvaprasādinī \|*  
*kṣemā ca jāhnavī caiva śāntā śāntipradāyinī \|\| 7 \|\|*

*etāni puṇyanāmāni snānakāle prakīrtayet \|*  
*bhavetsaṃnihitā tatra gaṅgā tripathagāminī \|\| 8 \|\|*

6-8. O Ganges! the Devas call Thee Nandini, Nalini, Daksha, Prithwi, Vihaga, Vishvakaya, Amrita, Shiva, Vidyadhari, Suprashanta, Vishva-prasadini, Kshema, Jahnavi, Santa, Santipradayani; these, too, are thy epithets; and one who recites these sacred names with true devotion, at the time of his bath, finds Tripathagamini (going three ways) Ganga there.”

**Комментарий:**

Note. — Nandini. — Lit. gladdening. An epithet of the Ganges, for Her waters are so refreshing and Her flow so pleasing.

Nalini — Lit. a lotus plant. A place abounding in lotuses. The intoxicating juice of the cocoanut. The Ganges, fur Her waters are so invigorating.

Daksha. — Lit. one who moves or acts quickly. The Ganges, because Her stream is so rapid and Her waters infuse freshness and vigour so quickly.

Prithivi. — Lit. Earth, one of the five elements. — The Ganges, because She is so invigorating. There can be no life without five elements, and the life cannot be sustained without there being some vigour.

Vihaga. — Lit. a bird. An arrow. The Ganges, because she flows so swiftly.

Vishva-Kaya. — This is a compound word made up of Vishva- universe and Kaya = Capital, abode, Principal, Body. The expression Vishva-kaya = Capital, abode, body or principal (tirtha) of, the universe, and is an epithet of the Ganges; for she is the Capital of all the Aryan tirthas. She is the abode of pious Aryans, who in their lifetime pass their days in contemplation on Her banks and their remains ultimately find an abode in the sacred waters. She is the principal tirtha of the universe. She is the body of the universe, in the sense that, water is one of the 5 elements in the body and the water, as each an element, means purest water. The Ganges water being so best can be compared with the purest water as one of the elements.

Vishvakaya, as one word, may also mean produced from the body of Shiva: A for Vishva is and epithet of Shiva also. It is said that the Ganges fell on the head of Shiva from the heaven, and thence she moved on to the world below, which is a simple fact, for the clouds hang about in the heavens and discharge themselves in form of snows on the lofty peaks of mountains. The Kailasa peak in the Himalayas is the region of perpetual snows, where the snow being crushed by its own weight flows downward, and reaching a certain level is converted into water which in its tarn flows onwards in form of a river. Now, Kailasa is the abode of Shiva, and the Ganges has its source in the Himalayas near it The snows of Kailasa being the chief feeder of the river.

Amrita, — Lit. imperishable, beautiful, agreeable, final beatitude, nectar of immortality, beverage of the Gods, sweet An epithet of the Ganges, because she is imperishable, beautiful, agreeable in the sense of refreshing. She is considered by the Aryans to be the giver of final beatitude. Her water is sweet and is often compared with the Nectar and the beverage of the gods.

Shiva, — Lit, final beatitude. Born of Shiva Vidyadhari. — Lit. a class of demi-gods. The Ganges, on account of her purific properties, is regarded as such.

Suprashanta — The giver of tranquility. Serene.

Vishva Prashadini. — The purifier of the universe.

Kshema. — The giver of happiness and comfort.

Jahnavi. — The Ganges, when brought down from heaven by the austerities of Bhagiratha, was forced to flow over earth to follow him to the lower regions. In its course it inundated the sacrificial ground of the King Jahnu who got very much vexed and swallowed the stream; but his wrath was appeased by the prayers of the Gods, gages and Bhagiratha, and he discharged the current from his ears, The Ganges is therefore regarded as his daughter and is called Jahnavi.

Shanti-pradayini = The giver of peace.

Santa = The peaceful.

## \|\| 102.9 \|\|

*saptavārābhijaptena karasampuṭayojitaḥ \|*  
*mūrdhni kuryādjalaṃ bhūyas tricatuṣpañcasaptakam \|*  
*snānaṃ kuryānmṛdā tadvad āmantrya tu vidhānataḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. One should hold water in both the hands, and after 7 times reciting the mantras mentioned above, sprinkle it on his head 8, 4, Sand 7 times and then bathe, after rubbing some earth on his body with proper invokation thus:

## \|\| 102.10 \|\|

*aśvakrānte rathakrānte viṣṇukrānte vasuṃdhare \|*  
*mṛttike hara me pāpaṃ yanmayā duṣkṛtaṃ kṛtam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. “O Earth! trodden by the horse (Ashvakranti) and the chariot (Rathakranti) and belonging to the base of the temple of Vishnu (Vishnukranti) dispel my sins stored from generations”.

## \|\| 102.11 \|\|

*uddhṛtāsi varāheṇa kṛṣṇena śatabāhunā \|*  
*mṛttike brahmadattāsi kāṣyapenābhimantritā \|*  
*āruhya mama gātrāṇi sarvaṃ pāpaṃ pracodaya \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. “O Earth! Krishna hast dug Thee out by assuming the form of the wild boar with a hundred hands. Thou art the element employed when empowered by the mantra of Kashyapa in the creation of all beings by Brahma. By your contact (as you encircle my bod y) purify my body of all sins.

## \|\| 102.12 \|\|

*mṛttike dehi naḥ puṣṭiṃ tvayi sarvaṃ pratiṣṭhitam \|*  
*namaste sarvalokānāṃ prabhavāraṇi suvrate \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. “O Earth, in Thee are all things. Thou givest us nourishment.

Thou art the source of all lokas (worlds). I salute Thee.”

## \|\| 102.13 \|\|

*evaṃ snātvā tataḥ paścād ācamya ca vidhānataḥ \|*  
*utthāya vāsasī śukle śuddhe tu paridhāya vai \|*  
*tatastu tarpaṇaṃ kuryāt trailokyāpyāyanāya vai \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. After thus taking his bath, one should again rinse his mouth and change his clothes, putting on white garments and present libations of water as follows:

## \|\| 102.14-15 \|\|

*devā yakṣāstathā nāgā gandharvāpsaraso 'surāḥ \|*  
*krūrāḥ sarpāḥ suparṇāśca taravo jambukāḥ khagāḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*vāyvādhārā jalādhārās tathaivākāśagāminaḥ \|*  
*nirādhārāśca ye jīvā ye tu dharmaratāstathā \|\| 15 \|\|*

14-15. Devas, Yakshas, Nagas, Gandharvas, Apsaras, Asuras, ferocious — serpents, suparnas (a class of bird like beings of a semi-Divine character), trees, jackals &c., the beings living in the air, the beings living in water.

the beings traversing in the sky, the beings without any one to offer them libations, the pious ones, I offer you all these libations.” Libations to the Devas should he made with the sacred thread on the right shoulder.

## \|\| 102.16-17 \|\|

*teṣāmāpyāyanāyaitad dīyate salilaṃ mayā \|*  
*kṛtopavītī devebhyo nivītī ca bhavettataḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*manuṣyāṃstarpayedbhaktyā brahmaputrānṛṣīṃstathā \|*  
*sanakaśca sanandaśca tṛtīyaśca sanātanaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

16-17. Then libations should he offered with devotion to the manes, sans of Brahma and the Rishis. “Sanaka, Sananda, Sanatana, Kapila, Bodhu, Panchasikha, receive and be gratified with the libations I offer you.

## \|\| 102.18 \|\|

*kapilaścāsuriścaiva voḍhuḥ pañcaśikhastathā \|*  
*sarve te tṛptimāyāntu maddattenāmbunā sadā \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Afterwards, Marichi, Atri, Angira, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu, Pracheta, Vasistha, Bhrigu, Narada, Devarshis and Brahmarshis should be offered libations with uncooked rice and water.

## \|\| 102.19-20 \|\|

*marīcimatryaṅgirasaṃ pulastyaṃ pulahaṃ kratum \|*  
*pracetasaṃ vasiṣṭhaṃ ca bhṛguṃ nāradameva ca \|*  
*devabrahmaṛṣīn sarvāṃs tarpayed akṣataudakaiḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

*apasavyaṃ tataḥ kṛtvā savyaṃ jānvācya bhūtale \|*  
*agniṣvāttāstathā saumyā haviṣmantastathoṣmapāḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

19-20. Then, with the sacred thread on the left shoulder and reclining on the left knee the Pitris, Agnishvata, Saumya. Havishmanta, Ushmapa, Sukalina, Barhishada, and Ajyapa, should he offered libations with water, sesamum and sandal, &c.

## \|\| 102.21-22 \|\|

*sukālino barhiṣadas tathānye vājyapāḥ punaḥ \|*  
*saṃtarpyāḥ pitaro bhaktyā satilodakacandanaiḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*yamāya dharmarājāya mṛtyave cāntakāya ca \|*  
*vaivasvatāya kālāya sarvabhṛtakṣayāya ca \|\| 22 \|\|*

21-22. After reciting the names which are synonyms of Yama, viz., Dharmaraja, Mrityu, Antaka, Vaivaswata, Kala, Sarvabhutakshavya, Audumbara, Dadhna, Nila, Paramesthi, Vrikodara, Chitra and Chitragupta libations should be offered to him; and then after holding the Kusha in hand as prescribed, libations to the manes should be offered by the wise.

## \|\| 102.23 \|\|

*audumbarāya dadhnāya nīlāya parameṣṭhine \|*  
*vṛkodarāya citrāya citraguptāya vai namaḥ \|*  
*darbhapāṇistu vidhinā pitrinsaṃtarpayedbudhaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Alter reciting the names and the gotras of fathers and maternal grandfathers, libations should be offered to them, after which the following mantra should be uttered with devotion:

## \|\| 102.24 \|\|

*pitrādīnnāmagotreṇa tathā mātāmahānapi \|*  
*saṃtarpya vidhinā bhaktyā imaṃ mantramudīrayet \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. “Those who may be my kith and kin, those who may have been my kith and kin in some other previous birth, may feel gratified by the libations that I offer them."

## \|\| 102.25 \|\|

*ye 'bāndhavā bāndhavā vā ye 'nyajanmani bāndhavāḥ \|*  
*te tṛptimakhilāṃ yāntu yaś cāsmatto 'bhivāñchati \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. After this, the devotee should again rinse his mouth and draw the figure of a lotus in front of him on which libations of water (arghya), mixed with uncooked rice, flowers and red sandal should be offered to the Sun, after which His (Sun's; names should be recited.

## \|\| 102.26 \|\|

*tataścācamya vidhivad ālikhetpadmamagrataḥ \|*  
*akṣatābhiḥ sapuṣpābhiḥ sajalāruṇacandanam \|*  
*arghyaṃ dadyātprayatnena sūryanāmāni kīrtayet \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. “I salute Thee, O Sun! Thou art Vishnu. Thou art the mouth of Vishnu. Thou hast thousands of rays. ‘Thou art full of lustre and potency."

## \|\| 102.27 \|\|

*namaste viṣṇurūpāya namo viṣṇumukhāya vai \|*  
*sahasraraśmaye nityaṃ namaste sarvatejase \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. “O Shiva! O Lord of all, O Father of all! I salute Thee. O Lord of the universe, whose body is painted with sandal, I salute Thee”.

## \|\| 102.28 \|\|

*namaste śiva sarveśa namaste sarvavatsala \|*  
*jagatsvāminnamaste 'stu divyacandanabhūṣita \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. “O Thou, seated on a lotus, salutations be to Thee, adorned with ear-rings and bracelets, the Lord of all the worlds! Thou bringest light to the worlds! I salute Thee.”

## \|\| 102.29 \|\|

*padmāsana namaste 'stu kuṇḍalāṅgadabhūṣita \|*  
*namaste sarvalokeśa jagatsarvaṃ vibodhase \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. “Thou seest good and had deeds of every one, always. Thou pervadest all. O Satya Deva! salutations be to Thee, Thou, O Bhaskara! be propitious to me.

## \|\| 102.30 \|\|

*sukṛtaṃ duṣkṛtaṃ caiva sarvaṃ paṣyasi sarvaga \|*  
*satyadeva namaste 'stu prasīda mama bhāskara \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. “O day-maker! I salute Thee.” After thus saluting the Sun, the devotee should circumambulate three times, and then, after touching a Brahmana, cow and gold, should go to the temple of Vishnu.

## Chapter 103

## \|\| 103.1 \|\|

*nandikeśvara uvāca*  
*ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi prayāgasyopavarṇanam \|*  
*mārkaṇḍeyena kathitaṃ yatpurā pāṇḍusūnave \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Nandikeshvara Said: — Narada! I shall now relate to you what the sage Markandeya narrated to Yudhisthira about Prayaga, in the days gone by.

## \|\| 103.2-4 \|\|

*bhārate tu yadā vṛtte prāptarājye pṛthāsute \|*  
*etasminnantare rājā kuntīputro udhiṣṭhiraḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*bhrātṛśokena saṃtaptaś cintayansa punaḥ punaḥ \|*  
*āsītsuyodhano rājā ekādaśacamūpatiḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*asmānsaṃtāpya bahuśaḥ sarve te nidhanaṃ gatāḥ \|*  
*vāsudevaṃ samāśritya pañca śeṣāstu pāṇḍavāḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

2-4. Yudhisthira, the son of Kunti became the Lord of the world after the great Mahabharata war. He was very much depressed by the grief of the death of his kinsmen. He said to himself: — “King Duryodhana, the master of armies of eleven akshauhinis, and the other kings who were his allies, are slain, causing me much pain and anguish; and we, five brothers, sons of Pandu, are alive under the shelter of Lord Krishna.

## \|\| 103.5-6 \|\|

*hatvā bhīṣmaṃ ca droṇaṃ ca karṇaṃ caiva mahābalam \|*  
*duryodhanaṃ ca rājānaṃ putrabhrātṛsamanvitam \|\| 5 \|\|*

*rājāno nihatāḥ sarve ye cānye śūramāninaḥ \|*  
*kiṃ no rājyena govinda kiṃ bhogairjīvitena vā \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. “I have killed Bhishma, Drona, the mighty Karna, the King Duryodhana, our kinsmen and other kings, who considered themselves brave soldiers and heroes. “O Govinda! what is now the good of my life, and how and why should I rule the empire?

## \|\| 103.8-9 \|\|

*labdhasaṃjño yadā rājā cintayansa punaḥ punaḥ \|*  
*kataro viniyogo vā niyamaṃ tīrthameva ca \|\| 8 \|\|*

*yenāhaṃ śīghram āmuñce mahāpātakikilbiṣāt \|*  
*yatra sthitvā naro yāti viṣṇulokamanuttamam \|\| 9 \|\|*

8-9. “Fie to me!” Thus oppressed with his thoughts, the mighty King Yudhisthira became very much despondent, and his head bending downwards he fainted. When he came back to his senses, he fell into thought, “Which could be the best religious act that would wash off all my sins, and which could be the sacred place of pilgrimage that would purify me and enable me to go and reside in the world of Vishnu.

## \|\| 103.10 \|\|

*kathaṃ pṛcchāmi vai kṛṣṇaṃ yenedaṃ kārito 'smyaham \|*  
*dhṛtarāṣṭraṃ kathaṃ pṛcche yasya putraśataṃ hatam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. “How possibly can I make enquiries on such points from Shri Krishna, because he has been so much instrumental in the great war. How can I ask Dhritarashtra about these things. I have slain all his song to the number of one hundred.”

## \|\| 103.11-12 \|\|

*vyāsaṃ kathamahaṃ pṛcche yasya gotrakṣayaḥ kṛtaḥ \|*  
*evaṃ vaiklavyamāpanno dharmarājo udhiṣṭhiraḥ \|*  
*rudanti pāṇḍavāḥ sarve bhrātṛśokapariplutāḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*ye ca tatra mahātmānaḥ sametāḥ pāṇḍavāḥ smṛtāḥ \|*  
*kuntī ca draupadī caiva ye ca tatra samāgatāḥ \|*  
*bhūmau nipatitāḥ sarve rudantastu samantataḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-12. Being thus overpowered with grief, Yudhisthira began to weep bitterly and the good men that were there also fell down on the ground, along with Draupadi and Kunti, and began to weep.

## \|\| 103.13-14 \|\|

*vārāṇasyāṃ mārkaṇḍeyas tena jñāto udhiṣṭhiraḥ \|*  
*yathā vaiklavyamāpanno rudamānastu duḥkhitaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*acireṇaiva kālena mārkaṇḍeyo mahātapāḥ \|*  
*samprāpto hāstinapuraṃ rājadvāre hyatiṣṭhata \|\| 14 \|\|*

13-14. At that time, the great sage Markandeya was in Kashi and he knew how much the king was upset with grief. He therefore instantly went to Hastinapura and appeared at the gate of the palace of Yudhishthira.

## \|\| 103.15-17 \|\|

*dvārapālo 'pi taṃ dṛṣṭvā rājñaḥ kathitavāndrutam \|*  
*tvāṃ draṣṭukāmo mārkaṇḍeyo dvāri tiṣṭhatyasau muniḥ \|*  
*tvarito dharmaputrastu dvāramāgādataḥ param \|\| 15 \|\|*

*yudhiṣṭhira uvāca*  
*svāgataṃ te mahābhāga svāgataṃ te mahāmune \|*  
*adya me saphalaṃ janma adya me tāritaṃ kulam \|\| 16 \|\|*

*adya me pitarastuṣṭās tvayi dṛṣṭe mahāmune \|*  
*adyāhaṃ pūtadeho 'smi yattvayā saha darśanam \|\| 17 \|\|*

15-17. The gate-keeper, on seeing the great sage Markandeya, immediately reported his arrival to the king, who, without the least delay, repaired to the door to accord him a fitting reception, and said “O Sage! you are most welcome. By your having so kindly graced me with your presence, I feel that the mission of my life has been fulfilled and that my family has been liberated from all sins. O Sage! the manes of my deceased ancestors have also become gratified by your presence, and I feel myself purified in your presence”.

## \|\| 103.18 \|\|

*nandikeśvara uvāca*  
*siṃhāsane samāsthāpya pādaśaucārcanādibhiḥ \|*  
*yudhiṣṭhiro mahātmā vai pūjayāmāsa taṃ munim \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Nandikeshvara said: — “O Narada! After thus according him a welcome, the king washed his, feet and seating him on his throne, he worshipped the great sage.

## \|\| 103.19 \|\|

*tataḥ sa tuṣṭo mārkaṇḍaḥ pūjitaścāha taṃ nṛpam \|*  
*ākhyāhi tvaritaṃ rājan kimarthaṃ ruditaṃ tvayā \|*  
*kena vā viklavībhūtaḥ kā bādhā te kimapriyam \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Markandeya said: — King! what ails your mind so much. Pray tell me at once without the least reserve the cause of your mental agony.

## \|\| 103.20 \|\|

*yudhiṣṭhira uvāca*  
*asmākaṃ caiva yadvṛttaṃ rājyasyārthe mahāmune \|*  
*etatsarvaṃ viditvā tu cintāvaśamupāgataḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20 Yudhisthira said: — “O great sage! my thoughts over my doings for the gaining of this kingdom haunt me and choke me with intense grief”.

## \|\| 103.21-22 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca*  
*śṛṇu rājanmahābāho kṣatradharmavyavasthitam \|*  
*naiva dṛṣṭaṃ raṇe pāpaṃ udhyamānasya dhīmataḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*kiṃ punā rājadharmeṇa kṣatriyasya viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*tadevaṃ hṛdayaṃ kṛtvā tasmātpāpaṃ na cintayet \|\| 22 \|\|*

21-22. Markandeya said: — “King! hear the duties of an ideal Kshatriya. It is no sin for a wise man to fight; and for a king there is absolutely no sin to wage war to acquire his kingdom. Do not therefore allow yourself to be carried away by any such feeling that you have committed a sin.

## \|\| 103.23-24 \|\|

*tato udhiṣṭhiro rājā praṇamya śirasā munim \|*  
*papraccha vinayopetaḥ sarvapātakanāśanam \|\| 23 \|\|*

*yudhiṣṭhira uvāca*  
*pṛcchāmi tvāṃ mahāprājña nityaṃ trailokyadarśinam \|*  
*kathaya tvaṃ samāsena yena mucyeta kilbiṣāt \|\| 24 \|\|*

23-24. On hearing these words of the sage Markandeya, Yudhisthira fell prostrate at his feet and begged him to tell something that would wash off all his sins.

## \|\| 103.25 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca*  
*śṛṇu rājanmahābāho sarvapātakanāśanam \|*  
*prayāgagamanaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ narāṇāṃ puṇyakarmaṇām \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Markandeya said: — King! I tell you the way how to destroy all your sins. Hear it with attention. It is very great merit for pious people to go to Prayaga.

## Chapter 104

## \|\| 104.1 \|\|

*yudhiṣṭhira uvāca*  
*bhagavañchrotumicchāmi purā kalpe yathāsthitam \|*  
*brahmaṇā devamukhyena yathāvatkathitaṃ mune \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Yudhisthira said: — Brahmana! I am desirous of hearing what Lord Brahma had said in the days gone by.

## \|\| 104.2 \|\|

*kathaṃ prayāgagamanaṃ narāṇāṃ tatra kīdṛśam \|*  
*mṛtānāṃ kā gatistatra snātānāṃ tatra kiṃ phalam \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. How should people go to the sacred place of Prayaga? Pray also tell me what benefits do they reap who die, bathe and live there?

## \|\| 104.3 \|\|

*ye vasanti prayāge tu brūhi teṣāṃ ca kiṃ phalam \|*  
*etanme sarvamākhyāhi paraṃ kautūhalaṃ hi me \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Markandeya said: — Son! I shall tell you the chief benefits from a pilgrimage to Prayaga, as I have heard them from the good sages in the past.

## \|\| 104.4 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca*  
*kathayiṣyāmi te vatsa yacchreṣṭhaṃ tatra yatphalam \|*  
*purā hi sarvaviprāṇāṃ kathyamānaṃ mayā śrutam \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. From the site of the sacred Prayaga, in the town of Pratisthana up to the deep pool of Vasuki, the Kambala, Ashvatara and Bahu Mulaka, consecrated to the Nagas, form the Prajapati-kshetra, which is renowned in the three worlds.

## \|\| 104.5-6 \|\|

*ā prayāgapratiṣṭhānād āpurādvāsukerhradāt \|*  
*kambalāśvatarau nāgau nāgaśca bahumūlakaḥ \|*  
*etatprajāpateḥ kṣetraṃ triṣu lokeṣu viśrutam \|\| 5 \|\|*

*tatra snātvā divaṃ yānti ye mṛtāste 'punarbhavāḥ \|*  
*tato brahmādayo devā rakṣāṃ kurvanti saṃgatāḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. People who bathe there go to heaven. People who die there are liberated from the cycle of birth. Those who live there are guarded by the Devas, Brahma, &c. O King! there are several other sacred tirthas that drive away sins which I would not be able to enumerate even in the course of centuries; consequently, I shall briefly confine myself to the narration of the virtues of Prayaga.

## \|\| 104.7-8 \|\|

*anye ca bahavastīrthāḥ sarvapāpaharāḥ śubhāḥ \|*  
*na śakyāḥ kathituṃ rājan bahuvarṣaśatairapi \|*  
*saṃkṣepeṇa pravakṣyāmi prayāgasya tu kīrtanam \|\| 7 \|\|*

*ṣaṣṭirdhanuḥsahasrāṇi yāni rakṣanti jāhnavīm \|*  
*yamunāṃ rakṣati sadā savitā saptavāhanaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8. The Ganges is guarded by 60,000 bows, the Yamuna (Jumna) by the Sun drawn by his seven horses, the sacred place Prayaga by Indra, and the circumference of it by Lord Vishnu, along with other Devas.

## \|\| 104.9 \|\|

*prayāgaṃ tu viśeṣeṇa sadā rakṣati vāsavaḥ \|*  
*maṇḍalaṃ rakṣati harir daivataiḥ saha saṃgataḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The Akshayavata tree is guarded by Shiva, and the Devas protect the sacred places that dispel sins.

## \|\| 104.10 \|\|

*taṃ vaṭaṃ rakṣati sadā śūlapāṇirmaheśvaraḥ \|*  
*sthānaṃ rakṣanti vai devāḥ sarvapāpaharaṃ śubham \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. O King! the sinners cannot go to that sacred place. All minor sins are washed off merely by the remembrance of that sacred place.

## \|\| 104.11 \|\|

*adharmeṇāvṛto loko naiva gacchati tatpadam \|*  
*svalpamalpataraṃ pāpaṃ yadā te syānnarādhipa \|*  
*prayāgaṃ smaramāṇasya sarvamāyāti saṃkṣayam \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. All the sins of a man disappear by the sight, remembrance, or the rubbing on the body of the clay of that place.

## \|\| 104.12 \|\|

*darśanāttasya tīrthasya nāmasaṃkīrtanādapi \|*  
*mṛttikālambhanādvāpi naraḥ pāpātpramucyate \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. O King! there are five deep channels in Prayaga. The Ganges flows in the middle of them. The sins disappear the moment one enters the boundary of Prayaga.

## \|\| 104.13 \|\|

*pañca kuṇḍāni rājendra teṣāṃ madhye tu jāhnavī \|*  
*prayāgasya praveśe tu pāpaṃ naṣyati tatkṣaṇāt \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. The mere remembrance of the Ganges, from the distance of a thousand yojanas, melts away all the sins. The doers of the evil deeds even attain emancipation by the mere mention of the sacred name of the Ganges.

## \|\| 104.14 \|\|

*yojanānāṃ sahasreṣu gaṅgāyāḥ smaraṇānnaraḥ \|*  
*api duṣkṛtakarmā tu labhate paramāṃ gatim \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. The sins disappear by the utterance of the name of the Ganges the sight of Her leads to prosperity, and the bathing in and drinking of Her sacred waters purifies one’s soul along with those of his ancestors, for 7 generations.

## \|\| 104.15-16 \|\|

*kīrtanānmucyate pāpād dṛṣṭvā bhadrāṇi paṣyati \|*  
*avagāhya ca pītvā tu punātyāsaptamaṃ kulam \|\| 15 \|\|*

*satyavādī jitakrodho hy ahiṃsāyāṃ vyavasthitaḥ \|*  
*dharmānusārī tattvajño gobrāhmaṇahite rataḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

15-16. Those who speak the truth, keep themselves free from anger and the vice of killing or causing pain to living beings, are wise and learned are the lovers of the cow and Brahmana are liberated from their sins and attain the fruits of their desire by bathing at the confluence of the Ganges and the Yamuna.

## \|\| 104.17 \|\|

*gaṅgāyamunayormadhye snāto mucyeta kilbiṣāt \|*  
*manasā cintayankāmān avāpnoti supuṣkalān \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Those who maintain their sexual purity for a month in that sacred place, protected by the Devas, and offer libations of water to the manes of the deceased ancestors and to the Gods, always attain what they desire, wherever they are born.

## \|\| 104.18 \|\|

*tato gatvā prayāgaṃ tu sarvadevābhirakṣitam \|*  
*brahmacārī vasenmāsaṃ pitrindevāṃśca tarpayet \|*  
*īpsitāṃllabhate kāmān yatra yatrābhijāyate \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. The Goddess Yamuna — the daughter of the Sun, renowned in all the three worlds — -is present in Prayaga, and the place where she meets is the abode of Shiva.

## \|\| 104.19 \|\|

*tapanasya sutā devī triṣu lokeṣu viśrutā \|*  
*samāgatā mahābhāgā yamunā tatra nimnagā \|*  
*tatra saṃnihito nityaṃ sākṣāddevo maheśvaraḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. The merit of a pilgrimage to the Ganges at the sacred place of Prayaga, does not fall to the lot of every one, O King! The Devas, the Danavas, the Rishis, the Siddhas and the Charanas — they all go to heaven by bathing at Prayaga.

## Chapter 105

## \|\| 105.1 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca*  
*śṛṇu rājanprayāgasya māhātmyaṃ punareva tu \|*  
*yacchrutvā sarvapāpebhyo mucyate nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Markandeya said: — King! Besides this, I shall now tell you about the great virtues of Prayaga; by the mere hearing of it one is rescued from all sins.

## \|\| 105.2 \|\|

*ārtānāṃ hi daridrāṇāṃ niścitavyavasāyinām \|*  
*sthānamuktaṃ prayāgaṃ tu nākhyeyaṃ tu kadācana \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. The sacred place of Prayaga is highly beneficial to the distressed, the poor whose faith is firmly fixed. No one should raise any controversy about it.

## \|\| 105.3-6 \|\|

*vyādhito yadi vā dīno vṛddho vāpi bhavennaraḥ \|*  
*gaṅgāyamunayormadhye yastu prāṇānparityajet \|\| 3 \|\|*

*dīptakāñcanavarṇābhair vimānaiḥ sūryasaṃnibhaiḥ \|*  
*gandharvāpsarasāṃ madhye svarge krīḍati mānavaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*īpsitāṃllabhate kāmān vadanti ṛṣipuṃgavāḥ \|*  
*sarvaratnamayairdivyair nānādhvajasamākulaiḥ \|*  
*varāṅganāsamākīrṇair modate śubhalakṣaṇaiḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*gītavādyavinirghoṣaiḥ prasuptaḥ pratibudhyate \|*  
*yāvanna smarate janma tāvatsvarge mahīyate \|\| 6 \|\|*

3-6. The good sages say that the diseased, the meek and the old who give up their lives at the confluence of the Ganges and the Yamuna go in a vimana, of the lustre of the gold, or that of the Sun surrounded by the celestial nymphs, and all his desires are fulfilled. The departed spirit till it thinks of re-birth, is honored in the heaven wearing precious stones and seated in a vimana, streaming with myriads of buntings and flags, surrounded by the celestial nymphs singing beautiful songs melodiously.

## \|\| 105.7 \|\|

*tataḥ svargātparibhraṣṭaḥ kṣīṇakarmā divaścyutaḥ \|*  
*hiraṇyaratnasampūrṇe samṛddhe jāyate kule \|*  
*tadeva smarate tīrthaṃ smaraṇāttatra gacchati \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. On consuming his store of virtue he is re-born in the house of a wealthy man where, too, he recollects the greatness of Prayaga and goes there.

## \|\| 105.8 \|\|

*deśastho yadi vāraṇye videśastho 'thavā gṛhe \|*  
*prayāgaṃ smaramāṇo 'pi yastu prāṇānparityajet \|*  
*brahmalokamavāpnoti vadanti ṛṣipuṃgavāḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. One who thinks of Prayaga in his own country, in the forests, in some foreign land, or even in his own house, on the point of one’s death, goes to the world of Brahma. This is the saying of the good sages.

## \|\| 105.9-11 \|\|

*sarvakāmaphalā vṛkṣā mahī yatra hiraṇmayī \|*  
*ṛṣayo munayaḥ siddhās tatra loke sa gacchati \|\| 9 \|\|*

*strīsahasrāvṛte ramye mandākinyāstaṭe śubhe \|*  
*modate ṛṣibhiḥ sārdhaṃ sukṛteneha karmaṇā \|\| 10 \|\|*

*siddhacāraṇagandharvaiḥ pūjyate divi daivataiḥ \|*  
*tataḥ svargātparibhraṣṭo jambūdvīpapatirbhavet \|\| 11 \|\|*

9-11. He goes to such regions where the earth is full of gold, where he would obtain all the fruits of his desire, where reside the Rishis and the sages. There, in their company, he enjoys on the banks of the Ganges, surrounded by thousands of beautiful women, sages, pilgrims and the Gandharvas. Leaving the heaven, he is born as a King of Jambudvipa.

## \|\| 105.12 \|\|

*tataḥ śubhāni karmāṇi cintayānaḥ punaḥ punaḥ \|*  
*guṇavānvittasampanno bhavatīha na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Then, constantly thinking of good deeds, he undoubtedly becomes wise and wealthy.

## \|\| 105.13-14 \|\|

*karmaṇā manasā vācā dharmasatyapratiṣṭhitaḥ \|*  
*gaṅgāyamunayormadhye yastu gāṃ samprayacchati \|\| 13 \|\|*

*suvarṇamaṇimuktāśca yadi vānyatparigraham \|*  
*svakārye pitṛkārye vā devatābhyarcane 'pi vā \|*  
*saphalaṃ tasya tattīrthaṃ yathāvatpuṇyamāpnuyāt \|\| 14 \|\|*

13-14. One who is devoted to virtue with all his mind, speech and deeds, and makes gifts of cows at the confluence of the Ganges and the Yamuna, and makes gifts of gold and jewels, &c., in course of Deva ‘or Pitri worship, attains great merit and virtue.

## \|\| 105.15 \|\|

*evaṃ tīrthe na gṛhṇīyāt puṇyeṣvāyataneṣu ca \|*  
*nimitteṣu ca sarveṣu hy apramatto bhaveddvijaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. A Brahmana should, however, avoid, as far as possible, the accepting of any gift at sacred places. He should be on his guard, that is, should not yield to temptation.

## \|\| 105.16-19 \|\|

*kapilāṃ pāṭalāvarṇāṃ yastu dhenuṃ prayacchati \|*  
*svarṇaśṛṅgīṃ raupyakhurāṃ kāṃsyadohāṃ payasvinīm \|\| 16 \|\|*

*prayāge śrotriyaṃ santaṃ grāhayitvā yathāvidhi \|*  
*śuklāmbaradharaṃ śāntaṃ dharmajñaṃ vedapāragam \|\| 17 \|\|*

*sā gaustasmai pradātavyā gaṅgāyamunasaṃgame \|*  
*vāsāṃsi ca mahārhāṇi ratnāni vividhāni ca \|\| 18 \|\|*

*yāvadromāṇi tasyā goḥ santi gātreṣu sattama \|*  
*tāvadvarṣasahasrāṇi svargaloke mahīyate \|\| 19 \|\|*

16-19. One who gives away a pale-red milk cow, after getting her horns plaited with gold, her hoofs with silver, along with a milking pot of: bell metal, cloth and jewels, to a virtuous and dispassionate Brahmans, well-versed in the Vedas, at the confluence of the Ganges and the Yamuna, goes to and resides in the heaven for as many years as there are hairs on the body of that cow.

## \|\| 105.21 \|\|

*gavāṃ śatasahasrebhyo dadyādekāṃ payasvinīm \|*  
*putrāndārāṃstathā bhṛtyān gaurekā prati tārayet \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. At the time of his re-birth, the very same cow saves him from hell. He is born in Uttara-Kuru, and enjoys a long life. One who makes a gift of only one milk cow of his many thousands, that same cow helps the donor, his son, wife and kinsmen, to cross the sea of troubles with ease.

## \|\| 105.22 \|\|

*tasmātsarveṣu dāneṣu godānaṃ tu viśiṣyate \|*  
*durgame viṣame ghore mahāpātakasambhave \|*  
*gaureva rakṣāṃ kurute tasmāddeyā dvijottame \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. For this reason the gift of a cow is said to be the beat of all charities, because a single cow protects the donor from all great sins. A cow should be given to a good Brahmana

## Chapter 106

## \|\| 106.1-2 \|\|

*yudhiṣṭhira uvāca*  
*yathā yathā prayāgasya māhātmyaṃ kathyate tvayā \|*  
*tathā tathā pramucye 'haṃ sarvapāpairna saṃśayaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*bhagavankena vidhinā gantavyaṃ dharmaniścayaiḥ \|*  
*prayāge yo vidhiḥ proktas tanme brūhi mahāmune \|\| 2 \|\|*

1-2. Yudhisthira said: — Sage! I feel I am gradually being freed from my sins by the-virtues of Prayaga that you have been pleased to relate to me. O, blessed saint, now be pleased to explain to me how one should go to Prayaga.

## \|\| 106.3 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca*  
*kathayiṣyāmi te rājaṃs tīrthayātrāvidhikramam \|*  
*ārṣeṇa vidhinānena yathādṛṣṭaṃ yathāśrutam \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Markandeya said: — King! I shall now relate to you what you wish to hear, exactly as I have heard from the sages and have seen them doing on such an occasion.

## \|\| 106.4-5 \|\|

*prayāgatīrthayātrārthī yaḥ prayāti naraḥ kvacit \|*  
*balīvardasamārūḍhaḥ śṛṇu tasyāpi yatphalam \|\| 4 \|\|*

*narake vasate ghore gavāṃ kroṣṭā hi dāruṇe \|*  
*salilaṃ na ca gṛhṇanti pitarastasya dehinaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. One who drives to Prayaga on a conveyance, drawn by bullocks, makes himself liable to a fearful hell, and his libations are not accepted by the manes of his ancestors.

## \|\| 106.6 \|\|

*yastu putrāṃstathā bālān snāpayet pāyayettathā \|*  
*yathātmanā tathā sarvaṃ dānaṃ vipreṣu dāpayet \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. The bathing of his children there and then drinking the sacred water, does not do them any good.

## \|\| 106.7 \|\|

*aiśvaryalobhamohādvā gacchedyānena yo naraḥ \|*  
*niṣphalaṃ tasya tatsarvaṃ tasmādyānaṃ vivarjayet \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. One who gives alms to the Brahmanas, with any feeling or conceit, does not derive any benefit. It is not therefore wise to visit a sacred place on any conveyance.

## \|\| 106.8-9 \|\|

*gaṅgāyamunayormadhye yastu kanyāṃ prayacchati \|*  
*ārṣeṇaiva vivāhena yathāvibhavasambhavam \|\| 8 \|\|*

*na sa paṣyati taṃ ghoraṃ narakaṃ tena karmaṇā \|*  
*uttarānsa kurūngatvā modate kālamakṣayam \|*  
*putrāndārāṃśca labhate dhārmikānrūpasaṃyutān \|\| 9 \|\|*

8-9. One who gives away his daughter (in marriage), according to the prescribed rites, between the Ganges and the Yamuna, according to his means, never goes to the fearful hell. He is born in the Uttara-Kuru and gets a good wife and dutiful sons, and enjoys long life.

## \|\| 106.10 \|\|

*tatra dānaṃ prakartavyaṃ yathāvibhavasambhavam \|*  
*tena tīrthaphalaṃ caiva vardhate nātra saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*svarge tiṣṭhati rājendra yāvadābhūtasaṃplavam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. O king! on account of these things, the giving away of charity at sacred places, according to one’s means, enhances his merits and makes him entitled to live in heaven till the dissolution of the world.

## \|\| 106.11 \|\|

*vaṭamūlaṃ samāsādya yastu prāṇānvimuñcati \|*  
*sarvalokānatikramya rudralokaṃ sa gacchati \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. One who departs from his body, near the Akshayavata in Prayaga, goes straight to the region of Shiva.

## \|\| 106.12 \|\|

*tatra te dvādaśādityās tapanti rudrasaṃśritāḥ \|*  
*nirdahanti jagatsarvaṃ vaṭamūlaṃ na dahyate \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. It is the very same Akshayavata which does not perish, in spite of the combined fury of all the suns that reduce the rest of the world to ashes.

## \|\| 106.13 \|\|

*naṣṭacandrārkabhuvanaṃ yadā caikārṇavaṃ jagat \|*  
*sthīyate tatra vai viṣṇur yajamānaḥ punaḥ punaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. The Lord Vishnu is present there, and worships constantly near the Akshayavata, even when the world becomes extinct.

## \|\| 106.14-18 \|\|

*devadānavagandharvā ṛṣayaḥ siddhacāraṇāḥ \|*  
*sadā sevanti tattīrthaṃ gaṅgāyamunasaṃgamam \|\| 14 \|\|*

*tato gaccheta rājendra prayāgaṃ saṃstuvaṃśca yat \|*  
*yatra brahmādayo devā ṛṣayaḥ siddhacāraṇāḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*lokapālāśca sādhyāśca pitaro lokasaṃmatāḥ \|*  
*sanatkumārapramukhās tathaiva paramarṣayaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*aṅgiraḥpramukhāścaiva tathā brahmarṣayaḥ pare \|*  
*tathā nāgāḥ suparṇāśca siddhāśca khecarāśca ye \|\| 17 \|\|*

*sāgarāḥ saritaḥ śailā nāgā vidyādharāśca ye \|*  
*hariśca bhagavanāste prajāpatipuraḥsaraḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

14-18. O King! The sacred place lying between the Ganges and the Yamuna is venerated even by the Devas, Asuras, Sages, Rishis, Gandharvas. One should therefore go there with devotion, for Brahma, Devas, Rishis, Sages, Lokapalas, Sadhya Devas, Pitris, Sanatkumara, etc., the greatest of the sages Amgira, etc. Brahma Rishis, serpents, suparnas, oceans, rivers, mountains, vidyadharas, Lord Vishnu Himself, along with Brahma, are present there.

## \|\| 106.19 \|\|

*gaṅgāyamunayormadhye pṛthivyā jaghanaṃ smṛtam \|*  
*prayāgaṃ rājaśārdūla triṣu lokeṣu viśrutam \|*  
*tataḥ puṇyatamaṃ nāsti triṣu lokeṣu bhārata \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. \[tis said that the site of the confluence of the Ganges and the Yamuna forms the middle or the waist of the earth. This Prayaga tirtha is known throughout the three worlds.

## \|\| 106.20-21 \|\|

*śravaṇāttasya tīrthasya nāmasaṃkīrtanādapi \|*  
*mṛttikālambhanādvāpi naraḥ pāpātpramucyate \|\| 20 \|\|*

*tatrābhiṣekaṃ yaḥ kuryāt saṃgame śaṃsitavrataḥ \|*  
*tulyaṃ phalamavāpnoti rājasūyāśvamedhayoḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

20-21. The remembrance of this sacred place or the hearing the name of it or the touch of its soil, liberates one from his sins; so also from bathing there. One who sprinkles the water of that place, has the benefit of performing Ashvamedha and Rajasuya sacrifices.

## \|\| 106.22 \|\|

*na devavacanāttāta na lokavacanāttathā \|*  
*matir utkramaṇīyā te prayāgagamanaṃ prati \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. You should not be dissuaded from going to Prayaga, my son! even by the preaching’s of the Devas.

## \|\| 106.23 \|\|

*daśa tīrthasahasrāṇi ṣaṣṭikoṭyastathā parāḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ sāṃnidhyamatraiva tatastu kurunandana \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. At the sacred Prayaga, there are sixty crores and ten thousand holy places, all gathered there.

## \|\| 106.24 \|\|

*yā gatir yogauktasya satyasthasya manīṣiṇaḥ \|*  
*sā gatistyajataḥ prāṇān gaṅgāyamunasaṃgame \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. The man dying at Prayaga derives the same benefits as one does by truly devoting himself to yaga.

## \|\| 106.25 \|\|

*na te jīvanti loke 'smiṃs tatra tatra udhiṣṭhira \|*  
*ye prayāgaṃ na samprāptās triṣu lokeṣu vañcitāḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Those who do not go to Prayaga are like the living dead, O Yudhisthira!

## \|\| 106.26 \|\|

*evaṃ dṛṣṭvā tu tattīrthaṃ prayāgaṃ paramaṃ padam \|*  
*mucyate sarvapāpebhyaḥ śaśāṅka iva rāhuṇā \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Those who go to Prayaga, in accordance with the rules laid down, are freed from their sins as the Moon liberates Himself from Rahu.

## \|\| 106.27 \|\|

*kambalāśvatarau nāgau vipule yamunātaṭe \|*  
*tatra snātvā ca pītvā ca sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. He who bathes in and drinks the water of the Yamuna, at the high banks presided by the Nagas, Kambala and Ashvatara, is freed of all his sins.

## \|\| 106.28 \|\|

*tatra gatvā ca saṃsthānaṃ mahādevasya viśrutam \|*  
*narastārayate sarvān daśa pūrvāndaśāparān \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. The man by going to the shrine where resides Lord Shiva, liberates from bondage his ancestors and posterity for ten generations.

## \|\| 106.29 \|\|

*kṛtvābhiṣekaṃ tu naraḥ so 'śvamedhaphalaṃ labhet \|*  
*svargalokamavāpnoti yāvadābhūtasaṃplavam \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. By the sprinkling of the holy waters over his body on that spot, he gets the merits of an Ashvamedha sacrifice, and resides in the heaven till the end of the world cycle.

## \|\| 106.30-31 \|\|

*pūrvapārśve tu gaṅgāyās triṣu lokeṣu bhārata \|*  
*kūpaṃ caiva tu sāmudraṃ pratiṣṭhānaṃ ca viśrutam \|\| 30 \|\|*

*brahmacārī jitakrodhas trirātraṃ yadi tiṣṭhati \|*  
*sarvapāpaviśuddhātmā so 'śvamedhaphalaṃ labhet \|\| 31 \|\|*

30-31. On the eastern bank of the Ganges, there is a well, by the name of Samudra-Kupa, and the place Pratishthana (modern Jhushi) which is renowned in the three worlds. If one resides there for three nights, observing sexual purity and keeping himself dispassionate, he is freed from all his sins and gets the merit of the performance of Ashvamedha sacrifice.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — The mention of Samudra-Kupa in modern Jhushi fixes the date of this portion of the Purana. The well called Samudra-Kupa was sunk by Samudra-Gupta, and so this Mahatmya must have been written after the Gupta.

## \|\| 106.32-33 \|\|

*uttareṇa pratiṣṭhānād bhāgīrathyāstu pūrvataḥ \|*  
*haṃsaprapatanaṃ nāma tīrthaṃ trailokyaviśrutam \|\| 32 \|\|*

*aśvamedhaphalaṃ tasmin snānamātreṇa bhārata \|*  
*yāvaccandraśca sūryaśca tāvatsvarge mahīyate \|\| 33 \|\|*

32-33. The Hamsaprapatana tirtha (the shrine where swans alight), that lies on the north of Pratisthana and on the east bank of the Ganges, is renowned in all the three worlds. By bathing there the devotee gets the benefit of Ashvamedha sacrifice and resides in heaven, as long as the sun and the moon shine in the firmament.

## \|\| 106.34-35 \|\|

*urvaśīramaṇe puṇye vipule haṃsapāṇḍure \|*  
*parityajati yaḥ prāṇāñ śṛṇu tasyāpi yatphalam \|\| 34 \|\|*

*ṣaṣṭivarṣasahasrāṇi ṣaṣṭivarṣaśatāni ca \|*  
*sevyate pitṛbhiḥ sārdhaṃ svargaloke narādhipa \|\| 35 \|\|*

34-35. One who dies at the sacred Urvashiramana, whose high bank becomes white by the swans that dwell there, goes to heaven and enjoys with the Pitris for a period of sixty thousand and s)x centuries.

## \|\| 106.36 \|\|

*urvaśīṃ tu sadā paśyet svargaloke narottama \|*  
*pūjyate satataṃ putra ṛṣigandharvakiṃnaraiḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. And o King! he is always in company of that famous celestial nymph, Urvashi, and is venerated by the Rishis, Gandharvas, and the Kinnaras, &c.

## \|\| 106.37-38 \|\|

*tataḥ svargātparibhraṣṭaḥ kṣīṇakarmā divaścyutaḥ \|*  
*urvaśīsadṛśīnāṃ tu kanyānāṃ labhate śatam \|\| 37 \|\|*

*madhye nārīsahasrāṇāṃ bahūnāṃ ca patirbhavet \|*  
*daśagrāmasahasrāṇāṃ bhoktā bhavati bhūmipaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

37-38. After consuming his store of virtue, he becomes the lord of ten thousand towns and of hundreds of maids, like Urvashi, in whose midst he revels as their husband.

## \|\| 106.39 \|\|

*kāñcīnūpuraśabdena supto 'sau pratibudhyate \|*  
*bhuktvā tu vipulān bhogāṃs tattīrthaṃ bhajate punaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. He wakes from his bed by the music of the sweet jingling of the waist chains and anklets of the ladies, and, after enjoying fully all his luxuries retires to that shrine again.

## \|\| 106.40-41 \|\|

*śuklāmbaradharo nityaṃ niyataḥ saṃyatendriyaḥ \|*  
*ekaṃ kālaṃ tu bhuñjāno māsaṃ bhūmipatirbhavet \|\| 40 \|\|*

*suvarṇālaṃkṛtānāṃ tu nārīṇāṃ labhate śatam \|*  
*pṛthivyām āsamudrāyāṃ mahābhūmipatirbhavet \|\| 41 \|\|*

40-41. One who wears white raiment’s and has his meals only once a day and preserves his sexual purity, becomes a king and gets hundreds of beautiful wives, adorned with fine ornaments. He rules over a vast territory, whose boundary reaches to the seas.

## \|\| 106.42 \|\|

*dhanadhānyasamāukto dātā bhavati nityaśaḥ \|*  
*bhuktvā tu vipulānbhogāṃs tattīrthaṃ labhate punaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. And, after enjoying the result of his wealth and of the practising of his charities, he again retires to that spot.

## \|\| 106.43 \|\|

*atha saṃdhyāvaṭe ramye brahmacārī jitendriyaḥ \|*  
*upavāsī śuciḥ saṃdhyāṃ brahmalokamavāpnuyāt \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. One who, preserving his sexual purity, observes a fast till the evening, at the Sandhya Vata , attains Brahmaloka.

## \|\| 106.44 \|\|

*koṭitīrthaṃ samāsādya yastu prāṇānparityajet \|*  
*koṭivarṣasahasrāṇāṃ svargaloke mahīyate \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. One who dies at Koti-tirtha, remains in Svarga for crores of years.

## \|\| 106.45 \|\|

*tataḥ svargātparibhraṣṭaḥ kṣīṇakarmā divaścyutaḥ \|*  
*suvarṇamaṇimuktāḍhya-kule jāyeta rūpavān \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. And, on coming back to the world after exhausting his virtues, is born a very bandsome person in a most wealthy family.

## \|\| 106.46-47 \|\|

*tato bhogavatīṃ gatvā vāsukeruttareṇa tu \|*  
*daśāśvamedhakaṃ nāma tīrthaṃ tatrāparaṃ bhavet \|\| 46 \|\|*

*kṛtābhiṣekastu naraḥ so 'śvamedhaphalaṃ labhet \|*  
*dhanāḍhyo rūpavāndakṣo dātā bhavati dhārmikaḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

46-47. One who goes and sprinkles water over him at the Dashashvamedha tirtha in the Bhogavati puri, to the north of the abode of Vasuki, attains the benefit of Ashvamedha sacrifice, and, in his next birth, is born as a very rich, pious, handsome, wise and generous man.

## \|\| 106.48 \|\|

*caturvedeṣu yatpuṇyaṃ yatpuṇyaṃ satyavādiṣu \|*  
*ahiṃsāyāṃ tu yo dharmo gamanādeva tatphalam \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. The merits accruing from truth speaking and abstention from inflicting injury to another, are obtained by a pilgrimage to Prayaga

## \|\| 106.49 \|\|

*kurukṣetrasamā gaṅgā yatra yatrāvagāhyate \|*  
*kurukṣetrāddaśaguṇā yatra vindhyena saṃgatā \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. The place where the Ganges alone flows, is as sacred as Kurukshetra, and the place where she flows touching the Vindhya range, is tenfold more sacred.

## \|\| 106.50 \|\|

*yatra gaṅgā mahābhāgā bahutīrthā tapodhanā \|*  
*siddhakṣetraṃ hi tadjñeyaṃ nātra kāryā vicāraṇā \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. The spot where the Ganges flows touching many tirthas is undoubtedly a most holy place.

## \|\| 106.51 \|\|

*kṣitau tārayate martyān nāgāṃstārayate 'pyadhaḥ \|*  
*divi tārayate devāṃs tena tripathagā smṛtā \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. The Ganges exercises Her elevating influence over mankind on earth, over the serpents in the lower regions, and over the Devas in Svarga; consequently, she is also known as Tripathagamini.

## \|\| 106.52 \|\|

*yāvadasthīni gaṅgāyāṃ tiṣṭhanti hi śarīriṇaḥ \|*  
*tāvadvarṣasahasrāṇi svargaloke mahīyate \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. Those whose bones are deposited in the Ganges, remain in Svarga for as many thousand years as there are bones deposited.

## \|\| 106.53 \|\|

*tataḥ svargātparibhraṣṭo jambūdvīpapatirbhavet \|*  
*tīrthānāṃ tu paraṃ tīrthaṃ nadīnāṃ tu mahānadī \|*  
*mokṣadā sarvabhūtānāṃ mahāpātakināmapi \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. The Ganges is the most sacred of all the Tirthas, the best of all the rivers, and is the giver of emancipation to the vilest sinners.

## \|\| 106.54 \|\|

*sarvatra sulabhā gaṅgā triṣu sthāneṣu durlabhā \|*  
*gaṅgādvāre prayāge ca gaṅgāsāgarasaṃgame \|*  
*tatra snātvā divaṃ yānti ye mṛtāste 'punarbhavāḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. The Ganges is easily accessible everywhere, excepting at Gangadvara, Prayaga and Ganga Sagara. Those who bathe at the above mentioned 3 places, go to heaven and are never re-born.

## \|\| 106.55 \|\|

*sarveṣāmeva bhūtānāṃ pāpopahatacetasām \|*  
*gatim anviṣyamāṇānāṃ nāsti gaṅgāsamā gatiḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. There is no other source of bliss to the sinner as the Ganges.

## \|\| 106.56 \|\|

*pavitrāṇāṃ pavitraṃ ca maṅgalānāṃ ca maṅgalam \|*  
*maheśvaraśirobhraṣṭā sarvapāpaharā śubhā \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. The Ganges has fallen from the head of Lord Shiva, who is the sacred of the most sacred and propitious of the most propitious.

## Chapter 107

## \|\| 107.1 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca*  
*śṛṇu rājanprayāgasya māhātmyaṃ punareva tu \|*  
*yacchrutvā sarvapāpebhyo mucyate nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Markandeya said: O King! I shall now relate to you further the greatness of the holy Prayaga by listening to which a man undoubtedly gets liberated from all sins.

## \|\| 107.2 \|\|

*mānasaṃ nāma tattīrthaṃ gaṅgāyā uttare taṭe \|*  
*trirātropoṣito bhūtvā sarvakāmānavāpnuyāt \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. On the banks of the Ganges, towards the west, lies the sacred Manasatirtha, where by keeping up a three days’ fast, the man gets freed from sins and attains all his desires.

## \|\| 107.3 \|\|

*gobhūhiraṇyadānena yatphalaṃ prāpnuyānnaraḥ \|*  
*sa tatphalamavāpnoti tattīrthaṃ smarate punaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. The merits acquired by the giving away of cows, land and gold are attained by the mere remembrance of this tirtha.

## \|\| 107.4 \|\|

*akāmo vā sakāmo vā gaṅgāyāṃ yo 'bhipadyate \|*  
*mṛtastu labhate svargaṃ narakaṃ ca na paṣyati \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. One who resides on the banks of the Ganges, with or without any object in view, and dies there, goes to heaven and remains far away out of ine sight of hell.

## \|\| 107.5 \|\|

*apsarogaṇasaṃgītaiḥ supto 'sau pratibudhyate \|*  
*haṃsasārasauktena vimānena sa gacchati \|*  
*bahuvarṣasahasrāṇi svargaṃ rājendra bhuñjati \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Such a man sits in a vimana, adorned by decent birds, like swans and flamingoes, where celestial nymphs sing lovely songs. Thus he enjoys long life in heaven.

## \|\| 107.6 \|\|

*tataḥ svargātparibhraṣṭaḥ kṣīṇakarmā divaścyutaḥ \|*  
*suvarṇamaṇimuktāḍhye jāyate vipule kule \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. On coming back from heaven, be is born in the house of a very wealthy man.

## \|\| 107.7 \|\|

*ṣaṣṭitīrthasahasrāṇi ṣaṣṭikoṭyastathāpagāḥ \|*  
*māghamāse gamiṣyanti gaṅgāyamunasaṃgamam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. During the month of Magha, sixty thousand tirthas and sixty crores of sacred streams are to be found at the confluence of the Ganges and the Yamuna.

## \|\| 107.8 \|\|

*gavāṃ śatasahasrasya samyagdattasya yatphalam \|*  
*prayāge māghamāse tu tryahasnānāttu tatphalam \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. The merits of giving away a lakh of cows are attained by bathing at Prayaga for 3 days.

## \|\| 107.9 \|\|

*gaṅgāyamunayormadhye karṣāgniṃ yastu sādhayet \|*  
*ahīnāṅgo hyarogaśca pañcendriyasamanvitaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. One who, at the confluence of the Ganges and the Yamuna, lights cowdung fires all round and sits in the midst of them, enjoys healthy body, with all his limbs in the best condition.

## \|\| 107.10 \|\|

*yāvanti romakūpāṇi tasya gātreṣu dehinaḥ \|*  
*tāvadvarṣasahasrāṇi svargaloke mahīyate \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. He remains in heaven for as many years as there are hair on his body.

## \|\| 107.11 \|\|

*tataḥ svargātparibhraṣṭo jambūdvīpapatirbhavet \|*  
*sa bhuktvā vipulānbhogāṃs tattīrthaṃ smarate punaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. And when he is re-incarnated on earth, he becomes the emperor of the world. After enjoying these, he again remembers the very same tirtha.

## \|\| 107.12-13 \|\|

*jalapraveśaṃ yaḥ kuryāt saṃgame lokaviśrute \|*  
*rāhugraste tathā some vimuktaḥ sarvakilbiṣaiḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*somalokamavāpnoti somena saha modate \|*  
*ṣaṣṭivarṣasahasrāṇi svargaloke mahīyate \|\| 13 \|\|*

12-13. One who immerses into the sacred waters at the junction of the Ganges and the Yamuna, during the time of the lunar eclipse, goes to the world of the Moon where he enjoys in His (Moon’s) company and remains in heaven for sixty thousand years, and is freed from all his sings

## \|\| 107.14 \|\|

*svarge ca śakraloke 'smin nṛṣigandharvasevite \|*  
*paribhraṣṭastu rājendra samṛddhe jāyate kule \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. At the end, he leaves the world of Indra where he was venerated by the Rishis and Gandharvas, etc., and is born in a rich family.

## \|\| 107.15 \|\|

*adhaḥśirāstu yo jvālām ūrdhvapādaḥ pibennaraḥ \|*  
*śatavarṣasahasrāṇi svargaloke mahīyate \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. One who uplifts: his legs and balances himself on his head, swings over the flames of fire, resides in heaven for a hundred thousand years.

## \|\| 107.16 \|\|

*paribhraṣṭastu rājendra so 'gnihotrī bhavennaraḥ \|*  
*bhuktvā tu vipulānbhogāṃs tattīrthaṃ bhajate punaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. And, on being born again, he becomes Agnihotri when, after various enjoyments, attains the same tirtha again.

## \|\| 107.17-18 \|\|

*yaḥ svadehaṃ tu kartitvā śakunibhyaḥ prayacchati \|*  
*vihagairupabhuktasya śṛṇu tasyāpi yatphalam \|\| 17 \|\|*

*śataṃ varṣasahasrāṇāṃ somaloke mahīyate \|*  
*tasmādapi paribhraṣṭo rājā bhavati dhārmikaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

17-18. One who cuts and offers his flesh to the birds, goes and resides in the domain of Chandra (Moon), and, on being born again, becomes a very pious king,

## \|\| 107.19 \|\|

*guṇavān rūpasampanno vidvāṃśca priyavācakaḥ \|*  
*bhuktvā tu vipulānbhogāṃs tattīrthaṃ bhajate punaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Full of wisdom, knowledge, beauty and sweetness of speech. After enjoying life, he again goes to that Tirtha.

## \|\| 107.20 \|\|

*yāmune cottare kūle prayāgasya tu dakṣiṇe \|*  
*ṛṇapramocanaṃ nāma tattīrthaṃ paramaṃ smṛtam \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. On the northern bank of the Yamuna, to the south of Prayaga, there is the most sacred Rinamochana tirtha.

## \|\| 107.21 \|\|

*ekarātroṣitaḥ snātvā ṛṇaiḥ sarvaiḥ pramucyate \|*  
*svargalokamavāpnoti anṛṇaśca sadā bhavet \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Where, by residing for a night and by bathing there, one remains no more liable to pay any debts, and goes to heaven and never runs into debts.

## Chapter 108

## \|\| 108.1 \|\|

*yudhiṣṭhira uvāca*  
*etacchrutvā prayāgasya yattvayā parikīrtitam \|*  
*viśuddhaṃ me 'dya hṛdayaṃ prayāgasya tu kīrtanāt \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Yudhisthira said: — “Bhagavan! my mind has become purified by hearing the greatness of Prayaga narrated by you.

## \|\| 108.2 \|\|

*anāśakaphalaṃ brūhi bhagavaṃstatra kīdṛśam \|*  
*yaṃ ca lokamavāpnoti viśuddhaḥ sarvakilbiṣaiḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. O, Rishi! now be good enough to tell me that great virtue that may lead one to some higher world and be the source of everlasting bliss after washing off all his sins.

## \|\| 108.3 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca*  
*śṛṇu rājanprayāge tu anāśakaphalaṃ vibho \|*  
*prāpnoti puruṣo dhīmāñ śraddadhāno jitendriyaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Markandeya said: — King! Now hear how one can attain everlasting bliss by going to Prayaga.

## \|\| 108.4 \|\|

*ahīnāṅgo 'pyarogaśca pañcendriyasamanvitaḥ \|*  
*aśvamedhaphalaṃ tasya gacchatastu pade pade \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. He enjoys the full bloom of his health and attains the benefit of Ashvamedha sacrifice at every step in his pilgrimage to Prayaga.

## \|\| 108.5 \|\|

*kulāni tārayedrājan daśa pūrvāndaśāparān \|*  
*mucyate sarvapāpebhyo gacchettu paramaṃ padam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Such a man gets emancipation from bondage for his manes and posterity for ten generations.

## \|\| 108.6 \|\|

*yudhiṣṭhira uvāca*  
*mahābhāgyaṃ hi dharmasya yattvaṃ vadasi me prabho \|*  
*alpenaiva prayatnena bahūndharmānavāpnute \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Yudhisthira said: — The way of getting everlasting happiness just explained by you, is very simple. It is the source of so many blessings.

## \|\| 108.7 \|\|

*aśvamedhaistu bahubhiḥ prāpyate suvratairiha \|*  
*imaṃ me saṃśayaṃ chinddhi paraṃ kautūhalaṃ hi me \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. “The merits of an Ashvamedha sacrifice are acquired with very great difficulties. How can one attain similar merits in such a simple way?

Pray remove my doubts, O blessed one.

## \|\| 108.8 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca*  
*śṛṇu rājanmahāvīra yaduktaṃ brahmayoninā \|*  
*ṛṣīṇāṃ saṃnidhau pūrvaṃ kathyamānaṃ mayā śrutam \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Markandeya said: — King! I have heard what Bramha first said to the sages.

## \|\| 108.9 \|\|

*pañcayojanavistīrṇaṃ prayāgasya tu maṇḍalam \|*  
*praviṣṭamātre tadbhūmāv aśvamedhaḥ pade pade \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The circumference of Prayaga is five yojanas in extent, and by the treading on its ground one acquires the merits of Ashvamedha sacrifice at every step.

## \|\| 108.10 \|\|

*vyatītānpuruṣānsapta bhaviṣyāṃśca caturdaśa \|*  
*narastārayate sarvān yastu prāṇānparityajet \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. One who passes away at Prayaga, liberates seven generations of his ancestors and fourteen of his coming generations from bondage.

## \|\| 108.11 \|\|

*evaṃ jñātvā tu rājendra sadā sevāparo bhavet \|*  
*aśraddadhānāḥ puruṣāḥ pāpopahatacetasaḥ \|*  
*na prāpnuvanti tatsthānaṃ prayāgaṃ devarakṣitam \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. King! Knowing this greatness of Prayaga, you should devote yourself unflinchingly to that sacred Tirtha, because those devoid of devotion and leading a life of sin cannot attain the benefits of this holy tirtha which is guarded by the Devas”.

## \|\| 108.12 \|\|

*yudhiṣṭhira uvāca*  
*snehādvā dravyalobhādvā ye tu kāmavaśaṃ gatāḥ \|*  
*kathaṃ tīrthaphalaṃ teṣāṃ kathaṃ puṇyaphalaṃ bhavet \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Yudhisthira. — “O Sire! how do they get the benefits of the sacred tirtha who yield to their desires, whether such be feelings of affection or greed of worldly objects.

## \|\| 108.13 \|\|

*vikrayaḥ sarvabhāṇḍānāṃ kāryākāryamajānataḥ \|*  
*prayāge kā gatistasya tanme brūhi pitāmaha \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. And what is the fate of the man who not knowing the difference between proper and improper, carries on a trade? Pray explain all this to me.

## \|\| 108.14 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca*  
*śṛṇu rājanmahāguhyaṃ sarvapāpapraṇāśanam \|*  
*māsamekaṃ tu yaḥ snāyāt prayāge niyatendriyaḥ \|*  
*mucyate sarvapāpebhyaḥ sa gacchetparamaṃ padam \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Markandeya said: — King! hear the rare greatness of the holy place. The man who has restrained all his passions, attains emancipation by bathing for a month at Prayaga.

## \|\| 108.15 \|\|

*viśrambhaghātakānāṃ tu prayāge śṛṇu yatphalam \|*  
*trikālameva snāyīta āhāraṃ bhaikṣyamācaret \|*  
*tribhirmāsaiḥ sa mucyeta prayāge tu na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Hear what Prayaga does to a man who treacherously kills another. He undoubtedy frees himself from his sins by living on alms and bathing 3 times a day, for a period of three months.

## \|\| 108.16 \|\|

*ajñānena tu yasyeha tīrthayātrādikaṃ bhavet \|*  
*sarvakāmasamṛddhastu svargaloke mahīyate \|*  
*sthānaṃ ca labhate nityaṃ dhanadhānyasamākulam \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. One who repairs to a holy place unintentionally, goes to heaven, and, after spending all his store of virtue there, is born in a well-to-do family.

## \|\| 108.17 \|\|

*evaṃ jñānena sampūrṇaḥ sadā bhavati bhogavān \|*  
*tāritāḥ pitarastena narakātprapitāmahāḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. One who goes to a sacred place intentionally, always remains happy and rescues all his ancestors from hell.

## \|\| 108.18 \|\|

*dharmānusāri tattvajña pṛcchataste punaḥ punaḥ \|*  
*tvatpriyārthaṃ samākhyātaṃ guhyametatsanātanam \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. O incarnation of Dharma and knower of all, in compliance with your repeated enquiries, I have unfolded to you the ancient virtue for your benefit.

## \|\| 108.19 \|\|

*yudhiṣṭhira uvāca*  
*adya me saphalaṃ janma adya me tāritaṃ kulam \|*  
*prīto 'smyanugṛhīto 'smi darśanādeva te mune \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Yudhisthira said: — O Sage! I was not born in vain, my family has been redeemed, I have become delighted by meeting you. Indeed, you have shown me very great kindness.

## \|\| 108.20 \|\|

*tvaddarśanāttu dharmātman mukto 'haṃ cādya kilbiṣāt \|*  
*idānīṃ vedmi cātmānaṃ bhagavangatakalmaṣam \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. O Pious one! I have been liberated from my sins by meeting you; and I now feel myself sinless.

## \|\| 108.21 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca*  
*diṣṭyā te saphalaṃ janma diṣṭyā te tāritaṃ kulam \|*  
*kīrtanādvardhate puṇyaṃ śrutātpāpapraṇāśanam \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Markandeya said: — By your own destiny your soul has become elevated, and your family has been redeemed. By the narration of the greatness of Prayaga one’s store of virtue is increased, and his sins are decreased by listening to it.

## \|\| 108.22 \|\|

*yudhiṣṭhira uvāca*  
*yamunāyāṃ tu kiṃ puṇyaṃ kiṃ phalaṃ tu mahāmune \|*  
*etanme sarvamākhyāhi yathādṛṣṭaṃ yathāśrutam \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Yudhisthira said: — O, Great Sage! Pray tell me, as seen or heard by you, the greatness of the Yamuna.

## \|\| 108.23 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca*  
*tapanasya sutā devī triṣu lokeṣu viśrutā \|*  
*samākhyātā mahābhāgā yamunā tatra nimnagā \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Markandeya said: — The Yamuna, the daughter of the Sun, renowned in all the three worlds is known as the great river of that name.

## \|\| 108.24 \|\|

*yenaiva niḥsṛtā gaṅgā tenaiva yamunā gatā \|*  
*yojanānāṃ sahasreṣu kīrtanātpāpanāśinī \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. The Yamuna has come from the same source as the Ganges, and She also dispels all sins by the mere utterance of Her name, from a distance of 1,000 yojanas.

## \|\| 108.25 \|\|

*tatra snātvā ca pītvā ca yamunāyāṃ udhiṣṭhira \|*  
*kīrtanāllabhate puṇyaṃ dṛṣṭvā bhadrāṇi paṣyati \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. The virtue is attained by bathing in, drinking the waters and relating the greatness of the Yamuna. The sight of Her gives happiness,

## \|\| 108.26 \|\|

*avagāhya ca pītvā ca punātyāsaptamaṃ kulam \|*  
*prāṇāṃstyajati yastatra sa yāti paramāṃ gatim \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. His seven generations are purified by once plunging into and sipping -the holy waters; and emancipation is obtained by dying there.

## \|\| 108.27 \|\|

*agnitīrthamiti khyātaṃ yamunādakṣiṇe taṭe \|*  
*paścime dharmarājasya tīrthaṃ tu narakaṃ smṛtam \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. On the south of the Yamuna lies the Agni tirtha and Dharmaraja tirtha. Naraka is situate on Her western bank.

## \|\| 108.28-30 \|\|

*tatra snātvā divaṃ yānti ye mṛtāste 'punarbhavāḥ \|*  
*evaṃ tīrthasahasrāṇi yamunādakṣiṇe taṭe \|\| 28 \|\|*

*uttareṇa pravakṣyāmi ādityasya mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*tīrthaṃ nirañjanaṃ nāma yatra devāḥ savāsavāḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*upāsate sma saṃdhyāṃ ye trikālaṃ hi udhiṣṭhira \|*  
*devāḥ sevanti tattīrthaṃ ye cānye vibudhā janāḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

28-30. One goes to heaven by bathing there; by dying there he is not born again. Similarly, there are thousands of tirthas on the southern bank of the Yamuna. I am now describing the Tirtha on the northern bank known as the Niranjana tirtha of Aditya, where the Devas, along with Indra, perform sandhya three times a day and worship the tirtha; otherwise men do the same.

## \|\| 108.31-32 \|\|

*śraddadhānaparo bhūtvā kuru tīrthābhiṣecanam \|*  
*anye ca bahavastīrthāḥ sarvapāpaharāḥ smṛtāḥ \|*  
*teṣu snātvā divaṃ yānti ye mṛtāste 'punarbhavāḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

*gaṅgā ca yamunā caiva ubhe tulyaphale smṛte \|*  
*kevalaṃ jyeṣṭhabhāvena gaṅgā sarvatra pūjyate \|\| 32 \|\|*

31-32. You should also get yourself devout fully sprinkled with its holy water There are many other tirthas, by bathing into which a man goes to heaven. Those who die there are not re-born. The Yamuna, too, has been described to be sacred like the Ganges, but the latter is held more in veneration as the older of the two, by all classes everywhere.

## \|\| 108.33 \|\|

*evaṃ kuruṣva kaunteya sarvatīrthābhiṣecanam \|*  
*yāvadjīvakṛtaṃ pāpaṃ tatkṣaṇādeva naṣyati \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Yudhisthira! you should sprinkle yourself with the holy waters of each tirtha, by doing which all the sins of life will be consumed.

## \|\| 108.34 \|\|

*yastvimaṃ kalya utthāya paṭhate ca śṛṇoti ca \|*  
*mucyate sarvapāpebhyaḥ svargalokaṃ sa gacchati \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. One who reads or hears this Mahatmya, in the morning, is freed from all his sins and goes to heaven.

## Chapter 109

## \|\| 109.1-2 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca*  
*śrutaṃ me brahmaṇā proktaṃ purāṇe brahmasambhave \|*  
*tīrthānāṃ tu sahasrāṇi śatāni niutāni ca \|*  
*sarve puṇyāḥ pavitrāśca gatiśca paramā smṛtā \|\| 1 \|\|*

*somatīrthaṃ mahāpuṇyaṃ mahāpātakanāśanam \|*  
*snānamātreṇa rājendra puruṣāṃstārayecchatam \|*  
*tasmātsarvaprayatnena tatra snānaṃ samācaret \|\| 2 \|\|*

1-2. Markandeya said: — The thousands of tirthas that I have heard described in the Brahma Purana by Brahma, are sacred, purifying and givers of emancipation. There is one Somatirtha which is the most sacred and the dispeller of all sins, where by mere bathing one gets the deliverance of hundreds of his ancestors; one should, therefore, unavoidably bathe in it,

## \|\| 109.3-5 \|\|

*yudhiṣṭhira uvāca*  
*pṛthivyāṃ naimiṣaṃ puṇyam antarikṣe ca puṣkaram \|*  
*trayāṇāmapi lokānāṃ kurukṣetraṃ viśiṣyate \|\| 3 \|\|*

*sarvāṇi tāni saṃtyajya kathamekaṃ praśaṃsasi \|*  
*apramāṇaṃ tu tatroktam aśraddheyamanuttamam \|\| 4 \|\|*

*gatiṃ ca paramāṃ divyāṃ bhogāṃścaiva yathepsitān \|*  
*kimarthamalpayogena bahu dharmaṃ praśaṃsasi \|*  
*etanme saṃśayaṃ brūhi yathādṛṣṭaṃ yathāśrutam \|\| 5 \|\|*

3-5. Yudhisthira said: — Naimisharanya tirtha on earth, Pushkara in Akasha, and Kurukshetra in the three worlds are the most famous. How do you then extol the greatness of Prayaga only and leave the rest. I feel it difficult to put my faith in your words, which seem to me to be not good without any proof. How does one attain emancipation, virtues and various kinds of happiness by residing there for a few days only? Pray do remove my doubts, from what you have seen and heard.

## \|\| 109.6 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca*  
*aśraddheyaṃ na vaktavyaṃ pratyakṣamapi yadbhavet \|*  
*narasyāśraddadhānasya pāpopahatacetasaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Markandeya said: — Anything in which faith cannot be ‘put, should not be uttered, even if it is based on the direct perception of a person without faith and whose mind is vitiated by sin.

## \|\| 109.7-9 \|\|

*aśraddadhāno hyaśucir durmatistyaktamaṅgalaḥ \|*  
*ete pātakinaḥ sarve tenedaṃ bhāṣitaṃ tvayā \|\| 7 \|\|*

*śṛṇu prayāgamāhātmyaṃ yathādṛṣṭaṃ yathāśrutam \|*  
*pratyakṣaṃ ca parokṣaṃ ca yathānyastaṃ bhaviṣyati \|\| 8 \|\|*

*yathaivānyadadṛṣṭaṃ ca yathādṛṣṭaṃ yathāśrutam \|*  
*śāstraṃ pramāṇaṃ kṛtvā ca ujyate yogamātmanaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

7-9. Those who are faithless, unchaste, evil minded and wicked, are great sinners. (You must have some sin) that is why you have said so.

Now hear the greatness of Prayaga, which I shall tell you as I have heard and seen it directly or indirectly. Whatever else is seen, heard or not seen should be clear to you, if you meditate on them with concentration, taking the Shastras as your ground of evidence.

## \|\| 109.10 \|\|

*kliṣyate cāparastatra naiva yogamavāpnuyāt \|*  
*janmāntarasahasrebhyo yogo labhyeta mānavaiḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Therefore, a man inclined to doubt gets pain and not Yoga. The latter 1s attained in thousands of lives.

## \|\| 109.11-12 \|\|

*yathā yogasahasreṇa yogo labhyeta mānavaiḥ \|*  
*yastu sarvāṇi ratnāni brāhmaṇebhyaḥ prayacchati \|\| 11 \|\|*

*tena dānena dattena yogaṃ nābhyeti mānavaḥ \|*  
*prayāge tu mṛtasyedaṃ sarvaṃ bhavati nānyathā \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-12. A man attains (true) Yoga after performing thousands of Yogas, and not by giving away thousands of gems to the Brahmans, but one dying at Prayaga undoubtedly gets all the benefits.

## \|\| 109.13-14 \|\|

*pradhānahetuṃ vakṣyāmi śraddadhatsva ca bhārata \|*  
*yathā sarveṣu bhūteṣu brahma sarvatra dṛṣyate \|\| 13 \|\|*

*brāhmaṇe vāsti yatkiṃcid abrāhmam iti vocyate \|*  
*evaṃ sarveṣu bhūteṣu brahma sarvatra pūjyate \|\| 14 \|\|*

13-14. King! Now hear this main reason in good faith. Though Brahma is omnipresent in every being, He is deemed to be particularly present in Brahmana, other things being called abrahma. He is, however, worshipped in all the beings.

## \|\| 109.15 \|\|

*tathā sarveṣu lokeṣu prayāgaṃ pūjayedbudhaḥ \|*  
*pūjyate tīrtharājastu satyameva udhiṣṭhira \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Therefore, O, Yudhisthira! the learned adore the holy Prayaga among all other tirthas. This Prayaga is indeed to be worshipped as the King of all tirthas.

## \|\| 109.16 \|\|

*brahmāpi smarate nityaṃ prayāgaṃ tīrthamuttamam \|*  
*tīrtharājam anuprāpya na cānyatkiṃcidarhati \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Because Brahma also thinks of the same holy place every day, that is why wise men after attaining the sacred Prayaga do not feel inclined for anything else.

## \|\| 109.17 \|\|

*ko hi devatvamāsādya manuṣyatvaṃ cikīrṣati \|*  
*anenaivopamānena tvaṃ jñāsyasi udhiṣṭhira \|*  
*yathā puṇyatamaṃ cāsti tathaiva kathitaṃ mayā \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. O, Yudhisthira! whoever wishes to be classed among the mortals after becoming one with the Devas? You will surely understand by these examples why \| have described Prayaga to you as the most sacred and a ready dispeller of sins among the various tirthas.

## \|\| 109.18 \|\|

*yudhiṣṭhira uvāca*  
*śrutaṃ cedaṃ tvayā proktaṃ vismito 'haṃ punaḥ punaḥ \|*  
*kathaṃ yogena tatprāptiḥ svargavāsastu karmaṇā \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Yudhisthira said: — I have heard the greatness of Prayaga and am wondering, by what virtue the holy tirtha is obtained and how one goes to reside in heaven?

## \|\| 109.19 \|\|

*dātā vai labhate bhogān gāṃ ca yatkarmaṇaḥ phalam \|*  
*tāni karmāṇi pṛcchāmi punastaiḥ prāpyate mahī \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. I venture to enquire from you the means by which the giver of charity enjoys the world, with a store of happiness, by constantly being born in it

## \|\| 109.20-21 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca*  
*śṛṇu rājanmahābāho yathoktakaraṇaṃ mahīm \|*  
*gāmagniṃ brāhmaṇaṃ śāstraṃ kāñcanaṃ salilaṃ striyaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*mātaraṃ pitaraṃ caiva ye nindanti narādhamāḥ \|*  
*na teṣāmūrdhvagamanam idamāha prajāpatiḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

20-21. Markandeya said: — King! Brahma has said that the wicked who despise the earth, the cow, the fire, the Brahmans, the Shastras, the gold, the water, the women, the mother and the father, do not reach to the higher regions.

## \|\| 109.22 \|\|

*evaṃ yogasya samprāpti-sthānaṃ paramadurlabham \|*  
*gacchanti narakaṃ ghoraṃ ye narāḥ pāpakarmiṇaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Similarly the attainment of Yoga has been said to be very difficult. Those who follow a sinful life go to the worst region in hell.

## \|\| 109.23-24 \|\|

*hastyaśvaṃ gām anaḍvāhaṃ maṇimuktādikāñcanam \|*  
*parokṣaṃ harate yastu paścāddānaṃ prayacchati \|\| 23 \|\|*

*na te gacchanti vai svargaṃ dātāro yatra bhoginaḥ \|*  
*anenakarmaṇā uktāḥ pacyante narake punaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

23-24. The one who steals elephants, horses, cows, bullocks, jewels, pearl and gold, and then gives them in charity, never goes to heaven where the giver in good faith enjoys himself. They become addicted to many a (sinful) act and go to hell.

## \|\| 109.23 \|\|

*hastyaśvaṃ gām anaḍvāhaṃ maṇimuktādikāñcanam \|*  
*parokṣaṃ harate yastu paścāddānaṃ prayacchati \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Similarly I am telling you about Yoga, Dharma, chief traits of a donor, the truth and the untruth and good and evil fruits; as enunciated by the Lord Sun in ancient times.

## Chapter 110

## \|\| 110.1-3 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca*  
*śṛṇu rājanprayāgasya māhātmyaṃ punareva tu \|*  
*naimiṣaṃ puṣkaraṃ caiva gotīrthaṃ sindhusāgaram \|\| 1 \|\|*

*gayā ca caitrakaṃ caiva gaṅgāsāgarameva ca \|*  
*ete cānye ca bahavo ye ca puṇyāḥ śiloccayāḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*daśa tīrthasahasrāṇi triṃśatkoṭyastathā parāḥ \|*  
*prayāge saṃsthitā nityam evamāhurmanīṣiṇaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

1-3. Markandeya said: — King! Hear from me something further about the greatness of Prayaga. ‘The sages have said that Naimisha, Pushkara, Gotirtha, Sindhusagara, Gaya, Chaitrakatirtha, Gangasagara and other sacred hills &c., along with 30 crores of other tirthas are present there.

## \|\| 110.4-5 \|\|

*trīṇi cāpyagnikuṇḍāni yeṣāṃ madhye tu jāhnavī \|*  
*prayāgādabhiniṣkrāntā sarvatīrthanamaskṛtā \|\| 4 \|\|*

*tapanasya sutā devī triṣu lokeṣu viśrutā \|*  
*yamunā gaṅgayā sārdhaṃ saṃgatā lokabhāvinī \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. In their midst are the three Agnikundas and the Ganges runs in the middle of them. The daughter of the Sun, the Yamuna — venerated by all the tirthas, has appeared in Prayaga and meets the Ganges at the confluence.

## \|\| 110.6-7 \|\|

*gaṅgāyamunayormadhye pṛthivyā jaghanaṃ smṛtam \|*  
*prayāgaṃ rājaśārdūla kalāṃ nārhati ṣoḍaśīm \|\| 6 \|\|*

*tisraḥ koṭyo 'rdhakoṭiśca tīrthānāṃ vāurabravīt \|*  
*divi bhuvyantarikṣe ca tatsarvaṃ jāhnavī smṛtā \|\| 7 \|\|*

6-7. The middle of the waist of the earth is said to be between the Ganges and the Yamuna and no other tirthas are even equal to 1/16th of its greatness. It is said by Vayu (or in Vayu purana?) that the 3½ crores of tirthas of Heaven, Akasha and the earth are to be found in the Ganges.

## \|\| 110.8 \|\|

*prayāgaṃ samadhiṣṭhānaṃ kambalāśvatarāvubhau \|*  
*bhogavatyatha yā caiṣā vedireṣā prajāpateḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Prayaga is the place where both Kambala and Ashvatara reside. This place of enjoyment is described as the altar of Prajapati.

## \|\| 110.9-10 \|\|

*tatra vedāśca yajñāśca mūrtimanto udhiṣṭhira \|*  
*prajāpatim upāsante ṛṣayaśca tapodhanāḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*yajante kratubhir devās tathā cakradharā nṛpāḥ \|*  
*tataḥ puṇyatamaṃ nāsti triṣu lokeṣu bhārata \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. There the incarnate Vedas and yajnas (sacrifices), O, Yudhisthira! adore Brahma, as do ascetics, the sages. The Devas, and the kings adore Prayaga by performing sacrifices. There is nothing more sacred than Prayaga in all the three worlds.

## \|\| 110.11-12 \|\|

*prabhāvātsarvatīrthebhyaḥ prabhavatyadhikaṃ vibho \|*  
*daśa tīrthasahasrāṇi tisraḥ koṭyastathā parāḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*yatra gaṅgā mahābhāgā sa deśastattapodhanam \|*  
*siddhakṣetraṃ ca vijñeyaṃ gaṅgātīrasamanvitam \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-12. The tirtha of Prayaga is by its own virtue sacred of all the tirthas. The place having the Ganges along with 3 crores and 10,000 tirthas is the holiest of all. The whole of Prayaga is sacred owing to its being situated on the banks of the Ganges.

## \|\| 110.12-15 \|\|

*yatra gaṅgā mahābhāgā sa deśastattapodhanam \|*  
*siddhakṣetraṃ ca vijñeyaṃ gaṅgātīrasamanvitam \|\| 12 \|\|*

*idaṃ satyaṃ vijānīyāt sādhūnāmātmanaśca vai \|*  
*suhṛdaśca japetkarṇe śiṣyasyānugatasya ca \|\| 13 \|\|*

*idaṃ dhanyamidaṃ svargyam idaṃ satyamidaṃ sukham \|*  
*idaṃ puṇyamidaṃ dharmyaṃ pāvanaṃ dharmamuttamam \|\| 14 \|\|*

*maharṣīṇāmidaṃ guhyaṃ sarvapāpapraṇāśanam \|*  
*adhītya ca dvijo 'pyetan nirmalaḥ svargamāpnuyāt \|\| 15 \|\|*

12-15. Know this to be the truth. The good should din it into the ears of their friends, pupils and the servants, that Prayaga is blessed, is the giver of heaven, is the very personification of bliss and truth; is sacred, and is the giver of Dharma, the dispeller of all sins, and is not (fully) known even to the great sages. The twice born by reading this Mahatmya become purified and go to heaven.

## \|\| 110.16 \|\|

*ya idaṃ śṛṇuyānnityaṃ tīrthaṃ puṇyaṃ sadā śuciḥ \|*  
*jātismaratvaṃ labhate nākapṛṣṭhe ca modate \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. One who, with a pure heart, listens every day to the greatness of this tirtha, remembers his past lives and enjoys heaven.

## \|\| 110.17-18 \|\|

*prāpyante tāni tīrthāni sadbhiḥ śiṣṭānudarśibhiḥ \|*  
*snāhi tīrtheṣu kauravya na ca vakramatirbhava \|\| 17 \|\|*

*tvayā ca samyakpṛṣṭena kathitaṃ vai mayā vibho \|*  
*pitarastāritāḥ sarve tathaiva ca pitāmahāḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

17-18. The good only attain this tirtha, therefore, O, Yudhisthira, you should also bathe in these tirthas after discarding all misgiving. O, King! I have explained all this has asked by you, you have saved your ancestors by putting all these questions to me.

## \|\| 110.19-20 \|\|

*vrataṃ dānaṃ tapastīrthaṃ yāgāḥ sarve sadakṣiṇāḥ \|*  
*yogāḥ sāṃkhyaṃ sadācāro ye cānye jñānahetavaḥ \|*  
*prayāgasya tu sarve te kalāṃ nārhanti ṣoḍaśīm \|\| 19 \|\|*

*evaṃ jñānaṃ ca yogaśca tīrthaṃ caiva udhiṣṭhira \|*  
*bahukleśena ujyante tena yānti parāṃ gatim \|*  
*trikālaṃ jāyate jñānaṃ svargalokaṃ gamiṣyati \|\| 20 \|\|*

19-20. O, Yudhisthira! The tirthas enumerated before do not reach even 1/16th the Sanctity of Prayaga. The pilgrimage to these tirthas removes all adverse tensions and one attains knowledge and go to the upper region by virtue of bathing in these tirthas.

## Chapter 111

## \|\| 111.1 \|\|

*\*yudhiṣṭhira uvāca*  
*kathaṃ sarvamidaṃ proktaṃ prayāgasya mahāmune*  
*etannaḥ sarvamākhyāhi yathā hi mama tārayet // MatsP\_111.1*

Yudhisthira  said:  “O  Great  sage,  you  have spoken  all  about  the  glory  of  Prayaga.  What  is the  reason  for  it?  You  speak  out  the  same  to enable  me  and  my  family  get  salvation.

## \|\| 111.2 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca*  
*śṛṇu rājanprayāge tu proktaṃ sarvamidaṃ jagat*  
*brahmā viṣṇustatheśāno devatāḥ prabhuravyayaḥ // MatsP\_111.2*

Markandeya said:  “You  listen to the  cause of  the  same.  It  is  stated  that  the  entire  universe lives  at  Prayaga.  The  most  competent  and eternal  Brahma,  Vispu  and  Siva,  besides  all  the gods  live  here.

## \|\| 111.3-4\|\|

*brahmā sṛjati bhūtāni sthāvaraṃ jaṅgamaṃ ca yat*  
*tānyetāni paraṃ loke viṣṇuḥ saṃvardhate prajāḥ // MatsP\_111.3*  
*kalpānte tatsamagraṃ hi rudraḥ saṃharate jagat*  
*tadā prayāgatīrthaṃ ca na kadācidvinaśyati // MatsP\_111.4*

Whatever  moveable  kate   immovable creatures  are  created  by  Brahma,  are  maintained here  on  earth  by  Visnu.  At  the  end  of  the  kalpa Siva  destroys  the  entire  universe.  But  the  place of  Prayaga  never  gets  destroyed.

## \|\| 111.5 \|\|

*īśvaraḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ yaḥ paśyati sa paśyati*  
*yatnenānena tiṣṭhanti te yānti paramāṃ gatim // MatsP\_111.5*

The  one  who  is  lord  of  all  the  living  beings and  takes  care  of  them,  and  the  people  who  live here  with  this  idea,  they  achieve  salvation.”

## \|\| 111.6 \|\|

*yudhiṣṭhira uvāca*  
*ākhyāhi me yathātathyaṃ yathaiṣā tiṣṭhati śrutiḥ*  
*kena vā kāraṇenaiva tiṣṭhante lokasattamāḥ // MatsP\_111.6*

Yudhisthira  said: "O  Sage,  how  do  the  best of  the  gods  live  in  Prayaga?  You  tell  me  about the  same,  as  provided  in  the  scriptures.”

## \|\| 111.7 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca*  
*prayāge nivasantyete brahmaviṣṇumaheśvarāḥ*  
*kāraṇaṃ tatpravakṣyāmi śṛṇu tattvaṃ yudhiṣṭhira // MatsP\_111.7*

Markandeya  said: “The  purpose  for  which Brahma, Visnu thāt‌ Maheshvara,  live  at  Prayaga, I am  going to reveal the same.  You listen from me  the  relevant  tattvas.

## \|\| 111.8-9 \|\|

*pañcayojanavistīrṇaṃ prayāgasya tu maṇḍalam*  
*tiṣṭhanti rakṣaṇāyātra pāpakarmanivāraṇāt // MatsP\_111.8*  
*uttareṇa pratiṣṭhānāc chadmanā brahma tiṣṭhati*  
*veṇīmādhavarūpī tu bhagavāṃstatra tiṣṭhati // MatsP\_111.9*

The  region  of  Prayaga  is  spread  over  an  area  of  five  yojanas.  The  aforesaid  gods  reside  here for  the  removal  of  the  sins  and  for  the  protection of  the  people.  Brahma  lives  to  the  north  of  
Pratisthanapura.  Lord  Vispu  is present  in Prayaga  in  the  form  of  Beni-Madhava.

## \|\| 111.10 \|\|

*māheśvaro vaṭo bhūtvā tiṣṭhate parameśvaraḥ*  
*tato devāḥ sagandharvāḥ siddhāśca paramarṣayaḥ*  
*rakṣanti maṇḍalaṃ nityaṃ pāpakarmanivāraṇāt // MatsP\_111.10*

Then  lord  Siva  is lodged  at  Prayaga  in  the form  of  Aksaya-vata.  Besides  them,  all  the gods,  with  Gandharvas,  Siddhas  and  the  groups  
of  the  great  sages,  protect  Prayaga  for  the removal  of  the  sins.

## \|\| 111.11-12 \|\|

*yasmiñjuhvansvakaṃ pāpaṃ narakaṃ ca na paśyati*  
*evaṃ brahmā ca viṣṇuśca prayāge sa maheśvaraḥ // MatsP\_111.11*  
*saptadvīpāḥ samudrāśca parvatāśca mahītale*  
*rakṣamāṇāśca tiṣṭhanti yāvadābhūtasaṃplavam // MatsP\_111.12*

A  person,  who performing  homa  with  his  sins,  does  not  have  to  cast  a  glance  at  the  hell, similarly  all  the  gods  like  Brahma,  Visnu, Mahesvara,  the  seven  islands,  the  seven  oceans, all  the  mountains  on  earth,  stay  at  Prayaga  till the  time  of  dissolution,  protecting  it.

## \|\| 111.13 \|\|

*ye cānye bahavaḥ sarve tiṣṭhanti ca yudhiṣṭhira*  
*yat pṛthivī tatsamāśritya nirmitā daivatais tribhiḥ // MatsP\_111.13*

O  Yudhisthira,  besides  them  such  of  the gods,  who,  taking  refuge  in  the  land,  live  here, the  dwelling  places  for  them  were  built  by  these gods.

## \|\| 111.14 \|\|

*prajāpateridaṃ kṣetraṃ prayāgamiti viśrutam*  
*etatpuṇyaṃ pavitraṃ vai prayāgaṃ ca yudhiṣṭhira*  
*svarājyaṃ kuru rājendra bhrātṛbhiḥ sahito 'nagha // MatsP\_111.14*

Prayaga  is  the  region  of  Prajapati  Brahma. This  is  well  known.  O  Yudhisthira,  the  place  of Prayaga  is  quite  auspicious  and  sacred.  O sinless  Rajendra,  you  better  take  care  of  your brothers  and  the  kingdom.

## Chapter 112

## \|\| 112.1 \|\|

*nandikeśvara uvāca*  
*bhrātṛbhiḥ sahitaḥ sarvair draupadyā saha bhāryayā \|*  
*brāhmaṇebhyo namaskṛtya gurūndevānatarpayat \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Nandikeshvara said: — Narada! Having placed full belief in the words of the Sage Markandeya, Yudhisthira along with the other Pandavas went to Prayaga where after saluting the Brahmanas they offered libations of water to the Pitris and the Devas &c.

## \|\| 112.2-3 \|\|

*vāsudevo 'pi tatraiva kṣaṇenābhyāgatastadā \|*  
*pāṇḍavaiḥ sahitaiḥ sarvaiḥ pūjyamānastu mādhavaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*kṛṣṇena sahitaiḥ sarvaiḥ punareva mahātmabhiḥ \|*  
*abhiṣiktaḥ svarājye ca dharmaputro udhiṣṭhiraḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

2-3. There in a few moments, Shrikrishna also turned up, when He and other Pandavas anointed Yudhisthira and proclaimed him Emperor.

## \|\| 112.4-5 \|\|

*etasminnantare caiva mārkaṇḍeyo mahāmuniḥ \|*  
*tataḥ svastīti coktvā tu kṣaṇādāśramamāgamat \|\| 4 \|\|*

*yudhiṣṭhiro 'pi dharmātmā bhrātṛbhiḥ sahito 'vasat \|*  
*mahādānaṃ tato dattvā dharmaputro mahāmanāḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. At the same hour, the Sage Markandeya also appeared there, and returned to his hermitage after pouring his blessings on Yudhisthira.

After that the virtuous Yudhisthira, with an easy mind, began to rule over his empire after bestowing great charity.

## \|\| 112.6 \|\|

*yastvidaṃ kalya utthāya māhātmyaṃ paṭhate naraḥ \|*  
*prayāgaṃ smarate nityaṃ sa yāti paramaṃ padam \|*  
*mucyate sarvapāpebhyo rudralokaṃ sa gacchati \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. One who reads this Mahatmya in the morning, and remembers Prayaga every day attains bliss and goes to the world of Shiva, after being free from his sins.

## \|\| 112.7-8 \|\|

*vāsudeva uvāca*  
*mama vākyaṃ ca kartavyaṃ mahārāja bravīmyaham \|*  
*nityaṃ japasva juhvasva prayāge vigatajvaraḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*
