*prayāgaṃ smara vai nityaṃ sahāsmābhiryudhiṣṭhira \|*  
*svayaṃ prāpsyasi rājendra svargalokaṃ na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8. Vasudeva said: — O, King! hear what I say. You will undoubtedly rise to heaven, if you will remember Prayaga every day.

## \|\| 112.9 \|\|

*prayāgamanugacchedvā vasate vāpi yo naraḥ \|*  
*sarvapāpaviśuddhātmā rudralokaṃ sa gacchati \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. One who goes to, or resides in, Prayaga goes to the world of Rudra, after being freed from all his sins.

## \|\| 112.10 \|\|

*pratigrahādupāvṛttaḥ saṃtuṣṭo niyataḥ śuciḥ \|*  
*ahaṃkāranivṛttaśca sa tīrthaphalamaśnute \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. The Brahmana who is contented and does not accept gifts, and is chaste and devoid of conceit, attains the merits of a pilgrimage to this tirtha.

## \|\| 112.11 \|\|

*akopanaśca satyaśca satyavādī dṛḍhavrataḥ \|*  
*ātmopamaśca bhūteṣu sa tīrthaphalamaśnute \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. One who is free from the feeling of anger, is truthful and regards all the beings like himself, also attains the merits of a pilgrimage to this tirtha.

## \|\| 112.12-13 \|\|

*ṛṣibhiḥ kratavaḥ proktā devaiścāpi yathākramam \|*  
*na hi śakyā daridreṇa yajñāḥ prāptuṃ mahīpate \|\| 12 \|\|*

*bahūpakaraṇā yajñā nānāsambhāravistarāḥ \|*  
*prāpyante pārthivairetaiḥ samṛddhairvai naraiḥ kvacit \|\| 13 \|\|*

12-13. O, King! The Yajnas, defined by the Seers and the Devas, cannot be performed by a man of limited means. Consequently the benefits accruing from such sacrifices are attainable only to the well-to-do and not to the poor.

## \|\| 112.14 \|\|

*yo daridrairapi vidhiḥ śakyaḥ prāptuṃ nareśvara \|*  
*tulyo yajñaphalaiḥ puṇyais tannibodha udhiṣṭhira \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Therefore, O, Yudhisthira! also hear from me the means by which the poor attain the benefits of such sacrifices.

## \|\| 112.15 \|\|

*ṛṣīṇāṃ paramaṃ guhyam idaṃ bharatasattama \|*  
*tīrthānugamanaṃ puṇyaṃ yajñebhyo 'pi viśiṣyate \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. The sages have said that it is highly beneficial to go to the sacred places.

## \|\| 112.16 \|\|

*daśa tīrthasahasrāṇi tisraḥ koṭyastathāpagāḥ \|*  
*māghamāse gamiṣyanti gaṅgāyāṃ bharatarṣabha \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. O, King! ten thousand tirthas and three crores of rivers go and dwell in the Ganges during the month of Magha.

## \|\| 112.17 \|\|

*svastho bhava mahārāja bhuṅkṣva rājyamakaṇṭakam \|*  
*punardrakṣyasi rājendra yajamāno viśeṣataḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17 O, King! you will also repeat visiting Prayaga, after performing sacrifices and ruling over your dominions with a balanced disposition.

## \|\| 112.18-19 \|\|

*nandikeśvara uvāca*  
*ityuktvā sa mahābhāgo mārkaṇḍeyo mahātapāḥ \|*  
*yudhiṣṭhirasya nṛpates tatraivāntaradhīyata \|\| 18 \|\|*

*tatastatra samāplāvya gātrāṇi sagaṇo nṛpaḥ \|*  
*yathoktenātha vidhinā parāṃ nirvṛtimāgamat \|\| 19 \|\|*

18-19. Nandikeshvara said: — After having described the glory of Prayaga, that great Seer Markandeya disappeared then and there; then the King Yudhisthira attained great happiness by going to, and bathing at, Prayaga along with his retinue following the prescribed rules.

## \|\| 112.20 \|\|

*tathā tvamapi devarṣe prayāgābhimukho bhava \|*  
*abhiṣekaṃ tu kṛtvādya kṛtakṛtyo bhaviṣyasi \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. O, Narada! you are also in Prayaga. Sanctify yourself by sprinkling the holy waters.

## \|\| 112.21 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*evamuktvātha nandīśas tatraivāntaradhīyata \|*  
*nārado 'pi jagāmāśu prayāgābhimukhastathā \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Sita said: — O Rishis! After thus narrating the whole thing to Narada, Nandikeshvara vanished at the spot, and the former instantly went to Prayaga.

## \|\| 112.22 \|\|

*tatra snātvā ca japtvā ca vidhidṛṣṭena karmaṇā \|*  
*dānaṃ dattvā dvijāgryebhyo gataḥ svabhavanaṃ tadā \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Thereafter, bathing and giving alms to the Brahmans, he returned to his abode.

## Chapter 113

## \|\| 113.1 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ*  
*kati dvīpāḥ samudrā vā parvatā vā kati prabho \|*  
*kiyanti caiva varṣāṇi teṣu nadyaśca kāḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. The Rishis said: — Sir, How many spheres (dvipas) are there of the world, as well as how many oceans and mountains are there? How many zones (varshas) are there, and what are the rivers mentioned as flowing In them?

## \|\| 113.2 \|\|

*mahābhūmipramāṇaṃ ca lokālokastathaiva ca \|*  
*paryāptiṃ parimāṇaṃ ca gatiścandrārkayostathā \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. What is the extent of the Great Earth and of the Lokaloka mountains? What are the circumference and size of the moon and the sun, and what is their course?

## \|\| 113.3 \|\|

*etadbravīhi naḥ sarvaṃ vistareṇa yathārthavit \|*  
*tvaduktametatsakalaṃ śrotumicchāmahe vayam \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Pray be good enough, O knower of truth, to explain all this to us at full length, because we are always anxious to hear all this from you.

## \|\| 113.4 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*dvīpabhedasahasrāṇi sapta cāntargatāni ca \|*  
*na śakyante krameṇeha vaktuṃ vai sakalaṃ jagat \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Suta said: — The Dvipas are several thousands in number, and out of them seven are important ones To describe them all, in this place, in their entirety is not possible.

## \|\| 113.5 \|\|

*saptaiva tu pravakṣyāmi candrādityagrahaiḥ saha \|*  
*teṣāṃ manuṣyatarkeṇa pramāṇāni pracakṣate \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. I shall explain to you something about the moon, the sun, the planets, along with the seven only of the important Dvipas, giving their dimensions as established by human calculation

## \|\| 113.6 \|\|

*acintyāḥ khalu ye bhāvās tāṃstu tarkeṇa sādhayet \|*  
*prakṛtibhyaḥ paraṃ yacca tadacintyasya lakṣaṇam \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. The things which are “inconceivable” should be established by reasoning. The definition of “inconceivable” is this, viz., “a thing not understood by common people (by their common sense)”.

## \|\| 113.7 \|\|

*sapta varṣāṇi vakṣyāmi jambūdvīpaṃ yathāvidham \|*  
*vistaraṃ maṇḍalaṃ yacca yojanaistānnibodhata \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. I shall now proceed to tell you something about the seven varshas (zones) and about Jambudvipa. Now listen to the entire extent of Jambudvipa in terms of Yojanas.

## \|\| 113.8 \|\|

*yojanānāṃ sahasrāṇi śataṃ dvīpasya vistaraḥ \|*  
*nānājanapadākīrṇaṃ puraiśca vividhaiḥ śubhaiḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Its breadth (diameter) is 100,000 yojanas, and many countries and beautiful cities are to be found in it.

## \|\| 113.9 \|\|

*siddhacāraṇasaṃkīrṇaṃ parvatairupaśobhitam \|*  
*sarvadhātupinaddhaistaiḥ śilājālasamudgataiḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. It is full of Siddhas and Charanas, and is adorned by mountains, full of ores of all metals streaming out (as lava) from the different sides of rocks.

## \|\| 113.10 \|\|

*parvataprabhavābhiśca nadībhistu samantataḥ \|*  
*prāgāyatā mahāpārśvāḥ ṣaḍime varṣaparvatāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Besides these, it is beautifully embellished by various rivers flowing from the mountains. There are these six ranges of mountains, running from east to west, demarcating the six varshas.

## \|\| 113.11 \|\|

*avagāhya hyubhayataḥ samudrau pūrvapaścimau \|*  
*himaprāyaśca himavān hemakūṭaśca hemavān \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Stretching to the sea on both sides, east and west stand (1) the Himalaya, full of snow (hima) and (2) Hemakuta full of gold (hema).

## \|\| 113.12 \|\|

*sarvataḥ sumukhaścāpi niṣadhaḥ parvato mahān \|*  
*cāturvarṇyastu sauvarṇo meruścolbamayaḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*caturviṃśatsahasrāṇi vistīrṇaḥ sa caturdiśam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Then comes the great (3) Nishadha mountain, which is beautiful to look at on all sides. Then there is the golden mountain (4) Meru, with its four colours on its four sides, said to be bleak and barren. Its extent is 24,000 yojanas on four sides,

## \|\| 113.13 \|\|

*vṛttākṛtipramāṇaśca caturasraḥ samāhitaḥ \|*  
*nānāvarṇaiḥ samaḥ pārśvaiḥ prajāpatiguṇānvitaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. It has a circular form, divided into four quadrants. Its sides (quadrants) are of various uniform colours, with properties conferred upon it by Brahma (the Lord of creatures).

## \|\| 113.14 \|\|

*nābhībandhanasambhūto brahmaṇo 'vyaktajanmanaḥ \|*  
*pūrvataḥ śvetavarṇastu brāhmaṇyaṃ tasya tena vai \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. On its navel peduncle (east quadrant) sprung from the self-born unmanifested) Brahma there is white colour. Consequently, it is said to have Brahmanical properties.

## \|\| 113.15 \|\|

*pītaśca dakṣiṇenāsau tena vaiṣyatvamiṣyeta \|*  
*bhṛṅgipattrīnabhaś caiva paścimena samanvitaḥ \|*  
*tenāsya śūdratā siddhā meror nāmārthakarmataḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. On its southern quadrant, there is yellow colour, on account of which it is said to have the properties of the Vaishya caste. On its western quadrant, there is the colour of the wing of a black bee, owing to which it is said to possess the properties of Shudras.

## \|\| 113.16 \|\|

*pārśvamuttaratastasya raktavarṇaṃ svabhāvataḥ \|*  
*tenāsya kṣatrabhāvaḥ syād iti varṇāḥ prakīrtitāḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. {ts northern quadrant is naturally of red colour, therefore it has the properties of Kshatriyas. Thus the four colours and castes have been enumerated.

## \|\| 113.17 \|\|

*nīlaśca vaiḍūryamayaḥ śvetaḥ pīto hiraṇmayaḥ \|*  
*mayūrabarhavarṇaśca śātakaumbhaḥ sa śṛṅgavān \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. The mountain Nala is studded with lapis-lazuli. The mountain Shveta is yellow and full of gold. ‘The mountain Shringin is made of gold (satakumbha), and has the colour of the tail of a peacock.

## \|\| 113.18 \|\|

*ete parvatarājānaḥ siddhacāraṇasevitāḥ \|*  
*teṣāmantaraviṣkambho navasāhasramucyate \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. These mountains are the kings among their kind, and are the abode of Siddhas and Charanas. Their inner diameter is 9,000 yojanas.

## \|\| 113.19 \|\|

*madhye tvilāvṛtaṃ nāma mahāmeroḥ samantataḥ \|*  
*caturviṃśatsahasrāṇi vistīrṇo yojanaiḥ samaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19.\* The varsha Ilavrita stands in the middle and encircles the MahaMeru on all sides. Its expanse is 24,000 yojanas.

**Комментарий:**

\* It should be 34,000 instead of 24.000 or chatroshtrimsat, instead of chaturvimsat.

## \|\| 113.20 \|\|

*madhye tasya mahāmerur vidhūma iva pāvakaḥ \|*  
*vedyardhaṃ dakṣiṇaṃ meror uttarārdhaṃ tathottaram \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. In the centre of this (Ilavrata) stands the Great Meru, shining in its majestic glory, like the fireblaze, devoid of smoke. Its southern portion is called the Dakshina Meru and the northern the Uttara Meru.

## \|\| 113.21 \|\|

*varṣāṇi yāni saptātra teṣāṃ vai varṣaparvatāḥ \|*  
*dve dve sahasre vistīrṇā yojanairdakṣiṇottaram \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Each of these seven varshas (zones) has a boundary mountain of its own, which from north to south extends to 2,000 yojanas, and the southern ones are 2,000 yojanas in circumference.

## \|\| 113.22 \|\|

*jambūdvīpasya vistāras teṣāmāyāma ucyate \|*  
*nīlaśca niṣadhaścaiva teṣāṃ hīnāśca ye pare \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. The sum of the breadths of these varshas and mountain ranges is breadth of the Jambudvipa, as mentioned above. Of these Nila, Nishadha are the longest, and those that come after them diminish in length.

## \|\| 113.23 \|\|

*śvetaśca hemakūṭaśca himavāñchṛṅgavāṃśca yaḥ \|*  
*jambūdvīpapramāṇeṇa ṛṣabhaḥ parikīrtyate \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. So are Shveta, Hema Kuta, Himavan and Shringavan. Rishabha (Meru) is said to have the same extent as Jambudvipa.

## \|\| 113.24 \|\|

*tasmāddvādaśabhāgena hemakūṭo 'pi hīyate \|*  
*himavānviṃśabhāgena tasmādeva prahīyate \|*  
*aṣṭāśītisahasrāṇi hemakūṭo mahāgiriḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Hema-Kuta is shorter (than Meru) by 12,000 yojanas, and Himavan is shorter (than Meru) by 20,000 yojanas. The great Hema-Kuta is 88,000 yojanas.

## \|\| 113.25 \|\|

*aśītirhimavāñchaila āyataḥ pūrvapaścime \|*  
*dvīpasya maṇḍalībhāvād dhrāsavṛddhī prakīrtite \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. The Mount Himavan is 80,000 yojanas, from east to west. The dvipa (Jambudvipa) being spherical, this difference in extent of the mountains has sprung up.

## \|\| 113.26 \|\|

*varṣāṇāṃ parvatānāṃ ca yathābhedaṃ tathottaram \|*  
*teṣāṃ madhye janapadās tāni varṣāṇi sapta vai \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. As there is a distribution of the. mountains, so there is a distribution of the Vargas (along with them) one after another. Many peopled districts are in them. These varshas are seven in number.

## \|\| 113.27 \|\|

*prapātaviṣamaistaistu parvatairāvṛtāni tu \|*  
*sapta tāni nadībhedair agamyāni parasparam \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. They (the varshas) are surrounded by precipitous and insurmountable mountains. All the seven are mutually inaccessible by different rivers.

## \|\| 113.28 \|\|

*vasanti teṣu sattvāni nānājātīni sarvaśaḥ \|*  
*imaṃ haimavataṃ varṣaṃ bhārataṃ nāma viśrutam \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. In those regions, various species of animals are found everywhere. This varsha of the Himavat is known as Bharata.

## \|\| 113.29 \|\|

*hemakūṭaṃ paraṃ tasmān nāmnā kimpuruṣaṃ smṛtam \|*  
*hemakūṭācca niṣadhaṃ harivarṣaṃ taducyate \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Beyond that, up to Hema-Kuta, is the land (varsha) of the Kimpurushas, and from the borders of Hema Kuta up to Nishadha is the Harivarsha.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — Kimpurusha — Low man. A mythical being, with a human head and the form of a horse.

Nishadha — Hard. Name of a mountain. Name of a country governed by Nala.

Harivarsha — One of the nine divisions of Jambudvipa.

## \|\| 113.30 \|\|

*harivarṣātparaṃ cāpi merostu tadilāvṛtam \|*  
*ilāvṛtātparaṃ nīlaṃ ramyakaṃ nāma viśrutam \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. The other limit of Hari-varsha is Meru, and further on is Ilavrata, beyond which extends Ramyaka to the Nila mountain.

## \|\| 113.31 \|\|

*ramyakādaparaṃ śvetaṃ viśrutaṃ taddhiraṇyakam \|*  
*hiraṇyakātparaṃ caiva śṛṅgaśākaṃkuraṃ smṛtam \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Next to Ramyaka stands the Shveta mountain in whose region is Hiranyaka (varsha) and next to it, is Shringashaka, which is also known as Kuru.

## \|\| 113.32 \|\|

*dhanuḥsaṃsthe tu vijñeye devarṣe dakṣiṇottare \|*  
*dīrghāṇi tasya catvāri madhyamaṃ tadilāvṛtam \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. On the north and south there are two bow-shaped continents, extending over 400 yojanas, and Il4vrata stands in the middle of them.

## \|\| 113.33 \|\|

*pūrvato niṣadhasyedaṃ vedyardhaṃ dakṣiṇaṃ smṛtam \|*  
*paraṃ tvilāvṛtaṃ paścād vedyardhaṃ tu taduttaram \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Half of it is Dakshina Ilavrita and the rest of it is Uttara Ilavrita.

## \|\| 113.34 \|\|

*tayormadhye tu vijñeyo meruryatra tvilāvṛtam \|*  
*dakṣiṇena tu nīlasya niṣadhasyottareṇa tu \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Between “hem is Meru in Ilavrita, to the south of Nila mountain and to the north of Nishadha.

## \|\| 113.35 \|\|

*udagāyato mahāśailo mālyavānnāma parvataḥ \|*  
*dvātriṃśatā sahasreṇa pratīcyāṃ sāgarānugaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. The Mount Malyavan, stretching north to south, which is 32,000 yojanas in length enters the sea on the west.

## \|\| 113.36 \|\|

*mālyavānvai sahasraika ā nīlaniṣadhāyataḥ \|*  
*dvātriṃśattvevamapyuktaḥ parvato gandhamādanaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Malyavan is a thousand yojanas from Nila to Nishadha and Gandha Madana, is 32 yojanas.

## \|\| 113.37 \|\|

*parimaṇḍalayormadhye meruḥ kanakaparvataḥ \|*  
*cāturvarṇyasamo varṇaiś caturasraḥ samucchritaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Within their circumferences is the square and lofty golden Sumeru Mountain, which is of fourfold colour, like the four castes.

## \|\| 113.38 \|\|

*nānāvarṇaḥ sa pārśveṣu pūrvānte śveta ucyate \|*  
*pītaṃ tu dakṣiṇaṃ tasya bhṛṅgipattranibhaṃ param \|*  
*uttaraṃ tasya raktaṃ vai iti varṇasamanvitaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. There are different colours on its sides: on the cast it is white, on the south, it is yellow, on the west, it is like the wing of the black-bees, on the north, it is red. These are the different colours.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — Bhringi — A poisonous plant, a fig tree.

## \|\| 113.39 \|\|

*merustu śuśubhe divyo rājavatsa tu veṣṭitaḥ \|*  
*ādityataruṇābhāso vidhūma iva pāvakaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. The Mount Meru shines out like the rising sun or the blaze of fire without smoke, in the heart of those Mountains, like a divine king.

## \|\| 113.40 \|\|

*yojanānāṃ sahasrāṇi caturāśītisūcchritaḥ \|*  
*praviṣṭaḥ ṣoḍaśādhastād aṣṭāviṃśativistṛtaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. That Sumeru is 84,000 yojanas high, 16,000 yojanas deep underground and 28,000 yojanas broad.

## \|\| 113.41 \|\|

*vistarāddviguṇaścāsya parīṇāhaḥ samantataḥ \|*  
*sa parvato mahādivyo divyauṣadhisamanvitaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Its circumference is double its breadth. It is a great divine mountain, abounding in celestial medicines.

## \|\| 113.42 \|\|

*bhuvanairāvṛtaḥ sarvair jātarūpapariṣkṛtaiḥ \|*  
*tatra devagaṇāścaiva gandharvāsurarākṣasāḥ \|*  
*śailarāje pramodante sarvato 'psarasāṃ gaṇaiḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. It is surrounded on all sides by lands of golden effulgence. On this king of mountains, the Devas, the Gandharvas and the Rakshasas enjoy and carry on their pastimes in the company of Apsaras.

## \|\| 113.43-44 \|\|

*sa tu meruḥ parivṛto bhuvanairbhūtabhāvanaiḥ \|*  
*yasyeme caturo deśā nānāpārśveṣu saṃsthitāḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

*bhadrāśvaṃ bhārataṃ caiva ketumālaṃ ca paścime \|*  
*uttarāścaiva kuravaḥ kṛtapuṇyapratiśrayāḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

43-44. That Sumeru is adorned by the Bhuta and Bhavana worlds, and has four realms on its sides, viz. — Bhadrashva (in the east), Bharata (in the south) and Ketumala in the west and the sacred Kuru on the north.

## \|\| 113.45 \|\|

*viṣkambhaparvatāstadvan mandaro gandhamādanaḥ \|*  
*vipulaśca supārśvaśca sarvaratnavibhūṣitāḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. The subjacent hills are: — Mandara, Gandhamadana, Vipula, and Suparshva, all full of precious stones.

## \|\| 113.46 \|\|

*aruṇodaṃ mānasaṃ ca sitodaṃ bhadrasaṃjñitam \|*  
*teṣāmupari catvāri sarāṃsi ca vanāni ca \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. And on these mountains there are four lakes and forests known as Arunoda, Manasa, Sitoda and Bhadra

## \|\| 113.47 \|\|

*tathā bhadrakadambastu parvate gandhamādane \|*  
*jambūvṛkṣastathāśvattho vipule 'tha vaṭaḥ param \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. And there are big trees of turmeric, rose — apple, Ashvattha on the Gaudhamadana and banyan on the Vipula.

## \|\| 113.48 \|\|

*gandhamādanapārśve tu paścime 'maragaṇḍikaḥ \|*  
*dvātriṃśacca sahasrāṇi yojanaiḥ sarvataḥ samaḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Amaragandaka is west of Gandhamadana which is 32,000 yojanas, equally on all sides.

## \|\| 113.49 \|\|

*tatra te śubhakarmāṇaḥ ketumālāḥ pariśrutāḥ \|*  
*tatra kālānalāḥ sarve mahāsattvā mahābalāḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. There reside the well-known Ketumalas, the doers of blessed deeds: — there everybody is like the destructive Fire of high spirit and great strength.

## \|\| 113.50 \|\|

*striyaś cotpalavarṇābhāḥ sundaryaḥ priyadarśanāḥ \|*  
*tatra divyo mahāvṛkṣaḥ panasaḥ pattrabhāsuraḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. The ladies of that place are beautiful like the lotus and lovely. On that mountain there is a divine jackfruit tree, looking effulgent through its leaves.

## \|\| 113.51 \|\|

*tasya pītvā phalarasaṃ saṃjīvanti samāutam \|*  
*tasya mālyavataḥ pārśve pūrve pūrvā tu gaṇḍikā \|*  
*dvātriṃśacca sahasrāṇi tatrāpi śatamucyate \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. The people of that region live up to 10,000 years by drinking the juice of those fruits. To the east of Malyavan flows the river Gandaki which is 32,000 yojanas in length.

## \|\| 113.52 \|\|

*bhadrāśvastatra vijñeyo nityaṃ muditamānasaḥ \|*  
*bhadramālavanaṃ tatra kālāmraśca mahādrumaḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. The inhabitants of Bhadrashva (khanda) always remain happy and the Bhadramala forest lies in the same clime, where there is a huge and black mango tree.

## \|\| 113.53 \|\|

*tatra te puruṣāḥ śvetā mahāsattvā mahābalāḥ \|*  
*striyaḥ kumudavarṇābhāḥ sundaryaḥ priyadarśanāḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. The people of that place are white in complexion and very sturdy and strong. The womenfolk are the most beautiful, like white lily, and very agreeable to look at.

## \|\| 113.54 \|\|

*candraprabhāś candravarṇāḥ pūrṇacandranibhānanāḥ \|*  
*candraśītalagātrāśca striyo hyutpalagandhikāḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. They possess the radiance and colour of the moon, their faces are like the full moon, and their body cool, as the moon, smells like lotus.

## \|\| 113.55 \|\|

*daśavarṣasahasrāṇi āusteṣāmanāmayam \|*  
*kālāmrasya rasaṃ pītvā te sarve sthirayauvanāḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. They live up to 10,000 years in good health. By drinking the kalamango juice, they always remain in full bloom of youth.

## \|\| 113.56 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*ityuktavānṛṣīnbrahmā varṣāṇi ca nisargataḥ \|*  
*pūrvaṃ mamānugrahakṛd bhūyaḥ kiṃ varṇayāmi vaḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. Suta said: — Rishis! Brahma has thus described the nature of the continents to the Rishis, and the same Brahma who had previously favoured me (with describing the same). Now, what am I to narrate to you next?

## \|\| 113.57 \|\|

*etacchrutvā vacaste tu ṛṣayaḥ saṃśitavratāḥ \|*  
*jātakautūhalāḥ sarve pratyūcuste mudānvitāḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. All the self-restrained seers, hearing these words of Suta, became curious, and said with great joy:

## \|\| 113.58-59 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ*  
*pūrvāparau samākhyātau yau deśau tau tvayā mune \|*  
*uttarāṇāṃ ca varṣāṇāṃ parvatānāṃ ca sarvaśaḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

*ākhyāhi no yathātathyaṃ ye ca parvatavāsinaḥ \|*  
*evamuktastu ṛṣibhis tebhyastvākhyātavānpunaḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

58-59. “Sage! Be pleased to say all about the two countries, eastern and western, which have been already mentioned by you and of the northern varshas and mountains, besides which, we are also desirous of hearing the account of the men living on those mountains.” On being thus urged by the seers, Sita again resumed the string of his narration.

## \|\| 113.60 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*śṛṇudhvaṃ yāni varṣāṇi pūrvoktāni ca vai mayā \|*  
*dakṣiṇena tu nīlasya niṣadhasyottareṇa tu \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Sita said: — Listen to (the account of) the varshas which have been already referred to by me to the south of the Nila and to the north of Nishadha.

## \|\| 113.61 \|\|

*varṣaṃ ramaṇakaṃ nāma jāyante yatra vai prajāḥ \|*  
*ratipradhānā vimalā jāyante yatra mānavāḥ \|*  
*śuklābhijanasampannāḥ sarve te priyadarśanāḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. That is Ramanaka (varsha), and the inhabitants of that place are very handsome and given to amicable delights, and of pure birth.

## \|\| 113.62 \|\|

*tatrāpi ca mahāvṛkṣo nyagrodho rohiṇo mahān \|*  
*tasyāpi te phalarasaṃ pibanto vartayanti hi \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. There, too, is a huge banyan tree, and the people of that place, live by drinking the juice of the fruits of it

## \|\| 113.63 \|\|

*daśavarṣasahasrāṇi daśavarṣaśatāni ca \|*  
*jīvanti te mahābhāgāḥ sadā hṛṣṭā narottamāḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. These best of men of great parts live happy.

## \|\| 113.64 \|\|

*uttareṇa tu śvetasya pārśve śṛṅgasya dakṣiṇe \|*  
*varṣaṃ hiraṇvataṃ nāma yatra hairaṇvatī nadī \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. To the north of Shveta Mountain and to the south of Shringa (Shringin) is the Hiranyavat continent (varsha) where flows the river Hiranvati

## \|\| 113.65 \|\|

*mahābalā mahāsattvā nityaṃ muditamānasāḥ \|*  
*śuklābhijanasampannāḥ sarve ca priyadarśanāḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. The people of Hiranyavat are very strong and of high spirit. They are of pure and noble birth and are a good-looking and happy lot.

## \|\| 113.66 \|\|

*ekādaśa sahasrāṇi varṣāṇāṃ te narottamāḥ \|*  
*āuṣpramāṇaṃ jīvanti śatāni daśa pañca ca \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. These first class men live up to the age of 11 thousand and 1,500 years.

## \|\| 113.67 \|\|

*tasminvarṣe mahāvṛkṣo lakucaḥ pattrasaṃśrayaḥ \|*  
*tasya pītvā phalarasaṃ tatra jīvanti mānavāḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. In that continent, there is a great bread-fruit tree of nice foliage, by drinking the juice of the fruits of which men live on.

## \|\| 113.68 \|\|

*śṛṅgasāhvasya śṛṅgāṇi trīṇi tāni mahānti vai \|*  
*ekaṃ maṇiutaṃ tatra ekaṃ tu kanakānvitam \|*  
*sarvaratnamayaṃ caikaṃ bhuvanairupaśobhitam \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. The Mount Shringa (Shringin) has three lofty peaks. One of them is full of precious stones, the other one is studded with gold and the third one, full of all gems, is adorned with the worlds.

## \|\| 113.69 \|\|

*uttare cāsya śṛṅgasya samudrānte ca dakṣiṇe \|*  
*kuravastatra tadvaryaṃ puṇyaṃ siddhaniṣevitam \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. The country situated to the north of this Shringa, to the south of the sea, is the renowned Kuru varsha where the saints (siddhas) have fixed their abode.

## \|\| 113.70 \|\|

*tatra vṛkṣā madhuphalā divyāmṛtamayāpagāḥ \|*  
*vastrāṇi te prasūyante phalaiścābharaṇāni ca \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. It also has trees producing sweet fruits, and the water of the rivers is like divine nectar. Those beautiful trees produce raiment’s and ornaments by their fruits.

## \|\| 113.71 \|\|

*sarvakāmapradātāraḥ kecidvṛkṣā manoramāḥ \|*  
*apare kṣīriṇo nāma vṛkṣāstatra manoramāḥ \|*  
*ye rakṣanti sadā kṣīraṃ ṣaḍrasaṃ cāmṛtopamam \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. Some of those beautiful trees are the givers of all the fruits of one’s desires, and the others are called Kshirina, always beautiful to look at, produce milk (juice) with the six tastes and sweet as panchamrita (the five best products of cow’s milk), productive of nectar-like milk.

## \|\| 113.72 \|\|

*sarvā maṇimayī bhūmiḥ sūkṣmā kāñcanavālukā \|*  
*sarvatra sukhasaṃsparśā niḥśabdāḥ pavanāḥ śubhāḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. The whole land of that place is full of gems and is inlaid with fine gold dust. There, the wind is most pleasant and salubrious and noiseless.

## \|\| 113.73 \|\|

*devalokacyutāstatra jāyante mānavāḥ śubhāḥ \|*  
*śuklābhijanasampannāḥ sarve te sthirayauvanāḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. The people falling down from Devaloka are born there. They are of pure and noble descent, having permanent youth.

## \|\| 113.74 \|\|

*mithunāni prajāyante striyaścāpsarasopamāḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ te kṣīriṇāṃ kṣīraṃ pibanti hyamṛtopamam \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. There, the daughter and the son are born as twins, and husband and wife like the manifestations of Gandharva and Apsara. There, they drink nectar-like milk of trees overflowing with them.

## \|\| 113.75 \|\|

*ekāhādjāyate ugmaṃ samaṃ caiva vivardhate \|*  
*samaṃ rūpaṃ ca śīlaṃ ca samaṃ caiva mriyanti vai \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. The twins are born in a day. They grow together and are possessed of like beauty and character. They die together.

## \|\| 113.76 \|\|

*ekaikamanuraktāśca cakravākamiva dhruvam \|*  
*anāmayā hyaśokāśca nityaṃ muditamānasāḥ \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. They are attached to each other with the fondness of the ruddy geese. They are healthy, without bereavement, and happy.

## \|\| 113.77 \|\|

*daśa varṣasahasrāṇi daśa varṣaśatāni ca \|*  
*jīvanti ca mahāsattvā na cānyā strī pravartate \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. These great souls live for 11,000 years, and are ever devoted to their own wives.

## \|\| 113.78 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*evameva nisargo vai varṣāṇāṃ bhārate uge \|*  
*dṛṣṭaḥ paramadharmajñāḥ kiṃ bhūyaḥ kathayāmi vaḥ \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. Suta said: — O Rishis! The nature of these continents of the Bharatavarsha has been brought to your notice O greatly pious ones! what more do you wish to hear now?

## \|\| 113.79 \|\|

*ākhyātāstvevamṛṣayaḥ sūtaputreṇa dhīmatā \|*  
*uttaraśravaṇe bhūyaḥ papracchuḥ sūtanandanam \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. The Rishis, being thus asked by the enlightened son of Suta again questioned him, being desirous of hearing something more in answer.

## Chapter 114

## \|\| 114.1-2 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ*  
*yadidaṃ bhārataṃ varṣaṃ yasmin svāyambhuvādayaḥ \|*  
*caturdaśaiva manavaḥ prajāsargaṃ sasarjire \|\| 1 \|\|*

*etad veditum icchāmaḥ sakāśāttava suvrata \|*  
*uttaraśravaṇaṃ bhūyaḥ prabrūhi vadatāṃ vara \|\| 2 \|\|*

1-2. The sages said: — We wish to hear from you an account of this Bharatavarsha, which was peopled by Svayambhuva and the rest of the fourteen Manus. O Blessed one! do tell us about their creation.

## \|\| 114.3-4 \|\|

*etacchrutvā ṛṣīṇāṃ tu prābravīllaumaharṣaṇiḥ \|*  
*paurāṇikastadā sūta ṛṣīṇāṃ bhāvitātmanām \|\| 3 \|\|*

*buddhyā vicārya bahudhā vimṛṣya ca punaḥ punaḥ \|*  
*tebhyastu kathayāmāsa uttaraśravaṇaṃ tadā \|\| 4 \|\|*

3-4. On hearing these words of the seers, Suta of the Puranas and son of Lomaharshana after a deep consideration, began to answer the queries of the seers of thoughtful mind.

## \|\| 114.5 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*athāhaṃ varṇayiṣyāmi varṣe 'sminbhārate prajāḥ \|*  
*bharaṇātprajanāccaiva manurbharata ucyate \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Suta said: — I shall tell you about the people of Bharatavarsha. Manu came to be known as Bharata by his creation end protection of the people (of Bharata).

## \|\| 114.6 \|\|

*niruktavacanaiścaiva varṣaṃ tadbhārataṃ smṛtam \|*  
*yataḥ svargaśca mokṣaśca madhyamaścāpi hi smṛtaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. According to Nirukta, that place is Bharatavarsha where human beings can obtain heaven, emancipation and a middle course of the two.

## \|\| 114.7-10 \|\|

*na khalvanyatra martyānāṃ bhūmau karmavidhiḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*bhāratasyāsya varṣasya nava bhedānnibodhata \|\| 7 \|\|*

*indradvīpaḥ kaśeruśca tāmraparṇo gabhastimān \|*  
*nāgadvīpastathā saumyo gandharvastvatha vāruṇaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*ayaṃ tu navamasteṣāṃ dvīpaḥ sāgarasaṃvṛtaḥ \|*  
*yojanānāṃ sahasraṃ tu dvīpo 'yaṃ dakṣiṇottaraḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*āyatastu kumārīto gaṅgāyāḥ pravahāvadhiḥ \|*  
*tiryagūrdhvaṃ tu vistīrṇaḥ sahasrāṇi daśaiva tu \|\| 10 \|\|*

7-10. There is no field of action for mankind without Bhadratavarsha. Bharatavarsha has nine divisions; Viz. — Indradvipa, Kashera, Tamraparni, Gabhastimana, Nagadvipa, Saumya, Gandharva, Varuna; and the ninth is this place, surrounded on all sides by the ocean. The whole of the dvipa is a thousand yojanas in extent, from north to south. It is gradually broader from Kumari (Cape Comorin) to the mouth of the Ganges, whence it has risen to a height of ten thousand yojanas in an oblique direction.

## \|\| 114.11 \|\|

*dvīpo hyupaniviṣṭo 'yaṃ mlecchairanteṣu sarvaśaḥ \|*  
*yavanāśca kirātāśca tasyānte pūrvapaścime \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. The Mlechhas live on its outskirts. The Kiratas and the Yavanas inhabit the cast and the west of it.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — Kirata = A degraded mountain tribe.

Yavana — Foreigner, especially the Greeks.

## \|\| 114.12 \|\|

*brāhmaṇāḥ kṣatriyā vaiśyā madhye śūdrāśca bhāgaśaḥ \|*  
*ijyāutavaṇijyādi vartayanto vyavasthitāḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. The Brahmanas, the Kshatriyas, the Vaishyas, and the Shudras inhabit in its centre and carry on (1.e., inside this boundary) their occupations of rituals (sacrifice, &c.) trade, commerce, &c.

## \|\| 114.13 \|\|

*teṣāṃ sa vyavahāro 'yaṃ vartanaṃ tu parasparam \|*  
*dharmārthakāmasaṃyukto varṇānāṃ tu svakarmasu \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. They all pursue their respective duties by adhering to the varnadharma, Artha and Kama.

## \|\| 114.14 \|\|

*saṃkalpapañcamānāṃ tu āśramāṇāṃ yathāvidhi \|*  
*iha svargāpavargārthaṃ pravṛttiriha mānuṣe \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Here exist the ashramas in their due order in which the fivefold desires of men are fulfilled (viz. nishkama dharma as well as the four ordinary desires, consisting of dharma, artha, kama and moksha). Here, men engage in activities for the sake of obtaining Heaven and emancipation.

## \|\| 114.15 \|\|

*yastvayaṃ mānavo dvīpas tiryagyāmaḥ prakīrtitaḥ \|*  
*ya enaṃ jayate kṛtsnaṃ sa samrāḍiti kīrtitaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. The Manavadvipa is also called Tiryag-yama (i.e., obliquely situate). One who conquers it entirely, is called Samrata.

## \|\| 114.16 \|\|

*ayaṃ lokastu vai samrāḍ antarikṣajitāṃ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*svarāḍasau smṛto lokaḥ punarvakṣyāmi vistarāt \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. This loka is known as the conqueror of Antariksha which in its turn is known as Svarat. I shall explain this at full length.

## \|\| 114.17-18 \|\|

*sapta cāsminmahāvarṣe viśrutāḥ kulaparvatāḥ \|*  
*mahendro malayaḥ sahyaḥ śuktimānṛkṣavānapi \|\| 17 \|\|*

*vindhyaśca pāriyātraśca ityete kulaparvatāḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ sahasraśaścānye parvatāstu samīpataḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

17-18. There are seven principal mountains in this continent, viz., Mahendra, Malaya, Sahya, Shaktiman, Rikshavan, Vindhya and Pariyatra; and there are thousands of smaller ones adjacent to each of these.

## \|\| 114.19 \|\|

*abhijñātāstataścānye vipulāścitrasānavaḥ \|*  
*anye tebhyaḥ parijñātā hrasvā hrasvopajīvinaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Some of these are known to have fine peaks and tablelands, covered with many kinds of trees, &c. The smaller ones are less productive, and are distinguished from the bigger ones by contrast.

## \|\| 114.20-32 \|\|

*tairvimiśrā jānapadā āryā mlecchāśca sarvataḥ \|*  
*pibanti bahulā nadyo gaṅgā sindhuḥ sarasvatī \|\| 20 \|\|*

*śatadruścandrabhāgā ca yamunā sarayūstathā \|*  
*airāvatī vitastā ca viśālā devikā kuhūḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*gomatī dhautapāpā ca bāhudā ca dṛṣadvatī \|*  
*kauśikī tu tṛtīyā ca niścalā gaṇḍakī tathā \|\| 22 \|\|*

*ikṣurlauhitam ityetā himavatpārśvaniḥsṛtāḥ \|*  
*vedasmṛtir vetravatī vṛtraghnī sindhureva ca \|*  
*parṇāśā narmadā caiva kāverī mahatī tathā \|\| 23 \|\|*

*pārā ca dhanvatīrūpā viduṣā veṇumatyapi \|*  
*śiprā hyavantī kuntī ca pāriyātrāśritāḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*śoṇo mahānadaścaiva nandanā sukṛśā kṣamā \|*  
*mandākinī daśārṇā ca citrakūṭā tathaiva ca \|*  
*tamasā pippalī śyenī tathā citrotpalāpi ca \|\| 25 \|\|*

*vimalā cañcalā caiva tathā ca dhūtavāhinī \|*  
*śuktimantī śunī ladjā mukuṭā hrādikāpi ca \|*  
*ṛṣyavantaprasūtās tā nadyo 'malajalāḥ śubhāḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*tāpī payoṣṇī nirvindhyā kṣiprā ca ṛṣabhā nadī \|*  
*veṇā vaitaraṇī caiva viśvamālā kumudvatī \|\| 27 \|\|*

*toyā caiva mahāgaurī durgamā tu śilā tathā \|*  
*vindhyapādaprasūtās tāḥ sarvāḥ śītajalāḥ śubhāḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

*godāvarī bhīmarathī kṛṣṇaveṇī ca vañjulā \|*  
*tuṅgabhadrā suprayogā vāhyā kāverī caiva tu \|*  
*dakṣiṇāpathanadyastāḥ sahyapādādviniḥsṛtāḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*kṛtamālā tāmraparṇī puṣpajā hyutpalāvatī \|*  
*malayaprasūtā nadyas tāḥ sarvāḥ śītajalāḥ śubhāḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

*tribhāgā ṛṣikulyā ca ikṣudā tridivācalā \|*  
*tāmraparṇī tathā mūlī śaravā vimalā tathā \|*  
*mahendratanayāḥ sarvāḥ prakhyātāḥ śubhagāminīḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

*kāśikā sukumārī ca mandagā mandavāhinī \|*  
*kṛpā ca pāśinī caiva śuktimantātmajās tu tāḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

20-32. The Mlechhas and the Aryan reside there mingling with each other without distinction, and they drink the waters of many rivers, such as the Ganges, the Sindhu, the Sarasvati, the Sutlej, the Chandrabhaga, the Yamuna, the Sarayu, the Airdvati, the Vitatsa, the Devika, the Kuhu, the Gomati, the Dhautapapa, the Vahuda, the Drishadvati, the Kaushiki, the Trittya, the Nishchala, the Gandaki, the Ikshu, the Lauhita (all these having their source in the snow-clad mountains of the Himalayas).

The Vedasmriti, the Vetravati, the Vritraghni, the Sindhu, the Parnasha, the Narmada, the Kaveri, the Mahi, the Para, the Dhanvati, the Rupa, the Vidusha, the Venumati, the Sipra, the Avanti, the Kunti (all these rivers having their source in the Pariyatra mountain).

The Mandakini, the Dasharna, the Chitrakuta, the Tamasa, the Pippali, the Shyeni, the Chitrotpala, the Vimala, the Chanchala, the Dhutavahini, the Shaktimanti, the Shuni, the Lajja, the Mukuta, the Hradika (these having their source in the Rishyavan mountain).

The Tapi, the Payoshni, the Nirvindhya, the Kshipra, the Rishabha, the Vena, the Vaitarani, the Vishvamala, the Kumudvati, the Toya, the Mahagauri, the Durgama, the Shila (these rivers of cool water having their source in the Vindhya mountains).

The Godavari, the Bhimarathi, the Krishnaveni, the Banjula, the Tungabhadra, the Suprayoga, the Vahya, the Kaveri (these rivers in the south having their source in the Sahya mountains).

The Kritamala, the Tamraparni, the Pushpaja, the Utpalavati (these rivers of the cool water having their source in the Malayachala mountain).

The Tribhaga, the Rishikulya, the Ikshuda, the Tridiva, the Chalatamraparni, the Mali, the Sarva, the Vimala (these having come from the Mahendra mountain), the Kasika, the Sukumari, the Madanga, the Mandavahini, the Kripa, the Pashini (these having come from Shaktimanta).

## \|\| 114.33 \|\|

*sarvāḥ puṇyajalāḥ puṇyāḥ sarvagāśca samudragāḥ \|*  
*viśvasya mātaraḥ sarvāḥ sarvapāpaharāḥ śubhāḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. All the rivers named above are sacred, and fall into the sea, and their waters are pure and sacred; and every one drinks from them.

They are the mothers of the universe and purge the sin of the world.

## \|\| 114.34-36 \|\|

*tāsāṃ nadyupanadyaśca śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ \|*  
*tāsvime kurupāñcālāḥ śālvāścaiva sajāṅgalāḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

*śūrasenā bhadrakārā bāhyāḥ sahapaṭaccarāḥ \|*  
*matsyāḥ kirātāḥ kulyāśca kuntalāḥ kāśikośalāḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

*āvantāśca kaliṅgāśca mūkāścaivāndhakaiḥ saha \|*  
*madhyadeśā janapadāḥ prāyaśaḥ parikīrtitāḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

34-36. From these rivers thousands of rivers are branched off, and into them thousands of tributaries fall.

On their banks are situated the following (janapadas) places:

Panchala, Kuru, Shalva, Jangala, Shurasena, Bhadrakasha, Vahya, Pattachara, Matsya, Kirata, Kulya, Kuntala, Kashi, Koshala, Avanti, Kalinga, Muka and Andhaka. Thus I have described almost all the countries of Madhyadesha.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — Madhyadesa the central region, the country lying between the Himalaya and the Vindhya. The Gangetic doab, Shurasena = Name of country about Mathura, Matsya = Another name for Virata — the country lying to the west of Dholpur. Kuntala =

S. W. portion of Hyderabad, Deccan. Avanta Country to the N, of Narmada. Kalinga =

Northern Sircars, Andhaka = Telangana.

## \|\| 114.37-38 \|\|

*sahyasyānantare caite tatra godāvarī nadī \|*  
*pṛthivyāmapi kṛtsnāyāṃ sa pradeśo manoramaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

*yatra govardhano nāma mandaro gandhamādanaḥ \|*  
*rāmapriyārthaṃ svargīyā vṛkṣā divyāstathauṣadhīḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

37-38. Now the following are between the Sahya mountain and the Godavari, most charming lands in the whole world, where there are (the mountains) Govardhana, Mandara and Gandhamadana as well as the celestial trees and herbs, for Rama’s benefit.

## \|\| 114.39 \|\|

*bharadvājena muninā priyārthamavatāritāḥ \|*  
*tataḥ puṣpavaro deśas tena jajñe manoramaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. These were brought down by Bharadvaja Muni, for Rama’s good, and by him was created a pleasant country decorated with flowers.

## \|\| 114.40-43 \|\|

*vāhlīkā vāṭadhānāśca ābhīrāḥ kālatoyakāḥ \|*  
*puraṃdhrāścaiva śūdrāśca pallavāś cāttakhaṇḍikāḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

*gāndhārā yavanāścaiva sindhusauvīramadrakāḥ \|*  
*śakā druhyāḥ pulindāśca pāradāhāramūrtikāḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

*rāmaṭhāḥ kaṇṭakārāśca kaikeyā daśanāmakāḥ \|*  
*kṣatriyopaniveśyāśca vaiśyāḥ śūdrakulāni ca \|\| 42 \|\|*

*atrayo 'tha bharadvājāḥ prasthalāḥ sadaserakāḥ \|*  
*lampakās talagānāśca sainikāḥ saha jāṅgalaiḥ \|*  
*ete deśā udīcyāstu prācyāndeśānnibodhata \|\| 43 \|\|*

40-43. Bahlika, Vatadhana, Abhira, Kalatoyaka, Purandhra Shudra, Pallava, Atta Khandika, Gandhara, Yavanas, Sindhu, Sauvira, Madraka, Shaka, Druhya, Pulinda, Parada, Harmurtika, Ramatha, Kantakara, Kaikeya, Dashanamaka, Prasthala, Daseraka, Lampaka, Talagana, Sainika, Jangala, and other places peopled by the Bharadvaja Brahmanas, Kshatriyas, Vaishyas, and Shudras: — These places (janapadas) are on the north. Now hear of those on the east.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — Bahlika = Balkha. Sindhu = The country of the Upper Indus. Shaka — The countries on the N.-W. Frontier. Kaikeya = Bordering on the Sindhu Desha,........

Abhira: — South of Sri Konkana and on the Western bank of the Tapti is the land of the Abhiras on the Vindhya hills.

## \|\| 114.44-45 \|\|

*aṅgā vaṅgā madgurakā antargiribahirgirī \|*  
*tataḥ plavaṃgamātaṃgā yamakā mallavarṇakāḥ \|*  
*suhmottarāḥ pravijayā mārgavā geyamālavāḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

*prāgjyotiṣāśca puṇḍrāśca videhāstāmraliptakāḥ \|*  
*śālvamāgadhagonardāḥ prācyā janapadāḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

44-45. Anga, Vanga, Madguraka, Antaragiri, Vahirgiri, Plavanga, Matanga, Yamaka, Mallavarnaka, Suhma, Uttara Pravijaya, Marga, Vageya, Malava, Pragjyotisha, Puddra, Videha, Tamraliptaka, Shalva, Magadha and Gonardla.

**Комментарий:**

Note — Anga = Near Bhagalpur. Vanga = Also called Samatala; Eastern Bengal.

Vidiha = Country lying to the N. = E. of Magadha. Magadha = Bihar.

## \|\| 114.46-51 \|\|

*teṣāṃ pare janapadā dakṣiṇāpathavāsinaḥ \|*  
*pāṇḍyāśca keralāścaiva colāḥ kulyāstathaiva ca \|\| 46 \|\|*

*setukāḥ sūtikāścaiva kupathāṃ vājivāsikāḥ \|*  
*navarāṣṭrā māhiṣikāḥ kaliṅgāścaiva sarvaśaḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

*kārūṣāśca sahaiṣīkā āṭavyāḥ śabarāstathā \|*  
*pulindā vindhyapuṣikā vaidarbhā daṇḍakaiḥ saha \|\| 48 \|\|*

*kulīyāśca sirālāśca rūpasās tāpasaiḥ saha \|*  
*tathā taittirikāścaiva sarve kāraskarāstathā \|\| 49 \|\|*

*vāsikyāścaiva ye cānye ye caivāntaranarmadāḥ \|*  
*bhārukacchāḥ samāheyāḥ saha sārasvataistathā \|\| 50 \|\|*

*kācchīkāścaiva saurāṣṭrā ānartā arbudaiḥ saha \|*  
*ityete aparāntāstu śṛṇu ye vindhyavāsinaḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

46-51. Those lying to the south (or in the Dakshinapatha) are: — Pandya, Kerala, Chola, Kulya, Setuka, Sutika, Kupatha, Vajivasika, Navarashtra, Mahishika, Kalinga, Karusha, Aishika, Atavya, Shavara, Pulinda, Vindhya, Pushika, Vidarbha, Dandaka, Kuliya, Sirala, Rupasa, Tapasa Taitirika, Karaskara, Vasika and the countries on the banks of the Narmada.

The following countries lie on the west: — Bhdarukachha, Samaheya, Sarasvata, Kachika, Saurdstra, Anarta and Arbuda.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — Kerala = Modern Malabar. The strip of land between Western Ghauts and the sea north of the Kaveri. Chola = Tanjore. Pandya = Tinnevelly. Vidarbha = Berar.

A district in the Deccan between the Narmada and the Godavari.

Note. — Shaurashtra or Anarta = Kathiawar. Arbuda = Abu.

## \|\| 114.52-55 \|\|

*mālavāśca karūṣāśca mekalāścotkalaiḥ saha \|*  
*auṇḍrā māṣā daśārṇāśca bhojāḥ kiṣkindhakaiḥ saha \|\| 52 \|\|*

*stośalāḥ kosalāścaiva traipurā vaidiśāstathā \|*  
*tumurās tumbarāścaiva padgamā naiṣadhaiḥ saha \|\| 53 \|\|*

*arūpāḥ śauṇḍikerāśca vītihotrā avantayaḥ \|*  
*ete janapadāḥ khyātā vindhyapṛṣṭhanivāsinaḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

*ato deśānpravakṣyāmi parvatāśrayiṇaśca ye \|*  
*nirāhārāḥ sarvagāśca kupathā apathāstathā \|\| 55 \|\|*

52-55. The following countries are on the western extremity of the Vindhyachala: — Malava, Karusha, Mekala, Utkala, Aundra, Masa, Dasharna, Bhoja, Kishkindhaka, Toshala, Koshala, Traipura, Vaidisha, Tumura, Tumvara Padgama, Naishadha, Arupa, Shaundikera, Vitihotra, Avanti.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — Malava = Malwa. Utkala = Orissa. Kishkindha = A city in the Deccan. Dasharna =

The country through which the Dagan flows. Koshala = The country along the banks of the Sarayu. Tripura = Tevur. Avanti = Country to the north of the Narmada.

## \|\| 114.56 \|\|

*kuthaprāvaraṇāścaiva ūrṇādavāḥ samudgakāḥ \|*  
*trigartā maṇḍalāścaiva kirātāścāmaraiḥ saha \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. The following countries are situated on the mountains: — Nirahara, Sarvaga, Kupatha, Apatha, Kuthupravarana, Urna, Darva, Samudgaka, Trigarta, Mandala, Kirata and Amara.

## \|\| 114.57 \|\|

*catvāri bhārate varṣe ugāni munayo 'bruvan \|*  
*kṛtaṃ tretā dvāparaṃ ca kaliśceti caturyugam \|*  
*teṣāṃ nisargaṃ vakṣyāmi upariṣṭācca kṛtsnaśaḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. There are four ages of the world, viz. — Satya, Treta, Dwapara and Kaliyuga. I am now going to give you an account of each.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — The duration of each age respectively is 1,728,000; 1,296,000, 864,000 and 422.000 years of men, the four together comprising 4,320,099 years which is equal to a Mahayuga, The regularly descending length of the Yagas represents a corresponding physical and moral deterioration in the people living in each age, the present age being Kaliyuga — the Iron Age.

## \|\| 114.58 \|\|

*matsya uvāca*  
*etacchrutvā tu ṛṣaya uttaraṃ punareva te \|*  
*śuśrūṣavastamūcuste prakāmaṃ laumaharṣaṇim \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. The Lord said: — King! Hearing this, the sages, desirous of hearing the narration, began to enquire from Sita, the son of L6maharsana.

## \|\| 114.59-60 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ*  
*yacca kimpuruṣaṃ varṣaṃ harivarṣaṃ tathaiva ca \|*  
*ācakṣva no yathātattvaṃ kīrtitaṃ bhārataṃ tvayā \|\| 59 \|\|*

*jambūkhaṇḍasya vistāraṃ tathānyeṣāṃ vidāṃvara \|*  
*dvīpānāṃ vāsināṃ teṣāṃ vṛkṣāṇāṃ prabravīhi naḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

59-60. The seers said: — Suta! You have told us about Bharatavarsha, now be pleased to tell us something about Kimpurusha Varsha and Hari Varsha; besides this, be good enough to tell us about the Jambudvipa, &c., as well as about their people and the trees that grow there.

## \|\| 114.61 \|\|

*pṛṣṭastvevaṃ tadā viprair yathāpraśnaṃ viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*uvāca ṛṣibhirdṛṣṭaṃ purāṇābhimataṃ tathā \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Thus exhorted by the Brahmanas, Sita began to relate to them what was in accordance with the Puranas and approved by the Rishis.

## \|\| 114.62 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*śuśrūṣavastu yadviprāḥ śuśrūṣadhvamatandritāḥ \|*  
*jambūvarṣaḥ kimpuruṣaḥ sumahānandanopamaḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. Suta said: — Rishis! As you desire to hear these things, listen to me attentively. The Kimpurusha of Jambudvipa is as great in magnitude as the Nandana- Vana.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — Nandana-Vana = The garden of Indra.

## \|\| 114.63 \|\|

*daśa varṣasahasrāṇi sthitiḥ kimpuruṣe smṛtā \|*  
*jāyante mānavāstatra sutaptakanakaprabhāḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. Kimpurusha: — The people of Kimpurusha-Khanda have a complexion like that of heated gold, and they live up to 10,000 years.

## \|\| 114.64 \|\|

*varṣe kimpuruṣe puṇye plakṣo madhuvahaḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*tasya kimpuruṣāḥ sarve pibanto rasamuttamam \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. A stream of honey flows from a Plaksha tree, in that sacred Khanda, which the Kinnaras residing there drink.

## \|\| 114.65 \|\|

*anāmayā hyaśokāśca nityaṃ muditamānasāḥ \|*  
*suvarṇavarṇāśca narāḥ striyaścāpsarasaḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. On account of which they remain so healthy, without any grief and happy, and cheerful in their minds. The people have a yellow complexion like shining gold, and the womenfolk are known as Apsaras,

## \|\| 114.66-67 \|\|

*tataḥ paraṃ kimpuruṣād dharivarṣaṃ pracakṣate \|*  
*mahārajatasaṃkāśā jāyante yatra mānavāḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

*devalokacyutāḥ sarve bahurūpāśca sarvaśaḥ \|*  
*harivarṣe narāḥ sarve pibantīkṣurasaṃ śubham \|\| 67 \|\|*

66-67. Hari Varsha: — Beyond Kimpurusha is Harivarsha, the inhabitants of which are silvery white in complexion. They are the fallen people of Devaloka. They all drink the juice of the sugarcane.

## \|\| 114.68 \|\|

*na jarā bādhate tatra tena jīvanti te ciram \|*  
*ekādaśa sahasrāṇi teṣāmāuḥ prakīrtitam \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. They do not get old, and consequently they live for a very long time.

Their average age is 11,000 years.

## \|\| 114.69 \|\|

*madhyamaṃ tanmayā proktaṃ nāmnā varṣamilāvṛtam \|*  
*na tatra sūryastapati na ca jānanti mānavāḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. Ilavrita-Khanda is in the middle, where there is no strong sunshine and of which men have little knowledge

## \|\| 114.70-73 \|\|

*candrasūryau sanakṣatrāv aprakāśāvilāvṛte \|*  
*padmaprabhāḥ padmavarṇāḥ padmapattranibhekṣaṇāḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

*padmagandhāśca jāyante tatra sarve ca mānavāḥ \|*  
*jambūphalarasāhārā aniṣpandāḥ sugandhinaḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

*devalokacyutāḥ sarve mahārajatavāsasaḥ \|*  
*trayodaśa sahasrāṇi varṣāṇāṃ te narottamāḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

*āuṣpramāṇaṃ jīvanti ye tu varṣa ilāvṛte \|*  
*merostu dakṣiṇe pārśve niṣadhasyottareṇa vā \|\| 73 \|\|*

70-73. The sun, the moon, as well as the stars are seldom seen in Ilavrita.

The people of that place are handsome like the lotus and their eyes are like the same, and their body, too, emits a scent like that of the lotus.

They seldom get excited and drink the juice of the rose-apple, (jambuphala).

They, too, are the fallen people of Svarga and wear silvery white garments, and live up to 13,000 years.

## \|\| 114.74 \|\|

*sudarśano nāma mahāñ jambūvṛkṣaḥ sanātanaḥ \|*  
*nityapuṣpaphalopetaḥ siddhacāraṇasevitaḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. To the south of Meru and north of Nishadha stands the rose-apple tree (jambuvriksha), which is called Sudarshana It is a huge tree, and always abounds in flowers and fruits, and is frequented by the Siddhas and Charanas.

## \|\| 114.75 \|\|

*tasya nāmnā samākhyāto jambūdvīpo vanaspateḥ \|*  
*yojanānāṃ sahasraṃ ca śatadhā ca mahānpunaḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. Jambudvipa is so called after this huge tree. It rises to a height of thousands of yojanas.

## \|\| 114.76 \|\|

*utsedho vṛkṣarājasya divam āvṛtya tiṣṭhati \|*  
*tasya jambūphalaraso nadī bhūtvā prasarpati \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. The tree is so high and big that it seems to cover all the heavens, and the juice of its fruits flows in the form of a river.

## \|\| 114.77 \|\|

*meruṃ pradakṣiṇaṃ kṛtvā jambūmūlagatā punaḥ \|*  
*taṃ pibanti sadā hṛṣṭā jambūrasamilāvṛte \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. It flows round Sumeru, and then waters the root of the tree, and people of Ilavrita drink it with great pleasure.

## \|\| 114.78 \|\|

*jambūphalarasaṃ pītvā na jarā bādhate 'pi tān \|*  
*na kṣudhā na klamo vāpi na duḥkhaṃ ca tathāvidham \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. By drinking it, they neither get infirm, nor do they ever feel hungry, tired or miserable.

## \|\| 114.79-80 \|\|

*tatra jāmbūnadaṃ nāma kanakaṃ devabhūṣaṇam \|*  
*indragopakasaṃkāśaṃ jāyate bhāsuraṃ ca yat \|\| 79 \|\|*

*sarveṣāṃ varṣavṛkṣāṇāṃ śubhaḥ phalarasastu saḥ \|*  
*skannaṃ tu kāñcanaṃ śubhraṃ jāyate devabhūṣaṇam \|\| 80 \|\|*

79-80. There is to be found a kind of gold, called the Jambunada, which is the ornament of the Devas. It is red like the Indragopa (insect). The fruits of this tree produce the best juice of all the fruits of trees of other Vargas. This tree exudes a gummy sap, like gold, which is also the ornament of the Devas,

## \|\| 114.81 \|\|

*teṣāṃ mūtraṃ purīṣaṃ vā dikṣvaṣṭāsu ca sarvaśaḥ \|*  
*īśvarānugrahādbhūmir mṛtāṃśca grasate tu tān \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. By the grace of God, the soil of that place swallows the excreta of the people and the dead.

## \|\| 114.82 \|\|

*rakṣaḥpiśācā yakṣāśca sarve haimavatāstu te \|*  
*hemakūṭe tu vijñeyā gandharvāḥ sāpsarogaṇāḥ \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. The Rakshasas, and the Pishachas live (in the dales) of Himavata.

The Gandharvas and the Apsaras are the inhabitants of Hemakuta.

## \|\| 114.83-84 \|\|

*sarve nāgā niṣevante śeṣavāsukitakṣakāḥ \|*  
*mahāmerau trayastriṃśat krīḍante yajñiyāḥ śubhāḥ \|\| 83 \|\|*

*nīlavaiḍūryayukte 'smin siddhā brahmarṣayo 'vasan \|*  
*daityānāṃ dānavānāṃ ca śvetaḥ parvata ucyate \|\| 84 \|\|*

83-84. Shesha, Vasuki, Takshakas and the Nagas, all haunt the Nishadha mountain, and the 33 blessed Yajnyias (Devas) sport on Mahameru. On the Ntla mountain, where sapphires abound, live the Siddhas, Maharshis and Danavas. The Shveta range is said to be the resort of Daityas.

## \|\| 114.85-86 \|\|

*śṛṅgavān parvataśreṣṭhaḥ pitriṇāṃ pratisaṃcaraḥ \|*  
*ityetāni mayoktāni navavarṣāṇi bhārate \|\| 85 \|\|*

*bhūtairapi niviṣṭāni gatimanti dhruvāṇi ca \|*  
*teṣāṃ vṛddhirbahuvidhā dṛṣyate devamānuṣaiḥ \|*  
*aśakyā parisaṃkhyātuṃ śraddheyā ca bubhūṣatā \|\| 86 \|\|*

85-86. Shringavan, the best of the mountains, is the haunt of the Pitris.

These are the nine continents in the world. The changeable (plains) and the fixed (mountains) are inhabited by various creatures. Men and Devas pee numerous increase in them. They cannot be counted, but should be taken on trust, by one who wishes his own good.

## Chapter 115

## \|\| 115.1-5 \|\|

*manur uvāca*  
*caritaṃ budhaputrasya janārdana mayā śrutam \|*  
*śrutaḥ śrāddhavidhiḥ puṇyaḥ sarvapāpapraṇāśanaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*dhenvāḥ prasūyamānāyāḥ phalaṃ dānasya me śrutam \|*  
*kṛṣṇājinapradānaṃ ca vṛṣotsargastathaiva ca \|\| 2 \|\|*

*śrutvā rūpaṃ narendrasya budhaputrasya keśava \|*  
*kautūhalaṃ samutpannaṃ tanmamācakṣva pṛcchataḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*kena karmavipākena sa tu rājā purūravāḥ \|*  
*avāpa tādṛśaṃ rūpaṃ saubhāgyamapi cottamam \|\| 4 \|\|*

*devāṃstribhuvanaśreṣṭhān gandharvāṃśca manoramān \|*  
*urvaśī saṃmatā tyaktvā sarvabhāvena taṃ nṛpam \|\| 5 \|\|*

1-5. Manu said: — Janardana! I have heard the doings of the son of Budha and have also heard the ways of performing sacred Shraddha that dispels all sins. I have heard the benefits of giving away a milk cow, a black deer skin, and the ways of letting loose a bull (at the end of funeral rites); but O Keshava! my curiosity is awakened on hearing about the beauty of the son of Budha. Pray now tell me what I ask. By virtue of what acts did he become so handsome and prosperous? How is it that Urvashi became so much attached to him in preference to all the Devas of the three worlds as well as the beautiful Gandharvas?

## \|\| 115.6-7 \|\|

*matsya uvāca*  
*śṛṇu karmavipākena yena rājā purūravāḥ \|*  
*avāpa tādṛśaṃ rūpaṃ saubhāgyamapi cottamam \|\| 6 \|\|*

*atīte janmani purā yo 'yaṃ rājā purūravāḥ \|*  
*purūravā iti khyāto madradeśādhipo hi saḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

6-7. Hearing those words of Manu, the Lord said: — King! Hear the actions, in virtue of which the King Pururava became so handsome and happy. In his previous life, the King Pururava was the lord of Madra, known as Pururava.

## \|\| 115.8 \|\|

*cākṣuṣasyānvaye rājā cākṣuṣasyāntare manoḥ \|*  
*sa vai nṛpaguṇairyuktaḥ kevalaṃ rūpavarjitaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. At the close of the Chakshusha Manvantara, the king was in the Chakshusha dynasty, endowed with all the royal qualities, except beauty alone.

## \|\| 115.9 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ*  
*purūravā madrapatiḥ karmaṇā kena pārthivaḥ \|*  
*babhūva karmaṇā kena rūpavāṃścaiva sūtaja \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The Rishis asked Suta how the Madra King, Pururava, became Lord of the Earth, and what act of his deprived him of his beauty.

## \|\| 115.10-12 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*dvijagrāme dvijaśreṣṭho nāmnā cāsītpurūravāḥ \|*  
*nadyāḥ kūle mahārājaḥ pūrvajanmani pārthivaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*sa tu madrapatī rājā yastu nāmnā purūravāḥ \|*  
*tasmiñjanmanyasau vipro dvādaśyāṃ tu sadānagha \|\| 11 \|\|*

*upoṣya pūjayāmāsa rājyakāmo janārdanam \|*  
*cakāra sopavāsaśca snānam abhyaṅgapūrvakam \|\| 12 \|\|*

10-12. Suta said. — Seers! In the village of Dvija, on the bank of a river, there was a Brahmana named Pururava, who in his after life became the King of Madra, named Pururava; because in his former life of a Brahmana, he always observed the Dwadashi fast and worshipped Janardana, with the desire of getting a kingdom. But though he kept the fast, he bathed, with his body rubbed with oil.

## \|\| 115.13 \|\|

*upavāsaphalātprāptaṃ rājyaṃ madreṣvakaṇṭakam \|*  
*upoṣitas tathābhyaṅgād rūpahīno vyajāyata \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. He obtained the kingdom of Madra by the virtue of his fast, but became, ugly on account of his rubbing his body with oil, before bathing on fast days.

## \|\| 115.14 \|\|

*upoṣitairnarais tasmāt snānam abhyaṅgapūrvakam \|*  
*varjanīyaṃ prayatnena rūpaghnaṃ tatparaṃ nṛpa \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Hence, one, who observes a fast, should not rub his body with oil on that day before bathing, and if he bathes after rubbing his body with unguent, he becomes ugly in his next life.

## \|\| 115.15 \|\|

*etadvaḥ kathitaṃ sarvaṃ yadvṛttaṃ pūrvajanmani \|*  
*madreśvaratvacaritaṃ śṛṇu tasya mahīpateḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. This is about the previous life of the King Pururava of Madra.

Now I shall tell you something about him, after he became the lord of Madra.

## \|\| 115.16 \|\|

*tasya rājaguṇaiḥ sarvaiḥ samupetasya bhūpateḥ \|*  
*janānurāgo naivāsīd rūpahīnasya tasya vai \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. In spite of his royal qualities, he was not loved by ‘his subjects, on account of his ugliness.

## \|\| 115.17 \|\|

*rūpakāmaḥ sa madreśas tapase kṛtaniścayaḥ \|*  
*rājyaṃ mantrigataṃ kṛtvā jagāma himaparvatam \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. He then decided to go and practise penances for the attainment of personal beauty, in the Himalayas, after making over charge of his realm to his ministers.

## \|\| 115.18 \|\|

*vyavasāyadvitīyastu padbhyam eva mahāyaśāḥ \|*  
*draṣṭuṃ sa tīrthasadanaṃ viṣayānte svake nadīm \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. That far-famed king, with his own enterprising spirit as the only companion, went on foot to that home of all the tirthas (i.e., Himalayas), and at the end saw the renowned and beautiful river Airavati.

## \|\| 115.19 \|\|

*airāvatīti vikhyātāṃ dadarśātimanoramām \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. The king, whose fame was like that vast icy region, saw that river of the mighty Himalayan torrent, whose waters are cold like the rays of the moon and white like snow.

## Chapter 116

## \|\| 116.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*sa dadarśa nadīṃ puṇyāṃ divyāṃ haimavatīṃ śubhām \|*  
*gandharvaiśca samākīrṇāṃ nityaṃ śakreṇa sevitām \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Suta said: — O Rishis! The King saw the glorious, blessed and sacred river of Haimavati where the Gandharvas abound and which Indra worshipped.

## \|\| 116.2-5 \|\|

*surebhamadasaṃsiktāṃ samantāttu virājitām \|*  
*madhyena śakracāpābhāṃ tasminnahani sarvadā \|\| 2 \|\|*

*tapasviśaraṇopetāṃ mahābrāhmaṇasevitām \|*  
*dadarśa tapanīyābhāṃ mahārājaḥ purūravāḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*sitahaṃsāvalicchannāṃ kāśacāmararājitām \|*  
*sābhiṣiktāmiva satāṃ paṣyanprītiṃ parāṃ yayau \|\| 4 \|\|*

*puṇyāṃ suśītalāṃ hṛdyāṃ manasaḥ prītivardhinīm \|*  
*kṣayavṛddhiutāṃ ramyāṃ somamūrtimivāparām \|\| 5 \|\|*

2-5. The King Pururava was greatly charmed to see that beautiful river, the waters of which were intermingled with the rut of the celestial elephants the middle of which was shaped like the bow of Indra.

It was the home of many ascetics, was worshipped by a multitude of Brahmans, and was of golden colours. Its surface is covered with a row of snow-white flamingoes, and seemed to be fanned by kasha chamara.

Many a pious one sprinkled its water on his head. It appeared to the king to be beautiful, and subject to waxing and waning like the moon, and the giver of great-joy.

## \|\| 116.6-7 \|\|

*suśītaśīghrapānīyāṃ dvijasaṃghaniṣevitām \|*  
*sutāṃ himavataḥ śreṣṭhāṃ cañcadvīcivirājitām \|\| 6 \|\|*

*amṛtasvādusalilāṃ tāpasairupaśobhitām \|*  
*svargārohaṇaniḥśreṇīṃ sarvakalmaṣanāśinīm \|\| 7 \|\|*

6-7. The rapid running stream of cold water, the best of daughters of the Himalayas, full of ripples and tasteful like nectar, full of birds, honoured by the Tapasas and Brahmanas, the sacred river destroys ail sins and raises men to heaven.

## \|\| 116.8-12 \|\|

*agryāṃ samudramahiṣīṃ maharṣigaṇasevitām \|*  
*sarvalokasya cautsukya-kāriṇīṃ sumanoharām \|\| 8 \|\|*

*hitāṃ sarvasya lokasya nākamārgapradāyikām \|*  
*gokulākulatīrāntāṃ ramyāṃ śaivālavarjitām \|\| 9 \|\|*

*haṃsasārasasaṃghuṣṭāṃ jalajairupaśobhitām \|*  
*āvartanābhigambhīrāṃ dvīporujaghanasthalīm \|\| 10 \|\|*

*nīlanīrajanetrābhām utphullakamalānanām \|*  
*himābhaphenavasanāṃ cakravākādharāṃ śubhām \|*  
*balākāpaṅktidaśanāṃ calanmatsyāvalibhruvam \|\| 11 \|\|*

*svajalodbhūtamātaṃga-ramyakumbhapayodharām \|*  
*haṃsanūpurasaṃghuṣṭāṃ mṛṇālavalayāvalīm \|\| 12 \|\|*

8-12. She is the senior consort of the ocean, adored by the seers, the producer of ardent zeal in all, the most beautiful, the giver of universal happiness and relief, the guide to heaven, the waters of which flow up to Gokula, most pleasing, devoid of moss and reeds, and decorated with lotuses, the geese and the cranes throwing out their melodious notes at rapid succession, having deep whirlpools as her navel pit, having little islands hither and thither looking as her thighs, the blue lotus flowers looking like her eyes, the blooming lotuses supplying her mouth, the crystal waters her dress, the cranes her beautiful lips, the train of Balakas (cranes) her row of teeth, the restive shoals of fish her eyebrows, the elephants of her waters (water spouts) her breasts, and adorned with the singing geese and the lotus flowers that looked her jingling anklets and bracelets respectively.

## \|\| 116.13-15 \|\|

*tasyāṃ rūpamadonmattā gandharvānugatāḥ sadā \|*  
*madhyāhnasamaye rājan krīḍantyapsarasāṃ gaṇāḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*tām apsarovinirmuktaṃ vahantīṃ kuṅkumaṃ śubham \|*  
*svatīradrumasambhūta-nānāvarṇasugandhinīm \|\| 14 \|\|*

*taraṃgavrātasaṃkrānta-sūryamaṇḍaladurdṛśam \|*  
*surebhajanitāghāta-vikūladvayabhūṣitām \|\| 15 \|\|*

13-15. Charmed with the beauty, the Gandharvas sport every noon in her with their Apsaras. Her waters are highly perfumed by the mixing of the sandal and other scents (kunkuma), used by the Apsaras, and also with the various aroma of the trees on its bank, they are so constantly rippled with the wind that the reflection of the sun is difficult to be seen; while her banks are broken here and there as the elephants of the Devas strike them with their tusks

## \|\| 116.16 \|\|

*śakrebhagaṇḍasalilair devastrīkucacandanaiḥ \|*  
*saṃyutaṃ salilaṃ tasyāḥ ṣaṭpadair upasevyate \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Such a magnificent stream, in which flows the ichor of the Airavata, the elephant of Indra, and the sandal perfume of the consorts of the Devas, is swarmed by a train of sweetly buzzing bees.

## \|\| 116.17-18 \|\|

*tasyāstīrabhavā vṛkṣāḥ sugandhakusumāñcitāḥ \|*  
*tathāpakṛṣṭasaṃbhrānta-bhramarastanitākulāḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*yasyāstīre ratiṃ yānti sadā kāmavaśā mṛgāḥ \|*  
*tapovanāśca ṛṣayas tathā devāḥ sahāpsarāḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

17-18. The ascetics, the seers and the Devas, in company of the Apsaras, derive happiness on her banks, where the humming bees were attracted by the aroma of sweet flowers of the trees on her banks and where the intoxicated deer gratify their passions.

## \|\| 116.19 \|\|

*labhante yatra pūtāṅgā devebhyaḥ pratimānitāḥ \|*  
*striyaśca nākabahulāḥ padmendupratimānanāḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. The celestial women, with their face like the lotus, and the moon, become sanctified by a bath in her water and are honoured by the Devas.

## \|\| 116.20-22 \|\|

*yā bibharti sadā toyaṃ devasaṃghairapīḍitam \|*  
*pulindairnṛpasaṃghaiśca vyāghravṛndairapīḍitam \|\| 20 \|\|*

*satāmarasapānīyāṃ satāragaganāmalām \|*  
*sa tāṃ paṣyanyayau rājā satāmīpsitakāmadām \|\| 21 \|\|*

*yasyāstīraruhaiḥ kāśaiḥ pūrṇaiścandrāṃśusaṃnibhaiḥ \|*  
*rājate vividhākārai ramyatīraṃ mahādrumaiḥ \|*  
*yā sadā vividhairviprair devaiścāpi niṣevyate \|\| 22 \|\|*

20-22. The water of this river is not disturbed by the Devas, Pulindas, (kings) and tigers, &c., is decked with lotus flowers, illumined by the reflection of the moon and stars. The king continued his journey while seeing this river, which satisfies the desire of the sages. On her banks, the groups of Devas and Brahmanas were sitting under the branches of trees, whose kasa flowers look like the rays of the moon.

## \|\| 116.25 \|\|

*prauktā ca kesarigaṇaiḥ karivṛndajuṣṭā saṃtānauktasalilāpi suvarṇauktā \|*  
*sūryāṃśutāpaparivṛddhivivṛddhaśītā śītāṃśutulyayaśasā dadṛśe nṛpeṇa \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. The king, who is famous like the moon, saw that the river was mundated with many rivulets and was the dispeller of sing of the devotees and worshipped by many sages, which gives nourishment to the people, as a mother does to her sons, and which is- surrounded by the Devas, and by other people, seeking their own benefit, which is sported by the lions and the elephants, whose waters are full of Parijata trees, and which is never increased or decreased by the heat of the sun.

## Chapter 117

## \|\| 117.1 \|\|

*Matsya-Purāṇa 117*  
*sūta uvāca*  
*ālokayannadīṃ puṇyāṃ tatsamīrahṛtaśramaḥ \|*  
*sa gacchanneva dadṛśe himavantaṃ mahāgirim \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Suta said: — Rishis! when the king’s fatigue was removed at the sight of the holy water of that river and by the contact of its wind he trudged along, and sometime after had a view of the majestic Himalayas.

## \|\| 117.2 \|\|

*khamullikhadbhirbahubhir vṛtaṃ śṛṅgaistu pāṇḍuraiḥ \|*  
*pakṣiṇāmapi saṃcārair vinā siddhagatiṃ śubhām \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. That mountain touching the skies with many of its gray (white?) peaks was accessible to the sages, although not accessible to birds.

## \|\| 117.3 \|\|

*nadīpravāhasaṃjāta-mahāśabdaiḥ samantataḥ \|*  
*asaṃśrutānyaśabdaṃ taṃ śītatoyaṃ manoramam \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Besides this the Himalayas resounded with the thundering sound of the rivers falling down in cascades and which rendered all other sounds inaudible, They, the Himalayas, looked charming with their reservoirs of cold water.

## \|\| 117.4-10 \|\|

*devadāruvanairnīlaiḥ kṛtādhovasanaṃ śubham \|*  
*meghottarīyakaṃ śailaṃ dadṛśe sa narādhipaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*śvetameghakṛtoṣṇīṣaṃ candrārkamukuṭaṃ kvacit \|*  
*himānuliptasarvāṅgaṃ kvaciddhātuvimiśritam \|\| 5 \|\|*

*candanenānuliptāṅgaṃ dattapañcāṅgulaṃ yathā \|*  
*śītapradaṃ nidāghe 'pi śilāvikaṭasaṃkaṭam \|*  
*sālaktakairapsarasāṃ mudritaṃ caraṇaiḥ kvacit \|\| 6 \|\|*

*kvacitsaṃspṛṣṭasūryāṃśuṃ kvacic ca tamasāvṛtam \|*  
*darīmukhaiḥ kvacidbhīmaiḥ pibantaṃ salilaṃ mahat \|\| 7 \|\|*

*kvacidvidyādharagaṇaiḥ krīḍadbhirupaśobhitam \|*  
*upagītaṃ tathā mukhyaiḥ kiṃnarāṇāṃ gaṇaiḥ kvacit \|\| 8 \|\|*

*āpānabhūmau galitair gandharvāpsarasāṃ kvacit \|*  
*puṣpaiḥ saṃtānakādīnāṃ divyaistam upaśobhitam \|\| 9 \|\|*

*suptotthitābhiḥ śayyābhiḥ kusumānāṃ tathā kvacit \|*  
*mṛditābhiḥ samākīrṇaṃ gandharvāṇāṃ manoramam \|\| 10 \|\|*

4-10. The blue forests of Devadaru trees looked like its lower garment, clouds formed its upper garment, the white cloud the turban; while the moon and the sun the diadem. Its body was covered with snow, (which servel the purpose of an unguent), while the presence of minerals here and there seemed to paint it with sandal. It gave out coolness even during the hot weather. It was decorated with massive rocks, at places imprinted red with the foot-prints of the nymphs (Apsaras), with places lit up by the sun, enveloped in darkness at others, drinking water somewhere through its deep chasms, adorned elsewhere by the multitude of playful Vidyadharas, and the chief Kinnaras at places looking beautiful with the flowers of Heaven (Santana, &e.) fallen from the Gandharvas and the nymphs (Apsaras), while they were busy in drinking, and elsewhere covered with the beds of flowers pressed down by the Gandharvas rising from their slumber, and thus looked beautiful.

## \|\| 117.11-13 \|\|

*niruddhapavanairdeśair nīlaśādvalamaṇḍitaiḥ \|*  
*kvacic ca kusumairyuktam atyantaruciraṃ śubham \|\| 11 \|\|*

*tapasviśaraṇaṃ śailaṃ kāmināmatidurlabham \|*  
*mṛgairyathānucaritaṃ dantibhinnamahādrumam \|\| 12 \|\|*

*yatra siṃhaninādena trastānāṃ bhairavaṃ ravam \|*  
*dṛṣyate na ca saṃśrāntaṃ gajānāmākulaṃ kulam \|\| 13 \|\|*

11-13. At places it was covered with blue grass, without a breath of wind, and spots abounded with pretty flowers. This mountain is the refuge of the ascetics and most inaccessible to lovers. Herds of deer graze at the foot of rocks, whose trees are broken down by the tusks of elephants who, bewildered by the roars of the lion, were making noisy uproar, and could not be seen to be at rest.

## \|\| 117.14 \|\|

*taṭāśca tāpasairyatra kuñjadeśairalaṃkṛtāḥ \|*  
*ratnairyasya samutpannais trailokyaṃ samalaṃkṛtam \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. In whose valleys and bowers were enshrined meditating seers, and precious stones from whose stores adorn the three worlds.

## \|\| 117.15 \|\|

*ahīnaśaraṇaṃ nityam ahīnajanasevitam \|*  
*ahīnaḥ paṣyati girim ahīnaṃ ratnasampadā \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. It is the refuge of the great, and always served by the great. The great see this mountain great in jewels and precious stoner

## \|\| 117.16-17 \|\|

*alpena tapasā yatra siddhiṃ prāpsyanti tāpasāḥ \|*  
*yasya darśanamātreṇa sarvakalmaṣanāśanam \|\| 16 \|\|*

*mahāprapātasampāta-prapātādigatāmbubhiḥ \|*  
*vāunītaiḥ sadā tṛpti-kṛtadeśaṃ kvacitkvacit \|\| 17 \|\|*

16-17. The hermits accomplish their course of asceticism in short duration. All the sins vanish merely by the sight of this mountain. The wind makes the landscape pleasant by blowing the sprays of water of its waterfalls.

## \|\| 117.18 \|\|

*samālabdhajalaiḥ śṛṅgaiḥ kvacic cāpi samucchritaiḥ \|*  
*nityārkatāpaviṣamair agamyairmanasā utam \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. (It is) decorated somewhere with summits bristling with waterfalls; at other places, with peaks, which, owing to hot sun shining are inaccessible, except by the wind.

## \|\| 117.19-20 \|\|

*devadārumahāvṛkṣa-vrajaśākhānirantaraiḥ \|*  
*vaṃśastambavanākāraiḥ pradeśairupaśobhitam \|\| 19 \|\|*

*himachattramahāśṛṅgaṃ prapātaśatanirjharam \|*  
*śabdalabhyāmbuviṣamaṃ himasaṃruddhakandaram \|\| 20 \|\|*

19-20. At places it looked beautiful, with clusters of the great overshadowing Devadarus which, owing to their thickness, looked like clusters of bamboos. At other places were huge icicles, hundreds of thundering waterfalls and fountains, as well as caves, with their mouths sealed with snow.

## \|\| 117.21 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvaiva taṃ cārunitambabhūmiṃ mahānubhāvaḥ sa tu madranāthaḥ \|*  
*babhrāma tatraiva mudā sametaḥ sthānaṃ tadā kiṃcidathāsasāda \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. The great King of Madra roamed about, seeing that beautiful valley, and (after a time) sat down for a time at a certain place.

## Chapter 118

## \|\| 118.1 \|\|

*\*sūta uvāca*  
*tasyaiva parvatendrasya pradeśaṃ sumanoramam*  
*agamyaṃ mānuṣair anyair daivayogād upāgataḥ // MatsP\_118.1*

Suta said- “O Sages, king Pururava, suddenly reached one of the beautiful places, in that mountain, which was beyond the reach of an ordinary' person.

## \|\| 118.2 \|\|

*airāvatī saricchreṣṭhā yasmāddeśādvinirgatā*  
*meghaśyāmaṃ ca taṃ deśaṃ drumakhaṇḍairanekaśaḥ // MatsP\_118.2*

The place from where the river Airavatl issues, is also beautiful in appearance like the clouds with plenty of trees and the thickets.

## \|\| 118.3-6 \|\|

*śālaistālaistamālaiśca karṇikāraiḥ saśāmalaiḥ*  
*nyagrodhaiśca tathāśvatthaiḥ śirīṣaiḥ śiṃśapadrumaiḥ // MatsP\_118.3*

*śleṣmātakair āmalakair harītakavibhītakaiḥ*  
*bhūrjaiḥ samuñjakair bāṇair vṛkṣaiḥ saptacchadadrumaiḥ // MatsP\_118.4*

*mahānimbaistathā nimbair nirguṇḍībhirharidrumaiḥ*  
*devadārumahāvṛkṣais tathā kāleyakadrumaiḥ // MatsP\_118.5*

*padmakaiścandanairbilvaiḥ kapitthai raktacandanaiḥ*  
*mātāmrariṣṭakākṣoṭair abdakaiśca tathārjunaiḥ // MatsP\_118.6*

It has enough of the following types of trees including Sala, Tala, Tamala, Karnikara, Sasamaia, Nyagrodha, Asvattha, Sirisa, Simsapa, Slesmataka, Amalaka, Hantaka, Bibhitaka, Bhurja, Munjaka, Bana, Saptachhada, Mahanimba, Nimba, Nirgundi, Hari, Devadaru, Kaleyaka, Kadamba, Candana, Bilva, Kapittha, Raktacandana, Mata, Amra, Aristha, Aksota, Abdaka, Arjuna,

## \|\| 118.7-8 \|\|

*hastikarṇaiḥ sumanasaiḥ kovidāraiḥ supuṣpitaiḥ*  
*prācīnāmalakaiścāpi dhanakaiḥ samarāṭakaiḥ // MatsP\_118.7*

*kharjūrairnārikelaiśca priyālāmrātakeṅgudaiḥ*  
*tantumālair dhavairbhavyaiḥ kāśmīrīparṇibhistathā // MatsP\_118.8*

Hastikarna, Sumanasa, Kovidara, Pracinamalaka, Dhanaka, Samarataka, Kharjura, Narikela, Priyala, Amarataka, Inguda, Tantumala, Dhava, Bhavya, Kasamiraparni,

## \|\| 118.9-10 \|\|

*jātīphalaiḥ pūgaphalaiḥ kaṭphalailāvalīphalaiḥ*  
*mandāraiḥ kovidāraiśca kiṃśukaiḥ kusumāṃśukaiḥ // MatsP\_118.9*

*yavāsaiḥ śamiparṇāsair vetasair ambuvetasaiḥ*  
*raktātiraṅganāraṅgair hiṅgubhiḥ sapriyaṅgubhiḥ // MatsP\_118.10*

Jatipahala, Pugaphala, Katphala, Lavaliphala,    Mandara, Kimsuka, Kusumamsuka, Yavasa, Samiparnasa, Vetas, Narangi, Hingu, Priyangu,

## \|\| 118.11-16 \|\|

*raktāśokais tathāśokair ākallair avicārakaiḥ*  
*mucukundaistathā kundair āṭarūṣaparūṣakaiḥ // MatsP\_118.11*

*kirātaiḥ kiṅkirātaiśca ketakaiḥ śvetaketakaiḥ*  
*śobhāñjanair añjanaiśca sukaliṅganikoṭakaiḥ // MatsP\_118.12*

*suvarṇacāruvasanair drumaśreṣṭhais tathāsanaiḥ*  
*manmathasya śarākāraiḥ sahakārairmanoramaiḥ // MatsP\_118.13*

*pītayūthikayā caiva śvetayūthikayā tathā*  
*jātyā campakajātyā ca tumbaraiścāpyatumbaraiḥ // MatsP\_118.14*

*mocairlocaistu lakucais tilapuṣpakuśeśayaiḥ*  
*tathā supuṣpāvaraṇaiś cavyakaiḥ kāmivallabhaiḥ // MatsP\_118.15*

*puṣpāṅkuraiśca bakulaiḥ pāribhadraharidrakaiḥ*  
*dhārākadambaiḥ kuṭajaiḥ kadambair girikuṭajaiḥ // MatsP\_118.16*

Asoka and red flowered Asoka, Akalla, Avicaraka, Mucukunda, Kunda, Atarus, Paruska, Kirata, Kinkirata, Ketaka, Svetaketaka, Sobhanjana, Anjana, Sukalinga, Nikotaka, Asana, Sarakara, Yuthika, Jati, Campaka, Tumbara, Atumbara, Mocha, Loca, Lakuca, Tila, Kusesaya, Cavyaka, Bakula, Paribhadra, Haridraka, Dharakadambuka, Kutaja, Kadamba.

## \|\| 118.17-30 \|\|

*ādityamustakaiḥ kumbhaiḥ kuṅkumaiḥ kāmavallabhaiḥ*  
*kaṭphalairbadarairnīpair dīpairiva mahojjvalaiḥ // MatsP\_118.17*

*raktaiḥ pālīvanaiḥ śvetair dāḍimaiścampakadrumaiḥ*  
*bandhūkaiśca subandhūkaiḥ kuñjakānāṃ tu jātibhiḥ // MatsP\_118.18*

*kusumaiḥ pāṭalābhiśca mallikākaravīrakaiḥ*  
*kurabakair himavarair jambūbhir nṛpajambubhiḥ // MatsP\_118.19*

*bījapūraiḥ sakarpūrair gurubhiścāgurudrumaiḥ*  
*bimbaiśca pratibimbaiśca saṃtānakavitānakaiḥ // MatsP\_118.20*

*tathā guggulavṛkṣaiśca hintāladhavalekṣubhiḥ*  
*tṛṇaśūnyaiḥ karavīrair aśokaiś cakramardanaiḥ // MatsP\_118.21*

*pīlubhirdhātakībhiśca ciribilvaiḥ samākulaiḥ*  
*tintiḍīkaistathā lodhrair viḍaṅgaiḥ kṣīrikādrumaiḥ // MatsP\_118.22*

*aśmantakaistathā kālair jambīraiḥ śvaitakadrumaiḥ*  
*bhallātakairindrayavair valgujaiḥ siddhisādhakaiḥ // MatsP\_118.23*

*nāgakesaravṛkṣaiśca sukesaramanoharaiḥ*  
*karamardaiḥ kāsamardair ariṣṭakavariṣṭakaiḥ*  
*rudrākṣairdrākṣasambhūtaiḥ saptāhvaiḥ putrajīvakaiḥ // MatsP\_118.24*

*kaṅkolakairlavaṅgaiśca tvagdrumaiḥ pārijātakaiḥ*  
*pratānaiḥ pippalīnāṃ ca nāgavalyaśca bhāgaśaḥ // MatsP\_118.25*

*marīcasya tathā gulmair navamallikayā tathā*  
*mṛdvīkāmaṇḍapairmukhyair atimuktakamaṇḍapaiḥ // MatsP\_118.26*

*trapuṣairnartikānāṃ ca pratānaiḥ saphalaiḥ śubhaiḥ*  
*kūṣmāṇḍānāṃ pratānaiśca alābūnāṃ tathā kvacit // MatsP\_118.27*

*cirbhiṭasya pratānaiśca paṭolīkāravellakaiḥ*  
*karkoṭakīvitānaiśca vārtākair bṛhatīphalaiḥ // MatsP\_118.28*

*kaṇṭakair mūlakairmūlaśākaistu vividhaistathā*  
*kahlāraiśca vidāryā ca rurūṭaiḥ svādukaṇṭakaiḥ // MatsP\_118.29*

*sabhāṇḍīravidūsārarājajambūkavālukaiḥ*  
*suvarcalābhiḥ sarvābhiḥ sarṣapābhistathaiva ca // MatsP\_118.30*

Adityamustaka, Kumbha, Kumkuma, Katphala, Vadara, Nipa, Palivata, Dadima, Campaka, Bandhuka, Subandhuka, Kunjakajati, Patala, Mallika, Karavira, Kurabaka, Jambu, Nrpajambu, Bijapura, Karpura, Aguru, Bimba, Pratibimba, Santanaka, Vitanaka, Guggula, Hintala, Iksu (of white colour), Karavira (without thorns), Cakramarda (relieving pain), Pilu, Dhataki, Ciribilva, Tintidika, Lodhra, Vidanga, Ksirika, Asmantaka, Jambira, Svetaka, Bhallataka, Indrayava, Vaiguja, Nagakesara, Karamarda, Kasamarda, Aristaka, Varistaka, Rudraksa, Putrajivaka (having seven synonyms), Kamkolaka, Lavanga, Parijataka, Pippali, Nagavalli, Marica, Navamallika, Mrdvika, Atimuktaka, Trapusa, Nartikapratana, (Creepers) Kusmanda, Alabu, Cirbhita, Patoli, Karavellaka, Karkotaki, Vartaka, Brhati, Kantaka, Mulaka and various kinds of edible roots. Kallaras, Vidari, Ruruta, (having tasteful thorns), Bhandira, Vidusara, Rajajambuka, Baluka, Suvarcala, Sarsapa,

## \|\| 118.31-40 \|\|

*kākolīkṣīrakākolī chattrayā cāticchatrayā*  
*kāsamardīsahāsadbhiḥ sakandalasakāṇḍakaiḥ // MatsP\_118.31*

*tathā kṣīrakaśākena kālaśākena cāpyatha*  
*śimbīdhānyaistathā dhānyaiḥ sarvairniravaśeṣataḥ // MatsP\_118.32*

*auṣadhībhirvicitrābhir dīpyamānābhireva ca*  
*āyuṣyābhiryaśasyābhir balyābhiśca narādhipa // MatsP\_118.33*

*jarāmṛtyubhayaghībhiḥ kṣudbhayaghnībhireva ca*  
*saubhāgyajananībhiśca kutsnābhiścāpyanekaśaḥ // MatsP\_118.34*

*tatra veṇulatābhiśca tathā kīcakaveṇubhiḥ*  
*kāśaiḥ śaśāṅkakāśaiśca śaragulmaistathaiva ca // MatsP\_118.35*

*kuśagulmaistathā ramyair gulmaiścekṣor manoramaiḥ*  
*kārpāsajātivargeṇa durlabhena śubhena ca // MatsP\_118.36*

*tathā ca kadalīkhaṇḍair manohāribhiruttamaiḥ*  
*tathā marakataprakhyaiḥ pradeśaiḥ śādvalānvitaiḥ // MatsP\_118.37*

*irāpuṃṣpasamāyuktaiḥ kuṅkamasya ca bhāgaśaḥ*  
*tagarātiviṣāmāṃsīgranthikaistu surāgadaiḥ // MatsP\_118.38*

*suvarṇapuṣpaiśca tathā bhūmipuṣpaistathāparaiḥ*  
*jambīrakairbhūstṛṇakaiḥ sarasaiḥ saśukaistathā // MatsP\_118.39*

*śaṅgaverājamodābhiḥ kuberakapriyālakaiḥ*  
*jalajaiśca tathā vaṇair nānāvarṇaiḥ sugandhibhiḥ // MatsP\_118.40*

Kakoli, Ksirakakoli, Chattra, Atichatra, Kasamardi, Ksirasaka, Kalasaka, Simbidhanya and various other kinds of grain and medicinal herbs which prolong life, procure fame, give strength, and remove the fear of old age, death and hunger; and give every kind of happiness. There arc also Venulata, Kicaka, Venu, Kasa. Sara clusters, Kusa, Iksu, Karpasa of various species. Kadali groves, as well as grassy plots (lawns) known as Marakata. There are also flowers of Ira, Kumkuma, Tagara, Ativisa, Mamsagranthi, Suragada, Suvarna, Bhumipuspa. There are also Jambira, Bhustrina, and Sasuka, Srngavera, Ajamoda, Kuveraka, Priyalaka, as well as sweet smelling lotuses of various colours.

## \|\| 118.41 \|\|

*udayādityasaṃkāśaiḥ sūryacandranibhaistathā*  
*tapanīyasavarṇaiśca atasīpuṣpasaṃnibhaiḥ // MatsP\_118.41*

Some of the blooming lotuses looked like the rising sun, some like the moon and the sun. Some looked like bright gold, and some resembled the San (hemp, or Crotalaria juncea) flower.

## \|\| 118.42 \|\|

*śūkapattranibhaiścānyaiḥ sthalapattraiśca bhāgaśaḥ*  
*pañcavarṇaiḥ samākīrṇair bahuvarṇaistathaiva ca // MatsP\_118.42*

The place was full of growing lotuses, of which some looked like the leaf of a Sirisa (Suka), some having five colours, others many.

## \|\| 118.43 \|\|

*draṣṭurdṛṣṭyā hitamudaiḥ kumudaiścandrasaṃnibhaiḥ*  
*tathā vahniśikhākārair gajavaktrotpalaiḥ śubhaiḥ // MatsP\_118.43*

There were Kumuda flowers, too, pleasing to the sight of the observer and looking like the moon lotuses, resembling the glow of fire, and like mouth of an elephant were there also.

## \|\| 118.44-45 \|\|

*nīlotpalaiḥ sakahlārair guñjātakakaserukaiḥ*  
*śṛṅgāṭakamṛṇālaiśca karaṭai rājatotpalaiḥ // MatsP\_118.44*  
*jalajaiḥ sthalajairmūlaiḥ phalaiḥ puṣpairviśeṣataḥ*  
*vividhaiścaiva nīvārair munibhojyairnarādhipa // MatsP\_118.45*

The species of blue lotus, Kahlaras, the Gunjataka berry, Kaseru, Srngataka, Mrinala (a species of louts), Rajotpala (a kind of lotus), various kinds of fruits, flowers and roots thriving in water as well as on land, various species of rice fit for the use of the Rsis, abounded on that mountain.

## \|\| 118.46 \|\|

*na taddhānyaṃ na tatsasyaṃ na tacchākaṃ na tatphalam*  
*na tanmūlaṃ na tatkandaṃ na tatpuṣpaṃ narādhipa // MatsP\_118.46*

О King! There is no such grain, grass, potherb, fruit, berry and herb that did not thrive on that mountain.

## \|\| 118.47 \|\|

*nāgalokodbhavaṃ divyaṃ naralokabhavaṃ ca yat*  
*anūpotthaṃ vanotthaṃ ca tatra yannāsti pārthivaḥ // MatsP\_118.47*

The varieties of berries and fruits, grown in the world of the serpents, in the world of men, and the products of water and of forest, all flourished on that mountain.

## \|\| 118.48 \|\|

*sadā puṣpaphalaṃ sarvam ajaryam ṛtuyogataḥ*  
*madreśvaraḥ sa dadṛśe tapasā hyatiyogataḥ // MatsP\_118.48*

The King of Madra, Pururava, by virtue of his asceticism, thus saw all those fruits and flowers of the season there.

## \|\| 118.49-55 \|\|

*dadṛśe ca tathā tatra nānārūpān patatriṇaḥ*  
*mayūrān śatapattrāṃśca kalaviṅkāṃśca kokilān // MatsP\_118.49*

*tathā kādambakānhaṃsān koyaṣṭīn khañjarīṭakān*  
*kurarānkālakūṭāṃśca khaṭvāṅgān lubdhakāṃs tathā // MatsP\_118.50*

*gokṣveḍakāṃstathā kumbhān dhārtarāṣṭrāñśukānbakān*  
*ghātukāṃścakravākāṃśca kaṭukānṭiṭṭibhān bhaṭān // MatsP\_118.51*

*putrapriyān lohapṛṣṭhān gocarmagirivartakān*  
*pārāvatāṃśca kamalān sārikā jīvajīvakān // MatsP\_118.52*

*lāvavartakavārtākān raktavartmaprabhadrakān*  
*tāmracūḍānsvarṇacūḍān kukkuṭān kāṣṭhakukkuṭān // MatsP\_118.53*

*kapiñjalānkalaviṅkāṃs tathā kuṅkumacūḍakān*  
*bhṛṅgarājān sīrapādān bhūliṅgān ḍiṇḍimān navān // MatsP\_118.54*

*mañjulītakadātyūhān bhāradvājāṃstathā caṣān*  
*etāṃścānyāṃśca subahūn pakṣisaṃghānmanoharān // MatsP\_118.55*
