Не also saw the following birds and animals living there - The peacock, the wood-pecker, the sparrow, the cuckoo, the goose, the swan, the lapwing, the wagtail, the osprey, the Kalakuta, the civet cat, the goksavaidaka, the kumbha, the parrot, the crane, the Dhatuka, the ruddy-goose, the Katuka, the Tittibha, the Bhata, the Putra-priya, the heron, the Gocarma, the Girivartaka, the pigeon, the Kamala, the Sarika, the Cikora, the quail, the duck, the Raktavartma, the Prabhadraka, the cock, the blue jay, the fowl, the Kurikumacudaka, the large bee, the porpoise, the Bhulinga, the Dindima, the crow, the gallinule, the Datyuha, the sky lark, the bees and several other birds, etc.

## \|\| 118.56-62 \|\|

*śvāpadānvividhākārān mṛgāṃścaiva mahāmṛgān*  
*vyāghrānkesariṇaḥ siṃhān dvīpinaḥ śarabhānvṛkān // MatsP\_118.56*

*ṛkṣāṃstarakṣūṃśca bahūn golāṅgūlān savānarān*  
*śaśalomān sakādambān mārjārān vāyuveginaḥ // MatsP\_118.57*

*mūṣakānnakulān kāvān siṃhān drumamanoharān*  
*tathā mattāṃśca mātaṃgān mahiṣān gavayān vṛṣān*  
*camarān sṛmarāṃścaiva tathā gaurakharānapi // MatsP\_118.58*

*urabhrāṃśca tathā meṣān sāraṅgānatha kūkurān*  
*nīlāṃścaiva mahānālān karālānmṛgamātṛkān // MatsP\_118.59*

*sadaṃṣṭrārāmasarabhān krauñcākārakaśambarān*  
*karālānkṛtamālāṃśca kālapucchāṃśca toraṇān // MatsP\_118.60*

*daṃṣṭrānkhaḍgānvarāhāṃśca turaṃgānkharagardabhān*  
*etān adviṣṭānmadreśo viruddhāṃśca parasparam // MatsP\_118.61*

*aviruddhānvane dṛṣṭvā vismayaṃ paramaṃ yayau*  
*taccāśramapadaṃ puṇyaṃ babhūvātreḥ purā nṛpam // MatsP\_118.62*

The king also beheld the following wild beasts- The dog, the deer, the leopard, the lion, the tiger, the elephant, the rhinoceros, the wolf, the bear, the ape, the monkey, the rabbit, the agile cat, the buffalo, the cow, the bull, the Camara, the Srlvara (a species of deer), the white mule, the Urabhra, the ram, the antelope, the blue ox, the doe, the sambara, the wild boar, the horse, the ass, the donkey. Besides them, he also saw the beasts, which are naturally hostile to one another, living in mutual friendship. He was very much amazed to see this. Sometime ago, the sage Atri had his hermitage there.

## \|\| 118.63 \|\|

*tatprasādātprabhāyuktaṃ sthāvarairjaṅgamaistathā*  
*hiṃsanti hi na cānyonyaṃ hiṃsakāstu parasparam // MatsP\_118.63*

On account of the glory of that sage, the place was full of plants, and animals which, though naturally hostile, did not exercise hostility to one another- men and Raksasas.

## \|\| 118.64 \|\|

*kravyādāḥ prāṇinastatra sarve kṣīraphalāśanāḥ*  
*nirmitāstatra cātyartham atriṇā sumahātmanā // MatsP\_118.64*

There all carnivorous beasts lived on fruits and milk. In such ways their character was built up by the influence of the Great sage Atri.

## \|\| 118.65-66 \|\|

*śailānitambadeśeṣu nyavasacca svayaṃ nṛpaḥ*  
*payaḥ kṣaranti te divyam amṛtasvādukaṇṭakam // MatsP\_118.65*

*kvacidrājanmahiṣyaśca kvacidājāśca sarvaśaḥ*  
*śilāḥ kṣīreṇa sampūrṇā dadhnā cānyatra vā bahiḥ // MatsP\_118.66*

King Pururava himself passed several days on the slopes of those mountains, where cowbuffaloes and she-goats gave out milk, and where even the thorns had the flavour of ambrosia. Everywhere, О king, the rocks are full of streams of milk and curds.

## \|\| 118.67 \|\|

*saṃpaśyanparamāṃ prītim avāpa vasudhādhipaḥ*  
*sarāṃsi tatra divyāni nadyaśca vimalodakāḥ // MatsP\_118.67*

The King Pururava was charmed to see that mountain. There also he saw the beautiful rivers and streams.

## \|\| 118.68 \|\|

*praṇālikāni coṣṇāni śītalāni ca bhāgaśaḥ*  
*kandarāṇi ca śailasya susevyāni pade pade // MatsP\_118.68*

There were hot and cold water springs and cosy caves at every turn, worth being made use of.

## \|\| 118.69-70 \|\|

*himapāto na tatrāsti samantātpañcayojanam*  
*upatyakā suśailasya śikharasya na vidyate // MatsP\_118.69*

*tatrāsti rājañchikharaṃ parvatendrasya pāṇḍuram*  
*himapātaṃ ghanā yatra kurvanti sahitāḥ sadā // MatsP\_118.70*

Snow did not fall within a radius of (five yojanas) and valleys were not visible near the peaks, for the thick clouds incessantly pour forth perpetual snows there.

## \|\| 118.71-72 \|\|

*tatrāsti cāparaṃ śṛṅgaṃ yatra toyaghanā ghanāḥ*  
*nityamevābhivarṣanti śilābhiḥ śikharaṃ varam // MatsP\_118.71*

*tadāśramaṃ manohāri yatra kāmadharā dharā*  
*suramukhyopayogitvāc chākhināṃ saphalāḥ phalāḥ // MatsP\_118.72*

Close to it, on a different peak, thick clouds pour out diurnal showers of rain. Its rocks are extremely beautiful. The land of this enchanting hermitage (of Atri), was the giver of all desires and the trees of which place bore fruits successfully, for they were worthy of being eaten by the Devas.

## \|\| 118.73 \|\|

*sadopagītabhramarasurastrīsevitaṃ param*  
*sarvapāpakṣayakaraṃ śailasyeva prahārakam // MatsP\_118.73*

That mount is, indeed, the dispeller of all sins, and is adorned by the Devaganas and the buzzing bees.

## \|\| 118.74 \|\|

*vānaraiḥ krīḍamānaiśca deśāddeśānnarādhipa*  
*himapuñjāḥ kṛtāstatra candrabimbasamaprabhāḥ // MatsP\_118.74*

The spot shines white, like the rays of the moon, on account of heaps of ungathered ice; while, here and there, the frolicsome herd of the white monkeys played about.

## \|\| 118.75 \|\|

*tadāśramaṃ samantācca himasaṃruddhakandaraiḥ*  
*śailavāṭaiḥ parivṛtam agamyaṃ manujaiḥ sadā // MatsP\_118.75*

The hermitage of Atri is almost impassable to a human being, owing to the pile of snows and inaccessible mountains surrounding it.

## \|\| 118.76 \|\|

*pūrvārādhitabhāvo 'sau mahārājaḥ purūravāḥ*  
*tadāśramapadaṃ prāpto devadevaprasādataḥ // MatsP\_118.76*

The King Pururava, by virtue of his devotion and by the grace of God, reached the sacred hermitage.

## \|\| 118.77 \|\|

*tadāśramaṃ śramaśamanaṃ manoharaṃ manoharaiḥ kusumaśatairalaṃkṛtam*  
*kṛtaṃ svayaṃ ruciramathātriṇā śubhaṃ śubhāvahaṃ ca hi dadṛśe sa madrarāṭ // MatsP\_118.77*

That lord of Madra saw that exquisitely enchanting, blessed hermitage, which is beautified with hundreds of flowers, and which removes all fatigue, and which was built by Maharsi Atri himself.

## Chapter 119

## \|\| 119.1-2 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*tatra yau tau mahāśṛṅgau mahāvarṇau mahāhimau \|*  
*tṛtīyaṃ tu tayormadhye śṛṅgamatyantamucchritam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*nityātaptaśilājātaṃ sadābhraparivarjitam \|*  
*tasyādhastādvṛkṣagaṇe diśāṃ bhāge ca paścime \|\| 2 \|\|*

1-2. Suta said: — There were two great snow-clad peaks, shining with variegated colours, and in their midst was a huge summit, covered with perpetual snows, never warmed (by the sun’s rays) and where there is no cloud. Below on the west are trees also.

## \|\| 119.3 \|\|

*jātīlatāparikṣiptaṃ vivaraṃ cārudarśanam \|*  
*dṛṣṭvaiva kautukāviṣṭas taṃ viveśa mahīpatiḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. The king entered the hermitage, his curiosity awakened on seeing a picturesque cave encircled by creepers.

## \|\| 119.4-5 \|\|

*tamasā cātinibiḍaṃ nalvamātraṃ susaṃkaṭam \|*  
*nalvamātramatikramya svaprabhābharaṇodjvalam \|\| 4 \|\|*

*tam ucchritam athātyantaṃ gambhīraṃ parivartulam \|*  
*na tatra sūryastapati na virājati candramāḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. About 400 cubits (palva) of that cave was enveloped in darkness, and further off, it was full of light of its own, where there was a dome-like round place, very high and somber. The sun and the moon did not shine there.

## \|\| 119.6 \|\|

*tathāpi divasākāraṃ prakāśaṃ tadaharniśam \|*  
*krośādhikaparīmāṇaṃ sarasā ca virājitam \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. It was bright like the day time, all night and day (probably owing to the presence of radium there) and there was a beautiful lake, more than 2 miles in length.

## \|\| 119.7 \|\|

*samantātsarasastasya śailalagnā tu vedikā \|*  
*sauvarṇai rājatairvṛkṣair vidrumairupaśobhitam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. On all the four sides of the lake, there were charming rock beds, full of trees of gold and silver and coral (colour).

## \|\| 119.8-18 \|\|

*nānāmāṇikyakusumaiḥ suprabhābharaṇodjvalaiḥ \|*  
*tasminsarasi padmāni padmarāgacchadāni tu \|\| 8 \|\|*

*vajrakesarajālāni sugandhīni tathā utam \|*  
*pattrair marakatair nīlair vaiḍūryasya mahīpate \|\| 9 \|\|*

*karṇikāśca tathā teṣāṃ jātarūpasya pārthiva \|*  
*tasminsarasi yā bhūmir na sā vajrasamākulā \|\| 10 \|\|*

*nānāratnairupacitā jalajānāṃ samāśrayaḥ \|*  
*kapardikānāṃ śuktīnāṃ śaṅkhānāṃ ca mahīpate \|\| 11 \|\|*

*makarāṇāṃ ca matsyānāṃ caṇḍānāṃ kacchapaiḥ saha \|*  
*tatra marakatakhaṇḍāni vajrāṇāṃ ca sahasraśaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*padmarāgendranīlāni mahānīlāni pārthiva \|*  
*puṣparāgāṇi sarvāṇi tathā karkoṭakāni ca \|\| 13 \|\|*

*tutthakasya tu khaṇḍāni tathā śeṣasya bhāgaśaḥ \|*  
*rājāvartasya mukhyasya rucirākṣasya cāpyatha \|\| 14 \|\|*

*sūryendukāntayaścaiva nīlo varṇāntimaśca yaḥ \|*  
*jyotīrasasya ramyasya syamantasya ca bhāgaśaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*suroragavalakṣāṇāṃ sphaṭikasya tathaiva ca \|*  
*gomedapittakānāṃ ca dhūlīmarakatasya ca \|\| 16 \|\|*

*vaiḍūryasaugandhikayos tathā rājamaṇernṛpa \|*  
*vajrasyaiva ca mukhyasya tathā brahmamaṇerapi \|\| 17 \|\|*

*muktāphalāni muktānāṃ tārāvigrahadhāriṇām \|\| 18 \|\|*

8-18. The flowers and leaves were glowing gems, and it was full of lotuses whose petals were of ruby, whose anthers were diamond, and endowed with sweet scents, whose leaves were of emeralds, sapphires and lapis lazuli, and whose pericarps were of gold. Not only was the bed of the lake of diamond, but it was full of various gems. There were to be found shells (cowries, oysters and conches), terrible crocodiles, fishes and tortoises.

There were to be found pieces of emerald slabs, thousands of diamonds, rubies, sapphires, topazes, karkotakas, pieces of Tuthaka stone (copper sulphate), pieces of ivory, diamonds of the first water as well as of inferior kind, yellow stone, Suryakantimani, Chandrakantimani, Syamantaka, Surora golaksha, crystal, Gomeda, Dhulimarakata, Pittaka, lapis lazuli, Saugandhika (a kind of ruby), Rajamani, Brahmamani, Mukhyamani, and starry pearls of various kinds.

## \|\| 119.19 \|\|

*sukhoṣṇaṃ caiva tattoyaṃ snānācchītavināśanam \|*  
*vaiḍūryasya śilā madhye sarasastasya śobhanā \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Its water is also lukewarm, and removes all feelings of cold. The site of the lake, in the midst of lapis lazuli stone (Vaiduryamani), looked beautiful indeed.

## \|\| 119.20 \|\|

*pramāṇena tathā sā ca dve ca rājandhanuḥśate \|*  
*caturasrā tathā ramyā tapasā nirmitātriṇā \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. It is a beautiful square piece of land, measuring 800 cubits (200 Dhava), and has been formed by the asceticism of the sage Atri.

## \|\| 119.21-22 \|\|

*biladvārasamo deśo yatra yatra hiraṇmayaḥ \|*  
*pradeśaḥ sa tu rājendra dvīpe tasminmanohare \|\| 21 \|\|*

*tathā puṣkariṇī ramyā tasminrājañśilātale \|*  
*suśītāmalapānīyā jalajaiśca virājitā \|\| 22 \|\|*

21-22. King! The entire locality was full of gold (or looked like gold), as the entrance cave was. There was a certain place in that beautiful region, where, below the rock, flows a lovely pond of cool water adorned with lotus flowers.

## \|\| 119.23 \|\|

*ākāśapratimā rājaṃś caturasrā manoharā \|*  
*tasyāstadudakaṃ svādu laghu śītaṃ sugandhikam \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. This pond, O King, was in shape a beautiful square and resembling the sky in clearness, the water of which is most delicious, cold and perfumed.

## \|\| 119.24 \|\|

*na kṣiṇoti yathā kaṇṭhaṃ kukṣiṃ nāpūrayatyapi \|*  
*tṛptiṃ vidhatte paramāṃ śarīre ca mahatsukham \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Without injuring the throat and without overfilling the stomach (or belly), it gives pleasure to mind and body.

## \|\| 119.25 \|\|

*madhye tu tasyāḥ prāsādaṃ nirmitaṃ tapasātriṇā \|*  
*rukmasetupraveśāntaṃ sarvaratnamayaṃ śubham \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. In the centre of the pond, the sage Atri, by virtue of his austerities, has built a palace, which can be reached by a golden bridge, studded with precious stones.

## \|\| 119.26-33 \|\|

*śaśāṅkaraśmeḥ saṃkāśaṃ prāsādaṃ rājataṃ hitam \|*  
*ramyavaiḍūryasopānaṃ vidrumāmalasārakam \|\| 26 \|\|*

*indranīlamahāstambhaṃ marakatāsaktavedikam \|*  
*vajrāṃśujālaiḥ sphuritaṃ ramyaṃ dṛṣṭimanoramam \|\| 27 \|\|*

*prāsāde tatra bhagavān devadevo janārdanaḥ \|*  
*bhogibhogāvalīsuptaḥ sarvālaṃkārabhūṣitaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

*jānunākuñcitastveko devadevasya cakriṇaḥ \|*  
*phaṇīndrasaṃniviṣṭo 'ṅghrir dvitīyaśca tathānagha \|\| 29 \|\|*

*lakṣautsaṅgagato 'ṅghristu śeṣabhogapraśāyinaḥ \|*  
*phaṇīndrabhogasaṃnyasta-bāhuḥ keyūrabhūṣaṇaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

*aṅgulīpṛṣṭhavinyasta-devaśīrṣadharaṃ bhujam \|*  
*ekaṃ vai devadevasya dvitīyaṃ tu prasāritam \|\| 31 \|\|*

*samākuñcitajānustha-maṇibandhena śobhitam \|*  
*kiṃcidākuñcitaṃ caiva nābhideśakarasthitam \|\| 32 \|\|*

*tṛtīyaṃ tu bhujaṃ tasya caturthaṃ tu tathā śṛṇu \|*  
*āttasaṃtānakusumaṃ ghrāṇadeśānusarpiṇam \|\| 33 \|\|*

26-33. The palace was of silver, white like the rays of the moon; its stairs are of beautiful Vaiduryamani (lapis lazuli); its pillars of the coral and sapphire, its altars (or quadrangles) are studded with emeralds Markatamani.

The reflection of the diamonds made it very beautiful and pleasant to the sight. In this (enchanting) palace, the Lord of all, the serene Janardana, decorated with every ornament, reposed in the midst, all the luxuries of the luxurious, with one of his knees drawn up and the foot placed on the King of Serpents, the other (foot) resting on the lap of Lakshmi (the Goddess of wealth). While thus sleeping on the coils of Shesha, the Lord had one of His hands, adorned with bracelets, on the hood of the Snake, another, stretched out, supported His sacred head (laid) on the back of his fingers, the third one resting on the knee-cap of the half raised leg, touched his navel. Now hear how the fourth hand was placed. It held a celestial (santana) flower and was raising to the nose.

## \|\| 119.34-35 \|\|

*lakṣmyā saṃvāhyamānāṅghriḥ padmapattranibhaiḥ karaiḥ \|*  
*saṃtānamālāmukuṭaṃ hārakeyūrabhūṣitam \|\| 34 \|\|*

*bhūṣitaṃ ca tathā devam aṅgadairaṅgulīyakaiḥ \|*  
*phaṇīndraphaṇavinyasta-cāruratnaśirodjvalam \|\| 35 \|\|*

34-35. (The graceful Deity of happiness — ) Lakshmi — is devotedly shampooing Her Lord of the Universe in His Serene repose with Her lotus hands.

He was adorned with the garland of santana (kalpa) flowers, and with necklace, bracelets, rings, &c. (Hara, Keyura, Angada, Angulaka); while His head, glittering with the decorations of precious stones, rested on the hood of Shesha.

## \|\| 119.36-38 \|\|

*ajñātavastucaritaṃ pratiṣṭhitam athātriṇā \|*  
*siddhānupūjyaṃ satataṃ saṃtānakusumārcitam \|\| 36 \|\|*

*divyagandhānuliptāṅgaṃ divyadhūpena dhūpitam \|*  
*surasaiḥ suphalairhṛdyaiḥ siddhairupahṛtaiḥ sadā \|\| 37 \|\|*

*śobhitottamapārśvaṃ taṃ devamutpalaśīrṣakam \|*  
*tataḥ sammukham udvīkṣya vavande sa narādhipaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

36-38. King Pururava went in front of the God, and made his salutation to the One, who was of mysterious character, consecrated there by Atri, worshipped by the seers, adored by the ascetics, always offered the Kalpa santana flowers, covered with divine sandals, offered the incense, his right side covered with the best sappy fruits, offered by the anchorites (Siddhas) and having a bed of lotus flowers for His pillow.

## \|\| 119.39-41 \|\|

*jānubhyāṃ śirasā caiva gatvā bhūmiṃ yathāvidhi \|*  
*nāmnāṃ sahasreṇa tadā tuṣṭāva madhusūdanam \|\| 39 \|\|*

*pradakṣiṇamatho cakre sa tūtthāya punaḥ punaḥ \|*  
*ramyamāyatanaṃ dṛṣṭvā tatrovāsāśrame punaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

*bilādbahirguhāṃ kāṃcid āśritya sumanoharām \|*  
*tapaścakāra tatraiva pūjayanmadhusūdanam \|\| 41 \|\|*

39-41. The king saluted the Sacred One with his knees and head touching the ground, and pleased the Lord by his recitations of the hymns in His praises, containing his thousand names, and repeatedly circumambulated Him. He rested a little in that hermitage. Then, taking his residence in a beautiful cavern, outside the entrance to the cave, commenced his austerities and worship of Madhusudana.

## \|\| 119.42-43 \|\|

*nānāvidhaistathā puṣpaiḥ phalamūlaiḥ sagorasaiḥ \|*  
*nityaṃ triṣavaṇasnāyī vahnipūjāparāyaṇaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

*devavāpījalaiḥ kurvan satataṃ prāṇadhāraṇam \|*  
*sarvāhāraparityāgaṃ kṛtvā tu manujeśvaraḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

42-43. The king, in process of time, gave up every kind of food, engaging himself only in the worship of Fire to whom he offered various kinds of fruits, flowers, incense, roots and cow’s milk, after bathing thrice a day and sustaining himself on the water of the pond.

## \|\| 119.44 \|\|

*anāstṛtaguhāśāyī kālaṃ nayati pārthivaḥ \|*  
*tyaktāhārakriyaścaiva kevalaṃ toyato nṛpaḥ \|*  
*na tasya glānimāyāti śarīraṃ ca tadadbhutam \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. He slept, without any bedding, on the bare floor in the cavern, and lived only on water, having discarded all the eatables.

## \|\| 119.45 \|\|

*evaṃ sa rājā tapasi prasaktaḥ sampūjayandevavaraṃ sadaiva \|*  
*tatrāśrame kālamuvāsa kaṃcit svargopame duḥkham avindamānaḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. The king did not experience any ailment in course of that period of life and most marvelously carried on his devotion of Vishnu by residing in that hermitage for some time.

## Chapter 120

## \|\| 120.1 \|\|

*sa tvāśramapade ramye tyaktāhāraparicchadaḥ \|*  
*krīḍāvihāraṃ gandharvaiḥ paṣyannapsarasāṃ saha \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Suta said: — Then that king, giving up all food and the use of raiment’s, saw the pastimes of the Gandharvas and the nymphs (apsaras).

## \|\| 120.3-4 \|\|

*puṣpoccayaprasaktānāṃ krīḍantīnāṃ yathāsukham \|*  
*ceṣṭā nānāvidhākārāḥ paṣyannapi na paṣyati \|\| 3 \|\|*

*kācitpuṣpoccaye saktā latājālena veṣṭitā \|*  
*sakhījanena saṃtyaktā kāntenābhisamudjhitā \|\| 4 \|\|*

3-4. He, after offering the garlands made of various flowers to Vishnu, presented them to the Gandharvas; and he saw, but did not take any notice of the pastimes of, the nymphs (apsaras), while gathering flowers in the gladness of the heart.

## \|\| 120.4 \|\|

*kācitpuṣpoccaye saktā latājālena veṣṭitā \|*  
*sakhījanena saṃtyaktā kāntenābhisamudjhitā \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Some of the nymphs, while gathering flowers, became entangled in the creepers and were forsaken and left behind by their companions and lords.

## \|\| 120.5-6 \|\|

*kācitkamalagandhābhā niḥśvāsapavanāhṛtaiḥ \|*  
*madhupairākulamukhī kāntena parimocitā \|\| 5 \|\|*

*makarandasabhākrānta-nayanā kācidaṅganā \|*  
*kāntaniḥśvāsavātena nīrajaskakṛtekṣaṇā \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. Some of them, exhaling lotus-scent, had their faces surrounded by the buzzing black bees and were freed of them by their lovers; while others had their eyes moistened with the juice of flowers which was removed by the breath of their lords.

## \|\| 120.7 \|\|

*kācid uccīya puṣpāṇi dadau kāntasya bhāminī \|*  
*kāntasaṃgrathitaiḥ puṣpai rarāja kṛtaśekharā \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Some offered the heap of flowers collected by them to their husbands, and some decorated their hair with the garlands of flowers woven by their lords.

## \|\| 120.8 \|\|

*uccīya svayam udgrathya kāntena kṛtaśekharā \|*  
*kṛtakṛtyamivātmānaṃ mene manmathavardhinī \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Some apsaras (the very sight of whom produces love in men) collected the flowers and wove garlands of them, and then by their lords had their tresses of hair decorated with them; and considered themselves very fortunate.

## \|\| 120.9 \|\|

*astvasmingahane kuñje viśiṣṭakusumā latā \|*  
*kācidevaṃ raho nītā ramaṇena riraṃsunā \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Some were called away by their lords to dabble into amorous pastimes with them, to a solitary bower, full of beautiful flowers.

## \|\| 120.10 \|\|

*kāntasaṃnāmitalatā kusumāni vicinvatī \|*  
*sarvābhyaḥ kācidātmānaṃ mene sarvaguṇādhikam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Some culled the flowers out of the branch bent by their lords and looked upon themselves exceedingly fortunate and happy.

## \|\| 120.11 \|\|

*kāścitpaṣyati bhūpālaṃ nalinīṣu pṛthakpṛthak \|*  
*krīḍamānāstu gandharvair devarāmā manoramāḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Some, while enjoying the company of their lords, undisturbed in the grove of lotuses, cast sidelong glances towards the King Pururava.

## \|\| 120.12 \|\|

*kācid ātāḍayat kāntam udakena śucismitā \|*  
*tāḍyamānātha kāntena prītiṃ kācidupāyayau \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Some of the nymphs overpowered their lords by sprinkling water on them, and then became pleased when they, in their turn, were overcome by their lords.

## \|\| 120.13 \|\|

*kāntaṃ ca tāḍayāmāsa jātakhedā varāṅganā \|*  
*adṛṣyata varārohā śvāsanṛtyatpayodharā \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. When the maidens ran down, their lords became sad, and it was seen that as they heaved sighs, their breasts rose and fell.

## \|\| 120.14 \|\|

*kāntāmbutāḍanākṛṣṭa-keśapāśanibandhanā \|*  
*keśākulamukhī bhāti madhupairiva padminī \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Some looked as handsome as the lotus surrounded by black bees, as their tresses of long hair streamed on their faces after being loosened by their lords in course of the pastime.

## \|\| 120.15 \|\|

*svacakṣuḥsadṛśaiḥ puṣpaiḥ saṃchanne nalinīvane \|*  
*channā kācic cirātprāptā kāntenānviṣya yatnataḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Some of them became concealed in the lotus groves that resembled their eyes, and were found out by their lords after a long search.

## \|\| 120.16 \|\|

*snātā śītāpadeśena kācitprāhāṅganā bhṛśam \|*  
*ramaṇāliṅganaṃ cakre mano 'bhilaṣitaṃ ciram \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Some kept their lords in a close embrace for a long time, on the pretext of feeling cold after their bath.

## \|\| 120.17 \|\|

*jalārdravasanaṃ sūkṣmam aṅgalīnaṃ śucismitā \|*  
*dhārayantī janaṃ cakre kācit tatra samanmatham \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Some, of an enchanting smile, thrilled the observer (lord) with amorous feeling by wearing the finest wet garment on her person.

## \|\| 120.18 \|\|

*kaṇṭhamālyaguṇaiḥ kācit kāntena kṛṣyatāmbhasi \|*  
*truṭyatsragdāmapatitaṃ ramaṇaṃ prāhasacciram \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Some apsara was laughing at her lord, who fell down into the water as the garland was torn which he was pulling.

## \|\| 120.19 \|\|

*kācidbhugnā sakhīdatta-jānudeśe nakhakṣatā \|*  
*saṃbhrāntā kāntaśaraṇaṃ magnā kācidgatā ciram \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. With their knees having been scratched by their companions, some bent low and modestly took shelter for a long time in the company of their lords.

## \|\| 120.20 \|\|

*kācitpṛṣṭhakṛtādityā keśanistoyakāriṇī \|*  
*śilātalagatā bhartrā dṛṣṭā kāmārtacakṣuṣā \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Some began to dry her wet hair by turning her back on the sun and was seen from a rock by her lord with eyes full of love and desire.

## \|\| 120.21 \|\|

*kṛttamālyaṃ vilulitaṃ saṃkrāntakucakuṅkumam \|*  
*ratikrīḍitakānteva rarāja tatsarodakam \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. At that time the lake with its water full of garlands of the nymphs fallen in it and mixed with the saffron washed out of their breasts, looked beautiful like a maiden after amorous enjoyment with her lover.

## \|\| 120.22 \|\|

*susnātadevagandharva-devarāmāgaṇena ca \|*  
*pūjyamānaṃ ca dadṛśe devadevaṃ janārdanam \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Pururava saw the group of Devas, Gandharvas and the consorts of the Devas worshipping Vishnu after their bath.

## \|\| 120.23 \|\|

*kvacic ca dadṛśe rājā latāgṛhagatāḥ striyaḥ \|*  
*maṇḍayantīḥ svagātrāṇi kāntasaṃnyastamānasāḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. He also saw some of the nymphs sitting in the bowers of the creepers and dressing and decorating themselves, their minds being engrossed with (the thoughts of) their lords.

## \|\| 120.24 \|\|

*kācid ādarśanakarā vyagrā dūtīmukhodgatam \|*  
*śṛṇvatī kāntavacanam adhikā tu tathā babhau \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Some while looking at the mirror heard the news of their lords through their maids with rapt attention.

## \|\| 120.25 \|\|

*kācit satvaritā dūtyā bhūṣaṇānāṃ viparyayam \|*  
*kurvāṇā naiva bubudhe manmathāviṣṭacetanā \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Some at the hint of the maid began to put on their ornaments hurriedly without being conscious that they put them wrongly, their mind Was 80 engrossed with passionate desire.

## \|\| 120.26-27 \|\|

*vāununnātisurabhi-kusumotkaramaṇḍite \|*  
*kācitpibantī dadṛśe maireyaṃ nīlaśādvale \|\| 26 \|\|*

*pāyayāmāsa ramaṇaṃ svayaṃ kācidvarāṅganā \|*  
*kācitpapau varārohā kāntapāṇisamarpitam \|\| 27 \|\|*

26-27. Pururava also saw some of the nymphs sitting on the blue grass amidst nicely smelling flowers and drinking wine there; some of these beautiful nymphs made their lovers drink from their own hands, while others drank the wine offered by their lords.

## \|\| 120.28-29 \|\|

*kācitsvanetracapala-nīlotpalautaṃ payaḥ \|*  
*pītvā papraccha ramaṇaṃ kva gate te mamotpale \|\| 28 \|\|*

*tvayaiva pītau tau nūnam ityuktā ramaṇena sā \|*  
*tathā viditvā mugdhatvād babhūva vrīḍitā bhṛśam \|\| 29 \|\|*

28-29. Some whilst drinking water saw the reflection of her lotus eyes in it and afterwards began to enquire from her Lord where her two lotuses disappeared, and on being told by him that they were undoubtedly drunk by herself became bashful as she realized with pleasure his meaning.

## \|\| 120.30 \|\|

*kācitkāntārpitaṃ subhrūḥ kāntapītāvaśeṣitam \|*  
*saviśeṣarasaṃ pānaṃ papau manmathavardhanam \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Some of them (with beautiful eyebrows) drank with great relish the desire producing wine offered by their lords after they had drank of them.

## \|\| 120.31 \|\|

*āpānagoṣṭhīṣu tathā tāsāṃ sa narapuṃgavaḥ \|*  
*śuśrāva vividhaṃ gītaṃ tantrīsvaravimiśritam \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. The king also heard in that drinking place the songs of the nymphs with stringed accompaniments.

## \|\| 120.32 \|\|

*pradoṣasamaye tāśca devadevaṃ janārdanam \|*  
*rājansadopanṛtyanti nānāvādyapuraḥsarāḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Those nymphs, O King, dance on music before Lord Vishnu in the evenings.

## \|\| 120.33-34 \|\|

*yāmamātre gate rātrau vinirgatya guhāmukhāt \|*  
*āvasansaṃyutāḥ kāntaiḥ pararddhiracitāṃ guhām \|\| 33 \|\|*

*nānāgandhānvitalatāṃ nānāgandhasugandhinīm \|*  
*nānāvicitraśayanāṃ kusumotkaramaṇḍitām \|\| 34 \|\|*

33-34. And as the night advanced they coming out of that cave began to retire into their beautiful caverns where they pass the night in the pleasant company of their husbands, reclining on the plushy mattresses strewn with various kinds of sweet flowers and decorated with lovely sweet scented creepers.

## \|\| 120.35 \|\|

*evam apsarasāṃ paṣyan krīḍitāni sa parvate \|*  
*tapastepe mahārājan keśavārpitamānasaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. King Pururava thus saw all the pastimes of those nymphs on that mountain, went on with his devotion, his mind firmly fixed on Vishnu.

## \|\| 120.36-37 \|\|

*tamūcurnṛpatiṃ gatvā gandharvāpsarasāṃ gaṇāḥ \|*  
*rājansvargopamaṃ deśam imaṃ prāpto 'syariṃdama \|\| 36 \|\|*

*vayaṃ hi te pradāsyāmo manasaḥ kāṅkṣitānvarān \|*  
*tānādāya gṛhaṃ gaccha tiṣṭheha yadi vā punaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

36-37. The train of the Gandharvas in company of their consorts went to the king, and said: — “King! You have come to this region resembling the heaven, we shall grant you the boons of your desire after which it would be left to your pleasure either to stay here or to go back to your country”.

## \|\| 120.38 \|\|

*rājovāca*  
*amoghadarśanāḥ sarve bhavantastvamitaujasaḥ \|*  
*varaṃ vitaratādyaiva prasādaṃ madhusūdanāt \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. The King Pururava said: — “All of you have superhuman powers, your presence is never in vain. I therefore beseech you to give me the boon that I may please Vishnu”.

## \|\| 120.39 \|\|

*evamastvityathoktastaiḥ sa tu rājā purūravāḥ \|*  
*tatrovāsa sukhī māsaṃ pūjayāno janārdanam \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. They all unanimously gave the desired boon and the king stayed there for another month, worshipping Janardana in a happy mind.

## \|\| 120.40 \|\|

*priya eva sadaivāsīd gandharvāpsarasāṃ nṛpaḥ \|*  
*tutoṣa sa jano rājñas tasyālaulyena karmaṇā \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. He became a great favourite of the Gandharvas and their consorts, who were pleased with his firm devotion (to Vishnu).

## \|\| 120.41-43 \|\|

*māsasya madhye sa nṛpaḥ praviṣṭastadāśramaṃ ratnasahasracitram \|*  
*toyāśanastatra hyuvāsa māsaṃ yāvatsitānto nṛpa phālgunasya \|\| 41 \|\|*

*phālgunāmalapakṣānte rājā svapne purūravāḥ \|*  
*tasyaiva devadevasya śrutavāngaditaṃ śubham \|\| 42 \|\|*

*rātryāmasyāṃ vyatītāyām atriṇā tvaṃ sameṣyasi \|*  
*tena rājansamāgamya kṛtakṛtyo bhaviṣyasi \|\| 43 \|\|*

41-43. After a month, that king entered a lovely hermitage, decorated with innumerable gems, where he lived on water alone till the end of the bright fortnight in the month of Phalguna, when he heard the following words of Vishnu in a dream: — “At the close of the night you will find the Sage Atri, in whose company you will get your desire”.

## \|\| 120.44-45 \|\|

*svapnamevaṃ sa rājarṣir dṛṣṭvā devendravikramaḥ \|*  
*pratyūṣakāle vidhivat snātaḥ sa prayatendriyaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

*kṛtakṛtyo yathākāmaṃ pūjayitvā janārdanam \|*  
*dadarśātriṃ muniṃ rājā pratyakṣaṃ tapasāṃ nidhim \|\| 45 \|\|*

44-45. That king, powerful as Indra, having thus dreamt, got up early in the morning and with his senses under control, had his bath, and having performed daily duties worshipped Janardana, after which he came across the great sage Atri.

## \|\| 120.46 \|\|

*svapnaṃ tu devadevasya nyavedayata dhārmikaḥ \|*  
*tataḥ śuśrāva vacanaṃ devatānāṃ samīritam \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. He then told him of his dream and heard the following words of the Devas.

## \|\| 120.47-48 \|\|

*evametanmahīpāla nātra kāryā vicāraṇā \|*  
*evaṃ prasādaṃ samprāpya devadevādjanārdanāt \|\| 47 \|\|*

*kṛtadevārcano rājā tathā hutahutāśanaḥ \|*  
*sarvānkāmānavāpto 'sau varadānena keśavāt \|\| 48 \|\|*

47-48. “King! It is just what it should be; there is not the least doubt about it.” Thus getting the boons of his desire from Lord Vishnu, he worshipped the Lord and poured his oblations in the Fire and attained his object.

## Chapter 121

## \|\| 121.1-2 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*tasyāśramasyottaratas tripurāriniṣevitaḥ \|*  
*nānāratnamayaiḥ śṛṅgaiḥ kalpadrumasamanvitaiḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*madhye himavataḥ pṛṣṭhe kailāso nāma parvataḥ \|*  
*tasminnivasati śrīmān kuberaḥ saha guhyakaiḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

1-2. Suta said: — To the north of that hermitage, on the back of the Himalaya, in the centre, stands the Mount Kailas the residence of Shiva which is full of Kalpa trees and the peaks of which are studded with gems. Kuvera also resides there with his Guhyakas.

**Комментарий:**

Note — Guhyaka = A class of demigods who are the attendants of Kuvera and the guardians of his untold treasures.

## \|\| 121.3-6 \|\|

*apsaro 'nugupto rājā modate hyalakādhipaḥ \|*  
*kailāsapādasambhūtaṃ puṇyaṃ śītajalaṃ śubham \|\| 3 \|\|*

*mandodakaṃ nāma saraḥ payastu dadhisaṃnibham \|*  
*tasmāt pravahate divyā nadī mandākinī śubhā \|\| 4 \|\|*

*divyaṃ ca nandanaṃ tatra tasyāstīre mahadvanam \|*  
*prāguttareṇa kailāsād divyaṃ saugandhikaṃ girim \|\| 5 \|\|*

*sarvadhātumayaṃ divyaṃ suvelaṃ parvataṃ prati \|*  
*candraprabho nāma giriḥ yaḥ śubhro ratnasaṃnibhaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

3-6. Kuvera the Lord of Alakapuri enjoys the company of the nymphs there. Here is a lake shining like the Devas and is covered with the aroma of Mandira flowers, and watered by the cold and sweet springs of Kailasa. From this source runs the sacred Mandakini. On it stands the picturesque Nandana forest of vast dimensions. To the N.E. of Kailasa is the Chandraprabha Mountain shining like gems and full of metal ores and thickets of sweet smelling flowers.

## \|\| 121.7-8 \|\|

*tatsamīpe saro divyam acchodaṃ nāma viśrutam \|*  
*tasmātprabhavate divyā nadī hyacchodakā śubhā \|\| 7 \|\|*

*tasyāstīre vanaṃ divyaṃ mahaccaitrarathaṃ śubham \|*  
*tasmingirau nivasati maṇibhadraḥ sahānugaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8. The famous Achhoda lake is situated near it from which flows the sacred river Achchhoda on whose banks is the Chaitraratha forest. Manibhadra resides on that mountain with his attendants.

## \|\| 121.9-13 \|\|

*yakṣasenāpatiḥ krūro guhyakaiḥ parivāritaḥ \|*  
*puṇyā mandākinī nāma nadī hyacchodakā śubhā \|\| 9 \|\|*

*mahīmaṇḍalamadhye tu praviṣṭe tu mahodadhim \|*  
*kailāsadakṣiṇe prācyāṃ śivaṃ sarvauṣadhiṃ girim \|\| 10 \|\|*

*manaḥśilāmayaṃ divyaṃ suvelaṃ parvataṃ prati \|*  
*lohito hemaśṛṅgastu giriḥ sūryaprabho mahān \|\| 11 \|\|*

*tasya pāde mahaddivyaṃ lohitaṃ sumahatsaraḥ \|*  
*tasmātprabhavate puṇyo lauhityaśca nado mahān \|\| 12 \|\|*

*divyāraṇyaṃ viśokaṃ ca tasya tīre mahadvanam \|*  
*tasmingirau nivasati yakṣo maṇidharo vaśī \|\| 13 \|\|*

9-13. Manibhadra is the formidable general of the army of the Yakshas and is always followed by his retinue of Guhyakas. The sacred Mandakini as well as the Achchhoda flowing through the earthly plains enters the sea. Towards the S. E. of the Kailasa is the Sarvaushadhi (full of every kind of herbs) Mount of red arsenic (manahshila) facing the Chandraprabha Mountain. The Mountain Hemashringa (near it) shines red like the sun, below which there is a large lake of red water out of which comes a big river called the Lauhitya on the banks of which is the great heavenly forest known as Vishoka. Manidhara Yaksha resides there.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — Lauhitya = The Brahmaputra.

## \|\| 121.14-15 \|\|

*saumyaiḥ sudhārmikaiścaiva guhyakaiḥ parivāritaḥ \|*  
*kailāsātpaścimodīcyāṃ kakudmānauṣadhīgiriḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*kakudmati ca rudrasya utpattiśca kakudminaḥ \|*  
*tadañjanaṃ traikakudaṃ śailaṃ trikakudaṃ prati \|\| 15 \|\|*

14-15. He remains with his well-behaved and pious attendants. To the N.W. of Kailasa is the Mount Kakudman where the herbs are plentiful (so called) because of the birth of the great bull of Rudra there.

In front of this Trikakuda Mount is the mount of Anjana of three peaks.

## \|\| 121.16-17 \|\|

*sarvadhātumayastatra sumahānvaidyuto giriḥ \|*  
*tasya pāde mahaddivyaṃ mānasaṃ siddhasevitam \|\| 16 \|\|*

*tasmātprabhavate puṇyā sarayūrlokapāvanī \|*  
*yasyāstīre vanaṃ divyaṃ vaibhrājaṃ nāma viśrutam \|\| 17 \|\|*

16-17. There is the Mount Vaidyuta, full of all kinds of ores, below which is the most lovely Manasarovara Jake which is resorted to by the siddhas. The sacred Sarayu runs from that lake and purifies the people. On its bank is the Vaibhraja forest.

## \|\| 121.18 \|\|

*kuberānucarastasmin prahetitanayo vaśī \|*  
*brahmadhātā nivasati rākṣaso 'nantavikramaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. In that forest resides the most valiant demon (Rakshas), Brahmadhata, the attendant of Kuvera and the son of Prehita.

## \|\| 121.19 \|\|

*kailāsātpaścimāmāśāṃ divyaḥ sarvauṣadhigiriḥ \|*  
*varuṇaḥ parvataśreṣṭho rukmadhātuvibhūṣitaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. The Aruna Mountain to the West of Kailasa is the most important one. It is full of efficacious herbs and gold and shines red.

## \|\| 121.20 \|\|

*bhavasya dayitaḥ śrīmān parvato haimasaṃnibhaḥ \|*  
*śātakaumbhamayairdivyaiḥ śilājālaiḥ samācitaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Mount Shriman, of golden colour, is the favourite of Shiva and is covered with lines of gold quartz.

## \|\| 121.21-22 \|\|

*śatasaṅkhyais tāpanīyaiḥ śṛṅgairdivamivollikhan \|*  
*śṛṅgavānsumahādivyo durgaḥ śailo mahācitaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*tasmingirau nivasati giriśo dhūmralohitaḥ \|*  
*tasya pādātprabhavati śailodaṃ nāma tatsaraḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

21-22. Next comes the great inaccessible Shringavan (full of peaks) Mount. Hundreds of ‘its lofty golden peaks touch the sky. It is the abode of Dhumralochana lord of the mountain and below it is the lake Sailoda.

## \|\| 121.23 \|\|

*tasmātprabhavate puṇyā nadī śailodakā śubhā \|*  
*sā cakṣusī tayormadhye praviṣṭā paścimodadhim \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Out of which flows the sacred river Sailodak4 which is also known as Chakshusha and flowing between these two mountains falls into the Western Sea.

## \|\| 121.24 \|\|

*astyuttareṇa kailāsāc chivaḥ sarvauṣadho giriḥ \|*  
*gauraṃ tu parvataśreṣṭhaṃ haritālamayaṃ prati \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. To the North of Kailasa is the blessed Mount Sarvaushadha near which is a majestic snow clad mountain full of yellow orpiment (Haritala).

## \|\| 121.25-26 \|\|

*hiraṇyaśṛṅgaḥ sumahād-ivyauṣadhimayo giriḥ \|*  
*tasya pāde mahaddivyaṃ saraḥ kāñcanavālukam \|\| 25 \|\|*

*ramyaṃ bindusaro nāma yatra rājā bhagīrathaḥ \|*  
*gaṅgārthe sa tu rājarṣir uvāsa bahulāḥ samāḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

25-26. There is a mountain with golden peaks teeming with herbs below which is the lake of golden (coloured) sand and known as beautiful Vindu lake. Here King Bhagiratha remained for a long time for the advent of the Ganges.

## \|\| 121.27 \|\|

*divaṃ yāsyantu me pūrve gaṅgātoyāplutāsthikāḥ \|*  
*tatra tripathagā devī prathamaṃ tu pratiṣṭhitā \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. He said: — “May my ancestors attain heaven, their bones being drenched with the Ganges water.” The Ganges which goes three ways made her first appearance on that very spot

## \|\| 121.28 \|\|

*somapādātprasūtā sā saptadhā pravibhajyate \|*  
*yūpā maṇimayāstatra vimānāśca hiraṇmayāḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. The Ganges coming out of Somapada divided Herself into seven streams. There are sacrificial posts (yupa) of precious stones and vimanas (heavenly cars) of gold.

## \|\| 121.29-30 \|\|

*tatreṣṭvā kratubhiḥ siddhaḥ śakraḥ suragaṇaiḥ saha \|*  
*divyaśchāyāpathas tatra nakṣatrāṇāṃ tu maṇḍalam \|\| 29 \|\|*

*dṛṣyate bhāsurā rātrau devī tripathagā tu sā \|*  
*antarikṣaṃ divaṃ caiva bhāvayitvā bhuvaṃ gatā \|\| 30 \|\|*

29-30. Indra attained bliss by performing sacrifices on that spot along with the Devas. Here is the milky way of heaven, the centre of the starry nebule. The Ganges appears to shed splendid lustre there at night. She has descended on the earth, having purified the Heaven and sky (Antariksha).

## \|\| 121.31-33 \|\|

*bhavottamāṅge patitā saṃruddhā yogamāyayā \|*  
*tasyā ye bindavaḥ kecit kruddhāyāḥ patitā bhuvi \|\| 31 \|\|*

*kṛtaṃ tu tairbahusaras tato bindusaraḥ smṛtam \|*  
*tatastasyā niruddhāyā bhavena sahasā ruṣā \|\| 32 \|\|*

*jñātvā tasyā hyabhiprāyaṃ krūraṃ devyāścikīrṣitam \|*  
*bhittvā viśāmi pātālaṃ srotasā gṛhya śaṃkaram \|\| 33 \|\|*

31-33. She first descended on the head of the mighty Lord Shiva, Who curbed Her force by His glory. Her waters falling on the Earth, owing to Shiva’s anger, formed the Bindu lake. When she was thus suddenly stopped by Shiva, she became angry as she understood his unkind motive and made an attempt to force Herself into the lower regions, having engulfed Shiva in her tumultuous current.

## \|\| 121.34 \|\|

*athāvalepaṃ taṃ jñātvā tasyāḥ kruddhastu śaṃkaraḥ \|*  
*tirobhāvayituṃ buddhir āsīdaṅgeṣu tāṃ nadīm \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Realizing this proud attitude of the Ganges, the Lord thought of absorbing Her within Himself,

## \|\| 121.35 \|\|

*etasminneva kāle tu dṛṣṭvā rājānamagrataḥ \|*  
*dhamanīsaṃtataṃ kṣīṇaṃ kṣudhāvyākulitendriyam \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. But, at the same moment, He perceived King Bhagiratha standing in front of Him. He appeared lean, his veins becoming visible, troubled and hungry.

## \|\| 121.36 \|\|

*anena toṣitaścāhaṃ nadyarthe pūrvameva tu \|*  
*buddhvā'sya varadānaṃ tu tataḥ kopaṃ nyayacchata \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. The Lord then remembered that the king had first pleased Him by his austerities to get the sacred river — Ganges — which boon He had already granted to him. He therefore suppressed His wrath.

## \|\| 121.37 \|\|

*brahmaṇo vacanaṃ śrutvā yaduktaṃ dhārayannadīm \|*  
*tato visarjayāmāsa saṃruddhāṃ svena tejasā \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Moreover, as He was absorbing the sacred stream, He heard the entreaties of Brahma. He, therefore, freed the current from His hold.

## \|\| 121.38-39 \|\|

*nadīṃ bhagīrathasyārthe tapasogreṇa toṣitaḥ \|*  
*tato visarjayāmāsa sapta srotāṃsi gaṅgayā \|\| 38 \|\|*

*trīṇi prācīmabhimukhaṃ pratīcīṃ trīṇyathaiva tu \|*  
*srotāṃsi tripathāyāstu pratyapadyanta saptadhā \|\| 39 \|\|*

38-39. Being pleased with the devotion of Bhagiratha, the Lord, for his sake, let the river loose into seven branches, three of which went to the East, three to the West (and one near Himself), thus the three-wayed Ganges become flowed in seven streams.

## \|\| 121.40-42 \|\|

*nalinī hlādinī caiva pāvanī caiva prācyagā \|*  
*sītā cakṣuśca sindhuśca tisrastā vai pratīcyagāḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

*saptamī tvanugā tāsāṃ dakṣiṇena bhagīratham \|*  
*tasmādbhāgīrathī sā vai praviṣṭā dakṣiṇodadhim \|\| 41 \|\|*

*sapta caitāḥ plāvayanti varṣaṃ tu himasāhvayam \|*  
*prasūtāḥ sapta nadyastu śubhā bindusarodbhavāḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

40-42. Nalini, Hladini and Pavani flow in the East, Sita, Sindhu and Chakshu in the West, and the seventh followed the King Bhagiratha to the South. Hence the name Bhagirathi which falls into the Dakshina Samudra (southern waters) washing the Himavarsha. Seven holy rivers trace their origin from the Bindu Sarovara.

## \|\| 121.43-44 \|\|

*tāndeśānplāvayanti sma mlecchaprāyāṃśca sarvaśaḥ \|*  
*saśailānkukurānraudhrān barbarānyavanānkhasān \|\| 43 \|\|*

*pulikāṃśca kulatthāṃśca aṅgalokyānvarāṃśca yān \|*  
*kṛtvā dvidhā himavantaṃ praviṣṭā dakṣiṇodadhim \|\| 44 \|\|*

43-44. Those seven rivers having pierced through the Himalayas fall into the Dakshina Samudra (southern waters) after flowing through the Mlechchha countries of the mountains, viz., Kukur, Randhra, Barbara, Yavana, Khasa Pulika, Kulattha and Angalokya.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — Kukur = Darshaha.

Khasa or Khasa = A mountainous country in the North of India.

## \|\| 121.45-51 \|\|

*atha vīramarūṃścaiva kālikāṃścaiva śūlikān \|*  
*tukarānbarbarākārān pahlavānpāradāñchakān \|\| 45 \|\|*

*etāñjanapadāṃścakṣuḥ plāvayitvodadhiṃ gatā \|*  
*daradorjaguḍāṃścaiva gāndhārānaurasānkuhūn \|\| 46 \|\|*

*śivapaurānindramarūn vasatīnsamatejasam \|*  
*saindhavānurvasānbarbān kupathānbhīmaromakān \|\| 47 \|\|*

*śunāmukhāṃścordamarūn sindhuretānniṣevate \|*  
*gandharvānkinnarānyakṣān rakṣovidyādharoragān \|\| 48 \|\|*

*kalāpagrāmakāṃścaiva tathā kimpuruṣānnarān \|*  
*kirātāṃśca pulindāṃśca kurūnvai bhāratānapi \|\| 49 \|\|*

*pāñcālānkauśikānmatsyān māgadhāṅgāṃstathaiva ca \|*  
*brahmottarāṃśca vaṅgāṃśca tāmraliptāṃstathaiva ca \|\| 50 \|\|*

*etāñjanapadānāryān gaṅgā bhāvayate śubhā \|*  
*tataḥ pratihatā vindhye praviṣṭā dakṣiṇodadhim \|\| 51 \|\|*

45-51. The Chakshu stream of the Ganges before entering the sea waters the following countries: — Vira (China?), Maru, Kalika, Shulika, (Chulaka?), Tasara, Barbara, Pahlava, Parada, and Shaka, while Darada, Urja, Guda, Gandhara, Adrasa, Kuha, Shivapaura, Indramaru, Vasati, Samtaija, Sindha, Urvasha, Barva, Kulatha, Bhimaramaka, Shunamukha, and Urdhamaru form the basin of the Sindhu stream. The abodes of the Gandharvas, Kinnaras, Yakshas, the Rakshasas, Vidyadharas, Sarpas, the countries of Kimpurusha Naras, Kiratas, and Pulindas, Kuru, (Bharaba), Panchalas, Kaushikas, Matsya, Magadha, Anga, Brahmottara, Banga (Bengal) and Tamralipta, these Aryan janapadas are watered by the sacred Ganges, which striking against the Vindhya Hills falls in the Southern Waters.

## \|\| 121.52-54 \|\|

*tatastu hlādinī puṇyā prācīnābhimukhī yayau \|*  
*plāvayantyupakāṃścaiva niṣādānapi sarvaśaḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

*dhīvarānṛṣikāṃścaiva tathā nalimukhānapi \|*  
*kekarānekakarṇāṃśca kirātānapi caiva hi \|\| 53 \|\|*

*kālañjarānvikarṇāṃśca kuśikānsvargabhaumakān \|*  
*sā maṇḍale samudrasya tīre bhūtvā tu sarvaśaḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

52-54. The Hladini Ganges runs eastward into the sea after passing through the following countries: — the countries of Upaka, Nishadha, Dhivara, Rishika, Nilamukha, Kekara, Ekakarna, Kirata, Kalanjara, Vikarna, Kushika and Svargabhaumaka.

## \|\| 121.55-57 \|\|

*tatastu nalinī cāpi prācīmeva diśaṃ yayau \|*  
*kupathānplāvayantī sā indradyumnasarāṃsyapi \|\| 55 \|\|*

*tathā kharapathāndeśān vetraśaṅkupathānapi \|*  
*madhyenodjānakamarūn kuthaprāvaraṇānyayau \|\| 56 \|\|*

*indradvīpasamīpe tu praviṣṭā lavaṇodadhim \|*  
*tatastu pāvanī prāyāt prācīmāśāṃ javena tu \|\| 57 \|\|*

55-57. The Nalini stream, too, runs to the east to the sea through the following countries: — Kupatha, Indradyumna Sarovara, Kharpatha, Ketra Saukupatha, Ujjanaka, Maru, Kutha, Pravarana.

## \|\| 121.58-59 \|\|

*tomarānplāvayatī ca haṃsamārgānsamūhakān \|*  
*pūrvāndeśāṃśca sevantī bhittvā sā bahudhā girim \|*  
*karṇaprāvaraṇānprāpya gatā sāśvamukhānapi \|\| 58 \|\|*

*siktvā parvatameruṃ sā gatvā vidyādharānapi \|*  
*śaimimaṇḍalakoṣṭhaṃ tu sā praviṣṭā mahatsaraḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

58-59. The swift running Pavani Ganges passes eastward through Tomara, Hansamarga, Samudhaka, various mountains and other eastern countries; and then through Karna, Pravarana, Ashvamukha, Sumeru Mountain, the land of the Vidyadharas; whence the mighty stream has entered the Shaimimandala Kostha a big lake.

## \|\| 121.60 \|\|

*tāsāṃ nadyupanadyo 'nyāḥ śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ \|*  
*upagacchanti tā nadyo yato varṣati vāsavaḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Thousands of tributaries and rivulets spring from the main streams. The God of rain — Indra — draws out His store of rainwater from there.

## \|\| 121.61-64 \|\|

*tīre vaṃśaukasārāyāḥ surabhirnāma tadvanam \|*  
*hiraṇyaśṛṅgo vasati vidvānkauberako vaśī \|\| 61 \|\|*

*yajñādapetaḥ sumahān amitaujāḥ suvikramaḥ \|*  
*tatrāgastyaiḥ parivṛtā vidvabhirdbrahmarākṣasaiḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

*kuberānucarā hyete catvārastatsamāśritāḥ \|*  
*evameva tu vijñeyā siddhiḥ parvatavāsinām \|\| 63 \|\|*

*paraspareṇa dviguṇā dharmataḥ kāmato 'rthataḥ \|*  
*hemakūṭasya pṛṣṭhe tu sarpāṇāṃ tatsaraḥ smṛtam \|\| 64 \|\|*

61-64. The Surabhi forest stands on the banks of the river Vanshankasara. There resides Hiranyashringa the most powerful and learned follower of Kuvera who has been forbidden to take any part in the sacrifices. Surrounded by the learned (progeny of Atri) and the Brahmarakshasas, the four attendants of Kuvera reside there. The residents of the hills and the mountains attain double powers (by practice, as compared to other folks.

## \|\| 121.65 \|\|

*sarasvatī prabhavati tasmādjyotiṣmatī tu yā \|*  
*avagāḍhe hyubhayataḥ samudrau pūrvapaścimau \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. At the back of the Hemakuta is the lake of the snakes (sarpa) out of which flow the two rivers, Sarasinati and Jyotishmati falling to the eastern and western seas respectively.

## \|\| 121.66 \|\|

*saro viṣṇupadaṃ nāma niṣadhe parvatottame \|*  
*yasmādagre prabhavati gandharvānukule ca te \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. A little further on is the lake Vishnupada on the Nishadha Mount. Both these lakes (Naya and Vishnupada) are the favourite resorts of the Gandharvas.

## \|\| 121.67-72 \|\|

*meroḥ pārśvātprabhavati hradaścandraprabho mahān \|*  
*jambūścaiva nadī puṇyā yasyāṃ jāmbūnadaṃ smṛtam \|\| 67 \|\|*

*payodastu hrado nīlaḥ sa śubhraḥ puṇḍarīkavān \|*  
*puṇḍarīkātpayodācca tasmād dve samprasūyatām \|\| 68 \|\|*

*sarasastu sarastvetat smṛtamuttaramānasam \|*  
*mṛgyā ca mṛgakāntā ca tasmād dve samprasūyatām \|\| 69 \|\|*

*hradāḥ kuruṣu vikhyātāḥ padmamīnakulākulāḥ \|*  
*nāmnā te vai jayā nāma dvādaśodadhisaṃnibhāḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

*tebhyaḥ śāntī ca madhvī ca dve nadyau samprasūyatām \|*  
*kimpuruṣādyāni yānyaṣṭau teṣu devo na varṣati \|\| 71 \|\|*

*udbhidānyudakānyatra pravahanti saridvarāḥ \|*  
*balāhakaśca ṛṣabho cakro maināka eva ca \|\| 72 \|\|*

67-72. The lake Chandraprabha and the sacred Jamba river, — the bed of Jamvanada gold, have their source in the Sumeru Mount. The two blue water lakes, the Payoda and the sacred Pundarika, are the mothers of two sister lakes one of which is called the Uttara Manasa from which the rivers Mrigya and Mrigak4anta trace their origin. In the Kuru country there are twelve Jakes under the name of Vaijaya that are full of lotus beds and fish, &c. They are all like the ocean (in extent (?). The rivers Shanti and Madhvi spring from them. There is no rainfall in the eight Jakes Kimpurusha, &c. They are full of water and (aquatic) vegetables.

## \|\| 121.73 \|\|

*viniviṣṭāḥ pratidiśaṃ nimagnā lavaṇāmbudhim \|*  
*candrakāntastathā droṇaḥ sumahāṃśca śiloccayaḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. The Mounts Valahaka, Rishabha, Chakra, Mainaka pervading in all directions merge into the sea.

## \|\| 121.74 \|\|

*udgāyatā udīcyāṃ tu avagāḍhā mahodadhim \|*  
*cakro badhirakaścaiva tathā nāradaparvataḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. The Mounts Chandrakanta, Drona and Sumah4n are spreading in the North till they have merged into the Great Northern ocean.

## \|\| 121.75 \|\|

*pratīcīmāyatāste vai pratiṣṭhāste mahodadhim \|*  
*jīmūto drāvaṇaścaiva mainākaścandraparvataḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. The Mounts Chakra, Vadhiraka and Narada spread in the West till they have also merged into the Great Western Ocean.

## \|\| 121.76 \|\|

*āyatāste mahāśailāḥ samudraṃ dakṣiṇaṃ prati \|*  
*cakramainākayormadhye divi san dakṣiṇāpathe \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. The Mounts Jimuta, Dravana, Mainaka and Chandra are spreading towards the South till they have submerged in the Dakshina Samudra.

## \|\| 121.77-79 \|\|

*tatra saṃvartako nāma so 'gniḥ pibati tadjalam \|*  
*agniḥ samudravāsastu aurvo 'sau vaḍavāmukhaḥ \|\| 77 \|\|*

*ityete parvatāviṣṭāś catvāro lavaṇodadhim \|*  
*chidyamāneṣu pakṣeṣu purā indrasya vai bhayāt \|\| 78 \|\|*

*teṣāṃ tu dṛṣyate candre śukle kṛṣṇe samāplutiḥ \|*  
*te bhāratasya varṣasya bhedā yena prakīrtitāḥ \|\| 79 \|\|*

77-79. Between the Mounts Chakra and Mainaka in the southern portion of the heaven is the Samvartaka Agni (volcanic mountain) which drinks the water of the seas. The Agni (volcanic) mountains Aurva, Barava mukha too are submerged into the Lavana Samudra. These four mountains merged into the ocean (for safety) when Indra began to destroy their wings (by His thunderbolt) and they are still visible on particular days in the bright and dark fortnights.

## \|\| 121.80 \|\|

*ihoditasya dṛṣyante anye tvanyatra coditāḥ \|*  
*uttarottarameteṣāṃ varṣam udricyate guṇaiḥ \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. The divisions of the Bharathavarsha are thus described. Those named within the limits of Bharathavarsha are visible there and the rest are described elsewhere.

## \|\| 121.81-82 \|\|

*ārogyāuḥpramāṇābhyāṃ dharmataḥ kāmato 'rthataḥ \|*  
*samanvitāni bhūtāni teṣu varṣeṣu bhāgaśaḥ \|\| 81 \|\|*

*vasanti nānājātīni teṣu sarveṣu tāni vai \|*  
*ityetaddhārayadviśvaṃ pṛthvī jagadidaṃ sthitā \|\| 82 \|\|*

81-82. The more northern (one of those mountains) the region, the better 1t is. The people residing there are healthy, pious, longlived and possessed of the sterling qualities (Dharma, Artha, Kama, &c.). Various classes of people live in those khandas. The universe thus holding the various regions on her is known as Prithvi or Jagat (Earth).

## Chapter 122

## \|\| 122.1-7 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*śākadvīpasya vakṣyāmi yathāvadiha niścayam \|*  
*kathyamānaṃ nibodha tvaṃ śākaṃ dvīpaṃ dvijottamāḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*jambūdvīpasya vistārād dviguṇastasya vistaraḥ \|*  
*vistārāttriguṇaścāpi pariṇāhaḥ samantataḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*tenāvṛtaḥ samudro 'yaṃ dvīpena lavaṇodadhiḥ \|*  
*tatra puṇyā janapadāś cirācca mriyate janaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*kuta eva ca durbhikṣaṃ kṣamātejoyuteṣviha \|*  
*tatrāpi parvatāḥ śubhrāḥ saptaiva maṇibhūṣitāḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*śākadvīpādiṣu tveṣu sapta sapta nagās triṣu \|*  
*ṛjvāyatāḥ pratidiśaṃ niviṣṭā varṣaparvatāḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*ratnākarādināmānaḥ sānumanto mahācitāḥ \|*  
*samoditāḥ pratidiśaṃ dvīpavistāramānataḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*ubhayatrāvagāḍhau ca lavaṇakṣīrasāgarau \|*  
*śākadvīpe tu vakṣyāmi sapta divyānmahācalān \|\| 7 \|\|*

1-7. Suta Said. — Now hear from me, O, holy twice born! the description of Shakadvipa. Its width is twice that of the Jambudvipa, while its perimeter is thrice its breadth. The Kshira Samudra is surrounded by this Dvipa.

It has many sacred janapadas and the people live for a long number of years. The people are full of power and forbearance. How can there be any famine then. There are seven white mountains full of precious stones.

Other three Dvipas have each seven mountains. These Ratnakara mounts are broad, extend in all directions and have most lofty peaks. All the mountains maintain a sort of uniform length in each direction.

Shakadvipa has Kshira Samudra and Kshira Samudra on its either sides respectively. Now I shall tell you something about the seven mountains of Shakadvipa.

## \|\| 122.8-10 \|\|

*devarṣigandharvautaḥ prathamo merurucyate \|*  
*prāgāyataḥ sa sauvarṇa udayo nāma parvataḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*tatra meghāstu vṛṣṭyarthaṃ prabhavantyapayānti ca \|*  
*tasyāpareṇa sumahāñ jaladhāro mahāgiriḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*sa vai candraḥ samākhyātaḥ sarvauṣadhisamanvitaḥ \|*  
*tasmānnityamupādatte vāsavaḥ paramaṃ jalam \|\| 10 \|\|*

8-10. The first of them is the Mount Meru inhabited by the Devarshis and the Gandharvas. It stretches out long in the East and has a amine of gold and is called the Udaya Mountain there. Clouds gather there to give rain and then disappear. Parallel to it stands the Mount Jaladhara which is described like the moon and is full of various kinds of herb and the God of rain draws out his store of rain from it in plenty.

## \|\| 122.11 \|\|

*nārado nāma caivokto durgaśailo mahācitaḥ \|*  
*tatrācalau samutpannau pūrvaṃ nāradaparvatau \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Further to it is the inaccessible Narada Mountain where were in ancient times the two hills of Narada and Parvata.

## \|\| 122.12 \|\|

*tasyāpareṇa sumahāñ śyāmo nāma mahāgiriḥ \|*  
*yatra śyāmatvamāpannāḥ prajāḥ pūrvamimāḥ kila \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Beyond it is the Mount Syama the inhabitants of which were dark in complexion.

## \|\| 122.13 \|\|

*sa eva dundubhirnāma śyāmaparvatasaṃnibhaḥ \|*  
*śabdamṛtyuḥ purā tasmin dundubhistāḍitaḥ suraiḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. (Not far from it) is the Dundubhi Mountain similar to Syama Mountain and here the Devas first placed a Dundubhi (drum), whose sound brought about death.

## \|\| 122.14-15 \|\|

*ratnamālāntaramayaḥ śālmalaścāntarālakṛt \|*  
*tasyāpareṇa rajato mahānasto giriḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*sa vai somaka ityukto devairyatrāmṛtaṃ purā \|*  
*saṃbhṛtaṃ ca hṛtaṃ caiva māturarthe garutmatā \|\| 15 \|\|*

14-15. The mighty Mount Sahnala is full of precious stones and near it is the big mountain of silver which is known as Somaka, on account of the Devas first drinking the draught of ambrosia there. It was there where Garuda stole the nectar for his mother.

## \|\| 122.16-1 \|\|

*tasyāpare cāmbikeyaḥ sumanāścaiva sa smṛtaḥ \|*  
*hiraṇyākṣo varāheṇa tasmiñchaile niṣūditaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*āmbikeyātparo ramyaḥ sarvauṣadhiniṣevitaḥ \|*  
*vibhrājastu samākhyātaḥ sphāṭikastu mahāngiriḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*yasmādvibhrājate vahnir vibhrājastena sa smṛtaḥ \|*  
*saiveha keśavetyukto yato vāuḥ pravāti ca \|\| 18 \|\|*

*sūta uvāca*  
*śākadvīpasya vakṣyāmi yathāvadiha niścayam \|*  
*kathyamānaṃ nibodha tvaṃ śākaṃ dvīpaṃ dvijottamāḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

16-18. Adjacent to it stands the Mount Ambikeya, also known as Sumana, where the demon Hirany4ksa was killed by the Lord Varaha. Near it stands the Crystal Mountain, Vibhraja, which is full of herbs and gems.

1t is a volcano, that is why it is called Vibhraja (fire agitator); it is also called Keshava. The wind there is very strong.

## \|\| 122.19 \|\|

*teṣāṃ varṣāṇi vakṣyāmi parvatānāṃ dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*śṛṇudhvaṃ nāmatastāni yathāvadanupūrvaśaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. I shall now name the mountains with the divisions, O, holy twice borns! and hear it attentively.

## \|\| 122.20 \|\|

*dvināmānyeva varṣāṇi yathaiva girayastathā \|*  
*udayasyodayaṃ varṣaṃ jaladhāreti viśrutam \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Those khandas have double names like the mountains. The mountain as well as Varsha of Udaya is known as Udaya and Jaladhara.

## \|\| 122.21 \|\|

*nāmnā gatabhayaṃ nāma varṣaṃ tatprathamaṃ smṛtam \|*  
*dvitīyaṃ jaladhārasya sukumāramiti smṛtam \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Udayakhanda is called the Gatabhayakhanda and the Jaladhara khanda is known as the Sukumara.

## \|\| 122.22 \|\|

*tadeva śaiśiraṃ nāma varṣaṃ tatparikīrtitam \|*  
*nāradasya ca kaumāraṃ tadeva ca sukhodayam \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. That is called the (Shaishira) Sitala khanda, and Kaumarakhanda is in the Narada Mountain which is also known as Sukhodaya,

## \|\| 122.23 \|\|

*śyāmaparvatavarṣaṃ tad anīcakam iti smṛtam \|*  
*ānandakamiti proktaṃ tadeva munibhiḥ śubham \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Anichaka is the name of the khanda on which is the Syama Mountain which has also been called the Anandaka by the sages.

## \|\| 122.24 \|\|

*somakasya śubhaṃ varṣaṃ vijñeyaṃ kusumotkaram \|*  
*tadevāsitam ityuktaṃ varṣaṃ somakasaṃjñitam \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Kusumotakara is the khanda on which les the Somaka Mountain which is also known as Asita.

## \|\| 122.25 \|\|

*āmbikeyasya mainākaṃ kṣemakaṃ caiva tatkṛtam \|*  
*kesaraḥ parvatasyāpi mahādrumamiti smṛtam \|*  
*tadeva dhavamityuktaṃ varṣaṃ vibhrājasaṃjñitam \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Mainaka is the khanda of the Mount Ambikeya. It is also called Ksemaka. The khanda of the Vibhraja Mountain is called Dhruva as well as Vibhraja.

## \|\| 122.26-28 \|\|

*dvīpasya pariṇāhaṃ ca hrasvadīrghatvameva ca \|*  
*jambūdvīpena saṃkhyātaṃ tasya madhye vanaspatiḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*śāko nāma mahāvṛkṣaḥ prajāstasya mahānugāḥ \|*  
*eteṣu devagandharvāḥ siddhāśca saha cāraṇaiḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

*viharanti ramante ca dṛṣyamānāśca taiḥ saha \|*  
*tatra puṇyā janapadāś cāturvarṇyasamanvitāḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

26-28. Of the same dimensions as Jambudvipa is the huge Shaka tree in the centre of the Dvipa itself, frequented by the people. Those regions were frequented by the Devas, the Gandharvas, the Bards (charanas), and the Siddhas (anchorites), who freely enjoy the beauty of the place.

It contains many janapadas peopled by the four varnd4s.

## \|\| 122.29 \|\|

*teṣu nadyaśca saptaiva prativarṣaṃ samudragāḥ \|*  
*dvināmnā caiva tāḥ sarvā gaṅgāḥ saptavidhāḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. There are seven rivers in each one of these mountains which fall into the sea and each one has a duplicate name; of which the Ganges is an exception, being sevenfold.

## \|\| 122.30 \|\|

*prathamā sukumārīti gaṅgā śivajalā śubhā \|*  
*munitaptā ca nāmnaiṣā nadī samparikīrtitā \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. First one is the Sukumari Ganges whose waters are clear and blessed.

It is also called the Munitapta.

## \|\| 122.31 \|\|

*sukumārī tapaḥsiddhā dvitīyā nāmataḥ satī \|*  
*nandā ca pāvanī caiva tṛtīyā parikīrtitā \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. The second one is called the Sukuméari-Tapsidh4 and Sati, the third one is the Nanda which is also known as Pavani.

## \|\| 122.32 \|\|

*śibikā ca caturthī syād dvividhā ca punaḥ smṛtā \|*  
*ikṣuśca pañcamī jñeyā tathaiva ca punaḥ kuhūḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. The fourth one is called the Shibika and Dvividha, the fifth one is known as Ikshu and Kuhu.

## \|\| 122.33 \|\|

*veṇukā cāmṛtā caiva ṣaṣṭhī samparikīrtitā \|*  
*sukṛtā ca gabhastī ca saptamī parikīrtitā \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. The sixth one is known as Venuka and Amrita and the seventh one is called the Sukrita and Gabhasti.

## \|\| 122.34 \|\|

*etāḥ sapta mahābhāgāḥ prativarṣaṃ śivodakāḥ \|*  
*bhāvayanti janaṃ sarvaṃ śākadvīpanivāsinam \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Of the above-mentioned seven rivers one flows in each sub-division of the Shakadvipa, and they all purify the people of those regions with their sacred waters.

## \|\| 122.35 \|\|

*abhigacchanti tāścānyā nadā nadyaḥ sarāṃsi ca \|*  
*bahūdakaparisrāvā yato varṣati vāsavaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. There are myriads of other rivers, and rivulets as well as Jakes, formed by copious supply of rain water let fall by Vasava (Indra) into these.

## \|\| 122.36-38 \|\|

*tāsāṃ tu nāmadheyāni parimāṇaṃ tathaiva ca \|*  
*na śakyaṃ parisaṃkhyātuṃ puṇyāstāḥ sariduttamāḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

*tāḥ pibanti sadā hṛṣṭā nadīrjanapadāstu te \|*  
*ete śāntabhayāḥ proktāḥ pramodā ye ca vai śivāḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

*ānandāśca sukhāścaiva kṣemakāśca navaiḥ saha \|*  
*varṇāśramācārautā deśāste sapta viśrutāḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

36-38. It is very difficult to enumerate and give proper measurements of all those rivers and rivulets. They are all sacred. The people of the janapadas who drink their waters get happiness. Shantabhaya, Pramada, Shiva, Ananda, Sukha, Kshemaka, and Nava; such are the seven janapadas situated there, where all the rules and customs (Achara) of Varna and Ashrama are observed.

## \|\| 122.39-40 \|\|

*ārogyā balinaścaiva sarve maraṇavarjitāḥ \|*  
*avasarpiṇī na teṣvasti tathaivotsarpiṇī punaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

*na tatrāsti ugāvasthā caturyugakṛtā kvacit \|*  
*tretāugasamaḥ kālas tathā tatra pravartate \|\| 40 \|\|*

39-40. The people are healthy, robust, and free from the clutches of death; neither are they prone to growth and decay. There the four ages do not prevail in succession. The age of Treta is eternal there.

## \|\| 122.41-44 \|\|

*śākadvīpādiṣu jñeyaṃ pañcasveteṣu sarvaśaḥ \|*  
*deśasya tu vicāreṇa kālaḥ svābhāvikaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

*na teṣu saṃkaraḥ kaścid varṇāśramakṛtaḥ kvacit \|*  
*dharmasya cāvyabhīcārād ekāntasukhinaḥ prajāḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

*na teṣu māyā lobho vā īrṣyāsūyā bhayaṃ kutaḥ \|*  
*viparyayo na teṣvasti tadvai svābhāvikaṃ smṛtam \|\| 43 \|\|*

*kālo naiva ca teṣvasti na daṇḍo na ca dāṇḍikaḥ \|*  
*svadharmeṇa ca dharmajñās te rakṣanti parasparam \|\| 44 \|\|*

41-44. Almost similar is the condition of age in the other five Dvipas, regard being had to the superiority and otherwise of the khandas. There is no confusion in the varnas there, and the people of that place are happy, as they seldom deviate from the path of virtue. There are no such things as fraud, greed, jealousy, fear and malicious fault finding. The country is free from vices and is truly natural. There is none to inflict punishment there, nor on whom punishment should be inflicted. The people being virtuous, get mutual protection from their own virtuous deeds.

## \|\| 122.45-46 \|\|

*parimaṇḍalastu sumahān dvīpo vai kuśasaṃjñakaḥ \|*  
*nadījalaiḥ parivṛtaḥ parvataścābhrasaṃnibhaiḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

*sarvadhātuvicitraiśca maṇividrumabhūṣitaiḥ \|*  
*anyaiśca vividhākārai ramyairjanapadaistathā \|\| 46 \|\|*

45-46. Kusha Dvipa.

The Kushadvipa is very great in circumference. It is full of rivers, lakes, and snow-clad mountains, in which are to be found various kinds of minerals, gems, trees and countries (janapadas).

## \|\| 122.47 \|\|

*vṛkṣaiḥ puṣpaphalopetaiḥ sarvato dhanadhānyavān \|*  
*nityaṃ puṣpaphalopetaḥ sarvaratnasamāvṛtaḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. The flowers, fruits, various varieties of trees, grains and wealth are in plenty there. The trees are always full of flowers and fruits: gems of every kind are there.

## \|\| 122.49 \|\|

*atha tṛtīyaṃ vakṣyāmi kuśadvīpaṃ ca kṛtsnaśaḥ \|*  
*kuśadvīpena kṣīrodaḥ sarvataḥ parivāritaḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. It is also full of domestic and wild animals. Now, hear, by degrees, a brief description of the Kusha Dvipa. I am going to give you an entire description of the third Varsha, — Kusha Dvipa. It is surrounded on all sides by the Kshirasamudra.

## \|\| 122.50 \|\|

*śākadvīpasya vistārād dviguṇena samanvitaḥ \|*  
*tatrāpi parvatāḥ sapta vijñeyā ratnayonayaḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. It is double, in its dimensions, of Shakadvipa and there are seven mountains containing various kinds of precious stones,

## \|\| 122.51 \|\|

*ratnākarāstathā nadyas teṣāṃ nāmāni me śṛṇu \|*  
*dvināmānaśca te sarve śākadvīpe yathā tathā \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. The number of rivers — the home of innumerable gems, — is also seven and the mountains have double names as in Shakadvipa, viz.

## \|\| 122.52 \|\|

*prathamaḥ sūryasaṃkāśaḥ kumudo nāma parvataḥ \|*  
*vidrumoccaya ityuktaḥ sa eva ca mahīdharaḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. The first is the Mount Kumuda, shining like the Sun and is also called the Vidrumochchaya.

## \|\| 122.53-55 \|\|

*sarvadhātumayaiḥ śṛṅgaiḥ śilājālasamanvitaiḥ \|*  
*dvitīyaḥ parvatastatra unnato nāma viśrutaḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

*hemaparvata ityuktaḥ sa eva ca mahīdharaḥ \|*  
*haritālamayaiḥ śṛṅgair dvīpamāvṛtya sarvaśaḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

*balāhakastṛtīyastu jātyañjanamayo giriḥ \|*  
*dyutimānnāmataḥ proktaḥ sa eva ca mahīdharaḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

53-55. The second mountain, containing all the metals and rocky peaks, is known as the Unnata or Hema and is covered with the yellow orpiment.

The third is the Valahaka or the Dyutiman, full of black pigment or antimony.

## \|\| 122.56-58 \|\|

*caturthaḥ parvato droṇo yatrauṣadhyo mahāgirau \|*  
*viśalyakaraṇī caiva mṛtasaṃjīvanī tathā \|\| 56 \|\|*

*puṣpavānnāma saivoktaḥ parvataḥ sumahācitaḥ \|*  
*kaṅkastu pañcamasteṣāṃ parvato nāma sāravān \|\| 57 \|\|*

*kuśeśaya iti proktaḥ punaḥ sa pṛthivīdharaḥ \|*  
*divyapuṣpaphalopeto divyavirutsamanvitaḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

56-58. The fourth is the Drona Mountain, also known as the Pushpavan, on the summit of which there are medicinal herbs efficacious in curing the wounds caused by the arrows Vishalyakarani), as well as the herbs that give new life (Mritasanjivani). The fifth one is the Kanka or the Kushaishaya Mountain. It is also full of choice herbs, fruits, flowers and creepers.

## \|\| 122.60-63 \|\|

*tasminso 'gnirnivasati mahiṣo nāma yo 'psujaḥ \|*  
*saptamaḥ parvatastatra kakudmānsa hi bhāṣate \|\| 60 \|\|*

*mandaraḥ saiva vijñeyaḥ sarvadhātumayaḥ śubhaḥ \|*  
*manda ityeṣa yo dhātur apāmarthe prakāśakaḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

*apāṃ vidāraṇāccaiva mandaraḥ sa nigadyate \|*  
*tatra ratnānyanekāni svayaṃ rakṣati vāsavaḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

*prajāpatimupādāya prajābhyo vidadhatsvayam \|*  
*teṣāmantaraviṣkambho dviguṇaḥ samudāhṛtaḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

60-63. The sixth one is the Mahisha or the Hari. It is black like the clouds; and Mahisha Agni (volcano?) begotten from the water (rising from the sea?) lives there (in the form of fire). And the seventh one is the Kukudmana also known as the Mandara. It is full of all kinds of minerals and precious stones, guarded by Indra Himself. The root ‘manda’ means water and since it scatters water, it is called Mandara, in company of Brahma, for the good of the people. The internal dimensions of these mountains are double.

## \|\| 122.64 \|\|

*ityete parvatāḥ sapta kuśadvīpe prabhāṣitāḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ varṣāṇi vakṣyāmi saptaiva tu vibhāgaśaḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. These are the seven mountains of Kushadvipa and now their subdivisions will be enumerated.

## \|\| 122.65-67 \|\|

*kumudasya smṛtaḥ śveta unnataśceva sa smṛtaḥ \|*  
*unnatasya tu vijñeyaṃ varṣaṃ lohitasaṃjñakam \|\| 65 \|\|*

*veṇumaṇḍalakaṃ caiva tathaiva parikīrtitam \|*  
*balāhakasya jīmūtaḥ svairathākāramityapi \|\| 66 \|\|*

*droṇasya harikaṃ nāma lavaṇaṃ ca punaḥ smṛtam \|*  
*kaṅkasyāpi kakun nāma dhṛtimaccaiva tatsmṛtam \|\| 67 \|\|*

65-67. Shvetadvipa is the name of the region where lies the Kumuda Mountain.

It is also known as Unnata. The second one is the Lohitakhanda also called the Venumandala, where lies the Unnata Mountain. Jimuta or Svairathakara is the khanda of the Valahvaka Mountain. Harika or Lavana is the khanda of the Drona Mountain. Kakuda or Dhritimat is the khanda of the Kanka Mountain.

## \|\| 122.68 \|\|

*mahiṣaṃ mahiṣasyāpi punaścāpi prabhākaram \|*  
*kakudminastu tadvarṣaṃ kapilaṃ nāma viśrutam \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. Mahisha or Prabhakara is the khanda of the Mahisha Mountain and Kakudmana or Kapila is the khanda of the Mountain Kakudman.

## \|\| 122.69 \|\|

*etānyapi viśiṣṭāni sapta sapta pṛthakpṛthak \|*  
*varṣāṇi parvatāścaiva nadīsteṣu nibodhata \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. Thus in every dvipa there are seven khadnas with an equal number of rivers and mountains.

## \|\| 122.70-76 \|\|

*tatrāpi nadyaḥ saptaiva prativarṣaṃ hi tāḥ smṛtāḥ \|*  
*dvināmavatyastāḥ sarvāḥ sarvāḥ puṇyajalāḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

*dhūtapāpā nadī nāma yoniścaiva punaḥ smṛtā \|*  
*sītā dvitīyā vijñeyā sā caiva hi niśā smṛtā \|\| 71 \|\|*

*pavitrā tṛtīyā vijñeyā vitṛṣṇāpi ca yā punaḥ \|*  
*caturthī hlādinītyuktā candrabhā iti ca smṛtā \|\| 72 \|\|*

*vidyucca pañcamī proktā śuklā caiva vibhāvyate \|*  
*puṇḍrā ṣaṣṭhī tu vijñeyā punaścaiva vibhāvarī \|\| 73 \|\|*

*mahatī saptamī proktā punaścaiṣā dhṛtiḥ smṛtā \|*  
*anyāstābhyo 'pi saṃjātāḥ śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

*abhigacchanti tā nadyo yato varṣati vāsavaḥ \|*  
*ityeṣa saṃniveśo vaḥ kuśadvīpasya varṇitaḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

*śākadvīpena vistāraḥ proktastasya sanātanaḥ \|*  
*kuśadvīpaḥ samudreṇa ghṛtamaṇḍodakena ca \|\| 76 \|\|*

70-76. There are seven rivers in each khanda. Their waters are pure and sacred and each one has a duplicate name. The first one is Dhutapapa which is also known as Yoni, Sita or Nisha is the second. The third one is Pavitra also called Vitrishna. The fourth one is Hladini or Chandrama.

The fifth one is Vidyuta or Shukla, the sixth one is Pundra or Vibhavasi.

The seventh one is Mahati also called Dhriti. There are thousands of their branches that run where Indra pours down rains. Thus I have described the Kusha Dvipa. Its measurement has been described while describing the measurement of Shakadvipa. It is surrounded by the Ghrita Manda Samudra.

## \|\| 122.77 \|\|

*sarvataḥ sumahāndvīpaś candravatpariveṣṭitaḥ \|*  
*vistārānmaṇḍalāccaiva kṣīrodāddviguṇo mataḥ \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. This huge dvipa, thus surrounded, looks like the moon and is twice as great as the Kshara Samudra in its magnitude.

## \|\| 122.78 \|\|

*tataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi krauñcadvīpaṃ yathā tathā \|*  
*kuśadvīpasya vistārād dviguṇastasya vistaraḥ \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. Krauncha Dvipa.

Now I shall speak of the Kraunchadvipa which is double the size of Kushadvipa.

## \|\| 122.79 \|\|

*ghṛtodakaḥ samudro vai krauñcadvīpena saṃvṛtaḥ \|*  
*cakranemipramāṇena vṛto vṛttena sarvaśaḥ \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. It surrounds the Ghritoda sea like the tyre of a wheel.

## \|\| 122.80 \|\|

*tasmindvīpe nagāḥ śreṣṭhā devano girirucyate \|*  
*devanātparataścāpi govindo nāma parvataḥ \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. The people of this Dvipa are of a superior class. Devana is the first mountain beyond which stands the Govinda.

## \|\| 122.81 \|\|

*govindātparataścāpi krauñcastu prathamo giriḥ \|*  
*krauñcātpare pāvanakaḥ pāvanādandhakārakaḥ \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. Further on, from Govinda is the beautiful Krauncha Mountain, after which is the Pavanaka and beyond it is the Andhakaraka.

## \|\| 122.82-83 \|\|

*andhakārātpare cāpi devāvṛn nāma parvataḥ \|*  
*devāvṛtaḥ pareṇāpi puṇḍarīko mahāngiriḥ \|\| 82 \|\|*

*ete ratnamayāḥ sapta krauñcadvīpasya parvatāḥ \|*  
*parasparasya dviguṇo viṣkambho varṣaparvataḥ \|\| 83 \|\|*

82-83. Next to Andhakaraka is the Devavrita Mountain, after which comes the mighty Pundarika. All these seven mountains of the Krauncha Dvipa are full of gems, each being twice the size of that preceding it.

## \|\| 122.84-86 \|\|

*varṣāṇi tasya vakṣyāmi nāmatastu nibodhata \|*  
*krauñcasya kuśalo deśo vāmanasya manonugaḥ \|\| 84 \|\|*

*manonugātpare coṣṇās tṛtīyo 'pi sa ucyate \|*  
*uṣṇātpare pāvanakaḥ pāvanādandhakārakaḥ \|\| 85 \|\|*

*andhakārakadeśāttu munideśastathā paraḥ \|*  
*munideśātpare cāpi procyate dundubhisvanaḥ \|\| 86 \|\|*

84-86. The sub-divisions of that dvipa are, wiz. — Kushala, Manonuga Vamana, Ushna, Pavanaka, Andhakdraka, Munidesha and Dundubhisvana.

## \|\| 122.87 \|\|

*siddhacāraṇasaṃkīrṇo gauraprāyaḥ śucirjanaḥ \|*  
*śrutāstatraiva nadyastu prativarṣaṃ gatāḥ śubhāḥ \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. Dundubhisvana Khanda is full of fair complexioned men, and peopled by holy persons, and siddhas and charanas. There is a sacred river in each khanda.

## \|\| 122.88 \|\|

*gaurī kumudvatī caiva saṃdhyā rātrirmanojavā \|*  
*khyātī ca puṇḍarīkā ca gaṅgā saptavidhā smṛtā \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. They are: — Gauri, Kumudvati, Sandhya, Ratri, Manojava, Khyati, Pundarika. They are known as the seven Ganges.

## \|\| 122.89-90 \|\|

*tāsāṃ sahasraśaścānyā nadyaḥ pārśvasamīpagāḥ \|*  
*abhigacchanti tā nadyo bahulāśca bahūdakāḥ \|\| 89 \|\|*

*teṣāṃ nisargo deśānām ānupūrvyeṇa sarvaśaḥ \|*  
*na śakyo vistarādvaktum api varṣaśatairapi \|\| 90 \|\|*

89-90. Thousands of rivers arising out of them flow close by. All of them are very deep. Nobody, even in course of centuries, would be able to describe fully all the countries through which these rivers pass, with the rise, growth and decay of the people inhabiting them.

## \|\| 122.91-92 \|\|

*sargo yaśca prajānāṃ tu saṃhāro yaśca teṣu vai \|*  
*ata ūrdhvaṃ pravakṣyāmi śālmalasya nibodhata \|\| 91 \|\|*

*śālmalo dviguṇo dvīpaḥ krauñcadvīpasya vistarāt \|*  
*parivārya samudraṃ tu dadhimaṇḍodakaṃ sthitaḥ \|\| 92 \|\|*

91-92. I shall now describe to you the Shalmaladvipa, which is double the size of Krauncha, and is surrounded by the Dadhi Ocean.

## \|\| 122.93 \|\|

*tatra puṇyā janapadāś cirācca mriyate janaḥ \|*  
*kuta eva tu durbhikṣaṃ kṣamātejoyutā hi te \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. Shalmala Dvipa.

The people residing in the sacred janapadas of that region are very long-lived. There are no visitations of famine there, and the inhabitants of that place are very forbearing, merciful, and illustrious.

## \|\| 122.93-99 \|\|

*tatra puṇyā janapadāś cirācca mriyate janaḥ \|*  
*kuta eva tu durbhikṣaṃ kṣamātejoyutā hi te \|\| 93 \|\|*

*prathamaḥ sūryasaṃkāśaḥ sumanā nāma parvataḥ \|*  
*pītastu madhyamaścāsīt tataḥ kumbhamayo giriḥ \|\| 94 \|\|*

*nāmnā sarvasukho nāma divyauṣadhisamanvitaḥ \|*  
*tṛtīyaścaiva sauvarṇo bhṛṅgapattranibho giriḥ \|\| 95 \|\|*

*sumahānrohito nāma divyo girivaro hi saḥ \|*  
*sumanāḥ kuśalo deśaḥ sukhodarkaḥ sukhodayaḥ \|\| 96 \|\|*

*rohito yastṛtīyastu rohiṇo nāma viśrutaḥ \|*  
*tatra ratnānyanekāni svayaṃ rakṣati vāsavaḥ \|\| 97 \|\|*

*prajāpatimupādāya prasanno vidadhatsvayam \|*  
*na tatra meghā varṣanti śītoṣṇaṃ ca na tadvidham \|\| 98 \|\|*

*varṇāśramāṇāṃ vārttā vā triṣu dvīpeṣu vidyate \|*  
*na graho na ca candro 'sti īrṣyāsūyā bhayaṃ tathā \|\| 99 \|\|*

93-99. The following are the mountains of that region: — The Sumana, shining like the sun, and of yellow colour. Kumbhamaya, the central one is also called Sarvasukha. It is full of herbs. The third is the great Rohita, of red hue (like that of Bhringa patra) and full of gold. The Kushala is the Varsha of the Sumana Mountain, while Sukhodoya is that of Kumbhamaya and Rohina of the Rohita Mountain, the precious stones of which are under the direct watch and ward of Indra, who, with Prajapati, gladly performs his duty there. Clouds do not rain there, there is neither summer nor winter. There is no prevalence of the Varna or Ashrama in those regions. No stars, planets or the moon shine there, nor is there any such thing as jealousy, hatred or fear.

## \|\| 122.100 \|\|

*udbhidānyudakānyatra giriprasravaṇāni ca \|*  
*bhojanaṃ ṣaḍrasaṃ tatra teṣāṃ svayamupasthitam \|\| 100 \|\|*

100\. There are fountains in the mountains, other sources of water, as well as the vegetable world. The people of this region obtain the best victuals of all the six flavors, without making any efforts on their part.

## \|\| 122.101-104 \|\|

*adhamottamaṃ na teṣvasti na lobho na parigrahaḥ \|*  
*ārogyabalavantaśca ekāntasukhino narāḥ \|\| 101 \|\|*

*triṃśadvarṣasahasrāṇi mānasīṃ siddhimāsthitāḥ \|*  
*sukhamāuśca rūpaṃ ca dharmaiśvaryaṃ tathaiva ca \|\| 102 \|\|*

*śālmalānteṣu vijñeyaṃ dvīpeṣu triṣu sarvataḥ \|*  
*vyākhyātaḥ śālmalāntānāṃ dvīpānāṃ tu vidhiḥ śubhaḥ \|\| 103 \|\|*

*parimaṇḍalastu dvīpasya cakravatpariveṣṭitaḥ \|*  
*surodena samudreṇa dviguṇena samanvitaḥ \|\| 104 \|\|*

101-104. The people there are all of equal rank, neither high nor low; they are not greedy; nor do they store things. They are all healthy, powerful and happy, attaining all siddhis of the mind, for a period of 30,000 years. The next three Dvipas enjoy the same happiness, life, beauty, virtue and prosperity. Thus I have described all the sacred Dvipas up to Shalmala (i.e., five). The Shalmaladvipa is encircled by the Sura Ocean, which is twice its size.

## Chapter 123

## \|\| 123.1-2 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*gomedakaṃ pravakṣyāmi ṣaṣṭhaṃ dvīpaṃ tapodhanāḥ \|*  
*surodakasamudrastu gomedena samāvṛtaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*śālmalasya tu vistārād dviguṇastasya vistaraḥ \|*  
*tasmindvīpe tu vijñeyau parvatau dvau samāhitau \|\| 2 \|\|*

1-2. Suta said: — Rishis! Now hear about the sixth dvipa, known as the Gomeda. It surrounds the Surodaka Ocean. Its size is double that of the Shalmaladvipa. It has two beautiful mountains

## \|\| 123.3-7 \|\|

*prathamaḥ sumanā nāma jātyañjanamayo giriḥ \|*  
*dvitīyaḥ kumudo nāma sarvauṣadhisamanvitaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*śātakaumbhamayaḥ śrīmān vijñeyaḥ sumahācitaḥ \|*  
*samudrekṣurasodena vṛto gomedakaśca saḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*ṣaṣṭhena tu samudreṇa surodāddviguṇena ca \|*  
*dhātakīkumudaścaiva havyaputrau suvistṛtau \|\| 5 \|\|*

*saumanaṃ prathamaṃ varṣaṃ dhātakīkhaṇḍamucyate \|*  
*dhātakinaḥ smṛtaṃ tadvai prathamaṃ prathamasya tu \|\| 6 \|\|*

*gomedaṃ yatsmṛtaṃ varṣaṃ nāmnā sarvasukhaṃ tu tat \|*  
*kumudasya dvitīyasya dvitīyaṃ kumudaṃ tataḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

3-7. The first one is Samana, full of antimony (Anjana), and the second one is the Kamada, full of all kinds of herbs. It is very lofty and full of gold. The Gomedadvipa is surrounded by the sixth ocean, Ikshurasoda, which is double the size of the Suroda Ocean. The Mountains Dhataki (or Sumana) and Kumuda are the sons of Havya. They are of vast dimensions. The first sub-division is Saumana, also known as Dhataki Khanda, after Dhataki, the first mountain. Gomeda Khanda is also called Sarvasukha. The Khanda of the Kumuda Mountain is called under the same name — Kumuda.

## \|\| 123.8-9 \|\|

*etau dvau parvatau vṛttau śeṣau sarvasamucchritau \|*  
*pūrveṇa tasya dvīpasya sumanāḥ parvataḥ sthitaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*prākpaścimāyataiḥ pādair āsamudrāditi sthitaḥ \|*  
*paścārdhe kumudastasya evameva sthitastu vai \|\| 9 \|\|*

8-9. Both the mountains are round in shape, spreading from.one end to the other, and are very lofty. To the east of the dvipa, stands the Mount Sumana, while Mount Kumuda is on the west; both extending to the sea by means of offshoots, stretching from the east to the west.

## \|\| 123.10-11 \|\|

*etaiḥ parvatapādaistu sa deśo vai dvidhākṛtaḥ \|*  
*dakṣiṇārdhaṃ tu dvīpasya dhātakīkhaṇḍamucyate \|\| 10 \|\|*

*kumudaṃ tūttare tasya dvitīyaṃ varṣamuttamam \|*  
*etau janapadau dvau tu gomedasya tu vistṛtau \|\| 11 \|\|*

10-11. That region is divided into two parts by the feet of these mountains. Half of the southern portion is known as the Dhataki Khanda, while the northern half is called the Kumuda Khanda. Both these countries (janapadas) belong to the Gomedadvipa, and they are of gigantic dimensions.

## \|\| 123.12-23 \|\|

*ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi saptamaṃ dvīpamuttamam \|*  
*samudrekṣurasaṃ caiva gomedāddviguṇaṃ hi saḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*āvṛtya tiṣṭhati dvīpaḥ puṣkaraḥ puṣkarairvṛtaḥ \|*  
*puṣkareṇa vṛtaḥ śrīmāṃś citrasānumahāgiriḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*kūṭaiścitrairmaṇimayaiḥ śilājālasamudbhavaiḥ \|*  
*dvīpasyaiva tu pūrvārdhe citrasānuḥ sthito mahān \|\| 14 \|\|*

*parimaṇḍalasahasrāṇi vistīrṇaḥ saptaviṃśatiḥ \|*  
*ūrdhvaṃ sa vai caturviṃśad-yojanānāṃ mahābalaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*dvīpārdhasya parikṣiptaḥ paścime mānaso giriḥ \|*  
*sthito velāsamīpe tu pūrvacandra ivoditaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*yojanānāṃ sahasrāṇi sārdhaṃ pañcāśaducchritaḥ \|*  
*tasya putro mahāvītaḥ paścimārdhasya rakṣitā \|\| 17 \|\|*

*pūrvārdhe parvatasyāpi dvidhā deśastu sa smṛtaḥ \|*  
*svādūdakenodadhinā puṣkaraḥ parivāritaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*vistārānmaṇḍalāccaiva gomedāddviguṇena tu \|*  
*triṃśadvarṣasahasrāṇi teṣu jīvanti mānavāḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

*viparyayo na teṣvasti etatsvābhāvikaṃ smṛtam \|*  
*ārogyaṃ sukhabāhulyaṃ mānasīṃ siddhimāsthitāḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*sukhamāuśca rūpaṃ ca triṣu dvīpeṣu sarvaśaḥ \|*  
*adhamottamau na teṣvāstāṃ tulyāste vīryarūpataḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*na tatra vadhyavadhakau nerṣyāsūyā bhayaṃ tathā \|*  
*na lobho na ca dambho vā na ca dveṣaḥ parigrahaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*satyānṛte na teṣvāstāṃ dharmādharmau tathaiva ca \|*  
*varṇāśramāṇāṃ vārttā ca pāśupālyaṃ vaṇikkṛṣiḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

12-23 Pushkara Dvipa.

I shall now speak of the seventh dvipa, the Great Pushkara, which surrounds the Ikshurasoda Sea, which is double of Gomeda. It is itself surrounded by the Pushkaras (lakes or lotuses?), Chitras4nu is the chief mountain, and it is full of lotuses and adorned with the rocks of wonderful gems. The Mount Chitrasanu stands on the eastern half. -Its circumference is 27,000 yojanas, and height is 24,000 yojanas.
