29-30. Hearing those words the Messenger returned and Tarakasura began to ponder. He said to himself: “Indra would not say so without having got support of some powerful ally, for I have several times subdued him in war. We have conquered him thoroughly; now all on a sudden how has he got another’s protection?”

## \|\| 159.31-39 \|\|

*pāṃśuvarṣamasṛkpātaṃ gaganādavanītale \|*  
*bhujanetraprakampaṃ ca vaktraśoṣamanobhramam \|\| 31 \|\|*

*svakāntāvaktrapadmānāṃ mlānatāṃ ca vyalokayat \|*  
*duṣṭāṃśca prāṇino raudrān so 'paṣyadduṣṭavedinaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

*tadacintvaiva ditijo nyastacinto 'bhavatkṣaṇāt \|*  
*yāvadgajaghaṭāghaṇṭā-raṇatkāraravotkaṭām \|\| 33 \|\|*

*tadvatturagasaṃghāta-kṣuṇṇabhūreṇupiñjarām \|*  
*cañcalasyandanodagra-dhvajarājivirājitām \|\| 34 \|\|*

*vimānaiścādbhutākāraiś calitāmaracāmaraiḥ \|*  
*tāṃ bhūṣaṇanibaddhāṃ ca kiṃnarodgatināditām \|\| 35 \|\|*

*nānānākatarūtphulla-kusumāpīḍadhāriṇīm \|*  
*vikośāstrapariṣkārāṃ varmanirmaladarśanām \|\| 36 \|\|*

*bandyudghuṣṭastutiravāṃ nānāvādyanināditām \|*  
*senāṃ nākasadāṃ daityaḥ prāsādastho vyalokayat \|\| 37 \|\|*

*cintayāmāsa sa tadā kiṃcidudbhrāntamānasaḥ \|*  
*apūrvaḥ ko bhavedyoddhā yo mayā na vinirjitaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

*tataścintākulo daityaḥ śuśrāva kaṭukākṣaram \|*  
*siddhabandibhirudghuṣṭam idaṃ hṛdayadāraṇam \|\| 39 \|\|*

31-39. Afterwards, the vicious minded Tarakasura experienced the following inauspicious signs. He saw the shower of dust, the fall of blood from the sky, felt the throbbing of the left eye, the drying up of the mouth, delusion of mind, the turning dull of the lotus faces of the ladies, the ferocious beings making inauspicious sounds. Afterwards, he saw the army of the Devas advancing in chariots with tinkling bells, streaming with lofty banners and fly flaps, having a multitude of singing Kinnaras in its force, with the warriors wearing garlands of celestial flowers, armour and weapons, playing on various kinds of music- He saw the armies getting dusky-coloured on account of the dust rising from the hoofs of the marching horses. The banners were flying on their running chariots. The wonderful chariots and chamaras over them were looking brilliant. The bards were singing praises of the Devas. He saw that army from the terrace of his mansion and anxiously said to himself: “Who can be such an extraordinary warrior whom I did not subdue in war previously.” Afterwards, the demon king heard the following sharp words uttered from the mouths of the bards.

## \|\| 159.40-43 \|\|

*atha gāthā*  
*jayātulaśaktidīdhitipiñjara bhujadaṇḍacaṇḍaraṇarabhasa \|*  
*suravadana kumudakānana-vikāsanendo kumāra jaya ditijakulamahodadhivaḍavānala \|\| 40 \|\|*

*ṣaṇmukha madhuraravamayūraratha suramukuṭakoṭighaṭṭitacaraṇanakhāṅkuramahāsana \|*  
*jaya lalitacūḍākalāpanavavimaladalakamalakānta daityavaṃśaduḥsahadāvānala \|\| 41 \|\|*

*jaya viśākha vibho jaya sakalalokatāraka jaya devasenānāyaka \|*  
*skanda jaya gaurīnandana ghaṇṭāpriya priya viśākha vibho dhṛtapatākaprakīrṇapaṭala \|*  
*kanakabhūṣaṇa bhāsuradinakaracchāya \|\| 42 \|\|*

*jaya janitasaṃbhrama līlālūnākhilārāte jaya sakalalokatāraka ditijāsuravaratārakāntaka \|*  
*skanda jaya bāla saptavāsara jaya bhuvanāvaliśokavināśana \|\| 43 \|\|*

40-43. He heard the bards of the Devas saying “O Kumara! You are shining with the lustre of unequalled prowess. By Your mighty valour you are well-skilled in the arts of warfare, victory to You! You are pleasing like the Moon, the Destroyer of the demons like the fire! Victory to You! O Rider of the chariot drawn by a peacock. Svamikartika! the fingernails of Your feet are being rubbed, by the coronets of the kotis and kotis of Devas, victory to You. You are the lord of the pure groups of the lotus-like heads of the Devas; It is You only who are the unbearable conflagration fire destroying the whole family of the demons, victory to You. O Vishakha! O Lord! The Redeemer of all the realms, may You be victorious. O Skanda! O son of Gauri, Vibhu, wearer of golden ornaments, conquer. You are the only one who can uproot the enemies by Your mere sport. May you conquer. Skanda! Bala, seven days old, the Dispeller of the grief of the three realms, conquer. You are the destroyer of Tarakasura, the Lord of the demons, conquer. You are the Destroyer of the sorrows of the world! may you conquer in every way.”

## Chapter 160

## \|\| 160.1-2 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*śrutvaitattārakaḥ sarvam udghuṣṭaṃ devabandibhiḥ \|*  
*sasmāra brahmaṇo vākyaṃ vadhaṃ bālādupasthitam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*smṛtvā gharmārdrasarvāṅgaḥ padātirapadānugaḥ \|*  
*mandirānnirjagāmāśu śokagrastena cetasā \|\| 2 \|\|*

1-2. Suta said: — Hearing that Tarakasura remembered the words of Brahma that he would be killed by a child. With his army he mournfully set out on foot without any coat of armour to meet the foe when Kalanemi, and others also came to him.

## \|\| 160.3 \|\|

*kālanemimukhā daityāḥ saṃrambhādbhrāntacetasaḥ \|*  
*sve sve svanīkeṣu tadā tvarāvismitacetasaḥ \|*  
*yodhā dhāvata gṛhīta yojayadhvaṃ varūthinīm \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Taraka said: O Kalanemi and other Daityas! why are you confounded. Take up your arms; collect your army and rush on the foe

## \|\| 160.4-5 \|\|

*kumāraṃ tārako dṛṣṭvā babhāṣe bhīṣaṇākṛtiḥ \|*  
*kiṃ bāla yoddhukāmo 'si krīḍa kandukalīlayā \|\| 4 \|\|*

*tvayā na dānavā dṛṣṭā yatsaṅgaravibhīṣakāḥ \|*  
*bālatvādatha te buddhir evaṃ svalpārthadarśinī \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. Seeing Svamikartika, the terrible Tarkasura said “Child! do you wish to fight? You ought to play with a hall. You have never seen ferocious demons. Is your understanding so limited on account of your infancy?”

## \|\| 160.6-8 \|\|

*kumāro 'pi tamagrasthaṃ babhāṣe harṣayansurān \|*  
*śṛṇu tāraka śāstrārthas tava caiva nirūpyate \|\| 6 \|\|*

*śāstrairarthā na dṛṣyante samare nirbhayairbhaṭaiḥ \|*  
*śiśutvaṃ māvamaṃsthā me śiśuḥ kālabhujaṃgamaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*duṣprekṣyo bhāskaro bālas tathāhaṃ durjayaḥ śiśuḥ \|*  
*alpākṣaro na mantraḥ kiṃ susphuro daitya dṛṣyate \|\| 8 \|\|*

6-8. Hearing those words, that Kumara also said words which were gratifying to the Devas: — “Tarakasura! now hear the meaning of the Shastras. During war time, the learned do not understand the real meaning of the writings of the scriptures. You should not look down on Me, as a mere child. A cobra may be a very young, one; see the Sun, though he may be small yet cannot be looked at. O Demon! have you not seen how a mantra of very few syllables contains wonderful force?”

## \|\| 160.9 \|\|

*kumāre proktavatyevaṃ daityaścikṣepa mudgaram \|*  
*kumārastaṃ nirasyātha vajreṇāmoghavarcasā \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. After the Kumara had said so, the demon hurled his club at Him which He destroyed by His unfailing Vajra.

## \|\| 160.10-13 \|\|

*tataścikṣepa daityendro bhindipālamayomayam \|*  
*kareṇa tacca jagrāha kārtikeyo 'marārihā \|\| 10 \|\|*

*gadāṃ mumoca daityāya ṣaṇmukhaḥ paramasvanām \|*  
*tayā hatastato daityaś cakampe 'calarāḍiva \|\| 11 \|\|*

*mene ca durjayaṃ daityas tadā ṣaḍvadanaṃ raṇe \|*  
*cintayāmāsa buddhyā vai prāptaḥ kālo na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*kupitaṃ tu tamālokya kālanemipurogamāḥ \|*  
*sarve daityeśvarā jaghnuḥ kumāraṃ raṇadāruṇam \|\| 13 \|\|*

10-13. Afterwards, the demon adjusting a ball of iron to his javelin flung it at Svamikartika which He caught by His hand and hit Tarakasura with His awful club by the blow of which the demon began to shiver and he said to himself that the Kumara was unconquerable and that his end was come. At that time Kalanemi and other demons seeing the rage of Svamikartika began to shower their weapons on Him.

## \|\| 160.14-20 \|\|

*sa taiḥ prahārairaspṛṣṭo vṛthākleśairmahādyutiḥ \|*  
*raṇaśauṇḍāstu daityendrāḥ punaḥ prāsaiḥ śilīmukhaiḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*kumāraṃ sāmaraṃ jaghnur balino devakaṇṭakāḥ \|*  
*kumārasya vyathā nābhūd daityāstranihatasya tu \|\| 15 \|\|*

*prāṇāntakaraṇo jāto devānāṃ dānavāhavaḥ \|*  
*devānnipīḍitāndṛṣṭvā kumāraḥ kopamāviśat \|\| 16 \|\|*

*tato 'strairvārayāmāsa dānavānāmanīkinīm \|*  
*tatastair niṣpratīkarais tāḍitāḥ surakaṇṭakāḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*kālanemimukhāḥ sarve raṇādāsanparāṅmukhāḥ \|*  
*vidruteṣvatha daityeṣu hateṣu ca samantataḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*tataḥ kruddho mahādaityas tārako 'suranāyakaḥ \|*  
*jagrāha ca gadāṃ divyāṃ hemajālapariṣkṛtām \|\| 19 \|\|*

*jaghne kumāraṃ gadayā niṣṭaptakanakāṅgadaḥ \|*  
*śarairmayūrapatraiśca cakāra vimukhānsurān \|\| 20 \|\|*

14-20. Those blows did not, in the least, affect Svamikartika; and all became futile. Then the chief demons all clever in warfare began to strike Prasa and Shilimukha weapons on Kumara. Kumara, though struck, did not feel any pain. That battle destroyed many Devas when Svamikartika seeing them in distress angrily took up His arms and began to cause disaster to the demons which made Kalanemi and others turn their backs on the battlefield. Many ' demons were killed and many fled. At that instant, Tarakasura seeing what was happening, turned up with a club decorated with the network of gold; and violently struck Svamikartika with it; His peacock struck by this, fled away.

## \|\| 160.21-25 \|\|

*tathā parairmahābhallair mayūraṃ guhavāhanam \|*  
*bibheda tārakaḥ kruddhaḥ sa sainye 'suranāyakaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*dṛṣṭvā parāṅmukhāndevān muktaraktaṃ svavāhanam \|*  
*jagrāha śaktiṃ vimalāṃ raṇe kanakabhūṣaṇām \|\| 22 \|\|*

*bāhunā hemakeyūra-rucireṇa ṣaḍānanaḥ \|*  
*tato javānmahāsenas tārakaṃ dānavādhipam \|\| 23 \|\|*

*tiṣṭha tiṣṭha sudurbuddhe jīvalokaṃ vilokaya \|*  
*hato 'syadya mayā śaktyā smara śastraṃ suśikṣitam \|\| 24 \|\|*

*ityuktvā ca tataḥ śaktiṃ mumoca ditijaṃ prati \|*  
*sā kumārabhujotsṛṣṭā tatkeyūraravānugā \|*  
*bibheda daityahṛdayaṃ vajraśailendrakarkaśam \|\| 25 \|\|*

21-25. Svamikartika seeing His peacock flying away and vomiting blood turned on the battlefield, rushed at Tarakasura, holding a Shakti javelin in His hand adorned with a bracelet and shining like gold, said “O wicked one! stop, stop. See this weapon and today count yourself among the dead. If you know of any better weapon, think of it now.” Saying so, He threw His Shakti which, making a jingling sound, rent open the rough heart of the demon who fell down like a mountain blasted by thunderbolt,

## \|\| 160.26-28 \|\|

*gatāsuḥ sa papātorvyāṃ pralaye bhūdharo yathā \|*  
*vikīrṇamukuṭoṣṇīṣo visrastākhilabhūṣaṇaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*tasminvinihate daitye tridaśānāṃ mahotsave \|*  
*nābhūt kaścit tadā duḥkhī narakeṣvapi pāpakṛt \|\| 27 \|\|*

*stuvantaḥ ṣaṇmukhaṃ devāḥ krīḍantaścāṅganāutāḥ \|*  
*jagmuḥ svāneva bhavanān bhūridhāmāna utsukāḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

26-28. The coronet fell down from the head of the dead demon, his turban was scattered and all the ornaments were strewn. The Devas were jubilant to see the fall of such a formidable demon. At that time no one, not even one in the hell, became sorry. The Devas were entirely free from sufferings. The Devas along with Their consorts prayed to Svamikartika and returned to Their regions after showering blessings on Him.

## \|\| 160.29-33 \|\|

*daduścāpi varaṃ sarve devāḥ skandamukhaṃ prati \|*  
*tuṣṭāḥ samprāptasarvecchāḥ saha siddhaistapodhanaiḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*devā ūcuḥ*  
*yaḥ paṭhetskandasambaddhāṃ kathāṃ martyo mahāmatiḥ \|*  
*śṛṇuyācchrāvayedvāpi sa bhavetkīrtimānnaraḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

*bahvāuḥ subhagaḥ śrīmān kāntimāñchubhadarśanaḥ \|*  
*bhūtebhyo nirbhayaścāpi sarvaduḥkhavivarjitaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

*saṃdhyāmupāsya yaḥ pūrvāṃ skandasya caritaṃ paṭhet \|*  
*sa muktaḥ kilbiṣaiḥ sarvair mahādhanapatirbhavet \|\| 32 \|\|*

*bālānāṃ vyādhijuṣṭānāṃ rājadvāraṃ ca sevatām \|*  
*idaṃ tatparamaṃ divyaṃ sarvadā sarvakāmadam \|*  
*tanukṣaye ca sāujyaṃ ṣaṇmukhasya vrajennaraḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

29-33. The Devas then said with glee “The wise who would read or listen to this narration relating to Svamikartika will be illustrious, long-lived, prosperous and handsome. Besides this, they will have no fear from any one and will be void of suffering. One who will read this after his morning sandhya will be liberated from all his sins and become exceedingly rich. The recitation of this is specially beneficial to the young one suffering pain and to one connected with state craft. This narration yields to all the fruits of their desires. Such devotees at the end are corporally united for ever with Svamikartika.”

## Chapter 161

## \|\| 161.1 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ*  
*idānīṃ śrotumicchāmo hiraṇyakaśiporvadham \|*  
*narasiṃhasya māhātmyaṃ tathā pāpavināśanam \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. The Rishis said: — “O Suta! we now wish to hear about, the destruction of the demon Hiranyaka4yapu and also the glory of Narasimha (Avatara) which is the dispeller of great sins.”

## \|\| 161.2-4 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*purā kṛtauge viprā hiraṇyakaśipuḥ prabhuḥ \|*  
*daityānāmādipuruṣaś cakāra sa mahattapaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*daśa varṣasahasrāṇi daśa varṣaśatāni ca \|*  
*jalavāsī samabhavat snānamaunadhṛtavrataḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*tataḥ śamadamābhyāṃ ca brahmacaryeṇa caiva hi \|*  
*brahmā prīto 'bhavattasya tapasā niyamena ca \|\| 4 \|\|*

2-4. Suta said O Brahmanas! The demon Hiranyakashyapu was the most ancient progenitor of the Daityas daring the Satyayuga (the golden age). He practised severe austerities for 11,000 years, taking his bath regularly and then plunging himself in water neck-deep and observed the vow of silence. He led a life of continence restraining and controlling his passions and was very humble. Brahma was highly pleased with his devotion.

## \|\| 161.5-9 \|\|

*tataḥ svayaṃbhūrbhagavān svayamāgamya tatra ha \|*  
*vimānenārkavarṇena haṃsauktena bhāsvatā \|\| 5 \|\|*

*ādityairvasubhiḥ sādhyair marudbhirdaivataistathā \|*  
*rudrairviśvasahāyaiśca yakṣarākṣasapannagaiḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*digbhiś caiva vidigbhiś ca nadībhiḥ sāgaraistathā \|*  
*nakṣatraiśca muhūrtaiśca khecaraiśca mahāgrahaiḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*devairbrahmarṣibhiḥ sārdhaṃ siddhaiḥ saptarṣibhistathā \|*  
*rājarṣibhiḥ puṇyakṛdbhir gandharvāpsarasāṃ gaṇaiḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*carācaraguruḥ śrīmān vṛtaḥ sarvairdivaukasaiḥ \|*  
*brahmā brahmavidāṃ śreṣṭho daityaṃ vacanamabravīt \|\| 9 \|\|*

5-9. Riding on His white swan illustrious like the sun and followed by twelve Adityas, Vasus, Sadhyas, Siddhas, Maruts, Rudras, Yakshas, Rakshasas, Demons, Serpents, Directions, Vidishas, Rivers, Oceans, Stars, Muhurtas, Planets, Devas, seven Rishis, Brahmarishis, Rajarishis, Gandharvas, Nymphs, Brahma, the Lord of the universe, went there and addressed the demon:

## \|\| 161.10 \|\|

*prīto 'smi tava bhaktasya tapasānena suvrata \|*  
*varaṃ varaya bhadraṃ te yatheṣṭaṃ kāmamāpnuhi \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. “O Suvrata! I am pleased with your asceticism and you may ask for a boon that may suit your wish. You shall attain all your desires through My kindness.”

## \|\| 161.11-15 \|\|

*hiraṇyakaśipuruvāca*  
*na devāsuragandharvā na yakṣoragarākṣasāḥ \|*  
*na mānuṣāḥ piśācā vā hanyurmāṃ devasattama \|\| 11 \|\|*

*ṛṣayo vā na māṃ śāpaiḥ śapeuḥ prapitāmaha \|*  
*yadi me bhagavānprīto vara eṣa vṛto mayā \|\| 12 \|\|*

*na cāstreṇa na śastreṇa giriṇā pādapena ca \|*  
*na śuṣkeṇa na cārdreṇa na divā na niśātha vā \|\| 13 \|\|*

*bhaveyamahamevārkaḥ somo vāurhutāśanaḥ \|*  
*salilaṃ cāntarikṣaṃ ca nakṣatrāṇi diśo daśa \|\| 14 \|\|*

*ahaṃ krodhaśca kāmaśca varuṇo vāsavo yamaḥ \|*  
*dhanadaśca dhanādhyakṣo yakṣaḥ kiṃpuruṣādhipaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

11-15. Hiranyakashyapu spoke: — O best of the Devas! Make me invulnerable from the Devas, demons, Gandharvas, Yakshas, Serpents, Rakshasas, men, Pishachas. The curses of the Rishis also may not affect me. If you are pleased with me, then also grant me O, Lord! the boon so that I may not die of any weapon, missile rocks, trees, wet and dry things., I may also not die during the day or night. Let me be (like) the Sun and the Moon, and perform the functions of the wind, fire, water, sky, stars, the ten directions. May I be Anger, Cupid, Indra, Varuna, Yama, Dhanapati, Kuvera, Yaksha, Kimpurusha.

## \|\| 161.16 \|\|

*brahmovāca*  
*ete divyā varāstāta mayā dattāstavādbhutāḥ \|*  
*sarvānkāmānsadā vatsa prāpsyasi tvaṃ na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Brahma Said: — “Son! I grant you all these extraordinary boons sought by you. You shall attain them all that you desire without any doubt.”

## \|\| 161.17 \|\|

*evamuktvā sa bhagavāñ jagāmākāśa eva hi \|*  
*vairājaṃ brahmasadanaṃ brahmarṣigaṇasevitam \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. After that, Brahma. returned to His realm Vairaja, through the aerial track accompanied by the Brahmarishis.

## \|\| 161.18-20 \|\|

*tato devāśca nāgāśca gandharvā ṛṣibhiḥ saha \|*  
*varapradānaṃ śrutvaiva pitāmahamupasthitāḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*varapradānādbhagavan vadhiṣyati sa no 'suraḥ \|*  
*tatprasīdāśu bhagavan vadho 'pyasya vicintyatām \|\| 19 \|\|*

*bhagavansarvabhūtānām ādikartā svayaṃ prabhuḥ \|*  
*sraṣṭā tvaṃ havyakavyānām avyaktaprakṛtir budhaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

18-20. Then the Devas, the serpents, the Gandharvas, and the Rishis, etc., hearing the nature of the boons conferred on the demon by Brahma went to Him and said “O Brahmana! By virtue of Your boons, the demon will kill us all; so You should devise some means of his destruction., Bhagavana! You are the prime cause of all, You are Supreme, You are the Creator of the Devas and the Pittris. The Kavyas and Ravyas, offerings to the Devas and the Pittris, are ordained by You. You are the unmanifested Prakriti. You are wise and you are self-born.”

## \|\| 161.21-22 \|\|

*sarvalokahitaṃ vākyaṃ śrutvā devaḥ prajāpatiḥ \|*  
*āśvāsayāmāsa surān suśītairvacanāmbubhiḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*avaṣyaṃ tridaśāstena prāptavyaṃ tapasaḥ phalam \|*  
*tapaso 'nte 'sya bhagavān vadhaṃ viṣṇuḥ kariṣyati \|\| 22 \|\|*

21-22. Hearing those words of the Devas, Brahma consoled them with His nectar-like words. He said: “The performance of asceticism is hound to bear its fruits; and when his merits will be exhausted, the Lord Vishnu will kill this demon.”

## \|\| 161.23-24 \|\|

*tacchrutvā vibudhā vākyaṃ sarve paṅkajajanmanaḥ \|*  
*svāni sthānāni divyāni viprajagmurmudānvitāḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

*labdhamātre vare cātha sarvāḥ so 'bādhata prajāḥ \|*  
*hiraṇyakaśipurdaityo varadānena darpitaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

23-24. Hearing those words, the Devas and the Brahmanas joyfully returned to Their realms and Hiranyakashyapu on getting those boons became proud and began to oppress the people. He greatly disturbed the peace of the honourable Munis who were practising austerities and following the true Dharma, remaining in their Ashrama.

## \|\| 161.25-27 \|\|

*āśrameṣu mahābhāgān sa munīñchaṃsitavratān \|*  
*satyadharmaparāndāntān dharṣayāmāsa dānavaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*devāṃstribhuvanasthāṃśca parājitya mahāsuraḥ \|*  
*trailokyaṃ vaśamānīya svarge vasati dānavaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*yadā varamadotsiktaś coditaḥ kāladharmataḥ \|*  
*yajñiyānakaroddaityān ayajñiyāśca devatāḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

25-27. After conquering the Devas residing in heaven he brought the three worlds under his thumb and directed his engines of oppression towards those living in the hermitages and persecuted those who led virtuous lives. He then began to interfere with the rights of the Devas by going to heaven and monopolizing their share of the sacrificial offerings.

## \|\| 161.28-29 \|\|

*tadādityāśca sādhyāśca viśve ca vasavastathā \|*  
*sendrā devagaṇā yakṣāḥ siddhadvijamaharṣayaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

*śaraṇyaṃ śaraṇaṃ viṣṇum upatasthurmahābalam \|*  
*devadevaṃ yajñamayaṃ vāsudevaṃ sanātanam \|\| 29 \|\|*

28-29. The Adityas, Sadhyas, Vishvedevas, Vasus, Indra and other Devas, Yakshas, Siddhas, Dvijas, Maharshis went to Lord Vishnu and jointly offered Their prayer to Him the great Protector of the refugees, highly powerful the Deva of the Devas, the Eternal, the Yajnapurusha, Vasudeva.

## \|\| 161.30-31 \|\|

*devā ūcuḥ*  
*nārāyaṇa mahābhāga devāstvāṃ śaraṇaṃ gatāḥ \|*  
*trāyasva jahi daityendraṃ hiraṇyakaśipuṃ prabho \|\| 30 \|\|*

*tvaṃ hi naḥ paramo dhātā tvaṃ hi naḥ paramo guruḥ \|*  
*tvaṃ hi naḥ paramo devo brahmādīnāṃ surottama \|\| 31 \|\|*

30-31. They said “Narayana! Mahabhaga! We have come to seek Thy shelter. Lord! do kill the demon Hiranyakashyapu and save us. Thou art Our Protector, Guru, Thou art the adorable of the Devas like Brahma, etc.”

## \|\| 161.32-34 \|\|

*viṣṇuruvāca*  
*bhayaṃ tyajadhvamamarā abhayaṃ vo dadāmyaham \|*  
*tathaiva tridivaṃ devāḥ pratipadyata mā ciram \|\| 32 \|\|*

*eṣo 'haṃ sagaṇaṃ daityaṃ varadānena darpitam \|*  
*avadhyamamarendrāṇāṃ dānavendraṃ nihanmyaham \|\| 33 \|\|*

*evamuktvā tu bhagavān visṛjya tridaśeśvarān \|*  
*vadhaṃ saṃkalpayāmāsa hiraṇyakaśipoḥ prabhuḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

32-34. Hearing such a prayer, Vishnu said “Devas! Cast aside Your fears. Go back to heaven, do not delay. I shall kill this haughty demon with all his attendants and give the Kingdom of Heaven to You. With such words, Vishnu bade adieu to the Devas and resolved to kill that demon,

## \|\| 161.35-36 \|\|

*sāhāyyaṃ ca mahābāhur oṃkāraṃ gṛhya satvaram \|*  
*athauṃkārasahāyastu bhagavānviṣṇuravyayaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

*hiraṇyakaśipusthānaṃ jagāma harirīśvaraḥ \|*  
*tejasā bhāskarākāraḥ śaśī kāntyeva cāparaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

35-36. Then the mighty armed undecaying Vishnu took the assistance of “Omkara” and then with his assistance went to the demon’s place. Shining like the Sun and the Moon, He assumed the form of Narasimha (the lower half of human form with the upper half of the lion).

## \|\| 161.37-44 \|\|

*narasya kṛtvārdhatanuṃ siṃhasyārdhatanuṃ tathā \|*  
*nārasiṃhena vapuṣā pāṇiṃ saṃspṛṣya pāṇinā \|\| 37 \|\|*

*tato 'paṣyata vistīrṇāṃ divyāṃ ramyāṃ manoramām \|*  
*sarvakāmautāṃ śubhrāṃ hiraṇyakaśipoḥ sabhām \|\| 38 \|\|*

*vistīrṇāṃ yojanaśataṃ śatamadhyardhamāyatām \|*  
*vaihāyasīṃ kāmagamāṃ pañcayojanavistṛtām \|\| 39 \|\|*

*jarāśokaklamāpetāṃ niṣprakampāṃ śivāṃ sukhām \|*  
*veśmaharmyavatīṃ ramyāṃ jvalantīmiva tejasā \|\| 40 \|\|*

*antaḥsalilasaṃyuktāṃ vihitāṃ viśvakarmaṇā \|*  
*divyaratnamayairvṛkṣaiḥ phalapuṣpapradairyutām \|\| 41 \|\|*

*nīlapītasitaśyāmaiḥ kṛṣṇairlohitakairapi \|*  
*avatānaistathā gulmair mañjarīśatadhāribhiḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

*sitābhraghanasaṃkāśā plavantīva vyadṛṣyata \|*  
*raśmivatī bhāsvarā ca divyagandhamanoramā \|\| 43 \|\|*

*susukhā na ca duḥkhā sā na śītā na ca gharmadā \|*  
*na kṣutpipāse glāniṃ vā prāpya tāṃ prāpnuvanti te \|\| 44 \|\|*

37-44. At that instant, Narasimha chanced to see the most beautiful assembly of that, valiant demon. It was full of every blessing, divinely beautiful, 100 yojanas in length and 50 in breadth. It had all the desires and wealth; it was serial; it could go wherever it liked. It was free from the sufferings of infirmity, grief and decay. It was full of lustre and prosperity and firm. It was located amongst enchanting surroundings such as beautiful gardens, &c. There were beautiful pools of water within its precincts designed and executed by Vishvakarma and the trees of gold studded with precious stones. Besides all that, there were charming awnings of blue, yellow, white, black colours and hundred of creepers loaded with clusters of blossoms that looked like the waving of rows of clouds of various colours. In that place full of light and, pervaded with the stupefying odour of unsurpassing sweetness, there was a total absence of grief and it was full of comforts. There, the sun, cold, hunger, thirst and decay were not visible. The demons were sitting at such a place of beauty and comfort.

## \|\| 161.45-47 \|\|

*nānārūpairupakṛtāṃ vicitrairatibhāsvaraiḥ \|*  
*stambhairna vibhṛtā sā vai śāśvatī cākṣapā sadā \|\| 45 \|\|*

*ati candraṃ ca sūryaṃ ca śikhinaṃ ca svayaṃprabhā \|*  
*dīpyate nākapṛṣṭhasthā bhāsayantīva bhāskaram \|\| 46 \|\|*

*sarve ca kāmāḥ pracurā ye divyā ye ca mānuṣāḥ \|*  
*rasauktaṃ prabhūtaṃ ca bhakṣyabhojyamanantakam \|\| 47 \|\|*

45-47. It had various and beautiful architectural forms and was supported on wonderfully extraordinary bright pillars. The self-luminous Sabha eclipsed the sun and the moon by its radiance. The Devas and the men were supplied in abundance with their objects of desires there. Nice and tasteful victuals were also in plenty there.

## \|\| 161.48-51 \|\|

*puṇyagandhasrajaścātra nityapuṣpaphaladrumāḥ \|*  
*uṣṇe śītāni toyāni śīte coṣṇāni santi ca \|\| 48 \|\|*

*puṣpitāgrā mahāśākhāḥ pravālāṅkuradhāriṇaḥ \|*  
*latāvitānasaṃchannā nadīṣu ca saraḥsu ca \|\| 49 \|\|*

*vṛkṣānbahuvidhāṃstatra mṛgendro dadṛśe prabhuḥ \|*  
*gandhavanti ca puṣpāṇi rasavanti phalāni ca \|\| 50 \|\|*

*nātiśītāni noṣṇāni tatra tatra sarāṃsi ca \|*  
*apaṣyatsarvatīrthāni sabhāyāṃ tasya sa prabhuḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

48-51. Sweet scented garlands were in abundance. It was full of trees bearing flowers and fruits. It was ornamented with handsome floral wreaths. The water was nice and cool during the hot weather and warm during the cold weather. Various kinds of trees laden with sprouts, flowers, fruits, leaves, creepers, and clusters were circling the wells and the tanks. Narasimha saw many such scenes there. There were sweet-smelling flowers, juicy fruits, beautiful pools and Tirthas.

## \|\| 161.52-55 \|\|

*nalinaiḥ puṇḍarīkaiśca śatapattraiḥ sugandhibhiḥ \|*  
*raktaiḥ kuvalayairnīlaiḥ kumudaiḥ saṃvṛtāni ca \|\| 52 \|\|*

*sukāntairdhārtarāṣṭraiśca rājahaṃsaiśca supriyaiḥ \|*  
*kāraṇḍavaiścakravākaiḥ sārasaiḥ kurarairapi \|\| 53 \|\|*

*vimalaiḥ sphāṭikābhaiśca pāṇḍuracchadanairdvijaiḥ \|*  
*bahuhaṃsopagītāni sārasābhirutāni ca \|\| 54 \|\|*

*gandhavatyaḥ śubhāstatra puṣṭamañjaridhāriṇīḥ \|*  
*dṛṣṭavānparvatāgreṣu nānāpuṣpadharā latāḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

52-55. He also beheld many reservoirs smiling with nice smelling blue and red lotuses and beautified with the lustresome swans, Karandavas, Chakravakas, cranes, Kuravas, etc., and various kinds of other birds echoing with the notes of cranes. Besides those, He saw nice creepers with highly smelling blossoms embracing the mountain tops.

## \|\| 161.56-58 \|\|

*ketakyaśokasaralāḥ puṃnāgatilakārjunāḥ \|*  
*cūtā nīpāḥ prasthapuṣpāḥ kadambā bakulā dhavāḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

*priyaṅgupāṭalāvṛkṣāḥ śālmalyaḥ saharidrakāḥ \|*  
*sālāstālāstamālāśca campakāśca manoramāḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

*tathaivānye vyarājanta sabhāyāṃ puṣpitā drumāḥ \|*  
*vidrumāśca drumāścaiva jvalitāgnisamaprabhāḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

56-58. He also noticed the following plants and flower trees there, vis., Ketaki, Ashoka, Sarala, Punnaga, Tilaka, Arjuna, Amra, Nipa, Kadamba, Vakula, Dhavamala, Patala, Haridraka, Shalmali, Sala, Tala, Tamala, and beautiful Champaka. Similarly He saw in that assembly various other kinds of flower plants and the dazzling lustre of Dramas (Trees of Paradise) and Vidrumas (Coral trees)

## \|\| 161.59-68 \|\|

*skandhavantaḥ suśākhāśca bahutālasamucchrayāḥ \|*  
*añjanāśokavarṇāśca bahavaścitrakā drumāḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

*varuṇo vatsanābhaśca panasāḥ saha candanaiḥ \|*  
*nīpāḥ sumanasaścaiva nimbā aśvatthatindukāḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

*pārijātāśca lodhrāśca mallikā bhadradāravaḥ \|*  
*āmalakyastathā jambū-lakucāḥ śailavālukāḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

*kharjūryo nārikelāśca harītakavibhītakāḥ \|*  
*kālīyakā drukālāśca hiṅgavaḥ pāriyātrakāḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

*mandārakundalaktāśca pataṅgāḥ kuṭajāstathā \|*  
*raktāḥ kuraṇṭakāścaiva nīlāścāgarubhiḥ saha \|\| 63 \|\|*

*kadambāścaiva bhavyāśca dāḍimā bījapūrakāḥ \|*  
*saptaparṇāśca bilvāśca madhupairāvṛtāstathā \|\| 64 \|\|*

*aśokāśca tamālāśca nānāgulmalatāvṛtāḥ \|*  
*madhūkāḥ saptaparṇāśca bahavaḥ kṣīrakā drumāḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

*latāśca vividhākārāḥ patrapuṣpaphalopagāḥ \|*  
*ete cānye ca bahavas tatra kānanajā drumāḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

*nānāpuṣpaphalopetā vyarājanta samantataḥ \|*  
*cakorāḥ śatapatrāśca mattakokilasārikāḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

*puṣpitāḥ puṣpitāgraiśca saṃpatanti mahādrumāḥ \|*  
*raktapītāruṇāstatra pādapāgragatāḥ khagāḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

59-68. Very many tall trees of various descriptions were there. Besides, many kinds of other trees such as Arjuna, A4oka, Varuna, Vatsyanabha, Panasa, Nila, Sumanasa, Chandana, Ashwatha, Tinduka, Parijata, Nimba, Mallika, Bhadra Dum, Amalaki, Jambu, Lakucha, Shailavaluka, date tree, Cocoanut tree, Haritaka, Vibhitak, Kaliaka, Drukala, Hingu, Pariyatraka, Mandara, Kundalata, Patanga, Kutaja, red Kuruntaka, blue Aguru, Kadamba, Bhavya, Pomegranate, Vijapuraka, Saptaparna, Bel and various other trees were there. Sweetly humming bees were there. Ashoka Tamala, Madhuka, Saptaparna and various other trees were covered with shrubs and bushes and enhanced the beauty of the garden, tanks and wells. Besides, various other creepers and forest trees with leaves, flowers and fruits were on all sides. The branches of some trees laden with flowers and fruits were hanging on other trees and various birds Chakora, Shatapatra, intoxicated cuckoos, Sarikas and other birds of red, yellow and various other colours were cooing sweetly there. The couple Jiva and Jivaka were looking at each other with great joy and satisfaction.

## \|\| 161.69-72 \|\|

*parasparamavekṣante prahṛṣṭā jīvajīvakāḥ \|*  
*tasyāṃ sabhāyāṃ daityendro hiraṇyakaśipustadā \|\| 69 \|\|*

*strīsahasraiḥ parivṛto vicitrābharaṇāmbaraḥ \|*  
*anarghyamaṇivajrārciḥ śikhājvalitakuṇḍalaḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

*āsīnaścāsane citre daśanalvapramāṇataḥ \|*  
*divākaranibhe divye divyāstaraṇasaṃstṛte \|\| 71 \|\|*

*divyagandhavahastatra mārutaḥ susukho vavau \|*  
*hiraṇyakaśipurdaitya āste jvalitakuṇḍalaḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

69-72. The demon Hiranyakashyapu was enjoying there in the company of hundreds of women. His garments and ornaments were wonderful. He was seated on a seat covered with cloth shining like the sun measuring ten hands. He was \_ wearing wonderful ornaments and his earrings were sparkling with diamonds, etc. A gentle and soothing breeze laden with perfume was beating at the place where the demon was seated.

## \|\| 161.73-76 \|\|

*upacerurmahādaityaṃ hiraṇyakaśipuṃ tadā \|*  
*divyatānena gītāni jagur gandharvasattamāḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

*viśvācī sahajanyā ca pramlocetyabhiviśrutā \|*  
*divyātha saurabheyī ca samīcī puñjikasthalī \|\| 74 \|\|*

*miśrakeśī ca rambhā ca citralekhā śucismitā \|*  
*cārukeśī ghṛtācī ca menakā corvaśī tathā \|\| 75 \|\|*

*etāḥ sahasraśaścānyā nṛtyagītaviśāradāḥ \|*  
*upatiṣṭhanti rājānaṃ hiraṇyakaśipuṃ prabhum \|\| 76 \|\|*

73-76. Various Gandharvas attending on him were singing beautiful songs to him and he was adored by the following nymphs: — Vishvachi, Sahajanya, Paramlocha, Saurabhaiyi, Samichi, Punjikasthali, Mishrakeshi, Rambha, sweet-smiling Chitralekha, Charukeshi, Ghritachi, Men aka, and Urvashi and thousands of other Apsaras, experts in singing and dancing, were in attendance on their lord, King Hiranya-Kashipu.

## \|\| 161.77 \|\|

*tatrāsīnaṃ mahābāhuṃ hiraṇyakaśipuṃ prabhum \|*  
*upāsate diteḥ putrāḥ sarve labdhavarāstathā \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. The sons of Diti who were all famous, were also waiting on Hiranyakashyapu,

## \|\| 161.78-82 \|\|

*tamapratimakarmāṇaṃ śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ \|*  
*balirvirocanastatra narakaḥ pṛthivīsutaḥ \|\| 78 \|\|*

*prahlādo vipracittiśca gaviṣṭhaśca mahāsuraḥ \|*  
*surahantā sunāmā ca pramatiḥ sumatirvaraḥ \|\| 79 \|\|*

*ghaṭodaro mahāpārśvaḥ krathanaḥ piṭharastathā \|*  
*viśvarūpaḥ surūpaśca svabalaśca mahābalaḥ \|\| 80 \|\|*

*daśagrīvaśca vālī ca meghavāsā mahāsuraḥ \|*  
*ghaṭāsyo 'kampanaścaiva prajanaścendratāpanaḥ \|\| 81 \|\|*

*daityadānavasaṃghāste sarve jvalitakuṇḍalāḥ \|*  
*sragviṇo vāgminaḥ sarve sadaiva caritavratāḥ \|\| 82 \|\|*

78-82. They were hundreds of thousands, such as Bali, Virochana, Prithivisuta, Narakasura, Prahlada, Viprachitti, Mahasura, Gavishtha, Surahanta, Sunama, Pramati, Vara, Ghatodara, Mahaparshva, Krathana, Pithara, Vishvarupa, Surupa, Svabala, Mahabala, Dashagriva, Bali, Meghavasa, Ghatasya, Akampana, Prajana, Indratapana. They were seated in groups wearing brilliant earrings,

## \|\| 161.83-84 \|\|

*sarve labdhavarāḥ śūrāḥ sarve vigatamṛtyavaḥ \|*  
*ete cānye ca bahavo hiraṇyakaśipuṃ prabhum \|\| 83 \|\|*

*upāsanti mahātmānaṃ sarve divyaparicchadāḥ \|*  
*vimānairvividhākārair bhrājamānairivāgnibhiḥ \|\| 84 \|\|*

83-84. They were also wearing garlands; and they were great speakers and had attained boons. They were valiant and free from death. They were clothed in nice divine dresses and all of them had chariots blazing like fire; their bodies were like Mahendra; and their arms and bodies were ornamented with various armlets and ornaments. They looked like mountains, and were of golden colour. They, along with other demons, were adoring Hiranyakashyapu.

## \|\| 161.85-89 \|\|

*mahendravapuṣaḥ sarve vicitrāṅgadabāhavaḥ \|*  
*bhūṣitāṅgā diteḥ putrās tamupāsanta sarvaśaḥ \|\| 85 \|\|*

*tasyāṃ sabhāyāṃ divyāyām asurāḥ parvatopamāḥ \|*  
*hiraṇyavapuṣaḥ sarve divākarasamaprabhāḥ \|\| 86 \|\|*

*na śrutaṃ naiva dṛṣṭaṃ hi hiraṇyakaśiporyathā \|*  
*aiśvaryaṃ daityasiṃhasya yathā tasya mahātmanaḥ \|\| 87 \|\|*

*kanakarajatacitravedikāyāṃ parihṛtaratnavicitravīthikāyām \|*  
*sa dadarśa mṛgādhipaḥ sabhāyāṃ suracitaratnagavākṣaśobhitāyām \|\| 88 \|\|*

*kanakavimalahārabhūṣitāṅgaṃ dititanayaṃ sa mṛgādhipo dadarśa \|*  
*divasakaramahāprabhājvalantaṃ ditijasahasraśatairniṣevyamāṇam \|\| 89 \|\|*

85-89. They, all seated in various kinds of Vimanas, looked splendid. They were gleaming like gold. Narasimha thus saw the great Hiranyakashyapu, the Lord of the Daityas who was shining with uncommon lustre like a mountain. His body was radiant like the sun. His like in wealth, in splendour, in everything else, has neither been heard of nor seen. His splendour was in keeping with his greatness. The valiant demon king was seated on a throne of gold with a necklace round his neck like a lion with perforated work of silver and gold all round him. The hall of assembly was decorated with variegated roads adorned with altars and studded with gems and nice windows. He was attended by thousands of demons shining like the sun and wearing garlands of gold.

## Chapter 162

## \|\| 162.1-3 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*tato dṛṣṭvā mahātmānaṃ kālacakramivāgatam \|*  
*narasiṃhavapuśchannaṃ bhasmacchannamivānalam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*hiraṇyakaśipoḥ putraḥ prahlādo nāma vīryavān \|*  
*divyena cakṣuṣā siṃham apaṣyaddevamāgatam \|\| 2 \|\|*

*te dṛṣṭvā rukmaśailābham apūrvāṃ tanumāśritam \|*  
*vismitā dānavāḥ sarve hiraṇyakaśipuśca saḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

1-3. Suta said: — Mahatma Prahlada, the son of Hiranyakashyapu, saw with his supernatural vision that, hidden within Narasimha, who came like the cycle of death, there was Lord Vishnu as cinders are embedded in the ashes. He was not the natural lion but Hari, the Lord of the Devas. Other demons, along with Hiranyakashyapu, were highly astonished to see Narasimha, whose body was very extraordinary and who looked like mountain of gold.

## \|\| 162.4-5 \|\|

*prahlāda uvāca*  
*mahābāho mahārāja daityānāmādisaṃbhava \|*  
*na śrutaṃ na ca no dṛṣṭaṃ nārasiṃhamidaṃ vapuḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*avyaktaprabhavaṃ divyaṃ kimidaṃ rūpamāgatam \|*  
*daityāntakaraṇaṃ ghoraṃ saṃśatīva mano mama \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. Prahlada said: — “O valiant king! the progenitor of the Daityas I have neither heard nor seen this divine Narasimha form. How wonderful this mystic form is? Whence has it come? his formidable lion form seems to indicate to me that He will annihilate the demons.

## \|\| 162.6-11 \|\|

*asya devāḥ śarīrasthāḥ sāgarāḥ saritaśca yāḥ \|*  
*himavānpāriyātraśca ye cānye kulaparvatāḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*candramāśca sanakṣatrair ādityair vasubhiḥ saha \|*  
*dhanado varuṇaścaiva yamaḥ śakraḥ śacīpatiḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*maruto devagandharvā ṛṣayaśca tapodhanāḥ \|*  
*nāgā yakṣāḥ piśācāśca rākṣasā bhīmavikramāḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*brahmā devaḥ paśupatir lalāṭasthā bhramanti vai \|*  
*sthāvarāṇi ca sarvāṇi jaṅgamāni tathaiva ca \|\| 9 \|\|*

*bhavāṃśca sahito 'smābhiḥ sarvairdaityagaṇairvṛtaḥ \|*  
*vimānaśatasaṃkīrṇā tathaiva bhavataḥ sabhā \|\| 10 \|\|*

*sarvaṃ tribhuvanaṃ rājaṃl lokadharmāśca śāśvatāḥ \|*  
*dṛṣyante nārasiṃhe 'smiṃs tathedamakhilaṃ jagat \|\| 11 \|\|*

6-11. The Devas are all within this form and- so are the oceans and the rivers. Huge mountains like the Himavana, Paripatra, etc., the Moon, the stars, Sun, Vasus, Kuvera, Varuna, Yama, Indra, the Maruts, the Devas, the Gandharvas, the Rishis, the Nagas % Yakshas, the Pishachas, the terrible Rakshas, Brahma and lava, etc., all animate and inanimate are revolving in his head. Yourself, with Jambha and all the Daityas, myself, hundreds of your assemblies with hundreds of aerial chariots and in fact the whole of the three worlds are visible to me in his form. The whole universe is within this form.

## \|\| 162.12-13 \|\|

*prajāpatiścātra manur mahātmā grahāśca yogāśca mahīruhāśca \|*  
*utpātakālaśca dhṛtirmatiśca ratiśca satyaṃ ca tapo damaśca \|\| 12 \|\|*

*sanatkumāraśca mahānubhāvo viśve ca devā ṛṣayaśca sarve \|*  
*krodhaśca kāmaśca tathaiva harṣo dharmaśca mohaḥ pitaraśca sarve \|\| 13 \|\|*

12-13. Prajapati, the high- scaled Mann, planets, Yogas, trees, destruction, stability, intellect, pleasure truth, asceticism, Dama, Sanatkumara, Vishvedeva, the Rishis, wish, anger, glee, righteousness, delusion, Pittris, are all confined within this form”.

## \|\| 162.14-15 \|\|

*prahlādasya vacaḥ śrutvā hiraṇyakaśipuḥ prabhuḥ \|*  
*uvāca dānavānsarvān gaṇāṃśca sa gaṇādhipaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*mṛgendro gṛhyatāmeṣa apūrvāṃ tanumāsthitaḥ \|*  
*yadi vā saṃśayaḥ kaścid vadhyatāṃ vanagocaraḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

14-15. The king Hiranyakashyapu on hearing those words of Prahlada addressed the other Danavas. He said “This wonderful lion should be caught and in case there be any difficulty in its being captured, kill him outright”.

## \|\| 162.16 \|\|

*te dānavagaṇā sarve mṛgendraṃ bhīmavikramam \|*  
*parikṣipanto muditās trāsayāmāsurojasā \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Hearing those words, those powerful Danavas began to ill treat Him 'in all sorts of vicious ways and became ready to torment that Narasimha with their weapons.

## \|\| 162.17-18 \|\|

*siṃhanādaṃ vimucyātha narasiṃho mahābalaḥ \|*  
*babhañja tāṃ sabhāṃ divyāṃ vyāditāsya ivāntakaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*sabhāyāṃ bhajyamānāyāṃ hiraṇyakaśipuḥ svayam \|*  
*cikṣepāstrāṇi siṃhasya roṣādvyākulalocanaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

17-18. Then Narasimha after sending forth a loud roar, opened wide His mouth and began to break down that assembly. After the assembly was devastated, Hiranyakashyapu boiling with rage attacked Narasimha with his arms.

## \|\| 162.19-28 \|\|

*sarvāstrāṇāmatha jyeṣṭhaṃ daṇḍamantraṃ sudāruṇam \|*  
*kālacakraṃ tathāghoraṃ viṣṇucakraṃ tathā param \|\| 19 \|\|*

*paitāmahaṃ tathātyugraṃ trailokyadahanaṃ mahat \|*  
*vicitrāmaśanīṃ caiva śuṣkārdraṃ cāśanidvayam \|\| 20 \|\|*

*raudraṃ tathograṃ śūlaṃ ca kaṅkālaṃ musalaṃ tathā \|*  
*mohanaṃ śoṣaṇaṃ caiva saṃtāpanavilāpanam \|\| 21 \|\|*

*vāyavyaṃ mathanaṃ caiva kāpālamatha kaiṅkaram \|*  
*tathāpratihatāṃ śaktiṃ krauñcamastraṃ tathaiva ca \|\| 22 \|\|*

*astraṃ brahmaśiraścaiva somāstraṃ śiśiraṃ tathā \|*  
*kampanaṃ śātanaṃ caiva tvāṣṭraṃ caiva subhairavam \|\| 23 \|\|*

*kālamudgaramakṣobhyaṃ tapanaṃ ca mahābalam \|*  
*saṃvartanaṃ mohanaṃ ca tathā māyādharaṃ param \|\| 24 \|\|*

*gāndharvamastraṃ dayitam asiratnaṃ ca nandakam \|*  
*prasvāpanaṃ pramathanaṃ vāruṇaṃ cāstramuttamam \|*  
*astraṃ pāśupataṃ caiva yasyāpratihatā gatiḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*astraṃ hayaśiraścaiva brāhmamastraṃ tathaiva ca \|*  
*nārāyaṇāstramaindraṃ ca sārpamastraṃ tathādbhutam \|\| 26 \|\|*

*paiśācamastramajitaṃ śoṣadaṃ śāmanaṃ tathā \|*  
*mahābalaṃ bhāvanaṃ ca prasthāpanavikampane \|\| 27 \|\|*

*etānyastrāṇi divyāni hiraṇyakaśipustadā \|*  
*asṛjannarasiṃhasya dīptasyāgnerivāhutim \|\| 28 \|\|*

19-28. Like the pouring of the sacrificial offerings in the fire the demon showered the following missiles on Narasimha: — The deadly club, Kalachakra, Vishnuchakra, Brahmastra, the consumer of the three realms, the wonderful Vajrastra, the two other sorts of Vajrastras (dry and wet), the formidable trident, club, Mohanastra, Shoshanastra, Santapanastra Bilapanastra, Vayavayastra, Mathanastra, Kapalastra, Kainkarastra, Shakti, Kraunchastra, Somastra, Brahmashirastra, Shishirastra, Kampanatra, Shatanastra, Tvashtastra, deadly club, Tapanastra, Samvartamastra, Madanastra, Mayadhara, Gandharvastra, Daita-Asiratna, Nandaka, Prasavanastra, Pramathanastra, Uttamavarana, Pashupatastra, Hayashirastra, Brahma-astra, Narayanastra, Aindrastra, Sarpastra, Paishachastra, Ajitastra, Shoshanastra, Samanastra, Bhavanastra, Prasthapanastra, Bikampanastra.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — Vishnu-astra, Brahmastra, &c. were all different arrows that were used after reciting the prescribed mantras. Most of them have been described in previous chapters so only the few new ones are explained in this note... Lit. the wheel of time. Deadly quoits. … A particular kind of missile… A destructive weapon of the thunderbolt. A missile which bewitches the person against whom it is used, …A particular kind of missile, missile which and subdues the adversary, … missile that produces chill to kill the foe. … A missile that shivers the foe. … The missile composed of the bright disc of Sangya trimmed off. The missile that produces heat. missile that produces destructive clouds. The missile that causes intoxication to the foe. … The missile that divides into many. … The missile that causes excessive torture and destruction. particular kind of missile. The missile sacred to Indra. … A missile that creates fiends who fight and devour the foe. A particular missile. .. A missile causing a deluge. missile causing the enemy to J retire. missile causing palpitation and unsteadiness to the foe.

## \|\| 162.29-30 \|\|

*astraiḥ prajvalitaiḥ siṃham āvṛṇodasurottamaḥ \|*  
*vivasvān gharmasamaye himavantamivāṃśubhiḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*sa hyamarṣānilodbhūto daityānāṃ sainyasāgaraḥ \|*  
*kṣaṇena plāvayāmāsa mainākamiva sāgaraḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

29-30. As the sun overshadows the Mount Himachala by his rays during the hot season, similarly did the valiant demon Hiranyakashyapu overpower Narasimha with the weapons. The angry demons drowned Narasimha with their missiles as the Mount Mainaka is buried in the sea.

## \|\| 162.31-32 \|\|

*prāsaiḥ pāśaiśca khaḍgaiśca gadābhirmusalaistathā \|*  
*vajrairaśanibhiścaiva sāgnibhiśca mahādrumaiḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

*mudgarairbhindipālaiśca śilolūkhalaparvataiḥ \|*  
*śataghnībhiśca dīptābhir daṇḍairapi sudāruṇaiḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

31-32. Spears, nooses, swords, clubs, huge fiery trees, javelins, bolts, rocks, staffs, burning Shataghni and various other weapons were piled on Narasimha, one after the other. They did not wave a bit; rather, they remained firm like the thunderbolt of Mahendra.

## \|\| 162.33 \|\|

*te dānavāḥ pāśagṛhītahastā mahendratulyāśanivajravegāḥ \|*  
*samantato 'bhyudyatabāhukāyāḥ sthitāstriśīrṣā iva nāgapāśāḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. The demons circled round Narasimha like an encircling fire, holding their noses and massive bolts, etc. They with their bodies and arms straight looked like Trishirsha Nagapasa (noose formed by three-headed serpents)

## \|\| 162.34-35 \|\|

*suvarṇamālākulabhūṣitāṅgāḥ pītāṃśukābhogavibhāvitāṅgāḥ \|*  
*muktāvalīdāmasanāthakakṣā haṃsā ivābhānti viśālapakṣāḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

*teṣāṃ tu vāupratimaujasāṃ vai keyūramaulīvalayotkaṭānām \|*  
*tānyuttamāṅgānyabhito vibhānti prabhātasūryāṃśusamaprabhāṇi \|\| 35 \|\|*

34-35. Those demons looked like a multitude of big- winged white cranes with their gold and pearl garlands hanging on their handsome forms dressed in yellow robes. The armlets and earrings of those agile demons shone like the rays of the Rising sun. All the demons were inspired like Vayu with vigour and energy.

## \|\| 162.36-37 \|\|

*kṣipadbhir ugrair jvalitair mahābalair mahāstrapūgaiḥ susamāvṛto babhau \|*  
*giriryathā saṃtatavarṣibhir ghanaiḥ kṛtāndhakārāntarakaṃdaro drumaiḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

*tairhanyamāno 'pi mahāstrajālair mahābalair daityagaṇaiḥ sametaiḥ \|*  
*nākampatājau bhagavānpratāpasthitaḥ prakṛtyā himavānivācalaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

36-37. Narasimha covered with the dangerous Burning missiles of the demons looked dark like a mountain covered with big trees and clouds showering incessant rains, and with dark eaves; but like the mighty Himalaya He did not move, inspite of so many blows; He remained firm and steady.

## \|\| 162.38 \|\|

*saṃtrāsitāstena nṛsiṃharūpiṇā diteḥ sutāḥ pāvakatulyatejasā \|*  
*bhayādviceluḥ pavanoddhutāṅgā yathormayaḥ sāgaravārisaṃbhavāḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. At which, the demons began to shiver with fear of Narasimha blazing like fire; they were agitated as the waves of the ocean become by blast of wind.

## Chapter 163

## \|\| 163.1-5 \|\|

*Matsya-Purāṇa 163*  
*sūta uvāca*  
*kharāḥ kharamukhāścaiva makarāśīviṣānanāḥ \|*  
*īhāmṛgamukhāścānye varāhamukhasaṃsthitāḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*bālasūryamukhāścānye dhūmaketumukhāstathā \|*  
*ardhacandrārdhavaktrāśca agnidīptamukhāstathā \|\| 2 \|\|*

*haṃsakukkuṭavaktrāśca vyāditāsyā bhayāvahāḥ \|*  
*siṃhāsyā lelihānāśca kākagṛdhramukhāstathā \|\| 3 \|\|*

*dvijihvakā vakraśīrṣās tatholkāmukhasaṃsthitāḥ \|*  
*mahāgrāhamukhāścānye dānavā baladarpitāḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*śailasaṃvarṣmaṇas tasya śarīre śaravṛṣṭibhiḥ \|*  
*avadhyasya mṛgendrasya na vyathāṃ cakrurāhave \|\| 5 \|\|*

1-5. Suta said: — A board of demons had various appearances, viz., like that of an ass, alligator, fish, serpent, deer, swine, Rising sun, .comets, half Moon, swan, blazing fire, cock, lion, with mouths wide open, crow, vulture, jackal, meteors; some of them had two tongues; others had faces like big sparks, some looked like mountains; they were all very proud of their strength. They began to shower arrows incessantly on Narasimha, but I He was not affected in the least.

## \|\| 163.6-7 \|\|

*evaṃ bhūyo 'parānghorān asṛjandānaveśvarāḥ \|*  
*mṛgendrasyopari kruddhā niḥśvasanta ivoragāḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*te dānavaśarā ghorā dānavendrasamīritāḥ \|*  
*vilayaṃ jagmurākāśe khadyotā iva parvate \|\| 7 \|\|*

6-7. Afterwards,, they became angry like furious hissing snakes and sent forth a volley of various kinds of terrible weapons which were all destroyed I in the air and became invisible like a firefly in the mountains.

## \|\| 163.8-9 \|\|

*tataścakrāṇi divyāni daityāḥ krodhasamanvitāḥ \|*  
*mṛgendrāyāsṛjannāśu jvalitāni samantataḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*tairāsīdgaganaṃ cakraiḥ saṃpatadbhiritastataḥ \|*  
*yugānte saṃprakāśadbhiś candrādityagrahairiva \|\| 9 \|\|*

8-9. The demons blinded with rage threw their mighty quoits at Narasimha which illumined the sky as the sun and the moon at the time of the destruction of the universe.

## \|\| 163.10-12 \|\|

*tāni sarvāṇi cakrāṇi mṛgendreṇa mahātmanā \|*  
*grastānyudīrṇāni tadā pāvakārciḥsamāni vai \|\| 10 \|\|*

*tāni cakrāṇi vadane viśamānāni bhānti vai \|*  
*meghodaradarīṣveva candrasūryagrahā iva \|\| 11 \|\|*

*hiraṇyakaśipurdaityo bhūyaḥ prāsṛjadūrjitām \|*  
*śaktiṃ prajvalitāṃ ghorāṃ dhautaśastrataḍitprabhām \|\| 12 \|\|*

10-12. Narasimha caught bold of and devoured the quoits shining like fire and thus their dazzle was lost as the sun and the moon are eclipsed by the clouds; then Hiranyakashyapu hurled his formidable bolt shining like lightning.

## \|\| 163.13-14 \|\|

*tāmāpatantīṃ samprekṣya mṛgendraḥ śaktimudjvalām \|*  
*huṃkāreṇaiva raudreṇa babhañja bhagavāṃstadā \|\| 13 \|\|*

*rarāja bhagnā sā śaktir mṛgendreṇa mahītale \|*  
*savisphuliṅgā jvalitā maholkeva divaścyutā \|\| 14 \|\|*

13-14. Narasimha broke the flying bolt with His roar, Humkara, which fell clattering on the ground and looked like a shooting star falling from the heaven.

## \|\| 163.15 \|\|

*nārācapaṅktiḥ siṃhasya prāptā reje 'vidūrataḥ \|*  
*nīlotpalapalāśānāṃ mālevodjvaladarśanā \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. The rows of arrows pierced into Narasimha looked like the garland of the petals of the blue lotus.

## \|\| 163.16-20 \|\|

*sa garjitvā yathānyāyaṃ vikramya ca yathāsukham \|*  
*tatsainyam utsāritavāṃs tṛṇāgrāṇīva mārutaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*tato 'śmavarṣaṃ daityendrā vyamṛjanta nabhogatāḥ \|*  
*nagamātraiḥ śilākhaṇḍair giriśṛṅgairmahāprabhaiḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*tadaśmavarṣaṃ siṃhasya mahanmūrdhani pātitam \|*  
*diśo daśa vikīrṇā vai khadyotaprakarā iva \|\| 18 \|\|*

*tadāśmaughair daityagaṇāḥ punaḥ siṃhamariṃdamam \|*  
*chādayāṃcakrire meghā dhārābhiriva parvatam \|\| 19 \|\|*

*na ca taṃ cālayāmāsur daityaughā devasattamam \|*  
*bhīmavego 'calaśreṣṭhaṃ samudra iva mandaram \|\| 20 \|\|*

16-20. Afterwards Narasimha with a loud roar tore up the demons as wind does with the leaves; when the chief Daityas flew up to the sky and showered rocks from there and the whole space became full of them and they fell on the head of Narasimha and gleamed like so many fireflies. Then the demons covered Narasimha with the rocks as the mountains are covered with rain. But even then the demons could not move Narasimha as the violent ocean cannot move the Mandarachala Mountain.

## \|\| 163.21-27 \|\|

*tato 'śmavarṣe vihate jalavarṣamanantaram \|*  
*dhārābhirakṣamātrābhiḥ prādurāsītsamantataḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*nabhasaḥ pracyutā dhārās tigmavegāḥ samantataḥ \|*  
*āvṛtya sarvato vyoma diśaścopadiśastathā \|\| 22 \|\|*

*dhārā divi ca sarvatra vasudhāyāṃ ca sarvaśaḥ \|*  
*na spṛśanti ca tā devaṃ nipatantyo 'niśaṃ bhuvi \|\| 23 \|\|*

*bāhyato vavṛṣurvarṣaṃ nopariṣṭācca vavṛṣuḥ \|*  
*mṛgendrapratirūpasya sthitasya udhi māyayā \|\| 24 \|\|*

*hate 'śmavarṣe tumule jalavarṣe ca śoṣite \|*  
*so 'sṛjaddānavo māyām agnivāusamīritām \|\| 25 \|\|*

*mahendrastoyadaiḥ sārdhaṃ sahasrākṣo mahādyutiḥ \|*  
*mahatā toyavarṣeṇa śamayāmāsa pāvakam \|\| 26 \|\|*

*tasyāṃ pratihatāyāṃ tu māyāyāṃ udhi dānavaḥ \|*  
*asṛjadghorasaṃkāśaṃ tamastīvraṃ samantataḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

21-27. After the shower of rocks, rain poured in on all sides to kill Narasimha. The whole space pervaded with those fearful torrents hut they did not touch Narasimha. After the showers of rocks and rain proved ineffectual, Hiranyakashyapu let out fire conjoint with wind which Indra warded off by rain after which the demon created pitched darkness.

## \|\| 163.28-29 \|\|

*tamasā saṃvṛte loke daityeṣvāttāudheṣu ca \|*  
*svatejasā parivṛto divākara ivābabhau \|\| 28 \|\|*

*triśikhāṃ bhrukuṭīṃ cāsya dadṛśurdānavā raṇe \|*  
*lalāṭasthāṃ triśūlāṅkāṃ gaṅgāṃ tripathagāmiva \|\| 29 \|\|*

28-29. The universe pervaded with darkness under the cover of which the demons again began to array themselves with arms, when Narasimha shone forth like the Sun, and the demons saw the three wrinkles on the forehead of Narasimha which were the trident mark looking like the stream of the Ganges flowing in three directions.

## \|\| 163.30-34 \|\|

*tataḥ sarvāsu māyāsu hatāsu ditinandanāḥ \|*  
*hiraṇyakaśipuṃ daityaṃ vivarṇāḥ śaraṇaṃ yayuḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

*tataḥ prajvalitaḥ krodhāt pradahanniva tejasā \|*  
*tasminkruddhe tu daityendre tamobhūtamabhūdjagat \|\| 31 \|\|*

*āvahaḥ pravahaścaiva vivaho 'tha hyudāvahaḥ \|*  
*parāvahaḥ saṃvahaśca mahābalaparākramāḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

*tathā parivahaḥ śrīmān utpātabhayaśaṃsinaḥ \|*  
*ityevaṃ kṣubhitāḥ sapta maruto gaganecarāḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

*ye grahāḥ sarvalokasya kṣaye prādurbhavanti vai \|*  
*te sarve gagane dṛṣṭā vyacaranta yathāsukham \|\| 34 \|\|*

30-34. When all Mayas raised up by the Daityas were annihilated, the demons went for shelter to Hiranyakashyapu with a heavy heart who burnt with rage and determined to destroy everything. At that hour, the whole universe was covered with darkness (Tamas); and the following very strong, fearful winds began to blow as ominous signs: — Abaha, Pravaha, Vivaha, Udavaha, Paravaha, Samvaha and Parivaha; and all the planets and asterisms visible at the time of the destruction of the world began to be seen in the sky.

## \|\| 163.35 \|\|

*ayogataścāpyacaran mārgaṃ niśi niśācaraḥ \|*  
*sagrahaḥ saha nakṣatrair ākāpatirariṃdamaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. The Sun turned pale. The evil spirits, headless Kavandhas, began to haunt in the sky and the full moon along with the stars began to be eclipsed.

## \|\| 163.36 \|\|

*vivarṇatāṃ ca bhagavān gato divi divākaraḥ \|*  
*kṛṣṇaṃ kabandhaṃ ca tathā lakṣyate sumahaddivi \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. The Sun went below the horizon and seemed to spread his rays and He was visible also frequently in the sky.

## \|\| 163.37-43 \|\|

*amuñcaccārciṣāṃ vṛndaṃ bhūmivṛttir vibhāvasuḥ \|*  
*gaganasthaśca bhagavān abhīkṣṇaṃ paridṛṣyate \|\| 37 \|\|*

*sapta dhūmranibhā ghorāḥ sūryā divi samutthitāḥ \|*  
*somasya gaganasthasya grahāstiṣṭhanti śṛṅgagāḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

*vāme tu dakṣiṇe caiva sthitau śukrabṛhaspatī \|*  
*śanaiścaro lohitāṅgo jvalanāṅgasamadyutiḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

*samaṃ samadhirohantaḥ sarve te gaganecarāḥ \|*  
*śṛṅgāṇi śanakairghorā ugāntāvartino grahāḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

*candramāśca sanakṣatrair grahaiḥ saha tamonudaḥ \|*  
*carācaravināśāya rohiṇīṃ nābhyanandata \|\| 41 \|\|*

*gṛhīto rāhuṇā candra ulkābhirabhihanyate \|*  
*ulkāḥ prajvalitāścandre vicaranti yathāsukham \|\| 42 \|\|*

*devānāmapi yo devaḥ so 'pyavarṣata śoṇitam \|*  
*apatangaganādulkā vidyudrūpā mahāsvanāḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

37-43 Seven fearful suns of the smoke colour were visible in the firmament. The planets were seen to reside in the horns in the Moon. Shukra and Brihaspati were situated on the left and the right sides respectively there. Saturn and Mars and all the stars at the time of dissolution of the universe arrived at their places in the horns respectively. The Moon also did not welcome the asterism Rohini, indicating, as it were, the destruction of the universe with planets and other stars. Rahu began to shadow the Moon, and meteors began to fall on Him as well as on the Moon. Devendra began to shower blood and meteors began to descend from the heaven and there was a fearful clattering noise.

## \|\| 163.44-46 \|\|

*akāle ca drumāḥ sarve puṣpanti ca phalanti ca \|*  
*latāśca saphalāḥ sarvā ye cāhurdaityanāśanam \|\| 44 \|\|*

*phalaiḥ phalānyajāyanta puṣpaiḥ puṣpaṃ tathaiva ca \|*  
*unmīlanti nimīlanti hasanti ca rudanti ca \|\| 45 \|\|*

*vikrośanti ca gambhīrā dhūmayanti jvalanti ca \|*  
*pratimāḥ sarvadevānāṃ vedayanti mahadbhayam \|\| 46 \|\|*

44-46. The trees blossomed and fructified out, of their seasons. The creepers also did the same to contribute to the other inauspicious signs for the demons. Fruits were produced from fruits and flowers from flowers. The grave, appearances of images of the Devas began sometimes, to, wink, sometimes to laugh, cry and shriek. Smoke came out of Them and They began to burn.

## \|\| 163.47 \|\|

*āraṇyaiḥ saha saṃsṛṣṭā grāmyāśca mṛgapakṣiṇaḥ \|*  
*cakruḥ subhairavaṃ tatra mahāuddhamupasthitam \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. The wild deer and birds mingling with the tame ones started a fearful noise in that fight.

## \|\| 163.48 \|\|

*nadyaśca pratikūlāni vahanti kaluṣodakāḥ \|*  
*na prakāśanti ca diśo raktareṇusamākulāḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. The water of the foul rivers flowed upwards and the particles of blood were diffused all round in the several quarters of the sky.

## \|\| 163.49 \|\|

*vānaspatyo na pūjyante pūjanārhāḥ kathaṃcana \|*  
*vāuvegena hanyante bhajyante praṇamanti ca \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. The adorable trees were neglected and not worshipped. Huge trees were knocked to the ground by wind.

## \|\| 163.50-53 \|\|

*yadā ca sarvabhūtānāṃ chāyā na parivartate \|*  
*aparāhṇagate sūrye lokānāṃ ugasaṃkṣaye \|\| 50 \|\|*

*tadā hiraṇyakaśipor daityasyopari veśmanaḥ \|*  
*bhāṇḍāgārāudhāgāre niviṣṭamabhavanmadhu \|\| 51 \|\|*

*asurāṇāṃ vināśāya surāṇāṃ vijayāya ca \|*  
*dṛṣyante vividhotpātā ghorā ghoranidarśanāḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

*ete cānye ca bahavo ghorotpātāḥ samutthitāḥ \|*  
*daityendrasya vināśāya dṛṣyante kālanirmitāḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

50-53. In the afternoon the shadows of persons did not change. In the store-rooms and arsenal of Hiranyakashyapu, honey began to drop from the upper floors and at the same time many signs indicative of the victory of the Devas and the destruction of the demons were visible.

## \|\| 163.54-55 \|\|

*medinyāṃ kampamānāyāṃ daityendreṇa mahātmanā \|*  
*mahīdharā nāgagaṇā nipeturamitaujasaḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

*viṣajvālākulairvaktrair vimuñcanto hutāśanam \|*  
*catuḥśīrṣāḥ pañcaśīrṣāḥ saptaśīrṣāśca pannagāḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

54-55. Along with that valiant demon, the whole universe trembled; the multitudes of the powerful serpents and high mountains began to tremble. The four, five and the seven-hooded serpents agitated and exhausted, hissed out their fiery venom.

## \|\| 163.56-67 \|\|

*vāsukistakṣakaścaiva karkoṭakadhanaṃjayau \|*  
*elāmukhaḥ kāliyaśca mahāpadmaśca vīryavān \|\| 56 \|\|*

*sahasraśīrṣā nāgo vai hematāladhvajaḥ prabhuḥ \|*  
*śeṣo 'nanto mahābhāgo duṣprakampyaḥ prakampitaḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

*dīptānyantarjalasthāni pṛthivīdharaṇāni ca \|*  
*tadā kruddhena mahatā kampitāni samantataḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

*nāgāstejodharāścāpi pātālatalacāriṇaḥ \|*  
*hiraṇyakaśipurdaityas tadā saṃspṛṣṭavānmahīm \|\| 59 \|\|*

*saṃdaṣṭauṣṭhapuṭaḥ krodhād vārāha iva pūrvajaḥ \|*  
*nadī bhāgīrathī caiva sarayūḥ kauśikī tathā \|\| 60 \|\|*

*yamunā tvatha kāverī kṛṣṇaveṇā ca nimnagā \|*  
*suveṇā ca mahābhāgā nadī godāvarī tathā \|\| 61 \|\|*

*carmaṇvatī ca sindhuśca tathā nadanadīpatiḥ \|*  
*kamalaprabhavaścaiva śoṇo maṇinibhodakaḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

*narmadā śubhatoyā ca tathā vetravatī nadī \|*  
*gomatī gokulākīrṇā tathā pūrvasarasvatī \|\| 63 \|\|*

*mahī kālamahī caiva tamasā puṣpavāhinī \|*  
*jambūdvīpaṃ ratnavaṭaṃ sarvaratnopaśobhitam \|\| 64 \|\|*

*suvarṇaprakaṭaṃ caiva suvarṇākaramaṇḍitam \|*  
*mahānadaṃ ca lauhityaṃ śailakānanaśobhitam \|\| 65 \|\|*

*pattanaṃ kośakaraṇam ṛṣivīrajanākaram \|*  
*māgadhāśca mahāgrāmā muṇḍāḥ śuṅgāstathaiva ca \|\| 66 \|\|*

*suhmā mallā videhāśca mālavāḥ kāśikosalāḥ \|*  
*bhavanaṃ vainateyasya daityendreṇābhikampitam \|\| 67 \|\|*

56-67. Vasuki, Takshaka, Karkotika, Dhananaya, Alamukha, Kaliya, Mahapadma and the mighty Shesha, and Ananta with thousand hoods began to shudder with fear, though they were very firm. The luminous beings within the waters supporting the universe began to tremble with rage. Besides, the fiery serpents in the Patala regions trembled frequently wrathful Hiranyakashyapu at that time biting his lips with rage stood up like the Adivaraha the Boar incarnation, and caused the Ganges, the Sarayu, the Kaushiki, the Yamuna, the Kaveri, the Krishnaveni, the Suvahini, the Godavari, the Charmanvati, the Sindhu, the oceans, the Sonatirtha, the Narmada, the Vaitravati, the Gomati, the Sarasvati, the Mahi, the Kalamahi, the Tamasa, the Pushpavahini, the Jambudvipa with the golden banyan tree, the gold producing Mahanada Lauhitya, the city Pattan inhabited by many of the Rishis, and inhabited by the brave, Magadha, Mundi, Sunga, Sumha, Malla, Videha, MaIava, Kashikosala, the realm of Garuda created by Vishvakarma and looking like Kailasa peak, all to quake.

## \|\| 163.68-82 \|\|

*kailāsaśikharākāraṃ yatkṛtaṃ viśvakarmaṇā \|*  
*raktatoyo mahābhīmo lauhityo nāma sāgaraḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

*udayaśca mahāśaila ucchritaḥ śatayojanam \|*  
*suvarṇavedikaḥ śrīmān meghapaṅktiniṣevitaḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

*bhrājamāno 'rkasadṛśair jātarūpamayairdrumaiḥ \|*  
*śālaistālaistamālaiśca karṇikāraiśca puṣpitaiḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

*ayomukhaśca vikhyātaḥ parvato dhātumaṇḍitaḥ \|*  
*tamālavanagandhaśca parvato malayaḥ śubhaḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

*surāṣṭrāśca sabāhlīkāḥ śūrābhīrāstathaiva ca \|*  
*bhojāḥ pāṇḍyāśca vaṅgāśca kaliṅgāstāmraliptakāḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

*tathaivauṇḍrāśca pauṇḍrāśca vāmacūḍāḥ sakeralāḥ \|*  
*kṣobhitāstena daityena sadevāścāpsarogaṇāḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

*agastyabhavanaṃ caiva yadagamyaṃ kṛtaṃ purā \|*  
*siddhacāraṇasaṃghaśca viprakīrṇaṃ manoharam \|\| 74 \|\|*

*vicitranānāvihagaṃ supuṣpitamahādrumam \|*  
*jātarūpamayaiḥ śṛṅgair apsarogaṇanāditam \|\| 75 \|\|*

*giripuṣpitakaścaiva lakṣmīvānpriyadarśanaḥ \|*  
*utthitaḥ sāgaraṃ bhittvā viśrāmaścandrasūryayoḥ \|*  
*rarāja sumahāśṛṅgair gaganaṃ vilikhanniva \|\| 76 \|\|*

*candrasūryāṃśusaṃkāśaiḥ sāgarāmbusamāvṛtaiḥ \|*  
*vidyutvānsarvataḥ śrīmān āyataḥ śatayojanam \|\| 77 \|\|*

*vidyutāṃ yatra saṃpātā nipātyante nagottame \|*  
*ṛṣabhaḥ parvataścaiva śrīmānvṛṣabhasaṃjñitaḥ \|\| 78 \|\|*

*kuñjaraḥ parvataḥ śrīmān yatrāgastyagṛhaṃ śubham \|*  
*viśālākṣaśca durdharṣaḥ sarpāṇāmālayaḥ purī \|\| 79 \|\|*

*tathā bhogavatī cāpi daityendreṇābhikampitā \|*  
*mahāseno giriścaiva pāriyātraśca parvataḥ \|\| 80 \|\|*

*cakravāṃśca giriśreṣṭho vārāhaścaiva parvataḥ \|*  
*prāgjyautiṣapuraṃ cāpi jātarūpamayaṃ śubham \|\| 81 \|\|*

*yasminvasati duṣṭātmā narako nāma dānavaḥ \|*  
*meghaśca parvataśreṣṭho meghagambhīraniḥsvanaḥ \|\| 82 \|\|*

68-82 He also stunned the fearful Lauhityasagara full of red water, the Mount Udayachala 100 yojanas high encircled by clouds looking like golden altars; the Ayomukha mountain adorned with golden trees, Shala, Tala and Tamala plantations; with beautiful flowers and trees and bristling with all the ores; the mount Malayachala diffusing strong perfume; the countries of Saurashtra, Vahlika, Shura, Abhira, Bhoja, Pandya, Vanga, Kalinga, Tamraliptaka, Ondra, Paundra, Vamachuda, and Kerala. He made the groups of the nymphs with the Devas tremble; the mount Vidyutman, 100 yojanas wide, shining like lightning where there was the inaccessible hermitage of Agastya Rishi inhabited by the Siddhas and Charanas, echoed by the cooing of various birds, decked with, flowering trees, with its high peaks, soaring high into the Heavens like the Sun and the Moon; the wonderful Rishabha mountain, the mounts Kunjara, the irresistible Vishalakshta mount river Bhogavati, the mounts Mahasena, Pariyatra, Chakravaha, Uttamavaraha , the golden town of Pragyotishapur inhabited by the wicked Naraka, the mountain Megha, and other sixty thousand mountains all to tremble.

## \|\| 163.83-91 \|\|

*ṣaṣṭistatra sahasrāṇi parvatānāṃ dvijottamāḥ \|*  
*taruṇādityasaṃkāśo merustatra mahāgiriḥ \|\| 83 \|\|*

*yakṣarākṣasagandharvair nityaṃ sevitakaṃdaraḥ \|*  
*hemagarbho mahāśailas tathā hemasakho giriḥ \|\| 84 \|\|*

*kailāsaścaiva śailendro dānavendreṇa kampitaḥ \|*  
*hemapuṣkarasaṃchannaṃ tena vaikhānasaṃ saraḥ \|\| 85 \|\|*

*kampitaṃ mānasaṃ caiva haṃsakāraṇḍavākulam \|*  
*triśṛṅgaparvataścaiva kumārī ca saridvarā \|\| 86 \|\|*

*tuṣāracayasaṃchanno mandaraścāpi parvataḥ \|*  
*uśīrabinduśca giriś candraprasthastathādrirāṭ \|\| 87 \|\|*

*prajāpatigiriścaiva tathā puṣkaraparvataḥ \|*  
*devābhraparvataścaiva tathā vai reṇuko giriḥ \|\| 88 \|\|*

*krauñcaḥ saptarṣiśailaśca dhūmravarṇaśca parvataḥ \|*  
*ete cānye ca girayo deśā janapadāstathā \|\| 89 \|\|*

*nadyaḥ sasāgarāḥ sarvāḥ so 'kampayata dānavaḥ \|*  
*kapilaśca mahīputro vyāghravāṃścaiva kampitaḥ \|\| 90 \|\|*

*khecarāśca satīputrāḥ pātālatalavāsinaḥ \|*  
*gaṇastathā paro raudro meghanāmāṅkuśāudhaḥ \|\| 91 \|\|*

83-91. The Mount Sumeru glittering like gold, the caves of which are incessantly full of the Yakshas, Rakshasas and the Gandharvas; the mounts Hemagarbha, Hemasakha, Kailasha, were all shaken by Hiranyakashyapu. The lakes Vaikhanasa with golden lotuses, the Mansarovara surrounded by swans; the mount Trishringa, the river Kumari, the mount Mandarachala, the mounts Ushiravindu, Chandraprastha, Prajapati, Pushkara, Devabhra, Renuka, Krauncha, the mount of the seven Rishis, the smoky mount; all these and other countries, rivers and oceans and all the realms were shaken. Kapila, Vyaghravan, the son of Mahi, the sons of Sat residing in the skies, the dwellers in the lower regions; the Raudras, Urdhagas, Bhimagas and other attendants of Shiva were also shaken by the demon. Afterwards Hiranyakashyapu took the club and the trident and assumed a ferocious appearance.

## \|\| 163.92-94 \|\|

*ūrdhvago bhīmavegaśca sarva evābhikampitāḥ \|*  
*gadī śūlī karālaśca hiraṇyakaśipustadā \|\| 92 \|\|*

*jīmūtaghanasaṃkāśo jīmūtaghananiḥsvanaḥ \|*  
*jīmūtaghananirghoṣo jīmūta iva vegavān \|\| 93 \|\|*

*devārirditijo vīro nṛsiṃhaṃ samupādravat \|*  
*samutpatya tatastīkṣṇair mṛgendreṇa mahānakhaiḥ \|*  
*tadoṃkārasahāyena vidārya nihato udhi \|\| 94 \|\|*

92-94. The demon, shining, moving and roaring like the clouds, the enemy of the Devas, rushed at Vishnu when Narasimha supported by “Om”, jumped and tore the demon with His pointed nails. At the time of the destruction of the demon, the Earth, the Time, the Moon, the sky, the stars, the Sun, the planets, the directions, the mountains, the rivers, the oceans were all delighted.

## \|\| 163.95-96 \|\|

*mahī ca kālaśca śaśī nabhaśca grahāśca sūryaśca diśaśca sarvāḥ \|*  
*nadyaśca śailāśca mahārṇavāśca gatāḥ prasādaṃ ditiputranāśāt \|\| 95 \|\|*

*tataḥ pramuditā devā ṛṣayaśca tapodhanāḥ \|*  
*tuṣṭuvurnāmabhirdivyair ādidevaṃ sanātanam \|\| 96 \|\|*

95-96 Afterwards, the gratified Devas, the Rishis and the Gandharvas, jointly praised the Eternal Vishnu “O Deva! Your Narasimha form is adored by the learned, knowing the highest and the lowest.”

## \|\| 163.97-102 \|\|

*yattvayā vihitaṃ deva nārasiṃhamidaṃ vapuḥ \|*  
*etadevārcayiṣyanti parāvaravido janāḥ \|\| 97 \|\|*

*devā ūcuḥ*  
*bhavānbrahmā ca rudraśca mahendro devasattamaḥ \|*  
*bhavānkartā vikartā ca lokānāṃ prabhavo 'vyayaḥ \|\| 98 \|\|*

*parāṃ ca siddhiṃ ca paraṃ ca devaṃ paraṃ ca mantraṃ paramaṃ haviśca \|*  
*paraṃ ca dharmaṃ paramaṃ ca viśvaṃ tvāmāhuragryaṃ puruṣaṃ purāṇam \|\| 99 \|\|*

*paraṃ śarīraṃ paramaṃ ca brahma paraṃ ca yogaṃ paramāṃ ca vāṇīm \|*  
*paraṃ rahasyaṃ paramāṃ gatiṃ ca tvāmāhuragryaṃ puruṣaṃ purāṇam \|\| 100 \|\|*

*evaṃ parasyāpi paraṃ padaṃ yat paraṃ parasyāpi paraṃ ca devam \|*  
*paraṃ parasyāpi paraṃ ca bhūtaṃ tvāmāhuragryaṃ puruṣaṃ purāṇam \|\| 101 \|\|*

*paraṃ parasyāpi paraṃ rahasyaṃ paraṃ parasyāpi paraṃ mahattvam \|*  
*paraṃ parasyāpi paraṃ mahadyat tvāmāhuragryaṃ puruṣaṃ purāṇam \|\| 102 \|\|*

97-102. Brahma said: — “O Lord! Thou art Brahma, Rudra, Mahendra. Thou art the foremost among the Devas. Thou art the Creator, the Destroyer, the ultimate source of power to all the beings. The sages declare Thee the Paramasiddha, Paramadeva, Paramamantra, Paramahari, Parmadharma, Parama-sharira, Parama Brahma, Parmayoga, Parama-vani. Thom art Paramarahasya, Parmagati, Paramapada, Parma Deva. Thou art Paratpara, Parama Pada, Paratpara Deva, Paratpara Parama Bhuta, Paratpara Param a Rahasya, Paratpara Parama Mahatva, Paratpara Parama Mahat, Paratpara Parama Nidhana, Paratpara Pavitra, Paratpara Parama Danta, the great Ancient Purusha.”

## \|\| 163.103-105 \|\|

*paraṃ parasyāpi paraṃ nidhānaṃ paraṃ parasyāpi paraṃ pavitram \|*  
*paraṃ parasyāpi paraṃ ca dāntaṃ tvāmāhuragryaṃ puruṣaṃ purāṇam \|\| 103 \|\|*

*evamuktvā tu bhagavān sarvalokapitāmahaḥ \|*  
*stutvā nārāyaṇaṃ devaṃ brahmalokaṃ gataḥ prabhuḥ \|\| 104 \|\|*

*tato nadatsu tūryeṣu nṛtyantīṣvapsaraḥsu ca \|*  
*kṣīrodasyottaraṃ kūlaṃ jagāma harirīśvaraḥ \|\| 105 \|\|*

103-105. Thus praising Narayana, Brahma went to Brahma-loka and afterwards various kinds of music began to be played, the nymphs began to dance. Vishnu then went to the northern coast of the ocean Kshirabdhi, where after establishing His Narasimha form, He assumed His old form and returned to His realm riding on Garuda and seated in a magnificent illustrious chariot of eight wheels.

## Chapter 164

## \|\| 164.1-2 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ*  
*kathitaṃ narasiṃhasya māhātmyaṃ vistareṇa ca \|*  
*punastasyaiva māhātmyam anyadvistarato vada \|\| 1 \|\|*

*padmarūpamabhūdetat kathaṃ hemamayaṃ jagat \|*  
*kathaṃ ca vaiṣṇavī sṛṣṭiḥ padmamadhye 'bhavatpurā \|\| 2 \|\|*

1-2. The Rishis said: — “O Suta! You have described in detail the glory of Narasimha; now tell us something more in detail about His other glorious works. How did this universe become the golden lotus? What was ' the nature of Vishnu’s creation inside the lotus? ”

## \|\| 164.3 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*śrutvā ca narasiṃhasya māhātmyaṃ ravinandanaḥ \|*  
*vismayotphullanayanaḥ punaḥ papraccha keśavam \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Suta said: — Vaivasvata Manu was astonished to hear the glory of Narasimha; his eyes expressed great joy and he again asked the Lord.

## \|\| 164.4-14 \|\|

*manuruvāca*  
*kathaṃ pādme mahākalpe tava padmamayaṃ jagat \|*  
*jalārṇavagatasyeha nābhau jātaṃ janārdana \|\| 4 \|\|*

*prabhāvātpadmanābhasya svapataḥ sāgarāmbhasi \|*  
*puṣkare ca kathaṃ bhūtā devāḥ sarṣigaṇāḥ purā \|\| 5 \|\|*

*etadākhyāhi nikhilaṃ yogaṃ yogavidāṃ pate \|*  
*śṛṇvatastasya me kīrtiṃ na tṛptirupajāyate \|\| 6 \|\|*

*kiyatā caiva kālena śete vai puruṣottamaḥ \|*  
*kiyantaṃ vā svapiti ca ko 'sya kālasya saṃbhavaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*kiyatā vātha kālena hy uttiṣṭhati mahāyaśāḥ \|*  
*kathaṃ cotthāya bhagavān sṛjate nikhilaṃ jagat \|\| 8 \|\|*

*ke prajāpatayastāvad āsanpūrvaṃ mahāmune \|*  
*kathaṃ nirmitavāṃścaiva citraṃ lokaṃ sanātanam \|\| 9 \|\|*

*kathamekārṇave śūnye naṣṭasthāvarajaṅgame \|*  
*dagdhe devāsuranare pranaṣṭoragarākṣase \|\| 10 \|\|*

*naṣṭānilānale loke naṣṭākāśamahītale \|*  
*kevalaṃ gahvarībhūte mahābhūtaviparyaye \|\| 11 \|\|*

*vibhurmahābhūtapatir mahātejā mahākṛtiḥ \|*  
*āste suravaraśreṣṭho vidhimāsthāya yogavit \|\| 12 \|\|*

*śṛṇuyāṃ parayā bhaktyā brahmannetadaśeṣataḥ \|*  
*vaktumarhasi dharmiṣṭha yaśo nārāyaṇātmakam \|\| 13 \|\|*

*śraddhayā copaviṣṭānāṃ bhagavanvaktumarhasi \|\| 14 \|\|*

4-14. Manu said: — “O Janardana! During the Padma Maha Kalpa how was the universe first created in the lotus springing from Thy navel when Thou wert reposing in the ocean? Thou art named Padmanabha; how were the Devas and the Seers born first in the lotus springing up in the navel of Vishnu? Yogavidampate! pray explain the whole of this yoga for I am not sufficiently satisfied by listening to an account of His glory. When did Vishnu repose? How long did He remain asleep? What was the length of that period? When did He awake from His sleep? How did He create the universe after awakening? Who were the Prajapatis at the time of creation? How was created this wonderful eternal creation? On the annihilation of the moving and non-moving worlds, only a wide expanse of water remains. The Devas, the demons and the men were all destroyed. Fire, air, earth and Akasha did not exist; all were extinct. The whole universe seemed a big cave; void as it were. How then Janardana rest? What mode did He adopt? That Lord of the great Bhutas, that great form highly energetic, that knower of yoga, that Bhagavan, the best of all the Devas. O knower of Dharma! O Brahman I wish to hear all this with great devotion. Kindly describe in detail all this to me. Lord! I am very eager to hear about these things.”

## \|\| 164.15-17 \|\|

*matsya uvāca*  
*nārāyaṇasya yaśasaḥ śravaṇe yā tava spṛhā \|*  
*tadvaṃśyānvayabhūtasya nyāyyaṃ ravikularṣabha \|\| 15 \|\|*

*śṛṇuṣvādipurāṇeṣu vedebhyaśca yathā śrutam \|*  
*brāhmaṇānāṃ ca vadatāṃ śrutvā vai sumahātmanām \|\| 16 \|\|*

*yathā ca tapasā dṛṣṭvā bṛhaspatisamadyutiḥ \|*  
*parāśarasutaḥ śrīmān gururdvaipāyano 'bravīt \|\| 17 \|\|*

15-17. Hearing such words of Manu the Lord Matsya said: — “0 Manu, the flower of the solar race! It is very satisfactory indeed that you feel inclined to hear about the glory of Narayana. Hear about it as stated in the Puranas and the Vedas and as heard from the Brahmanas. I shall tell you what Vedavyasa, the son of Parashara, illustrious like Brihaspati saw, by virtue of his great asceticism, in his vision.”

## \|\| 164.25-26 \|\|

*sa eva bhagavānsarvaṃ karoti vikaroti ca \|*  
*so 'smānkārayate sarvān so 'tyeti vyākulīkṛtān \|\| 25 \|\|*

*yajāmahe tamevādyaṃ tamevecchāma nirvṛtāḥ \|*  
*yo vaktā yacca vaktavyaṃ yaccāhaṃ tadbravīmi vaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

25-26. (Veda Vyasa said: — ) O Rishis! There is no one other than me and the chief Rishis, who can comprehend and adequately realize the Highest Narayana and I shall tell you as I have been able to form some idea about Him by the help of my limited intellect and from what I have heard about Him. Even Brahma, the Creator of the Universe, is not able to know His essence; Narayana is the mystery of all the Vedas; He is what is proved there. He is the mystery of the Maharishis, that for which all sacrifices are made; the Tattva of all the seers, the Aim of the Thinkers, and the Hell of the Wicked; the Adhidaiva, the Daiva, the Adhibhuta, and the highest wisdom of the ideal Rishis He is the Yajna as described in the Vedas Tapas as described by the poets, He is the Doer; He is the Agent, He is the Buddhi, He is mind, He is Kshetrajna. He is Omkara, He is the Purusha, the Great Instructor, the Great Governor, and He is the only One, He is the five Pranas, He Is the Eternal undecaying One. He is Kala, Paka (friction), Pakta (awarder of fruits), the seer, and the study of the Vedas, He is this Narayana Deva and there is absolutely nothing beyond Him.

He is the Doer of everything. He is the Annihilator of all. He is the Creator of us all. He makes all work. He remains above all things. We are all in quest of Him and we all adore and worship Him.

## \|\| 164.27-28 \|\|

*śrūyate yacca vai śrāvyaṃ yaccānyatparijalpyate \|*  
*yāḥ kathāścaiva vartante śrutayo vātha tatparāḥ \|*  
*viśvaṃ viśvapatiryaśca sa tu nārāyaṇaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

*yatsatyaṃ yadamṛtamakṣaraṃ paraṃ yad yadbhūtaṃ paramamidaṃ ca yadbhaviṣyat \|*  
*yatkiṃcic caramacaraṃ yadasti cānyat tatsarvaṃ puruṣavaraḥ prabhuḥ purāṇaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

27-28. All the narrations, Gratis, etc., tend towards Him. He is the Universe. He is the Lord of the Universe, Who is also known as Narayana. He is Truth and Immortality; He is Eternal, Past, Future and the Present, the Purana-Purusha and Brahma.”

## Chapter 165

## \|\| 165.1-5 \|\|

*matsya uvāca*  
*catvāryāhuḥ sahasrāṇi varṣāṇāṃ tu kṛtaṃ ugam \|*  
*tasya tāvacchatī saṃdhyā dviguṇā ravinandana \|\| 1 \|\|*

*yatra dharmaścatuṣpādas tv adharmaḥ pādavigrahaḥ \|*  
*svadharmaniratāḥ santo jāyante yatra mānavāḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*viprāḥ sthitā dharmaparā rājavṛttau sthitā nṛpāḥ \|*  
*kṛṣyāmabhiratā vaiśyāḥ śūdrāḥ śuśrūṣavaḥ sthitāḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*tadā satyaṃ ca śaucaṃ ca dharmaścaiva vivardhate \|*  
*sadbhirācaritaṃ karma kriyate khyāyate ca vai \|\| 4 \|\|*

*etatkārtaugaṃ vṛttaṃ sarveṣāmapi pārthiva \|*  
*prāṇināṃ dharmasaṅgānām api vai nīcajanmanām \|\| 5 \|\|*

1-5. Matsya said: — O Manu! The age of Satyayuga is four thousand divine years. Its twilight is of eight hundred divine years. During that age the four feet of Dharma are complete; and there is one part of adharma, the people devoted to their own dharmas are born in that Yuga. All the Brahmanas are engaged in. the pursuit of high class dharma. The Kshatryas rule the Empire and are ready to please their subjects, the Vaishyas take to agriculture, and the Shudras render menial service to the three castes; In that age, truth, cleanliness, and dharma increased and every one followed and propagated the dharma practised by the high castes. King! The people in that age lead such a virtuous life and the low also keep themselves on the track of their dharma.

## \|\| 165.6-9 \|\|

*trīṇi varṣasahasrāṇi tretāugamihocyate \|*  
*tasya tāvacchatī saṃdhyā dviguṇā parikīrtyate \|\| 6 \|\|*

*dvābhyāmadharmaḥ pādābhyāṃ tribhirdharmo vyavasthitaḥ \|*  
*yatra satyaṃ ca sattvaṃ ca tretādharmo vidhīyate \|\| 7 \|\|*

*tretāyāṃ vikṛtiṃ yānti varṇāstvete na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*cāturvarṇyasya vaikṛtyād yānti daurbalyamāśramāḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*eṣā tretāugagatir vicitrā devanirmitā \|*  
*dvāparasya tu yā ceṣṭā tāmapi śrotumarhasi \|\| 9 \|\|*

6-9. The Treta age lasts for a period of three thousand divine years and its twilight is of six hundred years duration. Two pad as of adharma exist during that age and there are only three padas of dharma. There is truth and Sattvaguna in that dharma. The castes become, vitiated with regard to their functions in that age and the disturbance weakens the Varnas. This is the cycle of Treta age, now I shall describe Dvapara and hear about it.

## \|\| 165.10-13 \|\|

*dvāparaṃ dve sahasre tu varṣāṇāṃ ravinandana \|*  
*tasya tāvacchatī saṃdhyā dviguṇā ugamucyate \|\| 10 \|\|*

*tatra cārthaparāḥ sarve prāṇino rajasā hatāḥ \|*  
*sarve naiṣkṛtikāḥ kṣudrā jāyante ravinandana \|\| 11 \|\|*

*dvābhyāṃ dharmaḥ sthitaḥ padbhyām adharmastribhirutthitaḥ \|*  
*viparyayācchanairdharmaḥ kṣayameti kalau uge \|\| 12 \|\|*

*brāhmaṇyabhāvasya tatas tathautsukyaṃ viśīryate \|*  
*vratopavāsāstyajyante dvāpare ugaparyaye \|\| 13 \|\|*

10-13. O Manu! The age of Dvapara is two thousand divine years and its evening is of four hundred years. In that age, all the beings are stupefied by Rajoguna and are jealous and mean. Dharma exists only twofold and adharma is threefold. In Kaliyuga the twofold dharma becomes extinct by and by The Brahmanas lose their spirit and become lukewarm in their lies at the: close of Drapers and the fasts and vows become abandoned.

## \|\| 165.14-18 \|\|

*tathā varṣasahasraṃ tu varṣāṇāṃ dve śate api \|*  
*saṃdhyayā saha saṃkhyātaṃ krūraṃ kaliugaṃ smṛtam \|\| 14 \|\|*

*yatrādharmaścatuṣpādaḥ syāddharmaḥ pādavigrahaḥ \|*  
*kāminastapasā hīnā jāyante tatra mānavāḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*naivātisāttvikaḥ kaścin na sādhurna ca satyavāk \|*  
*nāstikā brahmabhaktā vā jāyante tatra mānavāḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*ahaṃkāragṛhītāśca prakṣīṇasnehabandhanāḥ \|*  
*viprāḥ śūdrasamācārāḥ santi sarve kalau uge \|\| 17 \|\|*

*āśramāṇāṃ viparyāsaḥ kalau samparivartate \|*  
*varṇānāṃ caiva saṃdeho ugānte ravinandana \|\| 18 \|\|*

14-18. Kaliyuga remains for a thousand divine years and its evening lasts for a couple of centuries. There are four feet of adharma during that age and dharma consists of only one. Men are overpowered, by tamoguna and they become sensuous during that age. The people of Kaliyuga are full of vanity and egoism and do not feel any love towards Jivas. None of them is predominant with Sattvaguna. None is truthful. The Brahmanas become atheists, conceited, void of attachment and- follows the duties of the Shudras. During Kaliyuga the ashramas are upset and the end of the age, the Varnas also become mixed.

## \|\| 165.19-23 \|\|

*vidyāddvādaśasāhasrīṃ ugākhyāṃ pūrvanirmitām \|*  
*evaṃ sahasraparyantaṃ tadaharbrāhmamucyate \|\| 19 \|\|*

*tato 'hani gate tasmin sarveṣāmeva jīvinām \|*  
*śarīranirvṛtiṃ dṛṣṭvā lokasaṃhārabuddhitaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*devatānāṃ ca sarvāsāṃ brahmādīnāṃ mahīpate \|*  
*daityānāṃ dānavānāṃ ca yakṣarākṣasapakṣiṇām \|\| 21 \|\|*

*gandharvāṇāmapsarasāṃ bhujaṃgānāṃ ca pārthiva \|*  
*parvatānāṃ nadīnāṃ ca paśūnāṃ caiva sattama \|*  
*tiryagyonigatānāṃ ca sattvānāṃ kṛmiṇāṃ tathā \|\| 22 \|\|*

*mahābhūtapatiḥ pañca hṛtvā bhūtāni bhūtakṛt \|*  
*jagatsaṃharaṇārthāya kurute vaiśasaṃ mahat \|\| 23 \|\|*

19-23. The period of the aforementioned four yagas is 12,000 years, when that period elapses it makes one day of Brahma. On the lapse of Brahma’s one day, Ishvara feels inclined to annihilate the creation on finding it apathetic. He destroys all the Devas including Brahma, the demons, the Yakshas, the birds, the Gandharvas, the nymphs, the serpents, the mountains, the rivers, the creatures like scorpions, etc., and various kinds of insects. He also destroys the five elements.

## \|\| 165.24 \|\|

*bhūtvā sūryaścakṣuṣī cādadāno bhūtvā vāuḥ prāṇināṃ prāṇajālam \|*  
*bhūtvā vahnirnirdahansarvalokān bhūtvā megho bhūya ugro 'pyavarṣat \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. The destruction of the universe starts like that when Vishnu in the shape of the Sun absorbs the eyes of all the beings, dries up everything in the form of wind, consumes everything in the form of fire and sends forth heavy rain in the form of clouds.

## Chapter 166

## \|\| 166.1-6 \|\|

*matsya uvāca*  
*bhūtvā nārāyaṇo yogī sattvamūrtirvibhāvasuḥ \|*  
*gabhastibhiḥ pradīptābhiḥ saṃśoṣayati sāgarān \|\| 1 \|\|*

*tataḥ pītvārṇavān sarvān nadīḥ kūpāṃśca sarvaśaḥ \|*  
*parvatānāṃ ca salilaṃ sarvamādāya raśmibhiḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*bhittvā gabhastibhiścaiva mahīṃ gatvā rasātalāt \|*  
*pātālajalamādāya pibate rasamuttamam \|\| 3 \|\|*

*mūtrāsṛkkledam anyacca yadasti prāṇiṣu dhruvam \|*  
*tatsarvamaravindākṣa ādatte puruṣottamaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*vāuśca balavānbhūtvā vidhunvāno 'khilaṃ jagat \|*  
*prāṇāpānasamānādyān vāyūn ākarṣate hariḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*tato devagaṇāḥ sarve bhūtānyeva ca yāni tu \|*  
*gandho ghrāṇaṃ śarīraṃ ca pṛthivīṃ saṃśritā guṇāḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*
