22\. Seeing such a fearful chaos, Varuna prompted by Indra said

## \|\| 175.23 \|\|

*purā brahmarṣijaḥ śakra tapastepe sudāruṇam \|*  
*ūrvaḥ sapūrvatejasvī sadṛśo brahmaṇo guṇaiḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. “Indra! Aurva has been created by the Brahma-Rishi’s son Urva in ancient times. The Brahma-Rishi became like Brahma by means of his asceticism.

**Комментарий:**

Note: Aurva. A celebrated Rishi. The sons of Kartavirya with the desire of destroying the family of Aurva killed even the children in the womb. One of the women in the family, however, in order to preserve her embryo secreted it in her thigh (Uru), whence the child at its birth was called Aurva. Beholding him the sons of Kartavirya were struck with blindness and his wrath gave rise to a flame which threatened to consume the whole world, had he hot at the desire of the Pitris east it into the ocean w b ere it remained concealed with the face of a horse. Aurvanala is also known as Vadavagni or Vadavanala. It is the submarine fire.

## \|\| 175.24 \|\|

*taṃ tapantamivādityaṃ tapasā jagadavyayam \|*  
*upatasthurmunigaṇā divyā devarṣibhiḥ saha \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Then the Maharishis and the Devas began to pray to the sage Urva who was shining like the Sun by virtue of his asceticism.

## \|\| 175.25-30 \|\|

*hiraṇyakaśipuścaiva dānavo dānaveśvaraḥ \|*  
*ṛṣiṃ vijñāpayāmāsuḥ purā paramatejasam \|\| 25 \|\|*

*ūcurbrahmarṣayastaṃ tu vacanaṃ dharmasaṃhitam \|*  
*ṛṣivaṃśeṣu bhagavaṃś chinnamūlamidaṃ padam \|\| 26 \|\|*

*ekastvamanapatyaśca gotrajo 'nyo na vartate \|*  
*kaumāraṃ vratamāsthāya kleśamevānuvartase \|\| 27 \|\|*

*bahūni vipra gotrāṇi munīnāṃ bhāvitātmanām \|*  
*ekadehāni tiṣṭhanti viviktāni vinā prajāḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

*evamucchinnamūlaiśca putrairno nāsti kāraṇam \|*  
*bhavāṃstu tapasā śreṣṭho prajāpātasamadyutiḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*tatra vartasva vaṃśāya vardhayātmānam ātmanā \|*  
*tvayā dharmo 'rjitastena dvitīyāṃ kuru vai tanum \|\| 30 \|\|*

25-30. The demon Hiranyakashyapu also appeared there. The Brahmarishis then said ‘Bhagvan! this Your attempt is to root out the race of the Rishis. You are the only survivor and there is none in your family and you are devoting yourself to rigid austerities in the flower of your life. So many sages are all by themselves without any offspring and in the same way the families of the Rishis have died out ated in the absence of any progeny. The Rishis is look entirely cut off from the world. You have become illustrious like Prajapati by virtue of your asceticism, but you should also beget a son for the continuance of your family. You have renounced householder’s life; therefore create another body by getting another soul out of your own.’

## \|\| 175.31-36 \|\|

*sa evamukto munibhir munir marmasu tāḍitaḥ \|*  
*jagarhe tānṛṣigaṇān vacanaṃ cedamabravīt \|\| 31 \|\|*

*yathāyaṃ vihito dharo munīnāṃ śāśvataḥ purā \|*

*brahmayonau prasūtasya brāhmaṇasyātmadarśinaḥ \|*

*janānāṃ vṛttayastisro ye gṛhāśramavāsinaḥ \|*  
*asmākaṃ tu varaṃ vṛttir vanāśramanivāsinām \|\| 34 \|\|*

*abbhakṣā vāubhakṣāśca dantolūkhalinastathā \|*

*ete tapasi tiṣṭhanti vratairapi suduṣkaraiḥ \|*  
*brahmacaryaṃ puraskṛtya prārthayanti parāṃ gatim \|\| 36 \|\|*

31-36. Those words went deep into the heart of Urva who despising these Rishis said ‘ the highest duty of the Rishis, as enjoined by the Shastras, is to pass their days in the forest, living on the produce of nature, for a Brahmana ought to strictly observe Brahmacharya. In that case he can shake the position of Brahma. The householders have threefold duties to discharge, but those of them living in the forest ought to follow our ways. The Rishis living merely on water, air, grain and on things powdered by stones, simply warming themselves in the fires burning all round them, practising Dashatapah and Panchatapah, all of them thus pursuing the — course of rigid asceticism, seek final emancipation by leading a life of celibacy.

## \|\| 175.37-39 \|\|

*brahyacaryādbrāhmaṇasya brāhmaṇatvaṃ vidhīyate \|*  
*evamāhuḥ pare loke brahmacaryavido janāḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

*brahmacarye sthitaṃ satyaṃ brahmacarye sthitaṃ tapaḥ \|*  
*ye sthitā brahmacarye tu brāhmaṇā divi saṃsthitāḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

*nāsti yogaṃ vinā siddhir na vā siddhiṃ vinā yaśaḥ \|*  
*nāsti loke yaśomūlaṃ brahmacaryātparaṃ tapaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

37-39. A true Brahmana becomes as such only by virtue of Brahmacharya, and others, knowing what Brahmacharya is, also say that fortitude is established in Brahmacharya. And asceticism is also established in the practice of Brahmacharya. The Brahmana fixed in his austerities is really enshrined in heaven. There is no Siddhi without Yoga, and there is no fruit without Siddhi. There is no higher name and fame than Brahmacharya which is the root of all.

## \|\| 175.40 \|\|

*yo nigṛhyendriyagrāmaṃ bhūtagrāmaṃ ca pañcakam \|*

40\. There is no greater ascetic than the one who strictly follows Brahmacharya by subduing all his passions.

## \|\| 175.41 \|\|

*ayoge keśadharaṇam asaṃkalpavratakriyāṃ \|*

41\. It is hypocrisy to grow long hair without asceticism, to pursue any vow without any resolution, and to practise Tapasya without Brahmacharya. These three are simply signs of vanity.

## \|\| 175.42 \|\|

*kva dārāḥ kva ca saṃyogaḥ kva ca bhāvaviparyayaḥ \|*

42\. Where is wife? and where is Yoga? and where is the perversion of thought? Great differences he between these.

## \|\| 175.43 \|\|

*yadyasti tapaso vīryaṃ uṣmākaṃ viditātmanām \|*

43\. Brahma has created all these by His mental power. If one has the seed of asceticism within him, he can create a son from his mind. Verily you are the knowers of selves. Then why do you not create such children by the force of mind alone?

## \|\| 175.44-47 \|\|

*manasā nirmitā yonir ādhātavyā tapasvibhiḥ \|*  
*na dārayogo bījaṃ vā vratamuktaṃ tapasvinām \|\| 44 \|\|*

*yadidaṃ luptadharmārthaṃ uṣmābhiriha nirbhayaiḥ \|*  
*vyāhṛtaṃ sadbhiratyartham asadbhiriva me matam \|\| 45 \|\|*

*vapurdīptāntarātmānam etatkṛtvā manomayam \|*

*evamātmānamātmā me dvitīyaṃ janayiṣyati \|*

44-47. The ascetics ought to beget progeny out of the embryo created by their mind, and your address to me is bereft of dharma, and is like the speech of those who are not good. By the power of my inner self, I shall create a son, without the help of a woman, after illumining ray mind with the glory of asceticism. I shall create such a son out of my soul, who would be ready to consume the creation.”

## \|\| 175.48-50 \|\|

*ūrvastu tapasāviṣṭo niveśyoruṃ hutāśane \|*

*tasyoruṃ sahasā bhittvā jvālāmālī hyanindhanaḥ \|*  
*jagato dahanākāṅkṣī putro 'gniḥ samapadyata \|\| 49 \|\|*

*ūrvasyoruṃ vinirbhidya aurvo nāmāntako 'nalaḥ \|*  
*didhakṣanniva lokāṃstrīñ jajñe paramakopanaḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

48-50. Afterwards the sage Urva, absorbed in his asceticism, throwing his thighs into the fire rubbed them with a kusha grass. Then the son in the form of Fire, desirous of consuming the universe, was produced from his thigh, by its own force without the help of any firewood. In such a way the fearful fire Aurva was begotten from the thigh of the seer Urva.

## \|\| 175.51-52 \|\|

*utpannamātraścovāca pitaraṃ kṣīṇayā girā \|*  
*kṣudhā me bādhate tāta jagadbhakṣye tyajasva mām \|\| 51 \|\|*

*tridivārohibhirjvālair jṛmbhamāṇo diśo daśa \|*  
*nirdahansarvabhūtāni vavṛdhe so 'ntako 'nalaḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

51-52. That son of Urva said with a feeble voice, to his father, immediately on being born “Father! I am oppressed by hunger, pray direct me to consume the universe.” Saying so, the fire Aurva ascended to heaven, and with the intention of consuming everything all round, increased itself in bulk, and spread itself in all directions.

## \|\| 175.53 \|\|

*etasminnantare brahmā munimūrvaṃ sabhājayan \|*  
*uvāca vāryatāṃ putro jagataśca dayāṃ kuru \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Afterwards Brahma said to Urva ‘Pray save the universe from the fury of your son.

## \|\| 175.54 \|\|

*asyāpatyasya te vipra kariṣye sthānamuttamam \|*  
*tathyametadvacaḥ putra śṛṇu tvaṃ vadatāṃ vara \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. ‘Brahmana! I shall assign a very good place to your son. Have full confidence in my words.’

## \|\| 175.55-57 \|\|

*ūrva uvāca*  
*dhanyo 'smyanugṛhīto 'smi yanme 'dya bhagavāñchiśoḥ \|*  
*matimetāṃ dadātīha paramānugrahāya vai \|\| 55 \|\|*

*prabhātakāle samprāpte kāṅkṣitavye samāgame \|*  
*bhagavaṃstarpitaḥ putraḥ kairhavyaiḥ prāpsyate sukham \|\| 56 \|\|*

*kutra cāsya nivāsaḥ syād bhojanaṃ vā kimātmakam \|*  
*vidhāsyatīha bhagavān vīryatulyaṃ mahaujasaḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

55-57. Urva said: — “To-day I am blessed. You have shown me a great kindness by promising a place for my son. Bhagavan! what oblations will my son get when he feels hungry in the morning? What will be the place of his stay and what arrangements will be made for his food?’ Those things should be arranged in a manner be-fitting the position of my son.”

## \|\| 175.58-59 \|\|

*brahmovāca*  
*vaḍavāmukhe 'sya vasatiḥ samudre vai bhaviṣyati \|*  
*mama yonirjalaṃ vipra tasya pītavataḥ sukham \|\| 58 \|\|*

*yatrāhamāsa niyataṃ pibanvārimayaṃ haviḥ \|*  
*taddhavistava putrasya visṛjāmyālayaṃ ca tat \|\| 59 \|\|*

58-59. Brahma said: — ‘This son of yours will stay as the submarine fire in the ocean and: O Brahmana! I am also born of water. He will be gratified to drink it. I am giving the same butter-like water to your son which I also drink in course of my stay in it.

## \|\| 175.60-61 \|\|

*tato ugānte bhūtānām eṣa cāhaṃ ca putraka \|*  
*sahitau vicariṣyāvo niṣputrāṇāmṛṇāpahaḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

*eṣo 'gnir antakāle tu salilāśī mayā kṛtaḥ \|*  
*dahanaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ sadevāsurarakṣasām \|\| 61 \|\|*

60-61. ‘At the end of the yugas, your son and I will wander about in mutual company’ when we will repay the debts of those who are sonless. Later on, the same fire will dry up all the waters. Besides he will burn up all the Devas, Asuras, Yakshas, Rakshasas, etc., and all other elements.’

## \|\| 175.62-63 \|\|

*evamastviti taṃ so 'gniḥ saṃvṛtajvālamaṇḍalaḥ \|*  
*praviveśārṇavamukhaṃ prakṣipya pitari prabhām \|\| 62 \|\|*

*pratiyātastato brahmā ye ca sarve maharṣayaḥ \|*  
*aurvasyāgneḥ prabhāṃ jñātvā svāṃ svāṃ gatimupāśritāḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

62-63. Hearing those words of Brahma, Urva said ‘Be it so.’ When the fire merged into the ocean, after throwing his lustre into his father. Then Brahmi and other Rishis resumed their pursuits undisturbed, on realizing the glory of fire, the son of Urva.

## \|\| 175.64-67 \|\|

*hiraṇyakaśipurdṛṣṭvā tadā tanmahadadbhutam \|*  
*uccaiḥ praṇatasarvāṅgo vākyametaduvāca ha \|\| 64 \|\|*

*bhagavannadbhutamidaṃ saṃvṛttaṃ lokasākṣikam \|*  
*tapasā te muniśreṣṭha parituṣṭaḥ pitāmahaḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

*ahaṃ tu tava putrasya tava caiva mahāvrata \|*  
*bhṛtya ityavagantavyaḥ sādhyo yadiha karmaṇā \|\| 66 \|\|*

*tanmāṃ paṣya samāpannaṃ tavaivārādhane ratam \|*  
*yadi sīdenmuniśreṣṭha tavaiva syātparājayaḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

64-67. The demon Hiranyakashyapu beholding that wonder of Urva Rishi spoke, after making a series of salutations. “O Rishi! It is indeed highly surprising that Agni the witness of the universe has merged into you and Brahma has also become pleased with your devotion. Great sage! I have come to you as your and your son’s slave. Pray look with a favourable eye on your devotee. Sire! If I suffer it will be like your defeat.”

## \|\| 175.68-71 \|\|

*aurva uvāca*  
*dhanyo 'smyanugṛhīto 'smi yasya te 'haṃ guruḥ sthitaḥ \|*  
*nāsti me tapasānena bhayamadyeha suvrata \|\| 68 \|\|*

*tāmeva māyāṃ gṛhṇīṣva mama putreṇa nirmitām \|*  
*nirindhanāmagnimayīṃ durdharṣāṃ pāvakairapi \|\| 69 \|\|*

*eṣā te svasya vaṃśasya vaśagārivinigrahe \|*  
*saṃrakṣatyātmapakṣaṃ ca vipakṣaṃ ca pradhakṣyati \|\| 70 \|\|*

*evamastviti tāṃ gṛhya praṇamya munipuṃgavam \|*  
*jagāma tridivaṃ hṛṣṭaḥ kṛtārtho dānaveśvaraḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

68-71. Urva said: — ‘lam gratified, because I have now become your preceptor. I have now no fear of danger on account of my asceticism. You should also embrace the May! created by my son, who, though without any fuel is more violent than Pavaka the ordinary fire. This Maya will protect your family and destroy your enemies and will be unbearable to the adversary.’ Hearing those words the demon Hiranyakashyapu embracing her (Maya) went to heaven after bowing to Urva Muni very much gratified.

## \|\| 175.72 \|\|

*eṣā durviṣahā māyā devairapi durāsadā \|*  
*aurveṇa nirmitā pūrvaṃ pāvakenorvasūnunā \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. The mighty Maya, created by Aurva the son of the sage Urva, was unbearable even by the Devas.

## \|\| 175.74-75 \|\|

*yadyeṣā pratihantavyā kartavyo bhagavānsukhī \|*  
*dīyatāṃ me sakhā śakra toyayonirniśākaraḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

*tenāhaṃ saha saṃgamya yādobhiśca samāvṛtaḥ \|*  
*māyāmetāṃ haniṣyāmi tvatprasādānna saṃśayaḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

74-75. Now Hiranyakashyapu being dead, this Maya had become comparatively weak. Also the sage, who was the author of that Maya, cursed him. I have narrated this all to you, said Varuna to Indra; so that in case you want the Maya to be destroyed, you should let the Moon go with me to render me assistance, and I shall undoubtedly destroy it, with his co-operation, by means of water.

## Chapter 176

## \|\| 176.1 \|\|

*matsya uvāca*  
*evamastviti saṃhṛṣ̣ṭaḥ śakrastridaśavardhanaḥ\|*  
*saṃdideśāgrataḥ somaṃ yuddhāya śiśirāyudham*

Matsya said- After hearing the words of Varuna, Indra the lord of gods said ‘be it so’, and gladly directed the Moon to proceed for the war.

## \|\| 176.2 \|\|

*gaccha soma sahāyatvaṃ kuru pāśadharasya vai\|*  
*asurāṇāṃ vināśāya jayārthaṃ ca divaukasām*

He said “O Moon! Go and help Varuna; thus carry out the rescue of the gods and the destruction of the demons.

## \|\| 176.3-4\|\|

*tvaṃ mattaḥ prativīryaśca jyotiṣ̣āṃ ceśvareśvaraḥ\|*  
*tvanmayaṃ sarvalokeṣ̣u rasaṃ rasavido viduḥ \|\| 176.3 \|\|*

*kṣ̣ayavṛddhī tava vyakte sāgarasyeva maṇḍale\|*  
*parivartasyahorātraṃ kālaṃ jagati yojayan \|\| 176.4 \|\|*

You are more powerful than me. You are the Lord of the heavenly bodies. Knower of the Rasas, you know the place of all Rasa, of universe and you pervade all the realms with your elixir which like the ocean, waxing and waning exits in you. You bring about by your diurnal motion the day and the night.

## \|\| 176.5-7 \|\|

*lokacchāyāmayaṃ lakṣ̣ma tavāṅkaḥ śaśasaṃnibhaḥ\|*  
*na viduḥ soma devāpi ye ca nakṣ̣atrayonayaḥ \|\| 176.5 \|\|*

*tvamādityapathādūrdhvaṃ jyotiṣ̣āṃ copari sthitaḥ\|*  
*tamaḥ protsārya mahasā bhāsayasyakhilaṃ jagat \|\| 176.6 \|\|*

*śvetabhānurhimatanurjyotiṣ̣āmadhipaḥ śaśī\|*  
*adhikṛtkālayogātmā iṣ̣ṭo yajñaraso'vyayaḥ \|\| 176.7 \|\|*

Your spot, in the form of a hare, is indicative of your giving shelter to the universe and even the Devas and the celestial bodies do not know the full significance of your power. You are located above the Sun and the other heavenly bodies. You by your glory dispel the universal gloom and make it bright and luminous. Your rays are white; your body is made up of snow; you are the lord of stars, you are with the spot of a hare, you are eternal, the form of Kalayoga, and the final beatitude of sacrifices.

## \|\| 176.8-10 \|\|

*oṣ̣adhīśaḥ kriyāyonirharaśekharabhāktathā\|*  
*śītāṃśuramṛtādhāraścapalaḥ śvetavāhanaḥ \|\| 176.8 \|\|*

*tvaṃ kāntiḥ kāntivapuṣ̣āṃ tvaṃ somaḥ somapāyinām\|*  
*saumyastvaṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ timiraghnastvamṛkṣ̣arāṭ \|\| 176.9 \|\|*

*tadgaccha tvaṃ mahāsena varuṇena varūthinā\|*  
*śamaya tvāsurīṃ māyāṃ yayā dahyāma saṃyuge \|\| 176.10 \|\|*

You the Lord of the herbs, the source of actions, begotten from water, producer of lotus and other aquatic plants, most cool, the receptacle of nectar, nimble, having white conveyance, You are the beauty of the beautiful; you are the Soma of the drinkers of Soma; you are the very gentle among all beings; and you are the Lord of stars, the displler of darkness. О mighty one! go with the army of Varuna, and relieve us by destroying this Asurl Maya. We are all tormented in the battlefield.”

## \|\| 176.11-12 \|\|

*soma uvāca*  
*yanmāṃ vadasi yuddhārthe devarāja varaprada\|*  
*eṣ̣a varṣ̣āmi śiśiraṃ daityamāyāpakarṣ̣aṇam \|\| 176.11 \|\|*

*etānmacchītanirdagdhānpaśya tvaṃ himaveṣ̣ṭitān\|*  
*vimāyānvimadāṃścaiva daityasiṃhānmahāhave \|\| 176.12 \|\|*

The Moon said- “О Lord of the gods and giver of boons! on your words, I shall pour down a heavy dew for destruction of the demons. See the Demons in this great war void of their conceit and the store of their delusion exhausted. I will envelop the Daityas with severe cold; I will bum them chill and I will make the Demons void of their pride.”

## \|\| 176.13-15 \|\|

*teṣ̣āṃ himakarotsṛṣ̣ṭāḥ sapāśā himavṛṣ̣ṭayaḥ\|*  
*veṣ̣ṭayanti sma tānghorāndaityānmeghagaṇā iva \|\| 176.13 \|\|*

*Thus saying the Moon showered torrents of cold, while Varuna hurled his noose. The demons under the influence of these began to lie inert and dead.*

*tau pāśaśītāṃśudharau varuṇendū mahābalau\|*  
*jaghnuturhimapātaiśca pāśapātaiśca dānavān \|\| 176.14 \|\|*

*dvāvambunāthau samare tau pāśahimayodhinau\|*  
*mṛdhe ceraturambhombhobhiḥ kṣ̣ubdhāviva mahārṇavau \|\| 176.15 \|\|*

Thus Varuna and the Moon both started the annihilation of the demons by showering cold on them. Both those Lords of the waters, fighting by the store of their freezing resources, roamed about in the field like the ferocious oceans.

## \|\| 176.16-20\|\|

*tābhyāmāplāvitaṃ sainyaṃ taddānavamadṛśyata\|*  
*jagatsaṃvartakāmbhodaiḥ praviṣ̣ṭairiva saṃvṛtam \|\| 176.16 \|\|*

*tāvudyatāmbunāthau tu śaśāṅkavaruṇāvubhau\|*  
*śamayāmāsaturmāyāṃ devau daityendra nirmitām \|\| 176.17 \|\|*

*śītāṃśujālanirdagdhāḥ pāśaiśca spanditā raṇe\|*  
*na śekuścalituṃ daityā viśiraskā ivādra yaḥ \|\| 176.18 \|\|*

*śītāṃśunihatāste tu daityāstoyahimārditāḥ\|*  
*himāplāvitasarvāṅgā nirūṣ̣māṇa ivāgnayaḥ \|\| 176.19 \|\|*

*teṣ̣āṃ tu divi daityānāṃ viparītaprabhāṇi vai\|*  
*vimānāni vicitrāṇi prapatantyutpatanti ca \|\| 176.20 \|\|*

Varuna and the Moon pouring down showers of rain, like those that descend at the time of the annihilation of the universe, totally destroyed the delusive fire. The demons, benumbed by the cold showers of the Moon and entangled in the noose of Varuna, could not move their limbs any way, and they all looked like the mountains with dismantled crests. The Moon beams and the cold showers of Varuna entirely unhinged the demons. Their chariots deprived of all lustre fell down tossing from the heaven.

## \|\| 176.21-25 \|\|

*tānpāśahastagrathitāṃśchāditāñchītaraśmibhiḥ\|*  
*mayo dadarśa māyāvī dānavāndivi dānavaḥ \|\| 176.21 \|\|*

*sa śilājālavitatāṃ khaḍgacarmāṭṭahāsinīm\|*  
*pādapotkaṭakūṭāgrāṃ kandarākīrṇakānanām \|\| 176.22 \|\|*

*siṃhavyāghragaṇākīrṇāṃ nadadbhirgajayūthapaiḥ\|*  
*īhāmṛgagaṇākīrṇāṃ pavanāghūrṇitadrumām \|\| 176.23 \|\|*

*nirmitāṃ svena yatnena kūjitāṃ divi kāmagām\|*  
*prathitāṃ pārvatīṃ māyāmasṛjatsa samantataḥ \|\| 176.24 \|\|*

*sāsiśabdaiḥ śilāvarṣ̣aiḥ saṃpatadbhiśca pādapaiḥ\|*  
*jaghāna devasaṃghāṃśca dānavāṃścāpyajīvayat \|\| 176.25 \|\|*

Maya Danava saw the demons in the sky bound allside by the illusion created by the Moon and Varuna. He then introduced his Parvatl Maya which suddenly pervaded all space with rocks, swords, shields, dense forests teaming with yawning caves and roaring lions and elephants, full of herds of deer and wind, containing huge trees and moving by the force of wind in the heavens at will. Then Candri and VarunI Mayas of the Moon and Varuna suddenly disappeared. And the moment such a delusion was introduced swords, rocks, trees began to pour down upon the Devas, who began to be destroyed and the demons regained a safe footing.

## \|\| 176.26-29 \|\|

*naiśākarī vāruṇī ca māye'ntardadhatustataḥ\|*  
*asibhiścā’yasagaṇaiḥ kirandevagaṇānraṇe \|\| 176.26 \|\|*

*sāśmayantrāyudhaghanā drumaparvatasaṃkaṭā\|*  
*abhavadghorasaṃcārā pṛthivī parvatairiva \|\| 176.27 \|\|*

*aśmanā prahatāḥ kecicchilābhiḥ śakalīkṛtāḥ\|*  
*nāniruddho drumagaṇairdevo'dṛśyata kaścana \|\| 176.28 \|\|*

*tadapadhvastadhanuṣ̣aṃ bhagnapraharaṇāvilam\|*  
*niṣ̣prapatnaṃ surānīkaṃ varjayitvā gadādharam \|\| 176.29 \|\|*

All the delusions of the Moon and Varuna were made useless. The Devas began to die of the heavy sword blows. There was a huge shower of rocks, trees, etc., which filled the universe like the heavy rain. At that time many Devas were powdered by the rocks, several were divided into pieces by them, a good many were covered with trees. The bows of many were broken and they were all bewildered and helpless. No one excepting Lord Visnu remained powerful. The other Devas disappeared.

## \|\| 176.30-31 \|\|

*sa hi yuddhagataḥ śrīmānīśo na sma vyakampata\|*  
*sahiṣ̣ṇutvājжagatsvāmī na cukrodha gadādharaḥ \|\| 176.30 \|\|*

*kālajñaḥ kālameghābhaḥ samīkṣ̣ankālamāhave\|*  
*devāsuravimardaṃ tu dra ṣ̣ṭukāmastadā hariḥ \|\| 176.31 \|\|*

Maya demon in that battle waved the rocks over Lord Visnu, but Gadadhara showed His perseverance and did not show the least anger. The knower of Kala, Lord Visnu like the splendour of clouds at the time of the destruction of the universe, stood there with desire of looking the conflict of Devas and Asuras.

## \|\| 176.32-34 \|\|

*tato bhagavatā dṛṣ̣ṭau raṇe pāvakamārutau\|*  
*coditau viṣ̣ṇuvākyena tau māyāmapakarṣ̣atām \|\| 176.32 \|\|*

*tābhyāmudbhrāntavegābhyāṃ pravṛddhābhyāṃ mahāhave\|*  
*dagdhā sā pārvatī māyā bhasmībhūtā nanāśa ha \|\| 176.33 \|\|*

*so'nilo'nalasaṃyuktaḥ so'nalaścānilākulaḥ\|*  
*daityasenāṃ dadahaturyugānteṣ̣viva mūrchitau \|\| 176.34 \|\|*

Then Lord saw both Agni and Vayu in that conflict, and Lord inspired them both to dispel the delusion, at which they annihilated that Parvatl Maya. Vayu with Agni consumed the demons, just as beings are reduced to ashes at the destruction of the universe.

## \|\| 176.35 \|\|

*vāyuḥ pradhāvitastatra paścādagnistu mārutam\|*  
*ceraturdānavānīke krīḍantāvanilānalau \|\| 176.35 \|\|*

The wind blew fiercely and was followed by fire. In that way the Vayu and Agni started their play to havoc in the troop of Danavas.

## \|\| 176.36 \|\|

*bhasmāvayavabhūteṣ̣u prapatatsūtpatatsu ca\|*  
*dānavānāṃ vimāneṣ̣u nipatatsu samantataḥ \|\| 176.36 \|\|*

Agni in company of the wind burnt the limbs of the demons. The army of demons started to run away. The Vimanas of the demons started falling down with everything all round.

## \|\| 176.37 \|\|

*vātaskandhāpaviddheṣ̣u kṛtakarmaṇi pāvake\|*  
*māyābandhe nivṛtte tu stūyamāne gadādhare \|\| 176.37 \|\|*

When wind consumed the shoulders of the demons, and Fire has done all his deeds, the Parvatl Maya disappeared. At that time Visnu was praised by the gods.

## \|\| 176.38-40 \|\|

*niṣ̣prayatneṣ̣u daityeṣ̣u trailokye muktabandhane\|*  
*saṃprahṛṣ̣ṭeṣ̣u deveṣ̣u sādhu sādhviti sarvaśaḥ \|\| 176.38 \|\|*

*jaye daśaśatākṣ̣asya daityānāṃ ca parājaye\|*  
*dikṣ̣u sarvāsu śuddhāsu pravṛtte dharmavistare \|\| 176.39 \|\|*

*apāvṛte candra masi svasthānasthe divākare\|*  
*prakṛtistheṣ̣u lokeṣ̣u triṣ̣u cāritrabandhuṣ̣u \|\| 176.40 \|\|*

All Daityas became effortless and three worlds were freed from bondage. The Devas cried out “Victory! Victory!” and all the plans of the demons were frustrated. The three realms were liberated from bondage. The Devas were gratified and the din of “Bravo! Bravo!” filled the space. Indra was victorious and the demons were defeated. All the directions were cleared. Dharma increased and the Sun and the Moon returned to their respective realms, and the three realms were restored to their natural state. All beings started their work with good conduct and brotherhood.

## \|\| 176.41-42 \|\|

*yajamāneṣ̣u bhūteṣ̣u praśānteṣ̣u ca pāpmasu\|*  
*abhinnabandhane mṛtyau hūyamāne hutāśane \|\| 176.41 \|\|*

*yajñaśobhiṣ̣u deveṣ̣u svargārthaṃ darśayatsu ca\|*  
*lokapāleṣ̣u sarveṣ̣u dikṣ̣u saṃyānavartiṣ̣u \|\| 176.42 \|\|*

Every one began to perform sacrifices, sins were subdued, death was curbed, sacrificial oblations began to be poured into the fire, the Devas ascending to heaven began to survey the glory of the sacrifices and all the Lokapalas returned to their quarters.

## \|\| 176.43-46 \|\|

*bhāve tapasi siddhānāmabhāve pāpakarmaṇām\|*  
*devapakṣ̣e pramudite daityapakṣ̣e viṣ̣īdati \|\| 176.43 \|\|*

*tripādavigrahe dharme adharme pādavigrahe\|*  
*apāvṛtte mahādvāre vartamāne ca satpathe \|\| 176.44 \|\|*

*loke pravṛtte dharmeṣ̣u saddharmeṣ̣vāśrameṣ̣u ca\|*  
*prajārakṣ̣aṇayukteṣ̣u bhrājamāneṣ̣u rājasu \|\| 176.45 \|\|*

*praśāntakalmaṣ̣e loke śānte tamasi dānave\|*  
*agnimārutayostatra vṛtte saṅgrāmakarmaṇi \|\| 176.46 \|\|*

Ascetics flourished, the sinners declined. The followers of the Devas were pleased and those of the demons became sad. Dhanna reigned over three-fourths of the world and adharma existed in only one. The path of virtue flourished and the people became righteous. Every one began to follow his order of life and the kings began to devote themselves to the protection of their subjects. The sins of the universe were subdued by the subjugation of the demons by the Fire and the Wind.

## \|\| 176.47-51 \|\|

*tanmayā vipulā lokāstābhyāṃ kṛtajayakriyāḥ\|*  
*pūrvaṃ daityabhayaṃ śrutvā mārutāgnikṛtaṃ mahat \|\| 176.47 \|\|*

*kālanemīti vikhyāto dānavaḥ pratyadṛśyata\|*  
*bhāskarākāramukuṭaḥ śiñjitābharaṇāṅgadaḥ \|\| 176.48 \|\|*

*mandarādri pratīkāśo mahārajatasaṃvṛtaḥ\|*  
*śatapraharaṇodagraḥ śatabāhuḥ śatānanaḥ \|\| 176.49 \|\|*

*śataśīrṣ̣aḥ sthitaḥ śrīmāñchataśṛṅga ivācalaḥ\|*  
*kakṣ̣e mahati saṃvṛddho nidāgha iva pāvakaḥ \|\| 176.50 \|\|*

*dhūmrakeśo haricchmaśruḥ saṃdaṣ̣ṭauṣ̣ṭhapuṭānanaḥ\|*  
*trailokyāntaravistāri dhārayanvipulaṃ vapuḥ \|\| 176.51 \|\|*

The whole universe became radiant with the lustre of Agni. Kalanemi hearing about the violence of Agni and Vayu appeared on the field. He was wearing a coronet shining like the Sun and was bedecked with tingling armlets and ornaments. He looked tall like Mandara mountain; golden coloured; he had hundred arms, hundred faces, hundred heads and appeared like a mountain with hundred peaks.

## \|\| 176.52-56 \|\|

*bāhubhistulayanvyoma kṣ̣ipanpadbhyāṃ mahīdharān\|*  
*īrayanmukhaniḥśvāsairvṛṣ̣ṭiyuktānbalāhakān \|\| 176.52 \|\|*

*tiryagāyataraktākṣ̣aṃ mandarodagravarcasam\|*  
*didhakṣ̣antamivā’yāntaṃ sarvāndevagaṇānmṛdhe \|\| 176.53 \|\|*

*tarjayantaṃ suragaṇāṃśchādayantaṃ diśo daśa\|*  
*saṃvartakāle tṛṣ̣itaṃ dṛṣ̣ṭaṃ mṛtyumivotthitam \|\| 176.54 \|\|*

*sutalenocchrayavatā vipulāṅguliparvaṇā\|*  
*lambābharaṇapūrṇena kiṃciccalitakarmaṇā \|\| 176.55 \|\|*

*ucchritenāgrahastena dakṣ̣iṇena vapuṣ̣matā\|*  
*dānavāndevanihatānuttiṣ̣ṭhadhvamiti bruvan \|\| 176.56 \|\|*

He appeared like a blazing fire, measuring the sky with his massive arms, kicking the mountains with his feet, driving away the heavy banks of rain clouds by his breath, with his eyes knitted , persecuting the Devas, covering all the directions, looking like the messenger of death. He, stretching his arms clustered with heavy fingers, addressed the demons, saying “Demons! you should all get up now.” He overspread all the quarters with arrows and seemed ready to bum the Devas.

## \|\| 176.57 \|\|

*taṃ kālanemiṃ samare dviṣ̣atāṃ kālaceṣ̣ṭitam\|*  
*vīkṣ̣ante sma surāḥ sarve bhayavitrastalocanāḥ \|\| 176.57 \|\|*

He looked to enemies, like death at the time of the dissolution of the universe. All the Devas were bewildered to see Kalanemi in the conflict.

## \|\| 176.58-59 \|\|

*taṃ vīkṣ̣ante sma bhūtāni kramantaṃ kālaneminam\|*  
*trivikramādhikamataṃ nārāyaṇamivāparam \|\| 176.58 \|\|*

*so'tyucchrayapuraḥpādamārutāghūrṇitāmbaraḥ\|*  
*prakrāmannasuro yuddhe trāsayāmāsa devatāḥ \|\| 176.59 \|\|*

All the beings were looking upon that persevering Kalanemi like Narayana; he began to roam on the battlefield pacing his very tall legs to the fro and thereby raising wind and rolling as it were the firmament.

## \|\| 176.60-61 \|\|

*sa mayenāsurendre ṇa pariṣ̣vaktastato raṇe\|*  
*kālanemirbabhau daityaḥ saviṣ̣ṇuriva mandaraḥ \|\| 176.60 \|\|*

*atha vivyathire devāḥ sarve śakrapurogamāḥ\|*  
*kālanemiṃ samāyāntaṃ dṛṣ̣ṭvā kālamivāparam \|\| 176.61 \|\|*

The Devas were all very much terrified. Maya, the lord of the Asuras then embraced him. Kalanemi then with Visnu looked beautiful like the Mandara mountain. Indra and the other Devas were deeply pained to see the demon Kalanemi advancing as if the death of all.

## Chapter 177

## \|\| 177.1-11 \|\|

*matsya uvāca*  
*dānavānāmanīkeṣ̣u kālanemirmahāsuraḥ\|*  
*vyavardhata mahātejāstapānte jalado yathā \|\| 177.1 \|\|*

*taṃ trailokyāntaragataṃ dṛṣ̣ṭvā te dānaveśvarāḥ\|*  
*uttasthurapariśrāntāḥ pītvā'mṛtamanuttamam \|\| 177.2 \|\|*

*te vītabhayasaṃtrāsā mayatārapurogamāḥ\|*  
*tārakāmayasaṅgrāme satataṃ jitakāśinaḥ \|\| 177.3 \|\|*

*rejurāyodhanagatā dānavā yuddhakāṅkṣ̣iṇaḥ\|*  
*mantramabhyasatāṃ teṣ̣āṃ vyūhaṃ ca paridhāvatām \|\| 177.4 \|\|*

*prekṣ̣atāṃ cābhavatprītirdānavaṃ kālaneminam\|*  
*ye tu tatraṃ mayasyā’sanmukhyā yuddhapuraḥsarāḥ \|\| 177.5 \|\|*

*te tu sarve bhayaṃ tyaktvā hṛṣ̣ṭā yoddhumupasthitāḥ\|*  
*mayastāro varāhaśca hayagrīvaśca vīryavān \|\| 177.6 \|\|*

*vipracittisutaḥ śvetaḥ kharalambāvubhāvapi\|*  
*ariṣ̣ṭo baliputraśca kiśorākhyastathaiva ca \|\| 177.7 \|\|*

*svarbhānuścāmaraprakhyo vaktrayodhī mahāsuraḥ\|*  
*ete'stravedinaḥ sarve sarve tapasi susthitāḥ \|\| 177.8 \|\|*

*dānavāḥ kṛtino jagmuḥ kālanemiṃ tamuddhatam\|*  
*te gadābhirbhuśuṇḍībhiścakrairatha paraśvadhaiḥ \|\| 177.9 \|\|*

*kālakalpaiśca musalaiḥ kṣ̣epaṇīyaiśca mudgaraiḥ\|*  
*aśmabhiścādri sadṛśairgaṇḍaśailaiśca dāruṇaiḥ \|\| 177.10 \|\|*

*paṭṭiśairbhindipālaiśca parighaiścottamāyasaiḥ\|*  
*ghātanībhiḥ sugurvībhiḥ śataghnībhistathaiva ca \|\| 177.11 \|\|*

Matsya said- That highly energetic Asura Kalanemi, in the midst of the demons, appeared growing in strength like the heavy rain clouds gathering in strength after excessive heat. Then the chief Danavas, like Maya and Tarakasura and others, seeing Kalanemi were encouraged as if they had drunk the nectar; and stood up and made an advance; and all the demons casting off their fears and knocking off their fatigue, cherished Tarakasura’s victory and they all congregated in the field to resume fight, after duly holding a council of war. They arranged their phalanxes and the principal demons forming the vanguard of Tarkasura also turned up dauntlessly. All were pleased to see Kalanemi. The chief generals of Maya came off gladly from Maya’s side and joined Kalanemi, Maya, Tarkasura, Varaha, Hayagriva, Sveta the son of Vipracitti, Khara, Lamba, Arista, Kisora, Svarbhanu, Camara, and VakrayodhI, versed in warfare and learning and tapasya, also came armed with clubs, quoits, axes, discs, rocks, javelins, spears, nooses stoves, the terrible Gandsaila, Pattis'a, Bhindipala, iron Parighas, heavy Ghatani, Sataghni, etc., to render assistance to Kalanemi.

## \|\| 177.13-15 \|\|

*bhujaṃgavadanaiḥ krūrairlelihānaiśca sāyakaiḥ\|*  
*vajraiḥ praharaṇīyaiśca dīpyamānaiśca tomaraiḥ \|\| 177.13 \|\|*

*vikośairasibhistīkṣ̣ṇaiḥ śūlaiśca śitanirmalaiḥ\|*  
*daityāḥ saṃdīptamanasaḥ pragṛhītaśarāsanāḥ \|\| 177.14 \|\|*

*tataḥ puraskṛtya tadā kālanemiṃ mahāhave\|*  
*sā dīptaśastrapravarā daityānāṃ ruruce camūḥ \|\| 177.15 \|\|*

They were also armed with arrows resembling the mouths of the serpents bolts, keen swords, tridents, bows, and many other luminous weapons. The army of the demons, under the leadership of Kalanemi, looked awfully striking, as if the whole sky was covered with blue clouds.

## \|\| 177.16-21 \|\|

*dyaurnimīlitasarvāṅgā ghanānīlāmbudāgame\|*  
*devatānāmapi camūrmumude śakrapālitā \|\| 177.16 \|\|*

*upetā sitakṛṣ̣ṇābhyāṃ tārābhyāṃ candra sūryayoḥ\|*  
*vāyuvegavatī saumyā tārāgaṇapatākinī \|\| 177.17 \|\|*

*toyadā viddhavasanā grahanakṣ̣atrahāsinī\|*  
*yamendra varuṇairguptā dhanadena ca dhīmatā \|\| 177.18 \|\|*

*saṃpradīptāgninayanā nārāyaṇaparāyaṇā\|*  
*sā samudrau ghasadṛśī divyā devamahācamūḥ \|\| 177.19 \|\|*

*rarājāstravatī bhīmā yakṣ̣agandharvaśālinī\|*  
*tayoścamvostadānīṃ tu babhūva sa samāgamaḥ \|\| 177.20 \|\|*

*dyāvāpṛthivyoḥ saṃyogo yathā syādyugaparyaye\|*  
*tadyuddhamabhavaddhoraṃ devadānavasaṃkulam \|\| 177.21 \|\|*

The army of the Devas, guarded by Indra, looking white and black, extremely joyful, having the Sun and the Moon with them, with asterisms as banners, swift like the wind, located close to the heavenly bodies, under the protection of Indra, Varuna and Kubera, gleaming like fire blaze, under the chief leadership of Narayana like the mass of ocean, swelled by the Yaksas, and the Gandharvas armed with various kinds of weapons, shone forth and looked particularly splendid. Both the armies encountered each other, like the heaven and earth at the time of universal dissolution, and a fearful conflict ensued.

## \|\| 177.22-27 \|\|

*kṣ̣amāparākramaparaṃ darpasya vinayasya ca\|*  
*niścakramurbalābhyāṃ tu bhīmāstatra surāsurāḥ \|\| 177.22 \|\|*

*pūrvāparābhyāṃ saṃrabdhāḥ sāgarābhyāmivāmbudāḥ\|*  
*tābhyāṃ balābhyāṃ saṃhṛṣ̣ṭāśceruste devadānavāḥ \|\| 177.23 \|\|*

*vanābhyāṃ pārvatīyābhyāṃ puṣ̣pitābhyāṃ yathā’gamāḥ\|*  
*samājaghnustato bherīḥ śaṅkhāndadhmuranekaśaḥ \|\| 177.24 \|\|*

*sa śabdo dyāṃ bhuvaṃ khaṃ ca diśaśca samapūrayat\|*  
*jyāghātatalanirghoṣ̣o dhanuṣ̣āṃ kūjitāni ca \|\| 177.25 \|\|*

*duṃdabhīnāṃ ca ninado daityamantardadhuḥ svanam\|*  
*te'nyonyamabhisaṃpetuḥ pātayantaḥ parasparam \|\| 177.26 \|\|*

*babhañjurbāhubhirbāhūndvaṃdvamanye yuyutsavaḥ\|*  
*devāstu cāśaniṃ ghoraṃ parighāṃścottamāyasān \|\| 177.27 \|\|*

The Devas and the demons showed their valour, and arrogance. They fought furiously like the clouds emerging from the roaring eastern and western oceans. They began to tear down each other, as the infuriated elephants rend the mighty mountain trees. They also blew several kinds of conches and trumpets. The din of their conches filled earth, sky, heavens and the space all round, and so did the noise of the twanging of the bowstrings, clashing the swords, clap of the hands, etc. In the midst of the tumult raised by the kettle-drums, etc., the roars of the demons vanished; they began to break the heads of each other; some of them fought duels; some broke other’s arms, etc., many of them wrestled, the Devas used their heavy clubs and iron bolts, etc.

## \|\| 177.28-33 \|\|

*nistriṃśānsasṛjuḥ saṃkhye gadā gurvīśca dānavāḥ\|*  
*gadānipātairbhagnāṅgā bāṇaiśca śakalīkṛtāḥ \|\| 177.28 \|\|*

*paripeturbhṛśaṃ kecitpunaḥ kecittu jaghnire\|*  
*tato rathaiḥ saturagairvimānaiścā’śugāmibhiḥ \|\| 177.29 \|\|*

*samīyuste susaṃrabdhā roṣ̣ādanyonyamāhave\|*  
*saṃvartamānāḥ samare saṃdaṣ̣ṭauṣ̣ṭhapuṭānanāḥ \|\| 177.30 \|\|*

*rathā rathairnirudhyante pādātāśca padātibhiḥ\|*  
*teṣ̣āṃ rathānāṃ tumulaḥ sa śabdaḥ śabdavāhinām \|\| 177.31 \|\|*

*nabhonabhaśca hi yathā nabhasyairjaladasvanaiḥ\|*  
*babhañjustu rathānkecitkecitsaṃmarditā rathaiḥ \|\| 177.32 \|\|*

*saṃbādhamanye saṃprāpya na śekuścalitu rathāḥ\|*  
*anyonyamanye samare dorbhyāmutkṣ̣ipya daṃśitāḥ \|\| 177.33 \|\|*

Many warriors fell down with their limbs severed by the clubs and arrows. Several of them fought from their chariots and horses, biting their lips with rage. There was a tremendous uproar, when the infantry and the chariots started face to face fighting. They smashed the chariots of each other, fighting like two clouds in the months of Sravana, and Bhadra rushing into each other. Many were killed under the pressure of the chariots running over them. Most of the warriors were unable to guide their chariots, being impeded by other chariots; and several of them threw down their foes by the arm.

## \|\| 177.34-47 \|\|

*saṃhrādamānāmaraṇā jaghnustatrāpi carmiṇaḥ\|*  
*astrairanye vinirbhinnā vemū raktaṃ hatā yudhi \|\| 177.34 \|\|*

*kṣ̣arajжalānāṃ sadṛśā jaladānāṃ samāgame\|*  
*tadastraśastragrathitaṃ kṣ̣iptotkṣ̣iptagadāvilam \|\| 177.35 \|\|*

*devadānavasaṃkṣ̣ubdhaṃ saṃkulaṃ yuddhamābabhau\|*  
*taddānavamahāmeghaṃ devāyudhavirājitam \|\| 177.36 \|\|*

*anyonyabāṇavarṣ̣eṇa yuddhadurdinamābabhau\|*  
*etasminnantare kruddhaḥ kālanemiḥ sa dānavaḥ \|\| 177.37 \|\|*

*vyavardhata samudrau ghaiḥ pūryamāṇa ivāmbudaḥ\|*  
*tasya vidyuccalāpīḍāḥ pradīptāśanivarṣ̣iṇaḥ \|\| 177.38 \|\|*

*gātrairnāgagiriprakhyā vinipeturbalāhakāḥ\|*  
*krodhānniḥśvasatastasya bhrūbhedasvedavarṣ̣iṇaḥ \|\| 177.39 \|\|*

*sāgnisphuliṅgapratatā mukhānniṣ̣peturarciṣ̣aḥ\|*  
*tiryagūrdhvaṃ ca gagane vavṛdhustasya bāhavaḥ \|\| 177.40 \|\|*

*parvatādiva niṣ̣krāntāḥ pañcāsyā iva pannagāḥ\|*  
*so'strajālairbahuvidhairdhanurbhiḥ parighairapi \|\| 177.41 \|\|*

*divyamākāśamāvavre parvatairucchritairiva\|*  
*so'niloddhūtavasanastasthau saṅgrāmalālasaḥ \|\| 177.42 \|\|*

*saṃdhyātapagrastaśilaḥ sākṣ̣ānmerurivācalaḥ\|*  
*uruvegapramathitaiḥ śailaśṛṅgāgrapādapaiḥ \|\| 177.43 \|\|*

*apātayaddevagaṇānvajreṇeva mahāgirīn\|*  
*bahubhiḥ śastranistriṃśaiśchinnabhinnaśiroruhāḥ \|\| 177.44 \|\|*

*na śekuścalituṃ devāḥ kālanemihatā yudhi\|*  
*muṣ̣ṭibhirnihatāḥ kecitkecittu vidalīkṛtāḥ \|\| 177.45 \|\|*

*yakṣ̣agandharvapatayaḥ petuḥ saha mahoragaiḥ\|*  
*tena vitrāsitā devāḥ samare kālaneminā \|\| 177.46 \|\|*

*na śekuryatnavanto'pi yatnaṃ kartuṃ vicetasaḥ\|*  
*tena śakraḥ sahasrākṣ̣aḥ spanditaḥ śarabandhanaiḥ \|\| 177.47 \|\|*

Some of them killed their foes by pushing them by their shields. The warriors wounded in the battle vomited blood like the clouds pouring out rain. A fearful onslaught raged between the Devas and the demons. The dense volleys of arrows shot from both the armies covered the sky like clouds, and the weapons looked like rainbows in the heavens, afterwards Kalanemi came charged with wrath like the surging ocean. The clouds charged with lightning and making a thundering noise, began to be dispersed when they struck Kalanemi’s luminous coronet and his body hard like a mountain. When he began to breathe in his wrath, and with his twisted faces and wrinkled eyebrows sweats came out of his body and sparks of fire emitted. Sparks emitted from his mouth and his arm stretched towards the sky and the sides, and grew in magnitude, and looked as if five-hooded serpents had emerged from the mountains, and various kinds of weapons such as clubs, bows, etc., held by him looked beautiful like the mountain peaks touching the skies. When his garments were blown by wind, it seemed as if, the top of mount Meru was struck with the evening rays of the Sun. He knocked down many Devas by his violently striking them with mountain peaks and trees, and cut down many of them by his sword, who felt unable to move about. He killed a good many by his blows. The Devas, the Gandharvas and the serpents, thus belaboured by Kalanemi, became lustreless and utterly helpless, and even the mighty Indra of a thousand eyes were entangled in his network of arrows.

## \|\| 177.48-59 \|\|

*airāvatagataḥ saṃkhye calituṃ na śaśāka ha\|*  
*nirjalāmbhodasadṛśo nirjalārṇavasaprabhaḥ \|\| 177.48 \|\|*

*nirvyāpāraḥ kṛtastena vipāśo varuṇo mṛdhe\|*  
*raṇe vaiśravaṇastena parighaiḥ kāmarūpiṇā \|\| 177.49 \|\|*

*vittado'pi kṛtaḥ saṃkhye nirjitaḥ kālaneminā\|*  
*yamaḥ sarvaharastena mṛtyupraharaṇo raṇe \|\| 177.50 \|\|*

*yāmyāmavasthāṃ saṃtyajya bhītaḥ svāṃ diśamāviśat\|*  
*sa lokapālānutsārya kṛtvā teṣ̣āṃ ca karma tat \|\| 177.51 \|\|*

*dikṣ̣u sarvāsu dehaṃ svaṃ caturdhā vidadhe tadā\|*  
*sa nakṣ̣atrapathaṃ gatvā divyaṃ svarbhānudarśanam \|\| 177.52 \|\|*

*jahāra lakṣ̣mīṃ somasya ta cāsya viṣ̣ayaṃ mahat\|*  
*cālayāmāsa dīptāṃśuṃ svargadvārātsa bhāskaram \|\| 177.53 \|\|*

*sāyanaṃ cāsya viṣ̣ayaṃ jahāra dinakarma ca\|*  
*so'gniṃ devamukhaṃ dṛṣ̣ṭvā cakārā’tmamukhāśrayam \|\| 177.54 \|\|*

*vāyuṃ ca tarasā jitvā cakārā’tmavaśānugam\|*  
*sa samudrā nsamānīya sarvāśca sarito balāt \|\| 177.55 \|\|*

*cakārā’tmamukhe vīryāddehabhūtāśca sindhavaḥ\|*  
*apaḥ svavaśagāḥ kṛtvā divijā yāśca bhūmijāḥ \|\| 177.56 \|\|*

*sa svayaṃ bhūrivā’bhāti mahābhūtapatiryathā\|*  
*sarvalokamayo daityaḥ sarvabhūtabhayāvahaḥ \|\| 177.57 \|\|*

*sa lokapālaikavapuścandrā dityagrahātmavān\|*  
*sthāpayāmāsa jagatīṃ suguptāṃ dharaṇīdharaiḥ \|\| 177.58 \|\|*

*pāvakānilasaṃpāto rarāja yudhi dānavaḥ\|*  
*pārameṣ̣ṭhye sthitaḥ sthāne lokānāṃ prabhavāpyaye\|*  
*taṃ tuṣ̣ṭuvurdaityagaṇā devā iva pitāmaham \|\| 177.59 \|\|*

At that time Indra, riding on his Airavata, could not move about. Varuna was bereft of his noose and looked like the clouds and the oceans bereft of water. Afterwards, he belaboured Kubera with His club, and subdued Dharmaraja, who shuddering with fear, ran away abandoning His glory. He also overpowered the Lokapala and divided himself in four parts and located them in four directions. These parts did all his works. Then going up to the path of the stars, he took the splendour of the Moon and his kingdom what is so anxiously coveted by Rahu. He then dispelled the light of the Moon, and also drove away the shining Sun from the gates of heaven, and took under his charge His Sayana (procession of the equinoxes) and the diurnal functions. Knowing Agni to be the mouth of the Gods, Kalanemi swallowed Him also. He also conquered Vayu by his valour and controlled and swallowed all the heavenly and mundane streams along with the ocean. In such a way that demon after bringing under his control all waters of heaven and earth, shone forth Brahma and became the terror of the universe; and assuming the forms of Lokapalas and the Sun and the Moon, he controlled the affairs of the universe in a well-ordained manner. Then enthroning himself in the heavens in the place of Brahma, that demon, highly energetic like wind and fire, began to rule himself the celestial and terrestrial kingdoms. All the demons then prayed to him as the Devas do unto Brahma.

## Chapter 178

## \|\| 178.1 \|\|

*matsya uvāca*  
*pañca taṃ nābhyavartanta viparītena karmaṇā\|*  
*vedo dharmaḥ kṣ̣amā satyaṃ śrīśca nārāyaṇāśrayā \|\| 178.1 \|\|*

Lord Matsya said- The Vedas, Dharma, Forbearance, Truth and LaksmI, resorting to Narayana, these five were not attained by Kalanemi on account of his inferior deeds, performed against the prescribed rites.

## \|\| 178.2 \|\|

*sa teṣ̣āmanupasthānātsakrodho dānaveśvaraḥ\|*  
*vaiṣ̣ṇavaṃ padamanvicchanyayau nārāyaṇāntikam \|\| 178.2 \|\|*

Because of the absence of these five, the lord of demons became angry, and wanted to enthrone himself in place of Visnu and appeared before Him.

## \|\| 178.3-4 \|\|

*sa dadarśa suparṇasthaṃ śaṅkhacakragadādharam\|*  
*dānavānāṃ vināśāya bhrāmayantaṃ gadāṃ śubhām \|\| 178.3 \|\|*

*sajalāmbhodasadṛśaṃ vidyutsadṛśavāsasam\|*  
*svārūḍhaṃ svarṇapakṣ̣āḍhyaṃ śikhinaṃ kāśyapaṃ khagam \|\| 178.4 \|\|*

He saw the Lord riding on his vehicle Garuda and holding conch, disc, club, lotus, wearing white apparel and whirling his auspicious mace to destroy the demons. His garment appeared like lightning. He himself appeared like rain clouds. His carrier was Garuda, Kasyapa’s son having crest and golden wings.

## \|\| 178.5 \|\|

*dṛṣ̣ṭvā daityavināśāya raṇe svasthamavasthitam\|*  
*dānavo viṣ̣ṇumakṣ̣obhyaṃ babhāṣ̣e kṣ̣ubdhamānasaḥ \|\| 178.5 \|\|*

Seeing Him thus appearing in the battlefield with a calm composure, ready to destroy the demons, that demon angrily said.

## \|\| 178.6 \|\|

*ayaṃ sa ripurasmākaṃ pūrveṣ̣āṃ prāṇanāśanaḥ\|*  
*arṇavāvāsinaścaiva madhorvai kaiṭabhasya ca \|\| 178.6 \|\|*

“He is our enemy and the destroyer of our ancestors, He dwells in the ocean, He also destroyed the demons Madhu and Kaitabha.

## \|\| 178.7 \|\|

*ayaṃ sa vigraho'smākamāśāmyaḥ kila kathyate\|*  
*anena saṃyugeṣ̣vadya dānavā bahavo hatāḥ \|\| 178.7 \|\|*

There will be a most fearful fight between Him and me. It is said that there is no end. In this battle, many demons have been killed by Him.

## \|\| 178.8-9 \|\|

*ayaṃ sa nirghṛṇo loke strībālanirapatrapaḥ\|*  
*yena dānavanārīṇāṃ sīmantoddharaṇaṃ kṛtam \|\| 178.8 \|\|*

*ayaṃ sa viṣ̣ṇurdevānāṃ vaikuṇṭhaśca divaukasām\|*  
*ananto bhogināmapsu svapannādyaḥ svayaṃbhuvaḥ \|\| 178.9 \|\|*

He is very merciless towards the people. He is shameless as he has not shown his clemency even to the children and the women and He dragged the women of demons with their plait of heir. He is Visnu. He is the heaven of the deities. He sleeps in ocean on the Sesa serpent. He is the endless and Prime Soul.

## \|\| 178.10-12 \|\|

*ayaṃ sa nātho devānāmasmābhirvyathitātmanām\|*  
*asya krodhaṃ samāsādya hiraṇyakaśipurhataḥ \|\| 178.10 \|\|*

*asya cchāyāmupāśritya devā makhamukhe śritāḥ\|*  
*ājyaṃ maharṣ̣ibhirdattamaśnuvanti vidhau hutam \|\| 178.11 \|\|*

*ayaṃ sa nidhane hetuḥ sarveṣ̣āmamaradviṣ̣ām\|*  
*yasya vaktraṃ praviṣ̣ṭāni kulānyasmākamāhave \|\| 178.12 \|\|*

Не is the Lord of the gods and our tormentor. Hiranyakasyapu was the victim of His fury. The Devas under His guardianship enjoy the sacrificial oblations and the offerings of clarified butter poured into the fire thrice by the great Rsis. He is the Destroyer of all the enemies of the Devas. In the field of battle our race is annihilated by His cakra or quoit.

## \|\| 178.13-14 \|\|

*ayaṃ sa kila yuddheṣ̣u surārthe tyaktajīvitaḥ\|*  
*savitustejasā tulyaṃ cakraṃ kṣ̣ipati śatruṣ̣u \|\| 178.13 \|\|*

*ayaṃ sa kālo daityānāṃ kālabhūtaḥ samāsthitaḥ\|*  
*atikrāntasya kālasya phalaṃ prāpsyati keśavaḥ \|\| 178.14 \|\|*

It is true that for the welfare of the Devas, He has given up his own life. He throws his quoit shining like the Sun in midst of the demons. He is the Destroyer of the demons as in the form of death. He is Kesava and will receive his fruits of past time.

## \|\| 178.15-18 \|\|

*diṣ̣ṭyedānīṃ samakṣ̣aṃ me viṣ̣ṇureṣ̣a samāgataḥ\|*  
*adya madbāhuniṣ̣piṣ̣ṭo māmeva praṇayiṣ̣yati \|\| 178.15 \|\|*

*yāsyāmyapacitiṃ diṣ̣ṭyā pūrveṣ̣āmadya saṃyuge\|*  
*imaṃ nārāyaṇaṃ hatvā dānavānāṃ bhayāvaham \|\| 178.16 \|\|*

*kṣ̣iprameva haniṣ̣yāmi raṇe'maragaṇāṃstataḥ\|*  
*jātyantaragato'pyeṣ̣a bādhate dānavānmṛdhe \|\| 178.17 \|\|*

*eṣ̣o'nantaḥ purā bhūtvā padmanābha iti śrutaḥ\|*  
*jaghānaikārṇave ghore tāvubhau madhukaiṭabhau \|\| 178.18 \|\|*

Fortunately this Visnu has now come to me. Now He subdued by me and will salute to me. Today in this battlefield I shall kill Narayana-the terror of the demons and will then kill quickly all the other gods. Thus I will be free from the debt of my ancestors. This Vi§nu in all forms causes anguish to the demons. I have heard that this very same Visnu bears enmity to the demons even after he gets other births; and he has killed the demons Madhu and Kaitabha, when a lotus sprouted from His navel, and when there was only one vast expanse ofwater all over the universe.

## \|\| 178.19-22 \|\|

*dvidhā bhūtaṃ vapuḥ kṛtvā siṃhasyārdhaṃ narasya ca\|*  
*pitaraṃ me jaghānaiko hiraṇyakaśipuṃ purā \|\| 178.19 \|\|*

*śubhaṃ garbhamadhattainamaditirdevatāraṇiḥ\|*  
*trīṃlṁ! lokānujжahāraikaḥ kramamāṇastribhiḥ kramaiḥ \|\| 178.20 \|\|*

*bhūyastvidānīṃ saṅgrāme saṃprāpte tārakāmaye\|*  
*mayā saha samāgamya saha devairvinaṅkṣ̣yati \|\| 178.21 \|\|*

*evamuktvā bahuvidhaṃ kṣ̣ipannārāyaṇaṃ raṇe\|*  
*vāgbhirapratirūpābhiryuddhamevābhyarocayat \|\| 178.22 \|\|*

In the form of Narasimha, half man and half loin He killed my father Hiranyakas'yapu. He had measured the three realms by His three strides, when Aditi held Him auspiciously in Her womb. Now again in this Tarakamaya war He will be killed by fighting with me.” Having uttered such words in many ways, he got ready to encounter Visnu.

## \|\| 178.23-27 \|\|

*kṣ̣ipyamāṇo'surendre ṇa na cukopa gadādharaḥ\|*  
*kṣ̣amābalena mahatā sasmitaṃ cedamabravīt \|\| 178.23 \|\|*

*alpaṃ darpabalaṃ daitya sthiramakrodhajaṃ balam\|*  
*hatastvaṃ darpajairdoṣ̣airhitvā yadbhāṣ̣ase kṣ̣amām \|\| 178.24 \|\|*

*adhīrastvaṃ mama mato dhigetattava vāgbalam\|*  
*na yatra puruṣ̣āḥ santi tatra garjanti yoṣ̣itaḥ \|\| 178.25 \|\|*

*ahaṃ tvāṃ daitya paśyāmi pūrveṣ̣āṃ mārgagāmiṇam\|*  
*prajāpatikṛtaṃ setuṃ bhittvā kaḥ svastimānvrajet \|\| 178.26 \|\|*

*adya tvāṃ nāśayiṣ̣yāmi devavyāpāraghātakam\|*  
*sveṣ̣u sveṣ̣u ca sthāneṣ̣u sthāpayiṣ̣yāmi devatāḥ \|\| 178.27 \|\|*

Thus the lord of demons spoke such harsh words, but Gadadhara kept himself quite calm, and only said with a smile- “O Demon! you are somewhat conceited and that is why you are addressing Me so impatiently. The strength of conceit is no strength indeed; whereas the strength of angerlessness is more stable and really strong. Filled with conceit, in my opinion, you are void of valour. Fie to your words. Verily, women pose at a place where there are no men. О Daitya! I see, you are the follower on the footsteps of your ancestors. Who is fortunate can remain in comfort after breaking the bridge built by Lord Brahma? О one destroyer of the auspicious acts of the Devas! to day I shall kill you and shall install the Devas in their places.”

## \|\| 178.28-30 \|\|

*evaṃ bruvati vākyaṃ tu mṛdhe śrīvatsadhāriṇi\|*  
*jahāsa dānavaḥ krodhāddhastāṃścakre sahāyudhān \|\| 178.28 \|\|*

*sa bāhuśatamudyamya sarvāstragrahaṇaṃ raṇe\|*  
*krodhāddviguṇaraktākṣ̣o viṣ̣ṇuṃ vakṣ̣asyatāḍayat \|\| 178.29 \|\|*

*dānavāścāpi samare mayatārapurogamāḥ\|*  
*udyatāyudhanistriṃśā viṣ̣ṇumabhyadra vanraṇe \|\| 178.30 \|\|*

After the words of Lord Visnu, the holder of the mark of Srlvatsa, like that, the demon laughed with anger, holding missiles in his hands. Taking up the weapons in his hundreds of hands with red-eyed, he began to hit the chest of the Visnu. Maya and other valiant demons also ran after Visnu with their sharpened arms and Nistrinsa weapons in battlefield.

## \|\| 178.31 \|\|

*sa tāḍyamāno'tibalairdaityaiḥ sarvodyatāyudhaiḥ\|*  
*na cacāla tato yuddhe'kampamāna ivācalaḥ \|\| 178.31 \|\|*

Afflicted by the blows of the demons in the war, Lord Visnu was unable to move from there. He kept himself very steady like a mountain.

## \|\| 178.32-33 \|\|

*saṃsaktaśca suparṇena kālanemī mahāsuraḥ\|*  
*sarvaprāṇena mahatīṃ gadāmudyamya bāhubhiḥ \|\| 178.32 \|\|*

*ghorāṃ jvalantīṃ mumuce saṃrabdho garuḍopari\|*  
*karmaṇā tena daityasya viṣ̣ṇurvismayamāviśat \|\| 178.33 \|\|*  
*yadā tena suparṇasya pātitā mūrdhni sā gadā\|*

Then Garuda injured the great demon Kalanemi. Then taking up a ponderous and terrible club in his hand Kalanemi hurled it on Garuda with great force, which indeed astonished the Lord.

## \|\| 178.34-37 \|\|

*suparṇaṃ vyathitaṃ dṛṣ̣ṭvā kṣ̣ataṃ ca vapurātmanaḥ \|\| 178.34 \|\|*

*krodhasaṃraktanayano vaikuṇṭhaścakramādade\|*  
*vyavardhata sa vegena suparṇena samaṃ vibhuḥ \|\| 178.35 \|\|*

*bhujāścāsya vyavardhanta vyāpnuvanto diśo daśa\|*  
*pradiśaścaiva khaṃ gāṃ vai pūrayāmāsa keśavaḥ \|\| 178.36 \|\|*

*vavṛdhe ca punarlokānkrāntukāma ivaujasā\|*  
*tarjanāyāsurendrā ṇāṃ vardhamānaṃ nabhastale \|\| 178.37 \|\|*

Lord seeing Garuda thus distressed and Himself also in trouble, became very angry. Then he took up His Sudarsana cakra, and exhibited His majestic glory. At that time Visnu began to grow with Garuda; and covered all the ten directions with his arms. The Lord Visnu pervading all over the universe by splendour rose to heaven and started to destroy the demons.

## \|\| 178.38 \|\|

*ṛṣ̣ayaścaiva gandharvāstuṣ̣ṭuvurmadhusūdanam\|*  
*sarvānkirīṭena lihansābhramambaramambaraiḥ \|\| 178.38 \|\|*  
*padbhyāmākramya vasudhāṃ diśaḥ pracchādya bāhubhiḥ\|*

All Rsis and the Gandharvas began to chant hymns to destroyer of Madhu demon (Visnu), and at the same time the Lord rose so high that His crest touched the clouds, His feet covered the earth and His stretched arms spread in all directions.

## \|\| 178.39-46 \|\|

*sa sūryakaratulyābhaṃ sahasrāramarikṣ̣ayam \|\| 178.39 \|\|*

*dīptāgnisadṛśaṃ ghoraṃ darśanena sudarśanam\|*  
*suvarṇareṇuparyantaṃ vajranābhaṃ bhayāvaham \|\| 178.40 \|\|*

*medosthimajжārudhiraiḥ siktaṃ dānavasaṃbhavaiḥ\|*  
*advitīyapraharaṇaṃ kṣ̣uraparyantamaṇḍalam \|\| 178.41 \|\|*

*snagdāmamālāvitataṃ kāmagaṃ kāmarūpiṇam\|*  
*svayaṃ svayaṃbhuvā sṛṣ̣ṭaṃ bhayadaṃ sarvavidviṣ̣ām \|\| 178.42 \|\|*

*maharṣ̣iroṣ̣airāviṣ̣ṭaṃ nityamāhavadarpitam\|*  
*kṣ̣epaṇādyasya muhyanti lokāḥ sasthāṇujaṅgamāḥ \|\| 178.43 \|\|*

*kravyādāni ca bhūtāni tṛptiṃ yānti mahāmṛdhe\|*  
*tadapratimakarmograṃ samānaṃ sūryavarcasā \|\| 178.44 \|\|*

*cakramudyamya samare krodhadīpto gadādharaḥ\|*  
*sa muṣ̣ṇandānavaṃ tejaḥ samare svena tejasā \|\| 178.45 \|\|*

*ciccheda bāhuṃ cakreṇa śrīdharaḥ kālaneminaḥ\|*  
*tacca vaktraśataṃ ghoraṃ sāgnipūrṇāṭṭahāsi vai \|\| 178.46 \|\|*  
*tasya daityasya cakreṇa pramamātha balāddhariḥ\|*

Then He took His mighty Sudarasana quote, shining like the rays of the Sun, containing a thousand edges, the destroyer of the enemies, looking like a blaze of fire, its ends adorned with golden work and its middle bedecked with diamonds, having garlands on it, going and assuming forms at will, terrible to all the enemies, the eater of the blood, bone and marrow of the demons, made by Brahma Himself, conjoined with the fury and fortitude of the Maharsis, by the throwing of which the moveable and immoveable objects become burnt up, by virtue of which the goblins and the Raksasas get satisfaction (by getting blood and flesh to live upon). Raising such a Sudars'ana cakra, unmatched in accomplishing its objects and looking violent like the burning rays of the Sun, Visnu took away all the Danava’s energy and cut down the arms and the hundreds of the heads of Kalanemi looking like fires.

## \|\| 178.47-48 \|\|

*sa cchinnabāhurviśirā na prākampata dānavaḥ \|\| 178.47 \|\|*  
*kabandho'vasthitaḥ saṃkhye viśākha iva pādapaḥ\|*  
*saṃvitatya mahāpakṣ̣au vāyoḥ kṛtvā samaṃ javam \|\| 178.48 \|\|*  
*urasā pātayāmāsa garuḍaḥ kālaneminam\|*

Even having no arms and head, the demon still remained unmoved. Elis headless form like the trunk of a tree stood up in the field. Then Garuda swiftly like the air, threw down Kalanemi on the ground by his wings and by his breast.

## \|\| 178.49-50 \|\|

*sa tasya deho vimukho vibāhuḥ khātparibhraman \|\| 178.49 \|\|*  
*nipapāta divaṃ tyaktvā kṣ̣obhayandharaṇītalam\|*  
*tasminnipatite daitye devāḥ sarṣ̣igaṇāstadā \|\| 178.50 \|\|*

His armless and faceless body fell down from heaven with great violence on ground. Due to the falling down of the demon, the Devas together with Rsis cried out “excellent! excellent!” and they all adored Visnu.

## \|\| 178.51-56 \|\|

*sādhu sādhviti vaikuṇṭhaṃ sametāḥ pratyapūjayan\|*  
*apare ye tu daityāśca yuddhe dṛṣ̣ṭaparākramāḥ \|\| 178.51 \|\|*

*te sarve bāhubhirvyāptā na śekuścalituṃ raṇe\|*  
*kāṃścitkeśeṣ̣u jagrāha kāṃścitkaṇṭheṣ̣u pīḍayan \|\| 178.52 \|\|*

*cakarṣ̣a kasyacidvaktraṃ madhye'gṛhṇādathāparam\|*  
*te gadā cakranirdagdhā gatasattvā gatāsavaḥ \|\| 178.53 \|\|*

*gaganādbhraṣ̣ṭasarvāṅgā nipeturdharaṇītale\|*  
*teṣ̣u daityeṣ̣u sarveṣ̣u hateṣ̣u puruṣ̣ottamaḥ \|\| 178.54 \|\|*

*tasthau śakrapriyaṃ kṛtvā kṛtakarmā gadādharaḥ\|*  
*tasminvimarde saṅgrāme nivṛtte tārakāmaye \|\| 178.55 \|\|*

*taṃ deśamājagāmā’śu brahmā lokapitāmahaḥ\|*  
*sarvairbrahmarṣ̣ibhiḥ sārdhaṃ gandharvāpsarasāṃ gaṇaiḥ \|\| 178.56 \|\|*

Then all other demons seeing war in battlefield started to flight; but they all could not move obstructed by the stretching arms of Visnu who caught hold of their hair and necks. He powdered the faces of many and broke the waists of several. Many demons of them were cut down by the quoit and the club blows of the Lord and expired. Their strengths diminished, limbs were broken and several of them died falling on the ground from the heaven. When all the demons were thus killed, the Lord stayed there for the benefit of Indra. At the end of the Tarakamaya battle, Pitamaha Brahma along with the Rsis, the Gandharvas and the group of nymphs went there.

## \|\| 178.57 \|\|

*devadevo hariṃ devaṃ pūjayanvākyamabravīt\|*  
*kṛtaṃ deva mahatkarma surāṇāṃ śalyamuddhṛtam\|*  
*vadhenānena daityānāṃ vayaṃ ca paritoṣ̣itāḥ \|\| 178.57 \|\|*

After adoring Lord Visnu, Brahma said Him these words- “You have done a great work. You have removed the source of pain to the gods. You have gratified us all by killing the demons.

## \|\| 178.58-60 \|\|

*yo'yaṃ tvayā hato viṣ̣ṇo kālanemirmahāsuraḥ\|*  
*tvameko'sya mṛdhe hantā nānyaḥ kaścana vidyate \|\| 178.58 \|\|*

*eṣ̣a devānparibhavaṁ llokāṃśca sacarācarān\|*  
*ṛṣ̣īṇāṃ kadanaṃ kṛtvā māmapi prati garjati \|\| 178.59 \|\|*

*tadanena tavāgryeṇa parituṣ̣ṭo'smi karmaṇā\|*  
*yadayaṃ kālakalpastu kālanemirnipātitaḥ \|\| 178.60 \|\|*

This great demon Kalanemi killed by you, was not slyable by anyone else. He was a source of sufferings contempt to the gods and all the three realms. He caused a great pain to the Rsis and was bent on doing me harm as well. Therefore, by this act, I am much gratified that you have killed Kalanemi resembling the death.

## \|\| 178.61-63 \|\|

*tadāgaccha svabhavanaṃ gacchāmi divamuttamam\|*  
*brahmarṣ̣ayastvāṃ tatrasthāḥ pratīkṣ̣ante sadogatāḥ \|\| 178.61 \|\|*

*kaṃ cāhaṃ tava dāsyāmi varaṃ varavatāṃ vara\|*  
*sureṣ̣vatha ca daityeṣ̣u varāṇāṃ varado bhavān \|\| 178.62 \|\|*

*niryātayaitastrilokyaṃ sphītaṃ nihatakaṇṭakam\|*  
*asminneva mṛdhe viṣ̣ṇo śakrāya sumahātmane \|\| 178.63 \|\|*

May You be blessed. Now we move on to the excellent place of heaven, where the Brahmarsis are beholding you in the assembly. Deva! what boon can I confer on you, for you, Yourself are the giver of boons to all Devas and Daityas. You have removed the thorn of the three realms. Now hand over the fullest kingdom of the three realms to Indra.”

## \|\| 178.64 \|\|

*evamukto bhagavatā brahmaṇā hariravyayaḥ\|*  
*devāñchakramukhānsarvānuvāca śubhayā girā \|\| 178.64 \|\|*

Thus praised by lord Brahma, imperishable lord Visnu said to Indra and all other gods in sweet words.

## \|\| 178.65-67 \|\|

*viṣ̣ṇuruvāca*  
*śṛṇvantu tridaśāḥ sarve yāvanto'tra samāgatāḥ\|*  
*śravaṇāvahitaiḥ śrotraiḥ puraskṛtya puraṃdaram \|\| 178.65 \|\|*

*asmābhiḥ samare sarve kālanemimukhā hatāḥ\|*  
*dānavā vikramopetāḥ śakrādapi mahattarāḥ \|\| 178.66 \|\|*

*asminmahati saṅgrāme daiteyau dvau viniḥsṛtau\|*  
*virocanaśca daityendra ḥ! svarbhānuśca mahāgrahaḥ \|\| 178.67 \|\|*  
*svāṃ diśaṃ bhajatāṃ śakro diśaṃ varuṇa eva ca\|*

Visnu said- “O Gods! listen to this with highly attention what I say. In this warfare we all have killed a demon Kalanemi more valiant than Indra alongwith other mighty demons, but two have escaped from this great war. They are Virocana and Rahu, consequently Indra and Varuna should guard the eastern and western quarters respectively.

## \|\| 178.68-69 \|\|

*yāmyāṃ yamaḥ pālayitāmuttarāṃ ca dhanādhipaḥ \|\| 178.68 \|\|*  
*ṛkṣ̣aiḥ saha yathāyogaṃ gacchatāṃ caiva candra māḥ\|*  
*abdamṛtumukhe sūryo bhajatāmayanaiḥ saha \|\| 178.69 \|\|*  
*ājyabhāgāḥ pravartantāṃ sadasyairabhipūjitāḥ\|*

Dharmaraja and Kubera should keep guard on south and north respectively. The Moon along with His satellites should return to their realm. О Sun! Enjoy yourself with your northern and southern Ayanas and season throughout the year. The daily oblation of clarified butter, etc., poured into the sacrificial fire may now be resumed.

## \|\| 178.70-71 \|\|

*hūyantāmagnayo viprairvedadṛṣ̣ṭena karmaṇā \|\| 178.70 \|\|*  
*devāścāpyagnihomena svādhyāyena maharṣ̣ayaḥ\|*  
*śrāddhena pitaraścaiva tṛptiṃ yāntu yathāsukham \|\| 178.71 \|\|*

“O Brahmanas! Resume Agnihotras and other sacrifices according to the Vedic injunctions, and oblations be offered in Fire. The Devas may be gratified by sacrifices, the ancestors by the performance of Sraddhas, and the great sages by the study of the Vedas.

## \|\| 178.72-73 \|\|

*vāyuścaratu mārgasthastridhā dīpyatu pāvakaḥ\|*  
*trīṃstu varṇāṃśca lokāṃstrīṃstarpayaṃścā’tmajairguṇaiḥ \|\| 178.72 \|\|*

*kratavaḥ saṃpravartantāṃ dīkṣ̣aṇīyairdvijātibhiḥ\|*  
*dakṣ̣iṇāścopapādyantāṃ yājñikebhyaḥ pṛthakpṛthak \|\| 178.73 \|\|*

The wind may freely roam in His realm and blow from there. The three fires may now gratify the three realms and the three vamas. The sacrifices may be resumed through the Brahmanas, and the Yajnikas may accept their sacrificial fees.

## \|\| 178.74-75 \|\|

*gāṃ tu sūryo rasānsomo vāyuḥ prāṇāṃśca prāṇiṣ̣u\|*  
*tarpayantaḥ pravartantāṃ sarva eva svakarmabhiḥ \|\| 178.74 \|\|*

*yathāvadānupūrvyeṇa mahendra malayodbhavāḥ\|*  
*trailokyamātaraḥ sarvāḥ samudraṃ yāntu sindhavaḥ \|\| 178.75 \|\|*  
*daityebhyastyajyatāṃ bhīśca śāntiṃ vrajata devatāḥ\|*

The Sun may nourish the earth, the Moon may foster the Rasas, and the Wind may refresh all. Let all in this way resume Their allotted functions. Let the mother rivers rising from the mountains Mahendra, Malaya, etc., flow to the oceans. О Devas! cast aside your fears of the demons, be calm.

## \|\| 178.76-78 \|\|

*svasti vo'stu gamiṣ̣yāmi brahmalokaṃ sanātanam \|\| 178.76 \|\|*  
*svagṛhe svargaloke vā saṅgrāme vā viśeṣ̣ataḥ\|*  
*viśrambho vo na mantavyo nityaṃ kṣ̣udrā hi dānavāḥ \|\| 178.77 \|\|*  
*chidre ṣ̣u praharantyete na teṣ̣āṃ saṃsthitirdhruvā\|*  
*saumyānāmṛjubhāvānāṃ bhavatāmārjavaṃ dhanam \|\| 178.78 \|\|*

May you be blessed. I am going to eternal Brahmaloka. Do not ever be afraid of the demons either in your realms or in battlefield. The demons are mean and whenever possible will attack the Devas. They have no fixed abodes. You should remain careful in your abodes, in the Heavens and in battlefield. You are simple and good. Gentleness and sincerity are your wealth.”

## \|\| 178.79-80 \|\|

*evamuktvā suragaṇānviṣ̣ṇuḥ satyaparākramaḥ\|*  
*jagāma brahmaṇā sārdhaṃ svalokaṃ tu mahāyaśāḥ \|\| 178.79 \|\|*

*etadāścaryamabhavatsaṅgrāme tārakāmaye\|*  
*dānavānāṃ ca viṣ̣ṇośca yanmāṃ tvaṃ paripṛṣ̣ṭavān \|\| 178.80 \|\|*

After thus speaking to the Devas, mighty Lord Visnu returned to His realm in company of Brahma. Such was the wonder of the Tarakamaya war that waged between the Devas and the demons and I have related all that which you asked me.

## \|\| 178.80 \|\|

*etadāścaryamabhavatsaṅgrāme tārakāmaye\|*  
*dānavānāṃ ca viṣṇośca yanmāṃ tvaṃ paripṛṣṭavān \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. Lord Vishnu after thus speaking to the Devas retired to His realm in company of Brahma. Such was the wonder of the Tarakamaya war that waged between the Devas and the demons and I have related all that to You.

## Chapter 179

## \|\| 179.1 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ\|*  
*śrutaḥ padmodbhavastāta vistareṇa tvayeritaḥ\|*  
*samāsādbhavamāhātmyaṃ bhairavasyābhidhīyatām \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. The Rishis said “O Suta! we have heard the creation from the lotus and the glory of Lord Vishnu narrated by you at such a full length; pray now tell us about the glory of the Lord Bhairava Bhava. (Shiva) ”

## \|\| 179.2-7 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*tasyāpi devadevasya śṛṇudhvaṃ karma cottamam\|*  
*āsīddaityo'ndhako nāma bhinnāñjanacayopamaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*tapasā mahatā yukto hyavadhyastridivaukasām\|*  
*sa kadācinmahādevaṃ pārvatyā sahitaṃ prabhum \|\| 3 \|\|*

*krīḍamānaṃ tadā dṛṣṭvā hartuṃ devīṃ pracakrame\|*  
*tasya yuddhaṃ tadā ghoramabhavatsaha śaṃbhunā \|\| 4 \|\|*

*avantiviṣaye ghore mahākālavanaṃ prati\|*  
*tasminyuddhe tadā rudra ścāndhakenātipīḍitaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*mumuca bāṇamatyugraṃ nāmnā pāśupataṃ hi tat\|*  
*rudra bāṇavinirbhedādrudhirādandhakasya tu \|\| 6 \|\|*

*andhakāśca samutpannāḥ śataśo'tha sasraśaḥ\|*  
*teṣāṃ vidāryamāṇānāṃ rudhirādapare punaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

2-7. Suta spoke: — I shall relate the glory of Shiva the Lord of Devas, which please hear with attention.

In ancient times there was a demon, as black as soot, who was known by the name of Andhaka. He was invulnerable of the Devas and was constantly engaged in his asceticism. Seeing one day the Lord Shiva and Parvati enjoying in each other’s company, he wished to snatch away the latter from the Lord, when a most fearful battle ensued between Him and the demon. That battle was fought in the Mahakala forest, in the district of Avanti. The Lord was very much oppressed by the demon when the Lord, Rudra discharged the weapon called Pashupata. Out of the blood that gushed from the body of that demon by the blow of that formidable arrow, thousands of Andhaka demons sprang up, and the gore of those demons also similarly multiplied itself into hundreds of demons.

## \|\| 179.33-35 \|\|

*andhakānāṃ mahāghorāḥ papustadrudhiraṃ tadā\|*  
*tato'ndhakāsṛjaḥ sarvāḥ parāṃ tṛptimupāgatāḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

*tāsu tṛptāsu saṃbhūtā bhūya evāndhakaprajāḥ\|*  
*arditastairmahādevaḥ śūlamudgarapāṇibhiḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

*tataḥ sa śaṃkaro devastvandhakairvyākulīkṛtaḥ\|*  
*jagāma śaraṇaṃ devaṃ vāsudevamajaṃ vibhum \|\| 35 \|\|*

33-35. They looked very terrible. They all drank the blood of those demons and were exceedingly gratified. After they were quite full and could not drink more blood, the demons again began to multiply by leaps and bounds, when Lord Shiva went to seek the succor of Vishnu.

## \|\| 179.36-37 \|\|

*tatastu bhagavānviṣṇuḥ sṛṣṭavāñśuṣkarevatīm\|*  
*yā papau sakalaṃ teṣāmandhakānāmasṛkkṣaṇāt \|\| 36 \|\|*

*yathā yathā ca rudhiraṃ pibantyandhakasaṃbhavam\|*  
*tathā tathā'dhikaṃ devī saṃśuṣyati janādhipa \|\| 37 \|\|*

36-37. Then Lord Vishnu, with great wrath, created Shushka-Revati who in a moment drank the blood of all the Andhaka demons. She became more withered and dry as she drank their blood, and when all the blood was drunk, the demons were completely annihilated.

## \|\| 179.38-39 \|\|

*pīyamāne tayā teṣāmandhakānāṃ tathā'sṛji\|*  
*andhakāstu kṣayaṃ nītāḥ sarve te tripurāriṇā \|\| 38 \|\|*

*mūlāndhakaṃ tu vikramya tadā śarvastrilokadhṛk\|*  
*cakāra vegācchūlāgne sa ca tuṣṭāva śaṃkaram \|\| 39 \|\|*

38-39. When Shiva with His valour was ready to pierce Andhaka the primary Asura, with His trident, the demon prayed to the Lord and He being pleased with His demotion, bestowed Ganeshatva to Him, and also made him the attendant-in-chief, and allowed him to remain in His company (granted Samipya).

## \|\| 179.40-51 \|\|

*andhakastu mahāvīryastasya tuṣṭo'bhavadbhavaḥ\|*  
*sāmīpyaṃ pradadau nityaṃ gaṇeśatvaṃ tathaiva ca \|\| 40 \|\|*

*tato mātṛgaṇāḥ sarve śaṃkaraṃ vākyamabruvan\|*  
*bhagavanbhakṣayiṣyāmaḥ sadevāsuramānuṣān\|*  
*tvatprasādājжagatsarvaṃ tadanujñātumarhasi \|\| 41 \|\|*

*śaṃkara uvāca*  
*bhavatībhiḥ prajā sarvā rakṣaṇīyā na saṃśayaḥ\|*  
*tasmādghorādabhiprāyānmanaśīghraṃ nivartyatām \|\| 42 \|\|*

*ityevaṃ śaṃkareṇoktamanādṛtya vacastadā\|*  
*bhakṣayāmāsuratyugrāstrailokyaṃ sacarācaram \|\| 43 \|\|*

*trailokye bhakṣyamāṇe tu tadā mātṛgaṇena vai\|*  
*nṛsiṃhamūrtiṃ deveśaṃ pradadhyau bhagavāñchivaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

*anādinidhanaṃ devaṃ sarvalokabhavodbhavam\|*  
*daityendra vakṣorudhiracarcitāgramahānakham \|\| 45 \|\|*

*vidyujжihvaṃ mahādaṃṣṭraṃ sphuratkesarakaṇṭakam\|*  
*kalpāntamārutakṣubdhaṃ saptārṇavasamasvanam \|\| 46 \|\|*

*vajratīkṣṇanakhaṃ ghoramākarṇavyāditānanam\|*  
*meruśailapratīkāśamudayārkasameṣaṇam \|\| 47 \|\|*

*himādri śikharākāraṃ cārudaṃṣṭrojжvalānanam\|*  
*nakhaniḥsṛtaroṣāgnijvālākesaramālinam \|\| 48 \|\|*

*baddhāṅgadaṃ sumukuṭaṃ hārakeyūrabhūṣaṇam\|*  
*śroṇīsūtreṇa mahatā kāñcanena virājitam \|\| 49 \|\|*

*nīlotpaladalaśyāmaṃ vāsoyugavibhūṣaṇam\|*  
*tejasā’krāntasakalabrahmāṇḍāgārasaṃkulam \|\| 50 \|\|*

*pavanabhrāmyamāṇānāṃ hutahavyavahārciṣām\|*  
*āvartasadṛśākāraiḥ saṃyuktaṃ dehalomajaiḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

40-51. Then all the Divine Mothers said to Shiva “Bhagavan! We shall through your favour eat up all the Devas, demons and men residing in all the three realms. Pray order us accordingly.” Shiva said: — “You should all undoubtedly protect the creation; so you should abandon this ignoble desire of yours.” But they unmindful of the words of the Lord, started their campaign of destruction, assuming terrific appearance. Then Diva thought of Narasinha, birthless and deathless and the creator of all the Lokas, Who instantly appeared then and there with His claws besmeared with the gore of Hiranyakashyapu, His tongue flapping out like a spark of electricity, with His formidable fangs and long teeth, full of mighty energy and roaring like that of the rumbling clouds, agitated by the fearful wind that blows at the time of the destruction of the world, thundering like the oceans, with His mouth wide open, with His nails hard like thunderbolt, with His eyes gleaming red like the Sun, burning with the fire of fury, wearing a crown, garlands, armlets, girdle of bells, fine garments, spreading His lustre all over the universe, shining like the fire blaze, having majestic hair, and wearing garlands of various kinds of beautiful flowers.. His appearance looked like the mountain Meru, and His two eyes looked like the Suns. His fearful rows of teeth, though formidable yet beautiful, illumined His face. His colour was blue like blue lotuses.

## \|\| 179.52-61 \|\|

*sarvapuṣpavicitrāṃ ca dhārayantaṃ mahāsrajam\|*

*yādṛśenaiva rūpeṇa dhyāto rudre ṇa dhīmatā\|*

*praṇipatya tu deveśaṃ tadā tuṣṭāva śaṃkaraḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

*śaṃkara uvāca*  
*namaste'stu jagannātha narasiṃhavapurdhara\|*  
*daityanāthāsṛjāpūrṇanakhaśuktivirājita \|\| 55 \|\|*

*tataḥ sakalasaṃlagna hemapiṅgalavigraha\|*  
*nato'smi padmanābha tvāṃ suraśakrajagadguro \|\| 56 \|\|*

*kalpāntāmbhodanirghoṣa sūryakoṭisamaprabha\|*  
*sahasrayamasaṃkrodha sahasrendra parākrama \|\| 57 \|\|*

*sahasradhanadasphīta sahasravaruṇātmaka\|*  
*sahasrakālaracita sahasraniyatendri ya \|\| 58 \|\|*

*sahasrabhūrmahādhairya sahasrānantamūrtiman\|*  
*sahasracandra pratima sahasragrahavikrama \|\| 59 \|\|*

*sahasrarudra tejaska sahasrabrahmasaṃstuta\|*  
*sahasrabāhuvegogra sahasrāsyanirīkṣaṇa\|*  
*sahasrayantramathana sahasravadhamocana \|\| 60 \|\|*

*andhakasya vināśāya yāḥ sṛṣṭā mātaro mayā\|*  
*anādṛtya tu madvākyaṃ bhakṣayantyudyatāḥ prajāḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

52-61. Narasinha appeared before Shiva in the same form as was thought of by Him. He was adorned with a pair of garments. The whole universe was overpowered with His lustre. The waving of the hairs on His body looked like so many rays of fire moving in wind. The Lord saluting Him said: “Lord of the universe! Devadeva in the form of Narasinha, my salutations to Thee. Looking handsome with Thy claws dyed in the gore of the demons, shining like gold, Padmanabha (from whose navel sprouted the lotus) the superior of the universe, my salutations to Thee. Thundering like the clouds at the time of the dissolution of the universe, illustrious like the thousands of suns, charged with the fury of a thousand Yam as, powerful like the thousands of Indras, prosperous like thousand Kuveras, the soul of a thousand Varuna and Kala, calm like a thousand earths, lustresome like thousand Moons, glorified like a thousand Rudras, valiant like a thousand heavenly bodies, having a thousand arms and eyes, the destroyer of many weapons, the liberator of thousands, such you are.

Deva! the Divine Mothers that I had created for the destruction of And h aka are now ready to devour the whole universe with utter disgard of My orders. 1 have created them, but I cannot destroy them now Myself. How can I, being their Creator become their Destroyer.”

## \|\| 179.62-64 \|\|

*kṛtvā tāśca na śakto'haṃ saṃhartumaparājita\|*  
*svayaṃ kṛtvā kathaṃ tāsāṃ vināśamabhikāraye \|\| 62 \|\|*

*evamuktaḥ sa rudre ṇa narasiṃhavapurdharaḥ\|*  
*sasarja devo jihvāyāstadā vāgīśvarīṃ hariḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

*hṛdayācca tathā māyā guhyācca bhavamālinī\|*  
*asthibhyaśca tathā kālī sṛṣṭā pūrvaṃ mahātmanā \|\| 64 \|\|*

62-64. Hearing such words of Shiva, Narasinha created Vanishvari from His tongue, Maya from His mind, Bhavamalini from His hinder private parts, Kill from His bones who drank the blood of the high-bodied demon Andhaka. She is known in this world by Shushka-Revati.

## \|\| 179.65 \|\|

*yayā tadrudhiraṃ pītamandhakānāṃ durātmanām\|*  
*yā cāsminkathitā loke nāmataḥ śuṣkarevatī \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. I shall also name to You the thirty-two Divine Mothers created by Vishnu from His body. They are all prosperous and fortunate. Their names are:

## \|\| 179.66-72 \|\|

*dvātriṃśanmātaraḥ sṛṣṭā gātrebhyaścakriṇā tataḥ\|*  
*tāsāṃ nāmāni vakṣyāmi tāni me gadataḥ śṛṇu \|\| 66 \|\|*

*sarvāstāstu mahābhāgā ghaṇṭākarṇī tathaiva ca\|*  
*trailokyamohinī puṇyā sarvasattvavaśaṃkarī \|\| 67 \|\|*

*tathā ca cakrahṛdayā pañcamī vyomacariṇī\|*
