*ityetāḥ pṛṣṭhagā rājanvāgīśānucarāḥ smṛtāḥ\|*  
*saṃkarṣaṇī tathā'śvatthā bījabhāvā'parāṃjetā \|\| 69 \|\|*

*kalyāṇī madhudaṃṣṭrī ca kamalotpalahastikā\|*  
*iti devyaṣṭakaṃ rājanmāyānucaramucyate \|\| 70 \|\|*

*ajitā sūkṣmahṛdayā vṛddhāveśāśmadaṃśanā\|*  
*nṛsiṃhabhairavā bilvā garutmaddhṛdayā jayā \|\| 71 \|\|*

*bhavamālinyanucarā ityaṣṭau nṛpa mātaraḥ\|*  
*ākarṇanī saṃbhaṭā ca tathaivottaramālikā \|\| 72 \|\|*

66-72. Ghantakarni, Trailokyamohini, Sarvasattvavashamkari, Chakrahridaya, Vyomacharini, Shankhini, Lekhani, Kamasankarshini, are the maids of honour of Vanishvari; and Sankarshini, Ashvathama, Bijabhava, Aparajita, Kalyani, Madhudanshtri, Kamalotpalahastika, are the maids of Maya; and Ajita, Sukshmahridaya, Vriddha, Veshasmadanshana, Nrisinhabhairava, Vilva, Garutmahridaya, Jaya, these eight the maids of Bhavamalini; and Akarnani, Sabhata, Uttaramalika, Padmakara, Jwalamukhi, Bhishanika, Kamadhenu, Balika are the maids of Revati.

## \|\| 179.73-84 \|\|

*jvālāmukhī bhīṣaṇikā kāmadhenuśca bālikā\|*  
*tathā padmakarā rājanrevatyanucarāḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

*aṣṭau mahābalāḥ sarvā devagātrasamudbhavāḥ\|*  
*trailokyasṛṣṭisaṃhārasamarthāḥ sarvadevatāḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

*tāḥ sṛṣṭamātrā devena kruddhā mātṛgaṇasya tu\|*  
*pradhāvitā mahārāja krodhavisphāritekṣaṇāḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

*aviṣahyatamaṃ tāsāṃ dṛṣṭitejaḥ sudāruṇam\|*  
*tameva śaraṇaṃ prāptā nṛsiṃho vākyamabravīt \|\| 76 \|\|*

*yathā manuṣyāḥ paśavaḥ palayanti cirātsutān\|*  
*jayanti te tathaivā'śu yathā vai devatāgaṇāḥ \|\| 77 \|\|*

*bhavantyastu tathā lokānpālayantu mayeritāḥ\|*  
*manujaiśca tathā devairyajadhvaṃ tripurāntakam \|\| 78 \|\|*

*na ca bādhā prakartavyā ye bhaktāstripurāntake\|*  
*ye ca māṃ saṃsmarantīha te ca rakṣyāḥ sadā narāḥ \|\| 79 \|\|*

*balikarma kariṣyanti yuṣmākaṃ ye sadā narāḥ\|*  
*sarvakāmapradāsteṣāṃ bhaviṣyadhvaṃ tathaiva ca \|\| 80 \|\|*

*ucchāsanādikaṃ ye ca kathayanti mayeritam\|*  
*te ca rakṣyāḥ sadā lokā rakṣitavyaṃ ca śāsanam \|\| 81 \|\|*

*raudrī ṃ! caiva parāṃ mūrtiṃ mahādevaḥ pradāsyati\|*  
*yuṣmanmukhyā mahādevyastaduktaṃ parirakṣyatha \|\| 82 \|\|*

*mayā mātṛgaṇaḥ sṛṣṭo yo'yaṃ vigatasādhvasaḥ\|*  
*eṣa nityaṃ viśālākṣo mayaiva saha raṃsyate \|\| 83 \|\|*

*mayā sārdhaṃ tathā pūjāṃ narebhyaścaiva lapsyatha\|*  
*pṛthaksupūjitā lokaiḥ sarvānkāmānpradāsyatha \|\| 84 \|\|*

73-84. All of them are most powerful and have been created from the body of Vishnu. They are powerful enough to create and destroy the whole universe. The Divine Mothers created by Vishnu subdued those created by Shiva, because none can stand the flash of wrath beaming from their eyes. The Matrikas who were ready to destroy the world, now took refuge of Nrisingha Deva who then explained them the whole situation.

He said: — “You should also foster and guard the universe with My command; as the men and animals look after their off spring, and as the Devas protect the creation so do ye also, and work in every way like the Devas. Let the Devas and men worship the Deva Tripurari Never cause pain to the devotees of Shiva; and you should also protect those who contemplate on Me. Those who will offer you sacrifices every day, You should give them all their desired objects. You should also guard those who recite the praises uttered by Me, and you should protect My seat. Lord Shiva will give you His Raudra Devi. You all would occupy the position of the highest Devi and protect Her also. You should guard the universe in conjunction with Her. The Divine Mothers created by Me will remain with Me, and will attain the oblations made by the devotees along with Me. Those who will adore you separately, you should give them all their desires. Those desirous of progeny will get children no doubt, if they worship Shushkadevi.”

## \|\| 179.85-86 \|\|

*śuṣkāṃ saṃpūjayiṣyanti ye ca putrārthino janāḥ\|*  
*teṣāṃ putrapradā devī bhaviṣyati na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 85 \|\|*

*evamuktvā tu bhagavānsaha mātṛgaṇane tu\|*  
*jvālāmālākulavapustatraivāntaradhīyata \|\| 86 \|\|*

85-86. Saying so Lord Vishnu disappeared from that spot with the Matrikas and the sacred Kritashaucha tirtha sprang up there. And here Mahadeva the Dispeller of all the troubles gave His Divine Raudra form to the Matrikas created by Him. And He remained enshrined there amongst the Matrikas.

## \|\| 179.87-90 \|\|

*tatra tīrthaṃ samutpannaṃ kṛtaśauceti yajжaguḥ\|*  
*tatrāpi pūrvajo devo jagadārtiharo haraḥ \|\| 87 \|\|*

*raudra sya mātṛvargasya dattvā rudra stu pārthiva\|*  
*raudrī ṃ! divyāṃ tanuṃ tatra mātṛmadhye vyavasthitaḥ \|\| 88 \|\|*

*sapta tā mātaro devyaḥ sārdhanārīśvaraḥ śivaḥ\|*  
*niveśya raudraṃ tatsthānaṃ tatraivāntaradhīyata \|\| 89 \|\|*

*samātṛvargasya harasya mūrtiryadā yadā yāti ca tatsamīpe\|*  
*deveśvarasyāpi nṛsiṃhamūrteḥ pūjāṃ vidhatte tripurāndhakāriḥ \|\| 90 \|\|*

87-90. Shiva, half man and half woman, after installing the seven Matrikas there in that Raudrasthana disappeared. And whenever the Matrikas created by Shiva approach the form of Him, the Lord Shiva, the Destroyer of Tripurandhaka, then that enemy of Tripura and Andhaka pays homage and puja to the Lord Vishnu in His form of Man-Lion, (and thus Shiva worships Vishnu).

## Chapter 180

## \|\| 180.1-3 \|\|

*ṛṣ̣aya ūcuḥ\|*  
*śruto'ndhakavadhaḥ sūta yathāvattvadudīritaḥ\|*  
*vārāṇasyāstu māhātmyaṃ śrotumicchāma sāṃpratam \|\| 180.1 \|\|*

*bhagavānpiṅgalaḥ kena gaṇatvaṃ samupāgataḥ\|*  
*annadatvaṃ ca saṃprāpto vārāṇasyāṃ mahādyutiḥ \|\| 180.2 \|\|*

*kṣ̣etrapālaḥ kathaṃ jātaḥ priyatvaṃ ca kathaṃ gataḥ\|*  
*etadicchāma kathitaṃ śrotuṃ brahmasuta tvayā \|\| 180.3 \|\|*

The Rsis said- “О Suta! we have heard about the destruction of Andhaka as well explained by you. But now we are eager to know the glory of the sacred Varanasi. How did Bhagavan Pingala, endued with great splendour become Ganesvara and the giver of the food to all within the precincts of KasT? How did he became the Ksetrapala and how did he attain the Pingalahood? О the son of Brahman! We wish to hear ail these from you.”

## \|\| 180.4-5 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*śṛṇudhvaṃ vai yathā lebhe gaṇeśatvaṃ sa piṅgalaḥ\|*  
*annadatvaṃ ca lokānāṃ sthānaṃ vārāṇasī tviha \|\| 180.4 \|\|*

*pūrṇabhadra sutaḥ śrīmānāsīdyakṣ̣aḥ pratāpavān\|*  
*harikeśa iti khyāto brahmaṇyo dhārmikaśca ha \|\| 180.5 \|\|*

Suta explained to them- “Hear, how did Pingala attain the form of Ganes'vara and the giver of food to all and how he got his residence in the city of Varanasi? There was one Yaksa, who was the son of Pumabhadra and was renowned by the name of Harikesa. He was very glorious, pious and righteous.

## \|\| 180.6-7 \|\|

*tasya janmaprabhṛtyeva śarve bhaktiranuttamā\|*  
*tadāsīttannamaskārastanniṣ̣ṭhastatparāyaṇaḥ \|\| 180.6 \|\|*

*āsīnaśca śayānaśca gacchaṃstiṣ̣ṭhannanuvrajan\|*  
*bhuñjāno'tha pibanvā'pi rudra mevānvacintayat \|\| 180.7 \|\|*

Since his birthtime, he was firm into devotion of Lord Siva and at all hours, he was attached with Him and he was engaged in salutation to Siva and his heart was in Siva. Sitting, sleeping, walking, standing, drinking, eating, he thought of Siva at everytime.

## \|\| 180.8-9 \|\|

*tamevaṃ yuktamanasaṃ pūrṇabhadra ḥ! pitā'bravīt\|*  
*na tvāṃ putramahaṃ manye durjāto yastvamanyathā \|\| 180.8 \|\|*

*na hi yakṣ̣akulīnānāmetadvṛttaṃ bhavatyuta\|*  
*guhyakā bata yūyaṃ vai svabhāvātkrūracetasaḥ \|\| 180.9 \|\|*

His father Purnabhadra said tohisrighteous son- “O son! I do not recognise you as my son. Your birth is unfortunate and deplorable. It is not meet to lead such a life in the race of a Yaksa. You are all Guhyakaswhich are courageous and cruel by nature.

## \|\| 180.10-13 \|\|

*kravyādāścaiva kiṃbhakṣ̣ā hiṃsāśīlāśca putraka\|*  
*maivaṃ kārṣ̣īrna te vṛttirevaṃ dṛṣ̣ṭā mahātmanā \|\| 180.10 \|\|*

*svayaṃbhuvā yathā’diṣ̣ṭā tyaktavyā yadino bhavet\|*  
*āśramāntarajaṃ karma na kuryurgṛhiṇastu tat \|\| 180.11 \|\|*

*hitvā manuṣ̣yabhāvaṃ ca karmabhirvividhaiścara\|*  
*yattvamevaṃ vimārgastho manuṣ̣yājжāta eva ca \|\| 180.12 \|\|*

*yathāvadvividhaṃ teṣ̣āṃ karma tajжātisaṃśrayam\|*  
*mayā'pi vihitaṃ paśya karmaitannātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 180.13 \|\|*

0 son! we are addicted to hunting and flesheating. Do not follow this type as high-souled Brahma has not ordained us to that you pursue. One ought not to follow the life of a different order abandoning his own. You should, therefore, give up your humanbeings and follow the course according to your race. Seeing this wrong act, I think that you have been bom of men. These all acts are according to their order of life. Therefore, see my acts which have been performed pertaining to my class of being. You should not have any doubt therein.”

## \|\| 180.14-16 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*evamuktvā sa taṃ putraṃ pūrṇabhadra ḥ! pratāpavān\|*  
*uvāca niṣ̣ṭhuraṃ kṣ̣ipraṃ gaccha putra yathecchasi \|\| 180.14 \|\|*

*tataḥ sa nirgatastyaktvā gṛhaṃ saṃbandhinastathā\|*  
*vārāṇasīṃ samāsādya tapastepe suduścaram \|\| 180.15 \|\|*

*sthāṇubhūto hyanimiṣ̣aḥ śuṣ̣kakāṣ̣ṭhopalopamaḥ\|*  
*saṃniyamyendri yagrāmamavātiṣ̣ṭhata niścalaḥ \|\| 180.16 \|\|*

Suta said- After thus speaking to his son, that glorious Purnabhadra went out quickly and asked him- О my son, leave his home and go away to that place as you wish. On these words of his father, he left his home and all family members and went to Varanasi where he engaged himself to rigid asceticism. Controling on all senses he stood there motionless, vigilantly and like a dried up piece of wood or a piece of stone.

## \|\| 180.17-20 \|\|

*atha tasyaiva tapasi saṃsthitasya mahātmanaḥ\|*  
*sahasramekaṃ varṣ̣āṇāṃ divyamapyabhyavartata \|\| 180.17 \|\|*

*valmīkena samākrānto bhakṣ̣yamāṇaḥ pipīlikaiḥ\|*  
*vajrasūcimukhaistīkṣ̣ṇairvidhyamānastathaiva ca \|\| 180.18 \|\|*

*nirmāṃsarudhiratvakca kundaśaṅkhendusaprabhaḥ\|*  
*asthiśeṣ̣o'bhavaccharvaṃ devaṃ vai cintayannapi \|\| 180.19 \|\|*

*etasminnantare devī vyajñāpayata śaṃkaram \|\| 180.20 \|\|*

Having thus engaged in austerities like that, one thousand divine years have been passed. He was surrounded by ant-hills on all sides and white ants and insects began to feast on him by their hard and sharpened mouths like a thunderbolt. Thus devotee of Siva was looking like a white shell as he became without flesh, blood and skin. He remained with his bones only. In the meantime, the Goddess Parvatl requested to Siva.

## \|\| 180.21-23 \|\|

*devyuvāca*  
*udyānaṃ punarevedaṃ dra ṣ̣ṭumicchāmi sarvadā\|*  
*kṣ̣etrasya deva māhātmyaṃ śrotuṃ kautūhalaṃ hi me\|*  
*yataśca priyametatte tathā'sya phalamuttamam \|\| 180.21 \|\|*

*Goddess said- “O Lord! I want to see again that gardens and bowers and I am eager to hear the glory of KasT which is your dearest resort, it must bear excellent results.*

*iti vijñāpito devaḥ śarvāṇyā parameśvaraḥ\|*  
*sarvaṃ pṛṣ̣ṭhaṃ yathātathyamākhyātumupacakrame \|\| 180.22 \|\|*

*nirjagāma ca deveśaḥ pārvatyā saha śaṃkaraḥ\|*  
*udyānaṃ darśayāmāsa devyā devaḥ pinākadhṛk \|\| 180.23 \|\|*

Thus addressed by Parvatl, Siva started to explain the story of Kasi. Lord Siva, having a Pinaka bow went out with Parvatl and show Her the sylvan beauties of garden.

## \|\| 180.24-25 \|\|

*devadeva uvāca*  
*protphullanānāvidhagulmaśobhitaṃ latāpratānāvanataṃ manoharam\|*  
*virūḍhapuṣ̣paiḥ paritaḥ priyaṅgubhiḥ supuṣ̣pitaiḥ kaṇṭakitaiśca ketakaiḥ \|\| 180.24 \|\|*

*tamālagulmairnicitaṃ sugandhibhiḥ sakarṇikārairbakulaiśca sarvaśaḥ\|*  
*aśokapuṃnāgavaraiḥ supuṣ̣pitairdvirephamālākulapuṣ̣pasaṃcayaiḥ \|\| 180.25 \|\|*

Siva said- This garden is so beautiful with different types of flower clusters and beautified with longest creepers, flowers of Priyangu from all sides, and flowered with KetakI, sweet-scented Tamala, Karnikara (Pterospermum acerifolium), Vakula, As'oka, Punnaga, and various types of sweet-smelling flowers swarmed by the buzzing blackbees.

## \|\| 180.26 \|\|

*kvacitpraphullāmbujareṇurūṣ̣itairvihaṅgamaiścārukalapraṇādibhiḥ\|*  
*vināditaṃ sārasamaṇḍanādibhiḥ pramattadātyūharutaiśca valgubhiḥ \|\| 180.26 \|\|*

There are the sweet-singing birds are throwing their melodious notes on the blooming lotuses; somewhere beautiful swans and enchanted blackbees are creating a bustle.

## \|\| 180.27 \|\|

*kvacicca cakrāhvaravopanāditaṃ kvacicca kādambakadambakairyutam\|*  
*kvacicca kāraṇḍavanādanāditaṃ kvacicca mattālikulākulīkṛtam \|\| 180.27 \|\|*

At some places Cakravakas are echoing notes; at some places there are kala-harhsas and the trees of Kadambas; at other places Karandavas (a sort of ducks) are sounding notes. Some places are surrounded by the group of bees.

## \|\| 180.28 \|\|

*madākulābhistvamarāṅganādibhirniṣ̣evitaṃ cārusugandhipuṣ̣pam\|*  
*kvacitsupuṣ̣paiḥ sahakāravṛkṣ̣airlatopagūḍhaistilakadrumaiśca \|\| 180.28 \|\|*

Somewhere the celestial ladies are enjoying the aroma of flowers. At some places the garden is beautified with flavoured mango trees and somewhere the creepers circling round on the trees of Tilakas.

## \|\| 180.29 \|\|

*pragītavidyādharasiddhacāraṇaṃ pravṛttanṛtyāpsarasāṃ gaṇākulam\|*  
*prahṛṣ̣ṭanānāvidhapakṣ̣isevitaṃ pramattahārītakulopanāditam \|\| 180.29 \|\|*

Somewhere the Vidyadharas, Siddhas and Caranas were singing the songs, at some place, the group of nymphs were dancing, somewhere the cheerful birds repeating their captivating notes, somewhere the green pigeons were echoing notes.

## \|\| 180.30 \|\|

*mṛgendra nādākulasattvamānasaiḥ kvacitkvaciddvaṃdvakadambakairmṛgaiḥ\|*  
*praphullanānāvidhacārupaṅkajaiḥ sarastaḍāgairupaśobhitaṃ kvacit \|\| 180.30 \|\|*

At some places the roars of the lion were being heard; the deer were running away with fear at other places, somewhere this garden was beautified with the lakes flourished with full blown lotuses of many kinds.

## \|\| 180.31 \|\|

*nibiḍaniculanīlaṃ nīlakaṇṭhābhirāmaṃ madamuditavihaṅgavrātanādābhirāmam\|*  
*kusumitataruśākhālīnamattadvirephaṃ navakisalayaśobhāśobhitaprāntaśākham \|\| 180.31 \|\|*

This forest was blue coloured with closed Nicula trees (Barringtonia Acutangula), and was so delightful with peacocks. Somewhere a swarm of blackbees buzzed over the flowered branches of trees, somewhere the new foliage bedecked the branches.

## \|\| 180.32 \|\|

*kvacicca dantikṣ̣atacāruvīrudhaṃ kvacillatāliṅgitacāruvṛkṣ̣akam\|*  
*kvacidvilāsālasagāmibarhiṇaṃ niṣ̣evitaṃ kiṃpuruṣ̣avrajaiḥ kvacit \|\| 180.32 \|\|*

Somewhere it was beautified by the creepers, broken by being trampled by the elephants, somewhere were seen the charming trees embraced with creepers. At some places the sporting peacocks are going slowly and somewhere the Yaksas are walking for pleasure.

## \|\| 180.33-34 \|\|

*pārāvatadhvanivikūjitacāruśṛṅgairabhraṃkaṣ̣aiḥ sitamanoharacārurūpaiḥ\|*  
*ākīrṇapuṣ̣panikurambavimuktahāsairvibhrājitaṃ tridaśadevakulairanekaiḥ \|\| 180.33 \|\|*

*phullotpalāgurusahasravitānayuktaistoyāśayaiḥ samanuśobhitadeyamārgam\|*  
*mārgāntarāgalitapuṣ̣pavicitrabhāktisaṃbaddhagulmaviṭapairvihagairupetam \|\| 180.34 \|\|*

At some places the pigeons cooed over the peaks of the mountains, touching the clouds, Such a beautiful forest adorned with white flowers and the Devas were pointed out to Parvatl by Siva, where sports and amusements are held are being echoed by pigeons. They look white and exceedingly beautiful and were shining with the beauties of all sorts of flowers. The sight of them made one fancy that many inhabitants of the heavens were resorting there. The various kinds of birds were chirping on the branches of those trees.

## \|\| 180.35 \|\|

*tuṅgāgrairnīlapuṣ̣pastabakabharanataprāntaśākhairaśokai-\|*  
*rmattālivrātagītaśrutisukhajananairbhāsitāntarmanojñaiḥ\|*  
*rātrau candra sya bhāsā kusumitatilakairekatāṃ saṃprayātaṃ\|*  
*chāyāsuptaprabuddhasthitahariṇakulāluptadarbhāṅkurāgram \|\| 180.35 \|\|*

The Asoka trees with their branches bowing down to the ground by the weight of flowers looked highly beautiful. The beautiful blossoms, pervaded with the swarm of singing blackbees, were indistinguishable from the silvery moonbeams playing on them during the night. The herds of deer standing in thickets overshadowed by the trees were grazing on green meadows and exhibited a different kind of beauty.

## \|\| 180.36 \|\|

*haṃsānāṃ pakṣ̣apātapracalitakamalasvacchavistīrṇatoyaṃ\|*  
*toyānāṃ tīrajātapravikacakadalīvāṭanṛtyanmayūram\|*  
*sāyūraiḥ pakṣ̣acandrai ḥ! kvacidapi patita rañjitakṣ̣māpradeśaṃ\|*  
*deśe deśe vikīrṇapramuditavilasanmattahārītavṛkṣ̣am \|\| 180.36 \|\|*

Somewhere the wings of swans rubbing against the clean water, and by which the lotuses enhanced their beauty. Somewhere the peacocks are dancing near blown plantain tree on the bank of ponds. The beautiful spots on the peacock feathers dazzled by the reflection of the moonbeams, when those majestic birds danced at other places. At all places the trees looked exceedingly beautiful by moving sportly of Harita birds.

## \|\| 180.37 \|\|

*sāraṅgaiḥ kvacidapi sevitapradeśaṃ saṃchannaṃ kusumacayaiḥ kvacidvicitraiḥ\|*  
*hṛṣ̣ṭābhiḥ kvacidapi kiṃnarāṅganābhiḥ kṣ̣ībābhiḥ samadhuragītavṛkṣ̣akhaṇḍam \|\| 180.37 \|\|*

Some part of land is surrounded by the Saranga deers. Somewhere the groups of various flowers covered the land, somewhere the air resounded with the melodies of the enchanted Kinnara ladies.

## \|\| 180.38 \|\|

*saṃsṛṣ̣ṭaiḥ kvacidupaliptakīrṇapuṣ̣pairāvāsaiḥ parivṛtapādapaṃ munīnām\|*  
*āmūlātphalanicitaiḥ kvacidviśālairuttuṅgaiḥ panasamahīruhairupetam \|\| 180.38 \|\|*

Somewhere the Munis squatted themselves on the floor of their hermitages strewn with flowers, somewhere the large and high Panasa1 trees looked beautiful with their plethora of fruits.

## \|\| 180.39 \|\|

*phullātimuktakalatāgṛhasiddhalīlaṃ siddhāṅganākanakanūpuranādaramyam\|*  
*ramyapriyaṅgutarumañjarisaktabhṛṅgaṃ bhṛṅgāvalīskhalitacārukadambapuṣ̣pam \|\| 180.39 \|\|*

Somewhere the houses of Siddhas are beautified with the blown creeper of Atimukta2 where jingling of the anklets made of gold, of the Siddha ladies filled the space, somewhere the bees swarming on cluster of blossoms of the Priyangu plant and by the force of them, flowers of Ambu and Kadamba were falling  
down.

## \|\| 180.40 \|\|

*puṣ̣potkarānilavighūrṇitapādapāgramagresarairbhuvi nipātitavaṃśagulmam\|*  
*gulmāntaraprasṛtabhītamṛgīsamūhaṃ saṃmuhyatāṃ tanubhṛtāmapavargadātṛ \|\| 180.40 \|\|*

Somewhere the air loaded with the perfume of the flowers diffused a maddening smell all round on earth, somewhere the group of deer standing among the cluster of trees looked exceedingly charming, The thorough fares with the blooming trees looked beautiful like the Divine pathways.

## \|\| 180.41 \|\|

*candrā śuṃ!jāladhavalaistilakairmanojñaiḥ sindūrakuṅkumakusumbhanibhairaśokaiḥ\|*  
*cāmīkarapratisamairatha karṇikāraiḥ phullāravindaracitaṃ suviśālaśākhaiḥ \|\| 180.41 \|\|*

Somewhere were the beautiful flowers of Tilaka tree (Clerodendrum phlomoides) as white as the moonbeams, somewhere were the groups of As'oka trees like red coloured vermillion and saffron, somewhere were the Karnikaras (Pterospermum acerifolium) of yellow colour like heap of gold and were having large branches.

## \|\| 180.42 \|\|

*kvacidra jataparṇābhaiḥ kvacidvidrumasaṃnibhaiḥ\|*  
*kvacitkāñcanasaṃkāśaiḥ puṣ̣pairācitabhūtalam \|\| 180.42 \|\|*

Somewhere the garden land blossomed with the white coloured flowers like the silver-leaves, somewhere red like coral and somewhere looked like golden colours.

## \|\| 180.43 \|\|

*punnāgesu dvijagaṇavirutaṃ raktāśokastabakabharanamitam\|*  
*ramyopāntaśramaharapavanaṃ phullābjeṣ̣u bhramaravilasitam \|\| 180.43 \|\|*

The garden was filled with the cries of birds seated on the Punnaga trees, At some places the branches of As'oka tree are bent full of red flowers. Somewhere the pleasant wind was removing fatigue of all beings and the blackbees buzzed on the blown lotuses.

## \|\| 180.44 \|\|

*sakalabhuvanabhartā lokanāthastadānīṃ tuhinaśikhariputr! yāḥ sārdhamiṣ̣ṭairgaṇeśaiḥ\|*  
*vividhataruviśālaṃ mattahṛṣ̣ṭānyapuṣ̣ṭamupavanataruramyaṃ darśayāmāsa devyāḥ \|\| 180.44 \|\|*

The Lord Siva, the protector of whole universe and lord of all beings in company of their Ganas, pointed out to Parvatl, the daughter of Himalaya, the beautiful forest surrounded with many large pleasant trees.

## \|\| 180.45-46 \|\|

*devyuvāca*  
*udyānaṃ darśitaṃ deva śobhayā parayā yutam\|*  
*kṣ̣etrasya tu guṇānsarvānpunarvaktumihārhasi \|\| 180.45 \|\|*

*asya kṣ̣etrasya māhātmyamavimuktasya tattathā\|*  
*śrutvā'pi hi na me tṛptirato bhūyo vadasva me \|\| 180.46 \|\|*

Then Parvatl said- “O Lord! You have shown the majestic garden of this forest, now you are able to narrate the merits and glory of KasT, the Avimukta Ksetra, because I am not satisfied sufficiently hearing all, so I wish to hear it again.”

## \|\| 180.47-48 \|\|

*devadeva uvāca*  
*idaṃ guhyatamaṃ kṣ̣etraṃ sadā vārāṇasī mama\|*  
*sarveṣ̣āmeva bhūtānāṃ heturmokṣ̣asya sarvadā \|\| 180.47 \|\|*

*asminsiddhāḥ sadā devi madīyaṃ vratamāsthitāḥ\|*  
*nānāliṅgadharā nityaṃ mama lokābhikāṅkṣ̣iṇaḥ \|\| 180.48 \|\|*

*abhyasyanti paraṃ yogaṃ muktātmāno jitendri yāḥ\|*

Siva said- “This sacred place of KasI is My secret or mysterious place. It is cause of emancipation to all creatures. О Devi! there are many Siddhas, who have taken up vows and there are various orders of saints with various Lirigas or signs, wish to achieve my regions. Many high-souled saints controlling their senses practising highest yogas.

## \|\| 180.49-50 \|\|

*nānāvṛkṣ̣asamākīrṇe nānāvihagakūjite \|\| 180.49 \|\|*

*kamalotpalapuṣ̣pāḍhyaiḥ sarobhiḥ samalaṃkṛte\|*  
*apsarogaṇagandharvaiḥ sadā saṃsevite śubhe \|\| 180.50 \|\|*

*rocate me sadā vāso yena kāryeṇa tacchṛṇu\|*

This place is surrounded with various trees and filled with noise of many birds and adorned with lotus beds. The reason of my presence in this sacred, auspicious and beautiful place, which is always frequented by nymphs and Gandharvas; I shall now explain to you.

## \|\| 180.51-53 \|\|

*manmanā mama bhaktaśca mayi sarvārpitakriyaḥ \|\| 180.51 \|\|*

*yathā mokṣ̣amihā’pnoti hyanyatra na tathā kvacit\|*  
*etanmama puraṃ divyaṃ guhyādguhyataraṃ mahat \|\| 180.52 \|\|*

*brahmādayastu jānanti ye'pi siddhā mumukṣ̣avaḥ\|*  
*ataḥ priyatamaṃ kṣ̣etraṃ tasmācceha ratirmama \|\| 180.53 \|\|*

My devotees constantly meditating on Me and dedicating all their deeds to me, attain final emancipation, which they would not get anywhere else. This my city is more mysterious than all other secret places. Lord Brahma and other gods, the Siddhas and wishers of liberation from final beatitude, also reckon this sacred place as supreme. This is the reason of My attachment with this place.

## \|\| 180.54 \|\|

*vimuktaṃ na mayā yasmānmokṣ̣yate vā kadā ca na\|*  
*mahatkṣ̣etramidaṃ tasmādavimuktamidaṃ smṛtam \|\| 180.54 \|\|*

I never leave this sacred place Kasi, nor will I ever leave it. Hence name is Avimukta Ksetra of this highest place.

## \|\| 180.55-56 \|\|

*naimiṣ̣e'tha kurukṣ̣etre gaṅgādvāre ca puṣ̣kare\|*  
*snānātsaṃsevitādvā'pi na mokṣ̣aḥ prāpyate yataḥ \|\| 180.55 \|\|*

*iha saṃprāpyate yena tata etadviśiṣ̣yate\|*  
*prayāge ca bhavenmokṣ̣a iha vā matparigrahāt \|\| 180.56 \|\|*

One who take bath at Naimisaranya, Kuruksetra, Gangadvara, and Puskara or devoting his self there does not get final emancipation there, but he gets it here, and therefore; it is so superior to all the sanctified places. There is no doubt. The people get Moksa at Prayaga or at this place by my refuge.

## \|\| 180.57 \|\|

*prayāgādapi tīrthāgryādidameva mahatsmṛtam\|*  
*jaigīṣ̣avyaḥ parāṃ siddhiṃ yo gataḥ sa mahātapāḥ \|\| 180.57 \|\|*

This Varanasi is the chief of all pilgrimages, even Prayaga also. Rsi Jaiglsavya attained the highest emancipation by his yogic power.

## \|\| 180.58-60 \|\|

*asya kṣ̣etrasya māhātmyādbhaktyā ca mama bhāvanāt\|*  
*jaigīṣ̣avyo mahāśreṣ̣ṭho yogināṃ sthānamiṣ̣yate \|\| 180.58 \|\|*

*dhyāyatastatra māṃ nityaṃ yogāgnirdīpyate bhṛśam\|*  
*kaivalyaṃ paramaṃ yāti devānāmapi durlabham \|\| 180.59 \|\|*

*avyaktaliṅgairmunibhiḥ sarvasiddhāntavedibhiḥ\|*  
*iha saṃprāpyate mokṣ̣o durlabho devadānavaiḥ \|\| 180.60 \|\|*

The great ascetic Rsi Jaiglsavya, by the glory of this place and his devotion towards Me, desired to reach the goal of the yogis. He meditated on Me continuously. By his meditation, the fire of yoga was kindled in him, and he attained the Kaivalya (final goal or liberation from beatitude) which is very rare to the gods also. The seers, well-versed in all scriptures attain such Moksa here as is rarely attainable by the gods and the demons.

## \|\| 180.61-62 \|\|

*tebhyaścāhaṃ prayacchāmi bhogaiśvaryamanuttamam\|*  
*ātmanaścaiva sāyujyamīpsitaṃ sthānameva ca \|\| 180.61 \|\|*

*kuberastu mahāyakṣ̣astathā sarvārpitakriyaḥ\|*  
*kṣ̣etrasaṃvasanādeva gaṇeśatvamavāpa ha \|\| 180.62 \|\|*

I shall grant them great enjoyments, prosperity, and communion with Me, also the place that they desire. Kubera, the Lord of the Yaksas, residing at this place by dedicating all his deeds to me become like my attendant.

## \|\| 180.63 \|\|

*saṃvarto bhavitā yaśca so'pi bhakto mamaiva tu\|*  
*ihaivā’rādhya māṃ devi siddhiṃ yāsyatyanuttamām \|\| 180.63 \|\|*

О Devi! my devotee Samvarta will also attain in future the highest Siddhi here, by adoring Me with devotion.

## \|\| 180.64 \|\|

*parāśarasuto yogī ṛṣ̣irvyāso mahātapāḥ\|*  
*dharmakartā bhaviṣ̣yaśca vedasaṃsthāpravartakaḥ \|\| 180.64 \|\|*

*raṃsyate so'pi padmākṣ̣i kṣ̣etre'sminmunipuṃgavaḥ\|*

О lotus eyed one! The son of Parasara, the great Yogi, great ascetic Rsi Vyasa, who will be the propagator of the religion and promoter of Vedas, best of the Munis, will also live in this sacred place.

## \|\| 180.65-66 \|\|

*brahmā devarṣ̣ibhiḥ sārdhaṃ viṣ̣ṇurvāyurdivākaraḥ \|\| 180.65 \|\|*

*devarājastathā śakro ye'pi cānye divaukasaḥ\|*  
*upāsate mahātmānaḥ sarve māmeva suvrate \|\| 180.66 \|\|*

О noble one! Brahma, Visnu, Vayu the Sun alongwith the great sages, lord of the gods Indra and the other gods and many high-souled persons are also worshipping me here.

## \|\| 180.67 \|\|

*anye'pi yoginaḥ siddhāśchannarūpā mahāvratāḥ\|*  
*ananyamanaso bhūtvā māmihopāsate sadā \|\| 180.67 \|\|*

Many other Siddha Yogis, taking great vows and under disguise, with dedication to me residing here always adore me.

## \|\| 180.68-69 \|\|

*alarkaśca purīmetāṃ matprasādādavāpsyati\|*  
*sa caināṃ pūrvavatkṛtvā cāturvarṇyāśramākulām \|\| 180.68 \|\|*

*sphītāṃ janasamākīrṇāṃ bhaktyā ca suciraṃ nṛpaḥ\|*  
*mayi sarvārpitaprāṇo māmeva pratipatsyate \|\| 180.69 \|\|*

The king Alarka, also through my grace, will attain this city. This king will cause it to thrive as before, with great prosperity among the group of people of four castes and four order of life so long. Dedicating his whole life to me, he will then attain Me.

## \|\| 180.70-71 \|\|

*tataḥ prabhṛti cārvaṅgi ye'pi kṣ̣etranivāsinaḥ\|*  
*gṛhiṇo liṅgino vā'pi madbhaktā matparāyaṇāḥ \|\| 180.70 \|\|*

*matprasādādbhajiṣ̣yanti mokṣ̣aṃ paramadurlabham\|*  
*viṣ̣ayāsaktacitto'pi tyaktadharmaratirnaraḥ \|\| 180.71 \|\|*

*iha kṣ̣etre mṛtaḥ so'pi saṃsāraṃ na punarviśet\|*

О beautiful one! all the householders and ascetics who are residing in Kas'I, will be devoted and addicted to me. Through my fervour they will attain the highest goal of final emancipation, so very rare. Any one who is the most sensuous, and has no faith to dharma, will not be bom in this world after the death.

## \|\| 180.72-75 \|\|

*ye punarnirmamā dhīrāḥ sattvasthā vijitendri yāḥ \|\| 180.72 \|\|*

*vratinaśca nirārambhāḥ sarve te mayi bhāvitāḥ\|*  
*dehabhaṅgaṃ samāsādya dhīmantaḥ saṅgavarjitāḥ\|*  
*gatā eva paraṃ mokṣ̣am prasādānmama suvrate \|\| 180.73 \|\|*

*janmāntarasahasreṣ̣u yuñjanyogamavāpnuyāt\|*  
*tamihaiva paraṃ mokṣ̣aṃ maraṇādadhigacchati \|\| 180.74 \|\|*

*etatsaṃkṣ̣epato devi kṣ̣etrasyāsya mahatphalam\|*  
*avimuktasya kathitaṃ mayā te guhyamuttamam \|\| 180.75 \|\|*

Those who are free from all mundane cravings, have patience, and have stationed themselves in sattvaguna, with their passions subdued and devoted to me, dying here will undoubtedly attain liberation through my grace. The final rest attained by the people, through the continual practice of yoga in course of thousands of ages, is attained merely by dying here. Devi! I have related to you the glory of this sacred place Avimukta Ksetra, in brief, which is most mysterious.

## \|\| 180.76-77 \|\|

*ataḥ parataraṃ nāsti siddhiguhyaṃ maheśvari\|*  
*etadbudhyanti yogajñā ye ca yogeśvarā bhuvi \|\| 180.76 \|\|*

*etadeva paraṃ sthānametadeva paraṃ śivam\|*  
*etadeva paraṃ brahma etadeva paraṃ padam \|\| 180.77 \|\|*

O Mahes'varl! there is no other mysterious fact to obtain the Siddhi. Who are endued with the knowledge of Yoga and are the Yogis in this country, have this secret knowledge. This is the final goal, Supreme Brahman and the place of final emancipation.

## \|\| 180.78 \|\|

*vārāṇasī tu bhuvanatrayasārabhūtā ramyā sadā mama purī girirājaputri\|*  
*atrā’gatā vividhaduṣ̣kṛtakāriṇo'pi pāpakṣ̣ayādvirajasaḥ pratibhānti martyāḥ \|\| 180.78 \|\|*

This Varanasi is the essence of the three worlds. О Parvatl! my this city is very enchanting and beautiful. The people endued with sins of many ways, come to this place, are also freed from their all sins.

## \|\| 180.79 \|\|

*etatsmṛtaṃ priyatamaṃ mama devi nityaṃ kṣ̣etraṃ vicitratarugulmalatāsupuṣ̣pam\|*  
*asminmṛtāstanubhṛtaḥ padamāpnuvanti mūrkhāgamena rahitāpi na saṃśayo'tra \|\| 180.79 \|\|*

О goddess! this place is always dear to Me. This is splendid with various kinds of creepers, bowers and flowers. People dying here are liberated from the cycle of birth and death and attain the highest place. There is no doubt in this.

## \|\| 180.80-82 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*etasminnantare devo devīṃ prāha girīndra jām\|*  
*dātuṃ prasādaṃ yakṣ̣āya varaṃ bhaktāya bhāmini \|\| 180.80 \|\|*

*bhakto mama varārohe tapasā hatakilbiṣ̣aḥ\|*  
*arho varamasau labdhumasmatto bhuvaneśvari \|\| 180.81 \|\|*

*evamuktvā tato devaḥ saha devyā jagatpatiḥ\|*  
*jagāma yakṣ̣o yatrā’ste kṛśo dhamanisaṃtataḥ \|\| 180.82 \|\|*

Suta said- Meanwhile Lord Siva said to goddess Parvatl, the daughter of Himalaya for granting of boon to the devotee Yaksa. He said “O goddess of the universe! О beautiful one! this Yaksa, devotee of Mine is now sinless by his asceticism and he is able to get from Me some boon.” After saying so, Siva, the Lord of the universe, repaired to that spot in company of Parvatl, where the weak and full-veined Yaksa was practising austerities.

## \|\| 180.83-86 \|\|

*tatastaṃ guhyakaṃ devī dṛṣ̣ṭipātairnirīkṣ̣atī\|*  
*śvetavarṇaṃ vicarmāṇam snāyubaddhāsthipañjaram \|\| 180.83 \|\|*

*devī prāha tadā devaṃ darśayantī ca guhyakam\|*  
*satyaṃ nāma bhavānugro devairuktastu śaṃkara \|\| 180.84 \|\|*

*īdṛśe cāsya tapasi na prayacchasi yadvaram\|*  
*ataḥ kṣ̣etre mahādeva puṇye samyagupāsite \|\| 180.85 \|\|*

*kathamevaṃ parikleśaṃ prāpto yakṣ̣akumārakaḥ\|*  
*śīghramasya varaṃ yaccha prasādātparameśvara \|\| 180.86 \|\|*

After that, Parvatl, seeing the Yaksa’s bones shining white as he was reduced to a mere skeleton, said to Siva, showing him- “Verily the Gods describe You to be so stiff; it is quite right because you do not grant boon to even such of your devotees. In such a sacred place, it is not proper that this Yaksa’s boy should be subjected to such trouble. О Lord! grant him a boon quickly.

## \|\| 180.87 \|\|

*evaṃ manvādayo deva vadanti paramarṣ̣ayaḥ\|*  
*ruṣ̣ṭādvā cātha tuṣ̣ṭādvā siddhistūbhayato bhavet\|*  
*bhogaprāptistathā rājyamante mokṣ̣aḥ sadāśivāt \|\| 180.87 \|\|*

“O Lord! the Rsis, like Manu and others, say that success is always attained from Siva whether he is pleased or not pleased. Besides this, all beings attain the enjoyments and kingdoms during lifetime and also emancipation after death.”

## \|\| 180.88 \|\|

*evamuktastato devaḥ saha devyā jagatpatiḥ\|*  
*jagāma yakṣ̣o yatrā’ste kṛśo dhamanisaṃtataḥ \|\| 180.88 \|\|*

After addressing him, the Lord of the universe, repaired to that spot in company of Parvatl, where the Yaksa was practising austerities.

## \|\| 180.89-90 \|\|

*taṃ dṛṣ̣ṭvā praṇataṃ bhaktyā harikeśaṃ vṛṣ̣adhvajaḥ\|*  
*divyaṃ cakṣ̣uradāttasmai yenāpaśyatsa śaṃkaram \|\| 180.89 \|\|*

*atha yakṣ̣astadādeśācchanairunmīlya cakṣ̣uṣ̣ī\|*  
*apaśyatsagaṇaṃ devaṃ vṛṣ̣adhvajamupasthitam \|\| 180.90 \|\|*

Looking at him bowing down before the Lord with devotion, Siva approached the Yaksa. The Lord then granted him Divine vision, by which he was able to behold the Siva. After that by order of the Lord, Yaksa saw Him with all attendants through his eyes.

## \|\| 180.91 \|\|

*devadeva uvāca*  
*varaṃ dadāmi te pūrvaṃ trailokye darśanaṃ tathā\|*  
*sāvarṇyaṃ ca śarīrasya paśya māṃ vigatajvaraḥ \|\| 180.91 \|\|*

Then the Lord said “I am granting you a boon, by virtue of which you will see the three realms, and your body will also become like Mine. Look at me, being free from all disease.”

## \|\| 180.92-95 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*tataḥ sa labdhvā tu varaṃ śarīreṇākṣ̣atena ca\|*  
*pādayoḥ praṇatastasthau kṛtvā śirasi cāñjalim \|\| 180.92 \|\|*

*uvācātha tadā tena varado'smīti coditaḥ\|*  
*bhagavanbhaktimavyagrāṃ tvayyananyāṃ vidhatsva me \|\| 180.93 \|\|*

*annadatvaṃ ca lokānāṃ gāṇapatyaṃ tathā'kṣ̣ayam\|*  
*avimuktaṃ ca te sthānaṃ paśyeyaṃ sarvadā yathā\|\| 180.94 \|\|*  
*etadicchāmi deveśa tvatto varamanuttamam \|\| 180.95 \|\|*

Suta said - After having attained such a boon of imperishable form, he stood up and throwing himself at the feet of the Lord and said- “I have been granted a boon by you. “Be kind on me, О Lord! grant me such a boon so that I may have unflinching devotion for You and everlasting form of Ganapati. I will be the undecaying giver of food to the universe. “Besides these all О Lord, I also want a boon from you that Your this avimukla-tlrlha may always be before my eyes.”

## \|\| 180.96-98 \|\|

*devadeva uvāca*  
*jarāmaraṇasaṃtyaktaḥ sarvarogavivarjitaḥ\|*  
*bhaviṣ̣yasi gaṇādhyakṣ̣o dhanadaḥ sarvapūjitaḥ \|\| 180.96 \|\|*

*ajeyaścāpi sarveṣ̣āṃ yogaiśvaryaṃ samāśritaḥ\|*  
*annadaścāpi lokebhyaḥ kṣ̣etrapālo bhaviṣ̣yasi \|\| 180.97 \|\|*

*mahābalo mahāsattvo brahmaṇyo mama ca priyaḥ\|*  
*tr! yakṣ̣aśca daṇḍapāṇiśca mahāyogī tathaiva ca \|\| 180.98 \|\|*

Lord of gods said- “You will be liberated from birth and death, and all diseases. You will be the Ganadhyaksa, the lord of attendants, the giver of wealth, adorable by all. You will be unconquerable by any person, and will be crowned with the yogic power and prosperity. You will be giver of food to all Lokas and you will be Ksetrapala also. Besides this you will be most valiant, righteous, the knower of Brahman, dear to me, having three eyes, holding a Danda and gifted with supreme yoga.

## \|\| 180.99 \|\|

*udbhramaḥ saṃbhramaścaiva gaṇau te paricārakau\|*  
*tavā’jñayā kariṣ̣yete lokasyodbhramasaṃbhramau \|\| 180.99 \|\|*

“You will have two attendants named Udbhrama and Sambhrama in your service. By your order they wdl get respect for you from all the people; and they can create delusion in their people.”

## \|\| 180.100 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*evaṃ sa bhagavāṃstatra yakṣ̣aṃ kṛtvā gaṇeśvaram\|*  
*jagāma vāsaṃ deveśaḥ saha tena maheśvaraḥ \|\| 180.100 \|\|*

Suta said- Thus, there appointing Yaksa, as Ganesvara, Siva, the god of gods went back in his company.”

## Chapter 181

## \|\| 181.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*imāṃ puṇyodbhavāṃ snigdhāṃ kathāṃ pāpapraṇāśinīm \|*  
*śṛṇvantu ṛṣayaḥ sarve suviśuddhāstapodhanāḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Suta said: — “Hear you, O, pure souled holy Rishis! with attention, this righteous narration which is the dispeller of all ills, and the mother of all good merits.

## \|\| 181.2 \|\|

*gaṇeśvarapatiṃ divyaṃ rudra tulyaparākramam \|*  
*sanatkumāro bhagavānapṛcchannandikeśvaram \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Once upon a time, Bhagavan Sanat-Kumara asked Nandikeshvara: — the Lord of the ganas and as powerful as Rudra.

## \|\| 181.3-4 \|\|

*brūhi guhyaṃ yathātattvaṃ yatra nityaṃ bhavaḥ sthitaḥ \|*  
*mahātmā sarvabhūtānāṃ paramātmā maheśvaraḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*ghorarūpaṃ samāsthāya duṣkaraṃ devadānavaiḥ \|*  
*ābhūtasaṃplavaṃ yāvatsthāṇubhūto maheśvaraḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

3-4. He can assume terrible forms that the Devas and Danavas cannot assume. And in this terrible form He remains firm and stable, like a pillar, till Pralaya. He asked “Now kindly describe to me the sacred places, where Maheshvara always resides — this great mystery of all.”

## \|\| 181.5 \|\|

*nandikeśvara uvāca*  
*purā devena yatproktaṃ purāṇaṃ puṇyamuttamam \|*  
*tatsarvaṃ saṃpravakṣyāmi namaskṛtya maheśvaram \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Nandikeshvara said “I shall relate to you, after saluting, the Lord the most ancient event which Mahadeva Himself narrated first.

## \|\| 181.6 \|\|

*tato devena tuṣṭena umāyāḥ priyakāmyayā \|*  
*kathitaṃ bhuvi vikhyātaṃ yatra nityaṃ svayaṃ sthitaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. The Lord narrated it first to Parvati, for Her satisfaction, and afterwards it spread over the universe.

## \|\| 181.7 \|\|

*rudra syārdhāsanagatā meruśṛṅge yaśasvinī \|*  
*mahādevaṃ tato devī praṇatā paripṛcchati \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Sometime ago the illustrious Consort of Shiva — Parvati — on the summit of the Mount Meru, asked the Lord after making salutations to Him

## \|\| 181.8-12 \|\|

*devyuvāca*  
*bhagavandevadeveśa candrā rdhakṛtaśekhara \|*  
*dharmaṃ prabrūhi martyānāṃ bhuvi caivordhvaretasām \|\| 8 \|\|*

*japtaṃ dattaṃ hutaṃ ceṣṭaṃ tapastaptaṃ kṛtaṃ ca yat \|*  
*dhyānādhyayanasaṃpannaṃ kathaṃ bhavati cākṣayam \|\| 9 \|\|*

*janmāntarasahasreṇa yatpāpaṃ pūrvasaṃcitam \|*  
*kathaṃ tatkṣayamāyāti tanmamā’cakṣva śaṃkara \|\| 10 \|\|*

*yasminvyavasthito bhaktyā tuṣyasi tvaṃ maheśvara \|*  
*vratāni niyamāścaiva ācāro dharma eva ca \|\| 11 \|\|*

*sarvasiddhikaraṃ yatra hyakṣayyagatidāyakam \|*  
*vaktumarhasi tatsarvaṃ paraṃ kautūhalaṃ hi me \|\| 12 \|\|*

8-12. “O Bhagavan! O Lord of the Devas! O one with crescent of the Moon in His forehead! Pray explain to me the duties of those men, living in the world, as well as of those, who have subdued their passions. How do the charities, sacrifices, well-practised asceticism, meditations and recitations give everlasting fruits? And how are the sins of ages thereby destroyed? What are the ways, ordinances and duties and sadacharas, by the observance of which, you remaining there, become pleased with your Bhaktas and grant imperishable position to them? Pray explain all these to me, for I am very curious to know all these.”

## \|\| 181.13-18 \|\|

*maheśvara uvāca*  
*śṛṇu devi pravakṣyāmi guhyānāṃ guhyamuttamam \|*  
*sarvakṣetreṣu vikhyātamavimuktaṃ priyaṃ mama \|\| 13 \|\|*

*aṣṭaṣaṣṭiḥ purā proktā sthānānāṃ sthānamuttamam \|*  
*yatra sākṣātsvayaṃ rudra ḥ! kṛttivāsāḥ svayaṃ sthitaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*yatra saṃnihito nityamavimukte nirantaram \|*  
*tatkṣetraṃ na mayā muktamavimuktaṃ tataḥ smṛtam \|\| 15 \|\|*

*avimukte parā siddhiravimukte parā gatiḥ \|*  
*japtaṃ dattaṃ hutaṃ ceṣṭaṃ tapastaptaṃ kṛtaṃ ca yat \|\| 16 \|\|*

*dhyānamadhyayanaṃ dānaṃ sarvaṃ bhavati cākṣayam \|*  
*janmāntarasahasreṇa yatpāpaṃ pūrvasaṃcitam \|\| 17 \|\|*

*avimuktaṃ praviṣṭasya tatsarvaṃ vrajati kṣayam \|*  
*avimuktāgninā dagdhamagnau tūlamivā’hitam \|\| 18 \|\|*

13-18. Mahadeva said: — “O Devi! Hear with attention. I shall relate to you the glory of the Avimuktatirtha, which is the best among all the sacred places, and so dear and near to me. I am telling you a great secret.

Sixty-eight sacred places have been already described, and the one where Rudra is Omnipresent and never absent from there is called the avimuktatirtha and is the first best of all the rest. I never forsake Avimuktakshetra (Kashi); hence it is called Avimukta Kshetra. Emancipation is readily obtainable here, and the charities, meditations, sacrifices, recitations and other similar deeds performed there beget everlasting benefits, and the sins of thousands of ages are destroyed the moment one enters the sacred place. The sins are consumed like cotton in the fire.

## \|\| 181.19-21 \|\|

*brāhmaṇāḥ kṣattriyā vaiśyāḥ śūdrā vai varṇasaṃkarāḥ \|*  
*kṛmimlecchāśca ye cānye saṃkīrṇāḥ pāpayonayaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

*kīṭāḥ pipīlikāścaiva ye cānye mṛgapakṣiṇaḥ \|*  
*kālena nidhanaṃ prāptā avimukte śṛṇu priye \|\| 20 \|\|*

*candrā rdhamaulinaḥ sarve lalāṭākṣā vṛṣadhvajāḥ \|*  
*śive mama pure devi modante tatra mānavāḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

19-21. O Devi! the Brahmanas, Kshatriyas, Vaishyas, Shudras, bastards, sinners, animals, insects, flies, deer, birds, Mlechhas, dying in course of time in Avimuktatirtha, go to My realm (of Shiva) and become Rudras, who wear a crescent on their forehead, and get eyes on their foreheads, and become like Me.

## \|\| 181.22 \|\|

*akāmo vā sakāmo vā hyapi tiryaggato'pi vā \|*  
*avimukte tyajanprāṇānmama loke mahīyate \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Whether they aspire or not, but in every case they attain My realm, by dying in Avimukta, no matter whether they be men or lower animals.

## \|\| 181.23-24 \|\|

*avimuktaṃ yadā gacchetkadācitkālaparyayāt \|*  
*aśmanā caraṇau bhittvā tatraiva nidhanaṃ vrajet \|\| 23 \|\|*

*avimuktaṃ gato devi na nirgacchettataḥ punaḥ \|*  
*so'pi matpadamāpnoti nātra kāryā vicāraṇā \|\| 24 \|\|*

23-24. Far better it is for one when he goes to Kashi, to fix himself down to the earth, by tying a piece of stone on his legs, and never leave this place, and thereby enable him to go to My realm.

## \|\| 181.25-26 \|\|

*vastrapadaṃ rudra koṭiṃ siddheśvaramahālayam \|*  
*gokarṇaṃ rudra karṇaṃ ca suvarṇākṣaṃ tathaiva ca \|\| 25 \|\|*

*amaraṃ ca mahākālaṃ tathā kāyāvarohaṇam \|*  
*etāni hi pavitrāṇi sāṃnidhyātsaṃdhyayordvayoḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

25-26. He who never goes out of the precincts of Kashi, attains My realm there is no doubt in this. Vasraprada, Rudrakoti, Sidheshvara, Gokarna, Rudrakarna, Suvarnaksha, Amara, Mahakala and Kayavarohana, are all sanctified places, and I am present at all those places, in both the morning and evening Sandhyas.

## \|\| 181.27-28 \|\|

Besides these Harishchandra Tirtha, Amratakeshvara, Jaleshvara, Shtriparvata are also most sacred. They all are mysterious and secret.

29-30. Mahalaya, Krimichandeshvara, Kedaranath, Mahabhairava, are also highly sacred. As I am present at the aforementioned eight places always. Thus I am present at Avimukta at all times.

31-32. Dear 1 the other sacred places, that exist in the three Lokas, always remain at the feet of Avimukta. Your son, Svami Kartika will relate the glory of Avimukta and the glories of the Rishis, who will come in future”.

## Chapter 182

1-2. Suta said: — Once on a time, the Rishis Sanaka, Sanandana, ac, and the devotees of Shiva asked Svami Kartika, the chief of the knowers of Brahma, on the summit of Kailasha: “Brahmana! Pray explain to us about the abode of Shiva in the earth where Bhagavan Shiva always dwells.

## \|\| 182.3-4 \|\|

*skanda uvāca*  
*mahātmā sarvabhūtātmā devadevaḥ sanātanaḥ \|*

3-4. Svami Kartika said “The soul of all, the Eternal Lord Mahadeva, the High Soul, remains in his terrible form, rare to the Devas and Danavas, at Avimukta like a pillar, motionless and stable, till pralaya. This is the most mysterious place.

## \|\| 182.5-10 \|\|

*avimukte sadā siddhiryatra nityaṃ bhavaḥ sthitaḥ \|*

*sthānaṃ paraṃ pavitraṃ ca tīrthamāyatanaṃ tathā \|*

*bhūrloke naiva saṃyuktamantarikṣe śivālayam \|*  
*ayuktāstu na paśyanti yuktāḥ paśyanti cetasā \|\| 7 \|\|*

*brahmacaryavratopetāḥ siddhā vedāntakovidāḥ \|*  
*ā dehapatanādyāvattatkṣetraṃ yo na muñcati \|\| 8 \|\|*

*brahmacaryavrataiḥ samyaksamyagiṣṭaṃ makhairbhavet \|*  
*apāpātmā gatiḥ sarvā yā tūktā ca kriyāvatām \|\| 9 \|\|*

*yastatra nivasedvipro'saṃyuktātmā'samāhitaḥ \|*  
*trikālamapi bhuñjāno vāyubhakṣasamo bhavet \|\| 10 \|\|*

5-10. The Siddhas always remain there owing to the presence of the Lord. Shiva has described Avimukta to excel all the sacred places, nor is there any other place more sacred than it. Every part of it is holy and endowed with a holy tirtha. There exists a divine abode, over the cremation ground there, and it is not visible to all. Yet it is connected with the earth. There the abode of Shiva (Shivalaya) is situated in the space. Unworthy people, who are not yogis, cannot behold the Lord’s abode; but the Yogis, the Brahmacharis, and the knowers of the Vedas, can see it. Those who are Brahmacharis, the Siddhas, the Vedantis, and do not leave this place till death, they attaining all the benefits of sacrifices and washed off from all their sins, attain the highest position. The Brahmanas living thereon throe meals a day, and without any Yoga or their mind under control, attain virtues, like the one living merely on air, and get the highest position that an ascetic would get.

## \|\| 182.11-18 \|\|

*nimeṣamātramapi yo hyavimukte tu bhaktimān \|*  
*brahmacaryasamāyuktaḥ paramaṃ prāpnuyāttapaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*yo'tra māsaṃ vaseddhīro laghvāhāro jitendri yaḥ \|*  
*samyaktena vrataṃ cīrṇaṃ divyaṃ pāśupataṃ mahat \|\| 12 \|\|*

*janmamṛtyubhayaṃ tīrtvā sa yāti paramāṃ gatim \|*  
*naiḥśreyasīṃ gatiṃ puṇyāṃ tathā yogagatiṃ vrajet \|\| 13 \|\|*

*na hi yogagatirdivyā janmāntaraśatairapi \|*  
*prāpyate kṣetramāhātmyātprabhāvācchaṃkarasya tu \|\| 14 \|\|*

*brahmahā yo'bhigacchettu avimuktaṃ kadācana \|*  
*tasya kṣetrasya māhātmyādbrahmahatyā nivartate \|\| 15 \|\|*

*ā dehapatanādyāvatkṣetraṃ yo na vimuñcati \|*  
*na kevalaṃ brahmahatyā prākṛtaṃ ca nivartate \|\| 16 \|\|*

*prāpya viśveśvaraṃ devaṃ na sa bhūyo'bhijāyate \|*  
*ananyamānaso bhūtvā yo'vimuktaṃ na muñcati \|\| 17 \|\|*

*tasya devaḥ sadā tuṣṭaḥ sarvānkāmānprayacchati \|*  
*dvāraṃ yatsāṃkhyayogānāṃ sa tatra vasati prabhuḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

11-18. The one who leads a calm life, after subduing all his passions, in this place even for a moment, begets the fruits of highest asceticism, and the one who remains there like that for a month, begets the benefits of having observed the Pashupata ordinance. In other words, he attains bliss after being liberated from the cycle of births and deaths. He attains the position of yoga and the, final beatitude. The fruits derived here by the glory of Shiva and of this Avimukta kshettram, are not obtained even by the practice of yoga for ages the one who goes there is purified of the sin of even killing a Brahmana. One who continually resides there, for all his life, unmoved in mind, is not only purified of his sin committed in this life, but also of his Brahmahatya sin in his previous birth, and attains Shiva and does not get any other births. He gets the favour of Shiva and all his desires are fulfilled, and he gets the same end as the knower of Samkhya does. He remains there all his lives and never quits it.

## \|\| 182.19-24 \|\|

*sagaṇo hi bhavo devo bhaktānāmanukampayā \|*

*samudrā ṇāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ nāvimuktasya śakyate \|*

*vāyunā preryamāṇānāṃ smṛtirnaivopajāyate \|*

*karmabhiḥ preryamāṇānāṃ karṇajāpaṃ prayacchati \|*  
*maṇikarṇyāṃ tyajandehaṃ gatimiṣṭāṃ vrajennaraḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

19-24. Mahadeva resides in Avimukta with all His attendants, consequently one begets highest attainments and renunciation there. Emancipation is attained by living there permanently, and he is never re-born. Avimukta is the highest kshettram; it is the highest goal. One may be able to describe the seven islands round the Mount Meru and all the oceans, but I v cannot adequately relate the glory of Avimukta. People at the point of death suffer agonies, and do not remain conscious and lose their memories, but the j devotees of Shiva, giving up life at Avimukta, are blessed by being whispered I into their ear the most sacred formula “Taraka Brahma” by the Lord Shiva Himself. If one dies at Manikarnika ghat he attains his desired goal

## \|\| 182.25-27 \|\|

*īśvaraprerito yāti duṣprāpāmakṛtātmabhiḥ \|*

*avimuktaṃ niṣeveta saṃsāramayamocanam \|*

25-27. He is always blessed by the favour of Shiva, and attains that goal, which unmeritorious persons do not get. People should realise the unrealities of life, and that it is full of all sins, and in order to free themselves from the troubles of the world they ought to devote themselves to Avimukta-tirtha, which is the giver of yoga, peace, and the dispeller of fears of this world and of all other obstacles. One who remains at Avimukta, even bearing all troubles and difficulties, attains emancipation, in course of his life, being liberated from the cycle of birth and death. He attains union with Shiva,

Those who are practising austerities elsewhere, do not get so highest perfection, but who are living here in Avimukta, attain the heaven forever.

О beautiful lady! now I shall explain you the most secrets of the Avimukta-tlrtha accurately as told before by me. If any person by practising the Yoga during hundreds of lives, attains final emancipation is doubtful, but my devotee at Avimukta-tlrtha, attains final emancipation without any doubt, in course of one life.

## \|\| 183.40-41 \|\|

*caturmūrtiḥ sadā dharmastasminsaṃnihitaḥ priye \|*  
*caturṇāmapi varṇānāṃ gatistu paramā smṛtā \|\| 183.41 \|\|*

О Devi! people coming here with unshaken devotion attain highest place, final beatitude which is very rare. Like that there is no place on the earth, nor will be there. Dharma resides here in the form of four faces. People of all the four castes attain emancipation here.

## \|\| 183.42-44 \|\|

*devyuvāca*  
*śrutā guṇāste kṣ̣etrasya iha cānyatra ye prabho \|*  
*vadasva bhuvi viprendrā ḥ! kaṃ vā yajñairyajanti te \|\| 183.42 \|\|*

Parvatl said- “О Lord! I have heard here the glory of this sacred city of yours, now please tell me whom do the Brahmanas adore through sacrifices on the earth?”

## \|\| 183.43-44 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca*  
*ijyayā caiva mantreṇa māmeva hi yajanti ye \|*  
*na teṣ̣āṃ bhayamastīti bhavaṃ rudraṃ yajanti yat \|\| 183.43 \|\|*

*amantro mantrako devi dvividho vidhirucyate \|*  
*sāṃkhyaṃ caivātha yogaśca dvividho yoga ucyate \|\| 183.44 \|\|*

Lord Siva said- “They all worship Me, by performing sacrifices and also reciting the sacred mantras. Those who worship Rudra and Mahadeva have no fear in this world. О Divine lady! There is the method of worship of two types, viz., with mantra and without mantra. Thus there are two kinds of Yogas, viz.-Samkhya and Yoga.

## \|\| 183.45-46 \|\|

*sarvabhūtasthitaṃ yo māṃ bhajatyekatvamāsthitaḥ \|*  
*sarvathā vartamāno'pi sa yogī mayi vartate \|\| 183.45 \|\|*

*ātmaupamyena sarvatra sarvaṃ ca mayi paśyati \|*  
*tasyāhaṃ na praṇaśyāmi sa ca me na praṇaśyati \|\| 183.46 \|\|*

The Yogi, who pay reverence to Me, omnipresent, the soul of all the beings never separate Me from himself even his engagement in like a layman. He see all beings into Me. I never perish him and he never perish me.

## \|\| 183.47-48 \|\|

*nirguṇaḥ saguṇo vā'pi yogaśca kathito bhuvi \|*  
*saguṇaścaiva vijñeyo nirguṇo manasaḥ paraḥ \|\| 183.47 \|\|*

*etatte kathitaṃ devi yanmāṃ tvaṃ paripṛcchasi \|\| 183.48 \|\|*

Yoga had been said as Nirguna and Saguna of two types. Saguna yoga is comprehensible but Nirguna yoga is beyond the mind. О Devi! I have related all these, what you ask Me.

## \|\| 183.49 \|\|

*devyuvāca*  
*yā bhaktistrividhā proktā bhaktānāṃ bahudhā tvayā \|*  
*tāmahaṃ śrotumicchāmi tattvataḥ kathayasva me \|\| 183.49 \|\|*

Parvati said- “O Siva! You have narrated three types of devotion mentioned by you several time, I wish to hear this with true facts. Kindly tell me.”

## \|\| 183.50-51 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca*  
*śṛṇu pārvati deveśi bhaktānāṃ bhaktivatsale \|*  
*prāpya sāṃkhyaṃ ca yogaṃ ca duḥkhāntaṃ ca niyacchati \|\| 183.50 \|\|*

*sadā yaḥ sevate bhikṣ̣āṃ tato bhavati rañjitaḥ \|*  
*rañjanāttanmayo bhūtvā līyate sa tu bhaktimān \|\| 183.51 \|\|*

Lord Siva spoke- “O Goddess Parvatl, hear this. You are attached to your devotees! A man reaches the end of all passions through the knowledge of Samkhya and Yoga; and that devotee who always lives on alms, clings to Me, merges into Me.

## \|\| 183.52-54 \|\|

*śāstrāṇā tu varārohe bahukāraṇadarśinaḥ \|*  
*na māṃ paśyanti te devi jñānavākyavivādinaḥ \|\| 183.52 \|\|*

*paramārthajñānatṛptā yuktā jānanti yoginaḥ \|*  
*vidyayā viditātmāno yogasya ca dvijātayaḥ \|\| 183.53 \|\|*

*pratyāhāreṇa śuddhātmā nānyathā cintayecca tat \|*  
*tuṣ̣ṭiṃ ca paramāṃ prāpya yogaṃ mokṣ̣aṃ paraṃ tathā \|*  
*tribhirguṇaiḥ samāyukto jñānavānpaśyatīha mām \|\| 183.54 \|\|*

О handsome lady! О Devi! The people are not able to see me, who are deluded by seeing many causes in the Sastras and argue by their knowledge and speech. But the Yogins, who are contented by being possessed with the supreme knowledge, and incessantly think of me by being blessed with clear conscience, through Divine knowledge, get felicity and bliss. Here, a learned person sees me endowed with the three Gunas.

## \|\| 183.55 \|\|

*etatte kathitaṃ devi kimanyacchrotumarhasi \|*  
*bhūya eva varārohe kathayiṣ̣yāmi suvrate \|\| 183.55 \|\|*

О Devi! О beautiful one! О Suvrata! I have explained all the things before you, now let me know what you wish to hear anything more, I will relate to you.

## \|\| 183.56 \|\|

*guhyaṃ pavitramathavā yaccāpi hṛdi vartate \|*  
*tatsarvaṃ kathayiṣ̣yāmi śṛṇuṣ̣vaikamanāḥ priye \|\| 183.56 \|\|*

О beloved one! whatever is in my heart, I shall relate to you all the most secret and mysterious things for your satisfaction, hear attentively.

## \|\| 183.57 \|\|

*devyuvāca*  
*tvadrū paṃ kīdṛśaṃ deva yuktāḥ paśyanti yoginaḥ \|*  
*etaṃ me saṃśayaṃ brūhi namaste surasattama \|\| 183.57 \|\|*

Parvatl said- “O Mahadeva! which form of yours do the Yogis see? I beg you to remove My doubt. Salutation to you, О best of gods.”

## \|\| 183.58-59 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca*  
*amūrtaṃ caiva mūrtaṃ ca jyotīrūpaṃ hi tatsmṛtam \|*  
*tasyopalabdhimanvicchanyatnaḥ kāryo vijānatā \|\| 183.58 \|\|*

*guṇairviyukto bhūtātmā evaṃ vaktuṃ na śakyate \|*  
*śakyate yadi vaktuṃ vai divyairvarṣ̣aśatairna vā \|\| 183.59 \|\|*

Lord Siva said- My nature is formless, as well as formful, both the shapes of Mine consist of light. A learned person ought to make great efforts to attain it. The Lord of the creatures in his formless condition cannot be explained. It can only be explained, if at all, by the persistent efforts of hundreds of divine years. But it is also doubtful.

## \|\| 183.60 \|\|

*devyuvāca*  
*kiṃ pramāṇaṃ tu tatkṣ̣etraṃ samantātsarvatodiśam \|*  
*yatra nityaṃ sthito devo mahādevo gaṇairyutaḥ \|\| 183.60 \|\|*

Parvatl said- “O Mahadeva! What is the extent of that shrine where you reside always endowed with your attendants?”

## \|\| 183.61-63 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca*  
*dviyojanaṃ tu tatkṣ̣etraṃ pūrvapaścimataḥ smṛtam \|*  
*ardhayojanavistīrṇaṃ tatkṣ̣etraṃ dakṣ̣iṇottaram \|\| 183.61 \|\|*

*varaṇā'sī nadī yāvattāvacchuklanadī tu vai \|*  
*bhīṣ̣macaṇḍikamārabhya parvateśvaramantike \|\| 183.62 \|\|*

*gaṇā yatrāvatiṣ̣ṭhante saṃniyuktā vināyakāḥ \|*  
*kūṣ̣māṇḍagajatuṇḍaśca jayantaśca madotkaṭāḥ \|\| 183.63 \|\|*

Lord Siva said- “This land is extended in tv/o yojanas from east to west. Within that space Avimukta-tlrtha is situated having a width of half yojana extending from north and south; and holy Varuna and Asi rivers flow by it and their abode extends between Bhismacandika to Parvatesvara. The attendants of Siva, like Kusmanda, Gajatunda valorous Jayanta are appointed there.

## \|\| 183.64-66 \|\|

*siṃhavyāghramukhāḥ kecidvikaṭāḥ kubjavāmanāḥ \|*  
*yatra nandī mahākālaścaṇḍaghaṇṭo maheśvaraḥ \|\| 183.64 \|\|*

*daṇḍacaṇḍeśvaraścaiva ghaṇṭākarṇo mahābalaḥ \|*  
*ete cānye ca bahavo gaṇāścaiva gaṇeśvarāḥ \|\| 183.65 \|\|*

*mahodarā mahākāyā vajraśaktidharāstathā \|*  
*rakṣ̣anti satataṃ devi hyavimuktaṃ tapovanam \|*  
*dvāre dvāre ca tiṣ̣ṭhanti śūlamudgarapāṇayaḥ \|\| 183.66 \|\|*

О Devi! Some of them are having the face of lions and tigers, some are hunch-backed, some are dwarfs and crooked. On the same spot Mahakala, Candaghanta, Dandacandes'vara, mighty Ghanta-karna, and others, having huge stomachs, of great stature, holding Vajra and Sakti weapons, protect the holy Avimukta-ksetra continuously. Many of the attendants are standing at every gate armed with tridents and clubs.

## \|\| 183.67-68 \|\|

*suvarṇaśṛṅgīṃ raupyakhurāṃ cailājinapayasvinīm \|*  
*vārāṇasyāṃ tu yo dadyātsavatsāṃ kāṃsyabhājanām \|\| 183.67 \|\|*

*gāṃ dattvā tu varārohe brāhmaṇe vedapārage \|*  
*āsaptamaṃ kulaṃ tena tāritaṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 183.68 \|\|*

О Parvatl! one' who donates a cow, full of milk, with its horns mounted with gold, its hoofs covered with silver, with calf and vessel of bronze to a Brahmana well-versed in Vedas, on the banks of Varanasi, undoubtedly liberates seven generations of his ancestors from bondage.

## \|\| 183.69 \|\|

*yo dadyādbrāhmaṇe kiṃcittasminkṣ̣etre varānane \|*  
*kanakaṃ rajataṃ vastramannādyaṃ bahuvistaram \|*  
*akṣ̣ayaṃ cāvyayaṃ caiva syātāṃ tasya sulocane \|\| 183.69 \|\|*

О beloved one! one who also gives away in charity to a Brahmana, gold, silver, cloths, and grain, etc., in that place of Avimukta-tlrtha, acquires everlasting merits, О beautiful eyed!

## \|\| 183.70-71 \|\|

*śṛṇu tattvena tīrthasya vibhūtiṃ vyuṣ̣ṭimeva ca \|*  
*tatra snātvā mahābhāge bhavanti nīrujā narāḥ \|\| 183.70 \|\|*

*daśānāmaśvamedhānāṃ phalaṃ prāpnoti mānavaḥ \|*  
*tadavāpnoti dharmātmā tatra snātvā varānane \|\| 183.71 \|\|*

Hear with attention, the glory of this sacred place. People, who take bath here, become free from diseases and О beloved one! any virtuous man gets benefit of ten as'vamedha sacrifices by bathing there.

## \|\| 183.72 \|\|

*bahusvalpe ca yo dadyādbrāhmaṇe vedapārage \|*  
*śubhāṃ gatimavāpnoti agnivaccaiva dīpyate \|\| 183.72 \|\|*

Any person gives some sort of charity in larger or lesser quantity to a Brahmanas well-versed in Vedas, after his ablution attains felicity and shines like fire.

## \|\| 183.73-74 \|\|

*vārāṇasījāhnavībhyāṃ saṃgame lokaviśrute \|*  
*dattvā'nnaṃ ca vidhānena na sa bhūyo'bhijāyate \|\| 183.73 \|\|*

*etatte kathitaṃ devi tīrthasya phalamuttamam \|\| 183.74 \|\|*

One who gives away grain in charity at the confluence of the Varuna and Asi with the Ganga, according to the prescribed rites, is not re-bom. Thus I have narrated to you the great fmit of this sacred place.

## \|\| 183.75-76 \|\|

*punaranyatpravakṣ̣yāmi tīrthasya phalamuttamam \|*  
*upavāsaṃ tu yaḥ kṛtvā viprānsaṃtarpayennaraḥ \|*  
*sautrāmaṇeśca yajñasya phalaṃ prāpnoti mānavaḥ \|\| 183.75 \|\|*

*ekāhārastu yastiṣ̣ṭhenmāsaṃ tatra varānane \|*  
*yāvajжīvakṛtaṃ pāpaṃ sahasā tasya naśyati \|\| 183.76 \|\|*

Having done fast, a man feeds the Brahmanas in this tlrtha attains the benefit of Sautramani sacrifice. Dear Parvatl, one who lives on only one meal a day for a month washes off all sins of his whole life.

## \|\| 183.77-78 \|\|

*agnipraveśaṃ ye kuryuravimukte vidhānataḥ \|*  
*praviśanti mukhaṃ te me niḥsaṃdigdhaṃ varānane \|\| 183.77 \|\|*

*daśasauvarṇikaṃ puṣ̣paṃ yo'vimukte prayacchati \|*  
*agnihotraphalaṃ dhūpe gandhadāne tathā śṛṇu \|*  
*bhūmidānena tattulyaṃ gandhadānaphalaṃ smṛtam \|\| 183.78 \|\|*

The people enter the fire according to the prescribed rites undoubtedly they enter My mouth. One who gives away ten gold coins in charity gets the benefits of Agnihotra sacrifice, and one who gives away incense, etc., derives the benefit of having given away land in charity.

## \|\| 183.79 \|\|

*saṃmārjane pañcaśataṃ sahasramanulepane \|*  
*mālayā śatasāhasramanantaṃ gītavādyataḥ \|\| 183.79 \|\|*

One who gives away a broom gets the benefit of having given away five hundred gold coins. The giver of sandal gets the benefit of having given away 1,000 gold coins. The charity of flowers and garlands is equivalent to the giving away of 1,00,000 gold coins. The one who sings hymns accompanied by music begets everlasting benefits.”

## \|\| 183.80 \|\|

*devyuvāca*  
*atyadbhutamidaṃ deva sthānametatprakīrtitam \|*  
*rahasyaṃ śrotumicchāmi yadarthaṃ tvaṃ na muñcasi \|\| 183.80 \|\|*

Goddess Parvat! said- О Deva! you have narrated wonderful mysteries of this place. Now I wish to hear the reason, for which you do not leave this unique place.

## \|\| 183.81-83 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca*  
*āsītpūrvaṃ varārohe brahmaṇastu śiro varam \|*  
*pañcamaṃ śṛṇu suśroṇi jātaṃ kāñcanasaprabham \|\| 183.81 \|\|*

*jvalattatpañcamaṃ śīrṣ̣aṃ jātaṃ tasya mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*tadevamabravīddevi janma jānāmi te hyaham \|\| 183.82 \|\|*

*tataḥ krodhaparītena saṃraktanayanena ca \|*  
*vāmāṅguṣ̣ṭhanakhāgreṇa cchinnaṃ tasya śiro mayā \|\| 183.83 \|\|*

Lord said- “O beloved Parvatl! In ancient time the high-souled Lord Brahma had a fifth head, which was excellent and shining like gold. He Once told me that T know your birth’, then I angrily with red-eyed cut off this fifth head with the nail of my left toe.

## \|\| 183.84 \|\|

*brahmovāca*  
*yadā niraparādhasya śiraśchinnaṃ tvayā mama \|*  
*tasmācchāpasamāyuktaḥ kapālī tvaṃ bhaviṣ̣yasi \|*  
*brahmahatyākulo bhūtvā cara tīrthāni bhūtale \|\| 183.84 \|\|*

That time Brahma said- T am innocent and you have beheaded me, therefore by my curse you shall bear a skull as the badge of the sin of inflicting injury on Brahma. You shall roam about in the sacred places on earth.

## \|\| 183.85-86 \|\|

*tato'haṃ gatavāndevi himavantaṃ śiloccayam \|*  
*tatra nārāyaṇaḥ śrīmānmayā bhikṣ̣āṃ prayācitaḥ \|\| 183.85 \|\|*

*tatastena svakaṃ pārśvaṃ nakhāgreṇa vidāritam \|*  
*sravato mahatī dhārā tasya raktasya niḥsṛtā \|\| 183.86 \|\|*

О Devi! then I had been to the Himalaya mountain. There I begged Narayana to give me alms. He on his side dug His fingernail and a volume of blood rushed out.

## \|\| 183.87-89 \|\|

*prayātā sā'tivistīrṇā yojanārdhaśataṃ tadā \|*  
*na saṃpūrṇaṃ kapālaṃ tu ghoramadbhutadarśanam \|\| 183.87 \|\|*

*divyaṃ varṣ̣asahasraṃ tu sā ca dhārā pravāhitā \|*  
*provāca bhagavānviṣ̣ṇuḥ kapālaṃ kuta īdṛśam \|\| 183.88 \|\|*

*āścaryabhūtaṃ deveśa saṃśayo hṛdi vartate \|*  
*kutaśca saṃbhavo deva sarvaṃ me brūhi pṛcchataḥ \|\| 183.89 \|\|*

That volume of blood spreaded to the length of 50 yojanas, but the skull was not filled. After that, this stream of blood ran for a thousand Divine years. Then Lord Visnu asked me ‘How such a mysterious skull was brought into existence. Tell me all the things to remove my doubts.

## \|\| 183.90-93 \|\|

*devadeva uvāca*  
*śrūyatāmasya he deva kapālasya tu saṃbhavaḥ \|*  
*śataṃ varṣ̣asahasrāṇāṃ tapastaptvā sudāruṇam \|\| 183.90 \|\|*

*brahmā'sṛjadvapurdivyamadbhutaṃ lomaharṣ̣aṇam \|*  
*tapasaśca prabhāveṇa divyaṃ kāñcanasaṃnibham \|\| 183.91 \|\|*

*jvalattatpañcamaṃ śīrṣ̣aṃ jātaṃ tasya mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*nikṛttaṃ tanmayā deva tadidaṃ paśya durjayam \|\| 183.92 \|\|*

*yatra yatra ca gacchāmi kapālaṃ tatra gacchati \|*  
*evamuktastato devaḥ provāca puruṣ̣ottamaḥ \|\| 183.93 \|\|*

The god of gods said, ‘O Deva! Listen to the birth of this skull. In ancient times Brahma was endowed with Divine form after thousands of years asceticism and through. His asceticism He got a fifth head shining like gold. I cut it off in anger. It follows Me wherever I go.’ Having said thus lord Vishnu told me.

## \|\| 183.94-96 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca*  
*gaccha gaccha svakaṃ sthānaṃ brahmaṇastvaṃ priyaṃ kuru \|*  
*tasminsthāsyati bhadraṃ te kapālaṃ tasya tejasā \|\| 183.94 \|\|*

*tataḥ sarvāṇi tīrthāni puṇyānyāyatanāni ca \|*  
*gato'smi pṛthulaśroṇi na kvacitpratyatiṣ̣ṭhata \|\| 183.95 \|\|*

*tato'haṃ samanuprāpto hyavimukte mahāśaye \|*  
*avasthitaḥ svake sthāne śāpaśca vigato mama \|\| 183.96 \|\|*

Lord Visnu said ‘Go back and please Brahma. By His glorious power this skull will become fixed in your holy abode (ksetra). О Parvatl, after hearing that I went to all the sacred places, but nowhere did this skull leave Me. But when I came and settled Myself at My Avimukta-tlrtha the effects of the curse instantly disappeared.

## \|\| 183.97 \|\|

*viṣ̣ṇuprasādātsuśroṇi kapālaṃ tatsahasradhā \|*  
*sphuṭitaṃ bahudhā jātaṃ svapnalabdhaṃ dhanaṃ yathā \|\| 183.97 \|\|*

О excellent women! By the grace of lord Visnu the skull also fell down there and divided into thousand parts. It disappeared like the riches a man obtains in his dream.

## \|\| 183.98 \|\|

*brahmahatyāpahaṃ tīrthaṃ kṣ̣etrametanmayā kṛtam \|*  
*kapālamocanaṃ devi devānāṃ prathitaṃ bhuvi \|\| 183.98 \|\|*

О dear Parvatl, I have made this place as dispeller of the sin of killing a Brahmana (Brahma-hatya) and it is the cremation ground of all the Devas including myself.

## \|\| 183.99 \|\|

*kālo bhūtvā jagatsarvaṃ saṃharāmi sṛjāmi ca \|*  
*tatastatpatitaṃ tatra śāpaśca vigato mama \|\| 183.99 \|\|*

Becoming Kala (Destructor) I annihilate the universe and also create everything. О Devi! this sequestered place of mine is most dearest to me.

## \|\| 183.100 \|\|

*madbhaktāstatra gacchanti viṣ̣ṇubhaktāstathaiva ca \|*  
*ye bhaktā bhāskare devi lokanāthe divākare \|*  
*tatrastho yastyajeddehaṃ māmeva praviśettu saḥ \|\| 183.100 \|\|*

О Devi! my devotees as well as the devotees of Visnu and the devotees of the lord of lokas, Sun, who come and die there merge into Me.”

## \|\| 183.101 \|\|

*devyuvāca*  
*atyadbhutamidaṃ deva yaduktaṃ padmayoninā \|*  
*tripurāntakara sthānaṃ guhyametanmahādyute \|\| 183.101 \|\|*

Parvatl said- “O Deva, О having great lustre! this place is indeed most wonderful as described by lotus-bom you. This place of Siva, slayer of Tripura demon is very glorious.

## \|\| 183.102-104 \|\|

*yānyanyāni sutīrthāni kalāṃ nārhanti ṣ̣oḍaśīm \|*  
*yatra tiṣ̣ṭhati deveśo yatra tiṣ̣ṭhati śaṃkaraḥ \|\| 183.102 \|\|*

*gaṅgā tīrthasahasrāṇāṃ tulyā bhavati vā na vā \|*  
*tvameva bhaktirdeveśa tvameva gatiruttamā \|\| 183.103 \|\|*

*brahmādīnāṃ tu te deva gatiruktā sanātanī \|*  
*śrāvyametaddvijātīnāṃ bhaktānāmanukampayā \|\| 183.104 \|\|*

Because of your presence at this place, other sacred places cannot equal to it’s sixteenth part even. Where lord Visnu dwells, Mahadeva too dwells there. Ganga, worth a thousand of tlrthas also resides there. Therefore, О Lord! You are my devotion and salvation and you are also said to be the emancipation of Brahma and other gods and this is listened to by devotees because of your grace.

## Chapter 184

## \|\| 184.1-7 \|\|

*maheśvara uvāca*  
*sevitaṃ bahubhiḥ siddhairapunarbhavakāṅkṣibhiḥ \|*  
*viditvā tu paraṃ kṣetramavimuktanivāsinām \|\| 1 \|\|*

*tadguhyaṃ devadevasya tattīrthaṃ tattapovanam \|*  
*paraṃ sthānaṃ tu te yānti saṃbhavanti na te punaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*jñāne vihitaniṣṭhānāṃ paramānandamicchatām \|*  
*yā gatirvihitā sadbhiḥ sā'vimukte mṛtasya tu \|\| 3 \|\|*

*bhavasya prītiratulā hyavimukte hyanuttamā \|*  
*asaṃkhyeyaṃ phalaṃ tatra hyakṣayā ca gatirbhavet \|\| 4 \|\|*

*paraṃ guhyaṃ samākhyātaṃ śmaśānamiti saṃjñitam \|*  
*avimuktaṃ na sevante vañcitāste narā bhuvi \|\| 5 \|\|*

*avimukte sthitaiḥ puṇyaiḥ pāṃśubhirvāyuneritaiḥ \|*  
*api duṣkṛtakarmāṇo yāsyanti paramāṃ gatim \|\| 6 \|\|*

*avimuktaguṇānvaktuṃ devadānavamānavaiḥ \|*  
*na śakyate'prameyatvātsvayaṃ yatra bhavaḥ sthitaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

1-7. Mahadeva said: — Those who reside here, with the desire of winning emancipation, to them, this sacred place is like a wood of penance (tapovana). People residing here are never re-born. The dwellers of this place get the same end as those who are eager to acquire beatitude by means of Divine Knowledge. This place is extremely dear to Me. It gives everlasting fruits and immortality. This Avimukta-tirtha is also called the cremation ground, and is most mysterious. Those who do not feel attached to it are really the losers. The dust of this place falling on the sinners bestows on them beatitude. The piles of sins, huge as the mount Sumeru and Mandarachala, become annihilated there.

## \|\| 184.8-13 \|\|

*anāhitāgnirno yaṣṭā no'śucistaskaro'pi vā \|*  
*avimukte vasedyastu sa vasedīśvarālaye \|\| 8 \|\|*

*tatra nāpuṇyakṛtkaścitprasādādīśvarasya ca \|*  
*ajñānājжñānato vā'pi striyā vā puruṣeṇa vā \|\| 9 \|\|*

*yatkiṃcidaśubhaṃ karma kṛtaṃ mānuṣabuddhinā \|*  
*avimukte praviṣṭasya tatsarvaṃ bhasmasādbhavet \|\| 10 \|\|*

*saritaḥ sāgarāḥ śailāstīrthānyāyatanāni ca \|*  
*bhūtapretapiśācāśca gaṇā mātṛgaṇāstathā \|\| 11 \|\|*

*śmaśānikaparīvārāḥ priyāstasya mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*na te muñcanti bhūteśaṃ tānbhavastu na muñcati \|\| 12 \|\|*

*ramate ca gaṇaiḥ sārdhamavimukte sthitaḥ prabhuḥ \|*  
*dṛṣṭvaitānbhītakṛpaṇānpāpaduṣkṛtakāriṇaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

8-13. There is Avimukta temple which is renowned by the name of “The cremation ground.” It is the “cave of retreat and wood of ascetism” and the tap6vana of the Lord Suva. There Narayana, Brahma, etc., the Sadhya Devas, the Yogis etc., carry on Their worship of Sanatana Shiva and My devotees worship Me. Those who die at Avimukta-tirtha get the same "benefit as those who perform sacrifices and devote themselves to asceticism.

Brahma the Creator, the Destructor of the universe, the Virata manifestation of Bhagavan, the seven realms, — they all originate here; and Maharaloka, Janaloka, Tapaloka, Satyaloka, the great Yoga of the mind, all the immoveable and moveable creation upwards to Brahma, the origin of beings, — they all appear here.

## \|\| 184.14-19 \|\|

*anukampayā tu devasya prayānti paramāṃ gatim \|*  
*bhaktānukampī bhagavāṃstiryagyonigatānapi \|\| 14 \|\|*

*nayatyeva varaṃ sthānaṃ yatra yānti ca yājñikāḥ \|*  
*bhārgavāṅgirasaḥ siddhā ṛṣayaśca mahāvratāḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*avimuktāgninā dagdhā agnau tūlamivā'hitam \|*  
*na sā gatiḥ kurukṣetre gaṅgādvāre ca puṣkare \|\| 16 \|\|*

*sā gatirvihitā puṃsāmavimuktanivāsinām \|*  
*tiryagyonigatāḥ sattvā ye'vimukte kṛtālayāḥ \|*  
*kālena nidhanaṃ prāptāste yānti paramāṃ gatim \|\| 17 \|\|*

*merumandaramātro'pi rāśiḥ pāpasya karmaṇaḥ \|*  
*avimuktaṃ samāsādya tatsarvaṃ vrajati kṣayam \|\| 18 \|\|*

*śmaśānamiti vikhyātamavimuktaṃ śivālayam \|*  
*tadguhyaṃ devadevasya tattīrthaṃ tattapovanam \|\| 19 \|\|*

14-19. Those who never forsake this place remain in peace. This is the best and holiest of all the places. It is the best place among the Kshetras, the foremost of the cremation grounds. It is the best of all the streams, mountains and lakes; and, therefore, this Avimukta-tirtha is adored by the pious devotees of Shiva. This Avimukta-tirtha is the great seat of Brahma also. Brahma resides here. It is inhabited and guarded by Brahma. It is as if ail the realms are located here. The golden Mount Meru and the hard asceticism practised by Brahma are inherent here. Brahma remains merged in the image of Shiva. It is the holiest of the holy. It is inhabited by all the hoary people.

## \|\| 184.20-24 \|\|

*tatra brahmādayo devā nārāyaṇapurogamāḥ \|*  
*yoginaśca tathā sādhyā bhagavantaṃ sanātanam \|\| 20 \|\|*

*upāsante śivaṃ muktā madbhaktā matparāyaṇāḥ \|*  
*yā gatirjñānatapasāṃ yā gatiryajñayājinām \|\| 21 \|\|*

*avimukte mṛtānāṃ tu sā gatirvihitā śubhā \|*  
*saṃhartāraśca kartārastasminbrahmādayaḥ surāḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*samrāḍvirāṇmayā lokā jāyante hyapunarbhavāḥ \|*  
*maharjanastapaścaiva satyalokastathaiva ca \|\| 23 \|\|*

*manasaḥ paramo yogo bhūtabhavyabhavasya ca \|*  
*brahmādisthāvarāntasya yoniḥ sāṃkhādimokṣayoḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

20-24. The Brahmanas worshipping the sun have attained the position of Devas in this place. Those who remain firm in their devotion to Shiva and die at this Avimukta-tirtha, attain emancipation. Those who reside there for eight months and subdue their passions or stay there even for four months in sexual abstinence, also attain emancipation.

## \|\| 184.25-27 \|\|

*ye'vimuktaṃ na muñcanti narāste naiva vañcitāḥ \|*  
*uttamaṃ sarvatīrthānāṃ sthānānāmuttamaṃ ca yat \|\| 25 \|\|*

*kṣetrāṇāmuttamaṃ caiva śmaśānānāṃ tathaiva ca \|*  
*taḍāgānāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ kūpānāṃ srotasāṃ tathā \|\| 26 \|\|*

*śailānāmuttamaṃ śailaṃ tīrthānāmuttamaṃ tathā \|*  
*puṇyakṛdbhavabhaktaiśca hyavimuktaṃ tu sevyate \|\| 27 \|\|*

25-27. How far may I describe its glory? Even the unchaste women dying there attain bliss. Men attain here Yoga and bliss, unattainable by men elsewhere. Those who stick to Avimukta-tirtha and do not go elsewhere, undoubtedly become adorable by Brahmanas. One who resides in Avimuktatirtha becomes undoubtedly like Me.

## \|\| 184.28-32 \|\|

*brahmaṇaḥ paramaṃ sthānaṃ brahmaṇā'dhyāsitaṃ ca yat \|*  
*brahmaṇā sevitaṃ nityaṃ brahmaṇā caiva rakṣitam \|\| 28 \|\|*

*atraiva saptabhuvanaṃ kāñcano meruparvataḥ \|*  
*manasaḥ paramo yogaḥ prītyarthaṃ brahmaṇaḥ sa tu \|\| 29 \|\|*

*brahmā tu tatra bhagavāṃstrisaṃdhyaṃ ceśvare sthitaḥ \|*  
*puṇyātpuṇyatamaṃ kṣetraṃ puṇyakṛdbhirniṣevitam \|\| 30 \|\|*

*ādityopāsanaṃ kṛtvā viprāścāmaratāṃ gatāḥ \|*  
*anye'pi ye trayo varṇā bhavabhaktyā samāhitāḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

*avimukte tanuṃ tyaktvā gacchanti paramāṃ gatim \|*  
*aṣṭau māsānvihārasya yatīnāṃ saṃyatātmanām \|\| 32 \|\|*

28-32. It is called Avimukta-tirtha on account of My being present in it at all times. Those who do not resort to Avimukta-tirtha are idiots, full of the darkness of ignorance, Tamoguna. Such men always pass through the ordeal of birth and rebirth. Licentiousness, auger, greed, attachment, hypocrisy, drowsiness, sloth and backbiting, — these obstacles created by India are always present here and many hindrances overpower a man. In spite of all that, this sacred place is the most holy for the devotees. All the Rishis and Devas have also called it to be the most sacred place.

## \|\| 184.33-40 \|\|

*ekatra caturo māsānmāsau vā nivasetpunaḥ \|*  
*avimukte praviṣṭānāṃ vihārastu na vidyate \|\| 33 \|\|*

*na deho bhavitā tatra dṛṣṭaṃ śāstre purātane \|*  
*mokṣo hyasaṃśayastatra pañcatvaṃ tu gatasya vai \|\| 34 \|\|*

*striyaḥ pativratā yāśca bhavabhaktāḥ samāhitāḥ \|*  
*avimukte vimuktāstā yāsyanti paramāṃ gatim \|\| 35 \|\|*

*anyā yāḥ kāmacāriṇyaḥ striyo bhogaparāyaṇāḥ \|*  
*kālena nidhanaṃ prāptā gacchanti paramāṃ gatim \|\| 36 \|\|*

*yatra yogaśca mokṣaśca prāpyate durlabho naraiḥ \|*  
*avimuktaṃ samāsādya nānyadgacchettapovanam \|\| 37 \|\|*

*sarvātmanā tapaḥ sevyaṃ brāhmaṇairnātra saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*avimukte vasedyastu mama tulyo bhavennaraḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

*yato mayā na muktaṃ hi tvavimuktaṃ tataḥ smṛtam \|*  
*avimuktaṃ na sevante mūḍhā ye tamasā’vṛtāḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

*viṇmūtraretasāṃ madhye te vasanti punaḥpunaḥ \|*  
*kāmaḥ krodhaśca lobhaśca dambhastambho'timatsaraḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

33-40. The body made of clay and fat becomes purified at Avimukta-tirtha, because Lord Shiva keeps guard there. Consequently, the learned do not bury there. The devotees who worship f5iva, then merge in Him, like the offering of clarified butter in the fire. They consider their souls blessed on merging in the Lord, and the Rishis, Devas, Yatis, Rakshasas, reside in Avimukta-tirtha and devote themselves to meditation and sacrifices, etc. No one dying there goes to hell. There, by the favour of Shiva, every being gets his final bliss. This tirtha is two-and-a-half yojanas in extent towards the east and the west. The rivers Varanasi, etc., at the in distance of half a yojana from each other are situated there, and the Shukla river flows alongside.

## \|\| 184.41-43 \|\|

*nidrā tandrā tathā’lasyaṃ paiśunyamiti te daśa \|*  
*avimukte sthitā vighnāḥ śakreṇa vihitāḥ svayam \|\| 41 \|\|*

*nivāyakopasargāśca satataṃ mūrdhni tiṣṭhati \|*  
*puṇyametadbhavetsarvaṃ bhaktānāmanukampayā \|\| 42 \|\|*

*paraṃ guhyamiti jñātvā tataḥ śāstrānudarśanāt \|*  
*vyāhṛtaṃ devadevaistu munibhistattvadarśibhiḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

41-43. Mahadeva has thus described this Kshetra. People desirous of supreme felicity attain knowledge and yoga; and those who devoutfully always reside there are free from all cares. This place of asceticism always remains full of the Siddhas, the Gandharvas, etc. There is no river or mountain equal to this Avimukta-tirtha.

## \|\| 184.44-48 \|\|

*medasā viplutā bhūmiravimukte tu varjitā \|*  
*pūtā samabhavatsarvā mahādevena rakṣitā \|\| 44 \|\|*

*saṃskārastena kriyate bhūmeranyatra sūribhiḥ \|*  
*ye bhaktyā varadaṃ devamakṣaraṃ paramaṃ padam \|\| 45 \|\|*

*devadānavagandharvayakṣarakṣomahoragāḥ \|*  
*avimuktamupāsante tanniṣṭhāstatparāyaṇāḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

*te viśanti mahādevamājyāhutirivānalam \|*  
*taṃ vai prāpya mahādevamīśvarādhyuṣitaṃ śubham \|\| 47 \|\|*

*avimuktaṃ kṛtārtho'smītyātmānamupalabhyate \|*  
*ṛṣidevāsuragaṇairjapahomaparāyaṇaiḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

44-48. All the sacred places located on the earth as well as in the heaven are second to this place. It is the supreme of all. Those who, after renouncing the world and subduing their passions recite the Rudra Mantra a hundred times, such devotees of Shiva undoubtedly enjoy in the company of the Lord Mahadeva. Those who have forsaken all desires i and are firm and fixed in devotion, become free from fear after attaining Shiva and are never born.

## \|\| 184.49-53 \|\|

*yatibhirmokṣakāmaiśca hyavimuktaṃ niṣevyate \|*  
*nāvimukte mṛtaḥ kaścinnarakaṃ yāti kilbiṣī \|\| 49 \|\|*

*īśvarānugṛhītā hi sarve yānti parāṃ gatim \|*  
*dviyojanamathārdhaṃ ca tatkṣetraṃ pūrvapaścimam \|\| 50 \|\|*

*ardhayojanavistīrṇaṃ dakṣiṇottarataḥ smṛtam \|*  
*vārāṇasī tadīyā ca yāvacchuklanadī tu vai \|\| 51 \|\|*

*eṣa kṣetrasya vistāraḥ prokto devena dhīmatā \|*  
*labdhvā yogaṃ ca mokṣaṃ ca kāṅkṣanto jñānamuttamam \|\| 52 \|\|*

*avimuktaṃ na muñcanti tanniṣṭhāstatparāyaṇāḥ \|*  
*tasminvasanti ye martyā na te śocyāḥ kadācana \|\| 53 \|\|*

49-53. They are not born even after hundreds and billions of Kalpas. As I the ocean is full of various kinds of gems, so is Avimukta full of many attributes. This place is the giver of delusion to the non-devotees, and devotion to those who are staunch adherents of Shiva. The fools, regarding this as cremation ground, do not consider it to be the foremost of all the sacred places, and the learned do not abandon it, in spite of hundreds of obstacles. They go to such a place, whence they are never reborn and are — liberated from the pangs of old age, death, etc. They go direct to the realm of Shiva.

## \|\| 184.54-55 \|\|

*yogakṣetraṃ tapaḥkṣetraṃ siddhagandharvasevitam \|*  
*saritaḥ sāgarāḥ śailā nāvimuktasamā bhuvi \|\| 54 \|\|*

*bhūrloke cāntarikṣe ca divi tīrthāni yāni ca \|*  
*atītya vartate cānyadavimuktaṃ prabhāvataḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

54-55. Those who are desirous of beatitude beget such as causes them the j utmost gratification. The end attained by the mere residence at Avimuktatirtha is not obtained even by charities, asceticism, sacrifices and Divine Knowledge, etc.

## \|\| 184.56-63 \|\|

*ye tu dhyānaṃ samāsādya yuktātmānaḥ samāhitāḥ \|*  
*saṃniyamyendri yagrāmaṃ japanti śatarudri yam \|\| 56 \|\|*

*avimukte sthitā nityaṃ kṛtārthāste dvijātayaḥ \|*  
*bhavabhaktiṃ samāsādya ramante tu suniścitāḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

*saṃhṛtya śaktitaḥ kāmānviṣayebhyo bahiḥ sthitāḥ \|*  
*śaktitaḥ sarvato muktāḥ śaktitastapasi sthitāḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

*karaṇānīha cā’tmānamapunarbhavabhāvitāḥ \|*  
*taṃ vai prāpya mahātmānamīśvaraṃ nirbhayāḥ sthitāḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

*na teṣāṃ punarāvṛttiḥ kalpakoṭiśatairapi \|*  
*avimukte tu gṛhyante bhavena vibhunā svayam \|\| 60 \|\|*

*utpāditaṃ mahākṣetraṃ sidhyante yatra mānavāḥ \|*  
*uddeśamātraṃ kathitā avimuktaguṇāstathā \|\| 61 \|\|*

*samudra syeva ratnānāmavimuktasya vistaram \|*  
*mohanaṃ tadabhaktānāṃ bhaktānāṃ bhaktivardhanam \|\| 62 \|\|*

*mūḍhāste tu na paśyanti śmaśānamiti mohitāḥ \|*
