*hanyamāno'pi yo vidvānvasedvighnaśatairapi \|\| 63 \|\|*

56-63. The best remedy for all sinners is their attainment of Avimuktatirtha. The various classes of people dying at Avimukta-tirtha in their attachment for Shiva are never re-born. The meditation, sacrifices, asceticism and charity performed at Avimukta-tirtha beget everlasting fruits, and those who die there attain supreme bliss. The sinner, repenting on thousands of his sins, going there attains felicity. Those who die there need not think of Uttarayana or Dakshinayana; for every hour for them is equally auspicious. There is no occasion for thinking of auspiciousness or inauspiciousness there, for that place, owing to the glory of Shiva, is always sacred. Thus all the Rishis heard the glory of such a sanctified place and of Shiva from Svamikartika, and began to meditate over them.

## Chapter 185

## \|\| 185.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*avimukte mahāpuṇye cā’stikāḥ śubhadarśanāḥ \|*  
*vismayaṃ paramaṃ janmurharṣ̣agadgadanisvanāḥ \|\| 185.1 \|\|*

Suta said—“O Rsis! the devotees of gods, seers, and the pure-hearted persons residing at Avimukta were filled with astonishment and overcome with delight.

## \|\| 185.2 \|\|

*ūcuste hṛṣ̣ṭamanasaḥ skandaṃ brahmavidāṃ varam \|*  
*brahmaṇyo devaputrastvaṃ brāhmaṇo brāhmaṇapriyaḥ \|\| 185.2 \|\|*

They joyfully said to Skanda, the foremost among the knower of Brahman- “O Deva, you have been bom of the glory of Siva and Brahma. You are dear to the Brahmanas.

## \|\| 185.3 \|\|

*brahmiṣ̣ṭho brahmavidbrahmā brahmendro brahmalokakṛt \|*  
*brahmakṛdbrahmacārī tvaṃ brahmādirbrahmavatsalaḥ \|\| 185.3 \|\|*

You are Brahmana and the knower of Brahman. You are lord of Brahmanas, You have created the realm of Brahma and are kind to the Brahmanas. You are Brahmacarin and first then Brahma.

## \|\| 185.4-5 \|\|

*brahmatulyodbhavakaro brahmatulya namo'stu te \|*  
*ṛṣ̣ayo bhāvitātmānaḥ śrutvedaṃ pāvanaṃ mahat \|\| 185.4 \|\|*

*tattvaṃ tu paramaṃ jñātaṃ yajжñātvā'mṛtamaśnute \|*  
*svasti te'stu gamiṣ̣yāmo bhūrlokaṃ śaṃkarālayam \|\| 185.5 \|\|*

You are the Creator like Brahma and equal to him, salutation to you! All Rsis have become purified by listening to this narration. We have realized the highest secret, by which nobody gets rebirth.

## \|\| 185.6 \|\|

*yatrāsau sarvabhūtātmā sthāṇubhūtaḥ sthitaḥ prabhuḥ \|*  
*sarvalokahitārthāya tapasyugre vyavasthitaḥ \|\| 185.6 \|\|*

May you be blessed! We are now going to that mundane region of the Lord Siva where He, the Lord of all, is practising austerities unmoved, for the benefit of the Universe.

## \|\| 185.7-9 \|\|

*saṃyojya yogenā’tmānaṃ raudrī ṃ! tanumupāśritaḥ \|*  
*guhyakairātmabhūtastu ātmatulyaguṇairvṛtaḥ \|\| 185.7 \|\|*

*tato brahmādibhirdevaiḥ siddhaiśca paramarṣ̣ibhiḥ \|*  
*vijñaptaḥ parayā bhaktyā tvatprasādādgaṇeśvara \|\| 185.8 \|\|*

*vastumicchāma niyatamavimukte suniścitāḥ \|*  
*evaṃguṇo tathā martyā hyavimukte vasanti ye \|\| 185.9 \|\|*

By the virtue of His asceticism, He merges Himself in the formidable form and remains adorned with all His attributes along with His attendants. The Devas, Brahma, devotees and the Siddhas are eager to see the Lord, through your favour. We are, therefore, eager to pass our days at Avimukta; for blessed are those who reside there.

## \|\| 185.10 \|\|

*dharmaśīlā jitakrodhā nirmamā niyatendri yāḥ \|*  
*dhyānayogaparāḥ siddhiṃ gacchanti paramāvyayām \|\| 185.10 \|\|*

Those who are righteous, devoid of anger and lust, having their passions under their control, devoted to the practice of yoga, attain emancipation there.

## \|\| 185.11-12\|\|

*tenaiva cābhyanujñātāstanniṣ̣ṭhāstatparāyaṇāḥ \|*  
*avimukte tanuṃ tyaktvā śāntā yogagatiṃ gatāḥ \|\| 185.11 \|\|*

*sthānaṃ guhyaṃ śmaśānānāṃ sarveṣ̣āmetaducyate \|*  
*na hi yogādṛte mokṣ̣aḥ prāpyate bhuvi mānavaiḥ \|\| 185.12 \|\|*

The Yogis, skilled in yoga and calmed adore the Lord Siva, the giver of beatitude. They attain bliss. It is the most mysterious of all the cremation grounds; and no one attains bliss in this world without the help of yoga.

## \|\| 185.13-15 \|\|

*avimukte nivasatāṃ yogo mokṣ̣aśca sidhyati \|*  
*eka eva prabhāvo'sti kṣ̣etrasya parameśvari \|*  
*anena janmanaiveha prāpyate gatiruttamā \|\| 185.13 \|\|*

*avimukte nivasatā vyāsenāmitatejasā \|*  
*naiva labdhā kvacidbhikṣ̣ā bhramamāṇena yatnataḥ \|\| 185.14 \|\|*

*kṣ̣udhāviṣ̣ṭastataḥ kruddho'cintayacchāpamuttamam \|*  
*dinaṃ dinaṃ prati vyāsaḥ ṣ̣aṇmāsaṃ yo'vatiṣ̣ṭhati \|\| 185.15 \|\|*

People dwelling at Avimukta beget both yoga and beatitude. They can attain highest end in this life. “O Deva! the inhabitants of Avimukta get bliss during their lifetime, such is its glory.” Once upon a time splendid Vedavyasa could not get any alms there, and, agitated with the pangs of hunger he felt inclined, to pronounce a curse. He passed a period of six months with great privations.

## \|\| 185.16-17 \|\|

*kathaṃ mamedaṃ nagaraṃ bhikṣ̣ādoṣ̣āddhataṃ tvidam \|*  
*vipro vā kṣ̣attriyo vā'pi brāhmaṇī vidhavā'pi vā \|\| 185.16 \|\|*

*saṃskṛtā'saṃskṛtā vā'pi paripakvāḥ kathaṃ nu me \|*  
*na prayacchanti vai lokā brāhmaṇāścaryakārakam \|\| 185.17 \|\|*

He said to himself, ‘How has this place become cursed and doles me no alms. The Brahmanas, the Ksatriyas, the widows, the married ladies, none of them give me any alms-which is most strange.

## \|\| 185.18-20 \|\|

*eṣ̣āṃ śāpaṃ pradāsyāmi tīrthasya nagarasya tu \|*  
*tīrthaṃ cātīrthatāṃ yātu nagaraṃ śāpayāmyaham \|\| 185.18 \|\|*

*mā bhūttripauruṣ̣ī vidyā mā bhūttripauruṣ̣aṃ dhanam \|*  
*mā bhūttripauruṣ̣aṃ sakhyaṃ vyāso vārāṇasīṃ śapan \|\| 185.19 \|\|*

*avimukte nivasatāṃ janānāṃ puṇyakarmaṇām \|*  
*vighnaṃ sṛjāmi sarveṣ̣āṃ yena siddhirna vidyate \|\| 185.20 \|\|*

I shall pronounce my curse on all of them and on the whole city to the effect that this sacred place may become devoid of its sanctity and that there be no pelf and learning left among the people of all the three classes residing here. No friendship should exist among them. I shall also create such troubles for those residing at Avimukta as they may not attain their goal.’

## \|\| 185.21 \|\|

*vyāsacittaṃ tadā jñātvā devadeva umāpatiḥ \|*  
*bhītabhītastadā gaurīṃ tāṃ priyāṃ paryabhāṣ̣ata \|\| 185.21 \|\|*

Thinking over the intentions of Vedavyasa, the Lord of Uma became terrified and said to the beloved Parvatl.

## \|\| 185.22 \|\|

*śṛṇu devi vaco mahyaṃ yādṛśaṃ pratyupasthitam \|*  
*kṛṣ̣ṇadvaipāyanaḥ kopācchāpaṃ dātuṃ samudyataḥ \|\| 185.22 \|\|*

О  Devi!  Listen  to  my  words.  Now  angrily  Vedavyasa is ready to pronounce his curse.

## \|\| 185.23 \|\|

*devyuvāca*  
*kimarthaṃ śapate kruddho vyāsaḥ kena prakopitaḥ \|*  
*kiṃ kṛtaṃ bhagavaṃstasya yena śāpaṃ prayacchati \|\| 185.23 \|\|*

Parvatl said- “O Lord! Why is Vyasa so angry and ready to curse? Who has annoyed him? What harm has been done to him that he is disposed to pronounce a curse?”

## \|\| 185.24 \|\|

*devadeva uvāca*  
*anena sutapastaptaṃ bahūnvarṣ̣agaṇānpriye \|*  
*mauninā dhyānayuktena dvādaśābdānvarānane \|\| 185.24 \|\|*

Mahadeva said- ‘O Dear Parvatl? He has practised glorious asceticism for a long time. He has lived in contemplation by observing the vow of silence for a period of twelve years.

## \|\| 185.25-26 \|\|

*tataḥ kṣ̣udhā susaṃjātā bhikṣ̣āmaṭitumāgataḥ \|*  
*naivāsya kenacidbhikṣ̣ā grāsārdhamapi bhāmini \|\| 185.25 \|\|*

*evaṃ bhagavataḥ kāla āsītṣ̣āṇmāsiko muneḥ \|*  
*tataḥ krodhaparītātmā śāpaṃ dāsyati so'dhunā \|\| 185.26 \|\|*

О beautiful one! when he felt hungry, he came to beg for alms, but no one gave him even half a morsel. Thus the sage has passed the time of six months under serious privations; consequently, he has now made up his mind to pronounce a curse.

## \|\| 185.27-28 \|\|

*yāvannaiṣ̣a śapettāvadupāyastatra cintyatām \|*  
*kṛṣ̣ṇadvaipāyanaṃ vyāsaṃ viddhi nārāyaṇaṃ priye \|\| 185.27 \|\|*

*ko'sya śāpānna bibheti hyapi sākṣ̣ātpitāmahaḥ \|*  
*adaivaṃ daivataṃ kuryāddaivaṃ cāpyapadaivatam \|\| 185.28 \|\|*

Some plan should be devised to obviate the situation before he pronounces his curse. Vedavyasa has attained supernatural powers and everyone is afraid of his curse. He has the power to bring about what is not destined and to change the effects of destiny.

## \|\| 185.29 \|\|

*āvāṃ tu mānuṣ̣au bhūtvā gṛhasthāvihavāsinau \|*  
*tasya tṛptikarīṃ bhikṣ̣āṃ prayacchāvo varānane \|\| 185.29 \|\|*

We shall assume the form of a human being residing here as a householder and then О beautiful one, we shall give him the alms engaging him in the conversation.’

## \|\| 185.30-31 \|\|

*evamuktā tato devī devena śaṃbhunā tadā \|*  
*vyāsasya darśanaṃ dattvā kṛtvā veṣ̣aṃ tu mānuṣ̣am \|\| 185.30 \|\|*

*ehyehi bhagavansādho bhikṣ̣āṃ grāhaya sattama \|*  
*asmadgṛhe kadācittvaṃ nā’gato'smi mahāmune \|\| 185.31 \|\|*

Parvatl, thus instructed, also assumed human form, became present before Vedavyasa and said- “0 Bhagavan! come here and receive alms. О great seer! you never blessed my home.”

## \|\| 185.32-35 \|\|

*etacchrutvā prītamanā bhikṣ̣āṃ grahītumāgataḥ \|*  
*bhikṣ̣āṃ dattvā tu vyāsāya ṣ̣aḍrasāmamṛtopamām \|\| 185.32 \|\|*

*anāsvāditapūrvā sā bhakṣ̣itā muninā tadā \|*  
*bhikṣ̣āṃ vyāsastato bhuktvā cintayanhṛṣ̣ṭamānasaḥ \|\| 185.33 \|\|*

*vavande varadaṃ devaṃ devīṃ ca girijāṃ tadā \|*  
*vyāsaḥ kamalapatrākṣ̣a idaṃ vacanamabravīt \|\| 185.34 \|\|*

*devo devī nadī gaṅgā miṣ̣ṭamannaṃ śubhā gatiḥ \|*  
*vārāṇasyāṃ viśālākṣ̣i vāsaḥ kasya na rocate \|\| 185.35 \|\|*

Hearing thus, the sage joyfully came to accept the alms that contained tasteful food like nectar. Sage Vyasa took that delicious alms and was completely satisfied. Then the lotus-eyed sage Vyasa made his salutations to the Lord Mahadeva and Parvatl and said these words- “0 one with beautiful eyes! Lord Mahadeva and Parvatl reside in Varanasi, the Ganga flows through this place. Delicious eatables are also obtainable and emancipation is begotten. Who would not therefore reside in such a Kas'I?”

## \|\| 185.36-37 \|\|

*evamuktvā tato vyāso nagarīmavalokayan \|*  
*cintayānastato bhikṣ̣āṃ hṛdayānandakāriṇīm \|\| 185.36 \|\|*

*apaśyatpurato devaṃ devīṃ ca girijāṃ tadā \|*  
*gṛhāṅgaṇasthitaṃ vyāsaṃ devadevo'bravīdidam \|\| 185.37 \|\|*

Having said thus, Vedavyasa looked at the sacred KasI and began to think about the delicious alms, the giver of satisfaction to mind, obtained by him. He saw Mahadeva and Parvatl before him. Lord said to Vyasa, who was standing at the entrance of their home.

## \|\| 185.38 \|\|

*iha kṣ̣etre na vastavyaṃ krodhanastvaṃ mahāmune \|*  
*evaṃ vismayamāpanno devaṃ vyāso'bravīdvacaḥ \|\| 185.38 \|\|*

“O great seer! you have a very choleric temper and you should not therefore reside in KasI.” Then the astonished Vyasadeva said these words.

## \|\| 185.39 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca*  
*caturdaśyāmathāṣ̣ṭamyāṃ pradeśaṃ dātumarhasi \|*  
*evamastvityanujñāya tatraivāntaradhīyata \|\| 185.39 \|\|*  
*na tadgṛhaṃ na sā devī na devo jñāyate kvacit \|*

Then Vyasa requested them to allow him to reside at that place on the day of CaturdasI and Afjtaml. Then Lord said him- “be it so” and disappeared then and there was no abode, the Goddess and God also anywhere.

## \|\| 185.40-41 \|\|

*evaṃ trailokyavikhyātaḥ purā vyāso mahātapāḥ \|\| 185.40 \|\|*

*jñātvā kṣ̣etraguṇānsarvānsthitastasyaiva pārśvataḥ \|*  
*evaṃ vyāsaṃ sthitaṃ jñātvā kṣ̣etraṃ śaṃsanti paṇḍitāḥ \|\| 185.41 \|\|*

In that way, in ancient time, the renowned in three lokas and illustrious Vedavyasa, knowing the glory of that place, fixed his abode in its vicinity; and because of the presence of Vyasadeva there, all learned persons sing the praises of this sacred place.

## \|\| 185.42-44 \|\|

*avimuktaguṇānsarvānkaḥ samartho vadiṣ̣yati \|*  
*devabrāhmaṇavidviṣ̣ṭā devabhaktiviḍambakāḥ \|\| 185.42 \|\|*

*brahmaghnāśca kṛtaghnāśca tathā naiṣ̣kṛtikāśca ye \|*  
*lokadviṣ̣o gurudviṣ̣astīrthāyatanadūṣ̣akāḥ \|\| 185.43 \|\|*

*sadā pāparatāścaiva ye cānye kutsitā bhuvi \|*  
*teṣ̣āṃ nāstīti vāso vai sthito'sau daṇḍanāyakaḥ \|\| 185.44 \|\|*

Indeed, nobody can count the glory of Avimukta tlrtha. The malevolent of the Devas and the Brahmanas, the disrespected to the devotion of gods, the killers of the Brahmanas, those ungrateful and other sinners, the scoffers of the preceptors, sacred places and temples, the instigators, do not reside in the sacred KasI, as Dandanayaka, one of the attendants of Siva, is posted there to oust them.

## \|\| 185.45-46 \|\|

*rakṣ̣aṇārthaṃ niyuktaṃ vai daṇḍanāyakamuttamam \|*  
*pūjayitvā yathāśaktyā gandhapuṣ̣pādidhūpakaiḥ \|\| 185.45 \|\|*

*namaskāraṃ tataḥ kṛtvā nāyakasya tu mantravit \|*  
*sarvavarṇāvṛte kṣ̣etre nānāvidhasarīsṛpe \|\| 185.46 \|\|*

*īśvarānugṛhītā hi gatiṃ gāṇeśvarīṃ gatāḥ \|*

Dandanayaka is posted for guarding the place, so He ought to be adored with incense, flowers etc. He should be reverentially saluted, and his mantra should also be repeated and counted on the bead. Various classes of people reside in the sacred Kas'I and all kinds of snakes, scorpions, etc., also abound there. By the grace of lord Siva they become the attendants of Siva.

## \|\| 185.47-48 \|\|

*nānārūpadharā divyā nānāveṣ̣adharāstathā \|\| 185.47 \|\|*

*surā vai ye tu sarve ca tanniṣ̣ṭhāstatparāyaṇāḥ \|*  
*yadicchanti paraṃ sthānamakṣ̣ayaṃ tadavāpnuyuḥ \|\| 185.48 \|\|*

The Devas, having many divine forms and costumes, devoted to Siva and residing there, also attain the highest stage, according to their choice.

## \|\| 185.49 \|\|

*paraṃ puraṃ daivapurādviśiṣ̣yate taduttaraṃ brahmapurātpuraḥ sthitam \|*  
*tapobalādīśvarayoganirmitaṃ na tatsamaṃ brahmadivaukasālayam \|*  
*manoramaṃ kāmagamaṃ hyanāmayamatītya tejāṃsi tapāṃsi yogavat \|\| 185.49 \|\|*

The sacred KasI is superior even to the heaven of the Devas and also superior to Brahmaloka. It has been laid out by the Yogic power of the Lord and there is no other region like it. The sacred KasI is the fulfiller of cherished desires. It is free from diseases and the place of asceticism and yoga.

## \|\| 185.50-51 \|\|

*adhiṣ̣ṭhitastu tatsthāne devadevo virājate \|*  
*tapāṃsi yāni tapyante vratāni niyamāśca ye \|\| 185.50 \|\|*

*sarvatīrthābhiṣ̣ekaṃ tu sarvadānaphalāni ca \|*  
*sarvayajñeṣ̣u yatpuṇyamavimukte tadāpnuyāt \|\| 185.51 \|\|*

Lord Siva, enshrined there is shining in His full glory. Those who practise asceticism there, attain the benefits of all sacrifices, of bathing at sacred places and of giving charities.

## \|\| 185.52-53 \|\|

*atītaṃ vartamānaṃ ca ajñānājжñānato'pi vā \|*  
*sarvaṃ tasya ca yatpāpaṃ kṣ̣etraṃ dṛṣ̣ṭvā vinaśyati \|\| 185.52\|\|*

*śāntairdāntaistapastaptaṃ yatkiṃciddharmasaṃjñitam \|*  
*sarvaṃ ca tadavāpnoti avimukte jitendri yaḥ \|\| 185.53 \|\|*

The past and the present sins committed through ignorance or are dispelled by mere sight of Avimukta. Men of calm disposition and those who keep their passions curbed, whatever charities they perform at Avimukta, get a huge return.

## \|\| 185.54-55 \|\|

*avimuktaṃ samāsādya liṅgamarcayate naraḥ \|*  
*kalpakoṭiśataiścāpi nāsti tasya punarbhavaḥ \|\| 185.54 \|\|*

*amarā hyakṣ̣ayāścaiva krīḍanti bhavasaṃnidhau \|*  
*kṣ̣etratīrthopaniṣ̣adamavimuktaṃ na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 185.55 \|\|*

A man, who worships Siva-linga at Avimukta is not reborn in this world for crores of cycles. Thousands of Devas enjoy the company of Siva and therefore, this place is the best of all. There should not be any doubt in this fact.

## \|\| 185.56 \|\|

*avimukte mahādevamarcayanti stuvanti vai \|*  
*sarvapāpavinirmuktāste tiṣ̣ṭhantyajarāmarāḥ \|\| 185.56 \|\|*

Those who adore Mahadeva at Avimukta, are liberated from all sins and become immortal and devoid of old age.

## \|\| 185.57-58 \|\|

*sarvakāmāśca ye yajñāḥ punarāvṛttikāḥ smṛtāḥ \|*  
*avimukte mṛtā ye ca sarve te hyanivartakāḥ \|\| 185.57 \|\|*

*grahanakṣ̣atratārāṇāṃ kālena patanādbhayam \|*  
*avimukte mṛtānāṃ tu patanaṃ naiva vidyate \|\| 185.58 \|\|*

All the sacrifices performed with a motive are liable to ordain the rebirth of a man, but those who die at Avimukta are never bom. The stars and planets perish at a certain fixed period, but those dying at Avimukta are not liable to it.

## \|\| 185.59-60 \|\|

*kalpakoṭisahasraistu kalpakoṭiśatairapi \|*  
*na teṣ̣āṃ punarāvṛttirmṛtā ya kṣ̣atra uttame \|\| 185.59 \|\|*

*saṃsārasāgare ghore bhramantaḥ kālaparyayāt \|*  
*avimuktaṃ samāsādya gacchanti paramāṃ gatim \|\| 185.60 \|\|*

Those who die at this excellent place do not take rebirth even after crores of kalpas. Blessed are those who reach the sacred Manikarnika place of Avimukta, at their last hour, after wandering in this dreadful ocean of life.

## \|\| 185.61-62 \|\|

*jñātvā kaliyugaṃ ghoraṃ hāhābhūtamacetanam \|*  
*avimuktaṃ na muñcanti kṛtārthāste narā bhuvi \|\| 185.61 \|\|*

*avimuktaṃ praviṣ̣ṭastu yadi gacchettataḥ punaḥ \|*  
*tadā hasanti bhūtāni anyonyakaratāḍanaiḥ \|\| 185.62 \|\|*

Knowing the grim pinch of the Kali-age, men who do not leave this Avimukta tlrtha, they are blessed. The inhabitant of Avimukta, when he goes elsewhere, is ridiculed by everybody.

## \|\| 185.63 \|\|

*kāmakrodhena lobhena grastā ye bhuvi mānavāḥ \|*  
*niṣ̣kramante narā devi daṇḍanāyakamohitāḥ \|\| 185.63 \|\|*

O Devi! the people in this world, who succumb to the influence of lust, anger and greed, go away from that sacred place for fear of Dandanayaka.

## \|\| 185.64 \|\|

*japadhyānavihīnānāṃ jñānavarjitacetasām \|*  
*tato duḥkhahatānāṃ ca gatirvārāṇasī nṛṇām \|\| 185.64 \|\|*

Those who are ignorant, devoid of meditation and oppressed with miseries, attain emancipation there.

## \|\| 185.65-67 \|\|

*tīrthānāṃ pañcakaṃ sāraṃ viśveśānandakānane \|*  
*daśāśvamedhaṃ lolārkaḥ keśavo bindumādhavaḥ \|\| 185.65 \|\|*

*pañcamī tu mahāśreṣ̣ṭhā procyate maṇikarṇikā \|*  
*ebhistu tīrthavaryaiśca varṇyate hyavimuktam \|\| 185.66 \|\|*

*eka eva prabhāvo'sti kṣ̣etrasya parameśvari \|*  
*ekena janmanā devi mokṣ̣aṃ paśyantyanuttamam \|\| 185.67 \|\|*

The five principal places have been described in the blissful world of lord of universe, viz: Dasasvamedha, Lokarka, Kes'ava, Bindumadhava and the fifth Manikarnika. Because of these tlrthas, Avimukta is described. О Goddess, All places have same sacred effects. О Devi! the people attain beatitude in their one life because of these tlrthas.

## \|\| 185.68 \|\|

*etadvai kathitaṃ sarvaṃ devyai devena bhāṣ̣itam \|*  
*avimuktasya kṣ̣etrasya tatsarvaṃ kathitaṃ dvijāḥ \|\| 185.68 \|\|*

О Brahmanas, I have narrated evrything to you about the glory of Avimukta, which was said by Lord Siva to Parvati.

## Chapter 186

## \|\| 186.1-3 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*māhātmyamavimuktasya yathāvatkathitaṃ tvayā \|*  
*idānīṃ narmadāyāstu māhātmyaṃ vada sattama \|\| 1 \|\|*

*yatroṃkārasya māhātmyaṃ kapilāsaṃgamasya ca \|*  
*amareśasya caivā’hurmāhātmyaṃ pāpanāśanam \|\| 2 \|\|*

*kathaṃ pralayakāle tu na naṣṭā narmadā purā \|*  
*mārkaṇḍeyaśca bhagavānna vinaṣṭastadā kila \|*  
*tvayoktaṃ tadidaṃ sarvaṃ punarvistarato vada \|\| 3 \|\|*

1-3 The "Rishis said: — “Suta! you have well-described to us the glory of Avimukta. Now we are eager to hear the glory of the sacred Narmada which be good enough to describe to us; Omkara, the confluence of Kapila, and the dispeller of all sins, the Lord Amaresha, are also said to be situate there. How was the sacred Narmada saved from annihilation at the time of the destruction of the universe? How was Markandeya saved from annihilation? You have told us something about them, but we wish to hear more of them in detail.”

## \|\| 186.4-5 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*etadeva purā pṛṣṭaḥ pāṇḍavena mahātmanā \|*  
*narmadāyāstu māhātmyaṃ mārkaṇḍeyo mahāmuniḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*ugreṇa tapasā yukto vanastho vanavāsinā \|*  
*pṛṣṭaḥ pūrvāṃ mahāgāthāṃ dharmaputreṇa dhīmatā \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. Suta said: — Once before, the King Yudhisthira asked the sage Markandeya the glory of Narmada, when the king was practising austerities in the forest.

## \|\| 186.6-7 \|\|

*yudhiṣṭhira uvāca*  
*śrutā me vividhā dharmāstvatprasādāddvijottama \|*  
*bhūyaśca śrotumicchāmi tanme kathaya suvrata \|\| 6 \|\|*

*kathameṣā mahāpuṇyā nadī sarvatra viśrutā \|*  
*narmadā nāma vikhyātā tanme brūhi mahāmune \|\| 7 \|\|*

6-7. Yudhishthira said: — “Virtuous one! through your grace, I have heard about various kinds of Dharmas, but I feel eager to hear more about them which please narrate tome. First of all, please explain to me how the Narmada came into existence.”

## \|\| 186.8-12 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca*  
*narmadā saritāṃ śreṣṭhā sarvapāpapraṇāśinī \|*  
*tārayetsarvabhūtāni sthāvarāṇi carāṇi ca \|\| 8 \|\|*

*narmadāyāstu māhātmyaṃ purāṇe yanmayā śrutam \|*  
*tadetaddhi mahārāja tatsarvaṃ kathayāmi te \|\| 9 \|\|*

*puṇyā kanakhale gaṅgā kurukṣetre sarasvatī \|*  
*grāme vā yadi vā'raṇye puṇyā sarvatra narmadā \|\| 10 \|\|*

*tribhiḥ sārasvataṃ toyaṃ saptāhena tu yāmunam \|*  
*sadyaḥ punāti gāṅgeyaṃ darśanādeva nārmadam \|\| 11 \|\|*

*kaliṅgadeśe paścārdhe parvate'marakaṇṭake \|*  
*puṇyā ca triṣu lokeṣu ramaṇīyā manoramā \|\| 12 \|\|*

8-12. Markandeya said: — “The Narmada is the foremost among all the rivers. It is the dispeller of everybody’s sins. King Yudhisthira! the glory of the sacred Narmada as I have read in several Puranas, I shall explain to you. Sacred is the river Ganges at Kankhala, sacred is Sarasvati in Kurukshetra. The sacred Narmada is supreme everywhere — in the forest as well as in places of habitation. The waters of the Sarasvati purify one in course of five days, those of the Yamuna in seven days, of the Ganges instantaneously, and of the Narmada at the mere sight of it The Narmada is most charming and attractive of the country of Kalinga, the forest of Amarakantaka, and of all the three realms.

## \|\| 186.13-15 \|\|

*sadevāsuragandharvā ṛṣayaśca tapodhanāḥ \|*  
*tapastaptvā mahārāja siddhiṃ ca paramāṃ gatāḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*tatra snātvā naro rājanniyamastho jitendri yaḥ \|*  
*upoṣya rajanīmekāṃ kulānāṃ tārayecchatam \|\| 14 \|\|*

*jaleśvare naraḥ snātvā piṇḍaṃ dattvā yathāvidhi \|*  
*pitarastasya tṛpyanti yāvadābhūtasaṃplavam \|\| 15 \|\|*

13-15. King! the Devas, the demons the Gandharvas, the ascetics, the Rishis — they all attain emancipation on the banks of the Narmada. One who follows the prescribed order of religion and observes a complete fast for a day, after bathing m the Narmada, liberates his seven generations from sin. The manes of those who offer them libations at Jaleshvara, after bathing in it, remain happy till the end of the cycle.

## \|\| 186.16-22 \|\|

*parvatasya samantāttu rudra koṭiḥ pratiṣṭhitā \|*  
*snātvā yaḥ kurute tatra gandhamālyānulepanaiḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*prītastasya bhaveccharvo rudra koṭirna saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*paścime parvatasyānte svayaṃ devo maheśvaraḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*tatra snātvā śucirbhūtvā brahmacārī jitendri yaḥ \|*  
*pitṛkāryaṃ ca kurvīta vidhivanniyatendri yaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*tilodakena tatraiva tarpayetpitṛdevatāḥ \|*  
*āsaptamaṃ kulaṃ tasya svarge modeta pāṇḍava \|\| 19 \|\|*

*ṣaṣṭirvarṣasahasrāṇi svargaloke mahīyate \|*  
*apsarogaṇasaṃkīrṇe siddhacāraṇasevite \|\| 20 \|\|*

*divyagandhānuliptaśca divyālaṃkārabhūṣitaḥ \|*  
*tataḥ svargātparibhraṣṭo jāyate vipule kule \|\| 21 \|\|*

*dhanavāndānaśīlaśca dhārmikaścaiva jāyate \|*  
*punaḥ smarati tattīrthaṃ gamanaṃ tatra rocate \|\| 22 \|\|*

16-22. Lord Shiva becomes pleased with one who bathes in the Narmada, near the hill abounding with the group of Rudras, and worships Them with sandal, flower and incense. The Lord is enshrined close to that hill, to the west, where one ought to offer libations to the manes with v, devotion and by keeping one’s passions under control Libations of water mixed with barley should be offered to the Devas, and water mixed with sesamum should be offered to the manes. One who does so makes his seven generations go to the heaven, and he himself enjoys in heaven I for 60,000 years with the celestial nymphs, the Gandharvas and the I Siddhas. Afterwards he is born as a wealthy man; and, after a life of charities he returns to the very same sanctified place.

## \|\| 186.23-31 \|\|

*kulāni tārayetsapta rudra lokaṃ sa gacchati \|*  
*yojanānāṃ śataṃ sāgraṃ śrūyate sariduttamā \|\| 23 \|\|*

*vistāreṇa tu rājendra yojanadvayamāyatā \|*  
*ṣaṣṭistīrthasahasrāṇi ṣaṣṭikoṭyastathaiva ca \|\| 24 \|\|*

*sarvaṃ tasya samantāttu tiṣṭhatyamarakaṇṭake \|*  
*brahmacārī śucirbhūtvā jitakrodho jitendri yaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*sarvahiṃsānivṛttastu sarvabhūtahite rataḥ \|*  
*evaṃ sarvasamācāro yastu prāṇānparityajet \|\| 26 \|\|*

*tasya puṇyaphalaṃ rājañśṛṇuṣvāvahito mama \|*  
*śataṃ varṣasahasrāṇāṃ svarge modeta pāṇḍava \|\| 27 \|\|*

*apsarogaṇasaṃkīrṇe siddhacāraṇasevite \|*  
*divyagandhānuliptaśca divyapuṣpopaśobhitaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

*krīḍate devalokastho daivataiḥ saha modate \|*  
*tataḥ svargātparibhraṣṭo rājā bhavati vīryavān \|\| 29 \|\|*

*gṛhaṃ tu labhate vai sa nānāratnavibhūṣitam \|*  
*stambhairmaṇimayairdivyairvrajravaiḍūryabhūṣitaiḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

*ālekhyasahitaṃ divyaṃ dāsīdāsasamanvitam \|*  
*mattamātaṅgaśabdaiśca hayānāṃ hreṣitena ca \|\| 31 \|\|*

23-31. Then he goes to the domain of Shiva, after liberating his seven generations from sin. The length of the Narmada is 100 yojanas, and its breadth is 16 miles. There are 60,00,60,000 of tirthas round the Narmada. One who is calm and has his passions under his control, free from anger, and the sin of causing pain to others, and is a benefactor of t all the beings and a devotee to the Lord Shiva, if he happens to die at the banks of the Narmada, resides in heaven for a century, consisting of the length of days of the gods. There he is in the company of the nymphs, and is adored by the Siddhas and the Gandharvas with incense, flowers, &c. He has also the privilege to live in the company of the Devas of all classes; and, on being re-born, becomes a most illustrious I king! There, he is the owner of a majestic palace, studded with jewels; and supported on mighty pillars of precious stones, surrounded by a large retinue of servants and maids. Majestic elephants and a multitude i of neighing horses adorn his gateway.

## \|\| 186.32-33 \|\|

*kṣubhyate tasya taddvāramindra sya bhavanaṃ yathā \|*  
*rājarājeśvaraḥ śrīmānsarvastrījanavallabhaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

*tasmingṛha uṣitvā tu krīḍābhogasamanvite \|*  
*jīvedvarṣaśataṃ sāgraṃ sarvarogavivarjitaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

32-33. His gateway is also illustrious like that of Indra. In such a place I he is the beloved lord of beautiful ladies, and enjoys himself for a divine ' century, without being oppressed with any kind of disease.

## \|\| 186.34-38 \|\|

*evaṃ bhogo bhavettasya yo mṛto'marakaṇṭake \|*  
*agnau viṣajale vā'pi tathā caiva hyanāśake \|\| 34 \|\|*

*anivartikā gatistasya pavanasyāmbare yathā \|*  
*patanaṃ kurute yastu amareśe narādhipa \|\| 35 \|\|*

*kanyānāṃ trisahasrāṇi ekaikasyāpi cāpare \|*  
*tiṣṭhanti bhuvane tasya preṣaṇaṃ prārthayanti ca \|*  
*divyabhogaiḥ susaṃpannaḥ krīḍate kālamakṣayam \|\| 36 \|\|*

*pṛthivyāmāsamudrā yāmīdṛśo naiva jāyate \|*  
*yādṛśo'yaṃ nṛpaśreṣṭha parvate'marakaṇṭake \|\| 37 \|\|*

*tāvattīrthaṃ tu vijñeyaṃ parvatasya tu paścime \|*  
*hrado jaleśvaro nāma triṣu lokeṣu viśrutaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

34-38 One who dies at Amarakantaka gets many blessings and never perishes by fire, poison drowning. He gets the power of moving about in the space' with the rapidity of the wind. The man who dies at Amaresha is blessed with all kinds of enjoyments including 3,000 maids who are at his command for a considerable length of time. One who offers flowers, incense, &c., to the Rudras enshrined round the hill, after having his ablution in the river, undoubtedly wins the pleasure of all of Them.

## \|\| 186.39-46 \|\|

*tatra piṇḍapradānena saṃdhyopāsanakarmaṇā \|*  
*pitaro daśa varṣāṇi tarpitāstu bhavanti vai \|\| 39 \|\|*

*dakṣiṇe narmadākūle kapileti mahānadī \|*  
*sakalārjunasaṃchannā nātidūre vyavasthitā \|\| 40 \|\|*

*sā'pi puṇyā mahābhāgā triṣu lokeṣu viśrutā \|*  
*tatra koṭiśataṃ sāgraṃ tīrthānāṃ tu yudhiṣṭhira \|\| 41 \|\|*

*purāṇe śrūyate rājansarvaṃ koṭiguṇaṃ bhavet \|*  
*tasyāstīre tu ye vṛkṣāḥ patitāḥ kālaparyayāt \|\| 42 \|\|*

*narmadātoyasaṃspṛṣṭāste'pi yānti parāṃ gatim \|*  
*dvitīyā tu mahābhāgā viśalyakaraṇī śubhā \|\| 43 \|\|*

*tatra tīrthe naraḥ snātvā viśalyo bhavati kṣaṇāt \|*  
*tatra devagaṇāḥ sarve sakiṃnaramahoragāḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

*yakṣarākṣasagandharvā ṛṣayaśca tapodhanāḥ \|*  
*sarve samāgatāstatra parvate'marakaṇṭake \|\| 45 \|\|*

*taiśca sarvaiḥ samāgamya munibhiśca tapodhanaiḥ \|*  
*narmadāmāśritā puṇyā viśalyā nāma nāmataḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

39-46. To the west of the hill is enshrined Lord Maheshvara, where one “who offers libations, according to the prescribed rituals to the Devas and the Pitris after his bath, is the bestower of heaven on his seven generations, and he himself resides in heaven for sixty divine years, where various comforts and enjoyments fall to his lot. On coming down from heaven, he is born in a wealthy house, and is most charitable and righteous. He again remembers the sacred Narmada and goes there, where he again works out the salvation of his ancestors of the past seven generations, and then attains the abode of Shiva. When he is reborn, he becomes a matchless sovereign. Such is the glory of Amarakantaka. Now hear of the tirthas situated to the west of the hill The lake Jaleshvara, situated there, is renowned all over the world, where, by performing the daily prayers and by offering libations to the manes, the Pitris remain satiated to their fill, for a period of ten years.

## \|\| 186.47-48 \|\|

*utpāditā mahābhāgā sarvapāpapraṇāśinī \|*  
*tatra snātvā naro rājanbrahmacārī jitendri yaḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

*upoṣya rajanīmekāṃ kulānāṃ tārayecchatam \|*  
*kapilā ca viśalyā ca śrūyate rājasattama \|\| 48 \|\|*

47-48. The river Kapila is on the right bank of the Narmada which is covered with Arjuna and various kinds of trees. This river is renowned as the most sacred in all the three realms, and there are millions of tirthas round it.

## \|\| 186.49-50 \|\|

*īśvareṇa purā prokte lokānāṃ hitakāmyayā \|*  
*tatra snātvā naro rājannaśvamedhaphalaṃ labhet \|\| 49 \|\|*

*anāśakaṃ tu yaḥ kuryāttasmiṃstīrthe narādhipa \|*  
*sarvapāpaviśuddhātmā rudra lokaṃ sa gacchati \|\| 50 \|\|*

49-50. It is said in the Puranas that the trees on its banks also attain emancipation after they decay. The Vishalyakarani is the second river; by bathing in it one becomes purified instantly. All the Devas, the Kinnaras, the Gandharvas, the mighty serpents, the Rakshasas, the Yakshas and the ascetics, reside on the Mount Amarakantaka. The Rishis, going there, have sanctified that river. This river is also the dispeller of all sins. One who passes a night therein celibacy and observes a fast after bathing in it, liberates his seven generations. In ancient times, both the Kapila and the Vishalya were laid out by the God to fulfil their missions. The people bathing there derive the benefit of Ashvamedha sacrifice. Only he who dies there is liberated from all his sins and attains Rudraloka.

## \|\| 186.51-58 \|\|

*narmadāyāstu rājendra purāṇe yanmayā śrutam \|*  
*yatra yatra naraḥ snātvā cāśvamedhaphalaṃ labhet \|\| 51 \|\|*

*ye vasantyuttare kūle rudra loke vasanti te \|*  
*sarasvatyāṃ ca gaṅgāyāṃ narmadāyāṃ yudhiṣṭhira \|\| 52 \|\|*

*samaṃ snānaṃ ca dānaṃ ca yathā me śaṃkaro'bravīt \|*  
*parityajati yaḥ prāṇānparvate'marakaṇṭake \|\| 53 \|\|*

*varṣakoṭiśataṃ sāgraṃ rudra loke mahīyate \|*  
*narmadāyā jalaṃ puṇyaṃ phenormibhiralaṃkṛtam \|\| 54 \|\|*

*pavitraṃ śirasā vandyaṃ sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate \|*  
*narmadā ca sadā puṇyā brahmahatyāpahāriṇī \|\| 55 \|\|*

*ahorātropavāsena mucyate brahmahatyayā \|*  
*evaṃ ramyā ca puṇyā narmadā pāṇḍunandana \|\| 56 \|\|*

*trayāṇāmapi lokānāṃ puṇyā hyeṣā mahānadī \|*  
*vaṭeśvare mahāpuṇye gaṅgādvāre tapovane \|\| 57 \|\|*

*eteṣu sarvasthāneṣu dvijāḥ syuḥ saṃśitavratāḥ \|*  
*śrutaṃ daśaguṇaṃ puṇyaṃ narmadodadhisaṃgame \|\| 58 \|\|*

51-58. In fact, the devotee bathing in any tirtha situated on the hanks of the Narmada gets the benefit of Ashvamedha sacrifice. Those residing on the northern bank of this river attain Rudraloka. Shankara has said that by bathing in and giving charities at the Sarasvati, the Ganges and the Narmada, one begets equal benefits. The resident of Amarakantaka remains in Rudraloka for a 100 crores of years. The waters of the Narmada adorned with froth and ripples tire worthy of being saluted. The sacred waters dispel all the sins. The holy Narmada:, dispels all the sins, including those of killing Brahmanas, and bestows sublime lustre. This great river is held sacred in all the three worlds. The people residing at Vateshvara, Gangadvara, and Tapovana, are said to be great ascetics. By bathing in the Narmada and at its confluence with the sea, one gets tenfold merits.

## Chapter 187

## \|\| 187.1-4 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca*  
*narmadā tu nadī śreṣṭhā puṇyā puṇyatamā hitā \|*  
*munibhistu mahābhāgairvibhaktā mokṣakāṅkṣibhiḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*yajñopavītamātrāṇi pravibhaktāni pāṇḍava \|*  
*teṣu snātvā tu rājendra sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate \|\| 2 \|\|*

*śaleśvaraṃ paraṃ tīrthaṃ triṣu lokeṣu viśrutam \|*  
*tasyotpattiṃ kathayataḥ śṛṇu tvaṃ pāṇḍunandana \|\| 3 \|\|*

*purā suragaṇāḥ sarve sendrā ścaiva marudgaṇāḥ \|*  
*stuvanti te mahātmānaṃ devadevaṃ maheśvaram \|*  
*stuvantaste tu saṃprāptā yatra devo maheśvaraḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

1-4. Markandeya said: — The Narmada is most sacred and renowned and the sages desirous of emancipation have made numberless divisions, each of the measure of a Brahman's sacred thread. By bathing in them one is liberated from all sins. The sacred Maheshvara is renowned in the three worlds. In the days gone by the sages, the Maruts, and Indra, etc., shivering with fear spoke to Shiva “Protect us.”

## \|\| 187.5-6 \|\|

*vijñāpayanti deveśaṃ sendrā ścaiva marudgaṇāḥ \|*  
*bhayodvignā virūpākṣaṃ paritrāyasva naḥ prabho \|\| 5 \|\|*

*bhagavānuvāca*  
*svāgataṃ tu suraśreṣṭhāḥ kimarthamiha cā’gatāḥ \|*  
*kiṃ duḥkhaṃ ko nu saṃtāpaḥ kuto vā bhayamāgatam \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. The Lord said: “Devas! what is the fear in your mind which has brought you here? whom do you fear? what are your troubles? Tell me all about yourselves.”

## \|\| 187.7-10 \|\|

*kathayadhvaṃ mahābhāgā evamicchāmi veditum \|*  
*evamuktāstu rudre ṇākathayansaṃśitavratāḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*ativīryo mahāghoro dānavo baladarpitaḥ \|*  
*bāṇo nāmeti vikhyāto yasya vai tripuraṃ puram \|\| 8 \|\|*

*gagane satataṃ divyaṃ bhramate tasya tejasā \|*  
*tato bhītā virūpākṣa tvāmeva śaraṇaṃ gatāḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*trāyasva mahato duḥkhāttvaṃ hi naḥ paramā gatiḥ \|*  
*evaṃ prasādaṃ deveśa sarveṣāṃ kartumarhasi \|\| 10 \|\|*

7-10. Rishis said: — “O Mahadeva! the most illustrious and valiant demon Vanasura Is the owner of Tripura which moves about in the firmament Ye have come to seek your protection, being afraid of him. You are our salvation; pray, therefore, rescue us from the oppressions of that demon. Deva! be pleased to do what may be good to the Devas, the Gandharvas and the Rishis, etc.

## \|\| 187.11 \|\|

*yena devāḥ sagandharvāḥ sukhamedhanti śaṃkara \|*  
*parāṃ nirvṛtimāyānti tatprabho kartumarhasi \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Shiva said: — “Do not be anxious. I shall do everything. You will attain peace ere long.”

## \|\| 187.12 \|\|

*bhagavānuvāca*  
*etatsarvaṃ kariṣyāmi mā viṣādaṃ gamiṣyatha \|*  
*acireṇaiva kālena kuryāṃ yuṣmatsukhāvaham \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. After thus consoling them, the Lord went to the banks of the Narmada and began to devise plans for the destruction of that demon.

## \|\| 187.13-14 \|\|

*āśvāsya sa tu tānsarvānnarmadātaṭamāśritaḥ \|*  
*cintayāmāsa deveśastadvadhaṃ prati mānada \|\| 13 \|\|*

*atha kena prakāreṇa hantavyaṃ tripuraṃ mayā \|*  
*evaṃ saṃcintya bhagavānnāradaṃ cāsmarattadā \|*  
*smaraṇādeva saṃprāpto nāradaḥ samupasthitaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

13-14. He said to himself “How shall I kill the demon?” He then thought of the sage Narada who appeared then and there; and said “Mahadeva! what are your behests? Why have you summoned me? I shall carry out your commands.”

## \|\| 187.15-17 \|\|

*nārada uvāca*  
*ājñāpaya mahādeva kimarthaṃ ca smṛto hyaham \|*  
*kiṃ kāryaṃ tu mayā deva kartavyaṃ kathayasva me \|\| 15 \|\|*

*śrībhagavānuvāca*  
*gaccha nārada tatraiva yatraitattripuraṃ mahat \|*  
*bāṇasya dānavendra sya śīghraṃ gatvā ca tatkuru \|\| 16 \|\|*

*tā bhartṛdevatāstatra striyaścāpsarasāṃ samāḥ \|*  
*tāsāṃ vai tejasā vipra bhramate tripuraṃ divi \|\| 17 \|\|*

15-17. Shiva said: — “Narada! virtuous women reside within the Tripura of Vanasura and by their virtue the Tripura moves about in the space. You "should, therefore, go and delude those ladies in Tripura.”

## \|\| 187.18-19 \|\|

*tatra gatvā tu viprendra matimanyāṃ pracodaya \|*  
*devasya vacanaṃ śrutvā munistvaritavikramaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*strīṇāṃ hṛdayanāśāya praviṣṭastatpuraṃ prati \|*  
*śobhate yatpuraṃ divyaṃ nānāratnopaśobhitam \|\| 19 \|\|*

18-19. Hearing those words of the Lord, the sage went and did what he was directed to fulfil. That Tripura was decorated with various kinds of precious stones, was 100 yojanas broad and 200 yojanas in length. The sage saw Vanasura In such a magnificent place.

## \|\| 187.20-23 \|\|

*śatayojanavistīrṇaṃ tato dviguṇamāyatam \|*  
*tato'paśyaddhi tatraiva bāṇaṃ tu baladarpitam \|\| 20 \|\|*

*maṇikuṇḍalakeyūramukuṭena virājitam \|*  
*hemahāraśatai ratnaiścandra kāntavibhūṣitam \|\| 21 \|\|*

*raśanā tasya ratnāḍhyā bāhū kanakamaṇḍitau \|*  
*candra kāntamahāvajramaṇividrumabhūṣite \|\| 22 \|\|*

*dvādaśārkadyutinibhe niviṣṭaṃ paramāsane \|*  
*utthito nāradaṃ dṛṣṭvā dānavendro mahābalaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

20-23 The demon king who was seated on a majestic throne with the brilliance of the twelve suns, wearing earrings, coronet, garlands and armlets of gold studded with precious stones; stood up to receive the sage Narada p and said “Deva Rishi! you have come here of your own accord. I offer you an oblation and water for washing your feet.” He then saluted the sage and said “Let me know your commands and I shall carry them out You have come here after a long time. Pray take your seat”

## \|\| 187.24-25 \|\|

*bāṇa uvāca*  
*devarṣe tvaṃ svayaṃ prāpto hyarghyaṃ pādyaṃ nivedaye \|*  
*so'bhivādya yathānyāyaṃ kriyatāṃ kiṃ dvijottama \|\| 24 \|\|*

*cirāttvamāgato vipra āsyatāṃ munipuṃgava \|*  
*evaṃ saṃbhāṣayitvā tu nāradamṛṣisattamam \|*  
*tasya bhāryā mahādevī hyanaupamyā tu nāmataḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

24-25. Afterwards Anaupamya queen said: — “Narada! what dharma pleases the Devas? which ordinance is most gratifying to them?

## \|\| 187.26-37 \|\|

*anaupamyovāca*  
*bhagavanmānuṣe loke kena tuṣyati keśavaḥ \|*  
*vratena niyamenātha dānena tapasā'pi vā \|\| 26 \|\|*

*nārada uvāca*  
*tiladhenuṃ ca yo dadyādbrāhmaṇe vedapārage \|*  
*sasāgaravanadvīpā dattā bhavati medinī \|\| 27 \|\|*

*sūryakoṭipratīkāśairvimānaiḥ sārvakāmikaiḥ \|*  
*modate cākṣayaṃ kālaṃ yāvaccandrā rkatārakam \|\| 28 \|\|*

*āmrāmalakapitthāni badarāṇi tathaiva ca \|*  
*kadambacampakāśokapuṃnāgavividhadrumān \|\| 29 \|\|*

*aśvatthapippalaṃ caiva kadalīvaṭadāḍimān \|*  
*picumandaṃ madhūkaṃ ca upoṣya strī dadāti yā \|\| 30 \|\|*

*stanau kapitthasadṛśāvūrū ca kadalīsamau \|*  
*aśvatthe vandanīyā ca picumande sugandhinī \|\| 31 \|\|*

*campake campakāmā syādaśoke śokavarjitā \|*  
*madhūke madhuraṃ vakti vaṭe ca mṛdugātrikā \|\| 32 \|\|*

*badarī sarvadā strīṇāṃ mahāsaubhāgyadāyinī \|*  
*kukkuṭī karkaṭī caiva dra vyaṣaṣṭhī na śasyate \|\| 33 \|\|*

*kadambamiśrakanakamañjarīpūjanaṃ tathā \|*  
*anagnipakvamannaṃ ca pakvānnānāmabhakṣaṇam \|\| 34 \|\|*

*phalānāṃ ca parityāgaḥ saṃdhyāmaunaṃ tathaiva ca \|*  
*prathamaṃ kṣetrapālasya pūjā kāryā prayatnataḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

*tasyā bhavati vai bhartā mukhaprekṣī sadā'naghe \|*  
*aṣṭamī ca caturthī ca pañcamī dvādaśī tathā \|\| 36 \|\|*

*saṃkrāntirviṣuvaccaiva dinacchidra mukhaṃ tathā \|*  
*etāṃstu divasāndivyānupavasanti yāḥ striyaḥ \|*  
*tāsāṃ tu dharmayuktānāṃ svargavāso na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

26-37. Narada said: — One who gives away a cow and sesamum to a Brahmana well-versed in the Vedas gets the benefit of having given away lands beyond the seas. He enjoys himself in a Vimana shining like crores of suns for a considerable period- The lady who gives away after observing a fast the following trees: — Wood-apple, rose-apple, Kadamba, Champaka, Ashoka, Ashwattha, plantain, banyan, pomegranate, Neem and Mahua; her breasts take the form of the wood-apple, her thighs become like the trunk of the plantain tree. She becomes adorable like the sacred Ashwattha tree and sweet smelling like the Neem, illustrious like the Champaka, griefless like Ashoka, sweet like the Mahua, soft like the leaves of the banyan. She always gets prosperity. The giving of pumpkins and creepers is not considered high, and the husband of a lady who worships the Devas with Kadamba blossoms discarding the food cooked and uncooked as well as fruits, observing the vow of silence in the evening and worshipping Kshetrapala first; remains in happiness. The ladies who keep a fast on Ashtami, Chaturthi, Panchami, Dwadashi, Sankranti; undoubtedly go to heaven. They are liberated from the ills of the iron age and Dharmaraja does not admit such ladies in his town.

## \|\| 187.38-42 \|\|

*kalikāluṣyanirmuktāḥ sarvapāpavivarjitāḥ \|*  
*upavāsaratāṃ nārīṃ nopasarpati tāṃ yamaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

*anaupamyovāca*  
*asminkṛtena puṇyena purājanmakṛtena vā \|*  
*bhavadāgamanaṃ jātaṃ kiṃcitpṛcchāmyahaṃ vratam \|\| 39 \|\|*

*asti vindhyāvalirnāma balipatnī yaśasvinī \|*  
*śvaśrūrmamāpi viprendra na tuṣyati kadācana \|\| 40 \|\|*

*śvaśuro'pi sarvakālaṃ dṛṣṭvā cāpi na paśyati \|*  
*asti kumbhīnasī nāma nanāndā pāpakāriṇī \|\| 41 \|\|*

*dṛṣṭvā caivāṅgulībhaṅgaṃ sadākālaṃ karoti mām \|*  
*divyena tu pathā yāti mama saukhyaṃ kathaṃ vada \|\| 42 \|\|*

38-42. Anaupamya said “It is owing to the virtues performed in the past that you have, graced our home with your august presence and I venture to enquire about other ordinances from you. Vindhyabali the renowned queen of the king Bali is my mother-in-law. She is never pleased with me, and same is the case with my father-in-law. The vicious Kumbhivasi is my lord’s sister who always treats me with contempt. How can I be happy under such circumstances? Pray let me know by what ordinance they would turn friendly to me for which I shall remain very grateful to you.”

## \|\| 187.43-45 \|\|

*ūṣare na prarohanti bījāṅkurāḥ kathaṃcana \|*  
*yena vratena cīrṇena bhavanti vaśagā mama \|*  
*tadvrataṃ brūhi viprendra dāsabhāvaṃ vrajāmi te \|\| 43 \|\|*

*nārada uvāca*  
*yadetatte mayā pūrvaṃ vratamuktaṃ śubhānane \|*  
*anena pārvatī devī cīrṇena varavarṇini \|\| 44 \|\|*

*śaṃkarasya śarīrasthā viṣṇorlakṣmīstathaiva ca \|*  
*sāvitrī brahmaṇaścaiva vasiṣṭhasyāpyarundhatī \|\| 45 \|\|*

43-45. Narada said: — “By observing the ordinance just explained to you, Parvati became so dear to Shiva, and similarly Lakshmi has become so dear to Vishnu, and Sarasvati has become endeared to Brahma and Arundhati to Vasishtha. Your lord will also become beholden to you by keeping up the very same ordinance and your father-in-law and mother-in-law will also be silenced.”

## \|\| 187.46-48 \|\|

*etenopoṣiteneha bhartā sthāsyati te vaśe \|*  
*śvaśrūśvaśurayoścaiva mukhabandho bhaviṣyati \|\| 46 \|\|*

*evaṃ śrutvā tu suśroṇi yatheṣṭaṃ kartumarhasi \|*  
*nāradasya vacaḥ śrutvā rājñī vacanamabravīt \|\| 47 \|\|*

*prasādaṃ kuru viprendra dānaṃ grāhyaṃ yathepsitam \|*  
*suvarṇamaṇiratnāni vastrāṇyābharaṇāni ca \|\| 48 \|\|*

46-48. Hearing such words of Narada, that queen determined to observe that ordinance and said: — “Be pleased upon me, O sage! I shall offer you presents of gold, jewels, garments, which be pleased to accept. Let Lords Vishnu and Shiva be pleased upon me.”

## \|\| 187.49 \|\|

*tava dāsyāmyahaṃ vipra yaccānyadapi durlabham \|*  
*pragṛhāṇa dvijaśreṣṭha prīyetāṃ hariśaṃkarau \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Narada said: — “Lady! you should bestow these presents on some Brahmana who may be poor and in need of support. I am blessed with everything and you ought to show only your devotion to me.”

## \|\| 187.50-51 \|\|

*nārada uvāca*  
*anyasmai dīyatāṃ bhadre kṣīṇavṛttistu yo dvijaḥ \|*  
*ahaṃ tu sarvasaṃpanno madbhaktiḥ kriyatāmiti \|\| 50 \|\|*

*evaṃ tāsāṃ mano hṛtvā sarvāsāṃ tu pativratāt \|*  
*jagāma bharataśreṣṭha svakīyaṃ sthānakaṃ punaḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

50-51. In such a way Narada after having softened the minds of all the ladies in Tripura returned to his abode and a breach was thus created in Tripura.

## Chapter 188

## \|\| 188.1-2 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca*  
*yanmāṃ pṛcchasi kaunteya tanme kathayataḥ śṛṇu \|*  
*etasminnantare rudro narmadātaṭamāsthitaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*nāmnā māheśvaraṃ sthānaṃ triṣu lokeṣu viśrutam \|*  
*tasminsthāne mahādevo'cintayattripurakṣayam \|\| 2 \|\|*

1-2. Markandeya said: — Hear from me, Yudhisthira I what you have asked me to explain. The spot on the banks of the Narmada where the Lord is enshrined is renowned as Maheshvara in all the three worlds and at the very same place He devised His plans of annihilating 'Tripura.

## \|\| 188.3-5 \|\|

*gāṇḍīvaṃ mandaraṃ kṛtvā guṇaṃ kṛtvā ca vāsukim \|*  
*sthānaṃ kṛtvā tu vaiśākhaṃ viṣṇuṃ kṛtvā śarottamam \|\| 3 \|\|*

*śalye cāgniṃ pratiṣṭhāpya mukhe vāyuṃ samarpayan \|*  
*hayāṃśca caturo vedānsarvadevamayaṃ ratham \|\| 4 \|\|*

*abhīṣavo'śvinau devāvakṣo vajradharaḥ svayam \|*  
*sa tasyā'jñāṃ samādāya toraṇe dhanadaḥ sthitaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

3-5. The Lord seated there lifted up the mount Mandarachala to serve Is Gandiva bow. He then put the snake Vasuki in place of the bowstring and Svamikartika in place of the quiver. Vishnu in place of the ad the fire at the tip of it (the arrow). Afterwards the wind was o propel the arrow. The four Vedas took the place of the horses of the chariot. Ashvinikumara was employed in place of the reins and Indra in place of the axle. Kuvera formed the banner.

## \|\| 188.6-14 \|\|

*yamastu dakṣiṇe haste vāme kālastu dāruṇaḥ \|*  
*cakre tvamarakoṭyastu gandharvā lokaviśrutāḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*prajāpatiratha śreṣṭho brahmā caiva tu sārathiḥ \|*  
*evaṃ kṛtvā tu deveśaḥ sarvadevamayaṃ ratham \|\| 7 \|\|*

*so'tiṣṭhatsthāṇubhūtastu sahasraparivatsarān \|*  
*yadā trīṇi sametāni antarikṣe sthitāni vai \|\| 8 \|\|*

*triparvaṇā triśalyena tadā tāni vyabhedayat \|*  
*śaraḥ pracoditastena rudre ṇa tripuraṃ prati \|\| 9 \|\|*

*bhraṣṭatejāḥ striyo jātā balaṃ tāsāṃ vyaśīryata \|*  
*utpātāśca pure tasminprādurbhūtāḥ sahasraśaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*tripurasya vināśāya kālarūpā bhavaṃstadā \|*  
*aṭṭahāsaṃ pramuñcanti hayā kāṣṭhamayāstadā \|\| 11 \|\|*

*nimeṣonmeṣaṇaṃ caiva kurvanti citrarūpiṇaḥ \|*  
*svapne paśyanti cā’tmānaṃ raktāmbaravibhūṣitam \|\| 12 \|\|*

*svapne tu sarve paśyanti viparītāni yāni tu \|*  
*etānpaśyanti utpātāṃstatra sthāne tu ye janāḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*teṣāṃ balaṃ ca buddhiśca harakopena nāśite \|*  
*tataḥ sāṃvartako vāyuryugāntapratimo mahān \|\| 14 \|\|*

6-14. Yama put himself to the right-hand of the Lord and Kala to the left. The groups of the Devas and the Gandharvas formed the wheels of the chariot. Brahma was the charioteer. In that way, Shiva waited for thousands of years after making such preparations. When the three Puras (cities) fell in one line the Lord let out His arrow on Tripura when the inmates of Tripura became helpless and many kinds of destructive omens occurred there. The wooden horses began to neigh and painted ones to wink. All the demons saw themselves dressed in red in course of their dream. One who dreams of things hostile to him becomes void of power and intellect by the glory of the Lord. Then the wind Sambartaka that blows at the close of a cycle commenced.

## \|\| 188.15-24 \|\|

*samīrito'nalastena uttamāṅgena dhāvati \|*  
*jvalanti pādapāstatra patanti śikharāṇi ca \|\| 15 \|\|*

*sarvato vyākulībhūtaṃ hāhākāramacetanam \|*  
*bhagnodyānāni sarvāṇi kṣipraṃ tatpratyabhajyata \|\| 16 \|\|*

*tenaiva pīḍitaṃ sarvaṃ jvalitaṃ triśikhaiḥ śaraiḥ \|*  
*drumāścā’rāmakhaṇḍāni gṛhāṇi vividhāni ca \|\| 17 \|\|*

*daśadikṣu pravṛtto'yaṃ samṛddho havyavāhanaḥ \|*  
*manaḥśilāpuñjanibho diśo daśa vibhāgaśaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*śikhāśatairanekaistu prajajvāla hutāśanaḥ \|*  
*sarvaṃ kiṃśukavarṇābhaṃ jvalitaṃ dṛśyate puram \|\| 19 \|\|*

*gṛhādgṛhāntaraṃ naiva gantuṃ dhūmena śakyate \|*  
*harakopānalairdagdhaṃ krandamānaṃ suduḥkhitam \|\| 20 \|\|*

*pradīptaṃ sarvato dikṣu dahyate tripuraṃ puram \|*  
*prāsādaśikharāgrāṇi vyaśīryanta sahasraśaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*nānāmaṇivicitrāṇi vimānānyapyanekadhā \|*  
*gṛhāṇi caiva ramyāṇi dahyante dīptavahninā \|\| 22 \|\|*

*dhāvanti drumakhaṇḍeṣu valabhīṣu tathā janāḥ \|*  
*devāgāreṣu sarveṣu prajvalantaḥ pradhāvitāḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

*krandanti cānalapluṣṭā rudanti vividhaiḥ svaraiḥ \|*  
*girikūṭanibhāstatra dṛśyante'ṅgārarāśayaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

15-24. It produced fire on account of which the trees of Tripura began to crumble down. There was chaos everywhere. All the gardens were burnt down in an instant. The huge storm devastated the houses and trees that were on fire which furiously pervaded in all the directions. The dreadful tongues of fire gave a gory appearance to the whole of Tripura. Owing to the dense folds of smoke the demons could not go about from one house to another. The Tripura was thus agitated by the fury of the Lord. Thousands of palaces fell down in all directions and the inmates rushed towards the temples and thousands of demons were -reduced to ashes groaning and moaning piteously. Various kinds of Vimanas and picturesque places were consumed by the fearful fire.

## \|\| 188.25-28 \|\|

*gajāśca girikūṭābhā dahyamānā yatastataḥ \|*  
*stuvanti devadeveśaṃ paritrāyasva naḥ prabho \|\| 25 \|\|*

*anyonyaṃ ca pariṣvajya hutāśanapradīpitāḥ \|*  
*snehātpradahyamānāśca tathaiva vilayaṃ gatāḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*dahyante dānavāstatra śataśo'tha sahasraśaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

*haṃsakāraṇḍavākīrṇā nalinyaḥ sahapaṅkajāḥ \|*  
*dṛśyante'naladagdhāni purodyānāni dīrghikāḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

25-28. The pleasure gardens smiling with lotus beds were also burnt down along with the swans and cranes. The lofty palace tops looking like the mountain peaks, adorned with gems and lotuses, fell down on being burnt up, like a heap of clouds. The fire of the Lord’s fury burnt down quite unsparingly several children, cows, birds, horses, women, and many people sleeping as well as awake.

## \|\| 188.29-40 \|\|

*amlānapaṅkajacchannā vistīrṇā yojanāyatāḥ \|*  
*girikūṭanibhāstatra prāsādā ratnabhūṣitāḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*patantyanalanirdagdhā nistoyā jaladā iva \|*  
*varastrībālavṛddheṣu goṣu pakṣiṣu vājiṣu \|\| 30 \|\|*

*nirdayo vyadahadvahnirharakrodhena preritaḥ \|*  
*sahasraśaḥ prabuddhāśca suptāśca bahavo janāḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

*putramāliṅgya te gāḍhaṃ dahyante tripurāgninā \|*  
*nidāgho'bhūnmahāvahnerantakālo yathā tathā \|\| 32 \|\|*

*kecidguptāḥ pradagdhāstu bhāryotsaṅgagatāstathā \|*  
*pitrā mātrā ca suśliṣṭā dagdhāste tripurāgninā \|*  
*atha tasminpure dīpte striyaścāpsarasopamāḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

*agnijvālāhatāstatra hyapatandharaṇītale \|*  
*kācicchyāmā viśālākṣī muktāvalivibhūṣitā \|\| 34 \|\|*

*dhūmenā’kulitā sā tu patitā dharaṇītale \|*  
*kācitkanakavarṇābhā indra nīlavibhūṣitā \|\| 35 \|\|*

*bhartāraṃ patitaṃ dṛṣṭvā patitā tasya copari \|*  
*kācidādityasaṃkāśā prasuptā ca gṛhe sthitā \|\| 36 \|\|*

*agnijvālāhatā sā tu patitā gatacetanā \|*  
*utthito dānavastatra khaḍgahasto mahābalaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

*vaiśvānarahataḥ so'pi patito dharaṇītale \|*  
*meghavarṇā'parā nārī hārakeyūrabhūṣitā \|\| 38 \|\|*

*śvetavastraparīdhānā bālaṃ stanyaṃ nyadhāpayat \|*  
*dahyantaṃ bālakaṃ dṛṣṭvā rudatī meghaśabdavat \|\| 39 \|\|*

*evaṃ sa tu dahannagnirharakrodhena preritaḥ \|*  
*kāciccandra prabhā saumyā vajravaiḍūryabhūṣitā \|\| 40 \|\|*

29-40. The nymph like beauties of Tripura fell down burnt with their young ones hugged to their breasts. Some ladies wearing garlands of pearl and gold fell down on the ground consumed by flames and suffocated by smoke. Some beauties seeing their Lord lying on the ground jumped down from the upper storey of their mansion and were instantly eaten up by the flames. The belaboured demons lying on the ground got up with their sword but were soon consumed by the raging fire. Some ladies of the cloudy hue wearing garlands and armlets, some fair-complexioned beauties giving milk to their dear little ones were also consumed by fire. Some ladies seeing their children eaten up by the fire sent forth shrilling wails. Some ladies wearing diamond and emerald necklaces and shining like the moon with their children in their lap, fell down on the ground after being charred. Some moon-faced beauties waking up from their sleep found their mansion on fire and began to lament on realizing their children being burnt. Some ladies adorned with golden ornaments fell down on the ground holding their consumed children in their arms. Some fainted away by the fumes of smoke and -fell down grasping the hand of their maids.

## \|\| 188.41-48 \|\|

*sutamāliṅgya vepantī dagdhā patati bhūtale \|*  
*kācitkundenduvarṇābhā krīḍantī sva gṛhe sthitā \|\| 41 \|\|*

*gṛhe prajvalite sā tu pratibuddhā śikhārditā \|*  
*paśyantī jvalitaṃ sarvaṃ hā suto me kathaṃ gataḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

*sutaṃ saṃdagdhamāliṅgya patitā dharaṇītale \|*  
*ādityodayavarṇābhā lakṣmīvadanaśobhanā \|\| 43 \|\|*

*tvaritā dahyamānā sā patitā dharaṇītale \|*  
*kācitsuvarṇavarṇābhā nīlaratnairvibhūṣitā \|\| 44 \|\|*

*dhūmenā’kulitā sā tu prasuptā dharaṇītale \|*  
*anyā gṛhītahastā tu sakhi dahyati bālikā \|\| 45 \|\|*

*anekadiśyaratnāḍhyā dṛṣṭvā dahanamohitā \|*  
*śirasi hyañjaliṃ kṛtvā vijñāpayati pāvakam \|\| 46 \|\|*

*bhagavanyadi vairaṃ te puruṣeṣvapakāriṣu \|*  
*striyaḥ kimaparādhyanti gṛhapañjarakokilāḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

*pāpa nirdaya nirlajжa kaste kopaḥ striyaḥ prati \|*  
*na dākṣiṇyaṃ na te lajжā na satyaṃ śauryavarjita \|\| 48 \|\|*

41-48. Some overcome by the fury of the fire with their hands folded and uplifted began to pray as follows “Agni! if thou art angry with male population hostile to thee; what is the fault of the women confined in the houses like so many domesticated Kokilas pent up in cages? O sinner, merciless! why art thou, enraged with the women. Thou art devoid of right understanding, shame and heroic virtues and truth. O sinner! hast thou not heard commonly said in the world that the women of the enemy should not be killed?

To consume is thy attribute but thou hast no mercy and right understanding- Even a Mlechchha is moved to compassion to see a burning woman. This attribute of consumption is also useless in thee. It is simply thy vice, for what is the good of thy killing \_ women? O sinner, wicked, merciless, miserable wretch Agni! thou art indeed most unfortunate. Thou burnest us by force.”

## \|\| 188.49-50 \|\|

*anena hyupasargeṇa tūpālambhaṃ śikhinyadāt \|*  
*kiṃ tvayā na śrutaṃ loke hyavadhyāḥ śatruyoṣitaḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

*kiṃ tu tubhyaṃ guṇā hyete dahanotsādanaṃ prati \|*  
*na kāruṇyaṃ bhayaṃ vā'pi dākṣiṇyaṃ na striyaḥ prati \|\| 50 \|\|*

49-50. She was rendered senseless after thus wailing and thinking of her children for a long time. The fire like an old foe of the precious lives also dried up the wells and the tanks.

## \|\| 188.51-53 \|\|

*dayāṃ kurvanti mlecchāpi dahantīṃ vīkṣya yoṣitam \|*  
*mlecchānāmapi kaṣṭo'si durnivāro hyacetanaḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

*ete caiva guṇāstubhyaṃ dahanotsādanaṃ prati \|*  
*āsāmapi durācāra strīṇāṃ kiṃ te nipātane \|\| 52 \|\|*

*duṣṭa nirghṛṇa nirlajжa hutāśinmandabhāgyaka \|*  
*nirāśatvaṃ durāvāsa balāddahasi nirdaya \|\| 53 \|\|*

51-53. “Mlechchha! what will be thy faith after burning us? Hearing such speech of the ladies the Agni said “I am not consuming you of my own will. I have been born to cause destruction. I have no mercy. I make my way everywhere freely through the glory of Shiva.” Afterwards "Vanasura also saw Tripura burning.

## \|\| 188.54-55 \|\|

*evaṃ vilapamānāstā jalpantyaśca bahūnyapi \|*  
*anyāḥ krośanti saṃkruddhā bālaśokena mohitāḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

*dahate nirdayo vahniḥ saṃkruddhaḥ pūrvaśatruvat \|*  
*puṣkariṇyāṃ jalaṃ dagdhaṃ kūpeṣvapi tathaiva ca \|\| 55 \|\|*

54-55. He said from his throne “The wicked Devas of little valour have worked out my ruin which is decidedly due to the glory of Shiva. The Lord is consuming me without any examination of the reasons for his action. No one can kill me without the aid of Shiva.”

## \|\| 188.56-66 \|\|

*asmānsaṃdahya mleccha tvaṃ kāṃ gatiṃ prāpayiṣyasi \|*  
*evaṃ pralapitaṃ tāsāṃ śrutvā devo vibhāvasuḥ \|*  
*mūrtimānsahasotthāya vahnirvacanamabravīt \|\| 56 \|\|*

*agniruvāca*  
*svavaśo naiva yuṣmākaṃ vināśaṃ tu karomyaham \|*  
*ahamādeśa kartā vai nāhaṃ kartā'smyanugraham \|\| 57 \|\|*

*rudra krodhasamāviṣṭo vicarāmi yathecchayā \|*  
*tato bāṇo mahātejāstripuraṃ vīkṣya dīpitam \|\| 58 \|\|*

*siṃhāsanasthaḥ provāca hyahaṃ devairvināśitaḥ \|*  
*alpasattvairdurācārairīśvarasya niveditam \|\| 59 \|\|*

*aparīkṣya tvahaṃ dagdhaḥ śaṃkareṇa mahātmanā \|*  
*nānyaḥ śaktastu māṃ hantuṃ varjayitvā trilocanam \|\| 60 \|\|*

*utthitaḥ śirasā kṛtvā liṅgaṃ tribhuvaneśvaram \|*  
*nirgataḥ sa puradvārātparityajya suhṛtsutān \|\| 61 \|\|*

*ratnāni yānyanarghāṇi striyo nānāvidhāstathā \|*  
*gṛhītvā śirasā liṅgaṃ gacchangaganamaṇḍalam \|\| 62 \|\|*

*stuvaṃśca devadeveśaṃ trilokādhipatiṃ śivam \|*  
*tyaktā purī mayā deva yadi vadhyo'smi śaṃkara \|\| 63 \|\|*

*tvatprasādānmahādeva mā me liṅgaṃ vinaśyatu \|*  
*arcitaṃ hi mayā deva bhaktyā paramayā sadā \|\| 64 \|\|*

*tvatkopādyadi vadhyo'haṃ tadidaṃ mā vinaśyatu \|*  
*ślāghyametanmahādeva tvatkopāddahanaṃ mama \|\| 65 \|\|*

*pratijanma mahādeva tvatpādanirato hyaham \|*  
*toṭakacchandasā deva staumi tvāṃ parameśvara \|\| 66 \|\|*

56-66. Saying so the demon king abandoned his sons, friends, &c., and set out of the town with the idol of Shiva placed on his head putting many women and various kinds of jewels in front of the idol. He stood up on the aerial track and after making his salutations to the Lord of the three worlds said “ Deva! I have given up this town and you should not kill me. Deva if you, however, feel disposed to kill me, do not consume this idol of my worship which I have always adored with great devotion. Deva! I have been a slave of Thy feet in every past life and now I offer my prayer to Thee, composed in these Totaka stanzas. O Shiva, Shankara, 8arba, Hara, Bhima, Maheshvara, the Destroyer of Kama, the Annihilator of Tripura, the wielder of the Trident! I salute Thee. O Pramadapriya, the one saluted by the demons as well as by the Devas, having a most illustrious face wider than that of a horse, a monkey and a lion; I salute Thee. The Devas and the demons cause me pain. Deva! I am always engaged in my devotion to Thee. I have not the wealth in shape of sons, wife, horses, &c. I only depend on my attachment to Thee. I am greatly oppressed and feel as if I were in hell. My inborn vice does not show signs of decline and my understanding leaves off virtues. The vices can only be abandoned by Thy grace.”

## \|\| 188.67 \|\|

*śiva śaṃkara śarva harāya namo bhava bhīma maheśvara sarva namaḥ \|*  
*kusumāyudhadehavināśakara tripurāntaka andhakaśūladhara \|\| 67 \|\|*

67 One who would recite this prayer will be granted some handsome boon like the one granted to Vanasura by the Lord.

## \|\| 188.68 \|\|

*pramadāpriya kānta virakta namaḥ sasurāsurasiddhagaṇairnamita \|*  
*hayavānarasiṃhagajendra mukhairatihrasvasudīrghaviśālamukhaiḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. Mahadeva, on hearing the above beautiful prayer said joyfully.

## \|\| 188.69-71 \|\|

*upalabdhumaśakyatarairasuraiḥ prathito'smi ca bāhuśatairbahubhiḥ \|*  
*praṇato'smi bhavaṃ bhavabhaktirataścalacandra kalāṅkura deva namaḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

*na ca putrakalatrahayādi dhanaṃ mama tu tvadanusmaraṇaṃ śaraṇam \|*  
*vyathito'smi śarīraśatairbahubhirgamitā ca mahānarakasya gatiḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

*na nivartati janma na pāpamatiḥ śucikarma nibaddhamapi tyajati \|*  
*anukampati vibhramati trasati mama caiva kukarma nivārayati \|\| 71 \|\|*

69-71. “Son! Be not afraid. Get into the golden Pura and carry your family and relations with you. Vanasura! you will not be killed by the Devas from now till the time of your doom.” The Lord thus again granted such a boon to that demon; and told him to roam about in the world fearlessly and also quenched the raging fire.

## \|\| 188.72-74 \|\|

*yaḥ paṭhettoṭakaṃ divyaṃ prayataḥ śucimānasaḥ \|*  
*bāṇasyeva yathā rudra stasyāpi varado bhavet \|\| 72 \|\|*

*imaṃ stavaṃ mahādivyaṃ śrutvā devo maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*prasannastu tadā tasya svayaṃ vacanamabravīt \|\| 73 \|\|*

*maheśvara uvāca*  
*na bhetavyaṃ tvayā vatsa sauvarṇe tiṣṭha dānava \|*  
*putrapautrasuhṛdbandhubhāryābhṛtyajanaiḥ saha \|\| 74 \|\|*

72-74. For this reason the Lord did not consume his third Pura, which is sailing about the sky by the power of Shiva. The other two Puras fell down to the ground after being reduced to the ashes, Shrishaila mount was formed on the spot where the first city fell and similarly Amarakantaka sprang up on the spot where the second Pura fell down.”

## \|\| 188.75-77 \|\|

*adyaprabhṛti bāṇa tvamavadhyastridaśairapi \|*  
*bhūyastasya varo datto devadevena pāṇḍava \|\| 75 \|\|*

*akṣayaścāvyayo loke vicarasvākutobhayaḥ \|*  
*tato nivārayāmāsa rudra ḥ! saptaśikhaṃ tadā \|\| 76 \|\|*

*tṛtīyaṃ rakṣitaṃ tasya śaṃkareṇa mahātmanā \|*  
*bhramattu gagane divyaṃ rudra tejaḥ prabhāvataḥ \|\| 77 \|\|*

75-77. “Rajendra! On the top of those Puras the groups of Rudras were enshrined. The spot where the burning Pura fell down is marked by the famous Jwaleshvara. When the tongues of fire flashed into the sky from the burning city, there was a tremendous uproar among the Devas and the demons when the Lord took down His arrow from His bow. All this happened on the Mount Amarakantaka.

## \|\| 188.78-79 \|\|

*evaṃ tu tripuraṃ dagdhaṃ śaṃkareṇa mahātmanā \|*  
*jvālāmālāpradīptaṃ tatpatitaṃ dharaṇītale \|\| 78 \|\|*

*ekaṃ nipatitaṃ tatra śrīśaile tripurāntake \|*  
*dvitīyaṃ patitaṃ tasminparvate'marakaṇṭake \|\| 79 \|\|*

78-79. Consequently, the people observing fasts, &c., are born as sole monarchs in this world after a period of 30 crores and a thousand years when they have enjoyed the pleasures of the fourteen worlds.”

## \|\| 188.80-82 \|\|

*dagdheṣu teṣu rājendra rudra koṭiḥ pratiṣṭhitā \|*  
*jvalattadapatattatra tena jvāleśvaraḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 80 \|\|*

*ūrdhvena prasthitāstasya divyajvālā divaṃ gatāḥ \|*  
*hāhākārastadā jāto devāsurakṛto mahān \|\| 81 \|\|*

*śaramastambhayadrudro māheśvarapurottame \|*  
*evaṃ vṛttaṃ tadā tasminparvate'marakaṇṭake \|\| 82 \|\|*

80-82. O King Yudhisthira! in this way the sacred place Amarakantaka is the most sanctified and therefore one who goes there on the occasion of a solar or a lunar eclipse and gets the merits ten times more than that of the Ashvamedha sacrifice. One attains heaven by worshipping Maheshvara there. The sin of killing a Brahmana is driven away by going there on the occasion of a solar eclipse. This is the glory of the sacred Mount Amarakantaka.

## \|\| 188.83 \|\|

*caturdaśākhyaṃ bhuvanaṃ sa bhuktvā pāṇḍunandana \|*  
*varṣakoṭisahasraṃ tu triṃśatkoṭyastathā'parāḥ \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. One who thinks of this Mount Amarakantaka with devotion undoubtedly gets the benefit of a hundred Chandrayana ordinances.

## \|\| 188.84 \|\|

*tato mahītalaṃ prāpya rājā bhavati dhārmikaḥ \|*  
*pṛthivīmekacchatreṇa bhuṅkte sa tu na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. Amarakantaka is renowned in all the three worlds. It is adorned by the Siddhas, the Gandharvas, &c.

## \|\| 188.85-88 \|\|

*evaṃ puṇyo mahārāja parvato'marakaṇṭakaḥ \|*  
*candra sūryoparāge tu gacchedyo'markaṇṭakam \|\| 85 \|\|*

*aśvamedhāddaśaguṇaṃ pravadanti manīṣiṇaḥ \|*  
*svargalokamavāpnoti dṛṣṭvā tatra maheśvaram \|\| 86 \|\|*

*brahmahatyā gamiṣyanti rāhugraste divākare \|*  
*tadevaṃ nikhilaṃ puṇyaṃ parvate'marakaṇṭake \|\| 87 \|\|*

*manasā'pi smaredyastaṃ giriṃ tvamarakaṇṭakam \|*  
*cāndrā yaṇaśataṃ sāgraṃ labhate nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 88 \|\|*

85-88. It abounds with various kinds of flowers, creepers, deer, Siddhas and the Lord Shiva is enshrined there in company of His noble consort Parvati It is pervaded by Brahma, Vishnu, Indra, Vidyadhara, Rishis, Kinnaras, and Yakshas. The serpent Vasuki loiters there. One who circumambulates that sacred Amarakantaka gets the benefit of the Pundarika sacrifice.

## \|\| 188.89-90 \|\|

*trayāṇāmapi lokānāṃ vikhyāto'marakaṇṭakaḥ \|*  
*eṣa puṇyo giriśreṣṭhaḥ siddhagandharvasevitaḥ \|\| 89 \|\|*

*nānādrumalatākīrṇā nānāpuṣpopaśobhitaḥ \|*  
*mṛgavyāghrasahasraistu sevyamāno mahāgiriḥ \|\| 90 \|\|*

89-90. The Lord Jwaleshvara is also adored by the Siddhas there. People dying there after bathing in the sacred waters attain heaven. King Yudhisthira, hear the benefits attained by those who die there on the occasion of an eclipse — solar or lunar.

## \|\| 188.91 \|\|

*yatra saṃnihito devo devyā saha maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*brahmā viṣṇustathā cendro vidyādharagaṇaiḥ saha \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. Such blessed one after being liberated from all actions and endowed with supreme intellect go and reside in the region of Rudra till the end of the cycle.

## \|\| 188.92-94 \|\|

*ṛṣibhiḥ kiṃnarairyakṣairnityameva niṣevitaḥ \|*  
*vāsukiḥ sahitastatra krīḍate pannagottamaiḥ \|\| 92 \|\|*

*pradakṣiṇaṃ tu yaḥ kuryātparvate'marakaṇṭake \|*  
*pauṇḍarīkasya yajñasya phalaṃ prāpnoti mānavaḥ \|\| 93 \|\|*

*tatra jvāleśvaraṃ nāma tīrthaṃ siddhaniṣevitam \|*  
*tatra snātvā divaṃ yānti ye mṛtāste'punarbhavāḥ \|\| 94 \|\|*

92-94. Crores of Rishis practise asceticism on the either side of Amareshvara. This Mount Amarakantaka is one yojana in extent all round. Those who bathe in the sacred Narmada with or without an object in view, are liberated from all their sins and go to the realm of Rudra.

## Chapter 189

## \|\| 189.2-3 \|\|

*ākhyāhi bhayavaṃstathyaṃ kāverīsaṃgamaṃ mahat \|*  
*lokānāṃ ca hitārthāya asmākaṃ ca vivṛddhaye \|\| 2 \|\|*

*sadā pāparatā ye ca narā duṣkṛtakāriṇaḥ \|*  
*mucyante sarvapāpebhyo gacchanti paramaṃ padam \|*  
*etadicchāma vijñātuṃ bhagavanvaktumarhasi \|\| 3 \|\|*

2-3. Suta said: The king Yudhisthira along with the Rishis asked Markandeya. “Bhagvana! be pleased to relate to us about the junction of the sacred Kaveri. We are desirous of hearing from you the account of the sacred Kaveri by bathing into which the vilest of sinners get emancipation.”

## \|\| 189.4-5 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca*  
*śṛṇvantvavahitāḥ sarve yudhiṣṭhirapurogamāḥ \|*  
*asti vīro mahāyakṣaḥ kuberaḥ satyavikramaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*idaṃ tīrthamanuprāpya rājā yakṣādhipo'bhavat \|*  
*siddhiṃ prāpto mahārāja tanme nigadataḥ śṛṇu \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. Markandeya said O Yudhisthira and O Rishis! hear with attention that even the illustrious Kuvera the Lord of the Yakshas got his position by oblations in the sacred Kaveri. Now hear from me how he acquired all his glory.

## \|\| 189.6-8 \|\|

*kāverī narmadā yatra saṃgamo lokaviśrutaḥ \|*  
*tatra snātvā śucirbhūtvā kuberaḥ satyavikramaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*tapo'tapyata yakṣendro divyaṃ varṣaśataṃ mahat \|*  
*tasya tuṣṭo mahādevaḥ prādādvaramanuttamam \|\| 7 \|\|*

*bho bho yakṣa mahāsattva varaṃ brūhi yathepsitam \|*  
*brūhi kāryaṃ yatheṣṭaṃ tu yatte manasi vartate \|\| 8 \|\|*

6-8. At the confluence of the Kaveri and the Narmada, Kuvera practised asceticism after bathing in the sacred waters, for a divine century when the Lord Shiva on being pleased with him said “Kuvera! ask for what you wish.”

## \|\| 189.9 \|\|

*kubera uvāca*  
*yadi tuṣṭo'si me deva yadi deyo varo mama \|*  
*adyaprabhṛti sarveṣāṃ yakṣāṇāmadhipo bhave \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Kuvera said: “Devadeva! if you are pleased to grant me a boon, I wish to become the king of the Yakshas.”

## \|\| 189.10 \|\|

*kuberasya vacaḥ śrutvā parituṣṭo maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*evamastu tato devastatraivāntaradhīyata \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Hearing those words of Kuvera, the Lord said “Be it so” and vanished then and there.

## \|\| 189.11 \|\|

*so'pi labdhavaro yakṣaḥ śīghraṃ labdhaphalodayaḥ \|*  
*pūjitaḥ sa tu yakṣaiśca hyabhiṣiktastu pārthiva \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Afterwards Kuvera by virtue of that boon became the Lord of the Yakshas.

## \|\| 189.12-20 \|\|

*kāverīsaṃgamaṃ tatra sarvapāpapraṇāśanam \|*  
*ye narā nābhijānanti vañcitāste na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*tasmātsarvaprayatnena tatra snāyīta mānavaḥ \|*  
*kāverī ca gahāpuṇyā narmadā ca mahānadī \|\| 13 \|\|*

*tatra snātvā tu rājendra hyarcayedvṛṣabhadhvajam \|*  
*aśvamedhaphalaṃ prāpya rudra loke mahīyate \|\| 14 \|\|*

*agnipraveśaṃ yaḥ kuryādyaśca kuryādanāśakam \|*  
*anivartyā gatistasya yathā me śaṃkaro'bravīt \|\| 15 \|\|*

*sevyamāno varastrībhiḥ krīḍate divi rudra vat \|*  
*ṣaṣṭirvarṣasahasrāṇi ṣaṣṭikoṭyastathā parāḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*modate rudra lokastho yatra tatraiva gacchati \|*  
*puṇyakṣayātparibhraṣṭo rājā bhavati dhārmikaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*bhogavāndānaśīlaśca mahākulasamudbhavaḥ \|*  
*tatra pītvā jalaṃ samyakcāndrā yaṇaphalaṃ labhet \|\| 18 \|\|*

*svargaṃ gacchanti te martyā ye pibanti śubhaṃ jalam \|*  
*gaṅgāyamunayormadhye yatphalaṃ prāpnuyānnaraḥ \|*  
*kāverīsaṃgame snātvā tatphalaṃ tasya jāyate \|\| 19 \|\|*

*evamādi tu rājendra kāverīsaṃgame mahat \|*  
*puṇyaṃ mahatphalaṃ tatra sarvapāpapraṇāśanam \|\| 20 \|\|*

12-20. Such is the glory of the confluence of the sacred Kaveri with the Narmada. It is the dispeller of all sins. Those who do not know about it are undoubtedly deluded. One should, therefore, bathe there according to the prescribed rites. Both the sacred Kaveri and the Narmada are the most sacred. One who worships Shiva after bathing there begets the benefit of Ashvamedha sacrifice and goes to the realm of Rudra. One who is burnt there or keeps up a fast there, gets access everywhere. Mahadeva has said that such a person after getting access everywhere -enjoys the company of beautiful ladies in Rudraloka for 600060000 years. Afterwards he is born as a most illustrious king. One who drinks the water of the Kaveri and the Narmada gets the benefit of Chandrayana.

He gets the benefit of having bathed in the confluence of the Ganges and the Yamuna and attains heaven. King! such is the glory of the junction of the Kaveri and the Narmada where, to bathe and perform charities is to dispel all ills and sins.”

## Chapter 190

## \|\| 190.1-4 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca*  
*nārmade cottare kūle tīrthaṃ yojanavistṛtam \|*  
*yantreśvareti vikhyātaṃ sarvapāpaharaṃ param \|\| 1 \|\|*

*tatra snātvā naro rājandaivataiḥ saha modate \|*  
*pañca varṣasahasrāṇi krīḍate kāmarūpadhṛk \|\| 2 \|\|*

*garjanaṃ ca tato gacchedyatra meghacayotthitaḥ \|*  
*indra jinnāma saṃprāptastasya tīrthaprabhāvataḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*meghanādaṃ tato gacchedyatra meghānugarjitam \|*  
*meghanādo gaṇastatra paramāṃ gaṇatāṃ gataḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

1-4. Markandeya said: — To the north of the Narmada there is the sacred Mantreshvara extending to one yojana. One who bathes there goes to heaven and remains with the Devas for 5000 years. The sacred Garjana is quite close to it which has originated from the clouds. By virtue of the same the son of Ravana was named Indrajita. Here it is the Meghanada-tirtha by going where Meghanada attained great glory.

## \|\| 190.5 \|\|

*tato gacchettu rājendra tīrthamāmratakeśvaram \|*  
*tatra snātvā naro rājangosahasraphalaṃ labhet \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Further on is Amrataka by bathing where one gets the benefit of having given away a thousand cows.

## \|\| 190.6-7 \|\|

*narmadottaratīre tu dhārātīrthaṃ tu viśrutam \|*  
*tasmiṃstīrthe naraḥ snātvā tarpayetpitṛdevatāḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*sarvānkāmānavāpnoti manasā ye vicintitāḥ \|*  
*tato gacchettu rājendra brahmāvartamiti smṛtam \|\| 7 \|\|*

6-7. To the north of the Narmada is Vishruta. By bathing there and offering libation to the manes and the Devas one gets his desires fulfilled.

Afterwards the devotee should go to the Brahma varta-tirtha.

## \|\| 190.8 \|\|

*tatra saṃnihito brahmā nityameva yudhiṣṭhira \|*  
*tatra snātvā tu rājendra brahmaloke mahīyate \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Brahma resides at Brahma varta-tirtha almost every day. By bathing in it one goes to the realm of Brahma.

## \|\| 190.9 \|\|

*tato'ṅgāreśvaraṃ gacchenniyato niyatāśanaḥ \|*  
*sarvapāpavinirmukto rudra lokaṃ sa gacchati \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Then an advance should be made to the sacred Agareshvara after observing the prescribed ordinances. By going there one attains Rudraloka after being liberated from all his sins.

## \|\| 190.10 \|\|

*tato gacchecca rājendra kapilātīrthamuttamam \|*  
*tatra snātvā naro rājankapilādānamāpnuyāt \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Kapila-tirtha should be visited afterwards. By bathing in it the devotee gets the benefit of having given away a milk cow in charity.

## \|\| 190.11 \|\|

*gacchetkarañjatīrthaṃ tu devarṣigaṇasevitam \|*  
*tatra snātvā naro rājangolokaṃ samavāpnuyāt \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. One who goes to the sacred Karanja and bathes there attains the Goloka.

## \|\| 190.12 \|\|

*tato gacchettu rājendra kuṇḍaleśvaramuttamam \|*  
*tatra saṃnihito rudra stiṣṭhate hyumayā saha \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Then the devotee should proceed to Kundeshvara where Mahadeva is in residence with Parvati.

## \|\| 190.13-15 \|\|

*tatra snātvā tu rājendra sa vandyastridaśairapi \|*  
*pippaleśaṃ tato gacchetsarvapāpapraṇāśanam \|\| 13 \|\|*

*tatra snātvā tu rājendra rudra loke mahīyate \|*  
*tato gacchettu rājendra vimaleśvaramuttamam \|\| 14 \|\|*

*tatra devaśilā ramyā ceśvareṇa vinirmitā \|*  
*tatra prāṇaparityāgādrudra lokamavāpnuyāt \|\| 15 \|\|*

13-15. One who bathes there is invulnerable even by the Devas. The picturesque Vimaleshvara should then be visited where the Lord has consecrated the Devashila. Dying there one attains the realm of Rudra.

## \|\| 190.16 \|\|

*tataḥ puṣkariṇīṃ gacchettatra snānaṃ samācaret \|*  
*snātamātro narastatra hīndra syārdhāsanaṃ labhet \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Then he should go to the river Pushkarini by bathing into which the devotee becomes entitled to take his seat on the throne of Indra by his side.

## \|\| 190.17-21 \|\|

*narmadā saritāṃ śreṣṭhā rudra dehādviniḥsṛtā \|*  
*tārayetsarvabhūtāni sthāvarāṇi carāṇi ca \|\| 17 \|\|*

*sarvadevādhidevena tvīśvareṇa mahātmanā \|*  
*kathitā ṛṣisaṃghebhyo hyasmākaṃ ca viśeṣataḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*munibhiḥ saṃstutā hyeṣā narmadā pravarā nadī \|*  
*rudra dehādviniṣkrāntā lokānāṃ hitakāmyayā \|\| 19 \|\|*

*sarvapāpaharā nityaṃ sarvadevanamaskṛtā \|*  
*saṃstutā devagandharvairapsarobhistathaiva ca \|\| 20 \|\|*

*namaḥ puṇyajale hyādye namaḥ sāgaragāminī \|*  
*namaste pāpanirdāhe namo devi varānane \|\| 21 \|\|*

17-21. It is for these reasons that the sacred Narmada coming out from the Lord Shiva is the best of all the streams and the giver of bliss to the animate and the inanimate world. This Narmada has been described to be the most sacred by £Shiva the Lord of all the Devas before the Rishis. This river is adorable by all the Devas and is the dispeller of all sins and is venerated by the Devas, the Gandharvas and the nymphs. I make my salutations to the sacred and peace-giving Narmada that falls into the sea.

## \|\| 190.22 \|\|

*namo'stu te ṛṣigaṇasiddhasevite namo'stu te śaṃkaradehaniḥsṛte \|*  
*namo'stu te dharmabhṛtāṃ varaprade namo'stu te sarvapavitrapāvane \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. I make my salutations to the sacred Narmada adorned by the Siddhas, Rishis, born of Shiva, and the giver of boons to the virtuous.

## \|\| 190.23-25 \|\|

*yastvidaṃ paṭhate stotraṃ nityaṃśraddhāsamanvitaḥ \|*  
*brāhmaṇo vedamāpnoti kṣattriyo vijayī bhavet \|\| 23 \|\|*

*vaiśyastu labhate lābhaṃ śūdra ścaiva śubhāṃ gatim \|*  
*arthārthī labhate hyarthaṃ smaraṇādeva nityaśaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*narmadāṃ sevate nityaṃ svayaṃ devo maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*tena puṇyā nadī jñeyā brahmahatyāpahāriṇī \|\| 25 \|\|*

23-25. One who recites the foregoing prayers with devotion becomes well-versed in the Vedas if he is a Brahmana, and becomes victorious in war if he is a Kshatriya. The Vaidya becomes wealthy and the Shudra attains bliss. One anxious for wealth gets pelf. The sacred Narmada is daily i resorted to by the Lord Shiva in consequence of which it is the most sacred "and dispeller of all sins.

## Chapter 191

## \|\| 191.1 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca*  
*tadāprabhṛti brahmādyā ṛṣayaśca tapodhanāḥ \|*  
*sevante narmadāṃ rājanrāgakrodhavivarjitāḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Markandeya said: — O king! since that time the Devas, the Rishis and the Munis resort to the banks of the Narmada and become free from anger and passions.

## \|\| 191.2 \|\|

*yudhiṣṭhira uvāca*  
*kasminnipatitaṃ śūlaṃ devasya tu mahītale \|*  
*tatra puṇyaṃ samākhyāhi yathāvanmunisattama \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Yudhisthira said When did the trident of Shiva fall on this earth and what is the virtue of that spot where it fell? Pray explain it to me.

## \|\| 191.3-6 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca*  
*śūlabhedamiti khyātaṃ tīrthaṃ puṇyatamaṃ mahat \|*  
*tatra snātvā'rcayeddevaṃ gosahasraphalaṃ labhet \|\| 3 \|\|*

*trirātraṃ kārayedyastu tasmiṃstīrthe narādhipa \|*  
*arcayitvā mahādevaṃ punarjanma na vidyate \|\| 4 \|\|*

*bhīmeśvaraṃ tato gacchennāradeśvaramuttamam \|*  
*ādityeśaṃ mahāpuṇyaṃ smṛtaṃ kilbiṣanāśanam \|\| 5 \|\|*

*nandikeśaṃ pariṣvajya paryāptaṃ janmanaḥ phalam \|*  
*varuṇeśaṃ tataḥ paśyetsvatantreśvarameva ca \|*  
*sarvatīrthaphalaṃ tasya pañcāyatanadarśanāt \|\| 6 \|\|*

3-6. Markandeya said The place where the trident fell is known by the name of Shulabheda and one who worships there after bath gets the benefit of having given away a thousand cows in charity. One who remains there for three days and worships Shiva is liberated from the cycle of birth. Afterwards the devotee becomes blessed by worshipping Adityesha, Nandikesha at Bhimeshvara and Naradeshvara tirthas. Then Varunesha and Svatantreshvara should be worshipped. By going to these five tirthas the devotee gets the benefit of visiting all the sacred places.

## \|\| 191.7-13 \|\|

*tato gacchettu rājendra yuddhaṃ yatra susādhitam \|*  
*koṭitīrthaṃ tu vikhyātamasurā yatra mohitāḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*yatraiva nihatā rājandānavā baladarpitāḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ śirāṃsyagṛhṇanta sarve devāḥ samāgatāḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*taistu saṃsthāpito devaḥ śūlapāṇirvṛṣadhvajaḥ \|*  
*koṭirvinihatā tatra tena koṭīśvaraḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*darśanāttasya tīrthasya sadehaḥ svargamāruhet \|*  
*yadā tvindre ṇa kṣudra tvādvajraṃ kīlena yantritam \|\| 10 \|\|*

*tadāprabhṛtilokānāṃ svargamārgo nivāritaḥ \|*  
*yaḥ stutaṃ śrīphalaṃ dadyātkṛtvā cānte pradakṣiṇām \|\| 11 \|\|*

*parvataṃ sahadīpaṃ tu śirasā caiva dhārayet \|*  
*sarvakāmasusaṃpanno rājā bhavati pāṇḍava \|\| 12 \|\|*

*mṛto rudra tvamāpnoti tato'sau jāyate punaḥ \|*  
*svargādetya bhavedrā jā rājyaṃ kṛtvā divaṃ vrajet \|\| 13 \|\|*

7-13. Then a visit should be paid to Koti-tirtha where there was a great battle between the Devas and the demons and where the latter were deluded. There the heads of the valiant demons have been severed by the Devas and the latter have enshrined Shulapani Mahadeva. By worshipping Him one ascends to heaven even when he has not parted with his life. The portals of heaven have, been shut by Indra by means of Vajrakilaka out of the narrowness of his mind. One who having eaten a Bilva fruit and clarified butter carries a burning lamp on his head and perambulates Koti-tirtha becomes a most flourishing king. One who dies there goes to the region of Rudra and is born as a king in his next life after which he goes to heaven.

## \|\| 191.14 \|\|

*bahunetraṃ tataḥ paśyettrayodaśyāṃ tu mānavaḥ \|*
