*snātamātro narastatra sarvayajñaphalaṃ labhet \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. On the thirteenth day of a fortnight the devotee attains the benefits of all the sacrifices by bathing at the Bahunetra-tirtha.

## \|\| 191.15-18 \|\|

*tato gacchettu rājendra tīrthaṃ paramaśobhanam \|*  
*narāṇāṃ pāpanāśāya hyagastyeśvaramuttamam \|\| 15 \|\|*

*tatra snātvā naro rājanbrahmaloke mahīyate \|*  
*kārtikasya tu māsasya kṛṣṇapakṣe caturdaśī \|\| 16 \|\|*

*ghṛtena snāpayeddevaṃ samādhistho jitendri yaḥ \|*  
*ekaviṃśakulopeto na cyavedaiśvarātpadāt \|\| 17 \|\|*

*dhenumupānahau chatraṃ dadyācca ghṛtakambalam \|*  
*bhojanaṃ caiva viprāṇāṃ sarvaṃ koṭiguṇaṃ bhavet \|\| 18 \|\|*

15-18. After that the beautiful Agasteshvara-tirtha should be visited. By bathing there one goes to the region of Brahma. One who bathes the Lord in clarified butter on the fourteenth day of a dark fortnight and devotes himself to meditation observing perfect celibacy, resides in the realm of Shiva along with 21 generations of his Pitris and never falls from there. One who gives away a cow, a pair of shoes, umbrella, clarified-butter, blanket, etc., in charity and feeds the Brahmanas derives manifold benefits.

## \|\| 191.19 \|\|

*tato gacchecca rājendra balākeśvaramuttamam \|*  
*tatra snātvā naro rājansiṃhāsanapatirbhavet \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. After that Vileshvara-tirtha should be visited. By bathing there one becomes the Lord of a throne.

## \|\| 191.20-22 \|\|

*narmadādakṣiṇe kūle tīrthaṃ śakrasya viśrutam \|*  
*upoṣya rajanīmekāṃ snānaṃ tatra samācaret \|\| 20 \|\|*

*snānaṃ kṛtvā yathānyāyamarcayecca janārdanam \|*  
*gosahasraphalaṃ tasya viṣṇulokaṃ sa gacchati \|\| 21 \|\|*

*ṛṣitīrthaṃ tato gacchetsarvapāpaharaṃ nṛṇām \|*  
*snātamātro narastatra śivalokaṃ ca gacchati \|\| 22 \|\|*

20-22. The Indra-tirtha on the right bank of the Narmada is renowned. One who fasts there for one night and then worships Janardana after hath gets the merit of giving away a thousand cows in charity and goes to the region of Vishnu, Then the devotee gets the benefit of giving away a thousand cows merely by bathing at Rishi-tirtha.

## \|\| 191.23 \|\|

*nāradasya tu tatraiva tīrthaṃ paramaśobhanam \|*  
*snātamātro narastatra gosahasraphalaṃ labhet \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Afterwards a visit should be paid to the tirtha of Brahma, By bathing -into it one attains the realm of Brahma.

## \|\| 191.24 \|\|

*devatīrthaṃ tato gacchedbrahmaṇā nirmitaṃ purā \|*  
*tatra snātvā naro rājanbrahmaloke mahīyate \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Then merely by bathing at the shrine of Lord Amarakantaka en! the Devas one attains the realm of Rudra.

## \|\| 191.25 \|\|

*amarakaṇṭakaṃ gacchedamaraiḥ sthāpitaṃ purā \|*  
*snātamātro narastatra rudra loke mahīyate \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Afterwards the shrine of Ravaneshvara should be visited by whose grace the sin of killing a Brahmana is cleansed.

## \|\| 191.26 \|\|

*tato gacchecca rājendra rāvaṇeśvaramuttamam \|*  
*nityaṃ cā’yatanaṃ dṛṣṭva mucyate brahmahatyayā \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Then a visit should be paid to Rishi-tirtha which exonerates the devotee from all his debts (of duty) after which by going to Bateshvara he is blessed.

## \|\| 191.27-28 \|\|

*ṛṇatīrthaṃ tato gacchedṛṇebhyo mucyate dhruvam \|*  
*vaṭeśvaraṃ tato dṛṣṭvā paryāptaṃ janmanaḥ phalam \|\| 27 \|\|*

*bhīmeśvaraṃ tato gacchetsarvavyādhivināśanam \|*  
*snātamātro naro rājansarvaduḥkhaiḥ pramucyate \|\| 28 \|\|*

27-28. Bhimeshvara Mahadeva should be visited next. By bathing there one is freed from all his troubles. By worshipping Shiva at the Turasanga-tirtha after bathing there one earns his emancipation.

## \|\| 191.29-35 \|\|

*tato gacchettu rājendra turāsaṅgamanuttamam \|*  
*tatra snātvā mahādevamarcayansiddhimāpnuyāt \|\| 29 \|\|*

*somatīrthaṃ tato gacchetpaśyeccandra manuttamam \|*  
*tatra snātvā naro rājanbhaktyā paramayā yutaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

*tatkṣaṇāddivyadehasthaḥ śivavanmodate ciram \|*  
*ṣaṣṭirvarṣasahasrāṇi rudra loke mahīyate \|\| 31 \|\|*

*tato gacchettu rājendra piṅgaleśvaramuttamam \|*  
*ahorātropavāsena trirātraphalamāpnuyāt \|\| 32 \|\|*

*tasmiṃstīrthe tu rājendra kapilāṃ yaḥ prayacchati \|*  
*yāvanti tasyā romāṇi tatprasūtikuleṣu ca \|\| 33 \|\|*

*tāvadvarṣasahasrāṇi rudra loke mahīyate \|*  
*yastu prāṇaparityāgaṃ kuryāttatra narādhipa \|\| 34 \|\|*

*akṣayaṃ modate kālaṃ yāvaccandra divākarau \|*  
*narmadātaṭamāśritya tiṣṭheyurye narottamāḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

29-35. Afterwards the devotee should go and adore the moon at Soma-tirtha. By bathing there with devotion one gets divine form and remains in bliss for a considerable length of time like Shiva and enjoys life in the realm of Rudra for 60000 years. Later on a visit should be paid to the Lord Pingaleshvara where by observing a fast for 24 hours one derives the benefit of having observed it for three nights. One who gives away a milk cow in charity goes and enjoys in the realm of Rudra for as many years as there are hair on the body of, that cow. One who dies there remains in the realm of Rudra till the existence of the Sun and the Moon. Those residing on the banks of the Narmada remain in heaven like the pious. The devotee should also visit the shrines of Sureshvara and Karkotakeshvara.

## \|\| 191.36-38 \|\|

*te bhṛtāḥ svargamāyānti santaḥ sukṛtino yathā \|*  
*sureśvaraṃ tato gacchennāmnā karkoṭakeśvaram \|\| 36 \|\|*

*gaṅgā'vatarate tatra dine puṇye na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*nanditīrthaṃ tato gacchetsnānaṃ tatra samācaret \|\| 37 \|\|*

*tuṣyate tasya nandīśaḥ somaloke mahīyate \|*  
*tato dīpeśvaraṃ gacchedvyāsatīrthaṃ tapovanam \|\| 38 \|\|*

36-38 There, undoubtedly the sacred Ganges appears on an auspicious day. By bathing at the Nandi-tirtha, the Lord Nandisha becomes pleased with the devotee and he ascends to the world of the Moon. Lord Dipeshvara should be visited next where there is the tirtha of Vedavyasa in a beautiful forest. In the days gone by, the sacred Narmada for fear of the sage Vyasa flowed in the opposite direction and her course was turned to the south only when the sage forced her with a roaring cry.

## \|\| 191.39 \|\|

*nivartitā purā tatra vyāsabhītā mahānadī \|*  
*huṃkāritā tu vyāsena dakṣiṇena tato gatā \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. One who circumambulates that sacred place remains in the region of Shiva till the existence of the Sun and the Moon.

## \|\| 191.40-48 \|\|

*pradakṣiṇāṃ tu yaḥ kuryāttasmiṃstīrthe narādhipa \|*  
*akṣayaṃ modate kālaṃ yāvaccandra divākarau \|\| 40 \|\|*

*vyāsastasya bhavetprītaḥ prāpnuyādīpsitaṃ phalam \|*  
*sūtreṇa veṣṭayitvā tu dīpo deyaḥ savedikaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

*krīḍate cākṣayaṃ kālaṃ yathā rudra stathaiva ca \|*  
*tato gacchecca rājendra airaṇḍītīrthamuttamam \|\| 42 \|\|*

*saṃgame tu naraḥ snātvā mucyate sarvapātakaiḥ \|*  
*airaṇḍī triṣu lokeṣu vikhyātā pāpanāśinī \|\| 43 \|\|*

*athavā’śvayuje māsi śuklapakṣe tu cāṣṭamī \|*  
*śucirbhūtvā naraḥ snātvā sopavāsaparāyaṇaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

*brāhmaṇaṃ bhojayedekaṃ koṭirbhavati bhojitā \|*  
*airaṇḍīsaṃgame snātvā bhaktibhāvānurañjitaḥ \|*  
*mṛttikāṃ śirasi sthāpya hyavagāhya ca vai jalam \|\| 45 \|\|*

*narmadodakasaṃmiśraṃ mucyate sarvakilbiṣaiḥ \|*  
*pradakṣiṇaṃ tu yaḥ kuryāttasmiṃstīrthe narādhipa \|\| 46 \|\|*

*pradakṣiṇīkṛtā tena saptadvīpā vasuṃdharā \|*  
*tataḥ suvarṇasalile snātvā dattvā tu kāñcanam \|\| 47 \|\|*

*kāñcanena vimānena rudra loke mahīyate \|*  
*tataḥ svargāccyutaḥ kālādrā jā bhavati vīryavān \|\| 48 \|\|*

40-48. There, Vedavyasa becomes pleased and fulfills the desires of the devotee. One who list up a wick on a platform after tying it round with thread remains in the region of Rudra till the end of the cycle. Afterwards the devotee should go to the Airandi-tirtha and bathe at the junction of rivers which liberates him from all sins.. The river Airandi is renowned in all the three worlds and is the dispeller of all sins. The devotee should observe a complete fast after bathing there on the 8th day of the bright fortnight in the month of Ashvin and then he should feed a Brahmana. He gets the benefit of feeding crores of Brahmanas. One who dives in the sacred stream after rubbing on his head the earth of that place is freed from all his sins. One who circumambulates that sacred place gets the merits of circumambulating all the world along with the seven oceans. Afterwards one who gives away gold in charity after bathing in the water mingled with gold enjoys in Rudraloka seated in a Vimana of gold and is born as a king. Afterwards the devotee should go to the junction of the river Hikshu. That beautiful tirtha is renowned in the three worlds and the Lord Shiva resides there.

## \|\| 191.49-52 \|\|

*tato gacchecca rājendra ikṣunadyāstu saṃgamam \|*  
*trailokyaviśrutaṃ divyaṃ tatra saṃnihitaḥ śivaḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

*tatra snātvā naro rājangāṇapatyamāpnuyāt \|*  
*skandatīrthaṃ tato gacchetsarvapāpapraṇāśanam \|\| 50 \|\|*

*ājanma janitaṃ pāpaṃ snānamātrādvyapohati \|*  
*liṅgasāraṃ tato gacchetsnānaṃ tatra samācaret \|\| 51 \|\|*

*gosahasraphalaṃ tasya rudra loke mahīyate \|*  
*bhaṅgatīrthaṃ tato gacchetsarvapāpapraṇāśanam \|\| 52 \|\|*

49-52. The person bathing there becomes one of the chief attendants of Shiva. Then the Svamikartika-tirtha — the dispeller of all sins — should be visited. Merely by bathing there the devotee is purified of three kinds of sins. Then the devotee should bathe at Lingasara-tirtha by doing which one gets the merit of having given away a thousand cows in charity and he resides in the realm of Rudra. Bhanga-tirtha is the dispeller of all sins. By bathing there the sins of the seven generations are annihilated.

## \|\| 191.53 \|\|

*tatra gatvā tu rājendra snānaṃ tatra samācaret \|*  
*saptajanmakṛtaiḥ pāpairmucyate nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Then Bateshvara the foremost of all the sacred places should be visited. By bathing there one gets the merit of having given away thousand cows.

## \|\| 191.54 \|\|

*vaṭeśvaraṃ tato gacchetsarvatīrthamanuttamam \|*  
*tatra snātvā naro rājangosahasraphalaṃ labhet \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. Sangamesha-tirtha is venerated by all the Devas, by bathing there one becomes like Indra.

## \|\| 191.55-57 \|\|

*saṃgameśaṃ tato gacchetsarvadevanamaskṛtam \|*  
*snātamātrānnarastatra cendra tvaṃ labhate dhruvam \|\| 55 \|\|*

*koṭitīrthaṃ tato gacchetsarvapāpaharaṃ param \|*  
*tatra snātvā naro rājyaṃ labhate nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

*tatra tīrthaṃ samāsādya dattvā dānaṃ tu yo naraḥ \|*  
*tasya tīrthaprabhāveṇa sarvaṃ koṭiguṇaṃ bhavet \|\| 57 \|\|*

55-57. By bathing at Koti-tirtha one undoubtedly becomes the ruler of a kingdom. One who gives any charity there gets manifold blessings.

Any woman bathing there becomes the queen of Indra after becoming beautiful like Parvati.

## \|\| 191.58-59 \|\|

*atha nārī bhavetkācittatra snānaṃ samācaret \|*  
*gaurītulyā bhavetsā'pi tvindra patnī na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

*aṅgāreśaṃ tato gacchetsnānaṃ tatra samācaret \|*  
*snātamātro narastatra rudra loke mahīyate \|\| 59 \|\|*

58-59. Angare4a-tirtha should be visited next. By doing it one remains in bliss till the destruction of the universe.

## \|\| 191.60 \|\|

*aṅgārakacaturthyāṃ tu snānaṃ tatra samācaret \|*  
*akṣayaṃ modate kālaṃ śuciḥ prayatamānasaḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. One who bathes at Ayonisambhava-tirtha never experiences the sufferings of birth after which the devotee should bathe at Pandavesha.

## \|\| 191.61-63 \|\|

*ayonisaṃbhave snātvā na paśyedyonisaṃkaṭam \|*  
*pāṇḍaveśaṃ tu tatraiva snānaṃ tatra samācaret \|\| 61 \|\|*

*akṣayaṃ modate kālamavadhyastridaśairapi \|*  
*viṣṇulokaṃ tato gatvā krīḍate bhogasaṃyutaḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

*tatra bhuktvā mahābhogānmartyarājo'bhijāyate \|*  
*kaṭheśvaraṃ tato gacchettatra snānaṃ samācaret \|\| 63 \|\|*

61-63. By bathing there one gets lasting happiness and becomes invulnerable even by the Devas and goes and enjoys in the realm of Vishnu and on being reborn he becomes a king. Then the devotee should bathe at Katheeshvara tirtha and his desires are fulfilled by remaining there during the summer solstice. Afterwards he should bathe in the river Chandrabhaga.

## \|\| 191.64-68 \|\|

*uttarāyaṇasaṃprāptau yadicchettasya tadbhavet \|*  
*candra bhāgāṃ tato gacchettatra snānaṃ samācaret \|\| 64 \|\|*

*snātamātro naro rājansomaloke mahīyate \|*  
*tato gacchettu rājendra tīrthaṃ śakrasya viśrutam \|\| 65 \|\|*

*pūjitaṃ devarājena devairapi namaskṛtam \|*  
*tatra snātvā naro rājandānaṃ dattvā tu kāñcanam \|\| 66 \|\|*

*athavā nīlavarṇābhaṃ vṛṣabhaṃ yaḥ samutsṛjet \|*  
*vṛṣabhasya tu romāṇi tatprasūtikuleṣu ca \|\| 67 \|\|*

*tāvadvarṣasahasrāṇi naro harapure vaset \|*  
*tataḥ svargātparibhraṣṭo rājā bhavati vīryavān \|\| 68 \|\|*

64-68. The devotee bathing in the Chandrabhaga goes to the region of the Moon. Afterwards he should visit the Indra-tirtha where Indra performed his worship. One who gives away gold in charity after bathing there or a black bull, remains in the realm of Shiva for as many years as there are hair on the body of that bull and on its calf. He is afterwards reborn as a valiant king and is the master of thousands of white horses.

## \|\| 191.69-70 \|\|

*aśvānāṃ śvetavarṇānāṃ sahasrāṇāṃ narādhipa \|*  
*svāmī bhavati martyeṣu tasya tīrthaprabhāvataḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

*tato gacchettu rājendra brahmāvartamanuttamam \|*  
*tatra snātvā naro rājaṃstarpayetpitṛdevatāḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

69-70. Then the devotee should bathe at the Brahmavarta-tirtha and offer libation to the manes and the Devas and observe a fast for the night. One who offers the balls of rice to the manes on the Kanya-sankranta gets innumerable blessings.

## \|\| 191.71-72 \|\|

*upoṣya rajanīmekāṃ piṇḍaṃ dattvā yathāvidhi \|*  
*kanyāgate tathā’ditye akṣayaṃ syānnarādhipa \|\| 71 \|\|*

*tato gacchecca rājendra kapilātīrthamuttamam \|*  
*tatra snātvā naro rājankapilāṃ yaḥ prayacchati \|\| 72 \|\|*

71-72. One who gives away a milk cow after bathing at Kapila-tirtha gets the benefit of having given away the whole world in charity. The sacred place Narmadesha is unparalleled.

## \|\| 191.73-76 \|\|

*saṃpūrṇāṃ pṛthivīṃ dattvā yatphalaṃ tadavāpnuyāt \|*  
*narmadeśaṃ paraṃ tīrthaṃ na bhūtaṃ na bhaviṣyati \|\| 73 \|\|*

*tatra snātvā naro rājannaśvamedhaphalaṃ labhet \|*  
*narmadādakṣiṇe kūle saṃgameśvaramuttamam \|\| 74 \|\|*

*tatra snātvā naro rājansarvayajñaphalaṃ labhet \|*  
*tatra sarvodyato rājā pṛthivyāmeva jāyate \|\| 75 \|\|*

*sarvalakṣaṇasaṃpūrṇaḥ sarvavyādhivivarjitaḥ \|*  
*nārmade cottare kūle tīrthaṃ paramaśobhanam \|\| 76 \|\|*

73-76. The person bathing there gets the merit of having performed Ashvamedha sacrifice. Sangameshvara-tirtha is on the northern bank of the Narmada. By bathing there the devotee gets the benefit of all the sacrifices. There the man doing even the smallest act of virtue becomes free from all ills and attains kingship. On the same bank of the Narmada is the Parmashobhana-tirtha which is the best place of Aditya and Lord said that any charity performed there begets everlasting merits.

## \|\| 191.77 \|\|

*ādityāyatanaṃ divyamīśvareṇa tu bhāṣitam \|*  
*tatra snātvā tu rājendra dānaṃ dattvā tu śaktitaḥ \|*  
*tasya tīrthaprabhāveṇa dattaṃ bhavati cākṣayam \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. The ill-doers and those suffering from jaundice bathing there are freed from all the sins and go to the region of the Sun.

## \|\| 191.78-79 \|\|

*daridrā vyādhitā ye tu ye tu duṣkṛtakarmiṇaḥ \|*  
*mucyante sarvapāpebhyaḥ sūryalokaṃ tu yānti te \|\| 78 \|\|*

*māghamāse tu saṃprāpte śuklapakṣasya saptamī \|*  
*vasedāyatane tatra nirāhāro jitendri yaḥ \|\| 79 \|\|*

78-79. On the seventh day of the bright fortnight in the month of Magha, he who remains there after observing a fast, is free from the effects of, the old age, sufferings and is never dumb, blind and deaf. He is handsome and the beloved of women.

## \|\| 191.80 \|\|

*na jarāvyādhito mūko na cāndho badhiro'thavā \|*  
*subhago rūpasaṃpannaḥ strīṇāṃ bhavati vallabhaḥ \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. In such a way is the most sacred place and those who do not know about it are undoubtedly deluded.

## \|\| 191.81 \|\|

*evaṃ tīrthaṃ mahāpuṇyaṃ mārkaṇḍeyena bhāṣitam \|*  
*ye na jānanti rājendra vañcitāste na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. Afterwards one should go and bathe at Gangeshvara by means of which one attains heaven.

## \|\| 191.82-83 \|\|

*gargeśvaraṃ tato gacchetsnānaṃ tatra samācaret \|*  
*snātamātro narastatra svargalokamavāpnuyāt \|\| 82 \|\|*

*modate svargalokastho yāvadindrā ścaturdaśa \|*  
*samīpataḥ sthitaṃ tasya nāgeśvaratapovanam \|\| 83 \|\|*

82-83. He enjoys in the heaven till the conclusion of the sway of fourteen Indras. Nageshvara-tapovana is close to that tirtha. One who bathes; there attains Nagaloka and enjoys there for a long time.

## \|\| 191.84-88 \|\|

*tatra snātvā tu rājendra nāgalokamavāpnuyāt \|*  
*bahvībhirnāgakanyābhiḥ krīḍate kālamakṣayam \|\| 84 \|\|*

*kuberabhavanaṃ gacchetkubero yatra saṃsthitaḥ \|*  
*kāleśvaraṃ paraṃ tīrthaṃ kubero yatra toṣitaḥ \|\| 85 \|\|*

*tatra snātvā tu rājendra sarvasaṃpadamāpnuyāt \|*  
*tataḥ paścimato gacchenmārutālayamuttamam \|\| 86 \|\|*

*tatra snātvā tu rājendra śucirbhūtvā samāhitaḥ \|*  
*kāñcanaṃ tu tato dadyādyathāśakti subuddhimān \|\| 87 \|\|*

*puṣpakeṇa vimānena vāyulokaṃ sa gacchati \|*  
*yavatīrthaṃ tato gacchenmāghamāse yudhiṣṭhira \|\| 88 \|\|*

84-88. The devotee should also go to the shrine of Kuvera. There the Lord Kaleshvara is enshrined and there Kuvera was blessed. The devotee bathing there attains all kinds of bliss. Afterwards a visit should be paid to Marutalaya- tirtha. One who gives away gold in charity after bath with an easy mind, goes to Vishnuloka, seated in the Pushpaka-vimana.

A visit should be paid to Paya-tirtha, during the month of Magha. There the devotee should break his fast in course of the night after bathing there on the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight. Such a man does not experience the sufferings of birth.

## \|\| 191.89 \|\|

*kṛṣṇapakṣe caturdaśyāṃ snānaṃ tatra samācaret \|*  
*naktabhojyaṃ tataḥ kuryānna paśyedyonisaṃkaṭam \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. Then bathing should be performed at Ahalya-tirtha, and such a devotee enjoys intercourse with the nymphs.

## \|\| 191.90-93 \|\|

*ahalyātīrthaṃ tato gacchetsnānaṃ tatra samācaret \|*  
*snātamātro narastatra hyapsarobhiḥ pramodate \|\| 90 \|\|*

*ahalyā ca tapastaptvā tatra muktimupāgatā \|*  
*caitramāse tu saṃprāpte śuklapakṣe caturdaśī \|\| 91 \|\|*

*kāmadevadine tasminnahalyāṃ yastu pūjayet \|*  
*yatra yatra narotpanno narastatra priyo bhavet \|\| 92 \|\|*

*strīvallabho bhavecchrīmānkāmadeva ivāparaḥ \|*  
*ayodhyāṃ tu samāsādya tīrthaṃ rāmasya viśrutam \|\| 93 \|\|*

90-93. It was there where Ahalya attained emancipation after practising asceticism. One who worships Ahalya there on the 14th day of the lunar fortnight in the month of Chaitra, is always born as a mainland is the beloved of women and handsome like Cupid. In the sacred Ayodhya lies the tirtha of Shri Ramachandra where merely by bathing all the sins are dispelled after which, bathing should be performed at the Somatirtha.

## \|\| 191.94-99 \|\|

*snātamātro narastatra sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate \|*  
*somatīrthaṃ tato gacchetsnānaṃ tatra samācaret \|\| 94 \|\|*

*snātamātro narastatra sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate \|*  
*somagrahe tu rājendra pāpakṣayakaraṃ nṛṇām \|\| 95 \|\|*

*trailokyaviśrutaṃ rājansomatīrthaṃ mahāphalam \|*  
*yastu cāndrā yaṇaṃ kuryāttasmiṃstīrthe narādhipa \|\| 96 \|\|*

*sarvapāpaviśuddhātmā somalokaṃ sa gacchati \|*  
*agnipraveśe'tha jale athavā'pi hyanāśake \|\| 97 \|\|*

*somatīrthe mṛto yastu nāsau martye'bhijāyate \|*  
*śubhatīrthaṃ tato gacchetsnānaṃ tatra samācaret \|\| 98 \|\|*

*snātamātro narastatra goloke tu mahīyate \|*  
*tato gacchecca rājendra viṣṇutīrthamanuttamam \|\| 99 \|\|*

94-99. By bathing there all the ills are dispelled. The Somagra-tirtha is renowned all the world over. It is the dispeller of all sins. It has manifold virtues. One who observes Chandrayana fast there, attains the Chandraloka after being liberated from all the sins. One who enters into the fire there or plunges himself into the water or lives only on fruits till the time of his death, and gives up his life at that sacred place, is never re-born. Afterwards the devotee should bathe at Subhatirtha by means of which one attains Goloka. Then a move should be made to Vishnu-tirtha. There Yodhinipura is renowned where Lord Vishnu fought with millions of demons.

## \|\| 191.100 \|\|

*yodhanīpuramākhyātaṃ viṣṇusthānamanuttamam \|*  
*asurā yodhitāstatra vāsudevena koṭiśaḥ \|\| 100 \|\|*

100\. Lord Vishnu is pleased by observing a full-day’s fast at Shuka-tirtha and the sin of killing a Brahmana is dispelled there.

## \|\| 191.101-106 \|\|

*tatra tīrthaṃ samutpannaṃ viṣṇuḥ prīto bhavediha \|*  
*ahorātropavāsena brahmahatyāṃ vyapohati \|\| 101 \|\|*

*tato gacchettu rājendra tāpaseśvaramuttamam \|*  
*hariṇāṃ vyādhasaṃtrastā patitā yatra sā mṛgī \|\| 102 \|\|*

*jale prakṣiptagātrā tu antarikṣaṃ gatā ca sā \|*  
*vyādho vismitacittastu paraṃ vismayamāgataḥ \|\| 103 \|\|*

*tena tāpeśvaraṃ tīrthaṃ na bhūtaṃ na bhaviṣyati \|*  
*tato gacchettu rājendra brahmatīrthamanuttamam \|\| 104 \|\|*

*amohakamiti khyātaṃ pitriṃścaivātra tarpayet \|*  
*paurṇamāsyāmamāyāṃ tu śrāddhaṃ kuryādyathāvidhi \|\| 105 \|\|*

*tatra snātvā naro rājanpitṛpiṇḍaṃ tu dāpayet \|*  
*gajarūpā śilā tatra toyamadhye pratiṣṭhitā \|\| 106 \|\|*

101-106. Afterwards Tapaseshvara-tirtha should be visited where a deer fell — .down for fear of a hunter and dying in the sacred waters she ascended to the heaven which highly amazed the hunter. Such is the glory of that Tapaseshvara-tirtha. There is no such tirtha. Afterwards a visit should be paid to the sacred Brahma- tirtha, which is also known as Amohaka where libations should be offered to the manes and shraddha should be performed on the full moon-day or the Amavasya. There a huge-piece of rook like an elephant is lying in the water on which the balls of rice should be offered to the manes and there is very great merit in giving the balls of rice to the manes on the full moon-day during the month of Vishakha by which the manes remain gratified till the end of the world.

## \|\| 191.107 \|\|

*tasyāṃ tu dāpayetpiṇḍaṃ vaiśākhyāṃ tu viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*tṛpyanti pitarastatra yāvattiṣṭhati medinī \|\| 107 \|\|*

107\. Afterwards a visit should be paid to Siddheshvara-tirtha. By bathing here one becomes the chief attendant of Shiva.

## \|\| 191.108 \|\|

*tato gacchecca rājendra siddheśvaramanuttamam \|*  
*tatra snātvā naro rājangaṇapatyantikaṃ vrajet \|\| 108 \|\|*

108\. Then a visit should be paid to the shrine of Janardana. By bathing there one attains the realm of Vishnu.

## \|\| 191.109-113 \|\|

*tato gacchettu rājendra liṅgaṃ yatra janārdanaḥ \|*  
*tatra snātvā tu rājendra viṣṇuloke mahīyate \|\| 109 \|\|*

*narmadādakṣiṇe kūle tīrthaṃ paramaśobhanam \|*  
*kāmadevaḥ svayaṃ tatra tapo'tapyata vai mahat \|\| 110 \|\|*

*divyaṃ varṣasahasraṃ tu śaṃkaraṃ paryupāsata \|*  
*samādhibhaṅgadagdhastu śaṃkareṇa mahātmanā \|\| 111 \|\|*

*śvetaparvā yamaścaiva hutāśaḥ śukraparvaṇi \|*  
*ete dagdhāstu te sarve kusumeśvarasaṃsthitāḥ \|\| 112 \|\|*

*divyavarṣasahasreṇa tuṣṭasteṣāṃ maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*umayā sahito rudra stuṣṭasteṣāṃ varapradaḥ \|\| 113 \|\|*

109-113. Shobhana-Kusumeshvara-tirtha is on the right bank of the Narmada where the sage Vamadeva practised great austerities. He continued his austerities for a thousand years of the gods and on the same spot, Shvetaparva, Dharmaraja and Agni also practised penances and they were all overcome by the arrows of Cupid. At that time, Lord Shiva and Parvati became pleased and blessed them. After that the Lord weaned them from their asceticism and located them on the banks of the Narmada. By virtue of that asceticism they all became Devas again.

## \|\| 191.114-115 \|\|

*mokṣayitvā tu tānsarvānnarmadātaṭamāsthitaḥ \|*  
*tatastīrthaprabhāveṇa punardevatvamāgatāḥ \|\| 114 \|\|*

*ūcuśca parayā bhaktyā devadevaṃ vṛṣadhvajam \|*  
*tvatprasādānmahādeva tīrthaṃ bhavatu cottamam \|*  
*ardhayojanavistīrṇaṃ kṣetraṃ dikṣu samantataḥ \|\| 115 \|\|*

114-115. They all said to Mahadeva: — “Let this place become most sacred by Your blessing.” Afterwards that tirtha became four square miles in urea. One who bathes and fasts there becomes handsome like Cupid and attains the realm of Shiva.

## \|\| 191.116 \|\|

*tasmiṃstīrthe naraḥ snātvā vopavāsaparāyaṇaḥ \|*  
*kusumāyudharūpeṇa rudra loke mahīyate \|\| 116 \|\|*

116\. Agni, Dharmaraja and Vayu have attained emancipation by practising asceticism there.

## \|\| 191.117-123 \|\|

*vaiśvānaro yamaścaiva kāmadevastasthā marut \|*  
*tapastaptvā tu rājendra parāṃ siddhimavāpnuyuḥ \|\| 117 \|\|*

*aṅkolasya samīpe tu nātidūre tu tasya vai \|*  
*snānaṃ dānaṃ ca tatraiva bhojanaṃ piṇḍapātanam \|\| 118 \|\|*

*agnipraveśe'tha jale athavā tu hyanāśake \|*  
*anivartikā gatistasya mṛtasyāmutra jāyate \|\| 119 \|\|*

*tr! yambakeṇa tu toyena yaścaruṃ śrapayennaraḥ \|*  
*aṅkolamūle dattvā tu piṇḍaṃ caiva yathāvidhi \|\| 120 \|\|*

*tṛpyanti pitarastasya yāvaccandra divākarau \|*  
*uttare tvayane prāpte ghṛtasnānaṃ karoti yaḥ \|\| 121 \|\|*

*puruṣo vā'tha strī vā'pi vasedāyatane śuciḥ \|*  
*siddheśvarasya devasya prātaḥ pūjāṃ prakalpayet \|\| 122 \|\|*

*sa yāṃ gatimavāpnoti na tāṃ sarvairmahāmakhaiḥ \|*  
*yadā'vatīrṇaḥ kālena rūpavānsubhago bhavet \|\| 123 \|\|*

117-123. There is a tree of Alangium hexapetalum and the devotee bathing there, performing charity,, feeding the Brahmanas, offering balls of rice to the manes, entering into fire, living on meals of fruits and giving up life there gets access everywhere in his next life. One who offers balls of rice according to the prescribed rites at the root of the tree and pours libations into, the fire after reciting Tryamvaka mantra, gratifies his manes till the existence of the Sun and the Moon. A man or a woman who bathes there at the time, of the summer solstice gets a most sacred place to live.

One who worships the Lord Siddheshvara in the morning attains the benefit which is not otherwise obtainable even by performing sacrifices. When such a man is born he becomes an emperor of vast dominions.

## \|\| 191.124 \|\|

*martye bhavati rājā ca tvāsamudrā ntagocare \|*  
*kṣetrapālaṃ na paśyettu daṇḍapāṇiṃ mahābalam \|\| 124 \|\|*

124\. Without visiting Karna-kundala-tirtha the whole pilgrimage remains incomplete: and void of fruits. Such is the glory of the sacred place. The Kusumeshvara is so called because the Devas showered flowers on knowing its great glory.

## Chapter 192

## \|\| 192.1-8 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca*  
*bhārgaveśaṃ tato gacchedbhagno yatra janārdanaḥ \|*  
*asuraistu mahāyuddhe mahābalaparākramaiḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*huṃkāritāstu devena dānavāḥ pralayaṃ gatāḥ \|*  
*tatra snātvā tu rājendra sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate \|\| 2 \|\|*

*śuklatīrthasya cotpattiṃ śṛṇu tvaṃ pāṇḍunandana \|*  
*himavacchikhare ramye nānādhātuvicitrite \|\| 3 \|\|*

*taruṇādityasaṃkāśe taptakāñcanasaprabhe \|*  
*vajrasphaṭikasopāne citrapaṭṭaśilātale \|\| 4 \|\|*

*jāmbūnadamaye divye nānāpuṣpopaśobhite \|*  
*tatrā'sīnaṃ mahādevaṃ sarvajñaṃ prabhumavyayam \|\| 5 \|\|*

*lokānugrahakartāraṃ gaṇavṛndaiḥ samāvṛtam \|*  
*skandanandimahākālairvīrabhadra gaṇādibhiḥ \|*  
*umayā sahitaṃ devaṃ mārkaṇḍiḥ paryapṛcchata \|\| 6 \|\|*

*devadeva mahādeva brahmaviṣṇvindra saṃstuta \|*  
*saṃsārabhayabhīto'haṃ sukhopāyaṃ bravīhi me \|\| 7 \|\|*

*bhagavanbhūtabhavyeśa sarvapāpapraṇāśanam \|*  
*tīrthānāṃ paramaṃ tīrthaṃ tadvadasva maheśvara \|\| 8 \|\|*

1-8. Markandeya said: — Bhargavesha-tirtha should be visited where the valiant demons when they proved troublesome to Janardana. By bathing there one becomes free from all ills. Son of Pandu! I shall now relate to you about the Shukla-tirtha. I saw the Lord Shiva sitting along with Parvati, Svamikartika — the well-wisher of the universe — and other attendants like Nandi on the beautiful summit abounding with the flowers of the golden hue, shining like the rising sun, having steps studded with precious stones and beautiful rocks all round and I asked Him: — ‘ Devadeva! adored by Brahma, Vishnu and others I am oppressed with the troubles of the world, be pleased to point out to me some way leading to happiness. Bhagavan! Bhuta! Bhavesha! the Dispeller of all sins! pray tell me the best of all the sacred places.’

## \|\| 192.9 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca*  
*śṛnu vipra mahāprājña sarvaśāstraviśārada \|*  
*snānāya gaccha subhaga ṛṣisaṃghaiḥ samāvṛtaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Shiva said: — Hear, O learned Brahmana 1 you should go with the Rishis to bathe at the sacred places.

## \|\| 192.10-13 \|\|

*manvatrikaśyapāścaiva yājñavalyośanoṅgirāḥ \|*  
*yamāpastambasaṃvartāḥ kātyāyanabṛhaspatī \|\| 10 \|\|*

*nārado gautamaścaiva sevante dharmakāṅkṣiṇaḥ \|*  
*gaṅgā kanakhale puṇyā prayāgaṃ puṣkaraṃ gayām \|\| 11 \|\|*

*kurukṣetraṃ mahāpuṇyaṃ rāhugraste divākare \|*  
*divā vā yadi vā rātrau śuklatīrthaṃ mahāphalam \|\| 12 \|\|*

*darśanātsparśanāccaiva snānāddānāttapojapāt \|*  
*homāccaivopavāsācca śuklatīrthaṃ mahāphalam \|\| 13 \|\|*

10-13. Bear in mind that Manu, Atri, Kashyapa, Yajnavalkya, Shukra, Angira, Dharmaraja, Apastamba, Sambarta, Katyayana, Brihaspati, Narada and Gautama, etc., venerate the Ganges, Kankhala, Prayaga, Pushkara and Gaya, etc. They go to the most sacred Kurukshetra at the time of solar eclipse, but Shukla-tirtha is said to be sacred on all occasions. By seeing it, by touching its sacred waters, and thereby performing charities, practising penances, performing sacrifices, keeping up fasts, and by observing other similar austerities, the devotee gets the greatest of the boons.

## \|\| 192.14-16 \|\|

*śuklatīrthaṃ mahāpuṇyaṃ narmadāyāṃ vyavasthitam \|*  
*cāṇakyo nāma rājarṣiḥ siddhiṃ tatra samāgataḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*etatkṣetraṃ suvipulaṃ yojanaṃ vṛttasaṃsthitam \|*  
*śuklatīrthaṃ mahāpuṇyaṃ sarvapāpapraṇāśanam \|\| 15 \|\|*

*pādapāgreṇa dṛṣṭena brahmahatyāṃ vyapohati \|*  
*jagatīdarśanāccaiva bhrūṇahatyāṃ vyapohati \|\| 16 \|\|*

14-16. The Shukla-tirtha in the Narmada is the giver of the greatest boons. There Rajarishi Chanakya attained Siddhi. This sacred place — the dispeller of all ills — is most charming. It extends to a yojana in a circle. By the sight of the branches of the trees growing there one becomes cleansed of the sin of having killed a Brahmana; and by the sight of its sacred land one gets freed from the sin of infanticide.

## \|\| 192.17-19 \|\|

*ahaṃ tatra ṛṣiśreṣṭha tiṣṭhāmi hyumayā saha \|*  
*vaiśākhe caitramāse tu kṛṣṇapakṣe caturdaśī \|\| 17 \|\|*

*kailāsāccāpi niṣkramya tatra saṃnihito hyaham \|*  
*daityadānavagandharvāḥ siddhavidyādharāstathā \|\| 18 \|\|*

*gaṇāścāpsaraso nāgāḥ sarve devāḥ samāgatāḥ \|*  
*gaganasthāstu tiṣṭhanti vimānaiḥ sārvakāmikaiḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

17-19. O, good Rishis! on the fourth day of the dark fortnight in the months of Vaishakha and Chaitra, I go to reside there in company of my consort Parvati after leaving Kailasha. There also the demons, the Devas, the Siddhas, the Gandharvas, the Vidyadharas, the nymphs, the serpents, they all seated in their Vimanas stay on the aerial tract for the fulfilment of their aims.

## \|\| 192.26-29 \|\|

*śuklatīrthaṃ mahāpuṇyamṛṣisiddhaniṣevitam \|*  
*tatra snātvā naro rājanna punarjanmabhāgbhavet \|\| 26 \|\|*

*snātvā vai śuklatīrthe tu hyarcayedvṛṣabhadhvajam \|*  
*kapālapūraṇaṃ kṛtvā tuṣyatyatra maheśvaraḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

*ardhanārīśvaraṃ devaṃ paṭe bhaktyā likhāpayet \|*  
*śaṅkhatūryaninādaiśca brahmaghoṣaiśca sadvijaiḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

*jāgaraṃ kārayettatra nṛtyagītādimaṅgalaiḥ \|*  
*prabhāte śuklatīrthe tu snānaṃ vai devatārcanam \|\| 29 \|\|*

26-29. The devotees going there with a right frame of mind become purified like the cloth washed by the washerman. The Shukla-tirtha washes off all the sins of one’s lifetime. O Markandeya! by bathing at that sacred place and by performing charities there, one gets the highest of boons. In fact, neither there is nor will there ever be a sacred place to match with it. The sins committed during the first period of life are consumed by observing a fast of 24 hours. The merits that accrue there, by places. There one who bathes Lord Shiva in clarified butter on the 14th day of the dark fortnight during the month of Kartika and observes a fast for the night, goes to the domain of Suva along with his ancestors of 21 generations and also becomes liberated from the cycle of births.

This most sacred Shukla-tirtha is adored by the Rishis, one who bathes there is not re-born. There after bathing one should worship Shiva. The ardhanga image of the Lord and the Goddess should be inscribed on a slab of wood and worshipped, accompanied by the music of conches and cymbals and the recitations of the Vedas. The devotee should not sleep in the night. He should observe festivities and get sacred songs sung. On the following morning he should bathe at the Shukla-tirtha and worship Shiva again.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — …. Half-body. The composite image consisting of half Shiva and half Parvati blended into one form.

## \|\| 192.30 \|\|

*ācāryānbhojayetpaścācchivavrataparāñśucīn \|*  
*dakṣiṇāṃ ca yathāśakti vittaśāṭhyaṃ vivarjayet \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Afterwards he should feed the devotees of Shiva and give them presents according to his means without stint.

## \|\| 192.31-32 \|\|

*pradakṣiṇaṃ tataḥ kṛtvā śanairdevāntikaṃ vrajet \|*  
*evaṃ vai kurute yastu tasya puṇyaphalaṃ śṛṇu \|\| 31 \|\|*

*divyayānaṃ samārūḍho gīyamāno'psarogaṇaiḥ \|*  
*śivatulyabalopetastiṣṭhatyābhūtasaṃplavam \|\| 32 \|\|*

31-32. Then he should after circumambulating that sacred place go to Shiva’s temple. One who does this goes to heaven where he resides till the destruction of the universe in company of the nymphs seated in an aerial chariot.

## \|\| 192.33-34 \|\|

*śuklatīrthe tu yā nārī dadāti kanakaṃ śubham \|*  
*ghṛtena snāpayeddevaṃ kumāraṃ cāpi pūjayet \|\| 33 \|\|*

*evaṃ yā kurute bhaktyā tasyāḥ puṇyaphalaṃ śṛṇu \|*  
*modate śarvalokasthā yāvadindrā ścaturdaśa \|\| 34 \|\|*

33-34. The lady who gives away gold in charity at Shukla-tirtha, and bathes Shiva devoutfully with clarified butter and also worships Svamikartika, resides in the realm of the Lord during the sway of 14 Indras.

## \|\| 192.35-36 \|\|

*paurṇamāsyāṃ caturdaśyāṃ saṃkrāntau viṣuve tathā \|*  
*snātvā tu sopavāsaḥ sanvijitātmā samāhitaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

*dānaṃ dadyādyathāśaktyā prīyatāṃ hariśaṃkarau \|*  
*evaṃ tīrthaprabhāveṇa sarvaṃ bhavati cākṣayam \|\| 36 \|\|*

35-36. One who gives away charities after bathing on day of the full moon, the fourth day of a fortnight, and Sankranti, according to his means, pleases Lords Vishnu and Shiva. In such a way the charities performed there beget manifold blessings.

## \|\| 192.37-38 \|\|

*anāthaṃ durgataṃ vipraṃ nāthavantamathāpi vā \|*  
*udvāhayati yastīrthe tasya puṇyaphalaṃ śṛṇu \|\| 37 \|\|*

*yāvattadro masaṃkhyā ca tatprasūtikuleṣu ca \|*  
*tāvadvarṣasahasrāṇi śivaloke mahīyate \|\| 38 \|\|*

37-38. One who participates in the marriage of a poor or a wealthy Brahmana at that sacred place, remains in the realm of Shiva for as many years as there are hair on the person of that Brahmana or, even on the offspring begotten by that married couple.

## Chapter 193

## \|\| 193.1-2 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca*  
*tatastvanarakaṃ gacchetsnānaṃ tatra samācaret \|*  
*snātamātro narastatra narakaṃ ca na paśyati \|\| 193.1 \|\|*

*tasya tīrthasya māhātmyaṃ śṛṇu tvaṃ pāṇḍunandana \|*  
*tasmiṃstīrthe tu rājendra yasyāsthīni vinikṣ̣ipet \|\| 193.2 \|\|*

*vilayaṃ yānti pāpāni rūpavājāyate naraḥ \|*

Markandeya said- Those who go and bathe at the Anaraka-tirtha, never sees the hell. The one whose bones are deposited in that sacred tlrtha becomes purified of all his sins and is reborn as a most handsome man by the glory of that tirtha.

## \|\| 193.3-4 \|\|

*gotīrthaṃ tu tato gatvā sarvapāpātpramucyate \|\| 193.3 \|\|*

*tato gacchettu rājendra kapilātīrthamuttamam \|*  
*tatra snātvā naro rājangosahasraphalaṃ labhet \|\| 193.4 \|*

Thereafter one should go to Go-tirtha where he is liberated from all his sins. О king! then those who go to Kapila-tnr.ia get the benefit of having given away a thousand cows in charity.

## \|\| 193.5-7 \|\|

*jyeṣ̣ṭhamāse tu saṃprāpte caturdaśyāṃ viśeṣ̣ataḥ \|*  
*tatropoṣ̣ya naro bhaktyā kapilāṃ yaḥ prayacchati \|\| 193.5 \|\|*

*ghṛtena dīpaṃ prajvālya ghṛtena snāpayecchivam \|*  
*saghṛtaṃ śrīphalaṃ jagdhvā dattvā cānte pradakṣ̣iṇam \|\| 193.6 \|\|*

*ghaṇṭābharaṇasaṃyuktāṃ kapilāṃ yaḥ prayacchati \|*  
*śivatulyabalo bhūtvā naivāsau jāyate punaḥ \|\| 193.7 \|\|*

One who observes a fast there chiefly on the fourth day of the month of Jyestha and gives away a milch cow adorned with bells and cloth, with devotion, and lits up a wick in clarified butter and bathes Mahadeva in clarified butter and eats coconut and clarified butter, becomes valiant like the Lord Siva and resides in His realm and is never re-bom.

## \|\| 193.8-12 \|\|

*aṅgārakadine prāpte caturthyāṃ tu viśeṣ̣ataḥ \|*  
*pūjayettu śivaṃ bhaktyā brāhmaṇebhyaśca bhojanam \|\| 193.8 \|\|*

*aṅgārakanavamyāṃ tu amāyāṃ ca viśeṣ̣ataḥ \|*  
*snāpayettatra yatnena rūpavānsubhago bhavet \|\| 193.9 \|\|*

*ghṛtena snāpayelliṅgaṃ pūjayedbhaktito dvijān \|*  
*puṣ̣pakeṇa vimānena sahasraiḥ parivāritaḥ \|\| 193.10 \|\|*

*śaivaṃ padamavāpnoti yatra cābhimataṃ bhavet \|*  
*akṣ̣ayaṃ modate kālaṃ yathā rudra stathaiva saḥ \|\| 193.11 \|\|*

*yadā tu karmasaṃyogānmartyalokamupāgataḥ \|*  
*rājā bhavati dharmiṣ̣ṭho rūpavāñjāyate kule \|\| 193.12 \|\|*

On the fourth day of a fortnight falling on Tuesday, one who feeds the Brahmanas after devoutfully worshipping the Lord Siva and one who bathes Siva in clarified butter on the ninth day of a fortnight and on the Amavasya day falling on a Tuesday and then feeds the Brahmanas, goes to the domain of Siva seated in the Puspaka chariot where he enjoys like Rudra and on the completion of his virtues is reborn as a virtuous, handsome and powerful king. Such is the glory of the Go-tirtha.

## \|\| 193.13-14 \|\|

*tato gacchecca rājendra ṛṣ̣itīrthamanuttamam \|*  
*tṛṇabindurnāma ṛṣ̣iḥ śāpadagdho vyavasthitaḥ \|\| 193.13 \|\|*

*tattīrthasya prabhāveṇa śāpamukto'bhavaddvijaḥ \|*  
*tato gacchettu rājendra gaṅgeśvaramanuttamam \|\| 193.14 \|\|*

О best of kings! then the sacred Rsi-tlrtha should be visited. In ancient times the sage Tmabindu overpowered by his ills fixed up his abode there. By the glory of the tlrtha he was liberated from his ills as well as from the effects of the curses pronounced upon him. Afterwards Ganges'vara-tlrtha should also be visited.

## \|\| 193.15-17 \|\|

*śrāvaṇe māsi saṃprāpte kṛṣ̣ṇapakṣ̣e caturdaśī \|*  
*snātamātro narastatra rudra loke mahīyate \|\| 193.15 \|\|*

*pitriṇāṃ tarpaṇaṃ kṛtvā mucyate ca ṛṇatrayāt \|*  
*gaṅgeśvarasamīpe tu gaṅgāvadanamuttamam \|\| 193.16 \|\|*

*akāmo vā sakāmo vā tatra snātvā tu mānavaḥ \|*  
*ājanmajanitaiḥ pāpairmucyate nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 193.17 \|\|*

Those who bathe there on the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight in the month of Sravana go to Rudraloka. One who offers libations of water to the manes is liberated from all the three debts1. The most beautiful Gahga-vadana tlrtha is close to Ganges'vara where by bathing one is undoubtedly freed from all his sins.

## \|\| 193.18-19 \|\|

*tatra tīrthe naraḥ snātvā vrajedvai yatra śaṃkaraḥ \|*  
*sarvadā parvadivase snānaṃ tatra samācaret \|\| 193.18 \|\|*

*pitriṇāṃ tarpaṇaṃ kṛtvā hyaśvamedhaphalaṃ labhet \|*  
*prayāge yatphalam dṛṣ̣ṭaṃ śaṃkareṇa mahātmanā \|\| 193.19 \|\|*

One who bathes there goes before the Lord Siva. One who bathes and offers libations to the manes on the occasion of each festival, at that sacred places, gets the benefit of Asvamedha sacrifice. The devotee gets all the benefits that accrue at Prayaga as detailed by Sankaracarya.

## \|\| 193.20-22 \|\|

*tadeva nikhilaṃ dṛṣ̣ṭaṃ gaṅgāvadanasaṃgame \|*  
*tasyaiva paścime sthāne samīpe nātidūrataḥ \|\| 193.20 \|\|*

*daśāśvamedhajananaṃ triṣ̣u lokeṣ̣u viśrutam \|*  
*upoṣ̣ya rajanīmekāṃ māsi bhādra pade tathā \|\| 193.21 \|\|*

*amāyāṃ ca naraḥ snātvā vrajate yatra śaṃkaraḥ \|*  
*sarvadā parvadivase snānaṃ tatra samācaret \|\| 193.22 \|\|*

To the west of Gangavadana is the sacred Dasasvamedha-janana-tlrtha which is known in all the three realms. One who observes a fast for a night in the month of Bhadra and one who bathes there on Amavasya goes to the realm of Siva. One should bathe their on all festivals.

## \|\| 193.23-25 \|\|

*pitriṇāṃ tarpaṇaṃ kṛtvā cāśvamedhaphalaṃ labhet \|*  
*daśāśvamedhātpaścimato bhṛgurbrāhmaṇasattamaḥ \|\| 193.23 \|\|*

*divyaṃ varṣ̣asahasraṃ tu īśvaraṃ paryupāsate \|*  
*valmīkaveṣ̣ṭitaścāsau pakṣ̣iṇāṃ ca niketanaḥ \|\| 193.24 \|\|*

*āścaryaṃ sumahajжātamumāyāḥ śaṃkarasya ca \|*  
*gaurī papraccha deveśaṃ ko'yamevaṃ tu saṃsthitaḥ \|*  
*devo vā dānavo vā'tha kathayasva maheśvara \|\| 193.25 \|\|*

One who offers libations to the manes there gets all the merits of performing an Asvamedha sacrifice. The sage Bhrgu practised austerities to the west of Dasasvamedha for a thousand Divine years. He was covered with ant hills and nests of birds which amazed the Lord Siva and His consort Parvatl. Parvatl asked the Lord as to who he was. She said- “Is the Deva or demon?”

## \|\| 193.26 \|\|

*maheśvara uvāca*  
*bhṛgurnāma dvijaśreṣ̣ṭha ṛṣ̣īṇāṃ pravaro muniḥ \|*  
*māṃ dhyāyate samādhistho varaṃ prārthayate priye \|\| 193.26 \|\|*

Lord said, “O Dear Parvatl, He is the great Brahmana sage named Bhrgu, who meditated on me in contemplation for a boon”.

## \|\| 193.27 \|\|

*tataḥ prahasitā devī īśvaraṃ pratyabhāṣ̣ata \|*  
*dhūmavattacchikhā jātā tato'dyāpi na tuṣ̣yase \|*  
*durārādhyo'si tena tvaṃ nātra kāryā vicāraṇā \|\| 193.27 \|\|*

Then Goddess smilingly said to Siva, “His top-knot has become like smoke and even then you are not compassionate on him. Indeed you are very hard to be moved.”

## \|\| 193.28 \|\|

*maheśvara uvāca*  
*na jānāsi mahādevi hyayaṃ krodhena veṣ̣ṭitaḥ \|*  
*darśayāmi yathātathyaṃ pratyayaṃ te karomyaham \|\| 193.28 \|\|*

The Lord said- “O Devi! you do not know. This sage is foil of wrath which I shall show you practically.”

## \|\| 193.29 \|\|

*tataḥ smṛto'tha devena dharmarūpo vṛṣ̣astadā \|*  
*smaraṇāttasya devasya vṛṣ̣aḥ śīghramupasthitaḥ \|*  
*vadaṃstu mānuṣ̣īṃ vācamādeśo dīyatāṃ prabho \|\| 193.29 \|\|*

The Lord then thought of Dharma in the form of a bull that appeared then and there, and spoke in human speech- “O Lord! what are your commands for me?”

## \|\| 193.30 \|\|

*bhagavānuvāca*  
*valmīkaṃ tvaṃ khanasvainaṃ vipraṃ bhūmau nipātaya \|*  
*yogasthastu tato dhyāyanbhṛgustena nipātitaḥ \|\| 193.30 \|\|*

*tatkṣ̣aṇātkrodhasaṃtapto hastamutkṣ̣ipya so'śapat \|*

The Lord said- “Remove the anthills and the nests and then throw this Brahmana down on the ground.” Afterwards the bull threw down the sage on the ground when the latter overcome by anger pronounced the following curse on him.

## \|\| 193.31-32 \|\|

*evaṃ saṃbhāṣ̣amāṇastu kutra gacchasi bho vṛṣ̣a \|*  
*adyāhaṃ saṃprakopeṇa pralayaṃ tvāṃ naye vṛṣ̣a \|\| 193.31 \|\|*

*dharṣ̣itastu tadā vipraścāntarikṣ̣aṃ gato vṛṣ̣am \|*  
*ākāśe prekṣ̣ate vipra etadadbhutamuttamam \|\| 193.32 \|\|*

*tatra prahasito rudra ṛṣ̣iragre vyavasthitaḥ \|*  
*tṛtīyalocanaṃ dṛṣ̣ṭvā vailakṣ̣yātpatito bhuvi \|*

“Bull! whither are you going now? I shall destroy you by my fury.” Having said so, the sage Bhrgu rose to heaven, on seeing it the Lord stood in front of the sage and brought him down by opening His third eye on him.

## \|\| 193.33-35 \|\|

*praṇamya daṇḍavadbhūmau tuṣ̣ṭāva parameśvaram \|\| 193.33 \|\|*

*praṇipatya bhūtanāthaṃ bhavodbhavaṃ tvāmahaṃ divyarūpam \|*  
*bhavātīto bhuvanapate prabho tu vijñāpaye kiṃcit \|\| 193.34 \|\|*

*tvadguṇanikarānvaktuṃ kaḥ śakto bhavati mānuṣ̣o nāma \|*  
*vāsukirapi hi kadācidvadanasahasraṃ bhavedyasya \|\| 193.35 \|\|*

Then the sage after making his salutations to the Lord adored Him thus- “You are Divine. I am at your mercy. О Lord of all! I devoutfolly pray to You. Indeed none can enunciate Your glory adequately. Even the thousand-faced Sesa cannot do so.

## \|\| 193.36-37 \|\|

*bhaktyā tathā'pi śaṃkara bhuvanapate tvatstutau mukharaḥ \|*  
*vadataḥ kṣ̣amasva bhagavanprasīda me tava caraṇapatitasya \|\| 193.36 \|\|*

*sattvaṃ rajastamastvaṃ sthityutpattyorvināśane deva \|*  
*tvāṃ muktvā bhuvanapate bhuvaneśvara naiva daivataṃ kiṃcit \|\| 193.37 \|*

“Therefore, О Lord! I cannot adequately offer-my prayers to You, but I throw myself at your feet. You be kind to me. О Lord! You fill yourself in with Sattva, Rajas and Tamas gunas on the occasions of Sthiti (existence), Utpatti (creation) and Samhara (destruction), respectively. There is no other Lord than Yourself.

## \|\| 193.38-40 \|\|

*yamaniyamayajñadānavedābhyāsāśca dhāraṇā yogaḥ \|*  
*tvadbhakteḥ sarvamidaṃ nārhati hi kalāsahasrāṃśam \|\| 193.38 \|\|*

*ucchiṣ̣ṭarasarasāyanakhaḍgāñjanapādukāvivarasiddhirvā \|*  
*cihnaṃ bhavavratānāṃ dṛśyati ceha janmani prakaṭam \|\| 193.39 \|\|*

*śāṭhyena namati yadyapi dadāsi tvaṃ bhūtimicchato deva \|*  
*bhaktirbhavabhedakarī mokṣ̣āya vinirmitā nātha \|\| 193.40 \|\|*

“Yama, sacrifices, charities, study of the Vedas, cannot compare even in the smallest measure with devotion for You. Your devotees attain various kinds of Siddhis. Although your devotee does not become meek in his ignorance, still You bless him. Only devotion for You, can carry one across the sea of troubles and lead to final beatitude.

## \|\| 193.41-44 \|\|

*paradāraparasvarataṃ paraparibhavaduḥkhaśokasaṃtaptam \|*  
*paravadanavīkṣ̣aṇaparaṃ parameśvaraṃ māṃ paritrāhi \|\| 193.41 \|\|*

*mithyābhimānadagdhaṃ kṣ̣aṇabhaṅguradehavilasitaṃ krūram \|*  
*kupathābhimukhaṃ patitaṃ tvaṃ mā pāpātparitrāhi \|\| 193.42 \|\|*

*dīne dvijagaṇasārthe bandhujanenaiva dūṣ̣itā hyāśā \|*  
*tṛṣ̣ṇā tathā'pi śaṃkara kiṃ mūḍhaṃ māṃ viḍambayati \|\| 193.43 \|\|*

*tṛṣ̣ṇāṃ harasva śīghraṃ lakṣ̣mīṃ pradatsva yāvadāsinīṃ nityam \|*  
*chindhi madamohapāśānuttāraya māṃ mahādeva \|\| 193.44 \|\|*

“O Lord of Devas! be merciful to me inspite of my conceit, wickedness and viciousness. Protect this humble devotee of you, inspite of his being full of lust for the women and pelf of others; overcome by contempt, pain and sufferings. О Lord of the Universe! desires are killing this ignorant devotee of you. Please, do drive away my carvings by granting me accomplishment. О Mahadeva! cut the noose of conceit and delusion and work out my salvation.”

## \|\| 193.45 \|\|

*karuṇābhyudayaṃ nāma stotramidaṃ sarvasiddhidaṃ divyam \|*  
*yaḥ paṭhati bhaktiyuktastasya tuṣ̣yedbhṛgoryathā ca śivaḥ \|\| 193.45 \|\|*

The above Karunabhyudaya prayer is the giver of all divine benefits. One who reads it with devotion, pleases the Lord Mahadeva as they pleased on Bhrgu.

## \|\| 193.46 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca*  
*ahaṃ tuṣ̣ṭo'smi te vatsa prārthayasvepsitaṃ varam \|*  
*umayā sahito devo varaṃ tasya hyadāpayat \|\| 193.46 \|\|*

Markandeya said- On hearing the above prayer the Lord said, “I am pleased with you. Ask me what you wish.”

## \|\| 193.47 \|\|

*bhṛguruvāca*  
*yadi tuṣ̣ṭo'si deveśa yadi deyo varo mama \|*  
*rudra vedī bhavedevametatsaṃpādayasva me \|\| 193.47 \|\|*

Bhrgu said- “O Deva! if You are pleased with me and wishes to confer a boon on me, let me be the knower of Rudra, and let this spot be sacred after my name.”

## \|\| 193.48 \|\|

*īśvara uvāca*  
*evaṃ bhavatu viprendra krodhastvā na bhaviṣ̣yati \|*  
*na pitāputrayoścaiva tvaikamatyaṃ bhaviṣ̣yati \|\| 193.48 \|\|*

Siva said- “Be it so, О best of twice-born! now you will be free from anger. You will have harmony with your father and sons.”

## \|\| 193.49-51 \|\|

*tadāprabhṛti brahmādyā sarve devāḥ sakiṃnarāḥ \|*  
*upāsate bhṛgostīrthaṃ tuṣ̣ṭo yatra maheśvaraḥ \|\| 193.49 \|\|*

*darśanāttasya tīrthasya sadyaḥ pāpātpramucyate \|*  
*avaśāḥ svavaśā vā'pi mriyante yatra jantavaḥ \|\| 193.50 \|\|*

*guhyātiguhyā sugatisteṣ̣āṃ niḥsaṃśayaṃ bhavet \|*  
*etatkṣ̣etraṃ suvipulaṃ sarvapāpapraṇāśanam \|\| 193.51 \|\|*

Since then all the Devas including Brahma and the Kinnaras adore that Bhrgu tlrtha. Sins disappear by the mere sight of that tlrtha. Those who give up their lives there, attain bliss. This tlrtha is the most extensive and the dispeller of all sins.

## \|\| 193.52-58 \|\|

*tatra snātvā divaṃ yānti ye mṛtāste'punarbhavāḥ \|*  
*upānahau ca cchatraṃ ca deyamannaṃ ca kāñcanam \|\| 193.52 \|\|*

*bhojanaṃ ca yathāśaktyā hyakṣ̣ayaṃ ca tathā bhavet \|*  
*sūryoparāge yo dadyāddānaṃ caiva yathecchayā \|\| 193.53 \|\|*

*dīyamānaṃ tu taddānamakṣ̣ayaṃ tasya tadbhavet \|*  
*candra sūryoparāgeṣ̣u yatphalaṃ tvamarakaṇṭake \|\| 193.54 \|\|*

*tadeva nikhilaṃ puṇyaṃ bhṛgutīrthe na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*kṣ̣aranti sarvadānāni yajñadānatapaḥkriyāḥ \|\| 193.55 \|\|*

*na kṣ̣arettu tapastaptaṃ bhṛgutīrthe yudhiṣ̣ṭhira \|*  
*yasya vai tapasogreṇa tuṣ̣ṭenaiva tu śaṃbhunā \|\| 193.56 \|\|*

*sāṃnidhyaṃ tatra kathitaṃ bhṛgutīrthe narādhipa \|*  
*prakhyātaṃ triṣ̣u lokeṣ̣u yatra tuṣ̣ṭo maheśvaraḥ \|\| 193.57 \|\|*

*evaṃ tu vadato devīṃ bhṛgutīrthamanuttamam \|*  
*na jānanti narā mūḍhā viṣ̣ṇumāyāvimohitāḥ \|\| 193.58 \|\|*

Those who bathe there go to heaven and those who die there are not re-bom. Those who give away shoes, umbrellas, grain, gold and edibles in charity according to their means, get manifold blessings. Those who give charities on the occasion of solar eclipse also get many benefits. The benefits that accrue at Amarakantaka on the occasion of solar and lunar eclipses, are obtained without doubt at Bhrgu-tlrtha. All the stores of austerities and charities decline in process of time, but the penances practised at Bhrgu-tlrtha are never exhausted. The Lord Mahadeva on account of His having become pleased with Bhrgu stays at that tlrtha and so it is renowned in all the three worlds. О Devi! inspite of all this, people do not know the full glory of Bhrgu-tlrtha owing to the delusion caused by the Visnu.

## \|\| 193.59-61 \|\|

*narmadāyāṃ sthitaṃ divyaṃ bhṛgutīrthaṃ narādhipa \|*  
*bhṛgutīrthasya māhātmyaṃ yaḥ śṛṇoti naraḥ kvacit \|\| 193.59 \|\|*

*vimuktaḥ sarvapāpebhyo rudra lokaṃ sa gacchati \|*  
*tato gacchettu rājendra gautameśvaramuttamam \|\| 193.60 \|\|*

*tatra snātvā naro rājannupavāsaparāyaṇaḥ \|*  
*kāñcanena vimānena brahmaloke mahīyate \|\| 193.61 \|\|*

О king! The sacred tlrtha Bhrgu is situated on the banks of the Narmada. One who hears the glory of this place, goes to the realm of Rudra on being liberated from all sins. Beyond it, is the famous Gautamesvara-tlrtha where by bathing and keeping up fast one goes to Brahmaloka seated on a golden chariot.

## \|\| 193.62-64 \|\|

*dhautapāpaṃ tato gacchetkṣ̣etraṃ yatra vṛṣ̣eṇa tu \|*  
*narmadāyāṃ kṛtaṃ rājansarvapātakanāśanam \|\| 193.62 \|\|*

*tatra tīrthe naraḥ snātvā brahmahatyāṃ vimuñcati \|*  
*tasmiṃstīrthe tu rājendra prāṇatyāgaṃ karoti yaḥ \|\| 193.63 \|\|*

*caturbhujastrinetraśca śivatulyabalo bhavet \|*  
*vasetkalpāyutaṃ sāgraṃ śivatulyaparākramaḥ \|\| 193.64 \|\|*

*kālena mahatā prāptaḥ pṛthivyāmekarāḍbhavet \|*

Afterwards the devotee should go to Dhauta-papa tlrtha where Vrsabha washed off his sins. One who bathes there is freed from the sin of having killed a Brahmana. One who gives up his life there becomes valiant like Siva and gets four hands and three eyes and remains in the realm of Siva for ten thousand years of the gods. On being re-bom, he becomes a king.

## \|\| 193.65-67 \|\|

*tato gacchecca rājendra airaṇḍītīthamuttamam \|\| 193.65 \|\|*

*prayāge yatphalaṃ dṛṣ̣ṭaṃ mārkaṇḍeyena bhāṣ̣itam \|*  
*tatphalaṃ labhate rājansnātamātro hi mānavaḥ \|\| 193.66 \|\|*

*māsi bhādra pade caiva śuklapakṣ̣e caturdaśī \|*  
*upoṣ̣ya rajanīmekāṃ tasminsnānaṃ samācaret \|*  
*yamadūtairna bādhyeta rudra lokaṃ sa gacchati \|\| 193.67 \|\|*

The devotee should go to the sacred Airandi-tirtha. It brings the same benefits as are obtained by bathing at Prayaga. One who bathes there on the fourteenth day of the bright fortnight during the month of Bhadrapada after observing a fast for a night, is not persecuted by the attendants of Yama and goes to the realm of Rudra.

## \|\| 193.68 \|\|

*tato gacchettu rājendra siddho yatra janārdanaḥ \|*  
*hiraṇyadvīpavikhyātaṃ sarvapāpapraṇāśanam \|\| 193.68 \|\|*

Then the sacred Hiranyadvlpa should be visited. It is also the dispeller of all ills. Those who bathe there become wealthy and handsome.

## \|\| 193.69-71 \|\|

*tatra snātvā naro rājandhanavānrūpavānbhavet \|*  
*tato gacchettu rājendra tīrthaṃ kanakhalaṃ mahat \|\| 193.69 \|\|*

*garuḍena tapastaptaṃ tasmiṃstīrthe narādhipa \|*  
*prakhyātaṃ triṣ̣u lokeṣ̣u yoginī tatra tiṣ̣ṭhati \|\| 193.70 \|\|*

*krīḍate yogibhiḥ sārdhaṃ śivena saha nṛtyati \|*  
*tatra snātvā naro rājanrudra loke mahīyate \|\| 193.71 \|\|*

Afterwards the most sacred Kankhala should be visited where Garuda practised austerities. Yoginls reside there and they please themselves in the company of the Yogis and dance with Siva. This tirtha is renowned in all the three worlds. Those who bathe there go to the Rudraloka.

## \|\| 193.72-75 \|\|

*tato gacchettu rājendra haṃsatīrthamanuttamam \|*  
*haṃsāstatra vinirmuktā gatā ūrdhvaṃ na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 193.72 \|\|*

*tato gacchettu rājendra siddho yatra janārdanaḥ \|*  
*vārāhaṃ rūpamāsthāya arcitaḥ parameśvaraḥ \|\| 193.73 \|\|*

*varāhatīrthe naraḥ snātvā dvādaśyāṃ tu viśeṣ̣ataḥ \|*  
*viṣ̣ṇulokamavāpnoti narakaṃ na ca paśyati \|\| 193.74 \|\|*

*tato gacchettu rājendra candra tīrthamanuttamam \|*  
*paurṇamāsyāṃ viśeṣ̣eṇa snānaṃ tatra samācaret \|\| 193.75 \|\|*

*snātamātro narastatra candra loke mahīyate \|*

Afterwards Hamsa-tlrtha should be visited where the liberated Paramahamsasi undoubtedly ascend to higher realms. The place where Lord Janardana has been worshipped in His Varaha incarnation is known as the Varaha-tlrtha. One who bathes there on the 12th day of a fortnight goes to the region of Visnu and does not go to hell. Then the most sacred Candra-tlrtha should be visited. There one should bathe chiefly on the full moon day by doing which one goes to the Lunar region.

## \|\| 193.76-79 \|\|

*dakṣ̣iṇena tu dvāreṇa kanyātīrthaṃ tu viśrutam \|\| 193.76 \|\|*

*śuklapakṣ̣e tṛtīyāyāṃ snānaṃ tatra samācaret \|*  
*praṇipatya tu ceśānaṃ balistena prasīdati \|\| 193.77 \|\|*

*hariścandra puraṃ divyamantarikṣ̣e ca dṛśyate \|*  
*śakradhvaje samāvṛtte gupte nāgariketane \|\| 193.78 \|\|*

*narmadāsalilaughena tarūnsaṃplāvayiṣ̣yati \|*  
*asminsthāne nivāsaḥ syādviṣ̣ṇuḥ śaṃkaramabravīt \|\| 193.79 \|\|*

*dvīpeśvare naraḥ snātvā labhedbahu suvarṇakam \|*

On the right bank of the Candra-tlrtha is the Kanya-tlrtha where one should bathe on the third day of the bright fortnight. If salutations are made to Lord Siva there the demon Bali becomes pleased. When the people are fast sleep during the night, then sometimes a rainbow makes its appearance in which the city of the king Hariscandra is visible. The trees are drowned in the waters of the Narmada. In ancient times, Lord Visnu said to Siva that the place should be fixed as His residence, since then Dvlpes'vara-tlrtha exists there by bathing where one gets plenty of gold.

## \|\| 193.80-81 \|\|

*tato gacchettu rājendra kanyātīrthe susaṃgame \|\| 193.80 \|\|*

*snātamātro narastatra devyāḥ sthānamavāpnuyāt \|*  
*devatīrthaṃ tato gacchetsarvatīrthamanuttamam \|\| 193.81 \|\|*

*tatra snātvā tu rājendra daivataiḥ saha modate \|*

One who bathes at the confluence of the Kanya-tirtha goes to the realm of the Goddess Parvatl. Then Deva-tlrtha should be visited, which is the most sacred of all, bathing where one goes and enjoys in the company of the Devas.

## \|\| 193.82-84 \|\|

*tato gacchecca rājendra śikhitīrthamanuttamam \|\| 193.82 \|\|*

*yattatra dīyate dānaṃ sarvaṃ koṭiguṇaṃ bhavet \|*  
*aparapakṣ̣e tvamāyāṃ tu snānaṃ tatra samācaret \|\| 193.83 \|\|*

*brāhmaṇaṃ bhojayedekaṃ koṭirbhavati bhojitā \|*  
*bhṛgutīrthe tu rājendra tīrthakoṭirvyavasthitā \|\| 193.84 \|\|*

Then the sacred Sikhi-tirtha should be visited where the charities performed multiply infinitely. One who feeds a single Brahmana there after bathing on the Amavasya day gets the benefit of having fed a crore of them.

## \|\| 193.85-86 \|\|

*akāmo vā sakāmo vā tatra snānaṃ samācaret \|*  
*aśvamedhamavāpnoti daivataiḥ saha modate \|\| 193.85 \|\|*

*tatra siddhiṃ parāṃ prāpto bhṛgustu munipuṃgavaḥ \|*  
*avatāraḥ kṛtastatra śaṃkareṇa mahātmanā \|\| 193.86 \|\|*

A group of tirthas lie near Bhrgu tlrtha where one should bathe with or without motive. By bathing there one gets the benefits of performing As'vemedha sacrifice and then goes and enjoys in the company of the Devas. Lord Siva assumed His form there when the sage Bhrgu attained his siddhi.

## Chapter 194

## \|\| 194.1-3 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca*  
*tato gacchettu rājendra hyaṅkuśeśvaramuttamam \|*  
*darśanāttasya devasya mucyate sarvapātakaiḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*tato gacchecca rājendra narmadeśvaramuttamam \|*  
*tatra snātvā naro rājansvargaloke mahīyate \|\| 2 \|\|*

*aśvatīrthaṃ tato gacchetsnānaṃ tatra samācaret \|*  
*subhago darśanīyaśca bhogavāñjāyate naraḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

1-3. Markandeya said: — King! the devotee should next visit the Ahkude4vara-tirtha,’ by means of which he becomes freed from all sins. Then Narmade4vara-tirtha should be visited by bathing where one goes to heaven. Afterwards a visit should be paid to Ashva-tirtha by bathing there one becomes handsome and full of lustre.

## \|\| 194.4-6 \|\|

*paitāmahaṃ tato gacchedbrahmaṇā nirmitaṃ purā \|*  
*tatra snātvā naro bhaktyā pitṛpiṇḍaṃ tu dāpayet \|\| 4 \|\|*

*tiladarbhavimiśraṃ tu hyudakaṃ tatra dāpayet \|*  
*tasya tīrthaprabhāveṇa sarvaṃ bhavati cākṣayam \|\| 5 \|\|*

*sāvitrītīrthamāsādya yastu snānaṃ samācaret \|*  
*vidhūya sarvapāpāni brahmaloke mahīyate \|\| 6 \|\|*

4-6. The Pitamaha-tirtha made by Brahma where the merits accruing from the libations to the manes performed devoutfully with sesamum and Kusha become infinitely multiplied. One who bathes at the Savitri-tirtha goes to the domain of Brahma after being liberated from his sins.

## \|\| 194.7 \|\|

*manorahaṃ tato gacchettīrthaṃ paramaśobhanam \|*  
*tatra snātvā naro rājanpitṛloke mahīyate \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Those who bathe at the sacred Manohara-tirtha go to the realm of the Pitris.

## \|\| 194.8 \|\|

*tato gacchecca rājendra mānasaṃ tīrthamuttamam \|*  
*tatra snātvā naro rājanrudra loke mahīyate \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Afterwards Manasa-tirtha should be visited, by bathing there one goes to Rudraloka.

## \|\| 194.9-10 \|\|

*tato gacchecca rājendra kuñjatīrthamanuttamam \|*  
*vikhyātaṃ triṣu lokeṣu sarvapāpapraṇāśanam \|\| 9 \|\|*

*yānyānkāmayate kāmānpaśuputradhanāni ca \|*  
*prāpnuyāttāni sarvāṇi tatra snātvā narādhipa \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. Then Kunja-tirtha should be visited which is also renowned in all the three worlds as the dispeller of all ills. There one gets live stock, son, wealth and in fact anything that he desires for.

## \|\| 194.11-20 \|\|

*tato gacchettu rājendra tridaśajyotiviśrutam \|*  
*yatra tā ṛṣikanyāstu tapo'tapyanta suvratāḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*bhartā bhavatu sarvāsāmīśvaraḥ prabhuravyayaḥ \|*  
*prītastāsāṃ mahādevo daṇḍarūpadharo haraḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*vikṛtānanabībhatsurvratī tīrthamupāgataḥ \|*  
*tatra kanyā mahārāja varayanparameśvaraḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*kanyāmṛṣervarayataḥ kanyādānaṃ pradīyatām \|*  
*tīthaṃ tatra mahārāja ṛṣikanyeti viśrutam \|\| 14 \|\|*

*tatra snātvā naro rājansarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate \|*  
*tato gacchecca rājendra svarṇabindu tviti smṛtam \|\| 15 \|\|*

*tatra snātvā naro rājandurgatiṃ na ca paśyati \|*  
*apsareśaṃ tato gacchetsnānaṃ tatra samācaret \|\| 16 \|\|*

*krīḍate nāgalokastho'psarobhiḥ saha modate \|*  
*tato gacchettu rājendra narakaṃ tīrthamuttamam \|\| 17 \|\|*

*tatra snātvārcayeddevaṃ narakaṃ ca na paśyati \|*  
*bhārabhūtiṃ tato gacchedupavāsaparo janaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*etattīrthaṃ samāsādya cāvatāraṃ tu śāṃbhavam \|*  
*arcayitvā virūpākṣaṃ rudra loke mahīyate \|\| 19 \|\|*

*asmiṃstīrthe naraḥ snātvā bhārabhūtau mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*yatra yatra mṛtasyāpi dhruvaṃ gāṇeśvarī gatiḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

11-20. Then Tridashajyoti-tirtha, where the daughters of the Rishis practised severe austerities, should be visited. By the pleasure of the Lord Mahadeva, all those girls were blessed to have Lord Krishna as their husband. Beyond it is the Rishikanya-tirtha where once upon a time some one was asking for a girl from a Rishi where he was ultimately married to her. One who bathes there is freed from all sins. Further on is the Svarnavindu-tirtha by bathing where one does not undergo any reverse of fortune. Then comes the Apsaresha-tirtha where one should go and bathe; by virtue of which he goes to Nagaloka and enjoys there in company of the nymphs, Then the Naraka-tirtha should be visited where by bathing and worshipping Shiva one does not go to hell. One who observes a fast Bharabhutitirtha and then worships Shiva, goes to Rudraloka. Those who bathe at Bharabhuti become the attendant of Shiva after their death.

## \|\| 194.21-22 \|\|

*kārtikasya tu māsasya hyarcayitvā maheśvaram \|*  
*aśvamedhāddaśaguṇaṃ pravadanti manīṣinaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*dīpakānāṃ śataṃ tatra ghṛtapūrṇaṃ tu dāpayet \|*  
*vimānaiḥ sūryasaṃkāśairvrajate yatra śaṃkaraḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

21-22. On the 14th day in the month of Kartika one who worships Shiva there gets ten times the merits of having performed the Ashvamedha sacrifice.

Those who lit up a hundred wicks in lamps filled with clarified butter ascend to the realm of Shiva seated in a chariot shining like the sun.

## \|\| 194.23-25 \|\|

*vṛṣabhaṃ yaḥ prayacchettu śaṅkhakundendusaprabham \|*  
*vṛṣayuktena yānena rudra lokaṃ sa gacchati \|\| 23 \|\|*

*dhenumekāṃ tu yo dadyāttasmiṃstīrthe narādhipa \|*  
*pāyasaṃ madhusaṃyuktaṃ bhakṣyāṇi vividhāni ca \|\| 24 \|\|*

*yathāśaktyā ca rājendra brāhmaṇānbhojayettataḥ \|*  
*tasya tīrthaprabhāveṇa sarvaṃ koṭiguṇaṃ bhavet \|\| 25 \|\|*

23-25. One who gives away a couch and a bull goes to Rudraloka seated in a chariot drawn by bulls. One who gives away a cow in charity and feeds the Brahmanas with rice cooked in milk and sugar according to his means gets incalculable benefits.

## \|\| 194.26-35 \|\|

*narmadāyā jalaṃ pītvā hyarcayitvā vṛṣadhvajam \|*  
*durgatiṃ ca na paśyanti tasya tīrthaprabhāvataḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*etattīrthaṃ samāsādya yastu prāṇānvimuñcati \|*  
*sarvapāpavinirmukto vrajedvai yatra śaṃkaraḥ \|*  
*jalapraveśaṃ yaḥ kuryāttasmiṃstīrthe narādhipa \|\| 27 \|\|*

*haṃsayuktena yānena brahmalokaṃ sa gacchati \|*  
*yāvaccandra śca sūryaśca himavāṃśca mahodadhiḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

*gaṅgādyāḥ sarito yāvattāvatsvarge mahīyate \|*  
*anāśakaṃ tu yaḥ kuryāttasmiṃstīrthe narādhipa \|\| 29 \|\|*

*garbhavāse tu rājendra na punarjāyate pumān \|*  
*tato gacchettu rājendra āṣāḍhītīrthamuttamam \|\| 30 \|\|*

*tatra snātvā naro rājannindra syārdhāsanaṃ labhet \|*  
*striyāstīrthaṃ tato gacchetsarvapāpapraṇāśanam \|\| 31 \|\|*

*tatrāpi snātamātrasya dhruvaṃ gāṇeśvarī gatiḥ \|*  
*airaṇḍīnarmadayośca saṃgamaṃ lokaviśrutam \|\| 32 \|\|*

*tacca tīrthaṃ mahāpuṇyaṃ sarvapāpapraṇāśanam \|*  
*upavāsaparo bhūtvā nityavrataparāyaṇaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

*tatra snātvā tu rājendra mucyate brahmahatyayā \|*  
*tato gacchecca rājendra narmadodadhisaṃgamam \|\| 34 \|\|*

*jāmadagnyamiti khyātaṃ siddho yatra janārdanaḥ \|*  
*yatreṣṭvā bahubhiryajñairindro devādhipo'bhavat \|\| 35 \|\|*

26-35. One who worships Shiva and drinks the water of the sacred Narmada never fares ill. Be goes to Rudraloka seated in a Vimana, and resides in heaven till the existence of the Moon, the Sun, the Himalaya, the ocean, and the Ganges. One who keeps up a fast there is never subjected to the trial of births. Afterwards Ashadhi-tirtha should be visited, by bathing where one becomes entitled to occupy half the throne of Indra by his side. Then Stri-tirtha the dispeller of all ills should be visited, by bathing where one undoubtedly becomes Ganeshvara. The confluence of Airandi and the Narmada is renowned in all the three worlds where by bathing and observing a fast one becomes freed from the sins of having killed a Brahmana. Then the sacred Jamadagnya at the confluence of the Narmada and the ocean should be visited. There Lord Janardana attained siddhi and Indra became the Lord of the Devas by performing a series of sacrifices. One who bathes there gets three times the benefits of having performed the Ashvamedha sacrifice.

## \|\| 194.36-42 \|\|

*tatra snātvā tu rājendra narmadodadhisaṃgame \|*  
*triguṇaṃ cāśvamedhasya phalaṃ prāpnoti mānavaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

*paścimasyodadheḥ saṃdhau svargadvāravighaṭṭanam \|*  
*tatra devāḥ sagandharvā ṛṣayaḥ siddhacāraṇāḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

*ārādhayanti deveśaṃ trisaṃdhyaṃ vimaleśvaram \|*  
*tatra snātvā naro rājanrudra loke mahīyate \|\| 38 \|\|*

*vimaleśātparaṃ tīrthaṃ na bhūtaṃ na bhaviṣyati \|*  
*tatropavāsaṃ kṛtvā ye paśyanti vimaleśvaram \|\| 39 \|\|*

*saptajanmakṛtaṃ pāpaṃ hitvā yānti śivālayam \|*  
*tato gacchettu rājendra kauśikītīrthamuttamam \|\| 40 \|\|*

*tatra snātvā naro rājannupavāsaparāyaṇaḥ \|*  
*upoṣya rajanīmekāṃ niyato niyatāśanaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

*etattīrthaprabhāveṇa mucyate brahmahatyayā \|*  
*sarvatīrthābhiṣekaṃ tu yaḥ paśyetsāgareśvaram \|\| 42 \|\|*

36-42. On the western boundary of the ocean lies the Svargadvara-tirtha where the Devas, the Siddhas, the Gandharvas, the Rishis and the Charanas worship the Lord Vimaleshvara, Those who bathe there go to Rudraloka. There is no higher tirtha than Vimaleshvara. Those who keep up a fast and then adore Mahadeva at Vimaleshvara are freed from the sins of the past seven lives and go to heaven. Then the sacred Kaushiki-tirtha should be visited where one should keep up a fast for the night after having a bath. By the power of this tirtha the sin of having slain a Brahmana is dispelled. By the mere sight of Lord Sagaresha one gets the benefit of having sprinkled himself with the sacred waters of all the tirthas. There the Lord Mahadeva resides within an area of a yojana.

Merely by the sight of Him one gets the merit of having visited all the sacred places.

## \|\| 194.43-44 \|\|

*yojanābhyantare tiṣṭhannāvarte saṃsthitaḥ śivaḥ \|*  
*taṃ dṛṣṭvā sarvatīrthāni dṛṣṭānyeva na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

*sarvapāpavinirmukto yatra rudra ḥ! sa gacchati \|*  
*narmadāsaṃgamaṃ yāvadyāvaccāmarakaṇṭakam \|\| 44 \|\|*

43-44. After being freed from all sins the devotee goes to Rudraloka. Ten crores of tirthas are said to lie between the confluence of the Narmada and the Amarakantaka, and Rishis reside in each of them.

## \|\| 194.45-47 \|\|

*atrāntare mahārāja tīrthakoṭyo daśa smṛtāḥ \|*  
*tīrthāttīrthāntaraṃ yatra ṛṣikoṭiniṣevitam \|\| 45 \|\|*

*sāgnihotraistu vidvadbhiḥ sarvairdhyānaparāyaṇaiḥ \|*  
*sevitā'nena rājendra tvīpsitārthapradāyikā \|\| 46 \|\|*

*yastvidaṃ vai paṭhennityaṃ śṛṇuyādvā'pi bhāvataḥ \|*  
*tasya tīrthāni sarvāṇi hyabhiṣiñcati pāṇḍava \|\| 47 \|\|*

45-47. The Narmada has been resorted to by the Agnibotris and learned men. This river is the giver of one’s wishes. One who would devoutfully m read or listen to the glory of it would get the merit of having sprinkled on him the sacred waters of all the tirthas, and would please the Narmada, Markandeya and Mahadeva.

## \|\| 194.48-50 \|\|

*narmadā ca sadā prītā bhavedvai nātra saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*prītastasya bhavedrudro mārkaṇḍeyo mahāmuniḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

*bandhyā caiva labhetputrāndurbhagā subhagā bhavet \|*  
*kanyā labheta bhartāraṃ yaśca vāñchettu yatphalam \|*  
*tadeva labhate sarvaṃ nātra kāryā vicāraṇā \|\| 49 \|\|*

*brāhmaṇo vedamāpnoti kṣatriyo vijayī bhavet \|*  
*vaiśyastu labhate lābhaṃ śūdra ḥ! prāpnoti sadgatim \|\| 50 \|\|*

48-50. By listening to its glory a barren woman begets children, a maid gets a handsome husband, the Brahmana becomes versed in the Vedas, the unlucky becomes lucky, the Kshatriya becomes in war victorious, the Vaishya becomes wealthy, the Shudra attains emancipation from bondage, and the idiot becomes learned. One who hears it never suffers the pangs of separation and hell.

## Chapter 195

## \|\| 195.1-4 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*ityākarṇya sa rājendra oṃkārasyābhivarṇanam \|*  
*tataḥ papraccha deveśaṃ matsyarūpaṃ jalārṇave \|\| 1 \|\|*

*manuruvāca*  
*ṛṣīṇāṃ nāma gotrāṇi vaṃśāvataraṇaṃ tathā \|*  
*pravarāṇāṃ tathā sāmyamasāmyaṃ vistarādvada \|\| 2 \|\|*

*mahādevena ṛṣayaḥ śaptāḥ svāyaṃbhuve'ntare \|*  
*teṣāṃ vaivasvate prāpte saṃbhavaṃ mama kīrtaya \|\| 3 \|\|*

*dākṣāyaṇīnāṃ ca tathā prajāḥ kīrtaya me prabho \|*  
*ṛṣīṇāṃ ca tathā vaṃśaṃ bhṛguvaṃśavivardhanam \|\| 4 \|\|*

1-4. Suta said: — Yudhisthira! hearing the glory of the Narmada and Omkeshvara, king Vaivasvata Manu put these questions to the Lord Matsya in that vast ocean, viz. — “ Relate the gotra (clan), vamsha (dynasty), avatar (descent), and pravara (family) of the Rishis. Also explain the existence of the Vaivasvata-manvantara as well as about the curse that the Lord Shiva had pronounced on the Rishis during Svayambhuva-manvantara. Enumerate the progeny of Daksha and also the Rishis who are the promoters of Bhriguvamsha.

## \|\| 195.5 \|\|

*matsya uvāca*  
*manvantare'sminsaṃprāpte pūrvaṃ vaivasvate tathā \|*  
*caritraṃ kathyate rājanbrahmaṇaḥ parameṣṭhinaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Matsya said King! first hear the doings of Brahma during the Vaivasvata-manvantara.

## \|\| 195.6-8 \|\|

*mahādevasya śāpena tyaktvā dehaṃ svayaṃ tathā \|*  
*ṛṣayaśca samudbhūtā hute śukre mahātmanā \|\| 6 \|\|*

*devānāṃ mātaro dṛṣṭvā devapatnyastathaiva ca \|*  
*skannaṃ śukraṃ mahārāja brahmaṇaḥ parameṣṭhinaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*tajжuhāva tato brahmā tato jātā hutāśanāt \|*  
*tato jāto mahātejā bhṛguśca tapasāṃ nidhiḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

6-8. First, all the Rishis went to heaven after casting away their corporeal bodies by the curse of Shiva. There they were born of Brahma when the mothers and the consorts of the Devas saw the dripping of the semen- virile of Brahma and caused it to be poured as oblation into the fire which produced the most illustrious sage Bhrigu out of the fire.

## \|\| 195.9-10 \|\|

*aṅgāreṣvaṅgirā jāto harcirbhyo'tristathaiva ca \|*  
*marīcibhyo marīcistu tato jāto mahātapāḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*keśaistu kapiśo jātaḥ pulastyaśca mahātapāḥ \|*  
*keśaiḥ pralambaiḥ pulahastato jāto mahātapāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. The sage Angira was horn out of the cinders, Attri was begotten from the flame, and Marichi came out of the tongues of fire. Kapila and Pulastya were born of the hair of Brahma. The most illustrious Pulaha came out of the long tresses of hair.

## \|\| 195.11-14 \|\|

*vasumadhyātsamutpanno vasiṣṭhastu tapodhanaḥ \|*  
*bhṛguḥ pulomnastu sutāṃ divyāṃ bhāryāmavindata \|\| 11 \|\|*

*tasyāmasya sutā jātā devā dvādaśa yājñikāḥ \|*  
*bhuvano bhauvanaścaiva sujanyaḥ sujanastathā \|\| 12 \|\|*

*kraturvasuśca mūrdhā ca tyājyaśca vasudaśca ha \|*  
*prabhavaścāvyayaścaiva dakṣo'tha dvādaśastathā \|\| 13 \|\|*

*ityete bhṛgavo nāma devā dvādaśa kīrtitāḥ \|*  
*paulomyāṃ janayanviprā devānāṃ tu kanīyasaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

11-14. The lustre of fire produced Vasistha. The sage Bhrigu was married to the daughter of Puloma; and they gave birth to the following twelve Yajnika Devas: — Bhuvana, Bhauvana, Sujanya, Sujana, Shuchi, Kratu, Murdha, Tyaja, Vasuda, Prabhava, Avyaya and Daksha. They are known as the twelve Bhargavas. The same Paulomi gave birth to the Vipras.

## \|\| 195.15-28 \|\|

*cyavanaṃ tu mahābhāgamāpnuvānaṃ tathaiva ca \|*  
*āpnuvānātmajaścaurvo jamadagnistadātmajaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*aurvo gotrakarasteṣāṃ bhārgavāṇāṃ mahātmanām \|*  
*tatra gotrakarānvakṣye bhṛgorvai dīptatejasaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*bhṛguśca cyavanaścaiva āpnuvānastathaiva ca \|*  
*aurvaśca jamadagniśca vātsyo daṇḍirnaḍāyanaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*vaigāyano vītihavyaḥ pailaścaivātra śaunakaḥ \|*  
*śaunakāyanajīvantirāvedaḥ kārṣaṇistathā \|\| 18 \|\|*

*vaihīnarirvirūpākṣo rauhityāyanireva ca \|*  
*vaiśvānaristathā nīlo lubdhaḥ sāvarṇikaśca saḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

*viṣṇuḥ pauro'pi bālākirailiko'nantabhāginaḥ \|*  
*mṛgamārgeyamārkaṇḍajavino nītinastathā \|\| 20 \|\|*

*maṇḍamāṇḍavyamāṇḍūkaphenapāḥ stanitastathā \|*  
*sthalapiṇḍaḥ śikhāvarṇaḥ śārkarākṣistathaiva ca \|\| 21 \|\|*

*jāladhiḥ saudhikaḥ kṣubhyaḥ kutso'nyo maudgalāyanaḥ \|*  
*māṅkāyano devapatiḥ pāṇḍurociḥ sagālavaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*sāṃkṛtyaścātakiḥ sārpiryajñapiṇḍāyanastathā \|*  
*gārgyāyaṇo gāyanaśca ṛṣirgārhāyaṇastathā \|\| 23 \|\|*

*goṣṭhāyano vāhyayano vaiśampāyana eva ca \|*  
*vaikarṇiniḥ śārṅgaravo yājñeyirbhrāṣṭrakāyaṇiḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*lālāṭirnākuliścaiva laukṣiṇyoparimaṇḍalau \|*  
*ālukiḥ saucakiḥ kautsastathā'nyaḥ paiṅgalāyaniḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*sātyāyanirmālayaniḥ kauṭiliḥ kaucahastikaḥ \|*  
*sauhaḥ soktiḥ sakauvākṣiḥ kausiścāndra masistathā \|\| 26 \|\|*

*naikajihvo jihvakaśca vyādhājyo lauhavairiṇaḥ \|*  
*śāradvatikanetiṣyau lolākṣiścalakuṇḍalaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

*vāṃgāyaniścānumatiḥ pūrṇimāgatiko'sakṛt \|*  
*sāmānyena yathā teṣāṃ pañcaite pravarā matāḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

15-28. They are: — Chyavana, Apnuvana. Apnuvana gave birth to Aurva the father of Jamadagni. The sage Aurva was the chief promoter of the Bhargava Rishis. Now I shall describe to you the illustrious Rishis who promoted the Bhargava clan. They are: — Bhrigu, Chyavana, Apnuvana, Aurva, Jamadagni, Vatsya, Dandi, Nadayana, Vaigayana, Vitahavya, Paila, Shaunaka, Shaunakayana, Jivanti, Avaida, Karpina, Vaihaniri, Virupaksha, Rauhityayani, Vaishvanari, Nila, Lubdha, Savarnika, Vishnu, Paura, Balakirailika, Anantabhagi, Bhrita, Bhargaiya, Markanda, Jabi, Bitt, Manda, Mandavya, Manduka, Phainapa, Tanita, Sthala, Pinda, Sikhavarna, Shakrkarakshi, Jaladhi, Sandhika, Kshubhya, Kutsanya, Maudgalayana, Karmayana, Devapati, Pandurochi, GaIava, Samkritya, Chataki, Sarpi, Yagyapindayana, Gargyayana, Gayand, Garhayana, Goshthayana, Vahyayana, Vaishampayana, Vaikarnini Sharangarava, Yajneyi, Bhrashtakayani, Lalati, Nakuli, Laukshinya, Parimandali, Aluki, Sauchaki, Kautsa, Paingalayani, Satyayani, Malayani, Kautili, Kauchahastika, Sauha Shokti, Sakauvikshi, Kausi, Chandramasi, Naikajihva, Jihvaka, Vyadhajya, Lauhavairi, Saradvatika, Netishya, Lolakshi, Chalakundala, Bangayani, Anumati, Purnima, Agatika, and Asakrite, ordinarily each of these Rishis of the Bhriguvamsha are said to have, five Pravaras.

## \|\| 195.29 \|\|

*bhṛguśca cyavanaścaiva āpnuvānastathaiva ca \|*  
*aurvaśca jamadagniśca pañcaite pravarā matāḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Bhrigu, Chyavana, Apnuvana, Aurva, Jamadagni are the five Pravaras.

## \|\| 195.30-32 \|\|

*ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi śṛṇu tvanyānbhṛgūdvahān \|*  
*jamadagnirbidaścaiva paulastyo baijabhṛttathā \|\| 30 \|\|*

*ṛṣiścobhayajātaśca kāyaniḥ śākaṭāyanaḥ \|*  
*aurveyā mārutāścaiva sarveṣāṃ pravarāḥ śubhāḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

*bhṛguśca cyavanaścaiva apnuvānastathaiva ca \|*  
*parasparamavaivāhyā ṛṣayaḥ parikīrtitāḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

30-32. Now listen to the other descendants of Bhrigu, which I shall relate. (These are) Jamadagni Vida, Paulastya, Vaijavrita, Rishi Ubhayajata, Kayani, Shakatayana, Aurveya, and Maruta, are of all the most excellent Pravaras. Bhrigu, Chyavana, and Apnuvana cannot intermarry among themselves.

## \|\| 195.33-34 \|\|

*bhṛgudāso mārgapatho grāmyāyaṇikaṭāyanī \|*  
*āpastambistathā bilvirnaikaśiḥ kapireva ca \|\| 33 \|\|*

*ārṣṭiṣeṇo gārdabhiśca kārdamāyanireva ca \|*  
*āśvāyanistathā rūpiḥ pañcā’rṣeyāḥ prakīrtitāḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

33-34. Bhrigudasa, Margapatha, Gramyayani, Katayani, Apastambi, Bilvi, Naikashi, Kapi, Arshtishena, Gardabhi, Kardamayani, Ashvayani, and Rupi, are known as Arsheya.

## \|\| 195.35 \|\|

*bhṛguśca cyavanaścaiva āpnuvānastathaiva ca \|*  
*ārṣṭiṣeṇastathā rūpiḥ pravarāḥ pañca kīrtitāḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Bhrigu, Chyavana, Apnuvana, Arshishthishena and Rupi are the five Pravaras.

## \|\| 195.36-42 \|\|

*parasparamavaivāhyā ṛṣayaḥ parikīrtitāḥ \|*  
*yasko vā vītihavyo vā mathitastu tathā damaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

*jaivantyāyanirmauñjaśca piliścaiva calistathā \|*  
*bhāgilo bhāgavittiśca kauśāpistvatha kāśyapiḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

*bālapiḥ śramadāgepiḥ saurastithistathaiva ca \|*  
*gārgīyastvatha jābālistathā pauṣṇyāyano hyṛṣiḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

*rāmodaśca tathaiteṣāmārṣeyāḥ pravarā matāḥ \|*  
*bhṛguśca vītihavyaśca tathā raivasavaivasau \|\| 39 \|\|*

*parasparamavaivāhyā ṛṣayaḥ parikīrtitāḥ \|*  
*śālāyaniḥ śākaṭākṣo maitreyaḥ khāṇḍavastathā \|\| 40 \|\|*

*drau ṇāyano rakumāyaṇirāpiśiścāpikāyaniḥ \|*  
*haṃsajihvastathaiteṣāmārṣeyāḥ pravarā matāḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

*bhṛguścaivātha vaddhryaśvo divodāsastathaiva ca \|*  
*parasparamavaivāhyā ṛṣayaḥ parikīrtitāḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

36-42. They also cannot intermarry among themselves. Yaska, Vitivyaya, Mathita, Dama, Jaivantyayani, Maunja, Pili, Chali, Bhagili, Bhagavitti, Kaushapi, Kashyapi, Balapi, Shramadagepi, Saura, Tithi Gargiya, Javali, Paushnyayani, Ramada, are the Arsheya Pravaras. Bhrigu, Vitahavya, Raivasa, Vaivasa also cannot intermarry among themselves. Salayani, Sakataksha, Maitreya, Khandava, Draunayana, Raukmayana, Apishi, Kayani, Hamsajihva, are the Arsheya Pravaras. Bhrigu, Baddhryashva, Divodasa, also cannot Intermarry among themselves.

## \|\| 195.43-44 \|\|

*ekāyano yajñapatirmatsyagandhastathaiva ca \|*  
*pratyahaśca tathā sauriścaukṣirvai kārdamāyaniḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

*tathā gṛtsamado rājansanakaśca mahānṛṣiḥ \|*  
*pravarāstu tathoktānāmārṣeyāḥ parikīrtitāḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

43-44. Aikayana, Yajnapati, Matsyagandha, Pratyaha, Sauri, Aukshi, Kardamayani, Gritsamada and Sanaka are the Arsheya, Pravaras.

## \|\| 195.45 \|\|

*bhṛgurgṛtsamadaścaiva ārṣāvetau prakīrtitau \|*  
*parasparamavaivāhyā ityete parikīrtitāḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Bhrigu, Gritsamada are the two Arsha Pravaras and they cannot inter-marry.

## \|\| 195.46 \|\|

*ete tavoktā bhṛguvaṃśajātā mahānubhāvā nṛpagotrakārāḥ \|*  
*eṣāṃ tu nāmnāṃ parikīrtanena pāpaṃ samagraṃ vijahāti jantuḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. All these Rishis of the Bhriguvamsha are most illustrious. They are the promoters of the clan. By the mere mention of their name all the sins are dispelled.

## Chapter 196

## \|\| 196.1-11 \|\|

*matsya uvāca*  
*marīcitanayā rājansurūpā nāma viśrutā \|*  
*bhāryā cāṅgiraso devāstasyāḥ putrā daśa smṛtāḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*ātmāyurdamano dakṣaḥ sadaḥ prāṇastathaiva ca \|*  
*haviṣmāṃśca gaviṣṭhaśca ṛtaḥ satyaśca te daśa \|\| 2 \|\|*

*ete cā’ṅgiraso nāma devā vai somapāyinaḥ \|*  
*surūpā janayāmāsa ṛṣīnsarveśvarānimān \|\| 3 \|\|*

*bṛhaspatiṃ gautamaṃ ca saṃvartamṛṣimuttamam \|*  
*utathyaṃ vāmadevaṃ ca ajasyamṛṣijaṃ tathā \|\| 4 \|\|*

*ityete ṛṣayaḥ sarve gotrakārāḥ prakīrtitāḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ gotrasamutpannāngotrakārānnibodha me \|\| 5 \|\|*

*utathyo gautamaścaiva tauleyo'bhijitastathā \|*  
*sārdhanemiḥ salaugākṣiḥ kṣīraḥ kauṣṭikireva ca \|\| 6 \|\|*

*rāhukarṇiḥ saupuriśca kairātiḥ sāmalomakiḥ \|*  
*pauṣājitirbhārgavato hyṛṣiścairīḍavastathā \|\| 7 \|\|*

*kāroṭakaḥ sajīvī ca upabindusuraiṣiṇau \|*  
*vāhinīpativaiśālī kroṣṭā caivāruṇāyaniḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*somo'trāyanikāsorukauśalyāḥ pārthivāstathā \|*  
*rauhiṇyāyanirevāgnī mūlayaḥ pāṇḍureva ca \|\| 9 \|\|*

*kṣapāviśvakaro'riśca pārikārārireva ca \|*  
*ārṣeyāḥ pravarāścaiva teṣāṃ ca pravarāñchṛṇu \|\| 10 \|\|*

*aṅgirāḥ suvacotathya uśijaśca mahānṛṣiḥ \|*  
*parasparamavaivāhyā ṛṣayaḥ parikīrtitāḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

1-11. Matsya said :—‘‘ King ! the sons of Marichi are known as Surupa and the wife of the sage Angira gave birth to ten sons who became the Devas. They were:—Atma, Ayu, Damana, Daksha, Sada, Prana, Havishmana, Gairshtha, Rita, and Satya. These Angirasas are known as the Somapayi Devas.
