The following Rishis were born of Surupa: — Brihaspati, Gautama, Samvarta, Utathya, Vamadeva, Ajssya. They are all the propagators of the gotra. Now other Rishis of the same gotra who propagated other gotras are enumerated. Utathya, Gautama, Tauleya, Abhijita, Ardhanemi, Laugakshi, Kshira, Kaushtiki, Rahukarni, Saupuri, Kairati, Samalomaki, Paushajiti, Bhargavata, Airidava Rishi, Karotaka, Sajivi, Upabindu, Suraishina, Vahinipati, Vaishali, Kroshtha, Arunayani, Soma, Atrayani, Kasoru, Kaushalya, Parthiva, Rauhinyayani, Raivagni, Mulapa, Pandu, Kshapa, Vishvakara, Ari, Parikari. They are the Arsheya Pravara of the foregoing Rishis. Now hear their Pravaras, viz., Angira, Suvachotathya Ushija. They cannot intermarry among themselves.

## \|\| 196.12-20 \|\|

*ātreyāyaṇisauveṣṭyāvagniveśyaḥ śilāsthaliḥ \|*  
*bāliśāyaniścaikepī vārāhirbāṣkalistathā \|\| 12 \|\|*

*sauṭiśca tṛṇakarṇiśca prāvahiścā’śvalāyaniḥ \|*  
*vārāhirbarhisādī ca śikhāgrīvistathaiva ca \|\| 13 \|\|*

*kārakiśca mahākāpistathā coḍupatiḥ prabhuḥ \|*  
*kaucakirdhamitaścaiva puṣpānveṣistathaiva ca \|\| 14 \|\|*

*somatanvirbrahmatanviḥ sālaḍirbālaḍistathā \|*  
*devarārirdevasthānirhārikarṇiḥ saridbhuviḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*prāvepiḥ sādyasugrīvistathā gomedagandhikaḥ \|*  
*matsyācchādyo mūlaharaḥ phalāhārastathaiva ca \|\| 16 \|\|*

*gāṅgodadhiḥ kaurupatiḥ kaurukṣetristathaiva ca \|*  
*nāyakirjaityadrau ṇiśca jaihvalāyanireva ca \|\| 17 \|\|*

*āpastambirmauñjavṛṣṭirmārṣṭapiṅgalireva ca \|*  
*pailaścaiva mahātejāḥ śālaṅkāyanireva ca \|\| 18 \|\|*

*dvyākhyeyo mārutaścaiṣāṃ sarveṣāṃ pravaro nṛpa \|*  
*aṅgirāḥ prathamasteṣāṃ dvitīyaśca bṛhaspatiḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

*tṛtīyaśca bharadvājaḥ pravarāḥ parikīrtitāḥ \|*  
*parasparamavaivāhyā ityete parikīrtitāḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

12-20. Atraiyayani, Sauvashthya, Agnivaishya, Shilasthali, Balishayani, Aikepi, Barahi, Bashkali, Sauti, Trinakarni, Pravahi, Ashvalayani, Barhisadi, Shikhagrivi, Karaki, Mahakapi, Udupati, Kauchaki, Dhamita, Pushpanveshi, Somatanvi, Brahmatanvi, Saladi, Baladi, Devarari, Devasthani, Harikarni, Saridabhuvi, Pravepi, Sadyasugrivi, Gomedagandhika, Matsyachadya, Mulahara, Phalahara, Gangodadhi, Kaurupati, Kaurukshetri, Nayaki, Jaityadroni, Jaihvalayani, Apastambi, Maunjavrishti, Marshta, Pingali, Paila, Shalamkayani, Dvadhyakhaiya, Maruta. They are all Rishis and Amriga, Vrihaspati, Bharadvaja are the three Pravaras, they cannot intermarry among themselves.

## \|\| 196.21-32 \|\|

*kāṇvāyanāḥ kopacayāstathā vātsyatarāyaṇāḥ \|*  
*bhrāṣṭrakṛdrā ṣṭrapiṇḍī ca laindrā ṇiḥ sāyakāyaniḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*kroṣṭākṣī bahuvītī ca tālakṛnmadhurāvahaḥ \|*  
*lāvakṛdgālavidgāthī mārkaṭiḥ paulikāyaniḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*skandasaśca tathā cakrī gārgyaḥ śyāmāyanistathā \|*  
*balākiḥ sāhariścaiva pañcā’rṣeyāḥ prakīrtitāḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

*aṅgirāśca mahātejā devācāryo bṛhaspatiḥ \|*  
*bharadvājastathā gargaḥ saityaśca bhagavānṛṣiḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*parasparamavaivāhyā ṛṣayaḥ parikīrtitāḥ \|*  
*kapītaraḥ svastitaro dākṣiḥ śaktiḥ patañjaliḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*bhūyasirjalasaṃdhiśca bindurmādiḥ kusīdakiḥ \|*  
*ūrvastu rājakeśī ca vauṣaḍiḥ śaṃsapistathā \|\| 26 \|\|*

*śāliśca kalaśīkaṇṭa ṛṣiḥ kārīrayastathā \|*  
*kāṭyo dhānyāyaniścaiva bhāvāsyāyanireva ca \|\| 27 \|\|*

*bharadvājiḥ saubudhiśca laghvī devamatistathā \|*  
*tr! yārṣeyo'bhimataścaiṣāṃ pravaro bhūmipottama \|\| 28 \|\|*

*aṅgirā damavāhyaśca tathā caivāpyurukṣayaḥ \|*  
*parasparamavaivāhyā ṛṣayaḥ parikīrtitāḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*saṃkṛtiśca trimārṣṭiśca manuḥ saṃbadhireva vā \|*  
*taṇḍiścenātakiścaiva tailakā dakṣa eva ca \|\| 30 \|\|*

*nārāyaṇiścārṣiṇiśca laukṣirgārgyaharistathā \|*  
*gālavaśca anehaśca sarveṣāṃ pravaro mataḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

*aṅgirāḥ saṃkṛtiścaiva gauravītistathaiva ca \|*  
*parasparamavaivāhyā ṛṣayaḥ parikīrtitāḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

21-32. Kanvayana, Kopachaya, Vatsyatarayana, Bhrashtrakrita, Rashtrapindi, Laindrani, Sayakayani, Kroshtakshi, Bahuviti, Talakrit, Madhuravaha, Lavakrita, Kalavita, Gathi, Markati, Paulikayani, Skandasa, Chakri, Gargya, Shyamayani, Balaki, Sahari have the following five Arsheya Pravaras, viz., Amgira, Devacharya, Vrihaspati, Bharadvaja, Garga, and Saitya. They do not intermarry among themselves. Kapitara, Svastitara, Dakshi, Shakti, Patanjali, Bhuyasi, Jalasandhi, Vindurmadi, Kusidaki, Urva, Rajakaishi, Vaishadi, Sansapi, Shali, Kalashikantha, Kariraya, Katya, Dhanyayani, Bhavasyayani, Bharadvaji, Sanbudhi, Laghvi, Devamati, have Amgira, Damavahya and Urukshaya for their Arsheya Pravara and the Rishis of these Pravaras also do not intermarry among themselves. The above-mentioned Rishis are said to have Laukshi, Gargyahari, and Galavi for their Pravaras and also Angira, Samkrati, Gauraviti as well as Angira, Vrihaduktha, Vamadeva, who do not marry among themselves, and with those born in the Kutsa-gotra with Kutsa Pravara.

## \|\| 196.33-35 \|\|

*kātyāyano haritakaḥ kautsaḥ piṅgastathaiva ca \|*  
*haṇḍidāso vātsyāyanirmādri rmauliḥ kuberaṇiḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

*bhīmavegaḥ śāśvadarbhiḥ sarve tripravarāḥ smṛtāḥ \|*  
*aṅgirā bṛhadaśvaśca jīvanāśvastathaiva ca \|\| 34 \|\|*

*parasparamavaivāhyā ṛṣayaḥ parikīrtitāḥ \|*  
*bṛhaduktho vāmadevastathā tripravarā matāḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

33-35. Angira, Virupa, Rathitara are the Arsheya Pravaras of the Rishis of the Rathitara clan. They also do not intermarry in their gotra. Vishnuvridhi, Shivamati, Jatrina, Katrina, Putrava, Vairaparayana also have three Pravaras.

## \|\| 196.36 \|\|

*aṅgirā bṛhadukthaśca vāmadevastathaiva ca \|*  
*parasparamavaivāhyā ityete parikīrtitāḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Angira, Matsyadagdha, and Mudgala are also the three Pravaras do not intermarry among themselves.

## \|\| 196.37-41 \|\|

*kutsagotrodbhavāścaiva tathā tripravarā matāḥ \|*  
*aṅgirāśca sadasyuśca purukutsastathaiva ca \|*  
*kutsāḥ kutsairavaivāhyā evamāhuḥ purātanāḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

*rathītarāṇāṃ pravarāstr! yārṣeyāḥ parikīrtitāḥ \|*  
*aṅgirāśca virūpaśca tathaiva ca rathītaraḥ \|*  
*rathītarā hyavaivāhyā nityameva rathītaraiḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

*viṣṇusiddhiḥ śivamatirjatṛṇaḥ kattṛṇastathā \|*  
*putravaśca mahātejāstathā vairaparāyaṇaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

*tr! yārṣeyo'bhimatasteṣāṃ sarveṣāṃ pravaro nṛpa \|*  
*aṅgirāśca virūpaśca vṛṣaparvastathaiva ca \|*  
*parasparamavaivāhyā ṛṣayaḥ parikīrtitāḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

*sātyagugrirmahātejā hiraṇyastambimudgalau \|*  
*tr! yārṣeyo hi matasteṣāṃ sarveṣāṃ pravaro nṛpa \|\| 41 \|\|*

37-41. Hamsajihva, Devajihva, Agnijihva, Viradapa, Apagnaiya, Ashvaya, gala also have three Pravaras, vis., Amgira, Tandya, Maudgalya who also do not intermarry among themselves. Amgira, Ajamidha, Kanva are the Pravaras of: — Apandu, Guru, Shakatayana, Pragathama, Markanda, Marana, Shiva, Katu, Markatapa, Nadayana, Shyamayana.

## \|\| 196.42-46 \|\|

*aṅgirā matsyadagdhaśca mudgalaśca mahātapāḥ \|*  
*parasparamavaivāhyā ṛṣayaḥ parikīrtitāḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

*haṃsajihvo devajihvo hyagnijihvo virāḍapaḥ \|*  
*apāgneyastvaśvayuśca paraṇyastā vimaudgalāḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

*tr! yārṣeyābhimatāsteṣāṃ sarveṣāṃ pravarāḥ śubhāḥ \|*  
*aṅgirāścaiva tāṇḍiśca maudgalyaśca mahātapāḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

*parasparamavaivāhyā ṛṣayaḥ parikīrtitāḥ \|*  
*apāṇḍuśca guruścaiva tṛtīyaḥ śākaṭāyanaḥ \|*  
*tataḥ prāgāthamā nārī mārkaṇḍo maraṇaḥ śivaḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

*kaṭurmarkaṭapaścaiva tathā nāḍāyano hyṛṣiḥ \|*  
*śyāmāyanastathaivaiṣāṃ tr! yārṣeyāḥ pravarāḥ śubhāḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

42-46. They should not also intermarry among themselves. Titira, Kapibhu, Gargya, are the three Pravaras, so are Amgira, Titira, Kapibhu. They should not intermarry among themselves. Riksha, Bharadvaja, Rishivana, Manava, Maittravara Rishi, are also known as the Arsheya Pravaras, and Amgira, Bharadvaja, Vrihaspati, Mittravara Rishi, Rishivana, and Manava also cannot intermarry among themselves.

## \|\| 196.47-48 \|\|

*aṅgirāścājamīḍhaśca kaṭyaścaiva mahātapāḥ \|*  
*parasparamavaivāhyā ṛṣayaḥ parikīrtitāḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

*tittiriḥ kapibhūścaiva gārgyaścaiva mahānṛṣiḥ \|*  
*tr! yārṣeyo he matasteṣāṃ sarveṣāṃ pravaraḥ śubhaḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

47-48. Bharadvaja, Huta, Shaunga, Shaishiraiya belong to the Dvadhyamushyayana-gotra and they have the following five Arsheya Pravaras, vis. — Amgira, Bharadvaja, Vrihaspati, Maudgalya, and Shishira.

## \|\| 196.49 \|\|

*aṅgirāstittiriścaiva kapibhūśca mahānṛṣiḥ \|*  
*parasparamavaivāhyā ṛṣayaḥ parikīrtitāḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. “King! I have enumerated to you the Rishis of the Amgira-gotra, By the mere mention of their name one becomes freed from all ills and attains bliss.

## Chapter 197

## \|\| 197.1-8 \|\|

*matsya uvāca*  
*atrivaṃśasamutpannāngotrakārānnibodha me \|*  
*kardamāyanaśākheyāstathā śārāyaṇāśca ye \|\| 1 \|\|*

*uddālakiḥ śauṇakarṇirathau śaukratavaśca ye \|*  
*gauragrīvā gaurajinastathā caitrāyaṇāśca ye \|\| 2 \|\|*

*ardhapaṇyā vāmarathyā gopanāstakibindavaḥ \|*  
*karṇajihvo haraprītirlaidrā ṇiḥ śākalāyaniḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*tailapaśca savaileyo atrirgoṇīpatistathā \|*  
*jalado bhagapādaśca saupuṣpiśca mahātapāḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*chandogeyastathaiteṣāṃ tr! yārṣeyāḥ pravarā matāḥ \|*  
*śyāvāśvaśca tathā'triśca ārcanānaśa eva ca \|\| 5 \|\|*

*parasparamavaivāhyā ṛṣayaḥ parikīrtitāḥ \|*  
*dākṣirbaliḥ parṇaviśca ūrṇanābhiḥ śilārdaniḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*bījavāpi śirīṣaśca mauñjakeśo gaviṣṭhiraḥ \|*  
*bhalandanastathaiteṣāṃ tr! yārṣeyāḥ pravarā matāḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*atrirgaviṣṭhiraścaiva tathā pūrvātithiḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*parasparamavaivāhyā ṛṣayaḥ parikīrtitāḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

1-8. Matsya said: — “King! I shall now name to you the Rishis of the Atri clan, Sharayana, Udvalaki, Shona. Karniratha, Shaukratu, Gauragriva, Gaurajina, Chaitrayana, Ardhapanya, Bamarathya, Gopana, Takivindu, Karnajihva, Harapriti, Naidrani, Shakalayani, Tailapa, Bailaiya, Atri, Gonipati, Jalada, Bhagapada, Saupushpi, Chandogaiya of the Kardamayana Shakha (branch) have Shyavashva, Atri, Archanavatara for their Pravaras. They do not intermarry among themselves. Dakshi, Bali, Parnavi, Urnabhi, Mridani, Bijabapi, Shirika, Manuja, Kaisha, Gavishthira, Bhalandana have Atri, Gavishthira and Purvatithi for their Pravaras, and they also do not marry among themselves.”

## \|\| 197.9-10 \|\|

*ātreyaputrikāputrānata ūrdhvaṃ nibodha me \|*  
*kāleyāśca sabāleyā vāmarathyāstathaiva ca \|\| 9 \|\|*

*dhātreyāścaiva maitreyāstr! yārṣeyāḥ parikīrtitāḥ \|*  
*atriśca vāmarathyaśca pautriścaiva mahānṛṣiḥ \|*  
*parasparamavaivāhyā ṛṣayaḥ parikīrtitāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. Kalaiya, Balaiya, Vasarathya, Dhatraiya, Maitraiya, are the sons of the daughter of the sage Atraiya. They have Atri, Vamarathya and Pautri for their Pravara, and they do not intermarry among themselves.

## \|\| 197.11 \|\|

*ityatrivaṃśaprabhavāstavoktā mahānubhāvā nṛpa gotrakārāḥ \|*  
*yeṣāṃ tu nāmnā parikīrtitena pāpaṃ samagraṃ puruṣo jahāti \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. “King! I have described before you all the Brahmanas of the Atri family by the mere mention of whose name one becomes liberated from all ills.”

## Chapter 198

## \|\| 198.3-6 \|\|

*viśvāmitro devarātastathā vaikṛtigālavaḥ \|*  
*vataṇḍaśca śalaṅkaśca hyabhayaścāyatāyanaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*śyāmāyanā yājñavaklyā jābālāḥ saindhavāyanāḥ \|*  
*bābhravyāśca karīṣāśca saṃśrutyā atha saṃśrutāḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*ulūpā aupahāvāśca payodajanapādapāḥ \|*  
*kharavāco halayamāḥ sādhitā vāsukauśikāḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*tr! yārṣeyāḥ pravarāsteṣāṃ sarveṣāṃ parikīrtitāḥ \|*  
*viśvāmitro devarāta uddālaśca mahayaśāḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

3-6. Matsya said: — “King! I shall now relate to you other descendants of Atri. Chandrama has been born in the house of Atri in whose family Vishvamitra took his birth. By virtue of his asceticism Vishvamitra became a Brahmana from Kshatriya. I shall, now tell you about the family of Vishvamitra. 1-2

Vishvamitra, Daivarata, Vaikrita, Galava, Vatanda, Lanka, Abhaya, Ayatayana, Shyamayana, Yagyavalkya, Jabala, Saindhavayana, Babhravya, Karisha, Samshrutya, Uloopa, Anpagahaya, Payoda, Janapadapa, Kharavacha, Halayama, Sadhati, Vastukaushika. They have three Arsha Pravaras, viz., Vishvamitra, Devarata, and Uddalaka.

## \|\| 198.7-14 \|\|

*parasparamavaivāhyā ṛṣayaḥ parikīrtitāḥ \|*  
*devaśravāḥ sujāteyāḥ saumukāḥ kārukāyaṇāḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*tathā vaideharātā ye kuśikāśca narādhipa \|*  
*tr! yārṣeyo'bhimatasteṣāṃ sarveṣāṃ pravaraḥ śubhaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*devaśravā devarāto viśvāmitrastathaiva ca \|*  
*parasparamavaivāhyā ṛṣayaḥ parikīrtitāḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*dhanaṃjayaḥ kapardeyaḥ parikūṭaśca pārthiva \|*  
*pāṇiniścaiva tr! yārṣeyāḥ sarva ete prakīrtitāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*viśvāmitrastathā’dyaśca mādhucchandasa eva ca \|*  
*tr! yārṣeyāḥ pravarā hyete ṛṣayaḥ parikīrtitāḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*viśvāmitro madhucchandāstathā caivāghamarṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*parasparamavaivāhyā ṛṣayaḥ parikīrtitāḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*kāmalāyanijaścaiva aśmarathyastathaiva ca \|*  
*vañjuliścāpi tr! yārṣeyaḥ sarveṣāṃ pravaro mataḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*viśvāmitraścāśvaratho vañculiśca mahātapāḥ \|*  
*parasparamavaivāhyā ṛṣayaḥ parikīrtitāḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

7-14. They also do not intermarry among themselves. Daivashrava, Devarata; Vishvamitra are the three Pravaras of Daivashrava, Sujataiya, Sansuka, Karukaya, Vaidaiharata, Kushika. They also do not intermarry. Dhananjaya, Kapardaiya, Parikuta, Parthiha, Panini have Vishvamitra, Madhuchchhanda, Aghamarshana for their Pravaras. They also do not intermarry. Kamalayajina, Ashmarathya, Banjuli, are also the three Pravaras. They too do not intermarry.

## \|\| 198.15-17 \|\|

*viśvāmitro lohitaśca aṣṭakaḥ pūraṇastathā \|*  
*viśvāmitraḥ pūraṇaśca tayordvau pravarau smṛtau \|\| 15 \|\|*

*parasparamavaivāhyāḥ pūraṇāśca parasparam \|*  
*lohitā aṣṭakāścaiṣāṃ tr! yārṣeyāḥ parikīrtitāḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*viśvāmitro lohitaśca aṣṭakaśca mahātapāḥ \|*  
*aṣṭakā lohitairnityamavaivāhyāḥ parasparam \|\| 17 \|\|*

15-17. Vishvamitra, Lohita, Ashtaka, Purana have Vishvamitra, and Parana for their Pravaras. The Rishis of the Purana-gotra do not intermarry. Vishvamitra, Lohita and Ashtaka are the three Arsheya Pravaras of Lohita and Ashtaka, and there is no intermarriage between Ashtaka and Lohita gotras.

## \|\| 198.18-19 \|\|

*udareṇuḥ krathakaśca ṛṣiścodāvahistathā \|*  
*ārṣeyo'bhimatasteṣāṃ sarveṣāṃ pravaraḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*ṛṇavāngatinaścaiva viśvāmitrastathaiva ca \|*  
*parasparamavaivāhyā ṛṣayaḥ parikīrtitāḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

18-19. Udasainu, Krathaka, Udavahi, Shatyayani, Karirasi, Shalankayani, Lavaki, Manujayani, are also known to have three Arsheya Pravara, viz., Khilakhila, Vidya, Vishvamitra. They do not intermarry.

## \|\| 198.20 \|\|

*udumbaraḥ saiṣiriṭirṛṣistrākṣāyaṇistathā \|*  
*śāṭhyāyaniḥ karīrāśī śālaṅkāyanilāvakī \|*  
*mauñjāyaniśca bhagavāṃtr! yārṣeyāḥ parikīrtitāḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. “King! I have named the Rishis of the Vishvamitra clan before you, by the mere mention of whose names one becomes liberated from his sins.”

## Chapter 199

## \|\| 199.1-10 \|\|

*matsya uvāca*  
*marīceḥ kaśyapaḥ putraḥ kaśyapasya tathā kule \|*  
*gotrakārānṛṣīnvakṣye teṣāṃ nāmāni me śṛṇu \|\| 1 \|\|*

*āśrāyaṇiṛṣīgaṇo meṣakīriṭakāyanāḥ \|*  
*udagrajā māṭharāśca bhojā vinayalakṣaṇāḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*śālāhaleyāḥ kauriṣṭāḥ kanyakāścā’surāyaṇāḥ \|*  
*mandākinyāṃ vai mṛgayāḥ śrotanā bhautapāyanāḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*devayānā gomayānā hyadhaśchāyābhayāśca ye \|*  
*kātyāyanāḥ śakrayaṇā barhiryogagadāyanāḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*bhavanandirmahācakrirdākṣapāyaṇa eva ca \|*  
*yodhayānāḥ kārtivayo hastidānāstathaiva ca \|\| 5 \|\|*

*vātsyāyanā nikṛtajā hyāśvalāyaninastathā \|*  
*prāgāyaṇāḥ pailamaulirāśvavātāyanastathā \|\| 6 \|\|*

*kauberakāśca śyākārā agniśarmāyaṇāśca ye \|*  
*meṣapāḥ kaikarasapāstathā caiva tu babhravaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*prāceyo jñānasaṃjñeyā āgnā prāsevya eva ca \|*  
*śyāmodarā vaivaśapāstathā caivodbalāyanāḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*kāṣṭhāhāriṇamārīcā ājihāyanahāstikāḥ \|*  
*vaikarṇeyāḥ kāśyapeyāḥ sāsisāhāritāyanāḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*mātaṅginaśca bhṛgavastr! yārṣeyāḥ parikīrtitāḥ \|*  
*vatsaraḥ kaśyapaścaiva nidhruvaśca mahātapāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

1-10. Matsya said: — Marichis sons were known as Kashyapa and the following Rishis were the descendants of Kashyapa: — Ashrayani, Rishigana, Maishaki, Ritakayana, Udagraja, Mathara, Bhoja, Vinayalakshana, Sala, Halaiya, Kaurishta, Kanyaka, Surayana, Mandakini gave birth to Mrigaya, Shrutaya, Bhojayapana, Devayana, Gomayana, Adhashchaya, Katyayana, Shakrayana, Barhiyoga, Gadayana, Bhavanandi, Mahachakri, Dakshapayana, Yodhayana, Kartivaya, Hastidana, Vatsyayana, Kritaja, Ashvalayani, Pragayana, Paulamauli, Ashvavatayana, Kanvairaka, Shyakara, Agnisharmayana, Maishpa, Kaikarasapa, Vabhru, Prachaiya, Gyanasamgaiya, Agnaprasaivya, Syamodara, Vaivashapa, Udvalayana, Kastaharina, Mancha, Ajihayana, Hastika, Vaikarnaiya, Kashyapaiya, Sasisa, Haritayana, Mantagina and Bhrigava. They have Vatsara, Kashyapa, Nidhruva, for their Pravara. They do not intermarry.

## \|\| 199.11-19 \|\|

*parasparamavaivāhyā ṛṣayaḥ parikīrtitāḥ \|*  
*ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi dvāmuṣyāyaṇagotrajān \|\| 11 \|\|*

*anasūyo nākurayaḥ snātapo rājavartapaḥ \|*  
*śaiśirodavahiścaiva sairandhrī raupasevakiḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*yāmuniḥ kādrupiṅgākṣiḥ sajātambistathaiva ca \|*  
*divāvaṣṭāśca ityete bhaktyā jñeyāśca kāśyapāḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*tr! yārṣeyāśca tathaivaiṣāṃ sarveṣāṃ pravarāḥ śubhāḥ \|*  
*vatsaraḥ kaśyapaścaiva vasiṣṭhaśca mahātapāḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*parasparamavaivāhyā ṛṣayaḥ parikīrtitāḥ \|*  
*saṃyātiśca nabhaścobhau pippalyo'tha jalaṃdharaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*bhujātapūraḥ pūryaśca kardamo gardabhīmukhaḥ \|*  
*hiraṇyabāhukairātāvubhau kāśyapagobhilau \|\| 16 \|\|*

*kulaho vṛṣakaṇḍaśca mṛgaketustathottaraḥ \|*  
*nidāghamasṛṇau bhartsyā mahāntaḥ keralāśca ye \|\| 17 \|\|*

*śāṇḍilyo dānavaścaiva tathā vai devajātayaḥ \|*  
*paippalādiḥ sapravarā ṛṣayaḥ parikīrtitāḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*tr! yārṣeyābhimatāścaiṣāṃ sarveṣāṃ pravarāḥ śubhāḥ \|*  
*asito devalaścaiva kaśyapaśca mahātapāḥ \|*  
*parasparamavaivāhyā ṛṣayaḥ parikīrtitāḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

11-19. I shall now tell you the Rishis of Dvyamushyayana clan, vis. — Anashuya, Nakuraya, Snatapa, Rajavartapa, Shaishira, Davahi, Sairandhri, Ropasaivaka, Yamumi, Kadrupingakshi, Jatamvi, Divarashtashva who have Vatsara, Kashyapa, Vasishtha for their Pravara. They do not intermarry. Samyati, Nabha, Pipalya, Jalandhara, Bhujatapura, Purya, Kardama, Gardabhimukha, Hiranyabahu, Kairata, Kashyapa, Gobhila, Kulaha, Vrishkanda, Mrigaketu, Uttara Nidagha, Masrina, Bhartsya, Mahanta, Kerala, Shandilya. Danava, Deva. They are all Pravaras having Asita, Devala and Kashyapa for their Pravaras and consequently they are known as Tryarsheya Pravara. They do not intermarry.

## \|\| 199.20 \|\|

*ṛṣipradhānasya ca kaśyapasya dākṣāyaṇībhyaḥ sakalaṃ prasūtam \|*  
*jagatsamagraṃ manusiṃha puṇyaṃ kiṃ te pravakṣyāmyahamuttaraṃ tu \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. “Manu! I have told you the descendants of the chief Rishi Kashyapa. From Dakshayani, he begot the universe and how can it be described adequately.”

## Chapter 200

## \|\| 200.1-16 \|\|

*matsya uvāca*  
*vasiṣṭhavaṃśajānviprānnibodha vadato mama \|*  
*ekārṣeyastu pravaro vāsiṣṭhānāṃ prakīrtitaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*vasiṣṭhā eva vāsiṣṭhā avivāhyā vasiṣṭhajaiḥ \|*  
*vyāghrapādā aupagavā vaiklavāḥ śādvalāyanāḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*kapiṣṭhalā aupalomā alabdhāśca śaṭhāḥ kaṭhāḥ \|*  
*gaupāyanā bodhapāśca dākavyā hyatha vāhyakāḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*bāliśayāḥ pāliśayāstato vāggranthayaśca ye \|*  
*āpasthūṇāḥ śītavṛttāstathā brāhmapureyakāḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*lomāyanāḥ svastikarāḥ śāṇḍilirgauḍinistathā \|*  
*vāḍohaliśca sumanāścopāvṛddhistathaiva ca \|\| 5 \|\|*

*caulirvaulirbrahmabalaḥ pauliḥ śravasa eva ca \|*  
*pauḍavo yājñavalkyaśca akārṣeyā maharṣayaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*vasiṣṭha eṣāṃ pravaro hyavaivāhyāḥ parasparam \|*  
*śailālayo mahākarṇaḥ kauravyaḥ krodhinastathā \|\| 7 \|\|*

*kapiñjalā vālakhilyā bhāgavittāyanāśca ye \|*  
*kaulāyanaḥ kālaśikhaḥ korakṛṣṇāḥ surāyaṇāḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*śākāhāryāḥ śākadhiyaḥ kāṇvā upalapāśca ye \|*  
*śākāyanā uhākāśca atha māṣaśarāvayāḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*dākāyanā bālavayo vākayo gorathāstathā \|*  
*lambāyanāḥ śyāmavayo ye ca kroḍodarāyaṇāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*pralambāyanāśca ṛṣaya aupamanyava eva ca \|*  
*sāṃkhyāyanāśca ṛṣayastathā vai vedaśerakāḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*pālaṅkāyana udgāhā ṛṣayaśca balekṣavaḥ \|*  
*māteyā brahmamalinaḥ pannāgāristathaiva ca \|\| 12 \|\|*

*tr! yārṣeyo'bhimataścaiṣāṃ sarveṣāṃ pravarastathā \|*  
*bhagīvasurvasiṣṭhaśca indra pramadireva ca \|\| 13 \|\|*

*parasparamavaivāhyā ṛṣayaḥ parikīrtitāḥ \|*  
*aupasthalāsvasthalayo bālo hālo halāśca ye \|\| 14 \|\|*

*mādhyaṃdino mākṣatayaḥ paippalādirvicakṣuṣaḥ \|*  
*traiśṛṅgāyaṇasaibalkāḥ kuṇḍinaśca narottama \|\| 15 \|\|*

*tr! yārṣeyābhimatāścaiṣāṃ sarveṣāṃ pravarāḥ śubhāḥ \|*  
*vasiṣṭhamitrāvaruṇau kuṇḍinaśca mahātapāḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

1-16. Matsya said: — Hear from me about the Brahmanas of Vasistha family. They are Ekarsheya Pravara. Those of the Vasistha-gotra are known as Vasishtha. They do not intermarry among themselves. In this way it is one Pravara. Vyaghrapada, Aupagava, Vaiklava, Shadvalayana, Kapishthala, Aupaloma, Alabdha, Shatha, Katha, Gaupayana, Bodhapa, Dakavya, Vahyaka, Balishaya, Palishaya, Vagranthaya, Apasthuna, Sitavritta, Brahmapureyaka, Lomayana, Svastikara, Shandili, Gaudini, Vadohali, Sumana, Upavriddhi, Chauli, Vauli, Brahmabala, Pauli, Shravasa, Paudava, Yajnavalkya, are all Ekarsheya and Vasistha is their Pravara. They do not intermarry, Shailalaya, Mahakarna, Kauravya, Krodhina, Kapinjala, Valkhilya, Bhagavittayana, Kaulayana, Kalashikha, Korakrishna, Surayana, Sakaharya, Sakadhiya, Kanva, Upalapa, Shakayana, Uhaka, Mashasharavaya,

Dakayana, Balavaya, Vakaya, Goratha, Lambayana, Shyamavaya, Krododarayana, Pralambayana, Aupamanyava, Sankhyayana, Vedasheraka, Palankayana, Udgaha, Balaksheva, Mateya, Brahmamali, Pannaga, have three Pravaras, viz.— Bhigivasu, Vasistha and Indrapramadi. They do not intermarry. Aupasthala, Svasthali, Balo, Hilo, Hala, Madyandini, Maksataya, Paipalidi, Vichakshusha, Traishringayana, Saivalka, Kundina, have Vasistha, Mitravaruna and Kundina for their Pravara

## \|\| 200.17-18 \|\|

*dānakāyā mahāvīryā nāgeyāḥ paramāstathā \|*  
*ālambā vāyanaścāpi ye cakroḍādayo narāḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*parasparamavaivāhyā ṛṣayaḥ parikīrtitāḥ \|*  
*śivakarṇo vayaścaiva pādapaśca tathaiva ca \|\| 18 \|\|*

17-18. All these Rishis do not intermarry. Shivakarna, Vaya, Padapa have Jatukarnya, Vasistha, and Atri for their Pravara, O king! and they also cannot intermarry.

## \|\| 200.19 \|\|

*tr! yārṣeyo'bhimataścaiṣāṃ sarveṣāṃ pravarastathā \|*  
*jātūkarṇyo vasiṣṭhaśca tathaivātriśca pārthiva \|*  
*parasparamavaivāhyā ṛṣayaḥ parikīrtitāḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. “Manu! I have named to you all the Rishis of the Vasistha clan, By reciting their name one is freed from all ills.”

## Chapter 201

## \|\| 201.1-2 \|\|

*matsya uvāca*  
*vasiṣṭhastu mahātejā nimeḥpūrvapurohitaḥ \|*  
*babhūvuḥ pārthivaśreṣṭha yajñāstasya samantataḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*śrāntātmā pārthivaśreṣṭha viśaśrāma tadā guruḥ \|*  
*taṃ gatvā pārthivaśreṣṭho nimirvacanamabravīt \|\| 2 \|\|*

1-2. Matsya said: — O best of sovereigns, when the illustrious sage Vasishtha became the preceptor of king Nimi, the latter performed a series of sacrifices. The sage on the conclusion of those sacrifices feeling tired, took rest for a while. The illustrious king Nimi went and said to him.

## \|\| 201.3-4 \|\|

*bhagavanyaṣṭumicchāmi tanmāṃ yājaya mā ciram \|*  
*tamuvāca mahātejā vasiṣṭhaḥ pārthivottamam \|\| 3 \|\|*

*kaṃcitkālaṃ pratīkṣasva tava yajñaiḥ susattamaiḥ \|*  
*śrānto'smi rājanviśramya yājayiṣyāmi te nṛpa \|\| 4 \|\|*

3-4. “Lord! I wish, to perform more sacrifices, pray therefore do help me without delay.”

The sage Vasistha of great lustre replied: —

“King! wait a while, I have become quite tired by attending to the performances of your sacrifices, and shall get your farther sacrifices performed soon after 1 feel recouped.”

## \|\| 201.5-8 \|\|

*evamuktaḥ pratyuvāca vasiṣṭhaṃ nṛpasattamaḥ \|*  
*pāralaukikakārye tu kaḥ pratīkṣitumutsahet \|\| 5 \|\|*

*na ca me sauhṛdaṃ brahmankṛtāntena balīyasā \|*  
*dharmakārye tvarā kāryā calaṃ yasmāddhi jīvitam \|\| 6 \|\|*

*dharmapathyodano janturmṛto'pi sukhamaśnute \|*  
*śvaḥ kāryamadya kurvīta pūrvāhṇe cā’parāhṇikam \|\| 7 \|\|*

*na hi pratīkṣate mṛtyuḥ kṛtaṃ cāsya na vā kṛtam \|*  
*kṣetrāpaṇagṛhāsaktamanyatragatamānasam \|\| 8 \|\|*

5-8. Having been thus spoken to, the king said to Vasishtha Sage no one is dear to the messenger of death, nor has anyone a hold upon him. There is no certainty of life, therefore virtuous acts should be performed without a moment's delay.

## \|\| 201.7-10 \|\|

*dharmapathyodano janturmṛto'pi sukhamaśnute \|*  
*śvaḥ kāryamadya kurvīta pūrvāhṇe cā’parāhṇikam \|\| 7 \|\|*

*na hi pratīkṣate mṛtyuḥ kṛtaṃ cāsya na vā kṛtam \|*  
*kṣetrāpaṇagṛhāsaktamanyatragatamānasam \|\| 8 \|\|*

*vṛkīvoraṇamāsādya mṛtyurādāya gacchati \|*  
*na kālasya priyaḥ kaściddveṣyaścāsya na vidyate \|\| 9 \|\|*

*āyuṣye karmaṇi kṣīṇe prasahya harate janam \|*  
*prāṇavāyoścalatvaṃ ca tvayā viditameva ca \|\| 10 \|\|*

7-10. The soul engaged in righteousness is in a state of enjoyment within me. Virtuous deeds fixed to be performed on the morrow should he accomplished to-day; for death does not take into consideration that man has yet to accomplish certain things. Those who pin their interests »#' shops, houses, and other similar things, perish in a moment. Death is neither friendly nor hostile to anyone. The moment one exhausts his Store of Prarabdha karmas, Death lays its hand on him then and there. The breath of life is so transient which you know very well.

## \|\| 201.11-12 \|\|

*yadatra jīvyate brahmankṣaṇamātraṃ tadadbhutam \|*  
*śarīraṃ śāśvataṃ manye vidyābhyāse dhanārjane \|\| 11 \|\|*

*aśāśvataṃ dharmakārye ṛṇavānasmi saṃkaṭe \|*  
*so'haṃ saṃbhṛtasaṃbhāro bhavanmūlamupāgataḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-12. Brahmana! one should indeed wonder at his momentary existence. I look upon my life as lasting when I am' in my pursuit of knowledge and virtue, but consider it fleeting in the performance of righteous acts. l am overwhelmed with these ideas and feel that there is a heavy burden on me. I have therefore come to you to relieve me of my load.

## \|\| 201.13-16 \|\|

*ne cedyājayase māṃ tvamanyaṃ yāsyāmi yājakam \|*  
*evamuktastadā tena niminā brāhmaṇottamaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*śaśāpa taṃ nimiṃ krodhādvidehastvaṃ bhaviṣyasi \|*  
*śrāntaṃ māṃ tvaṃ samutsṛjya yasmādanyaṃ dvijottamam \|\| 14 \|\|*

*dharmajñastu narendra tvaṃ yājakaṃ kartumicchasi \|*  
*nimistaṃ pratyuvācātha dharmakāryaratasya me \|\| 15 \|\|*

*vighnaṃ karoṣi nānyena yājanaṃ ca tathecchasi \|*  
*śāpaṃ dadāmi tasmāttvaṃ videho'tha bhaviṣyasi \|\| 16 \|\|*

13-16. If thou wilt not help me in the performance of sacrifices, I shall have to get them performed through some other Brahmana.” Hearing those Words of the king, the sage pronounced the following curse on him: — “O, virtuous king! thou wishes to discharge me when I am feeling so tired and proposest to appoint another preceptor; become devoid of thine form.” The king also pronounced the following curse on the sage “Twice-born priest, thou art an obstacle in the path of my righteousness, thou wilt also therefore become devoid of thine form.”

## \|\| 201.17 \|\|

*evamukte tu tau jātau videhau dvijapārthivau \|*  
*dehahīnau tayorjīvau brahmāṇamupajagmatuḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. On account of those curses both the sage and the king were bereft of their forms, after which their souls went to Lord Brahma.

## \|\| 201.18-22 \|\|

*tāvāgatau samīkṣyāya brahmā vacanamabravīt \|*  
*adyaprabhṛti te sthānaṃ nime jīva dadāmyaham \|\| 18 \|\|*

*netrapakṣmasu sarveṣāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ bhaviṣyasi \|*  
*tvatsaṃbandhāttathā teṣāṃ nimeṣaḥ saṃbhaviṣyati \|\| 19 \|\|*

*cālayiṣyanti tu tadā netrapakṣmāṇi mānavāḥ \|*  
*evamukto manuṣyāṇāṃ netrapakṣmasu sarvaśaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*jagāma nimijīvastu varadānātsvayaṃbhuvaḥ \|*  
*vasiṣṭhajīvaṃ bhagavānbrahma vacanamabravīt \|\| 21 \|\|*

*mitrāvaruṇayoḥ putro vasiṣṭha tvaṃ bhaviṣyasi \|*  
*vasiṣṭheti ca te nāma tatrāpi ca bhaviṣyati \|\| 22 \|\|*

18-22 Seeing those souls approaching Him, Lord Brahma said: “King Nimi henceforth I shall give thee a foremost place. Thou shalt now be ever present in the eyes of all the creatures and they shall open and shut their eyes by virtue of thy glory,” By the ordinance of Brahma, Nimi accordingly became ever present in the eyes of ail the creatures. Afterwards, Brahma also said to Vasistha; — “Vasistha, thou shall be the son of Mitra and Varuna where thou wilt be known by thy present name.

## \|\| 201.23-25 \|\|

*janmadvayamatītaṃ ca tatrāpi tvaṃ smariṣyasi \|*  
*etasminneva kāle tu mitraśca varuṇastathā \|\| 23 \|\|*

*badaryāśramamāsādya tapastepaturavyayam \|*  
*tapasyatostayorevaṃ kadācinmādhave ṛtau \|\| 24 \|\|*

*puṣpitadrumasaṃsthāne śubhe dayitamārute \|*  
*urvaśī tu varārohā kurvatī kusumoccayam \|\| 25 \|\|*

23-25. Thou wilt have a recollection of your previous existence.” A wards, once upon a time, Mitra and Varuna were practising austerities in Badrikashrama, During spring when the balmy breeze was beating the flower-plants of the season, the 'most enchanting Ur vast herself with flowers,

## \|\| 201.26-27 \|\|

*susūkṣmaraktavasanā tayordṛṣṭipathaṃ gatā \|*  
*tāṃ dṛṣṭvendumukhīṃ subhrūṃ nīlanīrajalocanām \|\| 26 \|\|*

*ubhau cukṣubhaturdevau tadrū paparimohitau \|*  
*tapasyatostayorvīryamaskhalacca mṛgāsane \|\| 27 \|\|*

26-27. That nymph dressed in a fine spun thin attire of red colour appeared before Mitra and Varuna and on seeing her enchanting face, with eyes like the blue lotus? they both were moved and dropped their semen-virile.

## \|\| 201.28-29 \|\|

*skannaṃ retastato dṛṣṭvā śāpabhītā varāpsarā \|*  
*cakāra kalaśe śukraṃ toyapūrṇe manorame \|\| 28 \|\|*

*tasmādṛṣivarau jātau tejasā'pratimau bhuvi \|*  
*vasiṣṭhaścāpyagastyaśca mitrāvaruṇayoḥ sutau \|\| 29 \|\|*

28-29. Seeing it, both the Rishis for fear of a curse threw the semen-virile in a beautiful pitcher full of water; and out of it were born the illustrious sages Vasishtha and Agastya.

## \|\| 201.30-31 \|\|

*vasiṣṭhastūpayeme'tha bhaginīṃ nāradasya tu \|*  
*arundhatīṃ varārohāṃ tasyāṃ śaktimajījanat \|\| 30 \|\|*

*śakteḥ parāśaraḥ putrastasya vaṃśaṃ nibodha me \|*  
*yasya dvaipāyanaḥ putraḥ svayaṃ viṣṇurajāyata \|\| 31 \|\|*

30-31. Vasistha married Arundhati, the sister of Narada, who became the mother of Shakti. Shakti became the father of Parashara in whose family Lord Vishnu in the form of Vedavyasa was born. The very same family will now be enumerated.

## \|\| 201.32-33 \|\|

*prakāśo janito yena loke bhāratacandra māḥ \|*  
*yenājñānatamondhasya lokasyonmīlanaṃ kṛtam \|*  
*parāśarasya tasya tvaṃ śṛṇuvaṃśamanuttamam \|\| 32 \|\|*

*kauṇḍaśayo vāhanapo jaihmapo bhaumatāpanaḥ \|*  
*gopālireṣāṃ pañcama ete gaurāḥ parāśarāḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

32-33. Vedavyasa produced the moonlike Bharata in the world. The following is the family of Parashara, viz., Kandasapa, Vahanapa, Jaihyapa, Bhaumatapana, Gopali, these five are known as the Gaura Parashara.

## \|\| 201.34 \|\|

*prapohayā vāhyamayāḥ khyāteyāḥ kautujātayaḥ \|*  
*haryaśviḥ pañcamo hyeṣāṃ nīlā jñeyāḥ parāśarāḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Prapohaya, Vahyamaya, Khyataiya, Kantu race. Haryashva, are known as Nila Parashara.

## \|\| 201.35 \|\|

*kārṣṇāyanāḥ kapimukhāḥ kākeyasthā japātayaḥ \|*  
*puṣkaraḥ pañcamaścaiṣāṃ kṛṣṇā jñeyāḥ parāśarāḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Karshyayana, Kapisukha, Kakaiyastha, Japataya, Pushkara, are known as Krishna Parashara.

## \|\| 201.36 \|\|

*śrāviṣṭhāyanabāleyāḥ svāyaṣṭāścopayāśca ye \|*  
*iṣīkahastaścaite vai pañca śvetāḥ parāśarāḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Avishthayana, Valaiya, Svayashta, Upaya, Ishikahasta, are the five Shveta Parasharas.

## \|\| 201.37 \|\|

*vāṭiko bādariścaiva stambā vai krodhanāyanāḥ \|*  
*kṣaimireṣāṃ pañcamastu ete śyāmāḥ parāśarāḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Patika, Badari, Stamba, Krodhanayana and Kshaumi, are the five Shyama Parasharas.

## \|\| 201.38 \|\|

*khalyāyanā vārṣṇāyanāstaileyāḥ khalu yūthapāḥ \|*  
*tantireṣāṃ pañcamastu ete dhūmrāḥ parāśarāḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Khalyayana, Varshnayana, Jailaiya, Yuthapa and Panti, are the five Dhumra Parasharas

## \|\| 201.39 \|\|

*parāśarāṇāṃ sarveṣāṃ tr! yārṣeyaḥ pravaro mataḥ \|*  
*parāśaraśca śaktiśca vasiṣṭhaśca mahātapāḥ \|*  
*parasparamavaivāhyā sarva ete parāśarāḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. “King! I have related to you the chief Rishis of the Parashara family illustrious like the Sun. One who recites their names dispels all his sins”.

## Chapter 202

## \|\| 202.1-4 \|\|

*matsya uvāca*  
*ataḥ paramagastyasya vakṣye vaṃśodbhavāndvijān \|*  
*agastyaśca karambhaśca kauśalyāḥ śakaṭāstathā \|\| 1 \|\|*

*sumedhaso mayobhuvastathā gāndhārakāyaṇāḥ \|*  
*paulastyā paulahāścaiva kratuvaṃśabhavāstathā \|\| 2 \|\|*

*tr! yārṣeyābhimatāścaiṣāṃ sarveṣāṃ pravarāḥ śubhāḥ \|*  
*agastyaśca mahendra śca ṛṣiścaiva mayobhuvaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*parasparamavaivāhyā ṛṣayaḥ parikīrtitāḥ \|*  
*paurṇamāsāḥ pāraṇāśca tr! yārṣeyāḥ parikīrtitāḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

1-4. Matsya said: — “Now hear about the Brail manas born in the Agastya family. They are: — Agastya, Karambha, Kaushalya, Sakata, Sumedha, Mayobhuva, Gandharakayana and those born in the Pulastya, Pulaha and Kratu families are known also as Agastyas, all of them have three Pravaras, Agastya, Paurnamasa and Parana. These Rishis do not intermarry amongst each other. Those of the Agastya, Paurnamasa and Parana families do not also intermarry.

## \|\| 202.5-6 \|\|

*agastyaḥ paurṇamāsaśca pāraṇaśca mahātapāḥ \|*  
*parasparamavaivāhyāḥ paurṇamāsāstu pāraṇaiḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*evamukta ṛṣīṇāṃ tu vaṃśa uttamapauruṣaḥ \|*  
*ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi kiṃ bhavānadya kathyatām \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. The Paurnamasas particularly do not marry the Paranas. I have described to you the families of the renowned sages, now let me know what more do you wish to hear.”

## \|\| 202.7 \|\|

*manuruvāca*  
*pulahasya pulastyasya kratoścaiva mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*agastyasya tathā caiva kathaṃ vaṃśastaducyatām \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Manu said Pray let me know the origin of the families of Pulaha, Pulastya, and Kratu; how they came to be recognised as included in the family of Agastya.”

## \|\| 202.8-10 \|\|

*matsya uvāca*  
*kratuḥ khalvanapatyo'bhūdrā janvaivasvate'ntare \|*  
*idhmavāhaṃ sa putratve jagrāha ṛṣisattamaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*agastyaputraṃ dharmajñamāgastyāḥ kratavastataḥ \|*  
*pulahasya tathā putrāstrayaśca pṛthivīpate \|\| 9 \|\|*

*teṣāṃ tu janma vakṣyāmi uttaratra yathāvidhi \|*  
*pulahastu prajāṃ dṛṣṭvā nātiprītamanāḥ svakām \|\| 10 \|\|*

8-10. Matsya said: — “King! at the end of the Vaivasvata-manvantara Kratu was without an offspring when he adopted as his son Idhmavaha the virtuous son of Agastya; consequently those belonging to the family of Idhmavaha are called Agastya and Kratu. Paul aha had three sons.

Afterwards I will tell you of their origin. He was not pleased with them,

## \|\| 202.11 \|\|

*agastyajaṃ dṛḍhāsyaṃ tu putratve vṛtavāṃstataḥ \|*  
*paulahāśca tathā rājannāgastyāḥ parikīrtitāḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. He therefore adopted Dridhasya, the son of Agastya, on account of which those born in the family of Dridhasya are known as Agastya and Paulaha.

## \|\| 202.12 \|\|

*pulastyānvayasaṃbhūtāndṛṣṭvā rakṣaḥ samudbhavān \|*  
*agastyasya sutaṃ dhīmānputratve vṛtavāṃstataḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. The Rishi Pulastya finding his sons becoming Rakshasas became very sorry and adopted as his son the promising son of Agastya.

## \|\| 202.13 \|\|

*paulastyāśca tathā rājannāgastyāḥ parikīrtitāḥ \|*  
*sagotratvādime sarve parasparamananvayāḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. For this reason those born in the Paulastya family are known as Agastya. They being of the same gotra do not intermarry.

## \|\| 202.14 \|\|

*ete tavoktāḥ pravarā dvijānāṃ mahānubhāvā nṛpa vaṃśakārāḥ \|*  
*eṣāṃ tu nāmnā parikīrtitena pāpaṃ samagraṃ puruṣo jahāti \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. I have described to you the originators of the families and the Pravaras of the illustrious Brahmanas. One who recites their names is liberated from all sins.”

## Chapter 203

## \|\| 203.1 \|\|

*matsya uvāca*  
*asminvaivasvate prāpte śṛṇu dharmasya pārthiva \|*  
*dākṣāyaṇībhyaḥ sakalaṃ vaṃśaṃ daivatamuttamam \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Matsya said; — “O King! I shall relate to you now the families born of the daughters of Daksha from Dharmaraja at the beginning of the Vaivasvata-manvantara.. Please hear.”

## \|\| 203.2-4 \|\|

*parvatādimahādurgaśarīrāṇi narādhipa \|*  
*arundhatyāḥ prasūtāni dharmādvaivasvate'ntare \|\| 2 \|\|*

*aṣṭau ca vasavaḥ putrāḥ somapāśca vibhostathā \|*  
*dharo dhruvaśca somaśca āpaścaivānalānilau \|\| 3 \|\|*

*pratyūṣaśca prabhāsaśca vasavo'ṣṭau prakīrtitāḥ \|*  
*dharasya putro dra viṇaḥ kālaḥ putro dhruvasya tu \|\| 4 \|\|*

2-4. Arundhati through Dharma begot the eight Vasus and the Soma pa Devas who were most mighty and stalwart. Dhara, Dhruva, Soma, Apava Anila, Anala, Pratyasa, and Prabhasa were the eight Vasus. Dravina was the son of Dhara, and Kala of Dhruva.

## \|\| 203.5-8 \|\|

*kālasyāvayavānāṃ tu śarīrāṇi narādhipa \|*  
*mūrtimanti ca kālāddhi saṃprasūtānyaśeṣataḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*somasya bhavagānvarcāḥ śrīmāṃścā’pasya kīrtyate \|*  
*anekajanmajananaḥ kumārastvanalasya tu \|\| 6 \|\|*

*purojavāścānilasya pratyūṣasya tu devalaḥ \|*  
*viśvakarmā prabhāsasya tridaśānāṃ sa vardhakiḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*samīhitakarāḥ proktā nāgavīthyādayo nava \|*  
*lambāputraḥ smṛto ghoṣo bhānoḥ putrāśca bhānavaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

5-8. Years, etc., came into existence out of Kala; these were His sons. Soma begot the illustrious Varcha; Shriman was the son of Apa. Anala became the father of Anekajanmajanana and Purojava was the son of Anila. Pratyasa was the father of Devala and Prabhasa was the father of Vishvakarma who is the architect of the Devas. Nagavithis, etc., the nine sons, acted according to the wishes of others. Lamba’s son was Ghosa and his sons were known as the Bhanavas.

## \|\| 203.9 \|\|

*graharkṣāṇāṃ ca sarveṣāmanyeṣāṃ cāmitaujasām \|*  
*marutvatyāṃ marutvantaḥ sarve putrāḥ prakīrtitāḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The stars and planets and Marutvan were born of Marutvati and are known.as Marutvamsha.

## \|\| 203.10 \|\|

*saṃkalpāyāśca saṃkalpastathā putraḥ prakīrtitaḥ \|*  
*muhūrtāśca muhūrtāyāḥ sādhyāḥ sādhyāsutāḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Samkalpa gave birth to Samkalpa, Mahurta to Mahurtas, and Sadhya gave birth, to Sadhyas.

## \|\| 203.11-12 \|\|

*manormanuśca prāṇaśca naroṣā noca vīryavān \|*  
*cittahāryo'yanaścaiva haṃso nārāyaṇastathā \|\| 11 \|\|*

*vibhuścāpi prabhuścaiva sādhyā dvādaśa kīrtitāḥ \|*  
*viśvāyāśca tathā putrā viśve devāḥ prakīrtitāḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-12. Bhanu, Manu. Prana, Rosa, Nicha, Viryavana, Chiltaharya, Ayana, Hamsa, Narayana, Vibhu and Prabhu were the twelve Sadhyas. These were the sons of Sadhyas. Vishva gave birth to Vishvedevas.

## \|\| 203.13 \|\|

*kraturdakṣo vasuḥ satyaḥ kālakāmo munistathā \|*  
*kurajo manujo vījo rocamānaśca te daśa \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Kratu, Daksha, Vasu, Satya, Kalakama, Muni, Karaja, Manuja, Vija, Rochamana, were the ten Vishvedevas.

## \|\| 203.14 \|\|

*etāvaduktastava dharmavaṃśaḥ saṃkṣepataḥ pārthivavaṃśamukhya \|*  
*vyāsena vaktuṃ na hi śakyamasti rājanvinā varṣaśatairanekaiḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14 King! I have briefly narrated to you the family of Dharma and no one but Vyasa can describe it at full length for want of sufficient time.”

## Chapter 204

## \|\| 204.1-4 \|\|

*matsya uvāca*  
*etadvaṃśabhavā viprāḥ śrāddhe bhojyāḥ prayatnataḥ \|*  
*pitriṇāṃ vallabhaṃ yasmādeṣu śrāddhaṃ nareśvara \|\| 1 \|\|*

*ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi pitṛbhiryāḥ prakīrtitāḥ \|*  
*gāthāḥ pārthivaśārdūla kāmavadbhiḥ pure svake \|\| 2 \|\|*

*api syātsa kule'smākaṃ yo no dadyājжalāñjalim \|*  
*nadīṣu bahutoyāsu śītalāsu viśeṣataḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*api syātsa kule'smākaṃ yaḥ śrāddhaṃ nityamācaret \|*  
*payomūlaphalairbhakṣyaistilatoyena vā punaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

1-4. Matsya said: — “O King! the Brahmanas belonging to the families of Dharma are worthy of being feasted on the occasion of Shraddha as the gifts and food given to them with free will please the manes. O King I shall now tell you what the manes desire in their realms and thus sing songs there. They wish that some one of their family should offer them libations of water and balls of rice in some cool running stream; they thus say: — ‘Oh! will anyone be born in our families who will offer us simple handfuls of water in memory of us; especially offer us libations of water in some sacred rivers! Would any son be born in our families who offer ns daily libations of milk, roots and fruits along with other victuals and til (sesamum) and water?

## \|\| 204.5 \|\|

*api syātsa kule'smākaṃ yo no dadyāttrayodaśīm \|*  
*pāyasaṃ madhusarpirbhyāṃ varṣāsu ca maghāsu ca \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. ‘Oh! will there be born such a son amongst our families who would offer us libations of Payasa (cooked preparation of rice and milk and sugar) with clarified butter and honey on the thirteenth day of the lunar month in the rainy season under Magha asterism?

## \|\| 204.6 \|\|

*api syātsa kule'smākaṃ khaḍragamāṃsena yaḥ sakṛt \|*  
*śrāddhaṃ kuryātprayatnena kālaśākena vā punaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. ‘Who would also offer us the flesh of the rhinoceros or black herb according to the prescribed rites even for one day.

## \|\| 204.7 \|\|

*kālaśākaṃ mahāśākaṃ madhu munyannameva ca \|*  
*viṣāṇavarjā ye khaḍgā āsūryaṃ tadaśīmahi \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. The pittris say that the offerings of kala-shaka, maha-if4ka, honey, &c., and the appeasing grains used by the sages, the flesh of the rhinoceros that had not developed its horns keep them satisfied as long as sun exists.

## \|\| 204.8-9 \|\|

*gayāyāṃ darśane rāhoḥ khaḍgamāṃsena yoginām \|*  
*bhojayetkaḥ kule'smākaṃ chāyāyāṃ kuṃjarasya ca \|\| 8 \|\|*

*ākalpakālikī tṛptistenāsmākaṃ bhaviṣyati \|*  
*dātā sarveṣu lokeṣu kāmacāro bhaviṣyati \|\| 9 \|\|*

8-9. ‘One who appeases us by making offerings -of the rhinoceros flesh and feasting the yogis at Gaya during the solar and lunar eclipse or who will perform Shraddha and offer gifts during the Gajachchaya yoga so that we would be satisfied till the end of a kalpa, and the one who performs £Shraddha and make gifts will no doubt enjoy all pleasures in all the Lokas till the end of a kalpa and can go anywhere free at his will.

## \|\| 204.10-17 \|\|

*ābhūtasaṃplavaṃ kālaṃ nātra kāryā vicāraṇā \|*  
*yadetatpañcakaṃ tasmādekenāpi vayaṃ sadā \|\| 10 \|\|*

*tṛptiṃ prāpsyāma cānantāṃ kiṃ punaḥ sarvasaṃpadā \|*  
*api syātsa kule'smākaṃ dadyātkṛṣṇājinaṃ ca yaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*api syātsa kule'smākaṃ kaścitpuruṣasattamaḥ \|*  
*prasūyamānāṃ yo dhenuṃ dadyādbrāhmaṇapuṃgave \|\| 12 \|\|*

*api syātsa kule'smākaṃ vṛṣabhaṃ yaḥ samutsṛjet \|*  
*sarvavarṇaviśeṣeṇa śuklaṃ nīlaṃ vṛṣaṃ tathā \|\| 13 \|\|*

*api syātsa kule'smākaṃ yaḥ kuryācchraddhayā'nvitaḥ \|*  
*suvarṇadānaṃ godānaṃ pṛthivīdānameva ca \|\| 14 \|\|*

*api syātsa kule'smākaṃ kaścitpuruṣasattamaḥ \|*  
*kūpārāmataḍāgānāṃ vāpīnāṃ yaśca kārakaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*api syātsa kule'smākaṃ sarvabhāvena yo harim \|*  
*prayāyāccharaṇaṃ viṣṇuṃ deveśaṃ madhusūdanam \|\| 16 \|\|*

*api naḥ sa kule bhūyātkaścidvidvānvicakṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*dharmaśāstrāṇi yo dadyādvidhinā viduṣāmapi \|\| 17 \|\|*

10-17. Such a man undoubtedly gets the right of enjoying in every realm according to his pleasure till the end of the kalpa; and one who performs any of the above-mentioned five Shraddhas to the manes gives them satisfaction, for an infinite period. And if Shraddhas he performed with full ceremony they obtain unbounded pleasures. The pittris also say that if someone of their family gives away a skin of black deer in their name or a cow big with a young one to a Brahmana versed in the Vedas, or performs Vrishotsarga, i.e., sets free a bull in their name particularly a bull of white or bluish tint, or gives away gold or a cow with devotion, or a piece of land or a well, a tank, or a grove or attaches himself to Vishnu, or gives away Dharmashastras to the learned Brahmanas causes them unbounded satisfaction.

## \|\| 204.18 \|\|

*etāvaduktaṃ tava bhūmipāla śrāddhasya kalpaṃ munisaṃpradiṣṭam \|*  
*pāpāpahaṃ puṇyavivardhanaṃ ca lokeṣu mukhyatvakaraṃ tathaiva \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. King! I have narrated to yon what the sages have said in the Shraddha kalpa. The rituals pertaining to Shraddha drive away sins and bring virtue and comfort.”

## Chapter 205

## \|\| 205.1 \|\|

*manuruvāca*  
*prasūyamānā dātavyā dhenurbrāhmaṇapuṃgave \|*  
*vidhinā kena dharmajña dānaṃ dadyācca kiṃ phalam \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Manta said: — “O Knower of Dharma! pray tell me how under what prescribed rules, should a calving cow be given to a Brahmana and what are the benefits of such a charity?”

## \|\| 205.2-5 \|\|

*matsya uvāca*  
*svarṇaśṛṅgīṃ raupyakhurāṃ muktālāṅgūla bhūṣitām \|*  
*kāṃsyopadohanāṃ rājansavatsāṃ dvijapuṃgave \|\| 2 \|\|*

*prasūyamānāṃ gāṃ dattvā mahatpuṇyaphalaṃ labhet \|*  
*yāvadvatso yonigato yāvadgarbhaṃ na muñcati \|\| 3 \|\|*

*tāvadvai pṛthivī jñeyā saśailavanakānanā \|*  
*prasūyamānāṃ yo dadyāddhenuṃ dra viṇasaṃyutām \|\| 4 \|\|*

*sasamudra guhā tena saśailavanakānanā \|*  
*caturantā bhaveddattā pṛthivī nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

2-5. Matsya said: — “King! Its horns should be covered with gold, hoofs with silver, tail end with pearls. It should be given away along with her calf and utensils made of kansa, bell-metal. The giving away of such a cow begets immense good merits. The cow is like the earth with its mountains, forests, tic., till it bears her calf in her womb. One who gives it away at that time undoubtedly gets the benefits of having given away the land girt with four oceans.

## \|\| 205.6 \|\|

*yāvanti dhenuromāṇi vatsasya ca narādhipa \|*  
*tāvatsaṃkhyaṃ yugagaṇaṃ devaloke mahīyate \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. O King! the donor remains in heaven with great respect for as many years as there are hairs on the body of the calf and the cow.

## \|\| 205.7-8 \|\|

*pitrinpitāmahāṃścaiva tathaiva prapitāmahān \|*  
*uddhariṣyatyasaṃdehaṃ narakādbhūridakṣiṇaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*ghṛtakṣīravahāḥ kulyā dadhipāyasakardamāḥ \|*  
*yatra tatra gatistasya drumāścepsita kāmadāḥ \|*  
*golokaḥ sulabhastasya brahmalokaśca pārthiva \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8. Lots of fees (gifts) should be paid in this case. Thus the donor undoubtedly liberates his father, grandfather and great-grandfather from hell. He goes to the region where flow the rivers of clarified butter and milk and the land abounds with the mud of curds and milk and there are trees that give the desired fruits. He easily gets access to Goloka and Brahmaloka.

## \|\| 205.9 \|\|

*striyaśca taṃ candra samānavaktrāḥ prataptajāmbūnadatulyarūpāḥ \|*  
*mahānitambāstanuvṛttamadhyā bhajantyajasraṃ nalinābhanetrāḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. He gets a lady whose face is like the moon and whose colour is like burnished gold, her breasts are bloated, waist slender, and eyes are like-lotus.”

## Chapter 206

## \|\| 206.1 \|\|

*manuruvāca*  
*kṛṣṇājinapradānasya vidhikālau mamānagha \|*  
*brāhmaṇaṃ ca tathā'cakṣva tatra me saṃśayo mahān \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Manu said Deva! pray tell me how to make a gift of a black deer skin. Also explain to me who is the most worthy Brahmana of such a gift; and what is the proper time to do so; so that my doubts may be removed.

## \|\| 206.2-3 \|\|

*matsya uvāca*  
*vaiśākhī paurṇamāsī ca grahaṇe śaśisūryayoḥ \|*  
*paurṇamāsī tu yā māghī hyāṣāḍhī kārtikī tathā \|\| 2 \|\|*

*uttarāyaṇe ca dvādaśyāṃ tasyāṃ dattaṃ mahāphalam \|*  
*āhitāgnirdvijo yastu taddeyaṃ tasya pārthiva \|\| 3 \|\|*

2-3. Matsya said: — “On the full moon day in the month of Vaishakha, Magha, Asadha, and Kartika on the twelfth lunar day of the sun’s progress in the northern path, the giving away of the black deer skin begets incalculable benefits. It should be given to a Agnihotri Brahmana.

## \|\| 206.4-10 \|\|

*yathā yena vidhānena tanme nigadataḥ śṛṇu \|*  
*gomayenopalipte tu śucau deśe narādhipa \|\| 4 \|\|*

*ādāveva samāstīrya śobhanaṃ vastramāvikam \|*  
*tataḥ saśṛṅgaṃ sakhuramāstaretkṛṣṇamārgakam \|\| 5 \|\|*

*kartavyaṃ rukmaśṛṅgaṃ tadrau pyadantaṃ tathaiva ca \|*  
*lāṅgūlaṃ mauktikairyuktaṃ tilacchannaṃ tathaiva ca \|\| 6 \|\|*

*tilaiḥ supūritaṃ kṛtvā vāsasā’cchādayedbudhaḥ \|*  
*suvarṇanābhaṃ tatkuryādalaṃ kuryādviśeṣataḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*ratnairgandhairyathāśaktyā tasya dikṣu ca vinyaset \|*  
*kāṃsyapātrāṇi catvāri teṣu dadyādyathākramam \|\| 8 \|\|*

*mṛnmayeṣu ca pātreṣu pūrvādiṣu yathākramam \|*  
*ghṛtaṃ kṣīraṃ dadhi kṣaudra mevaṃ dadyādyathāvidhi \|\| 9 \|\|*

*campakasya tathā śākhāmavraṇaṃ kumbhameva ca \|*  
*bāhyopasthānakaṃ kṛtvā śubhacito niveśayet \|\| 10 \|\|*

4-10. Now listen how, it should be given away, king! First a cloth made of good goat wool should be spread on the floor washed with cow-dung. Over it should, be spread the skin of a black deer containing its horns and hoofs. The gold mounted horns, silver mounted teeth and the tail-end decorated with pearls should be covered with sesamum. Then everything should be covered with a piece of fine sacred cloth. Gold is to be placed on the navel. Afterwards it should also be decorated with jewels according to the means of the devotee and then incense is to be burnt round this. At all its four corners vessels -of bell-metal (kansa) should be placed and the clay pots on the eastern side should be filled in with clarified butter, milk, curd and honey. Another beautiful entire jar without any holes. in it should be placed for the sprinkling of water. It should be placed in a quiet corner after putting a Champaka twig on the east side of it.

## \|\| 206.11 \|\|

*sūkṣmavastraṃ śubhaṃ pītaṃ mārjanārthaṃ prayojayet \|*  
*tathā dhātumayaṃ pātraṃ pādayostasya dāpayet \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. There should be placed also a fine yellow or white cloth for wiping or cleaning. The vessels made of metals should be placed at both the hoofs.

## \|\| 206.12 \|\|

*yāni kāni ca pāpāni mayā lobhātkṛtāni vai \|*  
*lohapātrādidānena praṇaśyantu mamā’śu vai \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. The following formula should be recited: ‘Whatever sins I might have committed through avarice, be consumed by the giving away of this iron vessel’. Then the vessel is to be given over.

## \|\| 206.13-14 \|\|

*tilapūrṇaṃ tataḥ kṛtvā vāmapāde niveśayet \|*  
*yāni kāni ca pāpāni karmotthāni kṛtāni ca \|\| 13 \|\|*

*kāṃsyapātrapradānena tāni naśyantu me sadā \|*  
*madhupūrṇaṃ tu tatkṛtvā pāde vai dakṣiṇe nyaset \|\| 14 \|\|*

13-14. Afterwards the Queen’s metal vessel (i.e., kamsya vessel) filled with sesamum should be placed near the left foot; and the following formula should be uttered; ‘Whatever sins I may have committed through hearing be vanished by the gift of this vessel of Queen’s metal (white copper). Thus repeating the mantra, the vessel is to be given over. Then the vessel filled with honey should be placed at the right foot.

## \|\| 206.15 \|\|

*parāpavādapaiśunyādvṛthā māṃsasya bhakṣaṇāt \|*  
*tatrotthitaṃ ca me pāpaṃ tāmrapātrātpraṇaśyatu \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Then the following formulae should be recited ‘ Whatever sins I may have committed through insinuations, backbiting, or eating flesh not offered to the gods, be destroyed by the giving away of this copper vessel Then the vessel is to be given over.

## \|\| 206.16 \|\|

*kanyānṛtādgavāṃ caiva paradārābhimarṣaṇāt \|*  
*raupyapātrapradānāddhi kṣipraṃ nāśaṃ prayātu me \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. ‘Whatever sins I may have committed through false speaking in connection with a cow and a virgin and through lust for the women of others be vanished by the giving away of this silver vessel Then the vessel is to be given over.

## \|\| 206.17-19 \|\|

*ūrdhvapāde tvime kāryaṃ tāmrasya rajatasya ca \|*  
*janmāntarasahasreṣu kṛtaṃ pāpaṃ kubuddhinā \|\| 17 \|\|*

*suvarṇapātradānāttu nāśayā’śu janārdana \|*  
*hemamuktā vidrumaṃ ca dāḍimaṃ bījapūrakam \|\| 18 \|\|*

*praśastapātre śravaṇe khure śṛṅgāṭakāni ca \|*  
*evaṃ kṛtvā yathoktena sarvaśākaphalāni ca \|\| 19 \|\|*

17-19. Afterwards the copper and silver vessels should be placed at the fore-feet of the deer skin. Beautiful leaves containing gold, pearls, corals, pomegranates, citrons, etc., should be placed at the ears and (Sringatoka) pastry or dough is to be placed on the hoofs. Then various kinds of herb-vegetables and fruits should be placed and then the following formulae should be uttered: ‘Janardana! the sins that I may have committed through ignorance in thousands of my lives, be destroyed by the giving away of this vessel of gold

## \|\| 206.20-22 \|\|

*tatpratigrahavidvidvānāhitāgnirdvijottamaḥ \|*  
*snāto vastrayugacchannaḥ svaśaktyā cāpyalaṃ kṛtaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*pratigrahaśca tasyoktaḥ pucchadeśe mahīpate \|*  
*tata evaṃ samīpe tu mantramenamudīrayet \|\| 21 \|\|*

*kṛṣṇājineti kṛṣṇānhiraṇyaṃ madhusarpiṣī \|*  
*dadāti yastu viprāya sarvaṃ tarati duṣkṛtam \|\| 22 \|\|*

20-22. In such a way the Agnihotri Brahmana accepting the gift should take his bath, wear the pair of garments and he is to he bedecked according to the means of the devotee. He is then to accept the gift. The gift should be accepted at the tail-end and the following formulas should be uttered on that occasion: ‘Lord Mahadeva who wears the black-deer skin and who has a beautiful blue neck, therefore by the gift of this black deer skin He may be pleased. So Krishna be pleased.

## \|\| 206.23 \|\|

*yastu kṛṣṇājinaṃ dadyātsakhuraṃ śṛṅgasaṃyutam \|*  
*tilaiḥ pracchādya vāsobhiḥ sarvavastrairalaṃkṛtam \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. After thus giving away the gift to the Brahmana the devotee should not touch him for he becomes like the wood of a sacrificial post at the burning ceremonies not fit to be touched.

## \|\| 206.24-26 \|\|

*vaiśākhyāṃ paurṇamāsyāṃ tu viśākhāyāṃ viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*sasamudra guhā tena saśailavanakānanā \|\| 24 \|\|*

*saptadvīpānvitā dattā pṛthivī nātra saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*kṛṣṇakṛṣṇāṅgalo devaḥ kṛṣṇājina namo'stu te \|\| 25 \|\|*

*suvarṇadānāttvaddānāddhutapāpasya prīyatām \|*  
*trayastriṃśatsurāṇāṃ tvamādhāratve vyavasthitaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

24-26. That Brahmana should be avoided on the occasion of other gifts and Shraddha ceremony.' After sending him away the devotee should bathe.

He should pour over him the water full to the brim of the vase having a Champaka twig. The preceptor should first be called and the pitcher should be placed on the head. Then bath should be performed by the recitation of the sixteen Vedic hymns, as prescribed, viz., Apyayasva, Samudrajaishtha, etc. He is purified by putting on a pair of garments and making achaman after reciting ‘Ahtaivasasirita.’

## \|\| 206.27-28 \|\|

*kṛṣṇo'si mūrtimānsākṣātkṛṣṇājina namo'stu te \|*  
*suvarṇanābhikaṃ dadyātprīyatāṃ vṛṣabhadhvajaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

*kṛṣṇaḥ kṛṣṇagalo devaḥ kṛṣṇājinadharastathā \|*  
*taddānāddhūtapāpasya prīyatāṃ vṛṣabhadhvajaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

27-28. Then the jar along with the cloth should be lifted up and taken to a square where it should be dashed. The benefits accruing by the performance of such a charity cannot be fully described even by the Devas. To be brief the devotee gets the benefits of having given away the whole world in charity.

## \|\| 206.29 \|\|

*anena vidhinā dattvā yathāvatkṛṣṇamārgakam \|*  
*na spṛśyo'sau dvijo rājaṃścitiyūpasamo hi saḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. He conquers all the realms and moves about everywhere as he wills like a bird; and is paid great respect and undoubtedly remains in heaven till the annihilation of the universe.

## \|\| 206.30 \|\|

*taṃ dāne śrāddhakāle ca dūrataḥ parivarjayet \|*  
*svagṛhātpreṣya taṃ vipraṃ maṅgalasnānamācaret \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. His father and sons, etc., do not perish, nor is there a separation from his wife and he does not lose his wealth, realm, etc.

## \|\| 206.31 \|\|

*pūrṇakumbhena rājendra śākhayā campakasya tu \|*  
*kṛtvā’cāryaśca kalaśaṃ mantreṇānena mūrdhani \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. In this way the devotee gets such benefits and attains all his wishes. He is void of the cares of death”.

## Chapter 207

## \|\| 207.1 \|\|

*manuruvāca*  
*bhagavañchrotumicchāmi vṛṣabhasya tu lakṣaṇam \|*  
*vṛṣotsargavidhiṃ caiva tathā puṇyaphalaṃ mahat \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Manu said: — “Lord! I am desirous of knowing the qualities of a bull that ought to be set at liberty as mentioned in the previous chapters as well as the great merits resulting therefrom. Pray also tell me the ways of performing Vrishotsarga.”

**Комментарий:**

Note — Setting tree a bull (1) on the occasion of a funeral rite, or as a religious act generally.

## \|\| 207.2-8 \|\|

*matsya uvāca*  
*dhenumādau parīkṣeta suśīlāṃ ca guṇānvitām \|*  
*avyaṅgāmaparikliṣṭāṃ jīvavatsāmarogiṇīm \|\| 2 \|\|*

*snigdhavarṇāṃ snigdhakhurāṃ snigdhaśṛṅgīṃ tathaiva ca \|*  
*manoharākṛtiṃ saumyāṃ supramāṇāmanuddhatām \|\| 3 \|\|*

*āvartairdakṣiṇāvartairyuktāṃ dakṣiṇatastathā \|*  
*vāmāvartairvāmataśca vistīrṇajaghanāṃ tathā \|\| 4 \|\|*

*mṛdusaṃhatatāmroṣṭhīṃ raktagrīvāsuśobhitām \|*  
*aśyāmadīrghā sphuṭitā raktajihvā tathā ca yā \|\| 5 \|\|*

*visrāvāmalanetrā ca śaphairaviralairdṛḍhaiḥ \|*  
*vaidūryamadhuvarṇaiśca jalabudbudasaṃnibhaiḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*raktasnidhaiśca nayanaistathā raktakanīnikaiḥ \|*  
*saptacaturdaśadantā tathā vā śyāmatālukā \|\| 7 \|\|*

*ṣaḍunnatā suṣārśvoruḥ pṛthupañcasamāyatā \|*  
*aṣṭāyataśirogrīvā yā rājansā sulakṣaṇāḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

2-8. Matsya said: — “King! first of all the cow is to he examined; there should be a cow of gentle temper free from ailment and disease, strong, of nice colour, having beautiful hoofs and horns, well-built, of middle height, giving good milk, having curls on the body (especially curls turning to the left on the right side and turning to the right on the left side having all the lucky signs, with extensive thighs, red lips, neck and tongue, with eyes clear and beautiful (not red or having many hair) and hoofs large, having eyes of the lustre of Vaidurya, with lovely eye corners, having seven and seven teeth and bright palate, with lovely sides and thighs with six parts elevated, five parts level and eight parts' capacious and wide. A cow having these qualifications is said to have auspicious signs.”

## \|\| 207.9 \|\|

*manuruvāca*  
*ṣaḍunnatāḥ ke bhagavanke ca pañca samāyatāḥ \|*  
*āyatāśca tathaivāṣṭau dhenūnāṃ ke śubhāvahāḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Manu said Which six parts should be elevated? which five parts should be level? and which eight parts are to be capacious and wide?”

## \|\| 207.10 \|\|

*matsya uvāca*  
*uraḥ pṛṣṭhaṃ śiraḥ kukṣī śroṇī ca vasudhādhipa \|*  
*ṣaḍunnatāni dhenūnāṃ pūjayanti vicakṣaṇāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Matsya said “The following six parts of the cow’s body should be elevated, viz. — chest, hack, head, belly, loins.”

## \|\| 207.11-12 \|\|

*karṇau netre lalāṭaṃ ca pañca bhāskaranandana \|*  
*samāyatāni śasyante pucchaṃ sāsnā ca sakthinī \|\| 11 \|\|*

*catvāraśca stanā rājañjñeyā hyaṣṭau manīṣibhiḥ \|*  
*śiro grīvāyatāścaite bhūmipāla daśa smṛtāḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-12. “A cow with the following level parts of the body is said to be a fine one, viz. — ears, eyes, forehead, and the following eight parts should capacious viz., — tail, dewlap, udders, thighs; and extensive head and neck are also desirable.

## \|\| 207.13-15 \|\|

*tasyāḥ sutaṃ parīkṣeta vṛṣabhaṃ lakṣaṇānvitam \|*  
*unnataskandhakakudamṛjulāṅgūlakambalam \|\| 13 \|\|*

*mahākaṭitaṭaskandhaṃ vaidūryamaṇilocanam \|*  
*pravālagarbhaśṛṅgāgraṃ sudīrghapṛthuvāladhim \|\| 14 \|\|*

*navāṣṭādaśasaṃkhyairvā tīkṣṇāgrairdaśanaiḥ śubhaiḥ \|*  
*mallikākṣaśca moktavyo gṛhe'pi dhanadhānyadaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

13-15. The calf of such a cow should he also examined. It should have also auspicious signs. It should have elevated shoulders and hump, with a soft and straight tail, having tender cheeks, broad back, eyes shining like Vaiduryagem, sharp horns, and long and thick hairs on the tail having nine, nine, i e. eighteen nice teeth and eyes like Atallika flowers. If such a fine bull is set free, it increases the domestic pelf.

## \|\| 207.16-22 \|\|

*varṇatastāmrakapilo brāhmaṇasya praśasyate \|*  
*śveto raktaśca kṛṣṇaśca gauraḥ pāṭala eva ca \|\| 16 \|\|*

*madri ṇastāmrapṛṣṭhaśca śabalaḥ pañcavālakaiḥ \|*  
*pṛthukarṇo mahāskandhaḥ ślakṣṇaromā ca yo bhavet \|*  
*raktākṣaḥ kapilo yaśca raktaśṛṅgatalo bhavet \|\| 17 \|\|*

*śvetodaraḥ kṛṣṇapārśvo brāhmaṇasya tu śasyate \|*  
*snigdho raktena varṇena kṣatriyasya praśasyate \|\| 18 \|\|*

*kāñcanābhena vaiśyasya kṛṣṇenāpyantyajanmanaḥ \|*  
*yasya prāgāyate śṛṅge bhrūmukhābhimukhe sadā \|\| 19 \|\|*

*sarveṣāmeva varṇānāṃ sarvaḥ sarvārthasādhakaḥ \|*  
*mārjārapādaḥ kapilo dhanyaḥ kapilapiṅgalaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*śveto mārjārapādastu dhanyo maṇinibhekṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*karaṭaḥ piṅgalaścaiva śvetapādastathaiva ca \|\| 21 \|\|*

*sarvapādasito yaśca dvipādaśveta eva ca \|*  
*kapilañjalanibho dhanyastathā tittirisaṃnibhaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

16-22. The Brahmanas should set free the following class of bulls, viz. — red, tawny or reddish, white or black in colour, tawny reddish back, of variegated colours, with long ears and shoulders, with glossy hair, red eyes or having mi thrown colour near the horns, with white stomach, or black sides. The Kshatriyas should set free a bull of red and beautiful colour; the Vaishyas of golden colour and the Shudras of black colour. The bull with its horns pointing forward towards the eyebrows, ought to be set free by men of all classes. The bull having its feet like those of the whit© cat, with tawny or reddish in colour, with eyes shining like a jewel having white feet or with only two feet white, or of the colour of a pigeon or a partridge, is also said to be a good one. It is called Karat.

## \|\| 207.23 \|\|

*ākarṇamūlaṃ śvetaṃ tu mukhaṃ yasya prakāśate \|*  
*nandīmukhaḥ sa vijñeyo raktavarṇo viśeṣataḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. The bull whose face is white or reddish up to the ears and whose body is especially of red colour is called Nandimukha cow.

## \|\| 207.24-25 \|\|

*śvetaṃ tu jaṭharaṃ yasya bhavetpṛṣṭhaṃ ca gopateḥ \|*  
*vṛṣabhaḥ sa samudrā kṣaḥ satataṃ kulavardhanaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*mallikāpuṣpacitraśca dhanyo bhavati puṃgavaḥ \|*  
*kamalairmaṇḍalaiścāpi citro bhavati bhāgyadaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

24-25. The bull whose stomach and back are white is called Samudra and increases the progeny of the family. The bull of the colour of jasmin or having variegated circular spots is considered to increase the wealth of the donor.

## \|\| 207.28-29 \|\|

*dhvāṅkṣagṛdhrasavarṇāśca tathā mūṣakasaṃnibhāḥ \|*  
*kuṇṭhāḥ kāṇāstathā khañjāḥ kekarākṣāstathaiva ca \|\| 28 \|\|*

*viṣamaśvetapādāśca udbhrāntanayanāstathā \|*  
*naite vṛṣāḥ pramoktavyā na ca dhāryāstathā gṛhe \|\| 29 \|\|*

28-29. The bull having circles like lotus increase the fortune; the one of the colour of Atasi flower increases prosperity. All these, kinds of bulls are good. Now I shall tell you the kinds of bulls that are of bad signs and should neither be set at liberty nor kept in the house. Those are the bulls that have black palate, lips and mouth, and rugged horns and hoofs, indistinct colour, mouth resembling that of a wolf or a tiger, and colour like that of a crow, vulture, or a form like that of a rat, weak, having no teeth, squint-eyed, one-eyed, lame, with half of the white feet, and having restive eyes.

## \|\| 207.30-31 \|\|

*bhoktavyānāṃ ca dhāryāṇāṃ bhūyo vakṣyāmi lakṣaṇam \|*  
*svastikākāraśṛṅgāśca tathā meghaughanisvanāḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

*mahāpramāṇāśca tathā mattamātaṅgagāminaḥ \|*  
*mahoraskā mahocchrāyā mahābalaparākramāḥ \| śiraḥkarṇau lalāṭaṃ ca vāladhiścaraṇāstathā \|\| 31 \|\|*

30-31. I shall also tell you the kind of bulls that ought to be set at liberty or kept in the household. Those should be well-built, roaring like the thunder clouds, high in stature, walking like an infuriated elephant, with broad chest and very powerful.

## \|\| 207.32 \|\|

*netre pārśve ca kṛṣṇāni śasyante candra bhāsinām \|*  
*śvetānyetāni śasyante kṛṣṇasya tu viśeṣataḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. The white bull having its head, ears, forehead, tuft of hair at the tail-end, feet and eyes black, is described to be very excellent;

## \|\| 207.33-40 \|\|

*bhūmau karṣati lāṅgulaṃ pralambasthūlavāladhiḥ \|*  
*purastādudyato nīlo vṛṣabhaśca praśasyate \|\| 33 \|\|*

*śaktidhvajapatākāḍhyā yeṣāṃ rājī virājate \|*  
*anaḍvāhastu te dhanyāścitrasiddhijayāvahāḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

*pradakṣiṇaṃ nivartante svayaṃ ye vinivartitāḥ \|*  
*samunnataśirogrīvā dhanyāste yūthavardhanāḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

*raktaśṛṅgāgranayanaḥ śvetavarṇo bhavedyadi \|*  
*śaphaiḥ pravālasadṛśairnāsti dhanyatarastataḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

*ete dhāryāḥ prayatnena moktavyā yadi vā vṛṣāḥ \|*  
*dhāritāśca tathā muktā dhanadhānyapravardhanāḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

*caraṇāni mukhaṃ pucchaṃ yasya śvetāni gopateḥ \|*  
*lākṣārasasavarṇaśca taṃ nīlamiti nirdiśet \|\| 38 \|\|*

*vṛṣa eva sa moktavyo na saṃdhāryo gṛhe bhavet \|*  
*tadarthameṣā carati loke gāthā purātanī \|\| 39 \|\|*

*eṣṭavyā bahavaḥ putrā yadyeko'pi gayāṃ vrajet \|*  
*gaurīṃ cāpyudvahetkanyāṃ nīlaṃ vā vṛṣamutsṛjet \|\| 40 \|\|*

33-40. Similarly a black bull having all those things white is said to be the same. The bull whose tuft of hair at the tail-end may be long enough touching the ground, and the hairs of the tail long and thick, such a Nila bull is said to be specially good. The bulls having the signs of a pearl, a banner, etc., are exceptionally good. They are the givers of wonderful Siddhis and victory. The bulls when obstructed in their motion stop, and whose head and neck are elevated, are excellent. Those that have their forepart of the horns and the eyes red, body white, hoofs resplendent like coral, are said to be the best of all. These are to be kept in the house or set at liberty. These increase grains and wealth.

The balls should always be examined before being set at liberty or kept in the household. The bull whose four feet, face and tail are white, and whose colour is red like the juice of lac or red dye is known as Nila-vrishabha. It should be set free; it should never be kept in the household. It is a saying amongst the household that one should desire many sons for even if one son out of a many goes to Gaya or offers a Gauri (virgin) or sets a Nila-Vrishabha at liberty his family is blessed.

## \|\| 207.41 \|\|

*evaṃ vṛṣaṃ lakṣaṇasaṃprayuktaṃ gṛhodbhavaṃ krītamathāpi rājan \|*  
*muktvā na śocenmaraṇaṃ mahātmā mokṣaṃ gataścāhamato'bhidhāsye \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. King! the qualities of the bulls have thus been described. One who sets at liberty such a bull as described heretofore, should not worry himself about sorrow or death. He is bound to attain emancipation.”

## Chapter 208

## \|\| 208.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*tataḥ sa rājā deveśaṃ papracchābhitavikramaḥ \|*  
*pativratānāṃ māhātmyaṃ tatsaṃbaddhāṃ kathāmapi \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Suta said: — “King Vaivasvata Manu requested the Lord to explain to him the glory of the Pativrata ladies (chaste and virtuous ladies) and on other subjects.”

## \|\| 208.2 \|\|

*manuruvāca*  
*pativratānāṃ kā śreṣṭhā kayā mṛtyuḥ parājitaḥ \|*  
*nāmasaṃkīrtanaṃ kasyāḥ kīrtanīyaṃ sadā naraiḥ \|*  
*sarvapāpakṣayakaramidānīṃ kathayasva me \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Manu said: — “Among the chaste ladies who is the best? Who has subdued death? Whose name should the people recite every day? Pray tell me all this, their glory is the dispeller of all sins.”

## \|\| 208.3 \|\|

*matsya uvāca*  
*vailomyaṃ dharmarājo'pi nā’caratyatha yoṣitām \|*  
*pativratānāṃ dharmajña pūjyāstasyāpi tāḥ sadā \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Matsya said: — “Even the Dharmaraja does not dare to do anything against the wishes of the virtuous and chaste ladies who are worthy of being venerated by Him.”

## \|\| 208.4 \|\|

*atra te varṇayiṣyāmi kathāṃ pāpapraṇāśinīm \|*  
*yathā vimokṣito bhartā mṛtyupāśagataḥ striyā \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. “I shall now relate to you on this point a story which drives away all sin as a virtuous lady saved her lord from the meshes of death Hear.”

## \|\| 208.5-11 \|\|

*madre ṣu śākalo rājā babhūvāśvapatiḥ purā \|*  
*aputrastapyamāno'sau putrārthī sarvakāmadām \|\| 5 \|\|*

*ārādhayati sāvitrīṃ lakṣito'sau dvijottamaiḥ \|*  
*siddhārthakairhūyamānāṃ sāvitrīṃ pratyahaṃ dvijaiḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*śatasaṃkhyaiścaturthyāṃ tu māsāddaśadine gate \|*  
*kāle tu darśayāmāsa svāṃ tanuṃ manujeśvaram \|\| 7 \|\|*

*sāvitr! yuvāca*  
*rājanbhakto'si me nityaṃ dāsyāmi tvāṃ sutāṃ sadā \|*  
*tāṃ dattāṃ matprasādena putrīṃ prāpsyasi śobhanām \|\| 8 \|\|*

*etāvaduktvā sā rājñaḥ praṇatasyaiva pārthiva \|*  
*jagāmādarśanaṃ devī khe tathā nṛpa cañcalā \|\| 9 \|\|*

*mālatī nāma tasyā’sīdrā jñaḥ patnī pativratā \|*  
*suṣuve tanayāṃ kāle sāvitrīmiva rūpataḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*sāvitr! yā hutayā dattā tadrū pasadṛśī tathā \|*  
*sāvitrī ca bhavatveṣā jagāda nṛpatirdvijān \|\| 11 \|\|*

5-11. “In the country of Madra there was in ancient times a king named Sakala Ashvapati. With the object of begetting progeny be began to adore Savitri. The Brahmanas began to pour offerings of white sesamums into the fire daily, when ten months passed and Savitri Devi became pleased and appeared before the king; and said: ‘King! you are my constant devotee. I shall give you a progeny. A beautiful daughter will be born to yon by My favour.’ Saying so She vanished, and afterwards Malati, the virtuous queen of that king, gave birth to a daughter handsome like Savitri. The king then said to the Brahmanas: This daughter has been born by the favour of Savitri and she should therefore be named Savitri.”

## \|\| 208.12-16 \|\|

*nāmākurvandvijaśreṣṭhāḥ sāvitrīti nṛpottama \|*  
*kālena yauvanaṃ prāptā dadau satyavate pitā \|*  
*nāradastu tataḥ prāha rājānaṃ dīptatejasam \|\| 12 \|\|*

*saṃvatsareṇa kṣīṇāyurbhaviṣyati nṛpātmajaḥ \|*

*tathā'pi pradadau kanyāṃ dyumatsenātmaje śubhe \|*

12-16. “Afterwards the girl grew young and she was promised to Satyavana. At the same time Narada came and told the king: ‘ King! Satyavana with whom you think of marrying your daughter will die within a year.’ The king then said to himself: ‘I have already resolved to give my daughter to one particular person and under the circumstances I shall not change my determination.’ With that mind he gave her away to Satyavana, the son of Dyumati Sen. Savitri on becoming his wife became anxious on the recollection of the verdict of Narada and began to devoutfully serve her lord and her father-in-law and mother-in-law. Her blind father-in-law was deprived of his kingdom and resided with his son and his son’s wife in the forest. Savitri served them with great care and they were greatly satisfied.

## \|\| 208.17-21 \|\|

*caturthe'hani martavyaṃ tathā satyavatā dvijāḥ \|*  
*śvaśureṇābhyanujñātā tadā rājasutā'pi sā \|\| 17 \|\|*

*cakre trirātraṃ dharmajñā prāpte tasmiṃstadā dine \|*  
*dārupuṣpaphalāhārī satyavāṃstu yayau vanam \|\| 18 \|\|*

*śvaśureṇābhyanujñātā yācanābhaṅgabhīruṇā \|*  
*sāvitr! yapi jagāmā’rtā saha bhartrā mahadvanam \|\| 19 \|\|*

*cetasā dūyamānena gūhamānā mahadbhayam \|*  
*vane papraccha bhartāraṃ drumāṃścāsadṛśāṃstathā \|\| 20 \|\|*

*jāśvāsayāmāsa sa rājaputrīṃ klāntāṃ vane padmaviśālanetrām \|*  
*saṃdarśanenātha drumadvijānāṃ tathā mṛgāṇāṃ vipine nṛvīraḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

17-21. In the meantime only four days remained for Satyavana to die when Savitri with the permission of her father-in-law kept up a fast for three nights. On the fourth day Satyayana went to fetch flowers and fruits from the forest with his father’s permission, when Savitri also with her father-in-law’s permission followed him there. In the forest oppressed with the overwhelming grief of her lord’s approaching death, she in order not to disclose her mind, began to ask her lord the names of the various trees and flowers. Satyavana began to point out to his distressed consort the principal forest trees, birds and animals.”

The Kinshuka flowers look like a blaze of fire and are fragrant. Dear! in this forest flows the wind laden with the sweet aroma of flowers which is so soothing to me. To the west are visible the Karnikara flowers of the golden hue. Most of the thoroughfares of this forest are choked with luxuriant blossoms. Indeed the whole place abounds with flowers and looks charming.

*viṣāgnisarpaśastrebhyo na tathā jāyate bhayam \|*  
*akāraṇajagadvairikhalebhyo jāyate yathā \|\| 3 \|\|*

*santaḥ prāṇānapi tyaktvā parārthaṃ kurvate yathā \|*  
*tathā'santo'pi saṃtyajya parapīḍāsu tatparāḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*tyajatyasūnayaṃ lokastṛṇavadyasya kāraṇāt \|*  
*paropaghātaśaktāstaṃ paralokaṃ tathā'sataḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*nikāyeṣu nikāyeṣu tathā brahmā jagadguruḥ \|*  
*asatāmupaghātāya rājānaṃ jñātavānsvayam \|\| 6 \|\|*

1-6. Savitri said: — When a saint comes to a saint, who then of these feels pain and trouble? O best of the Devas! I do not feel any worry in remaining in your company. The saints are the refuge of all, whether they be saints or sinners. And the wicked are not of any good to the wicked or good, to anybody. There is no such fear from poison, fire, snake, weapons as it is from the man who is inimically disposed towards the rest of the world without any cause. The good give up their lives for the sake of others and the wicked are ever ready to cause pain to others even at the sacrifice of their lives. The wicked and mischief making people go against the next world and those who hold the view of the after-life give up their lives like straws. Brahma the Lord of the Universe has created therefore kings all over the world for the destruction of the wicked.

## \|\| 211.7-11 \|\|

*narānparīkṣayedrā jā sādhūnsaṃmānayetsadā \|*  
*nigrahaṃ cāsatāṃ kuryātsa loke lokajittamaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*nigraheṇāsatāṃ rājā satāṃ ca paripālanāt \|*  
*etāvadeva kartavyaṃ rājñā svargamabhīpsunā \|\| 8 \|\|*

*rājakṛtyaṃ hi lokeṣu nāstyanyajжagatīpate \|*  
*asatāṃ nigrahādeva satāṃ ca paripālanāt \|\| 9 \|\|*

*rajabhiścāpyaśāstānāmasatāṃ śāsitā bhavān \|*  
*tena tvamadhiko devo devebhyaḥ pratibhāsi me \|\| 10 \|\|*

*jagattu dhāryate sadbhiḥ satāmagryastathā bhavān \|*  
*tena tvāmanuyāntyā me klamo deva na vidyate \|\| 11 \|\|*

7-11. For the same reasons king should always examine his city and his people and respect the good. The king who chastises the wicked is the conqueror of the world. He should always control the wicked and support the good. This is the duty of a king who is eager for a place in Heaven. Besides this, there is no other pax-amount duty for the king. Whom the kings cannot control, you control them also. You are the chastiser e. wicked, therefore you seem to me superior even to the Devas. The whole Universe is supported by the good. You are the crown of the good. I therefore follow you without feeling any pain.

## \|\| 211.12 \|\|

*yama uvāca*  
*tuṣṭo'smi te viśālākṣi vacanairdharmasaṃgataiḥ \|*  
*vinā satyavataḥ prāṇādvaraṃ varaya mā ciram \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Dharmaraja said: — O, one with beautiful eyes! I have become pleased with thy words of righteousness. Ask for anything excepting Satyavan’s life, do not delay,

## \|\| 211.13 \|\|

*sāvitr! yuvāca*  
*sahodarāṇāṃ bhrātriṇāṃ kāmayāmi śataṃ vibho \|*  
*janapatyaḥ pitā prītiṃ putralābhātprayātu me \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Savitri said: — I wish to have a hundred brothers; let my father who is without any son be blessed with a son.

## \|\| 211.14-17 \|\|

*tāmuvāca yamo gaccha yathāgatamanindite \|*  
*aurdhvadehikakāryeṣu yatnaṃ bhartuḥ samācara \|\| 14 \|\|*

*nānugantumayaṃ śaktyastvayā lokāntaraṃ gataḥ \|*  
*pativratā'si tena tvaṃ muhūrtaṃ mama yāsyasi \|\| 15 \|\|*

*guruśuśrūṣaṇādbhadre tathā satyavatā mahat \|*  
*puṇyaṃ samarjitaṃ yena nayāmyenamahaṃ svayam \|\| 16 \|\|*

*etāvadeva kartavyaṃ puruṣeṇa vijānatā \|*  
*mātuḥ pituśca śuśrūṣā gurośca varavarṇini \|\| 17 \|\|*

14-17. Dharmaraja said: — “It will be so. Now you should return and perform the funeral rites of your husband. He has gone to the other realm, you cannot follow him there. You are chaste, therefore you can follow to a little distance. The great virtues collected by Satyavana by his devotion to his Guru have produced this result that 1 myself am taking him away. Indeed a wise man should always devote himself to his parents and preceptor.

## \|\| 211.18 \|\|

*toṣitaṃ trayametacca sadā satyavatā vane \|*  
*pūjitaṃ vijitaḥ svargastvayā'nena ciraṃ śubhe \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Satyavana has pleased them all by his devotion and consequently you also along with him have conquered Heaven.

## \|\| 211.19-28 \|\|

*tapasā brahmacaryeṇa agniśuśrūṣayā śubhe \|*  
*puruṣāḥ svargamāyānti guruśuśrūṣayā tathā \|\| 19 \|\|*

*ācāryaśca pitā caiva mātā bhrātā ca pūrvajaḥ \|*  
*na cai'tepyavamantavyā brāhmaṇena viśeṣataḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*ācāryo brahmaṇo mūrtiḥ pitā mūrtiḥ prajāpateḥ \|*  
*mātā pṛthivyā mūrtistu bhrātā vai mūrtirātmanaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*janmanā pitarau kleśaṃ sahete saṃbhave nṛṇām \|*  
*na tasya niṣkṛtiḥ śakyā kartuṃ varṣaśatairapi \|\| 22 \|\|*

*tayornityaṃ priyaṃ kuryādācāryasya tu sarvadā \|*  
*teṣveva triṣu tuṣṭeṣu tapaḥ sarvaṃ samāpyate \|\| 23 \|\|*

*teṣāṃ trayāṇāṃ śuśrūṣā paramaṃ tapa ucyate \|*  
*na ca tairananujñāto dharmamanyaṃ samācaret \|\| 24 \|\|*

*ta eva hi trayo lokāsta eva traya āśramāḥ \|*  
*ta eva ca trayo vedāstathaivoktāstrayo'gnayaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*pitā vai gārhapatyo'gnirmātā dakṣiṇataḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*gururāhavanīyaśca sā'gnitretā garīyasī \|\| 26 \|\|*

*triṣu pramādyate naiṣu trīṃllokāñjayate gṛhī \|*  
*dīpyamānaḥ svavapuṣā devavaddivi modate \|\| 27 \|\|*

*kṛtena kāmena nivarta bhadre bhaviṣyatīdaṃ sakalaṃ tvayoktam \|*  
*mamoparodhastava ca klamaḥ syāttathā'dhunā tena tava bravīmi \|\| 28 \|\|*

19-28. A man goes to Heaven by means of asceticism, self-restraint and Brahmacharya, preserving the fires, and devotion to Guru. Preceptor, father, mother, elder brother and specially a Brahmana should also be revered. They should not be hurt even when one is afflicted. Preceptor is like Brahma, father is like Prajapati, mother is like the earth, brother is another form of one’s own soul The sufferings undergone by the parents in begetting progeny cannot be repaid even in thousands of years, therefore the parents and preceptor should always be respected. The serving of these three is the highest asceticism. Asceticism is fully accomplished when these three are pleased. To serve them is the highest form of asceticism. Nothing should be done without their permission. They are in fact the three realms, the three orders, the three Vedas, and the three fires. Father is the Garhapatya Agni, mother is the Dakshinagni and the preceptor is the Ahvaniya Agni. One who devotes himself well to them, conquers the three realms and enjoys in Heaven all the pleasures, having a bright body. Now abandon your desire. You have fulfilled your mission and all that you asked you will get. Now you should return home. You are feeling tired. So I ask you had better go home.

## Chapter 212

## \|\| 212.1 \|\|

*sāvitr! yuvāca*  
*dharmārjane suraśreṣṭha kuto glāniḥ klamastathā \|*  
*tvatpādamūlasevā ca paramaṃ dharmakāraṇam \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Savitri said: — There is no suffering in the pursuit of Dharma, especially to adore your feet is the highest virtue.

## \|\| 212.2 \|\|

*dharmārjanaṃ tathā kāryaṃ puruṣeṇa vijānatā \|*  
*tallābhaḥ sarvalābhebhyo yadā deva viśiṣyate \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. A wise man should acquire Dharma by all means, for its attainment is superior to all achievements.

## \|\| 212.3 \|\|

*dharmaścārthaśca kāmaśca trivargo janmanaḥ phalam \|*  
*dharmahīnasya kāmārthau vandhyāsutasamau prabho \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Dharma, Artha and Kama are to be acquired by taking a human birth; to one who is bereft of Dharma, Kama and Artha are like progeny to a barren woman.

## \|\| 212.4 \|\|

*dharmādarthastathā kāmo dharmāllokadvayaṃ tathā \|*  
*dharma eko'nuyātyenaṃ yatrakvacanagāminam \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. From Dharma is obtained wealth and from Dharma again is obtained Kama, the fulfilment of desires; it is through Dharma that this world and the next are enjoyed.

## \|\| 212.5-6 \|\|

*śarīreṇa samaṃ nāśaṃ sarvamanyaddhi gacchati \|*  
*eko hi jāyate jantureka eva vipadyate \|\| 5 \|\|*

*dharmastamanu yātyeko na suhṛnna ca bāndhavāḥ \|*
