*kriyā saubhāgyalāvaṇyaṃ sarvaṃ dharmeṇa labhyate \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. It is Dharma only that accompanies the embodied soul wherever it goes, friends and relatives do not follow. All other things excepting Dharma perish with the body. The soul comes into existence by itself and leaves the body similarly. It is only followed by Dharma. It is not followed by any brother, friend, wife, son &c. Fortune &c. are begotten by Dharma.

## \|\| 212.7-8 \|\|

*brahmendro pendra śarvenduyamārkāgnyanilāmbhasām \|*  
*vasvaśvidhanadādyānāṃ ye lokāḥ sarvakāmadāḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*dharmeṇa tānavāpnoti puruṣaḥ puruṣāntaka \|*  
*manoharāṇi dvīpāni varṣāṇi susukhāni ca \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8. Cleverness in works, fortune, beauty, all spring from Dharma. The prosperous realms of Brahma, Indra, Upendra, Shiva, Chandrama, Yama, Sun, Agni, Vayu, Water, Vasa, Ashvanikumara, and Kuvera &c. are all attained by means of Dharma, and by virtue of it men are born amidst comfortable surroundings.

## \|\| 212.9-11 \|\|

*prayānti dharmeṇa narāstathaiva naragaṇḍikāḥ \|*  
*nandanādīni mukhyāni devodyānāni yāni ca \|\| 9 \|\|*

*tāni puṇyena labhyante nākapṛṣṭhaṃ tathā naraiḥ \|*  
*vimānāni vicitrāṇi tathaivāpsarasaḥ śubhāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*taijasāni śarīrāṇi sadā puṇyavatāṃ phalam \|*  
*rājyaṃ nṛpatipūjā ca kāmasiddhistathepsitā \|\| 11 \|\|*

9-11. Men attain Swarga, beautiful islands, pleasant Varsas, heavenly Nandan etc., by means of Dharma. Handsome Vimanas and nymphs are also attained through Dharma. The virtuous always get resplendent. They attain kingdoms and accomplish their desires complexion like gold, by means of Dharma.

## \|\| 212.12-13 \|\|

*saṃskārāṇi ca mukhyāni phalaṃ puṇyasya dṛśyate \|*  
*rukmavaidūryadaṇḍāni caṇḍāṃśusadṛśāni ca \|\| 12 \|\|*

*cāmarāṇi surādhyakṣa bhavanti śubhakarmaṇām \|*  
*pūrṇendumaṇḍalābhena ratnāṃśukavikāśinā \|\| 13 \|\|*

12-13. High attributes are the fruits of Dharma, kingdom, kingly worship, success of one’s will, and especial rise are seen in the virtuous. The regal sceptre of gold and silver studded with vaidurya gem is in the hands of the righteous and their faces always shine like the moon.

## \|\| 212.14 \|\|

*dhāryatāṃ yāti cchatreṇa naraḥ puṇyena karmaṇā \|*  
*jayaśaṅkhasvaraugheṇa sūtamāgadhaniḥsvanaiḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Only the righteous become kings and are entitled to sit- on the throne under a canopy, looking like a full moon, have garments studded with jewels and fanned by cowries bright as the sun. It is they who are aroused from their slumber by the chorus of ‘victory’, the blowing of the conches and by the praises sung by the bards.

## \|\| 212.15 \|\|

*varāsanaṃ sabhṛṅgāraṃ phalaṃ puṇyasya karmaṇaḥ \|*  
*varānnapānaṃ gītaṃ ca bhṛtyamālyānulepanam \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. High class seats, golden vases, good food and drink, music, servants, smell, grain &c. seek the virtuous persons only.

## \|\| 212.16-21 \|\|

*ratnavastrāṇi mukhyāni phalaṃ puṇyasya karmaṇaḥ \|*  
*rūpaudāryaguṇopetāḥ striyaścātimanoharāḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*vāsāḥ prāsādapṛṣṭheṣu bhavanti śubhakarmiṇām \|*  
*suvarṇakiṅkiṇīmiśracāmarāpīḍadhāriṇaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*vahanti turagā deva naraṃ puṇyena karmaṇā \|*  
*haimakakṣaiśca mātaṅgaiścalatparvatasaṃnibhaiḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*kheladbhiḥ pādavinyāsairyānti puṇyena karmaṇā \|*  
*sarvakāmaprade devasarvāghaduritāpahe \|\| 19 \|\|*

*vahanti bhaktiṃ puruṣāḥ sadā puṇyena karmaṇā \|*  
*tasya dvārāṇi yajanaṃ tapo dānaṃ damaḥ kṣamā \|\| 20 \|\|*

*brahmacaryaṃ tathā satyaṃ tīrthānusaraṇaṃ śubham \|*  
*svādhyāyasevā sādhūnāṃ sahavāsaḥ surārcanam \|\| 21 \|\|*

16-21. Jewels, fine garments, handsome form, generosity, high attributes, beautiful wife, these are all attained by virtuous persons. The virtuous are blessed with palatial mansions that are decorated with the perforated work in gold. They also get beautiful steeds to ride upon. Asceticism, sacrifices, charities, control of passions, forgiveness, celibacy, travelling in sacred places, the reading of the Vedas, the service of the good, worship of God, devotion and service of the Guru, veneration of the Brahmanas, humility, these are all the signs of virtue. The learned should always follow them. For Death never waits whether one has done such things or not.

## \|\| 212.22 \|\|

*gurūṇāṃ caiva śuśrūṣā brāhmaṇānāṃ ca pūjanam \|*  
*indri yāṇāṃ jayaścaiva brahmacaryamamatsaram \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. This body and life are quite uncertain, therefore one should begin to accomplish, virtue from childhood. Who knows when he is going to die?

## \|\| 212.23 \|\|

*tasmāddharmaḥ sadā kāryo nityameva vijānatā \|*  
*na hi pratīkṣate mṛtyuḥ kṛtamasya na vā kṛtam \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Death comes to all, defying everybody. Is it not so very strange that man although he foresees death, leads a life as if he was immortal?

## \|\| 212.24 \|\|

*bāla eva careddharmamanityaṃ deva jīvitam \|*  
*ko hi jānāti kasyādya mṛtyurevā’patiṣyati \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Children see young persons and young person’s see aged ones and may consider death far distant; but old ones do not see anybody before them.

## \|\| 212.25 \|\|

*paśyato'pyasya lokasya maraṇaṃ purataḥ sthitam \|*  
*amarasyeva caritamatyāścaryaṃ surottama \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. All are afraid of Death; nowhere there is fearlessness. But the virtuous saints never fear death and the state after death.

## \|\| 212.26 \|\|

*yuvatvāpekṣayā bālo vṛddhatvāpekṣayā yuvā \|*  
*mṛtyorutsaṅgamārūḍhaḥ sthaviraḥ kimapekṣate \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Dharmaraja said: — I am very much pleased with you. Ask for arty other boon excepting Satyavan’s life.” Do not make any delay.

## \|\| 212.27 \|\|

*tatrāpi vindatastrāṇaṃ mṛtyunā tasya kā gatiḥ \|*  
*na bhayaṃ maraṇādeva prāṇināmabhayaṃ kvacit \|*  
*tatrāpi nirbhayāḥ santaḥ sadā sukṛtakāriṇaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Savitri said: — Deva! I wish to beget a hundred sons through Satyavan by your favour as there is no relief in the next world without sons.

## \|\| 212.28 \|\|

*yama uvāca*  
*tuṣṭo'smi te viśālākṣi vacanairdharmasaṃgataiḥ \|*  
*vinā satyavataḥ prāṇānvaraṃ varaya mā ciram \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Dharmaraja said: — You will have your desires fulfilled, but do not follow Satyavana. You are feeling worry and fatigue. Therefore I am saying so. Go back.

## Chapter 213

## \|\| 213.1-2 \|\|

*sāvitr! yuvāca*  
*dharmādharmavidhānajña sarvadharmapravartaka \|*  
*tvameva jagato nāthaḥ prajāsaṃyamano yamaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*karmaṇāmanurūpeṇa yasmādyamayase prajāḥ \|*  
*tasmādvai procyase deva yama ityeva nāmataḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

1-2. Savitri said: — You are the knower of Dharma and Adharma, you are the propagator of all the virtues. You control all the people of the Universe. You# are Yama, the great Ruler of the people according to their Karmas.

## \|\| 213.3 \|\|

*dharmeṇemāḥ prajāḥ sarvā yasmādra ñjayase prabho \|*  
*tasmātte dharmarājeti nāma sadbhirnigadyate \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. You give pleasure to everyone by Dharma, consequently you are called Dharmaraja.

## \|\| 213.4 \|\|

*sukṛtaṃ duṣkṛtaṃ cobhe purodhāya yadā janāḥ \|*  
*tvatsakāśaṃ mṛtā yānti tasmāttvaṃ mṛtyurucyase \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. All the people doing either good or bad deeds go unto you after death and place them at your disposal, therefore you are known as ‘Death.’

## \|\| 213.5 \|\|

*kālaṃ kalārdhaṃ kalayansarveṣāṃ tvaṃ hi tiṣṭhasi \|*  
*tasmātkāleti te nāma procyate tattvadarśibhiḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5 You count and remember the time of every one’s existence, consequently thinkers call you Kala.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — … = L it. Time.

## \|\| 213.6 \|\|

*sarveṣāmeva bhūtānāṃ yasmādantakaro mahān \|*  
*tasmāttvamantakaḥ proktaḥ sarvadevairmahādyute \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. You are the annihilator of all beings, therefore the Devas call yon Antaka.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — … = Lit. That which brings end.

## \|\| 213.7 \|\|

*vivasvatastvaṃ tanayaḥ prathamaḥ parikīrtitaḥ \|*  
*tasmādvaivasvato nāmnā sarvalokeṣu kathyase \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. You were the first son of Vivasvana, therefore you are renowned as Vaivasvata in all the realms.

## \|\| 213.8-9 \|\|

*āyuṣye karmaṇi kṣīṇe gṛhṇāsi prasamaṃ janam \|*  
*tadā tvaṃ kathyase loke sarvaprāṇahareti vai \|\| 8 \|\|*

*tava prasādāddeveśa trayīdharmo na naśyati \|*  
*tava prasādāddeveśa dharme tiṣṭhanti jantavaḥ \|*  
*tava prasādāddeveśa saṃkaro na prajāyate \|\| 9 \|\|*

8-9. When the numbered days and their Karmas are over you drive away the subtle bodies of all the beings, therefore you are known as Sarva Pranahara, Lord. The Vedic Dharma does not become extinct through your favour! therefore the people remain in the path of Dharma and yon are the Emancipation of the Virtuous.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — T hat which takes away every one's life.

## \|\| 213.10 \|\|

*satāṃ sadā gatirdeva tvameva parikīrtitaḥ \|*  
*jagato'sya jagannātha maryādāparipālakaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Through your grace no intermixture of blood occurs. O, Lord of the Universe! you are the protector of the pride of the Universe, therefore protect me who has come to your mercy and refuge and my husband and his parents are helpless; so save us.

## \|\| 213.11 \|\|

*pāhi māṃ tridaśaśreṣṭha duḥkhitāṃ śaraṇāgatām \|*  
*pitarau ca tathaivāsya rājaputrasya duḥkhitau \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Dharmaraja said: — O, Virtuous one f I have become quite pleased with your prayer and, hereby liberate your lord. Now your wishes are ail fulfilled and you better return home quickly,

## \|\| 213.12-13 \|\|

*yama uvāca*  
*stavena bhaktyā gharmajñe mayā tuṣṭena satyavān \|*  
*tava bhartā vimukto'yaṃ labdhakāmā vrajābale \|\| 12 \|\|*

*rājyaṃ kṛtvā tvayā sārdhaṃ vatsarāśītipañcakam \|*  
*nākapṛṣṭhamathā’ruhya tridaśaiḥ saha raṃsyate \|\| 13 \|\|*

12-13. This husband of yours will reign with you for 500 years, and will enjoy your company. He will attain Heaven along with you where he will enjoy the company of the Gods. The hundred sons born to you of Satyavan, will also reign and will be illustrious like the Devas.

## \|\| 213.14-15 \|\|

*tvayi putraśataṃ cāpi satyavāñjanayiṣyati \|*  
*te cāpi sarve rājānaḥ kṣattriyāstridaśopamāḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*mukhyāstvannāma putrāste bhaviṣyanti hi śāśvatāḥ \|*  
*pituśca te putraśataṃ bhavitā tava mātari \|\| 15 \|\|*

14-15. All your sons will be renowned as true sons of yours and the hundred sons born of your father will be renowned after their mother. Your mother Malavi will beget children who will be known as Malavas. All your brothers will be Kings, illustrious like the Daivas.

## \|\| 213.16 \|\|

*mālavyāṃ mālavā nāma śāśvatāḥ putrapautriṇaḥ \|*  
*bhrātaraste bhaviṣyanti kṣattriyāstridaśopamāḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Righteous one! one who reads this prayer in the morning will be blessed with long life.

## \|\| 213.17 \|\|

*stotreṇānena dharmajñe kalyamutthāya yastu mām \|*  
*kīrtayiṣyati tasyāpi dīrghamāyurbhaviṣyati \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Matsya said: — Saying so Dharmaraja disappeared from there leaving Satyavan on the spot.

## Chapter 214

## \|\| 214.1-6 \|\|

*matsya uvāca*  
*sāvitrī tu tataḥ sādhvī jagāma varavarṇinī \|*  
*pathā yathāgatenaiva yatrā’sītsatyavānmṛtaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*sā samāsādya bhartāraṃ tasyotsaṅgagataṃ śiraḥ \|*  
*kṛtvā viveśa tanvaṅgī lambamāne divākare \|\| 2 \|\|*

*satyavānapi nirmukto dharmarājācchanaiḥ śanaiḥ \|*  
*unmīlayata netrābhyāṃ prāsphuracca narādhipa \|\| 3 \|\|*

*tataḥ pratyāgataprāṇaḥ priyāṃ vacanamabravīt \|*  
*kvāsau prayātaḥ puruṣo yo māmapyapakarṣati \|\| 4 \|\|*

*na jānāmi varārohe kaścāsau puruṣaḥ śubhe \|*  
*vane'smiṃścārusarvāṅgi suptasya ca dinaṃ gatam \|\| 5 \|\|*

*upavāsapariśrāntā duḥkhitā bhavatī mayā \|*  
*admaddurhṛdayenādya pitarau duḥkhitau tathā \|*  
*dra ṣṭumicchāmyahaṃ subhru gamane tvaritā bhava \|\| 6 \|\|*

1-6. Matsya said: — Afterwards the chaste Savitri returned to the spot where was lying the body of Satyavan a, and sat down placing her lord’s head on her lap as before. In the meantime the sun was going below the horizon. Shortly after the soul of Satyavana liberated by Dharmaraja entered into his body when the prince began to move slowly and opened his eyes and said to his wife: “Dear! who was dragging me away? Where has he gone? I cannot make out anything clearly. The day has been past here in this wood in my sleep. You were engaged in the pursuit of your fasts for me and to-day you had to put up with hardships on my account. My mother and father must be feeling pain at our separation, for so long a time, I therefore want to go and meet them without delay. So get up and be quick.”

## \|\| 214.7-17 \|\|

*sāvitr! yuvāca*  
*āditye'stamanuprāpte yadi te rucitaṃ prabho \|*  
*āśramaṃ tu prayāsyāvaḥ śvaśurau hīnacakṣuṣau \|\| 7 \|\|*

*yathāvṛttaṃ ca tatraiva tava vakṣyāmyathā’śrame \|*  
*etāvaduktvā bhartāraṃ saha bhartrā tadā yayau \|\| 8 \|\|*

*āsasādā’śramaṃ caiva saha bhartrā nṛpātmajā \|*  
*etasminneva kāle tu labdhacakṣurmahīpatiḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*dyumatsenaḥ sabhāryastu paryatapyata bhārgava \|*  
*priyaputramapaśyanvai snuṣāṃ caivātha karśitām \|\| 10 \|\|*

*āśvāsvamānastu tathā sa tu rājā tapodhanaiḥ \|*  
*dadarśa putramāyāntaṃ snuṣayā saha kānanāt \|\| 11 \|\|*

*sāvitrī tu varārohā saha satyavatā tadā \|*  
*vavande tatra rājānaṃ sabhāryaṃ kṣattrapuṃgavam \|\| 12 \|\|*

*pariṣvaktastadā pitrā satyavānrājanandanaḥ \|*  
*abhivādya tataḥ sarvānvane tasmiṃstapodhanān \|\| 13 \|\|*

*uvāsa tatra tāṃ rātrimṛṣibhiḥ sarvadharmavit \|*  
*sābitr! yapi jagādātha yathāvṛttamaninditā \|\| 14 \|\|*

*vrataṃ samāpayāmāsa tasyāmeva tadā niśi \|*  
*tatastūryaistriyāmānte sasainyastasya bhūpateḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*ājagāma janaḥ sarvo rājyārthāya nimantraṇe \|*  
*vijñāpayāmāsa tadā tatra prakṛtiśāsanam \|\| 16 \|\|*

*vicakṣuṣaste nṛpate yena rājyaṃ purā hṛtam \|*  
*amātyaiḥ sa hato rājā bhavāṃstasminpure nṛpaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

7-17. Savitri said: — “Lord! The sun has gone down. If you like we might go to the hermitage where are my blind father-in-law and mother-in-law. There I shall relate to you my history in detail.” With these words she accompanied her lord. When they reached the hermitage they found the blind King Dynmatsain who was restored to his sight getting very anxious along with the queen about his son and daughter-in-law. He was overjoyed to see them return at the same hour. The sages were consoling him at the time. Then Savitri along with her lord paid her respects to her father-in-law. Prince Satyavana also paid his reverence to the sages after meeting his father. That night they all spent with the Rishis and Savitri narrated everything before those present there; and she also broke her fast that very night. Afterwards, when the night came to a close, all the citizens and the army of King Dynmatsain gathered there and said to the King: — “The King who usurped your throne when. you became blind has been slain by your ministers. Pray come and occupy your throne.”

## \|\| 214.18-22 \|\|

*etacchrutvā yayau rājā balena caturaṅgiṇā \|*  
*lebhe ca sakalaṃ rājyaṃ dharmarājānmahātmanaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*bhrātriṇāṃ tu śataṃ lebhe sāvitr! yapi varāṅganā \|*  
*evaṃ pativratā sādhvī pitṛpakṣaṃ nṛpātmajā \|\| 19 \|\|*

*ujжahāra varārohā bhartṛpakṣaṃ tathaiva ca \|*  
*mocayāmāsa bhartāraṃ mṛtyupāśavaśaṃ gatam \|\| 20 \|\|*

*tasmātsādhvyaḥ striyaḥ pūjyāḥ satataṃ devavannaraiḥ \|*  
*tāsāṃ rājanprasādena dhāryate vai jagattrayam \|\| 21 \|\|*

*tāsāṃ tu vākyaṃ bhavatīha mithyā na jātu lokeṣu carācareṣu \|*  
*tasmātsadā tāḥ paripūjanīyāḥ kāmānsamagrānabhikāmayānaiḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

18-22. Hearing that the King followed by his 'four-fold army entered his Capital and occupied his throne. Similarly in due time Savitri was blessed with, hundred sons. In that way that chaste lady also fulfilled all the Ambitions of her father. So the chaste lady delivered both the families of her husband and father and saved the life of her husband from the hands of Death. People should therefore revere and worship chaste ladies. The whole Universe is held up and by the virtue of the righteous ladies. The words of the chaste ladies never go false; therefore, the people who are expecting their desires to be fulfilled should always revere such ladies.

## Chapter 215

## \|\| 215.1 \|\|

*manuruvāca*  
*rājño'bhiṣiktamātrasya kiṃ nu kṛtyatamaṃ bhavet \|*  
*etanme sarvamācakṣva samyagvetti yato bhavān \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. King Vaivasvata Manu said Lord! You are the knower of all I, therefore, beg you to please tell me what a king should do on ascending his throne.

## \|\| 215.2-3 \|\|

*matsya uvāca*  
*abhiṣekārdra śirasā rājñā rājyāvalokinā \|*  
*sahāyavaraṇaṃ kāryaṃ tatra rājyaṃ pratiṣṭhitam \|\| 2 \|\|*

*yadapyalpataraṃ karma tadapyekena duṣkaram \|*  
*puruṣeṇāsahāyena kimu rājyaṃ mahodayam \|\| 3 \|\|*

2-3. Matsya said A king succeeding to his throne should pick out worthy men for his assembly as his advisors and helpers on various subjects to work on his staff in order that his rule may be prosperous, for the prosperity of his kingdom depends solely on the men in his council and in various other departments. Even the smallest function cannot be successfully performed by one single man not helped by anybody. Now, then can a state be well administered without the assistance of competent ministers and helpers?

## \|\| 215.4-7 \|\|

*tasmātsahāyānvarayetkulīnānnṛpatiḥ svayam \|*  
*śūrānkulīnajātīyānbalayuktāñchriyā'nvitān \|\| 4 \|\|*

*rūpasattvaguṇopetānsajжanānkṣamayā'nvitān \|*  
*kleśakṣamānmahotsāhāndharmajñāṃśca priyaṃvadān \|\| 5 \|\|*

*hitopadeśakālajñānsvāmibhaktānyaśorthinaḥ \|*  
*evaṃvidhānsahāyāṃśca śubhakarmasu yojayet \|\| 6 \|\|*

*guṇahīnānapi tathā vijñāya nṛpatiḥ svayam \|*  
*karmasveva niyuñjīta yathāyogyeṣu bhāgaśaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

4- 7. A king should, therefore, choose his ministers and helpers from a respectable family who should be valiant, strong, imposing, capable of bearing hardships, ambitious, handsome, having Satva-guna and forbearance, good, virtuous, used to gentle speaking, able to give friendly advices, loyal, knowing to act in the proper time and place, eager for a good name. Such men should be employed by a king to discharge responsible and good functions. People unsuited to particular offices should be given places according to their respective merits where they can make themselves useful, after, they had been duly examined.

## \|\| 215.8-10 \|\|

*kulīnaḥ śīlasaṃpanno dhanurvedaviśāradaḥ \|*  
*hastiśikṣāśvaśikṣāsu kuśalaḥ ślakṣṇabhāṣitā \|\| 8 \|\|*

*nimitte śakunajñāne vettā caiva cikitsite \|*  
*kṛtajñaḥ karmaṇāṃ śūrastathā kleśasahastvṛjuḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*vyūhatattvavidhānajñaḥ phalgusāraviśeṣavit \|*  
*rājñā senāpatiḥ kāryo brāhmaṇaḥ kṣattriyo'thavā \|\| 10 \|\|*

8-10. A king should appoint a Brahmana or a Kshatrya to be his Commander-in-chief. He should be of a good family,' modest, having good manners, skilled in archery, expert in examining and managing horses and elephants, used to polite speaking, able to understand the science of omens and medicine, grateful, able to appreciate the prowess of the brave, valiant, used to bear hardships and having a knowledge of disposing troops in battle and of military affairs in particular.

## \|\| 215.11 \|\|

*prāṃśuḥ surūpo dakṣaśca priyavādī na coddhataḥ \|*  
*cittagrāhaśca sarveṣāṃ pratīhāro vidhīyate \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. A king’s door-keeper should be a man of long stature, clever, handsome, humble, accustomed to sweet speech, able to influence the minds of the people.

## \|\| 215.12-13 \|\|

*yathoktavādī dūtaḥ syāddeśabhāṣāviśāradaḥ \|*  
*śaktaḥ kleśasaho vāggmī deśakālavibhāgavit \|\| 12 \|\|*

*vijñātadeśakālaśca dūtaḥ sa syānmahīkṣitaḥ \|*  
*vaktā nayasya yaḥ kāle sa dūto nṛpaterbhavet \|\| 13 \|\|*

12-13. A king’s spy should be conscientious enough to submit true and accurate reports, obedient to the king’s injunctions,, have a knowledge of dialects of many countries, viable to speak fluently and put up with rough life, of quiet disposition and capable of discharging his functions adequately according to the circumstances.

## \|\| 215.14 \|\|

*prāṃśavo'śayanāḥ śūrā dṛḍhabhaktā nirākulāḥ \|*  
*rājñā tu rakṣiṇaḥ kāryāḥ sadā kleśasahā hitāḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. The personal guards of a king should be men of long size, robust, brave, firm in loyalty, free from uneasiness, used to bear always hardships, well-wishers of their lord.

## \|\| 215.15 \|\|

*anāhāryo'nṛśaṃsaśca dṛḍhabhaktiśca pārthive \|*  
*tāmbūladhārī bhavati nārī vā'pyatha tadguṇā \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. The betel bearer of the ting, it may be he or she, should be free from avarice, immune from all outside influences and most loyal.

## \|\| 215.16 \|\|

*ṣāḍguṇyavidhitattvajño deśabhāṣāviśāradaḥ \|*  
*sāṃdhivigrahikaḥ kāryo rājñā nayaviśāradaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. The man with full knowledge of king’s six-fold expedients in foreign politics Sandhi (peace), Vigraha (war), Yana (morals), Asana (halt), Dvaidhibhava (duplicate) and Asaraya (seeking shelter) and the languages of the country should be employed as minister for war.

## \|\| 215.17 \|\|

*kṛtākṛtajño bhṛtyānāṃ jñeyaḥ syāddeśarakṣitā \|*  
*āyavyayajño lokajño deśotpattiviśāradaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. The provincial rulers of the king should be men able to know the doings (merits and demerits) of the subordinate officials, the income and the expenditure and the produce of crops and many languages.

## \|\| 215.18-19 \|\|

*surūpastaruṇaḥ prāṃśurdṛḍhabhaktiḥ kulocitaḥ \|*  
*śūraḥ kleśasahaścaiva khaḍgadhārī prakīrtitaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*śūraśca balayuktaśca gajāśvarathakovidaḥ \|*  
*dhanurdhārī bhavedrā jñaḥ sarvakleśasahaḥ śuciḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

18-19. The men who will bear swords should be handsome, young, long in size, very loyal, of good family, brave, and able to bear hardships. Those who will be archers should be powerful, having a knowledge of riding on elephants, horses, chariots most righteous, and skilled in archery and able to bear all sorts of hardships.

## \|\| 215.20-21 \|\|

*nimittaśakunajñānī hayaśikṣāviśāradaḥ \|*  
*hayāyurvedatattvajño bhuvo bhāgavicakṣaṇaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*balābalajño rathinaḥ sthiradṛṣṭiḥ priyaṃvadaḥ \|*  
*śūraśca kṛtavidyaśca sārathiḥ parikīrtitaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

20-21. The charioteer of a king should have a good knowledge of the principles of the science of omens. He should be able to train and treat horses, know the divisions of the country, be aware of the power of warriors, firm in sight, used to gentle speech, learned, and versed in all the arts.

## \|\| 215.22-23 \|\|

*anāhāryaḥ śucirdakṣaścikitsitavidāṃ varaḥ \|*  
*sūpaśāstraviśeṣajñaḥ sūdādhyakṣaḥ praśasyate \|\| 22 \|\|*

*sūdaśāstravidhānajñāḥ parābhedyāḥ kulodgatāḥ \|*  
*sarve mahānase dhāryāḥ kṛttakeśanakhā narāḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

22-23. A man immune from avarice and outside influences, handsome, plucky, knowing the sciences of medicine and cookery, generous, particular about clipping his hair and finger nails should be employed as a cook in a royal kitchen.

## \|\| 215.24 \|\|

*samaḥ śatrau ca mitre ca dharmaśāstraviśāradaḥ \|*  
*vipramukhyaḥ kulīnaśca dharmādhikaraṇo bhavet \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. The members of his assembly should be Koolin Brahmanas equal in their dealings to friends and foes, be versed in the Dharmashastras.

## \|\| 215.25-29 \|\|

*kāryāstathāvidhāstatra dvijamukhyāḥ sabhāsadaḥ \|*  
*sarvadeśākṣarābhijñaḥ sarvaśāstraviśāradaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*lekhakaḥ kathito rājñaḥ sarvādhikaraṇeṣu vai \|*  
*śīrṣopetānsusaṃpūrṇānsamaśreṇigatānsamān \|\| 26 \|\|*

*akṣarānvai likhedyastu lekhakaḥ sa varaḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*upāyavākyakuśalaḥ sarvaśāstraviśāradaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

*bahvarthavaktā cālpena lekhakaḥ syānnṛpottama \|*  
*vākyābhiprāyatattvajño deśakālavibhāgavit \|\| 28 \|\|*

*anāhārye bhavetsakto lekhakaḥ syānnṛpottama \|*  
*puruṣāntaratattvajñāḥ prāṃśavaścāpyalolupāḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

25-29. The writers of a king should write neatly and legibly. The letters are to be full and placed at equal intervals. He should be clever in devising means, and in the use of stray expressions versed in all the Shastras and capable to express many meanings fully in short phrases.

O king! Those people ought to be placed in religious services, or in the Judicial Services who are expert in knowing the hearts of people, of long stature, free from greed, and of a charitable disposition. Such men should be engaged also as gate keepers.

## \|\| 215.30-31 \|\|

*dharmādhikāriṇaḥ kāryā janā dānakarā narāḥ \|*  
*evaṃvidhāstathā kāryā rājñā dauvārikā janāḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

*lohavastrājinādīnāṃ ratnānāṃ ca vidhānavit \|*  
*vijñātā phalgusārāṇāmanāhāryaḥ śuciḥ sadā \|\| 31 \|\|*

30-31. King’s Treasurer should know the ways of disposing of iron, cloth, deer-skin, and jewels. He should be able to value things, and be wise, clear in mind, and free from laziness and avarice. All his assistants should also be like him.

## \|\| 215.32 \|\|

*nipuṇaścāpramattaśca dhanādhyakṣaḥ prakīrtitaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. The officials in charge of disbursements should also be of the same type as in the exchequer.

## \|\| 215.33 \|\|

*āyadvāreṣu sarveṣu dhanādhyakṣasamā narāḥ \|*  
*vyayadvāreṣu ca tathā kartavyāḥ pṛthivīkṣitā \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. One who is skilled in the eight-fold medical science by heredity, incapable of being won over by anyone, free from avarice, virtuous, belonging to a good family, should be employed as a physician on whom asking, should look as the preceptor of his life. The king is to obey like ordinary persons, the words of his physician; for he deals with his life.

## \|\| 215.34-39 \|\|

*paramparāgato yaḥ syādaṣṭāṅge sucikitsite \|*  
*anāhāryaḥ sa vaidyaḥ syāddharmātmā ca kulodgataḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

*prāṇācāryaḥ sa vijñeyo vacanaṃ tasya bhūbhujā \|*  
*rājanrājñā sadā kāryaṃ yathā kāryaṃ pṛthagjanaiḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

*hastiśikṣāvidhānajño vanajātiviśāradaḥ \|*  
*kleśakṣamastathā rājño gajādhyakṣaḥ praśasyate \|\| 36 \|\|*

*etaireva guṇairyuktaḥ sthaviraśca viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*gajārohī narendra sya sarvakarmasu śasyate \|\| 37 \|\|*

*hayaśikṣāvidhānajñaścikitsitaviśāradaḥ \|*  
*aśvādhyakṣo mahībhartuḥ svāsanaśca praśasyate \|\| 38 \|\|*

*anāhāryaśca śūraśca tathā prājñaḥ kulodgataḥ \|*  
*durgādhyakṣaḥ smṛto rājña udyuktaḥ sarvakarmasu \|\| 39 \|\|*

34-39. A king should appoint different class of men in different departments according to requirements. One who knows the art of training elephants and is aware of the races of wild beasts, and is accustomed to bear hardships should he made the superintendent of royal elephants. Similar should be the elephant driver who should also be of the above qualifications and firm in his seat and clever all round. The groom of a King should know about horses and how to treat the horses when ill. The Commander of the royal fort should be a man who cannot be easily led away by any intrigue. He should also be brave, learned, of high family, and persevering and energetic in all actions. The Engineer of a King should know engineering, and be able to prepare plans and hardy and energetic and have nimble hands, keen foresight and should not get tired. Similar men should be employed in the art of using weapons who know the various ways of throwing weapons etc.'

## \|\| 215.40-42 \|\|

*vāstuvidyāvidhānajño laghuhasto jitaśramaḥ \|*  
*dīrghadarśī ca śūraśca sthapatiḥ parikīrtitaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

*yantramukte pāṇimukte vimukte muktadhārite \|*  
*astrācāryo nirudvegaḥ kuśalaśca viśiṣyate \|\| 41 \|\|*

*vṛddhaḥ kulodgataḥ sūktaḥ pitṛpaitāmahaḥ śuciḥ \|*  
*rājñāmantaḥ purādhyakṣo vinītaśca tatheṣyate \|\| 42 \|\|*

40-42. The custodian of the ladies’ apartments in a royal palace should be a man free from uneasiness, skillful, humble, advanced in age, belonging to a respectable family, devoted to his ancestors, chaste, meek and modest. Thus a King should appoint his retainers in these seven different departments after examining them fully. They should all be careful and thoroughly expert in the different works.

## \|\| 215.43-46 \|\|

*evaṃ saptādhikāreṣu puruṣāḥ sapta te pure \|*  
*parīkṣya cādhikāryaḥ syū rājñā sarveṣu karmasu \|*  
*sthāpanājātitattvajñāḥ satataṃ pratijāgṛtāḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

*rājñaḥ syādāyudhāgāre dakṣaḥ karmasu codyataḥ \|*  
*karmāṇyaparimeyāni rājño nṛpakulodvaha \|\| 44 \|\|*

*uttamādhamamadhyāni buddhvā karmāṇi pārthivaḥ \|*  
*uttamādhamamadhyeṣu puruṣeṣu niyojayet \|\| 45 \|\|*

*narakarmaviparyāsādrā jā nāśamavāpnuyāt \|*  
*niyogaṃ pauruṣaṃ bhaktiṃ śrutaṃ śauryaṃ kulaṃ nayam \|\| 46 \|\|*

43-46. The Controller of the arsenal should be wise, energetic and persevering. A King should always appoint men to hold offices after examining the responsibilities of different situations. Excellent, middling and mean are the three kinds of works. Improper discharge of duties leads to the extinction of a sovereign. A King should therefore always properly scrutinize the manliness, devotion, learning, courage, family status and gentility of a man as well as take advantage of expert advice before appointing him to hold an office of state.

## \|\| 215.47-49 \|\|

*jñātvā vṛttirvidhātavyā puruṣāṇāṃ mahīkṣitā \|*  
*puruṣāntaravijñānatattvasāranibandhanāt \|\| 47 \|\|*

*bahubhirmantrayetkāmaṃ rājā mantraṃ pṛthakpṛthak \|*  
*mantriṇāmapi no kuryānmantrimantraprakāśanam \|\| 48 \|\|*

*kvacinna kasya viśvāso bhavatīha sadā nṛṇām \|*  
*niścayastu sadā mantre kārya ekena sūriṇā \|\| 49 \|\|*

47-49. A King should consult his Councilors over a matter individually and separately and the advice of one Councilor should not be divulged to the other, for every one cannot be taken into full confidence. Therefore consultation in chief should be held with the prime minister but by seeking the advice of more people one very often gets confused. Therefore many men’s advice should not be taken. A king used to act on the counsel of others should always place confidence in the advice of his Councilor in chief.

## \|\| 215.50-52 \|\|

*bhavedvā niścayāvāptiḥ parabuddhyupajivanāt \|*  
*ekasyaiva mahībharturbhūyaḥ kāryo viniścayaḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

*brāhmaṇānparyupāsīta trayīśāstrasuniścitān \|*  
*nāsacchāstravato mūḍhāṃste hi lokasya kaṇṭakāḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

*vṛddhānhi nityaṃ seveta viprānvedavidaḥ śucīn \|*  
*tebhyaḥ śikṣeta vinayaṃ vinītātmā ca nityaśaḥ \|*  
*samagrāṃ vaśagāṃ kuryātpṛthivīṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

50-52. A King should always have by him and revere the Brahmanas versed in the three Vedas and should never encourage the votaries of unreal learning for their contact is always thorny and uncongenial to the learned. He should always venerate the learned in the Vedas, respect grey hairs and holy persons and imbibe from them meekness and statesmanship. Such a King undoubtedly influences the world, and many ill-behaved Kings without humility and modesty had gone to rack and ruin,

## \|\| 215.53-55 \|\|

*bahavo'vinayādbhraṣṭā rājānaḥ saparicchadāḥ \|*  
*vanasthāścaiva rājyāni vinayātpratipedire \|\| 53 \|\|*

*traividyebhyastrayīṃ vidyāṃ daṇḍanītiṃ ca śāśvatīm \|*  
*ānvīkṣikīṃ tvātmavidyāṃ vārtārambhāśca lokataḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

*indri yāṇāṃ jaye yogaṃ samātiṣṭheddivāniśam \|*  
*jitendri yo hi śaknoti vaśe sthāpayituṃ prajāḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

53-55. Many well-behaved Kings had regained their empires even when exiled. A King should read the Vedas from those who are learned in them. He should also master politics, logic, philosophy, and temporal science; he should collect information from ordinary people and keep his senses under control, for a King who can subdue his passions fascinates all his people. A King should also perform a series of sacrifices in which liberal gifts should be given to the Brahmanas.

## \|\| 215.56-57 \|\|

*yajeta rājā bahubhiḥ kratubhiśca sadakṣiṇaiḥ \|*  
*dharmārthaṃ caiva viprebhyo dadyādbhogāndhanāni ca \|\| 56 \|\|*

*sāṃvatsarikamāptaiśca rāṣṭrādāhārayedbalim \|*  
*syātsvādhyāyaparo loke varteta pitṛbandhuvat \|\| 57 \|\|*

56-57. Besides this for the sake of righteousness he should give various kinds of gifts to the Brahmanas and should collect revenues from his subjects annually, fie should propagate the study of the Vedas in his state and should be like a father and brother to his subjects. He should especially revere the members of his preceptor’s family.

## \|\| 215.58 \|\|

*āvṛttānāṃ gurukulāddvijānāṃ pūjako bhavet \|*  
*nṛpāṇāmakṣayo hyeṣa vidhirbrāhmo'bhidhīyate \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. This eternal rule to be observed by the Kings is established by Brahma. The King following it does not perish. He is amiable to all.

The wicked, thieves, and enemies cannot flourish.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — … King’s prescribed course of conduct.

## \|\| 215.59 \|\|

*taṃ ca stenā na vā'mitrā haranti na vinaśyati \|*  
*tasmādrā jñā vidhātavyo brāhmo vai hyakṣayo vidhiḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. And so he should always direct his actions according to Brahmabidhi which is known as Akshyabidhi. A King should look upon all classes of his subjects according to their merits and employ them accordingly.

## \|\| 215.60-84 \|\|

*samottamādhamai rājā hyāhūya pālayetprajāḥ \|*  
*na nivarteta saṅgrāmātkṣāttraṃ vratamanusmaran \|\| 60 \|\|*

*saṅgrāmeṣvanivartitvaṃ prajānāṃ paripālanam \|*  
*śuśrūṣā brāhmaṇānāṃ ca rājñāṃ niḥśreyasaṃ param \|\| 61 \|\|*

*kṛpaṇānāthavṛddhānāṃ vidhavānāṃ ca yoṣitām \|*  
*yogakṣemaṃ ca vṛttiṃ ca tathaiva parikalpayet \|\| 62 \|\|*

*varṇāśramavyavasthānaṃ tathā kāryaṃ viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*svadharmapracyutānrājā svadharme sthāpayettathā \|\| 63 \|\|*

*āśrameṣu tathā kāryamannaṃ tailaṃ ca bhājanam \|*  
*svayamevā’nayedrā jā satkṛtānnāvamānayet \|\| 64 \|\|*

*tāpase sarvakāryāṇi rājyamātmānameva ca \|*  
*nivedayetprayatnena devavacciramarcayet \|\| 65 \|\|*

*dve prajñe veditavye ca ṛjvī vakrā ca mānavaiḥ \|*  
*vakrāṃ jñātvā na seveta pratibādheta cā’gatām \|\| 66 \|\|*

*nāsya cchidraṃ paro vidyādvidyācchidraṃ parasya tu \|*  
*gūhetkūrma ivāṅgāni rakṣedvivaramātmanaḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

*na viśvasedaviśvaste viśvaste nātiviśvaset \|*  
*viśvāsādbhayamutpannaṃ mūlānyapi nikṛntati \|\| 68 \|\|*

*viśvāsayeccāpyaparaṃ tattvabhūtena hetunā \|*  
*bakavaccintayedarthānsiṃhavacca parākramet \|\| 69 \|\|*

*vṛkavaccāpi lumpeta śaśavacca vinikṣipet \|*  
*dṛḍhaprahārī ca bhavettathā śūkaravannṛpaḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

*citrākāraśca śikhivaddṛḍhabhaktastathā śvavat \|*  
*tathā ca madhurābhāṣī bhavetkokilavannṛpaḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

*kākaśaṅkī bhavennityamajñātavasatiṃ vaset \|*  
*nāparīkṣitapūrvaṃ ca bhojanaṃ śayanaṃ vrajet \|*  
*vastraṃ puṣpamalaṃkāraṃ yaccānyanmanujottama \|\| 72 \|\|*

*na gāhejжanasaṃbādhaṃ na cājñātajalāśayam \|*  
*aparīkṣitapūrvaṃ ca puruṣairāptakāribhiḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

*nā’rohetkuñjaraṃ vyālaṃ nādāntaṃ turagaṃ tathā \|*  
*nāvijñātāṃ striyaṃ gacchennaiva devotsave vaset \|\| 74 \|\|*

*narendra lakṣmyā dharmajña trātā'śrānto bhavennṛpaḥ \|*  
*sadbhṛtyāśca tathā puṣṭāḥ satataṃ pratimānitāḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

*rājñā sahāyāḥ kartavyāḥ pṛthivīṃ jetumicchatā \|*  
*yathārhaṃ cāpyasubhṛto rājā karmasu yojayet \|\| 76 \|\|*

*dharmiṣṭhāndharmakāryeṣū śūrānsaṅgrāmakarmasu \|*  
*nipuṇānarthakṛtyeṣu sarvatraiva tathā śucīn \|\| 77 \|\|*

*strīṣu ṣaṇḍaṃ niyuñjīta tīkṣṇaṃ dāruṇakarmasu \|*  
*dharme cārthe ca kāme ca naye ca ravinandana \|\| 78 \|\|*

*rājā yathārhaṃ kuryācca upadhābhiḥ parīkṣaṇam \|*  
*samatītopadānbhṛtyānkuryācchastavanecarān \|\| 79 \|\|*

*tatpādānveṣiṇo yattāṃstadadhyakṣāṃstu kārayet \|*  
*evamādīni karmāṇi nṛpaiḥ karyāṇi pārthiva \|\| 80 \|\|*

*sarvathā neṣyate rājastīkṣṇopakaraṇakramaḥ \|*  
*karmāṇi pāpasādhyāni yāni rājño narādhipa \|\| 81 \|\|*

*santastāni na kurvanti tasmāttāni tyajennṛpaḥ \|*  
*neṣyate pṛthivīśānāṃ tīkṣṇopakaraṇakriyā \|\| 82 \|\|*

*yasminkarmaṇi yasya syādveśeṣeṇa ca kauśalam \|*  
*tasminkarmaṇi taṃ rājā parīkṣya viniyojayet \|*  
*pitṛpaitāmahānbhṛtyānsarvakarmasu yojayet \|\| 83 \|\|*

*vinā dāyādakṛtyeṣu tatra te hi samāgatāḥ \|*  
*rājā dāyādakṛtyeṣu parīkṣya tu kṛtānnarān \|*  
*niyuñjīta mahābhāga tasya te hitakāriṇaḥ \|\| 84 \|\|*

60-84. A King should recollect his Kshatrya dharma and never retreat from war. Not to retire from battle-field, to protect his subjects, to serve the Brahmanas are the foremost duties of a King. He should also protect the distressed, the infirm, the widows and provide them with boarding and lodging and endowments and adjust the Varnashrama rules, should reclaim and restore the fallen ones in their respective religions, should give grain, cloth, oil, utensils, etc. to the good of all orders; should fulfil the objects of the ascetics and worship them like the Devas, and never disrespect those who have done good to him. He should interest himself in these things in such a way as to sacrifice his life and Kingdom for their sake in case of necessity.

## \|\| 215.65-66 \|\|

*tāpase sarvakāryāṇi rājyamātmānameva ca \|*  
*nivedayetprayatnena devavacciramarcayet \|\| 65 \|\|*

*dve prajñe veditavye ca ṛjvī vakrā ca mānavaiḥ \|*  
*vakrāṃ jñātvā na seveta pratibādheta cā’gatām \|\| 66 \|\|*

65-66. Men are said to have two kinds of minds viz. honest and equivocal, He should know what is meant by duplicate mind but should not bear it in practise. When he is influenced by the latter' he should suppress it and should not let anyone know of his weakness, but should try and realize the failings of others.

## \|\| 215.67-68 \|\|

*nāsya cchidraṃ paro vidyādvidyācchidraṃ parasya tu \|*  
*gūhetkūrma ivāṅgāni rakṣedvivaramātmanaḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

*na viśvasedaviśvaste viśvaste nātiviśvaset \|*  
*viśvāsādbhayamutpannaṃ mūlānyapi nikṛntati \|\| 68 \|\|*

67-68. He should guard his limbs of body and keep them secret just as a tortoise does actions. He should also take care of his weaknesses and not get them divulged. The man who has no defined religion should never be trusted nor should a man of affirmed religion be taken into confidence indiscriminately. If trust begets fear, then total destruction ensues. Confidence should however he inspired into others with tact.

## \|\| 215.69-74 \|\|

*viśvāsayeccāpyaparaṃ tattvabhūtena hetunā \|*  
*bakavaccintayedarthānsiṃhavacca parākramet \|\| 69 \|\|*

*vṛkavaccāpi lumpeta śaśavacca vinikṣipet \|*  
*dṛḍhaprahārī ca bhavettathā śūkaravannṛpaḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

*citrākāraśca śikhivaddṛḍhabhaktastathā śvavat \|*  
*tathā ca madhurābhāṣī bhavetkokilavannṛpaḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

*kākaśaṅkī bhavennityamajñātavasatiṃ vaset \|*  
*nāparīkṣitapūrvaṃ ca bhojanaṃ śayanaṃ vrajet \|*  
*vastraṃ puṣpamalaṃkāraṃ yaccānyanmanujottama \|\| 72 \|\|*

*na gāhejжanasaṃbādhaṃ na cājñātajalāśayam \|*  
*aparīkṣitapūrvaṃ ca puruṣairāptakāribhiḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

*nā’rohetkuñjaraṃ vyālaṃ nādāntaṃ turagaṃ tathā \|*  
*nāvijñātāṃ striyaṃ gacchennaiva devotsave vaset \|\| 74 \|\|*

69-74. He should think of acquiring wealth with the eyes of a crane, and he should show valour like that of a lion, 'he should take to his heels like a wolf, collect money like a hare, strike hard on others like a boar, he should be of variegated manners like a peacock, devoted like a dog, be afraid like a crow, speak sweet like a cuckoo. He should fix his; psid0nce in a quiet unknown place, and should not take his meals, go to bed or use flowers, clothes and ornaments without due observation and scrutiny. He should not without pre-examination go to a public scene or in the midst of a crowd, nor should he plunge into unknown waters. The not tested by experts should not be ridden by him. He should not interfere with a snake nor indulge with an unknown woman. He should not stay at a festival of a God.

## \|\| 215.75-78 \|\|

*narendra lakṣmyā dharmajña trātā'śrānto bhavennṛpaḥ \|*  
*sadbhṛtyāśca tathā puṣṭāḥ satataṃ pratimānitāḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

*rājñā sahāyāḥ kartavyāḥ pṛthivīṃ jetumicchatā \|*  
*yathārhaṃ cāpyasubhṛto rājā karmasu yojayet \|\| 76 \|\|*

*dharmiṣṭhāndharmakāryeṣū śūrānsaṅgrāmakarmasu \|*  
*nipuṇānarthakṛtyeṣu sarvatraiva tathā śucīn \|\| 77 \|\|*

*strīṣu ṣaṇḍaṃ niyuñjīta tīkṣṇaṃ dāruṇakarmasu \|*  
*dharme cārthe ca kāme ca naye ca ravinandana \|\| 78 \|\|*

75-78. He should always remain in the midst of his regal paraphernalia. He should protect the distressed and practise self-restraint. Besides all this, a king eager for conquests should have worthy and stalwart assistants. He should always feed the Sadhus and servants and respect them.

## \|\| 215.77-80 \|\|

*dharmiṣṭhāndharmakāryeṣū śūrānsaṅgrāmakarmasu \|*  
*nipuṇānarthakṛtyeṣu sarvatraiva tathā śucīn \|\| 77 \|\|*

*strīṣu ṣaṇḍaṃ niyuñjīta tīkṣṇaṃ dāruṇakarmasu \|*  
*dharme cārthe ca kāme ca naye ca ravinandana \|\| 78 \|\|*

*rājā yathārhaṃ kuryācca upadhābhiḥ parīkṣaṇam \|*  
*samatītopadānbhṛtyānkuryācchastavanecarān \|\| 79 \|\|*

*tatpādānveṣiṇo yattāṃstadadhyakṣāṃstu kārayet \|*  
*evamādīni karmāṇi nṛpaiḥ karyāṇi pārthiva \|\| 80 \|\|*

77-80. He should appoint the virtuous to conduct acts of righteousness, the brave to carry on warfare, the intelligent to control the revenue department, and persons of good character to all posts suited to them. Eunuchs should be employed in the female apartments of the palace, strong-minded men should be employed to fulfil difficult missions. A king should examine whether a man is of good character or not by privately making him presents through Dharma, Artha or Kama and then engage him. He should send as spies his trustworthy servants in the garb of Sanyasins as residing in forests to enquire privately into the truth.

## \|\| 215.81-83 \|\|

*sarvathā neṣyate rājastīkṣṇopakaraṇakramaḥ \|*  
*karmāṇi pāpasādhyāni yāni rājño narādhipa \|\| 81 \|\|*

*santastāni na kurvanti tasmāttāni tyajennṛpaḥ \|*  
*neṣyate pṛthivīśānāṃ tīkṣṇopakaraṇakriyā \|\| 82 \|\|*

*yasminkarmaṇi yasya syādveśeṣeṇa ca kauśalam \|*  
*tasminkarmaṇi taṃ rājā parīkṣya viniyojayet \|*  
*pitṛpaitāmahānbhṛtyānsarvakarmasu yojayet \|\| 83 \|\|*

81-83. A king should regulate his affairs like this. A king should not always administer justice with a strong hand. The unpleasant duties of a king cannot be performed through virtuous people, consequently a king should avoid the use of repressive measures, otherwise subjects become dissatisfied. Men should be appointed to hold offices to which they are best suited.

## \|\| 215.84-89 \|\|

*vinā dāyādakṛtyeṣu tatra te hi samāgatāḥ \|*  
*rājā dāyādakṛtyeṣu parīkṣya tu kṛtānnarān \|*  
*niyuñjīta mahābhāga tasya te hitakāriṇaḥ \|\| 84 \|\|*

*pararājagṛhātprāptāñjanasaṃgrahakāmyayā \|*  
*duṣṭānvā'pyathavā'duṣṭānāśrayīta prayatnataḥ \|\| 85 \|\|*

*duṣṭaṃ vijñāya viśvāsaṃ na kuryāttatra bhūmipaḥ \|*  
*vṛttiṃ tasyāpi varteta janasaṃgrahakāmyayā \|\| 86 \|\|*

*rājā deśāntaraprāptaṃ puruṣaṃ pūjayedbhṛśam \|*  
*mamāyaṃ deśasaṃprāpto bahumānena cintayet \|\| 87 \|\|*

*kāmaṃ bhṛtyārjanaṃ rājā naiva kuryānnarādhipa \|*  
*na ca vā'saṃvibhaktāṃstānbhṛtyānkuryātkathaṃcana \|\| 88 \|\|*

*śatravo'gnirviṣaṃ sarpo nistriṃśa iti caikataḥ \|*  
*bhṛtyā manujaśārdūla ruṣitāśca tathaikataḥ \|\| 89 \|\|*

84-89. The hereditary servants of the state may he employed in all departments without any hard and fast tests. One's own friends should also be placed in charge of works where a king’s relatives are not placed. Thus the good results are secured by the king. The wicked and the good emigrants from other empires should be accommodated with respect in his dominions by a king. The wicked when known should not however be trusted but to promote the fecundity of mankind they should also be provided with means of sustenance. The emigrants from the other empires should be well-treated on the understanding that they have come under his protection. Thus they would remain under obligation. The king should not himself be ready to collect his servants; nor should he allow dissensions to crop up amongst his servants.

## \|\| 215.90 \|\|

*teṣāṃ cāreṇa cāritraṃ rājā vijñāya nityaśaḥ \|*  
*guṇināṃ pūjanaṃ kuryānnirguṇānāṃ ca śāsanam \|*  
*kathitāḥ satataṃ rājanrājānaścāracakṣuṣaḥ \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. The servants not satisfied with the king should be kept under close watch and ward and the sovereign should keep himself well-informed about their conduct through his reliable spies. They are to be treated as he would behave towards enemies, fire,, poison, serpents and swords.

## \|\| 215.91 \|\|

*svake deśe pare deśe jñānaśīlānvicakṣaṇān \|*  
*anāhāryānkleśasahānniyuñjīta tathā carān \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. A king should award his capable servants and punish the wicked ones. He should keep himself informed about everyone through his spies. The spies are the eyes of the king.

## \|\| 215.92-94 \|\|

*janasyāviditānsaumyāṃstathā'jñātānparasparam \|*  
*vaṇijo mantrakuśalānsāṃvatsaracikitsakān \|*  
*tathā pravrājitākārāṃścārānrājā viyojayet \|\| 92 \|\|*

*naikasya rajā śraddadhyāccārasyāpi subhāṣitam \|*  
*dvayoḥ saṃbandhamājñāya śraddadhyānnṛpatistadā \|\| 93 \|\|*

*parasparasyāviditau yadi syātāṃ ca tāvubhau \|*  
*tasmādrā jā prayatnena gūḍhāṃścārānniyojayet \|\| 94 \|\|*

92-94. A king should secretly depute four spies in his country as well as in foreign countries to work out the policy of divide and rule. They should be intelligent, learned, free from avarice, able to put up with hardships, incapable of being recognised by others, simple in habits, able to mix with people, skilled in commerce or medicine. He should not pin his faith in one spy alone. The spies must recognize each other and be of gentle manners.

## \|\| 215.95-98 \|\|

*rājyasya mūlametāvadyā rājñaścāradarśitā \|*  
*cārāṇāmapi yatnena rājñā kāryaṃ parīkṣaṇam \|\| 95 \|\|*

*rāgāparāgau bhṛtyānāṃ janasya ca guṇāguṇān \|*  
*sarvaṃ rājñāṃ carāyattaṃ teṣu yatnaparo bhavet \|\| 96 \|\|*

*karmaṇā kena me loke janaḥ sarvo'nurajyate \|*  
*virajyate kena tathā vijñeyaṃ tanmahīkṣitā \|\| 97 \|\|*

*anurāgakaraṃ loke karma kāryaṃ mahākṣitā \|*  
*virāgajanakaṃ loke varjanīyaṃ viśeṣataḥ \|\| 98 \|\|*

95-98. The spies should roam in the garb of merchants, ministers, astrologers, physicians or Sannyasis. When at least two of such spies corroborate each other, the king should act accordingly. If they contradict each other then spies of more superior talents should be deputed to find out which of his actions are appreciated by his people as well as the causes of their dissatisfaction. The spies should be checked in return. He W should then abandon for good what may be against the wishes of the people.

## \|\| 215.99 \|\|

*janānurāgaprabhavā hi lakṣmī rājñāṃ yato bhāskaravaṃśacandra \|*  
*tasmātprayatnena narendra mukhyaiḥ kāryo'nurāgo bhuvi mānaveṣu \|\| 99 \|\|*

99\. O King of the Solar race! the beauty and prosperity of a king always lies in the contentment of his subjects, he should therefore act in such a manner as their love toward their king might be increased.

## Chapter 216

## \|\| 216.1 \|\|

*matsya uvāca*  
*yathā'nuvartitavyaṃ syānmano rājño'nujīvibhiḥ \|*  
*tathā te kathayiṣyāmi nibodha gadato mama \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Matsya said: — O King of Manus! I shall tell you now what a servant of the State should do. Hear.

## \|\| 216.2-7 \|\|

*jñātvā sarvātmanā kāryaṃ svaśaktyā ravinandana \|*  
*rājā yattu vadedvākyaṃ śrotavyaṃ tatprayatnataḥ \|*  
*ākṣipya vacanaṃ tasya na vaktavyaṃ tathā vacaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*anukūlaṃ priyaṃ tasya vaktavyaṃ janasaṃsadi \|*  
*rahogatasya vaktavyamapriyaṃ taddhitaṃ bhavet \|\| 3 \|\|*

*parārthamasya vaktavyaṃ svasthe cetasi pārthiva \|*  
*svārthaḥ suhṛdbhirvaktavyo na svayaṃ tu kathaṃ cana \|\| 4 \|\|*

*kāryātipātaḥ sarveṣu rakṣitavyaḥ prayatnataḥ \|*  
*na ca hiṃsyaṃ dhanaṃ kiṃcinniyuktena ca karmaṇi \|\| 5 \|\|*

*nopekṣyastasya mānaśca tathā rājñaḥ priyo bhavet \|*  
*rājñaśca na tathā kāryaṃ veṣabhāṣitaceṣṭitam \|\| 6 \|\|*

*rājalīlā na kartavyā tadvidviṣṭaṃ ca varjayet \|*  
*rājñaḥ samo'dhiko vā na kāryo veṣo vijānatā \|\| 7 \|\|*

2-7. A servant of the State should carefully listen to what the king says and never interrupt him in his speech. In an assemblage, he should speak sweet and agreeable words to the king, and unsavory things that may be unavoidable and necessary for his well-being should be communicated to him privately. When a sovereign is of a peaceful disposition he may then be approached with a prayer of conferring any favour upon someone, but no prayer should be made for one’s ownself. Such a prayer should always be made through some friend. He should be specially careful that one’s duty should not be neglected. He should not overwork any one, nor should he misappropriate any money. He should never shew any indifference to the honours conferred by the sovereign and should always try to keep himself in his good graces. He should never imitate the king in his dress, mode of talking nor any other actions. He should avoid what is not pleasing to him and should not equal or excel him in dress.

## \|\| 216.8 \|\|

*dyūtādiṣu tathaivānyatkauśalaṃ tu pradarśayet \|*  
*pradarśya kauśalaṃ cāsya rājānaṃ tu viśeṣayet \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. In course of gambling and at the game of dice one should show his skill to the king but make the latter Win.

## \|\| 216.9 \|\|

*antaḥpurajanādhyakṣairvairidūtairnirākṛtaiḥ \|*  
*saṃsargaṃ na vrajedrā janvinā pārthivaśāsanāt \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Without the king’s permission he should not go about with the custodians of the ladies’ apartments of the royal palace, nor should he do so with the spies of the enemies and the dismissed servants of the State.

## \|\| 216.10 \|\|

*niḥsnehatāṃ cāvamānaṃ prayatnena tu gopayet \|*  
*yacca guhyaṃ bhavedrā jño na talloke prakāśayet \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. He should keep secret the kindly or unkindly feelings of the king toward him. He should not utter before anyone a thing that is private to the king.

## \|\| 216.11 \|\|

*nṛpeṇa śrāvitaṃ yatsyādvācyāvācyaṃ nṛpottama \|*  
*na tatsaṃśrāvayelloke tathā rājño'priyo bhavet \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Anything reproachable or irreproachable communicated by the king should not be disclosed to any one for if one does so one loses the favour of the king.

## \|\| 216.12 \|\|

*ājñāpyamāne vā'nyasminsamutthāya tvarānvitaḥ \|*  
*kimahaṃ karavāṇīti vācyo rājā vijānatā \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. When a, king orders any. one to perform any service one should readily volunteer himself to do it.

## \|\| 216.13 \|\|

*kāryāvasthāṃ ca vijñāya kāryameva yathā bhavet \|*  
*satata kriyamāṇe'smiṁ llāghavaṃ tu vrajeddhruvam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Of course this should be done knowing the hours of business, otherwise if one does so at all times, one becomes an object of hatred and ridicule.

## \|\| 216.14 \|\|

*rājñaḥ priyāṇi vākyāni na cātyarthaṃ punaḥ punaḥ \|*  
*na hāsyaśīlastu bhavenna cāpi bhṛkuṭīmukhaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. One should not repeatedly repeat the favorite words of a king. One should always remain very modest and never knit his eyebrows in his august presence or laugh too much.

## \|\| 216.15 \|\|

*nātivaktā na nirvaktā na ca mātsarikastathā \|*  
*ātmasaṃbhāvitaścaiva na bhavettu kathaṃcana \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. He should not talk too much in the presence of the king, nor should he remain silent. He should not be artful or proud, nor should he speak too much of himself.

## \|\| 216.16-19 \|\|

*duṣkṛtāni narendra sya na tu saṃkīrtayetkvacit \|*  
*vastramastramalaṃkāraṃ rājñā dattaṃ tu dhārayet \|\| 16 \|\|*

*audāryeṇa na taddeyamanyasmai bhūtimicchatā \|*  
*na caivātyaśanaṃ kāryaṃ divā svapnaṃ na kārayet \|\| 17 \|\|*

*nānirdiṣṭe tathā dvāre praviśettu kathaṃcana \|*  
*na ca paśyettu rājānamayogyāsu ca bhūmiṣu \|\| 18 \|\|*

*rājñastu dakṣiṇo pārśve vāme copaviśettadā \|*  
*purastācca tathā paścādāsanaṃ tu vigarhitam \|\| 19 \|\|*

16-19. He should not say anything about the unjust deed of the sovereign and should put on the garments, Weapons, and ornaments presented to him by the king on momentous occasions. He should not give away any of the royal gifts and should not sleep during of the day. He should not pass through a forbidden thoroughfare and should not meet the king at an improper place. He should take his seat to the right or the left of the king according to his warrant of precedence and not behind or in front of him.

## \|\| 216.20 \|\|

*jṛmbhāṃ niṣṭhīvanaṃ kāsaṃ kopaṃ paryastikāśrayam \|*  
*bhṛkuṭiṃ vāntamudgāraṃ tatsamīpe vivarjayet \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. He should not yawn, show signs of weariness, cough, assume angry demeanour, rest himself against anything, knit his eyes, vomit and belch, in the presence of the sovereign.

## \|\| 216.21 \|\|

*svayaṃ tatra na kurvīta svaguṇākhyāpanaṃ budhaḥ \|*  
*svaguṇākhyāpane yuktyā parameva prayojayet \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. He should not indulge in self-praise but he should get others to do it for him.

## \|\| 216.22-23 \|\|

*hṛdayaṃ nirmalaṃ kṛtvā parāṃ bhaktimupāśritaiḥ \|*  
*anujīvigaṇairbhāvyaṃ nityaṃ rājñāmatandri taiḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*śāṭhyaṃ laulyaṃ ca paiśunyaṃ nāstikyaṃ kṣudra tā tathā \|*  
*cāpalpaṃ ca parityājyaṃ nityaṃ rājño'nujīvibhiḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

22-23. All the servants of the Estate should most loyally serve the sovereign with a clear mind and free from laziness, They should always shun craftiness, wicked ness, backbiting, atheism and low morals.

## \|\| 216.24 \|\|

*śrutena vidyāśīlaiśca saṃyojyā’tmānamātmanā \|*  
*rājasevāṃ tataḥ kuryādbhūtaye bhūtivardhanīm \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Those versed in the Vedas, possessing modesty should always serve the king well for their welfare.

## \|\| 216.25 \|\|

*namaskāryāḥ sadā cāsya putravallabhamantriṇaḥ \|*  
*sacivaiścāsya viśvāso na tu kāryaḥ kathaṃ cana \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. The sons, friends, and councilors of the king should be saluted every day, neither the king nor his minister should be trusted.

## \|\| 216.26-27 \|\|

*apṛṣṭaścāsya na brūyātkāmaṃ brūyāttathā yadi \|*  
*hitaṃ tathyaṃ ca vacanaṃ hitaiḥ saha suniścitam \|\| 26 \|\|*

*cittaṃ caivāsya vijñeyaṃ nityamevānujīvinā \|*  
*bharturārādhanaṃ kuryāccittajño mānavaḥ sukham \|\| 27 \|\|*

26-27. Nothing should be said without being asked; and if one says go, that ought to be true and lead to the general welfare. One should always take a measure of the king’s mind by his speech and then it is easy for him to act so as to please him; he is to worship the king.

## \|\| 216.28 \|\|

*rāgāparāgrau caivāsya vijñeyau bhūtimicchatā \|*  
*tyajedviraktaṃ nṛpatiṃ raktādvṛttiṃ tu kārayet \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. One who wants one’s own welfare should mark carefully whether the king is pleased or displeased with him and should act accordingly.

## \|\| 216.29 \|\|

*viraktaḥ kārayennāśaṃ vipakṣābhyudayaṃ tathā \|*  
*āśāvardhanakaṃ kṛtvā phalanāśaṃ karoti ca \|\| 29 \|\|*

29.20. If a king goes against anybody, his party will be ruined and his opposite party will rise. The king if disgusted gives hopes but does not confer benefits accordingly. He appears angry though there is no cause of anger and though he remains pleasant, he speaks unpleasant high words. The king may deprive him of his subsistence for his insane speeches.

## \|\| 216.31-32 \|\|

*pradeśavākyamudito na ca saṃbhāvayettathā \|*  
*ārādhanāsu sarvāsu suptavacca viceṣṭate \|\| 31 \|\|*

*kathāsu doṣaṃ kṣipati vākyabhaṅgaṃ karoti ca \|*  
*lakṣyate vimukhaścaiva guṇasaṃkīrtane'pi ca \|\| 32 \|\|*

31-32. Shay cane disgusted king shews his goodwill towards others but hates him with whom he is disgusted. He finds fault with his words and speaks other words not having any concern with the business. The king turns away his attention from the piece of work of his subordinate with whom he is disgusted. These signs shew that a king is disgusted.

## \|\| 216.33-36 \|\|

*dṛṣṭiṃ kṣipati cānyatra kriyamāṇe ca karmaṇi \|*  
*viraktalakṣaṇaṃ caitacchṛṇu raktasya lakṣaṇam \|\| 33 \|\|*

*dṛṣṭvā prasanno bhavati vākyaṃ gṛhṇāti cā’darāt \|*  
*kuśalādiparipraśnaṃ saṃprayacchati cā’sanam \|\| 34 \|\|*

*viviktadarśane cāsya rahasyenaṃ na śaṅkate \|*  
*jāyate hṛṣṭavadanaḥ śrutvā tasya tu tatkathām \|\| 35 \|\|*

*apriyāṇyapi vākyāni taduktānyabhinandate \|*  
*upāyanaṃ ca gṛhṇāti stokamapyādarāttathā \|\| 36 \|\|*

33-36. On the other hand when a king becomes pleased he always assumes a pleasant aspect towards him, accepts his words with gentleness, offers seat and asks about his welfare. Knew that the king is pleased, with him, seeing whom in private place he does not become afraid, hearing whose words his face becomes jolly; even whose unpleasant words he hears and whose humble offerings the King accepts and whom he remembers with a cheerful expression of his face.

## \|\| 216.37 \|\|

*kathāntareṣu smarati prahṛṣṭavadanastathā \|*  
*iti raktasya kartavyā sevā ravikulodvaha \|*  
*āpatsu na tyajetpūrvaṃ viraktamapi sevitam \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. A devoted one should serve the king in-the ways spoken by me.

The retainers of the king who do serve others not only in times of adversity but always and who adore the king in spite of his being ignorant, go to the domain of Indra that is inhabited by the Devas.

## Chapter 217

## \|\| 217.1-2 \|\|

*matsya uvāca*  
*rājā sahāyasaṃyuktaḥ prabhūtayavasendhanam \|*  
*ramyamānatasāmantaṃ madhyamaṃ deśamāvaset \|\| 1 \|\|*

*vaiśyaśūdra janaprāyamanāhāryaṃ tathā paraiḥ \|*  
*kiṃcidbrāhmaṇasaṃyuktaṃ bahukarmakaraṃ tathā \|\| 2 \|\|*

1-2. Matsya said A king should have his residence in a central place which should be beautiful, with abundance of grass and trees. It should be inhabited by a number of people and where the tributary kings, princes and subjects are loyal and submissive. It should also have some Brahmanas skilled in various rituals and many artisans in its vicinity.

## \|\| 217.3-5 \|\|

*adevamātṛkaṃ ramyamanuraktajanānvitam \|*  
*karairapīḍitaṃ cāpi bahupuṣpaphalaṃ tathā \|\| 3 \|\|*

*agamyaṃ paracakrāṇāṃ tadvāsagṛhamāpadi \|*  
*samaduḥkhasukhaṃ rājñaḥ satataṃ priyamāsthitam \|\| 4 \|\|*

*sarīsṛpavihīnaṃ ca vyāghrataskaravarjitam \|*  
*evaṃvidhaṃ yathālābhaṃ rājā viṣayamāvaset \|\| 5 \|\|*

3-5. It should he surrounded by sweet smelling flowers and fruits. It should be impassable to the foreigner’s army. There should be no tigers, scorpions, snakes, lions, thieves round about it. The place should be beautiful and should be elevated and well-supplied with water and should not be heavily, taxed. A king should live with his assistants in such a place of happiness where there should be absolutely nothing to agitate him.

## \|\| 217.6-7 \|\|

*tatra durgaṃ nṛpaḥ kuryātṣaṇṇāmekatamaṃ budhaḥ \|*  
*dhanurdurgaṃ mahīdurgaṃ naradurgaṃ tathaiva ca \|\| 6 \|\|*

*vārkṣaṃ caivāmbudurgaṃ ca giridurgaṃ ca pārthiva \|*  
*sarveṣāmeva durgāṇāṃ giridurgaṃ praśasyate \|\| 7 \|\|*

6-7. Amidst such surroundings he should have his fortress. There are six different kinds of forts viz. — Dhanushadurga, Mahidurga, Naradurga, Vrikshadurga, Jaladurga, Giridurga, and of these the last-named Giridurga is the best.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — … A castle surrounded by desert. …. = An earth fort. … = A place of safety formed by placing the army in a particular position. … A place densely surrounded by trees -which make it impassable. … = fort surrounded by water, … =A hill fortress.

## \|\| 217.8-13 \|\|

*durgaṃ ca parikhopetaṃ vaprāṭṭālakasaṃyutam \|*  
*śataghnīyantramukhyaiśca śataśaśca samāvṛtam \|\| 8 \|\|*

*gopuraṃ sakapāṭaṃ ca tatra syātsumanoharam \|*  
*sapatākaṃ gajārūḍho yena rājā viśetpuram \|\| 9 \|\|*

*catasraśca tathā tatra kāryāstvāyatavīthayaḥ \|*  
*ekasmiṃstatra vīthyagre devaveśma bhaveddṛḍham \|\| 10 \|\|*

*vīthyagre ca dvitīye ca rājaveśma vidhīyate \|*  
*dharmādhikaraṇaṃ kāryaṃ vīthyagre ca tṛtīyake \|\| 11 \|\|*

*caturthe tvatha vīthyagre gopuraṃ ca vidhīyate \|*  
*āyataṃ caturasraṃ vā vṛttaṃ vā kārayetpuram \|\| 12 \|\|*

*muktihīnaṃ trikoṇaṃ ca yavamadhyaṃ tathaiva ca \|*  
*ardhacandra prakāraṃ ca vajrākāraṃ ca kārayet \|\| 13 \|\|*

8-13. The castle should be surrounded by a ditch and ramparts. The buildings are to be in the centre. It should have abundance of weapons, e. g., Shataghni and others. Its doors should be beautifully made.

Its main entrance should be handsome and big enough to enable the king to pass through it riding on an elephant with his banner streaming.

Four roads should be laid out to form squares. There should be a temple in front of one road, the king’s mansions in front of the second road. Facing the third one should be the houses of judicial and military and the gateway of the city should be in front of the fourth. In such, a way a royal city should be laid out no matter if it is oblong, square or circular. Circular one is the best or it may be triangular or drum-shaped, or semi-circular or of other suitable shapes (in the form of military array, diamond-shaped, etc.).

## \|\| 217.14-16 \|\|

*ardhacandraṃ praśaṃsanti nadītīreṣu tadvasan \|*  
*anyatra tanna kartavyaṃ prayatnena vijānatā \|\| 14 \|\|*

*rājñā kośagṛhaṃ kāryaṃ dakṣiṇe rājaveśmanaḥ \|*  
*tasyāpi dakṣiṇe bhāge gajasthānaṃ vidhīyate \|\| 15 \|\|*

*gajānāṃ prāṅmukhī śālā kartavyā vā'pyudaṅmukhī \|*  
*āgneye ca tathā bhāge āyudhāgāramiṣyate \|\| 16 \|\|*

14-16. The palace on the banks of a river should be of the shape of a crescent; this is the best. Treasure should be kept in the southern portion of the palace, to the further south of which should be the place for the elephants. The elephantyard should have its doorway to the east or the north. The arsenal should be made south-east.

## \|\| 217.17-18 \|\|

*mahānasaṃ ca dharmajña karmaśālāstathā parāḥ \|*  
*gṛhaṃ purodhasaḥ kāryaṃ vāmato rājaveśmanaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*mantrivedavidāṃ caiva cikitsākartureva ca \|*  
*tatraiva ca tathā bhāge koṣṭhāgāraṃ vidhīyate \|\| 18 \|\|*

17-18. In the same direction should be the kitchen and houses for other works. The house of the royal priest should be to the left of the king’s mansion where should also be the places for ministers, Vedic professors and students, physicians, stables and cow-sheds and store-houses. The stables should face the north, or the south. It is not well if it faces any other direction.

## \|\| 217.21-26 \|\|

*kukkuṭānvānarāṃścaiva markaṭāṃśca viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*dhārayedaśvaśālāsu savatsāṃ dhenumeva ca \|\| 21 \|\|*

*ajāśca dhāryā yatnena turagāṇāṃ hitaiṣiṇā \|*  
*gogajāśvādiśālāsu tatpurīṣasya nirgamaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*astaṃ gate na kartavyo devadeve divākare \|*  
*tatra tatra yathāsthānaṃ rājā vijñāya sārathīn \|\| 23 \|\|*

*dadyādāvasathasthānaṃ sarveṣāmanupūrvaśaḥ \|*  
*yodhānāṃ śilpināṃ caiva sarveṣāmaviśeṣataḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*dadyādāvasathāndurge kālamantravidāṃ śubhān \|*  
*govaidyānaśvavaidyāṃśca gajavaidyāṃstathaiva ca \|\| 25 \|\|*

*āhareta bhṛśaṃ rājā durge hi prabalā rujaḥ \|*  
*kuśīlavānāṃ viprāṇāṃ durge sthānaṃ vidhīyate \|\| 26 \|\|*

21-26. All night there are to be lamps burning in the stables. The horses should stay there. Cocks, monkeys, she-goats and cows with calves should be kept near the stables. She-goats should also be kept for the benefit of the horses. Dung should always be cleared away from the stables, elephant and cow yards before sunset. The quarters for the grooms and elephant drivers and charioteers should be near the stables and the elephant yard. Besides them, soldiers, artisans,' those versed in formulas, veterinary doctors (about horses and elephants, etc.), guests should also be best accommodated within the fortress. For diseases are likely to prevail much in the fortress. Brahmanas and Charanas should also be accommodated.

## \|\| 217.29-34 \|\|

*saṃcayaścātra sarveṣāmāyudhānāṃ praśasyate \|*  
*dhanuṣāṃ kṣepaṇīyānāṃ tomarāṇāṃ ca pārthiva \|\| 29 \|\|*

*śarāṇāmatha khaḍgānāṃ kavacānāṃ tathaiva ca \|*  
*laguḍānāṃ guḍānāṃ ca huḍānāṃ parighaiḥ saha \|\| 30 \|\|*

*aśmanāṃ ca prabhūtānāṃ mudgarāṇāṃ tathaiva ca \|*  
*triśūlānāṃ paṭṭiśānāṃ kuṭhārāṇāṃ ca pārthiva \|\| 31 \|\|*

*prāsānāṃ ca saśūlānāṃ śaktīnāṃ ca narottama \|*  
*paraśvadhānāṃ cakrāṇāṃ varmaṇāṃ carmabhiḥ saha \|\| 32 \|\|*

*kuddālarajжuvetrāṇāṃ pīṭhakānāṃ tathaiva ca \|*  
*tuṣāṇāṃ caiva dātrāṇāmaṅgārāṇāṃ ca saṃcayaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

*sarveṣāṃ śilpibhāṇḍānāṃ saṃcayaścātra ceṣyate \|*  
*vāditrāṇāṃ ca sarveṣāmoṣadhīnāṃ tathaiva ca \|\| 34 \|\|*

29-34. A large number of people should not be allowed to enter the fortress. There should be various kinds of cannon and weapons in the fort as well as those who can use them, for weapons that can destroy thousands of people protect the king. There are to remain warriors also close by. Besides all these things there should be secret doors as well as other doors within the fort protected by those who killed thousand warriors or are skilled in shooting bows and arrows and throwing various other weapons. A number of bows, clubs, spears, arrows, swords, sticks, maces, big pieces of stones, tridents, battle-axes, quoits, etc., should always be kept ready within the fortress. Shields, skins, pharoas, ropes, canes, various things of artisanship, husks, loads of straw, wood, coals, etc., should also be kept. The tools of all the artisans, musical instruments, various kinds of medicines, drums, weapons, various clothing’s, gems, iron, etc., should also be kept ready.

## \|\| 217.35-39 \|\|

*yavasānāṃ prabhūtānāmindhanasya ca saṃcayaḥ \|*  
*guḍasya sarvatailānāṃ gorasānāṃ tathaiva ca \|\| 35 \|\|*

*vasānāmatha majжānāṃ snāyūnāmasthibhiḥ saha \|*  
*gocarmapaṭahānāṃ ca dhānyānāṃ sarvatastathā \|\| 36 \|\|*

*tathaivābhrapaṭānāṃ ca yavagodhūmayorapi \|*  
*ratnānāṃ sarvavastrāṇāṃ lohānāmapyaśeṣataḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

*kalāyamudgamāṣāṇāṃ caṇakānāṃ tilaiḥ saha \|*  
*tathā ca sarvasasyānāṃ pāṃsugomayayorapi \|\| 38 \|\|*

*śaṇasarjarasaṃ bhūrjaṃ jatu lākṣā ca ṭaṅkaṇam \|*  
*rājā saṃcinuyāddurge yaccānyadapi kiṃcana \|\| 39 \|\|*

35-39. A good quantity of grass, firewood, molasses, oils, milk, fat, sinews, cowhides, hides for drums, all kinds of grains, silk cloths, barley, wheat, jewels, other kinds of cloths, all kinds of irons, all kinds of pulses such as Moth, Munga and Urada, gram, sesamum, cowdung, grain-dust, hemp, resinous exudation of Sala-tree, bark of the birch-tree, wax, borax, etc., should also be kept in stock in abundance.

## \|\| 217.40-41 \|\|

*kubhāścā’śīviṣaiḥ kāryā vyālasiṃhādayastathā \|*  
*mṛgāśca pakṣiṇaścaiva rakṣyāste ca parasparam \|\| 40 \|\|*

*sthānāni ca viruddhānāṃ suguptāni pṛthakpṛthak \|*  
*kartavyāṇi mahābhāga yatnena pṛthivīkṣitā \|\| 41 \|\|*

40-41. Poisons of snakes should be kept locked up in jars and similarly lions, deer, birds, etc., should also be kept confined separately. Animals unfriendly to each, other should be carefully kept in secret spots, and apart from each other.

## \|\| 217.42-54 \|\|

*uktāni cāpyanuktāni rājadra vyāṇyaśeṣataḥ \|*  
*suguptāni pure kuryājжanānāṃ hitakāmyayā \|\| 42 \|\|*

*jīvakarṣabhakākolamāmalakyāṭarūṣakān \|*  
*śālaparṇī pṛśniparṇī mudgaparṇī tathaiva ca \|\| 43 \|\|*

*māṣaparṇī ca mede dve śārive dve balātrayam \|*  
*vīrā śvasantī vṛṣyā ca bṛhatī kaṇṭakārikā \|\| 44 \|\|*

*śṛṅgī śṛṅgāṭakī dro ṇī varṣābhūrdarbhareṇukā \|*  
*madhuparṇī vidārye dve mahākṣīrā mahātapāḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

*dhanvanaḥ sahadevāhvā kaṭukairaṇḍakaṃ viṣaḥ \|*  
*parṇī śatāhvā mṛdvīkā phalgukharjūrayaṣṭikāḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

*śukrātiśukrakāśmaryaśchatrāticchatravīraṇāḥ \|*  
*ikṣurikṣuvikārāśca phāṇitādyāśca sattama \|\| 47 \|\|*

*siṃhī ca sahadevī ca viśvedevāśvarodhakam \|*  
*madhukaṃ puṣpahaṃsākhyā śatapuṣpā madhūlikā \|\| 48 \|\|*

*śatāvarīmadhūke ca pippalaṃ tālameva ca \|*  
*ātmaguptā kaṭphalākhyā dārvikā rājaśīrṣakī \|\| 49 \|\|*

*rājasarṣapadhānyākamṛṣyaproktā tathotkaṭā \|*  
*kālaśākaṃ padmabījaṃ govallī madhuvallikā \|\| 50 \|\|*

*śītapākī kuliṅgākṣī kākajihvorupuṣpikā \|*  
*parvatatrapusau cobhau guñjātakapunarnave \|\| 51 \|\|*

*kaserukā tu kāśmīrī bilvaśālūkakesaram \|*  
*śūkadhānyāni sarvāṇi śamīdhānyāni caiva hi \|\| 52 \|\|*

*kṣīraṃ kṣaudraṃ tathā takraṃ tailaṃ majжā vasāghṛtam \|*  
*nīpaścāriṣṭakakṣoḍavātāmāsomabāṇakam \|\| 53 \|\|*

*evamādīni cānyāni vijñeyo madhuro gaṇaḥ \|*  
*rājā saṃcinuyātsarvaṃ pure niravaśeṣataḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

42-54. Besides these things a king wishing the well-being of all should also keep in stock well-preserved all the various articles of the state. The following medicinal plants and articles of purest quality should also be kept, viz. — Jivaka, Rishabhaka, Kakoli, Amalaki, Vasaka, Salaparni, Prishniparni, Mudgaparni, Masaparni, Sharivadvaya, Valatraya, Vara, Shasanti, Vrisya, Vrihati, Kantakari, Shringi, Shringataki, Droni, Varsha, Darbha, Renuka, Madhuparni, Vidaridvaya, Mahakshira, Mahatapa, Dhanvana, Sahadeva, Katuka, Eranda, Visha, Parni, Sataha, Mridvika, Phalgu, Kharjura, Yashtimadhu, Shukra, Atishaka, Kashmorya, Chhatra, Atichhatra, Virana, Ikshu, Ikushvikara, Phanitadi, Simhi, Sahadevi, Madhuka, Pushpahamsa Satapushpa, Madhuloka, Satavari, Madhuka, Ashvattha, Tala, Atmagupta, Katphala, Darvika, Rajashirshaki, Rajasharshapa, Dhanyaka, Rishyaprokta, Utkata, Kalashaka, Padmavija, Govalli, Madhuvalli, Shitapaki, Kalingakshi, Kakajihva, Urupushpika, Parvata, Trapusa, Guiya, Punarbhava, Kaseruka, Kashmiri, Villa, Saluka, Nagakesara, all sorts of husks, grains, Samidhanya, milk, honey, curds, oils, fat and marrow, Vasa, ghee, Nipa, Arishtaka, Akshota, Vatamra, Soma, Vanaka, etc.

## \|\| 217.55-59 \|\|

*dāḍimāmrātakau caiva tintiḍīkāmlavetasam \|*  
*bhavyakarkandhulakucakaramardakarūṣakam \|\| 55 \|\|*

*bījapūrakakaṇḍūre mālatī rājabandhukam \|*  
*kolakadvayaparṇāni dvayorāmrātayorapi \|\| 56 \|\|*

*pārāvataṃ nāgarakaṃ prācīnārukameva ca \|*  
*kapitthāmalakaṃ cukraphalaṃ dantaśaṭhasya ca \|\| 57 \|\|*

*jāmbavaṃ navanītaṃ ca sauvīrakaruṣodake \|*  
*surāsavaṃ ca madyāni maṇḍatakradadhīni ca \|\| 58 \|\|*

*śuklāni caiva sarvāṇi jñeyamāmlagaṇaṃ dvija \|*  
*evamādīni cānyāni rājā saṃcinuyātpure \|\| 59 \|\|*

55-59. The following things should also be stocked in a king's castle, viz. — Pomegranates, Amrataka, tamarinds, lemons, cucumbers, breadfruits, Karamardaka, Rushaka, Vijapura, Kandura, Malati, Rajabandhuka, Kolakadvaya, all sorts of Parna, Amratadvaya, Parevata, Nagaraka, Prachinaruka, Kahittha, Amalaka, Chukraphala, Dantashatha, Jambu, Navanita, Sanviraka, Rushodaka, all sorts of wines, Manda, Takra, curd and all sorts of white things, and other sour things.

## \|\| 217.60-61 \|\|

*saindhavodbhidapāṭheyapākyasāmudra lomakam \|*  
*kupyasauvarcalābilvaṃ bālakeyaṃ yavāhvakam \|\| 60 \|\|*

*aurvaṃ kṣāraṃ kālabhasma vijñeyo lavaṇo gaṇaḥ \|*  
*evamādīni cānyāni rājā saṃcinuyātpure \|\| 61 \|\|*

60-61. The following things should also be kept: — all the various kinds of salts, viz. — Saindhava, Sambhara, sea salt, salt made out of well water, Kshara, Maniyari, black salt, red salt, Sanvarchala, Udvida, Valaklya, Yavakhya, Aurva, Kshara, Kalabhasma.

## \|\| 217.62-67 \|\|

*pippalī pippalīmūlacavyacitrakanāgaram \|*  
*kuberakaṃ ca marikaṃ śigrubhallātasarṣapāḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

*kuṣṭhājamodā kiṇihī hiṅgumūlakadhānyakam \|*  
*kāravī kuñcikā yājyā sumukhā kālamālikā \|\| 63 \|\|*

*phaṇijжhako'tha laśunaṃ bhūstṛṇaṃ surasaṃ tathā \|*  
*kāyasthā ca vayaḥsthā ca haritālaṃ manaḥśilā \|\| 64 \|\|*

*amṛtā ca rudantī ca rohiṣaṃ kuṅkumaṃ tathā \|*  
*jayā eraṇḍakāṇḍīraṃ śallakī hañjikā tathā \|\| 65 \|\|*

*sarvapittāni mūtrāṇi prāyo haritakāni ca \|*  
*saṃgatāni ca mūlāni yaṭiścātiviṣāṇi ca \|*  
*phalāni caiva hi tathā sūkṣmailā hiṅgupatrikā \|\| 66 \|\|*

*evamādīni cānyāni gaṇaḥ kaṭukasaṃjñitaḥ \|*  
*rājā saṃcinuyāddurge prayatnena nṛpottama \|\| 67 \|\|*

62-67. The following pungent things should also be kept: — sacred figs and the root of sacred fig-tree, Pippali, Pippalimula, Chavya, Chitraka, Nagara, Kuvera, black pepper, Sigru, marking-nuts, mustard, Kushtha, Ligisticum, Ajowan, asaphoteda, Mulaka, Dhanyaka, Karavi, bamboo shoots Yajya, Susukha, Kalamalika, Fanijhak, garlic, Bhustrina, Surasa, Kayastha, Vayastha, Haritala, Manahshila, Amrita, Rudanti, Rohisha, Kankuma, Jaya, Eranda, Kandira, Shallaki, Hanjika, all, sorts of Pitta and Mutra, Haritaka, various other fruits, Sukmalia, Hingupatrika, and other T pungent things.

## \|\| 217.68-74 \|\|

*mustaṃ candanahrīberakṛtamālakadāravaḥ \|*  
*haridrā naladośīranaktamālakadambakam \|\| 68 \|\|*

*dūrvā paṭolakaṭukā dantītvakpatrakaṃ tvacā \|*  
*kirātatiktabhūtumbī viṣā cātiviṣā tathā \|\| 69 \|\|*

*tālīsapatratagaraṃ saptaparṇavikaṅkatāḥ \|*  
*kākodumbarikā divyāstathā caiva surodbhavā \|\| 70 \|\|*

*ṣaḍgranthā rohiṇī māṃsī parpaṭaścātha dantikā \|*  
*rasāñjanaṃ bhṛṅgarājaṃ pataṅgī paripelavam \|\| 71 \|\|*

*duḥsparśā guruṇī kāmā śyāmākaṃ gandhanākulī \|*  
*tuṣaparṇī vyāghranakhaṃ mañjiṣṭhā caturaṅgulā \|\| 72 \|\|*

*rambhā caivāṅkurāsphotā tālāsphotā hareṇukā \|*  
*vetrāgravetasastumbī viṣāṇī lodhrapuṣpiṇī \|\| 73 \|\|*

*mālatīkarakṛṣṇākhyā vṛścikā jīvitā tathā \|*  
*parṇikā ca guḍūcī ca sa gaṇastiktasaṃjñakaḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

68-74. The king should collect the following things in his own city: — Musta, Chandana, Hrivera, Kritamaluka, Daruharidra, Haridra, Nalada, Ushira, Naktamala, Kadambaka; Durva, Patali, Katuka, Gantt, Tvakpatri, Vacha, Chireta, Bhutumbo, Visa, Ativisa, Talishapatra, Tagara, Saptaparna, Vikankata, Kukodumbarika, Divya, Surodbhava, Sadgrantha, Rohini, Jatamanasi, Parpata, Danti, Rasanyana, Bhringaraja, Patangi, Paripelava, Dusparsha, Ajumdvaya, Kama, Syamaka, Gandhanakuli, Rupaparni, Vyaghranakha, Manjishtha, Chaturangula, Rambha, Ankara, Asphota, Talasphota, Harenuka, Vetragra, Vetasa, Tumbi, Vishani, Lodhrapushpini, Malati, Karakrishna, Vrishchika, Jivita, Parnika, Gudchi.

## \|\| 217.75-84 \|\|

*evamādīni cānyāni rājā saṃcinuyātpure \|*  
*abhayāmalake cobhe tathaiva ca bibhītakam \|\| 75 \|\|*

*priyaṅgudhātakīpuṣpaṃ mocākhyā cārjunāsanāḥ \|*  
*anantā strī tuvarikā śyoṇākaṃ kaṭphalaṃ tathā \|\| 76 \|\|*

*bhūrjapatraṃ śilāpatraṃ pāṭalāpatralomakam \|*  
*samaṅgātrivṛtāmūlakārpāsagairikāñjanam \|\| 77 \|\|*

*vidrumaṃ samadhūcchiṣṭaṃ kumbhikā kumudotpalam \|*  
*nyagrodhodumbarāśvatthakiṃśukāḥ śiṃśapā śamī \|\| 78 \|\|*

*priyālapīlukāsārīśirīṣāḥ padmakaṃ tathā \|*  
*bilvo'gnimanyaḥ plakṣaśca śyāmākaṃ ca bako ghanam \|\| 79 \|\|*

*rājādanaṃ karīraṃ ca dhānyakaṃ priyakastathā \|*  
*kaṅkolāśokabadarāḥ kadambakhadiradvayam \|\| 80 \|\|*

*eṣāṃ patrāṇi sārāṇi mūlāni kusumāni ca \|*  
*evamādīni cānyāni kaṣāyākhyo gaṇo mataḥ \|\| 81 \|\|*

*prayatnena nṛpaśreṣṭha rājā saṃcinuyātpure \|*  
*kīṭāśca māraṇe yogyā vyaṅgatāyāṃ tathaiva ca \|\| 82 \|\|*

*tātadhūmāmbumārgāṇāṃ dūṣaṇāni tathaiva ca \|*  
*dhāryāṇi pārthivairdurge tāni vakṣyāmi pārthiva \|\| 83 \|\|*

*viṣāṇāṃ dhāraṇaṃ kāryaṃ prayatnena mahībhujā \|*  
*vicitrāścāgadā dhāryā viṣasya śamanāstathā \|\| 84 \|\|*

75-84. The following things should also be kept: — Haritaki, Amalaki, Bhumyamalaki, Vibhitaka, Priyangu, Dhatakipushpa, Mocha, Arjuna, Asana, Ananta, Kamini, Tuvarika, Syonaka, Katphala, Bhurjapatra, Shilapatra, Patalapatra, Lomaka, Samanga, Trivrita, Mula, Karpasa, Gairika, Anjana, Vidruma, Madhuchhishta, Kandika, Kumuda, Utpala, Nyagrodha, Udumbara, Asvattha, Kinsuka, Sinasapa, Sami, Priyala, Pilu, Kasari, Sirisha, Padmaka, Vilva, Agnimantha, Plaksha, Syamaka, Vaka, Ghana, Rajadana, Karira, Dhanyaka, Priyaka, Karankala, Ashoka, Vadara, Kadamba, Khadiradvaya, the leaves, essence (resin), roots and flowers of all these. The king is to collect all sorts of poisons very carefully. Also he should collect various things of wonderful variegated properties that can destroy poisons, also that can destroy angadas, Rakshasas and Bhutas and Pishachas, that can destroy sins and prevent draught. The bacilli, the poisonous gases and fumes and similar destructive things should also be preserved by a king for the destruction of his enemies.

## \|\| 217.85-87 \|\|

*rakṣobhūtapiśācaghnāḥ pāpaghnāḥ puṣṭivardhanāḥ \|*  
*kalāvidaśca puruṣāḥ pure dhāryāḥ prayatnataḥ \|\| 85 \|\|*

*bhītānpramattānkupitāṃstathaiva ca vimānitān \|*  
*kubhṛtyānpāpaśīlāṃśca na rājā vāsayetpure \|\| 86 \|\|*

*yantrāyudhāṭṭālacayopapannaṃ samagradhānyauṣadhisaṃprayuktam \|*  
*vaṇigjanaiścā’vṛtamāvaseta durgaṃ suṣuptaṃ nṛpatiḥ sadaiva \|\| 87 \|\|*

85-87. The king should also keep within his fort people versed in dancing and music and versed also in the Kalashastras (various arts). He should not allow the timid, the infatuated, the intoxicated, those addicted to drugs, the angry dispositioned, the disgraced ones, the sinful and bad persons to remain in his stronghold. The monarch should always remain in a well-guarded citadel protected by charms, warriors, balconies, and well supplied with all kinds of grains and medicines and inhabited by the merchant classes.

## Chapter 218

## \|\| 218.1 \|\|

*manuruvāca*  
*rakṣoghnāni viṣaghnāni yāni dhāryāṇi bhūbhujā \|*  
*agadāni samācakṣva tāni dharmabhṛtāṃ vara \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Manu said: — Pray tell me, O Lord! the medicines that destroy the demons and dispel the effect of poisons and that ought to be kept in a king’s fort.

## \|\| 218.2-5 \|\|

*matsya uvāca*  
*bilvāṭakī yavakṣāraṃ pāṭalā bāhlikoṣaṇā \|*  
*śrīparṇī śallakīyukto nikvāthaḥ prokṣaṇaṃ param \|\| 2 \|\|*

*saviṣaṃ prokṣitaṃ tena sadyo bhavati nirviṣam \|*  
*yavasaindhavapānīyavastraśayyāsanodakam \|\| 3 \|\|*

*kavacābharaṇaṃ chatraṃ vālavyajanaveśmanām \|*  
*śeluḥ pāṭalyativiṣā śigru mūrvā punarnavā \|\| 4 \|\|*

*samaṅgā vṛṣamūlaṃ ca kapitthavṛṣaśoṣitam \|*  
*mahādantaśaṭhaṃ tadvatprokṣaṇaṃ viṣanāśanam \|\| 5 \|\|*

2-5. Matsya said: — The decoction of the following things dispels the poison, viz., Vilva, Ataki, Yavakshara, Panchaki, Vahlika, Ushana, Shriparni and Shallaki. By drinking and sprinkling the poisoned yava, salt, drinking water, bedding, clothes, seat, water, armor, ornaments, umbrella, chamara and fans with the decoction of the above materials, the effect of poison disappears. The decoctions of the following materials also readily drive away poisonous effects, viz. — Shelu, Patala, Ativisha, Shigru, Murva, Punamava, Samanga, Vrishamula, Kapittha, Vrishshronita, Mahadamta, Satha.

## \|\| 218.6-10 \|\|

*lākṣāpriyaṅgumañjiṣṭhā samamelā hareṇukā \|*  
*yaṣṭyāhvā madhurā caiva babhrupittena kalpitāḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*nikhanedgoviṣāṇasthaṃ saptarātraṃ mahītale \|*  
*tataḥ kṛtvā maṇiṃ hemnā baddhaṃ hastena dhārayet \|\| 7 \|\|*

*saṃsṛṣṭaṃ saviṣaṃ tena sadyo bhavati nirviṣam \|*  
*manohvayā śamīpatraṃ tumbikā śvetasarṣapāḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*kapitthakuṣṭhamañjiṣṭhāḥ pittena ślakṣṇakalpitāḥ \|*  
*śuno goḥ kapilāyāśca saumyākṣipto'paro gadaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*viṣajitparamaṃ kāryaṃ maṇiratnaṃ ca pūrvavat \|*  
*mūṣikā jatukā cāpi haste baddhvā viṣāpahā \|\| 10 \|\|*

6-10. Laksha, Priyangu, (long pepper, saffron or a particular kind of creeper 'said to blossom at the touch of women) Ela, Renuka, Yashtimadhu, Madhura, should be mixed with Nakulapitta and buried into the earth for seven nights in a vessel made of horn. Then it should be placed in a golden pendant studded with precious stones which should be used on the hand. It will dispel the poison from everything it touches.

Manahvya, Shamipattra, Tumvika, the white mustard, wood-apple, Kuda, Manjishtha, should be well-powdered and mixed with the bile of a dog and a Kapila cow. This great medicine prevents the effects of poisons. Besides these, there are various gems and pearls, Mushika and Jatuka which ought to be held in the arm. They also prevent the effects of poisons.

## \|\| 218.11-12 \|\|

*hareṇumāṃsī mañjiṣṭhā rajanī madhukā madhu \|*  
*akṣatvaksurasaṃ lākṣā śvapittaṃ pūrvavadbhuvi \|\| 11 \|\|*

*vāditrāṇi patākāśca piṣṭairetaiḥ pralepitāḥ \|*  
*śrutvā dṛṣṭvā samāghrāya sadyo bhavati nirviṣaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-12. By mixing Renuka, Jatamansi, turmeric, Madhuka, honey, the bark of Aksha, Surasa, Laksha, and the bile of a dog into a paste and applying it over the drums, sounding instruments, and banners; by hearing the sound of such drums and by seeing and smelling such banners one is freed from the effects of a poison.

## \|\| 218.13-14 \|\|

*tr! yūṣaṇaṃ pañcalavaṇaṃ mañjiṣṭhā rajanīdvayam \|*  
*sūkṣmailā trivṛtāpatraṃ viḍaṅgānīndra vāruṇī \|\| 13 \|\|*

*madhukaṃ vetasaṃ kṣaudraṃ viṣāṇe ca nidhāpayet \|*  
*tasmāduṣṇāmbunā mātraṃ prāguktaṃ yojayettataḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*
