13-14. Tryushana, five kinds of salts, Manjishtha, both kinds of turmeric, cardamoms, Trivrita leaves, Vidamga, colocynth, Madhuka, cane, Kshandra, should be deposited in a horn and then they should be mixed and boiled in hot water when they will dispel all poisonous effects.

## \|\| 218.15-16 \|\|

*viṣabhuktaṃ jaraṃ yāti nirviṣaṃ pittadoṣakṛt \|*  
*śuklaṃ sarjarasopetaṃ sarṣapā elavālukaiḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*suvegā taskarasurau kusumairarjunasya tu \|*  
*dhūpo vāsagṛhe hanti viṣaṃ sthāvarajaṅgamam \|\| 16 \|\|*

15-16. The white resinous exudation mixed with mustard, Elavaluka, Suvega Taskara, Sura, and Arjuna flowers and powdered together and used as incense in the fire drive away the poisonous effects from everything moveable and immoveable in the household.

## \|\| 218.17 \|\|

*na tatra kīṭā na viṣaṃ dardurā na sarīsṛpāḥ \|*  
*na kṛtyā karmaṇāṃ cāpi dhūpo'yaṃ yatra dahyate \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Where the above-mentioned incense is burnt worms, lizards, frogs, poisonous and creeping animals, or Krityas cannot thrive.

## \|\| 218.18-22 \|\|

*kalpitaiścandanakṣīrapalāśadrumavalkalaiḥ \|*  
*mūrvailāvālusarasānākulītaṇḍulīyakaiḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*kvāthaḥ sarvodakāryeṣu kākamācīyuto hitaḥ \|*  
*rocanāpatranepālīkuṅkumaistilakānvahan \|\| 19 \|\|*

*viṣairna bādhyate'smācca naranārīnṛpapriyaḥ \|*  
*cūrṇairharidrā mañjiṣṭhākiṇihīkaṇanimbajaiḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*digdhaṃ nirviṣatāmeti gātraṃ sarvaviṣārditam \|*  
*śirīṣasya phalaṃ patraṃ puṣpaṃ tvaṅmūlameva ca \|\| 21 \|\|*

*gomūtraghṛṣṭo hyagadaḥ sarvakarmakaraḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*ekavīra mahauṣadhyaḥ śṛṇu cātaḥ paraṃ nṛpa \|\| 22 \|\|*

18-22. When the bark of Palasha is mixed with the exudation of sandal-tree, milk, Murva, the juice of Lavala, Nakuli, Tanduliyaka, and Kakamachi and a thin decoction is prepared, it prevents all sorts of poisons. Gorochanapatra Nepali, Kumkuma and Tilaka, if held in the arm, make one from all sorts of poisons and he becomes the favourite of kings.

Turmeric, Manjishtha, Kinihi, Pippali and Nimba well-grounded together and made into an ointment massaged all over the body take away all the effects of the most deadly poison from the body. The fruits, flowers, leaves, bark and root of the Shirisha-tree grounded in cow’s urine and rubbed over the body also takes off all poison. Now hear about the most mighty medicines, O King! viz.

## \|\| 218.23-35 \|\|

*vandhyā karkoṭakī rājanviṣṇukrāntā tathotkaṭā \|*  
*śatamūlī sitānandā balā mocā paṭolikā \|\| 23 \|\|*

*somā piṇḍā niśā caiva tathā dagdharuhā ca yā \|*  
*sthale kamalinī yā ca viśālī śaṅkhamūlikā \|\| 24 \|\|*

*cāṇḍālī hastimagadhā go'jāparṇī karambhikā \|*  
*raktā caiva mahāraktā tathā barhiśikhā ca yā \|\| 25 \|\|*

*kośātakī naktamālaṃ priyālaṃ ca sulocanī \|*  
*vāruṇī vasugandhā ca tathā vai gandhanākulī \|\| 26 \|\|*

*īśvarī śivagandhā ca śyāmalā vaṃśanālikā \|*  
*jatukālī mahāśvetā śvetā ca madhuyaṣṭikā \|\| 27 \|\|*

*vajrakaḥ pāribhadra śca tathā vai sindhuvārakāḥ \|*  
*jīvānandā vasucchidrā natanāgarakaṇṭakā \|\| 28 \|\|*

*nālaṃ ca jālī jātī ca tathā ca vaṭapatrikā \|*  
*kārtasvaraṃ mahānīlā kundururhaṃsapādikā \|\| 29 \|\|*

*maṇḍūkaparṇī vārāhī dve tathā taṇḍulīyake \|*  
*sarpākṣī lavalī brāhmī viśvarūpā sukhākarā \|\| 30 \|\|*

*rujāpahā vṛddhikarī tathā caiva tu śalyadā \|*  
*patrikā rohiṇī caiva raktamālā mahauṣadhī \|\| 31 \|\|*

*tathā’malakavandākaṃ śyāmacitraphalā ca yā \|*  
*kākolī kṣīrakākolī pīluparṇī tathaiva ca \|\| 32 \|\|*

*keśinī vṛścikālī ca mahānāgā śatāvarī \|*  
*garuḍī ca tathā vegā jale kumudinī tathā \|\| 33 \|\|*

*sthale cotpalinī yā ca mahābhūmilatā ca yā \|*  
*unmādinī somarājī sarvaratnāni pārthiva \|\| 34 \|\|*

*viśikhā'marakanyā ca kīṭapakṣaṃ viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*jīvajātāśca maṇayaḥ sarve dhāryāḥ prayatnataḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

23-35. Bandhya, Karkotaki, Vishnukramta, Utkata, Shatamuli, Sita, Anamda, Vala, Mocha, Patolika, Soma, Panda, turmeric, Dagdharuha, Sthala-Kamala, Vishali, Shamkhamulika, Chamdali, Hastimagadha, Gojaparna, Karambhika, Rakta, Maharakta, Varhisikha, Ajaparni, Koshataki, Naktamala, Priyalama, Sulochani, Varuni, Vasugamdha, Gandha, Nakuli, Ishvari, Shivagamdha, Shyamala, Vamshanalika, Jatukali, Mahashveta, Shveta, Madhuyashtika, Vajraka, Paribhadra, Sindhuvaraka, Paribhadra, Jivanamda, Vasuharidra, Natanagara, Kamtakari, Nila, Jali, Jati, banyan leaves, Suvarna, Mahanila, Kunduru, Hansapadi, Mamdukaparni, Varahi, Sarpakshi, Lavali, Brahmi, Vishvarupa, Sukhakara, Rujapaha, Vridhikari, Shalyada, Rohini Patrika, Raktamala, Amalaka, Vamdaka, Shyama, Chitraphala, Kakoli, Kshira-Kakoli, Piluparni, Keshini, Vrishchikali, Mahanaga, Shatavari, Garudi, Vega, water lotus, land lotus, Mahabhumi creeper, Unmadini, Somaraji, and all kinds of jewels especially Marakatamani and other gems obtained from various creatures should be carefully preserved by a sovereign for the prevention of bad influences from Rakshasas, poisons, and Krityas.

## \|\| 218.36-38 \|\|

*rakṣoghnāśca viṣaghnāśca kṛtyā vaitālanāśanāḥ \|*  
*viśeṣānnaranāgāśca gokharoṣṭrasamudbhavāḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

*sarpatittiragomāyubabhrumaṇḍukajāśca ye \|*  
*siṃhavyāghrarkṣamārjāradvīpivānarasaṃbhavāḥ \|*  
*kapiñjalā gajā vājimahiṣaiṇabhavāśca ye \|\| 37 \|\|*

*ityevametaiḥ sakalairupetairdra vyaiḥ parārghyaiḥ parirakṣitaḥ syāt \|*  
*rājā vasettatra gṛhe suśubhre guṇānvite lakṣaṇasaṃprayukte \|\| 38 \|\|*

36-38. The various things obtained from men, elephants, serpents, cows, donkeys, camels, partridges, jackals, lions, bears tigers, cats, rhinoceros, monkeys, pigeons, horses, buffalos, deer should be most carefully preserved by the king, A sovereign should have his residence full of such things when he should build a most beautiful mansion for himself.

## Chapter 219

## \|\| 219.1 \|\|

*manuruvāca*  
*rājarakṣārahasyāni yāni durge nidhāpayet \|*  
*kārayedvā mahībhartā brūhi tattvāni tāni me \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Manu said: — Lord! pray tell me what other things are to be kept by a sovereign in his fort for his safety. Kindly reveal to us the secrets.

## \|\| 219.2 \|\|

*matsya uvāca*  
*śirīṣodumbaraśamībījapūraṃ ghṛtaplutam \|*  
*kṣudyogaḥ kathito rājanmāsārdhasya purātanaiḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Matsya said: The fruits of Shrisha, figs, Shami and Vijapura should be prepared in clarified butter and taken at an interval of fifteen days which is known as Kshudyoga.

**Комментарий:**

Note: ... Device of keeping hunger satisfied.

## \|\| 219.3-11 \|\|

*kaśeruphalamūlāni ikṣumūlaṃ tathā viṣam \|*  
*dūrvākṣīraghṛtairmaṇḍaḥ siddho'yaṃ māsikaḥ paraḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*naraṃ śastrahataṃ prāpto na tasya maraṇaṃ bhavet \|*  
*kalmāṣaveṇunā tatra janayettu vibhāvasum \|\| 4 \|\|*

*gṛhe trirapasavyaṃ tu kriyate yatra pārthiva \|*  
*nānyo'gnirjvalate tatra nātra kāryā vicāraṇā \|\| 5 \|\|*

*kārpāsāsthni bhujaṅgasya tena nirmocanaṃ bhavet \|*  
*sarpanirvāsane dhūpaḥ praśastaḥ satataṃ gṛhe \|\| 6 \|\|*

*sāmudra saindhavayavā vidyuddagdhā ca mṛttikā \|*  
*tayā'nuliptaṃ yadveśma nāgninā dahyate nṛpa \|\| 7 \|\|*

*divā ca durge rakṣyo'gnirvāti vāte viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*viṣācca rakṣyo nṛpatistatra yuktiṃ nibodha me \|\| 8 \|\|*

*krīḍānimittaṃ nṛpatirdhārayenmṛgapakṣiṇaḥ \|*  
*annaṃ vai prākparīkṣeta vahnau cānyatareṣu ca \|\| 9 \|\|*

*vastraṃ puṣpamalaṃkāraṃ bhojanācchādanaṃ tathā \|*  
*nāparīkṣitapūrvaṃ tu spṛśedapi mahīpatiḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*syāccāsau vaktrasaṃtaptaḥ sodvegaṃ ca nirīkṣate \|*  
*viṣado'tha viṣaṃ dattaṃ yacca tatra parīkṣate \|\| 11 \|\|*

3-11. Kasheru, its fruits and roots, Ikshumula, Bisa, Durva, should be cooked either in milk or clarified butter and made into a ball and eaten at an interval of a month. By using these medicines a man regains his life if wounded by weapons. The place where black bamboos are burnt, and circumambulation is made thrice towards the right is, no doubt, immune from other fire. By burning a snake’s sheath in the cotton fire and using it as incense, all the serpents of the household fly away. By washing the house with sea salt, Sambhara salt, barley water mixed with the earth of the place struck by lightning, the place becomes absolutely fireproof. Fire should well be placed in a fortress in course of the day when a strong wind blows. Now the means of protecting a sovereign from poisons will be described. A sovereign should keep a number of birds and deer. First of all the cooked food should be tested by fire or some other method. A sovereign should never touch his food, clothes, flowers, ornaments without testing them. The person who administers poison in king's food, etc., turns pale and very much confused, and uneasy when examination is being made.

## \|\| 219.12-14 \|\|

*srastottarīyo vimanāḥ stambhakuḍyādibhistathā \|*  
*pracchādayati cā’tmānaṃ lajжate tvarate tathā \|\| 12 \|\|*

*bhuvaṃ vilikhati grīvāṃ tathā cālayate nṛpa \|*  
*kaṇḍūyati ca mūrdhānaṃ pariloḍyā’nanaṃ tathā \|\| 13 \|\|*

*kriyāsu tvarito rājanviparītāsvapi dhruvam \|*  
*evamādīni cihnāni viṣadasya parīkṣayet \|\| 14 \|\|*

12-14. His sight becomes restless; he becomes absent-minded; he will drop his upper cloth in confusion, will turn speechless like a wall, agitated, nervous and will try to conceal his person, scratch ^the floor, shake his head, rub his mouth and scratch his forehead and will be hasty, in everything where haste ought not to be done. The king should find out by these signs the men who administer poison.

## \|\| 219.15-17 \|\|

*samīpairvikṣipedvahnau tadannaṃ tvarayā'nvitaḥ \|*  
*indrā yudhasavarṇaṃ tu rūkṣaṃ sphoṭasamanvitam \|\| 15 \|\|*

*ekāvartaṃ tu durgandhi bhṛśaṃ caṭacaṭāyate \|*  
*taddhūmasevanājжantoḥ śirorogaśca jāyate \|\| 16 \|\|*

*saviṣe'nne vilīyante na ca pārthiva makṣikāḥ \|*  
*nilīnāśca vipadyante saṃspṛṣṭe saviṣe tathā \|\| 17 \|\|*

15-17. The food mixed with poison will exhibit rainbow colour, look rough, with bubbles give out bad smell, make an explosive noise and cause headache to a person by its fume; 'when put info the fire. A fly will not sit on it and if it does, it will instantly die.

## \|\| 219.18-23 \|\|

*virajyati cakorasya dṛṣṭiḥ pārthivasattama \|*  
*vikṛtiṃ ca svaro yāti kokilasya tathā nṛpa \|\| 18 \|\|*

*gatiḥ skhalati haṃsasya bhṛṅgarājaśca kūjati \|*  
*krauñco madamathābhyeti kṛkavākurvirauti ca \|\| 19 \|\|*

*vikrośati śuko rājansārikā vamate tataḥ \|*  
*cāmīkaro'nyato yāti mṛtyuṃ kāraṇḍavastathā \|\| 20 \|\|*

*mehate vānaro rājanglāyate jīvajīvakaḥ \|*  
*hṛṣṭaromā bhavedbabhruḥ pṛṣataścaiva roditi \|\| 21 \|\|*

*harṣamāyāti ca śikhī viṣasaṃdarśanānnṛpa \|*  
*annaṃ ca saviṣaṃ rājaṃścireṇa ca vipadyate \|\| 22 \|\|*

*tadā bhavati niḥśrāvyaṃ pakṣaparyuṣitopamam \|*  
*vyāpannarasagandhaṃ ca candri kābhistathā yutam \|\| 23 \|\|*

18-23. By seeing poisoned food the sight of Chikore becomes fixed and the cuckoo loses its melody, the crane moves abrupt; blackbees begin to buzz, Kraumcha becomes stupefied, cooks begin to cry, parrots shrill, the female parrots begin to vomit, Chamikar goes to another place, Karanda instantly dies, monkey begins to make water, Jivajivaka becomes morose, mongoose shoots up its hair, Prishata deer begins to cry, peacocks become pleased, the poisoned stuff in a somewhat long time becomes rancid like anything kept for a fortnight. It begins to stink and ooze. Then it becomes juiceless and scentless.

## \|\| 219.24 \|\|

*vyañjanānāṃ tu śuṣkatvaṃ dra vāṇāṃ budbudodbhavaḥ \|*  
*sasaindhavānāṃ dra vyāṇāṃ jāyate phenamālitā \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Saka when poisoned dries up and watery dishes begin to bubble and the stuff prepared with Saindhava salt begins to froth.

## \|\| 219.25-29 \|\|

*sasyarājiśca tāmrā syānnīlā ca payasastathā \|*  
*kokilābhā ca madyasya toyasya ca nṛpottama \|\| 25 \|\|*

*dhānyāmlasya tathā kṛṣṇā kapilā kodra vasya ca \|*  
*madhuśyāmā ca takrasya nīlā pītā tathaiva ca \|\| 26 \|\|*

*ghṛtasyodakasaṃkāśā kapotāmā ca mastunaḥ \|*  
*haritā mākṣikasyāpi tailasya ca tathā'ruṇā \|\| 27 \|\|*

*phalānāmapyapakvānāṃ pākaḥ kṣipraṃ prajāyate \|*  
*prakopaścaiva pakvānāṃ mālyānāṃ mlānatā tathā \|\| 28 \|\|*

*mṛdutā kaṭhinānāṃ syānmṛdūnāṃ ca viparyayaḥ \|*  
*sūkṣmāṇāṃ rūpadalanaṃ tathā caivātiraṅgatā \|\| 29 \|\|*

25-29. Poisoned grain becomes coppercoloured, milk turns blue, wine and water become of the colour of cuckoo, rice becomes blackish, Kodao turns brownish, and curds become blackish, bluish or yellowish, clarified butter becomes watery, and poisoned matter becomes of the colour of a pigeon, fly turns green, oil gets red, and raw fruits by coming in contact with poison become untimely ripe, ripe ones go stale, garlands get faded, hard fruits become soft, soft ones turn hard, small fruits become disfigured.

## \|\| 219.30 \|\|

*śyāmamaṇḍalatā caiva vastrāṇāṃ vai tathaiva ca \|*  
*lohānāṃ ca maṇīnāṃ ca malapaṅkopadigdhatā \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Poisoned clothes lose their flush and become covered with black circular spots and iron and gems turn pale.

## \|\| 219.31-32 \|\|

*anulepanagandhānāṃ mālyānāṃ ca nṛpottama \|*  
*vigandhatā ca vijñeyā varṇānāṃ mlānatā tathā \|*  
*pītāvabhāsatā jñeyā tathā rājañjalasya tu \|\| 31 \|\|*

*dantā oṣṭhau tvacaḥ śyāmāstanusattvāstathaiva ca \|*  
*evamādīni cihnāni vijñeyāni nṛpottama \|\| 32 \|\|*

31-32. Poisoned flowers and sandal give most disagreeable smell and the bark of the tooth stick becomes black and gets thin. These are the signs of poisoned stuff.

## \|\| 219.33 \|\|

*tasmādrā jā sadā tiṣṭhenmaṇimantrauṣadhāgadaiḥ \|*  
*uktaiḥ saṃrakṣito rājā pramādaparivarjakaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. A sovereign should therefore peacefully live in his fortress, always guarded by all the mantras, medicines, and jewels as mentioned heretofore.

## \|\| 219.34 \|\|

*prajātarormūlamihāvanīśastadra kṣaṇādrā ṣṭramupaiti vṛddhim \|*  
*tasmātprayatnena nṛpasya rakṣā sarveṇa kāryā ravivaṃśacandra \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. A sovereign is the source of well-being to his subjects; under the royal protection the whole country flourishes; everyone should therefore guard the king by all means.

## Chapter 220

## \|\| 220.1-7 \|\|

*matsya uvāca*  
*rājanputrasya rakṣā ca kartavyā pṛthivīkṣitā \|*  
*ācāryaścātra kartavyo nityayuktaśca rakṣibhiḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*dharmakāmārthaśāstrāṇi dhanurvedaṃ ca śikṣayet \|*  
*rathe ca kuñjare cainaṃ vyāyāmaṃ kārayetsadā \|\| 2 \|\|*

*śilpāni śikṣayeccainaṃ nā’ptairmithyāpriyaṃ vadet \|*  
*śarīrarakṣāvyājena rakṣiṇo'sya niyojayet \|\| 3 \|\|*

*na cāsya saṅgo dātavyaḥ kruddhalubdhāvamānitaiḥ \|*  
*tathā ca vinayedenaṃ yathā yauvanagocare \|\| 4 \|\|*

*indri yairnāpakṛṣyeta satāṃ mārgātsudurgamāt \|*  
*guṇādhānamaśakyaṃ tu yasya kartuṃ svabhāvataḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*bandhanaṃ tasya kartavyaṃ guptadeśe sukhānvitam \|*  
*avinītakumāraṃ hi kulamāśu viśīryate \|\| 6 \|\|*

*adhikāreṣu sarveṣu vinītaṃ viniyojayet \|*  
*ādau svalpe tataḥ paścātkrameṇātha mahatsvapi \|\| 7 \|\|*

1-7. Matsya said: — O King I a king should well-guard his own son. A number of trustworthy servants should be retained to guard and a faithful teacher as well to give him instruction. He should be grounded in Dharma, Kama, Artha, archery, the use of chariot, elephants and horses, and mechanical arts, and various other physical exercises. A prince lot be so very truthful, should speak sweet words according to y that need not be rigorously true. Such instruction should be given to him. Men should be employed to guard him under the pretext of g his person. A prince should not be allowed to mix with men of angry or avaricious disposition, nor with persons who had been insulted and looked down upon. His custodians should train him up so that he may be gentle and may not abandon the difficult path of virtue and be led away by passions during his youth. The prince who cannot be easily trained up in all such good qualities by good instructions should be well-guarded in a secret place where he should have all his comforts. A prince devoid of politics and humility soon perishes. Persons well-trained should be employed in different departments of State, First they should be given small offices and then their sphere of work should be gradually widened.

## \|\| 220.8-9 \|\|

*mṛgayāpānamakṣāṃśca varjayetpṛthivīpatiḥ \|*  
*etāṃstu sevamānāstu vinaṣṭāḥ pṛthivīkṣitaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*bahavo nṛpaśārdūla teṣāṃ saṃkhyā na vidyate \|*  
*vṛthāṭanaṃ divāsvapnaṃ viśeṣeṇa vivarjayet \|\| 9 \|\|*

8-9. They should be kept away from the vices of drinking, hunting expeditions and gambling, for many kings addicted to them have been mined and their number is legion, A sovereign should also not let the princes sleep in course of the day, nor should they be allowed to travel with no purpose in view,-

## \|\| 220.10 \|\|

*vākpāruṣyaṃ na kartavyaṃ daṇḍapāruṣyameva ca \|*  
*parokṣanindā ca tathā varjanīyā mahīkṣitā \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. A sovereign should not inflict severe punishment, nor should he me harsh words and speak ill of anyone at his back.

## \|\| 220.11 \|\|

*arthasya dūṣaṇaṃ rājā dviprakāraṃ vivarjayet \|*  
*arthānāṃ dūṣaṇaṃ caikaṃ tathā'rtheṣu ca dūṣaṇam \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. A sovereign should avoid the two evils arising out of wealth, viz., — the evils arising out of not being used properly and of being used improperly.

## \|\| 220.12-13 \|\|

*prākārāṇāṃ samucchedo durgādīnāmasatkriyā \|*  
*arthānāṃ dūṣaṇaṃ proktaṃ viprakīrṇatvameva ca \|\| 12 \|\|*

*adeśakāle yaddānamapātre dānameva ca \|*  
*artheṣu dūṣaṇaṃ proktamasatkarmapravartanam \|\| 13 \|\|*

12-13. Not to guard well the enclosure walls, not to repair the forts, not to collect wealth from various places, to give out wealth to unfit countries, and to unfit persons in improper times, are regarded as not using wealth properly; whereas to use wealth in vicious and bad works is regarded as using wealth improperly.

## \|\| 220.14-15 \|\|

*kāmaḥ krodho mado māno lobho harṣastathaiva ca \|*  
*ete varjyāḥ prayatnena sādaraṃ pṛthivīkṣitā \|\| 14 \|\|*

*eteṣāṃ vijayaṃ kṛtvā kāryo bhṛtyajayastataḥ \|*  
*kṛtvā bhṛtyajayaṃ rājā paurāñjānapadāñjayet \|\| 15 \|\|*

14-15. A sovereign should tactfully drive away lust, anger, pride, avarice and too much pleasure. After conquering them he should win his retainers and afterwards he should endear himself to his country and city and his subjects.

## \|\| 220.16 \|\|

*kṛtvā ca vijayaṃ teṣāṃ śatrūnbāhyāṃstato jayet \|*  
*bāhyāśca vividhā jñeyāstulyābhyantarakṛtrimāḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Then he should conquer the external foes. These outside enemies are of various classes according as they are equal to him or under his control or quite accidental and so artificial arising out' of needs; and they should be treated with greater or less caution as they belong to the former or latter class.

## \|\| 220.17-18 \|\|

*guravaste yathāpūrvaṃ teṣu yatnaparo bhavet \|*  
*pitṛpaitāmahaṃ mitramamitraṃ ca tathā ripoḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*kṛtrimaṃ ca mahābhāga mitraṃ trividhamucyate \|*  
*tathā'pi ca guruḥ pūrvaṃ bhavettatrāpi cā’dṛtaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

17-18. The friends are of three kinds: (1) as they are the friends of the father and the grandfather, (2) the enemy’s enemy, and (3) an acquired friend arising out of necessity. Among them the previous kinds of friends are' superior.

## \|\| 220.19 \|\|

*svāmyamātyo janapado durgaṃ daṇḍastathaiva ca \|*  
*kośo mitraṃ ca dharmajña saptāṅgaṃ rājyamucyate \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. (1) King, (2) ministers, (3) country and subjects, (4) fort, (5) penal laws, (6) treasure, and (7) friends are the seven component parts of an Empire.

## \|\| 220.20-24 \|\|

*saptāṅgasyāpi rājyasya mūlaṃ svāmī prakīrtitaḥ \|*  
*tanmūlatvāttathā'ṅgānāṃ sa tu rakṣyaḥ prayatnataḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*ṣaḍaṅgarakṣā kartavyā tathā tena prayatnataḥ \|*  
*aṅgebhyo yastathaikasya dro hamācarate'lpadhīḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*vadhastasya tu kartavyaḥ śīghrameva mahīkṣitā \|*  
*na rājñā mṛdunā bhāvyaṃ mṛdurhi paribhūyate \|\| 22 \|\|*

*na bhāvyaṃ dāruṇenātitīkṣṇādudvijate janaḥ \|*  
*kāle mṛduryo bhavati kāle bhavati dāruṇaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

*rājā lokadvayāpekṣī tasya lokadvayaṃ bhavet \|*  
*bhṛtyaiḥ saha mahīpālaḥ parihāsaṃ vivarjayet \|\| 24 \|\|*

20-24. Of these seven, king is the root of the Empire, therefore he should be chiefly protected. A king should also guard the other six complements of his Empire, i l any of these components rise in rebellion, the king should in no time take away the life of that fool. A sovereign should not be mild and simple hearted. A mild sovereign is despised; nor should a sovereign be hard and grim that he may instill a thrill of dread in his people. A king who is both mild and strong according to circumstances is prosperous in this life as well as in the next one. A sovereign should never joke with his retainers.

## \|\| 220.25-27 \|\|

*bhṛtyāḥ paribhavantīha nṛpaṃ harṣavaśaṃ gatam \|*  
*vyasanāni ca sarvāṇi bhūpatiḥ parivarjayet \|\| 25 \|\|*

*lokasaṃgrahaṇārthāya kṛtakavyasanī bhavet \|*  
*śauṇḍīrasya narendra sya nityamudri ktacetasaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*janā virāgamāyānti sadā duḥsevyabhāvataḥ \|*  
*smitapūrvābhibhāṣī syātsarvasyaiva mahīpatiḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

25-27. For the latter begin then to despise him. Besides this he should give up all passionate habits. It is however meet for him to have his hobbies for the acquirement of realms. The subjects of a haughty sovereign are not amiable, he should therefore speak to everyone with a smiling face.

## \|\| 220.28 \|\|

*vadhyeṣvapi mahābhāga bhrūkuṭiṃ na samācaret \|*  
*bhāvyaṃ dharmabhṛtāṃ śreṣṭha sthūlalakṣyeṇa bhūbhujā \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. He should not show his temper even to those who may be fit to be condemned to death. He should always be dignified.

## \|\| 220.29-33 \|\|

*sthūlalakṣyasya vaśagā sarvā bhavati medinī \|*  
*adīrghasūtraśca bhavetsarvakarmasu pārthivaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*dīrghasūtrasya nṛpateḥ karmahānirdhruvaṃ bhavet \|*  
*rāge darpe ca māne ca dro he pāpe ca karmaṇi \|\| 30 \|\|*

*apriye caiva kartavye dīrghasūtraḥ praśasyate \|*  
*rājñā saṃvṛtamantreṇa sadā bhāvyaṃ nṛpottama \|\| 31 \|\|*

*tasyāsaṃvṛtamantrasya rājñaḥ sarvāpado dhruvam \|*  
*kṛtānyeva tu kāryāṇi jñāyante yasya bhūpateḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

*nā’rabdhāni mahābhāga tasya syādvasudhā vaśe \|*  
*mantramūlaṃ sadā rājyaṃ tasmānmantraḥ surakṣitaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

29-33. Such a king always makes himself dear to his subjects and he should be bountiful and generous for a generous king conquers the whole world. He should not give way to laziness, but he should be quick in doing everything; all the works of a procrastinate king suffer. But where too much affection, haughtiness, selfishness, quarrel, vicious and unpleasant acts are concerned, a king should be slow; he is then praised. He should always keep his policy confidential; one who makes it known brings ruination on him. The sovereign whose policy is not known to any until it is accomplished, conquers all the world, Empires always depend on the basis of sound policy, the latter should, therefore always be well-guarded.

## \|\| 220.34 \|\|

*kartavyaḥ pṛthivīpalairmantrabhedabhayātsadā \|*  
*mantravitsādhito mantraḥ saṃpattīnāṃ sukhāvahaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. A sovereign should solve his policy through wise and sound states- men for there is always a risk of its leaking out when placed in unreliable hands. The solution of a policy through desirable channels therefore is a source of incalculable benefit. Many kings are ruined owing to bad advices from ministers.

## \|\| 220.35-39 \|\|

*mantracchalena bahavo vinaṣṭāḥ pṛthivīkṣitaḥ \|*  
*ākārairiṅgitairgatyā ceṣṭayā bhāṣitena ca \|\| 35 \|\|*

*netravaktravikāraiśca gṛhyate'ntargataṃ manaḥ \|*  
*na yasya kuśalaistasya vaśe sarvā vasuṃdharā \|\| 36 \|\|*

*bhavatīha mahībhartuḥ sadā pārthivanandana \|*  
*naikastu mantrayenmantraṃ rājā na bahubhiḥ saha \|\| 37 \|\|*

*nā’rohedviṣamāṃ nāvamaparīkṣitanāvikām \|*  
*ye cāsya bhūmijayino bhaveyuḥ paripanthinaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

*tānānayedvaśe sarvānsāmādibhirupakramaiḥ \|*  
*yathā na syātkṛśībhāvaḥ prajānāmanavekṣayā \|\| 39 \|\|*

35-39. Many sovereigns have been ruined by the unsoundness of their policy. Appearance, signs, hearing, features, speech, eyes, and face indicate the inward feelings of a man. A king sound in politics has all the world at his command. A king should neither bold council with one man nor with too many. He should not get into a boat without knowing its rower. He should also deal with the robbers that accost him according to the rules of Sama, etc. He should, by all means, pursue the course that may not be against the wishes of his subjects and may not weaken them.

## \|\| 220.40-44 \|\|

*tathā rājñā prakartavyaṃ svarāṣṭraṃ parirakṣatā \|*  
*mohādrā jā svarāṣṭraṃ yaḥ karśayatyanavekṣayā \|\| 40 \|\|*

*so'cirādbhraśyate rājyājжīvitācca sabāndhavaḥ \|*  
*bhṛto vatso jātabalaḥ karmayogyo yathā bhavet \|\| 41 \|\|*

*tathā rāṣṭraṃ mahābhāga bhṛtaṃ karmasahaṃ bhavet \|*  
*yo rāṣṭramanugṛhṇāti rājyaṃ sa parirakṣati \|\| 42 \|\|*

*saṃjātamupajīvettu vindate sa mahatphalam \|*  
*rāṣṭrāddhiraṇyaṃ dhānyaṃ ca mahīṃ rājā surakṣitām \|\| 43 \|\|*

*mahatā tu prayatnena svarāṣṭrasya ca rakṣitā \|*  
*nityaṃ svebhyaḥ parebhyaśca yathā mātā yathā pitā \|\| 44 \|\|*

40-44. He should minister to every ones comfort in his state. The king who brings about weakness of his subjects out of delusion goes to rack and ruin and he is deprived of his kingdom and his brethren. As a nourished calf becomes fit to carry loads so is a very-well-looked after State able to bear the weight of regality. The king who is kind to his subjects assures the permanency of his rule and achieves great objects. The King should carefully protect by all means gold, grains and land in his Empire and bring them under his control. As a father and a. mother well-guard their sons, so a king should well guard his senses from his own persons and from others. He should always enjoy by his senses kept well under control.

## \|\| 220.45-47 \|\|

*gopitāni sadā kuryātsaṃyatānīndri yāṇi ca \|*  
*ajasramupayoktavyaṃ phalaṃ tebhyastathaiva ca \|\| 45 \|\|*

*sarvaṃ karmedamāyattaṃ vidhāne devamānuṣe \|*  
*tayordaivamacintyaṃ ca pauruṣe vidyate kriyā \|\| 46 \|\|*

*evaṃ mahīṃ pālayato'sya bharturlokānurāgaḥ paramo bhavettu \|*  
*lokānurāgaprabhavā ca lakṣmīrlakṣmīvataścāpi parā ca kīrtiḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

45-47. All the things in this world are under the control of Daiva and the exertions of men, Daiva cannot be clearly recognised, but the exertions are seen to bring about successful results. He should also keep all his passions under his control which should be applied to achieve something useful when there is an occasion for that. Such a king is universally loved which brings him great wealth name and fame from his Empire as well as from outside.

## Chapter 221

## \|\| 221.1 \|\|

*manuruvāca*  
*daive puruṣakāre ca kiṃ jyāyastadbravīhi me \|*  
*atra me saṃśayo deva cchettumarhasyaśeṣataḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Manu said Lord! which is superior, fate or one’s own exertion and effort? I have got doubts on this; kindly solve them.”

## \|\| 221.2-4 \|\|

*matsya uvāca*  
*svameva karma daivākhyaṃ viddhi dehāntarārjitam \|*  
*tasmātpauruṣameveha śreṣṭhamāhurmanīṣiṇaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*pratikūlaṃ tathā daivaṃ pauruṣeṇa vihanyate \|*  
*maṅgalācārayuktānāṃ nityamutthānaśālinām \|\| 3 \|\|*

*yeṣāṃ pūrvakṛtaṃ karma sāttvikaṃ manujottama \|*  
*pauruṣeṇa vinā teṣāṃ keṣāṃ ciddṛśyate phalam \|\| 4 \|\|*

2-4. Lord Matsya said: — The actions of the past life are known as fate or Daiva; consequently the wise have always held one’s own effort and perseverance as superior. A man who every day performs righteous and auspicious deeds turns even his ill-luck into a good one. Those who have performed good deeds, and are filled with Sattvaguna do not get the desired fruits without their personal efforts and exertions.

## \|\| 221.5-6 \|\|

*karmaṇā prāpyate loke rājasasya tathā phalam \|*  
*kṛcchreṇa karmaṇā viddhi tāmasasya tathā phalam \|\| 5 \|\|*

*pauruṣeṇā’pyate rājanprārthitavyaṃ phalaṃ naraiḥ \|*  
*daivameva vijānanti narāḥ pauruṣavarjitāḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. Rajoguna class of men get fruits according to their perseverance and efforts. A, man, by perseverance gets what he wants. Those who have performed Tamoguna deeds attain their desires with great difficulty. Those who are incapable of persevering regard- fate alone as supreme.

Know, O King! that men get all their desired ends by their energy and efforts.

## \|\| 221.7-8 \|\|

*tasmāttrikālaṃ saṃyuktaṃ daivaṃ tu saphalaṃ bhavet \|*  
*pauruṣaṃ daivasaṃpattyā kāle phalati pārthiva \|\| 7 \|\|*

*daivaṃ puruṣakāraśca kālaśca puruṣottama \|*  
*trayametanmanuṣyasya piṇḍitaṃ syātphalāvaham \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8. Consequently fate conjoint with the present, the past and the future gives fruits while perseverance in most cases bears fruit in the present. Fate, perseverance and time all three conjointly hear fruit to a man.

## \|\| 221.9 \|\|

*kṛṣivṛṣṭisamāyogāddṛśyante phalasiddhayaḥ \|*  
*tāstu kāle pradṛśyante naivākāle kathaṃ cana \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Agricultural prospects thrive by rain which again depends on fixed time and not otherwise.

## \|\| 221.10 \|\|

*tasmātsadaiva kartavyaṃ sadharmaṃ pauruṣaṃ naraiḥ \|*  
*vipattāvapi yasyeha paraloke dhruvaṃ phalam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. A man should therefore persevere righteously he then gets high fruits during adversity even. Even if he does not get fruits in this life, he is sure to get them in the next world.

## \|\| 221.11 \|\|

*nālasāḥ prāpnuvantyarthānna ca daivaparāyaṇāḥ \|*  
*tasmātsarvaprayatnena pauruṣe yatnamācaret \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Lazy people and those that only depend on fate do not ever gam their objects, so one should always persevere in the path of righteousness.

## \|\| 221.12 \|\|

*tyaktvā'lasāndaivaparānmanuṣyānutthānayuktānpuruṣānhi lakṣmīḥ \|*  
*anviṣya yatnādvṛṇuyānnṛpendra tasmātsadotthānavatā hi bhāvyam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Prosperity forsakes those who always dream of fate and favours those who persevere, one should therefore always be active and alert.

## Chapter 222

## \|\| 222.1 \|\|

*manuruvāca*  
*upāyāṃstvaṃ samācakṣva sāmapūrvānmahādyute \|*  
*lakṣaṇaṃ ca tathā teṣāṃ prayogaṃ ca surottama \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Manu said r — “Lord! be gracious to explain to me the policies of Sama, etc., along with their characteristic and applications.”

## \|\| 222.2-3 \|\|

*matsya uvāca*  
*sāma bhedastathā dānaṃ daṇḍaśca manujeśvara \|*  
*upekṣā ca tathā māyā indra jālaṃ ca pārthiva \|\| 2 \|\|*

*prayogāḥ kathitāḥ sapta tanme nigadataḥ śṛṇu \|*  
*dvividhaṃ kathitaṃ sāma tathyaṃ cātathyameva ca \|\| 3 \|\|*

2-3. Matsya said: — A sovereign should resort to the following seven policies or expedients at the time of necessity, vis., (1) Sama, (2) Bheda, (3) Dana, (4) Danda, (5) Upeksha, (6) Maya, (7) Indrajala. Sama is of two kinds, viz. — Satyasama and Asatyasama.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — (1), (2), (3) and (4) have been explained in previous chapters. Upeksha = Policy of overlooking or endurance. Maya = Policy diplomacy. Indrajala = The use of some stratagem in war. Satyasama Policy of, of genuine conciliation. Asatyasama =Perfidious policy of conciliation.

## \|\| 222.4-7 \|\|

*tatrāpyatathyaṃ sādhūnāmākrośāyaiva jāyate \|*  
*tatra sādhuḥ prayatnena sāmasādhyo narottama \|\| 4 \|\|*

*mahākulīnā ṛjavo dharmanityā jitendri yāḥ \|*  
*sāmasādhyā na cātathyaṃ teṣu sāma prayojayet \|\| 5 \|\|*

*tathyaṃ sāma ca kartavyaṃ kulaśīlādivarṇanam \|*  
*tathā tadupacārāṇāṃ kṛtānāṃ caiva varṇanam \|\| 6 \|\|*

*anayaiva tathā yuktyā kṛtajñākhyāpanaṃ svakam \|*  
*evaṃ sāmnā ca kartavyā vaśagā dharmatatparāḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

4-7. The policy of Asatyasama should never be employed m the case of the righteous and the saints for they can only be won over by Satyasama.

If Asatyasama be applied to them, then bitter and aggressive feelings are aroused virtuous and true and self-restrained saint-like sovereigns high pedigree should be endeared by praising their lineage and by i elating to them their deeds of virtue to make a good impression on them never should Atathyasama be applied to them.

## \|\| 222.8-9 \|\|

*sāmnā yadyapi rakṣāṃsi gṛhṇantīti parā śrutiḥ \|*  
*tathā'pyetadasādhūnāṃ prayuktaṃ nopakārakam \|\| 8 \|\|*

*atiśaṅkitamityevaṃ puruṣaṃ sāmavādinam \|*  
*asādhavo vijānanti tasmāttatteṣu varjayet \|\| 9 \|\|*

8-9. The following is the rule: — Tathyasama is to be applied in the following manner: — narration of the high pedigree and description of; # deeds done for one’s benefit and acknowledging one’s gratitude etc. Thus the religions persons are brought under subjection. Though it is heard that Rakshasas are brought over by the use of Sama, yet it be remembered that it should never be applied in the case of the wicked. For no benefits will be derived thereby. The policy of conciliation wins all, but it should never be employed in the case of the wicked for they look upon a conciliatory sovereign as one afraid of them. Therefore it should ne e be applied in the case of wicked persons.

## \|\| 222.10 \|\|

*ye śuddhavaṃśā ṛjavaḥ praṇītā dharme sthitāḥ satyaparā vinītāḥ \|*  
*te sāmasādhyāḥ puruṣāḥ pradiṣṭā mānonnatā ye satataṃ ca rājan \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Those born in a good family, noble, simple, virtuous and truthful and modest, are the persons with whom Sama principle is to be applied.

## Chapter 223

## \|\| 223.1 \|\|

*matsya uvāca*  
*parasparaṃ tu ye duṣṭāḥ kruddhā bhītāvamānitāḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ bhedaṃ prayuñjīta bhedasādhyā hi te matāḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Matsya said: — With the class of people who are hostile and wicked to one another, who become afraid and feel themselves insulted, the policy of divide; and rule should be employed; for they can best be conquered, by creating disunion among them so the politicians say.

## \|\| 223.2 \|\|

*te tu yenaiva doṣeṇa parasmānnāpi bibhyati \|*  
*te tu taddoṣapātena bhedanīyā bhṛśaṃ tataḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. The vices and the weaknesses on account of which a certain class of people become disagreeable to others, should be imputed to the latter in order to bring about a disunion among them. This is the rule.

## \|\| 223.3 \|\|

*ātmīyāṃ darśayedāśāṃ parasmāddarśayedbhayam \|*  
*evaṃ hi bhedayedbhinnānyathāvadvaśamānayet \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. They should be explained about their own faults and defects and they should be frightened by the opposite party. Thus that class of men can be gradually and easily be divided from their party and then brought under submission.

## \|\| 223.4-5 \|\|

*saṃhatā hi vinā bhedaṃ śakreṇāpi suduḥsahāḥ \|*  
*bhedameva praśaṃsanti tasmānnayaviśāradāḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*svamukhenā’śrayedbhedaṃ bhedaṃ paramukhena ca \|*  
*parīkṣya sādhu manyeta bhedaṃ paramukhācchrutam \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. When many kings are bound in alliance, one single king cannot conquer them without creating disunion among them, therefore to create i among them is the best policy. Even Indra is livable to bear e of the united ones. Therefore the policy of divide and rule i praised by the politicians. A, king shook, hear either directly from persons who are to be divided or through others; then he is to test It and if he be satisfied that ho is to take up the Bheda policy. Such, a policy should however not be launched personally by a sovereign, it should be given effect to through another agency for then it proves more effective.

## \|\| 223.6 \|\|

*sadyaḥ svakāryamuddiśya kuśalairye hi bheditāḥ \|*  
*bheditāste vinirdiṣṭā naiva rājñā'rthavādibhiḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. A sovereign should not believe in the efficiency of his men employed in working out a policy of divide and rule; for the people to be disunited may be mostly found anxious to serve their respective ends.

## \|\| 223.7-10 \|\|

*antaḥ kopo bahiḥ kopo yatra syātāṃ mahīkṣitām \|*  
*antaḥkopo mahāṃstatra nāśakaḥ pṛthivīkṣitām \|\| 7 \|\|*

*sāmantakopo bāhyastu kopaḥ prokto mahīmṛtaḥ \|*  
*mahiṣīyuvarājābhyāṃ tathā senāpaternṛpa \|\| 8 \|\|*

*amātyamantriṇaṃ caiva rājaputre tathaiva ca \|*  
*antaḥkopo vinirdiṣṭo dāruṇaḥ pṛthivīkṣitām \|\| 9 \|\|*

*bāhyakope samutpanne sumahatyapi pārthivaḥ \|*  
*śuddhāntastu mahābhāga śīghrameva jayī bhavet \|\| 10 \|\|*

7-10. In an Empire there are two sources from which bitter feelings of anger and enmity crop up; one is internal and the other external of these, the internal faction is most to be dreaded; for it is this internal faction that brings about the ruin of kings. The source of anger and enmity coming from outside, from other kings is known as external source of danger.

The queen, prince, commander-in-chief, ministers, prime-minister, the princes, the wrath and discontent of these are known as the internal source of wrath and danger. To a king this is Indeed terrible. If the internal condition of the Empire be good and satisfactory, then the external source of danger however great, can be easily conquered by a king. He easily wins victory.

## \|\| 223.11 \|\|

*api śakrasamo rājā antaḥkopena naśyati \|*  
*so'ntaḥkopaḥ prayatnena tasmādra kṣyo mahībhṛtā \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. On the other hand the sovereign who is beset with internal danger, perishes in spite of his being like Indra in power; consequently such a danger and wrath ought to be very carefully guarded against.

## \|\| 223.12-14 \|\|

*parataḥ kopamutpādya bhedena vijigīṣuṇā \|*  
*jñātīnāṃ bhedanaṃ kāryaṃ pareṣāṃ vijigīṣuṇā \|\| 12 \|\|*

*rakṣyaścaiva prayatnena jñātibhedastathā’tmanaḥ \|*  
*jñātayaḥ paritapyante satataṃ paritāpitāḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*tathā'pi teṣāṃ kartavyaṃ sugambhīreṇa cetasā \|*  
*grahaṇaṃ dānamānābhyāṃ bhedastebhyo mayaṃkaraḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

12-14. A sovereign using the policy of divide and rule in case of his compeers should first try and create disunion among their communities, and kith and kin; but he should very cautiously prevent a similar thing happening amongst his brethren, for distressed kith and kin bring suffering on their overlord; they should therefore be kept intact by gifts and royal regards as a dissension among them is so dangerous to a sovereign.

## \|\| 223.15 \|\|

*na jñātimanugṛhṇanti na jñātiṃ viśvasanti ca \|*  
*jñātibhirbhedanīyāstu ripavastena pārthivaiḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15 A wise ruler ought to conquer his foes by creating a division among their kinsmen whom the foreign king does not trust.

## \|\| 223.16 \|\|

*bhinnā hi śakyā ripavaḥ prabhūtāḥ svalpena sainyena nihantumājau \|*  
*susaṃhatānāṃ hi tadastu bhedaḥ kāryo ripūṇāṃ nayaśāstravidbhiḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. The greatest of the enemies when disunited are vanquished by a small force therefore it is meet to create disunion amongst the enemies.

## Chapter 224

## \|\| 224.1-8 \|\|

*matsya uvāca*  
*sarveṣāmapyupāyānāṃ dānaṃ śreṣṭhatamaṃ matam \|*  
*sudatteneha bhavati dānenobhayalokajit \|\| 1 \|\|*

*na so'sti rājandānena vaśago yo na jāyate \|*  
*dānena vaśagā devā bhavantīha sadā nṛṇām \|\| 2 \|\|*

*dānamevopajīvanti prajāḥ sarvā nṛpottama \|*  
*priyo hi dānavāṁ lloke sarvasyaivopajāyate \|\| 3 \|\|*

*dānavānacireṇaiva tathā rājā parāñjayet \|*  
*dānavāneva śaknoti saṃhatānbhedituṃ parān \|\| 4 \|\|*

*yadyapyalubdhagambhīrāḥ puruṣāḥ sāgaropamāḥ \|*  
*na gṛhṇanti tathā'pyete jāyante pakṣapātinaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*anyatrāpi kṛtaṃ dānaṃ karotyanyānyathā vaśe \|*  
*upāyebhyaḥ praśaṃsanti dānaṃ śreṣṭhatamaṃ janāḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*dānaṃ śreyaskaraṃ puṃsāṃ dānaṃ śreṣṭhatamaṃ param \|*  
*dānavāneva lokeṣu putratve dhriyate sadā \|\| 7 \|\|*

*na kevalaṃ dānaparā jayanti bhūrlokamekaṃ puruṣapravīrāḥ \|*  
*jayanti te rājasurendra lokaṃ sudurjayaṃ yo vibudhādhivāsaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

1-8. Matsya said “King!” The policy of winning over another by gifts (Dana) is the best one. There is scarcely any one who cannot be won over through gifts. Even the Devas also are brought round by mortals through gifts. The gifts are indeed highly beneficial to the people who live thereby; and one who confers gifts, on others is beloved of all. Such a sovereign readily wins over his enemies as well as a multitude of enemies conjoint together. Men free from avarice and grave like the ocean although they never accept presents, still they side with such a sovereign through gifts. Gifts and presents given elsewhere influence others and bring these people round. Therefore this policy is the best of all. Those who give gifts are known to be the best men in the world. They are always guarded by others like their sons. Such a king does not conquer only this world but he also wins the realm of Indra — the abode of the Devas.

## Chapter 225

## \|\| 225.1 \|\|

*matsya uvāca*  
*na śaktyā ye vaśe kartumupāyatritayena tu \|*  
*daṇḍena tānvaśī kuryāddaṇḍo hi vaśakṛnnṛṇām \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Matsya said: — Those who cannot be subdued by the three expedients above mentioned should be conquered by the unfailing Danda.

## \|\| 225.2-6 \|\|

*samyakpraṇayanaṃ tasya tathā kāryaṃ mahīkṣitā \|*  
*dharmaśāstrānusāreṇa susahāyena dhīmatā \|\| 2 \|\|*

*tasya samyakpraṇayanaṃ yathā kāryaṃ mahīkṣitā \|*  
*vānaprasthāṃśca dharmajñānnirmamānniṣparigrahān \|\| 3 \|\|*

*svadeśe paradeśe vā dharmaśāstraviśāradān \|*  
*samīkṣya praṇayeddaṇḍaṃ sarvaṃ daṇḍe pratiṣṭhitam \|\| 4 \|\|*

*āśramī yadi vā varṇī pūjyo vā'tha gururmahān \|*  
*nādaṇḍyo nāma rājño'sti yaḥ svadharmeṇa tiṣṭhati \|\| 5 \|\|*

*adaṇḍyāndaṇḍayanrājā daṇḍyāṃścaivāpyadaṇḍayan \|*  
*iha rājyātparibhraṣṭo narakaṃ ca prapadyate \|\| 6 \|\|*

2-6. A wise sovereign should conquer the people by launching his policy of Danda in conjunction with his ministers, according to Dharmashastra.

In his country as well as elsewhere he should use this policy according to the prescribed politics and after knowing his men for all things are established in Danda. He should first scan the race of those who have renounced the world, the Vanaprasthas, the sage-like people before resorting to his artifice of Danda. The above people do not come under the power of Danda. The people of the different orders in life, as well as those void of them, the worthy, the great, the preceptor in fact any of them found deviating from their prescribed order and duties should be adequately punished by a sovereign. A sovereign however who inflicts punishment on the innocent and lets off those who are guilty, loses his realm in this world and goes to hell in the next.

## \|\| 225.7 \|\|

*tasmādrā jñā vinītena dharmaśāstrānusārataḥ \|*  
*daṇḍapraṇayanaṃ kāryaṃ lokānugrahakāmyayā \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. A sovereign should therefore be most cautious in inflicting punishments. He must not go against the Dharmashastra and politics.

## \|\| 225.8 \|\|

*yatra śyāmo lohitākṣo daṇḍaścarati nirbhayaḥ \|*  
*prajāstatra na muhyanti netā cetsādhu paśyati \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. The subjects of a king in spite of his being of a very simple disposition do not get spoilt where the phantom of a penal code grim in appearance freely moves about and casts its bloodshot eyes on the people.

## \|\| 225.9 \|\|

*bālavṛddhāturayatidvijastrīvidhavā yataḥ \|*  
*mātsyanyāyena bhakṣyeranyadi daṇḍaṃ na pātayet \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. If a sovereign does not use his rod, there the children, aged persons, the saints, the Brahmanas and widows become severely oppressed by the powerful ones as a younger fish is swallowed up by a bigger fish.

## \|\| 225.10-15 \|\|

*devadaityoragagaṇāḥ sarve bhūtapatattriṇaḥ \|*  
*utkrāmayeyurmaryādāṃ yadi daṇḍaṃ na pātayet \|\| 10 \|\|*

*eṣa brahmābhiśāpeṣu sarvapraharaṇeṣu ca \|*  
*sarvavikramakopeṣu vyavasāye ca tiṣṭhati \|\| 11 \|\|*

*pūjyante daṇḍino devairna pūjyante tvadaṇḍinaḥ \|*  
*na brahmāṇaṃ vidhātāraṃ na pūṣāryamaṇāvapi \|\| 12 \|\|*

*yajante mānavāḥ kecitpraśāntāḥ sarvakarmasu \|*  
*rudra magniṃ ca śakraṃ ca sūryācandra masau tathā \|\| 13 \|\|*

*viṣṇuṃ devagaṇāṃścānyāndaṇḍinaḥ pūjayanti ca \|*  
*daṇḍaḥ śāsti prajāḥ sarvā daṇḍa evābhirakṣati \|\| 14 \|\|*

*daṇḍaḥ supteṣu jāgarti daṇḍaṃ dharmaṃ vidurbudhāḥ \|*  
*rājadaṇḍabhayādeva pāpāḥ pāpaṃ na kurvate \|\| 15 \|\|*

10-15. Even the Devas, the demons, the serpents, the birds; they all transgress their limits leaving their prescribed tracks if they be not made to fear the king’s rod. Danda is always seen to exist when a Brahmana curses; when all binds of blows are inflicted, when all sorts of powers are exhibited, when anger is manifested and when serious determinations are made. A sovereign inflicting punishments discriminately is revered by the Devas but the one who does not do so is not worshipped. In fact such a sovereign is revered more than many pious souls just as Brahma, Pusha, Aryama, Rudra, Agni, Indra, Surya, Chandrama, Vishnu, and other peaceful Devas are not so much revered and worshipped as other fierce Devas are worshipped. It is Danda that governs all the subjects, it protects all, it is always alert when everything else is asleep, it is known as Dharma by the learned; through its fear the sinners do not sin.

## \|\| 225.16 \|\|

*yamadaṇḍabhayādeke parasparabhayādapi \|*  
*evaṃ sāṃsiddhike loke sarvaṃ daṇḍe pratiṣṭhitam \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Some do not commit sins for fear of Dharmaraja and others do not sin for fear of the Icing’s rod; whereas others again do not commit sins for fear of both; others again not being punished, commit sins. So everything is established on Danda.

## \|\| 225.17-18 \|\|

*andhe tamasi majжeyuryadi daṇḍaṃ na pātayet \|*  
*yasmāddaṇḍo damayati durmadāndaṇḍayatyapi \|*  
*damanāddaṇḍanāccaiva tasmāddaṇḍaṃ vidurbudhāḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*daṇḍasya bhītaistridaśaiḥ sametairbhāgo dhṛtaḥ śūladharasya yajñe \|*  
*dattaṃ kumāre dhvajinīpatitvaṃ varaṃ śiśūnāṃ ca bhayādbalastham \|\| 18 \|\|*

17-18. The royal rod of punishment inflicts punishment on the wicked and guilty and also prevents others who have not committed sin from committing fresh sins. So the object is two-fold. It is out of the fear of Danda that the Devas assembled in the Daksha Yajna (sacrifice of the Prajapati Daksha) gave the share of sacrificial oblations to Mahadeva and gave the post of commander-in-chief to Kartikeya and Vala granted boons to children.

## Chapter 226

## \|\| 226.1 \|\|

*matsya uvāca*  
*daṇḍapraṇayanārthāya rājā sṛṣṭaḥ svayaṃbhuvā \|*  
*devabhāgānupādāya sarvabhūtādiguptaye \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Matsya said: — A king is created by Brahma for the preservation of all the beings, for awarding to the Devas their respective shares of sacrificial oblations and for inflicting proper punishment to the guilty.

## \|\| 226.2-3 \|\|

*tejasā yadamuṃ kaścinnaiva śaknoti vīkṣitum \|*  
*tato bhavati lokeṣu rājā bhāskaravatprabhuḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*yadā'sya darśane lokaḥ prasādamupagacchati \|*  
*nayanānandakāritvāttadā bhavati candra māḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

2-3. A king is like the Sun for none dare look at him with hostile eyes. Everyone is pleased at the sight of him, he satisfies all eyes, therefore he is like the Moon.

## \|\| 226.4 \|\|

*yathā yamaḥ priyadveṣye prāpte kāle prayacchati \|*  
*tathā rājñā vidhātavyāḥ prajāstaddhi yamavratam \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. A king like Dharmaraja bestows his affection and inflicts his punishment on the people according to circumstances. He has therefore the attributes of Dharmaraja.

## \|\| 226.5 \|\|

*varuṇena yathā pāśairbaddha eva pradṛśyate \|*  
*tathā pāpānnigṛhṇīyādvratametaddhi vāruṇam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Just as the God Varuna flings His noose round the enemy’s neck similarly a king also throws his fetters round the feet of the wicked. This is the king’s Varunavrata (vow).

## \|\| 226.6-7 \|\|

*paripūrṇaṃ yathā candraṃ dṛṣṭvā hṛṣyati mānavaḥ \|*  
*tathā prakṛtayo yasminsa candra pratimo nṛpaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*pratāpayuktastejasvī nityaṃ syātpāpakarmasu \|*  
*duṣṭasāmantahiṃsreṣu rājā’gneyavrate sthitaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

6-7. People are satisfied to look at their king as they are at the sight of the Moon. He is always rigorous and strong to curb the sinners and he should burn as fire does, all his enemies who are envious and wicked. This is his Agneyavrata.

## \|\| 226.8-10 \|\|

*yathā sarvāṇi bhūtāni dharā dhārayate svayam \|*  
*tathā sarvāṇi bhūtāni bibhrataḥ pārthivaṃ vratam \|\| 8 \|\|*

*indra syārkasya vātasya yamasya varuṇasya ca \|*  
*candra syāgneḥ pṛthivyāśca tejovrataṃ nṛpaścaret \|\| 9 \|\|*

*vārṣikāṃścaturo māsānyathendro 'pyabhivarṣati \|*  
*tathā'bhivarṣetsvaṃ rāṣṭraṃ kāmamindra vrataṃ smṛtam \|\| 10 \|\|*

8-10. He should always observe this Agneya vrata. As the earth holds up all the beings so a king nourishes all his subjects. This is his Parthivavrata. As all the subjects of a sovereign are steady in their devotion to him so is he in his devotion to Indra, Surya, Vayu, Yama, Varuna, Chandrama, Agni and Prithvi He sustains his subjects as Indra pours forth rain for four months during the rains. This is Indravrata. He takes revenues from his subjects as the Sun draws in moisture by his rays for eight months. This is Suryavrata.

## \|\| 226.11 \|\|

*aṣṭau māsānyathā’dityastoyaṃ harati raśmibhiḥ \|*  
*tathā haretkaraṃ rāṣṭrānnityamarkavrataṃ hi tat \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. As air pervades through and through all the being so does the king know the hearts of all his subjects through his spies. This is Vayuvrata.

## Chapter 227

## \|\| 227.1 \|\|

*matsya uvāca*  
*nikṣ̣epasya samaṃ mūlyaṃ daṇḍyo nikṣ̣epabhuk tathā \|*  
*vastrādikasamastasya tadā dharmo na hīyate \|\| 227.1 \|\|*

Matsya said- One who has misappropriated anything under his custody should be fined by a king which should be equivalent to the value of the thing misappropriated. A king will not thereby lose his religion.

## \|\| 227.2 \|\|

*yo nikṣ̣epaṃ nārpayati yaścānikṣ̣ipya yācate \|*  
*tāvubhau coravacchāsyau dāpyau vā dviguṇaṃ dhanam \|\| 227.2 \|\|*

One who does not return deposited thing to the depositor and one who mischievously asks for a thing from a person on the mere allegation of having placed it in his custody; are both guilty like a thief. They should be punished and fined twice amount of the value of the thing which is kept in his custody.

## \|\| 227.3 \|\|

*upadhābhiśca yaḥ kaścitparadra vyaṃ harennaraḥ \|*  
*sasahāyaḥ sa hantavyaḥ prakāmaṃ vividhairvadhaiḥ \|\| 227.3 \|\|*

A man who defrauds another’s property should be punished with death along with his accomplices or should be sentenced rigorously as the king considers fit.

## \|\| 227.4 \|\|

*yo yācitaṃ samādāya na taddadyādyathākramam \|*  
*sa nigṛhya balāddāpyo daṇḍyo vā pūrvasāhasam \|\| 227.4 \|\|*

A person who takes a loan from other person and does not return to him within a time-limit should be chastised and forcibly made by Purva Sahasa, to return it to its owner and fined by the sovereign.

## \|\| 227.5-6 \|\|

*ajñānādyadi vā kuryātparadra vyasya vikrayam \|*  
*nirdoṣ̣o jñānapūrvaṃ tu coravadvadhamarhati \|\| 227.5 \|\|*

*mūlyamādāya yo vidyāṃ śilpaṃ vā na prayacchati \|*  
*daṇḍyaḥ sa mūlyaṃ sakalaṃ dharmajñena mahīkṣ̣itā \|\| 227.6 \|\|*

One who sells away the property of another person unknowingly, is not guilty but one who does so knowingly should be punished like a thief. One who does not impart knowledge or mechanical training to his students after having received his fee for the same should be fined the whole amount of his wages.

## \|\| 227.7 \|\|

*dvijabhojye tu saṃprāpte prativeśmamabhojayan \|*  
*hiraṇyamāṣ̣akaṃ daṇḍyaḥ pāpe nāsti vyatikramaḥ \|\| 227.7 \|\|*

One who does not feed his neighbour and Brahmanas earns sin instead of virtue and he should be fined also one masa gold, but if he omits to invite any sinful Brahmanas he is not guilty.

## \|\| 227.8 \|\|

*āmantrito dvijo yastu vartamānaśca sve gṛhe \|*  
*niṣ̣kāraṇaṃ na gacchedyaḥ sa dāpyo'ṣ̣ṭaśataṃ damam \|\| 227.8 \|\|*

If a Brahmana be invited to join a feast and when he has to the house of one invited him and is made to go back without any food and proper reasons, then he should be fined hundred and eight Damas.

## \|\| 227.9-10 \|\|

*pratiśrutyāpradātāraṃ suvarṇaṃ daṇḍayennṛpaḥ \|\| 227.9 \|\|*  
*bhṛtyaścā’jñāṃ na kuryādyo darpātkarma yathoditam \|*  
*sa daṇḍyaḥ kṛṣ̣ṇalānyaṣ̣ṭau na deyaṃ cāsya vetanam \|\| 227.10 \|\|*

One who does not confer a promised gift on someone should be fined of gold by the king. A servant who does not follow the order avoiding his duty should be fined eight rattis of gold and not to be paid his salary too.

## \|\| 227.11 \|\|

*saṃgṛhītaṃ na dadyādyaḥ kāle vetanameva ca \|*  
*akāle tu tyajedmṛtyaṃ daṇḍyaḥ syācchatameva ca \|\| 227.11 \|\|*

If an owner does not pay his servant at the right time and dismisses him without a proper cause, should be fined hundred Krsnalas.

## \|\| 227.12 \|\|

*yo grāmadeśasasyānāṃ kṛtvā satyena saṃvidam \|*  
*visaṃvadennaro lobhāttaṃ rāṣ̣ṭrādvipravāsayet \|\| 227.12 \|\|*

One who promises to give away a village, country or grain fields, etc., and afterwards goes back upon his words and tells false should be banished from his kingdom by a sovereign.

## \|\| 227.13-14 \|\|

*krītvā vikrīya vā kiṃcidyasyehānuśayī bhavet \|*  
*so'ntardaśāhāttatsāmyaṃ dadyāccaivā’dadīta vā \|\| 227.13 \|\|*

*pareṇa tu daśāhasya na dadyānnaiva dāpayet \|*  
*ādadanna dadaccaiva rājñā daṇḍyaḥ śatāni ṣ̣aṭ \|\| 227.14 \|\|*

If anyone does not pay or get balance of the value of a thing that he bought or sold, within ten days of the bargain then the seller or purchaser should be fined six hundred Krsnalas by the king.

## \|\| 227.15-16 \|\|

*yastu doṣ̣avatīṃ kanyāmanākhyāya prayacchati \|*  
*tasya kuryānnṛpo daṇḍaṃ svayaṃ ṣ̣aṇṇavatiṃ paṇān \|\| 227.15 \|\|*

*akanyaiveti yaḥ kanyāṃ brūyāddoṣ̣eṇa mānavaḥ \|*  
*sa śataṃ prāpnuyāddaṇḍaṃ tasyā doṣ̣amadarśayan \|\| 227.16 \|\|*

One who marries a girl to another without telling her faults should be fined 96 Panas and one who mischievously and falsely declares a girl to be not good (a eunuch) should be fined 100 Panas.

## \|\| 227.17 \|\|

*yastvanyāṃ darśayitvā'nyāṃ voḍhuḥ kanyāṃ prayacchati \|*  
*uttamaṃ tasya kurvīta rājā daṇḍaṃ tu sāhasam \|\| 227.17 \|\|*

One who shows one girl and then marries a different one should be fined 1,080 Panas (Uttam Sahasa fine).

## \|\| 227.18 \|\|

*varo doṣ̣ānanākhyāya yaḥ kanyāṃ varayediha \|*  
*dattā'pyadattā sā tasya rājñā daṇḍyaḥ śatadvayam \|\| 227.18 \|\|*

The man who hiding his faults marries a girl is considered not to have married at all and should pay 200 Panas to the king.

## \|\| 227.19-20 \|\|

*pradāya kanyāṃ yo'nyasmai punastāṃ saṃprayacchati \|*  
*daṇḍaḥ kāryo narendre ṇa tasyāpyuttamasāhasaḥ \|\| 227.19 \|\|*

*satyaṃkāreṇa vā vācā yuktaṃ paṇyamasaṃśayam \|*  
*lubdho hyanyatra vikretā ṣ̣aṭśataṃ daṇḍamarhati \|\| 227.20 \|\|*

A man who weds his daughter to one and then again marries her to another should be fined 1080 Panas, (Uttam Sahasa fine). Similarly one who sells a thing to another after promising to sell it to some particular person should be fined 600 Panas.

## \|\| 227.21 \|\|

*duhituḥ śulkavikretā satyaṃkārāttu saṃtyajet \|*  
*dviguṇaṃ daṇḍayedenamiti dharmo vyavasthitaḥ \|\| 227.21 \|\|*

One who demands more money than agreed upon and promised at the time of a girl’s marriage should be fined twice the sum agreed upon. This is the rule of Dharmasastra.

## \|\| 227.22-24 \|\|

*mūlyaikadeśaṃ dattvā tu yadi kretā dhanaṃ tyajet \|*  
*sa daṇḍyo madhyamaṃ daṇḍaṃ tasya paṇyasya mokṣ̣aṇam \|\| 227.22 \|\|*

*duhyāddhenuṃ ca yaḥ pālo gṛhītvā bhaktavetanam \|*  
*sa tu daṇḍyaḥ śataṃ rājñā suvarṇaṃ cāpyarakṣ̣itā \|\| 227.23 \|\|*

*daṇḍaṃ dattvā tu virametsvāmitaḥ kṛtalakṣ̣aṇaḥ \|*  
*baddhaḥ kārṣ̣ṇāyasaiḥ pāśaistasya karmakaro bhavet \|\| 227.24 \|\|*

A man who pays part payment for a thing and then does not purchase it should be fined 540 Panas (Madhyama Danda) and the king should make him return the earnest money. One who after accepting his fee steals the milk of a cow under his charge or does not properly look after it should be fined 100 masas of gold and he should also be tied in iron chains and made to work in fetters.

## \|\| 227.25-26 \|\|

*dhanuḥśataparīṇāho grāmasya tu samantataḥ \|*  
*dviguṇaṃ triguṇaṃ vā'pi nagarasya tu kalpayet \|\| 227.25 \|\|*

*vṛttiṃ tatra prakurvīta yāmuṣ̣ṭro nāvalokayet \|*  
*chidraṃ vā vārayetsarvaṃ śvaśūkaramukhānugam \|\| 227.26 \|\|*

The prison (place of confinement) should be erected out of a city, it should be 100 Dhanusa wide and in big towns, the prison should be twice or thrice the above dimensions. Those prisons should be circled by a wall so high as a camel may not look into them and no inlet for a dog or a swine should be left in the wall.

## \|\| 227.27-30 \|\|

*yatrāparivṛtaṃ dhānyaṃ vihiṃsyuḥ paśavo yadi \|*  
*na tatra kārayeddaṇḍaṃ nṛpatiḥ paśurakṣ̣iṇe \|\| 227.27 \|\|*

*anirdaśāhāṃ gāṃ sūtāṃ vṛṣ̣aṃ devapaśuṃ tathā \|*  
*chidraṃ vā vārayetsarvaṃ na daṇḍyamanurabravīt \|\| 227.28 \|\|*

*ato'nyathā vinaṣ̣ṭasya daśāṃśaṃ daṇḍamarhati \|*  
*pālyasya pālakasvāmī vināśe kṣ̣attriyasya tu \|\| 227.29 \|\|*

*bhakṣ̣ayitvopaviṣ̣ṭastu dviguṇaṃ daṇḍamarhati \|*  
*viśaṃ daṇḍyāddaśaguṇaṃ vināśe kṣ̣attriyasya tu \|\| 227.30 \|\|*

If an animal gets into a field without any enclosure and eats some of the grass etc., stocked there, then the man incharge of such trespassing cattle should not be punished. Manu has laid down in his code that if a cow that has calved only ten days ago or a bull set free at the time of Sraddha consecrated to the Deity eats away corns of a field, though enclosed, the keeper of such animals should not be punished. Other cattle besides them, if found grazing in the fields of others, should however be punished by a fine ten times the damage done, being levied from the owner of the cattle, and if the above crime be done wilfully, twice the above fine should be levied. If a Ksatriya’s fields be harmed by Vaisya’s cattle the former should be compensated by the latter ten times the damage done.

## \|\| 227.31-33 \|\|

*gṛhaṃ taḍāgamārāmaṃ kṣ̣etraṃ vā'pi samāharan \|*  
*śatāni pañca daṇḍaḥ syādajñānāddviśato damaḥ \|\| 227.31 \|\|*

*sīmābandhanakāle tu sīmāntaṃ yo hi kārayet \|*  
*teṣ̣āṃ saṃjñāṃ dadānastu jihvācchedanamāpnuyāt \|\| 227.32 \|\|*

*athaināmapi yo dadyātsaṃvidaṃ vā'dhigacchati \|*  
*uttamaṃ sāhasaṃ daṇḍya iti svāyaṃbhuvo'bravīt \|\| 227.33 \|\|*

One who usurps anyone’s house, tank, forest, garden and fields should be fined 500 Panas. One who does so unknowingly should be fined 200 Panas. One who annihilates the boundary mark at the time of its laying it out, or one who gives a wrong advice or is a councillor of liars should be deprived of his tongue or should be fined 1,080 (Uttama sahasa) Panas. This is what Manu has enjoined.

## \|\| 227.34 \|\|

*varṇānāmānupūrvyeṇa trayāṇāmaviśeṣ̣ataḥ \|*  
*akāryakāriṇaḥ sarvānprāyaścittāni kārayet \|\| 227.34 \|\|*

If Brahmanas, Ksatriyas and Vaisyas do a thing contrary to their prescribed orders they should be made to perform the usual purificatory rites.

## \|\| 227.35-36 \|\|

*asatyena pramāpya strīṃ śūdra hatyāvrataṃ caret \|*  
*dānena ca dhanenaikaṃ sarpādīnāmaśaknuvan \|\| 227.35 \|\|*

*ekaikaṃ sa caretkṛcchraṃ dvijaḥ pāpāpanuttaye \|*  
*phaladānāṃ ca vṛkṣ̣āṇāṃ chedane japyamṛkśatam \|\| 227.36 \|\|*  
*gulmavallīlatānāṃ ca puṣ̣pitānāṃ ca vīrudhām \|*

A woman if she kills anybody should keep up the Stidrahatya ordinance. If a Brahmana cannot afford to spend as much as required for the performance M a purificatory rite in killing serpents, he should keep up Krcchravrata for the purification thereof. If a twice-born cuts a fruitbearing tree or flower creepers, he will be purified by chanting one hundred Vedic hymns.

## \|\| 227.37-38\|\|

*asthimatāṃ ca sattvānāṃ sahasrasya pramāpaṇe \|*  
*pūrṇe vā'nasyavasthātuṃ śūdra hatyāvrataṃ caret \|\| 227.37 \|\|*

*kiṃciddeyaṃ ca viprāya dadyādasthimatāṃ vadhe \|*  
*anasthnāṃ caiva hiṃsāyāṃ prāṇāyāmairviśudhyati \|\| 227.38 \|\|*

The sin of killing a thousand beings having bones is similar to that of killing a crore of boneless insects such as mosquitoes, lice, etc. To purify himself of such a sin one should observe the Stidrahatya ordinance and should also make some gift to a Brahmana incase of killing animals having bones. One becomes purified of the sin of killing boneless insects, etc., merely by Pranayama.

## \|\| 227.39-40 \|\|

*annādijānāṃ sattvānāṃ rasajānāṃ ca sarvaśaḥ \|*  
*phalapuṣ̣podgatānāṃ ca ghṛtaprāśo viśodhanam \|\| 227.39 \|\|*

*kṛṣ̣ṭānāmoṣ̣adhīnāṃ ca jātānāṃ ca svayaṃ vane \|*  
*vṛthā chedena gaccheta dinamekaṃ payovratī \|\| 227.40 \|\|*

The sin of killing the worms existing in grains, molasses and fruits and flowers is purified by eating clarified butter. By cutting the medicinal herbs of a jungle without any necessity one commits a sin of which he is purified by living on milk for a day.

## \|\| 227.41-42 \|\|

*etairvratairapohyaṃ syādeno hiṃsāsamudbhavam \|*  
*steyadoṣ̣āpahartriṇāṃ śrūyatāṃ vratamuttamam \|\| 227.41 \|\|*

*dhānyānnadhanacauryāṇi kṛtvā kāmāddvijottamaḥ \|*  
*sajātīyagṛhādeva kṛcchrārdhena viśudhyati \|\| 227.42 \|\|*

Such sins are cleansed by the observance of the ordinances mentioned above, now the ordinance which ought to be observed by a thief will be enumerated. By observing the Ardha-krcchra ordinance a Brahmana becomes purified of the sin of having committed a theft of com, money, etc., in the house of another of his own caste.

## \|\| 227.43 \|\|

*manuṣ̣yāṇāṃ tu haraṇe strīṇāṃ kṣ̣etragṛhasya tu \|*  
*kūpavāpījalānāṃ tu śuddhiścāndrā yaṇaṃ smṛtam \|\| 227.43 \|\|*

By observing Candrayana vrata, one is purified of the sin of having taken a woman, house, well, tank, etc., belonging to another.

## \|\| 227.44-45 \|\|

*dra vyāṇāmalpasārāṇāṃ steyaṃ kṛtvā'nyaveśmataḥ \|*  
*caretsāṃtapanaṃ kṛcchraṃ tanniryātya viśuddhaye \|\| 227.44 \|\|*

*bhakṣ̣yabhojyāpaharaṇe yānaśayyāsanasya tu \|*  
*puṣ̣pamūlaphalānāṃ tu pañcagavyaṃ viśodhanam \|\| 227.45 \|\|*

A man who steals trifles is purified by the observances of Santapana Krcchra ordinance. The stealing of eatables, conveyance, bedstead, flowers, berries and fruits is purified by drinking Pancagavya.

## \|\| 227.46-48 \|\|

*tṛṇakāṣ̣ṭhadrumāṇāṃ tu śuṣ̣kānnasya guḍasya ca \|*  
*cailacarmāmiṣ̣āṇāṃ tu trirātraṃ syādabhojanam \|\| 227.46 \|\|*

*maṇimuktāpravālānāṃ tāmrasya rajatasya ca \|*  
*ayaskāṃsyopalānāṃ ca dvādaśāhaṃ kaṇānnabhuk \|\| 227.47 \|\|*

*kārpāsakīṭajorṇānāṃ dviśaphaikaśaphasya ca \|*  
*pakṣ̣igandhauṣ̣adhīnāṃ ca rajжvāścaiva tr! yahaṃ payaḥ \|\| 227.48 \|\|*

One who steals hay, wood, tree, dried com, molasses, cloth, hide, fish and flesh becomes purified by keeping a fast for three days. One who steals pearls, gems, Prabala, copper, silver, iron, Kamsya and stones becomes purified if one eats for twelve days the refuse of rice. A thief of cotton, silk, animals of bisected hoofs, horses, birds, scents, medicines, rope, becomes purified by living on milk for three days.

## \|\| 227.49 \|\|

*etairvratairvyapoheta pāpaṃ steyakṛtaṃ dvijaḥ \|*  
*agamyāgamanīyaṃ tu vratairebhirapānudet \|\| 227.49 \|\|*

The ordinance mentioned above purify the twice-born ones of the sin of committing a theft, now the ordinances for the purification of illicit connections will be enumerated.

## \|\| 227.50-51 \|\|

*gurutalpavrataṃ kuryādre taḥ siktvā svayoniṣ̣u \|*  
*sakhyuḥ putrasya ca strīṣ̣u kumārīṣ̣vantyajāsu ca \|\| 227.50 \|\|*

*paitṛṣ̣vasrīyabhaginīṃ svasrīyāṃ mātureva ca \|*  
*bhrāturduhitaraṃ caiva gatvā cāndrā yaṇaṃ caret \|\| 227.51 \|\|*

One who is guilty of an illicit connection with his teacher’s wife should observe the ordinance prescribed for the sin of committing adultery with a lady of one’s own community. For the purification from the sin of having an illicit connection with one’s mother’s mad, son’s wife, virgin, Candall, father’s-sister’s daughter, sister, mother, mother’s-sister’s daughter and righteous lady or brother’s respected wife, Candrayana ordinance should be kept up.

## \|\| 227.52-53 \|\|

*etāḥ striyastu bhāryārthe nopagacchettu buddhimān \|*  
*jñātīnāṃ ca striyo yāstu patitānugatāśca yāḥ \|\| 227.52 \|\|*

*amānuṣ̣īṣ̣u puruṣ̣o udakyāyāmayoniṣ̣u \|*  
*retaḥ siktvā jale caiva kṛcchraṃ sāṃtapanaṃ caret \|\| 227.53 \|\|*

A wise man should not indulge with the above mentioned class of ladies nor should he marry one’s relation, a fallen woman, a woman in menses. He should also abstain from unnatural offence and indulging with lower animals. One who does so should keep up Krcchrasantapana penance to purify himself of the sin. If one discharges one’s semen in water, one is to perform Krcchrasantapana-vrata.

## \|\| 227.54-55 \|\|

*maithunaṃ ca samālokya puṃsi yoṣ̣iti vā dvijaḥ \|*  
*goyāne'psu divā caiva savāsāḥ snānamācaret \|\| 227.54 \|\|*

*cāṇḍālāntyastriyo gatvā bhuktvā ca pratigṛhya ca \|*  
*patatyajñānato vipro jñānātsāmyaṃ tu gacchati \|\| 227.55 \|\|*

A Brahmana who looks at a sexual intercourse or makes discharge in course of the day in water or on a bullock car, he should bath with his clothes. A Brahmana who indulges with a Candala woman or a woman of a different caste or eats their food or accepts a gift from them unknowingly falls from his position. If he does so knowingly, he becomes of that caste himself.

## \|\| 227.56-57 \|\|

*vipraduṣ̣ṭāṃ striyaṃ bhartā nirundhyādekaveśmani \|*  
*yatpuṃsaḥ paradāreṣ̣u taccaināṃ cārayedvratam \|\| 227.56 \|\|*

*sā cetpunaḥ praduṣ̣yettu sadṛśenopamantritā \|*  
*kṛcchraṃ cāndrā yaṇaṃ caiva tattasyāḥ pāvanaṃ smṛtam \|\| 227.57 \|\|*

A woman defiled by a Brahmana should be kept confined in the house by her husband and so should a woman be kept up who desires for another man. If even then she remains the same she should be made to keep up Krcchrasantapana ordinance which purifies her.

## \|\| 227.58-59 \|\|

*yaḥ karotyekarātreṇa vṛṣ̣alīsevanaṃ dvijaḥ \|*  
*tadbhakṣ̣yabhugjapennityaṃ tribhirvarṣ̣airvyapohati \|\| 227.58 \|\|*

*eṣ̣ā pāpakṛtāmuktā caturṇāmapi niṣ̣kṛtiḥ \|*  
*patitaiḥ saṃprayuktānāmimāṃ śṛṇuta niṣ̣kṛtim \|\| 227.59 \|\|*

A twice-born should have only one meal a day and turn the sacred Gayatrl on his beads for full three years to purify himself of the sin of having indulged with a girl of twelve years in whom menstruation has not commenced (or a barren woman) for a night. These ordinances purify one for having illicit connections now the ordinances prescribed for those who associate with the fallen will be mentioned.

## \|\| 227.60-61 \|\|

*saṃvatsareṇa patati patitena sahā’caran \|*  
*vājanādhyāpanādyaunāttulyayānāśanāsanāt \|\| 227.60 \|\|*

*yo yena patitenaiṣ̣āṃ saṃsargaṃ yāti mānavaḥ \|*  
*sa tasyaiva vrataṃ kuryāttatsaṃsargaviśuddhaye \|\| 227.61 \|\|*

A man who associates with a fallen lot for a year also becomes the same. One becomes fallen even by helping them in the performance of sacrifices, by teaching them, by making them his relation, by interdining with them. A man becomes purified of it by the ordinance prescribed for it. But he will remain like a Preta.

## \|\| 227.62-63 \|\|

*patitasyodakaṃ kāryaṃ sapiṇḍairbāndhavaiḥ saha \|*  
*nindite'hani sāyāhne jñātibhirgurusaṃnidhau \|\| 227.62 \|\|*

*dāsī ghaṭamapāṃ pūrṇaṃ parvasyetpretavatsadā \|*  
*ahorātramupāsīrannāśaucaṃ bāndhavaiḥ saha \|\| 227.63 \|\|*

A fallen person should be taken outside the village limits by his brethren and made to drink the water of the maid’s house. If a fallen man dies the sin that devolves thereby lasts for a whole day and night. One should not talk to a fallen man, nor should one sit on his seat. He should only get enough for his sustenance. On the evening of an inauspicious day, the near kinsmen of the fallen man would perform before the Guru his Udaka Kriya. His maid then would throw in the south-west comer one pitcher full of water. His friends are to fast the whole day and night and they would not accept the Asauca of the Preta.

## \|\| 227.64-65\|

*nivartayeraṃstasmāttu saṃbhāṣ̣aṇasahāsanam \|*  
*dāyādasya pramāṇaṃ ca yātrāmevaṃ ca laukikīm \|\| 227.64 \|\|*

*jyeṣ̣ṭhabhāvānnivarteta jyeṣ̣ṭhāvāptaṃ ca yatpunaḥ \|*  
*jyeṣ̣ṭhāṃśaṃ prāpnuyāccāsya yavīyānguṇato'dhikaḥ \|\| 227.65 \|\|*

The friends of the fallen man should not address him or sit with him or travel with him. Nor should they express that he is their near relative. This is the social rule. He should only get enough for his sustenance. He should not be made to entitle himself to his share as an elder brother inspite of his being senior, but the biggest share should go to the most deserving among the remaining ones.

## \|\| 227.66-68\|\|

*sthāpitāṃ cāpi maryādāṃ ye bhindyuḥ pāpakarmiṇaḥ \|*  
*sarve pṛthakpṛthagdaṇḍyā rājñā prathamasāhasam \|\| 227.66 \|\|*

*śataṃ brāhmaṇamākruśya kṣ̣attriyo daṇḍamarhati \|*  
*vaiśyastu dviśataṃ rājañchūdra stu vadhamarhati \|\| 227.67 \|\|*

*pañcāśadbrāhmaṇo daṇḍyaḥ kṣ̣attriyasyābhiśaṃsane \|*  
*vaiśyasyāpyardhapañcāśacchūdre dvādaśako damaḥ \|\| 227.68 \|\|*

A sinner, who injures the right code of conduct should be fined by the king a Prathama Sahasa (270 Panas). A Ksatriya who abuses a Brahmana should be fined 100 Panas, a Vaisya doing so should be fined 200 Panas and a Sudra if he does so should be sentenced to capital punishment. A Brahmana who abuses a Ksatriya should be fined 50 Panas, if he abuses a Vaisya, he should be fined 25 Panas and if he abuses a Sudra, the fine should be 12 Panas.

## \|\| 227.69-71 \|\|

*kṣ̣attriyasyā’pnuyādvaiśyaḥ sāhasaṃ punareva ca \|*  
*śūdra ḥ! kṣ̣attriyamākruśya jihvācchedanamāpnuyāt \|\| 227.69 \|\|*

*pañcāśatkṣ̣attriyo daṇḍyastathā vaiśyābhiśaṃsane \|*  
*śūdre caivārdhapañcāśattathā dharmo na hīyate \|\| 227.70 \|\|*

*vaiśvasyā’krośane daṇḍaḥ śūdra ścottamasāhasam \|*  
*śūdrā krośe tathā vaiśyaḥ śatārdhaṃ daṇḍamarhati \|\| 227.71 \|\|*

A Vais'ya abusing a Ksatriya should be fined Prathama Sahasa; if a Sudra abuses a Ksatriya his penalty should be that his tongue would be severed. If a Ksatriya abuses a Vais'ya he would be fined 50 Panas; and if he abuses a Sudra, he should be fined 25 Panas. If a Sudra abuses a Vaisya he should be fined 1080 Panas (Uttama Sahasa), but a Vaisya abusing a Sudra should be fined only 50 Panas.

## \|\| 227.72-74 \|\|

*savarṇākrośane daṇḍyastathā dvādaśakaṃ smṛtam \|*  
*vādeṣ̣vavacanīyeṣ̣u tadeva dviguṇaṃ bhavet \|\| 227.72 \|\|*

*ekajātirdvijātiṃ tu vācā dāruṇayā kṣ̣ipan \|*  
*jihvāyāḥ prāpnuyācchedaṃ jaghanyaḥ prathamo hi saḥ \|\| 227.73 \|\|*

*nāmajātigṛhaṃ teṣ̣āmabhidro heṇa kurvataḥ \|*  
*nikṣ̣epyo'yomayaḥ śaṅkurjvalannāsye daśāṅgulaḥ \|\| 227.74 \|\|*

People abusing men of their own community should be fined only 12 Panas and those who indulge in most foul abuse should be fined twice the amount prescribed. A Sudra should be deprived of his tongue if he abuses violently a twice-born, if his offence be moderate; if his offence be highest, he is to be fined Uttama Sahasa. A king should put a red, hot iron spike ten Angulas long in the mouth of a Sudra who vilifies violently one, taking his name, caste and house.

## \|\| 227.75-76 \|\|

*dharmopadeśaṃ śūdra stu dvijānāmabhikurvataḥ \|*  
*taptamāsecayettailaṃ vaktre śrotre ca pārthivaḥ \|\| 227.75 \|\|*

*śrutiṃ deśaṃ ca jātiṃ ca karma śārīrameva ca \|*  
*vitathaṃ ca bruvandaḍyo rājñā dviguṇasāhasam \|\| 227.76 \|\|*

A Sudra who teaches Dharma to the twice-born should also be punished by a sovereign by getting hot oil poured into his ears and mouth. The person who speaks a lie about his Veda, his country, his caste and corporeal duties, should be fined twice the Uttama Sahasa (2,160 Panas).

## \|\| 227.77-78 \|\|

*yastu pātakasaṃyuktaḥ kṣ̣ipedvarṇāntaraṃ naraḥ \|*  
*uttamaṃ sāhasaṃ daṇḍaḥ pātyastasminyathākramam \|\| 227.77 \|\|*

*rājño niveśaniyamaṃ vitathaṃ yānti vai mithaḥ \|*  
*sarve dviguṇadaṇḍyāste vipralambhānnṛpasya tu \|\| 227.78 \|\|*

A sinful person who abuses a high class man ought to be fined Uttama Sahasa (1080 Panas), one who violates the ordinance of a king ought to be fined double amount of the same for he is really a man who tries to upset the determination of the king.

## \|\| 227.79-80 \|\|

*prītyā mayā'syābhihitaṃ pramādenāthavā vadet \|*  
*bhūyo na caivaṃ vakṣ̣yāmi sa tu daṇḍārdhabhāgbhavet \|\| 227.79 \|\|*

*kāṇaṃ vā'pyathavā khañjamandhaṃ cāpi tathāvidham \|*  
*tathyenāpi bruvandāpyo daṇḍaṃ kārṣ̣āpaṇaṃ dhanam \|\| 227.80 \|\|*

If a person abuses another man and then says that he did this in a joke, or without any intention through love or intoxication and would never do so again, ought to be fined only half of the amount codified. A man who speaks ill towards the one-eyed, the blind, the baldheaded and the crippled by addressing them as such should be fined one tola of silver (Karsapana Danda).

## \|\| 227.81 \|\|

*mātaraṃ pitaraṃ jyeṣ̣ṭhaṃ bhrātaraṃ śvaśuraṃ gurum \|*  
*ākrośayañchataṃ daṇḍyaḥ panthānaṃ cārdayanguroḥ \|\| 227.81 \|\|*

One who does not pay respect his mother, father, elder brother, father in law and teacher and one who injures the way of his preceptor, should be fined 100 panas.

## \|\| 227.82-84 \|\|

*guruvarjyaṃ tu mānārhaṃ yo hi mārgaṃ na yacchati \|*  
*sa dāpyaḥ kṛṣ̣ṇalaṃ rājastasya pāpasya śāntaye \|\| 227.82 \|\|*

*ekajātirdvijātiṃ tu yenāṅgenāparādhnuyāt \|*  
*tadeva cchedayettasya kṣ̣ipramevāvicārayan \|\| 227.83 \|\|*

*avaniṣ̣ṭhīvato darpāddvāvoṣ̣ṭhau cchedayennṛpaḥ \|*  
*avamūtrayato meḍhramapaśabdayato gudam \|\| 227.84 \|\|*

One who does not show the way for another respected person other than his Guru should be fined one ratti of silver (one Krsnala). A king should get that limb of a Sudra severed from his body which he uses in causing pain to the twice-born. The lips of the man who haughtily spits on another should be cut down. One who mischievously makes water facing another should be deprived of his organ and similarly the hind part of the man should be dealt with who maliciously makes wind in the face of another.

## \|\| 227.85-86 \|\|

*sahāsanamabhiprepsurutkṛṣ̣ṭasyāpakṛṣ̣ṭajaḥ \|*  
*kaṭyāṃ kṛtāṅko nirvāsyaḥ sphicaṃ vā'pyasya kartayet \|\| 227.85 \|\|*

*keśeṣ̣u gṛhṇato hastaṃ chedayedavicārayan \|*  
*pādayornāsikāyāṃ ca grīvāyāṃ vṛṣ̣aṇeṣ̣u ca \|\| 227.86 \|\|*

The lips of a low class man occupying the seat of a high class man should be chopped off with a mark sealed on his lip. The hands of the one who extends them to catch hold of the hair, feet, nose, neck, scrotum of a high class man should be lopped off by a king.

## \|\| 227.87-88 \|\|

*tvagbhedakaḥ śataṃ daṇḍyo lohitasya ca darśakaḥ \|*  
*māṃsabhettā ca ṣ̣aṇniṣ̣kānnirvāsyastvasthibhedakaḥ \|\| 227.87 \|\|*

*aṅgabhaṅgakarasyāṅgaṃ tadevāpaharennṛpaḥ \|*  
*daṇḍapāruṣ̣yakṛddaṇḍyaḥ samutthānavyayaṃ tathā \|\| 227.88 \|\|*

The one who makes another bleed by his blows should be fined 100 panas and the one who pricks into the others flesh should be fined 24 tolas of gold or silver according to the seriousness of the offence. The one who breaks anyone’s bone should be exiled from the country. The king should get that limb of one’s body annihilated by which he breaks another’s bone; he should also be fined as much as would be necessary for the aggrieved person to spend in getting himself released from the court.

## \|\| 227.89-90 \|\|

*ardhapādakaraḥ kāryo gogajāśvoṣ̣ṭraghātakaḥ \|*  
*paśukṣ̣udra mṛgāṇāṃ ca hiṃsāyāṃ dviguṇo damaḥ \|\| 227.89 \|\|*

*pañcāśacca bhaveddaṇḍyastathaiva mṛgapakṣ̣iṣ̣u \|*  
*kṛmikīṭeṣ̣u daṇḍyaḥ syādra jatasya ca māṣ̣akam \|\| 227.90 \|\|*  
*tasyānurūpaṃ mūlyaṃ ca pradadyātsvāmine tathā \|*

Half portion of leg and hand of a man should be chopped off, who kills a cow, elephant, horse and camel. One who kills small animals should be fined twice Damas. One who kills deers and birds should be fined five hundred panas; and a man who kills insects and worms should be fined one masa of silver and the owner of the animals should be paid his price.

## \|\| 227.91-92 \|\|

*svasvāmikānāṃ sakalaṃ śeṣ̣āṇāṃ daṇḍameva tu \|\| 227.91 \|\|*  
*vṛkṣ̣aṃ tu saphalaṃ chittvā suvarṇaṃ daṇḍamarhati \|*  
*dviguṇaṃ daṇḍayeccainaṃ pathi sīmni jalāśaye \|\| 227.92 \|\|*

Now I tell about punishment for things which are free from ownership. One who cuts off the fruitful trees, should be fined one gold coin and double the fine should be imposed on those who cut a tree near a tank, a thoroughfare or a boundary line.

## \|\| 227.93 \|\|

*chedanādaphalasyāpi madhyamaṃ sāhasaṃ smṛtam \|*  
*gulmavallīlatānāṃ ca suvarṇasya ca māṣ̣akam \|\| 227.93 \|\|*

If one cuts trees void of fruits, he should be fined with Madhyama Sahasa. One who cuts arbours, creepers and floral plants should be fined one masa of gold.

## \|\| 227.94 \|\|

*vṛthācchedī tṛṇasyāpi daṇḍyaḥ kārṣ̣āpaṇaṃ bhavet \|*  
*tribhāgaṃ kṛṣ̣ṇalā daṇḍyāḥ prāṇinastāḍane tathā \|\| 227.94 \|\|*

Even a man chopping grass unnecessarily should be made liable to pay a fine of Karsapana; one who beats another should be fined three rattis of Krsnalas.

## \|\| 227.95 \|\|

*deśakālānurūpeṇa mūlyaṃ rājā drumādiṣ̣u \|*  
*tatsvāminastathā daṇḍyā daṇḍamuktastu pārthiva \|\| 227.95 \|\|*

Out of the fines levied for cutting trees, the king should use his own discretion; he must pay the owner of the trees the price for them and the rest should go to the royal exchequer.

## \|\| 227.96-97 \|\|

*yatrātivartate yugyaṃ vaiguṇyātprājakasya tu \|*  
*tatra svāmī bhaveddaṇḍyo nā’ptaścetprājako bhavet \|\| 227.96 \|\|*

*prājakaśca bhavedāptaḥ prājako daṇḍamarhati \|*  
*nāsti daṇḍaśca tasyāpi tathā vai hetukalpakaḥ \|\| 227.97 \|\|*

If any harm accrues through an untrained driver of a conveyance the fault lies with the master, but if any such thing occurs through a skilful man the fault lies with the driver for which he should be punished. If perchance anything happens through sheer accident none is to blame.

## \|\| 227.98-99 \|\|

*dra vyāṇi yo haredyasya jñānato'jñānato'pi vā \|*  
*sa tasyotpādayettuṣ̣ṭiṃ rājño dadyāttato damam \|\| 227.98 \|\|*

*yastu rajжuṃ ghaṭaṃ kūpāddharedbhindyācca tāṃ prapām \|*  
*sa daṇḍaṃ prāpnuyānmāṣ̣aṃ tacca saṃpratipādayet \|\| 227.99 \|\|*

One who knowingly or unknowingly usurps the properly of another should appease the man whose property he usurps and pay a fine to the sovereign. One who steals away a rope Ifom a well or breaks away the place where drinking water is supplied to the passers-by should be fined one ma§a of gold and the stolen articles should be made good and he should satisfy the master of the well.

## \|\| 227.100-102 \|\|

*dhānyaṃ daśabhyaḥ kumbhebhyo harato'bhyadhikaṃ vadhaḥ \|*  
*śeṣ̣e'pyekādaśaguṇaṃ tasya daṇḍaṃ prakalpayet \|\| 227.100 \|\|*

*tathā bhakṣ̣yānnapānānāṃ na tathā'pyadhike vadhaḥ \|*  
*suvarṇarajatādīnāmuttamānāṃ ca vāsasām \|\| 227.101 \|\|*

*puruṣ̣āṇāṃ kulīnānāṃ nārīṇāṃ ca viśeṣ̣ataḥ \|*  
*mahāpaśūnāṃ haraṇe śastrāṇāmauṣ̣adhasya ca \|\| 227.102 \|\|*  
*mukhyānāṃ caiva ratnānāṃ haraṇe vadhamarhati \|*

A persons stealing more than ten jars of grain should be killed and the one who steals less than that should be fined eleven times more the value of the stolen grain. The man stealing more than 10 jars of eatables should also be fined eleven times the value of the stolen things; but he should not be killed and a man stealing gold, silver, fine raiments, wife of a high class man, oxen, arms, medicines and principal jewels should be subjected to death.

## \|\| 227.103-105 \|\|

*dadhnaḥ kṣ̣īrasya takrasya pānīyasya rasasya ca \|\| 227.103 \|\|*

*veṇuvaidalabhāṇḍānāṃ lavaṇānāṃ tathaiva ca \|*  
*mṛnmayānāṃ ca sarveṣ̣āṃ mṛdo bhasmana eva ca \|\| 227.104 \|\|*

*kālamāsādya kāryaṃ ca rājā daṇḍaṃ prakalpayet \|*  
*goṣ̣u brāhmaṇasaṃsthāsu mahiṣ̣īṣ̣u tathaiva ca \|\| 227.105 \|\|*

A king should adequately punish one who steals curds, milk, water, juice, bamboos, utensils, clay pots, powders, according to the gravity of the offence. A man stealing cows, buffaloes and horses of a Brahmana should have half his leg cut off immediately.

## \|\| 227.106-108 \|\|
