*aśvāpahārakaścaiva sadyaḥ kāryo'rdhapādakaḥ \|*  
*sūtrakārpāsakiṇvānāṃ gomayasya guḍasya ca \|\| 227.106 \|\|*

*matsyānāṃ pakṣ̣iṇāṃ caiva tailasya ca ghṛtasya ca \|*  
*māṃsasya madhunaścaiva yaccānyadvastusaṃbhavam \|\| 227.107 \|\|*

*anyeṣ̣āṃ lavaṇādīnāṃ madyānāmodanasya ca \|*  
*pakvānnānāṃ ca sarveṣ̣āṃ tanmūlyāddviguṇo damaḥ \|\| 227.108 \|\|*

Those who steal cotton bales, cotton, wines, cowdung, molasses, fish, birds, oil, clarified butter, flesh, honey, salt, rice and cooked food should be fined twice the amount of the price of these articles.

## \|\| 227.109-111 \|\|

*puṣ̣peṣ̣u harite dhānye gulmavallīlatāsu ca \|*  
*anneṣ̣u paripūrṇeṣ̣u daṇḍaḥ syātpañcamāṣ̣akam \|*  
*paripūrṇeṣ̣u dhānyeṣ̣u śākamūlaphaleṣ̣u ca \|\| 227.109 \|\|*

*niranvaye śataṃ daṇḍyaḥ sānvaye dviśataṃ damaḥ \|*  
*yena yena yathāṅgena steno'nyeṣ̣u viceṣ̣ṭate \|\| 227.110 \|\|*

*tattadeva harettasya pratyādeśāya pārthivaḥ \|*  
*dvijo'dhvagaḥ kṣ̣īṇavṛttirdvāvikṣ̣ū dve ca mūlake \|\| 227.111 \|\|*

A man who steals grain out of a field, flowers, creepers and rice should be fined five masas of gold or silver and the theft of ripe crop, vegetables, berries and fruits, should be punished with a fine of 100 Panas if the thief has no sons and if the thief has son than 200 Dandas. The limbs of a thief employed in the accomplishment of his mission should be cut off. There is no sin if a Brahmana who is not carrying anything, through hunger plucks a couple of sugarcanes or berries on his way.

## \|\| 227.112-114 \|\|

*trapusorvārukau dvau ca tāvanmātraṃ phaleṣ̣u ca \|*  
*tathā ca sarvadhānyānāṃ muṣ̣ṭigrāheṇa pārthiva \|\| 227.112 \|\|*

*śāke śākapramāṇena gṛhyamāṇe na duṣ̣yati \|*  
*vānaspatyaṃ phalaṃ mūlaṃ dārvagnyarthaṃ tathaiva ca \|\| 227.113 \|\|*

*tṛṇaṃ gobhyavahārārthamasteyaṃ manurabravīt \|*  
*adevavāṭijaṃ puṣ̣paṃ devatārthaṃ tathaiva ca \|\| 227.114 \|\|*  
*ādadānaḥ parakṣ̣etrānna daṇḍaṃ dātumarhati \|*

Manu has said that there is no crime in taking a couple of cucumbers, two melons in fact any two fruits, two handfuls of grain, as well as the taking of saka in an equally small quantity, the fruits growing on forest trees, forest berries, a small quantity of firewood, grass, the plucking of flowers from elsewhere in the absence of a flower garden for divine worship. A man found doing any of these things should not be punished.

## \|\| 227.115-117 \|\|

*śṛṅgiṇaṃ nakhinaṃ rājandaṃṣ̣ṭriṇaṃ ca vadhodyatam \|\| 227.115 \|\|*  
*yo hanyānna sa pāpena lipyate manujeśvara \|*

О king! О best among the men! a man who kills any animals having horns, nails and fangs and wishing to slay lions, snakes, etc. does not commit any sin.

## \|\| 227.116 \|\|

*guruṃ vā bālavṛddhaṃ vā brāhmaṇaṃ vā bahuśrutam \|\| 227.116 \|\|*  
*ātatāyinamāyāntaṃ hanyādevāvicārayan \|*  
*nā’tatāyivadhe doṣ̣o hanturbhavati kaścana \|\| 227.117 \|\|*

If a Brahmana, a preceptor, a child, a learned man, who comes to attack and kills an Atatayi, then there is no sin in killing of that, (endeavouring to kill some one, a murderer)

## \|\| 227.118-119 \|\|

*prakāśaṃ vā'prakāśaṃ vā manyustaṃ manyumṛcchati \|*  
*gṛhakṣ̣etrābhihartārastathā'gamyābhigāminaḥ \|\| 227.118 \|\|*

*agnido garadaścaiva tathā cābhyudyatāyudhaḥ \|*  
*abhicāraṃ tu kurvāṇo rājagāmi ca paiśunam \|\| 227.119 \|\|*  
*ete hi kathitā loke dharmajñairātatāyinaḥ \|*

One, who commits the sin openly or hidely, becomes sinner. Those who deprive others of their houses and fields, those who indulge with the other class of women whom they ought to avoid, those who set fire to others property, those who give poison, those who treacherously kill another with a weapon, those who act mercilessly against a king are known as Atatayins by the knowers of Dharma.

## \|\| 227.120-121 \|\|

*bhikṣ̣uko'pyathavā nārī yo'pi vā syātkuśīlavaḥ \|\| 227.120 \|\|*  
*praviśetpratiṣ̣iddhastu prāpnuyāddviguṇaṃ damaḥ \|*  
*parastrīṇāṃ tu saṃbhāṣ̣e tīrthe'raṇye gṛhe'pi vā \|\| 227.121 \|\|*  
*nadīnāṃ caiva saṃbhede sa saṃgrahaṇamāpnuyāt \|*

If a beggar, a woman, or a vicious person, though prohibited, enters the house of someone, he should be fined double. Those who are found talking to another woman in a sacred place, forest, or in their own house, those who are detected in breaking a river dam should be punished by the sentence named Sangrahana.

## \|\| 227.122-124 \|\|

*na saṃbhāṣ̣etparastrībhiḥ pratiṣ̣iddhaḥ samācaret \|\| 227.122 \|\|*

*pratiṣ̣iddhe samābhāṣ̣ya suvarṇaṃ daṇḍamarhati \|*  
*naiṣ̣a cāraṇadāreṣ̣u vidhirātmopajīviṣ̣u \|\| 227.123 \|\|*

*sajжayanti manuṣ̣yaistā nigūḍhaṃ vā carantyuta \|*  
*kiṃcideva tu dāpyaḥ syātsaṃbhāṣ̣eṇāpacārayan \|\| 227.124 \|\|*  
*preṣ̣yāsu caiva sarvāsu gṛhapravrajitāsu ca \|*

Nobody should talk to another’s woman and it should be prohibited by the king. If anyone is found talking to women he should be fined a tola of gold, but there is no serious crime in talking to actresses in private or walking with them in private for it is their profession and they should therefore be given a little punishment for doing so. This should be applied for those who earn their livelihood by prostituting going outside from their homes.

## \|\| 227.125-127 \|\|

*yo'kāmāṃ dūṣ̣ayetkanyāṃ sa sadyo vadhamarhati \|\| 227.125 \|\|*

*sakāmāṃ dūṣ̣ayāṇastu prāpnuyāddviśataṃ damam \|*  
*yaśca saṃrakṣ̣akastatra puruṣ̣aḥ sa tathā bhavet \|\| 227.126 \|\|*

*pāradārikavaddaṇḍyo yo'pi syādavakāśadaḥ \|*  
*balātsaṃdūṣ̣ayedyastu parabhāryāṃ naraḥ kvacit \|\| 227.127 \|\|*

One who forcibly violates the modesty of a girl without her desire should be killed speedily. If some one does so with her permission he should be fined two hundred Panas and the person who is assisting, taking share therein, should also be punished with a equal penalty (i.e., death). One who allows another to commit such a thing in his house is also punishable like above man.

## \|\| 227.128 \|\|

*vadho daṇḍo bhavettasya nāparādho bhavetstriyāḥ \|*  
*rajastṛtīyaṃ yā kanyā svagṛhe pratipadyate \|\| 227.128 \|\|*  
*adaṇḍyā sā bhavedrā jñā varayantī patiṃ svayam \|*

The person who forcibly commits such an act with another woman is worthy of being killed outright, but the woman so outraged is faultless. If a virgin after getting menses for the third time in her father’s house, seeks a husband for herself, should not be punished by a sovereign.

## \|\| 227.129-130 \|\|

*svadeśe kanyakāṃ dattvā tāmādāya tathā vrajet \|\| 227.129 \|\|*  
*paradeśe bhavedvadhyaḥ strīcoraḥ sa yato bhavet \|*  
*adra vyāṃ mṛtapatnīṃ tu saṃgṛhṇannāparādhnute \|\| 227.130 \|\|*  
*sadra vyāṃ tāṃ saṃgrahītā daṇḍaṃ tu kṣ̣ipramarhati \|*

One who takes the girl away to a foreign land after marrying her in his own country is a thief and should be killed. If one is carrying away a woman who is without ornaments or property, and is widow, then he is not guilty; but if one carries away a widow with property, he is liable to be punished instantly.

## \|\| 227.131 \|\|

*utkṛṣ̣ṭaṃ yā bhajetkanyā deyā tasyaiva sā bhavet \|\| 227.131 \|\|*  
*yaccānyaṃ sevamānāṃ ca saṃyatāṃ vāsayedgṛhe \|*

A girl who desires to marry a high class man should be given to him according to prescribed rites; but if a girl wants to marry a lower class person, she be confined in the house only.

## \|\| 227.132 \|\|

*uttamāṃ sevamānastu jaghanyo vadhamarhati \|*  
*jaghanyamuttamā nārī sevamānā tathaiva ca \|\| 227.132 \|\|*

If a person of low caste wishes to marry a high class woman and does so would be punished with death; similarly a high class woman marrying a low caste man should also be punished with death.

## \|\| 227.133 \|\|

*bhartāraṃ laṅghayedyā strī jñātibhirbaladarpitā \|*  
*tāṃ ca niṣ̣kāsayedrā jā saṃsthāne bahusaṃsthite \|\| 227.133 \|\|*

If a woman disobedient to her husband on account of being proud of her community, should be driven out of the house and should be kept within resort of many people by the king.

## \|\| 227.134 \|\|

*hṛtādhikārāṃ malināṃ piṇḍamātropajīvinīm \|*  
*vāsayetsvairiṇīṃ nityaṃ savarṇenābhidūṣ̣itām \|\| 227.134 \|\|*

She should be deprived of her authority and given dirty clothes and food just enough for her to live upon when defiled by a man of her caste. She should be lodged in one’s own house in that condition.

## \|\| 227.135 \|\|

*jyāyasā dūṣ̣itā nārī muṇḍanaṃ samavāpnuyāt \|*  
*vāsaśca malinaṃ nityaṃ śikhāṃ saṃprāpnuyāddaśa \|\| 227.135 \|\|*

The head of the woman defiled by a superior man should be shaved and ten locks of hair left on her head and she should be given dirty clothes to put on.

## \|\| 227.136-137 \|\|

*brāhmaṇaḥ kṣ̣attriyo vaiśyaḥ kṣ̣attraviṭśūdra yoṣ̣itaḥ \|*  
*vrajandāpyo bhavedrā jñā daṇḍamuttamasāhasam \|\| 227.136 \|\|*

*vaiśyāgame ca viprasya kṣ̣attriyasyāntyajāgame \|*  
*madhyamaṃ prathamaṃ vaiśyo daṇḍyaḥ śūdrā gamādbhavet \|\| 227.137 \|\|*

A Brahmana, Ksatriya and a Vais'ya who indulges with a Ksatriya, Vais'ya and Sudra woman in lower order should be punished Uttama Sahasa (1080 Panas); and if a Brahmana indulges with a Vaisya woman, or a Ksatriya with a Sudra woman, they should be fined Madhyama Sahasa and if a Vais'ya indulges with a Sudra woman, he would be fined Prathama Sahasa.

## \|\| 227.138-139 \|\|

*śūdra ḥ! savarṇāgamane śataṃ daṇḍyo mahīkṣ̣itā \|*  
*vaiśyastu dviguṇaṃ rājankṣ̣attriyastriguṇaṃ tathā \|\| 227.138 \|\|*

*brāhmaṇaśca bhaveddaṇḍyastathā rājaṃścaturguṇam \|*  
*aguptāsu bhaveddaṇḍaḥ suguptāsvadhiko bhavet \|\| 227.139 \|\|*

O king! a Sudra should be fined 100 Panas for having illicit connection with a woman of his own community. If a Vaisya does so with a Vaisya woman will be fined twice, if a Ksatriya does so with a woman of his caste will be fined triple of that amount and four times the amount in case of a Brahmana when he does illicit connection with a Brahmana woman. This amount of fine is said for those women who are without any guardianship; but it should be increased if the crime committed with a woman who is under guardianship.

## \|\| 227.140 \|\|

*mātā pitṛṣ̣vasā śvaśrūrmātulānī pitṛvyajā \|*  
*pitṛvyasakhiśiṣ̣yastrī bhaginī tatsakhī tathā \|*  
*bhrātṛbhāryāgame pūrvāddaṇḍastu dviguṇo bhavet \|\| 227.140 \|\|*

One who has illicit connection with the sister of his father or mother, mother-in-law, maternal uncle’s wife, uncle’s daughter, aunt, sister, wife of a friend or a disciple, a brother’s wife, should be fined twice the amount of fine as above mentioned.

## \|\| 227.141-142 \|\|

*bhāgineyī tathā caiva rājapatnī tathaiva ca \|*  
*tathā pravrajitā nārī varṇotkṛṣ̣ṭā tathaiva ca \|\| 227.141 \|\|*

*ityagamyāśca nirdiṣ̣ṭāstāsāṃ tu gamane naraḥ \|*  
*śiśnasyotkartanaṃ kṛtvā tatastu vadhamarhati \|\| 227.142 \|\|*

The daughter of a sister, the wife of a king, the exiled woman and a high class woman are not fit to be approached. He who indulges with these, must have his penis cut off and killed.

## \|\| 227.143-144 \|\|

*caṇḍālīṃ ca śvapākīṃ ca gacchanvadhamavāpnuyāt \|\| 227.143 \|\|*

*tiryagyoniṃ ca govarjyaṃ maithunaṃ yo niṣ̣evate \|*  
*vapanaṃ prāpnuyāddaṇḍaṃ tasyāśca yavasodakam \|\| 227.144 \|\|*

One who indulges with a Candala’s wife, who eats dog’s flesh, should be killed; and one who has illicit connection with animals except cow, should be shaved his head and that animal should be served with food and water etc.

## \|\| 227.145 \|\|

*suvarṇaṃ ca bhaveddaṇḍyo gāṃ vrajanmanujottama \|*  
*veśyāgāmī dvijo daṇḍyo veśyāśulkasamaṃ paṇam \|\| 227.145 \|\|*

If a person indulges with a cow should be fined a gold piece and a twice-born indulging with a prostitute should be fined equal to her wages.

## \|\| 227.146 \|\|

*gṛhītvā vetanaṃ veśyā lobhādanyatra gacchati \|*  
*vetanaṃ dviguṇaṃ dadyāddaṇḍaṃ ca dviguṇaṃ tathā \|\| 227.146 \|\|*

If a prostitute after getting her wages from anyone, goes to another person she should be fined double the amount paid to her in advance, besides the twice punishment.

## \|\| 227.147 \|\|

*anyamuddiśya yo veśyāṃ nayedanyasya kāraṇāt \|*  
*tasya daṇḍo bhavedrā jansuvarṇasya ca māṣ̣akam \|\| 227.147 \|\|*

О king! If a man takes a call-girl to another person after promising her to some particular individual should be fined a masa of gold.

## \|\| 227.148 \|\|

*nītvā bhogānna yo dadyāddāpyo dviguṇavetanam \|*  
*rājñaśca dviguṇaṃ daṇḍaṃ tathā dharmo na hīyate \|\| 227.148 \|\|*

One who after taking a whore does not indulge with her, the king should make him pay her twice as much and should levy a similar amount of fine for himself. Dharma will not thereby be upset.

## \|\| 227.149 \|\|

*bahūnāṃ vrajatāmekāṃ sarve te dviguṇaṃ damam \|*  
*dadyuḥ pṛthakpṛthaksarve daṇḍaṃ ca dviguṇaṃ param \|\| 227.149 \|\|*

If many people forcibly indulge with a concubine at once, the king should make each one of them pay her double the amount of her wages.

## \|\| 227.150 \|\|

*na mātā na pitā na strī na ṛtvigyājyamānavāḥ \|*  
*anyonyaṃ patitāstyājyā yoge daṇḍyāḥ śatāni ṣ̣aṭ \|\| 227.150 \|\|*

Fallen father, mother, wife, preceptor, priests should not be abandoned, but a man doing so otherwise should be fined six hundred gold coins.

## \|\| 227.151 \|\|

*patitā guravastyājyā na tu mātā kathaṃ cana \|*  
*garbhadhāraṇapoṣ̣ābhyāṃ tena mātā garīyasī \|\| 227.151 \|\|*

Fallen Gurus are to be abandoned; and fallen mother should never be neglected. She is superior to all on account of her bearing the child in her womb and nourishing him.

## \|\| 227.152 \|\|

*adhīyāno'pyanadhyāye daṇḍyaḥ kārṣ̣āpaṇatrayam \|*  
*adhyāpakaśca dviguṇaṃ tathā’cārasya laṅghane \|\| 227.152 \|\|*  
*anuktasya bhaveddaṇḍaḥ suvarṇasya ca kṛṣ̣ṇalam \|*

If a student reads in a particular prohibited day, he should be fined of three Karsapana and the teacher is be fined doubled amount. If one is regardless of customs or law, he should be fined similarly. Where no fine is specifically mentioned, gold Krsnalas ought to be inferred.

## \|\| 227.153-154 \|\|

*bhāryā putraśca dāsaśca śiṣ̣yo bhrātā ca sodaraḥ \|\| 227.153 \|\|*  
*kṛtāparādhāstāḍyāḥ syū rajжvā veṇudalena vā \|*  
*pṛṣ̣ṭhatastu śarīrasya nottamāṅgaṃ kathaṃ cana \|\| 227.154 \|\|*

Wife, sons, servants, disciples, brothers should be beaten on their back with a rope or a cane when they commit a fault. They should never be beaten on their heads.

## \|\| 227.155 \|\|

*ato'nyathā praharataḥ prāpnuyāccorakilbiṣ̣am \|*  
*dūtīṃ samāhvayaṃścaiva yo niṣ̣iddhaṃ samācaret \|\| 227.155 \|\|*  
*pracchannaṃ vā prakāśaṃ vā sa daṇḍyaḥ pārthivecchayā \|*

One who does so should be punished like a thief. If a person sets animals to fight with each other or gambles he should be punished by the sovereign according to his discretion.

## \|\| 227.156-158 \|\|

*vāsāṃsi phalakaiḥ ślakṣ̣ṇairnirṇijyādra jakaḥ śanaiḥ \|\| 227.156 \|\|*  
*ato'nyathā hi kurvaṃstu daṇḍyaḥ syādrukmamāṣ̣akam \|*  
*rakṣ̣āsvadhikṛtānāṃ ca pradeyaṃ yairvilupyate \|\| 227.157 \|\|*  
*karṣ̣akebhyo'rthamādāya yaḥ kuryātkaramanyathā \|*  
*tasya sarvasvamādāya taṃ rājā vipravāsayet \|\| 227.158 \|\|*

A washerman should very carefully and cautiously wash fine clothes, on a wooden-plate or on a good stonepiece, he should be fined a masa of gold if he does not do so. If a thing is found missing under the custody of its custodians, they should be made to make it good. If the revenue obtained by servant from the cultivators be not paid to the king’s coffer or to the proprietor, his property is to be ruined and he should be exiled.

## \|\| 227.159 \|\|

*ye niyuktāḥ svakāryeṣ̣u hanyuḥ kāryāṇi kāryiṇām \|*  
*nirghṛṇāḥ krūramanasaḥ sarve karmāparādhinaḥ \|\| 227.159 \|\|*  
*dhanoṣ̣maṇā pacyamānāstānniḥsvānkārayennṛpaḥ \|*

The officials of any estate who spoil the interests of the subjects and who are found to be void of sympathy and full of wickedness should be deprived of all their wealth. Those who persecute the subjects by misrepresenting the mandates of the sovereign should also be similarly dealt with.

## \|\| 227.160-161 \|\|

*kūṭaśāsanakartṛṃśca prakṛtīnāṃ ca dūṣ̣akān \|\| 227.160 \|\|*  
*strībālabrāhmaṇaghnāṃśca vadhyāttatsevinastathā \|*  
*amātyaḥ prāṅvivāko vā yaḥ kuryātkāryamanyathā \|\| 227.161 \|\|*  
*tasya sarvasvamādāya taṃ rājā vipravāsayet \|*

Those who govern intricately who kill women, children, Brahmana and who eat .ashes, should be hanged and the minister or any other official of the state be he a minister or a chief of the judiciary (Pradvivaka) if he is working contrary to the policy of the crown should be banished after being deprived of all his wealth.

## \|\| 227.162-163 \|\|

*brahmaghnaśca surāpaśca taskaro gurutalpagaḥ \|\| 227.162 \|\|*  
*etānsarvānpṛthagghiṃsyānmahāpātakino narān \|*  
*mahāpātakino vadhyā brāhmaṇaṃ tu vivāsayet \|\| 227.163\|\|*  
*kṛtacihnaṃ svadeśācca śṛṇu cihnākṛtiṃ tataḥ \|*

Those who kill Brahmana, indulge in drinking, thieves and those who indulge with preceptor’s wife should be killed. If such a man be a Brahmana he should be banished; with a mark on his body; or they might be branded with different marks and then exiled.

## \|\| 227.164-165 \|\|

*gurutalpe bhagaḥ kāryaḥ surāpāne surādhvajaḥ \|\| 227.164 \|\|*  
*stene tu śvapadaṃ tadvadbrahmahaṇyaśirāḥ pumān \|*  
*asaṃbhāṣ̣yā hyasaṃbhojyā asaṃvāhyā viśeṣ̣ataḥ \|\| 227.165 \|\|*  
*tyaktavyāśca tathā rājañjñātisaṃbandhibāndhavaiḥ \|*

Those who have illicit connection with preceptor’s wife should be marked resembling the female privacy, those who drink should be marked with the sign of a flag hung at a tavern, a thief should be branded with the sign of dog feet and a man killing a Brahmana with the sign of a headless human body. О king, great sinners are not be taken in society of their community. None should speak with them, none should live with them and none should maintain the relation of marriage with them in any condition.

## \|\| 227.166 \|\|

*mahāpātakino vittamādāya nṛpatiḥsvayam \|\| 227.166 \|\|*  
*apsu praveśayeddaṇḍaṃ varuṇāyopapādayet \|*

The sovereign should undertake all their wealth in his custody and plunge it into the waters in the name of Lord Vamna.

## \|\| 227.167-168 \|\|

*sahoḍhaṃ na vinā coraṃ ghātayeddhārmiko nṛpaḥ \|\| 227.167 \|\|*  
*sahoḍhaṃ sopakaraṇaṃ ghātayedavicārayan \|*  
*grāmeṣ̣vapi ca ye keciccorāṇāṃ bhakṣ̣yadāyakāḥ \|\| 227.168 \|\|*  
*bhāṇḍāvakāśadāścaiva sarvāṃstānapi ghātayet \|*

A noble sovereign should not punish a thief having a wife. But when he is caught with all the stolen things with his wife he should be punished without any hesitation. In village those people are also to be punished who help thieves by providing them with food, utensils and shelter.

## \|\| 227.169 \|\|

*rāṣ̣ṭreṣ̣u rājñā'dhikṛtāḥ sāmantāścaiva dūṣ̣akāḥ \|\| 227.169 \|\|*  
*abhyāghāteṣ̣u madhyasthāḥ kṣ̣ipraṃ śāsyāstu coravat \|*

The officials of the state who may have created a depravity among the subjects should also be punished like a thief instantly.

## \|\| 227.170 \|\|

*grāmaghāte maṭhābhaṅge pathi moṣ̣ābhimardane \|\| 227.170 \|\|*  
*śaktito nābhidhāvanto nirvāsyāḥ saparicchadāḥ \|*

If the officials do not run and rescue according to their might, where there is a danger in a village, say a house fallen or when a woman is attacked on the way, should be deprived of all their wealth by the sovereign and then exiled with his family.

## \|\| 227.171-172 \|\|

*rājñaḥ kośāpahartuṃśca pratikūleṣ̣u saṃsthitān \|\| 227.171 \|\|*  
*arīṇāmupakartṛṃśca ghātayedvividhairvadhaiḥ \|*  
*saṃdhiṃ kṛtvā tu ye cauryaṃ rātrau kurvanti taskarāḥ \|\| 227.172 \|\|*  
*teṣ̣āṃ chittvā nṛpo hastau tīkṣ̣ṇaśūle niveśayet \|*

Those who plunder a royal treasure or assist the enemies of the sovereign should also be killed. Those who commit thefts by housebreaking or other similar devices in course of the night should be punished by their hands being cut and they should be hung on a trident.

## \|\| 227.173 \|\|

*taḍāgabhedakaṃ hanyādapsu śuddhavadhena tu \|\| 227.173 \|\|*  
*yastu pūrvaṃ niviṣ̣ṭaṃ syāttaḍāgasyodakaṃ haret \|*

One who breaks the pond should be punished by being drowned, or by any other means thus punished. Those who stop the course of water in a tank, should also be similarly punished.

## \|\| 227.174-176 \|\|

*āgamaṃ cāpyapāṃ bhindyātsa dāpyaḥ pūrvasāhasam \|\| 227.174 \|\|*  
*koṣ̣ṭhāgārāyudhāgāradevāgāravibhedakān \|*  
*pāpānpāpasamācārānghātayecchīghrameva ca \|\| 227.175 \|\|*  
*samutsṛjedrā jamārge yastvamedhyamanāpadi \|*  
*sa hi kārṣ̣āpaṇaṃ daṇḍyastattvamedhyaṃ ca śodhayet \|\| 227.176 \|\|*

Those who break into a royal arsenal or a temple should be killed outright. Those who, in times of no danger, throw unholy things on the royal road, should be fined one Karsapana and the king should make them clear off the road.

## \|\| 227.177-178 \|\|

*āpadgato'thavā vṛddho garbhiṇī bāla eva ca \|*  
*paribhāṣ̣aṇamarhanti na ca śodhyamiti sthitiḥ \|\| 227.177 \|\|*  
*prathamaṃ sāhasaṃ daṇḍyo yaśca mithyā cikitsate \|*  
*puruṣ̣e madhyamaṃ daṇḍamuttamaṃ ca tathottame \|\| 227.178 \|\|*

If these be crupple, old persons, pregnant women and children; a lame man, they will be chastised by mere speech. A physician who purposely spoils the treatment of a patient should be fined with 1060 Panas. Those whose treatment is blameable should be fined Madhyama Sahasa and the false ones should be fined Prathama Sahasa.

## \|\| 227.179-180 \|\|

*chatrasya dhvajayaṣ̣ṭīnāṃ pratimānāṃ ca bhedakāḥ \|*  
*pratikuryustataḥ sarve pañca daṇḍyāḥ śatāni ca \|\| 227.179 \|\|*  
*adūṣ̣itānāṃ dra vyāṇāṃ dūṣ̣aṇe bhedane tathā \|*  
*maṇīnāmapi bhedena daṇḍyaḥ prathamasāhasam \|\| 227.180 \|\|*

Those who break a state umbrella, banner or an idol should be fined 500 gold pieces and made to repair them. Those who break pure articles and also those who break jewels should be fined Prathama Sahasa.

## \|\| 227.181-182 \|\|

*samaṃ ca viṣ̣amaṃ caiva kurute mūlyato'pi vā \|*  
*samāpnuyātsa vai pūrvaṃ damaṃ madhyamameva ca \|\| 227.181 \|\|*  
*bandhanāni ca sarvāṇi rājamārge niveśayet \|*  
*karṣ̣anto yatra dṛśyante vikṛtāḥ pāpakāriṇaḥ \|\| 227.182 \|\|*

One who increases or decreases unjustly the value of anything should be fined accordingly. The prison and the place of capital punishment should be made on a public road at such a place as to enable the sovereign to have an eye on the culprits.

## \|\| 227.183 \|\|

*prākārasya ca bhettāraṃ parikhāṇāṃ ca bhedakam \|*  
*dvārāṇāṃ caiva bhettāraṃ kṣ̣ipraṃ nirvāsayetpurāt \|\| 227.183 \|\|*

Those who break the city walls, ditches or gates should be exiled as well; those who plough not well and instruct the vicious should be exiled.

## \|\| 227.184 \|\|

*mūlakarmābhicāreṣ̣u kartavyo dviśato damaḥ \|*  
*abījavikrayī yaśca bījotkarṣ̣aka eva ca \|\| 227.184 \|\|*  
*maryādāmedakaścāpi vikṛtaṃ vadhamāpnuyāt \|*

One who practices Vaslkarana and Abhicara practices, etc., should be fined 200 Panas. One who sells bad seeds calling them to be good and also one who interferes with the authority of the sovereign should be killed, after being disfigured.

## \|\| 227.185-187 \|\|

*sarvasaṃkarapāpiṣ̣ṭhaṃ hemakāraṃ narādhipa \|\| 227.185 \|\|*  
*anyāye vartamānaṃ ca cchedayellavaśaḥ kṣ̣uraiḥ \|*  
*dra vyamādāya vaṇijāmanardheṇāvarundhatām \|\| 227.186 \|\|*  
*dra vyāṇāṃ dūṣ̣ako yastu praticchannasya vikrayī \|*  
*madhyamaṃ prāpnuyāddaṇḍaṃ kūṭakartā tathottamam \|\| 227.187 \|\|*

The goldsmith who adulterates the articles of manufacture with mischief should be cut down to pieces by weapons and one who taking things from a trader does not pay the price or sells privately those things should be fined Madhyama Sahasa. A man found selling things by speaking a lie should also be similarly dealt with.

## \|\| 227.188-190 \|\|

*rājā pṛthakpṛthakkuryāddaṇḍaṃ cottamasāhasam \|*  
*śāstrāṇāṃ yajñatapasāṃ deśānāṃ kṣ̣epako naraḥ \|\| 227.188 \|\|*  
*devatānāṃ satīnāṃ ca uttamaṃ daṇḍamarhati \|*  
*ekasya daṇḍapāruṣ̣ye bahūnāṃ dviguṇo damaḥ \|\| 227.189 \|\|*  
*kalaho yadgato dāpyo daṇḍaśca dviguṇastataḥ \|*  
*madhyamaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ rājā viṣ̣ayādvipravāsayet \|\| 227.190 \|\|*

If a man finds fault with and blames weapons, sacrifices, asceticism, country idol, chaste woman should be fined 1060 Panas (Uttama Sahasa) and if a similar offence is committed by a group of persons, each one of them should be severally fined twice as much and one who gives rise to quarrels should also be punished.

## \|\| 227.191-192 \|\|

*laśunaṃ ca palāḍuṃ ca śūkaraṃ grāmakukkuṭam \|*  
*tathā pañcanakhaṃ sarvaṃ bhakṣ̣yādanyattu bhakṣ̣ayet \|\| 227.191 \|\|*  
*vivāsayetkṣ̣iprameva brāhmaṇaṃ viṣ̣ayātsvakāt \|*  
*abhakṣ̣yabhakṣ̣aṇe daṇḍyaḥ śūdro bhavati kṛṣ̣ṇalam \|\| 227.192 \|\|*

A Brahmana who eats garlic, onions, ham, chicken and animals of five nails and other uneatablea should be banished by a sovereign; and a Sudra doing so should be fined one ratt! (Krsnala) of gold.

## \|\| 227.193-194 \|\|

*brāhmaṇakṣ̣attriyaviśāṃ catustridviguṇaṃ smṛtam \|*  
*yaḥ sāhasaṃ kārayati sa daṇḍyo dviguṇaṃ damam \|\| 227.193 \|\|*  
*yastvevamuktvā'haṃ dātā kārayetsa caturguṇam \|*  
*saṃdiṣ̣ṭasyāpradātā ca samudra gṛhabhedakaḥ \|\| 227.194 \|\|*  
*pañcāśatpaṇiko daṇḍastayoḥ kāryo mahīkṣ̣itā \|*

Whereas Brahmanas, Ksatriyas and Vaisyas doing so are to be fined fourfold, threefold and twofold respectively greater than Sudra; the one who excites them should be fined twice as much. If one volunteers to finance and thus help them to eat uneatable should be fined four times, one who does not pay where ordered by a donor to do so and one who breaks open a lock or crosses an ocean should be fined 50 panas.

## \|\| 227.195-197 \|\|

*aspṛśyaṃ ca spṛśannāryo hyayogyo yogyakarmakṛt \|\| 227.195 \|\|*  
*puṃstvahartā paśūnāṃ ca dāsīgarbhavināśakṛt \|*  
*śūdra pravrajitānāṃ ca daive pitr! ye ca bhojakaḥ \|\| 227.196 \|\|*  
*avrajanbāḍhamuktvā tu tathaiva ca nimantraṇe \|*  
*ete kārṣ̣āpaṇaśataṃ sarve daṇḍyā mahīkṣ̣itā \|\| 227.197 \|\|*

One who is holy and of a superior class if he touches anything which he ought not, or attempts to do a hard thing, which he is unable to do, or gelds animals, or procures abortion to a maid, or eats in a Sudra’s Daiva and Pitr Karmas and does not attend the invitation after accepting it should be fined 100 Karsapanas.

## \|\| 227.198-199 \|\|

*duḥkhotpādi gṛhe dra vyaṃ kṣ̣ipedandhasya kṛṣ̣ṇalam \|*  
*pitāputravirodhe ca sākṣ̣iṇāṃ dviśato damaḥ \|\| 227.198 \|\|*  
*tulāśāsanamānānāṃ kūṭakṛnnānakasya ca \|*  
*ebhiśca vyavahartā ca sa daṇḍyo damamuttamam \|\| 227.199 \|\|*

One who throws about stones or thorns in the house of a good man should be fined one Krsnala of gold and one who gives evidence in a dispute between father and son should be fined 200 Damas, and if he be a honourable man, he should be fined 800 Dandas and one who gives a false evidence inspite of his being aware of the laws should be fined 800 Panas and one who uses false weights should be fined 1060 panas, (Uttama Sahasa).

## \|\| 227.200-201 \|\|

*viṣ̣āgnidāṃ patigurunijāpatyapramāpaṇīm \|*  
*vikarṇanāsikāṃ vyoṣ̣ṭhīṃ kṛtvā gobhiḥ pramāpayet \|\| 227.200 \|\|*  
*grāmasya dāhakā ye ca ye ca kṣ̣etrasya veśmanaḥ \|*  
*rājapatnyabhigāmī ca dagdhavyāste kaṭāgninā \|\| 227.201 \|\|*

One who kills his wife, son, husband, preceptor with poison or fire, etc., should be punished by his nose being clipped and ears and lips being chopped and then killed near a cow yard. One who sets fire to the farm, crops, stocks or house or indulges with a queen should be burnt in the fire of straw.

## \|\| 227.202-205 \|\|

*ūnaṃ vā'pyadhikaṃ cāpi likhedyo rājaśāsanam \|*  
*pāradārikacauraṃ vā muñcato daṇḍa uttamaḥ \|\| 227.202 \|\|*  
*abhakṣ̣yeṇa dvijaṃ dūṣ̣ya daṇḍya uttamasāhasam \|*  
*kṣ̣attriyaṃ madhyamaṃ vaiśyaṃ prathamaṃ śūdra mardhakam \|\| 227.203 \|\|*  
*mṛtāṅgalagnavikreturguruṃ tāḍayatastathā \|*  
*rājayānāsanāroḍhurdaṇḍa uttamasāhasaḥ \|\| 227.204 \|\|*  
*yo manyetājito'smīti nyāyenāpi parājitaḥ \|*  
*tamāyāntaṃ punarjitvā daṇḍayeddviguṇaṃ damam \|\| 227.205 \|\|*

A king’s writer, if he by some defects more and less, in his writing on a stamp-paper frees a thief, would be fined Uttama Sahasa (1060 Panas). If he be a Ksatriya, he would be fined Madhyama Sahasa; if a Vais'ya, he would be fined Prathama Sahasa and if a Sudra he would be fined half of it. One who defiles a Brahmana by making him eat anything unworthy should also be fined 1060 Panas, if he does so with a Ksatriya the fine should be 405 Panas, if he does so with a Vaisya, the fine should be 270 Panas and in case of a Sudra it should be 135 Panas.

## \|\| 227.206-208 \|\|

*āhvānakārī madhyaṃ syādanāhvāne tathā’hvayan \|*  
*dāṇḍikasya ca yo hastādabhiyuktaḥ palāyate \|\| 227.206 \|\|*

*hīnaḥ puruṣ̣akāreṇa taṃ daṇḍyāddāṇḍiko dhanam \|*  
*preṣ̣yāparādhātpreṣ̣yastu sa daṇḍyaścārdhameva ca \|\| 227.207 \|\|*

*daṇḍārthaṃ niyamārthaṃ ca nīyamāneṣ̣u bandhanam \|*  
*yadi kaścitpalāyeta daṇḍaścāṣ̣ṭaguṇo bhavet \|\| 227.208 \|\|*

One who does not present himself in obedience to a writ-royal or comes unasked and the man who being sentenced effects his escape from the judge and those who are without any manhood should be made liable to a fine of silver or gold as the case may be. A messenger for his fault should be fined half of the above mentioned fine. One who escapes from the lock-up where he is confined to meet his deserts or receive the award of his quota of punishment as codified, should be punished with eight times the punishment above prescribed.

## \|\| 227.209 \|\|

*anindite vivāde tu nakharomāvatāraṇam \|*  
*kārayedyaḥ sa puruṣ̣o madhyamaṃ daṇḍamarhati \|\| 227.209 \|\|*

One who gets another’s hair or nails clipped in course of innocent discussions should be fined 405 Panas.

## \|\| 227.210-211 \|\|

*bandhanaṃ cāpyavadhyasya balānmocayate tu yaḥ \|*  
*vadhyaṃ vimocayedyastu daṇḍyo dviguṇadaṇḍabhāk \|\| 227.210 \|\|*

*durdṛṣ̣ṭyavyavahārāṇāṃ sabhyānāṃ dviguṇo damaḥ \|*  
*rājñā triṃśadguṇo daṇḍaḥ prakṣ̣epya udake bhavet \|\| 227.211 \|\|*

One who sets at liberty a man kept in confinement or a culprit worthy of being set to the gallows should be punished twice as much as prescribed for the real culprit. If the countries of a king do anything unmindfully they should be fined thirty times the amount prescribed which the king should offer to God Vanina.

## \|\| 227.212-213 \|\|

*alpadaṇḍe'dhikaṃ kuryādvipule cālpameva ca \|*  
*ūnādhikaṃ tu taṃ daṇḍaṃ sabhyo dadyātsvakādgṛhāt \|\| 227.212 \|\|*

*yāvānavadhyasya vadhe tāvānvadhyasya rakṣ̣aṇe \|*  
*adharmo nṛpaterdṛṣ̣ṭa etayorubhayorapi \|\| 227.213 \|\|*

If an official of the state inflicts less or more fine than prescribed, he should be made to recoup the shortcomings out of his own pocket. The sin that a sovereign commits in taking the life of an innocent person is just the same as is accrued in protecting a man worthy of being condemned to death.

## \|\| 227.214 \|\|

*brāhmaṇaṃ naiva hanyāttu sarvapāpeṣ̣vavasthitam \|*  
*pravāsayetsvakādrā ṣ̣ṭrātsamagradhanasaṃyutam \|\| 227.214 \|\|*

A Brahmana, commiter of any crime, howsoever serious it may be, should not be condemned to death. He should only be deprived of his wealth and exiled.

## \|\| 227.215 \|\|

*na jātu brāhmaṇaṃ vadhyātpātakaṃ tvadhikaṃ bhavet \|*  
*yasmāttasmātprayatnena brahmahatyāṃ vivarjayet \|\| 227.215 \|\|*

A Brahmana should never be killed for there is a great sin in doing so, one should therefore avoid doing that.

## \|\| 227.216 \|\|

*adaṇḍyāndaṇḍayanrājā daṇḍyāṃścaivāpyadaṇḍayan \|*  
*ayaśo mahadāpnoti narakaṃ cādhigacchati \|\| 227.216 \|\|*

The king who does not punish a man worthy of being condemned and punishes an innocent man merits enormous discredit and goes to hell.

## \|\| 227.217 \|\|

*jñātvā'parādhaṃ puruṣ̣asya rājā kālaṃ tathā cānumataṃ dvijānām \|*  
*daṇḍyeṣ̣u daṇḍaṃ parikalpayettu yo yasya yuktaḥ sa samīkṣ̣ya kuryāt \|\| 227.217 \|\|*

A king should always punish a guilty person after knowing his crime and thinking over all aspects of the offence, in consultation with a twice-born.

## Chapter 228

## \|\| 228.1 \|\|

*manuruvāca*  
*divyāntarikṣabhaumeṣu yā śāntirabhidhīyate \|*  
*tāmahaṃ śrotumicchāmi mahotpāteṣu keśava \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Manu said: — “Lord! pray tell me how peace-offerings (Sant I) are made to avert the ominious signs seen in the celestial, intermediate and terrestrial regions”.

## \|\| 228.2 \|\|

*matsya uvāca*  
*athātaḥ saṃpravakṣyāmi trividhāmadbhutādiṣu \|*  
*viśeṣeṇa tu bhaumeṣu śāntiḥ kāryā tathā bhavet \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. The Lord Fish replied: — “King! I shall now mention to you the ceremonies that one ought to perform to appease the three classes of evils. Out of them those relating to the terrestrial region should be attended to without delay.”

## \|\| 228.3-7 \|\|

*abhayācāntarikṣeṣu saumyā divyeṣu pārthiva \|*  
*vijigīṣuḥ paraṃ rājanbhūtikāmastu yo bhavet \|\| 3 \|\|*

*vijigīṣuḥ parānevamabhiyuktastathā paraiḥ \|*  
*tathā'bhicāraśaṅkāyāṃ śatrūṇāmabhināśane \|\| 4 \|\|*

*bhaye mahati saṃprāpte abhayā śāntiriṣyate \|*  
*rājayakṣmābhibhūtasya kṣatakṣīṇasya cāpyatha \|\| 5 \|\|*

*saumyā praśasyate śāntiryajñakāmasya cāpyatha \|*  
*bhūkampe ca samutpanne prāpte cānnakṣaye tathā \|\| 6 \|\|*

*ativṛṣṭyāmanāvṛṣṭyāṃ śalabhānāṃ bhayeṣu ca \|*  
*pramatteṣu ca caureṣu vaiṣṇavī śāntiriṣyate \|\| 7 \|\|*

3-7. The Abhaya ceremony appeases the evils of the intermediate region.

The Saumya ceremony averts the evils of the celestial region. An ambitions man persecuted by another and desirous of prosperity and of conquering his enemies should perform Abhaya rites to obtain his desires and annihilate his enemies. When one becomes afraid in his abhichara practises (magic or charm for a malevolent purposes) or when one wants to destroy enemies, or when great danger comes up, Abhaya peace-offering should be performed, Saumya-Shanti should be performed by the people suffering from pthisis and other similar diseases. People used to the performance of sacrifices and those wounded should perform also Saumya-Shanti. Vaishnavi-Shanti is to be performed when there is an earthquake, or scarcity of grain, famine, excessive rain, drought, visitation of locusts or raid by daring thieves.

## \|\| 228.8 \|\|

*paśūnāṃ bhāraṇe prāpte narāṇāmapi dāruṇe \|*  
*bhūteṣu dṛśyamāneṣu raudrī śāntistatheṣyate \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. When lower animals and men begin mostly to die and when terrestrial ominous signs become visible, Raudri-Shanti should be performed.

## \|\| 228.9 \|\|

*vedanāśe samutpanne jane jāte ca nāstike \|*  
*apūjyapūjane jāte brāhmī śāntistatheṣyate \|\| 9 \|\|*

9 Brahmi-Shanti should be performed when the Vedic lore begins to decline, atheists begin to multiply and the unworthy ones begin to occupy the position of the worthy,

## \|\| 228.10 \|\|

*bhaviṣyatyabhiṣeke ca paracakrabhaye'pi ca \|*  
*svarāṣṭrabhede'rivadhe raudrī śāntiḥ praśasyate \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Raudri-Shanti should also be best performed when a sovereign ascends his throne, when there is a fear from any hostile monarch, when the country is disunited and when the destruction of enemies is intended.

## \|\| 228.11 \|\|

*tr! yahātirikte pavane bhakṣye sarvavigarhite \|*  
*vaikṛte vātaje vyādhau vāyavī śāntiriṣyate \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Vayavi-Shanti should be performed when an uncommonly high wind blows for three days and all the eatables go bad and diseases arising from wind crop up

## \|\| 228.12 \|\|

*anāvṛṣṭibhaye jāte prāpte vikṛtivarṣaṇe \|*  
*jalā śayavikāreṣu vāruṇī śāntiriṣyate \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Vayavi-Shanti should be performed when the rains hold off, agricultural prospects get ruined or when the tanks run foul.

## \|\| 228.13-16 \|\|

*abhiśāpabhaye prāpte bhārgavī ca tathaiva ca \|*  
*jāte prasavavaikṛtye prājāpatyā mahābhuja \|\| 13 \|\|*

*upaskarāṇāṃ vaikṛtye tvāṣṭrī pārthivanandana \|*  
*bālānāṃ śāntikāmasya kaumārī ca tathā nṛpa \|\| 14 \|\|*

*kuryācchāntimathā’gneyīṃ saṃprāpte vahnivaikṛte \|*  
*ājñābhaṅge tu saṃjāte tathā bhṛtyādisaṃkṣaye \|\| 15 \|\|*

*aśvānāṃ śāntikāmasya tadvikāre samutthite \|*  
*aśvānāṃ kāmayānasya gāndharvī śāntiriṣyate \|\| 16 \|\|*

13-16. Bhargavi-Shanti should be performed when one has to obviate the effects of a curse or spell. And Prajapatya-Shanti is to be performed when there is any irregularity in the delivery of children. Tastri-Shanti (+) should be performed when the vegetables become polluted. Kaumari-Shanti (+) is very beneficial for the your g ones, Agneiyi-Shanti (+) is necessary to subdue fire, and when commands are not duly executed by the servants, when servants begin to perish. Gandharvi-Shanti is performed when horses begin to get unruly and when horses are desired.

## \|\| 228.17 \|\|

*gajānāṃ śāntikāmasya tadvikāre samutthite \|*  
*gajānāṃ kāmayānasya śāntirāṅgirasī bhavet \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. When there is an epidemic among the elephants or when elephants are desired, then Angirasi-Shanti should be performed.

## \|\| 228.18-19 \|\|

*piśācādibhaye jāte śāntirvai nairṛtī smṛtā \|*  
*apamṛtyubhaye jāte duḥsvapne ca tathā sthite \|\| 18 \|\|*

*yāmyāṃ tu kārayecchāntiṃ prāpte tu mārake tathā \|*  
*dhananāśe samutpanne kauberī śāntiriṣyate \|\| 19 \|\|*

18-19. Nairitya-Shanti should be performed when evil-spirits cause danger, Yamya-Shanti should be performed when there is a fear of an untimely death, when one has bad dreams, and when there is a fear of hell Kauveri-Shanti should be performed when riches begin to decline.

## \|\| 228.20 \|\|

*vṛkṣāṇāṃ ca tathā'rthānāṃ vaikṛte samupasthite \|*  
*bhūtikāmastathā śāntiṃ pārthivīṃ pratiyojayet \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Parthivi-Shanti should be performed when the trees and their fruits begin to decline, when riches begin to decline and when prosperity is desired.

## \|\| 228.21-23 \|\|

*prathame dinayāme ca rātrau vā manujottama \|*  
*haste svātau ca citrāyāmāditye cā’śvine tathā \|\| 21 \|\|*

*aryāmṇi saumyajāteṣu vāyavyāṃ tvadbhuteṣu ca \|*  
*dvitīye dinayāme tu rātrau ca ravinandana \|\| 22 \|\|*

*puṣyāgneyaviśākhāsu pitr! yāsu bharaṇīṣu ca \|*  
*utpāteṣu tathā bhāga āgneyīṃ teṣu kārayet \|\| 23 \|\|*

21-23. Agneyi-Shanti should he performed when any untoward things happen before daybreak or during the night time in the first Yama when Hasta, Svati, Chitra or Ashvini aster isms are seen with the Sun in the northwestern corner; or when in the second Yama of day or night Pushya, Vishakha, and Bharani star go with the Sun and ominous signs are seen in the south-eastern corner.

## \|\| 228.24-25 \|\|

*tṛtīye dinayāme ca rātrau ca ravinandana \|*  
*rohiṇyāṃ vaiṣṇave brāhme vāsave vaiśvadevate \|\| 24 \|\|*

*jyeṣṭhāyāṃ ca tathā maitre ye bhavantyadbhutāḥ kvacit \|*  
*aindrī teṣu prayoktavyā śāntī ravikulodvaha \|\| 25 \|\|*

24-25. Aindri-Shanti should be performed when any ills occur in the third l; Yama of night or day when Hob ini or Jyestha star is seen with the Sun and ominous sign occurs in the south-east corner.

## \|\| 228.26-27 \|\|

*caturthe dinayāme ca rātrau vā ravinandana \|*  
*sārpe pauṣṇe tathā’drā ryā!mahirbuÞye ca dāruṇe \|\| 26 \|\|*

*mūle varuṇadaivatye ye bhavantyadbhutāstathā \|*  
*vāruṇī teṣu kartavyā mahāśāntirmahīkṣitā \|\| 27 \|\|*

26-27. Maha-Shanti should be performed when any ills happen in the fourth Yama, night or day when Ashlesha, Ardra, Pushya or Mu la star is seen with the Sun and ominous signs appear in the west.

## \|\| 228.28 \|\|

*mitramaṇḍalavelāsu ye bhavantyadbhutāḥ kvacit \|*  
*tatra śāntidvayaṃ kāryaṃ nimitteṣu ca nānyathā \|*  
*nirnimittakṛtā śāntirnimittenopayujyate \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. When any ills occur at noon during day two propitiatory rites should be performed. Riles performed when there are no disturbances beget no consequence.

## \|\| 228.29 \|\|

*bāṇaprahārā na bhavanti yadvadrā jannṛṇāṃ saṃnahanairyutānām \|*  
*daivopaghātā na bhavanti tadvaddharmātmanāṃ śāntiparāyaṇānām \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. The prescribed propitiatory rites avert the ills as an armour saves one from a volley of arrows.

## Chapter 229

## \|\| 229.1 \|\|

*manuruvāca*  
*adbhutānāṃ phalaṃ deva śamanaṃ ca tathā vada \|*  
*tvaṃ hi vetsi viśālākṣa jñeyaṃ sarvamaśeṣataḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Manu said “Lord! be gracious enough to tell me about the chief and peculiar ominous signs, the consequences “thereof and the ways of averting them, for you are the knower of all things.”

## \|\| 229.2-3 \|\|

*matsya uvāca*  
*atra te varṇayiṣyāmi yaduvāca mahātapāḥ \|*  
*atraye vṛddhagargastu sarvadharmabhṛtāṃ varaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*sarasvatyāḥ sukhāsīnaṃ gargaṃ srotasi pārthiva \|*  
*papracchāsau mahātejā atrirmunijanapriyam \|\| 3 \|\|*

2-3. Matsya said O King! I shall relate to you what the hoary sage Garga told to Atri once upon a time sitting oil the banks of the river Sarasvati when the fiery sage Atri asked the most illustrious Garga.

## \|\| 229.4 \|\|

*atriruvāca*  
*naśyatāṃ pūrvarūpāṇi janānāṃ kathayasva me \|*  
*nagarāṇāṃ tathā rājñāṃ tvaṃ hi sarvaṃ vadasva mām \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Atri asked: — “Sage! pray tell me how men, cities and kings look before their destruction.”

## \|\| 229.5-9 \|\|

*garga uvāca*  
*puruṣāpacārānniyatamaparajyanti devatāḥ \|*  
*tato'parāgāddevānāmupasargaḥ pravartate \|\| 5 \|\|*

*divyāntarikṣabhaumaṃ ca trividhaṃ saṃprakīrtitam \|*  
*graharkṣavaikṛtaṃ divyamāntarikṣaṃ nibodha me \|\| 6 \|\|*

*ulkāpāto diśāṃ dāhaḥ pariveṣastathaiva ca \|*  
*gandharvanagaraṃ caiva vṛṣṭiśca vikṛtā tu yā \|\| 7 \|\|*

*evamādīni loke'sminnāntarikṣaṃ vinirdiśet \|*  
*carasthirabhavo bhaumo bhūkampaścāpi bhūmijaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*jalāśayānāṃ vaikṛtyaṃ bhaumaṃ tadapi kīrtitam \|*  
*bhaume tvalpaphalaṃ jñeyaṃ cireṇa ca vipacyate \|\| 9 \|\|*

5-9. Garga said: — “The gods become angry at the incessant evil doings of men and then untoward things crop up. They are of three kinds, viz. ills pertaining to (1) Celestial, (2) Intermediate and (3) Terrestrial regions.

When stars and planets are malefic celestial, and intermediate portents become visible, e.g., the shooting of stars, the preternatural redness of the sky, modifications in the halo of the Sun and Moon the sight of the city of the Gandharvas in the sky, the unnatural rains, etc., are the portents in the intermediate regions. Disturbances among the movable and the immovable, earthquakes, changes in the waters of the rivers, etc., are the portents of the terrestrial region. The terrestrial portents show a little result and get fructified within a short time.

## \|\| 229.10-12 \|\|

*abhrajaṃ madhyaphaladaṃ madhyakālaphalapradam \|*  
*adbhute tu samutpanne yadi vṛṣṭiḥ śivā bhavet \|\| 10 \|\|*

*saptāhābhyantare jñeyamadbhutaṃ niṣphalaṃ bhavet \|*  
*adbhutasya vipākaśca vinā śāntyā na dṛśyate \|\| 11 \|\|*

*tribhirvarṣaistathā jñeyaṃ sumahadbhayakārakam \|*  
*rājñaḥ śarīre loke ca puradvāre purohite \|\| 12 \|\|*

10-12. The celestial portents produce middling effects; and get fructified within a comparatively longer time. If there is a good rain within seven -days of the happening of any kind of portent the latter becomes void of all effects. All the ills should be averted by the performance of the propitiatory rites, otherwise they are bound to produce their effect; the very terrible ones last for three years by endangering the king, his preceptor and city.

## \|\| 229.13 \|\|

*pākamāyāti putreṣu tathā vai kośavāhane \|*  
*ṛtusvabhāvādrā jendra bhavantyadbhutasaṃjñitāḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Their fructification takes place on the body of the kings, ordinary men, in. the entrance of the city, in the sons or in the treasury.

## \|\| 229.14-25 \|\|

*śubhāvahāste vijñeyāstāṃśca me gadataḥ śṛṇu \|*  
*vajrāśanimahīkampasaṃdhyānirghātaniḥsvanāḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*pariveṣarajodhūmaraktārkāstamayodayāḥ \|*  
*drumodbhedakarasneho bahuśaḥ saphalodgamaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*gopakṣimadhuvṛddhiśca śubhāni madhumādhave \|*  
*ṛkṣolkāpātakaluṣaṃ kapilārkendumaṇḍalam \|\| 16 \|\|*

*kṛṣṇaśvetaṃ tathā pītaṃ dhūsaradhvāntalohitam \|*  
*raktapuṣpāruṇaṃ sāṃdhyaṃ nabhaḥ kṣubdhārṇavopamam \|\| 17 \|\|*

*saritāṃ cāmbusaṃśoṣaṃ dṛṣṭvā grīṣme śubhaṃ vadet \|*  
*śakrāyudhaparīveṣaṃ vidyudulkādhirohaṇam \|\| 18 \|\|*

*kampodvartanavaikṛtyaṃ hrasanaṃ dāraṇaṃ kṣiteḥ \|*  
*nadyudapānasarasāṃ vidhūnataraṇaplavāḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

*śṛṅgiṇāṃ ca varāhāṇāṃ varṣāsu śubhamiṣyate \|*  
*śītānilatuṣāratvaṃ nardanaṃ mṛgapakṣiṇām \|\| 20 \|\|*

*rakṣobhūtapiśācānāṃ darśanaṃ vāgamānuṣī \|*  
*diśo dhūmāndhakārāśca sanabhovanaparvatāḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*uccaiḥ sūryodayāstau ca hemante śobhanāḥ smṛtāḥ \|*  
*divyastrīrūpagandharvavimānādbhutadarśanam \|\| 22 \|\|*

*grahanakṣatratārāṇāṃ darśanaṃ vāgamānuṣī \|*  
*gītavāditranirghoṣo vanaparvatasānuṣu \|\| 23 \|\|*

*sasyavṛddhī rasotpattiḥ śaratkāle śubhāḥ smṛtāḥ \|*  
*himapātānilotpātavirūpādbhutadarśanam \|\| 24 \|\|*

*kṛṣṇāñjanābhamākāśaṃ tārolkāpātapiñjaram \|*  
*citragarbhodbhavaḥ strīṣu gojāśvamṛgapakṣiṣu \|*  
*patrāṅkuralatānāṃ ca vikārāḥ śiśire śubhāḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

14-25. I shall also explain to you the influence of the various seasons of the;-, year on the various portents, that really turn their ills into good-luck, as for instance, the falling of a thunder-bolt, earthquake, the thunder in the evening, loss of agricultural prospects, the Sun and Moon being circled by a halo, the sky being covered with dust, or smoke the directions assuming a red hue at the time of sunrise or sunset, the gush of myrrh from a large number of trees, the increase of cattle, birds, and honey are all very lucky signs during the vernal season, the months of Chaitra, Vaishakha The appearance of a comet or a malignant star, the falling of meteorites, the Sun and sky in the evening turning tawny, the sky getting dark, tawny, red, or ocean-like, the loss of water in rivers, during the summer months are very lucky. The appearance of a rainbow, the falling of a thunder-bolt, lightning and meteors, the peal of laughter, the cracking’s in the earth, the shaking of bridges, earthquake, the overflow of rivers and tanks, the excitement among the horned animals and boars during the rainy season are very lucky. Cold winds, frost, the loud speaking of deer and birds, the sight of apparitions and spirits and voice speaking in the Heavens, the pervasion of smoky darkness in the directions, the blowing of high wind, the sunrise and sunset at great altitudes are very good signs during the Hemanta season. The sight of Divine ladies, Gandharvas, extraordinary things seen in the Vimanas, stars, planets, the Daivavani (celestial voice)

the sound of music coming from the hills and wood, the increase in agricultural produce, the production of juices, in crops are very lucky signs - during the autumnal season. Frost, wind, the production of young ones by the she-goats, birds and mares, the sprouting of leaves in the trees, the shooting of meteors, the sight of extraordinary forms, the sky looking black, the falling of stars are good signs during Sishira, the cold season.

## \|\| 229.26 \|\|

*ṛtusvabhāvena vinā'dbhutasya jātasya dṛṣṭasya tu śīghrameva \|*  
*yathāgamaṃ śāntiranantaraṃ tu kāryā yathoktā vasudhādhipena \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. These are the lucky signs if they occur during the periods mentioned above, if anything otherwise happens, a king should at once take measures to avert those ills

## Chapter 230

## \|\| 230.1-7 \|\|

*garga uvāca*  
*devatārcāḥ pranṛtyanti vepante prajvalanti ca \|*  
*vamantyagniṃ tathā dhūmaṃ snehaṃ raktaṃ tathā vasām \|\| 1 \|\|*

*āraṭanti rudantyetāḥ prasvidyanti hasanti ca \|*  
*uttiṣṭhanti niṣīdanti pradhāvanti dhamanti ca \|\| 2 \|\|*

*bhuñjate vikṣipante vā kośapraharaṇadhvajān \|*  
*avāṅmukhā vā tiṣṭhanti sthānātsthānaṃ bhramanti ca \|\| 3 \|\|*

*vamantyagniṃ tathā dhūmaṃ snahaṃ raktaṃ tathā vasām \|*  
*evamādyā hi dṛśyante vikārāḥ sahasotthitāḥ \|*  
*liṅgāyatanavipreṣu tatra vāsaṃ na rocayet \|\| 4 \|\|*

*rājño vā vyasanaṃ tatra sa ca deśo vinaśyati \|*  
*devayātrāsu cotpātāndṛṣṭvā deśabhayaṃ vadet \|\| 5 \|\|*

*pitāmahasya harmyeṣu tatra vāsaṃ na rocayet \|*  
*paśūnāṃ rudra jaṃ jñeyaṃ nṛpāṇāṃ lokapālajam \|\| 6 \|\|*

*jñeyaṃ senāpatīnāṃ tu yatsyātskandaviśākhajam \|*  
*lokānāṃ viṣṇuvasvindra viśvakarmasamudbhavam \|\| 7 \|\|*

1-7. Garga said: — Where the idols of the Devas begin to dance, shiver, shine like fire; vomit smoke, blood, any unctuous substance, fat; weep, laugh, perspire, stand up, walk, breathe, terrify, eat, throw away the banner, etc., at a long distance, cast their head down; or move from one place to another one should not stay there for the king with his Empire where such things occur, or sins increase, are ruined. Such things forebode ill of (he country where they happen. Such portents manifest through Lingas of the Devas or through the temple where the Deva is installed or through the Brahmanas in the temples. Know that the country is in danger where evil signs are seen when the Devas march in procession in Deva Yatras. One would quit that place even if it he the place of the grand-fathers The mischiefs amongst animals are caused by Rudra; the mischiefs amongst kings are caused by Lokapalas; Svamikartika causes them amongst the commanders of an army and Vishnu, Vasu, Indra, I and Vishvakarma cause the mischiefs among the rest of the creation.

## \|\| 230.8 \|\|

*vināyakodbhavaṃ jñeyaṃ gaṇānāṃ ye tu nāyakāḥ \|*  
*devapreṣyānnṛpapreṣyā devastrībhirnṛpastriyaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Ganesha causes them amongst the chieftains; the Divine spies cause mischief among the spies of a sovereign; and the Divine ladies cause mischief amongst the ladies of a sovereign.

## \|\| 230.9-11 \|\|

*vāsudevodbhavaṃ jñeyaṃ grahāṇāmeva nānyathā \|*  
*devatānāṃ vikāreṣu śrutivettā purohitaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*devatārcāṃ tu gatvā vai snānamācchādya bhūṣayet \|*  
*pūjayecca mahābhāga gandhamālyānnasaṃpadā \|\| 10 \|\|*

*madhuparkeṇa vidhivadupatiṣṭhedanantaram \|*  
*talliṅgena ca mantreṇa sthālīpākaṃ yathāvidhi \|*  
*purodhā juhuyādvahnau saptarātramatandri taḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

9-11. These evil portents by the grahas are caused by Vasudeva. When the Divine images and idols undergo such uncommon changes, the learned in the Vedas, the preceptors of a sovereign should worship the Divine images; with incense, flowers, madhuparka, etc., and then decorate them with ornaments and should sacrifice and offer oblations in the Fire for a week without giving way to laziness.

## \|\| 230.12 \|\|

*viprāśca pūjyā madhurānnapānaiḥ sadakṣiṇaṃ saptadinaṃ narendra \|*  
*prāpte'ṣṭame'hni kṣitigopradānaiḥ sakāñcanaiḥ śāntimupaiti pāpam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. They should also feed the Brahmanas with sweets and other things for a week and on the eighth day give away cows, land, gold, etc., which then averts the effects of all such omens.

## Chapter 231

## \|\| 231.1 \|\|

*garga uvāca*  
*anagnirdīpyate yatra rāṣṭre yasya nirindhanaḥ \|*  
*na dīpyate cendhanavāṃstadrā ṣṭraṃ pīḍyate nṛpaiḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Garga said: — The country where the burning takes place without fire and fuel and where fuel fails to produce it, is sure to be harassed by some foreigners.

## \|\| 231.2-3 \|\|

*prajvaledapsu māsaṃ vā tadardhaṃ vā'pi kiṃcana \|*  
*prākāraṃ toraṇaṃ dvāraṃ nṛpaveśma surālayam \|\| 2 \|\|*

*etāni yatra dīpyante tatra rājño bhayaṃ bhavet \|*  
*vidyutā vā pradahyante tadā'pi nṛpaterbhayam \|\| 3 \|\|*

2-3. Where flesh is cooked only in water; where a part of a kingdom is burnt, where forts, gateways, palaces, temples, catch fire or be struck by lightning; the sovereign is in danger.

## \|\| 231.4 \|\|

*anaiśāni tamāṃsi syurvinā pāṃśurajāṃsi ca \|*  
*dhūmaścānagnijo yatra tatra vidyānmahābhayam \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Where darkness pervades during the day, the sky becomes covered with dust without a dust-storm, smoke pervades without fire; great calamity befalls there.

## \|\| 231.5 \|\|

*taḍittvanabhre gagane bhayaṃ syādṛkṣavarjite \|*  
*divā satāre gagane tathaiva bhayamādiśet \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Where flashes of lightning are visible without clouds, stars are visible during the day time, great ills are sure to happen.

## \|\| 231.6-7 \|\|

*grahanakṣatravaikṛtye tārāviṣamadarśane \|*  
*puravāhanayāneṣu catuṣpānmṛgapakṣiṣu \|\| 6 \|\|*

*āyudheṣu ca dīpteṣu dhūmāyatsu tathaiva ca \|*  
*nirgamatsu ca kośācca saṅgrāmastumulo bhavet \|\| 7 \|\|*

6-7. When stars, planets become mortified and lose their colour or positions; where the stars become unusually mortified, where quadruped deer and birds are seen in cities, Vahanas and conveyances; where fiery weapons become pale; where wealth is being taken away from the Treasury, one should infer that great battle is sure to ensue.

## \|\| 231.8-11 \|\|

*vinā'gniṃ visphuliṅgāśca dṛśyante yatra kutracit \|*  
*svabhāvāccāpi pūryante dhanūṃṣi vikṛtāni ca \|\| 8 \|\|*

*vikāraścā’yudhānāṃ syāttatra saṅgrāmamādiśet \|*  
*trirātropoṣitaścātra purodhāḥ susamāhitaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*samidbhiḥ kṣīravṛkṣāṇāṃ sarṣapaiśca ghṛtena ca \|*  
*homaṃ kuryādagnimantrairbrāhmaṇāṃścaiva bhojayet \|\| 10 \|\|*

*dadyātsuvarṇaṃ ca tathā dvijebhyo gāścaiva vastrāṇi tathā bhuvaṃ ca \|*  
*evaṃ kṛte pāpamupaiti nāśaṃ yadagnivaikṛtyabhavaṃ dvijendra \|\| 11 \|\|*

8-11. Where without fire, sparks appear anywhere, where arrows are fixed in bows in an unusual way, where weapons get deranged, war is sure to ensue. When these bad omens appear, the royal priest should fast for three days and pour offerings of sesamum and ghee into the fire kindled up by the wood of milky trees and afterwards the Brahmanas should be fed and given gold, cloths, lands, which will then avert all the calamities that befall by the rage of fire.

## Chapter 232

## \|\| 232.1-5 \|\|

*garga uvāca*  
*pureṣu yeṣu dṛśyante pādapā devacoditāḥ \|*  
*rudanto vā hasanto vā sravanto vā rasānbahūn \|\| 1 \|\|*

*arogā vā vinā vātaṃ śākhāṃ muñcantyatha drumāḥ \|*  
*phalaṃ puṣpaṃ tathā'kāle darśayanti trihāyanāḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*pūrvavatsvaṃ darśayanti phalaṃ puṣpaṃ tathā'ntare \|*  
*kṣīraṃ snehaṃ tathā raktaṃ madhu toyaṃ sravanti ca \|\| 3 \|\|*

*śuṣyantyarogāḥ sahasā śuṣkā rohanti vā punaḥ \|*  
*uttiṣṭhantīha patitāḥ patanti ca tathotthitāḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*tatra vakṣyāmi te brahmanvipākaṃ phalameva ca \|*  
*rodane vyādhimabhyeti hasane deśavibhramam \|\| 5 \|\|*

1-5. Garga said: — Tim cities where the trees, inhabited by the Devas, begin to cry, laugh, eject sap, drop their branches without any cause or high wind; the plants that are only three years old bear fruit; trees begin to overflow with milk, oily substances, blood, honey, or water; they suddenly dry up without disease; the dried ones begin to sprout,; the fallen ones stand up, the standing ones fall down; all such things forebode ill of them. The weeping of the trees indicates the approach of some epidemic, and the country becomes annihilated by their laughing.

## \|\| 232.6-7 \|\|

*śākhāprapatanaṃ kuryātsaṅgrāme yodhapātanam \|*  
*bālānāṃ maraṇaṃ kuryurakāle puṣpitā drumāḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*svarāṣṭrabhedaṃ kurute phalapuṣpamathāntare \|*  
*kṣayaḥ sarvatra gokṣīre snehe durbhikṣalakṣaṇam \|\| 7 \|\|*

6-7. The breaking down of their branches foretells a war, the bearing of fruits by the three years’ old plants means the death of babies; plethora of fruit and flowers means the disunion in the empire, the flow of milk indicates the loss of milk in cows, and that of oil forebodes a famine.

## \|\| 232.8 \|\|

*vāhanāpacayaṃ madye rakte saṅgrāmamādiśet \|*  
*madhusrāve bhavedvyādhirjalasrāve na varṣati \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. The flow of wine means the destruction of conveyances, the flow of blood foretells war; the flow of honey means diffusion of great diseases, - i and the flow of water means drought

## \|\| 232.9 \|\|

*arogaśoṣaṇaṃ jñeyaṃ brahmandurbhikṣalakṣaṇam \|*  
*śuṣkeṣu saṃprarohastu vīryamannaṃ ca hīyate \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The drying up of trees without disease means famine; the sprouting of the dried op trees means the loss of vitality and grain.

## \|\| 232.10 \|\|

*utthāne patitānāṃ ca bhayaṃ bhedakaraṃ bhavet \|*  
*sthānātsthānaṃ tu gamane deśabhaṅgastathā bhavet \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. There is danger of disunion foretold by the fallen trees standing up and the standing ones falling down, and their moving from one place to another means the annihilation of the country.

## \|\| 232.11 \|\|

*jvalatsvapi ca vṛkṣeṣu rudatsvapi dhanakṣayam \|*  
*etatpūjitavṛkṣeṣu sarvaṃ rājño vipadyate \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. There is loss of wealth where the trees begin to weep or laugh and their barks are burnt. These are the portents which transpire through adorable trees.

## \|\| 232.12-14 \|\|

*puṣpe phale vā vikṛte rājño mṛtyuṃ tathā’diśet \|*  
*anyeṣu caiva vṛkṣeṣu vṛkṣotpāteṣvatandri taḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*ācchādayitvā taṃ vṛkṣaṃ gandhamālyairvibhūṣayet \|*  
*vṛkṣopari tathā chatraṃ kuryātpāpapraśāntaye \|\| 13 \|\|*

*śivamabhyarcayeddevaṃ paśuṃ cāsmai nivedayet \|*  
*rudre bhya iti vṛkṣeṣu hutvā rudraṃ japettataḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

12-14. Where the fruits and flowers of trees undergo change the sovereign is sure to die. Such ill-forebodings should be averted. The tree in which the above signs appear should be covered with clothe and adored with sandal, incense and then an umbrella should be stretched over it. Then Lord Shiva should be worshipped and an animal should be sacrificed near the tree.

## \|\| 232.15 \|\|

*madhvājyayuktena tu pāyasena saṃpūjya viprāṃśca bhuvaṃ ca dadyāt \|*  
*gītena nṛtyena tathā'rcayettu devaṃ haraṃ pāpavināśahetoḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Then the mantra “Rudrebhyoh, etc.” should be uttered and oblations offered unto Fire and the Rudra Mantra is to be muttered. Afterwards Brahmanas should be worshipped and fed with clarified butter, rice cooked in milk and sugar, sugar, etc., and then give them presents of land. Then rejoicings should be held in the house and Lord Shiva should be worshipped with music and dancing.

## Chapter 233

## \|\| 233.1-2 \|\|

*garga uvāca*  
*ativṛṣṭiranāvṛṣṭirdurbhikṣādi bhayaṃ matam \|*  
*anṛtau tu divā'nantā vṛṣṭirjñeyā bhayānakā \|\| 1 \|\|*

*anabhre vaikṛtā caiva vijñeyā rājamṛtyave \|*  
*śītoṣṇānāṃ viparyāse nṛpāṇāṃ ripujaṃ bhayam \|\| 2 \|\|*

1-2. Garga said: — There is always fear of a famine by excess of rain as well as by drought or want of rain. Copious rain at an improper time (other than the rainy season) is dangerous. Rain without clouds means death of a sovereign and the weather getting warm and cold at unusual times means danger to the sovereign from his foes.

## \|\| 233.3 \|\|

*śoṇitaṃ varṣate yatra tatra śastrabhayaṃ bhavet \|*  
*aṅgārapāṃśuvarṣeṣu nagaraṃ tadvinaśyati \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Where there is a downpour of blood, there is always fear, from weapons and war, and the city where there is a rain of dust and cinders perishes.

## \|\| 233.4-5 \|\|

*majжāsthisnehamāṃsānāṃ janamārabhayaṃ bhavet \|*  
*phalaṃ puṣpaṃ tathā dhānyaṃ pareṇātibhayāya tu \|\| 4 \|\|*

*pāṃśujantūpalānāṃ ca varṣato rogajaṃ bhayam \|*  
*chidre vā'nnapravarṣeṇa sasyānāṃ bhītivardhanam \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. Showers of marrow, bones, oily substances mean the increase in the death-rate of men. Showers of fruits, flowers, grain mean a great danger and a downpour of dust, stones and small beings indicate the approach of an epidemic and a shower of bored grains foretells the loss of agricultural prospects.

## \|\| 233.7-8 \|\|

*nirabhre vā'tha rātrau vā śvetaṃ yāmyottareṇa tu \|*  
*indrā yudhaṃ tathā dṛṣṭvā ulkāpātaṃ tathaiva ca \|\| 7 \|\|*

*digdāhapariveṣau ca gandharvanagaraṃ tathā \|*  
*paracakrabhayaṃ brūyāddeśopadra vameva ca \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8. If there be no shadow seen while the sun shines brilliantly, there being no clouds or dust in the sky, it means ill-luck to the country. — 6..If a rainbow is visible towards the north-west during the night in the absence of clouds, if meteors shoot, and the directions become unusually red, and the Gandharva regions are visible and the Sun and Moon surrounded by halos; then there is sure to happen some unrest in the land and fear from some foreign power.

## \|\| 233.9 \|\|

*sūryenduparjanyasamīraṇānāṃ yāgastu kāryo vidhivaddvijendra \|*  
*dhanāni gauḥ kāñcanadakṣiṇā ca deyā dvijānāmaghanāśahetoḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. To avert these ills, sacrifices should be performed in the name of the Sun, the Moon and the Wind and money, cows, and gold should be given to Brahmanas.

## Chapter 234

## \|\| 234.1-6 \|\|

*garga uvāca*  
*nagarādapasarpante samīpamupayānti ca \|*  
*nadyo hradaprasravāṇi virasāśca bhavanti ca \|\| 1 \|\|*

*vivarṇaṃ kaluṣaṃ taptaṃ phenavajжantusaṃkulam \|*  
*snehaṃ kṣīraṃ surāṃ raktaṃ vahante vā’kulodakāḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*ṣaṇmāsābhyantare tatra paracakrabhayaṃ bhavet \|*  
*jalāśayā nadante vā prajvalanti kathaṃcana \|\| 3 \|\|*

*vimuñcanti tathā brahmañjvālādhūmarajāṃsi ca \|*  
*akhāte vā jalotpattiḥ susattvā vā jalāśayāḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*saṃgītaśabdāḥ śrūyante janamārabhayaṃ bhavet \|*  
*divyamambhobhayaṃ sarpirmadhutailāvasecanam \|\| 5 \|\|*

*japtvā vāruṇā mantrāstaiśca homo jale bhavet \|\| 6 \|\|*

Garga said If rivers, lakes, or cascades advance close to the town or recede to a great distance away from it, and if the waters of the tanks and streamlets, etc., become tasteless and if the water of the rivers turns warm, dark, of an unnatural colour, and full of froth and sand if it turns milky, oily, winy, or bloody; the empire where such things happen is bound to pass into the hands of another sovereign within six months from the time of such happenings. When reservoirs make unusual noise, and kindle up, or look as if smoke, fire and dust are coming out of them or water suddenly springs up, without there being dug a well or so, or a multitude of beings plunge into water, and when all the reservoirs begin to produce musical sounds; there is always a great danger of dreadful epidemics. To avert the calamity, Ganges water or other holy water, clarified butter, honey and oil should be poured into the waters and the head should be turned on the mantra sacred to Lord Varuna and sacrificial offerings should be performed in the water.

## \|\| 234.7 \|\|

*madhvājyayuktaṃ paramānnamatra deyaṃ dvijānāṃ dvijabhojanārtham \|*  
*gāvaśca deyāḥ sitavastrayuktāstathodakumbhāḥ salilāghaśāntyai \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Afterwards Brahmanas should be fed with clarified butter, honey, and given cows covered with white cloth and jars full of water.

## Chapter 235

## \|\| 235.1-3 \|\|

*garga uvāca*  
*akālaprasavā nāryaḥ kālātītaprajāstathā \|*  
*vikṛtaprasavāścaiva yugmasaṃprasavāstathā \|\| 1 \|\|*

*amānuṣā hyatuṇḍāśca saṃjātavyasanāstathā \|*  
*hīnāṅgā adhikāṅgāśca jāyante yadi vā striyaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*paśavaḥ pakṣiṇaścaiva tathaiva ca sarīsṛpāḥ \|*  
*vināśaṃ tasya deśasya kulasya ca vinirdiśet \|\| 3 \|\|*

1-3. Garga said: — The bringing forth of children by women at unusual periods, their giving birth to twins, the birth of other beings from human foetus, the birth of mouthless offspring as well as of those having more than ordinary limbs, or of the lower beings, birds, scorpions, snakes mean the destruction of that country and family in which such birth, rakes place.

## \|\| 235.4 \|\|

*vivāsayettānnṛpatiḥ svarāṣṭrātstriyaśca pūjyāśca tato dvijendrā ḥ! \|*  
*kimicchakairbrāhmaṇatarpaṇaiśca loke tataḥ śāntimupaiti pāpam \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. The women giving birth to such progeny should be sent out of the country by the sovereign and he should then adore the women and the Brahmanas are to be fed satisfactorily.

## Chapter 236

## \|\| 236.1 \|\|

*garga uvāca*  
*yānti yānānyayuktāni yuktānyapi na yānti ca \|*  
*codyamānāni tatra syānmahadbhayamupasthitam \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Garga said: — It is a most unlucky sign when first class horses and other similar conveyances do not move in an orderly manner, when made to do so while they go regularly when not intended so. A great danger is sure to come.

## \|\| 236.2-4 \|\|

*vādyamānā na vādyante vādyante cāpyanāhatāḥ \|*  
*acalāśca calantyeva na calanti calāni ca \|\| 2 \|\|*

*ākāśe tūryanādāśca gītagandharvaniḥsvanāḥ \|*  
*kāṣṭhadarvīkuṭhārādi vikāraṃ kurute yadi \|\| 3 \|\|*

*gāvo lāṅgūlasaṃghaiśca striyaḥ strī ca vighātayet \|*  
*upaskārādivikṛtau ghoraṃ śastrabhayaṃ bhavet \|\| 4 \|\|*

2-4. The drums and other sounding instruments not giving any sound when beat or struck or emitting sounds without being struck, the moving of the immovables, the not going of the movable objects when made to move, the sound of the drums, etc., coming from the sky as well as the singing of the Gandharvas, the wooden ladles, axes, etc., undergoing unusual changes, cows fighting among themselves with their tails cocked up and women kill women and changes occur in young ones; these indicate a war.

## \|\| 236.5 \|\|

*vāyostu pūjāṃ dvijasaktubhiśca kṛtvā niyuktāṃśca japecca mantrān \|*  
*dadyātprabhūtaṃ paramānnamatra sadakṣiṇaṃ tena śamo'sya bhūyāt \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Brahmanas should be made to worship Lord Vayu with barley meal and the head should be turned on the formula sacred to Vayu, Afterwards presents should be given to Brahmanas and they should be fed with Paramana and be given fees in abundance.

## Chapter 237

## \|\| 237.1-2 \|\|

*garga uvāca*  
*praviśanti yadā grāmamāraṇyā mṛgapakṣiṇaḥ \|*  
*araṇyaṃ yānti vā grāmyāḥ sthalaṃ yānti jalodbhavāḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*sthalajāśca jalaṃ yānti ghoraṃ vāśanti nirbhayāḥ \|*  
*rājadvāre puradvāre śivā cāpyaśivapradā \|\| 2 \|\|*

1-2. Garga said: — The emigration of wild deer and jackals from the jungles into the town is a bad omen; so is the emigration of village birds and- deer from village into the jungles. The inauspicious howling of jackals fearlessly in front of a royal mansion and the entrance gate of the city is most unlucky. When the land animals go to water and when the aquatic animals come over to land, the time is very inauspicious.

## \|\| 237.3 \|\|

*divā rātriṃcarā vā'pi rātrāvapi divācarāḥ \|*  
*grāmyāstyajanti grāmaṃ ca śūnyatāṃ tasya nirdiśet \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. The roaming about freely of the animals in course of the night, that usually prowl in the day and vice versa as well as the desertion of their usual habitation by the village animals forebode the desolation of the place where such place where such things occur.

## \|\| 237.4 \|\|

*dīptā vāśanti saṃdhyāsu maṇḍalāni ca kurvate \|*  
*vāśanti visvaraṃ yatra tadā'pyetatphalaṃ labhet \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. The sauntering about of the dogs and other animals of habitation in a circle in the evening, and their waiting in an unpleasant chorus, also forebode the desolation of the place where they do so.

## \|\| 237.5 \|\|

*pradoṣe kukkuṭo vāśeddhemante vā'pi kokilaḥ \|*  
*arkodaye'rkābhimukhī śivā rauti bhayaṃ vadet \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. The crowing of the cock in the evening hoarsely, the laughing of the cuckoos and the howling of the she-jackal facing the rising sun are also most inauspicious signs.

## \|\| 237.6 \|\|

*gṛhaṃ kapotaḥ praviśetkravyādo mūrdhni līyate \|*  
*madhu vā makṣikāḥ kuryurmṛtyurgṛhapaterbhavet \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. The swarming of pigeons in a dwelling-house, the coming down of fire on a man’s head, the laying of the honeycomb by the bees within the house, foretell the death of the owner.

## \|\| 237.7-8 \|\|

*prākāradvārageheṣu toraṇāpaṇavīthiṣu \|*  
*ketucchatrāyudhādyeṣu kravyādaṃ prapatedyada \|\| 7 \|\|*

*jāyante vā'tha valmīkā madhu vā syandate yadi \|*  
*sa deśo nāśamāyāti rājā vā mriyate tathā \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8. If fire occurs on an enclosure entrance gate or within a house or on any entrance, or on a shop, mart, banner or weapon and if any such place or things be covered with an anthill or if the honey flows out of a honeycomb in their places, the desolation of the country and the death of its ruler are certain.

## \|\| 237.9-11 \|\|

*mūṣakāñchalabhāndṛṣṭvā prabhūtaṃ kṣudbhayaṃ bhavet \|*  
*kāṣṭholmukāsthiśṛṅgāḍhyāḥ śvāno markaṭavedanāḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*durbhikṣavedanā jñeyā kākā dhānyamukhā yadi \|*  
*janānabhibhavantīha nirbhayā raṇavedinaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*kāko maithunasaktaśca śvetastu yadi dṛśyate \|*  
*rājā vā mriyate tatra sa ca deśo vinaśyati \|\| 11 \|\|*

9-11. If a place be infested with too many rats and locusts, disease arises out of hunger or when there are seen charred pieces of wood bones, and dogs with horns, the diseases of the monkeys occur, where crows are seen with grains in their mouths and those who are skilled in the arts of warfare fearlessly subdue all people then a dire famine is sure to occur; and the people are doomed to bear the sufferings of a great war. If a monarch chances upon a white crow in course of his amorous pastimes he is either destined to die or his country and wealth are on the verge of ruin.

## \|\| 237.12 \|\|

*ulūko vāśate yatra nṛpadvāre tathā gṛhe \|*  
*jñeyo gṛhapatermṛtyurdhananāśastathaiva ca \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. The king in front of whose gateway or in whose palace an owl is visible, is doomed to die or lose his treasure.

## \|\| 237.14 \|\|

*gāvaśca deyā vidhivaddvijebhyaḥ sakāñcanā vastrayugottarīyāḥ \|*  
*evaṃ kṛte śāntimupaiti pāpaṃ mṛgairdvijairvā viniveditaṃ yat \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. To drive away the ill-effects of such unlucky forebodings a sacrifice should be performed, and terrestrial Shanti is to be performed; and fees presents should be given to the Brahmanas, and five Brahmanas should be made to turn their heads on the prescribed formulas viz., Devakapotah, etc.”

Afterwards some cows adorned with gold and cloth should be given away to obviate the impending disaster.

## Chapter 238

## \|\| 238.1 \|\|

*garga uvāca*  
*prāsādatoraṇāṭṭāladvāraprākāraveśmanām \|*  
*nirnimittaṃ tu patanaṃ dṛḍhānāṃ rājamṛtyave \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Garga said There is a fear of sovereign’s death when his palace, gateway, balcony, fort, etc., fall down abruptly

## \|\| 238.2 \|\|

*rajasā vā'tha dhūmena diśo yatra samākulāḥ \|*  
*ādityacandra tārāśca vivarṇā bhayavṛddhaye \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. The directions being covered with dust and smoke, the waning of the Sun, the Moon and the stars foretell the impending danger of a sovereign

## \|\| 238.3-11 \|\|

*rākṣasā yatra dṛśyante brāhmaṇāśca vidharmiṇaḥ \|*  
*ṛtavaśca viparyastā apūjyaḥ pūjyate janaiḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*nakṣatrāṇi viyogīni tanmahadbhayalakṣaṇam \|*  
*ketūdayoparāgau ca cchidraṃ vā śaśisūryayoḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*graharkṣavikṛtiryatra tatrāpi bhayamādiśet \|*  
*striyaśca kalahāyante bālā nighnanti bālakān \|\| 5 \|\|*

*kriyāṇāmucitānāṃ ca vicchittiryatra jāyate \|*  
*hūyamānastu yatrāgnirdīpyate na ca śāntiṣu \|\| 6 \|\|*

*pipīlikāśca kravyādā yānti cottaratastathā \|*  
*pūrṇakumbhāḥ sravante ca havirvā vipralupyate \|\| 7 \|\|*

*maṅgalyāśca giro yatra na śrūyante samantataḥ \|*  
*kṣavathurbādhate vā'tha prahasanti nadanti ca \|\| 8 \|\|*

*na ca deveṣu vartante yathāvadbrāhmaṇeṣu ca \|*  
*mandaghoṣāṇi vādyāni vādyante visvarāṇi ca \|\| 9 \|\|*

*gurumitradviṣo yatra śatrupūjāratā narāḥ \|*  
*brāhmaṇānsuhṛdo mānyāñjano yatrāvamanyate \|\| 10 \|\|*

*śāntimaṅgalahomeṣu nāstikyaṃ yatra jāyate \|*  
*rājā vā mriyate tatra sa deśo vā vinaśyati \|\| 11 \|\|*

3-11. When Rakshasas put on their appearance, when Brahmanas become void of their duties, when seasons are subverted, the unworthy ones are worshipped when stars fall, know these are the signs of death. When the Sun and Moon are eclipsed, when the halos of the Sun and the Moon appear porous; when Ketu rises and when the stars and planets look pale they forebode ills and great danger. Where women are quarrelsome where boys kill boys, where prescribed religions are not practised, where fire in course of propitiatory offerings does not shine well; where the marching of ants from the north into fire takes place, where jars full of water become empty or where the loss of clarified butter occurs or where there is the absence of propitious formulae, the waning of the voice of the Brahmanas, the dimness of the musical instruments in the temples, the hatred towards the preceptors and friends and the worship of the enemies, the loss of the prestige of the Brahmanas and friends, and honoured persons occur, where atheism prevails as to the auspicious effects of Homa and other sacred ceremonies and the destruction of the country or the death of its sovereign is at hand.

## \|\| 238.12-15 \|\|

*rājño vināśe saṃprāpte nimittāni nibodha me \|*  
*brāhmaṇānprathamaṃ dveṣṭi brāhaṇaiśca virudhyate \|\| 12 \|\|*

*brāhmaṇasvāni cā’datte brāhmaṇāṃśca jighāṃsati \|*  
*na ca smarati kṛtyeṣu yācitaśca prakupyati \|\| 13 \|\|*

*ramate nindayā teṣāṃ praśaṃsāṃ nābhinandati \|*  
*apūrvaṃ tu karaṃ lobhāttathā pātayate jane \|\| 14 \|\|*

*eteṣvabhyarcayecchakraṃ sapatnīkaṃ dvijottama \|*  
*bhojyāni caiva kāryāṇi surāṇāṃ balavastathā \|*  
*santo viprāśca pūjyāḥ syustebhyo dānaṃ ca dīyatām \|\| 15 \|\|*

12-15. Now hear the signs that are seen on the impending ruin of a king. The finding of faults of the Brahmanas by the king, the harassing Brahmanas and usurping their wealth, the wish of killing Brahmanas, the disregard of Brahmanas in the performance of religious rites, the presence of anger when anybody asks for cutting, the love for decrying them, the disinclination to praise them, the causing of pain to them out of avarice; not paying attention to one’s own duties, the levying of fresh taxes out of avarice, are also most unlucky signs to obviate the consequence of which Indra with Indrani should be worshipped, Brahmanas should be fed and sacrificial offerings should be made to the Devas. The Brahmanas and good men should be worshipped and; given presents.

## \|\| 238.6 \|\|

*kriyāṇāmucitānāṃ ca vicchittiryatra jāyate \|*  
*hūyamānastu yatrāgnirdīpyate na ca śāntiṣu \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. High class Brahmanas should be given cows, gold, and lands, sacrifices should be performed, and Devas should be worshipped. Thus sins will be destroyed and order restored again.

## Chapter 239

## \|\| 239.1-2 \|\|

*manuruvāca*  
*grahayajñaḥ kathaṃ kāryo lakṣahomaḥ kathaṃ nṛpaiḥ \|*  
*koṭihomo'pi vā deva sarvapāpapraṇāśanaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*kriyate vidhinā yena yaddṛṣṭaṃ śānticintakaiḥ \|*  
*tatsarvaṃ vistarāddeva kathayasva janārdana \|\| 2 \|\|*

1-2. i Manu said: — “Lord! How should a king perform Griha-yogya, Laksha-homa, and Koti-homa the dispeller of all evils? pray tell me all about them.” I want to hear in details the methods how these sacrifices are to be done by a king wanting to avert the danger and desirous of; Shanti.

## \|\| 239.3-6 \|\|

*matsya uvāca*  
*idānīṃ kathayiṣyāmi prasaṅgādeva te nṛpa \|*  
*rājñāṃ dharmaprasaktena prajānāṃ ca hitepsunā \|\| 3 \|\|*

*grahayajñaḥ sadā kāryo lakṣahomasamanvitaḥ \|*  
*nadīnāṃ saṃgame caiva surāṇāmagratastathā \|\| 4 \|\|*

*suṣabhe bhūmibhāge ca daivajñādhiṣṭhito nṛpaḥ \|*  
*guruṇā caiva ṛtvigbhiḥ sārdhaṃ bhūmiṃ parīkṣayet \|\| 5 \|\|*

*khanetkuṇḍaṃ ca tatraiva suṣamaṃ hastamātrakam \|*  
*dviguṇaṃ lakṣahome tu koṭihome caturguṇam \|\| 6 \|\|*

3-6. Lord said: — “King! I shall answer your question fully,, please listen tome.” A sovereign who has the well-being of his subjects, at heart should always perform Griha-yajna and Laksha-homa. Griha-yajna should be performed at the confluence of rivers as well as before the Divine images and on the plains. First a king should find out a suitable spot in company of his preceptor and Ritvikas which should be a level piece of ground. A sacrificial pit measuring one hand in length and breadth should be dug then. The sacrificial pit for a Laksha-homa should double the size (i.e., two hands in length and breadth) and that tor a Koti-homa, four times (i.e., four hands in length and breadth).

## \|\| 239.7-8 \|\|

*yugmāstu ṛtvijaḥ proktā aṣṭau vai vedapāragāḥ \|*  
*kandamūlaphalāhārā dadhikṣīrāśino'pi vā \|\| 7 \|\|*

*vedyāṃ nidhāpayeccaiva ratnāni vividhāni ca \|*  
*sikatāpariveṣāśca tato'gniṃ ca samindhayet \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8. There should be two Ritvikas and eight Brahmanas well-versed in the Vedas who should live on fruits or curds and milk before they perform the sacrifice. Various kinds of gems should be thrown by them on the pit, the enclosure of sand should be made and afterwards sacrificial fire should be lit.

## \|\| 239.9-14 \|\|

*gāyatr! yā daśasāhasraṃ mānastokena ṣaḍguṇaḥ \|*  
*triṃśadgrahāṇāṃ mantraiśca catvāro viṣṇudaivataiḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*kūṣmāṇḍairjuhuyātpañca kusumādyaistu ṣoḍaśa \|*  
*hotavyā daśasāhasra bādarairjātavedasi \|\| 10 \|\|*

*śriyo mantreṇa hotavyāḥ sahasrāṇi caturdaśa \|*  
*śeṣāḥ pañcasahasrāstu hotavyāstvindra daivataiḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*hutvā śatasahasraṃ tu puṇyasnānaṃ samācaret \|*  
*kumbhaiḥ ṣoḍaśasaṃkhyaiśca sahiraṇyaiḥ sumaṅgalaiḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*snāpayedyajamānaṃ tu tataḥ śāntirbhaviṣyati \|*  
*evaṃ kṛe! tu yatkiṃcidgrahapīḍāsamudbhavam \|\| 13 \|\|*

*tatsarvaṃ nāśamāyāti dattvā vai dakṣiṇāṃ nṛpa \|*  
*tasmātsarvaprayatnena pradhānā dakṣiṇā smṛtā \|\| 14 \|\|*

9-14. Ten thousand sacrificial offerings should be made by reciting the sacred Gayatri, 6,000 by reciting the formulae ‘manastokenau’, 30,000 by reciting the prescribed formulae of the Navagrahas (nine planets), 4,000 by reciting the formula sacred to Vishnu, 5,000 by reciting the Kushmanda richas, 16,000 by reciting the Kusumadi formulae, and 10,000 by reciting the Badana formulae, and 14,000 by reciting the formulae sacred to Lakshmi, 5,000 by reciting the formulae sacred to Indra. Thus 1,00,000 offerings should be made after which one should bathe out of the sixteen pitchers of the consecrated water containing a piece of gold. Such a bath brings peace to the devotee and then presents given to the Brahmanas avert all the ills of the household. The sacrificial fees given on such occasions are considered of high merit.

## \|\| 239.15 \|\|

*hastyaśvarathayānāni bhūmivastrayugāni ca \|*  
*anaḍudgośataṃ dadyādṛtvijāṃ caiva dakṣiṇām \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Elephants, horses, chariots, lands, clothes, oxen, and 100 cows and buffaloes should be given to the Ritvijas (priests).

## \|\| 239.16-17 \|\|

*yathāvibhavasāraṃ tu vittaśāṭhyaṃ na kārayet \|*  
*māse pūrṇe samāptastu lakṣahomo narādhipa \|\| 16 \|\|*

*lakṣahomasya rājendra vidhānaṃ parikīrtitam \|*  
*idānīṃ koṭihomasya śṛṇu tvaṃ kathayāmyaham \|\| 17 \|\|*

16-17. Presents should be given according to the means of the devotee, and he should never be miserly here. Laksha-homa should be concluded within a month.

## \|\| 239.18 \|\|

*gaṅgātaṭe'tha yamunāsarasvatyornareśvara \|*  
*narmadādevikāyāstu taṭe homo vidhīyate \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Koti-homa should be performed on the banks of the Ganges, on the confluence of the Yamuna and the Sarasvati or on the confluence of the Narmada and Devika.

## \|\| 239.19 \|\|

*tatrāpi ṛtvijaḥ kāryā ravinandana ṣoḍaśa \|*  
*sarvahome tu rājarṣe dadyādvipre'thavā dhanam \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. There should be 16 Ritvijas in this Laksha-homa and presents should be given to Brahmanas on the occasions of each sacrifice.

## \|\| 239.20-21 \|\|

*ṛtvigācāryasahito dīkṣāṃ sāṃvatsarīṃ sthitaḥ \|*  
*caitre māse tu saṃprāpte kārtike vā viśeṣataḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*prārambhaḥ karaṇīyo vā vatsaraṃ vatsaraṃ nṛpa \|*  
*yajamānaḥ payobhakṣī phalāśī ca tathā'nagha \|\| 21 \|\|*

20-21. A devotee should first commence the preliminary rites in the month of Chaitra, especially in the month of Kartika; then he should remain initiated for one year with Ritvijas and Acharyas and then sacrifice should be performed or he should perform it once every year. The devotee should live on fruits or milk.

## \|\| 239.22-23 \|\|

*yavādivrīhayo māṣāstilāśca saha sarṣapaiḥ \|*  
*pālāśāḥ samidhaḥ śastā vasordhārā tathopari \|\| 22 \|\|*

*māse'tha prathame dadyādṛtvigbhyaḥ kṣīrabhojanam \|*  
*dvitīye kṛsarāṃ dadyāddharmakāmārthasādhanīm \|\| 23 \|\|*
