22-23. Barley, rice, sesamum, mustard, Mashakalai, and Palasha fuel are best for the sacrificial fuel, and streamlets of clarified butter should also be run on walls. The priests should be fed with milk daring the first month and rice and pulse cooked together, which helps one in Dharma, Kama, and Artha, should be used during the next month.

## \|\| 239.24 \|\|

*tṛtīye māsi saṃyāvo deyo vai ravinandana \|*  
*caturthe modakā deyā viprāṇāṃ prītimāvahan \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. During the third month they should live on barley gruel and in the fourth month laddus should be given to the Brahmana priets.

## \|\| 239.25-26 \|\|

*pañcame dadhibhaktaṃ tu ṣaṣṭhe vai saktubhojanam \|*  
*pūpāśca saptame deyā hyaṣṭame ghṛtapūpakāḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*ṣaṣṭyodanaṃ ca navame daśame yavaṣaṣṭikā \|*  
*ekādaśe samāṣaṃ tu bhojanaṃ ravinandana \|\| 26 \|\|*

25-26. During the fifth month they should be given curds and rice, Sattu during the sixth month, malapuas during the seventh month, ghevara during the eighth month, Samthi rice during the ninth month, barley during the tenth month and urada during the eleventh month. The Ritvijas should thus be fed.

## \|\| 239.27-33 \|\|

*dvādaśa tvatha saṃprāpte māse ravikulodvaha \|*  
*ṣaḍrasaiḥ saha bhakṣyaiśca bhojanaṃ sārvakāmikam \|\| 27 \|\|*

*deyā dvijānāṃ rājendra māsi māsi ca dakṣiṇāḥ \|*  
*ahatavāsaḥsaṃvīto dinārdhaṃ homayecchuciḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

*tasmātsadotthitairbhāvyaṃ yajamānaiḥ saha dvijaiḥ \|*  
*indrā dyādisurāṇāṃ ca prīṇanaṃ sārvakāmikam \|\| 29 \|\|*

*kṛtvā surāṇāṃ rājendra paśughātasamanvitam \|*  
*sarvadānāni devānāmagniṣṭomaṃ ca kārayet \|\| 30 \|\|*

*evaṃ kṛtvā vidhānena pūrṇāhutiḥ śate śate \|*  
*sahasre dviguṇā deyā yāvacchatasahasrakam \|\| 31 \|\|*

*puroḍāśastataḥ sādhyo devatārthe ca ṛtvijaiḥ \|*  
*yukto vasanmānavaiśca punaḥ prāptārcanāndvijān \|\| 32 \|\|*

*prīṇayitvā surānsarvānpitrineva tataḥ kramāt \|*  
*kṛtvā śāstravidhānena piṇḍānāṃ ca samarpaṇam \|\| 33 \|\|*

27-33. During the twelfth month they should he given all the various kinds of eatables and fees should be given to them every month. The Brahmanas should put on pure clothes (never torn clothes) and perform sacrifice in the noon and the devotee should always remain with the Brahmanas which pleases Indra and other gods, and for the satisfaction of the gods animal sacrifice should also be made. Afterwards Agnishtoma sacrifice should also be performed; afterwards Purnahutis is to be duly performed. In one hundred Homas two hundred Purnah utis are to be performed; in one thousand (1,000) Homas twice that (i.e.) 2,000 Purnah utis are to be performed; thus up to one lakh Homas, this rule of doubling is to be followed. The Brahmanas should their offer the sacrificial offerings for the Purodasha for the satisfaction of the Devas. Afterwards the devotee should adore the manes, and offer libations as prescribed. Thus the ceremony Is completed.

## \|\| 239.34-37 \|\|

*samāsau tasya homasya viprāṇāmatha dakṣiṇām \|*  
*samāṃ caiva tulāṃ kṛtvā baddhvā śikyadvayaṃ punaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

*ātmānaṃ tolayettatra patnīṃ caiva dvitīyakām \|*  
*suvarṇena tathā’tmānaṃ rajatena tathā priyām \|\| 35 \|\|*

*tolayitvā dadedrā jā vittaśāṭhyavivarjitaḥ \|*  
*dadecchatasahasraṃ tu rūpyasya kanakasya ca \|\| 36 \|\|*

*sarvasvaṃ vā dadattatra rājasūyaphalaṃ labhat \|*  
*evaṃ kṛtvā vidhānena viprāṃstāṃśca visarjayet \|\| 37 \|\|*

34-37. A king should give handsome Dakshinas on the conclusion of this sacrifice. He should give his weight in gold and queen’s weight in silver.

He should not be led away by avarice. He should give one lakh umbrellas of gold or silver. In fact if anyone gives away everything in this sacrifice, he- will get the benefits of the Rajasuya sacrifice. The Ritvijas should, then be dismissed.

## \|\| 239.38 \|\|

*prīyatāṃ puṇḍarīkākṣaḥ sarvayajñeśvaro hariḥ \|*  
*tasmiṃstuṣṭe jagattuṣṭaṃ prīṇite prīṇitaṃ bhavet \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Then the following is to be recited. Let the lotus eyed Hari, the Lord of sacrifices be pleased. When Hari is pleased, the whole world becomes satisfied.

## \|\| 239.39-40 \|\|

*evaṃ sarvopaghāte tu devamānuṣakārite \|*  
*iyaṃ śāntistavā’khyātā yāṃ kṛtvā sukṛtī bhavet \|\| 39 \|\|*

*na śocejжanmamaraṇe kṛtākṛtavicāraṇe \|*  
*sarvatīrtheṣu yatsnānaṃ sarvayajñeṣu yatphalam \|*  
*tatphalaṃ samāvāpnoti kṛtvā yajñatrayaṃ nṛpa \|\| 40 \|\|*

39-40. Thus I have described to you all the ills due to Devas, men or other beings and show they ought he appeased and the devotee the performer of virtuous when he does not grieve even in death. In fact, nothing, more is left for him to accomplish. He gets the benefit of having bathed in all the sacred tirthas.

## Chapter 240

## \|\| 240.1 \|\|

*manuruvāca*  
*idānīṃ sarvadharmajña sarvaśāstraviśārada \|*  
*yātrākālavidhānaṃ me kathayasva mahīkṣitām \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Manu said: — Lord! now be pleased to tell me when and how a king should march for war?

## \|\| 240.2-6 \|\|

*matsya uvāca*  
*yadā manyeta nṛpatirākrandena balīyasā \|*  
*pārṣṇigrāhābhibhūto'ristadā yātrāṃ prayojayet \|\| 2 \|\|*

*yodhānmatvā prabhūtāṃśca prabhūtaṃ ca balaṃ mama \|*  
*mūlarakṣāsamartho'smi tadā yātrāṃ prayojayet \|\| 3 \|\|*

*aśuddhapārṣṇirnṛpatirna tu yātrāṃ prayojayet \|*  
*pārṣṇigrāhādhikaṃ sainyaṃ mūle nikṣipya ca vrajet \|\| 4 \|\|*

*caitr! yāṃ vā mārgaśīrṣyāṃ vā yātrāṃ yāyānnarādhipaḥ \|*  
*caitr! yāṃ paśyecca naidāghaṃ hanti puṣṭiṃ ca śāradīm \|\| 5 \|\|*

*etadeva viparyastaṃ mārgaśīrṣyāṃ narādhipaḥ \|*  
*śatrorvā vyasane yāyātkāla eva sudurlabhaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

2-6. Matsya said: — A king should march when he finds his enemy pressed by some valiant king or his tributary chiefs. He should first see that he has abundance of strength and fighting men and materials and then he should leave a powerful guard to protect his stronghold before starting to face his enemy, without which he should never set out. To protect his own country, the base of all operations, there should be many: more, fighting persons and generals than the other kings and chiefs engaged in conquering his enemy. He should never start when his tributary chiefs and the neighboring kings are not subject to him. It becomes very hot during the month of Chaitra, so Chaitra should be chosen for an expedition as far as possible; or the month of Agrahayana when rains cause might be chosen otherwise he should take every advantage of his enemies’ adverse circumstances.

## \|\| 240.7 \|\|

*divyāntarikṣakṣitijairutpātaiḥ pīḍitaṃ param \|*  
*ṣaḍakṣapīḍāsaṃtaptaṃ pīḍitaṃ ca tathā grahaiḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. A king should take every advantage of the planets and celestial, and terrestrial influences that completely harass for his enemy; or when his enemy has broken his hands or legs or is become defective in any of his organs.

## \|\| 240.8-13 \|\|

*jvalantī ca tathaivolkā diśaṃ yāṃ ca prapadyate \|*  
*bhūkampolkādi saṃyāti yāṃ ca ketuḥ prasūyate \|\| 8 \|\|*

*nirghātaśca patedyatra tāṃ yāyādvasudhādhipaḥ \|*  
*svabalavyasanopetaṃ tathā durbhikṣapīḍitam \|\| 9 \|\|*

*saṃbhūtāntarakopaṃ ca kṣipraṃ prāyādariṃ nṛpaḥ \|*  
*yūkāmākṣīkabahulaṃ bahupaṅkaṃ tathā’vilam \|\| 10 \|\|*

*nāstikaṃ bhinnamaryādaṃ tathā'maṅgalavādinam \|*  
*apetaprakṛtiṃ caiva niḥsāraṃ ca tathā jayet \|\| 11 \|\|*

*vidviṣṭanāyakaṃ sainyaṃ tathā bhinnaṃ parasparam \|*  
*vyasanāsaktanṛpatiṃ balaṃ rājā'bhiyojayet \|\| 12 \|\|*

*sainikānāṃ na śastrāṇi sphurantyaṅgāni yatra ca \|*  
*duḥsvapnāni ca paśyanti balaṃ tadabhiyojayet \|\| 13 \|\|*

8-13. He should set out to the direction that gets unusually red where there are myriads of falling meteors, or thunderbolts when there has been an earthquake, and meteors come out of the earth, when a comet is visible. He should also go to fight against the country when people lead a vicious life, where there are too many flies and insects, where the king is addicted to some particular hobby and is oblivious of his affairs, where the people are atheists and disrespectful, the country that is under the rage of diseases, plague or famine. He should certainly encounter foe upset with rage. A king is undoubtedly victorious when he invades the country of the infidels, of the thoughtless and of those who have bad generals in the army. Where the people are divided against themselves.

## \|\| 240.14-15 \|\|

*utsāhabalasaṃpannaḥ svānuraktabalastathā \|*  
*tuṣṭapuṣṭabalo rājā parānabhimukho vrajet \|\| 14 \|\|*

*śarīrasphuraṇe dhanye tathā duḥsvapnanāśane \|*  
*nimitte śakune dhanye jāte śatrupuraṃ vrajet \|\| 15 \|\|*

14-15. A king is to start against his enemy whose soldiers have no weapons and fighting materials, whose bodies tremble, and who see bad dreams. A king who is full of ambition, hilarity, and has valiant generals in his army and his soldiers energetic and glad; should face his foe. He should at once set ont against his foe when his auspicious limb vibrates and when there are other similar auspicious signs, when the sweet peacocks echo, etc.

## \|\| 240.16 \|\|

*ṛkṣeṣu ṣaṭsu śuddheṣu graheṣvanuguṇeṣu ca \|*  
*praśnakāle śubhe jāte parānyāyānnarādhipaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. He should start to conquer his foe when he is under the influence of the six lucky stars presiding over Janma, Sampat, Kshema, etc., when the planets are auspicious and when the astrologers predict auspicious times.

## \|\| 240.17-19 \|\|

*evaṃ tu daivasaṃpannastathā pauruṣasaṃyutaḥ \|*  
*deśakālopapannāṃ tu yātrāṃ kuryānnarādhipaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*sthale nakrastu nāgasya tasyāpi sajale vaśe \|*  
*ulūkasya niśi dhvāṅkṣaḥ sa ca tasya divā vaśe \|\| 18 \|\|*

*evaṃ deśaṃ ca kālaṃ ca jñātvā yātrāṃ prayojayet \|*  
*padātināgabahulāṃ senāṃ prāvṛṣi yojayet \|\| 19 \|\|*

17-19. A king should be blessed by the Devas, after worshipping them and he should consider the time, place, and circumstances and he should feel himself sufficiently powerful. An ambitious king should not lose the opportunity of vanquishing his foe who is under unlucky stars and has his country and times against him. As a crocodile is subdued by an elephant on land, an elephant by a crocodile in water, a crow by ah owl during the night, an owl by a crow during the day; so should a king start against Iris foe taking a measure of the current circumstances.

## \|\| 240.20-22 \|\|

*hemante śiśire caiva rathavājisamākulām \|*  
*kharoṣṭrabahulāṃ senāṃ tathā grīṣme narādhipaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*caturaṅgabalopetāṃ vasante vā śaradyatha \|*  
*senā padātibahulā yasya syātpṛthivīpateḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*abhiyojyo bhavettena śaturviṣamamāśritaḥ \|*  
*gamye vṛkṣāvṛte deśe sthitaṃ śatruṃ tathaiva ca \|\| 22 \|\|*

20-22. He should march with a good force of infantry and elephants during the rainy season; of cavalry and chariots during the dewy and cold season; he should march with camels and mules during the hot weather; and with four-fold forces during the vernal season. A king whose infantry is strong can attack his foe with great vigour.

## \|\| 240.23-25 \|\|

*kiṃcitpaṅke tathā yāyādbahunāgo narādhipaḥ \|*  
*rathāśvabahulo yāyācchatruṃ samapathasthitam \|\| 23 \|\|*

*tamāśrayanto bahulāstāṃstu rājā prapūjayet \|*  
*kharoṣṭrabahulo rājā śatrurbandhena saṃsthitaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*bandhanastho'bhiyojyo'ristathā prāvṛṣi bhūbhujā \|*  
*himapātayute deśe sthitaṃ grīṣme'bhiyojayet \|\| 25 \|\|*

23-25. An elephant corps can win a foe situated in a muddy surrounding, or in a woody country, and a cavalry and chariots can vanquish a foe on even land. If the king he helped by a number of allies, he should respect them by presents and kindness. If a king who has a strong mule and camel corps should be subdued during the rains and taken prisoner, he should still fight on as there is chance of his recovery.

## \|\| 240.26 \|\|

*yavasendhanasaṃyuktaḥ kālaḥ pārthiva haimanaḥ \|*  
*śaradvasantau dharmajña kālau sādhāraṇau smṛtau \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. During the winter season a king should have a good store of straw and fire wood to enable him to vanquish his f6e. Vernal season is known as the best time, A king should set out in the summer season against a country that is wetty and covered with snow.

## \|\| 240.27 \|\|

*vijñāya rājā dvijadeśakālau daivaṃ trikālaṃ ca tathaiva buddhvā \|*  
*yāyātparaṃ kālavidāṃ matena saṃcintya sārdhaṃ dvijamantravidbhiḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. A king should always think well over the present circumstances, past and future and take the advice of his minister and Brahmanas before setting out against his enemy.

## Chapter 241

## \|\| 241.1 \|\|

*manuruvāca*  
*brūhi me tvaṃ nimittāni aśubhāni śubhāni ca \|*  
*sarvadharmabhṛtāṃ śreṣṭhaṃ tvaṃ hi sarvaviducyate \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Manu asked: — “Lord! you are the knower of all, so be pleased to tell me the auspicious and the inauspicious omens.”

## \|\| 241.2 \|\|

*matsya uvāca*  
*aṅgadakṣiṇabhāge tu śastaṃ prasphuraṇaṃ bhavet \|*  
*apraśastaṃ tathā vāme pṛṣṭhasya hṛdayasya ca \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Matsya said: — The vibration of the right limbs is said to be generally auspicious. The left sides of the back and heart are also auspicious.

## \|\| 241.3 \|\|

*manuruvāca*  
*aṅgānāṃ spandanaṃ caiva śubhāśubhaviceṣṭitam \|*  
*tanme vistarato brūhi yena syāttadvidho bhuvi \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Manu asked: — “Lord! How should one know what is going to happen on the vibration of the several limbs of the body? Pray explain all that to me fully.”

## \|\| 241.4 \|\|

*matsya uvāca*  
*pṛthvīlābho bhavenmūrdhni lalāṭe ravinandana \|*  
*sthānaṃ vivṛddhimāyāti bhrūnasoḥ priyasaṃgamaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Matsya replied: — The vibration of the head in dreams means the acquirement of another empire; that of the forehead means acquisition of further lands; that of the eyebrows and the nose means the prospect of meeting some dear friend.

## \|\| 241.5-7 \|\|

*bhṛtyalabdhiścākṣideśe dṛgupānte dhanāgamaḥ \|*  
*utkaṇṭhopagamo madhye dṛṣṭaṃ rājanvicakṣaṇaiḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*dṛgbandhane saṃgare ca jayaṃ śīghramavāpnuyāt \|*  
*yoṣidbhogo'pāṅgadeśe śravaṇānte priyāśrutiḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*nāsikāyāṃ prītisaukhyaṃ prajāptiradharoṣṭhaje \|*  
*kaṇṭhe tu bhogalābhaḥ syādbhogavṛddhirathāṃsayoḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

5-7. The vibration of the eye means death; near about the eye begets wealth, if the centre of the eye throbs one becomes very anxious; the y closing of the eyes begets an early victory, and of the outer corner of the eye means the enjoyment with a handsome lady. The vibration of the ears makes one to bear good thing, that of the nose brings happiness, of the upper and lower lips begets progeny, of the neck bring enjoyments and pleasures, of the shoulders means the increase of enjoyments.

## \|\| 241.8 \|\|

*suhṛtsnehaśca bāhubhyāṃ haste caiva dhanāgamaḥ \|*  
*pṛṣṭhe parājayaḥ sadyo jayo vakṣaḥsthale bhavet \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. The vibration of the arm means the love of a friend, of the hand brings in wealth, of the back means defeat, of the chest means speedy victory.

## \|\| 241.9-10 \|\|

*kukṣibhyāṃ prītiruddiṣṭā striyāḥ prajananaṃ stane \|*  
*sthānabhraṃśo nābhideśe antre caiva dhanāgamaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*jānusaṃdhau paraiḥ saṃdhirbalavadbhirbhavennṛpa \|*  
*deśaikadeśanāśo'tha jaṅghābhyāṃ ravinandana \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. The trembling of the belly means affection, the vibration of the breast means the impregnation, that of the navel means the loss of one’s position, that within the navel begets wealth, that of the knees means the union with some powerful enemy, and that of the ankles forebodes the destruction of some portion of the country.

## \|\| 241.11 \|\|

*uttamaṃ sthānamāpnoti padbhyāṃ prasphuraṇānnṛpa \|*  
*salābhaṃ cādhvagamanaṃ bhavetpādatale nṛpa \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. The vibration of the feet begets good situation, that of the soles gets wealth and other dress and presents.

## \|\| 241.12 \|\|

*lāñchanaṃ piṭakaṃ caiva jñeyaṃ sphuraṇavattathā \|*  
*viparyayeṇa vihitaḥ sarvaḥ strīṇāṃ phalāgamaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. These are meant for men; that of the women are contrary. If the above mentioned right limbs of a woman vibrate, the results are contrary, but in the case of men they are most auspicious.

## \|\| 241.13 \|\|

*apraśaste tadā vāme tvapraśastaṃ viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*dakṣiṇe'pi praśaste'ṅge praśastaṃ syādviśeṣataḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Vibrations of the limbs contrary to those mentioned above are unlucky. Gold should be given, to Brahmanas to avert the evils arising out of their throbbing.

## Chapter 242

## \|\| 242.1 \|\|

*manuruvāca*  
*svapnākhyānaṃ kathaṃ deva gamane pratyupasthite \|*  
*dṛśyante vividhākārāḥ kathaṃ teṣāṃ phalaṃ bhavet \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Manu asked: — “Lord! be pleased to tell me all about the effects of the dreams that a king may see as well the auspicious signs when he goes out on some purpose. How should those different dreams be interpreted?”

## \|\| 242.2-15 \|\|

*matsya uvāca*  
*idānīṃ kathayiṣyāmi nimittaṃ svapnadarśane \|*  
*nābhiṃ vinā'nyagātreṣu tṛṇavṛkṣasamudbhavaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*cūrṇanaṃ mūrdhni kāṃsyānāṃ muṇḍanaṃ nagnatā tathā \|*  
*malināmbaradhāritvamabhyaṅgaḥ paṅkadigdhatā \|\| 3 \|\|*

*uccātprapatanaṃ caiva dolārohaṇameva ca \|*  
*arjanaṃ paṅkalohānāṃ hayānāmapi māraṇam \|\| 4 \|\|*

*raktapuṣpadrumāṇāṃ ca maṇḍalasya tathaiva ca \|*  
*varāharkṣakharoṣṭrāṇāṃ tathā cā’rohaṇakriyā \|\| 5 \|\|*

*bhakṣaṇaṃ pakṣimatsyānāṃ tailasya kṛsarasya ca \|*  
*nartanaṃ hasanaṃ caiva vivāho gītameva ca \|\| 6 \|\|*

*tantrīvādyavihīnānāṃ vādyānāmabhivādanam \|*  
*srato'vagāhagamanaṃ snānaṃ gomayavāriṇā \|\| 7 \|\|*

*paṅkodakena ca tathā mahītoyena cāpyatha \|*  
*mātuḥ praveśo jaṭhare citārohaṇameva ca \|\| 8 \|\|*

*śakradhvajābhipatanaṃ patanaṃ śaśisūryayoḥ \|*  
*divyāntarikṣabhaumānāmutpātānāṃ ca darśanam \|\| 9 \|\|*

*devadvijātibhūpālagurūṇāṃ krodha eva ca \|*  
*āliṅganaṃ kumārīṇāṃ puruṣāṇāṃ ca maithunam \|\| 10 \|\|*

*hāniścaiva svagātrāṇāṃ virekavamanakriyā \|*  
*dakṣiṇāśābhigamanaṃ vyādhinā'bhibhavastathā \|\| 11 \|\|*

*phalāpahāniśca tathā puṣpahānistathaiva ca \|*  
*gṛhāṇāṃ caiva pātaśca gṛhasaṃmārjanaṃ tathā \|\| 12 \|\|*

*krīḍā piśācakravyādavānararkṣanarairapi \|*  
*parādabhibhavaścaiva tasmācca vyasanodbhavaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*kāṣāyavastradhāritvaṃ tadvatstrīkrīḍanaṃ tathā \|*  
*snehapānāvagāhau ca raktamālyānulepanam \|\| 14 \|\|*

*evamādīni cānyāni duḥsvapnāni vinirdiśet \|*  
*eṣāṃ saṃkathanaṃ dhanyaṃ bhūyaḥ prasvāpanaṃ tathā \|\| 15 \|\|*

2-15. Matsya said: — “Now listen to the effects of the various kinds of dreams. IE one dreams that grass has grown all over his body excepting, j on the navel, or that pieces of bell-metal have been pasted on the head, or that his head is clean shaven, or that he is naked or that he has put on poor clothing’s or that he has fallen down from a height, or that he is besmeared with mud or oil, or that he is collecting molten iron, or sees the carcass of horses, red flowers, red trees, red halos, or that he is riding on a boar, bear, donkey or a camel, or that he is eating cooked flesh, oil or kichari (rice and pulse cooked together),, or sees dancing, merry-making, marriage, hears songs, etc., or the playing of musical instruments other than the Vina or the guitar, or that he is plunging himself in the source of a river, or that he is bathing after rubbing himself in waters dirty with cowdung, or that he is bathing in muddled water, or that he is in his mother’s womb, or that he is on a burning pole, or that the banner set up in honour of Indra has fallen, or the fall of the Sun and the Moon, or the various ills that arise in the Celestial, Intermediate or Terrestrial regions, or that the gods^ the twice-born, the king or the preceptor are angry, or that he is embracing virgins, or the males committing unnatural offence, or that he has lost a limb of his body, or that he is besmeared with vomit or stool, or that he is going towards the south, or that is laid up with some disease, or that the fruits and flowers are on the decline, or that the houses have tumbled down, or the houses are being swept, or that he is playing with demons, monkeys, bears or men, or that he is discarded by his enemies, the sight of one wearing gerua (red) cloth, or that he is drinking oil or bathing in it, or that he is wearing red garlands; or his body is besmeared with red paste are all unlucky signs. It is always good to tell such bad dreams to other people. Also it is advisable to go to sleep again after seeing such dreams.

## \|\| 242.16-18 \|\|

*kalkasnānaṃ tilairhomo brāhmaṇānāṃ ca pūjanam \|*  
*stutiśca vāsudevasya tathā tasyaiva pūjanam \|\| 16 \|\|*

*nāgendra mokṣaśravaṇaṃ jñeyaṃ duḥsvapnanāśanam \|*  
*svapnāstu prathame yāme saṃvatsaravipākinaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*ṣaḍbhirmāsairdvitīye tu tribhirmāsaistṛtīyake \|*  
*caturthe māsamātreṇa paśyato nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

16-18. By bathing after rubbing over his body some grain paste, performing a sacrifice with sesamums, or worshipping the Brahmanas, worshipping Vishnu, and by listening to the story of the liberation of the elephant by the Lord (Gajamokshan) the evil effects of bad dreams are driven away. A dream dreamt in the first part of the night gives its fruit in the first year; if it is dreamt in the second part of the night it gives its fruit in six months; if it occurs in the third part of the night it gives fruit in three months and if it comes in the fourth part of the night, it undoubtedly gives its fruit within a month.

## \|\| 242.19-20 \|\|

*aruṇodayavelāyāṃ daśāhena phalaṃ bhavet \|*  
*ekasyāṃ yadi vā rātrau śubhaṃ vā yadi vā'śubham \|\| 19 \|\|*

*paścāddṛṣṭastu yastatra tasya pākaṃ vinirdiśet \|*  
*tasmācchobhanake svapne paścātsvapno na paśyati \|\| 20 \|\|*

19-20. If one gets a dream just before sunrise, it gives fruit within ten days. If one gets a couple of dreams in the night, the last one bearsfruit consequently one should not go to sleep after he has dreamt a dream.

## \|\| 242.21 \|\|

*śailaprāsādanāgāśvavṛṣabhārohaṇaṃ hitam \|*  
*drumāṇāṃ śvetapuṣpāṇāṃ gamane ca tathā dvija \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. If one rides on a horse, an elephant or an ox or climbs a hill or a: palace or on a tree bearing white flowers; it is very auspicious.

## \|\| 242.22-34 \|\|

*drumatṛṇodbhavo nābhau tathaiva bahubāhutā \|*  
*tathaiva bahuśīrṣatvaṃ phalitodbhava eva ca \|\| 22 \|\|*

*suśuklamālyadhāritvaṃ suśuklāmbaradhāritā \|*  
*candrā rkatārāgrahaṇaṃ parimārjanameva ca \|\| 23 \|\|*

*śakradhvajāliṅganaṃ ca taducchrāyakriyā tathā \|*  
*bhūmyambudhīnāṃ grasanaṃ śatrūṇāṃ ca vadhakriyā \|\| 24 \|\|*

*jayo vivāde dyūte ca saṅgrāme ca tathā dvija \|*  
*bhakṣaṇaṃ cā’rdra māṃsānāṃ matsyānāṃ pāyasasya ca \|\| 25 \|\|*

*darśanaṃ rudhirasyāpi snānaṃ vā rudhireṇa ca \|*  
*surārudhiramadyānāṃ pānaṃ kṣīrasya cātha vā \|\| 26 \|\|*

*antrairvā veṣṭanaṃ bhūmau nirmalaṃ gaganaṃ tathā \|*  
*mukhena dohanaṃ śastaṃ mahiṣīṇāṃ tathā gavām \|\| 27 \|\|*

*siṃhīnāṃ hastinīnāṃ ca vaḍavānāṃ tathaiva ca \|*  
*prasādo devaviprebhyo gurubhyaśca tathā śubhaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

*ambhasā tvabhiṣekastu gavāṃ śṛṅgasrutena vā \|*  
*candrā dbhraṣṭena vā rājañjñeyo rājyaprado hi saḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*rājyābhiṣekaśca tathā chedanaṃ śirasastathā \|*  
*maraṇaṃ vahnidāhaśca vahnidāho gṛhādiṣu \|\| 30 \|\|*

*labdhiśca rājyaliṅgānāṃ tantrīvādyābhivādanam \|*  
*tathodakānāṃ taraṇaṃ tathā viṣamalaṅghanam \|\| 31 \|\|*

*hastinīvaḍavānāṃ ca gavāṃ ca prasavo gṛhe \|*  
*ārohaṇamathāśvānāṃ rodanaṃ ca tathā śubham \|\| 32 \|\|*

*varastrīṇāṃ tathā lābhastathā’liṅganameva ca \|*  
*nigaḍairbandhanaṃ dhanyaṃ tathā viṣṭhānulepanam \|\| 33 \|\|*

*jīvatāṃ bhūmipālānāṃ suhṛdāmapi darśanam \|*  
*darśanaṃ devatānāṃ ca vimalānāṃ tathā'mbhasām \|\| 34 \|\|*

22-34. It is also equally auspicious to see in dream that a tree or some grass has grown in one’s navel, or that he has several arms, heads, or the luxuriance of fruits, or that he is wearing white raimants and withered garlands, or that he sees the eclipse of the Sun, the Moon or the stars or that he catches hold of the rainbow, or that he sweeps a floor or so, or that the heaven and the earth are under his subjugation, or that he has killed his enemies. The seeing of these dreams brings victory in battle and gambling. When a man dreams that he has eaten raw flesh, fish or rise cooked in milk and sugar, or he sees a flow of blood, or that he is bathing in blood, or that he is drinking wine, blood, or milk, or that he is in twined in the intestines, or sees a clear sky, or the lioness, the she-elephant, and the mare or cow yields milk from their mouths, or that he is getting favours from the Devas, Brahmanas or his guru or spiritual teacher, all these are auspicious dreams. When a man dreams that he is being anointed with waters from the cow’s horns or moon, he will have chance of getting a kingdom. When a man dreams that he is being installed in a throne or that he is beheaded, or that he is burnt in a fire and dead, or that his house or person is on fire, or that he has been blessed with the regalia of kingship, or that he is hearing the playing of guitar these also indicate the getting of sovereignty. The dream of crossing the water by swimming, or that he is crossing an uneven country, or that a mare, a cow or a she-elephant is giving birth in his house, or that he is riding on horses, these are auspicious; or that he is weeping, or that he has obtained good women, or that he is embracing beautiful women, or that he is fettered, or that he is besmeared with filth, or is being visited by a living king or friends, or the sight of the Devas or crystal waters, these are auspicious.

## \|\| 242.35 \|\|

*śubhānyathaitāni narastu dṛṣṭvā prāpnotyayatnāddhruvamarthalābham \|*  
*svapnāni vai dharmabhṛtāṃ variṣṭha vyādhervimokṣaṃ ca tathā’turo'pi \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. One who sees such dreams readily gets wealth without any effort and if a sick person gets such dreams he is sure to be cured ere long.

## Chapter 243

## \|\| 243.1 \|\|

*manuruvāca*  
*gamanaṃ prati rājñāṃ tu saṃmukhādarśane ca kim \|*  
*praśastāṃścaiva saṃbhāṣya sarvānetāṃśca kīrtaya \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Manu asked: — Lord! be gracious enough to tell me the good omens that are propitious at the time when a king marches on his journey.

## \|\| 243.2-10 \|\|

*matsya uvāca*  
*auṣadhāni tvayuktāni dhānyaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ ca yadbhavet \|*  
*kārpāsaśca tṛṇaṃ rājanśuṣkaṃ gomayameva ca \|\| 2 \|\|*

*indhanaṃ ca tathā'ṅgāraṃ guḍaṃ tailaṃ tathā'śubham \|*  
*abhyaktaṃ malinaṃ muṇḍaṃ tathā nagnaṃ ca mānavam \|\| 3 \|\|*

*muktakeśaṃ rujārtaṃ ca kāṣāyāmbaradhāriṇam \|*  
*unmattakaṃ tathā sattvaṃ dīnaṃ cātha napuṃsakam \|\| 4 \|\|*

*ayaḥpaṅkastathā carma keśabandhanameva ca \|*  
*tathaivoddhṛtasārāṇi piṇyākādīni yāni ca \|\| 5 \|\|*

*caṇḍālaśvapacāścaiva rājabandhanapālakāḥ \|*  
*vadhakāḥ pāpakarmāṇo garbhiṇī strī tathaiva ca \|\| 6 \|\|*

*tuṣabhasmakapālāsthi bhinnabhāṇḍāni yāni ca \|*  
*riktāni caiva bhāṇḍāni mṛtaṃ śārṅgikameva ca \|\| 7 \|\|*

*evamādīni cānyāni aśastānyabhidarśane \|*  
*aśasto vādyaśabdaśca bhinnabhairavajarjaraḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*purataḥ śabda ehīti śasyate na tu pṛṣṭhataḥ \|*  
*gaccheti paścāddharmajña purastāttu vigarhitaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*kva yāsi tiṣṭha mā gaccha kiṃ te tatra gatasya tu \|*  
*anye śabdāśca ye'niṣṭāste vipattikarā api \|\| 10 \|\|*

2-10. Matsya said: — The following are the bad omens at the time of a journey, viz., the sight of useless medicinal herbs scattered, black grain, cotton, hay, dried up cowdung, firewood, cinders, molasses, oil, dirty men covered with oil, naked men, poor head dress, men with loose hair, diseased men, hermit clad in red, coloured robes, mad man, distressed person, eunuch, Chandala, iron, mud, hide, refuse, fowler, sinner, pregnant women, husks, ashes, skulls, broken utensils, utensils stained with blood.

Just before sunrise, at the Brahma Muhurta if an indistinct sound is heard, in front or a loud sound of a broken vessel letting waters flow in a stream be heard, it is auspicious; hut if the sound be heard from the back, it is inauspicious. “Go” if such a sound is heard in front it is auspicious, “go” on the other hand is most inauspicious, if it comes from the back. “Where do you go”, “Do not go” “Stay” “what use in going there”, these are all inauspicious words and indicate danger.

## \|\| 243.11-12 \|\|

*dhvajādiṣu tathā sthānaṃ kravyādānāṃ vigarhitam \|*  
*skhalanaṃ vāhanānāṃ ca vastrasaṅgastathaiva ca \|\| 11 \|\|*

*nirgatasya tu dvārādau śirasaścābhighātitā \|*  
*chatradhvajānāṃ vastrāṇāṃ patanaṃ ca tathā'śubham \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-12. If a Rakshasa sits on a banner it is unlucky and so are the falling down of the conveyances, the overlapping of the dress, the striking of the head against the door, the falling down of the banner, umbrella, cloth at the time of departure are unlucky signs.

## \|\| 243.13-14 \|\|

*dṛṣṭe nimitte prathamamamaṅgalyavināśanam \|*  
*keśavaṃ pūjayedvidvānstavena madhusūdanam \|\| 13 \|\|*

*dvitīye tu tato dṛṣṭe pratīpe praviśedgṛham \|*  
*atheṣṭāni pravakṣyāmi maṅgalyāni tathā'nagha \|\| 14 \|\|*

13-14. If there is thus seen one bad omen at the time of departure one should adore Vishnu and praise Madhusudana and then resume his mission, but if there is another one for the second time, he should return home.

## \|\| 243.15-21 \|\|

*śvetāḥ sumanasaḥ śreṣṭhāḥ pūrṇakumbhāstathaiva ca \|*  
*jalajāḥ pakṣiṇaścaiva māṃsamatsyāśca pārthiva \|\| 15 \|\|*

*gāvasturaṃgamā nāgā baddha ekaḥ paśustvajaḥ \|*  
*tridaśāḥ suhṛdo viprā jvalitaśca hutāśanaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*gaṇikā ca mahābhāga dūrvā cā’dra raṃ! ca gomayam \|*  
*rukmaṃ rūpyaṃ tathā tāmraṃ sarvaratnāni cāpyatha \|\| 17 \|\|*

*auṣadhāni ca dharmajña yavāḥ siddhārthakāstathā \|*  
*nṛvāhyamānaṃ yānaṃ ca bhadra pīṭhaṃ tathaiva ca \|\| 18 \|\|*

*khaḍgaṃ chatraṃ patākā ca mṛdaścā’yudhameva ca \|*  
*rājaliṅgāni sarvāṇi śavaṃ ruditavarjitam \|\| 19 \|\|*

*ghṛtaṃ dadhi payaścaiva phalāni vividhāni ca \|*  
*svastikaṃ vardhamānaṃ ca nandyāvartaṃ sakaustubham \|\| 20 \|\|*

*vāditrāṇāṃ sukhaḥ śabdo gambhīraḥ sumanoharaḥ \|*  
*gāndhāraṣaḍjaṛṣabhā ye ca śastāstathā svarāḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

15-21. The following are good omens, viz., the sight of white flowers, pitchers full of water, aquatic animals, bird’s flesh, fish, cows, horses, elephants, goats, Devas, idols, friends, Brahmanas, blazing fire, dancing girls, green grass, wet cowdung, gold, silver, copper, all the gems, all the medicines, barley, sesamum, bhadrapitha, sword, umbrella, banner, clay, weapons, emblems of regality, clarified butter, curds, milk, various kinds of fruits, the eddy of a river, Kaustubha gem, melodious music, nice and deep songs, the tunes Gamdhara, Shadaja, Rishabha, pot marked with Svastika sign.

## \|\| 243.22 \|\|

*vāyuḥ saśarkaro rūkṣaḥ sarvatra samupasthitaḥ \|*  
*pratilomastathā nīco vijñeyo bhayakṛddvija \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. If a dry dust storm blows against at the time of departure it is unlucky.

## \|\| 243.23-24 \|\|

*anukūlo mṛduḥ snigdhaḥ sukhasparśaḥ sukhāvahaḥ \|*  
*rūkṣā rūkṣasvarā bhadrā ḥ! kravyādāḥ parigacchatām \|\| 23 \|\|*

*meghāḥ śastā ghanāḥ snigdhā gajabṛṃhitaniḥsvanāḥ \|*  
*anulomāstaḍicchastāḥ śakracāpaṃ tathaiva ca \|\| 24 \|\|*

23-24. On the other hand if a gentle and pleasing wind blows favourably it is very auspicious and so is the chorus of kites, etc., as well as the mild thunder of glossy clouds resembling elephants, and the sight of rainbow".

## \|\| 243.25-26 \|\|

*apraśaste tathā jñeye pariveṣapravarṣaṇe \|*  
*anulomā grahāḥ śastā vākpatistu viśeṣataḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*āstikyaṃ śraddadhānatvaṃ tathā pūjyābhipūjanam \|*  
*śastānyetāni dharmajña yacca syānmanasaḥ priyam \|\| 26 \|\|*

25-26. The sight of Sun’s and Moon’s halo is inauspicious as well the rains the good influence of stars particularly the rising of Vrihaspati, (Jupiter) in anuloma, mind full of devotion, the adoration of the worthy, the sight of the things very dear to one’s mind are all lucky things at the time of departure.

## \|\| 243.27 \|\|

*manasastuṣṭirevātra paramaṃ jayalakṣaṇam \|*  
*ekataḥ sarvaliṅgāni manasastuṣṭirekataḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. The hilarity of mind at the time of journey is the indication of victory and in fact it equals all the good omens in point of good luck.

## \|\| 243.28 \|\|

*yānotsukatvaṃ manasaḥ praharṣaḥ śubhasya lābho vijayapravādaḥ \|*  
*maṅgalyalabdhiḥ śravaṇaṃ ca rājañjñeyāni nityaṃ vijayāvahāni \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. The king whose mind is full of joy is sure to win and so is the case with the one who hears auspicious words at the time of his departure and when all his conveyances are very eager to start.

## Chapter 244

## \|\| 244.1-2 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*rājadharmastvayā sūta kathito vistareṇa tu \|*  
*tathaivādbhutamaṅgalyaṃ svapnadarśanameva ca \|\| 1 \|\|*

*viṣṇoridānīṃ māhātmyaṃ punarvaktumihārhasi \|*  
*kathaṃ sa vāmano bhūtvā babandha balidānavam \|\| 2 \|\|*

1-2. The Rishis asked: — Suta! you have related to us the duties of a sovereign and also about the various omens and effects of dreams; now we are desirous of hearing the glory of Lord Vishnu. Tray tell us why the Lord in His Vamana incarnation made Bali the great demon king a captive? How did He make His Dwarfish form increase all over the three worlds?”

## \|\| 244.3-7 \|\|

*kramataḥ kīdṛśaṃ rūpamāsīllokatraye hareḥ \|*  
*sūta uvāca*  
*etadeva purā pṛṣṭaḥ kurukṣetre tapodhanaḥ \|*  
*śaunakastīrthayātrāyāṃ vāmanāyatane purā \|\| 3 \|\|*

*yadā samayabheditvaṃ drau padyāḥ pārthivaṃ prati \|*  
*arjunena kṛtaṃ tatra tīrthayātrāṃ tadā yayau \|\| 4 \|\|*

*dharmakṣetre kurukṣetre vāmanāyatane sthitaḥ \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā sa vāmanaṃ tatra arjuno vākyamabravīt \|\| 5 \|\|*

*arjuna uvāca*  
*kiṃ nimittamayaṃ devo vāmanākṛtirijyate \|*  
*varāharūpī bhagavānkasmātpūjyo'bhavatpurā \|*  
*kasmācca vāmanasyedamiṣṭaṃ kṣetramajāyata \|\| 6 \|\|*

*śaunaka uvāca*  
*vāmanasya ca vakṣyāmi varāhasya ca dhīmataḥ \|*  
*tyaktvā'tivistaraṃ bhūyo māhātmyaṃ kurunandana \|\| 7 \|\|*

3-7. Suta said: — Rishis! the same question was put by Arjuna to the Muni Shaunaka in Vamanayatan in days gone by when the former was on a pilgrimage. When Arjuna violated his promise with Yudhishthira about living with Draupadi, he went on pilgrimage for the expiation of his sin. The image of Vamana was installed in Kurukshetra. When Arjuna saw the image of Vamana, he asked Shaunaka why Vamana, was worshipped? and why did He assume the Dwarfish form? Why Lord Vishnu incarnated Himself as Varaha and how this Kshettra became so dear to "Vamana?”

## \|\| 244.8-9 \|\|

*purā nirvāsite śakre sureṣu vijiteṣu ca \|*  
*cintayāmāsa devānāṃ jananī punarudbhavam \|\| 8 \|\|*

*aditirdevamātā ca paramaṃ duścaraṃ tapaḥ \|*  
*tīvraṃ cacāra varṣāṇāṃ sahasraṃ pṛthivīpate \|\| 9 \|\|*

8-9. Shaunaka replied: — I shall relate to you in brief the glories of Vamana and Varaha.” In the past decade, when Indra was vanquished by the Devas, then Aditi the mother of the Devas began to practise rigid austerities for sons again.

## \|\| 244.10-12 \|\|

*ārādhanāya kṛṣṇasya vāgyatā vāyubhojanā \|*  
*daityairnirākṛtāndṛṣṭvā tanayānkurunandana \|\| 10 \|\|*

*vṛthāputrā'hamasmīti nirvedātpraṇatā harim \|*  
*tuṣṭāva vāgbhiriṣṭābhiḥ paramārthāvabodhinī \|*  
*devadevaṃ hṛṣīkeśaṃ natvā sarvagataṃ harim \|\| 11 \|\|*

*aditiruvāca*  
*namaḥ sarvārtināśāya namaḥ puṣkaramāline \|*  
*namaḥ paramakalyāṇakalyāṇāyā’divedhase \|\| 12 \|\|*

10-12. For one thousand years she worshipped Lord Krishna by living on air alone, and on seeing Her children oppressed by the Devas she said to Vishnu Herself that Her sons were horn in vain and she then saluted Lord and became very distressed,

## \|\| 244.13 \|\|

*namaḥ paṅkajanetrāya namaḥ paṅkajanābhaye \|*  
*śriyaḥ kāntāya dāntāya dāntadṛśyāya cakriṇe \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Aditi said: — O Lord! the Dispeller of all the troubles of the devotees on mere remembrance, the one who wears a garland of lotus flowers, the Prosperity of all beings, I salute Thee.

## \|\| 244.14 \|\|

*namaḥ paṅkajasaṃbhūtisaṃbhavāyā’tmayonaye \|*  
*namaḥ śaṅkhāsihastāya namaḥ kanakaretase \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. O Lotus-eyed one! Thou art the Prime Deva; Thou art more auspicious than the most auspicious. From thy navel sprang the lotus O Lord of Lakshmi, the One, armed with a quoit, I salute Thee.

## \|\| 244.15 \|\|

*tathā’tmajñānavijñānayogicintyātmayogine \|*  
*nirguṇāyāviśeṣāya haraye brahmarūpiṇe \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. My salutations to the One from whose lotus, navel has sprung Brahma; O Thou, the self-manifested! the One armed with a conch, sword, etc., Thy essence is gold-like; salutations to Thee.

## \|\| 244.16 \|\|

*jagatpratiṣṭhitaṃ yatra jagatā yo na dṛśyate \|*  
*namaḥ sthūlātisūkṣmāya tasmai devāya śaṅkhine \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. O Atmayogin! O Avishesha! O Yogachintya! O Atmajnana! O Vijnanasampanna! O Nirguna! my salutations to the One within whom the -universe exists but whose majestic glory the universe does not realize.

I salute that Being, the Deva Hari, who is the gross of the gross and the subtle of the subtle. Who hold conch in His hand.

## \|\| 244.17-33 \|\|

*yaṃ na paśyanti paśyanto jagadapyakhilaṃ narāḥ \|*  
*apaśyadbhirjagatyatra sa devo hṛdi saṃsthitaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*taminneva vinaśyeta yasyaitadakhilaṃ jagat \|*  
*tasmai samastajagatāmādhārāya namo namaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*ādyaḥ prajāpatipatiryaḥ prabhūṇāṃ patiḥ paraḥ \|*  
*patiḥ surāṇāṃ yastasmai namaḥ kṛṣṇāya vedhase \|\| 19 \|\|*

*yaḥ pravṛttau nivṛttau ca ijyate karmabhiḥ svakaiḥ \|*  
*svargāpavargaphalado namastasmai gadābhṛte \|\| 20 \|\|*

*yaścintyamāno manasā sadyaḥ pāpaṃ vyapohati \|*  
*namastasmai viśuddhāya parāya harivedhase \|\| 21 \|\|*

*yaṃ buddhvā sarvabhūtāni devadeveśamavyayam \|*  
*na punarjanmamaraṇe prāpnuvanti namāmi tam \|\| 22 \|\|*

*yo yajñe yajñaparamairijyate yajñasaṃjñitaḥ \|*  
*taṃ yajñapuruṣaṃ viṣṇuṃ namāmi prabhumīśvaram \|\| 23 \|\|*

*gīyate sarvavedeṣu vedavidbhirvidāṃ patiḥ \|*  
*yastasmai vedavedyāya viṣṇave jiṣṇave namaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*yato viśvaṃ samutpannaṃ yasmiṃśca layameṣyati \|*  
*viśvāgamapratiṣṭhāya namastasmai mahātmane \|\| 25 \|\|*

*brahmādistambamaryantaṃ yena viśvamidaṃ tatam \|*  
*māyājālaṃ samuttartuṃ tamupendraṃ namāmyaham \|\| 26 \|\|*

*yastu toyasvarūpastho bibhartyakhilamīśvaraḥ \|*  
*viśvaṃ viśvapatiṃ viṣṇuṃ taṃ namāmi prajāpatim \|\| 27 \|\|*

*yamārādhya viśuddhena manasā karmaṇā girā \|*  
*tarantyavidyāmakhilāṃ tamupendraṃ namāmyaham \|\| 28 \|\|*

*viṣādatoṣaroṣādyairyo'jasraṃ sukhaduḥkhajaiḥ \|*  
*nṛtyatyakhilabhūtasthastamupendraṃ namāmyaham \|\| 29 \|\|*

*mūrtaṃ tamo'suramayaṃ tadvadhādvinihanti yaḥ \|*  
*rātrijaṃ sūryarūpī tamupendraṃ namāmyaham \|\| 30 \|\|*

*kapilādisvarūpastho yaścājñānamayaṃ tamaḥ \|*  
*hanti jñānapradānena tamupendraṃ namāmyaham \|\| 31 \|\|*

*yasyākṣiṇī candra sūryau sarvalokaśubhāśubham \|*  
*paśyataḥ karma satatamupendraṃ taṃ namāmyaham \|\| 32 \|\|*

*yasminsarveśvare sarva satyametanmayoditam \|*  
*nānṛtaṃ tamajaṃ viṣṇuṃ namāmi prabhavāpyayam \|\| 33 \|\|*

17-33. I salute Him whom ordinary eyes do not see in spite of their seeing the universe, who although enshrined in every heart is not accessible to the mind of the wise even, in whom exist the grain, milk, rivers, and in fact the whole universe, the sustainer of the whole universe, who is the very first Prajapati, the Lord of all the creation, the Lord of all things, the Lord of all the Devas, who is Krishna, the ordainer, who is adored both in the Pravritti Marga and Nivritti Marga by one’s own karmas, who is the giver of heavenly joys and emancipation, who drives away all the ills by a mere devotional meditation of Him, by realizing whom the soul is liberated from the cycle of births and deaths, the Deva worshipped in the form of sacrifices, the One Who is said to be inherent in all the Devas, the One from whom the universe emanates, the One in whom the universe ultimately merges, in whose infinite glory the whole universe from Brahma downwards is sustained, the Supreme Lord Who sustains the universe in the form of water, by devoting to whom with all heart and soul people cross over all ignorance. Who exercises His influence in the minds of all beings by dancing in forms of dismay, contentment, anger, etc., the Great Deva who like the Sun destroys the demons, who destroys in the shape of wisdom and knowledge of Kapila, the darkness of ignorance, Who witnesses with His eyes the Sun and the Moon, all the actions of the beings of the universe, the Lord Vishnu Who is true to all my sayings. In Vishnu, the Lord of all, all the truths that I have expressed are existing; nothing false is there, I adore that Unborn, Undecaying Hari.

## \|\| 244.34 \|\|

*yacca tatsatyamuktaṃ me bhūyāṃścāto janārdanaḥ \|*  
*satyena tena sakalāḥ pūryantāṃ me manorathāḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. If what I have said in my prayer be true as I believe it to be, let all my wishes be fulfilled.

## \|\| 244.35-37 \|\|

*śaunaka uvāca*  
*evaṃ stutaḥ sa bhagavānvāsudeva uvāca tām \|*  
*adṛśyaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ tasyāḥ saṃdarśane sthitaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

*śrībhagavānuvāca*  
*manorathāṃstvamadite yānicchasyabhivāñchitān \|*  
*tāṃstvaṃ prāpsyasi dharmajñe matprasādānna saṃśayaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

*śṛṇuṣva sumahābhāge varo yaste hṛdi sthitaḥ \|*  
*tamāśu vriyatāṃ kāmaṃ śreyaste saṃbhaviṣyati \|*  
*maddarśanaṃ hi viphalaṃ na kadācidbhaviṣyati \|\| 37 \|\|*

35-37. Shaunaka said: — Lord Vishnu, unseen by all, instantly appeared before Aditi, and said “O Virtuous Aditi! you shall certainly have your desires fulfilled ere long. Ask for a thing that you may wish without delay, you will prosper for my sight never goes fruitless.”

## \|\| 244.38-40 \|\|

*aditiruvāca*  
*yadi deva prasannastvaṃ madbhaktyā bhaktavatsala \|*  
*trailokyādhipatiḥ putrastadastu mama vāsavaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

*hṛtaṃ rājyaṃ hṛtāścāsya yajñabhāgā mahāsuraiḥ \|*  
*tvayi prasanne varade tānprāpnotu suto mama \|\| 39 \|\|*

*hṛtaṃ rājyaṃ na duḥkhāya mama putrasya keśava \|*  
*sāpatnāddāyanirbhraṃśo bādhāṃ naḥ kurute hṛdi \|\| 40 \|\|*

38-40. Aditi replied “Lord! if you are pleased at my devotion, I wish my son Indra to become the Lord of the three regions, which boon be pleased to grant. The demons have deprived him of his realm and share of sacrificial offerings. Let all that be restored to him through your favour. Lord! I am not so much grieved at the defeat of my son in the hands of the Asuras as I am grieved at the loss of his realm and rights and that he has been driven out of Heaven.

## \|\| 244.41-42 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca*  
*kṛtaḥ prasādo hi mayā tava devi yathepsitaḥ \|*  
*svāṃśena caiva te garbhe saṃbhaviṣyāmi kaśyapāt \|\| 41 \|\|*

*tava garbhasamudbhūtastataste ye surārayaḥ \|*  
*tānahaṃ nihaniṣyāmi nivṛttā bhava nandini \|\| 42 \|\|*

41-42. Lord Vishnu said: — “O Devi! I am quite pleased with your devotion I shall therefore be born of you through Kashyapa when I shall kill all the demons.”

## \|\| 244.43-44 \|\|

*aditiruvāca*  
*prasīda devadeveśa namaste viśvabhāvana \|*  
*nāhaṃ tvāmudare deva voḍhuṃ śakṣyāmi keśava \|\| 43 \|\|*

*yasminpratiṣṭhitaṃ viśvaṃ yo viśvaṃ svayamīśvaraḥ \|*  
*tamahaṃ nodareṇa tvāṃ voḍhuṃ śakṣyāmi durdharam \|\| 44 \|\|*

43-44. Aditi replied: — “Lord! be pleased; how can I bear you in my womb? You in whom is established this universe; you are the Lord of the creation.”

## \|\| 244.45-47 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca*  
*satyamāttha mahābhāge mayi sarvamidaṃ jagat \|*  
*pratiṣṭhitaṃ na māṃ śaktā voḍhuṃ sendrā divaukasaḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

*dhārayiṣyāmi bhadraṃ te tadalaṃ saṃbhrameṇa te \|\| 46 \|\|*

*na te glānirna te khedo garbhasthe bhavitā mayi \|*  
*dākṣāyaṇi prasādaṃ te karomyanyaiḥ sudurlabham \|\| 47 \|\|*

45-47. Vishnu Said: — “What you say is true. Verily all the universe rests in Me. Even the Devas, Indra, etc., cannot hold Me; I hold you along with the universe, the Devas and Kashyapa, etc. Do not be anxious; you will be blessed. You will feel no trouble when 1 will enter within your womb. The favour of Mine that is so very difficult for others to get, you have got that.

## \|\| 244.48 \|\|

*garbhasthe mayi putrāṇāṃ tava yo'rirbhaviṣyati \|*  
*tejasastasya hāniṃ ca kariṣye mā vyathāṃ kṛthāḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. “When I am in your womb I shall deprive by My glory those who dare to despise your progeny. Do not be sorry.”

## \|\| 244.49 \|\|

*śaunaka uvāca*  
*evamuktvā tataḥ sadyo yāto'ntardhānamīśvaraḥ \|*  
*sā'pi kālena taṃ garbhamavāpa kurusattama \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Shaunaka said: — Saying so Lord Vishnu vanished from sight and Aditi bore Him in Her womb in due course.

## \|\| 244.50-52 \|\|

*garbhasthite tataḥ kṛṣṇe cacāla sakalā kṣitiḥ \|*  
*cakampire mahāśailāḥ kṣobhaṃ jagmustathā'bdhayaḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

*yato yato'ditiryāti dadāti lalitaṃ padam \|*  
*tatastataḥ kṣitiḥ khedānnanāma vasudhādhipa \|\| 51 \|\|*

*daityānāmatha sarveṣāṃ garbhasthe madhusūdane \|*  
*babhūva tejasāṃ hāniryathoktaṃ parameṣṭhinā \|\| 52 \|\|*

50-52. When Vishnu entered Her womb the universe began as if to go down in that direction where Aditi walked on the mountains began to quiver, and the oceans receded and all the demons began to decline.

## Chapter 245

## \|\| 245.1 \|\|

*śaunaka uvāca*  
*nistejaso'surāndṛṣṭvā samastānasureśvaraḥ \|*  
*prahlādamatha papraccha balirātmapitāmaham \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Shaunaka said: — Afterwards the demon king Bali on seeing the demons bereft of their fire and energy asked Prahlada, his own grandfather, thus: — “ O Sire!

## \|\| 245.2 \|\|

*baliruvāca*  
*tāta nistejaso daityā nirdagdhā iva vahninā \|*  
*kimete sahasaivādya brahmadaṇḍahatā iva \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. All the demons have become suddenly void of their glory\_ and look like coals charred in fire. They therefore appear as if visited by Providential calamity. How is this? Are these the symptoms of their approaching death?

## \|\| 245.3 \|\|

*ariṣṭaṃ kiṃ nu daityānāṃ kiṃ kṛtvā vairinirmitā \|*  
*nāśāyaiṣā samudbhūtā yayā nistejaso'surāḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Have the enemies raised up a kritya for their destruction. Will they now fall on account of having thus lost their glory?”

## \|\| 245.4-7 \|\|

*śaunaka uvāca*  
*iti daityapatirdhīraḥ pṛṣṭaḥ pautreṇa pārthiva \|*  
*ciraṃ dhyātvā jagādainamasurendraṃ baliṃ tadā \|\| 4 \|\|*

*prahlāda uvāca*  
*calanti girayo bhūmirjahāti sahajāṃ dhṛtim \|*  
*sarve samudrā ḥ! kṣubhitā daityā nistejasaḥ kṛtāḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*sūryodaye yathā pūrvaṃ tathā gacchanti na grahāḥ \|*  
*devānāṃ ca parā lakṣmīḥ kāraṇairanumīyate \|\| 6 \|\|*

*mahadetanmahābāho kāraṇaṃ dānaveśvara \|*  
*nahyalpamiti mantavyaṃ tvayā kāryaṃ surārdana \|\| 7 \|\|*

4-7. Prahlada after a long pause said to Bali: — “All the mountains are being shaked, this earth has become unstable, the demons have become day by day, void of their lustre; the planets do not follow the Sun. I believe the lustre of the demons has been eclipsed by the glory of the Devas. The Devi Lakshmi has become pleased with them. Lord of the demons! great calamity is going to befall us; do not consider this to be any ordinary sign of coming misfortune.

## \|\| 245.8 \|\|

*śaunaka uvāca*  
*ityuktvā dānavapatiṃ prahlādaḥ so'surottamaḥ \|*  
*atyantabhakto deveśaṃ jagāma manasā harim \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Shaunaka said: — Saying so, Prahlada concentrated his mind devoutfully and meditated on Hari, the Lord of the Devas.

## \|\| 245.9 \|\|

*sa dhyānayogaṃ kṛtvā'tha prahlādaḥ sumanoharam \|*  
*vicārayāmāsa tato yato devo janārdanaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. He brought to his mental vision where the Lord Vishnu was then.

## \|\| 245.10-13 \|\|

*sa dadarśodare'dityāḥ prahlādo vāmanākṛtim \|*  
*antaḥsthānbibhrataṃ sapta lokānādiprajāpatim \|\| 10 \|\|*

*tadantaḥsthānvasūnrudrā naśvinau marutastathā \|*  
*sādhyānviśvāṃstathā’dityāngandharvoragarākṣasān \|\| 11 \|\|*

*virocanaṃ svatanayaṃ baliṃ cāsuranāyakam \|*  
*jambhaṃ kujambhaṃ narakaṃ bāṇamanyāṃstathā'surān \|\| 12 \|\|*

*ātmānumurvīṃ gaganaṃ vāyumambho hutāśanam \|*  
*samudrā nvai drumasaritsarāṃsi ca paśūnmṛgān \|\| 13 \|\|*

10-13. He saw Hari, in the form of Vamana (dwarf) in the womb of Aditi and saw within Him the seven regions, Vasus, Rudras, Ashvani Kumaras, Maruts, Sadhyadevas, Vishvedevas, Adityas, Gandharvas, Uragas, Rakshasas, Virochana (his own son), Bali, Jambha, Kujambha, Narakasura, Vana and other Asuras, his own soul, the Seven oceans, sky, earth, air, water, fire, trees, Nandi, lower animals, deer, all the mankind, serpents, scorpions, Brahma, Ishana, the planets, stars, mountains, Daksha and other Prajapatis and became amassed; he then came back, to his senses and said.

## \|\| 245.14 \|\|

*vayomanuṣyānakhilāṃstathaiva ca sarīsṛpān \|*  
*samastalokasraṣṭāraṃ brahmāṇaṃ bhavameva ca \|*  
*grahanakṣatranāgāṃśca dakṣādyāṃśca prajāpatīn \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Prahlada: — “I now know the reason of these demons turning so lusterless; hear it from me.”

## \|\| 245.15-17 \|\|

*sa paśyanvismayāviṣṭaḥ prakṛtisthaḥ kṣaṇātpunaḥ \|*  
*prahlādaḥ prāha daityendraṃ baliṃ vairocaniṃ tadā \|\| 15 \|\|*

*prahlāda uvāca*  
*vatsa jñātaṃ mayā sarvaṃ yadarthaṃ bhavatāmiyam \|*  
*tejaso hānirutpannā tacchṛṇu tvamaśeṣataḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*devadevo jagadyonirayonirjagadādikṛt \|*  
*anādirādirviśvasya vareṇyo varado hariḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

15-17. “The Deva of the Devas, the source of the universe, the Unborn, the eternal, the beginning of the universe, the most best, the greatest of the great, the authority of the authorities, the Guru \_ of the Guru of the seven realms, the Lord of Lords, the one without beginning, middle and end, the Lord of the three regions, the Infinite, Lord Vishnu, has been born of Aditi by His one Amsha.

## \|\| 245.18 \|\|

*parāvarāṇāṃ paramaḥ paraḥ paravatāmapi \|*  
*pramāṇaṃ ca pramāṇānāṃ saptalokagurorguruḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Lord of the demons! He whom even Brahma, Rudra, Indra, Surya, Chandrama, and the sages like Marichi, etc., fail to know sufficiently that Lord Vasudeva has thus manifested Himself by His one Ama.

## \|\| 245.19 \|\|

*prabhuḥ prabhūṇāṃ paramaḥ parāṇāmanādimadhyo bhagavānanantaḥ \|*  
*trailokyamaṃśena sanāthameṣa kartuṃ mahātmā'ditijo'vatīrṇaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. The very same Lord killed my father in His form of Nrisimha in the past days, it is He who has now come down, the knower of all yogas, the Great Time and the Refuge of all.

## \|\| 245.20 \|\|

*na yasya rudro na ca padmayonirnendro na sūryendumarīcimukhyāḥ \|*  
*jānanti daityādhipa yatsvarūpaṃ sa vāsudevaḥ kalayā'vatīrṇaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. He is eternal Brahma, the knowers of whom through their knowledge are liberated from their sins and merge into Him. Those who merge into Him are not reborn, I salute the same Vasudeva every day.

## \|\| 245.21 \|\|

*yo'sau kalāṃśena nṛsiṃharūpī jaghāna pūrvaṃ pitaraṃ mameśaḥ \|*  
*yaḥ sarvayogīśamanonivāsaḥ sa vāsudevaḥ kalayāvatīrṇaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. As the surges emanate from the ocean, so do all the creation, and the infinite beings spring from Him. I salute the Lord Vasudeva in whom all the universe is ultimately absorbed.

## \|\| 245.22 \|\|

*yamakṣaraṃ vedavido viditvā viśanti yajжñānavidhūtapāpāḥ \|*  
*yasminpraviṣṭā na punarbhavanti taṃ vāsudevaṃ praṇamāmi nityam \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. I every day salute Lord Vasudeva, the Supreme Being whose form, glory and desire are not properly known even to the Devas like Brahmi and Shiva.

## \|\| 245.23-24 \|\|

*bhūtānyaśeṣāṇi yato bhavanti yathormayastoyanidherajasram \|*  
*layaṃ ca yasminpralaye prayānti taṃ vāsudevaṃ praṇamāmyacintyam \|\| 23 \|\|*

*na yasya rūpaṃ balaprabhāvau na yasya bhāvaḥ paramasya puṃsaḥ \|*  
*vijñāyate śarvapitāmahādyaistaṃ vāsudevaṃ praṇamāmyajasram \|\| 24 \|\|*

23-24. I salute the One who has given eyes to all the beings to see, the skin to feel the tongue to enjoy the taste, the ears to hear, the nose to smell, the One who brought the land from Patala on His one tusk in the form of Varaha for the good of mankind, in whom all the universe reposes, the eternal Vishnu, Who cannot be felt through the organs like the nose, and the ears, etc., and can only be discerned by the mind.

## \|\| 245.25-26 \|\|

*rūpasya cakṣurgrahaṇe tvagiṣṭā sparśe grahītrī rasanā rasasya \|*  
*śrotraṃ ca śabdagrahaṇe narāṇāṃ ghrāṇaṃ ca gandhagrahaṇe niyuktam \|\| 25 \|\|*

*yenaikadaṃṣṭrāgrasamuddhṛteyaṃ dharā'calāndhārayatīha sarvān \|*  
*yasmiṃśca śete sakalaṃ jagacca tamīśamādyaṃ praṇato'smi viṣṇum \|\| 26 \|\|*

25-26. I salute Him who has made the demons void of their lustre by coming into the womb of Aditi. He is endless, and is the hewer of the worldly tree (by ending there worldly phantasmagoria).

## \|\| 245.27 \|\|

*na ghrāṇacakṣuḥśravaṇādibhiryaḥ sarveśvaro veditumakṣayātmā \|*  
*śakyastamīḍyaṃ manasaiva devaṃ grāhyaṃ nato'haṃ harimīśitāram \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. He is the great cause of the universe, He has entered the womb of the mother of the Devas by His one-sixteenth part and He has taken away all your splendour and fire.”

## \|\| 245.28 \|\|

*aṃśāvatīrṇena ca yena garbhe hṛtāni tejāṃsi mahāsurāṇām \|*  
*namāmi taṃ devamanantamīśamaśeṣasaṃsārataroḥ kuṭhāram \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Bali said: — “Who is Hari who has caused us terror? There are demons more valiant than this Vasudeva.

## \|\| 245.29-31 \|\|

*devo jagadyonirayaṃ mahātmā sa ṣoḍaśāṃśena mahāsurendra \|*  
*sa devamāturjaṭharaṃ praviṣṭo hṛtāni vastena balādvapūṃṣi \|\| 29 \|\|*

*baliruvāca*  
*tāta ko'yaṃ harirnāma yato no bhayamāgatam \|*  
*santi me śataśo daityā vāsudevabalādhikāḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

*vipracittiḥ śibiḥ śaṅkurayaḥśaṅkustathaiva ca \|*  
*ayaḥ śirāścāśvaśirā bhaṅgakārī mahāhanuḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

29-31. Look at Viprachitti, Shivi, Samku Ayah Samku, Ayahashira, Ashvashira, Bhashmakari, Mahatanu, Pratapa, Praghasa, Shambhu, Kukura, and several other demons are the most valiant. They can lift the world even. Vishnu is not powerful like one of them even.

## \|\| 245.32 \|\|

*pratāpaḥ praghasaḥ śumbhaḥ kukuraśca sudurjayaḥ \|*  
*ete cānye ca me santi daiteyā dānavāstathā \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Shaunaka said: — Prahlada the most virtuous, hearing such words from his grandson, exclaimed: — “Fie, fie unto you.”

## \|\| 245.33-34 \|\|

*mahābalā mahāvīryā bhūbhāroddharaṇakṣamāḥ \|*  
*eṣāmekaikaśaḥ kṛṣṇo na vīryārdhena saṃmitaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

*śaunaka uvāca*  
*pautrasyaitadvacaḥ śrutvā prahlādo daityapuṃgavaḥ \|*  
*dhigdhigityāha sa baliṃ vaikuṇṭhākṣepavādinam \|\| 34 \|\|*

33-34. Bali! when there is a king like you, void of discrimination, vicious, I think all the demons will no doubt come to their end. Who else than you, so vicious, can utter such words regarding that Unborn illustrious Deva of the Devas, the Lord Vasudeva.

## \|\| 245.35 \|\|

*prahlāda uvāca*  
*vināśamupayāsyanti manye daiteyadānavāḥ \|*  
*yeṣāṃ tvamīdṛśo rājā durbuddhiravivekavān \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Which other sinner than yourself can blaspheme the most Supreme, the Eternal, Lord Vasudeva?

## \|\| 245.36 \|\|

*devadevaṃ mahābhāgaṃ vāsudevamajaṃ vibhum \|*  
*tvāmṛte pāpasaṃkalpaḥ ko'nya evaṃ vadiṣyati \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. All the demons named by you, the Devas like Brahma, etc., the Daityas, the world, the movable and immoveable, the oceans, the peninsulas, yourself, myself, the rivers, the trees, all the seven regions cannot become equal to the Lord Vishnu.

## \|\| 245.37-38 \|\|

*ya ete bhavatā proktāḥ samastā daityadānavāḥ \|*  
*sabrahmakāstathā devāḥ sthāvarānantabhūmayaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

*tvaṃ cāhaṃ ca jagaccedaṃ sādri drumanadīnadam \|*  
*samudra dvīpalokāśca na samaṃ keśavasya hi \|\| 38 \|\|*

37-38. Who else than you, who are on the road to destruction, indiscriminate, vicious and disrespectful of the sayings of the noble-minded old persons, can use such words of Lord Vishnu who is highly adored, all pervading, the Highest Self and on whose one foot this whole universe is established.

## \|\| 245.39 \|\|

*yasyātivandyavandyasya vyāpinaḥ paramātmanaḥ \|*  
*ekāṃśena jagatsarvaṃ kastamevaṃ pravakṣyati \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. I am awfully ashamed of your having been born in my house for you profane the name of Lord Vishnu.

## \|\| 245.40-42 \|\|

*ṛte vināśābhimukhaṃ tvāmekamavivekinam \|*  
*kubuddhimajitātmānaṃ vṛddhānāṃ śāsanātigam \|\| 40 \|\|*

*śocyo'haṃ yasya me gehe jātastava pitā'dhamaḥ \|*  
*yasya tvamīdṛśaḥ putro devadevasya nindakaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

*tiṣṭhatveṣā hi saṃsārasaṃbhṛtāghavināśinī \|*  
*kṛṣṇe bhaktirahaṃ tāvadavekṣyo bhavatā na kim \|\| 42 \|\|*

40-42. The devotion towards Vishnu is the dispeller of all the mundane sins. Nothing is dearer to me than the devotion to Krishna and everyone knows about it; but you wicked do not know it. Hari is dearer to me than my life. You have the audacity to show me disrespect by despising Hari.

## \|\| 245.43-44 \|\|

*na me priyatamaḥ kṛṣṇādapi deho mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*iti jānātyayaṃ loko na bhavānditijādhama \|\| 43 \|\|*

*jānannapa priyataraṃ prāṇebhyo'pi hariṃ mama \|*  
*nindāṃ karoṣi tasya tvamakurvangauravaṃ mama \|\| 44 \|\|*

43-44. Bali! Virochana is your father and I am his father and Narayana who is my Guru is the Lord of the universe whom you despise. You shall therefore lose your kingdom ere long.

## \|\| 245.45-46 \|\|

*virocanastava gururgurustasyāpyahaṃ bale \|*  
*mamāpi sarvajagatāṃ gurornārāyaṇo guruḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

*nindāṃ karoṣi yastasminkṛṣṇe gurugurorgurau \|*  
*yasmāttasmādihaiśvaryādacirādbhraṃśameṣyasi \|\| 46 \|\|*

45-46. Lord Vishnu, Janardana Is my Deva. He is my Guru. I have abandoned you for having despised Him and I pronounce my curse on you in consequence of it. Thus Hari will be pleased with me.

## \|\| 245.47 \|\|

*mama devo jagannātho bale tāvajжanārdanaḥ \|*  
*bhavatvahamupekṣyaste prītimānastu me guruḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. I feel as if you have wounded me more than if you had severed my head by using such words about the Lord. You shall now be soon bereft of your realm and I may see that.

## \|\| 245.48 \|\|

*etāvanmātramapyevaṃ ninditastrijagadguruḥ \|*  
*nāvekṣitaṃ tvayā yasmāttasmācchāpaṃ dadāmi te \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. I do not know of anyone else excepting Shrikrishna who could be my protector in this ocean of the world. And as you have blamed Hari, the Lord of the three worlds, I curse you thus. Love your kingdom and be fallen.

## \|\| 245.49 \|\|

*yathā me śirasaśchedādidaṃ gurutaraṃ vacaḥ \|*  
*tvayoktamacyutākṣepi rājyabhraṣṭastathā pata \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Shaunaka said That demon king hearing such words of Prahlada bowed down again and again and made repeated attempts to please him,

## \|\| 245.50 \|\|

*yathā ca kṛṣṇānna paraṃ paritrāṇaṃ bhavārṇave \|*  
*tathā'cireṇa paśyeyaṃ bhavantaṃ rājyavicyutam \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Bali said: — “Be pleased. I uttered such words through delusion, Ignorance and conceit.

## \|\| 245.51 \|\|

*śaunaka uvāca*  
*iti daityapatiḥ śrutvā gurorvacanamapriyam \|*  
*prasādayāmāsa guruṃ praṇipatya punaḥ punaḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Delusion clouded my intellect. I am indeed a sinner. You have done well in cursing me.

## \|\| 245.52 \|\|

*baliruvāca*  
*prasīda tāta mā kopaṃ kuru mohahate mayi \|*  
*balāvalepamattena mayaitadvākyamīritam \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. I shall certainly not be sadder to lose my realm than I am by being disowned by you.

## \|\| 245.53-54 \|\|

*mohopahatavijñānaḥ pāpo'haṃ ditijottama \|*  
*yacchapto'smi durācārastatsādhu bhavatā kṛtam \|\| 53 \|\|*

*rājyabhraṃśaṃ vasubhraṃśaṃ saṃprāpsyāmīti na tvaham \|*  
*viṣaṇṇo'smi yathā tāta tavaivāvinaye kṛte \|\| 54 \|\|*

53-54. It is not difficult to attain the realm of the three worlds nor is it difficult to acquire even more than that, but it is indeed very difficult to get a Guru (spiritual teacher) like your worthy self in this world; therefore be pleased upon me and shake off your anger. I am tormented by your wrath.”

## \|\| 245.55 \|\|

*trailokyarājyamaiśvaryamanyadvā nāti durlabham \|*  
*saṃsāre durlabhāste tu guravo ye bhavadvidhāḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Prahlada said: — I have no anger. It has sprung up by your ignorance and consequently I have cursed you.

## \|\| 245.56 \|\|

*tatprasīda na me kopaṃ kartumarhasi daityapa \|*  
*tvatkopadṛṣṭyā tātāhaṃ paritapye na śāpataḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. If my sense had not been overshadowed by your ignorance, how could I, the knower of Hari, the all-pervader, have cursed you in whom Hari too resides?

## \|\| 245.57-58 \|\|

*prahlāda uvāca*  
*vatsa kopena moho me janitastena te mayā \|*  
*śāpo datto vivekaśca mohenāpahṛto mama \|\| 57 \|\|*

*yadi mohena me jñānaṃ nā’kṣiptaṃ syānmahāsura \|*  
*tatkathaṃ sarvagaṃ jānanhariṃ kiṃcicchapāmyaham \|\| 58 \|\|*

57-58. Demon king! the curse that I have pronounced on you is bound to take its effect, but do not be sorry for from this time forward your devotion in Lord Vishnu will take place and He will be your protector.

## \|\| 245.59 \|\|

*yo'yaṃ śāpo mayā datto bhavato'surapuṃgava \|*  
*bhāvyametena nūnaṃ te tasmānmā tvaṃ viṣīda vai \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. Under the influence of this curse you will always remember me and I shall always seek your welfare.

## \|\| 245.60 \|\|

*adyaprabhṛti deveśe bhagavatyacyute harau \|*  
*bhavethā bhaktimānīśe sa te trātā bhaviṣyati \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Saying so Prahlada held his peace and later on in due time Lord Vishnu was born as Vamana.

## \|\| 245.61 \|\|

*śāpaṃ prāpyātha māṃ vīra saṃsmarethāḥ smṛtastvayā \|*  
*yathā tathā yatiṣye'haṃ śreyasā yojyase yathā \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. After the birth of the Lord, Aditi the mother of the Devas, was freed from all her troubles.

## \|\| 245.62 \|\|

*evamuktvā sa daityendraṃ virarāma mahāmatiḥ \|*  
*ajāyata sa govindo bhagavānvāmanākṛtiḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

62 Bracing and balmy breeze began to blow, the sky became quite clear of its dusty layer, and all the beings were fixed in the path of righteousness;

## \|\| 245.63 \|\|

*avatīrṇe jagannāthe tasminsarvāmareśvare \|*  
*devāśca mumucurduḥkhaṃ devamātā'ditistathā \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. And all the Devas, even the Demons, men, earth, heaven, sky became peaceful.

## \|\| 245.64 \|\|

*vavurvātāḥ sukhasparśā virajaskamabhūnnabhaḥ \|*  
*dharme ca sarvabhūtānāṃ tadā matirajāyata \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. On the birth of Vamana, Brahma performed the prescribed natal ceremonies, etc., and began to pray.

## \|\| 245.65-67 \|\|

*nodvegaścāpyabhūttatra manujendrā sureṣvapi \|*  
*tadādi sarvabhūtānāṃ bhūmyambaradivaukasām \|\| 65 \|\|*

*taṃ jātamātraṃ bhagavānbrahmā lokapitāmahaḥ \|*  
*jātakarmādikaṃ kṛtvā kṛṣṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā ca pārthiva \|*  
*tuṣṭāva devadeveśamṛṣīṇāṃ caiva śṛṇvatām \|\| 66 \|\|*

*brahmovāca*  
*jayā’dyeśa jayājeya jaya sarvātmakātmaka \|*  
*jaya janmajarāpena jayānanta jayācyuta \|\| 67 \|\|*

65-67. Brahma said: — “Victory to yon Eternal Lord. O, Omnipresent, free from birth, old age &c., endless, Achyuta, etc., O Unconquerable One! O destroyer of all! let victory attend on you! Thou art, the supreme object, the Supreme Knowledge, Victory, the Infinite, the great beholder of the universe, the Guru of the universe; Thou art immeasurable, unmanifested, Thou art the highest reality. Thou art knowable through knowledge; Thou always roamest in self. Victory to Thee.

## \|\| 245.68-71 \|\|

*jayājita jayāmeya jayāvyaktasthite jaya \|*  
*paramārthārtha sarvajña jñānajñeyā’tmaniḥsṛta \|\| 68 \|\|*

*jayāśeṣajagatsākṣiñjagatkartarjagadguro \|*  
*jagato'syantakṛddeva sthitiṃ pālayituṃ jaya \|\| 69 \|\|*

*jaya śeṣa jayāśeṣa jayākhilahṛdisthita \|*  
*jayādimadhyānta jaya sarvajñānanidhe jaya \|\| 70 \|\|*

*mumukṣubhiranirdeśya svayaṃdṛṣṭa jayeśvara \|*  
*yogināṃ muktiphalada damādiguṇabhūṣaṇa \|\| 71 \|\|*

68-71. Thou art the witness of the universe! Thou art the Lord of the world Thou art the world Teacher! Thou art endless. Victory to Thee. Thou art the protector of the world. Thou art limit; Thou art limitless, the beginning, the middle, the end, the ocean of supreme intellect, the incomparable, the giver of emancipation to Yogis, seated in the hearts of all, having thy ornament the virtues like Dama, &c; the most subtle, the incomprehensible, the image of the universe; victory to Thee. Corporeal, most subtle, the Cognizance of the senses, beyond the senses, fixed in the Yoga of the great illusion caused by the Self, the Imperishable, the uplifter of the earth by the tip of a single tusk; victory to Thee.

## \|\| 245.72 \|\|

*jayātisūkṣma durjñeya jaya sthūla jaganmaya \|*  
*jaya sthūlātisūkṣma tvaṃ jayātīndri ya sendri ya \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. Thou art all this universe; Thou art resting on Thy Maya; Thou sleepest on Shesha serpent O Aghora! Victory to Thee. The opener of the hearts of the’ enemies, Nrisimha, the Soul of the universe, Vamana, Keshava; victory to Thee.

## \|\| 245.73 \|\|

*jaya svamāyāyogastha śeṣabhogaśayākṣara \|*  
*jayaikadaṃṣṭrāprāntāgrasamuddhṛtavasuṃdhara \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. The unconquerable, covered by the Maya of Thyself, Janardana, Prabhu; victory to Thee.

## \|\| 245.74 \|\|

*nṛkesariñjayārātivakṣaḥsthalavidāraṇa \|*  
*sāṃprataṃ jaya viśvātmañjaya vāmana keśava \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. Hari, thou growest infinite by the evolution of the attributes of Maya; all the virtues are centered in Thee; victory to Thee.

## \|\| 245.75 \|\|

*nijamāyāpaṭacchanna jaganmūrte janārdana \|*  
*jayācintya jayānekasvarūpaikavidha prabho \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. Hari! even Shiva, Indra, Devas, Seers, Sanaka and other Rishis, ascetics cannot amply comprehend your nature.

## \|\| 245.76 \|\|

*vardhasva vardhitāśeṣavikāraprakṛte hare \|*  
*tvayyeṣā jagatāmīśe saṃsthitā dharmapaddhatiḥ \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. Deva! the whole universe is covered by Thy illusion; who can therefore penetrate this veil and realize you without Thy grace?

## \|\| 245.77 \|\|

*na tvāmahaṃ na ceśāno nendrā dyāstridaśā hare \|*  
*na jñātumīśā munayaḥ sanakādyā na yoginaḥ \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. Deva! the one who only thinks of Thee and loves Thee can know you. None else can realize you.

## \|\| 245.78 \|\|

*tvanmāyāpaṭasaṃvīto jagatyatra jagatpate \|*  
*kastvāṃ vetsyati sarveśa tvatprasādaṃ vinā naraḥ \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. Thou art sprung of Thyself for the creation of this universe, mayst Thou grow ever. Victory to Thee! Nandishvara, Liana, Lord, Vamana grow prosperous and sustain the universe.

## \|\| 245.79 \|\|

*tvamevā’rādhito yena prasādasumukhaprabho \|*  
*sa eva kevalo deva vetti tvāṃ netare janāḥ \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. Shaunaka said: — Vamana thus prayed by Brahma, smiled and gravely said:

## \|\| 245.80-81 \|\|

*nandīśvareśvareśāna prabho vardhasva vāmana \|*  
*prabhavāyāsya viśvasya viśvātmanpṛthulocanā \|\| 80 \|\|*

*śaunaka uvāca*  
*evaṃ stuto hṛṣīkeśaḥ sa tadā vāmanākṛtiḥ \|*  
*prahasya bhāvagambhīramuvācābjasamudbhavam \|\| 81 \|\|*

80-81. “Brahmana! Kashyapa had prayed to me along with you and the Devas like Indra, etc., and I knew your object. Later on when Aditi prayed, then I also said that Indra would be the Lord of the three realms free from any foes.

## \|\| 245.82 \|\|

*stuto'haṃ bhavatā pūrvamindrā dyaiḥ kaśyapena ca \|*  
*mayā ca vaḥ pratijñātamindra sya bhuvanatrayam \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. Again I say this truly unto you all, that I will keep my promise by making Indra the Lord of the three realms.”

## \|\| 245.83-85 \|\|

*bhūyaścāhaṃ stuto'dityā tasyāścāpi pratiśrutam \|*  
*yathā śakrāya dāsyāmi trailokyaṃ hatakaṇṭakam \|\| 83 \|\|*

*so'haṃ tathā kariṣyāmi yathendro jagataḥ patiḥ \|*  
*bhaviṣyati sahasrākṣaḥ satyametadbravīmi vaḥ \|\| 84 \|\|*

*tataḥ kṛṣṇājinaṃ brahmā hṛṣīkeśāya dattavān \|*  
*yajñopavītaṃ bhagavāndadau tasmai bṛhaspatiḥ \|\| 85 \|\|*

83-85. Then Brahma gave Vamana a deerskin, Vrihaspati invested Him with the sacred thread, Marichi the son of Brahma gave him Danda (mace),

the sage Vasistha gave him Kamandala, Amgira gave Him Kusha grass and the Vedas’ the sage Pulaha gave Him Akshasutra, Pulastya gave Him white raiments; then all the Vedas with the most sacred Omkara; the Sankhya and the Yoga Shastra and the Sakhas of the Vedas began to worship Him.

## \|\| 245.86-90 \|\|

*āṣāḍhamadadāddaṇḍaṃ marīcirbrahmaṇaḥ sutaḥ \|*  
*kamaṇḍaluṃ vasiṣṭhaśca kauśaṃ vedamathāṅgirāḥ \|\| 86 \|\|*

*akṣasūtraṃ ca pulahaḥ pulastyaḥ sitavāsasī \|*  
*upatasthuśca taṃ vedāḥ praṇavasvarabhūṣaṇāḥ \|*  
*śāstrāṇyaśeṣāṇi tathā sāṃkhyayogoktayaśca yāḥ \|\| 87 \|\|*

*sa vāmano jaṭī daṇḍī chatrī dhṛtakamaṇḍaluḥ \|*  
*sarvadevamayo bhūpa baleradhvaramabhyagāt \|\| 88 \|\|*

*yatra yatra padaṃ bhūyo bhūbhāge vāmano dadau \|*  
*dadāti bhūmirvivaraṃ tatra tatrātipīḍitā \|\| 89 \|\|*

*sa vāmano jaḍagatirmṛdu gacchansaparvatām \|*  
*sābdhidvīpavatīṃ sarvāṃ cālayāmāsa medinīm \|\| 90 \|\|*

86-90. All the Pastas such as Samkhya Yoga, etc., were also attained by Vamana. Afterwards Vamana with his long hair, danda, kamandala and umbrella visited the sacrifice of the demon king Bali. The portion of the land on which Vamana put His feet in walking sank down and a deep hole appeared there and He made the whole world with all its mountains to oceans, and earth with island quiver though He walked slowly.

## Chapter 246

## \|\| 246.1 \|\|

*śaunaka uvāca*  
*saparvatavanāmurvīṃ dṛṣṭvā saṃkṣobhitāṃ baliḥ \|*  
*papracchośanasaṃ śuddhaṃ praṇipatya kṛtāñjaliḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Shaunaka said: — The demon king Bali on seeing the land quaking with all its forests and mountains, bowed down to his preceptor Shri Shukracharya and said:

## \|\| 246.2 \|\|

*ācārya kṣobhamāyātā sābdhibhūbhṛdvanā mahī \|*  
*kasmācca nā’surānbhāgānpratigṛhṇanti vahnayaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. “Preceptor! why does this land with all its oceans, forests and mountains shake and why does Agni not accept the offerings made in the name of the demons?”

## \|\| 246.3-8 \|\|

*iti pṛṣṭo'tha balinā kāvyo vedavidāṃ varaḥ \|*  
*uvāca daityādhipatiṃ ciraṃ dhyātvā mahāmatiḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*avatīrṇo jagadyoniḥ kaśyapasya gṛhe hariḥ \|*  
*vāmaneneha rūpeṇa jagadātmā sanātanaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*sa eṣa jajñamāyāti tava dānavapuṃgava \|*  
*tatpādanyāsavikṣobhādiyaṃ pracalitā mahī \|*  
*kampante girayaścāmī kṣubhito makarālayaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*nainaṃ bhūtapatiṃ bhūmiḥ samarthā voḍhumīśvaram \|*  
*sadevāsuragandharvayakṣarākṣasakiṃnarā \|\| 6 \|\|*

*anenaiva dhṛtā bhūmirāpo'gniḥ pavano nabhaḥ \|*  
*dhārayatyakhilāndevo manvādīṃśca mahāsura \|\| 7 \|\|*

*iyameva jagaddhetormāyā kṛṣṇasya gahvarī \|*  
*dhāryadhārakabhāvena yayā saṃpīḍitaṃ jagat \|\| 8 \|\|*

3-8. On being thus questioned by Bali, Shukra said after a deep meditation: — “Lord Hari has been born as Vamana in the house of Kashyapa and He is coming to your sacrifice. This earth is trembling on account of the thumping of His feet. For the same reason the planets are quivering, the oceans are being agitated. This land cannot bear His weight. The Devas, the Gandharvas, the demons, the Yakshas, the Kinnaras united cannot bear the weight of Vishnu. He is holding this earth; therefore this earth is sustaining fire, water, sky, air, all the Manus, etc. He is the sustainer and the sustained; He is now tormenting this earth; it is the thick Maya of Shrikrishna that is the cause of this world.

## \|\| 246.9 \|\|

*tatsaṃnidhānādasurā bhāgārhā nāsurottama \|*  
*bhuñjate nā’surānbhāgānamī tenaiva cāgnayaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The earth is so much agitated on account of its becoming the holder instead of remaining the held. The sacrificial fire refuses to accept the offerings owing to the Lord being in such a close proximity.”

## \|\| 246.10-13 \|\|

*baliruvāca*  
*dhanyo'haṃ kṛtapuṇyaśca yanme yajñapatiḥ svayam \|*  
*yajñamabhyāgato brahmanmattaḥ ko'nyo'dhikaḥ pumān \|\| 10 \|\|*

*yaṃ yoginaḥ sadā yuktāḥ paramātmānamavyayam \|*  
*dra ṣṭumicchanti deveśaṃ sa bhe'dhvaramupaiṣyati \|\| 11 \|\|*

*hotā bhāgaprado'yaṃ ca yamudgātā ca gāyati \|*  
*tamadhvareśvaraṃ viṣṇuṃ mattaḥ ko'nya upaiṣyati \|\| 12 \|\|*

*sarveśvareśvare kṛṣṇe madadhvaramupāgate \|*  
*yanmayā kāvya kartavyaṃ tanmamā’deṣṭumarhasi \|\| 13 \|\|*

10-13. Bali said “I am indeed blessed for Lord Vishnu the lord of sacrifices is coming to grace my sacrifice with His presence, who can be really more blessed than myself. The Lord whom the Yogis wish to acquire through their asceticism will come to my sacrifice, which other man than myself will have the good luck of attaining the Lord whom the Hotas give a share in the sacrificial offerings and whose praises are sung by the Udgatas. Preceptor! be pleased to advise me as to what would be meet; for me when Shrikrishna the Lord of all comes here.”

## \|\| 246.14 \|\|

*śukra uvāca*  
*yajñabhāgabhujo devā vedagrāmāṇyato'sura \|*  
*tvayā tu dānavā daityā makhabhāgabhujaḥ kṛtāḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Shri Shukracharya said: — “Demon! on the authority of the Vedas only the Devas are entitled to the sacrificial offerings, but you have given only to the demons.

## \|\| 246.15-17 \|\|

*ayaṃ ca devaḥ sattvasthaḥ karoti sthitipālanam \|*  
*visṛṣṭeranu cānnena svayamatti prajāḥ prabhuḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*tvatkṛte bhavitā nūnaṃ devo viṣṇuḥ sthitau sthitaḥ \|*  
*viditvaitanmahābhāga kuru yatnamanāgatam \|\| 16 \|\|*

*tvayā hi daityādhipate svalpake'pi hi vastuni \|*  
*pratijñā na hi voḍhavyā vācyaṃ sāma vṛthāphalam \|\| 17 \|\|*

15-17. Lord Vishnu, pervades the universe and sustains it through Satva and the very same Lord annihilates the creation in His manifestation of Shiva. Now the Lord Vishnu is engaged in sustaining the creation, so you should be on your guard. Demon king! if Vishnu finds a place, in your sacrifice, He will grow stronger. So you should not commit yourself to Him. You should put Him off.

## \|\| 246.18 \|\|

*nālaṃ dātumahaṃ deva daitya vācyaṃ tvayā vacaḥ \|*  
*kṛṣṇasya devabhūtyarthaṃ pravṛttasya mahāsura \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. You should simply say that you are not in a position to give Him anything for Lord Krishna is coming here to fulfil the object of the Devas.”

## \|\| 246.19 \|\|

*baliruvāca*  
*brahmankathamahaṃ brūyāmanyenāpi hi yācitaḥ \|*  
*nāstīti kimu devena saṃsārāghaughahāriṇā \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Bali said: — “Deva! I never refuse the prayers of anyone, how can I possibly do so in case of the Lord Vishnu who is the dispeller of all ills?

## \|\| 246.20 \|\|

*vratopavāsairvividhaiḥ pratisaṃgrāhyate hariḥ \|*  
*sa cedvakṣyati dehīti govindaḥ kimato'dhikam \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Lord Vishnu is worshipped by means of various ordinances, what can be more to me than the asking of the Lord for something?

## \|\| 246.21-24 \|\|

*yadarthamupahārāḍhyāstapaḥśaucaguṇānvitaiḥ \|*  
*yajñāḥ kriyante deveśaḥ sa māṃ dehīti vakṣyati \|\| 21 \|\|*

*tatsādhu sukṛtaṃ karma tapaḥ sucaritaṃ mama \|*  
*yanmayā dattamīśeśaḥ svayamādāsyate hariḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*nāsti nāstītyahaṃ vakṣye tamapyāgatamīśvaram \|*  
*yadi vañcāmi taṃ prāptaṃ vṛthā tajжanmanaḥ phalam \|\| 23 \|\|*

*yajñe'sminyadi yajñeśo yācate māṃ janārdanaḥ \|*  
*nijamūrdhānamapyatra taddāsyāmyavicāritam \|\| 24 \|\|*

21-24. What can be the greater fruit of an asceticism to me than the asking of the Lord for something from me! It indeed means my uncommon good fortune that the Lord for whose sake various asceticisms, gifts, sacrifices, etc., are performed will accept my gift in person? Oh! certainly I did lots of good work in my previous births, I performed severe asceticism, and I did many sacrifices; therefore Hari will take gifts from my hand in my sacrifice.

## \|\| 246.23 \|\|

*nāsti nāstītyahaṃ vakṣye tamapyāgatamīśvaram \|*  
*yadi vañcāmi taṃ prāptaṃ vṛthā tajжanmanaḥ phalam \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. If I refuse to comply with the request of the Lord I shall indeed render my life fruitless.

## \|\| 246.24 \|\|

*yajñe'sminyadi yajñeśo yācate māṃ janārdanaḥ \|*  
*nijamūrdhānamapyatra taddāsyāmyavicāritam \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. If Lord Vishnu the Lord of sacrifices asks me to give him my head even, I shall not hesitate to comply with His request.

## \|\| 246.25 \|\|

*nāstīti yanmayā noktamanyeṣāmapi yācatām \|*  
*vakṣyāmi kathamāyāte tadanabhyastamacyute \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. How would it be possible for me to say ‘No’ to the Lord when I do not do so with any other person? It is not my habit to tell “No” when anybody asks anything from me.

## \|\| 246.26 \|\|

*ślāghya eva hi vīrāṇāṃ dānādāpatsamāgamaḥ \|*  
*nābādhakāri yaddānaṃ tadamaṅgalavatsmṛtam \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. It is said to be good even if one invites adversity on him through charity. The charity in the performance of which hitch arises is said to be void of good fortune.

## \|\| 246.27-32 \|\|

*madrā jye nāsukhī kaścinna daridro na cā'turaḥ \|*  
*nābhūṣito na codvigno na sragādivivarjitaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

*hṛṣṭastuṣṭaḥ sugandhiśca tṛptaḥ sarvasukhānvitaḥ \|*  
*janaḥ sarvo mahābhāga kimutāhaṃ sadā sukhī \|\| 28 \|\|*

*etadviśiṣṭapātro'yaṃ dānabījaphalaṃ mama \|*  
*viditaṃ bhṛguśārdūla mayaitattvatprasādataḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*etadvijānato dānabījaṃ patati cedguro \|*  
*janārdanamahāpātre kiṃ na prāptaṃ tato mayā \|\| 30 \|\|*

*matto dānamavāpyeśo yadi puṣṇāti devatāḥ \|*  
*upabhogāddaśaguṇaṃ dānaṃ ślāghyatamaṃ mama \|\| 31 \|\|*

*matprasādaparo nūnaṃ yajñenā’rādhito hariḥ \|*  
*tenābhyeti na saṃdeho darśanādupakārakṛt \|\| 32 \|\|*

27-32. There are in my kingdom no poor, unhappy suffering, agitated, angry people nor those void of ornaments, garland, etc. All my people are contented, strong, and happy. I am happy in every way. Through your favour I have got such an opportunity of giving a gift to such an worthy personage! If I sow the seed of my gift in the receptacle of the Lord Vishnu, what will remain for me to achieve? If the Devas prosper by virtue of my gift, even then I shall have tenfold benefit. This is indeed an opportunity to win eternal fame. All the objects are attained by the sight of Lord Vishnu, what can be greater bliss to me than the acquirement of the Lord’s grace?

## \|\| 246.33 \|\|

*atha kopena cābhyeti devabhāgoparodhinam \|*  
*māṃ nihantumanāścaiva vadhaḥ ślāghyataro'cyutām \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Deva! if the Lord comes to me in fury for my having stopped the sacrificial offerings of the Devas and even if He kills me in His wrath,, that too would be best for me as my death at the hands of Lord Vishnu would lead me to Emancipation.

## \|\| 246.34 \|\|

*tanmayaṃ sarvamevedaṃ nāprāpyaṃ yasya vidyate \|*  
*sa māṃ yācitumabhyeti nānugrahamṛte hariḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. It is indeed exceedingly kind of Lord Vishnu who has everything at His command to come and ask me for something.

## \|\| 246.35 \|\|

*yaḥ sṛjatyātmabhūḥ sarvaṃ cetasaiva ca saṃharet \|*  
*sa māṃ hantuṃ hṛṣīkeśaḥ kathaṃ yatnaṃ kariṣyati \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. How would Lord Vishnu who creates and sustains the universe and annihilates it at His pleasure, devise means to kill me?

## \|\| 246.36 \|\|

*etadviditvā na guro dānavighnakareṇa me \|*  
*tvayā bhāvyaṃ jagannāthe govinde samupasthite \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Noble Preceptor! keeping all this in view, you should not stand in the way of my charity Sri Govinda, the Lord of the universe, and you should also present yourself before Him when He comes.”

## \|\| 246.37 \|\|

*śaunaka uvāca*  
*ityevaṃ vadatastasya saṃprāptaḥ sa jagatpatiḥ \|*  
*sarvadevamayo'cintyo māyāvāmanarūpadhṛk \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Shaunaka said: — As the discourse between the preceptor and the pupil was going on, Lord Vishnu the great incomprehensible, appeared there in His (dwarfish) Vamana form.

## \|\| 246.38-39 \|\|

*taṃ dṛṣṭvā yajñavāṭāntaḥ praviṣṭamasurāḥ prabhum \|*  
*jagmuḥ sabhāsadaḥ kṣobhaṃ tejasā tasya niṣprabhāḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

*jepuśca munayastatra ye sametā mahādhvare \|*  
*baliścaivākhilaṃ janma mene saphalamātmanaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

38-39. At His sight all the demons present at the sacrifice lost their lustre and all the sages present there began to pray the Lord and mutter Japam and the demon king Bali also thought himself blessed.

## \|\| 246.40 \|\|

*tataḥ saṃkṣobhamāpanno na kaścitkiṃciduktavān \|*  
*pratyekaṃ devadeveśaṃ pūjayāmāsa cetasā \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. The demons did not speak anything to any one and all present there adored the Lord mentally with great devotion.

## \|\| 246.41-42 \|\|

*athāsurapatiṃ prahvaṃ dṛṣṭvā munivarāṃśca tān \|*  
*devadevapatiḥ sākṣī viṣṇurvāmanarūpadhṛk \|\| 41 \|\|*

*tuṣṭāva yajñavahniṃ ca yajamānamatharttvijaḥ \|*  
*yajñakarmādhikārasthānsadasyāndra vyasaṃpadaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*
