41-42. Lord Vamana, the witness of all, the Lord of the Deva of the Devas seeing the demon king Bali so meek and mild and looking at the seers assembled there; began to praise sacrificial Agni, Yajamana, Ritvijas, sacrificial articles and the courtiers engaged in the performance of sacrifices.

## \|\| 246.43-44 \|\|

*tataḥ prasannamakhilaṃ vāmanaṃ prati tatkṣaṇāt \|*  
*yajñavāṭasthitaṃ vīraḥ sādhu sādhvityudīrayan \|\| 43 \|\|*

*sa cārghamādāya baliḥ prodbhūtapulakastadā \|*  
*pūjayāmāsa govindaṃ prāha cedaṃ mahāsuraḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

43-44. After a few moments all assembled there became highly pleased with Vamana and Bali the demon king also shared the feelings of all present, said: — “Sadhu! Sadhu!” and got up to offer Argha to the Lord, and said:

## \|\| 246.45-46 \|\|

*baliruvāca*  
*suvarṇaratnasaṃghātaṃ gajāśvamamitaṃ tathā \|*  
*striyo vastrāṇyalaṃkārāṃstathā grāmāṃśca puṣkalān \|\| 45 \|\|*

*sarvasvaṃ sakalāmurvīṃ bhavato vā yadīpsitam \|*  
*taddadāmi vṛṇuṣva tvaṃ yenārthī vāmanaḥ priyaḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

45-46. “Lord Vamana! you look so dear and charming. I shall be pleased to give you heaps of gold, gems, elephants, horses, fairest women, clothes, ornaments, villages, the land of the seven oceans. Ask for anything out of these that you may like best. I will give that to you.”

## \|\| 246.47-48 \|\|

*śaunaka uvāca*  
*ityukto daityapatinā prītigarbhānvitaṃ vacaḥ \|*  
*prāha sasmitagambhīraṃ bhagavānvāmanākṛtiḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

*vāmana uvāca*  
*mamāgniśaraṇārthāya dehi rājanpadatrayam \|*  
*suvarṇagrāmaratnāni tadarthibhyaḥ pradīyatām \|\| 48 \|\|*

47-48. When Bali uttered such words with so much feeling, Lord Vamana smiled and gravely said “King! give Me simply land measured by My three feet. Give gems, gold, villages, etc., to those who ask for them.”

## \|\| 246.49 \|\|

*baliruvāca*  
*tribhiḥ prayojanaṃ kiṃ te pādaiḥ padavatāṃ vara \|*  
*śataṃ śatasahasrāṇāṃ padānāṃ mārgatāṃ bhavān \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Bali said: — “Why do you ask for three feet of land only? What purpose of yours will be served by that? You are most welcome to take hundred or thousand feet of land.”

## \|\| 246.50 \|\|

*vāmana uvāca*  
*dharmabuddhyā daityapate kṛtakṛtyo'smi tāvatā \|*  
*anyeṣāmarthināṃ vittamīhitaṃ dāsyate bhavān \|\| 50 \|\|*  
*śaunaka uvāca*  
*etacchrutvā tu gaditaṃ vāmanasya mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*dadau tasmai mahābāhurvāmanāya padatrayam \|\| 51 \|\|*

50\. Vamana said: — “I shall be amply satisfied with this much land. I only want this much. The rest of your gifts you may confer on other people who ask for them”.

## \|\| 246.52 \|\|

*pāṇau tu patite toye vāmano'bhūdavāmanaḥ \|*  
*sarvadevamayaṃ rūpaṃ darśayāmāsa tatkṣaṇāt \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. Hearing those words of Vamana, the demon king Bali gave three feet of land to the Lord. — 51. V After the Lord had received the promise that Bali would make the required gift. He instantly began to grow, who is composed of all the Devas.

*candra sūryau ca nayane dyaurmūrdhā caraṇau kṣitiḥ \|*

*pramathya sarvānasurānpādahastatalairvibhuḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

53-65. He had the Sun and the Moon for His eyes, the heaven was His forehead, the earth became His feet, the demons were the fingers of His feet, the Guhyakas the fingers of His hand, the Vishvedevas in His knees, Sadhya Devas in His ankles, the Yakshas in His fingernails, the nymphs da Sa streaky all the solar rays in His hairs of the head, stars in His eyes and hairs, the Rishis in His small hair over the body. Similarly His arms were the intermediate directions, ears were the directions in which were enshrined Ashvani Kumars, the wind was located in the nose; the Moon in His cheerfulness, Dharma in His mind, Truth in His speech, the Goddess Sarasvati in His tongue, the Divine mother Aditi in his neck, the knowledge in His wrists, Maitra on top of the skull, the door to. Heaven Tvasta and Pusha; in His eye-brows, Agni was the mouth, Prajapati the testicles, Para-Brahma the heart, the sage Kashyapa His manliness, Vasus the back, Marudgana in all the joints, the Suktas and the Rich as the teeth, planets and stars in His lustre. Lord Shiva was in His chest, the ocean was the forbearance, the valiant Gandharvas were the stomach, the Goddess Lakshmi, Intellect (Medha), Steadiness (Dhriti, Lustre, (Kanti), and all Knowledge (Vidya) were in the waist. Then supernatural strength and energy came to that Being and the Munis saw that in His belly, breasts were the Vedas; in His belly, the great sacrifices and the loins were the eyes. The demons also saw that Form composed of the Devas and they were also blessed. They all were attracted to Him like the insects in the fire of His glory and Lord Vamana assuming the huge form rubbed the sole of His feet, as if He was bringing the destruction of the race of the demons.

*vaivasvate tathā'tīte bale manvantare hyatha \|*

66-72. Thus, to protect the Devas, He spread His vast Form and He measured the earth in the twinkling of an eye. Then the Sun and the Moon came in a line with His breast, and when He brought out his third foot, they fell in a line with His thighs; when He started measuring the still more higher regions. They reached His knees. Thus the mighty Divine form of Vishnu spread all over and conquered all the three realms and killed the great Asuras for the benefit of the Devas. He triumphed over all the demons and bestowed the three realms on Indra, and gave the lower region of Sutala to Bali to live in and said “King Bali! since you have given Me a gift which I have accepted therefore you will live a good long life for a Kalpa. After Vaivasvata Manu is succeeded by Savarni Manu, you will become Indra.

Bali in ancient times you had worshipped me most devoutfully, so I will always destroy your enemies. You go and live in Patala at My behest. You go and enshrine yourself in the region abounding in excellent gardens, palaces, luxuriant flowers, lakes, rivers, beatified by the dancing of dancing girls, where you will have various kinds of eatables at your command.

## \|\| 246.80-81 \|\|

You will prosper as long as you do not molest the Devas and the Brahmanas and the moment you do so, you will he undoubtedly entangled in the noose of Varuna, knowing which you should never go against the Devas and the Brahman as.”

82-83. Hearing such words of the Lord, king Bali saluted the Lord and most cheerfully said: — “Lord! be. pleased to tell me how I will be able to get all the things of enjoyments in Patala”.

84-85. Shri Bhagavana said: — “Bali! you shall attain all such good things through misguided charities, through the Shraddha ceremonies void of Brahmanas, oblations on the Fire without any faith, sacrifices without any fees, works without following any rule, through studies without any vow — performed by various persons.

88-92. Thus the Lord had tied the demon king Bali for the benefit of the Devas, in the Patala who is there unto this day. O Arjuna.! your kith and kin, Lord Sri Krishna Who is enshrined at Dvarika, is also there with the object of vanquishing the demons. He will be your charioteer. O Arjuna! as you wanted to hear the history of Lord Yamuna, I have narrated to you all about Him.

Arjuna said: — O Lord! I have heard from you all about the glory of Vishnu. Now permit me to go to Gangadvara. Suta said: — Thus saying Arjuna went away; and Shaunaka went to the forest of Naimisharanya. One who reads or listens to this piece of glory of Lord Vishnu will be liberated from all sins.”

1-4. Arjuna said: — “In the Puranas are narrated the glorious deeds of the Omnipotent Lord Vishnu but I do not know the doings, virtue, intelligence, of His Varaha manifestation. Which form did the Lord assume in His Varaha manifestation? What Deva was He? What did he do in that manifestation? Pray be pleased to tell me all about Him in detail, especially before, this assemblage of Brahmanas”.

## \|\| 247.5-9 \|\|

*śaunaka uvāca*

*chandogīrbhirudārābhiḥ śrutibhiḥ samalaṃkṛtaḥ \|*

*idaṃ purāṇaṃ paramaṃ puṇyaṃ vedaiśca saṃmitam \|*

*purāṇaṃ vedamakhilaṃ sāṃkhyaṃ yogaṃ ca veda yaḥ \|*  
*kārtsnyena vidhinā proktaṃ so'syārthaṃ vedayiṣyati \|\| 9 \|\|*

5-9. Manila said.: — “Arjuna! I shall relate to you all about the Varaha manifestation of the wonderful Krishna. Hear the most interesting history of Varaha as sung in the Vedas. Hear attentively how He raised the earth from the oceans, assuming the form of a boar, and lifting the earth on His tusks. It is most sacred and you should listen to it attentively. It should never be related before an atheist but before one who believes in the Vedas, the Puranas, the Samkhya, the Yoga etc.

10-23. Vishvedevas, Sadhyas, Rudras, Adityas, Ashvani-Kumaras, Prajapati, Sapta Rishis, other seers born out of mind and thought, Vasus, Marudgana, Gandharvas, Yashas, Rakshasas, demons, evil spirits, serpents, all individual souls, Brahmanas, Kshatriyas, Vaishyas, Shudras, Mlechchhas, lower animals, birds, other moveables, and immoveables; all go to Nirvana after thousand yugas pass and a day of Brahma elapses, when Vrishakapi manifests Himself like Fire and consumes the three worlds by His threefold flashes. Then all the things and persons above mentioned become burnt and discoloured by the rays coming out of that Fire. At that moment the Upanishadas, Vedas, Puranas, Itihasas, entire knowledge, Dharmas, the 33 crores of Devas with Brahma merge into Narayana the Supreme Being having mouths on all sides that high-souled, Supremely imperishable soul, the Lord Hamsa. This is known as their death as the Sun rises and sets continually; so the creation and re-absorption again and again, of all these worlds which I am relating to you. When the thousand yugas forming a kalpa expire, all the karmas of all the Jivas get finished. Then the universe sleeps within the Supreme Brahma. In other words Lords Vishnu aft6r annihilating the Devas, demons, men and all the regions remains all by Himself. He then begins to create the universe in the beginning of the next kalpa and destroys everything at the end of it. He is Avikashi, (eternal) Dhruva and the whole universe belongs to Him

## \|\| 247.24-37 \|\|

*naṣṭārkakiraṇe loke candra grahavivarjite \|*  
*tyaktadhūmāgnipavane kṣīṇayajñavaṣaṭkriye \|\| 24 \|\|*

*sa sarvamiti vijñeyo hyeṣa yajñaḥ prajāpatiḥ \|*  
*yadveditavyastridaśaistadeṣa parikīrtyate \|\| 37 \|\|*

24-37. When the Sun loses his lustre, the Moon and the planets vanish, when wind emits fire and smoke, when the sacrifices and Vasat become weak and powerless, when the roads become void of birds and other beings, when the Raudra become void of their honour, when all the quarters become covered with darkness, and when all the regions or Lokas disappear due to the want of any work, then there being no enmity everything assumes a peaceful aspect and this universe rests in Narayana. When He goes to sleep He looks beautiful with His red eyes, yellow garments and cloud-like colour, and with his thousands of black rays resembling matted hairs. A garland of one thousand lotuses hangs on his breast; He becomes anointed with red-sandal paste; Lakshmi Devi rests on Him. Then He goes to wonderful yogic sleep, that peaceful Soul, bringing good to all the worlds, till the completion of a thousand yugas. Then discarding His yogic contemplation He gets up, becoming the Lord himself. He thinks to create the world and through the perseverance of Brahma, He creates the universe with the Devas, men, insects, etc. The very same Narayana is the Creator, Abstainer from business, Annihilator and Prajapati. Verily Narayana is the supreme truth, final beatitude, the Highest region, the highest sacrifice, the self-manifested; He is Sarva, the All worthy of being known by the Devas, etc. He is the sacrifice and Prajapati.

## \|\| 247.38-40 \|\|

*yattu vedyaṃ bhagavato devā api na tadviduḥ \|*  
*prajānāṃ patayaḥ sarve ṛṣayaśca sahāmaraiḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

*nāsyāntamadhigacchanti vicinvanta iti śrutiḥ \|*  
*yadasya paramaṃ rūpaṃ na tatpaśyanti devatāḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

*prādurbhāve tu yadrū paṃ tadarcanti divaukasaḥ \|*  
*darśitaṃ yadi tenaiva tadavekṣanti devatāḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

38-40. "What is worthy of being comprehended by the Supreme Lord of the universe, cannot be known by anyone, Prajapati along with the Devas and Rishis contemplate and do not get the end of the very same supreme spirit, His highest form cannot be seen by the Devas. Brahma and the Devas only adore that form of His which He manifests Himself and which the Devas see.

## \|\| 247.41 \|\|

*yanna darśitavāneṣa kastadanveṣṭumīhate \|*  
*grāmaṇīḥ sarvabhūtānāmagnimārutayorgatiḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. And if he does not like to show His form, His form then cannot he seen by any. He is the strength inherent in the Devas, Agni, Vayu and all the beings of the village.

## \|\| 247.42-44 \|\|

*tejasastapasaścaiva nidhānamamṛtasya ca \|*  
*caturāśramadharmeśaścāturhotraphalāśanaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

*catuḥsāgaraparyantaścaturyuganivartakaḥ \|*  
*tadeṣa saṃhṛtya jagatkṛtvā garbhasthamātmanaḥ \|*  
*mumocāṇḍaṃ mahāyogī dhṛtaṃ varṣasahasrakam \|\| 43 \|\|*

*surāsuradvijabhujagāpsarogaṇairdrumauṣadhikṣitidharayakṣaguhyakaiḥ \|*  
*prajāpatiḥ śrutibhirasaṃkulaṃ kila tadā'sṛjajжagadidamātmanā prabhuḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

42-44 He is the repository of fire, asceticism and immortality, the ruler of the Dharmas of the four Ashramas, the enjoyer of the sacrificial fruits of Chaturhotra, the grantor of salvation up to the four oceans and the originator and mover of the four yugas. He withdraws Himself the whole universe and places it within His comb for one thousand years.

He then brings forth the great egg of the universe. That Lord then created the whole universe with all the Devas, demons, lower animals, birds, serpents, Siddhas, Charanas, Gandharvas, Yakshas, nymphs, mankind, mountains, trees, medicinal herbs and Guhyakas; by means of His glory. At that time the Vedas did not exist.

## Chapter 248

## \|\| 248.1 \|\|

*śaunaka uvāca*  
*jagadaṇḍamidaṃ pūrvamāsīddivyaṃ hiraṇmayam \|*  
*prajāpateriyaṃ mūrtiritīyaṃ vaidikī śrutiḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Shaunaka said: — In olden days, this world was is in the form of a golden egg; and this egg was in the form of Prajapati. This is the Vedic Shruti.

## \|\| 248.2-3 \|\|

*tattu varṣasahasrānte bibhedordhvamukhaṃ vibhuḥ \|*  
*lokasarjanahetostu bibhedādhomukhaṃ punaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*bhūyo'ṣṭadhā bibhedāṇḍaṃ viṣṇurvai lokajanmakṛt \|*  
*cakāra jagataścātra vibhāgaṃ sa vibhāgakṛt \|\| 3 \|\|*

2-3. This very egg was ripped open on its upper side by Lord Vishnu at the end of a thousand years; O king! The Creator then pierced the lower end of the egg, for the creation of Lokas.

## \|\| 248.4-5 \|\|

*yacchidra mūrdhvamākāśaṃ vivarākṛtitāṃ gatam \|*  
*vihitaṃ viśvayogena yadadhastadra sātalam \|\| 4 \|\|*

*yadaṇḍamakarotpūrvaṃ devo lokacikīrṣayā \|*  
*tatra yatsalilaṃ skannaṃ so'bhavatkāñcano giriḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. Again it was divided by Vishnu, the Creator and the great Divider, into eight parts. The bole in the upper half of it became the sky, and that in the lower half formed the Patala. Kamchanagiri was formed by the water that came out first of the egg created by Vishnu for the formation of the Lokas.

## \|\| 248.6-11 \|\|

*śailaiḥ sahasrairmahatī medinī viṣamā'bhavat \|\| 6 \|\|*

*taiśca parvatajālaughairbahuyojanavistṛtaiḥ \|*  
*pīḍitā gurubhirdevī vyathitā medinī tadā \|\| 7 \|\|*

*mahāmate bhūribalaṃ divyaṃ nārāyaṇātmakam \|*  
*hiraṇmayaṃ samutsṛjya tejo vai jātarūpiṇam \|\| 8 \|\|*

*aśaktā vai dhārayitumadhastātprāviśattadā \|*  
*pīḍyamānā bhagavatastejasā tasya sā kṣitiḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*pṛthvīṃ viśantīṃ dṛṣṭvā tu tāmadho madhusūdanaḥ \|*  
*uddhārārthaṃ manaścakre tasyā vai hitakāmyayā \|\| 10 \|\|*

*bhagavānuvāca*  
*matteja eṣā vasudhā samāsādya tapasvinī \|*  
*rasātalaṃ praviśati paṅke gauriva durbalā \|\| 11 \|\|*

6-11. Then thousands of mountains sprang up, and these extended to many thousands of yojanas wide; the earth was overweighed with them and, becoming unable to bear the load, the earth became very much tormented. She became void of the golden tejas (energy) of the all-powerful Divine Narayana, and being oppressed with the weight of the above energy became unable to bear the weight and sank down. Seeing the earth sinking down, Vishnu wanted to raise Her for Her welfare, and He said: — “This Universe, unable to bear my glory, is going down like a cord sinking in a swanp.”

## \|\| 248.12-13 \|\|

*pṛthivyuvāca*  
*trivikramāyāmitavikrāya mahāvarāhāya surottamāya \|*  
*śrīśārṅgacakrāsigadādharāya namo'stu te devavara prasīda \|\| 12 \|\|*

*tava dehājagajжātaṃ puṣkaradvīpamutthitam \|*  
*brahmāṇamihalokānāṃ bhūtānāṃ śāśvataṃ viduḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

12-13. Hearing those words of the Lord, the Universe began to pray to Lord Vishnu: “I salute you, O, the most valiant one, in all the three realms, the most illustrious Mahavar4ha, the most powerful of all the Devas, the one armed with sword, quoit, club, &c. This world has come out of you, and the Pushkara land is born of you. Brahma, the Creator of the Universe, has been born out of your body and has acquired sempiternity amongst the beings.

## \|\| 248.14-16 \|\|

*tava prasādāddevo'yaṃ divaṃ bhuṅkte puraṃdaraḥ \|*  
*tava krodhāddhi balavāñjanārdana jito baliḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*dhātā vidhātā saṃhartā tvayi sarvaṃ pratiṣṭhitam \|*  
*manuḥ kṛtānto'dhipatirjvalanaḥ pavano ghanaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*varṇāścā’śramadharmāśca sāgarāstaravo'calāḥ \|*  
*nadyo dharmaśca kāmaśca yajñā yajñasya ca kriyāḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

14-16. Through your glory alone, Lord Indra enjoys the pleasures of heaven, O, Lord Janardana! the demon king Bali, has been conquered by your wrath. You are the Sustainer, the Creator and the Ainnihilator. The whole creation rests in you. The Manus, the Dharmaraja, Agni, Vayu, Clouds, Varnashramadharmas, oceans, trees, rivers, Dharma, Kama, sacrifices, with rituals, are all the component parts of your supreme person.

## \|\| 248.17-18 \|\|

*vidyā vedyaṃ ca sattvaṃ ca hrīḥ śrīḥ kīrtirdhṛtiḥ kṣamā \|*  
*purāṇaṃ vedavedāṅgaṃ sāṃkhyayogau bhavābhavau \|\| 17 \|\|*

*jaṅgamaṃ sthāvaraṃ caiva bhaviṣyaṃ ca bhavacca yat \|*  
*sarvaṃ tacca trilokeṣu prabhāvopahitaṃ tava \|\| 18 \|\|*

17-18. You are knowledge and that which is to he realised through knowledge. You are all these beings, Modesty, Lakshmi, fame, stability, forgiveness, Puranas, Vedas, Vedangas, Samkhya, birth and death, immoveable objects, the three periods; these all are the products of your glory.

## \|\| 248.19-26 \|\|

*tridaśodāraphaladaḥ svargastrīcārupallavaḥ \|*  
*sarvalokamanaḥkāntaḥ sarvasattvamanoharaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

*vimānānekaviṭapastoyadāmbumadhusravaḥ \|*  
*divyalokamahāskandhaḥ satyalokapraśākhavān \|\| 20 \|\|*

*sāgarākāraniryāso rasātalajalāśrayaḥ \|*  
*nāgendra pādapopeto jantupakṣiniṣevitaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*śīlācārāryagandhastvaṃ sarvalokamayo drumaḥ \|*  
*dvādaśārkamayadvīpo rudrai kādaśapattanaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*vasvaṣṭācalasaṃyuktastrailokyāmbhomahodadhiḥ \|*  
*siddhasādhyormikalilaḥ suparṇānilasevitaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

*daityalokamahāgrāho rakṣoragajhaṣākulaḥ \|*  
*pitāmahamahādhairyaḥ svargastrīratnabhūṣitaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*dhīśrīhrīkāntibhirnityaṃ nadībhirupaśobhitaḥ \|*  
*kālayogamahāparvaprayāgagativegavān \|\| 25 \|\|*

*tvaṃ svayogamahāvīryo nārāyaṇa mahārṇavaḥ \|*  
*kālo bhūtvā prasannābhiradbhirhlādayase punaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

19-26. You are the giver of higher fruits to the Devas, you are the winner of the hearts of heavenly ladies, you are the mind of all, you captivate, you are the great, forest-like, wide expanse of ether (mahakasa), the minds of all; of which the rain clouds are the shoulders; Satyaloka is the branches; the oceans are the juice extracted; the nether regions are the basis for water dug round the tree. Airavata is the foot of the tree, all the beings are the birds, and you are the great tree, consisting of all the Lokas, with goodness, gentleness and the other best qualities forming the sweet scent; you are the great ocean in the form of the three Lokas the twelve Adityas are the islands thereof; the eleven Rudras are the foundations and towns; the eight Vasus are the mountains, the Siddhas and the Sadhyas are the billows; the birds are the winds; the Daityas are the crocodiles; the Uragas and Rakshasas the fishes Brahma is the great patience; the heavenly ladies are the gems; Buddhi Lakshmi, modesty and fame, are the rivers. Time is the great knot; sacrifices are the moments thereof. O Narayana! you are mighty by your yoga; you are the great time and become delighted by the clear waters of your own.

## \|\| 248.27-28 \|\|

*tvayā sṛṣṭāstrayo lokāstvayaiva pratisaṃhṛtāḥ \|*  
*viśanti yoginaḥ sarve tvāmeva pratiyojitāḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

*yuge yuge yugāntāgniḥ kālamegho yuge yuge \|*  
*mama bhārāvatārāya deva tvaṃ hi yuge yuge \|\| 28 \|\|*

27-28. The three regions created by you are annihilated again by your fury. All the yogis, impelled by you, again merge into you. You are the fire that is ablaze at the end of each yoga, you are the time, the clouds, and you manifest yourself in all the yogas to bring deliverance to the universe.

## \|\| 248.29-32 \|\|

*tvaṃ hi śuklaḥ kṛtayuge tretāyāṃ campakaprabhaḥ \|*  
*dvāpare raktasaṃkāśaḥ kṛṣṇaḥ kaliyuge bhavān \|\| 29 \|\|*

*vaivarṇyamabhidhatse tvaṃ prāpteṣu yugasaṃdhiṣu \|*  
*vaivarṇyaṃ sarvadharmāṇāmutpādayasi vedavit \|\| 30 \|\|*

*bhāsi vāsi pratapasi tvaṃ ca pāsi viceṣṭase \|*  
*krudhyasi kṣāntimāyāsi tvaṃ dīpayasi varṣasi \|\| 31 \|\|*

*tvaṃ hāsyasi na niryāsi nirvāpayasi jāgrasi \|*  
*niḥśeṣayasi bhūtāni kālo bhūtvā yugakṣaye \|\| 32 \|\|*

29-32. You assume white appearance during Satyayuga, like champaka during Treta and red in Dwapara, and black in Kaliyuga; and you get discoloured and pale in the evening of the yugas, and the Dharmas also get pale. You are shining, you are walking, giving heat, protecting, trying, becoming angry, getting fame, illumining, giving rains, laughing, remaining quiet, waking, and annihilating all the beings at the end of a yuga.

## \|\| 248.32-34 \|\|

*tvaṃ hāsyasi na niryāsi nirvāpayasi jāgrasi \|*  
*niḥśeṣayasi bhūtāni kālo bhūtvā yugakṣaye \|\| 32 \|\|*

*śeṣamātmānamālokya viśeṣayasi tvaṃ punaḥ \|*  
*yugāntāgnyavalīḍheṣu sarvabhūteṣu kiṃcana \|\| 33 \|\|*

*yāteṣu śeṣo bhavasi tasmāccheṣo'si kīrtitaḥ \|*  
*cyavanotpattiyukteṣu brahmendra varuṇādiṣu \|\| 34 \|\|*

32-34. You mark the time of progress, cessation, unconsciousness, and the end of the age; you annihilate everything. You are Shesha, for you alone are left, when all else is destroyed by the fire that burnt at the end of the age. You do not fall even when Brahma, Indra, Varuna and other Devas fall; therefore, you are known as Achyuta.

**Комментарий:**

Note — The rest.

## \|\| 248.35-38 \|\|

*yasmānna cyavase sthānāttasmātsaṃkīrtyase'cyutaḥ \|*  
*brahmāṇamindraṃ ca yamaṃ rudraṃ varuṇameva ca \|\| 35 \|\|*

*nigṛhya harase yasmāttasmāddharirihocyase \|*  
*saṃtānayasi bhūtāni vapuṣā yaśasā śriyā \|\| 36 \|\|*

*pareṇa vapuṣā deva tasmāccāsi sanātanaḥ \|*  
*yasmādbrahmādayo devā munayaścogratejasaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

*na te'ntaṃ tvadhigacchanti tenānantastvamucyase \|*  
*na kṣīyase na kṣarase kalpakoṭiśatairapi \|\| 38 \|\|*

35-38. You control Brahma, Indra, Yama, Rudra, Varuna, and other Devas, and \_ then attract them to you; and that is why you are known as Hari. You are known as Sanatana, for you give body, fame and prosperity, etc., to all the beings; you are Atlanta, for the Devas, Brahma, etc., and sages do not find your end.

## \|\| 248.39-44 \|\|

*tasmāttvamakṣaratvācca akṣaraśca prakīrtitaḥ \|*  
*viṣṭabdhaṃ yattvayā sarvaṃ jagatsthāvarajaṅgamam \|\| 39 \|\|*

*jagadviṣṭambhanāccaiva viṣṇureveti kīrtyase \|*  
*viṣṭabhya tiṣṭhase nityaṃ trailokyaṃ sacāracaram \|\| 40 \|\|*

*yakṣagandharvanagaraṃ sumahadbhūtapannagam \|*  
*vyāptaṃ tvayaiva viśatā trailokyaṃ sacarācaram \|\| 41 \|\|*

*tasmādviṣṇuriti proktaḥ svayameva svayaṃbhuvā \|*  
*nārā ityucyate hyāpo hyṛṣibhistattvadarśibhiḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

*ayanaṃ tasya tāḥ pūrvaṃ tena nārāyaṇaḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*yuge yuge pranaṣṭāṃ gāṃ viṣṇo vindasi tattvataḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

*govindeti tato nāmnā procyase ṛṣibhistathā \|*  
*hṛṣīkāṇīndri yāṇyāhustattvajñānaviśāradāḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

39-44. You do not wane or perish, even in course of crores of Kalpas consequently, you are called Akshaya Vishnu; you are Vishnu, for you pervade the universe, moveable and immoveable. You are omnipresent in the three Lokas in the immoveable objects; and the Yakshas, Gandharvas, serpents and the Universe rest in you; hence Brahma calls you Vishnu. The philosophers call the waters Nara, and you first reposed yourself in the Waters; therefore, you are called Narayana. You revive at the end of every yuga the lost Vedas; that is why you are known by the Rishis as Govinda. You are the master of the senses (Rishis); therefore, you are known as Hrishi Kesha.

## \|\| 248.45-51 \|\|

*īśitā ca tvameteṣāṃ hṛṣīkeśastathocyase \|*  
*vasanti tvayi bhūtāni brahmādīni yugakṣaye \|\| 45 \|\|*

*tvaṃ vā vasasi bhūteṣu vāsudevastathocyase \|*  
*saṃkarṣayasi bhūtāni kalpe kalpe punaḥ punaḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

*tataḥ saṃkarṣaṇaḥ proktastattvajñānaviśāradaiḥ \|*  
*prativyūhena tiṣṭhanti sadevāsurarākṣasāḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

*pravidyuḥ sarvadharmāṇāṃ pradyumnastena cocyase \|*  
*niroddhā vidyate yasmānna te bhūteṣu kaścana \|\| 48 \|\|*

*aniruddhastataḥ proktaḥ pūrvameva maharṣibhiḥ \|*  
*yattvayā dhāryate viśvaṃ tvayā saṃhriyate jagat \|\| 49 \|\|*

*tvaṃ dhārayasi bhūtāni bhuvanaṃ tvaṃ cibharṣi ca \|*  
*yattvayā dhāryate kiṃcittejasā ca balena ca \|\| 50 \|\|*

*mayā hi dhāryate paścānnādhṛtaṃ dhāraye tvayā \|*  
*na hi tadvidyate bhūtaṃ tvayā yannātra dhāryate \|\| 51 \|\|*

45-51. You are Vasudeva, for at the end of the ages Brahma and other Devas rest in you, as well as on account of your Omnipresence in all the beings. You absorb everything by drawing them unto you at the end of each Kalpa, that is why you are named Samkarshana. You are Pradyumna, for the Devas, the demons are sustained in their respective orders and taught duties by yon. You are Aniruddha, for there is none other in the creation that can act as a brake on all the beings. You bear the whole universe, you annihilate it; I only hold what is held by your glory. I can never hold anything which you do not hold yourself.

## \|\| 248.52 \|\|

*tvameva kuruṣe deva nārāyaṇa yuge yuge \|*  
*mahābhārāvataraṇaṃ jagato hitakāmyayā \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. Narayana! You give deliverance to the world at the end of each age, when it is oppressed heavily.

## \|\| 248.53 \|\|

*tavaiva tejasā’krāntāṃ rasātalatalaṃ gatām \|*  
*trāyasva māṃ suraśreṣṭha tvāmeva śaraṇaṃ gatām \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Supreme One! come to my rescue. I have gone down on account of my not being able to cope with your glory. I am at your mercy.

## \|\| 248.54 \|\|

*dānavaiḥ pīḍyamānā'haṃ rākṣasaiśca durātmabhiḥ \|*  
*tvāmeva śaraṇaṃ nityamupayāmi sanātanam \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. I am greatly oppressed by the demons and Rakshasas; and O, Sanitaria I I am at your mercy since eternity.

## \|\| 248.55-56 \|\|

*tāvanme'sti bhayaṃ deva yāvanna tvāṃ kakudminam \|*  
*śaraṇaṃ yāmi manasā śataśo'pyupalakṣaye \|\| 55 \|\|*

*upamānaṃ na te śaktāḥ kartuṃ sendrā divaukasaḥ \|*  
*tattvaṃ tvameva tadvetsi niruttaramataḥ param \|\| 56 \|\|*

55-56. Deva! You are the Bull; and I had all fears till I do not seek mentally your support from my heart, and now what is the fear when I have placed myself under your shelter. Lord of the Devas! when the Devas, like Indra, etc., are not in a position to sing your praises adequately how can I do so? ” There is no other equal to you. You alone are your equal, and you know only who is your equal.

## \|\| 248.57-60 \|\|

*śaunaka uvāca*  
*tataḥ prītaḥ sa bhagavānpṛthivyai śārṅgacakradhṛk \|*  
*kāmamasyā yathākāmamabhipūritavānhariḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

*abravīcca mahādevi mādhavīyaṃ stavottamam \|*  
*dhārayiṣyati yo martyo nāsti tasya parābhavaḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

*lokānniṣkalmaṣāṃścaiva vaiṣṇavānpratipatsyate \|*  
*etadāścaryasarvasvaṃ mādhavīyaṃ stavottamam \|\| 59 \|\|*

*adhītavedaḥ puruṣo muniḥ prītamanā bhavet \|\| 60 \|\|*

57-60. Shaunaka said: — Hearing such a prayer of the Earth, Lord Vishnu was pleased to meet its wishes, and said: — “Devi! One who repeats the prayer just uttered by you will never he overtaken by any misfortune. He will also attain the pure loka of Vaishnavas. Its repetition will give the benefit that one attains by reading the Vedas.

## \|\| 248.61 \|\|

*mā bhairdharaṇi kalyāṇi śāntiṃ vraja mamāgrataḥ \|*  
*eṣa tvāmucitaṃ sthānaṃ prāpayāmi manīṣitam \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Dharani! Kalyani! do not fear. Be in peace I shall situate you nicely.”

## \|\| 248.62-63 \|\|

*śaunaka uvāca*  
*tato mahātmā manasā divyaṃ rūpamacintayat \|*  
*kiṃ nu rūpamahaṃ kṛtvā uddhareyaṃ dharāmimām \|\| 62 \|\|*

*jalakrāḍārucistasmādvārāhaṃ vapurāsthitaḥ \|*  
*adhṛṣyaṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ vāṅmayaṃ brahma saṃsthitam \|\| 63 \|\|*

62-63. Afterwards Lords Vishnu thought of all His Divine manifestations as to which would he most appropriate to enable Him to relieve the sufferings of the Earth at that moment.

## \|\| 248.64-78 \|\|

*śatayojanavistīrṇamucchritaṃ dviguṇaṃ tataḥ \|*  
*nīlajīmūtasaṃkāśaṃ meghastanitaniḥsvanam \|\| 64 \|\|*

*girisaṃhananaṃ bhīmaṃ śvetatīkṣṇāgradaṃṣṭriṇam \|*  
*vidyudagnipratīkāśamādityasamatejasam \|*  
*pīnavṛttāyataskandhaṃ dṛptaśārdūlagāminam \|\| 65 \|\|*

*pīnonnatakaṭīdeśaṃ vṛṣalakṣaṇapūjitam \|*  
*rūpamāsthāya vipulaṃ vārāhamajito hariḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

*pṛthivyuddharaṇāyaiva praviveśa rasātalam \|*  
*vedapādo yūpadaṃṣṭraḥ kratudantaścitīmukhaḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

*agnijihvo darbhalomā brahmaśīrṣo mahātapāḥ \|*  
*ahorātrekṣaṇadharo vedāṅgaśrutibhūṣaṇaḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

*ājyanāsaḥ sruvatuṇḍaḥ sāmaghoṣasvano mahān \|*  
*satyadharmamayaḥ śrīmānkarmavikramasatkṛtaḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

*prāyaścittanakho ghoraḥ paśujānurmakhākṛtiḥ \|*  
*udgīthahomaliṅgo'tha bījauṣadhimahāphalaḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

*vāyvantarātmā yajñāsthivikṛtiḥ somaśoṇitaḥ \|*

*tato jagāma nirvāṇaṃ medinī tasya dhāraṇāt \|*

*athoddhṛtya kṣitiṃ devo jagataḥ sthāpanecchayā \|*  
*pṛthivīpravibhāgāya manaścakre'mbujekṣaṇaḥ \|\| 78 \|\|*

64-78. Then the Lord manifested Himself as a boar that He might enjoy the playing waters. That mighty Lord, incomprehensible by mind and speech of all the beings, that Brahma extended Himself to hundred yojanas in length and twice that in height. Shining and thundering like the blue clouds, looking like a mountain, with white sharp tusks, full of lustre like the sun, lightning and fire, with a high waist; with such a formidable form, adorable by all, He sank down into the Rasatala to lift the world. The Lord, in that mighty manifestation, having the Vedas for His feet, the sacrificial post for His tusks, the sacrificial pit for his mouth, the fire for His tongue, the Kusha grass for His hair, Brahma for His head, night and day for His eyes, Vedangas for His ears, sacrificial clarified butter for His nose, the sacrificial ladel for his snout, the chant of the Samaveda for His breast, truth, virtue and deeds for His courage and effort, purificatory rights for His claws, sacrificial beings for His knees, all the sacrificial emblems as the seed, medicines for the results; the sacrificial altar for His inner self, sacrifices for His. bones, soma, for His blood, the Vedas for His shoulders, Sakalya for His aroma, conjoint with the divisions of havya and kavya, the sacrificial fees for His heart, the Vedas as His passages, Upavarmas for His lips, Pravargyas for his ornaments, with mysterious Upanishadas for His seat, the protector of His shadow like better-half, majestic like the mountain; He raised up the earth on His tusk from the Rasatala, and located it in its proper place. In other words, He let the Earth drop that was sticking to His tusk, though holding Her mentally, after which She felt blessed and made Her obeisance to the Lord. Thus Varaha came to the rescue of the Earth for the welfare of all, and then wished to make partitions on Her.

## \|\| 248.79 \|\|

*rasāṃ gatāmevamacintyavikramaḥ surottamaḥ pravaravarāharūpadhṛk \|*  
*vṛṣākapiḥ prasabhamathaikadaṃṣṭrayā samuddharaddharaṇimatulyapauruṣaḥ \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. The Lord Vrishakapi, of unequalled valour and prowess, has thus brought deliverance to the Earth in the most excellent Boar-form, by means of His single tusk.

## Chapter 249

## \|\| 249.1-2 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*nārāyaṇasya māhātmyaṃ śrutvā sūta yathākramam \|*

1-2. The Rishis asked: — We do not feel amply satisfied by listening to the glory of Narayana that you have been pleased to relate to us. We feel keen to hlear more and more about it. Pray tell us how the Devas became immortal. What karmas they did, what tapasya they practised, or whose favor they gained, or whose energy they imbibed, that they obtained immortality in ancient days.

## \|\| 249.3 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*

*tatrāmaratve sarveṣāṃ sahāyau tatra tau smṛtau \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Suta said: — They became immortal when Narayana and fava helped the Devas in ancient days.

4-12. In days gone by, when war ensued between the Devas and the Asuras, hundreds of Devas used to be killed; but amongst the Daityas, when they were killed, they were restored to their lives by Shukracharya, the son of Bhrigu, with the help of Sanjivani mantra. Lord Shiva was pleased with Bhargava and gave him this wonderful Mrita Sanjivani mantra. Knowing that Shukracharya was acquainted with the above Maheshvari Vidya, direct from the mouth of Lord Shiva, the Daityas began to fight with the Devas, when Shukra restored to life the Daityas that were killed Shukra obtained from Shankara that knowledge, which all the worlds, the Devas, Rakshasas, Nagas, Rishis, Brahma, Chandra and Vishnu could not get so Shukra became very pleased. Thus, when the great war ensued again between the Devas and the Danavas, the Danavas” army, when killed, were early called to their lives. Then Indra and Vrihaspati, and the other Devas became powerless and greatly depressed. It dismayed the Devas, seeing which, Brahma addressed them thus on the summit of the Mount Meru.

## \|\| 249.13-16 \|\|

*brahmovāca*

13-16. “Devas! You should follow My advice and make peace with the distracted demons; then you should make an effort to churn the ocean of milk for nectar. You should win the sympathies of Lord Varuna, and then appeal to the mighty Vishnu for help. You should in churning the ocean employ the Mount Meru as churning-stick, the Shesha serpent as the string of the churning-stick. For the time being you should appease Bali, the king of the demons, so that he may be the supervisor in this work and pray to Kurma, the tortoise- incarnation of the eternal Vishnu, in the Patala, as the base, and the Mount Mandara also for help.

17-22. Healing those words of Brahma, all the Devas went to Patala and said to the demon king Bali: — “Bali! Do not be hostile to us now, we are your slaves. Endeavours should be made to churn the milk-ocean for nectar, for which purpose £3asa has to be utilized as the string of the churning-stick. Demon-king! we will undoubtedly become immortal by the nectar obtained through your grace.” Bali said “Devas! I shall do what you say. I can alone churn the milky ocean. I shall certainly acquire nectar to help you to become immortal, because one who does not oblige his enemies that come from far, is ruined in this life as well as m the next. I shall therefore give you my full support.”

24\. “Mandarachala! the king of the mountains, be pleased to help us in churning the milk-ocean for nectar. Befriend us, for this is a great work for the Devas and the demons.”

25-28. In accepting their prayer, the lord of the mountains said: “ I shall he tire churning-stick, and let someone who may be strong enough to volunteer himself to act as a receptacle, off which I can revolve, then I will be able to chum the ocean; also the Shesha serpent to coil round the stick.

Afterwards the most valiant turtle and Shesha, endowed with of Vishnu’s power, went to support the Earth, and haughtily the Turtle said: — “When I can easily hold all the three regions on my back, bow can I feel the weight of this Mandara mountain?”

30-36. Afterwards all the Devas and the demons hurled Mandarachala into the milk-ocean, after which coiled round it, and Kurma (turtle) placed Himself underneath it as the support of the mountains. When the demons and the Devas could not manage to turn, the floating Mandarachala, all the Devas with Bali went to the abode of the Lord Vishnu, in Vaikuntha, that was shedding its lustre like a white lotus, where the mighty Lord was lying absorbed in deep meditation, wearing yellow clothes, adorned with armlets, &c., shampooed by the Goddess Lakshmi, fanned by the wings of Garuda and prayed for by the Siddhas and Charanas and the Vedas incarnate, reclining on His left hand, placed under His head. All the Devas and the demons prayed to the Lord:

*devadānavā ūcuḥ \|*

37-38. By surrounding Him with folded hands, they all saluted Him, and said: “Lord of the three regions, overpowering by your lustre more than the myriads of the suns, the enemy of Kaitabha, the Great Cause of the universe, the Protector of the creation, we all salute you.

39\. O Annihilator of all, invincible even by the trident, enemy of and as it were a conflagration of the demons, we salute you.

40-41. From your navel-like lake, the lotus-wombed great mountain has sprung up; you are the creator of Brahma; we salute you. O, one who measured the universe with three strides, the Creator of the three regions, the destroyer of the formidable demons, the originator of the highest attributes, shining like a great blaze, the Creator of the universe out of the lotus stick springing up in your navel, the most dear one to all, we salute you.

42-45. Lord of all the realms, the cause of deeds and all causes, the destroyer of the enemies of the Devas, Participator in the great war, we salute you. The one who draws in the honeyed aroma of the Goddess Lakshmi’s lotus-like face, the receptacle of fame, we salute you. Pray, do churn the ocean by holding the mountain by one of your valiant arms to make us immortal. Hearing this prayer, Lord Vishnu shook off His yogic repose, and said:

46\. “Devas and others! Hope you had no inconvenience in the way Pray tell me the object of your having come here.”

## \|\| 249.47-54 \|\|

*nārāyaṇenaivamuktāḥ procustatra divaukasaḥ \|*

*prāptuṃ tadamṛtaṃ nātha tato'gne bhava no vibho \|*

*viṣabhītāstato devā yataḥ pucchaṃ tataḥ sthitāḥ \|*

*sahasravadanaṃ cāsya śiraḥ savyena pāṇinā \|*  
*dakṣiṇena balirdehaṃ nāgasyā’kṛṣṭavāṃstathā \|\| 52 \|\|*

*dadhārāmūtamanthānaṃ mandaraṃ cārukaṃdaram \|*  
*nārāyaṇaḥ sa bhagavānbhujayugmadvayena tu \|\| 53 \|\|*

*tato devāsuraiḥ sarvairjayaśabdapuraḥsaram \|*

47-54. The Devas said: — “Deva! In order to obtain nectar to make Ourselves immortal, we all are churning this ocean, but without your assistance we are helpless. We will be successful, if you lead us,” Hearing those words, Lord Vishnu followed the Devas to that spot where Mandara was floating. The great mountain was then encircled by the Shesha and the Devas and the Asuras took hold of the string. The Devas took hold of the tail end of the Shesha, and the demons, Rahu and others, took the head ends. Lord Vishnu caught hold of the summit of Meru with His left hand and Bali held the thousand heads of Shesha with His left hand, and with his right hand he caught hold of his body; Shesha firmly coiled round the Mandarachala, after which the Devas and the demons started to churn the ocean for a hundred Divine years.

## \|\| 249.55-57 \|\|

*tataḥ śrāntāstu te sarve devā daityapuraḥsarāḥ \|*  
*śrānteṣu teṣu devendro megho bhūtvā'mbuśīkarān \|\| 55 \|\|*

*vavarṣāmṛtakalpāṃstānvavau vāyuśca śītalaḥ \|*  
*bhagnaprāyeṣu deveṣu śānteṣu kamalāsanaḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

*mathyatāṃ mathyatāṃ sindhurityuvāca punaḥ punaḥ \|*  
*avaśyamudyogavatāṃ śrīrapārā bhavetsadā \|\| 57 \|\|*

55-57. When all the Devas and the demons were overcome with fatigue in churning the ocean, Indra caused the rains and cool wind to refresh them. But, in spite of all that, when the Lord Brahma found them giving way to fatigue, He shouted out: “Go on churning. Those who persevere are undoubtedly blessed with the highest prosperity.”

## \|\| 249.58-59 \|\|

*brahmaprotsāhitā devā mamanthuḥ punarambudhim \|*  
*bhrāmyamāṇe tataḥ śaile yojanāyutaśekhare \|\| 58 \|\|*

*nipeturhastiyūthāni varāhaśarabhādayaḥ \|*  
*śvāpadāyutalakṣāṇi tathā puṣpaphaladrumāḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

58-59. The Devas, thus encouraged, applied themselves heart and soul to the task of churning the ocean, when the motion of the Mandarachala 1,000 yojanas high, caused herds of elephants, wild boar, Sharabha, other animals residing on that mountain, trees began to fall down into the ocean.

## \|\| 249.60 \|\|

*tataḥ phalānāṃ vīryeṇa puṣpauṣadhirasena ca \|*  
*kṣīramambudhijaṃ sarvaṃ dadhirūpamajāyata \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Afterwards the juice of the fruits, flowers, the sap of the medicinal herbs, falling into the ocean, was churned along with it, when all the contents of the ocean assumed a curdy appearance.

## \|\| 249.61-63 \|\|

*tatastu sarvajīveṣu cūrṇiteṣu sahasraśaḥ \|*  
*tadambumedasotsargādvāruṇī samapadyata \|\| 61 \|\|*

*vāruṇīgandhamāghrāya mumudurdevadānavāḥ \|*  
*tadāsvādena balino devadaityādayo'bhavan \|\| 62 \|\|*

*tato'tivegājжagṛhurnāgendraṃ sarvato'surāḥ \|*  
*manthānaṃ manthayaṣṭistu merustatrācalo'bhavat \|\| 63 \|\|*

61-63. Innumerable beings were powdered in that violent churning, the fat and marrow of whom, coming in contact with the waters, produced wine, the smell of which pleased all the Devas and the demons, and the taste of it recouped the vigour of the latter. They then churned the ocean most vigorously and the Mount Mandarachala became fixed.

## \|\| 249.64-66 \|\|

*abhavaccāgrato viṣṇurbhujamandarabandhanaḥ \|*  
*savāsukiphaṇālagnapāṇiḥ kṛṣṇo vyarājata \|\| 64 \|\|*

*yathā nīlotpalairyukto brahmadaṇḍo'tivistaraḥ \|*  
*dhvanirmeghasahasrasya jaladherutthitastadā \|\| 65 \|\|*

*bhāge dvitīye maghavānādityastu tataḥ param \|*  
*tato rudrā mahotsāhā vasavo guhyakādayaḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

64-66. Vishnu came forward, and with his arms, holding the lotus and as long as Brahmanda, caught hold of the Mandara mountain, placing His hand on the hood of Vasuki. Vishnu turned black on account of His having covered the mouth of Shesha. Then emitted from the oceans sounds like thousands of thunders. Indra, Surya, Rudra and Vasus, Guhyakas placed themselves at the second end of Vasuki.

## \|\| 249.67-68 \|\|

*purato vipracittiśca namucirvṛtraśambarau \|*  
*dvimūrdhā vajradaṃṣṭraśca saiṃhikeyo balistathā \|\| 67 \|\|*

*ete cānye ca bahavo mukhabhāgamupasthitāḥ \|*  
*mamanthurambudhiṃ dṛptā balatejovibhūṣitāḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

67-68. At head of them, Viprachitta, Namuchi, Vritra, Shamvara, Dvimurdha, Vagrudamshtra, Rahu, Bali, &c., facing the mouth of Shesha, applied themselves to the churning of the ocean.

## \|\| 249.69-70 \|\|

*babhūvātra mahāghoṣo mahāmegharavopamaḥ \|*  
*udadhermathyamānasya mandareṇa surāsuraiḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

69-70. Now here, then, was a thundering din caused by the churning of the ocean, thousands of the aquatic beings fell dead by the blow of the Mandara mountain.

## \|\| 249.71 \|\|

*vāruṇāni ca bhūtāni vividhāni mahīdharaḥ \|*  
*pātālatalavāsīni vilayaṃ samupānayat \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. Many of the aquatic beings living in Patala also met with the same fate.

## \|\| 249.72 \|\|

*tasmiṃśca bhrāmyamāṇe'drau saṃghṛṣṭāśca parasparam \|*  
*nyapatanpatagopetāḥ parvatāgrānmahādrumāḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. Later on, the trees on Mandarachala fell down into the ocean along with birds on them rubbing against one another.

## \|\| 249.73-75 \|\|

*teṣāṃ saṃgharṣaṇāccāgnirarṣibhiḥ prajvalanmuhuḥ \|*  
*vidyudbhiriva nīlābhramāvṛṇonmandaraṃ girim \|\| 73 \|\|*

*dadāha kuñjarāṃścaiva siṃhāṃścaiva viniḥsṛtān \|*  
*vigatāsūni sarvāṇi sattvāni vividhāni ca \|\| 74 \|\|*

*tamagnimamaraśreṣṭhaḥ pradahantamitastataḥ \|*  
*vāriṇā meghajenendra ḥ! śamayāmāsa sarvataḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

73-75. The rubbing of the trees produced a blaze of fire like lightning which enveloped all that mountain and also consumed all the elephants, lions, &c., residing on it, which also fell charred dead into the ocean. Afterwards Indra quenched the fire by bringing down rain.

## \|\| 249.76 \|\|

*tato nānārasāstatra susruvuḥ sāgarāmbhasi \|*  
*mahādrumāṇāṃ niryāsā bahavaścauṣadhīrasāḥ \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. When myrrh of the various trees and the juice of several plants trickled into the ocean.

## \|\| 249.78 \|\|

*atha tasya samudra sya tajжātamudakaṃ payaḥ \|*  
*rasāntarairvimiśraṃ ca tataḥ kṣīrādabhūddhṛtam \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. Through the potent sap of those plants the Devas of golden colour felt themselves immortal (?)

Then the ocean turned like milk and clarified butter came out of it by admixture of the various saps.

## \|\| 249.82 \|\|

*viṣṇuruvāca*  
*balaṃ dadāmi sarveṣāṃ karmaitadye samāsthitāḥ \|*  
*kṣobhyatāṃ kramaśaḥ sarvairmandaraḥ parivartyatām \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. The Devas, then said to Brahma We all feel quite exhausted and the nectar has not yet come out. Excepting Narayana, the Devas and the Daityas won’t get nectar, even if they go on churning for a long, long period.” Hearing which Brahma prayed to Narayana; “You are the supporter of them all, therefore, be pleased to impart them strength.”

Vishnu said: — “I am imparting strength to those that are exhausted; move the Mandarachala carefully and steadily.”

## Chapter 250

*sūta uvāca*

*śrīranantaramutpannā ghṛtātpāṇḍuravāsinī \|*

*upāviśannabdhitaṭe śiraḥ saṃgṛhya pāṇinā \|*

*anantaraṃ samudbhūtāstasmāḍḍuṇḍubhajātayaḥ \|*

3-10. Next came out the Goddess Lakshmi, wearing white raiments followed by Sura Devi; after whom was obtained the horse Uchaishrava; later on came the precious divine Kaustubha gem, nectar-like, cheering which Vishnu took it and placed on His chest. Afterwards came out the charming Parijata flower shrub with bunches of golden flowers. Shortly after the Devas and the demons found the sky covered with smoke which gradually spread in every direction and caused terrible headache to everyone making them senseless and he down. They all sat down on the coast holding their heads. In the meantime that smoke turned out to be the unbearable Barabanala (conflagration) by the heat of which many Devas and demons were singed and began to run about in all directions after it Dundubha snakes, various kinds of red and black snakes, living on air alone, came forth. Also came out serpents with long teeth, red-coloured snakes, snakes living on air alone, also white, yellow and variously coloured snakes, also snakes came out of Gnasa class.

## \|\| 250.11-12 \|\|

*śvetapītāstathā cānye tathā gonasajātayaḥ \|*  
*maśakā bhramarā daṃśā makṣikāḥ śalabhāstathā \|\| 11 \|\|*

*karṇaśalyāḥ kṛkalāsā aneke caiva babhramuḥ \|*  
*prāṇino daṃṣṭriṇo raudrā stathā hi viṣajātayaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-12. Next came forth mosquitoes, flies, centipedes, and innumerable kinds of venomous insects and terrible beings.

## \|\| 250.13 \|\|

*śārṅgahālāhalāmustavatsakaṃgūrubhasmagāḥ \|*  
*nīlapatrādayaścānye śataśo bahubhedinaḥ \|*  
*yeṣāṃ gandhena dahyante giriśṛṅgāṇyapi drutam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Then came out most deadly poisons by the mere fumes of which the mountain summits were consumed as well as Sharuga, Halahala, Musta, Vatsa, Kangaru, Bhasmaga, and Nilapatra and hundreds of other poisonous things.

## \|\| 250.14-17 \|\|

*anantaraṃ nīlarasaughabhṛṅgabhinnāñjanābhaṃ viṣamaṃ śvasantam \|*  
*kāyena lokāntarapūrakeṇa keśaiśca vahnipratimairjvaladbhiḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*suvarṇamuktāphalabhūṣitāṅgaṃ kirīṭinaṃ pītadukūlajuṣṭam \|*  
*nīlotpalābhaṃ kusumaiḥ kṛtārghaṃ garjantamambhodharabhīmavegam \|\| 15 \|\|*

*adrā kṣurambhonidhimadhyasaṃsthaṃ savigrahaṃ dehibhayāśrayaṃ tam \|*  
*vilokya taṃ bhīṣaṇamugranetraṃ bhūtāśca vitresurathāpi sarve \|\| 16 \|\|*

*kecidvilokyaiva gatā hyabhāvaṃ niḥsaṃjñatāṃ cāpyapare prapannāḥ \|*  
*vemurmukhebhyo'pi ca phenamanye kecittvavāptā viṣamāmavasthām \|\| 17 \|\|*

14-17. Shortly after the Devas and the demons beheld in that vast ocean a terrible form of blue colour, like Bhringa Anjana and mountain, shining like golden clouds, full of precious gems and roaring like clouds; the most deadly poison — Kalakuta — strong like fire. It is throwing off awful breath; and enveloping all the Lokas by its body; its hairs blazing like fire. Its body was decked with golden gems; it was dressed in yellow robes a crown on the head and adorned with various flowers. It began to make dreadful noise in the ocean. Its fumes pervaded all round and caused an awful consternation among those present there. Under its deadly influence, many became petrified, most of them began to vomit froth. They all were awfully terrified and most of them were rendered senseless.

## \|\| 250.18 \|\|

*śvāsena tasya nirdagdhāstato viṣṇvindra dānavāḥ \|*  
*dagdhāṅgāranibhā jātā ye bhūtā divyarūpiṇaḥ \|*  
*tatastu saṃbhramādviṣṇustamuvāca surātmakam \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. By its fumes Vishnu, Indra, demons, etc., became burst and other divine beings turned into cleaned coals. Lord Vishnu addressing this form said:

## \|\| 250.19-20 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca*  
*ko bhavānantakaprakhyaḥ kimicchasi kuto'pi ca \|*  
*kiṃ kṛtvā te priyaṃ jāyedevamācakṣva me'khilam \|\| 19 \|\|*

*tacca tasya vacaḥ śrutvā viṣṇoḥ kālāgnisaṃnibhaḥ \|*  
*uvāca kālakūṭastu bhinnaduṃdubhinisvanaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

19-20. “Who are you of this death-like nature and what is your object? Whence have you come? How will you be pleased?” Hearing those words of Lord Vishnu, Kalakuta thundered out like a huge kettle-drum.

## \|\| 250.21-22 \|\|

*kālakūṭa uvāca*  
*ahaṃ hi kālakūṭākhyo viṣṇo'mbudhisamudbhavaḥ \|*  
*yadā tīvratarāmarṣaiḥ parasparavadhaiṣibhiḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*surāsurairvimathito dugdhāmbhonidhiradbhutaḥ \|*  
*saṃbhūto'haṃ tadā sarvānhantuṃ devānsadānavān \|\| 22 \|\|*

21-22. “I am Kalakuta poison born out of the churning of the ocean. I am horn to kill the Devas and the demons for their having churned the ocean so furiously.

## \|\| 250.23 \|\|

*sarvānahaṃ haniṣyāmi kṣaṇamātreṇa dehinaḥ \|*  
*māṃ vā grasata vai sarve yāta vā giriśāntikam \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. I shall now destroy them in a moment. They should now either swallow me or go to Lord Shiva.”

## \|\| 250.24-27 \|\|

*śrutvaitadvacanaṃ tasya tato bhītāḥ surāsurāḥ \|*  
*brahmaviṣṇū puraskṛtya gatāste śaṃkarāntikam \|\| 24 \|\|*

*niveditāstato dvāḥsthaiste gaṇeśaiḥ surāsurāḥ \|*  
*anujñātāḥ śivenātha viviśurgiriśāntikam \|\| 25 \|\|*

*mandarasya guhāṃ haimīṃ muktāmaṇivibhūṣitām \|*  
*susvacchamaṇisopānāṃ vaidūryastambhamaṇḍitām \|\| 26 \|\|*

*tatra devāsuraiḥ sarvairjānubhirdharaṇiṃ gataiḥ \|*  
*brahmāṇamagrataḥ kṛtvā idaṃ stotramudāhṛtam \|\| 27 \|\|*

24-27. Hearing those fearful words, the Devas and the demons placing Brahma and Vishnu in front of them repaired to the abode of Lord Shiva and stood at His gateway. They were announced to the Lord by His attendant Ganesha and with His permission went inside His cave in the golden Mandarachala the steps of which were studded with precious Stones, having pillars of Vaidurya gem. Then they knelt down and prayed to the Lord under the leadership of Brahma.

## \|\| 250.28 \|\|

*devadānavā ūcuḥ \|*  
*namastubhyaṃ virūpākṣa namaste divyacakṣuṣe \|*

28\. The Devas and the demons: — “Virupaksha! having divine eyes, armed with how, thunderbolt and Pinaka, we salute you.

## \|\| 250.29 \|\|

*namastriśūlahastāya daṇḍahastāya dhūrjaṭe \|*  
*namastrilokyanāthāya bhūtagrāmaśarīriṇe \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. O, One armed with trident, the Lord of the three realms, the receptacle of all the beings, we all salute you.

## \|\| 250.30-31 \|\|

*namaḥ surārihantre ca somāgnyarkāgryacakṣuṣe \|*

30-31. O, destroyer of the enemies of the Devas, having for your eyes, the Sun, the Moon and the fire, the one who manifest yourself as Brahma, Vishnu and Rudra, Samkhya Yoga, ordaining Welfare to all the beings, we salute you.

## \|\| 250.32-36 \|\|

*manmathāṅgavināśāya namaḥ kālakṣayaṃkara \|*

*śuddhabodhaprabuddhāya muktakaivalyarūpiṇe \|*  
*lokatrayavidhātre ca varuṇendrā gnirūpiṇe \|\| 34 \|\|*

*ṛgyajuḥsāmavedāya puruṣāyeśvarāya ca \|*  
*agryāya caiva cogrāya viprāya śruticakṣuṣe \|\| 35 \|\|*

*rajase caiva sattvāya tamase timirātmane \|*  
*anityanityabhāvāya namo nityacarātmane \|\| 36 \|\|*

32-36. Annihilator of Cupid! destroyer of the Lokas and time! the Lord, bf ail the; Devas, our salutations to you. Ekavira! Sharba, the one with plaited hair, the Lord of Parvati the destroyer of the sacrifice of Daksha and Tripura, the cause of the universe and giver of bliss and freedom to all, of the forms of Indra, Agni, Varuna, the three Vedas, Rik, Yajur, Sama; you are the Purusha, you are Ishvara, Vipra, having Shrutis for your eyes as well, you are Sattva, Raj o and Tamogunas, eternal, we salute you. You are the foremost; you are the formidable.

**Комментарий:**

Note. … = Pre-eminent warrior, hero.

…. = An epithet of Shiva.

## \|\| 250.37 \|\|

*vyaktāya caivāvyaktāya vyaktāvyaktāya vai namaḥ \|*

37\. The darkness is also Your Form; you are eternal and changeful you are manifested; you are unmanifested; you are both manifest and unmanifest; you are dear to Narayana; we salute you.

## \|\| 250.38-40 \|\|

*umāpriyāya śarvāya nandivaktrāñcitāya ca \|*

*nānārūpāya muṇḍāya varūthapṛthudaṇḍine \|*

38-40. I Beloved of the Goddess Parvati, residing in the mouth of Nandi, you are the seasons, the Manvantaras, the Kalpas, fortnights, months, days; the one who manifests himself in many ways; you are Mundi (with Shaved heads), Rathi, Dhanvi Yati, and Brahmachari. Holder of the lotus, having directions for your garments, we salute you.”

## \|\| 250.41-42 \|\|

*evaṃ surāsuraiḥ sthāṇuḥ stutastoṣamupāgataḥ \|*

41-42. After that prayer the Lord Shiva became pleased and said: — “Devas and demons! why have you come here? Why do you look so helpless and suffering? What shall I do for you? Tell me your object outright.” Hearing such words of the Lord the Devas and the demons said:

## \|\| 250.43-44 \|\|

*surāsurā ūcuḥ \|*  
*amṛtārthe mahādeva mathyamāne mahodadhau \|*

*sa uvācātha sarveṣāṃ devānāṃ bhayakārakaḥ \|*  
*sarvānvo bhakṣayiṣyāmi athavā mā pibantvatha \|\| 44 \|\|*

43-44. “We have churned the mighty ocean for nectar, out of which has come out the most deadly Kalakuta poison which threatens to destroy us if we do not gulp it down.

## \|\| 250.45-46 \|\|

*tamaśaktā vayaṃ grastuṃ so'smāñchakto balotkaṭaḥ \|*  
*eṣa niḥśvāsamātreṇa śataparvasamadyutiḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

*viṣṇuḥ kṛṣṇaḥ kṛtastena yamaśca viṣamātmavān \|*  
*mūrchitāḥ patitāścānye vipraṇāśaṃ gatāḥ pare \|\| 46 \|\|*

45-46. We are unable to devour that poison. We have come to you being overpowered by it. It sends up its fumes powerful like the flashes of lightning and has blackened Vishnu, dismayed Dharmaraja, rendered many unconscious and killed several.

## \|\| 250.47-48 \|\|

*artho'narthakriyāṃ yāti durbhagāṇāṃ yathā vibho \|*  
*durbalānāṃ ca saṃkalpo yathā bhavati cā'padi \|\| 47 \|\|*

*viṣametatsamudbhūtaṃ tasmādvā'mṛtakāṅkṣayā \|*  
*asmādbhayānmocaya tvaṃ gatistvaṃ ca parāyaṇam \|\| 48 \|\|*

47-48. Lord! as the pelf of the unfortunate becomes the source of misfortune, and as in misfortunes the objects of the weak are not fulfilled, similarly this deadly poison has come deadly to us. We have, therefore, come to you for succor and be pleased to give your helping hand to us.

## \|\| 250.49-50 \|\|

*bhaktānukampī bhāvajño bhuvanādīśvaro vibhuḥ \|*  
*yajñāgramuksarvahaviḥ saumyaḥ somaḥ smarāntakṛt \|\| 49 \|\|*

*tvameko no gatirdeva gīrvāṇagaṇaśarmakṛt \|*  
*rakṣāsmānmakṣasaṃkalpādvirūpākṣa viṣajvarāt \|\| 50 \|\|*

49-50. You are clement on your devotees, knower of all motives, the recipient of the first share of sacrificial offerings, the most Supreme Lord, the annihilator of Kama; you are Soma, and Saumya and doing well to the Devas; you alone are our strength, you are the protector of the attendants; pray be p\] eased to swallow it and thus rescue us from the danger of our being destroyed by the formidable poison.”

## \|\| 250.51-52 \|\|

*tacchrutvā bhagavānāha bhaganetrāntakṛdbhavaḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

*devadeva uvāca*  
*bhakṣayiṣyāmyahaṃ ghoraṃ kālakūṭaṃ mahāviṣam \|*  
*tathā'nyadapi yatkṛtyaṃ kṛcchrasādhyaṃ surāsurāḥ \|*  
*taccāpi sādhayiṣyāmi tiṣṭhadhvaṃ vigatajvarāḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

51-52. Mahadeva said: — “I shall swallow the Kalakuta; and shall also fulfil if there is any other difficult mission to be accomplished by you.”

## \|\| 250.53 \|\|

*ityuktā hṛṣṭaromāṇo bāṣpagadgadakaṇṭhinaḥ \|*

*surā brahmādayaḥ sarve samāśvastāḥ sumānasāḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. The Devas and the demons were filled with extraordinary delight on hearing those words of the Lord; their eyes were moist with tears of joy and their voices got choked.

## \|\| 250.54 \|\|

*tato'vrajaddrutagatinā kakudminā haro'mbare pavanagatirjagatpatiḥ \|*  
*pradhāvitairasurasurendra nāyakaiḥ svavāhanairyicalitaśubhracāmaraiḥ \|*  
*puraḥsaraiḥ sa tu śuśubhe śubhāśrayaiḥ śivo vaśī śikhikapiśordhvajūṭakaḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. Afterwards Lord Mahadeva set out on his quick-going buffalo as swift as wind on the aerial track when the Devas and the demons also followed Him on their respective conveyances, favouring the Lord with chowries.

## \|\| 250.55 \|\|

*āsādya dugdhasindhuṃ taṃ kālakūṭaṃ viṣaṃ yataḥ \|*  
*tato devo mahādevo vilokya viṣamaṃ viṣam \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. The Lord’s knotted hairs, standing up on high became tawny coloured by the fire of His third eye. Then the Lord saw Kalakuta on getting to the coast of the ocean.

## \|\| 250.56-59 \|\|

*chāyāsthānakamāsthāya so'pibadvāmapāṇinā \|*  
*pīyamāne viṣe tasmiṃstato devā mahāsurāḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

*jaguśca nanṛtuścāpi siṃhanādāṃśca puṣkalān \|*  
*cakruḥ śakramukhādyāśca hiraṇyākṣādayastathā \|\| 57 \|\|*

*stuvantaścaiva deveśaṃ prasannāścābhavaṃstadā \|*  
*kaṇṭhadeśaṃ tataḥ prāpte viṣe devamathā'bruvan \|\| 58 \|\|*

*viriñcipramukhā devā balipramukhato'surāḥ \|*  
*śobhate deva kaṇṭhaste gātre kundanibhaprabhe \|\| 59 \|\|*

56-59. He went to a shady place and quaffed it holding it in His left hand. The Devas and the demons thundered out with glee when they saw the Lord drinking it. They also danced and sang, and Brahma and other Devas began to pray. When the venom was deposited in the throat of the Lord, Bali along with the Devas and the demons said: “O Lord! white like the lotus, the venom looks awfully beautiful like bees in your throat.

## \|\| 250.60-61 \|\|

*bhṛṅgamālānibhaṃ kaṇṭhe'pyatraivāstu viṣaṃ tava \|*  
*ityuktaḥ śaṃkaro devastathā prāha purāntakṛt \|\| 60 \|\|*

*pīte viṣe devagaṇānvimucya gato haro mandaraśailameva \|*  
*tasmingate devagaṇāḥ punastaṃ mamanthurabdhiṃ vividhaprakāraiḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

60-61. It looks as if you are wearing a garland of black bees. Let this remain in your throat.” The Lord replied that if that be the case He would let it lie there and not allow it to settle down, Shiva thus returned home after quaffing the poison and the Devas and the demons again resumed the churning of the ocean.

## Chapter 251

## \|\| 251.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*

2\. Next came out the broad-eyed Madira, the nectar and the cow Surabhi, the dispeller of the fears of all beings.

## \|\| 251.2-3 \|\|

*madirā cā’yatākṣī sā lokacittapramāthinī \|*

2-3. Lord Vishnu took Lakshmi and Kaustubha gem. Later on came out the famous elephant Airavata; and they were taken by Indra and Dhanvantari, the giver of health to all the beings, was taken by the Sun.

## \|\| 251.4 \|\|

*dhanvantariṃ ca jagrāha lokārogyapravartakam \|*

4\. Dhanvantari, the great professor of Ayurveda, brought relief to the sufferings of the creation. The famous umbrella that came out of the ocean was taken by Varuna. Then came out two earrings which were taken by Vayu,

## \|\| 251.5-7 \|\|

*pārijātataruṃ vāyurjagrāha muditastathā \|*

*śvetaṃ kamaṇḍaluṃ bibhradamṛtaṃ yatra tiṣṭhati \|*  
*etadatyadbhutaṃ dṛṣṭvā dānavānāṃ samutthitaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*amṛtārthe mahānādo mamedamiti jalpatām \|*

5-7. Parijata tree was taken by Indra. Then Dhanvantari assuming a charming form and taking a Kamandalu came out with the pot of nectar in his hand. At that time the Devas and the demons shouted out for nectar “It is ours, It is ours,” when Lord Vishnu assumed the appearance of a bewitching damsel.

## \|\| 251.8-12 \|\|

*strīrūpamatulaṃ kṛtvā dānavānabhisaṃsṛtaḥ \|*  
*tatastadamṛtaṃ tasyai daduste mūḍhacetanāḥ \|*  
*striyai dānavadaiteyāḥ sarve tadgatamānasāḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*athāstrāṇi ca mukhyāni mahāpraharaṇāni ca \|*  
*pragṛhyābhyadra vandevānsahitā daityadānavāḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*tatastadamṛtaṃ devo viṣṇurādāya vīryavān \|*  
*jahāra dānavendre bhyo nareṇa sahitaḥ prabhuḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*tato devagaṇāḥ sarve papustadamṛtaṃ tadā \|*

*tataḥ pibatsu tatkālaṃ deveṣvamṛtamīpsitam \|*  
*rāhurvibudharūpeṇa dānavo'pyapibattadā \|\| 12 \|\|*

8-12. And He fascinated the demons, who, being deluded, placed the pitcher of nectar into the hands of the Lord and then ran towards the Devas to fight with them, with various arms in their hands. In the meantime the Lord most ingeniously brought the pot of nectar before the Devas and the demons, when the Devas began to drink it. The demon Rahu, assumed the form of a Deva took his seat along with the Devas and was going to drink the nectar.

## \|\| 251.13-16 \|\|

*tasya kaṇṭhamanuprāpte dānavasyāmṛte tadā \|*  
*ākhyātaṃ candra sūryābhyāṃ surāṇāṃ hitakāmyayā \|\| 13 \|\|*

*tato bhagavatā tasya śiraśchinnamalaṃkṛtam \|*  
*cakrāyudhena cakreṇa pibato'mṛtamojasā \|\| 14 \|\|*

*tacchailaśṛṅgapratimaṃ dānavasya śiro mahat \|*  
*cakreṇotkṛttamapataccālayadvasudhātalam \|\| 15 \|\|*

*tato vairavinirbandhaḥ kṛto rāhumukhena vai \|*  
*śāśvataścandra sūryābhyāṃ prasahyādyāpi bādhate \|\| 16 \|\|*

13-16. The Sun and the Moon drew the attention of the Devas to this for their benefit. When the nectar had gone into the throat of Rahu, Lord Vishnu severed his head by His quoit; but the severed head of the mountain like demon, that fell down and shook the earth remained alive and became immortal which is known as Rahu. Thus Rahu became the enemy of the Sun and the Moon and he takes vengeance on them even up to the present day at the time of their eclipses.

## \|\| 251.17 \|\|

*vihāya bhagavāṃścāpi strīrūpamatulaṃ hariḥ \|*  
*nānāpraharaṇairbhīmairdānavānsamakampayat \|*  
*prāsāḥ suvipulāstīkṣṇāḥ patantaśca sahasraśaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Afterwards Lord Vishnu leaving His form of that enchanting damsel began to inflict blows on the demons with his various weapons.

## \|\| 251.18 \|\|

*te'surāścakranirbhinnā vamanto rudhiraṃ bahu \|*  
*asiśaktigadābhinnā nipeturdharaṇītale \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Hundreds and thousands of powerful sharp Pashastras then began to fall. The Asuras got pierced with Chakra which made them vomit blood.

## \|\| 251.19 \|\|

*bhinnāni paṭṭiśaiścāpi śirāṃsi yudhi dāruṇaiḥ \|*  
*taptakāñcanamālyāni nipeturaniśaṃ tadā \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Most of them fell on the ground by the blows of sword, trident, etc., and the skulls of many were ripped by the terrible Pattishastra and fell down with garlands round them.

## \|\| 251.20 \|\|

*rudhireṇāvaliptāṅgā nihatāśca mahāsurāḥ \|*  
*adri ṇāmiva kūṭāni dhāturaktāni śerate \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Then most of the mighty demons, soaked in blood, shining like burnished gold fell dead on the ground.

## \|\| 251.21 \|\|

*tato halahalāśabdaḥ saṃbabhūva samantataḥ \|*  
*anyonyaṃ chindatāṃ śastrairāditye lohitāyati \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. The battle went on till evening. They fell down like the mountains of red chalk and a huge din was made by their fight and fall.

## \|\| 251.22-23 \|\|

*parighaiścā’yasaiḥ pātaiḥ saṃnikarṣaiśca muṣṭibhiḥ \|*  
*nighnatāṃ samare'nyonyaṃ śabdo divamivāspṛśat \|\| 22 \|\|*

*chindi bhindhi pradhāveti pātayābhisareti vai \|*  
*viśrūyante mahāghorāḥ śabdāstatra samantataḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

22-23. In that terrible fighting all the arms were dyed in gore and the ’universe resounded with the war cries “ Cut them clean into two, break them, run away, throw them down, etc.”

## \|\| 251.24-28 \|\|

*evaṃ sutumule yuddhe vartamāne mahābhaye \|*  
*naranārāyaṇau devau samājagmaturāhavam \|\| 24 \|\|*

*tatra divyaṃ dhanurdṛṣṭvā narasya bhagavānapi \|*  
*cintayāmāsa vai cakraṃ viṣṇurdānavasūdanaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*tato'mbarāccintitamātramāgataṃ mahāprabhaṃ cakramamitranāśanam \|*  
*vibhāvasostulyamakuṇṭhamaṇḍalaṃ sudarśanaṃ bhīmamasahyavikramam \|\| 26 \|\|*

*tadāgataṃ jvalitahutāśanaprabhaṃ bhayaṃkaraṃ karikarabāhuracyutaḥ \|*  
*mahāprabhaṃ danukuladaityadāraṇaṃ tathojжvalajжvalanasamānavigraham \|\| 27 \|\|*

*mumoca vai tadatulamugravegavānmahāprabhaṃ ripunagarāvadāraṇam \|*  
*saṃvartakajvalanasamānavarcasaṃ punaḥpunarnyapatata vegavattadā \|\| 28 \|\|*

24-28 When the universe was filled with that din then Nara and Narayana resorted to the battlefield; Lord Vishnu, seeing the bow in Nara’s hand remembered His Sudarshana quoit; and at that very instant Sudarshana, the destroyer of the enemies defended from the heaven and seeing that mighty weapon, the annihilator of the enemies, shining like the Sun, burning like fire; Lord Vishnu violently hurled the terrible Chakra at the demons which repeatedly struck them.

## \|\| 251.29-34 \|\|

*vyadārayaddititanayānsahasraśaḥ kareritaṃ puruṣavareṇa saṃyuge \|*  
*dahatkvacijжvalana ivānileritaḥ prasahya tānasuragaṇāna kṛntata \|\| 29 \|\|*

*tatpreritaṃ viyati muhuḥ kṣitau tadā papau raṇe rudhiramayo piśācavat \|*  
*athāsurā giribhiradīnamānasā muhurmuhuḥ suragaṇamardayaṃstadā \|\| 30 \|\|*

*mahābalā vigalitameghavarcasaḥ sahasraśo gaganamahāprapātinaḥ \|*  
*athāsurā bhayajananāḥ prapedire sapādapā bahuvidhamegharūpiṇaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

*mahādra yaḥ pavigalitāgrasānavaḥ parasparaṃ drutamabhipatya sasvarāḥ \|*  
*tato mahī pracalitasādri kānanā tadā'dri pātābhihatā samantataḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

*parasparaṃ samabhinigarjatāṃ muhū raṇājire bhṛśamabhisaṃpravartite \|*  
*narastato varakanakāgrabhūṣaṇairmaheṣubhiḥ pavanapathaṃ samāvṛṇot \|\| 33 \|\|*

*vidārayangiriśikharāṇi patribhirmahābhaye suragaṇavigrahe tadā \|*  
*tato mahīṃ lavaṇajalaṃ ca sāgaraṃ mahāsurāḥ praviviśurarditāḥ suraiḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

29-34. Then that quoit shining like the brilliant form of fire, mercilessly killed thousands of demons At some places it burnt them like fire aided by wind; it cut them into pieces; then it rose into the air and hurled flames of fire on the demons and drank their gore The demons began to hurl mountains after mountains on the Devas and crushed’ them But by the force of that quoit many mountain chains looking like the banks of clouds fell down with mighty trees when the world began to quake and rumble. The mountain tops were also shattered by the arrows of the Devas and the demons. Then Nara hurled his great arrow, decked at its fore-end with gold, and covered the atmosphere. The Devas were frightened when He cut asunder all the tops of the mountains by arrows. Then the demons harassed by the Devas entered into the ocean, and others down into the bottom of the earth.

## \|\| 251.35-36 \|\|

*viyadgataṃ jvalitahutāśanaprabhaṃ sudarśanaṃ parikupitaṃ niśamya ca \|*  
*tataḥ surairvijayamavāpya mandaraḥ svameva deśaṃ gamitaḥ supūjitaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

*vitatya svaṃ divamatha caiva sarvaśastato gatāḥ saliladharā yathāgatam \|*  
*tato'mṛtaṃ sunihitameva cakrire surāḥ parāṃ mudamabhigamya puṣphalām \|*
