18\. The one with flat face and eyes causes grief and anguish, the blind image causes injury to the eyes, the one without a mouth or with decrepit limbs causes misery.

## \|\| 259.19-20 \|\|

*hīnāṅgā hīnajaṅghā ca bhramonmādakarī nṛṇām \|*  
*śuṣkavaktrā tu rājānaṃ kaṭihīnā ca yā bhavet \|\| 19 \|\|*

*pāṇipādavihīno yo jāyate mārako mahān \|*  
*jaṅghājānuvihīnā ca śatrukalyāṇakāriṇī \|\| 20 \|\|*

19-20. The one with defective limbs, especially without thighs, causes fear madness, the one with a dried face or without waist troubles the king, one void of hands and feet brings some epidemic, the one bereft of 3 and knees causes joy to the enemies.

## \|\| 259.21-26 \|\|

*putramitravināśāya hīnavakṣaḥsthalā tu yā \|*  
*saṃpūrṇāvayavā yā tu āyurlakṣmīpradā sadā \|\| 21 \|\|*

*evaṃ lakṣaṇamāsādya kartavyaḥ parameśvaraḥ \|*  
*stūyamānaḥ suraiḥ sarvaiḥ samantāddarśayedbhavam \|\| 22 \|\|*

*śakreṇa nandinā caiva mahākālena śaṃkaram \|*  
*praṇatā lokapālāstu pārśve tu gaṇanāyakāḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

*nṛtyadbhṛṅgiriṭiścaiva bhūtavetālasaṃvṛtāḥ \|*  
*sarve hṛṣṭāstu kartavyāḥ stuvantaḥ parameśvaram \|\| 24 \|\|*

*gandharvavidyādharakiṃnarāṇāmathāpsaroguhyakanāyakānām \|*  
*gaṇairanekaiḥ śataśo mahendrai rmunipravīrairapi namyamānam \|\| 25 \|\|*

*dhṛtākṣasūtraiḥ śataśaḥ pravālapuṣpopahārapracayaṃ dadadbhiḥ \|*  
*saṃstūyamānaṃ bhagavantamīḍyaṃ netratrayeṇāmaramartyapūjyam \|\| 26 \|\|*

21-26. The one without a chest destroys sons and friends. The image complete in every way brings prosperity and long life. So the image of Lord Shiva should be made in full as described heretofore and all the Devas, Indra, Nandikeshvara, eight Lokapalas, Ganeshvara, should be located surrounding the image in a praying posture so that one can have a view of the Lord. The devils, fiends and Vetalas should also be made in a dancing posture and praying before the Lord. All these images should have the appearance of infinite joy and absorbed in their devotion to the Lord. The image of the Lord should be made with three eyes, surrounded by the praying Gandharvas, Vidyadharas, Kinnaras, nymphs, Guhyakas, attendants, sages etc., etc.

## Chapter 260

## \|\| 260.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*adhunā saṃpravakṣyāmi ardhanārīśvaraṃ param \|*  
*ardhena devadevasya nārīrūpaṃ suśobhanam \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Suta said: — “Rishis! I shall now tell you about the Ardhanarishvara image.”

**Комментарий:**

Note. = The imago of Lord Shiva with half male and half female form blended into one.

## \|\| 260.2 \|\|

*īśārdhe tu jaṭābhāgo bālendukalayā yutaḥ \|*  
*umārdhe cāpi dātavyau sīmantatilakāvubhau \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. In the one-half of the image, in the plaited hair of the Lord, a crescent should be made and in the other half-portion of the body the image of the Goddess Parvati should be beautifully made. Here a partition is to be made in the hair of the head and the tilaka (a sectarian mark on the forehead) is to be marked on the forehead.

## \|\| 260.3-4 \|\|

*vāsukiṃ dakṣiṇe karṇe vāme kuṇḍalamādiśet \|*  
*bālikā copariṣṭāttu kapālaṃ dakṣiṇe kare \|*  
*triśūlaṃ vā'pi kartavyaṃ devadevasya śūlinaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*vāmato darpaṇaṃ dadyādutpalaṃ ca viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*vāmabāhuśca kartavyaḥ keyūravalayānvitaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

3-4. In the right ear the serpent Vasuki should be made and in the left one an ear-ring should be put on. In the right hand should be placed the skull or trident and in the left one,, a mirror or a lotus.

Garlands are to be suspended from His neck.

## \|\| 260.5-6 \|\|

*upavītaṃ ca kartavyaṃ maṇimuktāmayaṃ tathā \|\| 5 \|\|*

*stanabhāraṃ tathā'rdhe tu vāme pītaṃ prakalpayet \|*  
*hārārdhamujжvalaṃ kuryācchroṇyardha tu tathaiva ca \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. The left arm should be adorned with armlets, etc., and a sacred thread of pearl string or gems should be put in the proper place. A chubby breast and a bulky lip, should be made chi the left hand side and a girdle should be put on the half part of the waist.

## \|\| 260.7-9 \|\|

*liṅgārdhamūrdhagaṃ kuryādvyālājinakṛtāmvaram \|*  
*vāme lambaparīdhānaṃ kaṭisūtratrayānvitam \|\| 7 \|\|*

*nānāratnasamopetaṃ dakṣiṇaṃ bhujagānvitam \|*  
*devasya dakṣiṇaṃ pādaṃ padmopari susaṃsthitam \|\| 8 \|\|*

*kiṃcidūrdhvaṃ tathā vāmaṃ bhūṣitaṃ nūpureṇa tu \|*  
*ratnairvibhūṣitānkuryādaṅgulīṣvaṅgulīyakān \|\| 9 \|\|*

7-9. Then in the half-portion of the body covered with tiger skin an organ should he made and the left part is to be covered with hanging cloth decked with various jewels and the right side is to be covered with serpents. The right foot of the Lord should be made to rest oh a lotus and a little above that the left one should be adorned with gems and ornaments worn by ladies.

## \|\| 260.10-11 \|\|

*sālaktakaṃ tathā pādaṃ pārvatyā darśayetsadā \|*  
*ardhanārīśvarasvedaṃ rūpamasminnudāhṛtam \|\| 10 \|\|*

*umāmaheśvarasyāpi lakṣaṇaṃ śṛṇuta dvijāḥ \|*  
*saṃsthānaṃ tu tayorvakṣye līlālalitavibhramam \|\| 11 \|\|*

10-11. The feet of the Goddess Parvati should always be made to appear dyed in myrtle (red lac dye). Such should be the image of the Lord and the Goddess blended into one. “Now hear about the location of their several limbs in their Leela (sportive) forms.”

## \|\| 260.12-16 \|\|

*caturbhujaṃ dvibāhuṃ vā jaṭāmārendubhūṣitam \|*  
*locanatrayasaṃyuktamumaikaskandhapāṇinam \|\| 12 \|\|*

*dakṣiṇenotpalaṃ śūlaṃ vāme kucabhare karam \|*  
*dvīpicarmaparīdhānaṃ nānāratnopaśobhitam \|\| 13 \|\|*

*supratiṣṭhaṃ suveṣaṃ ca tathā'rdhendukṛtāsanam \|*  
*vāme tu saṃsthitā devī tasyorau bāhugūhitā \|\| 14 \|\|*

*śirobhūṣaṇasaṃyuktairalaṃkairlalitānanā \|*  
*sabālikā karṇavatī lalāṭatilakojжvalā \|\| 15 \|\|*

*maṇikuṇḍalasaṃyuktā karṇikābharaṇā kvacit \|*  
*hārakeyūrabahulā haravaktrāvalokinī \|\| 16 \|\|*

12-16. The image of the Lord and Uma should be made either with 4 or 2 hands; the matted hair on the head are to be adorned with a crescent of the Moon; having three eyes, with one hand resting on the right shoulder o! Parvati, having trident and lotus oil the right side; placing the left hand on the breast of the Goddess, wearing the tiger skin, decked with various jewels. The situation is charming and pleasant and half the face is adorned with semi-moon; the right hand of the Lord lies on the thigh of Uma. The Goddess Uma should he seated on the left side of the Lord. The head of the Goddess should be decorated with the usual ornaments, and having nice tresses of hair, with Alaka and Tilaka, adorned with the beautiful ear-rings, armlets, and fondly looking at the face of the Lord,

## \|\| 260.17-20 \|\|

*dhāmāṃsaṃ devadevasya spṛśantī līlayā tataḥ \|*  
*dakṣiṇaṃ tu bahiḥ kṛtvā bāhuṃ dakṣiṇatastathā \|\| 17 \|\|*

*skandhe vā dakṣiṇe kukṣau spṛśantyaṅgulijaiḥ kvacit \|*  
*vāme tu darpaṇaṃ dadyādutpalaṃ vā suśobhanam \|\| 18 \|\|*

*kaṭisūtratrayaṃ caiva nitambe syātpralambakam \|*  
*jayā ca vijayā caiva kārtikeyavināyakau \|\| 19 \|\|*

*pārśvayordarśayettatra toraṇe gaṇaguhyakān \|*  
*mālā vidyādharāṃstadvadvīṇāvānapsarogaṇaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

17-20. Sportively touching the loft side of the Lord, with Her left arm stretched out and touching the abdomen of the Lord with Her fingers. A looking glass and a beautiful lotus, are to be placed on Her left side and a girdle is to be hung on the waist. On both the sides of the image of the Goddess should be placed the forms of Jaya, Vijaya, Svami Kartika, and Ganesha; near the gateway should be placed the images of Guhyakas. The images of the Vidyadharas wearing garlands and the nymphs holding guitars in standing postures.

## \|\| 260.21 \|\|

*etadrū pamumeśasya kartavyaṃ bhūtimicchatā \|*  
*śivanārāyaṇaṃ vakṣye sarvapāpapraṇāśanam \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. A man eager for prosperity should make such an image of Uma and Maheshvara, Now hear about the form of Shivanarayana, destructive of all sins.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — … = The forms of Lords Shiva and Narayana blended into one single image.

## \|\| 260.22-24 \|\|

*vāmārdhe mādhavaṃ vidyāddakṣiṇe śūlapāṇinam \|*  
*bāhudvayaṃ ca kṛṣṇasya maṇikeyūrabhūṣitam \|\| 22 \|\|*

*śaṅkhacakradharaṃ śāntamāraktāṅgulivibhramam \|*  
*cakrasthāne gadāṃ vā'pi pāṇau dadyādadhastale \|\| 23 \|\|*

*śaṅkhaṃ caivottare dadyātkaṭyardhaṃ bhūṣaṇojжvalam \|*  
*pītavastraparīdhānaṃ caraṇaṃ maṇibhūṣaṇam \|\| 24 \|\|*

22-24. Narayana should be made in the left half of. the body and Lord Shiva in the right. Both the arms of Lord Vishnu should be decorated with jewels and armlets holding conch and quoit. The fingers should fee reddish. Instead of quoit, club can be placed or conch can be placed on the opposite side. In the waist yellow cloth studded with white gems should be made to be worn. The feet should be adorned with the ornaments, and gems.

## \|\| 260.25-27 \|\|

*dakṣiṇārdhaṃ jaṭābhāramardhendukṛtabhūṣaṇam \|*  
*bhujaṅgahāravalayaṃ varadaṃ dakṣiṇaṃ karam \|\| 25 \|\|*

*dvitīyaṃ cāpi kurvīta triśūlavaradhāriṇam \|*  
*vyālopavītasaṃyuktaṃ kaṭyardhaṃ kṛtivāsasam \|\| 26 \|\|*

*maṇiratnaiśca saṃyuktaṃ pādaṃ nāgavibhūṣitam \|*  
*śivanārāyaṇasyaivaṃ kalpayedrū pamuttamam \|\| 27 \|\|*

25-27. The half of the right side of the body should he, adorned with plaited hair and crescent, the right arm with armlets of serpents should be made in the posture of making a gift, the other one should be decorated with a trident, putting on a serpent in place of the sacred thread, wearing a tiger-skin, and the two feet adorned with jewels and serpents. Such Should be the image of Shiva and Narayana blended into one.

## \|\| 260.28-31 \|\|

*mahāvarāhaṃ vakṣyāmi padmahastaṃ gadādharam \|*  
*tīkṣṇadaṃṣṭrāgradhoṇāsyaṃ medinī vāmakūrpare \|\| 28 \|\|*

*daṃṣṭrāgreṇoddhṛtāṃ dāntāṃ dharaṇīmutpalānvitām \|*  
*vismayotphullavadanāmupariṣṭātprakalpayet \|\| 29 \|\|*

*dakṣiṇaṃ kaṭisaṃsthaṃ tu karaṃ tasyāḥ prakalpayet \|*  
*kūrmopari tathā pādamekaṃ nāgendra mūrdhani \|\| 30 \|\|*

*saṃstūyamānaṃ lokeśaiḥ samantātparikalpayet \|*  
*nārasiṃhaṃ tu kartavyaṃ bhujāṣṭakasamanvitam \|\| 31 \|\|*

28-31. Now I am describing to you the form of the Maha Varaha. Lotus and club should be placed in the hands of Vara Ira, the teeth should be sharp, and at the left elbow (knee) should be placed the world uplifted by the teeth from the Pa, tala and which bears calmly everything on Her, His teeth are very sharp and face full of joy and wonder. Thus for the upper part. The right foot should be the turtle, the left foot on the hood of the Shesha and his right hand is to be locate on his left Shakti. All round the image should be made the images of the Lokapalas in praying postures. Now about the image of Nara Simha. The image of Nrisimha be made with eight hands.

## \|\| 260.32-33 \|\|

*raudraṃ siṃhāsanaṃ tadvadvidāritamukhekṣaṇam \|*  
*stabdhapīnasaṭākarṇaṃ dārayantaṃ diteḥ sutam \|\| 32 \|\|*

*vinirgatāntrajālaṃ ca dānavaṃ parikalpayet \|*  
*vamantaṃ rudhiraṃ ghoraṃ bhrukuṭīvadanekṣaṇam \|\| 33 \|\|*

32-33. The altar or seat of Nrisimha should be made formidable, his face terrible, the eyes should be split, the main should be raised, and the scene of ripping the breast of the demon Hiranyakashyapu with blood gushing from it, as well as the angry looks of the Lord should also be well depicted.

## \|\| 260.34 \|\|

*yudhyamānaśca kartavyaḥ kvacitkaraṇabandhanaiḥ \|*  
*pariśrāntena daityena tarjyamāno muhurmuhuḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. The fight of the Lord Nrisimha with the demon with His nails and His terrible form and the attacks of the latter made repeatedly should also be shown.

## \|\| 260.35 \|\|

*daityaṃ pradarśayettatra khaḍgakheṭakadhāriṇam \|*  
*stūyamānaṃ tathā viṣṇuṃ darśayedamarādhipaiḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. At the same place the image of the demons armed with swords should also be made and the Lord is to be represented as frequently chastising the demons, and the images of Indra and the other Devas m praying posture should he made near Nrisimha.

## \|\| 260.36-37 \|\|

*tathā trivikramaṃ vakṣye brahmāṇḍakramaṇolbaṇam \|*  
*pādapārśve tathā bāhumupariṣṭātprakalpayet \|\| 36 \|\|*

*adhastādvāmanaṃ tadvatkalpayetsakamaṇḍalum \|*  
*dakṣiṇe chatrikāṃ dadyānmukhaṃ dīnaṃ prakalpayet \|\| 37 \|\|*

36-37. Now about the Vamana form of the Lord striding the three worlds, as if pervading all the Universe. The upper portion of the image of Vamana should be made with arms by the side of His legs raised upwards, and the form of Vamana holding a goblet in the left hand and a small umbrella in the right. This is to be represented in the lower part of the figure. The face of the Lord should be extremely meek and appealing.

## \|\| 260.38-39 \|\|

*bhṛṅgāradhāriṇaṃ tadvadbaliṃ tasya ca pārśvataḥ \|*  
*bandhanaṃ cāsya kurvantaṃ garuḍaṃ tasya darśayet \|\| 38 \|\|*

*matsyarūpaṃ tathā matsyaṃ kūrmaṃ kūrmākṛtiṃ nyaset \|*  
*evaṃrūpastu bhagavānkāryo nārāyaṇo hariḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

38-39. Nearby should be made the image of Garuda holding the Bhringara. The image of Matsya should be in the form of a fish and that of Kurma in that of a turtle

## \|\| 260.40 \|\|

*brahmā kamaṇḍaludharaḥ kartavyaḥ sa caturmukhaḥ \|*  
*haṃsārūḍhaḥ kvacitkāryaḥ kvacicca kamalāsanaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. The image of Lord Brahma should be made with four heads holding a kamandalu in one hand. He should be made riding on a swan or seated on a lotus, as the case may be.

## \|\| 260.41-43 \|\|

*varṇataḥ padmagarbhābhaścaturbāhuḥ śubhekṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*kamaṇḍaluṃ vāmakare sruvaṃ haste tu dakṣiṇe \|\| 41 \|\|*

*vāme daṇḍadharaṃ tadvatsruvaṃ cāpi pradarśayet \|*  
*munibhirdevagandharvaiḥ stūyamānaṃ samantataḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

*kurvāṇamiva lokāṃstrīñchuklāmbaradharaṃ vibhum \|*  
*mṛgacarmadharaṃ cāpi divyayajñopavītinam \|\| 43 \|\|*

41-43. The complexion should be reddish, like the bed of the lotus with four hands, five faces holding a kamandalu in the left hand, sacrificial ladle in the right and a staff and Sruva in the left and right of e other sot of hands and -with the Devas, seers, Gandharvas praying all round Him.

He should be represented as engaged in the work of creation, wearing white raiments, deer skin, and a sacred thread.

## \|\| 260.44-46 \|\|

*ājyasthālīṃ nyasetpārśve vedāṃśca caturaḥ punaḥ \|*  
*vāmapārśve'sya sāvitrīṃ dakṣiṇe ca sarasvatīm \|\| 44 \|\|*

*agre ca ṛṣayastadvatkāryāḥ paitāmahe pade \|*  
*kārtikeyaṃ pravakṣyāmi taruṇādityasaprabham \|\| 45 \|\|*

*kamalodaravarṇābhaṃ kumāraṃ sukumārakam \|*  
*daṇḍakaiścīrakairyuktaṃ mayūravaravāhanam \|\| 46 \|\|*

44-46. To the right of the image should be located the site for Homa with ghee, etc., and the four Vedas, and to the left should be placed the image of Savitri, and on the right that of Sarasvati. The Rishis should be placed in front of the Lord. Now about the image of Kartikeya. The image of Svami Kartika should be made with a youthful appearance illustrious like the newly risen sun, of the hue of a lotus, holding a staff and a deer-skin, having a peacock for His conveyance.

## \|\| 260.47 \|\|

*sthāpayetsveṣṭanagare bhujāndvādaśa kārayet \|*  
*caturbhujaḥ kharvaṭe syādvane grāme dvibāhukaḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. The image of Svami Kartika with twelve hands should be placed in His newly chosen city, with 4 hands in a small town and the one with2 hands in a forest or a small village.

## \|\| 260.48 \|\|

*śaktiḥ pāśastathā khaḍgaḥ śaraḥ śūlaṃ tathaiva ca \|*  
*varadaścaiva hastaḥ syādatha cābhayado bhavet \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. In the right hand decorated with a golden armlet should be placed a javelin, a noose, a sword, an arrow and a trident and the other hand should be left blank, but in the posture of offering some gift, and holding out the idea “No fear.”

## \|\| 260.49-51 \|\|

*ete dakṣiṇato jñeyāḥ keyūrakaṭakojжvalāḥ \|*  
*dhanuḥ patākāmuṣṭiśca tarjanī tu prasāritā \|\| 49 \|\|*

*kheṭakaṃ tāmracūḍaṃ ca vāmahaste tu śasyate \|*  
*dvibhujasya kare śaktirvāme syātkukkuṭopari \|\| 50 \|\|*

*caturbhuje śaktipāśau vāmato dakṣiṇe tvasiḥ \|*  
*varado bhayado vā'pi dakṣiṇaḥ syātturīyakaḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

49-51. All the arms, arrow, and legs, fist, pointed ‘ring-fingers and other ornaments and a sword should be made in the left hand. The two-armed figure is to have a Shakti in His right hand. and the left hand resting on the peacock. The one with 4 hands should be made with a noose and a javelin in the left hand ‘and Varabhya in the right hand.

## \|\| 260.52-55 \|\|

*vināyakaṃ pravakṣyāmi gajavaktraṃ trilocanam \|*  
*lambodaraṃ caturbāhuṃ vyālayajñopavītinam \|\| 52 \|\|*

*dhvastakarṇaṃ bṛhattuṇḍamekadaṃṣṭraṃ pṛthūdaram \|*  
*svadantaṃ dakṣiṇakara utpalaṃ cāpare tathā \|\| 53 \|\|*

*modakaṃ paraśuṃ caiva vāmataḥ parikalpayet \|*  
*bṛhattvātkṣiptavadanaṃ pīnaskandhāṅghripāṇikam \|\| 54 \|\|*

*yuktaṃ tu ṛddhibuddhibhyāmadhastānmūṣakānvitam \|*  
*kātyāyanyāḥ pravakṣyāmi rūpaṃ daśabhujaṃ tathā \|\| 55 \|\|*

52-55. Now about the image of Ganesha; the face of Ganesha should have the trunk of an elephant, with three eyes, four arms, huge stomach, ears like those of an elephant, wearing a sacred thread, one large and long tusk holding with his right hand, a lotus and above a ball of sweet and with his left hand a battle axe and a bail of sweet, with extensive shoulders and huge arms and feet full of bliss, riding a mouse. He is the owner of Riddhi (success, prosperity') and Buddhi (intelligence).

## \|\| 260.57-58 \|\|

*locanatrayasaṃyuktāṃ pūrṇendusadṛśānanām \|*  
*atasīpuṣpavarṇābhāṃ supratiṣṭhāṃ sulocanām \|\| 57 \|\|*

*navayauvanasaṃpannāṃ sarvābharaṇabhūṣitām \|*  
*sucārudaśanāṃ tadvatpīnonnatapayodharām \|\| 58 \|\|*

57-58. The image of the Goddess Katyayani should be made of ten hands and as holding the weapons that are seen in the hands of Brahma, Vishnu and Shiva; with matted hair on Her head and a crescent with three eyes, face like the moon, shining like the atasi flower, having beautiful eyes, youthful in appearance, adorned with all the ornaments, having fine teeth and full breasts; standing with Her body curved in three directions.

## \|\| 260.59-65 \|\|

*tribhaṅgasthānasaṃsthānāṃ mahiṣāsuramardinīm \|*  
*triśūlaṃ dakṣiṇe dadyātkhaḍgaṃ cakraṃ kramādadhaḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

*tīkṣṇabāṇaṃ tathā śaktiṃ vāmato'pi nibodhata \|*  
*kheṭakaṃ pūrṇacāpaṃ ca pāśamaṅkuśameva ca \|\| 60 \|\|*

*ghaṇṭāṃ vā paraśuṃ vā'pi vāmataḥ saṃniveśayet \|*  
*adhastānmahiṣaṃ tadvadviśiraskaṃ pradarśayet \|\| 61 \|\|*

*śiraśchedodbhavaṃ tadvaddānavaṃ khaḍgapāṇinam \|*  
*hṛdi śūlena nirbhinnaṃ niryadantravibhūṣitam \|\| 62 \|\|*

*raktaraktīkṛtāṅgaṃ ca raktavisphāritekṣaṇam \|*  
*veṣṭitaṃ nāgapāśena bhrukuṭībhīṣaṇānanam \|\| 63 \|\|*

*sapāśavāmahastena dhṛtakeśaṃ ca durgayā \|*  
*vamadrudhiravaktraṃ ca devyāḥ siṃhaṃ pradarśayet \|\| 64 \|\|*

*devyāstu dakṣiṇaṃ pādaṃ samaṃ siṃhopari sthitam \|*  
*kiṃcidūrdhvaṃ tathā vāmamaṅguṣṭhaṃ mahiṣopari \|\| 65 \|\|*

59-65. The Destroyer of Mahishasura, armed with a quoit, a trident, sharp pointed arrows, a javelin, holding a sword, a bow, a noose, a goad, a bell, a battle axe in the left hands. Below Her image should be made the figure of the monster Mahishasura with his severed head, holding a sword in one hand, soaked in blood, ferocious looking, tied in the noose, ejecting blood, his breast being pierced by the javelin of the Devi and his intestines coming out. The conveyance of the Goddess in the form of a lion should also be made. The right foot of the Goddess should be placed on the back of the lion and the toe of the left foot should be made touching body of Mahishasura. Mahisha is made as encircled by a snake and Durga Devi as holding the hairs of the Demon with Her left hand. Such a form of the Goddess should be made and Devas should be placed all round in praying posture.

## \|\| 260.66-69 \|\|

*stūyamānaṃ ca tadūpamamaraiḥ saṃniveśayet \|*  
*idānīṃ surarājasya rūpaṃ vakṣye viśeṣataḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

*sahasranayanaṃ devaṃ mattavāraṇasaṃsthitam \|*  
*pṛthūruvakṣovadanaṃ siṃhaskandhaṃ mahābhujam \|\| 67 \|\|*

*kirīṭakuṇḍaladharaṃ pīvarorubhujekṣaṇam \|*  
*vajrotpaladharaṃ tadvannānābharaṇabhūṣitam \|\| 68 \|\|*

*pūjitaṃ devagandharvairapsarogaṇasevitam \|*  
*chatracāmaradhāriṇyaḥ striyaḥ pārśve pradarśayet \|\| 69 \|\|*

66-69. Now about the image of Indra: the image of Indra should be made with a thousand eyes riding on an infuriated elephant with extensive thigh, chest, and face, shoulders broad like those of a lion, having long and mighty arms, holding a thunderbolt and lotus, wearing a coronet and a couple of ear-rings, having beautiful eyes, armed with a club, adorned with various ornaments, adored by the Devas, the Gandharvas, and the nymphs, surrounded by a retinue of lady attendants, each holding an umbrella and waiving chamara, seated on a throne with Indrani on his left holding a lotus in Her hand.

## Chapter 261

## \|\| 261.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*prabhākarasya pratimāmidānīṃ śṛṇuta dvijāḥ \|*  
*rathasthaṃ kārayeddevaṃ padmahastaṃ sulocanam \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Suta said: — The image of the Sun should be made with beautiful seated in a chariot and holding a lotus.

## \|\| 261.2 \|\|

*saptāścaṃ caikacakraṃ ca rathaṃ tasya prakalpayet \|*  
*mukuṭena vicitreṇa padmagarbhasamaprabham \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. There should, be seven horses and one chakra (wheel) in the chariot 'of the Sun and a coronet beaming red should be placed on His head.

## \|\| 261.3-4 \|\|

*nānābharaṇabhūṣābhyāṃ bhujābhyāṃ dhṛtapuṣkaram \|*  
*skandhasthe puṣkare te tu līlayaiva dhṛte sadā \|\| 3 \|\|*

*colakacchannavapuṣaṃ kvaciccitreṣu darśayet \|*  
*vastrayugmasamopetaṃ caraṇau tejasā’vatau \|\| 4 \|\|*

3-4. He should be decorated well with ornaments and the two hands g blue lotuses, the latter should also be placed on His shoulders as if in a sport. His body should be shown covered with a bodice and two pieces of cloth. The feet should be made brilliant.

## \|\| 261.5 \|\|

*pratīhārau ca kartavyau pārśvayordaṇḍipiṅgalau \|*  
*kartavyau khaḍgahastau tau pārśvayoḥ puruṣāvubhau \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Two other figures named Dandi and Pingala should be placed as guards with sword in their hands,

## \|\| 261.8-11 \|\|

*bhujaṅgarajжubhirbaddhāḥ saptāśvā raśmisaṃyutāḥ \|*  
*padmasthaṃ vāhanastha vā padmahastaṃ prakalpayet \|\| 8 \|\|*

*vahnestu lakṣaṇaṃ vakṣye sarvakāmaphalapradam \|*  
*dīptaṃ suvarṇavapuṣamardhacandrā sane sthitam \|\| 9 \|\|*

*bālārkasadṛśaṃ tasya vadanaṃ cāpi darśayet \|*  
*yajñopavītinaṃ devaṃ lambakūrcadharaṃ tathā \|\| 10 \|\|*

*kamaṇḍaluṃ vāmakare dakṣiṇe tvakṣasūtrakam \|*  
*jvālāvitānasaṃyuktamajavāhanamujжvalam \|\| 11 \|\|*

8-11. Somewhere close to the image of the Sun an image of Brahma should also be made holding a pen. The image of the Sun should be surrounded „ by a number of Devas. Aruna, the charioteer of the Sun, is resplendent like the lotus leaves and the horses nice and with long necks and well.

decked are to be on His either side. They should also be properly held by reins of snakes. The seven horses yoked to the chariot of the Sun should be tied together with the string of the serpent. The image of the Sun should thus be made either seated in the chariot or on the lotus and holding a lotus. The image of Agni, the bestower of all desires, should be made shining like gold seated on a throne looking like crescent, having the face like that of the Sun, wearing a sacred thread, and holding a pendant kurcha (bunch) with broad shoulders, holding a Kamandalu in the left hand and a rosary of beads in the right. A shining canopy \[over its head\] should also be made, and also the conveyance of goat.

## \|\| 261.12-14 \|\|

*kuṇḍasthaṃ vā'pi kurvīta mūrdhni saptaśikhānvitam \|*  
*tathā yamaṃ pravakṣyāmi daṇḍapāśadharaṃ vibhum \|\| 12 \|\|*

*mahāmahiṣamārūḍhaṃ kṛṣṇāñjanacayopamam \|*  
*siṃhāsanagataṃ cāpi dīptāgnisamalocanam \|\| 13 \|\|*

*mahiṣaścitraguptasya karālāḥ kiṃkarāstathā \|*  
*samantāddarśayettasya saumyāsaumyānsurāsurān \|\| 14 \|\|*

12-14. Or he is to have seven heads with seven burning rays and He is to be placed in the kunda (sacrificial pit). The image of Dharmaraja should be made holding a mace and a noose, riding a huge buffalo black like soot and seated on a throne, with eyes sparkling like fire. Round His image should be made the images of Chitragupta, some formidable attendants,, groups of quiet and formidable Demons and the great buffalo,

## \|\| 261.15-22 \|\|

*rākṣasendraṃ tathā vakṣye lokapālaṃ ca nairṛtam \|*  
*narārūḍhaṃ mahākāyaṃ rakṣobhirbahubhirvṛtam \|\| 15 \|\|*

*khaḍgahastaṃ mahānīlaṃ kajжalācalasaṃnibham \|*  
*narayuktavimānasthaṃ pītābharaṇabhūṣitam \|\| 16 \|\|*

*varuṇaṃ ca pravakṣyāmi pāśahastaṃ mahābalam \|*  
*śaṅkhasphaṭikavarṇābhaṃ sitahārāmbarāvṛtam \|\| 17 \|\|*

*jhaṣāsanagataṃ śāntaṃ kirīṭāṅgadadhāriṇam \|*  
*vāyurūpaṃ pravakṣyāmi dhūmraṃ tu mṛgavāhanam \|\| 18 \|\|*

*citrāmbaradharaṃ śāntaṃ yuvānaṃ kuñcitabhruvam \|*  
*mṛgādhirūḍhaṃ varadaṃ patākādhvajasaṃyutam \|\| 19 \|\|*

*kuberaṃ ca pravakṣyāmi kuṇḍalābhyāmalaṃkṛtam \|*  
*mahodaraṃ mahākāyaṃ nidhyaṣṭakasamanvitam \|\| 20 \|\|*

*guhyakairbahibhiryuktaṃ dhanavyagrakaraistathā \|*  
*hārakeyūraracitaṃ sitāmbaradharaṃ sadā \|\| 21 \|\|*

*gadādharaṃ ca kartavyaṃ varadaṃ mukuṭānvitam \|*  
*narayuktavimānasthamevaṃ rītyā ca kārayet \|\| 22 \|\|*

15-22. The image of Nairita Lokapala, the Lord of the Rakshas, should be made riding on a human being followed by a band of demons, armed with a sword, resplendent like a mountain of soot, wearing yellow robes decked with ornaments and having a chariot drawn by men. The image of Lord Varuna should be made holding a noose in his hand, looking courageous, having a colour white as a crystal, wearing white apparel, riding a fish, peaceful in appearance, adorned with armlets and a coronet.

The image of Vayu should be made seated on a deer, smoky in complexion, nicely dressed looking quite young, with knitted brows, adorned with banners, granting boons. The image of Kuvera should be made wearing ear-rings, with a huge form, and a huge abdomen having a huge store of pelf and eight Nidhis surrounded by a number of attendants Guhyakas adorned with armlets, &c., wearing white dress and a coronet, seated on a Vimana drawn by men and giving wealth. He is holding a club in one hand and with the other hand He is holding out the idea of “No fear”.

## \|\| 261.23 \|\|

*tathaiveśaṃ pravakṣyāmi dhavalaṃ dhavalekṣaṇam \|*  
*triśūlapāṇinaṃ devaṃ tr! yakṣaṃ vṛṣagataṃ prabhum \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. The image of Lord Kana should be made white with white eyes, armed with a trident, having three eyes, riding on a bull.,

## \|\| 261.24-25 \|\|

*mātriṇāṃ lakṣaṇaṃ vakṣye yathāvadanupūrvaśaḥ \|*  
*brahmāṇī brahmasadṛśī caturvaktrā caturbhujā \|\| 24 \|\|*

*haṃsādhirūḍhā kartavyā sākṣasūtrakamaṇḍaluḥ \|*  
*maheśvarasya rūpeṇa tathā māheśvarī matā \|\| 25 \|\|*

24-25. The images of the different Matrikas should be made according to the forms of their respective Lords, viz. — the image of Brahmani should be seated on a crane having a Kamandalu and, a rosary with four heads and four arms, Maheshvari should similarly be made according to the resemblance of Maheshvara.

## \|\| 261.26 \|\|

*jaṭāmukuṭasaṃyuktā vṛṣasthā candra śekharā \|*  
*kapālaśūlakhaṭvāṅgavaradāḍyacaturbhujā \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. She should have matted hairs, seated on a bull with Her forehead adorned with a crescent, armed with a sword and holding a skull, trident, khatvanga, having 4 hands.

## \|\| 261.27 \|\|

*kumārarūpā kaumārī mayūravaravāhanā \|*  
*raktavastradharā tadvacchūlaśaktidharā matā \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. The image o! Kaumari should be made of the form of Kartika riding on a peacock, dressed in red, armed with a trident and a javelin, adorned with armlets, garlands, holding a cock in Her hand.

## \|\| 261.28-29 \|\|

*hārakeyūrasaṃpannā kṛkavākudharā tathā \|*  
*vaiṣṇavī viṣṇusadṛśī garuḍe samupasthitā \|\| 28 \|\|*

*caturbāhuśca varadā śaṅkhacakragadādharā \|*  
*siṃhāsanagatā vā'pi bālakena samanvitā \|\| 29 \|\|*

28-29. The image of Vaishnavi should be made with 4 hands, riding on Garuda holding a conch, a quoit, a club, &c., seated on a throne, having a child.

## \|\| 261.30-32 \|\|

*vārāhīṃ ca pravakṣyāmi mahiṣopari saṃsthitām \|*  
*varāhasadṛśī devī śiraścāmaradhāriṇī \|\| 30 \|\|*

*gadācakradharā tadvaddānavendra vināśinī \|*  
*indrā ṇīmindra sadṛśīṃ vajraśūlagadādharām \|\| 31 \|\|*

*gajāsanagatāṃ devīṃ locanairbahubhirvṛtām \|*  
*taptakāñcanavarṇābhāṃ divyābharaṇabhūṣitām \|\| 32 \|\|*

30-32. The image of the Goddess Varahi should be made riding on a buffalo, armed with a club, a quoit with a cowrie over Her head.

The image of Indrani should be made like Indra armed with a bolt, a club, and trident riding on an elephant, having many eyes, holding a keen sword, adorned with various divine ornaments, and of the colour of burnished gold.

## \|\| 261.33-36 \|\|

*tīkṣṇakhaḍgadharāṃ tadvadvakṣye yogeśvarīmimām \|*  
*dīrghajihvāmūrdhvakeśīmasthikhaṇḍaiśca maṇḍitām \|\| 33 \|\|*

*daṃṣṭrākarālavadanāṃ kuryāccaiva kṛśodarīm \|*  
*kapālamālinīṃ devīṃ muṇḍamālāvibhūṣitām \|\| 34 \|\|*

*kapālaṃ vāmahaste tu māṃsaśoṇitapūritam \|*  
*mastiṣkāktaṃ ca bibhrāṇāṃ śaktikāṃ dakṣiṇe kare \|\| 35 \|\|*

*gṛdhrasthā vāyasasthā vā nirmāṃsā vinatodarī \|*  
*karālavadanā tadvatkartavyā sā trilocanā \|\| 36 \|\|*

33-36. The image of Jogeshvari should be made with a long tongue, hair, standing on their end adorned with pieces of hones, having a set of ferocious teeth, slender waist, wearing a garland of skulls and heads covered with flesh and blood, holding a head in the left hand, soaked in a fatty liquid, holding a Shakti in the right hand, riding on a vulture or a crow, lean, with a scanty stomach, having a ferocious appearance. She has three eyes.

## \|\| 261.37-38 \|\|

*cāmuṇḍā baddhaghaṇṭā vā dvīpicarmadharā śubhā \|*  
*digvāsāḥ kālikā tadvadrā sabhasthā kapālinī \|\| 37 \|\|*

*suraktapuṣpābharaṇā vardhanīdhvajasaṃyutā \|*  
*vināyakaṃ ca kurvīta mātriṇāmantike sadā \|\| 38 \|\|*

37-38. When she assumes the form of Sri Chamunda she is to wear tiger skin having a bell in the Land. When she assumes the form of Kalika she is represented as riding on an ass, holding a skull, undressed, adorned with red flowers and banners with Vardhani. The image of Ganesha’s should be made near the images of these Matrikas.

## \|\| 261.39 \|\|

*vīreśvaraśca bhagavānvṛṣārūḍho jaṭādharaḥ \|*  
*vīṇāhastastriśūlī ca mātriṇāmagrato bhavet \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. The image of Bhagavan Vireshvara should be placed in front of the images of the Matrikas, it should be on a bull, having plaited hairs, holding Vina and trident in a standing posture.

## \|\| 261.40-47 \|\|

*śriyaṃ devīṃ pravakṣyāmi nave vayasi saṃsthitām \|*  
*suyauvanāṃ pīnagaṇḍāṃ raktauṣṭhīṃ kuñcitabhruvam \|\| 40 \|\|*

*pīnānnatastanataṭāṃ maṇikuṇḍaladhāriṇīm \|*  
*sumaṇḍalaṃ mukhaṃ tasyāḥ śiraḥ sīmantabhūṣaṇam \|\| 41 \|\|*

*padmasvastikaśaṅkhairvā bhūṣitāṃ kuṇḍalālakaiḥ \|*  
*kañcukābaddhagātrī ca hārabhūṣau payodharau \|\| 42 \|\|*

*nāgahastopamau bāhū keyūrakaṭakojжvalau \|*  
*padmaṃ haste pradātavyaṃ śrīphalaṃ dakṣiṇe bhuje \|\| 43 \|\|*

*mekhalābharaṇāṃ tadvattaptakāñcanasaprabhām \|*  
*nānābharaṇasaṃpannāṃ śobhanāmbaradhāriṇīm \|\| 44 \|\|*

*pārśve tasyāḥ striyaḥ kāryāścāmaravyagrapāṇayaḥ \|*  
*padmāsanopaviṣṭā tu padmasiṃhāsanasthitā \|\| 45 \|\|*

*karibhyāṃ snāpyamānā'sau bhṛṅgārābhyāmanekaśaḥ \|*  
*prakṣālayantau kariṇau bhṛṅgārābhyāṃ tathā'parau \|\| 46 \|\|*

*stūyamānā ca lokeśaistathā gandharvaguhyakaiḥ \|*  
*tathaiva yakṣiṇī kāryā siddhāsuraniṣevitā \|\| 47 \|\|*

40-47. The image of Shri Devi Lakshmi should be made with a very youthful appearance, having thick cheeks, red lips, knitted brows, with thick and raised breasts, adorned with jewels and earrings, with a round face, wearing head ornaments and lotus, having conch, and beautiful separated tresses of hair, adorned with garlands, armlets, having arms like the trunk of an elephant holding a lotus in the left hand, the fruit of an wood apple tree in the right, agorned with a lotus, a svastik, a conch, earrings and Alaka; breast covered with a bodice and wearing a necklace; with a girdle of bells, shining like gold, dressed in fine robes. Close by the image should be made the images of two female attendants holding chamaras in their hands. The Goddess should be seated on a lotus-bed surrounded by the buzzing black bees and bathed by a couple of elephants with vases, prayed by the Gandharvas, Guhyakas. Similarly should be made the image of Yakshini prayed by the Gods and placed close to the Lakshmi Devi.

## \|\| 261.48 \|\|

*pārśvayoḥ kalaśau tasyāstoraṇe devadānavāḥ \|*  
*nāgāścaiva tu kartavyāḥ khaḍgakheṭakadhāriṇaḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Near Her image should be placed vases. The images of the Gods and the demons armed with swords as well as of the serpents should be made close by.

## \|\| 261.49 \|\|

*adhastātprakṛtisteṣāṃ nābherūrdhvaṃ tu pauruṣī \|*  
*phaṇāśca mūrdhni kartavyā dvijihvā bahavaḥ samāḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. The lower parts of the serpents should be like (Prakriti) those of the natural serpents and the upper part is to be represented Paurushi and hoods on the head. They have each a pair of tongues.

## \|\| 261.50 \|\|

*piśācā rākṣasāścaiva bhūtavetālajātayaḥ \|*  
*nirmāṃsāścaiva te sarve raudrā vikṛtarūpiṇaḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Many demons, Rakshasas, Bhutas and Vetalas should be made to reside at the gateway of Lakshmi Devi. They are without flesh, terrible and hideous looking.

## \|\| 261.51-52 \|\|

*kṣetrapālaśca kartavyo jaṭilo vikṛtānanaḥ \|*  
*digvāsā jaṭilastadvacchvagomāyuniṣevitaḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

*kapālaṃ vāmahaste tu śiraḥ keśasamāvṛtam \|*  
*dakṣiṇe śastrikāṃ dadyādasurakṣayakāriṇīm \|\| 52 \|\|*

51-52. The images of Kshetrapalas should be made with plaited hair, formidable in appearance, undressed, surrounded by dogs and jackals, holding a head covered with the hair in the left hand, and a javelin in the right to destroy the demons.

## \|\| 261.53 \|\|

*athātaḥ saṃpravakṣyāmi dvibhujaṃ kusumāyudham \|*  
*pārśve cāśvamukhaṃ tasya makaradhvajasaṃyutam \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Afterwards the image of Cupid with two hands should be made and close to it should be placed the head of a horse with the sign of a Makara (crocodile).

## \|\| 261.54-55 \|\|

*dakṣiṇe puṣpabāṇaṃ ca vāme puṣpamayaṃ dhanuḥ \|*  
*prītiḥ syāddakṣiṇe tasya bhojanopaskarānvitā \|\| 54 \|\|*

*ratiṃśca vāmapārśve tu śayanaṃ sārasānvitam \|*  
*paṭaśca paṭahaścaiva kharaḥ kāmāturastathā \|\| 55 \|\|*

54-55. A floral arrow should he placed in the right hand of Cupid and a floral bow in the left one. To the right should be made the image of Priti holding all kinds of victuals and to the left should be made Rati in a reposing posture having a bed and a crane. the drums and the figure of a donkey passionate with sexual desire, wells and Nandana garden should also be made.

## \|\| 261.56 \|\|

*pārśvato jalavāpī ca vanaṃ nandanameva ca \|*  
*suśobhanaśca kartavyo bhagavānkusumāyudhaḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. Nearby should also be made a pleasure grove with a pool of water reached by nice steps. The god Cupid is very well dressed and his posture is somewhat bent.

## \|\| 261.57 \|\|

*saṃsthānamīṣadvakraṃ syādvismayasmitavaktrakam \|*  
*etaduddeśataḥ proktaṃ pratimālakṣaṇaṃ mayā \|*  
*vistareṇa na śaknoti bṛhaspatirapi dvijāḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Suta. — Rishis! I have just given you a rough idea of the consstruction of the different images. It is indeed very difficult to explain all the broad details which even Vrihaspati cannot do.”

## Chapter 262

## \|\| 262.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*pīṭhikālakṣaṇaṃ vakṣye yathāvadanupūrvaśaḥ \|*  
*pīṭhocchrāyaṃ yathāvacca bhāgānṣoḍaśa kārayet \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Suta said: — “Now I shall tell you about the pedestals of the different idols.” The pedestal should be divided into 10 parts.

## \|\| 262.2-3 \|\|

*bhūmāvekaḥ praviṣṭaḥ syāccaturbhirjagatī matā \|*  
*vṛtto bhāgastathaikaḥ syādvṛtaḥ paṭalabhāgataḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*bhāgaistribhistathā kaṇṭhaḥ kaṇṭhapaṭṭastu bhāgataḥ \|*  
*bhāgābhyāmūrdhvapaṭṭaśca śeṣabhāgena paṭṭikā \|\| 3 \|\|*

2-3. The first part should be put underground. Above that, the earth should be taken in 4 parts. Afterwards the round part should be covered with a coating. Then the neck of the pedestal should be made in three parts and the throne should be made in the other three parts.

The next four parts are known as Jagati; the next one part is termed Vritta"; the next one is Panchala or Vrita; above it three parts are denominated Kantha; next two parts are named Urdhapatta; and the last part Is Pattika.

## \|\| 262.4 \|\|

*praviṣṭaṃ bhāgamekaikaṃ jagatīṃ yāvadeva tu \|*  
*nirgamastu punastasya yāvadvai śeṣapaṭṭikā \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. The first five parts up to Jagati are imbedded within the earth the other parts up to Pattika are above the ground and on the uppermost part Pattika, a passage is to be made for the outlet of water.

## \|\| 262.5 \|\|

*vārinirgamanārthaṃ tu tatra kāryaḥ praṇālakaḥ \|*  
*pīṭhikānāṃ tu sarvāsāmetatsāmānyalakṣaṇam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. This is the general characteristic of all the pedestals.

## \|\| 262.6-7 \|\|

*viśeṣāndevatābhedāñchṛṇudhvaṃ dvijasattamāḥ \|*  
*sthaṇḍilā vā'tha vāpī vā yakṣī vedī ca maṇḍalā \|\| 6 \|\|*

*pūrṇacandrā ca vajrā ca padmā vārdhaśaśī tathā \|*  
*trikoṇā daśamī tāsāṃ saṃsthānaṃ vā nibodhata \|\| 7 \|\|*

6-7. The following are the ten different kinds of seats for different Devatas viz. — (1) Sthandila, (2) Vapi, (3) Yakshi, (4) Vedi, (5) Mandate, (6) Purnachandra, (7) Vajra, (8) Padma, (9) Ardhashashi, (10) Trikona

## \|\| 262.8-9 \|\|

*sthaṇḍilā caturasrā tu varjitā mekhalādibhiḥ \|*  
*vāpī dvimekhalā jñeyā yakṣī caiva trimekhalā \|\| 8 \|\|*

*caturasrāyatā vedī na tāṃ liṅgeṣu yojayet \|*  
*maṇḍalā vartulā yā tu mekhalābhirgaṇapriyā \|\| 9 \|\|*

8-9. Sthandila is the one that is without any girdle or circular boundary and is square-shaped. Vapi has two girdles, Yakshi has three girdles. The Vedi is rectangular.

## \|\| 262.10 \|\|

*raktā dvimekhalā madhye pūrṇacandrā tu sā bhavet \|*  
*mekhalātrayasaṃyuktā ṣaḍasrā vajrikā bhavet \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Purnachandra has two girdles variously coloured, Vajrisha has six corners and three girdles.

## \|\| 262.11 \|\|

*ṣoḍaśāsrā bhavetpadmā kiṃciddhrasvā tu mūlataḥ \|*  
*tathaiva dhanuṣākārā sārdhacandrā praśasyate \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Padma has sixteen corners and it is shorter below. Ardhashashi is like a bow.

## \|\| 262.12 \|\|

*triśūlasadṛśī tadvattrikoṇā hyūrdhvato matā \|*  
*prāgudakpravaṇā tadvatpraśastā lakṣaṇānvitā \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Trikona is triangular in shape like the upper part of a trident. The one that is lower towards the east and the north is said to be somewhat sloping, and extended and endowed with auspicious signs.

## \|\| 262.13-14 \|\|

*pariveṣaṃ tribhāgena nirgamaṃ tatra kārayet \|*  
*vistāraṃ tatpramāṇaṃ ca mūle cāgre tathordhvataḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*jalamārgaśca kartavyastribhāgena suśobhanaḥ \|*  
*liṅgasyārdhavibhāgena sthaulyena samadhiṣṭhitā \|\| 14 \|\|*

13-14 The three parts of the circumference should be outside and outlet for water should also be made there and at the base, front and top, there should be space equal to that amount and there a good outlet for water should be made ; and half of the Phallus should be made thick.

## \|\| 262.15 \|\|

*mekhalā tattribhāgena khātaṃ caiva pramāṇataḥ \|*  
*athavā pādahīnaṃ tu śobhanaṃ kārayetsadā \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Then the girdle is to be made of a dimension of the three parts of the Linga or the girdle should be without any foot. Only the prescribed limit should be dug or it should be artistically made without any division.

## \|\| 262.16 \|\|

*uttarasthaṃ praṇālaṃ ca pramāṇādadhikaṃ bhavet \|*  
*sthaṇḍilāyāmathā’rogyaṃ dhanaṃ dhānyaṃ ca puṣkalam \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. To the north a channel should be made a little bigger than the prescribed -dimensions. Sthandila is the giver of much health grain and wealth.

## \|\| 262.17 \|\|

*gopradā ca bhavedyakṣī vedī saṃpatpradā bhavet \|*  
*maṇḍalāyāṃ bhavetkīrtirvaradā pūrṇacandri kā \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Yakshi is the giver of cows, Vedi of prosperity, Mandala of fame Purnachandrika good boons

## \|\| 262.18 \|\|

*āyuṣpradā bhavevajrā padmā saubhāgyadā bhavet \|*  
*putrapradā'rdhacandrā syāttrikoṇā śatrunāśinī \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Vraja, of life; Padma, of good luck; Ardhachandra, of sons; Trikona is the destroyer of enemies.

## \|\| 262.19-21 \|\|

*devasya yajanārthaṃ tu pīṭhikā daśa kīrtitāḥ \|*  
*śaile śailamayīṃ dadyātpārthive pārthivīṃ tathā \|\| 19 \|\|*

*dāruje dārujāṃ kuryānmiśre miśrāṃ tathaiva ca \|*  
*nānyayonistu kartavyā sadā śubhaphalepsubhiḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*acāyāmasamaṃ dairghyaṃ liṅgāyāmasamaṃ tathā \|*  
*yasya devasya yā patnī tāṃ pīṭhe parikalpayet \|*  
*etatsarvaṃ samākhyātaṃ samāsātpīṭhalakṣaṇam \|\| 21 \|\|*

19-21. Ten such thrones have been described for Divine worship. If the Devata be made of stone, then the pedestal is also to be made of stone, If the Devata is made of earth, then the pedestal is to be also made of earth and if of wood, then the pedestal also of wood; and if the Deva be of a mixture, then the pedestal should be also of both mixed. The persons desirous of auspicious results should not deviate from the above prescribed rules.

Round the idol a big platform should be made and the Consort of the Lord should be located with His image.

## Chapter 263

## \|\| 263.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*athātaḥ saṃpravakṣyāmi liṅgalakṣaṇamuttamam \|*  
*susnigdhaṃ ca suvarṇaṃ ca liṅgaṃ kuryādvicakṣaṇaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Suta.—“I shall now explain to you the good points of the Phallus of Siva.” A wise man should make it of gold and agreeable looking.

## \|\| 263.2 \|\|

*prāsādasya pramāṇena liṅgamānaṃ vidhīyate \|*  
*liṅgamānena vā vidyātprāsādaṃ śubhalakṣaṇam \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. The size of the Phallus should be according to the size of the temple or vice-versa.

## \|\| 263.3 \|\|

*caturasre same garte brahmasūtraṃ nipātayet \|*  
*vāmena brahmasūtrasya arcāyā liṅgameva ca \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. On an even square pit the Brahma Sutra (sacred thread) should be placed and left to it should be located an image or the Phallus of Shiva that is to be worshipped.

## \|\| 263.5 \|\|

*pūrveṇa cāparaṃ dvāraṃ māhendraṃ dakṣiṇottaram \|*  
*dvāraṃ vibhajya pūrvaṃ tu ekaviṃśatibhāgikam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. The eastern entrance should be made towards the other side of the city; it is to point towards the north-east (and south). — I.

The Mahendra entrance door should be made in the southern or northern part of the town. The eastern entrance should be divided into twenty one parts.

## \|\| 263.6 \|\|

*tato madhyagataṃ jñātvā brahmasūtraṃ prakalpayet \|*  
*tasyārdhaṃ tu tridhā kṛtvā bhāgaṃ cottaratastyajet \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. The Brahma Sutra should be put in the centre and its half should be divided into three parts, and the northern portion should be left out.

## \|\| 263.7 \|\|

*evaṃ dakṣiṇatastyaktvā brahmasthānaṃ prakalpayet \|*  
*bhāgārdhena tu yalliṅgaṃ kāryaṃ tadiha śasyate \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Similarly the southern portion should also be left out and then Brahmasthana should be determined and the Phallus should be located in the half portion.

## \|\| 263.8-11 \|\|

*pañcabhāgavibhakteṣu tribhāgo jyeṣṭha ucyate \|*  
*bhājite navadhā garbhe madhyamaṃ pāñcabhāgikam \|\| 8 \|\|*

*ekasminneva navadhā garbhe liṅgāni kārayet \|*  
*samasūtraṃ vibhajyātha navadhā garbhabhājitam \|\| 9 \|\|*

*jyeṣṭhamardhaṃ kanīyo'rdhaṃ tathā madhyamamadhyamam \|*  
*evaṃ garbhaḥ samākhyātastribhirbhāgairvibhājayet \|\| 10 \|\|*

*jyeṣṭhaṃ tu trividhaṃ jñeyaṃ madhyamaṃ trividhaṃ tathā \|*  
*kanīyastrividhaṃ tadvalliṅgabhedā navaiva tu \|\| 11 \|\|*

8-11. If the Phallus be located in the 3rd or 5th part, it is called Jyestha. If it be divided into 9 parts, the fifth part is the central one. This central part is to be divided again into nine parts and the phallus is to be placed in it. Thus the central part is divided equally into three parts; these are termed Jyestha, Kanishtha and Madhyama. There are again three sorts of Jyestha, three sorts of Kanishtha, and three sorts of Madhyama parts. Thus nine sorts of Lingas are to be known.

## \|\| 263.12-21 \|\|

*nābhyardhamaṣṭabhāgena vibhajyātha samaṃ budhaiḥ \|*  
*bhāgatrayaṃ parityajya viṣkambhaṃ caturasrakam \|\| 12 \|\|*

*aṣṭāsraṃ madhyabhaṃ jñeyaṃ bhāgaṃ liṅgasya vai dhruvam \|*  
*vikīrṇe cettato gṛhya koṇābhyāṃ lāñchayedbudhaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*aṣṭāsraṃ kārayettadvadūrdhvamapyevameva tu \|*  
*ṣoḍaśāsrīkṛtaṃ paścādvartulaṃ kārayettataḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*āyāmaṃ tasya devasya nābhyāṃ vai kuṇḍalīkṛtam \|*  
*māheśvaraṃ tribhāgaṃ tu ūrdhvavṛttaṃ tvavasthitam \|\| 15 \|\|*

*adhastādbrahmabhāgastu caturasro vidhīyate \|*  
*aṣṭāsro veṣṇavo bhāgo madhyastasya udāhṛtaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*evaṃ pramāṇasaṃyuktaṃ liṅgaṃ vṛddhipradaṃ bhavet \|*  
*tathā'nyadapi vakṣyāmi garbhamānaṃ pramāṇataḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*garbhamānapramāṇena yalliṅgamucitaṃ bhavet \|*  
*caturdhā tadvibhajyātha viṣkambhaṃ tu prakalpayet \|\| 18 \|\|*

*devatāyatanaṃ sūtraṃ bhāgatrayavikalpitam \|*  
*adhastāccaturasraṃ tu aṣṭāsraṃ madhyabhāgataḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

*pūjyabhāgastato'rdhaṃ tu nābhibhāgastathocyate \|*  
*āyāme yadbhavetsūtraṃ nāhasya caturasrake \|\| 20 \|\|*

*caturasraṃ parityajya aṣṭāsrasya tu yadbhavet \|*  
*tasyāpyardhaṃ parityajya tato vṛttaṃ tu kārayet \|\| 21 \|\|*

12-21. Eight divisions should he made below the navel and three should be discarded and the rest should be made into a square. The centre of the Lingam should be made octagonal and the upper part of the Phallus likewise so. The head should be made round. The navel of the Phallus is to be made into a circular knot. The upper portion of the Phallus of Shiva is round and the lower portion of Brahma should be made square and the central one, Vaishnava portion should be octagonal. Such an image is known as the giver of ever-increasing prosperity. “Now I shall explain to you other forms (Garbhamana) of the Phallus and their measurements.” The Phallus (its height) should be divided into four parts. One part of this is to be made the diameter of the Phallus of Shiva. Divide by means of threads the Phallus inter three parts. The lower portion should be made into a square, the central one should be made of an octagonal shape. The upper third portion of which is worshipped and is called Nabhi, it should be made circular. The base is to he made samkshipta (compressed'. The square portion should be buried in the ground, the central one should be kept in water.

## \|\| 263.22-23 \|\|

*śiraḥ pradakṣiṇaṃ tasya saṃkṣiptaṃ mūlato nyaset \|*  
*bhraṣṭapūjaṃ bhavelliṅgamadhastādvipulaṃ ca yat \|\| 22 \|\|*

*śirasā ca sadā nimnaṃ manojñaṃ lakṣaṇānvitam \|*  
*saumyaṃ tu dṛśyate yattu liṅgaṃ tadvṛddhidaṃ bhavet \|\| 23 \|\|*

22-23. The Phallus with a slender base and thick in the part under water is known as Jyestha; its lower part and its head is to be made always somewhat low, beautiful, and endowed with good qualities. The Linga that looks elegant is the giver of prosperity.

## \|\| 263.24-25 \|\|

*atha mūle ca madhye tu pramāṇaṃ sarvataḥ samam \|*  
*evaṃvidhaṃ tu yalliṅgaṃ bhavettatsārvakāmikam \|\| 24 \|\|*

*anyathā yadbhavelliṅgaṃ tadasatsaṃpracakṣate \|*  
*evaṃ ratnamayaṃ kuryātsphāṭikaṃ pārthivaṃ tathā \|*  
*śubhaṃ dārumayaṃ cāpi yadvā manasi rocate \|\| 25 \|\|*

24-25. The Phallus which is even at the base as well as in the middle is also the giver of all desires. The one that has not such a construction brings bad luck. One may make a Phallus according to the prescribed dimensions of ruby, diamond, crystal, clay, wood according to one’s choice and means.

## Chapter 264

## \|\| 264.1 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*devatānāmathaitāsāṃ pratiṣṭhāvidhimuttamam \|*  
*vada sūta yathānyāyaṃ sarveṣāmapyaśeṣataḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. The Rishis said :—‘ Pray now tell us about the consecration of the different Divine images and idols.”

## \|\| 264.2 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*athātaḥ saṃpravakṣyāmi pratiṣṭhāvidhimuttamam \|*  
*kuṇḍamaṇḍapavedīnāṃ pramāṇaṃ ca yathākramam \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Suta said :—“ Rishis! now listen to it and I shall relate it to you. I shall also tell you the dimensions of kundas (sacrificial pits), mandapas, altars.”

## \|\| 264.3 \|\|

*caitre vā phālgune vā'pi jyeṣṭhe vā mādhave tathā \|*  
*māghe vā sarvadevānāṃ pratiṣṭhā śubhadā bhavet \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Magha, Phalguna, Chaitra, Vaishakha and Jyaishtha are the most auspicious months for the consecration of the images.

## \|\| 264.4-5 \|\|

*prāpya pakṣaṃ śubhaṃ śuklamatīte dakṣiṇāyane \|*  
*pañcamī ca dvitīyā ca tṛtīyā saptamī tathā \|\| 4 \|\|*

*daśamī paurṇamāsī ca tathā śreṣṭhā trayodaśī \|*  
*āsu pratiṣṭhā vidhivatkṛtā bahuphalā bhavet \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. In the Uttarayana season, the second, third, fifth, seventh and tenth days of a bright fortnight, the full moon-day, especially the thirteenth day of a bright fortnight are most auspicious for the consecration of idols.

## \|\| 264.6-7 \|\|

*āṣāḍhe dve tathā mūlamuttarādvayameva ca \|*  
*jyeṣṭhāśravaṇarohiṇyaḥ pūrvābhādra padā tathā \|\| 6 \|\|*

*hastāśvinī revatī ca puṣyo mṛgaśirastathā \|*  
*anurādhā tathā svātī pratiṣṭhādiṣu śasyate \|\| 7 \|\|*

6-7. Purvashadha, Uttarashadha, Mala, Purvabhadrapada, Uttarabhadrapada, Hasta, Ashvini, Revati, Pusy4, Mrigashira, Anuradha, and. Svati are the best asterisms for the consecration of idols.

## \|\| 264.8 \|\|

*budho bṛhaspatiḥ śukrastrayo'pyete śubhagrahāḥ \|*  
*ebhirnirīkṣitaṃ lagnaṃ nakṣatraṃ ca praśasyate \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Mercury, Jupiter, and Venus are the auspicious planets for the consecration of an image, and the asterisms and Lagnas under the influence of these three are also auspicious.

## \|\| 264.9-11 \|\|

*grahatārābalaṃ labdhvā grahapūjāṃ vidhāya ca \|*  
*nimittaśakunaṃ labdhvā varjayitvā'dbhutādikam \|\| 9 \|\|*

*śubhayoge śubhasthāne krūragrahavivarjite \|*  
*lagna ṛkṣe prakurvīta pratiṣṭhādikamuttamam \|\| 10 \|\|*

*ayane viṣuve tadvatṣaḍaśītimukhe tathā \|*  
*eteṣu sthāpanaṃ kāryaṃ vidhidṛṣṭena karmaṇā \|\| 11 \|\|*

9-11. At such a conjunction of auspicious planets and stars avoiding the influence of evil stars, one should consecrate an idol in an auspicious place after worshipping the planets (doing the Graha puja). Good omens are to be watched for ; evils, e.g., Adbhuta, etc., are to be avoided. And on an auspicious day and in an auspicious place, when the Lagna (rising asterism) is free from malefic planets and under an auspicious star one should consecrate an idol.

## \|\| 264.12 \|\|

*prājāpatye tu śayanaṃ śvete tūtthāpanaṃ tathā \|*  
*muhūrte sthāpanaṃ kuryātpunarbrāhme vicakṣaṇaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Installation is best when it is done according to the rules prescribed for Ayanas, Vishuba and Shadasiti. The installation is to be performed in the Brahma Muhurta at the time of Prajapatya Sayana and Shukla Utthapanam.

## \|\| 264.13 \|\|

*prāsādasyottare vā'pi pūrve vā maṇḍapo bhavet \|*  
*hastānṣoḍaśa kurvīta daśa dvādaśa vā punaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. The Mandapa should be made on the east or north of the temple. It should be of 16, 10 or 12 hands in length.

## \|\| 264.15-16 \|\|

*caturbhistoraṇairyukto maṇḍapaḥ syāccaturmukhaḥ \|*  
*plakṣadvāraṃ bhavetpūrvaṃ yāmye caudumbaraṃ bhavet \|\| 15 \|\|*

*paścādaśvatthaghaṭitaṃ naiyagrodhaṃ tathottare \|*  
*bhūmau hastapraviṣṭāni caturhastāni cocchraye \|\| 16 \|\|*

15-16. An altar should be made in the centre of the Mandapa which should be 5, 7, or 4 hands long. The altar is to be neat and clean.

There should be 4 doors with archways round the Mandapa and of those the eastern door should be of Plaksha tree, the southern one of the fig-tree, the western one of ashvattha tree and the northern one of Nyagrodha tree. The Mandapa should be buried 1 hand in the ground and it should be 4 hands in height.

## \|\| 264.17 \|\|

*sūpaliptaṃ tathā ślakṣṇaṃ bhūtalaṃ syātsuśobhanam \|*  
*vastrairnānāvidhaistadvatpuṣpapallavaśobhitam \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. The earth should be washed well and cleaned and then the interior should be decorated well with various kinds of cloths, flowers and leaves.

## \|\| 264.18 \|\|

*kṛtvaivaṃ maṇḍapaṃ pūrvaṃ caturdvāreṣu vinyaset \|*  
*avraṇānkalaśānaṣṭau jvalatkāñcanagarbhitān \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. After making such a Mandapa, eight jars full of water and containing 4, lump of gold should be placed at each doorway on either side. Those vases should not be leaky.

## \|\| 264.19 \|\|

*cūtapallavasaṃchannānsitavastrayugānvitān \|*  
*sarvauṣadhiphalopetāṃścandanodakapūritān \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. They should be covered with mango leaves and should be filled in with medicinal herbs, flowers, sandal, water, and covered with white cloth.

## \|\| 264.20 \|\|

*evaṃ niveśya tadgarbhe gandhadhūpārcanādibhiḥ \|*  
*dhvajādirohaṇaṃ kāryaṃ maṇḍapasya samantataḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. After thus placing the vases within the Mandapa, flags and buntings should be hung all-round the pandal and incense and fragrant gums, burnt before the idols.

## \|\| 264.21 \|\|

*dhvajāṃśca lokapālānāṃ sarvadikṣu niveśayet \|*  
*patākā jaladākārā madhye syānmaṇḍapasya ta \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Mandapa is a temporary building created for performing a ceremony.

The banners of the Lokapalas should be hung all round and in the centre of the pandal a banner of the shape of the clouds should be hung.

## \|\| 264.22 \|\|

*gandhadhūpādikaṃ kuryātsvaiḥ svairmantrairanukramāt \|*  
*baliṃ ca lokapālebhyaḥ svamantreṇa nivedayet \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Afterwards offerings should be made to the Lokapalas and worship offered to them by repeating their prescribed mantras and giving Bali’s (making sacrifices) in honour of them.

## \|\| 264.23 \|\|

*ūrdhvaṃ tu brahmaṇe deyaṃ tvadhastāccheṣavāsukeḥ \|*  
*saṃhitāyāṃ tu ye mantrāstadvaivatyāḥ śubhāḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. The offerings to Brahma above should be made by reciting the first part of the mantra, to Vasuki below by reciting the middle portion of the mantra and then to the Lokapalas in all directions. The mantras given in Samhita and Shruti are to be repeated.

## \|\| 264.24-25 \|\|

*taiḥ pūjā lokapālānāṃ kartavyā ca samantataḥ \|*  
*trirātramekarātraṃ vā pañcarātramathāpi vā \|\| 24 \|\|*

*athavā saptarātraṃ tu kāryaṃ syādadhivāsanam \|*  
*evaṃ satoraṇaṃ kṛtvā adhivāsanamuttamam \|\| 25 \|\|*

24-25. Preliminary ceremonies (Adhivas) of images should be observed for three nights, one night or 5 nights, or 7 nights as the case may be.

## \|\| 264.26 \|\|

*tasyāpyuttarataḥ kuryātsnānamaṇḍapamuttamam \|*  
*tadardhena tribhāgena caturbhāgena vā punaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Thus finishing the gateways and Adhivas ceremonies the bathing ceremony of the Mandal should be performed in the second, third, or fourth period.

## \|\| 264.27-28 \|\|

*ānīya liṅgamarcāṃ vā śilpinaḥ pūjayedbudhaḥ \|*  
*vastrābharaṇaratnaiśca ye'pi tatparicārakāḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

*kṣamadhvamiti tānbrūyādyajamāno'pyataḥ param \|*  
*devaṃ prastaraṇe kṛtvā netrajyotiḥ prakalpayet \|\| 28 \|\|*

27-28. Then the wise should bring the Phallus or the image and worship the sculptor with cloth, jewels and ornaments. Then “excuse me” should be said by the Yajaman (the sacrificer or worshipper) and the sculptors, &c., dismissed.

## \|\| 264.29-30 \|\|

*akṣṇoruddharaṇaṃ vakṣye liṅgasyāpi samāsataḥ \|*  
*sarvatastu baliṃ dadyātsiddhārthaghṛtapāyasaiḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*śuklapuṣpairalaṃkṛtya ghṛtagugguladhūpitam \|*  
*viprāṇāṃ vācanaṃ kuryāddadyācchaktyā ca dakṣiṇām \|\| 30 \|\|*

29-30. Then the idol is to be placed on the seat and his eyes are to be imparted. The following, in brief, is the way: — First, offerings should be made all round with sesamum, clarified butter, rice cooked in milk and sugar. Then after decorating the Brahmanas with white flowers, guggula, incense with clarified butter should he offered to the image and then gifts to the Brahmanas should be offered according to his means.

## \|\| 264.31 \|\|

*gāṃ mahīṃ kanakaṃ caiva sthāpakāya nivedayet \|*  
*lakṣaṇaṃ kārayedbhaktyā mantreṇānena vai dvijaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Cows, land, gold, &c., should be given to the priest who officiates at the consecration of the image, arid the Brahmana should name the image after reciting the mantra contained in the following couplet.

## \|\| 264.32 \|\|

*oṃnamo bhagavate tubhyaṃ śivāya paramātmane \|*  
*hiraṇyaretase viṣṇo viśvarūpāya te namaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Salutations to the Lord Vishnu, Shiva, Thou art the Supreme Being, the Hiranya-reta; Salutation to Thee! O Vishnu!

## \|\| 264.33 \|\|

*mantro'yaṃ sarvadevānāṃ netrajyotiḥṣvapi smṛtaḥ \|*  
*evamāmantr! ya deveśaṃ kāñcanena vilekhayet \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. The above mantra is generally used to impart light in the eyes of all idols. After invoking the Divine spirit into the image, the eyes should be given sight to with a bar of gold.

## \|\| 264.34 \|\|

*maṅgalyāni ca vādyāni brahmaghoṣaṃ sagītakam \|*  
*vṛddhyarthaṃ kārayedvidvānamaṅgalyavināśanam \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Pleasant music should be played and sweet hymns. should be sung, and Vedic hymns chanted. To win prosperity and dispel ill-luck the Vedas should be recited.

## \|\| 264.35-36 \|\|

*lakṣaṇoddharanaṃ vakṣye liṅgasya susamāhitaḥ \|*  
*tridhā vibhajya pūjyāyāṃ lakṣaṇaṃ syādvibhājakam \|\| 35 \|\|*

*lekhātrayaṃ tu kartavyaṃ yavāṣṭāntarasaṃyutam \|*  
*na sthūlaṃ na kṛśaṃ tadvanna vakraṃ chedavarjitam \|\| 36 \|\|*

35-36. The image should be divided into three parts and afterwards three lines at a distance of eight Yavas from one another should be drawn which should be broad, thin and crooked. They should not be broken (a«., should be continuous).

## \|\| 264.37 \|\|

*nimnaṃ yavapramāṇena jyeṣṭhaliṅgasya kārayet \|*  
*sūkṣmāstatastu kartavyā yathā madhyamake nyaset \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. In the Jaishtha Phallus, the lowermost line should be of the dimension of one Yava, the middle one is to be finer still.

## \|\| 264.38-40 \|\|

*aṣṭabhaktaṃ tataḥ kṛtvā tyaktvā bhāgatrayaṃ budhaḥ \|*  
*lambayetsapta rekhāstu pārśvayorubhayoḥ samāḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

*tāvatpralambayedvidvānyāvadbhāgacatuṣṭayam \|*  
*bhrāmyate pañcabhāgādhvaṃ kārayetsaṃgamaṃ tataḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

*rekhayoḥ saṃgame tadvatpṛṣṭhe bhāgadvayaṃ bhavet \|*  
*evametatsamākhyātaṃ samāsāllakṣaṇaṃ mayā \|\| 40 \|\|*

38-40. Then eight divisions should be made and three of them should be discarded. Then seven lines should be drawn on either side and four divisions are to be noted. Afterwards the lines should be allowed to meet at the top of the fifth line. This is the union of the lines; on the back of these lines, two divisions are to be made. These are, in brief, the Lakshanas (characteristics). Thus the Lakshanoddhara of the Lingam is described.

## Chapter 265

## \|\| 265.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi mūrtipānāṃ tu lakṣaṇam \|*  
*sthāpakasya samāsena lakṣaṇaṃ śṛṇuta dvijāḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Suta said: — “I shall now tell you about the persons who should consecrate and worship the idols.”

## \|\| 265.2-12 \|\|

*sarvāvayavasaṃpūrṇo vedamantraviśāradaḥ \|*  
*purāṇavettā tattvajño dambhalobhavivarjitaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*kṛṣṇasāramaye deśe ya utpannaḥ śubhākṛtiḥ \|*  
*śaucācāraparo nityaṃ pāṣaṇḍakulaniḥspṛhaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*samaḥ śatrau ca mitre ca brahmopendra harapriyaḥ \|*  
*ūhāpohārthatattvajño vāstuśāstrasya pāragaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*ācāryastu bhavennityaṃ sarvadoṣavivarjitaḥ \|*  
*mūrtipāstu dvijāścaiva kulīnā ṛjavastathā \|\| 5 \|\|*

*dvātriṃśatṣoḍaśāthāpi aṣṭau vā śrutipāragāḥ \|*  
*jyeṣṭhamadhyakaniṣṭheṣu mūrtipā vaḥ prakīrtitāḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*tato liṅgamathārcāṃ vā nītvā snapanamaṇḍapam \|*  
*gītamaṅgalaśabdena snapanaṃ tatra kārayet \|\| 7 \|\|*

*pañcagavyakaṣāyeṇa mṛdbhirbhasmodakena ca \|*  
*śaucaṃ tatra prakurvīta vedamantracatuṣṭayāt \|\| 8 \|\|*

*samudra jyeṣṭhamantreṇa āpo divyeti cāparaḥ \|*  
*yāsāṃ rājeti mantrastu āpo hi ṣṭheti cāparaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*evaṃ snāpya tato devaṃ pūjya gandhānulepanaiḥ \|*  
*pracchādya vastrayugmena abhivastretyudāhṛtam \|\| 10 \|\|*

*utthāpayettato devamuttiṣṭha brahmaṇaspate \|*  
*āmūrajeti ca tathā rathe tiṣṭheti cāparaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*rathe brahmarathe vā'pi dhṛtāṃ śilpigaṇena tu \|*  
*āropya cā'nayedvidvānākṛṣṇena praveśayet \|\| 12 \|\|*

2-12. Now, in brief, about the qualifications of the Sthapaka (who places the idol). The Sthapaka or Acharya should be well-versed in the Vedas, Puranas, Samkhya, free from avarice, born in a country abounding with black deer, handsome, of full limbs, of clean habits, free from hypocrisy, making no difference between friend and foe, having equal devotion for Shiva, Vishnu and Brahma, accomplished in Logic, having no vices, belonging to a good Kulin family and versed in the building science or Vastu Shastra. The Murtipa Brahmanas should consecrate the images according to the prescribed rites. Thirty-two, 16 or 8 persons should be employed for consecration. These three distinctions indicate as superior, middling, and ordinary. There should be great rejoicings at the time of consecrating the idols, which should first be taken to the bathing mandapa and washed with Panchagavya, Panchakashaya, earth, ash, and water while reciting the four Vedic mantras, viz., (1) Samudra Jyeshtha etc., (2) Apodivya, (3) Yasamraja (4) Apohishtha. Then the idol should be purified with Panchagavya and other three substances and then bathed; it should then be adored with sandal and incense after which it should be covered with two pieces of cloth by reciting “Abhi Vastre”; then after reciting the-mantra “ Uttshtha Brahmanaspate” the idols should be placed in standing posture. By reciting the two mantrams “Amuraja and rathetishtha, ” they should be placed in the chariot and conducted into the temple.

## \|\| 265.13-17 \|\|

*tataḥ prāstīrya śayyāyāṃ sthāpayecchanakairbudhaḥ \|*  
*kuśānāstīrya puṣpāṇi sthāpayetprāṅmukhaṃ tataḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*tatastu nidrā kalaśaṃ vastrakāñcanasaṃyutam \|*  
*śirobhāge tu devasya japannevaṃ nidhāpayet \|\| 14 \|\|*

*āpo devīti mantreṇa āpo'smānmātaro'pi ca \|*  
*tato dukūlapaṭṭaiśca cchādya netropadhānakam \|\| 15 \|\|*

*dadyācchirasi devasya kauśeyaṃ vā vicakṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*madhunā sarpiṣā'bhyajya pūjya siddhārthakaistataḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*āpyāyasveti mantreṇa yā te rudra śiveti ca \|*  
*upaviśyārcayeddevaṃ gandhapuṣpaiḥ samantataḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

13-17. Later on it should be placed flat on a bed after strewing kusha grass and: then by turning the face to the east flowers should he strewn and at the head of the idol should be placed a vase full of water, with gold also and then the image should be covered with a piece of silk cloth after reciting the mantra “Apodeve aposmana matarapi” or the silk cloth may be put upon the head of the idol. The Deva is then to be bathed with honey, ghee, mustard and then worshipped with the mantras “Apyasva” and then worshipped with the mantras “Apyasva” and “Yate Rudra Shiva” and with incense and flowers also.

## \|\| 265.18-25 \|\|

*sitaṃ pratisaraṃ dadyādbārhaspatyeti mantrataḥ \|*  
*dukūlapaṭṭaiḥ kārpāsairnānācitrairathāpi vā \|\| 18 \|\|*

*ācchādya devaṃ sarvatra cchatracāmaradarpaṇam \|*  
*pārśvataḥ sthāpayettatra vitānaṃ puṣpasaṃyutam \|\| 19 \|\|*

*ratnānyoṣadhayastatra gṛhopakaraṇāni ca \|*  
*bhājanāni vicitrāṇi śayanānyāsanāni ca \|\| 20 \|\|*

*abhi tvā śūra mantreṇa yathā vibhavato nyaset \|*  
*kṣīraṃ kṣaudraṃ ghṛtaṃ tadvadbhakṣyabhojyānnapāyasaiḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*ṣaḍvidhaiśca rasaistadvatsamantātparipūjayet \|*  
*baliṃ dadyātprayatnena mantreṇānena bhūriśaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*tr! yambakaṃ yajāmaha iti sarvataḥ śanakairbhuvi \|*  
*mūrtipānsthāpayetpaścātsarvadikṣu vicakṣaṇaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

*caturo dvārapālāṃśca dvāreṣu viniveśayet \|*  
*śrīsūktaṃ pāvamānaṃ ca somasūktaṃ sumaṅgalam \|\| 24 \|\|*

*tathā ca śāntikādhyāyamindra sūktaṃ tathaiva ca \|*  
*rakṣoghnaṃ ca tathā sūktaṃ pūrvato bahvṛco japet \|\| 25 \|\|*

18-25. By reciting “Barhaspataye” mantra a white thread should be tied round the wrist of the idol,) which should then be covered with various kinds of fine clothes; and umbrella, chamara, mirror, awning with flowers, should be placed close by as well as jewels, various kinds of medicinal herbs, utensils, bed, seats. All these should be placed after reciting the mantra “Abhi twa Shura “ and then gradually make offerings of milk, honey, clarified butter, other eatables, rice cooked in sugar and milk.

Then after reciting the mantra “tryamvakam yajamahe” a number of Valis (sacrifices) are to be offered in ali directions and then the image is to be installed. Then four gate keepers should be placed at the gates; and the Brahman priest Bahvricha is to recite in low voice Shrisukta, Pachamana Sukta, auspicious Soma Shukta, Shantikadhyaya, Indra Sukta and Rakshoghna Sukta (facing towards the east.)

## \|\| 265.26 \|\|

*raudraṃ puruṣasūktaṃ ca ślokādhyāyaṃ saśukriyam \|*  
*tathaiva maṇḍalādhyāyamadhvaryurdakṣiṇe japet \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. The learned Adharyu seated to the south should recite Raudra Purufasfikta, ^lokadhyaya Shukriya and Mandaladhaya.

## \|\| 265.27-29 \|\|

*vāmadevyaṃ bṛhatsāma jyeṣṭhasāma rathaṃtaram \|*  
*tathā puruṣasūktaṃ ca rudra sūktaṃ saśāntikam \|\| 27 \|\|*

*bhāruṇḍāni ca sāmāni cchandogaḥ paścime japet \|*  
*atharvāṅgirasaṃ tadvannīlaṃ raudraṃ tathaiva ca \|\| 28 \|\|*

*tathā'parājitādevīsaptasūktaṃ saraudra kam \|*  
*tathaiva śāntikādhyāyamatharvā cottare japet \|\| 29 \|\|*

27-29. The Chhandoga Brahmanas sitting in the west should recite Varnadevya, Vrihatsama, Jyesthasama, Rathantara, Purushasukta, Rudrasukta with Santika and Bharunda Sama. And in the north, the Atharvans should recite Nilaraudra, Aparajita, Sap ta sukta and Rudrasuktaantikadhyaya

## \|\| 265.30 \|\|

*śiraḥsthāne tu devasya sthāpako homamācaret \|*  
*śāntikaiḥ pauṣṭikaistadvanmantrairvyāhṛtipūrvakaiḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Towards the head of the idol the priest who consecrates it, should perform H5ma ceremony with Vyarhiti and Santik and Paushtik mantras.

## \|\| 265.31-36 \|\|

*palāśodumbarāśvatthā apāmārgaḥ śamī tathā \|*  
*hutvā sahasramekaikaṃ devaṃ pāde tu saṃspṛśet \|\| 31 \|\|*

*tato homasahasreṇa hutvā hutvā tatastataḥ \|*  
*nābhimadhyaṃ tathā vakṣaḥ śiraścāpyālabhetpunaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

*hastamātreṣu kuṇḍeṣu mūrtipāḥ sarvatodiśam \|*  
*samekhaleṣu te kuryuryonivaktreṣu cā’darāt \|\| 33 \|\|*

*vitastimātrā yoniḥ syādgajoṣṭhasadṛśī tathā \|*  
*āyatā chidra saṃyuktā pārśvataḥ kalayocchritā \|\| 34 \|\|*

*kuṇḍātkalānusāreṇa sarvataścaturaṅgulā \|*  
*vistāreṇocchrayāttadvaccaturasrā samā bhavet \|\| 35 \|\|*

*vedibhittiṃ parityajya trayodaśabhiraṅgulaiḥ \|*  
*evaṃ navasu kuṇḍeṣu lakṣaṇaṃ caiva dṛśyate \|\| 36 \|\|*

31-36. The wood of Palasha, Udumbara, Asvattha, Apamarga and Sami should be used as sacrificial fuel in the Homa ceremony and a thousand offerings should be made, taking at each time a stick and every time the feet of the image should be touched and when the thousand offerings are over the navel, chest and head should be similarly touched. Afterwards the four priests officiating at the consecration ceremony should perform Homa ceremony over the Kunda (pit) with a girdle and a Yoni measuring one hand with the greatest care. Nest a Yoni is to ho made on it one cubit long and resembling the lips of an elephant. It should have a hole and be extended and ornamented on both sides with beautiful ornamental workmanship. This Yoni is to be 4 fingers higher than the level of the sacrificial hollow (Kunda.) This part should be square and be made to look beautiful.

At a distance' of thirteen Angulas from the foundation of the Vedi (altar), nine other Kundas are to be similarly made.

## \|\| 265.37 \|\|

*āgneyaśākrayāmyeṣu hotavyamudagānanaiḥ \|*  
*śāntaye lokapālebhyo mūrtibhyaḥ kramaśastathā \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Then the priests should perform Achman and with a calm mind perform Homa ceremonies by reciting the mantras sacred to Agni in the East and Indra and the other Lokapalas in the South. Afterwards rites to propitiate the several Devas should be performed.

## \|\| 265.38-39 \|\|

*tathā mūrtyadhidevānāṃ homaṃ kuryātsamāhitaḥ \|*  
*vasudhā vasuretāśca yajamāno divākaraḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

*jalaṃ vāyustathā soma ākāśaścāṣṭamaḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*devasya mūrtayastvaṣṭāvetāḥ kuṇḍeṣu saṃsmaret \|\| 39 \|\|*

38-39. Afterwards the sacrificial offerings should be made to the presiding Deity of the idol. (Earth) Vasudha, Vasureta (Agni), Yajamana, Surya, Jala, Vayu, Chandrama, Akasha are the eight Devas to be remembered in the Kunda.

## \|\| 265.43 \|\|

*etebhyo vaidikaimantrairyathāsvaṃ homamācaret \|*  
*tathā śāntighaṭaṃ kuryātpratikuṇḍeṣu sarvataḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Prithvi is protected by Sarva Mahadeva, Agni by Pashupati, Yajamana by Ugra, Aditya by Rudra, Jala by Bhava, Vayu by Ishana, Chandra by Mahadeva, Akasha by Bhima Murti. In this way at the time of the conseration of any idol these eight are (he Murtipas, he., protectors of the component parts of the idol. — -Id-12, Homa ceremonies should be performed according to one’s means by reciting the prescribed Vedic mantra and a vase (Shantighata) should be placed in each Kunda.

## \|\| 265.44-47 \|\|

*śatānte vā sahasrānte saṃpūrṇāhutiriṣyate \|*  
*samapādaḥ pṛthivyāṃ tu praśāntātmā vinikṣipet \|\| 44 \|\|*

*āhutīnāṃ tu saṃpātaṃ pūrṇakumbheṣu vai nyaset \|*  
*mūlamadhyottamāṅgeṣu devaṃ tenāvasecayet \|\| 45 \|\|*

*sthitaṃ ca snāpayettena saṃpātāhutivāriṇā \|*  
*pratiyāmeṣu dhūpaṃ tu naivedyaṃ candanādikam \|\| 46 \|\|*

*punaḥ punaḥ prakurvīta homaḥ kāryaḥ punaḥ punaḥ \|*  
*punaḥpunaśca dātavyā yajamānena dakṣiṇā \|\| 47 \|\|*

44-47. Purnahuti should be offered after 100 or 1,000 Homas. These offerings are to be poured on the Puma Kumbha (jar filled with water.) The base, middle and head of the Devata are to be sprinkled with water, also the several Devas there are to be bathed also with the water frequently. At each prahara incense, sandal, etc., should be offered and Homas (libations of ghee) should be offered and the devotee should repeatedly make gifts (offer sacrificial fees) to the priests.

## \|\| 265.48-49 \|\|

*sitavastraiśca te sarve pūjanīyāḥ samantataḥ \|*  
*vicitrairhemakaṭakairhemasūtrāṅgulīyakaiḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

*vāsobhiḥ śayanīyaiśca pratiyāme ca śaktitaḥ \|*  
*bhojanaṃ cāpi dātavyaṃ yāvatsyādadhivāsanam \|\| 49 \|\|*

48-49. The priests should be given white garments, golden ear-rings, girdle, rings, etc., as well as a bedstead with all the necessary things. As long as they officiate, they should be provided with food.

## \|\| 265.50 \|\|

*balistrisaṃdhyaṃ dātavyo bhūtebhyaḥ sarvatodiśam \|*  
*brāhmaṇānbhojayetpūrvaṃ śeṣānvarṇāṃstu kāmataḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Offerings should be made to the Bhutas in all the three parts of the day. The Brahmans should be fed first and afterwards the members of all the castes arc to be fed.

## \|\| 265.51-52 \|\|

*rātrau mahotsavaḥ kāryo nṛtyagītakamaṅgalaiḥ \|*  
*sadā pūjyāḥ prayatnena caturthīkarmayāvatā \|\| 51 \|\|*

*trirātramekarātraṃ vā pañcarātramathāpi vā \|*  
*saptarātramatho kuryātkvacitsadyo'dhivāsanam \|*  
*sarvayajñaphalo yasmādadhivāsotsavaḥ sadā \|\| 52 \|\|*

51-52. In course of the night festivities should be observed. Dancing, singing should be performed. Till Chaturthi Karma Brahmanas should be fed. Adhvasa should be observed for 3, 5, 7 or 1 nights. On some occasions Adhivasa may be observed at once. The Adhivasa ceremony performed on such occasions gives the benefit of having performed all the sacrifices.

## Chapter 266

## \|\| 266.1-3 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*kṛtvā'dhivāsaṃ devānāṃ śubhaṃ kuryātsamāhitaḥ \|*  
*prāsādasyānurūpeṇa mānaṃ liṅgasya vā punaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*puṣpodakena prāsādaṃ prokṣya mantrayutena tu \|*  
*pātayetpakṣasūtraṃ tu dvārasūtraṃ tathaiva ca \|\| 2 \|\|*

*āśrayetkiṃcidīśānīṃ madhyaṃ jñātvā diśaṃ budhaḥ \|*  
*īśānīmāśritaṃ devaṃ pūjayanti divaukasaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

1-3. Suta said: — After performing the Adhivasa ceremony of the Devas the dimensions of the Lingam are to be determined in proportion to those of the temple. It is to be sprinkled with clean water and flowers after uttering mantras over them and a string should be spread in front of the door to the side and N. E. should be determined, for the Devas adore the Deva of the North-eastern corner,

## \|\| 266.4 \|\|

*āyurārogyaphaladamathottarasamāśritam \|*  
*śubhaṃ syādaśubhaṃ proktamanyathā sthāpanaṃ budhaiḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. The idol of Shiva when located facing the North, gives long life, health, prosperity. Other directions are not auspicious and bring ill-luck.

## \|\| 266.5-10 \|\|

*adhaḥ kūrmaśilā proktā sadā brahmaśilādhikā \|*  
*uparyavasthitā tasyā brahmabhāgādhikā śilā \|\| 5 \|\|*

*tatastu piṇḍikā kāryā pūrvoktairmānalakṣaṇaiḥ \|*  
*tataḥ prakṣālitāṃ kṛtvā pañcagavyena piṇḍikām \|\| 6 \|\|*

*kaṣāyatoyena punarmantrayuktena sarvataḥ \|*  
*devatārcāśrayaṃ mantraṃ piṇḍikāsu niyojayet \|\| 7 \|\|*

*tata utthāpya deveśamuttiṣṭha brahmaṇeti ca \|*  
*ānīya garbhabhavanaṃ pīṭhānte sthāpayetpunaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*ardhyapādyādikaṃ tatra madhuparkaṃ prayojayet \|*  
*tato muhūrtaṃ viśramya ratnanyāsaṃ samācaret \|\| 9 \|\|*

*vajramauktikavaidūryaśaṅkhasphaṭikameva ca \|*  
*puṣparāgendra nīlaṃ ca nīlaṃ pūrvādidikkramāt \|\| 10 \|\|*

5-10. The Kurma-shila should be put under the Lingam ; above the Kurma-shila should be placed the Brahmasil4 and above it the idol Siva mentioned before which should be bathed with Panchagavya. The mantras prescribed for the Divine worship should be recited and then the idol should be taken to the pedestal by reciting the mantra “Uttistha-Brahmana.”

Then water should be offered and afterwards Madhuparka. After one muhurta one should place precious stones, viz., pearls, Vaidurya, crystal lapis lazuli, sapphire, according to one’s means, in the directions, according to the prescribed rites.

## \|\| 266.11-18 \|\|

*tālakaṃ ca śilāvajramañjanaṃ śyāmameva ca \|*  
*kākṣī kāśī samākṣīkaṃ gairikaṃ cā’ditaḥ kramāt \|\| 11 \|\|*

*godhūmaṃ ca yavaṃ tadvattilamudgaṃ tathaiva ca \|*  
*nīvāramatha śyāmākaṃ sarṣapaṃ vrīhimeva ca \|\| 12 \|\|*

*nyasya krameṇa pūrvādi candanaṃ raktacandanam \|*  
*agaruṃ cāñjanaṃ cāpi uśīraṃ ca tataḥ param \|\| 13 \|\|*

*vaiṣṇavīṃ sahadevīṃ ca lakṣmaṇāṃ ca tataḥ param \|*  
*svarlokapālanāmnā tu nyasedoṃkārapūrvakam \|\| 14 \|\|*

*sarvabījāni dhātūṃśca ratnānyoṣadhayastathā \|*  
*kāñcanaṃ padmarāgaṃ tu pāradaṃ padmameva ca \|\| 15 \|\|*

*kūrmaṃ dharāṃ vṛṣaṃ tatra nyasetpūrvāditaḥ kramāt \|*  
*brahmasthāne tu dātavyāḥ saṃhatāḥ syuḥ parasparam \|\| 16 \|\|*

*kanakaṃ vidrumaṃ tāmraṃ kāṃsyaṃ caivā’rakūṭakam \|*  
*rajataṃ vimalaṃ puṣpaṃ lohaṃ caiva krameṇa tu \|\| 17 \|\|*

*kāñcanaṃ haritālaṃ ca sarvābhāve'pi nikṣipet \|*  
*dadyādbījauṣādhesthāne sahadevīṃ yavānapi \|\| 18 \|\|*

11-18. Afterwards yellow orpiment, Shilavajra, soot, yellow clay, lead, red chalk, wheat, barley, sesamum, munga, Nivara, Sama, mustard, Vrihi, rice, sandal, red sandal wood, aguru, anjana, Ushira khas, Vaishnavi, Sahadevi, Lakshana, should be placed after repeating their Devas and Om, in all the directions. Then after reciting the name of Svarga and the prescribed mantras conjointly with the sacred Om, all sorts of seeds, metals, jewels, gold, Padamaraga, mercury, lotus Pad m aka, and the images of turtle, ox and earth should be placed duly in all the directions commencing from the east. In the consecration of Brahma-Shila, gold, coral, copper bellmetal, brass, silver, nice flowers, iron, and harital should be placed in due order. If all these are not available then only gold and yellow orpiment should be put and in the place of seeds and herbs Sahadevi or barley should be substituted.

## \|\| 266.19-21 \|\|

*nyāsamantrānato vakṣye lokapālātmakāniha \|*  
*indra stu mahasā dīptaḥ sarvadevādhipo mahān \|\| 19 \|\|*

*vajrahasto mahāsattvastasmai nityaṃ namo namaḥ \|*  
*āgneyaḥ puruṣo raktaḥ sarvadevamayaḥ śikhī \|\| 20 \|\|*

*dhūmaketuranādhṛṣyastasmai nityaṃ namo namaḥ \|*  
*yamaścotpalavarṇābhaḥ kirīṭī daṇḍadhṛksadā \|\| 21 \|\|*

19-21. The following are the Nyasa mantras for the consecration of the Lokapalas, viz.: — The most valiant Indra is the Lord of the Devas. He is armed with a thunderbolt and is always illumined by His fire. I salute Him every day. Agni is red, is the emblem of all the Devas, conjoint with flashes, has smoke for His banner, unbearable to all, I salute Him, the presiding Person in the fire.

## \|\| 266.22-23 \|\|

*dharmasākṣī viśuddhātmā tasmai nityaṃ namo namaḥ \|*  
*nirṛtistu pumānkṛṣṇaḥ sarvarakṣodhipo mahān \|\| 22 \|\|*

*khaḍgahasto mahāsattvastasmai nityaṃ namo namaḥ \|*  
*varuṇo dhavalo viṣṇuḥ puruṣo nimnagādhipaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

22-23. Salutations always to Dharmaraja who is shining like the blue lotus, adorned with a coronet and sceptre. He is the witness of all actions, and righteousness. Salutations always to Niritti who is black in appearance, the Lord of all the Rakshasas, armed with a sword and endowed with glory.

## \|\| 266.24-32 \|\|

*pāśahasto mahābāhustasmai nityaṃ namo namaḥ \|*  
*vāyuśca sarvavarṇo vai sarvagandhavahaḥ śubhaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*puruṣo dhvajahastaśca tasmai nityaṃ namo namaḥ \|*  
*gauro yaśca pumānsaumyaḥ sarvauṣadhisamanvitaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*nakṣatrādhipatiḥ somastasmai nityaṃ namo namaḥ \|*  
*īśānapuruṣaḥ śuklaḥ sarvavidyādhipo mahān \|\| 26 \|\|*

*śūlahasto virūpākṣastasmai nityaṃ namo namaḥ \|*  
*padmayoniścaturmūrtirvedavāsāḥ pitāmahaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

*yajñādhyakṣaścaturvaktrastasmai nityaṃ namo namaḥ \|*  
*yo'sāvanantarūpeṇa brahmāṇḍaṃ sacarācaram \|\| 28 \|\|*

*puṣpavaddhārayenmūrdhni tasmai nityaṃ namo namaḥ \|*  
*oṃkārapūrvakā hyete nyāse balinivedane \|\| 29 \|\|*

*mantrāḥ syuḥ sarvakāryāṇāṃ vṛddhiputraphalapradāḥ \|*  
*nyāsaṃ kṛtvā tu mantrāṇāṃ pāyasenānulepitam \|\| 30 \|\|*

*paṭenā’cchādayecchvabhraṃ śuklenopari yatnataḥ \|*  
*tata utthāpya deveśamiṣṭadeśe tu śobhane \|\| 31 \|\|*

*dhruvā dyauriti mantreṇa śvabhropari niveśayet \|*  
*tataḥ sthirīkṛtasyāsya hastaṃ dattvā tu mastake \|\| 32 \|\|*

24-32. Salutations always to Varuna who is white in appearance, the image of Vishnu, the Lord of waters, armed with a noose, having sturdy arms.

Salutations to Vayu who diffuses all the aromas, has a banner in His hand.

I salute Chandrama. who is fair, simple, presiding over all herbs, the Lord of all the stars and planets. My salutations to Ishana Purusha who is white, the master of all the lores, armed with a trident and of three eyes. I always salute Lord Brahma born of a lotus, with four faces, dressed in the garment of the Vedas, the Lord of sacrifices. My salutations to Vishnu of infinite form who holds the whole universe, and who holds this earth as if she were a flower. At the time of sacrifices and of making gifts these mantras should be recited and the mantras should he prefixed with the sacred Om. They are the givers of prosperity and progeny.

After finishing the Nyasa with these mantras the consecrated idols should be rubbed with clarified, butter and then they should be dressed in white cloths and devout-fully worshipped.

## \|\| 266.33-34 \|\|

*dhyātvā paramasadbhāvāddevadevaṃ ca niṣkalam \|*  
*devavrataṃ tathā somaṃ rudra sūktaṃ tathaiva ca \|\| 33 \|\|*

*ātmānamīśvaraṃ kṛtvā nānābharaṇabhūṣitam \|*  
*yasya devasya yadrū paṃ taddhyāne saṃsmarettathā \|\| 34 \|\|*

33-34. Then raising the Deva with the mantra “Dhruva Dyau”, it should be placed on the desired Shvahhra, fully ornamented. Then placing one’s hand on the head of the Deva, one shoukljecite Soma and Rudra Suktas. At that time one should make himself Divine like by placing himself under the influence of Somasukta or Rudrasukta mantras and should then meditate on the Deva according to His form.

## \|\| 266.35 \|\|

*atasīpuṣpasaṃkāśaṃ śaṅkhacakragadādharam \|*  
*saṃsthāpayāmi deveśaṃ devo bhūtvā janārdanam \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. He should say: I consecrate Lord Vishnu the holder of conch and who has the lustre of atasi flower after making myself Divine.

## \|\| 266.36 \|\|

*akṣaraṃ daśabāhuṃ ca candrā rdhakṛtaśekharam \|*
