*gaṇeśaṃ vṛṣasaṃsthaṃ ca sthāpayāmi trilocanam \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. I consecrate the three eyed Shiva riding on a bull, adorned with a crescent, having ten hands, and the waster of the attendants.

## \|\| 266.37 \|\|

*ṛṣibhiḥ saṃstutaṃ devaṃ caturvaktraṃ jaṭādharam \|*  
*pitāmahaṃ mahābāhuṃ sthāpayāmyambujodbhavam \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. T consecrate Lord Brahma born from the Lotus prayed by die seers, having four faces, plaited hair, and mighty arms.

## \|\| 266.38 \|\|

*sahasrakiraṇaṃ śāntamapsarogaṇasaṃyutam \|*  
*padmahastaṃ mahābāhuṃ sthāpayāmi divākaram \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. I consecrate the Lord Sun having thousand rays, peaceful in appearance, surrounded by nymphs, having a lotus in His hand.

## \|\| 266.39 \|\|

*devamantrāṃstathā raudrā nrudra sya sthāpane japet \|*  
*viṣṇostu vaiṣṇavāṃstadvadbrāhmānvai brahmaṇo budha \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. In consecrating Shiva the mantras sacred to Him, the Deva mantra and Rudra Mantra should be recited; and similarly in the consecration of Vishnu mantras sacred to Him, the Vaishnava and Brahma mantras should be recited.

## \|\| 266.40 \|\|

*saurāḥ sūryasya japtavyāstathā'nyeṣu tadāśrayāḥ \|*  
*vedamantrapratiṣṭhā tu yasmādānandadāyinī \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. In the consecration of the Sun, the mantras sacred to the Sun should be recited; and similarly in the consecration of the other Devas mantras sacred to them should he recited, for one gets even-lasting benefits by consecrating the Divine idols by reciting the Vedic mantras of the respective Devas.

## \|\| 266.42-43 \|\|

*gaṇaṃ nandimahākālaṃ vṛṣaṃ bhṛṅgiṃ riṭiṃ guham \|*  
*devīṃ vināyakaṃ caiva viṣṇuṃ brahmāṇameva ca \|\| 42 \|\|*

*rudraṃ śakraṃ jayantaṃ ca lokapālānsamantataḥ \|*  
*tathaivāpsarasaḥ sarvā gandharvagaṇaguhyakām \|\| 43 \|\|*

42-43. The Deva consecrated in a temple should be looked upon as the chief God and other images placed close by should be treated as secondary Deities. They are also to be worshipped. — 41, All round Mahadeva should be located the attendants Nandi bull, Mahakala, Bhringi, Riti, Guha, the Goddess Parvati, Ganesha, Vishnu, Brahma, Rudra, Indra, Jayanta, Lokapala, nymphs, Gandharvas, and Guhyakas.

## \|\| 266.44 \|\|

*yo yatra sthāpyate devastasya tānparitaḥ smaret \|*  
*āvāhayettathā rudraṃ mantreṇānena yatnataḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. The meditation of the particular Deity should be made on the spot where His image is located and the Lord Shiva should be invoked with the mantra mentioned below.

## \|\| 266.45-48 \|\|

*yasya siṃhā rathe yuktā vyāghrabhūtāstathoragāḥ \|*  
*ṛṣayo lokapālāśca devaḥ skandastathā vṛṣaḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

*priyo gaṇo mātaraśca somo viṣṇuḥ pitāmahaḥ \|*  
*nāgā yakṣāḥ sagandharvā ye ca divyā nabhaścarāḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

*tamahaṃ tr! yakṣamīśānaṃ śivaṃ rudra mumāpatim \|*  
*āvāhayāmi sagaṇaṃ sapatnīkaṃ vṛṣadhvajam \|\| 47 \|\|*

*āgaccha bhagavanrudrā nugrahāya śivo bhava \|*  
*śāśvato bhava pūjāṃ me gṛhāṇa tvaṃ namo namaḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

45-48. “I invoke Lord Shiva in whose chariot are yoked lions, demons, serpents, seers, Lokapalas, Svamikartika, oxen, attendants, Matara, Soma, Vishnu, Brahma, Naga, Yaksha, Gandharva, and the other celestial inhabitants. I invoke Him with His Consort and attendants. Lord! be gracious enough to come. I salute you. Be pleased to accept my worship.

## \|\| 266.49 \|\|

*oṃ namaḥ svāgataṃ bhagavate namaḥ oṃ namaḥ somāya sagaṇāya saparivārāya pratigṛhṇātu bhagavanmantrapūtamidaṃ sarvamarghyapādyamācamanīyamāsanaṃ brahmaṇā'bhihitaṃ namo namaḥ svāhā \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. O Bhagavan! O Rudra i kindly grant my welfare. O Bhava! you are the eternal Purusha; accept my worship. I salute you. O Bhagavan welcome to you! O Soma! be pleased to accept along with your attendants and relations this mantra purified Padya, Arghya, Achamaniya and Asana. I salute you.”

## \|\| 266.50-51 \|\|

*tataḥ puṇyāhaghoṣeṇa brahmaghoṣaiśca puṣkalaiḥ \|*  
*snāpayettu tato devaṃ dadhikṣīraghṛtena ca \|\| 50 \|\|*

*madhuśarkarayā tadvatpuṣpagandhodakena ca \|*  
*śivadhyānaikacittastu mantrānetānudīrayet \|\| 51 \|\|*

50-51. Afterwards Vedic hymns should be recited for a long time and then the idol of Suva should be bathed in curds, milk, clarified butter, water, sugar, honey, flowers, and incense along with sweet' music. Then Lord Shiva should be devoutfully worshipped and the following mantras should be recited.

## \|\| 266.52-53 \|\|

*yajжāgrato dūramudeti tato virāḍajāyata iti ca \|*  
*sahasraśīrṣā puruṣa iti ca \|*  
*abhi tvā śūra nonuma iti ca \|*  
*puruṣa evedaṃ sarvamiti \|*  
*tripādūrdhvamiti \|*  
*yenedaṃ bhūtamiti \|*  
*natvā vāṁ anya iti \|\| 52 \|\|*

*sarvāṃścaitānpratiṣṭhāsu mantrāñjaptvā punaḥpunaḥ \|*  
*catuṣkṛtvaḥ spṛśedadbhirmūle madhye śirasyapi \|\| 53 \|\|*

52-53. “Yajagratodaraj muda,” ‘viradajayata, Sahasrashirha purusha, abhitviguranonuma purusaevedam, tripadurdhva,’ yenedamabhttama, &c., natva vamanya.” These mantras should be constantly repeated in the installation ceremonies, and then the middle, the base and the head of the idol should be touched four times with water. After the idol has been duly consecrated, the devotee should give with due respect dresses and ornaments to the officiating priest, Murtipa, Acharya.

## \|\| 266.54-55 \|\|

*sthāpite tu tato deve yajamāno'tha mūrtipam \|*  
*ācāryaṃ pūjayedbhaktyā vastrālaṃkārabhūṣaṇaiḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

*dīnāndhakṛpaṇāṃstadvadye cānye samupasthitāḥ \|*  
*tatastu madhunā devaṃ prathame'hani lepayet \|\| 55 \|\|*

54-55. Then the Wind, the poor, the miser, etc., assembled should be dismissed with clothings, ornaments, etc., At the time of adhivasa the installed Deva should be rubbed with honey, the first clay, with turmeric and mustard the second day, with sandal and barley on the third day.

## \|\| 266.56-58 \|\|

*haridra yā'tha siddhārthairdvitīye'hani tattvataḥ \|*  
*candanena yavaistadvattṛtīye'hani lepayet \|\| 56 \|\|*

*manaḥśilāpriyaṅgubhyāṃ caturthe'hani lepayet \|*  
*saubhāgyaśubhadaṃ yasmāllepanaṃ vyādhināśanam \|\| 57 \|\|*

*paraṃ prītikaraṃ nriṇāmetadvedavido viduḥ \|*  
*kṛṣṇāñjanaṃ tilaṃ tadvatpañcame'pi nivedayet \|\| 58 \|\|*

56-58. With red arsenic and Priyangu (a kind of creeper, long flapper) on the fourth day. By performing these ceremonies, one gets prosperity, happiness and health, and the diseases are all cured. The idols should be rubbed with krishnanjan and sesamum on the 5th day and with clarified butter, sandal, lotus-dust, saffron on the 6th day, and gorochana, agurnu flowers on the 7th day.

## \|\| 266.59-61 \|\|

*ṣaṣṭhe tu saghṛtaṃ dadyāccandanaṃ padmakesaram \|*  
*rocanāgarupuṣpaṃ tu saptame'hani dāpayet \|\| 59 \|\|*

*yatra sadyodhivāsaḥ syāttatra sarvaṃ nivedayet \|*  
*sthitaṃ na cālayeddevamanyathā doṣabhāgbhavet \|\| 60 \|\|*

*pūrayetsikatābhistu niśchidraṃ sarvato bhavet \|*  
*lokapālasya digbhāge yasya saṃcalate vibhuḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

59-61. These things should be used all at one time when the period of adhivasa is instantaneous. The image once installed and fixed should not be removed again from the spot; for it is a sin to do so. The holes should be filled in with sand, lime, etc., The Lokapala in whose direction the image leans should be appeased and the following offerings should be made, viz.:

## \|\| 266.62 \|\|

*tasya lokapateḥ śāntirdeyāścemāśca dakṣiṇāḥ \|*  
*indrā ya vāraṇaṃ dadyātkāñcanaṃ cālpavittavān \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. Ornaments should be offered to Indra; and gold to Agni; buffalo to Dharmaraja; goat and wealth to Nairita-Rakshasa;

## \|\| 266.63-64 \|\|

*agneḥ suvarṇameva syādyamasya mahiṣaṃ tathā \|*  
*ajaṃ ca kāñcanaṃ dadyānnairṛtaṃ rākṣasaṃ prati \|\| 63 \|\|*

*varuṇaṃ prati muktāni saśuktīni pradāpayet \|*  
*rītikaṃ vāyave dadyādvastrayugmena sāṃpratam \|\| 64 \|\|*

63-64. Pearls and mother of pearl to Varuna; brass and cloth to Vayu cow to Chandrama; bull and silver to Shiva.

## \|\| 266.65 \|\|

*somāya dhenurdātavyā rājataṃ vṛṣabhaṃ śive \|*  
*yasyāṃ yasyāṃ saṃcalanaṃ śāntiḥ syāttatra tatra tu \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. The Lokapalas towards whom the idol is drawn, should be appeased with Shanti. And if the prescribed worship be not performed under such circumstances there is always a fear of destruction of the family so the chinks round the idol should be well filled in with sand, in order to make it fixed and immovable.

## \|\| 266.66 \|\|

*anyathā tu bhavedghoraṃ bhayaṃ kulavināśanam \|*  
*acalaṃ kārayettasmātsikatābhiḥ sureśvaram \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. Festivities should be held for 3, 5, 7 or 10 days at the time of the consecration of the idol when grain, cloth, etc., should be freely distributed. The Kirtan (singing the name of Hari), reciting Ramayana, Katkakata and other meetings should be performed.

## \|\| 266.67 \|\|

*annaṃ vastraṃ ca dātavyaṃ puṇyāhajayamaṅgalam \|*  
*tripañca saptadaśa vā dināni syānmahotsavaḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. At the end of the. fourth day, one should perform the Chaturthi-karma after having his bath and gifts should be made accordingly.

## \|\| 266.68 \|\|

*caturthe'hni mahāsnānaṃ caturthīkarma kārayet \|*  
*dakṣiṇā ca punastadvaddeyā tatrātibhaktitaḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. I have explained to you the ceremonials of consecration that drive away all ills as described by the learned and performed by the Vidyadharas and Devas.

## Chapter 267

## \|\| 267.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*athātaḥ saṃpravakṣyāmi devasnapanamuttamam \|*  
*arghasyāpi samāsena śṛṇu tvaṃ vidhimuttamam \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Suta said: — “I shall now tell you briefly how an image is installed and the best way of offering Arghya.

## \|\| 267.2-4 \|\|

*dadhyakṣatakuśāgrāṇi kṣīraṃ dūrvāstathā madhu \|*  
*yavāḥ siddhārthakāstadvadaṣṭāṅgo'rghaḥ phalaiḥ saha \|\| 2 \|\|*

*gajāśvarathyāvalmīkavarāhotkhātamaṇḍalāt \|*  
*agnyagārāttathā tīrthādvrajādgomaṇḍalādapi \|\| 3 \|\|*

*kumbhe tu mṛttikāṃ dadyāduddhṛtā'sītimantravit \|*  
*śaṃ no devītyapāṃ mantramāpo hi ṣṭheti vai tathā \|\| 4 \|\|*

2-4. Arghya consists in the offering of eight things, viz., of curds, uncooked rice, Kusha, milk, Durv-grass, honey, barley and bustard (Siddharathak). Fruits should also be offered. The earth of the stable, elephant yard, chariot house, anthill, earth dug out by a wild boar, that of a sacrificial hollow, of the cowshed and of the beds of the sacred rivers like the Ganges, etc., should be placed in the jar (kumbha) by reciting the mantra “Udhritusi”, etc., and afterwards the jars should be filled with water by reciting the mantras “Sannodevi, etc.” and “apohishtha, etc.”

## \|\| 267.5-6 \|\|

*sāvitr! yā’dāya gomūtraṃ gandhadvāreti gomayam \|*  
*āpyāyasveti ca kṣīraṃ dadhikrāvṇeti vai dadhi \|\| 5 \|\|*

*tejo'sīti ghṛtaṃ tadvaddevasya tveti codakam \|*  
*kuśamiśraṃ kṣipedvidvānpañcagavyaṃ bhavettataḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. Cow’s urine should be placed after reciting the sacred Gayatri, cowdung by reciting “ Gandhadvara,” milk after reciting “ Apyayasva,” curds by reciting “ Dadhikravna,” clarified butter after reciting “Tejost, etc.,” water after reciting “ Tad Devasya-tva etc.” All these are mixed and then Km At is thrown therein. Thus Panchagavya is prepared. The idol should be bathed with this Panchagavya of the jar thus filled in.

## \|\| 267.7-10 \|\|

*snāpyātha pañcagavyena dadhnā śuddhena vai tataḥ \|*  
*dadhikāvṇetimantreṇa kartavyamabhimantraṇam \|\| 7 \|\|*

*āpyāyasveti payasā tejo'sīti ghṛtena ca \|*  
*madhuvāteti madhunā tataḥ puṣpodakena ca \|\| 8 \|\|*

*sarasvatyai bhaiṣajyena kāryaṃ tasyābhimantraṇam \|*  
*hiraṇyākṣeti mantreṇa snāpayedra tnavāriṇā \|\| 9 \|\|*

*kuśāmbhasā tataḥ snānaṃ devasya tveti kārayet \|*  
*phalodakena ca snānamagna āyāhi kārayet \|\| 10 \|\|*

7-10. Afterwards they should be bathed with curds, and then with water repeating the mantra “ Devasya tvam ” and then again with the Dadhi Kravn, etc., with the juice of fruits by reciting die mantra “Agnayahi,” and then water should be sprinkled with Kusha grass after reciting the mantra “ Devasyatva,” and then again with perfumed water after reciting the sacred Gayatri. Then the idol of Lord Shiva should be bathed with 1000, 500, 125, 64, 32, 16, 8 or only with 4 jars \[of water\].

Those jars should be made of gold, silver, copper, brass, bell-metal or of earth if one cannot afford the more expensive ones. Tire following medicinal herbs should be mixed with the water iu the jar, viz. — (1) Sahadevi, (2) Vacha, (3) Vyaghri, (4) Vala, (5) Ativala, (6) Samkhyapushpi, (7) Simhi (8) Suvarchala, These eight are necessary in the Mahasnana. The powder of barley, Nivara, sesamuin, Syamuka, Sali-rice, Priyangu, Vrihi, should be rubbed on the idol before bathing it.

## \|\| 267.17-20 \|\|

*svastikaṃ padmakaṃ śaṅkhamutpalaṃ kamalaṃ tathā \|*  
*śrīvatsaṃ darpaṇaṃ tadvannandyāvartamathāṣṭakam \|\| 17 \|\|*

*etāni gomayaiḥ kuryānmṛdā ca śubhayā tataḥ \|*  
*pañcavarṇādikaṃ tadvatpañcavarṇaṃ rajastathā \|\| 18 \|\|*

*pūrvāḥ kṛṣṇatilāndadyānnīrājanavidhirmataḥ \|*  
*evaṃ nīrājanaṃ kṛtvā dadyādācamanaṃ budhaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

*mandākinyāstu yadvāri sarvapāpāpahaṃ śubham \|*  
*tato vastrayugaṃ dadyānmantreṇānena yatnataḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

17-20. The following substances viz. — Svastika, Padmaka, Shankha, Shvetapadma, Kamala, Shrivatsa, Darpana, and Nandyavarta and cowdung, auspicious earth, five colours, etc., five coloured powders, Durva grass and black Sesamum should be used in Nirajana ceremony after which should be offered water for rinsing the mouth and then Ganges water should be offered. Then two pieces of dress should be put on after reciting the following mantra:

## \|\| 267.21 \|\|

*devasūtrasamāyukte yajñadānasamanvite \|*  
*sarvavarṇe śubhe deva vāsasī te vinirmite \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Note: .. = adoration of the idol by waving lights, perfumes, fans, &c.

“Be gracious enough to put on the clothes of variegated colours woven with Deva sutra and conjoint with sacrifice and gifts. These are very nice. Accept them.”

## \|\| 267.22-23 \|\|

*tatastu candanaṃ dadyātsamaṃ karpūrakuṅkumaiḥ \|*  
*imamuccārayenmantraṃ darbhapāṇiḥ prayatnataḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*śarīraṃ te na jānāmi ceṣṭāṃ naiva ca naiva ca \|*  
*mayā niveditāngandhānpratigṛhya vilipyatām \|\| 23 \|\|*

22-23. Afterwards taking kusha grass in the hand camphor should be offered mixed with saffron, when the following mantra should be recited, viz.: — “Deva! I do not know your body and form and your movements, be gracious enough to accept this incense offered by me.”

## \|\| 267.24-25 \|\|

*catvāriṃśattato dīpāndadyāccaiva pradakṣiṇān \|*  
*tvaṃ sūryacandra jyotīṃṣi vidyudagnistathaiva ca \|\| 24 \|\|*

*tvameva sarvajyotīṃṣi dīpo'yaṃ pratigṛhyatām \|*  
*tatastvanena mantreṇa dhūpaṃ dadyādvicakṣaṇaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

24-25. Then 40 lights should be lit up and offered after circumambulation, by reciting the following mantra: — “You are the light of the sun and the moon. You are the flash of lightning and fire. You are the light of all. Be gracious enough to accept the light offered by me.” Then incense should be offered by reciting the following mantra, viz.:

## \|\| 267.26 \|\|

*vanaspatiraso divyo gandhāḍhyo gandha uttamaḥ \|*  
*mayā nivedito bhaktyā dhūpo'yaṃ pratigṛhyatām \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. “Deva! Be pleased to accept this incense made of herbs and choice ions odour.”

## \|\| 267.27-28 \|\|

*tatastvābharaṇaṃ dadyānmahābhūṣāya te namaḥ \|*  
*anena vidhinā kṛtvā saptarātraṃ mahotsavam \|\| 27 \|\|*

*devakumbhaistataḥ kuryādyajamāno'bhiṣecanam \|*  
*caturbhiraṣṭabhirvā'pi dvābhyāmekena vā punaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

27-28. Then after reciting the mantra “Mahabhushaya te namah,” ornaments should be put on. Thus after keeping up rejoicings for seven nights, the devotee should get himself sprinkled with the remainder of the Abhiseka water.

## \|\| 267.29-32 \|\|

*sapañcaratnakalaśaiḥ sitavastrābhiveṣṭitaiḥ \|*  
*devasya tveti mantreṇa sāmnā cā’tharvaṇena ca \|\| 29 \|\|*

*abhiṣeke ca ye mantrā navagrahamakhe smṛtāḥ \|*  
*sitāmbaradharaḥ snātvā devānsaṃpūjya yatnataḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

*sthāpakaṃ pūjayedbhaktyā vastrālaṃkārabhūṣaṇaiḥ \|*  
*yajñabhāṇḍāni sarvāṇi maṇḍapopaskarādikam \|\| 31 \|\|*

*yaccānyadapi tadgehe tadācāryāya dāpayet \|*  
*suprasanne gurau yasmāttṛpyanti sarvadevatāḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

29-32. The sprinkling should be performed out of the water of 8, 4, 2, or 1 jar or from Pancharatna jar wrapped up in a white piece of cloth after reciting the mantra “Devasyatva”. The other mantras of the occasion have been mentioned in Atharvana mantra of Navagraha-sacrifice which might also be recited. Afterwards he should bathe, put on white clothes and worship the idols and give to the officiating priest gifts of money, ornaments, dresses with great devotion; and should send all the utensils employed in the sacrifice, mandapa, &c., to the house of the priest for the Devas are satisfied by the satisfaction of the Guru.

## \|\| 267.33 \|\|

*naitadviśīlena ca dāmbhikena na liṅginā sthāpanamatra kāryam \|*  
*vipreṇa kāryaṃ śrutipārageṇa gṛhasthadharmābhiratena nityam \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. The consecration of an idol should not be performed by men of angry disposition, hypocrites, Lingis who put on some peculiar garb, &c. It should always be performed by a virtuous householder who is well accomplished in the Vedas and is a Brahmana.

## \|\| 267.34-35 \|\|

*pāṣaṇḍinaṃ yastu karoti bhaktyā vihāya viprāñchrutidharmayuktān \|*  
*guruṃ pratiṣṭhādiṣu tatra nūnaṃ kulakṣayaḥ syādacirādapūjyaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

*sthānaṃ piśācaiḥ parigṛhyate vā apūjyatāṃ yātyacireṇa loke \|*  
*vipraiḥ kṛtaṃ yacchubhadaṃ kule syātprapūjyatāṃ yāti ciraṃ ca kālam \|\| 35 \|\|*

34-35. He who discarding a man versed in the Vedas gets a hypocrite to officiate at the consecration ceremony, surely brings ruination on his household or an evil spirit gets hold of the temple and no one worships the idol thus consecrated. But "where Brahmanas officiate there is always prosperity in that house and the idol thus consecrated is worshipped for a very ‘long time to come.

## Chapter 268

## \|\| 268.1 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*prāsādāḥ kīdṛśāḥ sūta kartavyā bhūtimicchatā \|*  
*pramāṇaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ tadvadvada vistarato'dhunā \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. The Rishis said: — Suta! of what dimensions and how should the temples be made by those eager for prosperity? Kindly describe in detail their measurements and characteristics.

## \|\| 268.2 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*athātaḥ saṃpravakṣyāmi prāsādavidhinirṇayam \|*  
*vāstau parīkṣite samyagvāstudehavicakṣaṇaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Suta replied: — The one well versed in the art- and the science of house-building should first examine and select a site.

## \|\| 268.3-11 \|\|

*vāstūpaśamanaṃ kuryātsamidbhirbalikarmaṇā \|*  
*jīrṇoddhāre tathodyāne tathā gṛhaniveśane \|\| 3 \|\|*

*navaprāsādabhavane prāsādaparivartane \|*  
*dvārābhivartane tadvatprāsādeṣu gṛheṣu ca \|\| 4 \|\|*

*vāstūpaśamanaṃ kuryātpūrvameva vicakṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*ekāśītipadaṃ likhya vāstumadhye ca pṛṣṭhataḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*homastrimekhale kāryaḥ kuṇḍe hastapramāṇake \|*  
*yavaiḥ kṛṣṇatilaistadvatsamidbhiḥ kṣīravṛkṣajaiḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*pālāśaiḥ khādiraiścāpi madhusarpiḥsamanvitaiḥ \|*  
*kuśadūrvāmayairvā'pi madhusarpiḥsamanvitaiḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*kāryastu pañcabhirbilvairbilvabījairathāpi vā \|*  
*homānte bhakṣyabhojyaistu vāstudeśe baliṃ haret \|\| 8 \|\|*

*tadvadviśeṣanaivedyamevaṃ dadyātkrameṇa tu \|*  
*īśakoṇe ghṛtāktaṃ tu śikhine vinivedayet \|\| 9 \|\|*

*odanaṃ saphalaṃ dadyātparjanyāya ghṛtānvitam \|*  
*jayāya ca dhvajānpītānpaiṣṭaṃ kūrmaṃ ca saṃnyaset \|\| 10 \|\|*

*indrā ya pañcaratnāni paiṣṭaṃ ca kuliśaṃ tathā \|*  
*vitānakaṃ ca sūryāya dhūmraṃ saktuṃ tathaiva ca \|\| 11 \|\|*

3-11. Afterwards propitiatory rites as prescribed should be performed to appease the Vastu. Deity and sacrificial oblations should be offered. Such rites and preliminary propitiation of the Vastu Deity should be performed at the time of repairing a temple, laying out a garden, or a door entering a new building, and erecting a new building. As stated before in previous chapters Vastu mandalam of 81 squares should be drawn in the middle of Vastu and then a sacrificial pit (kunda) measuring one hand and having three girdles should be made. Wood of milky trees should be employed as sacrificial fuel and Homa ceremony and libations of black sesamum and barley should be offered mixed with chips of Butea frondosa, catcheu, honey and wood-apple. At the end of the Homa ceremony, vails (offerings) are to be given with five vilva (Bael) twigs or the seeds thereof along with other eatables. Afterwards other sacrificial offerings should be made, viz. — clarified butter and grain should be offered to Agni in the N-E., boiled rice and fruits with clarified butter to Parjanya, yellow flag, ground corn and turtle to Jay a, Pancharatna (five jewel), ground corn and bolt to Indra; smoke colour awning and barley-meal to the Surya.

## \|\| 268.12-16 \|\|

*satyāya ghṛtagodhūmaṃ matsyaṃ dadyādbhṛśāya ca \|*  
*śaṣkulīścāntarikṣāya dadyātsaktūṃśca vāyave \|\| 12 \|\|*

*lājāḥ pūṣṇe tu dātavyā vitathe caṇakaudanam \|*  
*gṛhakṣatāya madhvannaṃ yamāya piśitaudanam \|\| 13 \|\|*

*gandhaudanaṃ ca gandharve bhṛṅgarājasya bhṛṅgikām \|*  
*mṛgāya yāvakaṃ dadyātpitṛbhyaḥ kṛsarā matā \|\| 14 \|\|*

*dauvārike dantakāṣṭhaṃ paiṣṭaṃ kṛṣṇabaliṃ tathā \|*  
*sugrīve'pūpakaṃ dadyātpuṣpadantāya pāyasam \|\| 15 \|\|*

*kuśastambena saṃyuktaṃ tathā padmaṃ ca vāruṇe \|*  
*piṣṭaṃ hiraṇmayaṃ dadyādasurāya surā matā \|\| 16 \|\|*

12-16. Clarified butter and wheat to Satya, fish to Bhrisha, fried cakes to Antariksha, barley meal to Vayu, fried rice to Pusha, gram to Vitatha, honey and grain to Grihakshata, powered meals to Yama, incense and food to the Gandharvas, green leaves to Bhringaraja, barley to Mriga, rice and pulse boiled together to the manes, Dantakashtha and powdered grain, and flowers to Sugriva, golden coloured cakes and wine to Asura.

## \|\| 268.17 \|\|

*ghṛtaudanaṃ ca śoṣāya yavānnaṃ pāpayakṣmaṇe \|*  
*ghṛtalaḍḍukāṃstu rogāya nāge puṣpaphalāni ca \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Payasa to Pushpadanta, lotus with Kushastamba to Varuna, rice and clarifield butter to Shosha, barley to Papa-yakshama, balls of clarified butter to Roga, fruits and flowers to Naga;

## \|\| 268.18 \|\|

*sarpirmukhyāya dātavyaṃ mudgaudanamataḥ param \|*  
*bhallāṭasthānake dadyātsomāya ghṛtapāyasam \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Clarified butter to Mukhya, clarified butter and milk to Sonia, cooked munga to Bhallata;

## \|\| 268.19 \|\|

*bhagāya śālikaṃ piṣṭamadityai polikāstathā \|*  
*dityai tu pūrikā dadyādityevaṃ bāhyato baliḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Powdered Shali rice to Bhaga, fried cakes stuffed with powdered grain to Aditi, fried cakes to Diti. All these offerings should be made outside the Mandal.

## \|\| 268.20 \|\|

*kṣīraṃ yamāya dātavyamāpavatsāya vai dadhi \|*  
*sāvitre laḍḍukāndadyātsamarīcaṃ kuśaudanam \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Milk should be offered to Yama, curds to Apavatsa, balls of sweet, chillies and Kusha to Savitra;

## \|\| 268.21 \|\|

*saviturguḍapūpāṃśca jayāya ghṛtacandanam \|*  
*vivasvate punardadyādra ktacandanapāyasam \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Fried cakes of flour and red sugar to Savita, clarified butter and sandal to Jaya, red sandal and rice cooked in milk and sugar to Vivasvan;

## \|\| 268.22 \|\|

*haritālaudanaṃ dadyādindrā ya ghṛtasaṃyutam \|*  
*ghṛtaudanaṃ ca mitrāya rudrā ya ghṛtapāyasam \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Yellow orpiment, rice, clarified butter to Indra; clarified butter and rice to Mitra; plain rice and rice cooked in milk and sugar to Rudra;

## \|\| 268.23 \|\|

*āmaṃ pakvaṃ tathā māṃsaṃ deyaṃ syādrā jayakṣmaṇe \|*  
*pṛthvīdharāya māṃsāni kūṣmāṇḍāni ca dāpayet \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Cooked and raw meat to Raja Yakshma, meat and pumpkin to Prithvidhara;

## \|\| 268.24-25 \|\|

*śarkarāpāyasaṃ dadyādaryamṇe punareva hi \|*  
*pañcagavyaṃ yavāṃścaiva tilākṣatamayaṃ carum \|\| 24 \|\|*

*makṣyaṃ bhojyaṃ ca vividhaṃ brahmaṇe vinivedayet \|*  
*evaṃ saṃpūjitā devāḥ śāntiṃ kurvanti te sadā \|\| 25 \|\|*

24-25. Clarified butter and sugar to Aryama, Panchagavya, sesamum, rice, and othej victuals to Brahma. The Devas residing in Vastu thus worshipped give peace and prosperity.

## \|\| 268.26 \|\|

*sarvebhyaḥ kāñcanaṃ dadyādbrāhmaṇe gāṃ payasvinīm \|*  
*rākṣasīnāṃ balirdeyaḥ api yādṛgyathā śṛṇu \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Gold is to be given to all and a milk cow and gold should be given to Brahma in the name of all these Deities, blow hear about the offerings that ought to be made to the Rakshasis, viz.

## \|\| 268.27-28 \|\|

*māṃsaudanaṃ ghṛtaṃ padmakesaraṃ rudhirānvitam \|*  
*īśānabhāgamāśritya carakyai vinivedayet \|\| 27 \|\|*

*māṃsaudanaṃ ca rudhiraṃ haridrau danameva ca \|*  
*āgneyīṃ diśamāśritya vidāryai vinivedayet \|\| 28 \|\|*

27-28. Flesh, rice, clarified butter, lotus, blood, and these should be offered to Chavaki in the N.-E., flesh, rice, blood, turmeric and cooked grain should be given to Vidari in the S.-E.;

## \|\| 268.29-31 \|\|

*dadhyodanaṃ sarudhiramasthikhaṇḍaiśca saṃyutam \|*  
*pītaraktaṃ baliṃ dadyātpūtanāyai sarakṣase \|\| 29 \|\|*

*vāyavyāṃ pāparākṣasyai matsyamāṃsaṃ surāsavam \|*  
*pāyasaṃ cāpi dātavyaṃ svanāmnā sarvataḥ kramāt \|\| 30 \|\|*

*namaskārāntayuktena praṇavādyena saṃyutaḥ \|*  
*tataḥ sarvauṣadhīsnānaṃ yajamānasya kārayet \|\| 31 \|\|*

29-31. Curds, rice, blood, chips of bones should be given to Putana along with her Rakshasa; fish, wine, rice cooked in milk and sugar to Papa in the N.-W. and all round. At every sacrificial offering one should mention his name and use the sacred expression Om, Afterwards the devotee should bathe in the water mixed with herbs.

## \|\| 268.32 \|\|

*dvijānsupūjayedbhaktyā ye cānye gṛhamāgatāḥ \|*  
*etadvāstūpaśamanaṃ kṛtvā karma samārabhet \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. The Brahmanas who come to the house should he well honoured and in such a way Vastu should be worshipped.

## \|\| 268.33-34 \|\|

*prāsādabhavanodyānaprārambhe vinivartane \|*  
*puraveśmapraveśeṣu sarvadoṣāpanuttaye \|\| 33 \|\|*

*rakṣoghnapāvamānena sūktena bhavanādikam \|*  
*nṛtyamaṅgalavādyena kuryādbrāhmaṇavācanam \|\| 34 \|\|*

33-34. At the time of starting the building of palaces, temples, gardens and entering newly laid cities and houses, festivities should be held, dancing should be given, music should be played and Rakshoghana and Pavamana Suktas should be recited by the Brahmanas.

## \|\| 268.35-36 \|\|

*anena vidhinā yastu pratisaṃvatsaraṃ budhaḥ \|*  
*gṛhe vā’yatane kuryānna sa duḥkhamavāpnuyāt \|\| 35 \|\|*

*na ca vyādhibhayaṃ tasya na ca bandhudhanakṣayaḥ \|*  
*jīvedvarṣaśataṃ svarge kalpamekaṃ ca tiṣṭhati \|\| 36 \|\|*

35-36. One who observes these ceremonies in his house and temples every year never gets any calamity, nor does he get any serious illness and his brethren and riches do not perish. he lives for a hundred years and remains in heaven for a kalpa after death.

## Chapter 269

## \|\| 269.1-2 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*evaṃ vāstubaliṃ kṛtvā bhajetṣoḍaśabhāgikam \|*  
*tasya madhye caturbhistu bhāgairgarbhaṃ tu kārayet \|\| 1 \|\|*

*bhāgadvādaśakaṃ sārdhaṃ tatastu parikalpayet \|*  
*caturdikṣu tathā jñeyaṃ nirgamaṃ tu tato budhaiḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

1-2. Suta said: — After thus making sacrificial offerings to "Vastu the of the temple should be divided into 16 parts. In the centre, the Garbha consisting of 4 parts should be thought of and this again is to be divided into 12 parts and a half. A wise man should then plan the doorways on the four sides of the temple.

## \|\| 269.3-7 \|\|

*caturbhāgena bhittīnāmucchrāyaḥ syātpramāṇataḥ \|*  
*dviguṇaḥ śikharocchrāyo bhittyucchrāyapramāṇataḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*śikharārdhasya cārdhena vidheyā tu pradakṣiṇā \|*  
*garbhasūtradvayaṃ cāgre vistāro maṇḍapasya tu \|\| 4 \|\|*

*āyataḥ syāttribhirbhāgairbhadra yuktaḥ suśobhanaḥ \|*  
*pañcabhāgena saṃbhajya garbhamānaṃ vicakṣaṇaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*bhāgamekaṃ gṛhītvā tu prāggrīvaṃ kalpayedbudhaḥ \|*  
*garbhasūtrasamo bhāgādagrato mukhamaṇḍapaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*etatsāmānyamuddiṣṭaṃ prāsādasyeha lakṣaṇam \|*  
*tathā'nyaṃ tu pravakṣyāmi prāsādaṃ liṅgamānataḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

3-7. The depth of the foundations should be one-fourth of the room and the dome (or top) should be double the height of that of the foundations, — The height of the passage for circumambulation should be a quarter of that of the dome and in front of the two Garbha Sutras, the Mandapa should be deter- mined; and in one third part of the Mandapa, Bhadrasan (one’s house) is to be built. After dividing the Garbha Mana into five parts, one part is to be taken and in that the eastern doorway (Prakgriva) is to be de- signed; then the front Mandapa of the Garbha Sutra is to be located. These are the ordinary characteristics of the temple. Now other characteristics are being mentioned with reference to the measurement of the Lingam.

## \|\| 269.8-14 \|\|

*liṅgapūjāpramāṇena kartavyā pīṭhikā budhaiḥ \|*  
*piṇḍikārdhena bhāgaḥ syāttanmānena tu bhittayaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*bāhyabhittipramāṇena utsedhastu bhavetpunaḥ \|*  
*bhittyucchrāyāttu dviguṇaḥ śikharasya samucchrayaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*śikharasya caturbhāgātkartavyā ca pradakṣiṇā \|*  
*pradakṣiṇāyāstu samastvagrato maṇḍapo bhavet \|\| 10 \|\|*

*tasya cārdhena kartavyastvagrato mukhamaṇḍapaḥ \|*  
*prāsādānnirgatau kāryau kapolau garbhamānataḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*ūrdhvaṃ bhittyucchrayāttasya mañjarīṃ tu prakalpayet \|*  
*mañjaryāścārdhabhāgena śukanāsāṃ prakalpayet \|\| 12 \|\|*

*ūrdhvaṃ tathā'rdhabhāgena vedībandho bhavediha \|*  
*vedyāścopari yaccheṣaṃ kaṇṭhaścāmalasārakaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*evaṃ vibhajya prāsādaṃ śobhanaṃ kārayedbudhaḥ \|*  
*athānyacca pravakṣyāmi prāsādasyeha lakṣaṇam \|\| 14 \|\|*

8-14. The pedestal should be symmetrical to the size of the Phallus... In half of the pedestal, the foundation is to be laid; the height should be in accordance with the height of the outer foundations. The height of the temple top should be twice that of the foundations and the (height of the) circumambulating passage a quarter of that of the top, the front Mandapa, should be as high as the passage for circumambulation; and the entrance to the Mandapa may be half of its height. The corners of the door-way should be made projecting outside the temple and on the wall above it should be made the manjari (the top-most part) and in half of it should be made the Shukanasa (looking like the aquiline nose) and above it should be made a quadrangular spot in the dome and above it the top of the dome.

## \|\| 269.15-18 \|\|

*garbhamānapramāṇena prāsādaṃ śṛṇuta dvijāḥ \|*  
*vibhajya navadhā garbhaṃ madhye syālliṅgapīṭhikā \|\| 15 \|\|*

*pādāṣṭakaṃ tu ruciraṃ pārśvataḥ parikalpayet \|*  
*mānena tena vistāro bhittīnāṃ tu vidhīyate \|\| 16 \|\|*

*pādaṃ pañcaguṇaṃ kṛtvā bhittīnāmucchrayo bhavet \|*  
*sa eva śikharasyāpi dviguṇaḥ syātsamucchrayaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*caturdhā śikharaṃ bhajya ardhabhāgadvayasya tu \|*  
*śukanāsaṃ prakurvīta tṛtīye vedikā matā \|\| 18 \|\|*

15-18. Now another set of measurements with reference to Garbhamana. The Vastu Garbha should be divided into 9 parts and the phallus should be located in the centre; the side of the pedestal is to comprise eight padas and should be artistically finished. The width of the wall should be of eight padas and the height five times that. The top should be twice the height of the walls, which should be divided in two parts and Shukanasa should be made in one of them and a quadrangular spot (Vedika) in the third part of it.

## \|\| 269.19-20 \|\|

*kaṇṭhamāmalasāraṃ tu caturthe parikalpayet \|*  
*kapolayostu saṃhāro dviguṇo'tra vidhīyate \|\| 19 \|\|*

*śobhanaiḥ patravallībhiraṇḍakaiśca vibhūṣitaḥ \|*  
*prāsādo'yaṃ tṛtīyastu mayā tubhyaṃ niveditaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

19-20. The Amalashara Kantha (top-most part) should be made in the 4th part and the projecting parts (Kapala) should be made twice the length it should be decorated with floral designs. Such is the plan of the 3rd kind of temple. The other characteristics of the temple are now being mentioned.

## \|\| 269.21-27 \|\|

*sāmānyamaparaṃ tadvatprāsādaṃ śṛṇuta dvijāḥ \|*  
*tribhedaṃ kārayetkṣetraṃ yatra tiṣṭhanti devatāḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*rathāṅkastena mānena bāhyabhāgavinirgataḥ \|*  
*nemī pādena vistīrṇā prāsādasya samantataḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*garbhaṃ tu dviguṇaṃ kuryāttasya mānaṃ bhavediha \|*  
*sa eva bhitterutsedhā dviguṇaḥ śikharo mataḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

*prāggrīvaḥ pañcabhāgena niṣkāsastasya cocyate \|*  
*kārayetsuṣiraṃ tadvatprākārasya tribhāgataḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*prāggrīvaṃ pañcabhāgena niṣkāṣeṇa viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*kuryādvā pañcabhāgena prāggrīvaṃ karṇamūlataḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*sthāpayetkanakaṃ tatra garbhānte dvāramūlataḥ \|*  
*evaṃ tu trividhaṃ kuryājжyeṣṭhamadhyakanīyasam \|\| 26 \|\|*

*liṅgamānānubhedena rūpabhedena vā punaḥ \|*  
*ete samāsataḥ proktā nāmataḥ śṛṇutādhunā \|\| 27 \|\|*

21-27. Suta said: — Twice born! Now hear about the dimensions of the other kind of temples. Divide the place where the image is to be located into 3 parts; and in the outer portion of the above dimensions the Rathanga is to be designed; and the Nemi is to be one-fourth wide and the temple (or buildings) to be built all around. The Garbha is to be made twice the size of the Nemi. The walls are to be of the dimensions of Garbha manas. And the top should be twice the height of the walls and in the 5th part of the temple a door-way should be made. Now about the outlet. In the 3rd part of the round walls the Sushira (hole) is to be made. In some particular cases in the fifth part Prakgriva is to be located. In the fifth part at the Karnamula the two Prakgrivas are to be located. And golden pieces should be put at the base of the door. The temples are of three sorts, Jyeshtha, Madhya (middling) and Kanishtha (small) according to the differences between the sizes of the temples and Lingams. Now hear the names of the different kinds of temples.

## \|\| 269.28-30 \|\|

*merumandarakailāsakumbhasiṃhamṛgāstathā \|*  
*vimānacchandakastadvaccaturasrastathaiva ca \|\| 28 \|\|*

*aṣṭāsraḥ ṣoḍaśāsraśca vartulaḥ sarvabhadra kaḥ \|*  
*siṃhāsyo nandanaścaiva nandivardhanakastathā \|\| 29 \|\|*

*haṃso vṛṣaḥ suvarṇeśaḥ padmako'tha samudra kaḥ \|*  
*prāsādā nāmataḥ proktā vibhāgaṃ śṛṇuta dvijāḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

28-30. They are: — The Meru, Mandara, Kailasa, Kumbha, Simha, Mriga, Vimana, Chhandaka, Chaturasra, Ashtasra, Sodashasra, Vartula, Sarvabhadraka, Simhasya, Nandana, Nandivardhanaka, Hamsa, Vrisha, Suvarnesha, B Padmaka and Samudgaka. Now hear about their descriptions:

## \|\| 269.31 \|\|

*śataśṛṅgaścaturdvāro bhūmikāṣoḍaśocchritaḥ \|*  
*nānāvicitraśikharo meruḥ prāsāda ucyate \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. A temple with hundreds of tops, having four doors, 16 flats, lofty, imposing and beautiful looking is called Meru.

## \|\| 269.32-35 \|\|

*mandaro dvādaśa proktaḥ kailāso navabhūmikaḥ \|*  
*vimānacchandakastadvadanekaśikharānanaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

*sa cāṣṭabhūmikastadvatsaptabhirnandivardhanaḥ \|*  
*viṣāṇakasamāyukto nandanaḥ sa udāhṛtaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

*ṣoḍaśāsrasamāyukto nānārūpasamanvitaḥ \|*  
*anekaśikharastadvatsarvatobhadra ucyate \|\| 34 \|\|*

*citraśālāsamopeto vijñeyaḥ pañcabhūmikaḥ \|*  
*valabhīcchandakastadvadanekaśikharānanaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

32-35. A temple with 12 flats (Bhumikas) is Mandara; with O flats is Kailasa; one with several tops and doors is called Vimana and Chhandaka. One that has 8 flats, or 7 flats is Nandivardhana; one with several tops is Nandana, one with 16 petals (or corners) and various tops and 5 flats and with Chitrashala, is Sarvatobhadra. One with many faces is Balabhichhandaka; one like a bull and void of petals is Mandate.

## \|\| 269.36-39 \|\|

*vṛṣasyocchrāyatastulyo maṇḍalaścāsravarjitaḥ \|*  
*siṃhaḥ siṃhākṛtirjñeyo gajo gajasamastathā \|\| 36 \|\|*

*kumbhaḥ kumbhākṛtistadvadbhūmikānavakocchrayaḥ \|*  
*aṅgulīpuṭasaṃsthānaḥ pañcāṇḍakavibhūṣitaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

*ṣoḍaśāsraḥ samantācca vijñeyaḥ sa samudgakaḥ \|*  
*pārśvayoścandra śāle'sya ucchrāyo bhūmikādvayam \|\| 38 \|\|*

*tathaiva padmakaḥ prokta ucchrāyo bhūmikātrayam \|*  
*ṣoḍaśāsraḥ sa vijñeyo vicitraśikharaḥ śubhaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

36-39. One with the appearance of Simha and having figures of lions is the Simha. One with the appearance of an elephant is called Gaja. One with 9 flats and of the appearance of a pitcher is known as the Kumbhaka. One with 16 petals all round ornamented with Panchandaka is called Samudgaka, and it has two Chandrashalas measuring two flats on either side and two flats; such is also Padmaka. One with 16 petals and nice tops is called Sodashasra. Its height is three flats.

## \|\| 269.40-43 \|\|

*mṛgarājastu vikhyātaścandra śālo vibhūṣitaḥ \|*  
*prāggrīveṇa viśālena bhūmikāsu ṣaḍunnataḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

*anekaścandra śālaśca gajaḥ prāsāda iṣyate \|*  
*paryastagṛharājo vai garuḍo nāma nāmataḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

*saptabhūmyucchrayastadvaccandra śālātrayānvitaḥ \|*  
*bhūmikāṣaḍaśītistu bāhyataḥ sarvato bhavet \|\| 42 \|\|*

*tathā'nyo garuḍastadvaducchrayāddaśabhūmikaḥ \|*  
*padmakaḥ ṣoḍaśāsrastu bhūmidvayamathādhikaḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

40-43. One adorned with Chandrashala and big Praggriva is called Mrigaraja; one with many Chandrashalas is Gaja. The Garuda class is superior to Griharaja; its height is seven flats, and it has three Chandrashalas; outside this there are 8-6 flats.

## \|\| 269.44-45 \|\|

*padmatulyapramāṇena śrīvṛkṣaka iti smṛtaḥ \|*  
*pañcāṇḍako dvibhūmiśca garbhe hastacatuṣṭayam \|\| 44 \|\|*

*vṛṣo bhavati nāmnā'yaṃ prāsādaḥ sārvakāmikaḥ \|*  
*saptakāḥ pañcakāścaiva prāsādā vai mayoditāḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

44-45. O Another class of Garuda Prasada is 10 flats high, sixteen petalled, and has two flats in addition to those mentioned before. Grikrikshaka Prasada is like Padma. Panchandaka has two flats and 40 hands square. Ashtasra and Chaturasra are octagonal and quarto in shape respectively.

The one resembling a crane in appearance is called Hamsa. Vrisha has one flat, one top of 10 hands an ground from all sides. It yields all desires.

## \|\| 269.46 \|\|

*siṃhāsyena samā jñeyā ye cānye tatpramāṇakāḥ \|*  
*candra śālaiḥ samopetāḥ sarve prāggrīvasaṃyutāḥ \|*  
*aiṣṭakā dāravāścaiva śailā vā syuḥ satoraṇāḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. The other ones like those mentioned above are like Simhasya having Chandrashalas. All these are made of bricks, wood or stone, and flags and buntings should be put on to them.

## \|\| 269.47 \|\|

*meruḥ pañcāśaddhastaḥ syānmandaraḥ pañcahīnakaḥ \|*  
*catvāriṃśattu kailāsaścatustriṃśadvimānakaḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Meru is 50 hands in extent. Mandara is 45 hands in measurement.

## \|\| 269.48 \|\|

*nandivardhanakastadvaddvātriṃśatsamudāhṛtaḥ \|*  
*triṃśatā nandanaḥ proktaḥ sarvatobhadra kastathā \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Kailasa is 44 hands, Vimanaka is 34 hands, Nandivardhana is 32 hands, Nandana is of 30 hands, and Sarvatobhadra is of 20 hands circular and having Padmakas.

## \|\| 269.49-51 \|\|

*vartulaḥ padmakaścaiva viṃśaddhasta udāhṛtaḥ \|*  
*gajaḥ siṃhaśca kumbhaśca valabhīcchandakastathā \|\| 49 \|\|*

*ete ṣoḍaśahastāḥ syuścatvāro devavallabhāḥ \|*  
*kailāso mṛgarājaśca vimānacchandako mataḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

*ete dvādaśahastāḥ syureteṣāmiha manmatam \|*  
*garuḍo'ṣṭakaro jñeyo haṃso daśa udāhṛtaḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

49-51. Gaja, Simha, Kumbha and Valabhhichhandaka are of 16 hands, and dear to the Devas; Kailasa, Mrigaraja, Vimanachandaka are 12 hands, Garuda is 8 hands, Hamsa of 10 hands.

## \|\| 269.52 \|\|

*evametaṃ pramāṇena kartavyāḥ śubhalakṣaṇāḥ \|*  
*yakṣarākṣasanāgānāṃ mātṛhastātpraśasyate \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. All these temples if of these dimensions are lucky. The hands of the Yakshas, Rakshasas, and serpents, are said to be good and called Matrika hands.

## \|\| 269.53 \|\|

*tathā mervādayaḥ sapta jyeṣṭhaliṅge śubhāvahāḥ \|*  
*śrīvṛkṣakādayaścāṣṭau madhyamasya prakīrtitāḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. It brings good luck to locate a big phallus Jyestha Linga in each of the 7 temples such as the Meru, &c. Medium sized phallus should be located in the 8 temples such, as Shri-Vrikshaka, &c., and small size phallus should be put in the 5 temples such as Hamsa, &c.

## \|\| 269.54 \|\|

*tathā haṃsādayaḥ pañca kanyase śubhadā matāḥ \|*  
*valabhīcchandake gaurī jaṭāmukuṭadhāriṇī \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. In the Valabhichhandaka temple the goddess with plaited hair and a coronet should be located. She grants boons, fearlessness; she holds a rosary and a Kamandalu: she is fair and giver of auspicious things.

## \|\| 269.55 \|\|

*varadā'bhayadā tadvatsākṣasūtrakamaṇḍaluḥ \|*  
*gṛhe tu raktamukuṭā utpalāṅkuśadhāriṇī \|*  
*varadā'bhayadā cāpi pūjaṃnīyā sabhartṛkā \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. The Goddess holding a goblet, adorned with a red coronet, lotus and goad along with Lord diva should always be worshipped in the Prasada named Griha.

## \|\| 269.56 \|\|

*tapovanasthāmitarāṃ tāṃ tu saṃpūjayedbudhaḥ \|*  
*devyā vināyakastadvadvalabhīcchandake śubhaḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. The other kinds of the images of Goddess should be placed in a forest and worshipped there. Ganesha the son of Gami should be located in Valabhichhandaka temple and is auspicious.

## Chapter 270

## \|\| 270.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*athātaḥ saṃpravakṣyāmi maṇḍapānāṃ tu lakṣaṇam \|*  
*maṇḍapapravarānvakṣye prāsādasyānurūpataḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Suta said “I shall now relate' to you the characteristics of the various Mandapas (halls attached to the temple) in accordance with the dimensions of the temples.

## \|\| 270.2 \|\|

*vividhā maṇḍapāḥ kāryā jyeṣṭhamadhyakanīyasaḥ \|*  
*nāmatastānpravakṣyāmi śṛṇudhvamṛṣisattamāḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. The Mandapas are of three kinds; viz. uttama, madhyama and kanishtha.

## \|\| 270.3-6 \|\|

*puṣpakaḥ puṣpabhadra śca suvrato'mṛtanandanaḥ \|*  
*kauśalyo buddhisaṃkīrṇo gajabhadro jayāvahaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*śrīvatso vijayaścaiva vāstukīrtiḥ śrutiṃjayaḥ \|*  
*yajñabhadro viśālaśca suśliṣṭaḥ śatrumardanaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*bhāgapañco nandanaśca mānavo mānabhadra kaḥ \|*  
*sugrīvo haritaścaiva karṇikāraḥ śatardhikaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*siṃhaśca śyāmabhadra śca subhadra śca tathaiva ca \|*  
*saptaviṃśatirākhyātā lakṣaṇaṃ śṛṇuta dvijāḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

3-6. Their names are: — (1) Pushpaka, (2) Pushpabhadra, (3) Suvrata, (4) Amritanandana, (5) Kaushalya, (6) Budhisankirna, (7) Gajabhadra, (8j Jayavaha, (9) Shrivatsa, (10) Vijaya, (11) Vastu-kirti, (12) Shrutimjaya, (13) Yajnabhadra, (14) Vishala, (15) Sushlishta, (10) Shatrumardana, (17) Bhagapancha, (18) Nandana, (19) Manava, (20) Manabhadraka, (21) Sugriva, (22) Harita, (23) Karnikara, (24) Shatardhika, (25) Simha, (26) Shyama, and (27) Subhadra. Thus twenty-seven classes of Mandapas are named.

## \|\| 270.7-14 \|\|

*stambhā yatra catuḥṣaṣṭiḥ puṣpakaḥ samudāhṛtaḥ \|*  
*dviṣaṣṭiḥ puṣpabhadra stu ṣaṣṭiḥ suvrata ucyate \|\| 7 \|\|*

*aṣṭapañcāśakastambhaḥ kathyate'mṛtanandanaḥ \|*  
*kauśalyaḥ ṣaṭ ca pañcāśaccatuṣpañcāśatā punaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*nāmnā tu buddhisaṃkīrṇo dvihīno gajabhadra kaḥ \|*  
*jayāvahastu pañcāśacchrīvatsastadvihīnakaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*vijayastadvihīnaḥ syādvāstukīrtistathaiva ca \|*  
*dvābhyāmeva prahīyeta tataḥ śrutiṃjayo'paraḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*catvāriṃśadyajñabhadra stadvihīno viśālakaḥ \|*  
*ṣaṭtriṃśaccaiva suśliṣṭo dvihīnaḥ śatrumardanaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*dvātriṃśadbhāgapañcastu triṃśadbhirnandanaḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*aṣṭāviṃśanmānavastu mānabhadro dvihīnakaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*caturviṃśastu sugrīvo dvāviṃśo harito mataḥ \|*  
*viṃśatiḥ karṇikāraḥ syādaṣṭādaśa śatardhikaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*siṃho bhavedvihīnaśca śyāmabhadro dvihīnakaḥ \|*  
*subhadra stu tathā prokto dvādaśastambhasaṃyutaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

7-14. Now hear their characteristics. A Mandapa with 64 pillars is Pushpaka, one with 62 pillars is Pushpabhadra, one with 60 pillars is Suvrata, one with 58 pillars is Amritamanthana, one with 56 pillars is Kaushalya, one with 54 pillars is Budhisamkirna, one with 52 pillars is Gajabhadra, one with 50 pillars is Jayavaha, one with 48 pillars is Shrivatsa, one with 46 pillars is Vijaya, one with 44 pillars is Vastukirti, one with 42 pillars is Shrutinjaya, one with 40 pillars is Yajnabhadra, one with 38 pillars is Vishalaka, one with 36 pillars is Sushlishta, one with 34 pillars is Shatrumandana, one with 32 pillars is Bhagapancha, one with 30 pillars is Nandana, one with 28 pillars is Manava, one with 26 pillars is Manabhadra, one with 24 pillars is Sugriva, one with 22 pillars is Harita, one with 20 pillars is Karnikara, one with 18 pillars is Shatardhika, one with 16 pillars is Simha, one with 14 pillars is Shyamabhadra, one with 12 pillars is Subhadra.

## \|\| 270.15-17 \|\|

*maṇḍapāḥ kathitāstubhyaṃ yathāvallakṣaṇānvitāḥ \|*  
*trikoṇaṃ vṛtamarddhandumaṣṭakoṇaṃ dviraṣṭakam \|\| 15 \|\|*

*catuṣkoṇaṃ tu kartavyaṃ saṃsthānaṃ maṇḍapasya tu \|*  
*rājyaṃ ca vijayaścaiva āyurvardhanameva ca \|\| 16 \|\|*

*putralābhaḥ śriyaḥ puṣṭistrikoṇādikramādbhavet \|*  
*evaṃ tu śubhadāḥ proktāścānyathā tvaśubhāvahāḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

15-17. Now the plan of the Mandapas:—They should be made triangular, circular, octagonal or with 16 sides or they are square. They promote kingdoms, victory, longevity, sons, wife and nourishment respectively. Temples of other shape than these are inauspicious.

## \|\| 270.18-21 \|\|

*catuḥṣaṣṭipadaṃ kṛtvā madhye dvāraṃ prakalpayet \|*  
*vistārāddviguṇocchrāyaṃ tattribhāgaḥ kaṭirbhavet \|\| 18 \|\|*

*vistārārdho bhavedgarbho bhittayo'nyāḥ samantataḥ \|*  
*garbhapādena vistīrṇaṃ dvāraṃ triguṇamāyatam \|\| 19 \|\|*

*tathā dviguṇavistīrṇamukhastadvadudumbaraḥ \|*  
*vistārapādapratimaṃ bāhulyaṃ śākhayoḥ smṛtam \|\| 20 \|\|*

*tripañcasaptanavabhiḥ śākhābhirdvāramiṣyate \|*  
*kaniṣṭhamadhyamaṃ jyeṣṭhaṃ yathāyogaṃ prakalpayet \|\| 21 \|\|*

18-21. In the centre of the hall should be made the doorway measured

by sixty-four Padas (feet). The height of the temple should be twice

its breadth, the plinth should be one-third the breadth and the Garbha

(inside) should be half the breadth, and walls should be made all round,

Taking one-fourth of the Garbha as the unit, three times of this will be the

Ayata (breadth), twice will be the width of the entrance and it will pe built

of Udumbara wood, The two Shakhas should be a quarter of the width of

the door. There should be 3, 5, 7 or nine Shakhas which will make up the

door. The doors are divided into three classes, Kanishtha, Madhyama, and Jyestha.

## \|\| 270.22-25 \|\|

*aṅgulānāṃ śataṃ sārdhaṃ catvāriṃśattathonnatam \|*  
*triṃśadviṃśottaraṃ cānyaddhanyamuttamameva ca \|\| 22 \|\|*

*śataṃ cāśītisahitaṃ vātanirgamane bhavet \|*  
*adhikaṃ daśabhistadvattathā ṣoḍaśabhiḥ śatam \|\| 23 \|\|*

*śatamānaṃ tṛtīyaṃ ca navatyā'śītibhistathā \|*  
*daśa dvārāṇi caitāni krameṇoktāni sarvadā \|\| 24 \|\|*

*anyāni varjanīyāni mānasodvegadāni tu \|*  
*dvāravedhaṃ prayatnena sarvavāstuṣu varjayet \|\| 25 \|\|*

22-25. The principal doorway is to be 140½ Angulas high; other medium and good doors are 120 and 130 fingers high. A door 180 fingers in height is the best for ventilation. 110, 116, 100, 90, and 80 fingers are the other prescribed heights of doors. Doors of other heights than these are not good. There should be no obstruction in front of the doorway. It is to be carefully avoided in every case.

## \|\| 270.26 \|\|

*vṛkṣakoṇabhramidvārastambhakūpadhvajādibhiḥ \|*  
*kuḍyaśvabhreṇa vā viddhaṃ dvāraṃ na śubhadaṃ bhavet \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. The obstruction caused by a tree, a corner, a curve, a pillar, a banner, a well, a wall and a svabhra are not good.

## \|\| 270.27-28 \|\|

*kṣayaśca durgatiścaiva pravāsaḥ kṣudbhayaṃ tathā \|*  
*daurbhāgyaṃ bandhanaṃ rogo dāridra yaṃ! kalahaṃ tathā \|\| 27 \|\|*

*virodhaścārthanāśaśca sarvaṃ vedhādbhavetkramāt \|*  
*pūrveṇa phalino vṛkṣāḥ kṣīravṛkṣāstu dakṣiṇe \|\| 28 \|\|*

27-28. Destruction, misery, banishment, starvation, ill-luck, imprisonment, disease, poverty, quarrel, disunion and loss of wealth are caused by the obstruction of a doorway. Fruit trees to the east and milky trees to the south of it- are the best.

## \|\| 270.29 \|\|

*paścimena jalaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ padmotpalavibhūṣitam \|*  
*uttare saralaistālaiḥ śubhā syātpuṣpavāṭikā \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. To the west should be made a charming pool of water full of lotus flowers, to the north should be planted palm trees and flowers.

## \|\| 270.30 \|\|

*sarvatastu jalaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ sthiramasthirameva ca \|*  
*pārśvataścāpi kartavyaṃ parivārādikālayam \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Round the Vastu there should be flowing waters as well, as still waters; this is a good thing; and close to the main temple should he made the pagodas of other Deities.

## \|\| 270.31-33 \|\|

*yāmye tapovanasthānamuttare mātṛkāgṛham \|*  
*mahānasaṃ tathā’gneye nairṛtye'tha vināyakam \|\| 31 \|\|*

*vāruṇe śrīnivāsastu vāyavye gṛhamālikā \|*  
*uttare yajñaśālā tu nirmālyasthānamuttare \|\| 32 \|\|*

*vāruṇe somadaivatye balinirvapaṇaṃ smṛtam \|*  
*purato vṛṣabhasthānaṃ śeṣe syātkusumāyudhaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

31-33. To the south should be made the tapovana, to the north the house for Matrikas, to the S.-E. should be the kitchen, to the S.-W. the temple of Ganesha, to the west the resting place of Lakshmi, to the N. W. the platform of all the asterisms, to the north the sacrificial place as well as the place for Nirmalya; to the west the place for offerings Soma and other Devas, in front the place of Shiva should be the place of Nandi, and lastly the place of Cupid.

## \|\| 270.34 \|\|

*jalavāpī tathaiśāne viṣṇustu jalaśāyyapi \|*  
*evamāyatanaṃ kuryātkuṇḍamaṇḍapasaṃyutam \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. And to the X.-E. should be the store of water and the resting place of Lord Vishnu in water.

## \|\| 270.35-36 \|\|

*ghaṇṭāvitānakasatoraṇacitrayuktaṃ nityotsavapramuditena janena sārdham \|*  
*yaḥ kārayetsuragṛhaṃ vividhadhvajāṅkaṃ śrīstaṃ na muñcati sadā divi pūjyate ca \|\| 35 \|\|*

*evaṃ gṛhārcanavidhāvapi śaktitaḥ syātsaṃsthāpanaṃ sakalamantravidhānayuktam \|*  
*govastrakāñcanahiraṇyadharāpradānaṃ deyaṃ gurudvijavareṣu tathā'nnadānam \|\| 36 \|\|*

35-36. The temple should be thus decorated with Kundas, Mandapas, flags, bells and buntings. One who thus makes a temple and carries on rejoicings there, gets everlasting riches, and is worshipped in heaven. Thus the consecration of temples, etc., are described according to the prescribed rites.

## Chapter 271

## \|\| 271.1-3 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*pūrorvaṃśastvayā sūta sabhaviṣyo niveditaḥ \|*  
*sūryavaṃśe nṛpā ye tu bhaviṣyanti hi tānvada \|\| 1 \|\|*

*tathaiva yādave vaṃśe rājānaḥ kīrtivardhanāḥ \|*  
*kalau yuge bhaviṣyanti tānapīha vadasva naḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*vaśānte jñātayo yāśca rājyaṃ prāpsyanti suvratāḥ \|*  
*brūhi saṃkṣepatastāsāṃ yathābhāvyamanukramāt \|\| 3 \|\|*

1-3. Rishis said: O Suta, yon have described to ns the dynasty of Puru, along with the future kings in that dynasty. Now tell us about those kings who will be in the Solar (Surya) dynasty. So also tell us here about those illustrious kings in that Yadava family, who will exist in the Kaliyuga. And when those dynasties (Surya and Yadava) will come to an end, then, tell us briefly about those pious kings who were kinsmen of these families and who will obtain the kingdom after them, in due order as far as possible.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — The future Kings of Paurava dynasty have been described in Chapter 50. See p. 163.

## \|\| 271.4 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*bṛhadbalasya dāyādo vīro rājā hyurukṣayaḥ \|*  
*urukṣayasutaścāpi vatsadro ho mahāyaśāḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Suta said: — Now, after this, I shall tell you, of the high-souled Ikshvakus.

(1) Brihadbala's heir \[was (2) Brihatkshaya, his heir\] was tine heroic ling (3) Urukshaya. The son of Urukshaya was the famous (4) Vatsadroha (Vatsavyuha).

## \|\| 271.5 \|\|

*vatsadro hātprativyomastasya putro divākaraḥ \|*  
*tasyaiva madhyadeśe tu ayodhyā nagarī śubhā \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. \[According to Mr. Pargiter, the verse ought to be: “Brihadbala’s heir was the warrior king Brihatkshaya his son was Urukshaya.\]

(5) Prativyoma was after Vatsadroha. His son is (6) Divakara to whom in the Madhyadesha, belongs the beautiful city of Ayodhya.

**Комментарий:**

Note: — According to Vayu, the reading is who now roles the city of Ayodhya in Madhyadesha,” showing that Purana was the ruling prince, when this Purana was recited.

## \|\| 271.6 \|\|

*divākarasya bhavitā sahadevo mahāyaśāḥ \|*  
*sahadevasya bhavitā dhruvāśvo vai mahāmanāḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Divakara’s (successor) will be the illustrious (7) Sahadeva, whose (successor) will be (8) Dhruvasva, the high-minded.

## \|\| 271.7 \|\|

*tasya bhāvyo mahābhāgaḥ pratīpāśvaśca tatsutaḥ \|*  
*pratīpāśvasutaścāpi supratīpo bhaviṣyati \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. His (successor) will be the most lucky (9) Bhavya (Bhanuratha or Bhavyaratha). And his son will be (10) Pratipashva. The son of Pratipashva will be even, (11) Supratipa.

## \|\| 271.9 \|\|

*kiṃnarāśvādantarikṣo bhaviṣyati mahāmanāḥ \|*  
*suṣeṇaścāntarikṣācca sumitraścāpyamitrajit \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. (12) Marudeva will be his (Supratipa’s) son, after whom was (13) Sunakshatra. After Sunakshatra will be (14) Kinnarashra, the harasser of his foes. – 8

After Kinnarashra will be the high-minded (15) Antariksha. After Antariksha will be (16) Susena, and (17) Sumitra, the conqueror of his enemies (Amitrajit).

**Комментарий:**

Note. - According to another reading, Sushena was the son of Antariksha, whose son was Sumitra-Amitrajit. Or, after, Antariksha will be Suparna (Sushena), and after him Amitrajit.

## \|\| 271.10 \|\|

*sumitrajo bṛhadrā jo bṛhadrā jasya vīryavān \|*  
*punaḥ kṛtaṃjayo nāma dhārmikaśca bhaviṣyati \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. (18) Brihadraja will be the son of Sumitra. Brihadraja’s (son) will be (19) Viryavan (Dharmavan). Again (20) Kritanjaya, by name, (will be) the virtuous (Dharmika) son of Viryavan.

## \|\| 271.11 \|\|

*kṛtaṃjayasuto vidvānbhaviṣyati raṇejayaḥ \|*  
*bhavitā saṃjayaścāpi vīro rājā raṇejayāt \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. The son of Kritanjaya, will be the wise (21) Ranejaya, (22) Sanjaya, the warrior king will come after Ranejaya.

## \|\| 271.12 \|\|

*saṃjayasya sutaḥ śākyaḥ śākyācchuddhaudano nṛpaḥ \|*  
*śuddhaudanasya bhavitā siddhārthaḥ puṣkalaḥ sutaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. \[Sanjaya’s son will be (23) Shakya. After Shakya will be the king (24) Sudhandana. The son of Sudhandana will be (25) Siddhartha, the eminent (26) Pushhala or Rahula will be the son of Siddhartha\].

## \|\| 271.13 \|\|

*prasenajittato bhāvyaḥ kṣudra ko bhavitā tataḥ \|*  
*kṣudra kātkulako bhāvyaḥ kulakātsurathaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. After him will be l27) Prasenajit. After him will be (28) Kshudraka. After Kshudraka will be (29) Kulaka. After Kulaka is remembered (30) Suratha.

## \|\| 271.14 \|\|

*sumitraḥ surathājжāto hyantyastu bhavitā nṛpaḥ \|*  
*ete caikṣvākavaḥ proktā bhaviṣyā ye kalau yuge \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. From Suratha was born (31) Sumitra. He will be the last king. These Aikshvakus have been declared, who will exist in the Kali-yuga.

## \|\| 271.15 \|\|

*bṛhadbalānvavāye tu bhaviṣyāḥ kulavardhanāḥ \|*  
*atrānuvaṃśaśloko'yaṃ viprairgītaḥ purātanaiḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. These will be in the line of Brihadbala, they will be the glory of their family. Here the following genealogical verse is sung by ancient poets.

## \|\| 271.16 \|\|

*ikṣvākūṇāmayaṃ vaṃśaḥ sumitrānto bhaviṣyati \|*  
*sumitraṃ prāpya rājānaṃ saṃsthāṃ prāpsyati vai kalau \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. “This dynasty of the Ikshvakus will end with Sumitra. On reaching King Sumitra it will come to its close in the Kaliyuga.”

## \|\| 271.17 \|\|

*ityevaṃ mānavo vaṃśaḥ prāgeva samudāhṛtaḥ \|*  
*ata ūrdhvaṃ pravakṣyāmi māgadhā ye bṛhadra thāḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. This is thus the dynasty of Manu, even as declared before. Hereafter I will relate Brihadratha (dynasty of Magadha).

## \|\| 271.18 \|\|

*pūrveṇa ye jarāsaṃdhātsahadevānvaye nṛpāḥ \|*  
*atītā vartamānāśca bhaviṣyāṃśca nibodhata \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Listen about the kings, those past, those present, and those to come in future; from (the stock of) Jarasandha (and) in the line of Sahadeva.

## \|\| 271.19 \|\|

*saṅgrāme bhārate vṛtte sahadeve nipātite \|*  
*somādhistasya dāyādo rājā'bhūtsa girivraje \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. After (1) Sahadeva was killed, when the great of Bharata took place, (2) Samadhi succeeded him as his heir, and became king in Giriraja.

## \|\| 271.20 \|\|

*pañcāśataṃ tathā'ṣṭau ca samā rājyamakārayat \|*  
*śrutaśravāścatuḥṣaṣṭiṃ samāstasyānvaye'bhavat \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. He reined for fifty-eight years and then (3) Shrutashrava in his line reigned for sixty-four yeas.

## \|\| 271.21 \|\|

*apratīpī ca ṣaṭtriṃśatsamā rājyamakārayat \|*  
*catvāriṃśatsamāstasya niramitro divaṃ gataḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. (4) Apratipi reigned for thirty-six years and (5) Niramitra after reigning for forty-years went to heaven.

## \|\| 271.22 \|\|

*pañcāśataṃ samāḥ ṣaṭ ca surakṣaḥ prāptavānmahīm \|*  
*bṛhatkarmā trayoviṃśadabdaṃ rājyamakārayat \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Afterwards (6) Suraksha got the earth for fifty-six years and (7) Brihatkarma reigned for twenty-three years.

## \|\| 271.23 \|\|

*senājitsaṃprayātaśca bhuktvā pañcaśataṃ mahīm \|*  
*śrutaṃjayastu varṣāṇi catvāriṃśadbhaviṣyati \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. (8) Senajit has just pasted away alter enjoying the earth for fifty years.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — Another reading according to the Vayu Purana is “Senajit is now enjoying the earth, the same number (23) of years”.

## \|\| 271.24 \|\|

*aṣṭāviṃśativarṣāṇi mahīṃ prāpsyati vai vibhuḥ \|*  
*aṣṭapañcāśataṃ ṣaṭ ca rājye sthāsyati vai śuciḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24 He will be succeeded by (9) Shrutanjaya who will be for forty years. Afterwards (10) Vibhu will obtain the earth and will reign for twenty-eight years, and then (11) Shuchi will rule the kingdom for fifty-eight plus six years (i.e. 64).

## \|\| 271.25 \|\|

*aṣṭāviṃśatsamā rājā kṣemo bhokṣyati vai mahīm \|*  
*anuvrataścatuḥṣaṣṭiṃ rājyaṃ prāpsyati vīryavān \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. The king (12) Kshema will enjoy the earth for twenty-eight years. After whom the powerful (13) Anuvrata will reign for sixty-four years.

## \|\| 271.26 \|\|

*pañcaviṃśativarṣāṇi sunetro bhokṣyate mahīm \|*  
*bhokṣyate nirvṛtiścemāmaṣṭapañcāśataṃ samāḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. (14) Sunetra will enjoy the earth for twenty-five (another reading thirty-five) years. (15) Nirvriti will enjoy it for fifty-eight years.

## \|\| 271.27 \|\|

*aṣṭāviṃśatsamā rājyaṃ trinetro bhokṣyate tataḥ \|*  
*catvāriṃśattathā'ṣṭau ca dyumatseno bhaviṣyati \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. After that (16) Trinetra, will enjoy the kingdom for twenty-eight, years. (17) Dyumatsena (Dridhasena) will be for forty-eight years.

## \|\| 271.28 \|\|

*trayastriṃśattu varṣāṇi mahīnetraḥ prakāśyate \|*  
*dvātriṃśattu samā rājā hyacalastu bhaviṣyati \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. (18) Mahinetra will be resplendent for thirty-three years (19) Achala or (Suchala) will be king for thirty-two years

## \|\| 271.29 \|\|

*ripuṃjayastu varṣāṇi pañcāśatprāpsyate mahīm \|*  
*dvātriṃśattu nṛpā hyete bhavitāro bṛhadra thāḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. (20) Ripunjaya will obtain the earth for fifty-years, and these 32 kings will be the future Brihadrathas.

King Sunetra will next enjoy the kingdom for forty years. King Satyajit will enjoy the earth for eighty-three years, (eighty years). And Vishvajit will obtain this earth and be king for twenty-five years.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — The following three lines are omitted in our text of the Matsya Purana but supplied by Mr. Pargiter.

Note. — Our reading is “dvatrimshattu nripa hyeta”. Another reading is ”Sonash-aite nripa jneya bhavitaro Brihadrathah.” And then the verse will mean these sixteen kings are to be known as the future Brihadrathas. Then there is further this line in the same manuscript: — Trayo-vims-adhikam tesham rajyam cha sata-saptakam.” And it means: — and their kingdom will last seven-hundred twenty-three years.” According to this reading the sixteen future Barhadrathas will reign for 723 years. Of course this includes Senajit also.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — The text says that there are ten Maura kings, but its enumeration is short of that number. The following note from Mr. Pargiter is appropriate: — “This dynasty by all five Puranas, but the account of it has suffered more than that of any other dynasty. Three versions exist here, the earliest in the Matsya the second in the Vayu, and the third In the Vayu generally and the Brahmanda. They agree in general purport, bull have many differences. The second forms a stage of recensions intermediate between first and the third, and Is the only copy that has preserved the names of all the kings. The Matsya version In all copies is incomplete and has one of its verses misplaced, thus only 5 MSS mention Chandragupta, the second king always omitted, and the account generally begins with that verse 25 putting the two kings first, and then mentions only four kings, Ashoka and his three successors.”

\[Though the Matsya mentions only seven kings, and that also in a confused manner, the fall list of ten kings is given in the Vishnu Purana (Book IV. Chap. 24. verses 7-8).

The years of accession noted against their names are taken from Mr. V.A. Smith’s History page 197.

Date of ascension

(1) Chandra Gupta 322 B.C.

(2) Bindusara Amitraghata 298 B.C.

(3) Ashoka 273 B.C.

Asoka died 232 B.C.

(4) Suyashas

(5) Dasharatha 232 B.C.

(6) Sangata 224 B.C.

(7) Salishuka 216 B.C.

(8) Somasharman 206 B.C.

(9) Shatadhanva 199 B.C.

(10) Brihadratha 191-185 B.C.

*bhavitā vajramitrastu samā rājā punarbhavaḥ \|*

*bhaviṣyati sutastasya devabhūmiḥ samā daśa \|*  
*daśaite kṣudra rājāno bhokṣyantīmāṃ vasuṃdharām \|\| 31 \|\|*

*amātyo vasudevastu prasahya hyavanīṃ nṛpaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

30-32. Then Vajramitra will be king for 9 years. Then Samabhaga will reign for 32 years. Then after him his son Devabhumi will reign for 10 years. These ten petty kings will enjoy this earth for full 112 years. And then the earth will go to the Kanvas.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — The Purana enumerates only 8 kings while there ought to be ten. This omission is supplied by the names of Agnimitra and Ghoshavasu as given in the Vishnu Purana. The ten kings, therefore, are the following. —

(1) Pushyamitra 185 B.C. (36 years)

(2) Agnimitra 149 B.C. (8 years)

(3) Sujeshtha or Vasujeshtha 141 B.C. (7 years)

(4) Vasumitra 134 B.C. (10 years)

(5) Antaka 124 B.C. (2 years)

(6) Pulindaka 122 B.C. (3 years)

(7) Ghoshavasu 119 B.C. (3 years)

(8) Vajramitra 116 B.C. (9 years)

(9) Bhagayata or Sambhaga 107 B.C. (32 years)

(10) Devabhuti or Devabhumi 75 B.C. (10 years)

Total 120 years.

\[The aggregate of the reigns is, however, 120 years and not 112, but all the Puranas agree in giving 112 years as the dynasty. This discrepancy might be explained by from the list. He perhaps never reigned as a king apart from his father Pushyamitra, who though de facto king always styled himself Senapati or Commander-in-chief and so Agnimitra’s name is not mentioned by the Matsya Purana. There is much uncertainty about b out by Mr. Pargiter. Or may it be that Agnimitra was a king during the life-time of his father on certain parts of the vast empire. And verse “tat-suto’ gnimitr-astau bhavishyati sama nirpah” may be read as “tat-suto’ ganimitrastu bhavishyati sama nripah.” According to this calculation Sunga dynasty would appear to have in 65 B. C. but in 73 The Matsya Parana verse 32 is rather inaccurate.

It says: — “These ten Kshudra kings will enjoy this earth full 100 and 200 (total 300) years. Then it will go to the Sungas." This is the earth could not have gone to the Sungas after the Sungas. Nor did the Sungas reign for 300 years. Instead of tatah Sungan gamishyati, another reading is “tatah svargam gamishyati, which may refer to the last king namely, Devabhumi who will go to heaven. This is reading appropriate than Sungan gamishyati. Moreover who are these petty kings Ksudrarajanah which the text mentions. It only mentions 8 kings and not 10 for it does not mention Agnimitra and Ghoshavasu. We have therefore adopted Mr. Pargiter’ reading: - Dashaite Sunga-rajano bhokshyant-imam vasundharam Shatam purnam dasha dve cha tatah kanvan gamishyati.” This is in accordance with Vishnu purana also which in IV. 24.11 say.

*caṇḍaśrīḥ śāntikarṇastu tasya putraḥ samā daśa \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Then after him (30) Vijaya will be king 6 years. Then (31) Chandashri Shantikarna, his son will be 10 years.

## \|\| 273.16-17 \|\|

*pulomā sapta varṣāṇi anyasteṣāṃ bhaviṣyati \|*  
*ekonaviṃśatirhyete āndhrā bhokṣyanti vai mahīm \|\| 16 \|\|*

*teṣāṃ varṣaśatāni syuścatvāri ṣaṣṭireva ca \|*  
*āndhrāṇāṃ saṃsthitā rājye teṣāṃ bhṛtyānvaye nṛpāḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

16-17. Then (32) Puloma, another of them, (viz., Puloma II) will reign 7 years.

These 19 Andhras will enjoy the 460 years. On the kingdom of the Andhras coming to an end, there will be kings belonging to the lineage of their servants.

## \|\| 273.17 \|\|

*teṣāṃ varṣaśatāni syuścatvāri ṣaṣṭireva ca \|*  
*āndhrāṇāṃ saṃsthitā rājye teṣāṃ bhṛtyānvaye nṛpāḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. On the kingdom of the Andhras coming to an end, there will be kings in the lineage of their servants who would be called Shriparvatiya Andhras.

## \|\| 273.18 \|\|

*saptaivā’ndhrā bhaviṣyanti daśā’bhīrāstathā nṛpāḥ \|*  
*sapta gardabhilāścāpi śakāścāṣṭādaśaiva tu \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. There will be 7 (kings in the line of the servants of) Andhras, 10 Abhira kings, also 7 Gardabhilas and 18 Sakas.

## \|\| 273.19 \|\|

*yavanāṣṭau bhaviṣyanti tuṣārāśca caturdaśa \|*  
*trayodaśa guruṇḍāśca hūṇā hyekonaviṃśatiḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. There will be 8 Yavana kings, and 14 Tushara kings and 13 Gurunda kings and 19 (or 11 Mauna) Huna kings.

## \|\| 273.20 \|\|

*yavanāṣṭau bhaviṣyanti saptāśītiṃ mahīmimām \|*  
*sapta gardabhilā bhūyo bhokṣyantīmāṃ vasuṃdharām \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. The 8 Yavana kings will reign for 87 years. The 7 Gardabhilas will enjoy this earth again (no years given.72 according to Vayu.).

## \|\| 273.21 \|\|

*saptavarṣasahasrāṇi tuṣārāṇāṃ mahī smṛtā \|*  
*śatāni trīṇyaśītiṃ ca śatānyaṣṭādaśaiva tu \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. The earth is recorded to have belonged to the Tusaras for 7000 years. And 18 kinds for 183 years as well \[printed text corrupt. Ought to be: — “Eighteen Sakas for 183 years.”\]

## \|\| 273.22 \|\|

*śatānyardhacatuṣkāṇi bhavitavyāstrayodaśa \|*  
*guruṇḍā vṛṣalaiḥ sārdhaṃ bhokṣyante mlecchasaṃbhavāḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. For half four hundred years there will reign the 13 Gurundas of Mlechchha origin along with Shudra kings. (Or, the 13 future Gurundas along with low caste men, all of Mlechchha origin, will enjoy it half four hundred years, i.e., 200 years.

## \|\| 273.23 \|\|

*śatāni trīṇi bhokṣyante varṣāṇyekādaśaiva tu \|*  
*āndhrāḥ śrīpārvatīyāśca te dvipañcāśataṃ samāḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. For 103 years the 11 kings will enjoy the earth (no name). (The word Huna should be supplied to complete the years, and it would then mean “the 11 Hunas will enjoy the earth for 103 years”). The (seven) Shriparvatiya Andhras will endure 52 years.

## \|\| 273.24 \|\|

*saptaṣaṣṭistu varṣāṇi daśā’bhīrāstathaiva ca \|*  
*teṣūtsanneṣu kālena tataḥ kilakilā nṛpāḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. The 10 Abhira kings will be for 67 years. When they are over thrown by time, then there will be Kilakila kings.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — These local dynasties, with their periods of reign, may be thus shown in a tabular form:-

Note: — The account of these dynasties consists of three parts, the first of which summarizes the number of kinds in each dynasty, and the second states its duration, while the third adds certain subsequent kings. In the first part, the Matsya, Vayu, and Brahmanda agree generally, but in the seconds, the Matsya has one versions and the two others another. Here the dynastic matter in the Matsya ends.

“These local dynasties are all classed together as more or less contemporaneous. The number of years assigned to them must be considered according to the remarks in introduction Sec. 42 ff., and with reference to the middle of the 3rd century A.D. When the account was first compiled as preserved in the Mt, for the revised versions in Va and Bd did not revise the periods. If those remarks be sound, the Shriparvatya Andhrabhrityas had at that time reigned 52 years, or (if we read dvipanchasatam) possibly 100 roundly, according to Mt, while the Va. And Bd reading is no doubt corrupt and should perhaps be 112 or 102 years. The Abhiras had then reigned 67 years, the Gardabhilas 72 years, the Sakas 183 years, the Yavanas 87 years, and the Tusaras

7,000 or 500 according to the proper construction of the sentences but perhaps 107 or 105 is realli meant. The 13 Gurundas or Murundas had then reigned half of the quadruple of 100 years, that is 200, according to Mt, or 350 according to Va and Bd, but the latter is probably a corruption of the former reading, for Vs and Bh say precisely 199 years. The 11 Hunas or Maunas had then lasted 103 years.

“Mention of these races is found in the inscriptions, thus Abhiras in Luder’s ‘List of Brahmi inscriptions, Nos. 963, 1137 (Epig. Indx, Appendix) and Fleet’s Gupta inscriptions, p.14, Sakas, Luder’s

List, Nos. 1123,1135,1137,1148,1149,1162, and perhaps 1001-2, and FGI p,14, Yavanas. Luder’s list, Nos. 669, 965, 1093,1123, 1140, 1154, 1156, Murundas in FGI,p. 14. And Murundadevi, id., pp.128. 132,138 Hunas. FGI, pp. 56, 148, 206, A Vakataka, prince Vindhyasakti is mentioned in Kielhorn’s Inscriptions of Northern India, No.622 (Epig. Ind. Appendix).” (Pargiter’s Kali Dynasty p. 44.)

## \|\| 273.25 \|\|

*bhaviṣyantīha yavanā dharmataḥ kāmato'rthataḥ \|*  
*tairvimiśrā janapadā āryā mlecchāśca sarvaśaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. There will be Yavanas here for the sake of religions feeling (pilgrim age or propaganda) or pleasure or profit. The Aryas and the Mlechchhas (will dwell) mixed up in all provinces (janapadas).

## \|\| 273.26 \|\|

*viparyayeṇa vartante kṣayameṣyanti vai prajāḥ \|*  
*lubdhānṛtabruvāścaiva bhavitāro nṛpāstathā \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. The people will steadily deteriorate by adopting a contrary course of life, so also the kings will be greedy and speakers of untruth.

## \|\| 273.27 \|\|

*kalkinā tu hatāḥ sarve āryā mlecchāśca sarvataḥ \|*  
*adhārmikāśca ye'tyarthaṃ pāṣaṇḍāścaiva sarvaśaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. All will be overpowered (killed) everywhere by Kalki whether they be Aryas or Mlechchhas. They will be irreligious, avaricious, and heretical and cruel hypocrites everywhere.

## \|\| 273.28 \|\|

*pranaṣṭe nṛpavaṃśe tu saṃdhyāśiṣṭe kalau yuge \|*  
*kiṃcicchiṣṭāḥ prajāstā vai dharme naṣṭe'parigrahāḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. When the royal family will be destroyed, and the close of the Kali Age will come and righteousness will perish, there will remain few good people not given to coveteousness.

## \|\| 273.29 \|\|

*asādhavo hyasattvāśca vyādhiśokena pīḍitāḥ \|*  
*anāvṛṣṭihatāścaiva parasparavadhepsavaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. The people will be unholy, unrighteous and oppressed with disease and sorrow; and goaded by failure of rain they will be eager to destroy each other.

## \|\| 273.30 \|\|

*aśaraṇyāḥ paritrastāḥ saṃkaṭaṃ ghoramāśritāḥ \|*  
*saritparvatavāsinyo bhaviṣyantyakhilāḥ prajāḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Unprotected by anyone, always living in terror, surrounded by deep difficulties, the entire population will begin to live on (the top of) Mountains and on the banks of rivers.

## \|\| 273.31 \|\|

*nṛpavaṃśeṣu naṣṭeṣu prajāḥ sarvagṛhāṇi ca \|*  
*naṣṭasnehā nirāpatrāstyaktabhrātṛsuhṛdgaṇāḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. When the royal families will be destroyed, the people, will desert their homes; and devoid of affection they will abandon their brothers and friends, and will have no one to protect them.

## \|\| 273.32 \|\|

*varṇāśramaparibhraṣṭā adharmaniratāśca tāḥ \|*  
*patramūlaphalāhārāścīrapatrājināmbarāḥ \|*  
*vṛttyarthamabhilipsantyaścariṣyanti vasuṃdharām \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. They will not observe the rules of caste and order of life, and be addicted to unrighteousness. They will subsist on fruits, roots and leaves of trees, and will be clothed in tattered garments, barks and skins, and thus they will wander over the earth in search of livelihood.

## \|\| 273.33 \|\|

*evaṃ kaṣṭamanuprāptāḥ prajāḥ kaliyugāntake \|*  
*niḥśeṣāstu bhaviṣyanti sārdhaṃ kaliyugena tu \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Thus the people having suffered (innumerable) miseries during the close of the Kali Age will become totally extinct, extinction of the Kali Age.

## \|\| 273.34 \|\|

*kṣīṇe kaliyuge tasmindivye varṣasahasrake \|*  
*sasaṃdhyāṃśe suniḥśeṣe kṛtaṃ tu pratipatsyate \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. When the Kali Age will be exhausted, after having been on earth for full 1000 divine years together with the Sandhi periods, then on its end, the Krita Age will come.

## \|\| 273.35 \|\|

*evaṃ vaṃśakramaḥ kṛtsnaḥ kīrtito yo mayā kramāt \|*  
*atīto vartamānaśca tathaivānāgataśca yaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Thus have I declared in due order the entire series of genealogy — the kings who have passed away, and those who exist now and those who have not yet come to existents.

## \|\| 273.36 \|\|

*mahāpadmābhiṣekāttu yāvajжanma parīkṣitaḥ \|*  
*evaṃ varṣasahasraṃ tu jñeyaṃ pañcāśaduttaram \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Now from Mahapadma\`s inauguration up till the birth of Parikshit, this interval is indeed known as 1050 years (1015 according to Vishnu, and 1500 according to our reading.)

**Комментарий:**

Note. — In manuscripts of Matsya Purana marked c, e, j the reading is Sat-ottaram. Similarli in Mss. I, n of Matsya and V, 1, of Vishnu the reading is Pancha-sat-ottaram,meaning 1500. This period of 1500 is the true interval obtained by adding up the periods of reigns of the Barhadrathas, Pradyotas and Shishunagas as the Vishnu Purana and other Puranas. Thus: -

Barhadrathas from Somapi to Ripunjaya ……..1000 years.

Pradyotas ……….138

Shishunagas ……….362

Note.- In manuscripts of Matsya Purana marked c,e,j the reading is Sat-ottaram.

Similarly in Mss. I, n of Matsya and V, I, of Vishnu the reading is Pancha-sat-ottaram, meaning 1500. This period of 1500 is the true interval obtained by adding up the periods of reigns of the Barhadrathas, Pradyotas and Shishunagas as given in the Vishnu Purana and other Puranas. This:-

………….

Barhadrathas from Somapi to Ripunjaya……………………………………………………1000 years

Pradyotas …………………………………………………….138

Shishunagas ………………………………………………………362

………………………..

Therefore the Mss. of the Matsya referred to by Mr. Pargiter are more correct than the printed text. This verse, therefore, should read….

This is the reading we prefer Vishnu Purana. Mahapadma Nanda horn in 422 B.C. Therefore, Parikshit was born in 1922 B.C. which was the year of the Great Bear.

*saptarṣayastu vartante yatra nakṣatramaṇḍale \|*

## \|\| 273.41 \|\|

*saptarṣīṇāmuparyetatsmṛtaṃ vai divya saṃjñayā \|*

41\. This is the cycle, of the Great Bear, and is remembered as being, according to divine reckoning, 6 divine months and 7 divine years. According to those constellations divine time proceeds by means of the Great Bear.

## \|\| 273.42-43 \|\|

*ebhiḥ pravartate kālo divyaḥ saptarṣibhistu vai \|*  
*saptarṣīṇāṃ ca yau pūrvau dṛśyete huditau niśi \|\| 42 \|\|*

*tayormadhye tu nakṣatraṃ dṛśyate yatsamaṃ divi \|*

42-43. The two front stars of the Great Bear, which are seen when risen at night, the lunar constellation which is seen situated equally between them in the sky, the Great Bear is to be known as conjoined with that constellation 100 years in the sky.

## \|\| 273.44 \|\|

*nakṣatrāṇāmṛṣīṇāṃ ca yogasyaitannidarśanam \|*  
*saptarṣayo maghāyuktāḥ kāle pārīkṣite śatam \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. This is the exposition of the conjunction of the lunar constellations and the Great Bear. The Great Bear was conjoined with the Maghas in Parikshit’s time 100 years.

## \|\| 273.45 \|\|

*brāhmaṇāstu caturviṃśe bhaviṣyanti śataṃ samāḥ \|*

45\. The Brahmanas (the Seven Seers) will be in the 24th constellation 100 years (when) at the termination of the Andhras Pargiter.

**Комментарий:**

Note. — The 24th constellation from Magha counting retrograde is Chitra According to this calculation the interval between Parikshit and the termination of Andhra 16 2400 years. Subtracting 836, we get 1564, or the interval between Nanda and Parikshit. Or in Round number the Great War took place 1500 years before Nanda’s time.

## \|\| 273.46 \|\|

*anṛtopahatā lubdhā dharmataḥ kāmato'rthataḥ \|*

46\. Thenceforward all this world will {all upon very bad times. Men Will be liars, greedy, and destitute of righteousness, affection and wealth, le religion of Shrutis and Shrutis will become very lax, and so also will be destroyed the orders and castes.

## \|\| 273.47 \|\|

*saṃkaraṃ durbalātmānaḥ pratipatsyanti mohitāḥ \|*

47\. The people will be of mixed origin, weak in body and will be led astray and deluded. Brahmanas will sacrifice for Madras (or will study under Shudras) and Shudras will take to teaching Mantras.

## \|\| 273.48 \|\|

*upasthāsyanti tānviprāstadarthamabhilipsavaḥ \|*

48\. Those Brahmanas will adore such Madras anxious to acquire wealth from them (or anxious to get the meaning of the Mantras from them). And gradually there will be seen all the causes which go towards the removing a man from his own caste.

## \|\| 273.49 \|\|

*kṣayameva gamiṣyanti kṣīṇaśeṣā yugakṣaye \|*

49\. Thus towards the end of the age, the few weaklings that will remain on earth will also go to extinction.

## \|\| 273.50 \|\|

*pratipannaṃ kaliyugaṃ pramāṇaṃ tasya me śṛṇu \|*

50\. On that very day and in that very moment when Krishna went to heaven, the Kali Yuga arrived on earth. Now listen to its duration from me. The wise say that its duration is 400,000 years

## \|\| 273.51 \|\|

*catvāryaṣṭasahasrāṇi saṃkhyātaṃ mānuṣeṇa tu \|*

51\. Together with four times eight (32) thousand years according to human calculation (i.e., 400,000 + 32,000 = 432,000). Or in other words its duration is 1000 divine years together with the twilights (i.e., 1000 + 200 = 1200 divine years = 1200 x 360 = 432,000).

## \|\| 273.52 \|\|

*niḥśeṣe tu tadā tasminkṛtaṃ vai pratipatsyate \|*

## \|\| 273.53 \|\|

*ikṣvākoḥ saṃsmṛtaṃ kṣattraṃ sumitrāntaṃ bhaviṣyati \|*

The dynasty of the Ikshvakus (the Surya-vamsha) is remembered to have come to an end with Sumitra when Ikshvaku Kshatriyas will cease. The Aila Kshatriyas (Chandra-vamsha) were contemporary with these (or the last of the Aila Kshatriyas was Kshemaka. — Vayu,) so the knower’s of the Soma-vamsha understand it.

54\. All these are declared to be the glorious descendants of Vivasvat those who are passed, those who exist now and those who will be in the future.

*brāhmaṇāḥ kṣattriyā vaiśyāstathā śūdrā śca vai smṛtāḥ \|*

*etau kṣatrapraṇetārau navaviṃśe caturyuge \|*
