## \|\| 273.60-62 \|\|

*kṣīṇe kaliyuge caiva tiṣṭhantīti kṛte yuge \|*  
*saptarṣayastu taiḥ sārdhaṃ madhye tretāyuge punaḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

*bījārthaṃ vai bhaviṣyanti brahmakṣattrasya vai punaḥ \|*  
*evamevaṃ tu sarveṣu tiṣyānteṣvantareṣu ca \|\| 61 \|\|*

*saptarṣayo nṛpaiḥ sārdhaṃ saṃtānārthaṃ yuge yuge \|*  
*evaṃ kṣattrasya cotsedhaḥ saṃbandho vai dvijaiḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

60-62. Even after the close of the Kali Yuga, the Seven Sages who continue to exist along with these two throughout the Krita Yuga, then will incarnate in the middle of the \[future\] Treta Yuga. They will take birth in order to be the seeds of Brahmanas and Kshatriyas \[of Brahmanic parentage\] again. Thus at the end of the Pushya asterism \[when the Great Bear is m a line with that asterism\] the Seven Sages, along with those kings \[take birth on earth\] for the sake of procreating children in every Yuga. Thus the Brahmanas know the close relationship of the Kshatriyas with the Brahmanas \[and how several\] Kshatriya dynasties had Brahman paternity\].

## \|\| 273.63 \|\|

*manvantarāṇāṃ saṃtāne saṃtānāśca śrutau smṛtāḥ \|*  
*atikrāntayugāścaiva brahmakṣattrasya saṃbhavāḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. Thus at the close of each Manvantara, these \[two\] immortal Kshatriyas and \[seven\] Brahmanas, who cross over from one Yuga to another \[in their full consciousness\], are called Santanas in the Shruti or founders of future human races. They become the origins of \[the future\] Brahmanas and Kshatriyas.

## \|\| 273.64 \|\|

*yathā praśāntisteṣāṃ vai prakṛtīnāṃ yathā kṣayaḥ \|*

64\. The Seven Sages know thus the rise, and fall, and the longevity of as the decline and rise of the dynasties.

## \|\| 273.65 \|\|

*etena kramayogena ailā ikṣvākavo nṛpāḥ \|*  
*utpadyamānāstretāyāṃ kṣīyamāṇāḥ kalau yuge \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. Thus in their due order the Aila birth in the Ikshvaku kings take their birth in the Treta and come to an end in the Kali age.

**Комментарий:**

Note. – Thus in the Krita or Satya Yuga and up to the middle of Treta there exists no four-fold caste, or only one caste that of the fighters or warriors (Kshatriyas who are the pioneers of emigration and open up new lands. It takes 4900 + 1500 = 5500 years to settle fully and completely for a new race. After that the four-fold division takes place.

## \|\| 273.66 \|\|

*anuyānti yugākhyaṃ tu yāvanmanvantarakṣayam \|*  
*jāmadagnyena rāmeṇa kṣatre niravaśeṣite \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. These kings will follow in due succession \[through Treta and Dvapara and Kali according to the characteristics of the age till the Manvantara comes to an end.)

## \|\| 273.67 \|\|

*rikteyaṃ vasudhā sarvā kṣattriyairvasudhādhipaiḥ \|*  
*dvivaṃśakaraṇaṃ sarvaṃ kīrtayiṣye nibodha me \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. When Parashurama, the son of Jamadagni, annihilated the Kshatriyas, then the whole world became destitute of Kshatriya-born. They all belonged to mixed dynasties \[Brahman-Kshatriyas or Ila and Ikshvaku kings.\] All the kings owed their or Brahmanas and Kshatriyas. I shall declare that dynastic paternity. Hear it from me.

## \|\| 273.68 \|\|

*ailaṃ caikṣvākuvaṃśaṃ ca prakṛtiṃ paricakṣate \|*  
*rājānaḥ śreṇibaddhāśca tathā'nye kṣattriyā bhuvi \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. The dynasties of Aila and Aikshvaku are said to be the origin of all kings who belonged to a certain class \[who ruled in dynastic succession\] as well as other Kshatriyas on earth who were not rulers.

## \|\| 273.69 \|\|

*ailavaṃśāstu bhūyāṃso na tathekṣvākavo nṛpāḥ \|*  
*eṣāmekaśataṃ pūrṇaṃ kulānāmabhirocate \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. The descendants of the Aila family were numerous, not so however the kings of the Aikshvaku dynasty. They gave rise to full 100 famous dynasties.

## \|\| 273.70 \|\|

*tāvadeva tu bhojānāṃ vistārāddviguṇaṃ smṛtam \|*  
*bhojānāṃ dviguṇaṃ kṣattraṃ caturdhā tadyathātatham \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. Similarly the extent of the Bhoja dynasty was double that of the above, and double of the Bhojas were the other spread on all quarters, and the Bhoja clan became divided into four branches.

## \|\| 273.71 \|\|

*te hyatītāḥ sanāmāno bruvatastānnibodha me \|*  
*śataṃ vai prativindhyānāṃ śataṃ nāgāḥ śataṃ hayāḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. Now those who are past and those who were their contemporaries together with their names I shall declare. Listen to me.

## \|\| 273.72 \|\|

*śatamekaṃ dhārtarāṣṭrā hyaśītirjanamejayāḥ \|*  
*śataṃ vai brahmadattānāṃ vīrāṇāṃ kuravaḥ śatam \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. There will be 100 kings of the dynasty of Prativindhyas, 100 Nagas, 100 Hayas, 100 Dharmarashtras and 80 Janamedjayas. 100 in the family of Brahmadattas and hero kings in the Kaurava family (or 100 Siri and Viri kings or Siri and Karna kings).

## \|\| 273.73 \|\|

*tataḥ śataṃ ca pañcālāḥ śataṃ kāśikuśādayaḥ \|*  
*tathā'pare sahasre dve ye nīpāḥ śaśabindavaḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. Then 100 were Panchala kings, 100 Kashi-kusha kings, then 2000 Nipas and Shashavindus.

## \|\| 273.74-75 \|\|

*iṣṭavantaśca te sarve sarve niyutadakṣiṇāḥ \|*  
*evaṃ rājarṣayo'tītāḥ śaptaśo'tha sahasraśaḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

*manorvaivasvatasyā’sanvartamāne'ntare vibhoḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ tu nidhanotpattau lokasaṃsthitayaḥ sthitāḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

74-75. All these were performers of sacrifices and all of them were givers of myriads of gold coins in feasts to the Brahmanas. Thus hundreds and thousands of royal Rishi kings have passed away. They belonged to the family of Lord Vaivasvata Manu and they exist in the present day also. Their births and deaths are for the sake of the maintenance of the world.

## \|\| 273.76 \|\|

*na śakyo vistarasteṣāṃ saṃtānasya parasparam \|*  
*tatpūrvāparayogeṇa vaktuṃ varṣaśatairapi \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. Even in one hundred years I cannot finish the recital of the descendants of these kings and the mutual co-relationship to each other.

## \|\| 273.77 \|\|

*aṣṭāviṃśasamākhyātā gatā vaivasvate'ntare \|*  
*ete devagaṇaiḥ sārdhaṃ śiṣṭā ye tānnibodhata \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. In the Vaivasvata Manvantara 27 Mahayugas have passed away and the current one is the 28th Mahayuga. Those Sishtas (the Holy Seeds) along with the Devas who are their companions are now to be declared Listen to that.

## \|\| 273.78 \|\|

*catvāriṃśattrayaścaiva bhaviṣyāste mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*avaśiṣṭā yugākhyāste tato vaivasvato hyayam \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. In the remaining portion of the Mahayuga of the Vaivasvata-manvantara there be (or there are existing) 43 Mahatmas.

## \|\| 273.79 \|\|

*etadvaḥ kīrtitaṃ samyaksamāsavyāsayogataḥ \|*  
*punarvaktuṃ bahutvāttu na śakyaṃ vistareṇa tu \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. Thus have I declared to you fully and briefly the whole history and I cannot repeat it in its entirety on account of its being too large.

## \|\| 273.80 \|\|

*uktā rājarṣayo ye tu atītāste yugaiḥ saha \|*  
*ye te yayātivaṃśyānāṃ ye ca vaṃśā viśāṃpate \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. I have declared all the Rajarishis who have passed away along with the passing away of the Yugas as well as the kings belonging to the dynasty of Yayati and those belonging to the dynasties of the Lord of the Vyas.

## \|\| 273.81 \|\|

*kīrtitā dyutimantaste ya etāndhārayennaraḥ \|*  
*labhate sa varānpañca durlabhāniha laukikān \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. All these illustrious ones have been declared to you. He who hears the recital of this history obtains all the five worldly-blessings, so difficult of attainment here.

## \|\| 273.82 \|\|

*āyuḥ kīrtiṃ dhanaṃ svargaṃ putravāṃścābhijāyate \|*  
*dhāraṇācchravaṇāccaiva paraṃ svargasya dhīmataḥ \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. He gets long life, fame, wealth, heaven and progeny. By hearing and committing to memory this genealogy of kings, one verily goes to the highest heaven.

## Chapter 274

## \|\| 274.1 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*nyāyenārjanamarthānāṃ vardhanaṃ cābhirakṣaṇam \|*  
*satpātrapratipattiśca sarvaśāstreṣu paṭhyate \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. The Rishis said “Suta! one should acquire, increase and protect wealth by fair means. The acquirement of wealth by a virtuous person has been said to be most lucky in all the Shastras.

## \|\| 274.2 \|\|

*kṛtakṛtyo bhavetkena manasvī dhanavānbudhaḥ \|*  
*mahādānena dattena tanno vistarato vada \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Be good enough to tell by what charity a wealthy and learned man feels blessed.”

## \|\| 274.3-4 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*athātaḥ saṃpravakṣyāmi mahādānānukīrtanam \|*  
*dānadharme'pi yannoktaṃ viṣṇunā prabhaviṣṇunā \|\| 3 \|\|*

*tadahaṃ saṃpravakṣyāmi mahādānamanuttamam \|*  
*sarvapāpakṣayakaraṃ nṛṇāṃ duḥsvapnanāśanam \|\| 4 \|\|*

3-4. Suta Said: — “I shall now explain to you about that great charity, (Maha Dan) which has been mentioned to us by Lord Vishnu in connection ^ with the enunciation of the righteous ordinances. It has been kept so ' secret. It is the dispeller of all the ills and the effects of bad dreams.”

## \|\| 274.5-6 \|\|

*yattatṣoḍaśadhā proktaṃ vāsudevena bhūtale \|*  
*puṇyaṃ pavitramāyuṣyaṃ sarvapāpaharaṃ śubham \|\| 5 \|\|*

*pūjitaṃ devatābhiśca brahmaviṣṇuśivādibhiḥ \|*  
*ādyaṃ tu sarvadānānāṃ tulāpuruṣasaṃjñakam \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. The Maha Danas are of sixteen varieties. Among the sixteen kinds of Maha Dana described by the Lord, the Tula Purusha Dana is the first and best of all. It is the giver of virtue, long life, dispeller of all ills, venerated by Lords Brahma, Vishnu and Shiva and other Devas.

## \|\| 274.7-12 \|\|

*hiraṇyagarbhadānaṃ ca brahmāṇḍaṃ tadanantaram \|*  
*kalpapādapadānaṃ ca gosahasraṃ ca pañcamam \|\| 7 \|\|*

*hiraṇyakāmadhenuśca hiraṇyāśvastathaiva ca \|*  
*hiraṇyāśvarathastadvaddhemahastirathastathā \|\| 8 \|\|*

*pañcalāṅgalakaṃ tadvaddharādānaṃ tathaiva ca \|*  
*dvādaśa viśvacakra tu tataḥ kalpalatātmakam \|\| 9 \|\|*

*saptasāgaradānaṃ ca ratnadhenustathaiva ca \|*  
*mahābhūtaghaṭastadvatṣoḍaśaṃ parikīrtitam \|\| 10 \|\|*

*sarvāṇyetāni kṛtavānpurā śambarasūdanaḥ \|*  
*vāsudevastu bhagavānambarīṣo'tha bhārgavaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*kārtavīryārjuno nāma prahlādaḥ pṛthureva ca \|*  
*kuryuranye mahīpālāḥ kecicca bharatādayaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

7-12. The other Danas are — Hiranyagarbha Dana, Brahmanda Dana, Kalpapadapa Dana, Gosahasraka Dana, Hiranyakamadhenu Dana, Hiranyashva Dana, Hiranyashvaratha Dana, Hemahastiratha Dana, Panchalamgalaka Dana, Dhara Dana, Vishvachakra Dana, Kalpalata Dana, Saptasagaraka Dana, Ratnadhenu Dana, Mahabhutaghata Dana, which were first observed by Bhagavan Vasudeva, the Destroyer of Sambara, by Ambarisha, Bhargava, Sahasravahu, Prahlada, Prithu, Bharata and other kings. These Danas are always performed for the removal of all obstacles; and as a result of these they were all protected by the Devas.

## \|\| 274.13 \|\|

*yasmādvighnasahasreṇa mahādānāni sarvadā \|*  
*rakṣante devatāḥ sarvā ekaikamapi bhūtale \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. The Devas ward these observers of ordinances from all ills.

## \|\| 274.14 \|\|

*eṣāmanyatamaṃ kuryādvāsudevaprasādataḥ \|*  
*na śakyamanyathā kartumapi śakreṇa bhūtale \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. If one of these Danas be accomplished without any obstacles through the favour of Lord Vishnu then Indra was not able to do any injury to the devotee.

## \|\| 274.15 \|\|

*tasmādārādhya gauvindamumāpativināyakau \|*  
*mahādānamakhaṃ kuryādvipraiścaivānumoditaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. So a devotee should adore Lords Vishnu, Shiva and Ganesha and then with the advice of the Brahmanas should commence the performance of sacrifices, pertaining to these Maha Danas.

## \|\| 274.16 \|\|

*etadevā’ha manave paripṛṣṭo janārdanaḥ \|*  
*yathāvadanuvakṣyāmi śṛṇudhvamṛṣisattamāḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. “King Manu had put the following question to the Lord Janardana, which. I heard and now shall try to make clear according to my understanding. Please listen to it.”

## \|\| 274.17 \|\|

*manuruvāca*  
*mahādānāni yānīha pavitrāṇi śubhāni ca \|*  
*rahasyāni pradeyāni tāni me kathayācyuta \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Manu said: — “Lord, be pleased to tell me about the Maha Danas, tie most auspicious, sacred and mysterious”.

## \|\| 274.18 \|\|

*matsya uvāca*  
*yāni noktāni guhyāni mahādānāni ṣoḍaśa \|*  
*tāni te kathayiṣyāmi yathāvadanupūrvaśaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Matsya said: — The 16 great ordinances that have not been mentioned elsewhere up to now, I shall now explain before to you”.

## \|\| 274.19-23 \|\|

*tulāpuruṣayogo'yaṃ yeṣāmādau vidhīyate \|*  
*ayane viṣuve puṇye vyatīpāte dinakṣaye \|\| 19 \|\|*

*yugādiṣūparāgeṣu tathā manvantarādiṣu \|*  
*saṃkrāntau vaidhṛtidine caturdaśyaṣṭamīṣu ca \|\| 20 \|\|*

*sitapañcadaśīparvadvādaśīṣvaṣṭakāsu ca \|*  
*yajñotsavavivāheṣu duḥsvapnādbhutadarśane \|\| 21 \|\|*

*dra vyabrāhmaṇalābhe vā śraddhā vā yatra jāyate \|*  
*tīrthe vā’yatane goṣṭhe kūpārāmasaritsu ca \|\| 22 \|\|*

*gṛhe vā’yatane vā'pi taḍāge rucire tathā \|*  
*mahādānāni deyāni saṃsārabhayabhīruṇā \|\| 23 \|\|*

19-23. Tula Purusha Dana is the first and best of all, and it should be performed on the days of Ayana, Vishuvak, Vyatipata, Dinaksyaya, on the first clay of the Yugas and Manvantaras, Sankranti, Sankranti Vaidhriti, Yoga, Chaturdashi, Astana, white Panchadashi, on the Parva days, on the Dvadashi, Ashtakadoga, on the occasions of sacrifices, festivities, marriages, after having seen bad dreams or seen wonderful things, on getting wealth and Brahmanas, on the occasion of Shraddha, in desired times, in a sacred place, in temples, cowsheds, near a well or a garden or a beautiful tank, etc. Thus in these days, on such occasions and at such places, Maha Danas must be made.

## \|\| 274.24 \|\|

*anityaṃ jīvitaṃ yasmādvasu cātīva cañcalam \|*  
*keśeṣveva gṛhītaḥ sanmṛtyunā dharmamācaret \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Life is momentary, wealth is transient and every being is in the clutches of death. Under such circumstances a man should always follow the course of Dharma and righteous actions.

## \|\| 274.25-26 \|\|

*puṇyāṃ tithimathā’sādya kṛtvā brāhmaṇavācanam \|*  
*ṣoḍaśāratnimātraṃ tu daśa dvādaśa vā karān \|\| 25 \|\|*

*maṇḍapaṃ kārayedvidvāṃścaturbhadrā nanaṃ budhaḥ \|*  
*saptahastā bhavedvedī madhye pañcakarā tathā \|\| 26 \|\|*

25-26. On an auspicious day the devotee should make the Brahmanas recite Svastivachana and then make a panda! of 10 or 12 hands or 16 aratnis.

It should have four Bhadrasanas and the altar should be of seven hands and within this another Vedi of five hands.

**Комментарий:**

Note. … — palm of hand.

## \|\| 274.27-29 \|\|

*tanmadhye toraṇaṃ kuryātsāradārumayaṃ budhaḥ \|*  
*kuryātkuṇḍāni catvāri caturdikṣu vicakṣaṇaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

*samekhalāyoniyutāni kuryātsaṃpūrṇakumbhāni mahāsanāni \|*  
*sutāmrapātradvayasaṃyutāni suyajñapātrāṇi suviṣṭarāṇi \|\| 28 \|\|*

*hastapramāṇāni tilājyadhūpapuṣpopahārāṇi suśobhanāni \|*  
*pūrvottare hastamitā'tha vedī grahādideveśvarapūjanāya \|\| 29 \|\|*

27-29. In this central Vedi the doorways of fine wood should be made and four sacrificial cavities should be dug, one in each direction. Each cavity (kunda) should have a girdle and a jar filled with water, an asana (seat), two copper vessels, sacrificial utensils, Vistara, clarified butter, sesamum, incense, lights, flowers, etc., That Kunda is to be made of one hand and should be made in the north-east. In this Vedi, the Graha Devatas (Deities of the planets' are to be worshipped.

## \|\| 274.30-32 \|\|

*atrārcanaṃ brahmaśivācyutānāṃ tatraiva kāryaṃ phalamālyavastraiḥ \|*  
*lokeśavarṇāḥ paritaḥ patākā madhye dhvajaḥ kiṅkiṇikāyutaḥ syāt \|\| 30 \|\|*

*dvāreṣu kāryāṇi ca toraṇāni catvāryapi kṣīravanaspatīnām \|*  
*dvāreṣu kumbhadvayamatra kāryaṃ sraggandhadhūpāmbararatnayuktam \|\| 31 \|\|*

*śāleṅgudīcandanadevadāruśrīparṇibilvapriyakāñcanottham \|*  
*stambhadvayaṃ hastayugāvakhātaṃ kṛtvā dṛḍhaṃ pañcakarocchritaṃ ca \|\| 32 \|\|*

30-32. Here the Brahma, Vishnu and Shiva should be worshipped with flowers, fruits, clothing’s, etc. All round, banners of various colours resembling the complexion of the four Lokapalas should be made. In the centre a beautiful banner should be made, decorated with little bells and network and four buntings of bo-tree and other milky trees should be tied on four doorways and then two jars full of water and decorated with garlands, incense, etc., should be placed and two pillars of the wood of any of the following trees, viz. — Sala, Ingudi, Sandal, Deodar, Shriparni, Vilva, and Priya Kachanara — should be made. They should be two hands underground and five hands above it. The two pillars are to be four hands apart. Another piece of wood, sufficiently strong, is to be placed. across on the two pillars.

## \|\| 274.33-38 \|\|

*tadantaraṃ hastacatuṣṭayaṃ syādathodaraṅgaśca tadaṅgameva \|*  
*samānajātiśca tulā'valambyā haimena madhye puruṣeṇa yuktā \|\| 33 \|\|*

*dairghyeṇa sā hastacatuṣṭayaṃ syātpṛthutvamasyāstu daśāṅgulāni \|*  
*suvarṇapaṭṭābharaṇā tu kāryā sā lohapāśadvayaśṛṅkhalābhiḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

*yutā suvarṇena tu ratnamālā vibhūṣitā mālyavilepanābhyām \|*  
*cakraṃ likhedvārijagarbhayuktaṃ nānārajobhirbhuvi puṣpakīrṇam \|\| 35 \|\|*

*vitānakaṃ copari pañcavarṇaṃ saṃsthāpayetpuṣpaphalopaśobham \|*  
*athartvijo vedavidaśca kāryāḥ surūpaveśānvayaśīlayuktāḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

*vidhānadakṣāḥ paṭavo'nukūlā ye cā’ryadeśaprabhavā dvijendrā ḥ! \|*  
*guruśca vedāntavidāryavaṃśasamudbhavaḥ śīlakulābhirūpaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

*purāṇaśāstrābhirato'tidakṣaḥ prasannagambhīrasarasvatīkaḥ \|*  
*sitāmbaraḥ kuṇḍalahemasūtrakeyūrakaṇṭhābharaṇābhirāmaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

33-38. Then a casteman should suspend the scales and in, the middle of it should be placed a golden image. A rod of four hands should be put above the scales and the latter should be made 10 fingers thick and should be decorated with a plate of gold and ornaments. Both the scales should be suspended to the rod by means of iron chains and then they should be decorated with garlands studded with precious stones, flowers and sandal. A lotus should also be drawn with powders of different colours, and flowers, etc., should be strewn there, and above the beam of the scales a canopy of five colours should be erected.. Afterwards those versed in the Vedas, handsome in appearance, of nice disposition, knowing all the rituals, born in the Bharatavarsha, should be made the priests, and the man accomplished in the Vedanta, born in an Aryan family, knowing Puranas, of cheerful disposition, wearing white clothes, earrings, a golden girdle, armlets and other ornaments, should be made the Preceptor (Guru).

## \|\| 274.39-40 \|\|

*pūrveṇa ṛgvedavidāvathā’stāṃ yajurvidau dakṣiṇataśca śastau \|*  
*sthāpyau dvijau sāmavidau tu paścādātharvaṇāvuttaratastu kāryau \|\| 39 \|\|*

*vināyakādigrahalokapālavasvaṣṭakādityamarudgaṇānām \|*  
*brahmācyuteśārkavanaspatīnāṃ svamantrato homacatuṣṭayaṃ syāt \|\| 40 \|\|*

39-40. To the east of the Mandapa two Brahmanas versed in the Rigveda should be seated, to the south should be seated two Brahmanas accomplished in the Yajurveda, two to the west knowing the Samaveda and two to the north versed in the Atharvaveda, All those learned men should offer Ho m as or sacrificial libations four times in four directions by reciting the Vedic hymns on their respective altars to Ganesha, Grahas, Lokapals, Ashtavasu, Aditya, Marudgana, Brahmi, Vishnu, Shiva, Surya and the Vanaspatis.

## \|\| 274.41 \|\|

*japyāni sūktāni tathaiva caiṣāmanukrameṇāpi yathāsvarūpam \|*  
*homāvasāne kṛtatūryanādo gururgṛhītvā balipuṣpadhūpam \|*  
*āvāhayellokapatīnkrameṇa mantrairamībhiryajamānayuktaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Afterwards the mind should be turned to the mantras sacred to them. At the close of the sacrifice when the Hamas are over, the preceptors should get the music played and then taking the Valis, flowers and incense in order and invoke the Lokapals.

## \|\| 274.42 \|\|

*ehyehi sarvāmarasiddhasādhyairabhiṣṭuto vajradharo'mareśaḥ \|*  
*saṃvījyamāno'psarasāṃ gaṇena rakṣādhvaraṃ no bhagavannamaste \|*  
*oṃ indrā ya namaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. The following mantras should be uttered at the time of invoking the Lokapalas, viz. — O Indra! adored by the Devas, Sadhyas, Siddhas, come. O, one armed with a thunderbolt and surrounded and fanned by the nymphs, I salute you. Pray guard my sacrifice, Om Indraya Namah.

## \|\| 274.43 \|\|

*ehyehi sarvāmarahavyavāha munipravīrairabhito'bhijuṣṭaḥ \|*  
*tejasvinā lokagaṇena sārdhaṃ mamādhvaraṃ rakṣa kave namaste \|*  
*oṃ agnaye namaḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Agni come, come, be gracious enough to come. You are adored by the seers, all the Immortals and carrier of oblations to the gods Be pleased to guard my sacrifice by your power and through your powerful attendants. I salute you. Om Agnaye Namah.

## \|\| 274.44 \|\|

*ehyehi vaivasvata dharmarāja sarvāmarairarcita divyamūrte \|*  
*śubhāśubhānandaśucāmadhīśa śivāya naḥ pāhi makhaṃ namaste \|*  
*oṃ yamāya namaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. O Vaivasvata! O Divine Personage! Dharmaraja! be good enough to come. You are adored by all the Devas. You are of the Divine form.

You are the cause of men’s misery and prosperity. Please guard this sacrifice for my benefit. I salute you. Om Yamaya Namah.

## \|\| 274.45 \|\|

*ehyehi rakṣogaṇanāyakastvaṃ viśālavetālapiśācasaṃghaiḥ \|*  
*mamādhvaraṃ pāhi śubhādinātha lokeśvarastvaṃ bhagavannamaste \|*  
*oṃ nirṛtaye namaḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Rakshogananayaka! be good enough to come with your demon attendants, Vetalas and Pishachas, be pleased to guard this sacrifice, you are the Lord of Rakshasas and the Lokas. I salute you. Om Nirritaye Namah.

## \|\| 274.46 \|\|

*ehyehi yādogaṇavāridhīnāṃ gaṇena parjanyamahāpsarobhiḥ \|*  
*vidyādharendrā maragīyamāna pāhi tvamasmānbhagavannamaste \|*  
*oṃ varuṇāya namaḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Come, O Lord! with the seas and the aquatic animals, come with the clouds and Apsarasas. The Vidyadharas and gods will sing praises of you. Do you protect us. I salute you. Om Varunaya Namah.

## \|\| 274.47 \|\|

*ehyehi yajñe mama rakṣaṇāya mṛgādhirūḍhaḥ saha siddhasaṃghaiḥ \|*  
*prāṇādhipaḥ kālakaveḥ sahāyo gṛhāṇa pūjāṃ bhagavannamaste \|*  
*oṃ vāyave namaḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Come, O Lord! to protect me in my sacrifice. Come seated on a stage and in company with the Siddhas (demigods). The lord of the Pranas the great helper of the author of destruction, do you accept my worship. I salute you. Om Vayave Namah.

## \|\| 274.48 \|\|

*ehyehi yajñeśvara yajñarakṣāṃ vidhatsva nakṣatragaṇena sārdham \|*  
*sarvauṣadhībhiḥ pitṛbhiḥ sahaiva gṛhāṇa pūjāṃ bhagavannamaste \|*  
*oṃ somāya namaḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Come, O Yajneshwava O (Lord of the sacrifice)! Come and save the sacrificial ceremony, with the Nakshatras (stars). In company with the Oshadhis and the Pitris do you accept my offerings, O Lord! Om Somaya Namah.

## \|\| 274.49 \|\|

*ehyehi viśveśvara nastriśūlakapālakhaṭvāṅgadhareṇa sārdham \|*  
*lokeśa yajñeśvara yajñasiddhyai gṛhāṇa pūjāṃ bhagavannamaste \|*  
*oṃ īśānāya namaḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Come O Vishveshvara! come, with the Bearer of Nastri, Shula, skull and Khatvanga. O Lord of the worlds! Master of the sacrifice! Do you accept my worship to fulfil my sacrifice. I salute you. O Lord! Om Ishanaya Namah

## \|\| 274.50 \|\|

*ehyehi pātāladharādharendra nāgāṅganākiṃnaragīyamāna \|*  
*yakṣoragendrā maralokasārdhamananta rakṣādhvaramasmadīyam \|*  
*oṃ anantāya namaḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Come O Lord of the Patala (netherworlds) and of the mountains Come you praised in song by the Naga women and the Kinnaras. O Ananta (Endless One)! Save our sacrifice with the great Yakshas, and Uragus and the various gods. Om Anantaya Namah.

## \|\| 274.51 \|\|

*ehyehi viśvādhipate munīndra lokena sārdhaṃ pitṛdevatābhiḥ \|*  
*sarvasya dhātā'syamitaprabhāva viśādhvaraṃ no bhagavannamaste \|*  
*oṃ brahmaṇe namaḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

51 Come you the Lord of the universe! the Greatest Savant! Come you with the gods and the Pitris. You are the Creator of all-being of unparalleled might. Come to grace our Sacrifice. O Lord! Om Brahmane Namah.

## \|\| 274.52 \|\|

*trailokye yāni bhūtāni sthāvarāṇi carāṇi ca \|*  
*brahmaviṣṇuśivaiḥ sārdhaṃ rakṣāṃ kurvantu tāni me \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. All The beings that are in the three worlds moving or fixed-may they with Brahman, Vishnu and Shiva protect me.

## \|\| 274.53-54 \|\|

*devadānagandharvā yakṣarākṣasapannagāḥ \|*  
*ṛṣayo madano gāvo devamātara eva ca \|\| 53 \|\|*

*sarve mamādhvare rakṣāṃ prakurvantu mudā'nvitāḥ \|*  
*ityāvāhya surāndadyādṛtvigbhyo hemabhūṣaṇam \|\| 54 \|\|*

53-54. O Devas, Danavas, Yakshas, Gandharvas, Serpents, Rakshasas, seers, men Go, Devamataras, he pleased and come and protect me in the performance of my sacrifice. After thus invoking the Deities, offer the ornaments of gold to the Ritvikas.

## \|\| 274.55-56 \|\|

*kuṇḍalāni ca haimāni sūtrāṇi kaṭakāni ca \|*  
*aṅgulīyapavitrāṇi vāsāṃsi śayanāni ca \|\| 55 \|\|*

*dviguṇaṃ gurave dadyādbhūṣaṇācchādanāni ca \|*  
*japeyuḥ śāntikādhyāyaṃ jāpakāḥ sarvatodiśam \|\| 56 \|\|*

55-56. They should he given earrings, girdle of gold, rings clean clothes, and bedstead and double of these should be given to the Preceptor. All the Brahmanas sitting in the different directions should turn their heads on Shantikadhyaya.

## \|\| 274.57 \|\|

*tatroṣitāstu te sarve kṛtvaivamadhivāsanam \|*  
*ādāvante ca madhye ca kuryādbrāhmaṇavācanam \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. The Brahmanas engaged for the sacrifice who fast, should follow all these things, and the devotee should make the Brahman vachana (svastivachana) in the beginning, middle and the end.

## \|\| 274.58-64 \|\|

*tato maṅgalaśabdena snāpito vedapuṃgavaiḥ \|*  
*triḥpradakṣiṇamāvṛtya gṛhītakusumāñjaliḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

*śuklamālyāmbaro bhūtvā tāṃ tulāmabhimantrayet \|*  
*namaste sarvadevānāṃ śaktistvaṃ satyamāsthitā \|\| 59 \|\|*

*sākṣibhūtā jagaddhātrī nirmitā viśvayoninā \|*  
*ekataḥ sarvasatyāni tathā'nṛtaśatāni ca \|\| 60 \|\|*

*dharmādharmakṛtāṃ madhye sthāpitā'si jagaddhite \|*  
*tvaṃ tule sarvabhūtānāṃ pramāṇamiha kīrtitā \|\| 61 \|\|*

*māṃ tolayantī saṃsārāduddharasva namo'stu te \|*  
*yo'sau tattvādhipo devaḥ puruṣaḥ pañcaviṃśakaḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

*sa eko'dhiṣṭhito devi tvayi tasmānnamo namaḥ \|*  
*namo namaste govinda tulāpuruṣasaṃjñaka \|\| 63 \|\|*

*tvaṃ hare tārayasvāsmānasmātsaṃsārakardamāt \|*  
*puṇyakālaṃ samāsādya kṛtvaivamadhivāsanam \|\| 64 \|\|*

58-64. Afterwards the devotee should get himself bathed by the Brahmanas and the Brahmanas should recite the Vedic hymns and then he is to take a handful of flowers after circumambulation and wear a garland of white flowers and cloth. He should then invoke the scale and say you are the strength of all the Devas and rest on truth I salute you; O Jagaddhatri! you have been designed by the Lord Brahma as the witness. You hold yourself between the Truth and the Untruth. You are the life between the Virtuous and the vicious. You weigh all. Weigh me then, and carry me across the ocean of the world. I salute you. Only m you is the Lord of the twenty-five elements inherent. I therefore salute you. I salute you O, Govinda! in the form of this scale O Hari! be gracious enough to see me taken across this ocean of the world.

## \|\| 274.65 \|\|

*punaḥ pradakṣiṇaṃ kṛtvā tulāmārohayedbudhaḥ \|*  
*sakhaḍgacarmakavacaḥ sarvābharaṇabhūṣitaḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. Then after circumambulating and putting on a coat of mail, sword, shield and ornaments the devotee should sit in one of the scales.

## \|\| 274.66-72 \|\|

*dharmarājamathā’dāya haimaṃ sūryeṇa saṃyutam \|*  
*karābhyāṃ baddhamuṣṭibhyāmāste paśyanharermukham \|\| 66 \|\|*

*tato'pare tulābhāge nyaseyurdvijapuṃgavāḥ \|*  
*samādabhyadhikaṃ yāvatkāñcanaṃ cātinirmalam \|\| 67 \|\|*

*puṣṭikāmastu kurvīta bhūmisaṃsthaṃ nareśvaraḥ \|*  
*kṣaṇamātraṃ tataḥ sthitvā punarevamudīrayet \|\| 68 \|\|*

*namaste sarvabhūtānāṃ sākṣibhūte sanātani \|*  
*pitāmahena devi tvaṃ nirmitā parameṣṭhinā \|\| 69 \|\|*

*tvayā dhṛtaṃ jagatsarvaṃ tule sthāvarajaṅgamam \|*  
*sarvabhūtātmabhūtasthe namaste viśvadhāriṇi \|\| 70 \|\|*

*tato'vatīrya gurave pūrvamardhaṃ nivedayet \|*  
*ṛtvigbhyo'paramardhaṃ tu dadyādudakapūrvakam \|\| 71 \|\|*

*gurave grāmaratnāni ṛtvigbhyaśca nivedayet \|*  
*prāpya teṣāmanujñāṃ tu tathā'nyebhyo'pi dāpayet \|\| 72 \|\|*

66-72. Seeing the face of Lord Sri Hari and taking the golden image of Dharmaraja with that of the Sun by both of his hands. The Brahmanas should then weigh the devotee with excellent gold pieces until the scale kicks the ground. Then the king eager for his prosperity should place more gold than that of his weight on the floor and remaining in the scale for some time utter the following words Devi! you are the witness of all, I therefore salute you. You were first created by Brahma and the whole of the moveable and the immoveable world is held by you. O Vishvadharini, you are the soul of all beings. You are the holder of the universe. I salute you.” After saying so he should alight from the scale and give first of all hall of the whole offerings to the preceptor (Guru) and the rest should be made over to the Ritvijas and with their permission should distribute a portion of that wealth among others also.

## \|\| 274.73-74 \|\|

*dīnānāthaviśiṣṭādīnpūjayedbrāhmaṇaiḥ saha \|*  
*na ciraṃ dhārayedgehe suvarṇaṃ prokṣitaṃ budhaḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

*tiṣṭhedbhayāvahaṃ yasmācchokavyādhikaraṃ nṛṇām \|*  
*śīghraṃ parasvīkaraṇācchreyaḥ prāpnoti mānavaḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

73-74. The poor, the helpless, the good, the worthy and the Brahmanas should all be duly honoured. The offerings of the tuladana, should not be allowed to lie in the house even for some time. One who does so is visited by fear, privation and pestilence. By readily distributing it among others one gets blessings from superiors.

## \|\| 274.75 \|\|

*anena vidhinā yastu tulāpuruṣamācaret \|*  
*pratilokādhipasthāne pratimanvantaraṃ vaset \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. Those who observe this Maha Dana in such a way reign over a Loka for one manvantara.

## \|\| 274.76 \|\|

*vimānenārkavarṇena kiṅkiṇījālamālinā \|*  
*pūjyamāno'psarobhiśca tato viṣṇupuraṃ vrajet \|*  
*kalpakoṭiśataṃ yāvattasmiṁ lloke mahīyate \|\| 76 \|\|*

76 He becomes illustrious like the Sun and then goes to the realm of Vishnu seated in a Vimana decorated with beautiful perforated work, bells, garlands and. adorned by the nymphs where he remains for crores of kalpas.

## \|\| 274.77-78 \|\|

*karmakṣayādiha punarbhuvi rājarājo bhūpālamaulimaṇirañjitapādapīṭhaḥ \|*  
*śraddhānvito bhavati yajñasahasrayājī dīptapratāpajitasarvamahīpalokaḥ \|\| 77 \|\|*

*yo dīyamānamapi paśyati bhaktiyuktaḥ kālāntare smarati vācayatīha loke \|*  
*yo vā śṛṇoti paṭhatīndra samānarūpaḥ prāpnoti dhāma sa puraṃdaradevajuṣṭam \|\| 78 \|\|*

77-78. On the completion of his store of virtues he is born as an illustrious emperor on this land and conquers thousands of kings after performing sacrifices. The one who witnesses such an ordinance and thinks of it at the close of his life, or repeats it to others, or reads about it or hears it, goes to heaven adorned by Indra.

## Chapter 275

## \|\| 275.1 \|\|

*matsya uvāca*  
*athātaḥ saṃpravakṣyāmi mahādānamanuttamam \|*  
*nāmnā hiraṇyagarbhākhyaṃ mahāpātakanāśanam \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Matsya said: “I shall now tell you about the excellent Hiranyagarbha Maha Danam which is the dispeller of all sins.

## \|\| 275.2-6 \|\|

*puṇyaṃ dinamathā’sādya tulāpuruṣadānavat \|*  
*ṛtviṅmaṇḍapasaṃbhārabhūṣaṇācchādanādikam \|\| 2 \|\|*

*kuryādupoṣitastadvallokeśāvāhanaṃ budhaḥ \|*  
*puṇyāhavācanaṃ kṛtvā tadvatkṛtvā'dhivāsanam \|\| 3 \|\|*

*brāhmaṇairānayetkumbhaṃ tapanīyamayaṃ śubham \|*  
*dvisaptatyaṅgulocchrāyaṃ hemapaṅkajagarbhavat \|\| 4 \|\|*

*tribhāgahīnavistāramājyakṣīrābhipūritam \|*  
*daśāstrāṇi ca ratnāni dātrasūcīṃ tathaiva ca \|\| 5 \|\|*

*hemanālaṃ sapiṭakaṃ bahirādityasaṃyutam \|*  
*tathaivā’varaṇaṃ nābherupavītaṃ ca kāñcanam \|\| 6 \|\|*

2-6. On an auspicious day the devotee should observe fasting and arrange for a pandal, articles, ornaments, canopy, Ritvikas, etc., as needed for the tuladana. He should then invoke Bhagavan Vishnu and the Lokapalas, Then after Punyahavachana and Adhivasana he should get an auspicious jar of gold which should be 72 fingers in height and of the shape of a lotus having its third part filled in with clarified butter and milk and also with ten weapons, jewels, needles, a sickle, gold, and then the jar should be provided with a pedestal and golden stalk of lotus and it should have an image of the Sun on their outer circumference and a golden thread put round its navel.

## \|\| 275.7-8 \|\|

*pārśvataḥ sthāpayettadvaddhaimadaṇḍakamaṇḍalū \|*  
*padmākāraṃ pidhānaṃ syātsamantādaṅgulādhikam \|\| 7 \|\|*

*muktāvalīsamopetaṃ padmarāgasamanvitam \|*  
*tiladro ṇoparigataṃ vedimadhye vyavasthitam \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8. Close to that Hiranyagarbha jar should be placed the golden staff and Kamandalu on either of the sides respectively and then a lotus should be drawn on the space all-round the jar measuring a few more fingers. Then pearl strings and sapphires should be placed, afterwards sesamum and an oval wooden vessel should be placed on the altar above which should be placed the Hiranyagarbha jar.

## \|\| 275.9-10 \|\|

*tato maṅgalaśabdena brahmaghoṣaraveṇa ca \|*  
*sarvauṣadhyudakasnānasnāpito vedapuṃgavaiḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*śuklamālyāmbaradharaḥ sarvābharaṇabhūṣitaḥ \|*  
*imamuccāsyenmantraṃ gṛhītakusumāñjaliḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. Then after uttering propitiatory words and getting the Brahmanas to read the Vedas, the devotee after bathing in water, mixed with all the herbs, is to put on a garland of white flowers, clothes, ornaments and utter the following mantras with flowers in his hands.

## \|\| 275.11 \|\|

*namo hiraṇyagarbhāya hiraṇyakavacāya ca \|*  
*saptalokasurādhyakṣa jagaddhātre namo namaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. O Hiranyagarbha! O Hiranyakavacha! O Lord of the Devas and the seven Lokas! salutations to you Salutations to Lord Vishnu and the Holder of the Universe.

## \|\| 275.12 \|\|

*bhūrlokapramukhā lokāstava garbhe vyavasthitāḥ \|*  
*brahmādayastathā devā namaste viśvadhāriṇe \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Deva! Bhuloka and other regions are contained in you and so are Brahma and other Devas, You are the holder of the universe. I salute you.

## \|\| 275.13 \|\|

*namaste bhuvanādhāra namaste bhuvanāśraya \|*  
*namo hiraṇyagarbhāya garbhe yasya pitāmahaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. O Supporter of the Universe, the golden-wombed One! Creator of the Universe is contained in you. Salutations to You.

## \|\| 275.14 \|\|

*yatastvameva bhūtātmā bhūte bhūte vyavasthitaḥ \|*  
*tasmānmāmuddharāśeṣaduḥkhasaṃsārasāgarāt \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. You are the soul of all the beings. You are inherent in each being, pray, therefore, drive away all my endless troubles of the world.

## \|\| 275.15-17 \|\|

*evamāmantr! ya tanmadhyamāviśyā’sta udaṅmukhaḥ \|*  
*muṣṭibhyāṃ parisaṃgṛhya dharmarājacaturmukhau \|\| 15 \|\|*

*jānumadhye śiraḥ kṛtvā tiṣṭheducchvāsapañcakam \|*  
*garbhādhānaṃ puṃsavanaṃ sīmantonnayanaṃ tathā \|\| 16 \|\|*

*kuryurhiraṇyagarbhasya tataste dvijapuṃgavāḥ \|*  
*gītamaṅgalaghoṣeṇa gururutthāpayettataḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

15-17. After thus invoking the Lord the devotee should enter the precincts of the altar and keeping his face north-wards hold the images of Dharmaraja and Brahma in both his hands and take five deep breaths after placing his head between his ankles. Then the Brahmana versed in the Vedas should perform the Garbhadhana Punsavana and Si manta ceremonies of the Hiranyagarbha. Then the Preceptor and Brahmanas should make the devotee to sit up after chanting the Vedic hymns and getting the music played.

## \|\| 275.18 \|\|

*jātakarmādikāḥ kuryuḥ kriyāḥ ṣoḍaśa cāparāḥ \|*  
*sūcyādikaṃ ca gurave dadyānmantramimaṃ japet \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Afterwards the sixteen ceremonies such as Yatakarma, etc., should be duly performed, and then the devotee should utter the following mantras and make over the needles, etc., to the preceptor.

## \|\| 275.19 \|\|

*namo hiraṇyagarbhāya viśvagarbhāya vai namaḥ \|*  
*carācarasya jagato gṛhabhūtāya vai namaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. I salute you Hiranyagarbha and Vishvagarbha. You are the Soul of the Universe.

## \|\| 275.20 \|\|

*yathā'haṃ janitaḥ pūrvaṃ martyadharmā surottama \|*  
*tvadgarbhasaṃbhavādeṣa divyadeho bhavāmyaham \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. O Best of the Devas! as I was born of you in the mortal world so let me be born again of Divine form on account of my being born again of you. You have created me virtuous and truthful.

## \|\| 275.21-22 \|\|

*caturbhiḥ kalaśairbhūyastataste dvijapuṃgavāḥ \|*  
*snāpayeyuḥ prasannāṅgāḥ sarvābharaṇabhūṣitāḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*devasya tveti mantreṇa sthitasya kanakāsane \|*  
*adya jātasya te'ṅgāni abhiṣekṣyāmahe vayam \|\| 22 \|\|*

21-22. Afterwards that Brahmana should decorate a blessed cow with the ornaments and bathe her with four vases, He should seat her on the golden seat and bathe her by reciting these mantras, viz. — “Devasyartvan” and say ‘I shall now bathe all the limbs born of you’.

## \|\| 275.23 \|\|

*divyenānena vapuṣā ciraṃ jīva sukhī bhava \|*  
*tato hiraṇyagarbhaṃ taṃ tebhyo dadyādvicakṣaṇaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. May all of you live long and happy, holding Divine bodies. Afterwards he should make over that golden thing to the Ritvika Brahmana chosen for the performance of the sacrifice.

## \|\| 275.24 \|\|

*te pūjyāḥ sarvabhāvena bahavo vā tadājñayā \|*  
*tatropakaraṇaṃ sarvaṃ gurave vinivedayet \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. The Ritvikas who may be few or many in number should all be worshipped and the things used in the worship should all be given to the Guru.

## \|\| 275.25 \|\|

*pādukopānahacchatracāmarāsanabhājanam \|*  
*grāmaṃ vā viṣayaṃ vā'pi yadanyadapi saṃbhavet \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Gift of sandals, shoes, umbrella, chamara, seats, utensils, villages, countries and any other thing should also be made according to the means of the devotee.

## \|\| 275.26 \|\|

*anena vidhinā yastu puṇye'hani nivedayet \|*  
*hiraṇyagarbhadānaṃ sa brahmaloke mahīyate \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. One who performs this Hiranyagarbha ordinance on an auspicious day according to the prescribed rites will go to Brahmaloka and be worshipped there and live for koti kalpas,

## \|\| 275.27-28 \|\|

*pureṣu lokapālānāṃ pratimanvantaraṃ vaset \|*  
*kalpakoṭiśataṃ yāvadbrahmaloke mahīyate \|\| 27 \|\|*

*kalikaluṣavimuktaḥ pūjitaḥ siddhasādhyairamaracamaramālābījyamāno-'psarobhiḥ \| \|*  
*pitṛśatamatha bandhūnputrapautrānprapautrānapi narakanimagnāṃstārayedeka eva \|\| 28 \|\|*

27-28. And at the end of the manvantara will reside in the realm of all the Lokapalas one after another, after being freed from the sins of the iron age and adored by the Siddhas, Sadhyas, nymphs. He also liberates from hell one hundred Pitri Lokas. friends, brothers, sons, grandsons, all by himself.

## \|\| 275.29 \|\|

*iti paṭhati ya itthaṃ yaḥ śṛṇotīha samyaṅmadhuripuriva loke pūjyate so'pi siddhaiḥ \| \|*  
*matimapi ca janānāṃ yo dadāti priyārthaṃ vibudhapatijanānāṃ nāyakaḥ syādamogham \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. One who reads or hears this Hiranyagarbha Dina goes to the realm of Vishnu and one who advises others to perform this ordinance, becomes like Indra the Lord of the Devas in heaven, and the leader of the hosts of wise persons.

## Chapter 276

## \|\| 276.1 \|\|

*matsya uvāca*  
*athātaḥ saṃpravakṣyāmi brahmāṇḍavidhimuttamam \|*  
*yacchreṣṭhaṃ sarvadānānāṃ mahāpātakanāśanam \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Matsya said: — “ I shall now explain to you the ways of performing the Brahmanda Mahadana which is the dispeller of all sins of the highest degree and one of the best ordinances ”

## \|\| 276.2-4 \|\|

*puṇyaṃ dinamathā’sādya tulāpuruṣadānavat \|*  
*ṛtviṅmaṇḍapasaṃbhārabhūṣaṇācchādanādikam \|\| 2 \|\|*

*lokeśāvāhanaṃ kuryādadhivāsanakaṃ tathā \|*  
*kuryādviṃśapalādūrdhvamā sahasrācca śaktitaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*kalaśadvayasaṃyuktaṃ brahmāṇḍaṃ kāñcanaṃ budhaḥ \|*  
*diggajāṣṭakasaṃyuktaṃ ṣaḍvedāṅgasamanvitam \|\| 4 \|\|*

2-4. The devotee should make similar arrangements as before of Ritvika, pandal, articles, ornaments, clothing’s, etc., as required for Tuladana and then on an auspicious day he should invoke the Lokapalas and perform Adhivasana, etc. The golden universe (Brahma egg) should be made from 20 palas to 1,000 palas (one pala is equal to four tolas) according to the means of the devotee which and two jars should also be provided. All round the Brahmanda eight Diggajastakas and six Vedanga Shastras should be located.

## \|\| 276.5-7 \|\|

*lokapālāṣṭakopetaṃ madhyasthitacaturmukham \|*  
*śivācyutārkaśikharamumālakṣmīsamanvitam \|\| 5 \|\|*

*vasvādityamarudgarbhaṃ mahāratnasamanvitam \|*  
*vitasteraṅgulaśataṃ yāvadāyāmavistaram \|\| 6 \|\|*

*kauśeyavastrasaṃvītaṃ tiladro ṇopari nyaset \|*  
*tathā'ṣṭādaśa dhānyāni samantātparikalpayet \|\| 7 \|\|*

5-7. The Brahmanda should be made with four-faced Brahma in the centre and all round it should be made the images of the eight Lokapalas, Shiva, Vishnu, Surya, Parvati, Lakshmi, Vasu, Marudgana and with precious jewels. The length of the Brahmanda should be from one cubit to 100 fingers and it should be covered with a piece of silk cloth and located on a mound of 32 seers of sesamum. After that the eight sorts of grains should be placed all round it.

## \|\| 276.8-9 \|\|

*pūrveṇānantaśayanaṃ pradyumnaṃ pūrvadakṣiṇe \|*  
*prakṛtiṃ dakṣiṇe deśe saṃkarṣaṇamataḥ param \|\| 8 \|\|*

*paścime caturo vedānaniruddhamataḥ param \|*  
*agnimuttarato haimaṃ vāsudevamataḥ param \|\| 9 \|\|*

8-9. To the east should be the Lord Sri Hari lying on Ananta, to the south-east Pradyumna. To the south should also be placed the images of Prakriti and Sankarshana; to the west should be located Aniruddha and the four Vedas. To the north should be made the images of Agra and golden Vasudeva.

## \|\| 276.10-11 \|\|

*samantāduḍapīṭhasthānarcayetkāñcanānbudhaḥ \|*  
*sthāpayedvastrasaṃvītānpūrṇakumbhāndaśaiva tu \|\| 10 \|\|*

*daśaiva dhenavo deyāḥ sahemāmbaradohanāḥ \|*  
*pādukopānahacchatracāmarāsanadarpaṇaiḥ \|*  
*bhakṣyabhojyānnadīpekṣuphalamālyānulepanaiḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

10-11. All round the gods should be placed on golden pedestals covered with red cloths after molasses being placed over them (in jars), and then worshipped. Ten jars filled with water and covered with cloths should also be placed. Ten cows should be given away, and the devotee should be bathed along with gold, cloth, milking vessel, sandals, umbrella, chamara, looking-glass, seats, eatables, sugarcane, lighting-bowls, flowers, garlands and sandal, and incense, etc., after the Brahmanas, versed in the Vedas have performed Homa ceremonies with Adhivasa.

## \|\| 276.12-16 \|\|

*homādhivāsanānte ca snāpito vedapuṃgavaiḥ \|*  
*imamuccārayenmantraṃ triḥ kṛtvā'tha pradakṣiṇam \|\| 12 \|\|*

*namo'stu viśveśvara viśvadhāma jagatsavitre bhagavannamaste \|*  
*saptarṣilokāmarabhūtaleśa garbheṇa sārdhaṃ vitarābhirakṣām \|\| 13 \|\|*

*ye duḥkhitāste sukhino bhavantu prayāntu pāpāni carācarāṇām \|*  
*tvaddānaśastrāhatapātakānāṃ brahmāṇḍadoṣāḥ pralayaṃ vrajantu \|\| 14 \|\|*

*evaṃ praṇamyāmaraviśvagarbhaṃ dadyāddvijebhyo daśadhā vibhajya \|*  
*bhāgadvayaṃ tatra guroḥ prakalpya samaṃ bhajeccheṣamanukrameṇa \|\| 15 \|\|*

*svalpe ca homaṃ gurureka eva kuryādathaikāgnividhānayuktyā \|*  
*sa eva saṃpūjyatamo'lpavitte yathoktavastrābharaṇādikena \|\| 16 \|\|*

12-16. Lord of the universe, Vishvadhama! I salute you. The devotee, thus bathed, would circumambulate and repeat the following mantra You are the Lord of all of the seven Rishis, of the Immortals and of this earth. Protect me. Deva! Let the aggrieved and sinners also become blessed by your grace on their calamities being cut off by the blade of ordinances and charities performed in your name. Let the sins of all the beings moving and non-moving be destroyed. Even those who are freed from their sins by the merit of their Mahadana, be cured of all their faults and defects. After reciting this prayer and saluting Sri Bari, all the articles of worship should be divided into ten parts and then two parts are to be given to the Guru and the rest given away to the Brahmanas In an ordinance in which only a small amount is spent by the devotee, only the preceptor should offer libations into the sacrificial fire as is done in Agnihotra and he should be given away all the cloths, ornaments, etc.

## \|\| 276.17 \|\|

*itthaṃ ya etadakhilaṃ puruṣo'tra kuryādbrahmāṇḍadānamadhigamya mahadvimānam \|*  
*nirdhūtakalmaṣaviśuddhatanurmurārerānandakṛtpadamupaiti sahāpsarobhiḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. One who thus performs this Brahmanda Mahadana is liberated from all sins and goes to the region of Vishnu seated on a chariot and Is adored by the nymphs.

## \|\| 276.18 \|\|

*saṃtārayetpitṛpitāmahaputrapautrabandhupriyātithikalatraśatāṣṭakaṃ saḥ \|*  
*brahmāṇḍadānaśakalīkṛtapātakaughamānandayecca jananīkulamapyaśeṣam \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. By the glory of this Brahmanda ordinance the devotee liberates the whole family of mother and father and grandfather, grandmother, brethren, wife, son, grandson, friends, acquaintances and guests and gives pleasure and happiness to all of them.

## \|\| 276.19 \|\|

*iti paṭhati śṛṇoti vā ya etatsurabhavaneṣu gṛheṣu dhārmikāṇām \|*  
*matimapi ca dadāti modate'sāvamarapaterbhavane sahāpsarobhiḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. One who reads this in a temple or in a virtuous man’s premises or hears about it or advises others to perform this ordinance goes to the realm of Indra where he enjoys the company of the nymphs.

## Chapter 277

## \|\| 277.1 \|\|

*matsya uvāca*  
*kalpapādapadānākhyamataḥ paramanuttamam \|*  
*mahādānaṃ pravakṣyāmi sarvapātakanāśanam \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Matsya said “ Now I shall tell you about the Kalpapadapa Maha Dana which is also the dispeller of all sins.”

## \|\| 277.2 \|\|

*puṇyaṃ dinamathā’sādya tulāpuruṣadānavat \|*  
*puṇyāhavācanaṃ kṛtvā lokeśāvāhanaṃ tathā \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. On an auspicious day the devotee should invoke the Lokapalas of the Punyaha-Vachana as prescribed in the Tuladana ordinance.

## \|\| 277.3-4 \|\|

*ṛtviṅmaḍapasaṃbhārabhūṣaṇācchādanādikam \|*  
*kāñcanaṃ kārayedvṛkṣaṃ nānāphalasamanvitam \|\| 3 \|\|*

*nānāvihagavastrāṇi bhūṣaṇāni ca kārayet \|*  
*śaktitattripalādūrdhvamāsahasraṃ prakalpayet \|\| 4 \|\|*

3-4. The Ritvikas, pandal, ornaments, cloths, &c., should also be arranged as before. A golden tree yielding all desires (Kalpa-padapa) of various kinds of fruits should be made; and also birds sitting on that tree; the cloths and various ornaments should also be made. The tree should be of four to one thousand pals according to the means of the devotee. The gold used is mixed with alloy.

## \|\| 277.5 \|\|

*ardhakḷptasuvarṇasya kārayetkalpapādapam \|*  
*guḍaprasthopariṣṭācca sitavastrayugānvitam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. It should be located on a mound of molasses of 32 seers, covered with a piece of white cloth.

## \|\| 277.6-7 \|\|

*brahmaviṣṇuśivopetaṃ pañcaśākhaṃ sabhāskaram \|*  
*kāmadevamadhastācca sakalatraṃ prakalpayet \|\| 6 \|\|*

*saṃtānaṃ pūrvatastadvatturīyāṃśena kalpayet \|*  
*mandāraṃ dakṣiṇe bhāge śriyā sārdhaṃ ghṛtopari \|\| 7 \|\|*

6-7. Five branches along with the images of Brahma, Vishnu, Shiva, Surya and Cupid should be made, on the lower branch should be placed Cupid with Rati. Santanaka tree, ¼ of the golden Kalpa tree, should be located to the east of the latter. Mandara tree along with an image of Lakshmi should be located on a pot of clarified butter in the south, Parijata tree along with the image of Savitri should be located to the west on a mound of cumin seed (Jiraka). Similarly, Harichandana tree should be located to the north along with Surabhi cow on a mound of sesamum. The tree is to be adorned on one-fourth part of it with flowers.

## \|\| 277.8 \|\|

*paścime pāribhadraṃ tu sāvitr! yā saha jīrake \|*  
*surabhīsaṃyutaṃ tadvattileṣu haricandanam \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. All the other trees should be made of the golden Kalpa tree and covered with a yellow cloth and decorated with flowers, sugarcane, etc.

## \|\| 277.9-11 \|\|

*turīyāṃśena kurvīta saumyena phalasaṃyutam \|*  
*kauśeyavastrasaṃvītānikṣumālyaphalānvitān \|\| 9 \|\|*

*tathā'ṣṭau pūrṇakalaśānpādukāśanabhājanam \|*  
*dīpikopānahacchatracāmarāsanasaṃyutam \|\| 10 \|\|*

*phalamālyayutaṃ tadvadupariṣṭādvitānakam \|*  
*tathā'ṣṭādaśa dhānyāni samantātparikalpayet \|\| 11 \|\|*

9-11. Then eight jars filled with water and provided with, fruits, should be placed near the tree with a pair of sandals, cooking-utensils, lamps, shoes, umbrella, chamara, seats, etc. After placing fruits, flowers, and buntings over them, 8 or 10 sorts of grains should be put in all the directions. Over the tree a canopy is to be stretched, decked with fruits and garlands of flowers.

## \|\| 277.12 \|\|

*homādhivāsanānte ca snāpito vedapuṃgavaiḥ \|*  
*triḥ pradakṣiṇamāvṛtya mantrametamudīrayet \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. After Homa ceremony and Adhivasa, the devotee should get himself bathed by the Brahmanas versed in the Vedas with the recitation of the sacred Vedic hymns and then he is to utter the following mantra after circumambulating the tree thrice:

## \|\| 277.13 \|\|

*namaste kalpavṛkṣāya cintitārthapradāyine \|*  
*viśvaṃbharāya devāya namaste viśvamūrtaye \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. “Salutations to the Kalpa tree, the giver of the desired objects, the protector of the universe and the image of the Creation.

## \|\| 277.15 \|\|

*tvamevāmṛtasarvasvamanantaḥ puruṣo'vyayaḥ \|*  
*saṃtānādyairupetaḥ sanpāhi saṃsārasāgarāt \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. “You are Brahma;, the Lord of the universe. You are the Lord of the day. You are the supreme soul; therefore be pleased to protect me- You are the Immoveable, the soul of the universe. You are the Sun; you are the material; yon are the immaterial; you are the Highest cause. Salutations to you. You are the nectar, you are the Infinite, you are the undecaying Person. In conjunction with Santanas be gracious enough to protect me and deliver me from this ocean of world.”

## \|\| 277.16 \|\|

*evamāmantr! ya taṃ dadyādgurave kalpapādapam \|*  
*catubhyaścātha ṛtvigbhyaḥ saṃtānādīnprakalpayet \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. After this, the Kalpa tree should be given to the preceptor and the other trees should be given to the four Ritvikas.

## \|\| 277.17 \|\|

*svalpe tvekāgnivatkuryādgurave cābhipūjanam \|*  
*na vittaśāṭhyaṃ kurvīta na ca vismayavānbhavet \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. If the devotee cannot afford much money, he should worship the preceptor only. He should free himself from feelings of avarice and not be miserly in the expenditure of money.

## \|\| 277.18 \|\|

*anena vidhinā yastu pradadyātkalpapādapam \|*  
*sarvapāpavinirmuktaḥ so'śvamedhaphalaṃ bhavet \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. One who makes this Maha Dan in this way, obtains the merits of the Ashvamedha sacrifice.

## \|\| 277.19 \|\|

*apsarobhiḥ parivṛtaḥ siddhacāraṇakiṃnaraiḥ \|*  
*bhūtānbhavyāṃśca manujāṃstārayedgotrasaṃyutān \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. He is also adored by the nymphs, the Siddhas, the Charanas and the Kinnaras. Besides that he liberates his manes and the members of the present and future generations.

## \|\| 277.20 \|\|

*stūyamāno divaḥ pṛṣṭhe putrapautraprapautrakaiḥ \|*  
*vimānenārkavarṇena viṣṇulokaṃ sa gacchati \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. After being seated in a Vimana resplendent like the Sun, he goes to the realm of Lord Vishnu venerated by the Devas.

## \|\| 277.21 \|\|

*divi kalpaśataṃ tiṣṭhedrā jarājo bhavettataḥ \|*  
*nārāyaṇabalopeto nārāyaṇaparāyaṇaḥ \|*  
*nārāyaṇakathāsakto nārāyaṇapuraṃ vrajet \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Thereafter residing for hundreds of Kalpas as the King of Kings in Heaven and then through the grace of Narayana, he becomes His devotee and inclined to hear about Him when he goes to the city of Narayana.

## \|\| 277.22 \|\|

*yo vā paṭhetsakalakalpatarupradānaṃ yo vā śṛṇoti puruṣo'lpadhanaḥ smaredvā \|*  
*so'pīndra lokamadhigamya sahāpsarobhirmanvantaraṃ vasati pāpavimuktadehaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. One who reads about it or remembers it also gets himself freed from sins and goes to the realm of India and lives there for one Manvantara happily with Apsaras.

## Chapter 278

## \|\| 278.2-4 \|\|

*puṇyāṃ tithiṃ samāsādya yugamanvantarādikām \|*  
*payovrataṃ trirātraṃ syādekarātramathāpi vā \|\| 2 \|\|*

*lokeśāvāhanaṃ kuryāttulāpuruṣadānavat \|*  
*puṇyāhavācanaṃ kuryāddhomaḥ kāryastathaiva ca \|\| 3 \|\|*

*ṛtviṅmaṇḍapasaṃbhārabhūṣaṇācchādanādikam \|*  
*vṛṣaṃ lakṣaṇasaṃyuktaṃ vedimadhye'dhivāsayet \|\| 4 \|\|*

2-4. Matsya said: — “I shall now tell you about the Gosahasra Maha Dana the dispeller of all great sins and the yielder of all desires,” — On an auspicious day before carrying out this ordinance devotee should live on milk for three nights or one. Afterwards the Lokapalas should he invoked as is done in Tuladana and Homa ceremony and adhivasa should be performed. Ritviks, Mandapas, articles, ornaments and covering cloths all are to be arranged; and within the enclosure of the Vedi, a bull with all auspicious signs is to he brought. Outside the Vedi then a thousand cows with their horns mounted with gold and hoofs with silver, should be placed after being adorned with ornaments, cloths, flowers and garlands.

## \|\| 278.5-10 \|\|

*gosahasrādviniṣkṛṣya gavāṃ daśakameva ca \|*  
*gosahasraṃ bahiḥ kuryādvastramālyavibhūṣitam \|*  
*suvarṇaśṛṅgābharaṇaṃ raupyapādasamanvitam \|\| 5 \|\|*

*antaḥ praveśya daśakaṃ vastramālyaiśca pūjayet \|*  
*suvarṇaghaṇṭikāyuktaṃ kāṃsyadohanakānvitam \|\| 6 \|\|*

*suvarṇatilakopetaṃ hemapaṭṭairalaṃkṛtam \|*  
*kauśeyavastrasaṃvītaṃ mālyagandhasamanvitam \|\| 7 \|\|*

*hemaratnamayaiḥ śṛṅgaiścāmarairupaśobhitam \|*  
*pādukopānahacchatrabhājanāsanasaṃyutam \|\| 8 \|\|*

*gavāṃ daśakamadhye syātkāñcano nandikeśvaraḥ \|*  
*kauśeyavastrasaṃvīto nānābharaṇabhūṣitaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*lavaṇadro ṇaśikhare mālyekṣuphalasaṃyutaḥ \|*  
*kuryātpalaśatādūrdhvaṃ sarvametadaśeṣataḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

5-10. Then after decorating ten cows with cloths, garlands, golden-bells, milking-pots of bell-metal, gold plait and red cloth, the devotee should arrange a pair- of sandals, shoes, umbrella, vessels, seats, etc., these are to be worshipped and in their midst should be made a golden bull, Nandikeshvara which should be located on a mound of salt after being covered with a silken cloth and decorated with ornaments. Sugarcane and fruits should be placed closed by. The bull, etc., should not be less than one hundred palas in weight and should go up to three thousand palas. In the case of gift of one hundred (100) cows, one-tenth of that should he arranged for.

## \|\| 278.11-12 \|\|

*śaktitaḥ palasāhasratritayaṃ yāvadeva tu \|*  
*gośate'pi daśāṃśena sarvametatsamācaret \|\| 11 \|\|*

*puṇyakālaṃ samāsādya gītamaṅgalaniḥsvanaiḥ \|*  
*sarvauṣadhyudakasnānasnāpito vedapuṃgavaiḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-12. On an auspicious day auspicious Vedic songs should he sung and then the devotee should bathe in water mixed with herbs and medicinal plants. The Brahmanas accomplished in the Vedas should bathe the devotee after which the latter should recite the following formulas by holding a handful of flowers “O Rohini’s, the inhabitants of the Lokas You are the form of the Universe;. you are the world-mother; salutations to you!

## \|\| 278.13-18 \|\|

*imamuccārayenmantraṃ gṛhītakusumāñjaliḥ \|*  
*namo'stu viśvamūrtibhyo viśvamātṛbhya eva ca \|\| 13 \|\|*

*lokādhivāsinābhyaśca rohiṇībhyo namo namaḥ \|*  
*gavāmaṅgeṣu tiṣṭhanti bhūvanānyekaviṃśatiḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*brahmādayastathā devā rohiṇyaḥ pāntu mātaraḥ \|*  
*gāvo me agrataḥ santu gāvaḥ pṛṣṭhata eva ca \|\| 15 \|\|*

*gāvaḥ śirasi me nityaṃ gavāṃ madhye vasāmyaham \|*  
*yasmāttvaṃ vṛṣarūpeṇa dharma eva sanātanaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*aṣṭamūrteradhiṣṭhānamataḥ pāhi sanātana \|*  
*ityāmantr! ya tato dadyādgurave nandikeśvaram \|\| 17 \|\|*

*sarvopakaraṇopetaṃ goyutaṃ ca vicakṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*ṛtvigbhyo dhenumekaikāṃ daśakādvinivedayet \|\| 18 \|\|*

13-18. “O Cow-Mother! within your body are the 21 bhuvans, Devas, Brahma, etc., therefore protect me. O Cows! be on my front; be at my back and also on my bead. I am living in the midst of Cows for you are existing incarnate in the form of Vrisha, the eternal Dharma. You are the resting place of the eight Murtis. Therefore, O Eternal one! protect me.” Afterwards the golden bull Nandikeshvara should be given away with all materials to the preceptor and a cow out of the ten should be given to the Ritvikas. Then each of the Ritvikas and the priests should be given 100, 50, 20 or 10 cows and with their permission other Brahmanas should also be given ten or five cows each. One cow should not be given to many. This is sinful. A sensible devotee eager for his health and prosperity should give many cows to one man.

## \|\| 278.19-23 \|\|

*gavāṃ ca śatamekaikaṃ tadardhaṃ vā'tha viṃśatim \|*  
*daśa pañcātha vā dadyādanyebhyastadanujñayā \|\| 19 \|\|*

*naikā bahubhyo dātavyā yato doṣakarī bhavet \|*  
*bahvyaścaikasya dātavyā dhīmatā’rogyavṛddhaye \|\| 20 \|\|*

*payovrataḥ punastiṣṭhedekāhaṃ gosahasradaḥ \|*  
*śrāvayecchṛṇuyādvā'pi mahādānānukīrtanam \|\| 21 \|\|*

*taddine brahmacārī syādyadīcchedvipulāṃ śriyam \|*  
*anena vidhinā yastu gosahasraprado bhavet \|*  
*sarvapāpavinirmuktaḥ siddhacāraṇasevitaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*vimānenārkavarṇena kiṅkiṇījālamālinā \|*  
*sarveṣāṃ lokapālānāṃ loka saṃpūjyate'maraiḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

19-23. After thus giving away one thousand cows, the devotee should live again on milk for a day and one eager for a store of wealth should lead a life of celibacy on the day of performing this ordinance and hearing the glories of this Dana and making it heard by others. One who thus makes the gift of 1,000 cows is liberated from all sins and honoured by the Siddhas, Charanas, etc., is venerated in the realm of all the Lokapalas after being seated in a chariot shining like the sun and decorated with a beautiful network of bells, etc. He remains in those realms along with his sons and grandsons for a Manvantara in each. Thus he goes beyond the seven realms and attains the domain of Shiva.

## \|\| 278.24-25 \|\|

*pratimanvantaraṃ tiṣṭhetputrapautrasamanvitaḥ \|*  
*sapta lokānatikramya tataḥ śivapuraṃ vrajet \|\| 24 \|\|*

*śatamekottaraṃ tadvatpitriṇāṃ tārayedbudhaḥ \|*  
*mātāmahānāṃ tadvacca putrapautrasamanvitaḥ \|*  
*yāvatkalpaśataṃ tiṣṭhedrā jarājo bhavetpunaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

24-25. Besides this he liberates 101 manes and grandmothers, etc. He reigns a king for 100 Kalpas; after that he becomes devoted to Shiva and performing one hundred Ashvamedha sacrifices attains the realm of Lord Vishnu and becomes liberated from bondage.

## \|\| 278.26-27 \|\|

*aśvamedhaśataṃ kuryācchivadhyānaparāyaṇaḥ \|*  
*vaiṣṇavaṃ yogamāsthāya tato mucyeta bandhanāt \|\| 26 \|\|*

*pitaraścābhinandanti gosahasrapradaṃ sutam \|*  
*api syātsa kule'smākaṃ putro dauhitra eva vā \|*  
*gosahasraprado bhūtvā narakāduddhariṣyati \|\| 27 \|\|*

26-27. The manes also eagerly look forward to a son who would make a gift of 1,000 cows. They wish that a son or a grandson should liberate them by making such a gift. One who does so is ministered to by his manes in every respect.

## \|\| 278.28 \|\|

*tasya karmakaro vā syādapi dra ṣṭā tathaiva ca \|*  
*saṃsārasāgarādasmādyo'smānsaṃtārayiṣyati \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. One who reads about this or thinks about it, will go to the realm of Indra after leaving his mortal evil and liberated from all sins.

## Chapter 279

## \|\| 279.1 \|\|

*matsya uvāca*  
*athātaḥ saṃpravakṣyāmi kāmadhenuvidhiṃ param \|*  
*sarvakāmapradaṃ nriṇāṃ mahāpātakanāśanam \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Matsya said: — “I shall now tell you about the Kamadhenu Dan which fulfills all the desires of the people after driving away all great sins.”

## \|\| 279.3-6 \|\|

*svalpe tvekāgnivatkuryādgururekaḥ samāhitaḥ \|*  
*kāñcanasyātiśuddhasya dhenuṃ vatsaṃ ca kārayet \|\| 3 \|\|*

*uttamā palasāhasrā tadardhena tu madhyamā \|*  
*kanīyasī tadardhena kāmadhenuḥ prakīrtitā \|\| 4 \|\|*

*śaktitastripalādūrdhvamaśakto'pīha kārayet \|*  
*vedyāṃ kṛṣṇājinaṃ nyasya guḍaprasthasamanvitam \|\| 5 \|\|*

*nyasedupari tāṃ dhenuṃ mahāratnairalaṃkṛtām \|*  
*kumbhāṣṭakasamopetāṃ nānāphalasamanvitām \|\| 6 \|\|*

3-6. First the Lokapalas should be invoked and then Homa and Adhivas should be performed after erecting Kundas, pandal, and an altar. If the devotee cannot afford much money then only the preceptor may offer sacrificial oblations as is done in Ekagni ceremony. In this ceremony a cow and her calf are to be made of pure gold. To give away Kamadhenu with one thousand fruits is the best; with 500 fruits is middling; and with 250 fruits is Kanishtha. The Kamadhenu should be made of not less than three tolas of gold, whether the devotee is able or not. A black deerskin should be spread on a mound of molasses and above it should be placed the cow decorated with various kinds of gems. Close to it should be placed eight pitchers full of water containing jewels and various flowers.

## \|\| 279.7-9 \|\|

*tathā'ṣṭādaśa dhānyāni samantātparikalpayet \|*  
*ikṣudaṇḍāṣṭakaṃ tadvannānāphalasamanvitam \|*  
*bhājanaṃ cā'sanaṃ tadvattāmradohanakaṃ tathā \|\| 7 \|\|*

*kauśeyavastradvayasaṃyutāṃ gāṃ dīpātapatrābharaṇābhirāmām \|*  
*sacāmarāṃ kuṇḍalinīṃ saghaṇṭāṃ suvarṇaśṛṅgīṃ parirūpyapādām \|\| 8 \|\|*

*rasaiśca sarvaiḥ parito'bhijuṣṭāṃ haridra yā puṣpaphalairanekaiḥ \|*  
*ajājikustumburuśarkarādibhirvitānakaṃ copari pañcavarṇam \|\| 9 \|\|*

7-9. Round it should be placed 8 or 10 sorts of grains, sugarcane, fruits, utensils, seats, copper milking-pot, red cloth, lamp, umbrella, chamara, ear-rings, bell, golden horns foils, silver hoofs, turmeric, cumin seed, daniya, sugar, etc. An awning of five colours is to be spread over the altar. The cow is to be anointed all over well with turmeric, etc.

## \|\| 279.10 \|\|

*snātastato maṅgalavedaghoṣaiḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya sapuṣpahastaḥ \|*  
*āvāhayettāṃ guruṇoktamantrairdvijāya dadyādatha darbhapāṇiḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Then after the chant of Vedic hymns, the devotee should make three circumambulations, get himself bathed and taking a handful of kusha grass and flowers he should invoke the Kamadhenu while the preceptor recites the Vedic mantras.

## \|\| 279.11-13 \|\|

*tvaṃ sarvadevagaṇamandiramaṅgabhūtā viśveśvari tripathagodadhiparvatānām \|*  
*tvaddānaśastraśakalīkṛtapātakaughaḥ prāpto'smi nirvṛtimatīva parāṃ namāmi \|\| 11 \|\|*

*loke yathepsitaphalārthavidhāyinīṃ tvāmāsādya ko hi bhavaduḥ-khamupaiti martyaḥ \| \|*  
*saṃsāraduḥkhaśamanāya yatasva kāmaṃ tvāṃ kāmadhenumiti devagaṇā vadanti \|\| 12 \|\|*

*āmantr! ya śīlakularūpaguṇānvitāya viprāya yaḥ kanakadhenumimāṃ pradadyāt \|*  
*prāpnoti dhāma sa puraṃdaradevajuṣṭaṃ kanyāgaṇaiḥ parivṛtaḥ padamindumauleḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

11-13. He should say, “O, Kamadhenu! You on the temple of all the Devas are; you are Tripathaga; you are the essence of oceans and mountains you are the protector of the universe. I have attained the final bliss by making a gift of you and have been liberated from all the sins. I salute you. Who is there that undergoes sufferings when he has attained you? You are Kamadhenu because you drive away all ills and sufferings.

One who thus gives away a Kamadhenu to a Brahmana of noble lineage, of good qualities and handsome appearance goes to the realm of Indra inhabited by the Devas.

## Chapter 280

## \|\| 280.1 \|\|

*matsya uvāca*  
*athātaḥ saṃpravakṣyāmi hiraṇyāśvavidhiṃ param \|*  
*yasya pradānādbhuvane cānantaṃ phalamaśnute \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Matsya said: — “I shall now tell you the sacred Hiranyashva Maha Dana which confers numberless benefits on the devotee.”

## \|\| 280.2 \|\|

*puṇyāṃ tithimathā’sādya kṛtvā brāhmaṇavācanam \|*  
*lokeśāvāhanaṃ kuryāttulāpuruṣadānavat \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. On an auspicious' day the devotee should invoke the and recite Brahmana Vachanam as done in Tuladana.

## \|\| 280.3 \|\|

*ṛtviṅmaṇḍapasaṃbhārabhūṣaṇācchādanādikam \|*  
*svalpe tvekāgnivatkuryāddhemavājimakhaṃ budhaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Afterwards Ritvikas, pandal, ornaments, cloths, &c., should be arranged for as before. If the devotee cannot spend more money then he should get a sacrifice performed by the Guru only according to the rite.

## \|\| 280.4-7 \|\|

*sthāpayedvedimadhye tu kṛṣṇājinatilopari \|*  
*kauśeyavastrasaṃvītaṃ kārayeddhemavājinam \|\| 4 \|\|*

*śaktitastripalādūrdhvamā sahasrapalādbudhaḥ \|*  
*pādukopānahacchatracāmarāsanabhājanaiḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*pūrṇakumbhāṣṭakopetaṃ mālyekṣuphalasaṃyutam \|*  
*śayyāṃ sopaskarāṃ tadvaddhemamārtaṇḍasaṃyutām \|\| 6 \|\|*

*tataḥ sarvauṣadhisnānasnāpito vedapuṃgavaiḥ \|*  
*imamuccārayenmantraṃ gṛhītakusumāñjaliḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

4-7. Afterwards a golden horse should be made and placed on a heap of sesamum placed on the skin of a black deer over the Vedi (altar). It should then be covered with a silk cloth. The horse should be made from three to 1,000 (one thousand) tolas of gold according to the means of the devotee. Sandals, shoes, umbrella, chamara, seats, utensils, eight (8) pitchers full of water, garlands, sugarcane, fruits, bedstead with all its equipment’s, and an image of the sun made of gold, should be placed near it. Then the devotee should get himself bathed by the Vedic Brahmanas (accompanied with the recitation of the Vedic hymns) with water in which some medicinal herbs have been put and then taking a handful of flowers recite the following mantra

## \|\| 280.8 \|\|

*namaste sarvadeveśa vedāharaṇalampaṭa \|*  
*vājirūpeṇa māmasmātpāhi saṃsārasāgarāt \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. “O, Sarvadevesha! O Vishnu, the revealer of the sacred Vedas; please work out my salvation from this mundane ocean. Salutations to you.

## \|\| 280.9 \|\|

*tvameva saptadhā bhūtvā chandorūpeṇa bhāskara \|*  
*yasmādbhāsayase lokānataḥ pāhi sanātana \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. “O Sun! You are divided into seven parts, the seven Chhandas whereby you illumine all the Lokas. You illumine the universe. Pray protect me. O Eternal one!

## \|\| 280.10-11 \|\|

*evamuccārya gurave tamaśvaṃ vinivedayet \|*  
*dattvā pāpakṣayādbhānorlokamabhyeti śāśvatam \|\| 10 \|\|*

*gobhirvibhavataḥ sarvānṛtvijaścāpi pūjayet \|*  
*sarvadhānyopakaraṇaṃ gurave vinivedayet \|\| 11 \|\|*

10-11. While reciting this mantra, the devotee is to make over the golden horse to the preceptor. One who does so becomes freed of sins and attains the realm of the Sun. Afterwards the devotee should give away cows to the Ritvikas and various sorts of grains to the preceptor.

## \|\| 280.12 \|\|

*sarvaṃ śayyādikaṃ dattvā bhuñjītātailameva hi \|*  
*purāṇaśravaṇaṃ tadvatkārayedbhojanādanu \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. On the conclusion of the ceremony the devotee should not take anything cooked in oil. He should hear the Puranas and feed the Brahmanas.

## \|\| 280.13 \|\|

*imaṃ hiraṇyāśvavidhiṃ karoti yaḥ puṇyaṃ samāsādya dinaṃ narendra \|*  
*vimuktapāpaḥ sa puraṃ murāreḥ prāpnoti siddhairabhipūjitaḥ san \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. One who observes this ordinance is freed from all his sins and attains the domain of Vishnu, and is honoured by the Siddhas.

## \|\| 280.14-15 \|\|

*iti paṭhati ya etaddhemavājipradānaṃ sakalakaluṣamuktaḥ so'śvamedhena yuktaḥ \| \|*  
*kanakamayavimānenārkalokaṃ prayāti tridaśapativadhūbhiḥ pūjyate yo'bhipaśyet \|\| 14 \|\|*

*yo vā śṛṇoti puruṣo'lpadhanaḥ smaredvā hemāśvadānamabhinandayatīha loka \| \|*  
*sā'pi prayāti hatakalmaṣaśuddhadehaḥ sthānaṃ puraṃdaramaheśvaradevajuṣṭam \|\| 15 \|\|*

14-15. One who reads or hears this Hiranyashva ordinance or witnesses it or thinks of it or one who is poor but yearns to perform it, is liberated from all his sins and goes to the region of Sun with a bright body seated in a Vimana shining like the Sun, where he is a worshipped by the celestial women.

## Chapter 281

## \|\| 281.1 \|\|

*matsya uvāca*  
*athātaḥ saṃpravakṣyāmi mahādānamanuttamam \|*  
*puṇyamaśvarathaṃ nāma mahāpātakanāśanam \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Matsya said: — “I shall now tell you about the auspicious Ashvaratha Maha Dana which is the dispeller of all great sins.”

## \|\| 281.2 \|\|

*puṇyaṃ dinamathā'sādya kṛtvā brāhmaṇavācanam \|*  
*lokeśāvāhanaṃ kuryāttulāpuruṣadānavat \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. On an auspicious day after Svastivachana the Lokapalas should be invoked by the sacrificer as is done in course of Tuladana.

## \|\| 281.3-11 \|\|

*ṛtviṅmaṇḍapasaṃbhārabhūṣaṇācchādanādikam \|*  
*kṛṣṇājine tilānkṛtvā kāñcanaṃ sthāpayedra tham \|\| 3 \|\|*

*saptāśvaṃ caturaśvaṃ vā catuścakraṃ sakūbaram \|*  
*aindra nīlena kumbhena dhvajarūpeṇa saṃyutam \|\| 4 \|\|*

*lokapālāṣṭakopetaṃ padmarāgadalānvitam \|*  
*caturaḥ pūrṇakalaśāndhānyānyaṣṭādaśaiva tu \|\| 5 \|\|*

*kauśeyavastrasaṃyuktamupariṣṭādvitānakam \|*  
*mālyekṣuphalasaṃyuktaṃ puruṣeṇa samanvitam \|\| 6 \|\|*

*yo yadbhaktaḥ pumānkuryātsa tannāmnā'dhivāsanam \|*  
*chatracāmarakauśeyavastropānahapādukam \|\| 7 \|\|*

*gobhirvibhavataḥ sārdhaṃ dadyācca śayanādikam \|*  
*abhāvāttripalādūrdhvaṃ śaktitaḥ kārayedbudhaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*aśvāṣṭakena saṃyuktaṃ caturbhiratha vājibhiḥ \|*  
*dvābhyāmapi yutaṃ dadyāddhemasiṃhadhvajānvitam \|\| 9 \|\|*

*cakrarakṣāvubhau tasya turagasthāvathāśvinau \|*  
*puṇyakālamathāvāpya pūrvavatsnāpito dvijaiḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*triḥ pradakṣiṇamāvṛtya gṛhītakusumāñjaliḥ \|*  
*śuklamālyāmbaro dadyādimaṃ mantramudīrayet \|\| 11 \|\|*

3-11. Afterwards, Ritvikas, mandapa, necessary articles, ornaments, etc., should be brought, and then a golden chariot- should be put on the black deer skin over which the sesamums are scattered. There should be four wheels in the chariot and the number of horses should be four or eight. A flag-staff and a pitcher of sapphire should be made and the eight Lokapalas ' should be made of lapis-lazuli. Four pitchers full of water and 18 kinds of grains should be placed; and the chariot should be covered with silk cloth and there is to be a canopy over the altar. Afterwards there should be placed on the chariot garlands, sugarcane, fruits, and Purushas. The devotee should consecrate the Deity to whom he is devoted. Then umbrella, chamara, red cloth, ghee, cow, bedstead with all the necessary equipment’s should be supplied. The chariot should be made of over three palas to one bhara of gold according to the means of the devotee. Eight, four or only a pair of horses may be made. The banner should be adorned with a lion of gold. The two Ashvini Kumaras riding on horses should be made to go to and fro as guards of the chariot wheels. The devotee should then bathe as before with the recitation of the Vedic hymns and then make three circumambulations and after holding a handful of flowers and putting on garlands of white flowers and white clothes recite the following mantras.

## \|\| 281.12-13 \|\|

*namo namaḥ pāpavināśanāya viśvātmane vedaturaṃgamāya \|*  
*dhāmnāmadhīśāya divākarāya pāpaughadāvānala dehi śāntim \|\| 12 \|\|*

*vasvaṣṭakādityamarudgaṇānāṃ tvameva dhātā paramaṃ nidhānam \|*  
*yatastato me hṛdayaṃ prayātu dharmaikatānatvamaghaughanāśāt \|\| 13 \|\|*

12-13. “O, Lord Sun! the Soul of the universe, the Destroyer of all sins, the Ocean and Master of splendour or brilliancy, whose chariot is drawn. by the horses of the Vedas, I salute you. Give me peace. You axe the creator and supporter of the eight Vasus and the Maruts. Dispel my sins, and infuse virtue in me.”

## \|\| 281.14 \|\|

*iti turagarathapradānametadbhavabhayasūdanamatra yaḥ karoti \|*  
*sa kaluṣapaṭalairvimuktadehaḥ paramamupaiti padaṃ pinākapāṇeḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. One who thus gives away a golden chariot attains beatitude after being freed from all his sins.

## \|\| 281.15 \|\|

*dedīpyamānavapuṣā vijitaprabhāvamākramya maṇḍalamakhaṇḍitacaṇḍabhānoḥ \| \|*  
*siddhāṅganānayanaṣaṭpadapīyamānavaktrāmbujo'mbujabhavena ciraṃ sahā’ste \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. He becomes illustrious and goes to the realm of the Lord Shiva after attaining and going beyond the domain of the piercing Sun where the nymphs like the black bees drink the aroma of his lotus like face and live there with Ambuja Bhava.

## \|\| 281.16 \|\|

*iti paṭhati śṛṇoti vā ya itthaṃ kanakaturagarathapradānamasmin \|*  
*na sa narakapuraṃ vrajetkadācinnarakariporbhavanaṃ prayāti bhūyaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. One who reads or hears about this ordinance never goes to hell He repeatedly goes to heaven.

## Chapter 282

## \|\| 282.1 \|\|

*matsya uvāca*  
*athātaḥ saṃpravakṣyāmi hemahastirathaṃ śubham \|*  
*yasya pradānādbhavanaṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ yāti mānavaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Matsya said: — “I shall now tell you about the greatly auspicious Hemahasti Ratha Maha Dana by performing which one attains the realm of Lord Vishnu.”

## \|\| 282.2-4 \|\|

*puṇyāṃ tithimathā’sādya tulāpuruṣadānavat \|*  
*vipravācanakaṃ kuryāllokeśāvāhanaṃ budhaḥ \|*  
*ṛtviṅmaṇḍapasaṃbhārabhūṣaṇācchādanādikam \|\| 2 \|\|*

*atrāpyupoṣitastadvadbrāhmaṇaiḥ saha bhojanam \|*  
*kuryātpuṣparathākāraṃ kāñcanaṃ maṇimaṇḍitam \|\| 3 \|\|*

*valabhībhirvicitrābhiścatuścakrasamanvitam \|*  
*kṛṣṇājine tiladro ṇaṃ kṛtvā saṃsthāpayedra tham \|\| 4 \|\|*

2-4. On an auspicious day after Svastivachana, the devotee should invoke the Lokapalas as prescribed in course of Tuladana. Then he should find out Ritvikas, canopy, ornaments, cloth, etc., and observe a fast. He should break his fast with the Brahman as. A chariot of the shape of Pushpaka (airplane) should be made of gold studded with precious stones. It should have artistic tiled covering on domes and four wheels. Then a mound of sesamum should be placed on a black deer skin and above it should be located the chariot

## \|\| 282.5 \|\|

*lokapālāṣṭakopetaṃ brahmārkaśivasaṃyutam \|*  
*madhye nārāyaṇopetaṃ lakṣmīpuṣṭisamanvitam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Round it the eight Lokapalas, Brahma, Sun and Shiva should be made and in the centre should be made the image of Narayana with the Goddess Lakshmi,

## \|\| 282.6-7 \|\|

*tathā'ṣṭādaśa dhānyāni bhājanāsanacandanaiḥ \|*  
*dīpikopānahacchatradarpaṇaṃ pādukānvitam \|\| 6 \|\|*

*dhvaje tu garuḍaṃ kuryātkūbarāgre vināyakam \|*  
*nānāphalasamāyuktamupariṣṭādvitānakam \|\| 7 \|\|*

6-7. Then twelve kinds of grain, seats, utensils, sandal, lighting-bowls, shoes, umbrella, mirror, a pair of sandals should be placed. A flag-staff should be made with an image of Garuda on it and in front of the yoke should be made an image of Ganesha. Above it should be placed a canopy with bunting of various kinds of fruits.

## \|\| 282.8-11 \|\|

*kauśeyaṃ pañcavarṇaṃ tu amlānakusumānvitam \|*  
*caturbhiḥ kalaśaiḥ sārdhaṃ gobhiraṣṭābhiranvitam \|\| 8 \|\|*

*caturbhirhemamātaṅgairmuktādāmavibhūṣitaiḥ \|*  
*svarūpataḥ karibhyāṃ ca yuktaṃ kṛtvā nivedayet \|\| 9 \|\|*

*kuryāpañcapalādūrdhvamā bhārādapi śaktitaḥ \|*  
*tathā maṅgalaśabdena snāpito vedapuṃgavaiḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*triḥ pradakṣiṇamāvṛtya gṛhītakusumāñjaliḥ \|*  
*imamuccārayenmantraṃ brāhmaṇebhyo nivedayet \|\| 11 \|\|*

8-11. Five kinds of coloured silk cloths, flowers, four pitchers and eight cows should be placed next to the chariot. Then four elephants made of gold and decorated with pearl strings should be made and yoked to the chariot. Two real elephants shoud be offered with four golden elephants. The golden elephants should be made from five palas to one bhara of gold according to the means of the devotee. After bathing with the recitation by Brahmanas versed in the Vedas of the Vedic hymns the devotee should circumambulate the chariot three times. Taking a handful of flowers he should utter the following mantras and then should give it away to the Brahmanas:

## \|\| 282.14 \|\|

*yasmāttvameva bhavasāgarasaṃplutānāmānandabhāṇḍamṛtamadhvarapānapātram \|*  
*tasmādaghaughaśamanena kuru prasādaṃ cāmīkarebharatha mādhava saṃpradānāt \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. “O, illustrious chariot! You are made use of by Shiva, Brahma, Surya, Vidyadhara, Vasudeva, in Vedas, Puranas and Yajnas. I therefore salute you. Your blissful form is the lotus of heart which the Munis see through Yoga, and where is seated Murari! You bring deliverance to those entangled in the \[meshes of the\] ocean of the world. O, Madhava! therefore protect me after dispelling all my sins.”

## \|\| 282.15 \|\|

*itthaṃ praṇamya kanakebharathapradānaṃ yaḥ kārayetsakalapāpavimuktadehaḥ \|*  
*vidyādharāmaramunīndra gaṇābhijuṣṭhaṃ prāpnotyasau padamatīndri yamindumauleḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. One who gives away a golden chariot after thus saluting it, goes to the domain of Shiva after being liberated from all his sins and there he is adored by the seers and the Vidyadharas, the immortals and Munindras.

## \|\| 282.16 \|\|

*kṛtaduritavitānaprajvaladvahnijālavyatikarakṛtadāhodvegabhājo'pi bandhūn \|*  
*nayati sa pitṛputrānbāndhavānapyaśeṣānkṛtagajarathadānācchāśvataṃ sadma viṣṇoḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Even a sinner who gives away this golden chariot assumes a good form and liberates his manes, brethren, sons, etc., and carries them to the region of Vishnu.

## Chapter 283

## \|\| 283.1 \|\|

*matsya uvāca*  
*athātaḥ saṃpravakṣyāmi mahādānamanuttamam \|*  
*pañcalāṅgalakaṃ nāma mahāpātakanāśanam \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Matsya said: — “I shall now tell you about the Pancha Langalaka ordinance which is the dispeller of all great sins.”

## \|\| 283.2 \|\|

*puṇyāṃ tithimathā’sādya yugādigrahaṇādikām \|*  
*bhūmidānaṃ naro dadyātpañcalāṅgalakānvitam \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. On an auspicious moment, e.g., the commencement of a Yuga or on the occasion of an eclipse, a plot of land measuring five ploughs should be given away.

## \|\| 283.3 \|\|

*kharvaṭaṃ kheṭakaṃ vā'pi grāmaṃ vā sasyaśālinam \|*  
*nivartanaśataṃ vā'pi tadardhaṃ vā'pi śaktitaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Any market town or a village at the foot of a mountain, or any other village should be given away after making the fields prosperous with harvest, or only half the village may be given with its good harvest according to one’s means.

## \|\| 283.4-6 \|\|

*sāradārumayānkṛtvā halānpañca vicakṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*sarvopakaraṇairyuktānanyānpañca ca kāñcanān \|*  
*kuryātpañcapalādūrdhvamāsahasrapalāvadhi \|\| 4 \|\|*

*vṛṣāllaṁ kṣaṇasaṃyuktāndaśa caiva dhuraṃdharān \|*  
*suvarṇaśṛṅgābharaṇānmuktālāṅgūlabhūṣaṇān \|\| 5 \|\|*

*rūpyapādāgratilakānraktakauśeyabhūṣaṇān \|*  
*sragdāmacandanayutāñśālāyāmadhivāsayet \|\| 6 \|\|*

4-6. Five ploughs of good wood should he made and five ploughs of gold from five palas to one thousand palas should also be made according to the means of the devotee. Then five pairs of oxen should be procured and their horns should be covered with gold and tails studded with pearls and their hoofs mounted with silver and then a silk cloth should be thrown over them and they should then be worshipped with floral garlands, sandals, etc., and tied in the devotee’s cowshed.

## \|\| 283.7-8 \|\|

*parjanyādityarudre bhyaḥ pāyasaṃ nirvapeccarum \|*  
*ekasminneva kuṇḍe tu gurustebhyo nivedayet \|\| 7 \|\|*

*palāśasamidhastadvadājyaṃ kṛṣṇatilāstathā \|*  
*tulāpuruṣavatkuryāllokeśāvāhanaṃ budhaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8. Afterwards sacrificial oblations of rice cooked in milk and sugar and other things should be made in the name of Prithivi, Aditya, Rudra in the same sacrificial pit. The wood of butea-frondosa, clarified butter, sesamum should also be used in course of the sacrificial offerings. The Lokapalas should be invoked as prescribed in the Tuladana ceremony.

## \|\| 283.9-13 \|\|

*tato maṅgalaśabdena śuklamālyāmbaro budhaḥ \|*  
*āhūya dvijadāṃpatyaṃ hemasūtrāṅgulīyakaiḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*kauśeyavastrakaṭakairmaṇibhiścābhipūjayet \|*  
*śayyāṃ sopaskarāṃ dadyāddhenumekāṃ payasvinīm \|\| 10 \|\|*

*tathā'ṣṭādaśa dhānyāni samantādadhivāsayet \|*  
*tataḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya gṛhītakusumāñjaliḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*imamuccārayenmantramatha sarvaṃ nivedayet \|*  
*yasmāddevagaṇāḥ sarve sthāvarāṇi carāṇi ca \|\| 12 \|\|*

*dhuraṃdharāṅge tiṣṭhanti tasmādbhaktiḥ śive'stu me \|*  
*yasmācca bhūmidānasya kalāṃ nārhanti ṣoḍaśīm \|\| 13 \|\|*

9-13. Then, after the recitation of propitiatory hymns, the wise priest should put on white clothes and white garlands and call the devotee with his consort and give him a girdle of gold, a ring, a piece of redcloth, a few gems, a bed with all its equipment’s and a milk cow.
