Eighteen grains should be placed all round and then the devotee holding a handful of flowers should circumambulate the Man dap and utter the following: —

“All the Devas and all other beings, moveable and non-movable, are present on the harnessed body of this ox, so let them remain devoted towards Shiva. There is no ordinance like one-sixteenth part of the gift of a plot of land; so let my intellect be fixed in Dharma.

## \|\| 283.14-16 \|\|

*dānānyanyāni me bhaktirdharma eva dṛḍhā bhavet \|*  
*daṇḍena saptahastena triṃśaddaṇḍaṃ nivartanam \|\| 14 \|\|*

*tribhāgahīnaṃ gocarmamānamāha prajāpatiḥ \|*  
*mānenānena yo dadyānnivartanaśataṃ budhaḥ \|*  
*vidhinā'nena tasyā’śu kṣīyate pāpasaṃhatiḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*tadardhamathavā dadyādapi gocarmamātrakam \|*  
*bhavanasthānamātraṃ vā so'pi pāpaiḥ pramucyate \|\| 16 \|\|*

14-16. A plot of land that can hold thirty poles of seven hands each is called the Nirvartana. This is told by Prajapati. One who gives away a plot of land of 100 Nirvartanas in area according to the prescribed rites, is freed at once of all his sins. And one who gives away an area of land half of that on measuring a Gocharma or sufficient for a house to be built upon also frees himself from all his sins.

## \|\| 283.17 \|\|

*yāvanti lāṅgalakamārgamukhāni bhūmerbhāsāṃ paterduhituraṅgajaromakāṇi \|*  
*tāvanti śaṃkarapure sa samā hi tiṣṭhedbhūmipradānamiha yaḥ kurute manuṣyaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. The donor of such plots of land remains in the realm of Shiva for as many years as there are hairs on the body of the oxen or as many pores there are in the soil at the time of sowing seeds after ploughing the plot.

## \|\| 283.18 \|\|

*gandharvakiṃnarasurāsurasiddhasaṃghairādhūtacāmaramupetya mahadvimānam \|*  
*saṃpūjyate pitṛpitāmahabandhuyuktaḥ śaṃbhoḥ padaṃ vrajati cāmaranāyakaḥ san \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. The Gandharvas, Devas, demons, Siddhas, they all wave chamaras on him and the devotee goes to the domain of Shiva seated in a huge Vimana along with his fathers, grandfathers, friends, etc.

## \|\| 283.19 \|\|

*indra tvamapyadhigataṃ kṣayamabhyupaiti gobhūmilāṅgaladhuraṃdharasaṃpradānāt \|*  
*tasmādaghaughapaṭalakṣayakāri bhūmerdānaṃ vidheyamiti bhūtibhavodbhavāya \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. By this gift of oxen, lands, and ploughs with yokes, etc., the donor is freed of his sins and obtains the position of Indra. A wealthy man should therefore give this gift to remove his sins and acquire prosperity for himself.

## Chapter 284

## \|\| 284.1 \|\|

*matsya uvāca*  
*athātaḥ saṃpravakṣyāmi dharādānamanuttamam \|*  
*pāpakṣayakaraṃ nriṇāmamaṅgalyavināśanam \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Matsya said: — “I shall now tell you about the sacred Dharadana that drives away all the ills and sins of the devotee and promotes his welfare.”

## \|\| 284.2-6 \|\|

*kārayetpṛthivīṃ haimīṃ jambūdvīpānukāriṇīm \|*  
*maryādāparvatavatīṃ madhye merusamanvitām \|\| 2 \|\|*

*lokapālāṣṭakopetāṃ navavarṣasamanvitām \|*  
*nadīnadasamopetāṃ saptasāgaraveṣṭitām \|\| 3 \|\|*

*mahāratnasamākīrṇāṃ vasurudrā rkasaṃyutām \|*  
*hemnaḥ palasahasreṇa tadardhenātha śaktitaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*śatatrayeṇa vā kuryāddviśatena śatena vā \|*  
*kuryātpañcapalādūrdhvamaśakto'pi vicakṣaṇaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*tulāpuruṣavatkuryāllokeśāvāhanaṃ budhaḥ \|*  
*ṛtviṅmaṇḍapasaṃbhārabhūṣaṇācchādanādikam \|\| 6 \|\|*

2-6. The Yajaman (sacrificer) should make an earth of gold in imitation of Jambudvipa.

This golden Jambudvipas, having mountains, with Meru in the centre, with eight Lokapalas and ’nine Varsas, with rivers and oceans, full of gems, conjoint with Vasu, Rudra and the Sun should he made of 1,000 palas or 500 or 30O, or 200 or 100 palas of gold. It should however be more than five palas. The Lokapalas should be invoked as m course of the Tuladana and Ritvikas, pandal, ornaments, clothings, etc., should be similarly arranged.

## \|\| 284.7-10 \|\|

*vedyāṃ kṛṣṇājinaṃ kṛtvā tilānupari vinyaset \|*  
*tathā'ṣṭādaśa dhānyāni rasāṃśca lavaṇādikān \|\| 7 \|\|*

*tathā'ṣṭau pūrṇakalaśānsamantātparikalpayet \|*  
*vitānakaṃ ca kauśeyaṃ phalāni vividhāni ca \|\| 8 \|\|*

*tathāṃ'śukāni ramyāṇi śrīkhaṇḍaśakalāni ca \|*  
*ityevaṃ kārayitvā tāmadhivāsanapūrvakam \|\| 9 \|\|*

*śuklamālyāmbaradharaḥ śuklābharaṇabhūṣitaḥ \|*  
*pradakṣiṇaṃ tataḥ kṛtvā gṛhītakusumāñjaliḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

7-10. On the altar (Vedi) the black deer skin should be spread and over it should be made a mound of sesamum. Above the heap should be placed the image of the earth and round it should be placed salt, etc., along with 18 kinds of grains. Then 8 pitchers full of water should be placed covered over with silk awning as well as various kinds of fruits and cocoanuts and clothings. Afterwards the devotee should put on white clothes, white garlands and taking a handful of flowers,

## \|\| 284.11-15 \|\|

*puṇyaṃ kālamathā’sādya mantrānetānudīrayet \|*  
*namaste sarvadevānāṃ tvameva bhavanaṃ yataḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*dhātrī tvaṃ sarvabhūtānāmataḥ pāhi vasuṃdhare \|*  
*vasu dhārayase yasmādvasu cātīva nirmalam \|\| 12 \|\|*

*vasuṃdharā tato jātā tasmātpāhi bhayādalam \|*  
*caturmukho'pi no gacchedyasmādantaṃ tavācale \|\| 13 \|\|*

*anantāyai namastasmātpāhi saṃsārakardamāt \|*  
*tvameva lakṣmīrgovinde śive gaurīti cā’sthitā \|\| 14 \|\|*

*gāyatrī brahmaṇaḥ pārśve jyotsnā candre ravau prabhā \|*  
*buddhirbṛhaspatau khyātā medhā muniṣu saṃsthitā \|\| 15 \|\|*

11-15. Recite the following mantras at an auspicious moment: — “O Mother Universe! You are the refuge of all the Devas, I therefore salute you.

You protect all the Jivas; therefore protect me. O Vasundhare! You hold the Vasus, all the beings, pray protect me. O Achale! Even the four-faced Lord Brahma does not adequately know your limit. Therefore you are Ananta. My salutations to you. O, one without any beginning or an end, Guard me from the perils of this vast and fearful ocean of the world.

You are with Vishnu in the form of Lakshmi, with Shiva in the form of Gauri, with Brahma in the form of Savitri. You are the light of the Sun and the Moon, intellect in Vrihaspati, Medha (intelligence) retentive faculty in the Munis.

## \|\| 284.16-18 \|\|

*viśvaṃ vyāpya sthitā yasmāttato viśvaṃbharā smṛtā \|*  
*dhṛtiḥ sthitiḥ kṣamā kṣoṇī pṛthvī vasumatī rasā \|\| 16 \|\|*

*etābhirmūrtibhiḥ pāhi devi saṃsārasāgarāt \|*  
*evamuccārya tāṃ devīṃ brāhmaṇebhyo nivedayet \|\| 17 \|\|*

*dharārdhaṃ vā caturbhāgaṃ gurave pratipādayet \|*  
*śeṣaṃ caivātha ṛtvigbhyaḥ praṇipatya visarjayet \|\| 18 \|\|*

16-18. “O mother! You are fixed, you pervade all the universe, therefore you are called Vishvambhara. Devi! you are known by the names Dhriti, Sthiti, Kshama, Kshauni, Prithvi, Vasumati and Rasa. Pray do protect me by all your above-mentioned forms. Afterwards the devotee should give away the Devi to the Brahmanas. One-half or one-fourth of the earth made of gold should be given to the preceptor (Guru) and the rest should be given away to the Ritvikas. Then the Brahmanas should be dismissed after being saluted.

## \|\| 284.19-21 \|\|

*anena vidhinā yastu dadyāddhemadharāṃ śubhām \|*  
*puṇyakāle tu saṃprāpte sa padaṃ yāti vaiṣṇavam \|\| 19 \|\|*

*vimānenārkavarṇena kiṅkiṇījālamālinā \|*  
*nārāyaṇapuraṃ gatvā kalpatrayamathā’vaset \|*  
*pitrinputrāṃśca pautrāṃśca tārayedekaviṃśatim \|\| 20 \|\|*

*iti paṭhati ya itthaṃ yaḥ śṛṇoti prasaṅgādapi kaluṣavitānairmuktadehaḥ samantāt \|*  
*divamamaravadhūbhiryāti saṃprārthyamāno padamamarasahasraiḥ sevitaṃ candra mauleḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

19-21. In such a way one who gives away that golden universe in an auspicious moment attains bliss and goes to the realm of Narayana seated in a Viman bright as the Sun and decorated with beautiful network and bells where he remains for 3 Kalpas and liberates his manes, sons, grand-children for twenty-one generations. One who reads this or hears it is, also liberated from all sins and goes to the realm of Shiva resided by thousands of Devas where nymphs yearn for him.

## Chapter 285

## \|\| 285.1 \|\|

*matsya uvāca*  
*athātaḥ saṃpravakṣyāmi mahādānamanuttamam \|*  
*viśvacakramiti khyātaṃ mahāpātakanāśanam \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Matsya said: — “I shall now tell you about the Vishvachakra Maha which is the dispeller of all heinous sins.”

## \|\| 285.2-3 \|\|

*tapanīyasya śuddhasya viśvacakraṃ tu kārayet \|*  
*śreṣṭhaṃ palasahasreṇa tadardhena tu madhyamam \|\| 2 \|\|*

*tasyārdhena kaniṣṭhaṃ syādviśvacakramudāhṛtam \|*  
*anyadviṃśatpalādūrdhvamaśakto'pi nivedayet \|\| 3 \|\|*

2-3. On the day when the Sun enters the point of equinox or on any auspicious day an image of golden Vishvachakra (the wheels of the universe) should be made. The image of 1,000 palas of gold is the best, of 500 palas is medium and of 250 palas is the Kanishtha. If the devotee cannot afford much he should get an image of over 20 palas made It should however not be less than that.

## \|\| 285.4-11 \|\|

*ṣoḍaśāraṃ tataścakraṃ bhramannemyaṣṭakāvṛtam \|*  
*nābhipadme sthitaṃ viṣṇuṃ yogārūḍhaṃ caturbhujam \|\| 4 \|\|*

*śaṅkhacakre'sya pārśve tu devyaṣṭakasamāvṛtam \|*  
*dvitīyāvaraṇe tadvatpūrvato jalaśāyinam \|\| 5 \|\|*

*atrirbhṛgurvasiṣṭhaśca brahmā kaśyapa eva ca \|*  
*matsyaḥ kūrmo varāhaśca narasiṃho'tha vāmanaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*rāmo rāmaśca kṛṣṇaśca buddhaḥ kalkīti ca kramāt \|*  
*tṛtīyāvaraṇe gaurī mātṛbhirvasubhiryutā \|\| 7 \|\|*

*caturthe dvādaśā’dityā vedāścatvāra eva ca \|*  
*pañcame pañca bhūtāni rudrā ścaikādaśaiva tu \|\| 8 \|\|*

*lokapālāṣṭakaṃ ṣaṣṭhe diṅmātaṅgāstathaiva ca \|*  
*saptame'strāṇi sarvāṇi maṅgalāni ca kārayet \|\| 9 \|\|*

*antarāntarato devānvinyasedaṣṭame punaḥ \|*  
*tulāpuruṣavaccheṣaṃ samantātparikalpayet \|\| 10 \|\|*

*ṛtviṅmaṇḍapasaṃbhārabhūṣaṇācchādanādikam \|*  
*viśvacakraṃ tataḥ kuryātkṛṣṇājinatilopari \|\| 11 \|\|*

4-11. The wheel should be made of sixteen spokes and eight fellies. In the middle of it should be made the image of Lord Vishnu in Yoga posture, of four arms, a conch and a disc should be placed beside him. The images of the eight Goddesses should also be made to reside within the wheel.

Another image of Vishnu in a lying posture should be made in the east and the images of Atri, Bhrigu, Vasistha, Brahma, Kashyapa, Matsya, Karma, Varaha, Nrisimha, Vamana, Parashurama, Ramachandra, Krishna, Buddha and Kalki should also be made in due order as the secondary attendants.

In the third row of attendants on the wheel should be placed the images of Gauri, the 16 Matrikas, 8 Vasus; in the fourth one should be placed the 12 Adityas, 4 Vedas; in the fifth one the five elements and eleven Rudras, in the 6th one, the 8 Lokapalas, the Diggajas; in the 7th one, all the auspicious things, arms and weapons and in the 8th one the Devas. Thus the Vishvachakra has 8 avaranas. Afterwards all the things mentioned in the Tuladana should be placed all-round the Vishvachakra and then Ritvikas, pandal, ornaments, etc., should be arranged accordingly. Then the Vishvachakra should be placed on a mound of sesamum placed on the skin of a black deer.

## \|\| 285.12-14 \|\|

*tathā'ṣṭādaśa dhānyāni rasāṃśca lavaṇādikān \|*  
*pūrṇakumbhāṣṭakaṃ caiva vastrāṇi vividhāni ca \|\| 12 \|\|*

*mālyekṣuphalaratnāni vitānaṃ cāpi kārayet \|*  
*tato maṅgalaśabdena snātaḥ śuklāmbaro gṛhī \|*  
*homādhivāsanānte vai gṛhītakusumāñjaliḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*imamuccārayenmantraṃ triḥ kṛtvā tu pradakṣiṇam \|*  
*namo viśvamayāyeti viśvacakrātmane namaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

12-14. Eighteen sorts of grains and salt, etc., as well as eight pitchers full of water covered with cloths and adorned with garlands of flowers, sugarcane, fruits, gems and awnings should also be placed. The householder should bathe as before accompanied with Vedic hymns and put on white clothes and then commence the sacrifice. After Homa and Adhivasana. he should take a handful of flowers and make three circumambulations and utter the following mantras: — “ O Vishvamaya! O Vishvachakratman! My salutations to you in whom is contained the universe and who is the master of the cycle of the universe.

## \|\| 285.15-17 \|\|

*paramānandarūpī tvaṃ pāhi naḥ pāpakardamāt \|*  
*tejomayamidaṃ yasmātsadā paśyanti yoginaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*hṛdi tattvaṃ guṇātītaṃ viśvacakraṃ namāmyaham \|*  
*vāsudeve sthitaṃ cakraṃ cakramadhye tu mādhavaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*anyonyādhārarūpeṇa praṇamāmi sthitāviha \|*  
*viśvacakramidaṃ yasmātsarvapāpaharaṃ param \|\| 17 \|\|*

15-17. “O, one full of the highest bliss, do save me from the mundane sea of troubles. The illustrious Tattva which is seen constantly in the hearts by the Yogis in meditation is saluted by me. I bow down to the Vishvachakra above all the attributes. O Chakra! you are contained in Lord Vishnu and vice versa. It is therefore the remover of all sins.

## \|\| 285.18-20 \|\|

*āyudhaṃ cāpi vāsaśca bhavāduddhara māmataḥ \|*  
*ityāmantr! ya ca yo dadyādviśvacakraṃ vimatsaraḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*vimuktaḥ sarvapāpebhyo viṣṇuloke mahīyate \|*  
*vaikuṇṭhalokamāsādya caturbāhuḥ sanātanaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

*sevyate'psarasāṃ saṃghaistiṣṭhetkalpaśatatrayam \|*  
*praṇamedvā'tha yaḥ kṛtvā viśvacakraṃ dine dine \|*  
*tasyā’yurvardhate nityaṃ lakṣmīśca vipulā bhavet \|\| 20 \|\|*

18-20. “Vishvachakra is the supreme weapon of Vishnu. You are the resting place of the Lord, Pray therefore rescue me from the sufferings of the world.” One who thus gives away the Vishvachakra, is liberated from all sins and goes to the realm of Vishnu where he is blessed with 4 hands and eternal form in Vaikuntha and remains there for 300 Kalpas in the midst of the Apsaras. One who salutes the Vishvachakra every day gets prosperity and wealth in this life His life becomes long.

## \|\| 285.21 \|\|

*iti sakalajagatsurādhivāsaṃ vitarati yastapanīyaṣoḍaśāram \|*  
*haribhavanamupāgataḥ sa siddhaiściramabhigamya namasyate śirobhiḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. One who gives away a Vishvachakra of gold with 16 spokes and 8 fellies, the refuge of the Devas and this world, goes to the realm of Vishnu and the Siddhas salute him.

## \|\| 285.22 \|\|

*asudarśanatāṃ prayāti śatrormadanasudarśanatāṃ ca kāminībhyaḥ \|*  
*sa sudarśanakeśavānurūpaḥ kanakasudarśanadānadagdhapāpaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. His appearance also becomes very fascinating to women,. This ordinance destroys all the enemies of the devotee and removes all his sins.

## \|\| 285.23 \|\|

*kṛtaguruduritāni ṣoḍaśārapravitaraṇe pravarākṛtirmurāreḥ \|*  
*abhibhavati bhavodbhavāni bhittvā bhavamabhito bhavane bhayāni bhūyaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Most heinous sins vanish by the glory of this ordinance in the name of Hari and the devotee never gets into any peril of rebirth and death.

## Chapter 286

## \|\| 286.1 \|\|

*matsya uvāca*  
*athātaḥ saṃpravakṣyāmi mahādānamanuttamam \|*  
*mahākalpalatānāma mahāpātakanāśanam \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Matsya said: — “I shall now tell you about the Mahakalpalata, an excellent gift, which is the destroyer of great sins.”

## \|\| 286.4-5 \|\|

*nānāpuṣpaphalopetā nānāṃśukavibhūṣitāḥ \|*  
*vidyādharasuparṇānāṃ mithunairupaśobhitāḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*puṣpāṇyāditsubhiḥ siddhaiḥ phalāni ca vihaṃgamaiḥ \|*  
*lokapālānukāriṇyaḥ kartavyāstāsu devatāḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. On an auspicious Tithi after Svastivachana, the devotee should arrange for the Ritvikas, panda!, articles, ornaments, clothings as before and invoke Lokapalas as is done in the Tuladana. Then Kalpalatas (creepers yielding all desires) of gold should be made and they should be adorned with various fruits, flowers and kinds of birds, couples of Vidyadharas, pairs of golden birds, Siddhas culling flowers and fruits. Birds should be made along with the images of the ascetics living only on fruits; as well as the images of the Devas the attendant of the Lokapalas should also be made.

## \|\| 286.6 \|\|

*brāhmīmanantaśaktiṃ ca lavaṇasyopari nyaset \|*  
*adhastāllatayormadhye padmaśaṅkhakare śubhe \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Beneath the two creeper twigs on a mound of salt should be placed the image of the Goddess Brahmi of infinite power and glory holding lotus and conch, as well as of the Goddess of Ananta Shakti.

## \|\| 286.7 \|\|

*ibhāsanasthā tu guḍe pūrvataḥ kuliśāyudhā \|*  
*rajanyajasthitā'gnāyī suvapāṇirathānale \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. On a mound of molasses to the east should be located the image of the Goddess Indrani on a seat on an elephant holding a thunderbolt in Her hand. The consort of Agni should be located in the S.-E. corner on a mound of turmeric holding a sacrificial ladle in Her hand.

## \|\| 286.8 \|\|

*yāmye ca mahiṣārūḍhā gadinī taṇḍulopari \|*  
*ghṛte tu nairṛtī sthāpyā sakhaḍgā dakṣiṇāpare \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. In the south should be located the image of the Goddess Gadini riding a buffalo, in the N.-W. corner should be placed the image of the Goddess Nairitya on a mound of clarified butter holding a sword.

## \|\| 286.9 \|\|

*vāruṇe vāruṇī kṣīre jhaṣasthā nāgapāśinī \|*  
*patākinī ca vāyavye mṛgasthā śarkaropari \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. In the west should be placed the image of the Goddess Varuni with her weapon of Nagapasha, riding a fish, on a pot of milk and in the N.-W. corner should be placed the image of the Goddess Patakini riding a deer, on a mound of sugar.

## \|\| 286.10 \|\|

*saumyā tileṣu saṃsthāpyā śaṅkhinī nidhisaṃsthitā \|*  
*māheśvarī vṛṣārūḍhā navanīte triśūlinī \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. The Goddess Samkhini should be located in the north on a mound of sesamum and in the N.-E. corner should be placed the image of the Goddess Maheshvari riding a bull and holding a trident, on a seat of fresh butter.

## \|\| 286.11 \|\|

*maulinyo varadāstadvatkartavyā bālakānvitāḥ \|*  
*śaktyā pañcapalādūrdhvamā sahasrātprakalpayet \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. The images of these Goddesses should be made in their girlish forms with a coronet on their heads, with Their hand in the posture of offering some boon. They should be made of from five palas to one thousand palas of gold.

## \|\| 286.12-13 \|\|

*sarvāsāmupari sthāpyaṃ pañcavarṇaṃ vitānakam \|*  
*dhenavo daśa kumbhāśca vastrayugmāṇi caiva hi \|\| 12 \|\|*

*madhyame dve tu gurave ṛtvigbhyo'nyāstathaiva ca \|*  
*tato maṅgalaśabdena snātaḥ śuklāmbaro budhaḥ \|*  
*triḥ pradakṣiṇamāvṛtya mantrametamudīrayet \|\| 13 \|\|*

12-13. Over Them should be made awnings and arches of different colours and close to them should be kept 10 cows, 10 vases, and pairs of cloths.

The central image, and the two cows along with the two vases should be given to the preceptor and the rest should be given to the Ritvikas. After a bath with Vedic chants the devotee should put on white clothes and utter the following formulae after circumambulating thrice.

## \|\| 286.14 \|\|

*namo namaḥ pāpavināśinībhyo brahmāṇḍalokeśvarapālinībhyaḥ \|*  
*āśaṃsitādhikyaphalapradābhyo digbhyastathā kalpalatāvadhūbhyaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. “Salutations to the better halves of the Directions and the Kalpalata Vadhus that dispel all sins; protect the universe along with the Lokapalas and give the desired objects.”

## \|\| 286.15 \|\|

*iti sakaladigaṅganāpradānaṃ bhavabhayasūdanakāri yaḥ karoti \|*  
*abhimataphalade sa nāgaloke vasati pitāmahavatsarāṇi triṃśat \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. One who thus gives away these consorts of the Directions goes to tree Nagaloka, the satisfier of all desires, where he remains for 30 years of Brahma.

## \|\| 286.16-17 \|\|

*pitṛśatamatha tārayedbhavābdherbhavaduritaughavighātaśuddhadehaḥ \|*  
*surapativanitāsahasrasaṃkhyaiḥ parivṛtamambujasaṃsadā'bhivandyaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*iti vidhānamidaṃ digaṅganānāṃ kanakakalpalatāvinivedakam \|*  
*paṭhati yaḥ smaratīha tathaikṣate sa padameti puraṃdarasevitam \|\| 17 \|\|*

16-17. He liberates one hundred generations of his manes from this sea of troubles and is adored by thousands of nymphs. The Diganganas have ordained this Mahadana. On© who reads, listens to or sees the Kalpalatadana and the Dikvadhudana goes to the realm of Indra.

## Chapter 287

## \|\| 287.2-3 \|\|

*puṇyaṃ dinamathā’sādya kṛtvā brāhmaṇavācanam \|*  
*tulāpuruṣavatkuryāllokeśāvāhanaṃ budhaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*ṛtviṅmaṇḍapasaṃbhārabhūṣaṇācchādanādikam \|*  
*kārayetsapta kuṇḍāni kāñcanāni vicakṣaṇaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

2-3. Matsya said “ I shall now relate to you Saptasagara ordinance, the dispeller of all great sins.” — L On an auspicious day after Svastivachana the Lokapalas should be invoked as is done in Tuladana. Then Ritvikas, Mandapa, articles, ornaments, clothings and coverings should be collected and seven sacrificial pits should be made of gold.

## \|\| 287.4 \|\|

*prādeśamātrāṇi tathā'ratnimātrāṇi vai punaḥ \|*  
*kuryātsaptapalādūrdhvamā sahasrācca śaktitaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. They should be of the size of Pradesha (of the span of the thumb and forefinger) or Aratni and should be made of from seven palas to one thousand palas of gold according to the means of the devotee.

**Комментарий:**

\[N. B. Aratni — a cubit of the middle length from the elbow to the tip of the little finger.\]

## \|\| 287.5-9 \|\|

*saṃsthāpyāni ca sarvāṇi kṛṣṇājinatilopari \|*  
*prathamaṃ pūrayetkuṇḍaṃ lavaṇena vicakṣaṇaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*dvitīyaṃ payasā tadvattṛtīyaṃ sarpiṣā punaḥ \|*  
*caturthaṃ tu guḍenaiva dadhnā pañcamameva ca \|\| 6 \|\|*

*ṣaṣṭhaṃ śarkarayā tadvatsaptamaṃ tīrthavāriṇā \|*  
*sthāpayellavaṇasthaṃ tu brahmāṇaṃ kāñcanaṃ śubham \|\| 7 \|\|*

*keśavaṃ kṣīramadhye tu ghṛtamadhye maheśvaram \|*  
*bhāskaraṃ guḍamadhye tu dadhimadhye niśādhipam \|\| 8 \|\|*

*śarkarāyāṃ nyasellakṣmīṃ jalamadhye tu pārvatīm \|*  
*sarveṣu sarvaratnāni dhānyāni ca samantataḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

5-9. Then they should be located on a black deer skin overspread with sesamum. The first pit should be filled in with salt; the second one with milk, the third one with clarified butter, the fourth one with molasses, the fifth one with curds, the sixth one with sugar, the seventh one with the sacred waters of the holy Tirthas. The golden image of Brahma should be put in the one filled with salt; Keshava in the second one filled with milk, Shiva in the third one filled with clarified butter, the Sun in the fourth one filled with molasses, the Moon in the 5th one filled with curds, Lakshmi in the 6th one filled with sugar, Parvati in the 7th one filled with the sacred waters. Gems and grains (Dhanyam) should be put in each one of them and grains all round

## \|\| 287.10-11 \|\|

*tulāpuruṣavaccheṣamatrāpi parikalpayet \|*  
*tato vāruṇahomānte snāpito vedapuṃgavaiḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*triḥ pradakṣiṇamāvṛtya mantrānetānudīrayet \|*  
*namo vaḥ sarvasiṃdhūnāmādhārebhyaḥ sanātanāḥ \|*  
*jantūnāṃ prāṇadebhyaśca samudre bhyo namo namaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

10-11. All the ceremonies should be performed as is done in Tuladana and at the end of the Varuna Homa the devotee should bathe assisted by the Brahmanas versed in the Vedas. He should then make three circumambulations and then recite the following formula: — “O Eternal Oceans You are the basis of all the beings. You are eternal. You are the giver of life to all beings. I salute you”.

## \|\| 287.12 \|\|

*kṣīrodakājyadadhimādhuralāvaṇekṣusārāmṛtena bhuvanatrayajīvasaṃghān \|*  
*ānandayanti vasubhiśca yato bhavantastasmānmamāpyaghavighātamalaṃ diśantu \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. “You satisfy the three realms with your store of milk, clarified butter, water, curds, honey, salt, sugar-cane, gems; pray therefore drive away my sins also”.

## \|\| 287.13 \|\|

*yasmātsamastabhuvaneṣu bhavanta eva tīrthāmarāsurasubaddhamaṇipradānam \|*  
*pāpakṣayāmṛtavilepanabhūṣaṇāya lokasya bibhrati tadastu mamāpi lakṣmīḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. “You dispel the ills of the Devas, the demons in all the regions, bestow nectar unto them and give them gems for their ornaments, pray let therefore there be an increase in the store of wealth in my house.”

## \|\| 287.14 \|\|

*iti dadāti rasāmṛtasaṃyutāñchuciravismayavāniha sāgarān \|*  
*amalakāñcanavarṇamayānasau padamupaiti hareramarārcitaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. One who thus gives away these seven oceans in such a way, attains the realm of Vishnu venerated by the Devas.

## \|\| 287.15 \|\|

*sakalapāpavidhautavirājitaḥ pitṛpitāmahaputrakalatrakam \|*  
*narakalokasamākulamapyayaṃ jhaṭiti so'pi nayecchivamandiram \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. He also liberates his sons, wife, father, grandfather, etc., from sins and sends them to heaven from hell.

## Chapter 288

## \|\| 288.1 \|\|

*matsya uvāca*  
*athātaḥ saṃpravakṣyāmi mahādānamanuttamam \|*  
*ratnadhenviti vikhyātaṃ golokaphaladaṃ nṛṇām \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Matsya said: — “I shall now tell you about the Ratnadhenu ordinance the giver of high benefits, and which leads to Go-loka.

## \|\| 288.2 \|\|

*puṇyaṃ dinamathā’sādya tulāpuruṣadānavat \|*  
*lokeśāvāhanaṃ kṛtvā tato dhenuṃ prakalpayet \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. On an auspicious day the Lokapals should be invoked as in Tuladana and then a cow studded with precious stones should be made.

## \|\| 288.3-4 \|\|

*bhūmau kṛṣṇājinaṃ kṛtvā lavaṇadro ṇasaṃyutam \|*  
*dhenuṃ ratnamayīṃ kuryātsaṃkalpya vidhipūrvakam \|\| 3 \|\|*

*sthāpayetpadmarāgāṇāmekāśītiṃ mukhe budhaḥ \|*  
*puṣparāgaśataṃ tadvadghoṇāyāṃ parikalpayet \|\| 4 \|\|*

3-4. A skin of black deer should be spread on the floor and then a mound of 32 seers of sesamum should be placed and above it should be put 81 sorts of gems.

## \|\| 288.5-6 \|\|

*lalāṭe hematilakaṃ muktāphalaśataṃ dṛśoḥ \|*  
*bhrūyuge vidrumaśataṃ śuktī karṇadvaye smṛte \|\| 5 \|\|*

*kāñcanāni ca śṛṅgāṇi śiro vajraśatātmakam \|*  
*grīvāyāṃ netrapaṭalaṃ gomedakaśatānvitam \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. On the head a tilaka should be made in gold and 100 pearls should be placed in the eyes, and 100 corals should be placed in the brows. Mother o’pearl should be placed in the ears and the horns should be made of gold. On the head should be placed one hundred diamonds and in the neck 100 Gomeda stones should be placed. The eyes are to be lotus-like extended.

## \|\| 288.7-8 \|\|

*indra nīlaśataṃ pṛṣṭhe vaidūryaśatapārśvake \|*  
*sphāṭikairudaraṃ tadvatsaugandhikaśataiḥ kaṭim \|\| 7 \|\|*

*khurā hemamayāḥ kāryāḥ pucchaṃ muktāvalīmayam \|*  
*sūryakāntendukāntau ca ghrāṇe karpūracandane \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8. One hundred sapphires (Indranila-mani) should be placed on the back and Vaidurya-manis in place of the ribs, and Sphatikamani in place of the stomach. Musk and other scented things should be placed in place of the waist. The hoofs should be made of gold, the tail of pearls, nose of Suryakamta and Chandrakanta stones. The knee is to be studded with camphor.

## \|\| 288.9 \|\|

*kuṅkumāni ca romāṇi raupyanābhiṃ ca kārayet \|*  
*gārutmataśataṃ tadvadapāne parikalpayet \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The hair should be of Kunkuma (saffron) and the navel of silver and there should be a 100 rubies in place of the arms.

## \|\| 288.10-11 \|\|

*tathā'nyāni ca ratnāni sthāpayetsarvasaṃdhiṣu \|*  
*kuryāccharkarayā jihvāṃ gomayaṃ ca guḍātmakam \|\| 10 \|\|*

*gomūtramājyena tathā dadhidugdhaṃ svarūpataḥ \|*  
*pucchāgre cāmaraṃ dadyātsamīpe tāmradohanam \|\| 11 \|\|*

10-11. Other precious stones should he placed in the other joints. The tongue should be made of sugar and molasses should be substituted for dung, clarified butter in place of urine, curds in place of curds and milk in place of milk. Chamara should be placed in front of the tail-end and a copper milking pot should be placed close by the cow.

## \|\| 288.12 \|\|

*kuṇḍalāni ca haimāni bhūṣaṇāni ca śaktitaḥ \|*  
*kārayedevamevaṃ tu caturthāṃśena vatsakam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Earrings should he made of gold and other ornaments should be made according to the means of the devotee. In the same way a calf of one-fourth of the cow prescribed according to rule should be made.

## \|\| 288.13-14 \|\|

*tathā dhānyāni sarvāṇi pādāścekṣumayāḥ smṛtāḥ \|*  
*nānāphalāni sarvāṇi pañcavarṇaṃ vitānakam \|\| 13 \|\|*

*evaṃ viracanaṃ kṛtvā tadvaddhomādhivāsanam \|*  
*ṛtvigbhyo dakṣiṇāṃ dadyāddhenumāmantrayettataḥ \|*  
*guḍadhenuvadāvāhya idaṃ codāharettataḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

13-14. All the grains, sugarcane, various kinds of fruits. should be provided and an arch of various colours should be made. Afterwards Homa should be performed and gifts should he made to the Ritvikas. Afterwards the cow should be invoked and the following mantras should be recited.

## \|\| 288.15 \|\|

*tvāṃ sarvadevagaṇadhāma yataḥ paṭhanti rudre ndra sūryakamalāsanavāsudevāḥ \|*  
*tasmātsamastabhuvanatrayadehayuktā māṃ pāhi devi bhavasāgarapīḍyamānam \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Cow! O Devi! Your body contains the three worlds; you are said to be the resting place of all the Devas; so Rudra, Brahma, and Vasudeva say; pray protect me from the troubles of the world.

## \|\| 288.16 \|\|

*āmantr! ya cetthamabhitaḥ parivṛtya bhaktyā dadyāddvijāya gurave jalapūrvikāṃ tām \|*  
*yaḥ puṇyamāpya dinamatra kṛtopavāsaḥ pāpairvimuktatanureti padaṃ murāreḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. One is to observe fasting, and after invoking the above mantras, should circumambulate and with devotion make the gift, touching the waters. The cow should be given away to the preceptor. One who does so goes to the region of Vishnu, being freed from sins.

## \|\| 288.17 \|\|

*iti sakalavidhijño ratnadhenupradānaṃ vitarati sa vimānaṃ prāpya dedīpyamānam \|*  
*sakalakaluṣamukto bandhubhiḥ putrapautraiḥ sa hi madanasarūpaḥ sthānamabhyeti śaṃbhoḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Seated in a brilliant chariot, with his sons, grandsons, &c., and freed from all sins he goes to Sambhu.

## Chapter 289

## \|\| 289.1 \|\|

*matsya uvāca*  
*athātaḥ saṃpravakṣyāmi mahādānamanuttamam \|*  
*mahābhūtaghaṭaṃ nāma mahāpātakanāśanam \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Matsya said: — “I shall now relate to you about the Mahabhuta-ghata ordinance, the destroyer of all sins”.

## \|\| 289.2-4 \|\|

*puṇyāṃ tithi mathā’sādya kṛtvā brāhmaṇavācanam \|*  
*ṛtviṅmaṇḍapasaṃbhārabhūṣaṇācchādanādikam \|\| 2 \|\|*

*tulāpuruṣavatkuryāllokeśāvāhanādikam \|*  
*kārayetkāñcanaṃ kumbhaṃ mahāratnācitaṃ budhaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*prādeśādaṅgulaśataṃ yāvatkuryātpramāṇataḥ \|*  
*kṣīrājyapūritaṃ tadvatkalpavṛkṣasamanvitam \|\| 4 \|\|*

2-4. On an auspicious day after Svastivachana, the devotee should call the Ritvikas and arrange for the pandal, ornaments, cloths, etc., as prescribed for the Tuladana and should then invoke the Lokapalas. The pitcher or kumbha should be made of gold studded with precious stones.

It should measure one Pradesha to 100 fingers of gold according to the means of the devotee. It should then be filled in with clarified butter, milk and made to go hand in hand with Kalpavriksha.

## \|\| 289.5-9 \|\|

*padmāsanagatāṃstatra brahmaviṣṇumaheśvarān \|*  
*lokapālānmahendrā ścaṃ! svasvavāhanamāsthitān \|*  
*varāheṇoddhṛtāṃ tadvatkuryātpṛthvīṃ sapaṅkajām \|\| 5 \|\|*

*varuṇaṃ cā’sanagataṃ kāñcanaṃ makaropari \|*  
*hutāśanaṃ meṣagataṃ vāyuṃ kṛṣṇamṛgāsanam \|\| 6 \|\|*

*tathā kośādhipaṃ kuryānmūṣakasthaṃ vināyakam \|*  
*vinyasya ghaṭamadhye tānvedapañcakasaṃyutān \|\| 7 \|\|*

*ṛgvedasyākṣasūtraṃ syādyajurvedasya paṅkajam \|*  
*sāmavedasya vīṇā syādveṇuṃ dakṣiṇato nyaset \|\| 8 \|\|*

*atharvavedasya punaḥ sruksruvau kamalaṃ kare \|*  
*purāṇavedo varadaḥ sākṣasūtrakamaṇḍaluḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

5-9. Images of Brahma, Vishnu and Shiva should be made seated on lotuses with their Vahanas; and so those of the Lokapalas seated on Padmasana; and the Earth along with the lotus raised up by the Lord Varaha. All these images should be made of gold. There should also be made the images of Varuna on a seat of golden crocodile, Agni riding on a goat, Vayu seated on a black deer. All these Devas with the Deva Panchakam are to be placed within the pitcher. Ganesha is to be chosen as the Lord of Kosha. Afterwards the images should be invoked with the recitations of the prescribed Vedic hymns and then put inside the vase. The image of the Rig veda decorated with an Aksha Sutra (rosary), of the Yajurveda with a lotus, Samaveda with a guitar, and bamboos are to be placed on the right side of the pitcher. Atharvaveda with the sacrificial utensils sruk, sruva should also be placed.

## \|\| 289.10-11 \|\|

*paritaḥ sarvadhānyāni cāmarāsanadarpaṇam \|*  
*pādukopānahacchatraṃ dīpikābhūṣaṇāni ca \|\| 10 \|\|*

*śayyāṃ ca jalakumbhāṃśca pañcavarṇaṃ vitānakam \|*  
*snātvā'dhivāsanānte tu mantrametamudīrayet \|\| 11 \|\|*

10-11. Round the vase should be placed by a wise man holding Aksha sutra and kamandalu, and versed in the Puranas all the grains, Chamara, seats, mirror, sandals, shoes, ornaments, bed, vase of water, five kinds of buntings. The devotee should then recite the following mantras after Adhivasa both:

## \|\| 289.12 \|\|

*namo vaḥ sarvadevānāmādhārebhyaścarācare \|*  
*mahābhūtādhidevebhyaḥ śāntirastu śivaṃ mama \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. O thou, the support of all the Devas, and the Universe the Lord of the Mahabhutas, I salute you. Pray bring me peace and prosperity.

## \|\| 289.13 \|\|

*yasmānna kiṃcidapyasti mahābhūtairvinā kṛtam \|*  
*brahmāṇḍe sarvabhūteṣu tasmācchrīrakṣayā'stu me \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. There is no other thing in this Universe than the elements. The whole creation is made of elements. Let there be an attainment of inexhaustible wealth to me by virtue of this ordinance.

## \|\| 289.14 \|\|

*ityuccārya mahābhūtaghaṭaṃ yo vinivedayet \|*  
*sarvapāpavinirmuktaḥ sa yāti paramāṃ gatim \|\| 14 \|\|*

14 One who thus gives away the Mahabhuta-ghata is liberated from all sins and attains beatitude.

## \|\| 289.15 \|\|

*vimānenārkavarṇena pitṛbandhusamanvitaḥ \|*  
*stūyamāno varastrībhiḥ padamabhyeti vaiṣṇavam \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. In other words he goes to the kingdom of Vishnu seated in a Vimana resplendent like the Sun along with his manes and' relation and is adored by the nymphs.

## \|\| 289.16 \|\|

*ṣoḍaśaitāni yaḥ kuryānmahādānāni mānavaḥ \|*  
*na tasya punarāvṛttiriha loke'bhijāyate \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. One who performs the 16 kinds of ordinances mentioned before is not reborn.

## \|\| 289.17 \|\|

*iha paṭhati ya itthaṃ vāsudevasya pārśve sasutapitṛkalatraḥ saṃśṛṇotīha samyak \|*  
*muraripubhavane vai mandire vā'rkalakṣmyā tvamarapuravadhūbhirmodate so'pi kalpam \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. One who hears about them in company of one’s wife and sons etc., in a temple of Vishnu, also attains the realm of the Lord Vishnu, and remains there for one kalpa.

## Chapter 290

## \|\| 290.1 \|\|

*manuruvāca*  
*kalpamānaṃ tvayā proktaṃ manvantarayugeṣ̣u ca \|*  
*idānīṃ kalpanāmāni samāsātkathayācyuta \|\| 290.1 \|\|*

Manu said- “O Lord! be gracious enough to name, in brief, the Kalpas mentioned by you in course of your description of the measurement and duration of Kalpas.”

## \|\| 290.2-11 \|\|

*matsya uvāca*  
*kalpānāṃ kīrtanaṃ vakṣ̣ye mahāpātakanāśanam \|*  
*yasyānukīrtanādeva vedapuṇyena yujyate \|\| 290.2 \|\|*

*prathamaḥ śvetakalpastu dvitīyo nīlalohitaḥ \|*  
*vāmadevastṛtīyastu tato rāthaṃtaro'paraḥ \|\| 290.3 \|\|*

*rauravaḥ pañcamaḥ proktaḥ ṣ̣aṣ̣ṭho deva iti smṛtaḥ \|*  
*saptamo'tha bṛhatkalpaḥ kandarpo'ṣ̣ṭama ucyate \|\| 290.4 \|\|*

*sadyo'tha navamaḥ prokta īśāno daśamaḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*tama ekādaśaḥ proktastathā sārasvataḥ paraḥ \|\| 290.5 \|\|*

*trayodaśa udānastu gāruḍo'tha caturdaśaḥ \|*  
*kaurmaḥ pañcadaśaḥ proktaḥ paurṇamāsyāmajāyata \|\| 290.6 \|\|*

*ṣ̣oḍaśo nārasiṃhastu samānastu tato'paraḥ \|*  
*āgneyo'ṣ̣ṭādaśaḥ proktaḥ somakalpastathā paraḥ \|\| 290.7 \|\|*

*mānavo viṃśatiḥ proktastatpumāniti cāparaḥ \|*  
*vaikuṇṭhaścāparastadvallakṣ̣mīkalpastathāparaḥ \|\| 290.8 \|\|*

*caturviṃśatimaḥ proktaḥ sāvitrīkalpasaṃjñakaḥ \|*  
*pañcaviṃśastato ghoro vārāhastu tato'paraḥ \|\| 290.9 \|\|*

*saptaviṃśo'tha vairājo gaurīkalpastathā paraḥ \|*  
*māheśvarastu sa proktastripuraṃ yatra ghātitam \|\| 290.10 \|\|*

*pitṛkalpastathā'nte tu yā kuhūrbrahmaṇaḥ purā \|*  
*ityevaṃ brahmaṇo māsaḥ sarvapātakanāśanaḥ \|\| 290.11 \|\|*

Lord Matsya said— “I shall narrate the description of the Kalpas, the dispeller of all sins. Even by reciting the names of Kalpas, one gets the merit of the study of Vedas. They are-(1) Sveta, (2) Nllalohita, (3) Vamadeva, (4) Rathantrara, (5) Raurava, (6) Deva, (7) Brhat, (8) Kandarpa, (9) Sadya, (10) Isana, (11) Tama, (12) Sarasvata, (13) Udana, (14) Garuda, (15) Kaurma, (16) Narasiriiha, (17) Samana, (18) Agneya, (19) Soma, (20) Manava, (21) Tatpuman, (22) Vaikuntha, (23) Lak§ml, (24) Savitrl, (25) Ghora, (26) Varaha, (27) Vairaja, (28) Gaurl, (29) Mahesvara, in course of which Tripura was killed, (30) Pittr, at the end of which occurs Lord Brahma's Kuhu. These Kalpas form one month of 30 days of Brahma, each Kalpa forming a day; and one who hears them is freed from all sins.

## \|\| 290.12 \|\|

*ādāveva hi māhātmyaṃ yasminyasya vidhīyate \|*  
*tasya kalpasya tannāma vihitaṃ brahmaṇā purā \|\| 290.12 \|\|*

The kalpas have been named by the Lord Brahma after the names of the significant events taking place in them and after the name of who had the highest glorious career in the beginning of each.

## \|\| 290.13 \|\|

*saṃkīrṇāstāmasāścaiva rājasāḥ sāttvikāstathā \|*  
*rajastamomayāstadvadete triṃśadudāhṛtāḥ \|\| 290.13 \|\|*

These 30 Kalpas are divided into Sanklma, Tamas, Rajas, Sattvik and are classified according to Rajastama.

## \|\| 290.14 \|\|

*saṃkīrṇeṣ̣u sarasvatyāḥ pitriṇāṃ vyuṣ̣ṭirucyate \|*  
*agneḥ śivasya māhātmyaṃ tāmaseṣ̣u divākare \|*  
*rājaseṣ̣u ca māhātmyamadhikaṃ brahmaṇaḥ smṛtam \|\| 290.14 \|\|*

In the Sanklma Kalpas, Sarasvatl and the Pittrs are glorified; the Tamasa Kalpas are endowed with the glories of Agni and Siva. During the Rajas Kalpa, the glory of Brahma is prominent.

## \|\| 290.15-16 \|\|

*yasminkalpe tu yatproktaṃ purāṇaṃ brahmaṇā purā \|*  
*tasya tasya tu māhātmya tatsvarūpeṇa varṇyate \|\| 290.15 \|\|*

*sāttvikeṣ̣vadhika tadvadviṣ̣ṇormāhātmyamuttamam \|*  
*tathaiva yogasaṃsiddhā gamiṣ̣yanti parāṃ gatim \|\| 290.16 \|\|*

The Puranas as revealed by Brahma in each Kalpa are glorified in the corresponding Kalpa. During the Satvika Kalpas, the glory of Vi$nu is most prominent and in course of the same Kalpas men advanced in the practice of yoga for attaining emancipation.

## \|\| 290.17-19 \|\|

*brāhmaṃ pādmamimaṃ yastu paṭhetparvaṇi parvaṇi \|*  
*tasya dharme matirbrahmā karoti vipulāṃ śriyam \|\| 290.17 \|\|*

*yastu dadyādimānkṛtvā haimānparvaṇi parvaṇi \|*  
*brahmaviṣ̣ṇupure vāsaṃ munibhiḥ pūjyate divi \|\| 290.18 \|\|*

*sarvapāpakṣ̣ayakaraṃ kalpadānaṃ yato bhavet \|*  
*munirūpāṃstataḥ kṛtvā dadyātkalpānvicakṣ̣aṇaḥ \|\| 290.19 \|\|*

One who reads Brahma Purana and Padma Purana on the occasion of each festival, is granted abundance of wealth and prosperity and Dharma by the Lord Brahma. He who hears these Puranas at every festival and gives away things made of gold on the occasion of each festival, goes to the realm of Visnu or Brahma where he is venerated by the seers. It drives away all his sins. One should give away the images of the Kalpas in the form of Munis.

## \|\| 290.20-22 \|\|

*purāṇasaṃhitā ceyaṃ tava bhūpa mayoditā \|*  
*sarvapāpaharā nityamārogyaśrīphalapradā \|\| 290.20 \|\|*

*brahmasaṃvatsaraśatādekāha śaivamucyate \|*  
*śivavarṣ̣aśatādekaṃ nimeṣ̣aṃ vaiṣ̣ṇavaṃ viduḥ \|\| 290.21 \|\|*

*yadā sa viṣ̣ṇurjāgarti tadedaṃ ceṣ̣ṭate jagat \|*  
*yadā svapiti śāntātmā tadā sarvaṃ nimīlati \|\| 290.22 \|\|*

О king! this Purana Samhita has been thus described to you, which is the dispeller of all sins and the giver of health and wealth. Twenty years of Brahma are equal to one day of Siva, and hundred years of Siva to one wink of the eye of Visnu. When Visnu awakes the universe becomes conscious, and when He reposes it is annihilated.

## \|\| 290.23-24 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*ityuktvā devadeveśo matsyarūpī janārdanaḥ \|*  
*paśyatāṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ tatraivāntaradhīyata \|\| 290.23 \|\|*

*vaivasvato hi bhagavānvisṛjya vividhāḥ prajāḥ \|*  
*svāntaraṃ pālayāmāsa mārtaṇḍakulavardhanaḥ \|\| 290.24 \|\|*

Suta said- Having said these words, Lord of gods in the form of Matsya disappeared before all creatures then and there. In this Manvantara, Bhagavan Vaivasvata Manu, the scion of the family of Sun, is ruling after creating various beings.

## \|\| 290.25 \|\|

*yasya manvantaraṃ caitadadhunā cānuvartate \|*  
*puṇyaṃ pavitrametadvaḥ kathitaṃ matsyabhāṣ̣itam \|*  
*purāṇaṃ sarvaśāstrāṇāṃ yadetanmūrdhni saṃsthitam \|\| 290.25 \|\|*

His manvantara is going on unto this day. I have narrated the most sacred and auspicious Matsya Purarta to you. It is established on the head of all the Sastras.”

## Chapter 291

## \|\| 291.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*etadvaḥ kathitaṃ sarvaṃ yaduktaṃ viśvarūpiṇā \|*  
*mātsyaṃ purāṇamakhilaṃ dharmakāmārthasādhanam \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Suta said: — “I have related to you, O, sages! the whole of the Matsya Purana according to my intellect, as it was revealed by the Lord before the king 'Vaivasvata Manu for Dharma, Kama, and Artha.

## \|\| 291.2-4 \|\|

*yatrā’dau manusaṃvādo brahmāṇḍakathanaṃ tathā \|*  
*sāṃkhyaṃ śārīrakaṃ proktaṃ caturmukhamukhodbhavam \|\| 2 \|\|*

*devāsurāṇāmutpattirmārutotpattireva ca \|*  
*madanadvādaśī tadvallokapālābhipūjanam \|\| 3 \|\|*

*manvantarāṇāmuddeśo vainyarājābhivarṇanam \|*  
*sūryavaivasvatotpattirbudhasaṃgamanaṃ tathā \|\| 4 \|\|*

2-4. It begins with the discourses of Manu and the Lord, known as Manusamvad and deals with the following subjects in successive order, viz. — the history of Brahmanda, the Shariraka Samkhya as described by Brahma, the birth of the Devas, demons and the Maruts. The descriptions of the Madanadvadashi ordinance, the ways of the worship of the Lokapalas, the description of the Manvantaras, the history of king Vena, the birth ^ of the Sun and Vaivasvata and the coming of Buddha.

## \|\| 291.5-6 \|\|

*pitṛvaṃśānukathanaṃ śrāddhakālastathaiva ca \|*  
*pitṛtīrthapravāsaśca somotpattistathaiva ca \|\| 5 \|\|*

*kīrtanaṃ somavaṃśasya yayāti caritaṃ tathā \|*  
*kārtavīryasya māhātmyaṃ vṛṣṇivaṃśānukīrtanam \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. Then it deals with the families of the manes, the times of performing Shraddha, Pitritirtha Pravasa, the birth of the moon, the history of Yayati, the glory of Svamikartika, the history of the Vrishni and Yadava houses.

## \|\| 291.7-9 \|\|

*bhṛguśāpastathā viṣṇordaityaśāpastathaiva ca \|*  
*kīrtanaṃ puruṣeśasya vaṃśo hautāśanastathā \|\| 7 \|\|*

*purāṇakīrtanaṃ tadvatkriyāyogastathaiva ca \|*  
*vrataṃ nakṣatrasaṃkhyākaṃ mārtaṇḍaśayanaṃ tathā \|\| 8 \|\|*

*kṛṣṇāṣṭamīvrataṃ tadvadro hiṇīcandra saṃjñitam \|*  
*taḍāgavidhimāhātmyaṃ pādapotsarga eva ca \|\| 9 \|\|*

7-9. The curse of Bhrigu, the curses of Vishnu on the Daityas, the glory of Lord Purushesha, the history of Agni family, the names and the bulk of the Puranas, Kriya Yoga, the Nekshatva Samkhyaka Vrata, Martanda Sayana Vrata, Krishnashtami Vrata, the Rohini and Moon’s ordinances, the ways of laying out tanks, &c., and of planting trees.

## \|\| 291.10-11 \|\|

*saubhāgyaśayanaṃ tadvadagastyavratameva ca \|*  
*tathā'nantatṛtīyā tu rasakalyāṇinī tathā \|\| 10 \|\|*

*ādrā rna!ndakarī tadvadvrataṃ sārasvataṃ punaḥ \|*  
*uparāgābhiṣekaśca saptamīsnapanaṃ punaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

10-11. The descriptions of Saubhagyadayana Vrata, Agastya Vrata, Anantatritiyn Vrata, Rasakalyani Vrata, Ardranandakari Vrata, Sarasvata Vrata.

## \|\| 291.12-13 \|\|

*bhīmākhyā dvādaśī tadvadanaṅgaśayanaṃ tathā \|*  
*aśūnyaśayanaṃ tadvattathaivāṅgārakavratam \|\| 12 \|\|*

*saptamīsaptakaṃ tadvadviśokadvādaśī tathā \|*  
*merupradānaṃ daśadhā grahaśāntistathaiva ca \|\| 13 \|\|*

12-13. As well as about the Uparagabhishekavrata, Saptamisvpana Vrata, Bhimadvadashi, Anamgashayana, Ashunyashayana Vrata, Amgara, the seven Saptamis, Vishokadvadashi, ordinances and the ways of giving away the gifts of the Sumeru tenfold and performing the worship of Navagrahas.

## \|\| 291.14-16 \|\|

*grahasvarūpakathanaṃ tathā śivacaturdaśī \|*  
*tathā sarvaphalatyāgaḥ sūryavāravrataṃ tathā \|\| 14 \|\|*

*saṃkrāntisnapanaṃ tadvadvibhūtidvādaśīvratam \|*  
*ṣaṣṭivratānāṃ māhātmyaṃ tathā snānavidhikramaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*prayāgasya tu māhātmyaṃ bhuvanasyānukīrtanam \|*  
*ailāśramavrataṃ tadvaddvīpalokānukīrtanam \|\| 16 \|\|*

14-16. The form of the nine Grahas, about the Shivachaturdashi, Sarvaphala-tyaga Vrata, Samkramti Vibhatidvadashi, Shashtivrata, ordinances, the benefits of the 60 ordinances, the kinds of baths, the glories of Prayaga, the names of all the sacred places, the benefits of Pailashrama, the description of the dvipas and the Lokas;

## \|\| 291.17 \|\|

*sūryacandra gatistadvadādityarathavarṇanam \|*  
*tathā'ntarikṣacāraśca dhruvamāhātmyameva ca \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. The description of the movements of the San and Moon, on the chariot of the Sun; on the celestial luminous bodies, the glory: of Dhruva, the description of the realms of the Devas and Tripurasura;

## \|\| 291.18-20 \|\|

*bhuvanāni surendrā ṇāṃ tripurāghoṣaṇaṃ tathā \|*  
*pitṛpracāramāhātmyaṃ manvantaravinirṇayaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*vajrāṅgasya tu saṃbhūtistārakotpattireva ca \|*  
*tārakāsuramāhātmyaṃ brahmadevānumantraṇam \|\| 19 \|\|*

*pārvatīsaṃbhavastadvattathā śivatapovanam \|*  
*anaṅgadehadāhastu ratiśokastathaiva ca \|\| 20 \|\|*

18-20. The benefits of offerings of Pinda to the manes, the durations of the periods of the Manvantaras, the birth and greatness of the demon Vajramga, the birth of Tarakasura, the glory of Tarakasura, Divanumantrana, the birth of Parvati, the asceticism of Shiva, the burning of Cupid, the lament of Rati, the going of the goddess Parvati to the place of asceticism and the joy of f3iva;

## \|\| 291.21-22 \|\|

*gaurītapovanaṃ tadvadviśvanāthaprasādanam \|*  
*pārvatī ṛṣisaṃvādastathaivodvāhamaṅgalam \|\| 21 \|\|*

*kumārasaṃbhavastadvatkumāravijayastathā \|*  
*tārakasya vadho ghoro narasiṃhopavarṇanam \|\| 22 \|\|*

21-22. The dialogue of Parvati and the sage, the rejoicings of the marriage of Parvati, the birth of Svamikartika. the conquering of Tarakasura and his death, the description of Nrisimha, the coming into being of the Brahmanda out of the lotus, the history of the annihilation, the death of Andhaka;

## \|\| 291.23-24 \|\|

*padmodbhavavisargastu tathaivāndhakaghātanam \|*  
*vārāṇasyāstu māhātmyaṃ narmadāyāstathaiva ca \|\| 23 \|\|*

*pravarānukramastadvatpitṛgāthānukīrtanam \|*  
*tathobhayamukhīdānaṃ dānaṃ kṛṣṇājinasya ca \|\| 24 \|\|*

23-24. The glory of Kashi, Narmada, the description of Gotras and Pravaras, the history of the manes, about the giving away of cows, and the skin of a black deer, the history of Savitri, the duties of kings;

## \|\| 291.25-26 \|\|

*tathā sāvitr! yupākhyānaṃ rājadharmāstathaiva ca \|*  
*yātrānimittakathanaṃ svapnamāṅgalyakīrtanam \|\| 25 \|\|*

*vāmanasya tu māhātmyaṃ tathaivātha varāhajam \|*  
*kṣīrodamathanaṃ tadvatkālakūṭābhiśāsanam \|\| 26 \|\|*

25-26. The times of setting out on a journey, the fruits and effects of dreams, the glory of Vamana, the history if Varaha, the churning of the milky ocean.

## \|\| 291.27-28 \|\|

*devāsuravimardaśca vāstuvidyāstathaiva ca \|*  
*pratimālakṣaṇaṃ tadvaddevatārādhanaṃ tataḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

*prāsādalakṣaṇaṃ tadvanmaṇḍapānāṃ tu lakṣaṇam \|*  
*bhaviṣyadrā janirdeśo mahādānānukīrtanam \|*  
*kalpānukīrtanaṃ tadvadgranthānukramaṇī tathā \|\| 28 \|\|*

27-28. The drinking of poison by Shiva; the fight between the Devas and the Asuras, worship of the Devas, on the characteristics of palaces, pandals, and housebuilding, the forms of the temples and pandals, the history of Puru dynasty, the narration of the coming sovereigns, the description of the 16 gifts such as Tuladana, etc., the names of the Kalpas, which completes the index of the Purina.

## \|\| 291.29 \|\|

*etatpavitramāyuṣyametatkīrtivivardhanam \|*  
*etatpavitraṃ kalyāṇaṃ mahāpāpaharaṃ śubham \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. This the Matsya Purana is most sacred. It is the giver of long life, fame, prosperity and dispeller of all sins.

## \|\| 291.30 \|\|

*asmātpurāṇātsukṛtaṃ narāṇāṃ tīrthāvalīnāmavagāhanānām \|*  
*samastadharmācaraṇodbhavānāṃ sadaiva lābhaśca mahāphalānām \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. One who reads even one pada of this Puranam is liberated from all sins and attains the realm of the Lord Vishnu where one enjoys all bliss after getting a form as handsome as that of Cupid.
